THE HOOK AND THE HEW is basically guard breaking: the power to pull a man forward off his feet and out of his guard with the axe, and cut what the pull has opened. It is the wall reaching out, and it works because she is the one thing in the exchange that does not move.
Capabilities
The bearded war-axe does two things, and she does them as one. The beard goes over the rim of a shield, or behind a knee, or round a lance-haft, and she pulls with her whole weight from the heels. A pull is the one load Petralon does not answer, because nothing ever asked a foundation to hold on, so she does not pull with the arm at all. She sets her Anchoring through the heels and lets her whole weight fall back like a counterweight on a rope, with the haft as the rope. The man’s shield is levered off his body over its own rim, his weight goes forward past his toes with his feet still behind him, and for that half-step nothing under his collarbone is braced against anything.
The edge lands there, on collarbone or neck or arm, before he has his feet back. Both damages are real and separate: the pull wrenches the shield arm and takes his balance, and the hew lands on a body that could not stiffen to meet it. The collarbone is the strut that props the shoulder off the chest, and on a body pulled forward with nothing braced beneath it, it breaks clean under an edge that mail alone would have turned. The hooked spike at the top finishes what the edge did not.
Applications

Levering a shield off the man behind it
Hooking a knee or a lance-haft to bring a man forward
Breaking the collarbone, opening the neck or taking the arm on a body that cannot brace
Finishing with the hooked spike

Associations

Petralon, for the set of her heels only; the pull and the hew are honest steel
The Body Path
The bearded war-axe, which she taught herself when her father said no
Drilled, and learned by living it

Limitations

It takes about three percent of her reserve to set her Anchoring through the pull and the hew
The hook needs a rim, a limb or a haft to catch
Its tell is the axe-beard going over the rim
A man who lets go of his shield when he feels the beard takes the pull out of it
A shield with no rim to catch gives it nothing

THE GREY FILE · School Art, Greymane
THE GREY FILE is basically shield wall formation: the power to lock a line of shields into one thing that takes each blow down through every pair of boots at once. It is the school art of the Greymanes, taught, and she held the Thornwall’s north face with it.
Capabilities
Greymane shields lock rim to rim, and a line of Shieldwardens stands like the ridge it is named for. The file is the same arch as the art’s, laid on its side. The iron lip on each Greymane rim locks into the next, so a blow on one shield is shared sideways into its neighbors and goes down through every pair of boots in the line. She calls it as an order, numbers first.
Applications

Holding a wall face or a section against an assault
Sharing one shield’s blow across the whole line

Associations

Petralon
The Body Path, with the walked Fate Path’s share for the line
The Greymane yard, where it is taught, and the iron lip on each file shield

Limitations

Its limit is its ends: an arch stands only while something holds its two ends, which masons call the abutments, and a file has none
The man on the end has one neighbor where the rest have two, and the load that reaches him has only him to go through
The file pays for it, and she does not
Its tell is the shields locking rim to rim
It is beaten by breaking the file’s end and rolling it up

SHIELD-HANDS · House Drill, Greymane
SHIELD-HANDS is basically sacrificial blocking: the power to put her own hands between a blow and her heart, and let them be spent. It is the yard’s drill for a Shieldwarden caught without a shield.
Capabilities
The hands come down crossed in front of the breast, palms out, a wall of two hands, and take what was aimed at the heart. It is the shield-line’s first lesson done with nothing on the arm: put something of yours between the blow and the thing that must not be hit, and let it be spent. No working is shown in it.
Applications

Taking a strike meant for the heart when she has no shield
Crossed against a claw strike meant to take her heart out, held by the throat with burned hands, the claws came through the palms and reached her side, a rip as long as a thumb over the bottom rib on the left, and no deeper

Associations

House Greymane’s drill, taught in the yard
No Wellspring and no working

Limitations

It takes no reserve; its price is the hands
Flesh is not a shield and stops only what it can be spent on
Its tell is the hands crossing
A point fine enough to go through a palm keeps going

Releases
STONEFAST · Setting the Stone · First Release, Greymane
STONEFAST is basically immovability: the power to lock her whole body into one column that a blow cannot knock back. It is the house release, called aloud as one flat word, the way she gives a report.
Capabilities
She sinks her heels, and Fixatio and Petralon lock every joint from the shield-boss down to the heel into one column, so that a blow’s weight goes down through her into the ground and the ground does not give. As a Body release it transforms the flesh and what a blow does to it: set, she is one stacked column from boss to heel, and a blow has to move the ground to move her.
A stroke from a fighter many Stages over her, which the road under her could not take, came out through the air onto her shield and down the column, and STONEFAST held it, and her heels never left the ground. The ground left with her, plowed back eight paces in two long furrows, still locked from the shield-boss to the heel. The art did everything it claims. The road was the weak stone, and she was not.
Applications

Standing under a blow that would otherwise knock her back
Holding in front of someone against a far stronger fighter for as long as the ground lasts

Associations

Petralon, with the Fixatio the house’s release names
The Fixatio is the house’s lens, carried in its drill and never harmonized by her, so it fires at the away rate
The Body Path
House Greymane, whose release it is

Limitations

It takes about four percent of her reserve to set, and it holds as long as she does not move her feet
The feet are its limit: set, she cannot step
Its tells are the rust-and-gold aura coming up off her shoulders like heat off a forge, and dust and grit settling in a ring round her boots
It promises the heels and nothing past them: when the ground itself gives, she goes with it still locked, upright and whole, and stops where the ground stops
It is beaten by pulling her, lifting her or fighting her on ice
Ice, a lift or a pull takes the footing away without breaking anything, and then the column has nothing to stand on and comes apart at once

characters/ability-accounts/bett-bodkin-.title: Bett Bodkin — Abilities in full
characters/ability-accounts/bett-bodkin-.content:
Card: Bett Bodkin
Techniques
NEEDLEWORK · Signature art, plain yard skill under her own colors
NEEDLEWORK is basically enhanced precision: the power to stab as fast as a blink and stop before the skin. She has no Traits; what she has is twenty years of one stop.
Capabilities
The thrust goes straight from the shoulder to the button at a speed the eye does not catch, and it stops a barleycorn short because she fires every pulling muscle against every throwing one at the last instant. That is the whole art, and it is a real thing a body can do. A fencer’s arm is thrown by one set of muscles and reined by the set across the joint, and when both sets fire together the elbow and shoulder lock stiff as a braced gate, so the arm’s whole speed is eaten inside the arm and never reaches the point. Anybody can do it slowly. Bett does it at full speed, and the stop lands where she chose to the width of a grain of barley.
There is no charge to read, because she sets nothing. The iron hangs point-down by her knee, she stands with her weight so exactly over her feet that neither foot gives her away, and she reads the other fighter’s start, a lifting stroke by the hips or a rake by the hands, and is in through the opening before the stroke is half done. She does it with her colors held down. The soul’s own Essence, which would lie on the body like a coat and make flesh harder than flesh, is kept under the hide, so the candidate in front of her fights her body alone, and the yard sees a pale thin woman with a blunt sword.
Her guard is not a choice. A fighter’s body keeps a guard of its own under all the holding, and it comes up faster than any decision when something touches the place every fencer covers first. Touched at the throat, hers brings the whole pewter coat up at once. Because a reflex has no time to choose a place, it comes up everywhere in the same instant, crown to boots, over the iron and the old buckler too, as thin and as even as wax on a candle. Under the touch it goes hard and very slightly brighter, a thimble over the one place the needle came, and the point finds nothing to bite and slides off. The Measurewrights put it down to pressure, the same push spread over a fingertip’s width pressing less than it would on a pinprick, and they have the how much of it right. The coat comes up cold, with tin and cold water on the air, and every bit of tin in the yard flashes with it for a breath.
Applications

Running the yard test: three passes, each ended on a touch or a word
Taking a candidate’s measure with two stops placed like a tailor’s shoulder pins, so that she knows the width of them
Turning a point off her own throat and past her shoulder

Techniques

NEEDLEWORK! - a straight thrust from the shoulder to the button, faster than the eye, stopped a barleycorn short, one on each collarbone a finger in from the shoulder point; she says the name flat, like a sum
THIMBLE - touch her throat and the whole pewter coat is up before she has decided anything, hardest where she was touched, and the point skates off it

Associations

No Wellspring is in it; what it runs on is twenty years of drill and her own colors
The Form is a Strike; her Path is not given
She came by it living, twenty years on Wolstan Kemp’s line
Her colors are thin bright pewter, new-cast tin-gray with a cold blue light like a winter river, and a winter-morning cold comes off her
The rebated yard-iron, its grip cracked from the cross to the pommel by her own clench and bound in red thread
The old steel fist-buckler, which is hers and not bonded

Limitations

The stop is the dearer half of every thrust, and it is harder than the thrust
With her colors in the arm the thrust is far faster and the hand far stronger, and the stop has to eat all of that in the same barleycorn; when it does, the button hangs shaking a barleycorn off the collarbone and the speed goes back down the iron into her fist
Lit, the stop is paid by what she grips, and it breaks whatever she is holding before it breaks the terms: it can crack her iron’s grip from the cross to the pommel, and past a wooden grip the next thing in that line is her own hand
That failure is the art’s own and has nothing to do with any Wellspring
With her colors down NEEDLEWORK! spends nothing; THIMBLE spends a breath of reserve, by reflex
NEEDLEWORK! has no tell worth the name: the only warning anybody gets is the word, said flat, and it comes with the thrust
THIMBLE has no tell either, being a reflex; afterward, putting her colors back down, the jaw muscle jumps and sets, a flush climbs her throat, her collar sweats dark, and she says one carter’s word
THIMBLE turns a point, and it was never shown against weight
A touch that asks nothing of her skin has already made her show
She does not show her colors on the line until her body does it for her, and she has been made to show once in twenty years, by four feet of reach she had not measured
NEEDLEWORK! is beaten by a move with no start to read, such as a yardwand slid from the ell notch to the ferrule, with reach she has not measured

characters/ability-accounts/cozbi-mahuo-.title: Cozbi Mahuo — Abilities in full
characters/ability-accounts/cozbi-mahuo-.content:
Card: Cozbi Mahuo
THE TABLE FOR THE DEAD
THE TABLE FOR THE DEAD (제사상 · Jesasang) is basically paradox manipulation: the power to make one place where a thing both is and is not, and to hold it there until the world gives way. He lays a place at his table for somebody who is not there, and they come and sit down. It is his signature art, and his Ability and his three summoning arts are this one idea. It has made him one of the great summoners the Continuum has ever recorded, the one called the God of Summons.
Capabilities
Every piece of it is the same act at a different size. A place set at a table for a dead woman is that act done with a cup. THE SEAM is that act done with the air, a point that is a sink and a source together. A Founding is that act done with a person: someone who never existed is given a place to exist in first, and then stands up in it. A compact is a wild will that is free and held at once. A conscript is a soul that has died and is still standing in the room. It is also why he speaks of his dead in the present tense; that habit and the art are one thing, and the Continuum entered it at Principality under its own name, Antithesis.
Summoning is a three-plane crossing, a vessel shaped on the Physical Plane, an identity donated on the Soul Plane and a recognition held on the Plane of Fate, and he pays at all three. He is a Spirit Path summoner, so the work is authored and mostly spent through the Essence Core, at the Ferryman’s rung, where the Veil opens and the dead know a man by name. The vessel is grown by Eidolyn, the Shaping Mind, whose idea is a thing imagined so hard that it stands up and has to answer for itself, and whose operation is coagulation: what is imagined is set solid along the pattern the maker holds in mind. Frost ferning across a windowpane along the ice already there is the nearest picture of it, and the Measurewrights call it templated growth. In Eidolyn the pattern is his intent, and what he holds clearly comes out as real hair and bone and a beating heart. The self is carried by Anima Spirare, the Soul’s Breath and the Mahuo house current, whose idea is the breath of the whole, a body that remembers being whole and answers a small hurt with everything it has, and whose operation is fermentation, the whole quickened round one small start, so a small donated self catches and fills the whole vessel. Physicians know the shape of it from blood, which clots as a cascade in which each step sets off many of the next, and takes up breath faster the more it already carries. On the Plane of Fate he has no grip at all, no blood and no blessing, so every compact and every charter is written out of his own share, the way a vow is, and pulls nothing down. Under all three stands Mortalis, the Black Gate, whose idea is ending looked at squarely and understood as a passage with its own law, and whose operation is dissolution, a thing’s hold on what it is loosed lawfully and in order. He knows that gate as a road, and works its edge the other way, keeping the spending going in what should have stopped. The Measurewrights call a living body a structure held far from equilibrium by constant spending, and death the spending stopping.
Every summoner pays twice: once in Essence for the form and again for the self that animates it, a piece of their own Core lent out and strained. Cozbi pays the first in his own coin and the second in other people’s, harvested soul-fragment spent as if it were his, and founds beings with cores of their own besides. That is why he can field a host where other masters field a squad, and it is, in plain terms, the crime the Zettari–Mahou Accord names. Every other summoner in the Accord’s register works from a roster. He works from a gap: the Accord’s list of sealed forms has been out of date for four hundred years, and he drafts to the problem. The Commission’s assessors gave up trying to list his forms after the third year, and one of them wrote in the margin of the file, in a hand that was not entirely steady, that he founds a being the way a host lays a table, for exactly the guest who is coming.
Applications

Fighting at the length of his table, through whoever he has seated at it
Putting a founded hero or a drafted wall where the fight needs it faster than legs could
Taking the ground from under whoever his guest is about to strike
Opening the plate a breath before the guest’s edge arrives, so that the cut that kills is somebody else’s and the wound it goes through is his
Fielding a host where other masters field a squad

Techniques

ANTITHESIS - the idea in a point of air, a sink and a source together
THE FOUNDING - the idea given a body: someone who never existed, given a place to exist in and standing up in it
THE BOUND WILD - a wild will that is free and held at once
THE CONSCRIPTS - souls that have died and are still standing in the room

Associations

Antithesis, his own registered law, which runs on no Wellspring
Eidolyn, the Shaping Mind, grows the vessel along the pattern of his intent
Anima Spirare, the Soul’s Breath and the Mahuo house current, carries the self into the vessel
Mortalis, the Black Gate, keeps the spending going in what should have stopped
The Spirit Path does the work, through the Essence Core; the Fate Path, which he walks, carries the compacts and charters; his Body is only Studied
His best ground is the south’s own: the iron hills and salt pans, and any place where the dead have soured a site
He has no Releases, though his Stage has long since opened both the Releases his Spirit road allows, and he carries no weapon
His guests, compacts and conscripts work at their own Grade and add nothing to his
He says every name at a host’s volume, pleasantly, as if announcing the next course, and will explain any of them at length and with real pride

Limitations

Every guest is one more thread out of his own chest, paid for every second it stands
He does not sleep, cannot keep food down on campaign, and his own table is wearing him to bones
He has no blow for any of it to ride; it rides his guests’ blows
Nine parts in ten of what he spends reach the work, which is his yield, and the lost tenth is paid in his Core, showing as no more than a faint warmth at his collar
The charge can always be read, and he does not trouble to hide it
His resolve holds every seam, leash and thread, so the way to beat him is to strike the host and not the guests
It is also beaten by counting the threads, collapsing the boundary, finding the line the charter forgot, or staying beyond the gradient
Mortalis fails by its flaw: a soul that has stopped fearing the gate has stopped holding out against it, and he cools toward the boundary he stands at, which the Measurewrights call equilibration
Anima Spirare fails by its flaw: the whole answers a small hurt with everything it has and cannot answer with less, so when it loses the place of the hurt it answers everywhere at once until he bleeds from the gums, the nose and the eyes; the Measurewrights call it disseminated activation
Eidolyn fails by its flaw: a thing imagined hard enough to stand up stands up exactly as it was imagined, so every flaw in his memory is cast into the body, which the Mahuo founders called the defect of the template and feared more than any enemy
Antithesis fails by turning inward

Ability
ANTITHESIS (상극 · Sanggeuk) · Ability, his registered law
ANTITHESIS is basically attraction and repulsion: the power to hold one point where a pull and its exact opposite are both true and neither yields. It is the one phenomenon his whole architecture is built around. Everything he borrows from other souls is coin; Antithesis is the root current of his own.
Capabilities
Sanggeuk is the old word for two forces that overcome each other, as water quenches fire. In Cozbi it is no contest between two things. It is one place where a thing and its contradiction are both true, and Cozbi is Antithesis. He holds a single point in the air beside him where one claim has two opposite faces at once: an attraction and its exact negation, a sink and a source sharing one location.
The two claims are laid one over the other there, and because neither yields they do not cancel; they answer at different reaches. The pull carries far and the push stays close, so matter far out feels mostly the pull and matter close in feels mostly the push. The Measurewrights draw it as a potential and its opposite falling away with distance at different rates, and reach for the way two grains of anything draw together across a gap and shove apart when pressed too close.
What breaks a thing in it is being made to answer both claims at once, one face of it drawn in and the other driven off. Plate is made to stand against a push that comes all one way and has no answer to being drawn two ways along its own thickness, so it parts along its weakest line. The Measurewrights call it a tidal gradient and the parting shear: the same difference from one side of a thing to the other, they say, that raises a tide and, close to a heavy enough body, pulls a moon to rubble. It is active and rooted, his own and neither conscripted nor borrowed, and it scales with his resolve and not his reserve, which is why an opponent who has beaten every borrowed soul on his structure has not yet met it.
Applications

Parting armor that has nothing to resist with, since it is split and not pushed
Taking a blade out of a hand, or pulling a charging fighter onto his guard
Flinging a host’s bodies where he needs them, and moving his own constructs faster than their legs
Removing ground from under a fighter, collapsing a stair, or closing a gap without moving
Holding a founded core together

Techniques

THE SEAM (이음새 · Ieumsae) - a pinprick in the air at his shoulder that swallows the light and shines at once; everything else he does is hung on it
THE CONTRADICTION (모순 · Mosun) - named for the old story of the spear that pierces any shield and the shield that stops any spear; where the seam’s pull and push overlap, a breastplate is not dented, it is parted like bread, and at the smallest scale a thing that meets its own negation is let go entirely, which the Measurewrights call annihilation, in the loose sense, and reckon as stored mass-energy set free
TIDES (조류 · Joryu) - the same two claims used gently: anything between him and a held seam is dragged, then thrown, so the sword leaves a hand and goes to him, the charging man arrives early and off his feet, and his own guests cross the yard thrown
THE FOLD (접기 · Jeopgi) - a seam drawn out along a line, a door that opens in one place and closes in another, so the stair a fighter stood on is somewhere else and he is a pace nearer without having moved; it scales with how much space the seam is stretched across

Associations

His own law, registered by the Continuum at Principality; no Wellspring
The Spirit Path: held in the Core as a registered law, written there, and what it does to matter leaves by the Shell
THE FOUNDING, whose cores it holds together
His resolve, which it scales with

Limitations

He can hold one seam comfortably and a few with strain
It has no price in reserve, and it tears at whatever holds it: the seam’s two faces pull on his own attention, and a flinch is a collapse
Its tell is in the light: it bends toward the point and away from it at once, so the seam looks like a pinprick that both swallows and shines
The air tastes of struck flint, and there is a faint ring in the ears that the Measurewrights put down to a pressure gradient
When he is angry the light bends at his shoulder with no seam called
A seam is held by concentration, so a fighter who strikes at his resolve and not at the seam makes it lapse
Distance beats the gradient; stay beyond its reach
It fails by turning inward: a point that holds both claims will, if his hold slips, hold both claims in him

Techniques
THE FOUNDING (건국 · Geonguk) · Signature Technique
THE FOUNDING is basically life creation: the power to make a small world with a wall round it and a person inside it who has a heart of their own and knows what they are for. It is the Mahuo house art and runs in the blood.
Capabilities
A summon at this level is a founding and no projection. He creates a small Realm, a micro-world with its own boundary, and in it a being that exists as a semi-independent presence with a core, a shell and an attraction layer of its own. It thinks, adapts, feels and persists beyond his immediate attention. It is the art behind eidolons that are people.
He calls it with one quiet word in Common, “Summoning,” and it is a building more than a calling, in three steps anyone watching can follow: the boundary, then the core, then the charter. The near-white of his aura sharpens at its fringe to arterial red, like red glass held up to the sun, a black-violet seam opens under it where Eidolyn runs, and the boundary of the little Realm unfolds with the seam’s own bent light round its edge, because it is Antithesis that holds a founded core together. A founded heartbeat is heard from the wrong side of a door, with a fine crystal ticking under it as the shape is laid down.
Stage XII is the minimum for the art, and Stage XIV is the usual gate for genuine autonomy. He founds autonomous beings at XIII because Antithesis gives the founding a core that holds without recognition from a Hollow Throne.
Applications

A warden to hold a gate, a general to hold a field, a scholar to answer questions
A second self in a fight: a being that fights as the hero it was written to be, with judgment he does not have to supply, which leaves his attention for the point at his shoulder
Dari, the elders’ nine-tailed fox of the crossings, founded in the Post’s yard and chartered to follow and protect his nephew Hiromi, serve him, and report every great change

Techniques

The Boundary (경계 · Gyeonggye) - the Realm is a cavity with a wall, a doorway of a place where there had been no place; a being needs somewhere to be real, so he builds the place first, and inside the wall his law holds
The Core Analog (핵 · Haek) - a point of his own Crystal pressed into the middle of it the way a potter presses a thumb into clay to start the hollow, giving the being a core, shell and attraction analog of its own
The Charter (칙령 · Chikryeong) - the being’s purpose, written into it in the moment of its making; it obeys its charter and not his word of the moment, and a charter written from a story carries the story whole

Associations

The Spirit Path, with the walked Fate Path for the Realm’s claim and the charter
Eidolyn makes the body, Anima Spirare the core, and Antithesis holds it
The Mahuo blood: a child of the house can raise a crude one
He came to it by living it

Limitations

Founding takes about a third of a percent of his reserve, and keeping a founded being lasts about ten hours from full
The keeping is one more thread from his chest to its heart, so a guest who stays is a weight he carries every second
He founds one, or two with strain, and only when a fight deserves it
The being’s coherence is his, and if the Realm’s boundary cracks, the strain lands on him
A founded being cannot leave the wall without him, which is both leash and shelter; outside it the being is a stranger
Whatever he forgot to write in the charter is a gap in the being
Every flaw in his memory is cast into the body: a child’s crude founding shows a wing a hand too long where the memory was surer of one side
Dari never once did a thing the way she was asked, and he wrote her that way knowing it; her upkeep is a thread down the Kessen road, less than he recovers and one more thing to carry
Its tell is a small Realm unfolding around a boundary, with a being that has a core of its own standing in it
It is beaten by collapsing the boundary, outlasting the founding’s stability, or finding the line the charter forgot
It is the most dangerous form, because a founded being with enough internal coherence begins to resist dissolution: he has made a person and cannot always unmake it

THE BOUND WILD (야생의 결박 · Yasaeng-ui Gyeolbak) · Signature Technique
THE BOUND WILD is basically contract binding: the power to bind a living power by a sealed compact and call it by its seal. He binds beasts, Well-born creatures and the great creatures of the Bestiary’s Summoned and Bound.
Capabilities
Binding ties the creature’s state to a leash he holds, so that it answers his hand the way a hawk answers the glove; the Measurewrights call it a coupled system. A compact he has sealed is powered by the creature’s own Essence, so he pays only the leash. Unlike his drafts, a sealed compact gets cheaper each time it answers, because recognition accumulates, so his oldest compacts cost him almost nothing and answer almost at once. He is the rare drafter who keeps a standing roster alongside an infinite catalog.
A seal of his house color opens on a great beast’s brow before the binding sets, and it arrives already knowing how to be what it is. It scales with the creature’s power and his resolve, not his reserve.
Applications

Calling a war-beast, a storm-creature or a ward-guardian by its seal
Keeping the great beast of the white mantle, the oldest compact he wears, alive on the Roster; the fur is its rent, shed each winter under the compact’s terms
Pressing many presences into one worse thing

Techniques

The Compact (계약 · Gyeyak) - written on the Plane of Fate with the creature’s own name as the address and a price both sides can read
The Roster (명부 · Myeongbu) - his living list of sealed compacts, each with a price and a clause
The Leash (고삐 · Gobi) - his will holding the creature’s will down
SPIRIT SINGULARITY (정령 합일 · Jeongnyeong Hapil) - the whole table pressed into one guest: where lawful practice restricts it to drafted forms, he compresses bound presences into one core entity carrying the aggregate, and one thing gets up that is worse than the sum was

Associations

The Fate Path, Walked: the compact is written on the Plane of Fate out of his own share; Spirit holds the leash
No lens; the compact is its own instrument, a binding with a call
The creature’s own Essence, which powers it
He came to it by living it

Limitations

The leash takes about 60,000 EU a second, falling with every answering; the creature’s own Essence pays the rest
The compact’s price is paid in what the creature wants, and the great ones want things that cost
A bound will tests its leash, so a second great binding at once strains his attention
In SPIRIT SINGULARITY the constituent presences do not survive as themselves, so he does it with drafted forms and conscripts and never with a bound creature he respects
Its tell is the seal of his house color opening on the creature’s brow before the binding sets
The compact runs on the creature’s own Essence, so exhausting it breaks the compact
A fighter who strikes at his resolve while his attention is on the leash, and not at the beast, is hitting the real weak point
It fails with a creature that decides the price was unfair

THE CONSCRIPTS (징집 · Jingjip) · Signature Technique
THE CONSCRIPTS is basically soul summoning: the power to field a host of forms on threads spun from other people’s souls. It is the art the Accord names without qualification, and he is called the reason the art is regulated.
Capabilities
It is legion and Infinite practice combined, on a foundation of harvested soul-fragment in place of lawful draft. He fragments his Core output into threads, each thread anchoring one call, and the Essence he spends on the call is not all his own. Some of it is taken from people who were not asked. Mortalis keeps the fragment this side of the Gate, and Eidolyn gives it a form.
Black-violet threads run out of his chest by the dozen, and at the end of every one stands something that used to be somebody. Most people cannot see the threads. Mahuo blood can, a little: very fine, like the lines a spider lets out into the wind, dozens and more than dozens, going off through the walls of the house in every direction. It is active, mass-produced and economical.
Applications

Standing forms at Apprentice to Journeyman rank: an eidolon with tactical intelligence, an ancestral echo, a scout or a wall
Ending a long fight richer than he began it
A form that hardens when he is resolute

Techniques

The Harvest (수확 · Suhwak) - he draws soul-fragment, the small residue of Essence a living soul sheds, from willing and unwilling sources over years, and folds it until it stops being a draft and becomes a thread bent to the shape of his will; a hundred unwilling sources can give him a hundred threads
The Thread (실 · Sil) - one thread anchors one standing form, and each is a separate load on his body
Axis Binding (축 결박 · Chuk Gyeolbak) - a form’s traits tied to one of his own Spirit Axes shift as his own state does; the most responsive technique in the art
Echo Manifestation (잔향 · Janhyang) - remnants of dissolved forms are gathered and folded into new ones

Associations

The Spirit Path, as a call with a binding
Mortalis for the fragment kept this side of the Gate, Eidolyn for the form
The Zettari–Mahou Accord, which names it as the crime
He came to it by living it

Limitations

Each form takes about 150,000 EU to raise and 25,000 EU a second to keep
The souls inside are not paid for, which is the crime
Each thread is a separate load on his body: a drafter at his scale does not sleep normally, cannot digest properly in a campaign and is the thinnest man in the camp
Axis Binding is the least deniable technique in the art, because damage to the form reaches him as a change in himself, and the form falters when he is not resolute
Forms destroyed by dissolution leave nothing for Echo Manifestation to gather
Its tell is the threads, and the people near him feel a draft where their own warmth should be; when he is tired the threads shake, and where they leave his chest it looks as though it hurts
The threads are readable: anyone with comparable Perception can count them, so his exact commitment is visible before the first form lands
Cut his line of attention and the Feed lapses, leaving only what the Binding alone will hold
It fails at the seam in a structure built from many borrowed souls, which a Harmonia-trained ear can find

characters/ability-accounts/edric-ashmor.title: Edric Ashmore — Abilities in full
characters/ability-accounts/edric-ashmor.content:
Card: Edric Ashmore
THE UNTOUCHED WINE
THE UNTOUCHED WINE is basically indomitable will: the power to hold every answer back until the whole thing has been weighed, and then to spend all of himself on the answer. It is his signature art. He won’t say yes until the wine has gone cold, and once he says it nothing on earth turns his horse.
Capabilities
It is one idea, and a grain lord’s: weigh the sack before you put the seal on it, and once the seal is on, the sack is sold. Ashmore has lived for twenty years by owning the bread at tables where other men owned the roads, and a man in that seat who says yes quickly gets eaten. So his soul learned to keep every answer back until the whole of the thing has been looked at, and then to spend all of itself on the answer.
The wine is the weighing, the stone is the answer made fast, and the Line is the answer delivered at the gallop. None of the three is a Wellspring’s work. He has harmonized no lens for them. They are a habit of the soul, a custom of his house and a way of riding, and they take their limits from themselves.
Applications

Weighing a thing whole before answering
Making the answer fast once it is given
Delivering it with everything he has

Techniques

THE UNTOUCHED WINE - the weighing, during which nothing moves him
THE JUNCTION STONE - the answer made fast, a promise set on stone
THE ASHMORE LINE - the answer delivered at the gallop

Associations

No Wellspring and no lens: a habit of the soul, a custom of the house and a way of riding
The Body Path does the Line
The Fate Path carries the stone and the Pressure

Limitations

While he weighs, the chance can ride straight past him
Once he goes, he cannot turn, even when he should

Traits
THE UNTOUCHED WINE · Primary Trait
THE UNTOUCHED WINE is basically persuasion immunity: the power to be moved by no bribe, threat or shove while he is weighing a thing. He does not move until he has weighed it all, and then he does not stop.
Capabilities
What a watcher sees is a man gone still: the dark eyes on the map and not on the man holding it, the hands empty, the cup at his elbow losing its steam. Under the stillness the russet of his aura draws in close around him, the way a horse gathers before a fence.
A man is rushed into a bad bargain by a handful of ordinary levers: a price that will be gone by morning, a threat, a flattery, a crowd already nodding. Each of them works by getting the body to answer before the head has finished. In him the answer is simply not there to be had yet.
His Dominion (the stat of a soul’s command over what stands around it) sits heaviest of all his Primaries, and while he weighs it is turned inward and holds his own yes and no the way it will later hold six hundred horses, so that a bribe or a threat lands on him like rain on a slate roof. Once he has committed, his horse goes in at full tilt and does not turn.
Applications

Reading a map, a price and the man holding them for as long as it takes, and giving nothing away while he does
Sitting across a table from Tenrai factors without being hurried
Going in whole once the weighing is done

Associations

His Dominion, turned inward
His own hall, across the table from Tenrai factors
The cup of wine at his elbow

Limitations

Its limit is time: a man who needs his answer before the wine is poured gets no answer at all
A battle that will not wait for the cup to cool goes on without Ashmore in it
It costs nothing, because nothing is made or thrown; no reserve leaves him
Its tell is the cup going cold
To beat it, make him decide fast: put the thing in front of him already moving, with no table, no map and no steward, so that not answering is itself the answer

THE JUNCTION STONE · Secondary Trait
THE JUNCTION STONE is basically oath binding: the power to make a promise with his hand flat on stone that sets like the stone, so that nobody talks, buys or frightens it loose. Ashmore oaths are sworn hand-on-stone at the crossroads below Ashbury, and the stone holds them.
Capabilities
A vow is the small end of Fate, and anybody’s to make: the soul writes the terms down where it cannot pretend later that it did not, and breaking them lands on the breaker at once, by those same terms.
What the stone adds is a place to stand the promise. He walks the Fate Path a little under half his practice, enough to feel a promise as a thing with weight, and when the flat hand goes down he ties the words to one object that will still be there tomorrow, hard and cold and exactly where he left it. After that, every attempt to talk the oath round, buy it back or turn it against him has to shift the stone’s weight as well as his. His Oath (the Sub-Stat that says how well a vow stands up to being cut, twisted or used against its maker) reads as if he were still standing at the crossroads with his palm down.
He swore there to Hayato in the king’s name, and swore again with his hand on the black stone of the dais, as he had on the junction stone.
Applications

Swearing to Hayato in the king’s name at the junction stone
Swearing again on the black stone of the dais
Keeping a promise against talk, coin and fear

Associations

The Fate Path, as a binding
The junction stone at the crossroads below Ashbury, where his house swears
His Oath Sub-Stat

Limitations

The limit is the stone’s: it holds one promise at a time cleanly
Two set on the same stone grind, each wearing at the terms of the other, until the weaker cracks or he is left keeping both badly
It gives him no strength of arm and no step on the hidden scale; it only makes the promise as hard to move as he was while he was weighing it
It takes no reserve
Its tell is the flat hand
To beat it, set two oaths against each other: get a second promise out of him on the same stone that cannot be kept beside the first

Techniques
THE ASHMORE LINE · House Art, Ashmore · Signature
THE ASHMORE LINE is basically cavalry charge command: the power to bring five or six hundred big southern horses in at the gallop in one long ragged line, with his will holding it together and the weight of him rolling out in front. He calls it with two words, said once: “My horse.” Every Ashmore rider is taught the Line; only the lord’s Command and Pressure make it what hit the Skeldmere.
Capabilities
The riders come with lances and long swords out of the Kessen road. The charge is visible from a long way off and is meant to be: the russet coming over the rise, picked so that anyone across five miles of snow can tell whose horse it is, then the pennants dropping level as the lances come down, and the sound of it arriving before the riders do.
A war-horse and an armored man together weigh well over half a ton, and at the gallop the whole of that weight is traveling behind one hand’s breadth of steel at the end of an ash pole tucked hard under the arm, so that the rider is less a man with a spear than the point of a moving wall. That is momentum (weight multiplied by speed), and a standing man has none to answer it with. But the old truth of horse against foot is that the blow itself does a small part of the work. A line of men that stays shoulder to shoulder with its points out will stop horses, because a horse will not run onto a hedge of spikes. A charge wins when the men in front of it look at what is coming and decide, each one separately, to be somewhere else, and then the gaps open and the horses pour through them.
That is where the lord comes in. Command keeps six hundred frightened animals and six hundred frightened riders together and at one pace, ragged as the line looks, so that it arrives all at once and nobody hangs back half a length. Pressure, the plain weight of a Stage V soul that has stopped being polite, rolls out ahead of the hooves on the Fate side of him, where reach and presence live, and gets to the enemy first. Men below his Stage feel their attention bend toward the russet and their stomachs turn before a single lance has touched them, and their own horses feel it sooner than they do. The line that was going to hold becomes a line that was always going to flinch, and the lances find it already open.
Applications

Breaking a line of foot before the lances reach it
Riding straight at a flank at full tilt
The cut down from the saddle with the long swords once the lances are spent, his being the Kessen sword

Associations

House Ashmore, which teaches every rider the Line, and where he has it Mastered
The Body Path, as a strike, for the Line itself
The Fate Path, for the Pressure that goes ahead of it
His Command and his Pressure
The Kessen sword and the ash lances

Limitations

Its limit is ground: it needs a field the horses can take at speed
On ice or in broken country it is a line of men on frightened animals
It costs the house its horses, and the lord nothing he would call a working
The ash goes by the cartload
A charge that goes in cannot be called back out
Its tell is the russet coming over the rise
Pikes, set, beat it, as Thornwall knows: foot who have been drilled to stand, on ground of their choosing, under a captain whose own Stage shrugs off the weight coming ahead of the horses

characters/ability-accounts/edward-lambe.title: Edward Lambert — Abilities in full
characters/ability-accounts/edward-lambe.content:
Card: Edward Lambert
ITERUM
ITERUM is basically truth compulsion: the power to ask a thing twice, so that whatever answered false the first time must answer true the second. The word is the house’s own, the Court’s Latin for again, and the last form of the Computus, the Second Asking, which every Lambert child learns at the kitchen table: asked twice, with the weight of the list behind it, a man who lies the second time knows precisely what he is doing. Edward is the first Lambert to make it a working. Every ability below is one question, asked at a different size.
Capabilities
A body has to obey an order it cannot hide. The shoulder commits before the hand, the heel takes the weight before the cut, the breath stops before the thrust, and the Computus has been reading that order in the Lambert blood for longer than the Sea has had a Palatine. What the house could never do was read a lie. A feint is a sentence the whole body speaks falsely, and the oldest advice on the Stair for beating a Lambert is to feint with everything you have and then strike with no thought at all.
Edward answers it with Judicium. The Scale parts a thing from what it claims to be, by the mark it cannot help leaving, and a feint is a claim. Under his asking the false line comes away from the true one, and he sees them both, the feint edged in a fringe of color like a word read through a prism and the real blow plain underneath it. Its operation is separation: the lie set on one side of the counter and the truth on the other.
Then he closes the account. Transference is the Give-and-Take, and everything spent is an exchange: whatever a man laid out on the lie, his breath and his Aether and his whole committed weight, is owed somewhere. ITERUM makes it owed to Edward, and he collects it on his point.
Judicium’s flaw comes with it. Discernment tells everything apart and cannot choose to leave anything untold, and pushed past reading, telling a thing apart becomes taking it apart, and it takes the reader with it. Each warrant he breaks opens a fine line in his own face. The price at the far end of the road is his own memory, and he knows it, and he has begun to count what he would lose first.
The house’s bill arrives too. The Computus never turns off.
Applications

Reading a feint before it is thrown, and taking the one finish through it
Breaking an oath, a title or a working that stands on a lie
Following an exchange to whoever profits from it
Pricing a war to the copper, and being off by none
Interrogating a witness who has already lied once

Techniques

ONE BEFORE - the Computus in the body
SUMMA - the whole field in one count
THE STRUCK LIST - a column that has never held a false number
QUAERO! - the first asking, an opening offered and a lie entered
REDDE RATIONEM! - the second asking, and the account collected on the point
QUO WARRANTO? - by what warrant?
CUI BONO? - who profits?
THE EXCHEQUER - the Domain where every spend is entered

Associations

Judicium, the Scale, governing: the feint parted from the blow
Transference, the Give-and-Take, deep: the account closed and collected
The Computus, the house’s inheritance, which charges no Essence and bills elsewhere
The Spirit Path carries all of it; the Fate side carries the warrant

Limitations

It needs a will and a first answer. A falling wall, a panicked horse or a working that runs by itself never lies to him and never tells him anything
An honest fighter pays nothing into it. A man who answers the open door with a true blow gets a true thrust back, and the fight is only a fight
He offers a real opening every time he asks, and a man fast enough to use it may kill him in it
Every warrant broken scars his face, and the far end of Judicium takes memory
A clerk’s body under the gold: whoever reaches him has hurt him

Traits
ONE BEFORE · Inherited Trait
ONE BEFORE is basically precognitive reflex: the power to stand where a blow is not before it begins. It is the Computus in the body, and every woken Lambert carries it.
Capabilities
Every blow with a will behind it begins somewhere a Lambert can count: a shoulder, a heel, a breath. The family has filed several generations of those beginnings in the blood, and the read comes up as a forecast in the body ahead of the blow. Against a blow with a will behind it, his Reflex reads a step high on the hidden scale. He is not fast. Nobody who has lost to a Lambert has ever accepted that.
Applications

Every fight he has ever been in

Associations

The Computus; House Lambert
The Spirit Path

Limitations

Slower against anything with no intent in it
Cost: nothing in reserve
Tell: none to the eye
Counter: do something nobody has done; strike with no thought at all

SUMMA · Primary Trait
SUMMA is basically omni-observation: the power to read a whole field at once and feel the false return in it. It is the house’s Sum, at the tenth Stage.
Capabilities
Men, horses, remounts, days of grain, the loads on the carts and the depth of the ruts under them: as far as his eye and the reports go, the whole field goes into one count. A false number in it feels wrong in his hand, heavy, like a weight with lead cased inside it, and with Judicium under it the false thing shows its fringe. His Forecast and Analysis read a step high while he counts. He priced the war in the ruins this way, in one afternoon on the Sallowgate wall.
Applications

Pricing a campaign
Finding the one company in a muster whose roll is padded
Knowing how many came with you

Associations

Judicium; the Computus
The Spirit Path

Limitations

As far as the eye and the reports go; a field unseen is a hole in the sum
Cost: nothing while he only reads; past an hour, a nail behind the eye
Tell: his eyes go past you to count who came with you
Counter: a false report he cannot check; fog, smoke, iron walls

THE STRUCK LIST · Secondary Trait
THE STRUCK LIST is basically oath binding: the power to make a true contract hold against chance. The house keeps a Struck List of the Lamberts who entered a false number, and nobody wants to stand next to one at the gate, because the family’s count runs through the same bench.
Capabilities
Edward has never entered a false number. Any oath sworn to him, or contract he has countersigned, holds against chance for as long as it is true: the seal does not crack, the courier is not robbed, the clause stands. At the first false line in it, it gives, and he knows which line.
Applications

The Hammerford contracts
The charter of the six

Associations

A kept count; Fate II
Oath 440

Limitations

It holds only what is true
Cost: the whole house stands on his column; one false entry spreads
Tell: he signs with his left hand, so the right thumb can keep counting
Counter: prove one line in the contract false

Techniques
QUAERO! · Signature Technique
QUAERO! is basically feint detection: the power to read a lie out of an opponent’s body. Quaero: I ask.
Capabilities
He offers an opening as plain as a door: the blade dips, the hands go wide, like a clerk turning a ledger round on the counter for you to read. It is a real opening. Whatever the other man answers it with, Edward reads, and if the body answers with a feint, the feint is entered as a lie, and Judicium parts it from the blow underneath. He sees the true line plain and the false one fringed with color, one feint a breath.
Applications

The first half of every fight he finishes

Associations

Judicium; ONE BEFORE
The Spirit Path

Limitations

One opponent, one exchange
Cost: about 2% of his reserve, near 1.2 million EU, and the opening, which is real
Tell: the blade dips and the hands go wide
Counter: answer the open door with an honest blow, which he must then meet honestly

REDDE RATIONEM! · Signature Technique
REDDE RATIONEM! is basically debt collection: the power to take back on his point everything an opponent spent on a lie. Redde rationem: render an account.
Capabilities
The second asking. Every feint QUAERO! entered is a debt, and Transference moves it: what the other man laid out on the lie, the breath and the Aether and the whole committed weight, changes hands and goes onto Edward’s point. Then the left hand goes halfway up QUIETUS, the point comes up under the jaw, the hip turns it, never the wrist, and there is one movement. The more a man has lied, the harder it lands. A Moto captain on the Ashbury road threw four feints at him and took the fifth thrust’s worth in the throat.
Applications

The one finish

Associations

Transference on Judicium; QUAERO!
The Spirit Path

Limitations

Only what was spent on a lie he has read; an honest fighter pays nothing into it
Cost: about 4% of his reserve, near 2.4 million EU
Tell: the left hand going halfway up the blade
Counter: never feint him

QUO WARRANTO? · Technique
QUO WARRANTO? is basically authority negation: the power to break whatever stands on a lie. Quo warranto: by what warrant? It is the oldest writ in the Court, the one it sends to a lord who holds a right he cannot show the grant for.
Capabilities
He asks it of a working, an oath, a title or an authority, and arc-blue lines cross his eyes, and he reads what the thing stands on. If it stands on a lie, the lie comes away from it in front of everyone, and whatever rested on the lie gives: a forged commission goes slack in a captain’s hand, a working built on a false vow fails in the air, a man’s title stops being obeyed by the men who were obeying it. A true warrant answers him and stands.
Applications

The forged land grant at the Sallowgate assize
A Mahuo summoner’s binding, on the Ashbury road, which rested on a dead man’s name
Eleven times on the record

Associations

Judicium on the Fate side; Fate II
The Spirit Path, with the Studied Fate

Limitations

It breaks only what is false, and a true warrant costs him the price for nothing
At Fate II the pull is only a lean, held, so he must read the lie whole first
Cost: about 6% of his reserve, near 3.6 million EU, and a fine line opens in his face
Counter: a true warrant; or a lie nobody is standing on

CUI BONO? · Technique
CUI BONO? is basically benefit tracing: the power to follow an exchange to whoever gained by it. Cui bono: to whose good?
Capabilities
He lays a hand on anything that has changed hands, a coin, a letter, a sealed order or a working that has been spent, and gold threads come up under his fingertips and run along the exchange to the one who profited. He found the Tenrai factor at Sallowgate this way, from one silver penny in a dead courier’s boot.
Applications

Finding who paid
Finding who gained from a death

Associations

Transference; the Fate side

Limitations

One exchange at a time; a gift with no gain in it leaves no road
Cost: about 1% of his reserve, near 600,000 EU
Tell: gold threads under his fingers
Counter: a chain of hands long enough that the gain is spent before he reaches the end

Releases
SUMMA! · First Release
SUMMA! is basically enhanced perception: the power to make the house’s Sum his whole body. The call is “Summa.”
Capabilities
Every colored fringe in his aura comes up at once, and so does every fringe in the room. His Gnosis and Dexterity read a step high on the hidden scale, and nothing in him passes the roof of his Stage.
Associations

Judicium; the Spirit Path

Limitations

Cost: about 60,000 EU a second, near 16 minutes from a full reserve
Counter: heat, smoke, fog, anything that takes the line of sight

AD SCACCARIUM! · Second Release
AD SCACCARIUM! is basically domain activation: the power to open THE EXCHEQUER. The call is “Ad scaccarium”, to the Exchequer.
Capabilities
The cloth goes down. With SUMMA! under it, his Gnosis and Dexterity stand two steps over his line. At Refraction it lit the cloth’s seed for one breath; from Transcendence it opens the whole Exchequer.
Associations

Transference; the Spirit Path

Limitations

Cost: about 90,000 EU a second; with SUMMA! under it, 150,000, near 6 minutes 40 from a full reserve
It fills the cap with the First
Counter: anything that breaks the Domain

QUIETUS! · First Release, its last stage
QUIETUS! is basically singular focus: the power to close the account on one man. The call is “Quietus”, the word the Exchequer clerks write when an account is quit.
Capabilities
The field drops out of his count. For a Lambert that is a terror, and the house says it is the bravest thing he does. The whole Computus goes onto one man, and Forecast, Analysis and Reflex read two steps high against him and against nobody else. He looks at that one man as if the room were empty.
Associations

Judicium; the Spirit Path
A stage of SUMMA!, the house’s Sum narrowed onto one man: a Spirit soul holds two Releases, and this is the First’s last stage, opened at Invocation

Limitations

He is blind to everyone else in the field while it holds; a second man with a knife has him
Cost: about 240,000 EU a second, near 4 minutes from a full reserve; it fills the cap alone
Counter: bring a second fighter

Domain
THE EXCHEQUER · Domain
THE EXCHEQUER is basically transaction enforcement: the power to make everyone inside a place pay for what they spend. The Court’s old Exchequer was a table covered in a chequered cloth, where the accounts of a kingdom were reckoned with counters moved square to square, and the sheriffs stood in front of it and answered.
Capabilities
Its law: every spend is entered. AD SCACCARIUM! opens it, and the ground goes white and ink-black in squares, the house colors. Every working spent inside it, every draw on a reserve and every feint lays a counter of bone or jet on the cloth where anyone can read it, clicking, and he reads it first. Nothing is hidden on the cloth. At his word the account is struck, and whoever has spent more than he holds is in arrears, and pays the difference out of the body.
Since Realization the floor of the Sallowgate tariff-hall has kept the squares, and smugglers declare their horses.
Associations

Transference, read by Judicium; AD SCACCARIUM!

Limitations

A plain blade with no working and no will spent through it lays no counter
Counter: another Domain whose law will not be counted, or an honest swordsman with no working at all, which is the one thing he has been trying to get you to be

characters/ability-accounts/faisal-—-abi.title: Faisal — Abilities in full
characters/ability-accounts/faisal-—-abi.content:
Card: Faisal
I DO NOT LET THINGS FALL · Signature art
I DO NOT LET THINGS FALL is basically oath embodiment: the power to give a kept promise back its shape, so that the shape bears weight. Every promise anybody ever kept is a great gold hand, and he catches the whole world with them. The Midreach Choir calls the act Visualization, the First Technique, and his Traits, his techniques and his Domain are all that one act done at a different size.
Capabilities
An oath sworn and kept is a real thing. It stays written in the outer layer of the world after the words are gone, the way a footprint stays in clay after the foot has lifted, and a Midreach Celestial can read that record and make it stand up: a promise kept becomes a hand, a gate held becomes a wall, a deathbed vow becomes a light that will not go out. It is no illusion. What stands up has exactly the weight of what was sworn. The Choir gives the art to every Oath-Keeper at the Singing, the way a mortal child is given a tongue, and in most of the Choir it is a modest art, the oaths of one hall or one battlefield, a door that will not open. Faisal carries every oath sworn on honor under the Lawbell for eleven thousand years and every one sworn in the Material for seven hundred more, so in him the same clerk’s art fills a sky.
This is the Fate Path, the hardest one, worked through the Attraction Layer, the outermost of the soul’s three layers, the one that holds a soul’s share of fate. His lens is Order: the Choir’s Order Magic, the law the Lawbell Sang into the Host, and no Wellspring. Order does one thing under all its uses. It makes things agree, with their word, with their nature and with each other. It can settle particles that have been shaken apart back into their places the way a shaken sieve sorts sand from gravel, lay the panic in a fighting heart flat as still water, or come down on a field as the weight of every kept promise on the backs of those who mean to break one. He pulls Aether (mana) out of the place he stands in like anyone else, and his anchored Crystal turns it to Essence (spiritual energy), so about seventeen parts in twenty arrive as gold, which is his yield, and the rest is paid on his Layer as the knot every pull ties, though all anyone standing near him feels of it is a honey warmth.
He does not ride a blow of his own, because he throws none. A hand takes the stroke on its palm and holds it there, and the stroke is not stopped in the hand; it is passed along, because Order makes the weight agree with the ground it is going to. Masons know the shape of it from the arch, where weight is not resisted in any one stone and runs down through all of them to the footing. A kneeling body is the best footing a man has, low and wide and braced in three places. A pressure meant to crush him ran through him into the plain and left a fathom of new stone under his knee. Against disorder the hands do better than hold, because ordering it is what feeds them. They close on a grain of chaos and set it in its place, as a weaver lays a dropped thread back into the warp, and they grow brighter for every grain.
The bigger works are the same law. THE STRAIGHT LIGHT is Order made of light: one breath twisted until every strand of it agrees, so that the light keeps one step and falls in rods in place of spreading. The Measurewrights call it coherence, and say ordinary light is a crowd, every wave at its own pace, which is why it spreads. The rods converge on one seed point, and order spreads from the seed the way ice races across a pond that was cold enough to freeze and only wanted a first crystal.
Applications

Catching what falls, from a bird to a world
Taking a blow and passing its force into the ground
Holding an enemy still without striking him
Setting disorder in order, grain by grain
Making a spoken word weigh what it was sworn to weigh

Techniques

VOW-LIGHT - the warm heavy gold he gives off, under which a lie is hard to say
I DO NOT LET THINGS FALL, the Trait - the soul’s reflex that puts a hand under whatever is falling
THE BOUND FLAME - the kneel under the weight of every oath in the world
FAIETH - the Thousand Hands, the kept oaths given back as gold palms
THE STRAIGHT LIGHT - a move of the art itself: one long breath twisted until every strand of it agrees, and the sky cracks from rim to rim and lets down gold light in rods as straight as plumb lines, under which a whole world finds lying hard to think
THE AXIOM OF THE KEPT - one premise set under everything, with four works called under it
TALGRIM - choosing the order in which things happen
DIVINE FIST · PARU 86 · COMBINATION - every open hand closed, once, at the price of the Crystal
OTHSAL - the Domain, the record itself opened and hung in the air to be read

Associations

Order, the Choir’s Order Magic, the law the Lawbell Sang into the Host, is the lens, and there is no Wellspring in it
The Fate Path, mastered, worked through the Attraction Layer
The Midreach Choir, the Oath-Keepers, who call the act Visualization
Vow-Cant, the script with no grammar for a lie, and Parunic, the script the Archons’ lattice is read in; when he writes glyphs, on the Axiom’s works and on the fists, each one tells the working what it is for
He has no Release, because a Celestial’s Crystal was anchored and not grown, and no bonded weapon; he has carried no weapon since the Bell cracked
His aura is Vow-Light, a warm heavy gold like late sun through honey, with a pale silver line where his wings meet his back

Limitations

Only what was sworn and kept has any weight to give, so the hands can catch, hold, set down and press, and have nothing in them that strikes first
A man who promises nothing gives OTHSAL nothing to bind
Vow-Cant has no grammar for a lie, so he cannot feint, bluff or hide what he is about to do
Every hand he puts out is a hand that is not under the Bell, and the great works are paid in pieces of him that do not come back
THE STRAIGHT LIGHT takes about half of what he came down with, in one breath
The pale silver line between his wings is the gauge, and it thins as he spends
Because there is no Wellspring in it, there is no glyph on the plain hands and no Wellspring failure
A watcher sees it first: he sets his fingertips together before his breast and breathes in, and a ring of Vow-Light turns round him at the height of his heart, once, twice, faster, with a bell’s note held under water
Then the hands come, out of his shoulders and back when the catch is his soul’s own reflex, out of the ground on long gold arms when he sends them, with a rushing sound like a tide
The air goes warm, heavy and very clear, liars cough, grass and dust lie flat away from him, and corrupted ground under the ring goes dull and stiff and stops spreading
It is beaten by saying nothing and promising nothing, by making him choose between two falling things, by swearing two oaths of equal weight that cannot both be kept, or by making him stand and keeping him standing
The named failure is the Midreach Paradox, the old wound of his Choir: two oaths of equal weight that cannot both be kept, sworn where he can hear them, are an instruction his Crystal cannot resolve, and every hand stops where it is and the Domain seizes with him inside it
He broke one such seizure by binding himself in Vow-Cant as the difference between every impossible pair and paying for both out of his own substance, which is an answer and a ruinous one
Order is made against Chaos and cannot outlive it: the one who embodies the other thing is his exact weight, feeds his hands and is fed by them, and can never be beaten by this art, only met
One thing was seen and put down unused: THE STILLED WORLD, a single rule written under every law, no oath may contradict itself; it would have won the plain and ended every creature’s freedom to change its mind, and him with it

Traits
VOW-LIGHT · Inherited Trait
VOW-LIGHT is basically truth inducement: the power to make a lie hard to say. It is what every Celestial’s Aether carries, and in him it comes at a Grand Angel’s weight.
Capabilities
It is a heavy, warm-pressure radiance under which a spoken lie becomes physically hard to say: a labored breath, a tightening throat, a headache that will not lift until the speaker takes it back. In the Midreach it reaches further than in any other Choir and compels truth across the whole room rather than discouraging it in one man. People near him find themselves wanting to tell him things.
Poured out at the scale of THE STRAIGHT LIGHT it stops being a room’s discomfort and becomes a world’s: under a whole sky of it a falsehood is hard to think, let alone say, and a thief forgets why he meant to pretend.
Applications

Making a room tell the truth
Drawing a confession nobody asked for
Making up the gold of the hands of FAIETH

Associations

Order is its lens, the Host’s sung law, with no Wellspring
The Fate Path
His Celestial nature, the Midreach Choir

Limitations

It makes a lie cost and does not detect it; a man willing to pay can still lie to him, once
It costs nothing and takes no reserve
Its tell is that people near him want to confess
It is beaten by saying nothing at all

I DO NOT LET THINGS FALL · Primary Trait
I DO NOT LET THINGS FALL, the Trait, is basically reflexive rescue: the power to have a hand under anything that falls within his reach before he has decided anything. “It is the only thing I was ever made to do.”
Capabilities
His soul does it before it does anything else. Whatever is falling within his reach, a man off a cliff, a boy out of his own body on the Skeldmere, a city wall, a world, a gold hand is already under it. The catch is a reflex of the soul and no choice: a lark that dropped out of the sky was in a gold palm before it had fallen the height of a man. It has a reach, too. When a city came down a hundred leagues off, a dozen hands rose out of his shoulders and back of their own will and hung open in the air with nothing in them.
While he is catching, his Anchoring and Fortitude read two steps high on the hidden scale and nothing he holds can be torn out of his hands. He also hears every oath sworn on honor, even at the edge, even under the Bell’s weight; he heard Muken’s at the woodpile and Yukazuri’s last one in the Shirogane house, and every word of both was true.
Applications

Catching a bird, a boy, a city wall or a world
Holding a thing so that nothing can tear it out of his hands
Hearing every oath sworn on honor, and whether it was true

Associations

Order is its lens, with no Wellspring
The Fate Path: a kept oath called up as a hand
The catch fills his cap of two steps by itself

Limitations

He can catch, and hold, and set down; he does not strike first, and a thing that is not falling he can only stand in front of
The catch takes no reserve
Its tell is that a hand is already under you
It is beaten by making him choose which of two falling things to catch

THE BOUND FLAME · Secondary Trait
THE BOUND FLAME is basically burden bearing: the power to carry the weight of every oath in the world so that it does not come down on what is underneath. It began when Malakar cracked the Lawbell.
Capabilities
A cracked Bell could no longer hold the weight it was built for, and that weight was every oath sworn under it for eleven thousand years. Faisal went to the edge of creation, to the place where the threads run, took the weight onto his own shoulders, and has knelt there ever since. While he kneels, the oaths of the world have somewhere to rest. Malakar has gone to the edge more than once to break him, and he is still kneeling.
The kneel is a working posture and no penance: one knee, one flat hand and the bowed back make a road for the weight to go down. His body goes to it by habit, even landing.
Applications

Giving the oaths of the world somewhere to rest
Passing a crushing weight through his body into the ground
Teaching the same road: he taught it to Muken as the Work of Bearing Load

Associations

Order is its lens, with no Wellspring
The Fate Path, the load carried through his own body
The Lawbell, whose weight it is
TALETH, the Axiom’s first work, which is the same thing as the kneel

Limitations

Its limit is the kneeling itself: standing, he is only borrowing time from the weight
It costs everything he does not spend elsewhere, and has for seven centuries, which is why he comes to Muken only when he is needed and when he can, and why what kneels at the edge does not go far from it
Its tell is that he does not stand up
It is beaten by making him stand, and keeping him standing

Techniques
FAIETH · the Weight Kneeling · the Thousand Hands · Signature Technique
FAIETH is basically giant hand constructs: the power to fill the air with great gold hands that catch, hold and press. It is a Host-name, the kneeling and the weight; mortals who have seen it call it the Thousand Hands.
Capabilities
Every oath he carries is a hand that was given, and he gives them back. The air around him fills with hands of solid gold Vow-Light, colossal, a man’s height from wrist to fingertip, open-palmed and held out, hundreds of them at once, rushing out from him in a tide like a wave breaking sideways. Each hand carries what it catches into the ground the way his own knees do.
Turned on an enemy, they come in from every side, open, and close, pressing the weight of every kept oath down onto one body from all directions at once until it cannot move, cannot breathe, and is held. The ground under the target cracks in a ring and the target goes to its knees, the way he has knelt for seven hundred years.
Applications

Catching what falls and setting it down
Taking a blow on the palm and holding it there
Closing on an enemy from every side and pressing him to his knees
Feeding on disorder: what the hands close on they set in order grain by grain, and they come away brighter and heavier than they went in

Associations

Order is its lens, with no Wellspring
The Fate Path: the kept oaths called up as hands
Vow-Light, which the hands are made of
Mastered

Limitations

The hands only hold, catch and press; there is no fist among them that strikes first
He has never used them to kill
Keeping them out takes about two tenths of one percent of his reserve a breath, about five hundred breaths from a full reserve
Its tell is the air filling with gold palms, open, held out
It is beaten by the Choir’s old wound: present him two oaths of equal weight that cannot both be kept, and every hand stops where it is

THE AXIOM OF THE KEPT · Technique, with four works under it
THE AXIOM OF THE KEPT is basically axiom manipulation: the power to set one premise under everything where he stands, so that everything built on it follows. The premise is: what is kept, is.
Capabilities
He says one word, “Axiom,” and white script comes up across the back of his right hand. It answers an enemy who feeds on correction. A steersman who corrects late overcorrects, and each correction swings wider, so he stops correcting and sets a single premise as the first stone of the law where he stands. Everything built on it follows, and nothing downstream needs correcting. The script is Parunic, and each glyph tells the working what it is for.
Applications

Passing a load through him into the ground
Starving a storm
Voiding a contract made under the knife
Running one consistent line back to its source

Techniques

TALETH · the Tally’s Weight ([Th] Foundation, [Grv] Gravity, [Ur] Balance) - the oldest thing he knows, older than the Thousand Hands: a load need not stop in him, it can pass through him into the ground, and it is the same thing as the kneel
DAHLREN · the Walked Boundary ([RenB] Boundary, [Ur] Balance) - makes the fast and the slow round a storm agree; a storm lives on difference, a fast current beside a slow one, and with the differences leveled it has nothing to tear at
SARNRUTH · the Seal Entered ([Sel] Measure, [Va] Law, [Vo] Voice) - weighs the intent in a contract by the oldest rule of contract: a yes given under the knife carries no intent, binds nobody, and is entered void
OTHANTHA · the Unbroken Line ([Len] Line, [Ho] Order, [Ir] Continuum, [Ed] Edgetruth, [Ora] Truth) - every path is tried at once and only the kept one stands, the one consistent line running back to its source; the Measurewrights tell it as the principle of least action, the paths that disagree cancelling crest against trough

Associations

Order is its lens, with no Wellspring, written in Parunic glyphs
The Fate Path
The kneel and THE BOUND FLAME, which TALETH is

Limitations

It holds only where he stands
Each use puts a little of him into the foundation for good; the first took two fingertips, which went clear as glass
Its tell is the one word, “Axiom,” and white script running down the back of his right hand
It is beaten by making him go on paying

TALGRIM · the Order of Precedence · Technique
TALGRIM is basically event rearrangement: the power to choose what order things happen in. It is the quiet art under every other art of the Midreach, tal the tally kept and grim the order in which things are entered, and the thing about him the Host feared more than his hands.
Capabilities
Every event is a member of a set, and every set can be arranged. He cannot unmake a verdict or stop a thing happening, and he can decide which falls first. It works the way an army breaks step on a bridge: the same blows in an order that never falls in time with itself.
Applications

Breaking the step of his own shaking Domain: the same true verdicts in a sequence that never fell in time with itself

Associations

Order is its lens, with no Wellspring, written [Len] Line, [VaM] Moment, [Ho] Order
The Fate Path

Limitations

It changes order and nothing else
At a Domain’s scale it costs the rearrangement by hand of a hundred thousand moments a breath, and the small vessels of his eyes, which burst and run
Its tell is the rhythm of the room going ragged and blood running from the corners of his eyes
It is beaten by patience: a patient enemy learns any new rhythm

DIVINE FIST · PARU 86 · COMBINATION · Last Technique
DIVINE FIST · PARU 86 · COMBINATION is basically a sacrificial final attack: the power to close every open hand at once, for the first time in eleven thousand years. It can be thrown only by a Grand Angel who has broken his own Crystal with his own hands.
Capabilities
It is called in three breaths, clearly and without raising his voice: “Divine Fist.” “Paru Eighty-Six.” “Combination.” Breaking the Crystal pulls everything he carried into his body at once, with the hope of mortals poured in where the Crystal was. Every palm of FAIETH folds into a fist, Parunic script comes up across the knuckles in white fire, and the fists take up the fourteen stations of the Archons’ lattice, so that the whole field is one sentence of law written in three dimensions, eighty-six strokes long, all of them pointing in.
The first comes straight down the center line. The second, the one open hand in the sentence, rises from behind and hauls toward the first. The other eighty-four close from every angle and herd the spent chaos back in on its author.
Applications

Herding spent chaos back in on its author

Associations

Order is its lens, with the hope of mortals poured in where the Crystal was
The Fate Path: the hands called, and the sentence bound
FAIETH, whose palms become the fists
Parunic script and the fourteen stations of the Archons’ lattice

Limitations

His own refusal held even here: the fists closed only on one who had already struck first
Its price is the Crystal and everything after
Its tell is every open palm closing at once, and he has to break his own Crystal to do it
Its counter is the plainest he has, which is not to strike first

Domain
OTHSAL · the Position Held · Covenant Domain
OTHSAL is basically oath enforcement: the power to make every spoken promise physically binding on the ground it covers. It is the art turned inside out, the record itself opened and hung in the air to be read, the only Domain the Midreach Choir has ever grown, and the thing that made him a person rather than an instrument.
Capabilities
He has no Release to open it with, so it is opened by a spoken call, his hands drawn apart: “Domain Expansion. OTHSAL.” It forms as it is named, petal behind petal. The oaths he carries come out of him as script: lines of gold Vow-Cant, fine as hair and bright as wire drawn hot from a die, every oath ever sworn on honor and kept, unfurling from one point in long curving ribbons like a lotus opening, until the whole space around him is written in them. It takes up every word already spoken on the ground it covers and hangs them in the script like banners, so that a boast made an hour before it opened is a promise inside it.
Inside it, every spoken commitment becomes visibly, physically binding. The air thickens a little each time an oath is sworn, and breaking one parts with a snap like a cord, which everyone present hears whether they speak the language or not. Vow-Cant has no grammar for lying, so nothing false can be written there at all.
Applications

Raising whoever swears inside it and keeps it one step in Oath and Anchoring, for as long as they keep it
Knocking an oath-breaker to his knees by the weight of what he dropped
Turning a boast made before it opened into a promise

Associations

Order is its lens, with no Wellspring
The Fate Path, mastered: a claim on what a spoken word is worth
Vow-Cant, the script it is written in
It was grown out of him over eleven thousand years and was never lent

Limitations

It binds what is sworn and nothing else; a man who promises nothing walks through it untouched
