It takes about one percent of his reserve to open, and a slow bleed while it stays open
A kept oath inside it lifts him too, but adds nothing to him while he is already catching
A thing grown out of him is not separate from him: what shakes the petals shakes his ribs
A Domain that is broken returns its held verdicts to the one who grew it, so whatever breaks it breaks his body along the lines it grew from
Silence walks through it
Its deeper counter is the one every Midreach Celestial fears: two oaths of equal weight that cannot both be kept, sworn inside it, seize the Domain and him with it

characters/ability-accounts/gerrit-marri.title: Gerrit Marrick — Abilities in full
characters/ability-accounts/gerrit-marri.content:
Card: Gerrit Marrick
THE LONG SPEAR
THE LONG SPEAR is basically collective strength: the power to gather a whole signed rank into one body and put all of its weight behind one point. The Fields gave his art the name of his office, because by the time he was elected nobody could tell the two apart. Every ability below is the one rank made into one body at a different size.
Capabilities
The Shoulder is the house’s art, and anyone who signs a Marrick contract has it: a rank under one contract, touching at the shoulder, shares its load, and a blow that lands on one man goes down the file and into the ground. Gerrit runs it backward. Where the Shoulder sends the file’s load down, the Long Spear sends it forward, up the shafts and into the man at the point, who is him, and out through one spearhead.
The idea is Coagula’s: gathering the broken. A rank is sixteen scattered men, and under him they come back into one body without ever melting, each man keeping his own shape, his own boots and his own bad back. Its operation is coagulation, the scattered pieces set into one thing. What the one thing does is lean. Sixteen men lean on the drum, and their weight and their coats come up the ash to the front, and Gerrit is the front.
Coagula’s flaw comes with it. A body gathered without melting keeps every gap between the pieces, and the seams between the men are where the next break starts. An enemy who knows the Fields hits the rank between the fourth man and the fifth, where the coat is thinnest and the lean has to cross from one shoulder to another, and the Long Spear comes apart there, all at once, into sixteen ordinary men.
The price is the house’s price, doubled. Everyone pays. When the Shoulder spreads a blow, sixteen men keep the injury; when the Long Spear throws one, sixteen men keep the recoil, the same sprain in the same right wrist, and old companies at Hotwell walk with the same limp because of him. The Measurewrights have an account of it, spreading the impulse over a greater mass and then gathering it again, and they have filed a complaint with the Moot that it does not balance. Gerrit has asked them what they are paid.
Applications

Breaking a gatehouse with one file
Breaking a cavalry charge, and then the cavalry
Throwing a whole afternoon of blows back at the man who dealt them
Standing a Stage X off with sergeants

Techniques

THE CORNER - the coat run down the whole file
THE SETTLING - every blow sent down through him into the ground
TO THE HOUR - the contract held against chance
SIXTEEN DEEP! - one file’s lean through one spearhead
HEAVE! - the ground gives back what it took
THE WHOLE WALL! - several companies behind one point
THE DRILL SQUARE - the Domain where everyone keeps step

Associations

Coagula, the Mending, deep: the rank gathered into one body
Petralon, the Foundation Stone, governing: the load taken and sent down
Transference, the Give-and-Take, trace: the coat moving down a file
The Shoulder, the house’s art, which anyone who signs may have
The Body Path carries all of it

Limitations

It needs the rank: signed, touching, in term. Alone, he is a big man with a Common spear and a Reflex of D
The contract ends at the hour named, and the Long Spear ends with it
The seams between the men are where it breaks
Everyone pays, in the same bone
It does nothing at all against a working on the soul, because no one ever shared a soul’s hurt with a shoulder

Traits
THE CORNER · Passive Trait
THE CORNER is basically aura extension: the power to run his coat down a whole signed rank. On the Fields a corner is the one fighter at the outside angle of a file who can take a blow, “shining for the whole file,” and Gerrit has been a corner for forty years.
Capabilities
A corner’s coat runs along the rank thin as paint on the back row. His does not go thin. It holds at full strength sixteen ranks deep, and thinly along a whole Wall, so that the unwoken back rank of a company stands in a share of something none of them could make for themselves. The gray comes up on the back of every helmet in the file at the same moment, which is how the enemy knows the Old Man has arrived.
Applications

Making a file of farmers into a wall
Holding ground a much higher Stage would like to walk through

Associations

Petralon; the house’s Shoulder
The Body Path

Limitations

It needs a rank under one contract, shoulders touching
Cost: Charge from him alone, about 1,800 EU a second for a file; near an hour and three quarters from full on bad ground, and the whole afternoon on beaten earth, where he draws back nearly as fast as he spends
Tell: the gray on every helmet at once
Counter: break the file, or go past the Shell

THE SETTLING · Primary Trait
THE SETTLING is basically force redirection to the ground: the power to send every blow that lands on him, or on any signed man touching him, down through his bones and into the earth. It is Petralon’s foundation, which becomes what other things stand on.
Capabilities
Every blow that lands goes down. It goes through his skeleton and his boots and into the ground, and the ground keeps it: the earth under a square he has held all afternoon has a settled look, cracked in lines as straight as a rule. That is what HEAVE! draws on. It also settles him. He is a hand’s breadth lower in the hips than he was at forty, his stance sinks a little after every fight and does not come all the way back up, and one day, the Fields say, he will plant his feet and not be able to lift them.
Petralon’s flaw is the flaw of every foundation. A foundation bears whatever presses down on it, and nothing ever asked it to hold on. Pull him, and he parts.
Applications

Taking blows that would kill a Stage IX and staying up
Storing a day’s load in the ground for HEAVE!

Associations

Petralon, the Foundation Stone
The Body Path

Limitations

It needs ground under it: a deck, loose sand, open water or a drop takes nothing
Cost: he sinks a little with every fight
Tell: the earth under the square settles and cracks in a straight line
Counter: a pull. Lift him, drag him or take the ground away, and a foundation does not give gracefully

TO THE HOUR · Secondary Trait
TO THE HOUR is basically oath binding: the power to make a signed contract hold against chance until the hour it names. It is forty years of kept contracts, which are vows and the only Fate a Marrick has; a vow binds without a rung, and it pulls nothing down.
Capabilities
Anyone may make a vow, and a kept one binds without a rung on any ladder, so a Marrick who keeps his reads no Fate Mastery at all and is held by them anyway. Gerrit has kept every contract he has ever signed, to the hour, on both sides of every war, and while one of them is in term, nothing his company depends on gives by chance. The strap does not snap. The drumhead does not split. The pay wagon arrives. A Fate fighter who reaches for what the Wall depends on finds every strap held by forty years of kept words, and has to pull against all of them.
Applications

Keeping a Fate fighter’s hands off the company’s straps and drums
Being on time to the minute, every time, for money

Associations

A kept word: a vow, which binds without a rung
The contract, which is the law

Limitations

The instant the hour passes, it is gone, and so is the Shoulder
Cost: a knot for every town he has watched burn because it was not noon
Tell: he checks his feet at noon, every day, contract or no contract
Counter: a pull made after the hour, or anything that is not chance

Techniques
SIXTEEN DEEP! · Signature Technique
SIXTEEN DEEP! is basically force concentration: the power to put one file’s whole lean through one spearhead in one thrust.
Capabilities
He shouts it, the file leans on the drum, and over a breath and a half sixteen men’s weight and coats come up the ash to him and go out through the point. Alone his thrust lands at his Penetration of 220; with a file behind it, it lands a full step higher on the hidden scale, and it breaks a gatehouse. The Keld who took one at Hessel Down was found forty yards behind his own shield.
Applications

The barbican at Oxley, in one afternoon
A Keld shield wall at Hessel Down
A Stage X who has stopped in front of the rank to gloat

Associations

Coagula; the Long Spear
The Body Path

Limitations

One file, one thrust
Cost: about 3% of his reserve, near 354,000 EU, and sixteen sprained right wrists
Tell: “Sixteen deep!” and the lean
Counter: not to be where the file is pointed; or to take it on a slope, so the lean runs off downhill

HEAVE! · Technique
HEAVE! is basically damage reflection: the power to gather back up out of the ground every blow his square has sent down into it, and throw them out of his spear together.
Capabilities
All afternoon the blows have gone down through THE SETTLING into the earth under the square. A foundation only bears; it gives nothing back. What gives them back is Coagula. The day’s blows lie scattered in the ground like the pieces of a broken pot, and the Mending gathers scattered pieces into one body without melting them, each keeping the shape it had while broken. At sundown, or whenever he likes, the ground cracks open in a straight line from the square to his boots, and the whole day comes up through him over two or three breaths, every blow still the shape it was dealt in, and goes out through the spearhead at the man who dealt most of it. The Fields consider it the funniest thing the Captain does, and the Midmarch kings do not.
Applications

Ending a siege at sundown
Answering a high-Stage fighter who has spent the day hitting the rank

Associations

Coagula, which gathers what Petralon only bore; THE SETTLING
The Body Path

Limitations

Only what went down under him today, on this ground
Cost: about 5% of his reserve, near 590,000 EU, and every man in the square feels the day’s blows a second time
Tell: the crack running through the ground to his boots
Counter: move him off the ground he stood on; fight him on a deck

THE WHOLE WALL! · Technique
THE WHOLE WALL! is basically army-scale force concentration: the power to put several companies’ lean behind one point, with himself as the point.
Capabilities
It takes time, four or five breaths. The drums of every company in the Wall stop together, and the lean goes along the files and up to him the way water runs to the low corner of a field. Anyone watching can see it coming, and nobody who has seen it arrive has had to watch twice. It is on record four times.
Applications

The curtain wall at Harl’s Keep, on the third try
A Grandmaster’s Domain, once, at the Long Barrow

Associations

Coagula and Transference
The Body Path

Limitations

It is slow, and the lean must cross every seam in the Wall to reach him
Cost: about 8% of his reserve, near 943,000 EU, and every soul in the Wall breaks the same bone, the left collarbone by custom, since Wick Bottom
Tell: every drum stops
Counter: strike before the lean arrives, or hit the Wall from two sides at once, so the force has nowhere to go

Releases
SHOULDER! · First Release
SHOULDER! is basically body hardening: the power to make the house’s first order his own body. The call is “Shoulder!”, the first order of any Marrick fight.
Capabilities
The gray comes up on him hard and square, with corners, and his Vitality and Dominion read a step high on the hidden scale, though nothing in him passes the roof of his Stage. Every rank in earshot closes up without being told, because it is the word they have closed up on since they were nine.
Applications

Every contract that runs to noon

Associations

Petralon; the Body Path

Limitations

Cost: about 30,000 EU a second, near six and a half minutes from a full reserve
Tell: everybody on the field heard him shout it
Counter: a working on the soul

DRUMS! · Second Release
DRUMS! is basically domain activation: the power to open THE DRILL SQUARE. The call is “Drums!”
Capabilities
Every drum in reach takes up his beat, the enemy’s included, and the Domain opens around him. At Refraction it only lit the Domain’s seed; from Transcendence it opens the whole square. With SHOULDER! under it, his Vitality, Resilience and Dominion stand two steps over his line.
Applications

Opening THE DRILL SQUARE

Associations

Coagula; the Body Path

Limitations

Cost: about 60,000 EU a second; with SHOULDER! under it, 90,000, near two minutes from a full reserve
It fills the cap with the First
Counter: anything that breaks the Domain

OLD MARGET’S CART! · Third Release
OLD MARGET’S CART! is basically immovability: the power to take the whole load of every signed rank in reach into his own body and become the thing nothing goes past. The call is “Old Marget’s cart!”
Capabilities
The cart has stood broken at the ford since 631, because Old Marget wrote that the hire stands as long as the cart stands, and nobody has dared find out what happens if it moves. Released, Gerrit is that cart. The ground sinks a foot in a square around him, the penny in his circlet rings, and every blow on every signed man in reach comes to rest in him and goes down. His Vitality and Resilience read two steps high, and his feet do not move again until he lets it go. Nothing gets past him while the clause stands.
Applications

The bridge on the Tolly Wash
The barrow-field, when the ghouls came up in step
The last minute before the hour

Associations

Petralon; the Body Path

Limitations

He cannot walk out from under it either
A pull parts him, sudden and total
Cost: about 110,000 EU a second, near a minute and three quarters from a full reserve; it fills the cap alone
Tell: the ground sinking in a square, and the penny ringing
Counter: drag him, lift him, or take the ground away

Domain
THE DRILL SQUARE · Domain
THE DRILL SQUARE is basically rhythm imposition: the power to make everyone inside a place keep step. The Fields say a Captain’s Domain is a drill square, and his is the one they mean.
Capabilities
DRUMS! opens it. The ground goes ochre and black in squares like the stubble at Musterfield, his drum sets the beat, and every foot inside comes down on it, the enemy’s too. Coagula gathers scattered things into one body, and in here the enemy is gathered into the rank’s body as well, which means he marches. The rank always knows where he will be on the next beat, and so do the spears.
Applications

Making a skirmisher march into a file
Making a cavalry charge arrive on the beat

Associations

Coagula; the Body Path; DRUMS!

Limitations

It needs feet: a flier, a man who will not walk, or a working that runs by itself passes through
Counter: another Domain with a law that refuses it, or a deaf man, which has happened once and is not discussed

characters/ability-accounts/gimbzo-—-abi.title: Gimbzo — Abilities in full
characters/ability-accounts/gimbzo-—-abi.content:
Card: Gimbzo
THE WHOLE BURNING
THE WHOLE BURNING (全焼 · Zenshō) is basically all-out destruction: the power to hit everything as hard as he can, with a breaking that never stops where he hit. It was his signature art, and his Traits, his techniques, his Releases and his Domain are this one idea at different sizes. The eye it aimed by and the Work it ended with were the Kōkan blood’s and not his own making; he was the one who put his fire behind both.
Capabilities
Every piece of it is the same act: commit everything, and let nothing give. It runs on three lenses, an eye, and a fire that is none of them. Fractura, the Crack, is the idea that everything has a place where it will go, and a soul that has become that idea finds the place and sends the ending to it: the blow goes to the fault, and the thing comes apart along a line that was already in it, where the same blow sent to sound material would only shake it. The Measurewrights call it stress concentration and will show you on a cracked tile how the load crowds at the crack’s tip; their figure for how much is good, and they have no idea why a soul can find the tip. Coagulatio, the Seed, is the idea of settling round a seed, and its operation is coagulation. In his Shell the whole of what he could raise set around one grain, the striking knuckle, at one instant, so that nothing was early and nothing was spread: a thing gathered to one point is all of it in one place. A hammer drives a nail that a hand’s push never would, and that is the comparison every Kōkan yard uses. Judicium, the Scale, did one job in him, which was to rank: every fault in a field listed worst first. The limit sat at the contact: one point, one instant, and nothing held back to steer with afterward.
It all rode one blow, and the blow was real: bone and iron and the weight of a locked body arriving first. Coagulatio set it to a point as it landed, so the first damage was the plain one, the thing struck staved in at the place it was struck. Fractura carried what was left out along the target’s own faults, so the second damage was the thing coming apart on lines that were already in it. Then the Work of Ruins took hold, if there was rot there to take hold of, and ended what was already ending. What followed was weight and nothing stranger. When one member of a structure fails, the load it carried falls on its neighbors, and neighbors that were sound enough for their own share are not sound enough for two, so the failure walks. Builders call it progressive collapse, and it is why a gatehouse follows its gate and a street follows its wall.
The fire has no lens. Seven parts in ten of what he spent reached the thing he struck, which is his yield, and the other three burned in the furnace of his Shell and came off him as heat, light and noise, and at his rate of flow those three parts were enough to run snow off a hillside. A cleaner soul at his Stage would have burned low and quiet, and the Kōkan before him were not hot at all. The vow of the black shut the red line’s own Wellspring-heat out of his Crystal, so his furnace had no hearth to bank it in and burned in the open, and the Overchannel the vow fed pushed more through the Shell than the Shell could pass. What the north called the King’s Fire is a Body soul’s furnace with its door off: what burns when a man spends everything, every time, and does not care what the spending costs. It is real heat, it burns real things, and he shed almost none of it away from himself.
Applications

Breaking walls, gates, keeps and anything massive, brittle and already carrying a load
Ranking a field by where it is weakest and going to the worst of it first
Breaking a levy line with the weight of his coming, before he reached it
Ending a rotten thing so that everything leaning on it goes after it
Fighting past his own ceiling on a vow
Laying four hundred yards of ground where everything struck either holds or breaks

Techniques

AS HARD AS HE COULD - a blow that is all of him
FOREST FIRE - an intent so whole that it arrives before he does
THE GOLD AT THE EDGES - an eye that ranks a field by where it is weakest and aims him at the worst of it
THE BLACK - a vow that lets him spend past his own ceiling
SHINGAN - the Moto sight the gold sits in
HAMETSU NO GŌ - what happens when a blow like his is given a thing that was already ending
TETSUTSUI - the body locked into one piece behind one knuckle
ENJŌ - the First Release, which sets his own body alight with it
NOBI - the Second Release and the Domain, which lay the same refusal over four hundred yards of ground
SHŌDO - the Third Release, which burns down everything in reach that can be burned, and he is in reach

Associations

Fractura, the Crack, finds the place a thing will go and runs the blow out along its faults
Coagulatio, the Seed, sets the whole of what he can raise around one knuckle at one instant
Judicium, the Scale, ranks a field worst first
The Body Path does the blow; the Fate Path, which he walked, carries his Pressure, his vow and his Domain
The Kōkan blood gives the gold in the eye and the grip on the Work of Ruins
He had no bonded weapon; he struck with his hands and with whatever the field put in them

Limitations

He could throw nothing less than everything, at twice the rate a man of his Stage should spend
The breaking took whatever stood nearest him: his line, his Crystal, and the woman who loved him
There is no hidden charge anywhere in it: his intent goes out ahead of him, the black of his aura cracks and shows ember-red, the ground breaks around what he is aiming at before he has thrown anything, and his eyes go gold at the rims
For the set the whole body locks, heels to fist, for one breath in which he is planted and cannot turn
His ground is the hard kind; loose sediment, marsh and open water starve Fractura and Coagulatio both, and the last field of the war was mud
A sound thing with no fault in it gives the Work nothing and takes only the hit, and a thing that will not stand gives the hit nothing either
Against a higher Stage it thins from the outside in: the Pressure does nothing to a soul that outweighs his, the field falls to a stronger Domain, and a fighter who can read him has three moves to be elsewhere, which leaves only the blow
It is beaten by reading him, which anyone can, and being somewhere else; by giving way, or carrying the blow through the body into the ground; by standing where nothing is rotten; or by putting the Kōkan red on him and taking the vow out from under it
Coagulatio fails as the many seeds: start more than one grain setting at once and the reserve thickens in the arms with no way out, which is why he never learned a second blow, a combination or a feint
Fractura’s sight has no outward-only setting, and force sent into a thing that will not take it comes home along the striker’s worst fault, which in him ran from the breastbone to the back of the left eye
Judicium ranks whatever is put on it, and when he put his own line on it, it ranked them
Heat that is not shed stays, and a body run past its ceiling for forty years is a field that has been burned every spring and has nothing left under the ash

Traits
He carried two Trait risks. AS HARD AS HE COULD hardened into the only thing he knew how to do, which is Rigidity. His Shear Break condition was wearing red before he had made it worth wearing, which he never did.
AS HARD AS HE COULD · Primary Trait
AS HARD AS HE COULD is basically all-out force: the power to put the whole of himself into every blow. It is a commitment made in the Core before the body moves.
Capabilities
Before he ever tried anything, his soul committed all of itself to it. Every blow he threw carried the whole of the force he could raise at that instant, Coagulatio drawing it to one point and Fractura running it out along the target’s faults, and nothing he struck took a partial blow. Against a thing that stood and took it, his Penetration counted a full step higher on the hidden scale.
It could not be argued with from inside. By the time he might have chosen a lighter hand, the whole reserve had already set around the knuckle. The doubled spending is the same fact seen from the purse: a fighter who feints pays for the blows he lands, and he paid in full for every blow he began.
Applications

Breaking whatever stands and takes the blow
Putting the full weight of a strike behind the Work of Ruins
Folding iron gauntlets like tin, one pair to a blow

Associations

The Body Path, Mastered, in the form of a strike
Coagulatio sets the force to one point, and Fractura runs it out along the target’s faults
TETSUTSUI is the blow it was built to throw, and ENJŌ raises it as far as his Body IV will carry it

Limitations

He could not throw anything less: no feint, no test and no blow held back
His reserve emptied twice as fast as a man of his Stage should have spent it
It has no tell, because he never once disguised a blow
Its limit is the target’s willingness to stand: a thing that gave way, rolled, or let the blow pass through it into the ground took far less than he sent
What is committed must arrive somewhere, and when the thing in front of him declined it, the force often went back into him
It is beaten by yielding, so that the blow spends itself on nothing
It hardened into the only thing he knew how to do

FOREST FIRE · Passive Trait
FOREST FIRE is basically killing intent: the power to be felt coming before he is seen. It is the same commitment as the blow, made visible.
Capabilities
His Shell put out his intent ahead of him the way a fire puts out heat ahead of the flame. A soul that has already decided has nothing left to hide the decision behind, and a Shell as thin and lucid as his passed intent as cleanly as it passed force. His Pressure rode out on it, so that a levy line a field away felt the weight of a thing already coming and already certain, and most men broke before he arrived.
Naiser Yukari, meeting the son, thought only that the Kōkan King had fought like a forest fire, and the north had been saying it for forty years before that. His son reads as a page with no ink on it. Gimbzo read like a forest fire.
Applications

Breaking levies before he reached them
Emptying a wall with nothing more than the black coming over a rise

Associations

The Fate Path, Walked: Aura Pressure and presence, his by right of the Path and unchosen in how they show
No lens; it is a claim, carried on his Pressure
His thin, lucid Shell, which passes intent as cleanly as force

Limitations

It cost him nothing, and gained him a great deal in Pressure
His intent was readable three moves out by anyone with a reading sense; Shigure Tenrai, who stood behind him twenty years, said so
No ambush he ever planned came off, and he stopped planning them
Anyone who could read him and keep their nerve could be somewhere else when the blow arrived, and that is how it is beaten

THE GOLD AT THE EDGES · Inherited Trait
THE GOLD AT THE EDGES is basically weakness detection: the power to see where everything is weakest, listed worst first. It is the Kōkan blood in the Moto heart-eye.
Capabilities
The gold is the first seam of the Kamigan, the crown eye that takes what the other eyes see and ranks it, and in him it never went further than the seam. What it added to the common Shingan was order. Where any Moto sees every fault in a wall at once, he saw them listed, the worst at the top, and went to the top of the list.
In forty years Shigure never once read the red line in his eyes, in a fight or out of one, even the night he went down into the cellars after it. At the end, at Shimane, his eyes went gold to the edges.
Applications

Finding a gate’s rotten hinge above its sound one
Picking the weak company out of a field of Zettari
Knowing who in a hall will break first

Associations

The Kōkan blood; it spends his own share and pulls nothing down
Judicium does the ranking, on top of SHINGAN’s Fractura sight
The Kamigan, of which the gold is the first seam

Limitations

It resolved fault and load and ranked them; it could not show him intent
It could not show him that what he was ranking was his own house: a scale weighs what is set on it and has no opinion about whether it should have been
Holding his Shingan open with it lasted near fourteen minutes from full, and at the end it was open all the time
Held open without rest it paid out as heat behind the eyes and the gold creeping outward from the rims
Its tell is gold coming up through the gray of his eyes
It is beaten by giving it nothing whole enough to read

THE BLACK · Secondary Trait, a vow
THE BLACK is basically oath empowerment: the power to fight past what his body can bear, bought by swearing off the red. He swore it before his captains after what the Recension made of the red line.
Capabilities
He swore that he would not wear the red line’s color until he had made it worth wearing again, and he wore black lacquer, black lacing and black everything for twenty years. The vow bound his Attraction Layer to a red he would not touch and fed the Overchannel that let him fight past his ceiling: a step of Overchannel inside the two-step stack. The step it bought was real, and was most of how a body of sixty stood in front of the Zettari for the war’s last four years.
A vow’s price shows on the body at once, and this one showed as the fire. The red line’s heat, shut out of the Crystal by his own word, had no hearth to sit in and burned in the open, so the man who would not wear red burned red at every seam when he pushed. It was never broken. He died in black.
Applications

Buying a step of Overchannel for twenty years
Standing in front of the Zettari at sixty

Associations

A vow, small Fate, spending his own share and pulling nothing down; a binding laid on himself, which anyone may swear
No lens
The Overchannel it feeds, and the King’s Fire it sheds
The black harness, which in twenty years never showed one thread of red

Limitations

It was paid in a Crystal that never once in twenty years let the red line’s own Wellspring-heat into him cleanly
Its tell is that there is no red on him anywhere
Its terms are its counter: put the Kōkan red on him, and the vow breaks and takes the Overchannel with it
The terms were never read to an enemy, because his captains were the only witnesses and none of them would have dared, so the one clean counter went the whole war unused
A red sash thrown over his shoulders would have done what forty years of spears could not
Wearing red before he had made it worth wearing was his Shear Break condition

Techniques
SHINGAN (心眼 · Shingan, the heart-eye) · Bloodline Faculty, Moto
SHINGAN is basically structural perception: the power to see where everything is carrying its weight. It is the Moto sight, inherited, and his was the Kōkan Shingan with the gold in it.
Capabilities
Any Moto can see where a wall wants to fall; the gold in it is the Kōkan’s alone. His was wide and loud and always aimed outward. Aimed outward, it gave him the gate’s worst hinge and the company that would run.
Applications

Reading where a wall, a gate or a company will break first

Associations

The Moto blood; a bloodline eye gives no Path
Seen in him through his Fractura
The Kōkan gold in it opens the road to the Kamigan
THE GOLD AT THE EDGES, which ranked what it saw and in the last years held it open

Limitations

It could not see intent, and it could not see itself
It never once in sixty years turned round to show him the crack that ran from his own breastbone to the back of his left eye
It cost him little until the last years
Its tell is the eye going still
A sound wall, a fresh company or a fighter with nothing flawed to offer gives the eye a blank page and leaves him only his fists

HAMETSU NO GŌ (破滅の業 · the Work of Ruins), the Obsession face · Bloodline Art, Hataraki
HAMETSU NO GŌ is basically ruin inducement: the power to end what is already failing, and in his hands the ending ran on past it. The Kōkan had Hataraki from the Head of Fate; Gimbzo had the Work of Ruins and nothing that tempered it.
Capabilities
A Work is an inherited grip on one function, and this one’s function is ending: what is already failing, at the seam where it fails, and nothing sound. That is why the price is so small. He reached for nothing that was not already on its way, the weight gathered in the fault did the carrying, and the grip only found the seam and held it while the blow went in. His Dominion Fate was nothing, so the Work in his hands never once closed on a sound thing.
The Attraction face ends only what is already dead and stops at the edge of the rot. The Obsession face ends what was rotten and then what was near the rot, and it does not stop, and that was the face he worked in. The house’s law is that a long life in one grip becomes a long life in its worse face, and the bearer does not notice.
With all of AS HARD AS HE COULD behind the strike, the dead thing did not merely come apart along its fault. It went all at once, everything that had been leaning on it took its load in the same instant and failed in its turn, and what leaned on that failed after. No thread was pulled for any of it. The Work ended one rotten beam, and plain weight and a king who would not close the edges ended the granary.
Applications

A gate, and the gatehouse after it
A wall, and the street under it
A granary at Hiroe, with the children still inside

Associations

The Kōkan grip, inherited; no Wellspring
Fate where the grip takes hold, at Fate III, the Spinner’s rung, with the Work of Ruins for his grip, and the breaking done by Body through Fractura
His Dominion Fate against the target’s Persistence and Continuity, and his was nothing
AS HARD AS HE COULD, which put the full weight behind it
SHŌDO, which is this face given a whole field

Limitations

The Work itself closes only on what is already failing; a sound thing gives it nothing
It took about two percent of his reserve a strike, and the cost to the field was without limit
Its tell is the ground cracking around what he aimed at, not only under it
It is beaten by standing where nothing is rotten, or by having someone close the edges faster than it can run
It has no failure of its own beyond the face: a breaker ends what was rotten, then what was near the rot, and then does not stop, and by then the people who could have told him were in the cellar

TETSUTSUI (鉄槌 · Tetsutsui, the Iron Hammer) · Signature Technique
TETSUTSUI is basically an absolute punch: the power to land one blow with the whole locked body behind one knuckle. It is the art’s one blow, and he came to it by living it.
Capabilities
The lock is the technique. A loose body loses a blow at every joint, a little in the ankle, the knee, the hip, the spine, the shoulder and the wrist, each one a soft link that takes up force in bending. With every one of them braced, the ground under his heels and the knuckle at the far end are the two ends of a single iron bar, and the whole mass of him arrives at once, with the earth behind it for an anvil.
Coagulatio then does to the Charge what the lock has done to the bones, setting all of it around the one grain at the one instant, so that nothing is spray and nothing is early. It hit like a ram in a gate. The ground behind his heels was found cratered after, because the bar pushes back as hard as it pushes forward.
Applications

Breaking a gate the way a ram does
Folding the iron hands like tin, one pair to a blow
Thrown inside NOBI, at a thing forbidden to give, it was the blow the whole art was built to deliver

Associations

The Body Path, Mastered, in the form of a strike
Coagulatio sets the force to one instant at one point
AS HARD AS HE COULD, which means there is never a lighter one
The iron hands, black-lacquered gauntlets that never lasted

Limitations

It took about five percent of his reserve and delivered force at his Penetration of 440, and he could throw one every turn until the reserve gave out
The whole body sets before the strike; the set takes a breath, and in that breath he is planted and cannot turn
A fighter who read him, and anyone could, was out of the line before it landed
During it, the answer is to give way, roll, or carry it through the body into the ground
After it there is a breath when everything he had is spent forward and nothing is left behind it

Releases
He called all three with one word, “Moyase,” burn it, in the Kōkan’s old tongue, roared. Called silent they came weaker, and he never once called them silent. He had no bonded weapon.
ENJŌ (炎上 · Enjō, the Burning) · First Release
ENJŌ is basically a heat aura: the power to set his own body alight with the fire he sheds. The north called it the King’s Fire.
Capabilities
On the word the release opens the furnace door. The three parts in ten that a quieter soul would bank and let burn slowly come out through every seam of the aura at once. The black of his aura splits along every seam and the ember-red comes up through it, and heat pours off him so that snow runs and lamp-flames lean away for twenty paces. AS HARD AS HE COULD rises as far as his Body IV will carry it. In ENJŌ it is his own body that will not give.
Applications

Raising AS HARD AS HE COULD as far as his Body IV will carry it
Bringing heat for twenty paces round him, as weather and not as a weapon he aims

Associations

The Body Path: the transformed body, opened at Stage IV
No fire lens; the heat is his own furnace, unbanked
The black harness, heat-crazed down both arms from it

Limitations

It lasted a little under eleven minutes from full
The body under the harness ran hot enough to craze the lacquer down both arms
The heat cooked him first, because he did not shed it
Cold and distance beat it, and so does its own heat: a fight that keeps him burning and keeps him at arm’s length is a fight he loses to his own skin
Called silent it would have come weaker

NOBI (野火 · Nobi, the Field Fire) · Second Release
NOBI as a Release is basically field projection: the power to send the fire out of himself and into the ground. The north called it the Wildfire.
Capabilities
As a release it changes where the refusal lives. In ENJŌ it is his own body that will not give, and in NOBI the ground is told the same thing. The fire leaves him and runs out across the ground to four hundred yards, and the field burns without burning anything, and nothing in it can give way. It opens and powers the Domain of the same name.
Applications

Opening the Domain and paying for it

Associations

The NOBI Domain, which it opens and powers
ENJŌ, the same refusal held in the body

Limitations

It lasted about four and a half minutes from full
Called aloud it formed as it was named, in about six seconds
He never once called it silent, and by the rule of such things it would have come at half the reach

SHŌDO (焦土 · Shōdo, Scorched Earth) · Third Release
SHŌDO is basically a suicidal attack: the power to burn down everything in reach that can be burned, himself among it. He called it twice in forty years that anyone lived to tell.
Capabilities
The fire goes inward as well as out, and everything within the field and within him burns down to what will not burn. It is the Work’s Obsession face given the entire field at once. Where a strike of HAMETSU NO GŌ ends one rotten thing and lets the weight walk, SHŌDO lays the ending on everything inside NOBI together, and the only things left standing are the ones with no fault in them at all.
Applications

Ending everything that can be ended in reach

Associations

A Third Release, opened at Stage IX
HAMETSU NO GŌ, whose Obsession face it is
NOBI, whose field it fills

Limitations

It emptied him in about forty seconds from full, and his own body’s reserve was among what it ended
By the law of the stack it fills the whole two-step cap alone, with nothing left over for the vow to add
A thing with no fault in it at all is left standing
He had faults: the first calling he survived whole, and the second ran home along the worst line in him, breastbone to left eye
The second calling fractured his Crystal along the line his son carries, and it stayed Fractured

Domain
NOBI (野火 · Nobi, the Field Fire) · Domain
NOBI as a Domain is basically law imposition: the power to lay down ground where nothing is allowed to give way, so everything struck in it either holds or breaks. Nobi is the old word for the fire set in early spring to burn the dead grass off a field, and the name is the whole of what he thought he was doing to the north.
Capabilities
A field set alight runs ahead of the wind, and nothing standing in it is spared because it is green. Inside NOBI his doctrine outranked the ground. Like every Domain it is a claim laid on the ground and pulls no thread: it adds no force to any blow and moves nothing that had no way of happening. What it takes away is the give.
A struck body ordinarily spends most of a blow in moving, in the flex of a shield arm, the step back, the roll of a shoulder, the slide of a boot. The field forbids every one of those, so all of a blow’s work is done on the thing struck and none on the air. Every blow struck inside it, his own and everyone else’s, landed whole, with no yielding, no rolling with it and no passing a load down into the earth.
Called aloud it formed as it was named, the red running out along the ground from his feet in a ring like fire through stubble, some four hundred yards out from him, with no flame in it anywhere and the roar of one over all of it. For forty years it was the most terrible ground in the north to fight on.
Applications

Breaking a levy line that cannot recoil, cannot buckle and re-form, and cannot be driven back a pace and hold there: it stands or it bursts
Giving TETSUTSUI a target that is forbidden to give

Associations

The Fate Path, Walked: a claim on conditions, authored in the Core and opened at Stage VIII
No lens of its own; his doctrine is the law
The Second Release opens and powers it
Its reach and hold are read from his Dominion Radius and Sovereignty

Limitations

It held about four and a half minutes from a full reserve, and took about six seconds to form
It served him only while he was the harder thing in the field
The field’s law has no exception for the man who laid it: inside NOBI he cannot give way either, his own blows cannot be pulled, and a blow that lands on him lands whole
A stronger Domain beats it, and so does breaking his reserve or his attention
There is one lawful road through it: do not give way, and pass the whole weight through your bones into the ground, which obeys the field’s law to the letter
His son learned that kneeling under the Lawbell; Gimbzo never did

characters/ability-accounts/godfrey-grey.title: Godfrey Greymane — Abilities in full
characters/ability-accounts/godfrey-grey.content:
Card: Godfrey Greymane — The Shieldwarden
THE KING’S WALL · Signature art
THE KING’S WALL is basically kinetic force redirection: the power to stand between a blow and the people behind him, and give the blow somewhere to go that is not them. Hit him as hard as you like: he stays where he is, and the ground breaks instead of him. The art is the Greymanes’, and every shield on the Ridgewall knows its first lesson; the name is northern Common, the one the Stark long houses gave to him. His Traits, his techniques and his Release are all that one act done at a different size.
Capabilities
Alone, the act is THE RIDGE DOES NOT MOVE, and the blow goes into the ground. With a shield it is LOAD PATH. With a king beside him it is THE SWORN WARD, and the king’s blow goes through Godfrey into the ground. With a frightened boy in a chair it is THE FLAT HAND, and what goes to ground is the boy’s shaking. With the Greymane foot beside him it is THE GREY FILE. STONEFAST is the same body made stone to the knee, and the Domain the house is waiting for would be the same law laid over a whole ridge. The idea, the transformed body, the world obeying it.
Petralon, the Foundation Stone, is the lens for nearly all of it, and its idea is the foundation: to become what other things stand on, the load taken, carried and sent down, at the price of slowly settling. Its operation is coagulation, the soul fixed as the foundation, set to bear and never to rise, and it makes his set body one voussoir, one wedge-stone, of an arch whose other end is the world. Masons know the shape of it: a round arch carries a cathedral roof by turning every weight on it into squeeze, each stone pressing on the next down the curve into the footings, and no stone in it is ever asked to stretch. The Measurewrights call the route the weight takes the load path, the squeeze compression, and what a stopped blow carries its momentum. When his feet are planted on ground that is one with the earth beneath it, the weight of a blow, all that has to go somewhere when a moving body is stopped, is not allowed to gather in him as motion. A foundation’s office is to send weight down, so it is handed joint to joint the whole way, out through his heels, and the ground takes it. The ground is very large and he is not, so it is the ground that shows the damage: a ring of cracks, a flagstone sunk an inch, a puff of dust.
It rides a blow in the plainest way there is. He does not win by hitting, and his sheet says so. The real catch lands on the shield and the working goes in with it, so both are true at once: the ash and iron take the dent, and the ground takes the building’s worth of blow that would have gone through the man behind it. Then the short sword comes flat over the rim into whatever the attacker left open by committing, or the ground comes back. Something under half of what he spends reaches the work, which is his yield. The rest burns in the furnace of his Shell and leaves as warmth in his boot soles and knee joints, as the low grinding note, and as the fine grit that drifts down round his feet, which is why a tired Shieldwarden stands in a little pale ring of dust.
Applications

Holding a post so that nobody behind him has to
Guarding one king
Keeping a young king in his chair
Anchoring the end of a shield line

Techniques

THE RIDGE DOES NOT MOVE - feet set, and the blow goes into the ground
THE SWORN WARD - a blow aimed at the king taken through his own body
THE FLAT HAND - a steady hand beside an ally, and the ally’s temper finds it can wait
LOAD PATH - the shield squared and every joint in one straight column
THE RIDGE GIVES BACK - the ground handing back what it just took
THE GREY FILE - shields locked rim to rim, one blow shared down the whole line
STONEFAST - the First Release, the body made stone to the knee

Associations

Petralon, the Foundation Stone, the Wellspring under the Ridgewall, on which the house has stood for generations
Basilithe, the Stone Will, for the one piece that deals in rhythm
House Greymane, whose art it is
His ground is bedrock and old masonry, and on the Ridgewall’s own stone, where Petralon runs under the floor, he fills faster than anywhere
No Domain yet; the house expects that when it comes it will be the ridge

Limitations

He cannot take a step while it holds, and everything it spares the people behind him lands on the one body that will not leave the post
The law has one condition, and it is the footing: the path has to be unbroken from the point of the blow to the bedrock, and anything that is not one with the ground, loose snow, ice, mud, open water, a deck, a cart, a high stair, breaks it and leaves the load nowhere to go but him
A foundation bears whatever presses down on it and was never asked to hold on; masons say the same of stone, which will carry a tower on its back and snap under a tenth of that load hung from it
The charge is easy to read for anyone who has been told what to look for: his heels sink, and the dust in the air near him stops drifting and settles straight down
The heavy gray of his aura, warm and dark with the ochre of Basilithe only hinted at its edge, thickens toward his boots as if it had weight, with a smell of cut stone, a pressing on the shoulders, and under it the low settling note
Against a higher Stage it thins from the ground up: Petralon routes the load and does not make the floor any stronger than the floor is
A catch is good to about a building’s worth, the 176 to 275 step on the hidden scale, and a blow well above that breaks the thing he is standing on, after which the path is cut and he is a tall man in the air with a shield
A fighter two Stages over him who knows it will hit the floor first and him second
It is beaten by never pushing the Shieldwarden: hook the shield and pull, lift him, fight him on ice, or strike him and his king in the same breath
Petralon fails by its flaw: a foundation bears whatever presses down on it, and nothing ever asked it to hold on, so the column that holds any push has no strength at all against a pull, and a hooked rim, a lifted belt or a line dragged sideways opens him joint from joint without bending him, with the working still running; the Measurewrights call it tensile exposure
Its slow failure is the settling, the price the house accepts for never cracking and the Measurewrights call creep: held too long under too much, he sinks and stiffens without breaking, and comes off a long watch moving like a man twice his age
Basilithe fails by its flaw: a soul that holds one note can never change it, even to get out of the way, so nothing that beats against him in another rhythm can shake him, and the one rhythm that sings his own note builds in him with nothing to let it go and rattles him apart; the Measurewrights call it resonant catastrophe
The Trait risks he carries: he will not leave a post even when leaving would save it, which is Rigidity, and being made to abandon a ward he was sworn to is his Shear Break condition

Traits
THE RIDGE DOES NOT MOVE · Primary Trait
THE RIDGE DOES NOT MOVE is basically immovability: the power to stay exactly where he stands, whatever comes into him. They are his house’s words, become the law of his soul before he could say them.
Capabilities
When his feet are set on solid ground, a load that comes into him does not move him. Petralon hands it down through his bones into the ground, the way an arch carries a cathedral roof into its footings. He goes on standing. The ground under him takes the blow: it cracks in a ring, or settles, or sinks an inch, and a fine dust rises round his boots.
Petralon’s flaw is the pull. A foundation bears whatever presses down on it, and nothing ever asked it to hold on. Push it and it holds; pull it, hook the shield and haul, lift him by the belt, drag him off his line, and it does not give gracefully. It parts. Builders say the same of stone, which carries about ten times in squeeze what it carries in pull, and is why an arch stands for a thousand years and a stone beam cracks across its underside.
Applications

Standing under a blow so that the floor cracks in a ring round his boots
Keeping a Greymane line of shields from breaking

Associations

Petralon is its lens
The Body Path; its gates are Fortitude and Fortification on the Body side and Anchoring on the Fate side
The house words of the Greymanes

Limitations

Its limit is the footing: loose snow, ice, mud, open water, a ship’s deck, a moving cart, a high stair, anything that is not one with the ground beneath, gives the load nowhere to go but him
The law routes a load without strengthening the floor: a blow far past what the ground under him can bear breaks the ground, and with the footing gone the path is gone with it
It is constant and nearly free while his feet are set
Its price is that he cannot move while it holds; a set foot is a planted foot, and lifting it drops the law
Its tell is his heels sinking and dust settling round his feet
Its counter is written in the Wellspring’s own failure: never push the Shieldwarden; pull him, lift him, or fight him on the ice

THE SWORN WARD · Secondary Trait
THE SWORN WARD is basically damage transfer: the power to take a blow aimed at his king through his own body. It came of the oath his father swore him to on the ridge.
Capabilities
His father swore him on the ridge, the night before he rode south to the Kurenai blade, to carry the secret of Muken’s blood until it could be carried by someone with a better right. Godfrey carried it every morning at the boy’s right hand and said sire and said nothing, and it was the hardest thing he had ever done, and his Crystal kept the shape of it.
It rides the Spirit Axis that formed between him and his king, and the oath, which is why it is the Fate Path’s piece of the art. A bond is a real connection, and Petralon will route a load along it as a builder uses a tie-beam, so the one he is sworn to guard is tied into his own load path like a bay tied to a buttress. Within a few paces, the reach of a long stride, with his feet set, a blow that reaches the king is carried across the bond into Godfrey’s set body and down into the ground. The king keeps a shove. Godfrey keeps the rest, on whatever part of him the path happens to run through, braced or not. It pulls no thread down. The bond was already there.
Applications

Taking a blow meant for Muken, so that the king feels only a shove

Associations

Petralon is its lens
The walked Fate Path: a bond and an oath, landing through the Body; its gate is Oath
The Spirit Axis between him and Muken, and his father Wystan’s oath

Limitations

He can hold one ward, and the ward is Muken
It reaches a long stride, and it needs his feet set
It moves weight and nothing else: a blade’s edge still has to be met by something, so he turns the shield or his own shoulder into the line as the load arrives
A working that goes past the body to the soul is not a load and does not cross
Each catch costs him the full hit, landing on a body that may not be braced for it, and about one and a half percent of his reserve on top
Its tell is his eyes going to the ward an instant before any blow lands
It is beaten by two blows at once, one to the king and one to the warden, or by a strike to Godfrey first, while he is still turning to the king

THE FLAT HAND · Passive Trait
THE FLAT HAND is basically a calming presence: the power to steady whoever sits beside him. It is the one piece of the art that deals in rhythm and not in weight.
Capabilities
Basilithe, the Stone Will, is one note the soul holds that nobody can retune, and its operation is coagulation, the soul fixed on that note past any retuning, so no rhythm outside him can drive his own. Builders know the danger it answers: a push timed to the rate a thing sways at builds on itself, which is how a marching column can shake a bridge down. The Measurewrights call the rate a natural frequency and the building resonance.
A tall tower in a gale is steadied by a great weight hung near its top and swinging against the tower’s sway, and Godfrey is that weight for whoever sits beside him; the Measurewrights call it a tuned mass damper. A soul that cannot be retuned is a standard for other people, and his Stability spreads his note a little way: within arm’s reach, a frightened or furious ally’s pulse and breath start to fall in with his, and the urge to stand up or lash out comes on slower.
Applications

Letting a young king sit through a room full of enemies without moving, because a long gray hand has come down flat on the pine beside his own

Associations

Basilithe is its lens
The walked Fate Path: presence, the plainest thing that Path gives; its gate is Gravity
His Stability, which spreads it

Limitations

It never touches, and it never compels; it only steadies, and anyone who decides to stand up stands up
It reaches an arm’s length, and it needs the ally’s own willingness
It cannot steady Godfrey himself, who has nobody’s hand beside his
It costs nothing
Its tell is a long gray hand laid flat beside someone, not touching
It is beaten by distance: separate them, and the king’s temper is his own again

Techniques
LOAD PATH · Signature Technique, Greymane Shield Art
LOAD PATH is basically shield blocking: the power to send a blow that lands on his shield straight down into the floor. It is the house’s first lesson and his best.
Capabilities
He squares the Greymane shield into the blow, sinks his knees, and sets every joint from the shield-boss down through the forearm, the shoulder, the spine, the hips and the knees to the heel into one straight column, so the blow’s weight goes down the column into the earth, and his body is only the road it travels.
It is the Primary Trait given a tool and a drill. The Trait routes whatever reaches his body, and the technique chooses where the blow reaches him and lines the bones up behind that point, so the road is straight and nothing in it is asked to bend. The shield still takes the dent. What it is spared is being driven back through the arm that holds it.
Applications

Sending a blow that would bring down a house into the floor, spent in cracking the stone round his feet

Associations

Petralon is its lens
The Body Path; its gates are Fortitude and Anchoring
THE RIDGE DOES NOT MOVE, which it gives a tool and a drill
The Greymane shield
Taught by the house, and mastered

Limitations

It needs the footing, as his Primary Trait does
A column has one line: a blow that comes from the side of it, or two that come at once, shears it
Each catch takes about one and a half percent of his reserve
Its tell is the squared shield and the knees going down before the hit
Its counter is the one every Greymane is taught to fear, the hook: catch the shield’s rim with an axe-beard or a hand, and pull, and the column that holds any push parts at the one load a foundation was never asked to bear
Before the catch, stay off his line and attack the flank; during it, hook and pull; after it, he must reset his feet, and that reset is a beat

THE RIDGE GIVES BACK · Signature Technique
THE RIDGE GIVES BACK is basically attack reversal: the power to hand a blow back to the man who threw it. It is the only strong blow he owns, and every grain of it was the other man’s first.
Capabilities
It is the foundation’s idea turned round: what was laid on it is still there in it. Petralon keeps the last catch’s load in the ground under his feet for a breath or two, the way a bent bow keeps the pull, and then he may let it all go at once in one direction, up and forward, under the attacker’s feet and behind his own shield. The Measurewrights call what the rock holds elastic strain energy.
The ground heaves up under the attacker in a cracked ring, and the shield comes forward with the earth’s own rebound behind it in a bash that can throw a man in plate across a yard. At the most it is a rockfall’s worth.
Applications

Throwing a man in plate across a yard
Breaking the ground under an attacker’s feet

Associations

Petralon is its lens
The Body Path, with no gates beyond the Trait’s
The catch before it, by THE RIDGE DOES NOT MOVE or LOAD PATH
Drilled

Limitations

It can give back only what the ground took; with no catch before it, there is nothing to return
It has to leave by the same feet that took it in, so he cannot give back on ground that would not have held the catch
The ground holds the load only a breath or two
It takes about six percent of his reserve
For the instant of the bash his weight is going forward off his heels, which is the one moment in his whole art when a push will move him
Its tell is the ring of cracks running out from his boots a heartbeat before he moves
It is beaten by giving him nothing to give back: do not strike his shield, strike round it, or wait out the two breaths until the ground lets go of the load by itself

THE GREY FILE · House Art, Greymane
THE GREY FILE is basically a shield wall: the power to share one blow down a whole line of men. It is the art of the Greymane foot.
Capabilities
The Greymane foot lock their shields rim to rim in a long gray line, and Petralon in each of them ties into the next, so a blow on any shield runs along the whole file and down through every set of boots in it. The locked rims are the tie: a rim proud enough to seat against its neighbor carries the squeeze sideways from shield to shield, as the stones of a wall share a weight laid on one of them.
Applications

Holding a line that does not break under a blow on one man
Holding the end, which is the Shieldwarden’s work, because he is the man the end can be trusted to

Associations

Petralon is its lens, in every man of the file
The Body Path, each man tied to the next by the house’s drill
House Greymane, which teaches it; he has it mastered

Limitations

The file is as strong as its weakest pair of feet and as long as its ends
It asks the same footing of every pair of boots, and a file drawn up across a frozen ford is so many men on their own
Each man pays his own catch and no more
Its tell is shields locking rim to rim
It is beaten by breaking the file’s end, where the load has only one man to go through

Releases
STONEFAST · First Release
STONEFAST is basically stone armor: the power to become part of the floor, stone to the knee. The folk call it Setting the Stone.
Capabilities
The gray wolf-fur of his mantle stiffens and grays and sets into layered stone-scale over his shoulders like slate on a roof, a skin of ridge-stone climbs from his boots to his knees, his amber-hinted aura flares to the full of what Flourishing allows, and the ground under him groans as Petralon takes him into it. THE RIDGE DOES NOT MOVE strikes at the top of its base, as far as a soul below Glory can carry it.
As a Body release it changes the body and nothing past it. The stone is his own Shell thickened onto cloth, fur and skin, real slate to the hand and the weight of it too, and while it holds he is part of the floor in fact as well as in law, so the catches that cracked the ground before now only make it groan.
Applications

Taking catches that would have cracked the ground
Holding off the settling for as long as it lasts

Techniques

Called - low in northern Common, never shouted, the way his father called it, for the full rise
Silent - weaker: the stone stays at his boots and never reaches the shoulders

Associations

Petralon is its lens
The Body Path; it is his Stage IV release
THE RIDGE DOES NOT MOVE, which it lifts
The Greymane shield, his bonded weapon, carries STONEFAST’s load path

Limitations

It lasts about two and a half minutes from full, and ends at a tenth of his reserve
When it ends the stone-scale lets go and slides off him as grit, and the settling it was holding off arrives all at once in his knees and back
With the shield taken from him, the release holds his body but not the line in front of it
Its counter is the same as its Trait’s, and worse: a man set in stone to the knee cannot step off a pull at all

characters/ability-accounts/gyuro-—-abil.title: Gyuro — Abilities in full
characters/ability-accounts/gyuro-—-abil.content:
Card: Gyuro
THE INNER WAY (내도 內道 · Naedo, “the way inside”)
NAEDO is basically inner world manipulation: the power to live so deep inside himself that nothing in the world can reach him, and to carry anyone who reaches him and asks down into Rooms where nothing can reach them either. It is his signature, the one idea his Traits, his moves, his Releases, his Domain and his Realm each say at a different size, counted in Rooms, and spoken slowly in the plain speech of the hill country, each syllable given the same weight.
Capabilities
In the hill tongue nae is the inside and do is a road walked so long it has become a rule, and a house there is measured in kan, the space between four posts. A poor man’s house has three. Thaloré’s idea is feeling given its true weight, and its operation is dissolution: a thing is let down through the whole of the soul until it rests at the depth its weight earns. The old saying of that water is that a soul under it takes the shape of what holds it. What held Gyuro for fifty years was a shell, a pen and a flood-door, and so his soul took the shape of a house. He lives at the bottom of it, where every feeling he has ever had has sunk and settled, and where no light from the yard comes down.
The house has ninety-nine Rooms, the most a subject may keep, and the Core of him is ordered as they are, each bay lying deeper than the last with the Crystal in the deepest. The shell is the outer wall and nothing more. Fixatio, whose idea is that what is bound stays bound, is on every door: a door he has shut is set past melting, and the way back through it stops existing until someone opens it from inside. Petralon and Orrenthal are in the wall, the one sending a load down and the other sharing it through the whole frame, and Pyraeon is the banked fire under the floors, the flare given up and the heat kept. The work goes by the Spirit road, Essence through the Core, laid on souls and on what things mean. It touches matter only through the shell, by the Body road he walks beside it.
So a thing that hunts the self, a Pressure, a read, a drain, a compulsion, a curse laid on a name, must come down through every door between the yard and wherever the master is sitting, and it stops at the first door that was not opened to it. A blow is simpler. It lands on the wall, the whole frame takes it, the ground under him takes what is left, and none of it goes in. A soul one Stage above him reaches the outer Rooms and can make them ring. A soul two Stages above could walk in, and few souls living stand there. The Measurewrights say the weight on a thing under water depends on how far down it sits and nothing else. They have the water right. They have no account of why it parts for a knock.
Because it does part. One who reaches him and asks is taken in, and the asking is the only key the house has. It may be a word, a knock on the shell, a hand held up, or a child holding on. It must come from the one to be carried, and it must be real. Fear counts, and despair, and so does a hidden purpose: a killer who truly wants in is truly asking. A compelled word does not count, since that is the yard speaking and the soul silent, and no one may ask for another. The sleeping, the drugged, the senseless, the gagged and the infant too young to hold on cannot ask, and he cannot carry them. A load is another matter. He will bear a river, a wall or a siege for anyone who asks it of him, and the people under it climb out on their own feet.
Applications

Going so deep that no Pressure, read, drain, curse or compulsion reaches him
Carrying the soul of anyone who reaches him and asks, hunted, cursed or dying, into a Room
Bearing a load no body should bear, a flood-door, a river, nine days of an Archmaster’s blows, and sending it down
Setting the whole of a borne load down in one blow, once
Laying his law over a house and its yard
Taking other people’s Domains in as Rooms of his house

Techniques

EMPTY YARD - nothing kept on the surface, always on
THE CARRIED HOUSE - the Tortoisekin shell, his by birth
HEARD - every real asking reaches him, wherever he is
BEARING - a blow on one point borne by the whole frame
GOING IN - the master goes down Room by Room, shutting the doors behind him
COME IN - one who reaches him and asks is carried into a Room
THE GREAT BEAM - a held load sent down through him into the ground, for days
ALL WHO KNOCKED - everyone who asked inside his yard, taken in at once
SETTING DOWN - everything he has borne put into one blow, once
MAY I COME IN - the last movement of the inner way, which he has never made
AT HOME - the First Release: at home in the yard and in every Room at once
I WILL BEAR IT - the Second Release: whatever is laid on a guest is borne by the whole house
THE ASKING GATE - the Domain: no one is carried who has not asked
THE NINETY-NINE ROOMS - the Realm: other fields held as Rooms of the house

Associations

Thaloré is his home lens, and both his depth and the heaviness of any room he sits in come from it. Fixatio binds the doors and the rule. Petralon and Orrenthal are the shell. Pyraeon is the fire under the floors, patience kept as a fire is kept
The Spirit road does the work, at the rung its schools call Ferryman, the soul that carries others across and holds many. The Body road, walked beside it, carries the shell and gives his field its claim on matter
The Tortoisekin blood gives the shell, the long life and the drawing-in. The art is his own, and no bloodline’s instrument
His Class has had five names, Jimkkun the porter, Munjigi the doorkeeper, Jipjigi the housekeeper, Daedeulbo the great beam and Jipjuin the master of the house, and each left him a move. His students shorten the last to Juin, the one the house belongs to
Naedomun at Gwibong, which outsiders call the Turtle School. The words over its door are “The shell is the house. The master is inside.”
It began at the Gate under the Greaves pit, where a starving Wellspring drained every keeper on the stair and found nothing on a bearer’s surface to take

Limitations

The held house costs him almost nothing. From full he could hold it eleven days empty and five with every Room taken. Whatever he does past holding is dear: one committed exchange takes between a hundredth and a thirtieth of everything he has, and at full output he is empty in about three minutes. Rest gives back a tenth a minute
It opens only to an asking, and only at his reach. An asker must touch his hand or his shell, or stand within thirty paces of him. An enemy who knows him fights beside those who cannot ask, or does the work somewhere he is not
It cannot imprison. Nothing is dragged in, an enemy least of all, and a guest leaves when the guest wishes. He cannot keep anyone, as he could not keep his sister Ohra
A house is opened from inside. A guest is past the outer wall and may open any door on the way down, and the road from the yard to the master then stands open behind them. The surest way to reach him is to be invited, and he honors a real asking from a hostile hand
The refusal is set in the house under Fixatio and cannot be undone, even if it is wrong. To go on denying the truth beneath it, that rescue done to a person is the same hand as sale, is his Shear Break condition
He tells himself he waits for the one he wronged out of respect, and he waits because he fears being refused a second time. While he believes the first, every great art of the way runs a little under his Stage
He is slow and has no range. Whatever will not come to him can wait him out, and whatever strikes from past thirty paces is outside his law
His one true seam is a pull. A foundation bears what presses down on it, and nothing ever asked it to hold on, so a lift, an uprooting or a drawing-out parts him. The Measurewrights call it tensile exposure
His worst contrary is Abython, which stands against his home lens and his shell together and matches pressure away until he has no load to bear. Nyxial and Cymorath answer him too, and Fractura reads the seams of a shared frame
Dry ground and thin air starve the home lens, a moving deck loosens the doors, an iron cage or a thick fog troubles the frame, and soaking cold puts out the floors. A dry iron cell in winter is the worst room in the world for him
The tell is the room. The air thickens and goes faintly blue, voices drop, and the cyan lattice along the joins of his plates lights or dims, one pane for every guest he carries
Run too long it fails in Thaloré’s manner. The weight he has laid on the room presses back when the support within gives way, and he is crushed under his own house. The Measurewrights’ word for it is implosion

Traits
EMPTY YARD (빈 마당 · Bin madang, “the empty yard”) · Primary Trait
EMPTY YARD is basically psychic immunity: the power to keep nothing on the surface for anything to read, grip or talk round. It is his Primary Trait, always on, the lesson of the Gate made into his nature.
Capabilities
A swept yard tells a visitor nothing about the family. Under Thaloré each feeling is let down to the bottom the moment it is felt, so nothing floats where a caller could see it, and Orrenthal joins the whole soul in common, so that no part of him holds an opinion the rest does not share. One who reads him finds still water and a shell. A worker of minds, an inscriber or a patient talker goes looking for the part of a man that already half agrees, and in him there is no such part; he is the hardest soul in any room to argue with, because nothing in him argues back.
It was this that saved two hundred and six people at the Greaves pit. The Wellspring under the stair had stopped knowing its keepers and begun to take from them, and it took from every soul that had anything on its surface. It passed over a bearer with his back to a flood-door for seventy-one hours and found nothing there to eat.
Applications

Going unread and unmoved by mind-work, inscription and persuasion
Walking where a hungry Wellspring drains everyone else
Sitting through any argument without any part of him changing sides

Associations

Thaloré and Orrenthal, on the Spirit road, read at the height of his mastery there
Lived and never taught: seventy-one hours on the flood-door
Opened downward, it becomes GOING IN

Limitations

It costs him nothing. It is part of the held house
Everything he feels sinks to its true weight and none of it comes back up. No one has seen him weep, and the grief that would have shown presses on the room instead; people who sit an evening with him go home tired and cannot say why. Comfort reaches the surface and stops there. No one has comforted him in four hundred years
A reader much his better at reading can still get through
It is no armor. A spear has no interest in what lies on the surface
It is not empty while AT HOME stands
The tell is a room growing heavy and quiet around a man who shows nothing

THE CARRIED HOUSE (진 집 · Jin jip, “the house borne on the back”) · Inherited Trait, the Tortoisekin blood
THE CARRIED HOUSE is basically organic exoskeleton: the power to carry a shell that is a second skin and a roof at once. It is blood and no working, and it belongs to his people and not to NAEDO.
Capabilities
Every child of the Carried House is hatched under one: a domed and plated shell whose scutes wear pale with the years, a long corded neck that draws back into the collar, a heart that beats slowly and a body that mends slowly, and five centuries in which to use them. Buyers priced the line as carrying stock for exactly these things, since a Tortoisekin will stand under a load no rope is trusted with and will outlive the man who bought him.
All of his people have the shell. Only Gyuro made a house of it. The reflex of drawing head and limbs in under a blow is the seed the whole inner way grew from, and the plate that cracked at the Gate and healed crooked is the one fault in the wall. A wound set wrong stays as it was set, and so every Room in the house carries that same crooked line.
Applications

Bearing ordinary loads no rope would be trusted with
Drawing head and limbs in under a blow

Associations

The Testudine line, the Carried House
The Labor Provision, which prices this body as stock
It has no Path, no lens and no Form

Limitations

It costs nothing and does not grow
It is slow and heavy, poor at climbing, dangerous to be turned on its back, and slow to heal
The crooked plate is the weak place, and everything built on the shell inherits it

HEARD (들었소 · Deureosso, “heard”) · Passive Trait, left by Principality
HEARD is basically danger detection turned to pleas: the power to hear every real asking made anywhere near him. It is the price Principality took from him, the last of his privacy, and he cannot shut it.
Capabilities
An asking is a knock, and a house hears its own door. When the world entered his law it left the door standing open in him: every real asking made within a day’s walk of where he sits comes to him clear, and nothing else comes at all. He knows who asks, from where, and for what. The harder half is that he knows who did not. The drowning man too proud to call is plain to him, and so are the penned who have stopped hoping, each one a silence with a shape. A compelled plea reaches him as a silence wearing somebody’s voice, and he is not fooled by it.
He throws nothing to do this. The askings come to him, as a great soul’s country carries his doctrine back to its source. His answer still goes only as far as his hand.
Applications

Knowing who in a valley wants to be carried
Knowing that a compelled asking is none
Knowing which of the dead never asked

Associations

Thaloré, on the Spirit road, and the law the world entered at Principality
His one word for it, said to whoever has finally reached him: “Heard.”

Limitations

It never switches off. A day’s walk of fear reaches him every night, and what it costs him is sleep
He hears far and reaches near. He can answer only those who come to him, or those he can walk to at a tortoise’s pace
It can be flooded. A city in terror asks with ten thousand voices at once; he hears each of them and can answer almost none, and a panic raised on purpose drowns him

Techniques
BEARING (지다 · Jida, “to bear on the back”)
BEARING is basically impact absorption: the power to take a blow on one point into the whole frame, so nothing gathers and nothing breaks. It is the move his first Class gave him, when the soul named him a porter.
Capabilities
Jida is to bear a thing on the back. It is also to lose, and it is what the sun does at evening, and his school teaches all three meanings together. Orrenthal’s idea is a heart held in common, a frame whose every part owns the goods and the debts of the whole, and its operation is conjunction: the blow is joined to all of him. Petralon lies under it and hands down what is left. A maul that ought to split one plate spends itself through every plate at once, and the remainder goes into the earth he stands on. He bends under it, and he comes back.
This is Body work, raw Aether packed in the shell and told where to send a force. A small part of every spend burns in the shell’s own furnace, and his plates run warm to the hand after a long day of it. It is how he stood for nine days on the Kneeling Hill under the blows of a man a Stage above him.
Applications

Standing under an Archmaster’s blows for as long as the man cares to throw them
Shielding whoever stands in the shell’s shadow, asked or unasked, since a load is no person and bearing is no carrying

Associations

Orrenthal and Petralon, through the Body road he walks
THE CARRIED HOUSE, and a century and a half in the Porters’ Hall

Limitations

It runs inside the cost of the held house. A blow taken costs him nothing more, and the toll is the warmth in the plates
It bears what presses and what strikes. A pull, a lift or a grapple that uproots goes straight past it
Petralon settles. His stance sinks a little under every great load and does not always rise again. He stands a hand shorter than the day he left the pens, and the floors of his own house are stone because the wooden ones gave
Struck along the seams between its parts, the frame fails at the seam while the bulk still stands, and the crooked plate is the first seam
The tell is dust sagging toward the ground about his feet, a smell of stone and hot metal, and a faint metal sheen on the skin
It is countered by one who reads seams, by a hold that lifts, and by an iron-caged room

GOING IN (들어가오 · Deureogao, “I go in”)
GOING IN is basically inner world internalization: the power to go down Room by Room, binding each door behind him, until nothing that hunts him can follow. It came with the Class name Doorkeeper, and it is the first thing his school teaches.
Capabilities
It is a rite, done slowly and in order, one door at a time. Thaloré takes him down, and at each threshold Fixatio sets the door: once shut it is fixed past melting, and the way back through it is gone until a hand opens it from within. The outer Rooms stop a Pressure or a read. Deeper, a blow meant for the soul finds only wall. Deeper still, a claim laid on his name arrives at an empty house and has no one to serve. At the ninety-ninth nothing reaches him that has not first found him, and nothing living has.
