A block caught strung out on the march or half formed is twelve hundred men carrying long poles
It costs the house its pikemen, and her nothing she would call a working
Thornwall pikes are among the ninety-one names the north paid for the Seat beside Rob Stark’s
Its tell is a drum, and the thorn-horn every hundred paces
Horse on open ground before the hedge is set beats it
So do bolts and arrows from beyond the reach of the ash, which a slow block in felt with no plate anywhere can only walk through

characters/ability-accounts/hodge-toller.title: Hodge Toller — Abilities in full
characters/ability-accounts/hodge-toller.content:
Card: Hodge Toller
Techniques
Reeve’s Reckoning · Office art, handed down
Reeve’s Reckoning is basically lie detection, bought and paid for: the power to hear a lie ring flat once his two copper are in his fist. It is the reeve’s art of the Kingsbridge board, and it belongs to the office and not to the man. He opens it every morning with the words “Two copper, and tell me no lies,” a warning to the queue.
Capabilities
Nobody on the bridge claims to know how it works, and this is Ned Chapman’s reckoning from the outside. It is a bargain, the oldest small kind, and the fee is the whole condition. The copper buys his ear for the truth of what you say is in your pack, and once his two copper are shut in his fist your word is a paid thing between the two of you, as good or as bad as money.
So he hears it the way a money-changer hears a coin. A sound coin is one metal all the way through, and struck it sings, because the whole disc shakes together. A cased coin, good metal skinned over a base core, has a seam inside it where the two metals meet; the shake dies at the seam and the coin answers the hammer with a dull knock. A paid word that lies has the same seam in it, between what the mouth says and what the speaker knows, and it rings flat and dead in his ear.
What anyone watching sees is the charge. The two copper go into his palm, the fist shuts on them and is set against his breastbone the way a man holds a thing he means to keep, and his head goes over on one side. There is no Wellspring in it and no fire to throw. It is a small term of the kind any two people can set between them, kept by an office, and every way it fails comes straight out of the term.
Applications

Hearing whether what a person says is in their pack is true
Leaving the chain on its hook for a liar, who gets no blow from him

Associations

The office of toll-reeve at the Kingsbridge end of the great bridge; the art is handed down with the board, the brush, the paint pot and the coat
It has no Wellspring; by what it does, its Form is a Read
His Path is not given, whether he is woken is not shown, and no colors have been shown on him
The toll, two copper a pack, paid first

Limitations

Paid first: unpaid, there is no bargain, and he hears no more than any fat man would; when he coined the Warrior Merchant nobody had paid him, so there was no art in it at all
It weighs the word against what the speaker knows, so it tells him whether you lie and never why
A morning of liars gives him a headache by noon that only beer shifts, which is why he loves an honest pack
Its tell, when a word rings wrong, is his face going still and gray about the mouth in a tight sour grimace, and the chain staying on its hook
A true answer built to mislead has no seam in it to hear and walks straight past it
Refusing the fee stops his ear too, and gets you the chain
His “And?” to every pack is a ritual that catches nothing

characters/ability-accounts/hollis-drayc.title: Hollis Draycott — Abilities in full
characters/ability-accounts/hollis-drayc.content:
Card: Hollis Draycott
WHAT’S YOUR OLDEST
WHAT’S YOUR OLDEST is basically oath attunement: the power to hear what a man has promised before looking at his face, and to be held steady by his own promise. It is a Trait-art named for the greeting of his whole country. Between merchants in Nalūn the first question is what’s your oldest, and the answer is the token on the belt, shown before the name. Hollis Draycott asks that question of everyone he meets without opening his mouth, and he has spent his working life being the answer to it for the Vessant house.
Capabilities
A seal-token is a small disc of bronze or iron that sounds for as long as its contract is sound and goes dead and cold the moment the contract is breached. Oblation, the Wellspring of what is given up, a Fate Wellspring pooled deep under the salt cities, enforces what is sealed there, because a contract is two parties giving something up in front of a witness. The note is that enforcement made audible, kept in the metal for as long as the terms are kept on the road.
A sealed Nalūn contract is an oath with a house name and a Wellspring behind it, and every soul has a layer that holds such things: the Attraction Layer, the fate-side layer, the part that holds bonds, debts and oaths. So a token is a bond that can be heard from outside, and a bond kept long enough takes hold of the keeper. One half of this art is hearing another man’s bond. The other half is being held by his own.
Applications

Reading a person by what they are bound to
Standing unmoved in a room for as long as the house’s paper is kept

Techniques

READS THE BELT - the hearing half: he hears the contract in another man’s token
THE OLDEST CONTRACT - the held half: thirty-one years of a sound contract steady him

Associations

Oblation, the Wellspring under the salt, keeps the seal’s note in the bronze; he has harmonized no Wellspring of his own
The Spirit Path does the reading, in the Form of a Read, and Fate holds the bond, in the Form of a Bind
The Vessant house, whose seal and purse do his work
His aura is a faint bronze sheen, the color of a well-handled seal-token, with the steady hum of a sound contract under it

Limitations

Both halves run on tokens: one reads another man’s, and the other leans on his own
None of it is for fighting; he hires people for that
Nothing in it costs reserve

Traits
READS THE BELT · Primary Trait
READS THE BELT is basically bond perception: the power to hear in a seal-token’s note what its wearer is bound to. It is how a man of the factor houses reads a room, the way a sailor looks at the sky: before a face, the belt, and the bronze seal-token on it, and the note it hums.
Capabilities
Every factor in Halcrest can hear that a token hums. Draycott hears the contract in it, the way other men hear a tune. He is on the Spirit Path, whose work is what a thing means, and a token’s note means a bond: a house name written in the book, terms, and a term of years. His Core (the center of the soul, where a person’s own identity sits) does the listening, and his trained Perception and Attunement turn the note into what he can say aloud about its wearer. No Aether (mana) is pulled and no Essence (his own spiritual energy) is spent, any more than a listening man spends his ear.
What his ear works with is plain enough to any bell-founder. A disc of metal has its own pitch, set by its size, its thickness and its stiffness, so two tokens are never quite the same note. A ringing thing has a quality as well as a pitch, clean when it is whole and dull or buzzing when something in it has begun to give, which is how a potter raps a jar and knows it is cracked before he can find the crack. And two notes that are close but not the same beat against each other, a slow throb that can be counted; that is how a choir takes its pitch, and it is why the factors of Halcrest tune an ear to the Vessant token. His own bronze has held one note for thirty-one years, and he wears it at his hip as a tuning fork. Every other token in a room is heard against it.
Applications

Knowing who holds a man, for how much, since when, and whether the thing is starting to give
Telling a token higher or lower, steadier or wavering, sound or failing, old or new
Knowing from a silent disc on a belt that something is wrong

Associations

The Spirit Path, through the Core, in the Form of a Read
Oblation, which keeps the note in the metal
His own Vessant token, the tuning fork every other note is heard against
He learned token-reading in the Vessant counting rooms, from the agent who wore the token before him

Limitations

It reads the token and nothing else: a person with no token gives it nothing to read
Without a token to read he falls back on the plain eye, which a working life of belts has left a good deal less practiced than a soldier’s
A token tells him what a man has sealed, and never what the man will do with an open hand
A stolen token will not hum for the thief, so a silent disc tells him only that something is wrong and not what
A junior contract worn in front of an old one says exactly what its wearer wants said
It costs nothing, because nothing is made and nothing is thrown, which is also why there is no charge to see beyond the glance
Its tell is that glance, quick and open: his eyes go to your belt, then to the belt of whoever is with you, and only then come back up
It is beaten by wearing no token, or one that tells him nothing

THE OLDEST CONTRACT · Secondary Trait
THE OLDEST CONTRACT is basically indomitable will, lent by a contract: the power to stay calm, courteous and very hard to shift for as long as he is keeping the Vessant house’s oldest paper. Two agents wore the token before him and wore its rim thin with their thumbs, and when it came to his belt, the bond came with it.
Capabilities
Thirty-one years of a sound contract have bound his Attraction to the Vessant house’s oldest paper, and he has walked the Fate Path a little way, about three parts in ten of his practice, simply by keeping it every day. He works nothing with it and pulls no thread. What it does is hold him, the way ballast holds a ship: a hull with weight set low and fixed in one place rolls and comes back upright, and a man whose soul rests on one settled obligation does the same.
When the contract is threatened, his thumb goes to his token and runs once round the rim, and it is the only part of him that moves. He is checking, though he would not put it so: a token that has been breached goes still, and for thirty-one years the proof that all was well has been a hum under the right thumb.
Applications

Taking threats, flattery, a raised voice and a bigger man standing up over him, and coming back level
Lying for the house with a steady face

Associations

The Fate Path, through the Attraction Layer, in the Form of a Bind
The Vessant house’s oldest contract, thirty-one years sound
The Vessant token on his belt, Uncommon bronze, its rim worn bright and thin by his thumb and by the thumbs of the two agents before him

Limitations

It is loyal to the paper, not the people on the road: twenty-two men dead or missing did not breach the contract, so the token kept its note, and so did he
The steadiness is the contract’s, lent to him, and he has not found out what he is with the bronze gone quiet
It takes nothing from his reserve; the price is that he is the paper’s man before he is his own, and his breath pays for every lie he tells on its behalf
The bond steadies what he wills and has no hold on what his body does by itself: a lie told under strain pulls the breath up out of the belly into the top of the chest, so it comes in high and short, right up under the collarbone, and stops there a moment before it goes out
He has good control of his face and none of that, and a surgeon, a singer or anyone who has watched the dying breathe can read it across a room
Its tells are the thumb, once round the rim of the token, and the breath high under the collarbone when he lies
It is beaten by asking him what the contract has cost and not what it pays, because the paper has no column for that and he has to answer as a man: ask how many came back, not how many died, and watch his collarbone when he answers

characters/ability-accounts/kasane-byaku.title: Kasane Byakuya — Abilities in full
characters/ability-accounts/kasane-byaku.content:
Card: Kasane Byakuya
HALF A STEP AHEAD
HALF A STEP AHEAD (半歩先 · Hanpo-saki) is basically attack prediction: the power to see where a blow is going to end and to be standing there already, between it and her king. It was her signature art, and her Traits, her techniques and her Releases are this one idea at different sizes. The oath that pointed all of it at one man is the Byakuya house’s.
Capabilities
Every piece of it is the same act: be at the end of the road before the thing that is traveling down it. A blow is a road, a man’s next movement is a road, and a hall with a king in it is a hundred roads that all have to pass one place. It runs on two lenses, an eye and an oath. Fixatio, the Knot, is the idea of commitment, the bond with no way back, and its operation is coagulation, what is bound set past melting. Scholars set it beside a resin that has cured: a wax can be melted and poured again forever, but a cured resin has grown bridges through its whole body and will char before it flows. When she set her feet, the lens cured her stance into the stone, and for that breath she and the floor were one piece. That is what makes stepping in front of a blow worth doing. A blow carries a moving weight, and a moving weight is stubborn: it is never lost, only handed on, which the Measurewrights call momentum. An unanchored guard who catches a great blow is thrown backward into the man she is guarding, and has saved him nothing. An anchored one hands the whole of it down through her legs into the foundations, and the king feels a wind and hears the floor ring.
Judicium, the Scale, is the idea of truth told apart, discernment that knows a thing by the mark it cannot help leaving, and its operation is separation. Every substance shows its own lines to a trained light, and nothing can show another’s. The lens turned her Forecast and Vigilance on a room the same way, and what came back was the room ranked, worst first, with one thin arc-blue line laid on the threat that would reach the king. The Moto heart-eye added where a body’s weight was gathering before the limb had moved, since every real blow is paid for in advance by a shift of the hips and the back foot that the striker cannot hide. Between the two she did not need to see the blow. She saw the bill for it.
It all rode on blows, hers and other people’s. The guard’s step is a blow received on purpose, and the cut is the same read spent the other way. Nine parts in ten of what she spent reached the work, which is her yield. The lost tenth burned in the furnace of her Shell and left her as heat under the lacquer and as the red in her aura.
Applications

Getting in front of a blow aimed at the one she guards, and handing its force down into the floor
Ranking every threat in a room, worst first
Cutting a man at the place his own movement is carrying him to
Seeing where a road, a man, a marriage or a war ends
Stepping out from the end of a search before it arrives

Techniques

THE RED BEFORE THE WHITE - the house’s oath, which aims all of it at one man and his children
UNMEI NO SAMURAI - a body that is already in the way, in the one place every road has to pass
DOWN THE ROAD - the read turned on a life, which saw where her marriage went
THE GUARD’S STEP - standing at the end of a blow
AKAITO - cutting where a man’s next movement ends
SHINGAN - the Moto eye that confirms the nearest body
FŪIN - the same step taken ahead of a search
AKAZONAE - the First Release, which makes the stepping free

Associations

Fixatio, the Knot, holds her where she sets her feet and holds the blow where it meets her
Judicium, the Scale, ranks every threat in the room and marks the one that will reach the king
The Body Path leads: the foot, the lacquer and the cut, the full force of it at contact
The red harness of the Samurai of Fate, and the guard’s blade of the red chair, her bonded weapon, both left in the white house
Her ground is a guard’s ground: Fixatio loves worked stone, deep foundation and mineral rock, and Judicium wants dry air and a clear line of sight, so a king’s stone hall was the best ground in the world for her, and so was a salt mine

Limitations

It only ever puts her ahead of what is coming at someone else: every blow she stops lands on her
It has no answer at all when the one she guards is holding the knife
Fixatio’s glyph is Topology, which rules only what is joined to what; it can make her and the ground one thing and cannot make that thing stronger than her lacquer and her bones
Judicium’s glyph is Measure, which ranks only what is there to be read, so an end a man has not chosen yet has no line on it
Fixatio hates open water and anything that moves underfoot, and Judicium goes half blind in fog or behind an iron grille; on a ship’s deck in a sea mist she would have been a very fast woman with a sword and little more
The charge is small and always the same, and anyone who knows it can read her: her eyes go past the man in front of her, the near-white of her aura draws in and the red under it brightens along the edges, and the silk-cord note tightens
Under her feet the floor takes a faint amber shine for a breath, with a sweetish sharp smell of resin, and those nearest feel a prickle on the skin and a taste of hot copper as the Scale’s line goes out
Against a higher Stage the read fails first, because a stronger soul’s movement leaves fainter lines and its Pressure fogs the Scale; the step still arrives, and then the question is only whether her body behind its lacquer can live through what it stepped in front of
It is beaten by making the king the knife, by selling her a feint she believes, by changing your mind in the middle of your own movement, by coming at him from where she cannot stand, or by sending more than one body can meet
Fixatio fails as Irreversibility: what is set stays set, and a binding placed in error is a permanent feature of what it was placed on
Judicium fails as spectral overload, every line in view reporting at once until none can be ranked

Traits
She carried three Trait risks. The oath outliving the king it was sworn to is her Rigidity. Her Shear Break condition was the king as the knife, which happened. Her Reflex and her Oath both sit on the fracture line of her Stage.
THE RED BEFORE THE WHITE · Inherited Trait
THE RED BEFORE THE WHITE is basically oath embodiment: the power to be bound, body and soul, to the protection of one man and his children. It is the house’s and not her art: every Byakuya child has it said over them, and her sister carries the same words.
Capabilities
It was said over her at nine with her grandmother’s hand on her head: purity before power, peace before the blade, and the red line before the white, until the end of the red line. It bound her Attraction Layer to the Kōkan king and his children, and near him, keeping it, nothing frightened her and nothing got past her.
What it does for the art is aim it. A vow is small Fate, spent out of the swearer’s own share, and this one told her soul whose road she was standing at the end of, so that the step and the read both took their bearing from one man and his children.
Applications

Aiming the step and the read at the king and his children
Keeping her unafraid at his side

Associations

The Byakuya house and her grandmother, who taught the oath over the lamp
The Fate Path, Walked: a vow, kept on her own share and pulling nothing down, in the form of a binding
No Wellspring; the lens is the house’s oath

Limitations

It gave her dominion over the protection of the king and the king’s children, and it had nothing to say when the king himself was the one holding the knife
Its terms named the king as the one protected and never as the one protected against
She was strong enough to have stopped him in the cellars, and her blade would not leave its scabbard against him, and that is the whole of why she walked
Its tell is her lips moving over the words of the oath
It is beaten by making the king the knife
It has no Wellspring and so no Wellspring’s failure; its failure is its own terms

UNMEI NO SAMURAI (運命の侍 · Unmei no Samurai, the Samurai of Fate) · Primary Trait
UNMEI NO SAMURAI is basically bodyguard power: the power to be, always, the body between her king and whatever is coming. It is the idea itself, before any technique is made of it.
Capabilities
The Samurai of Fate are the guard of the red chair, every one of them a Byakuya or raised by the Byakuya, red lacquer for the red line and white lacing for the white line that kept it. She stood at the Kōkan king’s shoulder in every hall he ever walked into, half a step ahead and to his left, and her soul did that before it did anything else.
Fixatio cured the place into her the way it cures a stance into stone, so that the half step ahead and to the left was where her soul rested when it was doing nothing else, and leaving it was the thing that took effort. Her Reflex and Anchoring held a step higher on the hidden scale while he stood behind her. The step is the lens doing what it does for any anchored thing.
Applications

Standing at the one place every road to the king has to pass
Holding Reflex and Anchoring a step higher while he stands behind her

Associations

The Body Path, shaped by Fixatio
The Byakuya guard of the red chair
AKAZONAE, which lets this Trait off its limit

Limitations

It lends the step only while there is someone behind her to be anchored for; with nobody at her back it is a woman standing oddly in an empty hall
It guards from outside; it cannot stand between a man and what is in his own ear
It takes no reserve; it cost her nothing, and in the end everything
Its tell is where she stands: always half a step ahead of the king and to his left
It is beaten by coming at the king from where she cannot stand

DOWN THE ROAD (道の先 · Michi no Saki) · Secondary Trait
DOWN THE ROAD is basically destiny perception: the power to look at a road, a man, a marriage or a war and see where it ends. She could always see further down a road than the rest of them, and it formed into a law the night she understood where Gimbzo’s road was going.
Capabilities
A road has many ends, and Judicium lays its line on the one that the weight of everything already on the road is carrying it to, the way a trained eye picks the one flawed link in a coat of mail. The Measurewrights would call it reading composition from signature. Her sister said it more plainly: she saw things coming that the rest of them did not believe until they were standing in the door.
It is a read and never a pull. It moves nothing, brings no thread down, and costs her no reserve, which is why a soul on her low rung of Fate Mastery, Fate II, could hold it. The night it formed into law she sent four lines to her sister by runner, telling her to stay home, and walked into the salt with the boy before anyone knew she was going.
Applications

Seeing the end of a movement, a mood, a marriage or a war
Leaving before anyone else understands there is something to leave

Associations

Judicium does the ranking
The Fate Path, Walked, landing as a read through a Studied Spirit’s eye: a small use that opens no gate
Her Forecast, at the top of what her Stage holds
AKAITO, which is this Trait at the length of a sword, and SAIGO NO MICHI, which is this Trait made law

Limitations

It shows her the end of a road and gives her no way to change it, only to step off
It shows an end and offers no other, and the night it formed into law it showed her a cellar
It takes no reserve
Its tell is that by the time anyone else understands, she has already packed
It is beaten by a road whose end she cannot see

Techniques
THE GUARD’S STEP (先の先 · Sen no Sen) · Bloodline Art, the Byakuya guard
THE GUARD’S STEP is basically hyper interception: the power to move before a blow is thrown, so that it lands on her and not on him. It is the Samurai of Fate’s first lesson, taught on the Byakuya training ground.
Capabilities
The training ground’s name for it is the old one, sen no sen, the moment before the moment. A blow is paid for in advance by the hips and the back foot, and the guard learns to move on the payment. Her Reflex and Celerity put her across the line of a strike between one breath and the next, and the blow met the guard’s lacquer and not the king.
What Fixatio adds is the arrival. Her feet cure to the floor in the instant she lands, so that she and the foundations are one piece, and the blow’s weight, which is never lost and has to go somewhere, goes down through her into the stone and not back through her into him. The read, the crossing, the feet curing to the stone and the lacquer turned to meet the edge are one movement, and the wound is the one she chose over his.
Applications

Taking a blow meant for the king on red lacquer
Getting in front of any blow in the north, if she sees it coming
Stepping for nothing while AKAZONAE holds

Associations

The Body Path, shaped by Fixatio and aimed by the read
The Byakuya guard, who taught it
The red harness, which takes the edge at the breast and the right shoulder, where it has been relaid in patches

Limitations

It is a movement and a guard, and it deals no wound
Each step took about half a percent of her reserve, the price of the cure, set and broken again, and nothing she noticed until she had done it a thousand times
The blow still has to be taken on the harness and survived
It answers only a blow she sees coming; a feint she believes moves her out of the way of the real one
Its tell is that she is already moving
Before it, the counter is to show her a blow she will believe; during it there is nothing to be done, since she is already there
After it she is rooted for the length of a breath, and a second blow from another quarter finds her still set

AKAITO (赤糸 · Akaito, the Red Thread) · Signature Technique
AKAITO is basically trajectory prediction with a blade: the power to make one cut at the place a man has not reached yet. It is DOWN THE ROAD at the length of a sword.
Capabilities
She does not cut where the man is. She looks past him, down the road of his next movement, to where it ends, Judicium ranks the end that will reach the king, and she cuts there, so that the man arrives at the end of his own movement and the blade is already in the place he arrived. An archer leads a running deer the same way, loosing at the place it will be and trusting the deer to keep its appointment.
The cut is a plain cut and the damage is a blade’s, driven by her Penetration and a long arm of gray-bright steel. What the reserve buys is the force laid along the edge and the certainty of the place. Because the man is still arriving when the steel is already there, his own speed is added to hers, and the faster he came the worse it is for him. Both damages are real: the edge opens what an edge opens, and the blow follows it down the line of the one cut, laid along an edge and not thrown wide, and takes what is behind that.
For the length of the cut a thin red line hangs in the air from the scabbard’s mouth to the end of the man’s movement, with Judicium’s arc-blue fringing it. She never called it aloud, and the Hall never saw the blade out at all.
Applications

Ending a threat with one cut from the scabbard and back
Turning an attacker’s own speed against him
Beating Instrument plate

Associations

The Body Path: one cut from the scabbard, in the form of a strike, aimed by the read
Judicium picks the end
The guard’s blade of the red chair
She came to it by living it

Limitations

It took about six percent of her reserve
It cuts the end of a road she can see; a man who changes his mind in the middle of his own movement, or does not know himself where he is going, gives her an end that moves
It fails against Storied plate
A guard who cuts second cuts once
Its tells are her eyes going past the man to where he will be, and the red line, which is the whole of the warning
It is beaten by a road whose end changes

SHINGAN (心眼 · Shingan, the heart-eye) · Bloodline Faculty, Moto
SHINGAN is basically initial movement sense: the power to see where the next blow’s weight is gathering before the limb has moved. It is the common Moto sight, inherited, held low and quiet in her.
Capabilities
Every real blow is paid for in advance by a shift of the hips and the back foot that the striker cannot hide, and the heart-eye shows her that weight as it gathers. The Scale ranks the room, and the eye only confirms the nearest body in it.
Applications

Confirming the nearest body’s next blow

Associations

The Moto blood’s eye; no lens, and it spends her own share and pulls nothing down
Judicium, which does the ranking it only confirms

Limitations

In her it never passed Drilled, because she never needed it to

FŪIN (封印 · Fūin, the Salt Seal)
FŪIN is basically self-sealing: the power to shut her own soul so that there is nothing left to find. It is the last piece of HALF A STEP AHEAD: she saw where his search would end, and was gone from the end of it before he got there.
Capabilities
The Byakuya guard has never let the seven lines see what stands at the king’s shoulder, because the guard’s strength known is the guard’s strength planned for. GLASS was her sister’s; Kasane hid the plain way, by never once letting anything reach the king that she would have had to show herself to stop. When she walked into the salt she could not hide that way any more. A Crystal like hers changes the air round it: frost goes strange, flames lean, the fate-readers feel it from a valley off, and Gimbzo was looking for her with every eye he had.
So on the third gallery of the Orrel Cuttings, with the boy asleep in a salt niche, she turned Fixatio inward and tied the knot round her own Shell, three turns and a fourth no Byakuya had tied before. The Crystal shut to the lowest rung of the Aether ladder, the Dormant, sealed and silent, with no stat output above Hollow and nothing for a reader to find.
Fixatio’s flaw is that commitment cannot tell a true binding from a mistaken one, because the way back is closed for both alike; the Measurewrights call it irreversibility, and every other working of hers courts it as a risk. The Seal is that flaw chosen on purpose and used as the working: a knot whose undoing no longer exists as a place she could reach, which is the whole of why a fate-reader a valley off found nothing to read. Salt rock is deep, still, mineral ground, the kind Fixatio loves best, and the third gallery cured it harder than any hall floor would have.
Applications

Vanishing from every eye a king could send after her
Keeping her son hidden with her for sixteen years

Associations

Fixatio, turned inward on her own Shell, on the Body Path
The Byakuya knot, with a fourth turn of her own
The salt rock of the Orrel Cuttings
Her vow to herself, on the third gallery, never to be found

Limitations

It cost everything she was, at once, for good, and it has no clean undoing
She never tried to undo it, and cut salt at a mortal’s strength for sixteen years
She dropped her own humming token down a dead shaft, because a thing that hums can be heard
It was never an enemy’s to find; what beat it was sixteen years of salt dust in a mortal woman’s throat, and she died of salt-throat at forty-two with the Seal still tied

Releases
The only thing she ever called aloud was the one word, “Mae,” before. She was a guard and a legend and she did not shout.
AKAZONAE (赤備え · Akazonae, the Red Harness) · First Release
AKAZONAE is basically protection mode: the power to make the guard’s place true of every step she takes, so that nothing she steps in front of costs her anything. The word is the old one for a company armored all in red, and the release is the harness worn on the soul.
Capabilities
Called, it is the one word, said no louder than she says anything. The red comes up through the white of her aura like blood through a bandage, the silk-cord sound of the harness lacing becomes a thousand cords drawn tight at once, and the field goes the color of old blood. Reflex, Anchoring and Celerity strike a step high on the hidden scale. THE GUARD’S STEP costs her nothing while it holds, the cure which cost half a percent each time setting and breaking for nothing.
People in a hall with her have said afterward that they could not remember her moving, only that she was in front of each thing in turn.
Applications

Stepping in front of everything, for free, for four minutes
Raising Reflex, Anchoring and Celerity a step

Associations

The Body Path: the flesh and the blow transformed, through Fixatio
UNMEI NO SAMURAI, the Primary Trait let off its limit
THE GUARD’S STEP, which it makes free

Limitations

It lasts four minutes from full
Called silent it comes weaker, the red showing only at her throat and wrists
The red stays in her face for a day afterward, the lost tenth of four minutes’ spending, the furnace’s heat with nowhere to have gone under the lacquer
Time beats it

characters/ability-accounts/kimizu-moto-.title: Kimizu Moto — Abilities in full
characters/ability-accounts/kimizu-moto-.content:
Card: Kimizu Moto
KAGAMI (鏡), the Mirror
KAGAMI is basically Attack Replication: the power to read anything completely and give it back. It is his signature, the one idea his Traits, his moves and his rapier each express in their own way.
Capabilities
In the old stories a mirror shows what a thing truly is, and a demon that looks into one sees its own face and cannot pretend any longer. The idea Kimizu works by is the oldest idea any scholar or appraiser ever lived on: nothing is what it says; everything is exactly what it is. Its operation is separation, a thing parted from what it claims to be until the true parts show at the edges, each in its own color. A soul that has become that idea cannot look at anything without reading it.
What reaches the world is the Moto’s Work of Knowledge, held further than the house has seen it held, and run through Judicium, the Scale. Through YOMI he reads a person, a sword or a technique down to the last stitch: what it is made of, what job it was made for, how strong it is, and the one loose stitch where it will come apart. Through ISSHUN he has all the time he needs to do it, between one heartbeat and the next. Then he answers with exactly what they showed him: their own technique, their own weakness, their whole art played back at them. Fighting Kimizu is fighting a reflection of yourself, held by a ten-year-old who has already seen how it ends.
The glyph’s limit is his own strength: a mirror gives back the shape of a thing, not its weight, so every copy runs at Kimizu’s own power and not the original’s. The flaw follows from the idea: a mirror cannot close its eyes, and he cannot stop reading, so every face, wall and wound tells itself to him all day. Its contrary is concealment, the art of leaving no mark; and the thing that is exactly what it says it is, which gives a mirror nothing to show.
Applications

Reading anyone’s window, which nobody is supposed to be able to do
Copying a technique after seeing it once
Finding the one weak seam in armor, an art, a person or an argument
Breaking a disguise or an illusion by reading what is under it
Playing an enemy’s whole art back at them, flaw included
Learning anything faster than anyone

Techniques

YOMI - the principle as sight, always on
ISSHUN - the world gone still while his mind runs
THE RAPIER - the blade he carries, and the point his reading arrives through
KANTEI - a full read of anything
UTSUSHI - a technique copied after one sight of it
HOKOROBI - the strike at the one loose stitch
MASUKAGAMI - the enemy’s whole art at once, played back

Associations

Judicium, the Scale, whose idea is truth told apart and whose readers read weakness the way the lettered read text
The Spirit Path does the reading; the Fate half holds his grip on the Work of Knowledge
His Gnosis, already at the top of what his Stage allows
His father sees where a thing will break; Kimizu sees why it was built that way, and how to build it again
Tenma, who stands in front of him while he reads

Limitations

His copies run at his own strength, and his Ardency and Vitality are a child’s; he copies the clever moves, never the heavy ones
Copying a bloodline art or a Fate art fails or hurts him badly
He knows what a thing is, not what a person will choose
He cannot stop reading; after a big read his eyes bleed and he goes flat and empty the way the Moto do after a verdict
The tell: his eyes go still on one point just past the person, the arc-blue shows in them with thin lines of color at the edges, and he smiles a moment before he answers
His aura is the arc-blue of the Scale, and it shows mostly in his eyes
It is countered by concealment that leaves no mark, by brute force he cannot copy and cannot stop, by a thing that is exactly what it says it is, and by keeping him reading until he burns out
Under strain it fails the way a reader drowns: too much at once, and he cannot tell which of the hundred things he has read is the one that matters

Traits
YOMI (読み), the Reading · Primary Trait
YOMI is basically Information Analysis: the power to read anything completely, find its weakness and copy what it does. It is his Primary Trait, always on, and KAGAMI starts from it.
Capabilities
“Read” is the Moto house’s own verb for a person, and in Go and shogi yomi is a master seeing the board many moves ahead. Kimizu does both. He looks at a person, a sword, a wall, a technique or a Wellspring, and it opens to him like a book. At its height it is the Work of Knowledge at full strength: he reads a thing’s true name aloud, and it can no longer pretend. Disguises fall, illusions break, and a lie stops working in front of him. Yomi is also the old name for the land of the dead, and the house has noticed.
Applications

Reading windows, weaknesses and true names
Catching a lie as it is told

Associations

Judicium, the Scale; the Work of Knowledge
His Gnosis Perception and Analysis

Limitations

He cannot stop
Bleeding eyes and the Moto’s flatness after a big read

ISSHUN (一瞬), the Instant · Secondary Trait
ISSHUN is basically Accelerated Thought: the power to think so fast that the world goes still around him.
Capabilities
When Kimizu is in danger, his mind leaves the world behind. A falling sword hangs in the air, an arrow sits frozen in flight, and a man’s face is caught halfway through deciding what to do. In that stillness YOMI has all the time it needs, and he weighs every choice and picks the best one between one heartbeat and the next. To everyone watching he simply answers instantly and perfectly.
Applications

Reading a whole fight before it moves
The perfect parry, the perfect riposte, chosen at leisure

Associations

His Gnosis Cognition and Forecast, and his Dexterity Reflex

Limitations

His body does not speed up with his mind; he has time to choose, not more time to act
When the instant ends he comes out shaking, with a pounding head and a bleeding nose
Held too long or called too often, it costs him a full day before he can read again

Techniques
THE RAPIER · Blade (all swords)
THE RAPIER is basically Swordsmanship: Kimizu can use any blade, and he fights with the rapier.
Capabilities
He learned every sword the yard at the Seat would hand him, read each master who taught him, and settled on the rapier because it rewards exactly what he has and forgives what he lacks. A rapier is a long, light blade made for the thrust, fought at a careful distance from the other blade, where everything turns on measure and timing and very little on strength. He keeps the point in line, waits at the edge of the other man’s reach, and answers the attack with a thrust into the opening he read before it opened. ISSHUN gives him all the time in the world to choose the moment; YOMI tells him where the point should go; HOKOROBI is usually where it goes. He can handle a katana or a heavier sword well enough to win a lesson with it, but against a grown man’s weight only the rapier keeps him alive.
Associations

HOKOROBI rides the point; UTSUSHI lets him borrow a master’s footwork after watching it once
His Dexterity Reflex, and ISSHUN’s stillness

Limitations

A ten-year-old’s reach and a ten-year-old’s arm; a man who closes the distance and bears down on his blade beats him
A thrust that finds the stitch still needs enough behind it to go in

KANTEI (鑑定), the Appraisal · Move of KAGAMI
A full read of anything: what it is made of, what it was made for, how strong it is, and the window nobody else can see. It takes a moment of stillness and leaves a dull ache behind the eyes.
UTSUSHI (写し), the Copy · Move of KAGAMI
In Japanese an utsushi is a faithful copy of a master’s sword or painting. He copies a technique after seeing it once and uses it himself, at his own strength.
HOKOROBI (綻び), the Loose Stitch · Move of KAGAMI
Hokorobi is a seam starting to come apart. He strikes the one weak stitch in anything: armor, an art, a person, an argument. On the field it is usually his rapier’s point.
MASUKAGAMI (真澄鏡), the Clear Mirror · Finisher of KAGAMI
A masukagami is a perfectly clear mirror. He reads the enemy’s whole art at once and plays all of it back at them, the way they would have used it, flaw included. It burns so hot that afterward he cannot read anything for a day.

characters/ability-accounts/kit-quarrel-.title: Kit Quarrel — Abilities in full
characters/ability-accounts/kit-quarrel-.content:
Card: Kit Quarrel
Techniques
A PULL AT A TIME · Body art
A PULL AT A TIME is basically incremental strength: the power to pay for any load in small steps and keep every step paid. It is a paymaster’s idea: a big bill can always be paid in small coin, provided the coin already paid stays paid. Kit has built his whole way of fighting on it, and he has no Traits.
Capabilities
What anyone watching sees first is the smoky steel gray held close to his skin, with fine darker lines running through it the way rope runs over a pulley. That is his aura, the visible coat of his own power. The hue and the dry creak of it are nearest Ascensio’s, the Wellspring the scholars call the Ladder of Ascent, whose idea is the ladder: the whole height climbed by steps, with no single step large enough to break you. Kit has not said. Ascensio is a Wild Wellspring, a transformation of matter, and its operation is distillation, the same work passed up again and again by degrees until the whole height is reached; on a Body fighter it comes out plain: the body takes its load in steps. He pulls Aether (mana) up out of the ground he stands on, packs it raw into his Shell, the body-side layer of the soul, as Charge, and lays it on his hands and forearms as a harder coat. About two fifths of what he spends reaches the work, which is his yield. The rest burns in the furnace of his Shell and goes off as warmth in the knuckles and as the dry creak itself.
A heavy crossbow keeps the draw in its bent limbs, and a bow costs the same to bend by any road; the Measurewrights write it as force multiplied by distance. A windlass adds nothing to a man’s strength. Its crank and pulleys let him pay the draw as a small pull over a long way, twenty turns of the handle while the string comes back a hair at a time, and its pawl, the little catch that clicks into each tooth of a ratchet, keeps the string from running back between turns. Kit carries no windlass because his coat is one. The dark lines tighten all at once, like ropes taking up the load over a block, and the string comes back a hand’s breadth, and stops, and holds, because the lines stand on it the way a pawl stands in a tooth; then they run and tighten again, and it comes back another. Each pull is small enough for his joints to bear, and each one stands on the last, so his muscles never carry the whole draw at once and never have to hold it between pulls. Five breaths, and the string is on the nut, the catch in the stock that holds a spanned string, where the bow keeps the work without costing him anything more.
The shot itself is plain skill, with no Wellspring in it; the art has already done its part by putting the work into the bow. A crossbow lets its whole span go in the time a hand falls, the same work in far less time, which is why a bolt goes in to the fletching. He spends it where the body is thinnest: low in the side behind the ribs, where nothing but hide and gut wall covers the belly, or an inch behind the eye and below the ear, where the skull is thin.
Applications

Spanning by hand a horn-and-sinew crossbow that no man can draw
Keeping the bow spanned at no further cost; he sat a whole night by the fire with it spanned across his lap
Putting the whole span into one bolt, in the one place that ends it
Letting the price alone do the work, so that nobody has to be shot
Drawing the coat to one place and taking a bend slowly enough that nothing breaks, as with a surgeon’s needle straight off the coals

Techniques

THE HAND-SPAN - the boot into the stirrup, both bare hands on the string, a hand’s breadth to a pull, and the bow is spanned in five breaths where a windlass takes twenty turns
THREE COPPER - he lifts the bow a hair, so the light runs once along the notched stock, says in a flat, unhurried voice what the bolt costs, waits for the thing to stand still, and shoots once
THE NEEDLE - the same grip made small: a needle held over the coals in bare fingers until the steel went straw-colored, then bent into a new moon between finger and thumb, slowly, as one might bend a hot grass stalk

Associations

Ascensio, the Ladder of Ascent, a Wild Wellspring, is the nearest match to his color and sound; he has not named it himself
The Body Path, in the Form of a Shape
The crossbow, a big plain bow of horn and sinew with twenty-three notches along its stock, kept and not bonded
The Short Measure has only ever seen him do it, never learn it

Limitations

The lines hold only what has already been pulled, a step at a time, and they add no strength to any single pull
The art makes the pull bearable and does not make it quick: THE HAND-SPAN costs time, five breaths to a bolt, and for those five breaths he is a man standing on a bowstring with both hands full
Its failure is the ladder’s own: knock him mid-pull and a step lets go, and everything already paid runs back through his fingers at once, the string first
It is one bolt to a span, and he will not pay for a second one
About three fifths of what he spends burns in his Shell’s furnace and comes off as warmth and the creak
THE HAND-SPAN shows as the boot going into the stirrup and the gray coming up round both hands on the string; afterward, when he opens and shuts his fingers, the gray round the knuckles has thinned, like breath going off a cold glass, and is a moment coming back
THREE COPPER shows as the bow lifted a hair and the price said aloud
THE NEEDLE shows as the gray brightening at finger and thumb, a little clearer, the lines in the smoke tightening and running, before it sinks back close to the skin; no cost showed, and that it took the heat off his skin and lent the fingers strength is Ned’s guess
It is beaten by reaching him in the five breaths it takes, or by knocking him mid-pull so the steps run back
Against the shot, do not be the thing standing still: keep moving, keep a cart or a man between you and the bow, or close while he is still paying for the next one

characters/ability-accounts/kiyome-byaku.title: Kiyome Byakuya — Abilities in full
characters/ability-accounts/kiyome-byaku.content:
Card: Kiyome Byakuya
THE LAMP AND THE KNOT
THE LAMP AND THE KNOT (灯りと結び · Akari to Musubi) is basically clear sight and binding: the power to see the seam in everything, and to make whatever she ties stay tied. It is her signature art, and her Traits, her techniques and her Releases are this one idea done at a different size. The art counts its releases in Turns, for the three quick turns of the cord. When the third turn is made the knot is tied, and she is the knot.
Capabilities
Every piece of it is one act: find the seam, and hold. The Lamp finds. The Knot holds. A reading laid on her has a surface it must cross, a room has a seam in the moment a hand goes to a hilt, a working has a seam where its law was told where to act, a body has an inside, and a moment has a state. She meets each one the same way, and then the same idea goes bigger: the idea, the transformed body, the world obeying it. It all rides one blow. The Knot stops the thing for a breath, the Lamp shows the seam in it, and the edge goes to the seam: bind, read, cut.
The Lamp is Luminalis, the hidden light, whose idea is that seeing what hides and hiding what shows are one act run in two directions, and whose operation is separation: what is seen is parted from what is there. Her Shell does both. Looking out, it reaches under the surface to the mechanism, the warmth of a man behind a screen, the old break under the skin, the weld under the polish. Looked at, it turns the look back carrying only what the surface holds up, a mirror from that side only. The Measurewrights set it beside two facts about light: that most of what a thing gives off is light the eye was never built for, and that clear glass, slanted far enough from a ray, stops passing it and sends all of it back, which they call total internal reflection.
The Knot is Fixatio, the idea of commitment, the bond with no way back, and its operation is coagulation, what is bound set past melting. Scholars set it beside a resin that has cured: a wax can be melted and poured again forever, but a cured resin has grown bridges through its whole body and will char before it flows, because the softer state is no longer anywhere it can go. What she binds is held the same way, by the other arrangement having stopped being reachable, and force has nothing to do with it. Like any practitioner she pulls Aether (mana, in the common word) out of the ground she stands on, refines it in the Soul Crystal into Essence (spiritual energy), and drives it out through whichever layer the working lands through.
Applications

Returning every reading of her level
Holding a peace in a room past the point it should break
Parting a working at the join where it was put together
Stopping one thing for a heartbeat, for an ally’s arrow or her own edge
Lighting a body through and reading everything inside it at once
A draw that is over before its own sound arrives
Showing every seam, hidden wound, veil and lie on a field to everyone standing in it
Standing between the Kōkan heir and every blow meant for him

Techniques

THE WHITE KNOT - the Knot in its first and smallest form, tied across the seam of a room
BROKEN AND MENDED - the Knot turned on herself
THE RED BEFORE THE WHITE - the house’s oath, which the Third Turn makes law
GLASS - the Lamp run backward, turning a reading back at her surface
HAKKŌ - the Byakuya draw, laid along the one straightest line
KAGAMI-WARI - the Lamp turned on workings, cut at the join
MUSUBI - the Knot tied on a moment where it stands
SHINGAN - the Moto eye, with the Lamp in it
SHIROBANE - the lamp thrown ahead of her, lighting a body through
YUKIAKARI - the First Turn: her body made the lamp, glass gone to a prism
HAKUREN - the Second Turn: a hall of it, a hundred and fifty meters with no shadow in it
KŌKAN NO MAE - the Third Turn: the knot tied round her own body, between the heir and whatever is coming for him

Associations

Luminalis, the Lamp, her governing Wellspring; its glyph is Depth and its Titan is Nysera, who keeps the line between what is seen and what is there
Fixatio, the Knot; its glyph is Topology and its Titan is Atla’zon, who decides whether Essence stays inside the shape it was poured into
Fate, her mastered Path, carries the oath and the knot; Spirit, Walked, carries the reading of a room and the lamp; Body, Studied, is the draw, one movement trained ten thousand times behind a closed door
The Byakuya guard’s school, taught behind a closed door and never shown
Her katana, her bonded weapon, which carries HAKKŌ’s channel in its steel and the memory of an ancestor’s knot in its guard

Limitations

The Lamp’s glyph shows her how a thing is put together and never what the thing will choose, and it tells her nothing about what to do with what she sees
The Knot’s glyph freezes one small grid of outcomes for one short window: one thing, a thing she can see and name, in the state it was already in, for as long as she keeps paying; it holds an arm and never a will
She cannot hide in her own light and she cannot put down what she has tied: the oath is the crack in her Crystal and the thing holding the crack shut
Luminalis favors dry air, a clear line of sight and ground that carries a charge, and hates dense fog and iron-caged rooms
Fixatio favors worked stone and deep foundation, and hates open water and anything that moves under the feet
The Hall of Verdicts on a dry morning is the best ground she will ever stand on, and a steaming wood in a thaw is the worst
About twenty-three parts in twenty-five of what she spends reaches the work, which is her yield; what shows of the lost share is the cold rainbow at the edge of her aura and a faint clean warmth with the smell of fresh linen and of air after a storm
Mastery is quiet, and hers is nearly silent: the only sound is the glass at her temples
The charge is always there for anyone who knows the house: three quick turns before the white cord and before the white light that copies it, her eyes leaving the owner before KAGAMI-WARI, the split shadows and ringing beads before SHIROBANE, the violet line before HAKKŌ
At half her reserve the beads at her temples stop clicking and hang still; at a quarter the cold rainbow at her edges goes out; at a tenth the near-white flickers to gray and she has to put a hand on something to stand
At full output she would empty in about twenty seconds, and nobody has ever seen her spend at full
Against a higher Stage the art thins from the Knot down: MUSUBI holds a stronger Sovereignty for a heartbeat and no longer, and the Hall is dimmed from its edge inward
GLASS still reads level there, because it is a surface and no contest; KAGAMI-WARI still parts any working that has a join, whatever its weight, and still does nothing at all to a Trait; the draw does not care about Stage, it cares about the weather
Luminalis fails by birefringence: the Shell splits its own output into two paths that travel at different speeds, as some clear crystals show two images of one candle, and a complex working arrives out of step with itself, the cut in one place and its light in another
The shadows that split in two near her are that fault at its smallest and most harmless, and they are the warning to stop stacking workings
Fixatio fails by irreversibility: a binding placed in error stays placed, and she carries the largest example in the north in her own chest, an oath that outlived the reason for it and could not be put down
It is beaten by wet air, rain or a grounded iron for the draw, by a working with no seam, by a will stronger than her Sovereignty, by two blows inside one breath, or by setting the heir against his own good and making her choose

Traits
THE WHITE KNOT · Primary Trait
THE WHITE KNOT is basically peace inducement: the power to tie her own sword shut and have the peace she walked in with hold better than it should. It is the second half of her art in its first and smallest form: a thing tied so that the way back is a cut somebody has to make, and answer for.
Capabilities
A Byakuya ties it when she goes into a house where she means to keep the peace, whatever comes: three quick turns of the white cord round the guard of the sword and the mouth of the scabbard, so that the blade cannot leave its sheath without the cord being cut. Fixatio holds the knot to the oath sworn over it. Fixatio’s cure is the law under it, and the Topology glyph is its limit, since the glyph freezes only one small grid of outcomes: the cord joins her blade to its sheath and her word to the room.
She untied it at the Foot, slowly, as if the movement had been waiting in her body for sixteen years, and gave the cord to her sister’s son. It is Tsugigane’s sageo, its scabbard cord, now. It was always his. Her blade has been free to leave its scabbard since that day, and nobody but Tetsugen and Hayato understood what that meant. The knot survives in her as a working, MUSUBI.
Applications

Bringing tempers down in a room
Taking hands off hilts
Making a parley last

Associations

Fixatio, the Knot
The Fate Path: a bond tied on a thing and on a room
The oath sworn over the knot
Her katana, whose guard carried an ancestor’s knot for three hundred and twelve years
MUSUBI, which is the knot as a working

Limitations

It holds her own peace and her own sword; it cannot make another man keep his, and it has no say over a hand that is not hers
It takes about two percent of her reserve to tie and nothing to keep
The three quick turns of white cord round the guard and the scabbard mouth are its sign
It is beaten by cutting the cord, and the cutting costs the cutter, because the Dawi who made her sword felt her ancestor’s knot in the steel for three hundred and twelve years and walked four hundred miles when it came undone
The cord itself is gone from her sword now

BROKEN AND MENDED · Secondary Trait
BROKEN AND MENDED is basically self-restoration: the power to break where the whole room can see it and be whole again inside a breath. It formed at the Verdict of Six, when her voice shook in the Hall for the first time, and it is the Knot turned on herself.
Capabilities
When something strikes her the fine silver rings in her eyes turn once, very slowly, and her composure breaks, visibly, and mends in a breath. The breaking is the Trait as much as the mending, and the mending is real. Her Crystal has been cured, broken and cured again so many times that mending is the shape it sets in. Stability holds her through it.
At Dissonance it holds her Crystal too. The fracture of the four lines opens a hair every time she breaks and closes every time she mends, which is why she can stand at Stage XI without the Crystal running away from her.
Applications

Taking a blow to her composure and coming back whole
Holding a Dissonance Crystal that would otherwise run away from her

Associations

No lens: it is the Crystal’s own habit
The Spirit Path, Walked: the Core mending its own break
Her Stability
The Lamp’s half of the bargain, since nothing in it is hidden

Limitations

Nothing in it is hidden: the room sees the break, and that is the price of a mend that is real
Past that it costs nothing she shows
It mends one break at a time; a second blow inside the breath finds her still open, and a second break she does not always mend
The silver rings in her eyes turning once give it away
It is beaten by striking twice before she mends

THE RED BEFORE THE WHITE · Inherited Trait
THE RED BEFORE THE WHITE is basically oath empowerment: the power to stand stronger and steadier beside the one she is sworn to guard. It is the Byakuya oath to the Kōkan heir. It is the house’s and not her art: every Byakuya child has it said over them, and her sister carried the same words to the red chair.
Capabilities
She stands between the red king’s child and anything that comes for him, and he owes her nothing back. The oath is spoken over every child of the house at nine, with a grandmother’s hand on her head, and it is in the blood as much as in the words: her Attraction Layer is bound to the Kōkan heir and his seat. Near him, keeping it, her Oath and Ward stand a step higher on the hidden scale, fear reaches her late, and her hands do not leave the work.
It is a vow, which is small Fate, kept on her own share with no thread pulled down for it, and that is why it costs no reserve. Fixatio is only what has made it impossible for her to put down. For sixteen years it bound her to nothing, a red line she believed had ended in the cellars, and she kept it anyway. The pressure of keeping it with nothing at the end is what drove her up through the Stages alone in the white house: an oath with no object is a load with no ground under it, and her Crystal grew to carry it.
Applications

Guarding the Kōkan heir with her Oath and Ward a step higher
Keeping her hands on the work when fear should have reached her
Giving KŌKAN NO MAE the sentence it makes law

Associations

The house’s oath, with no Wellspring behind it
The Fate Path: a vow, kept on her own share and pulling nothing down
The Kōkan heir and his seat
Fixatio, which has made it impossible to put down

Limitations

It binds her to the boy and does not bind the boy to her; she can serve him and cannot command him
It obeys as well as serves: when the heir orders her, her lips move over the words and she goes, because she cannot command the red line and the red line can command her
When the king himself is holding the knife, as Gimbzo was, the oath has nothing to say, and her blade will not leave its scabbard against him
It costs nothing to keep and everything to break
Her lips moving over the words give it away
Its Rigidity is the oath outliving the reason for it, as it did for sixteen years
Setting the red line behind the white is her Shear Break condition
Her Oath stands at 725, past the fracture line of Dissonance; an oath broken now would break the Crystal with it
It is beaten by setting the heir against his own good and making her choose

GLASS (玻璃 · Hari) · Passive Trait
GLASS is basically reading reflection: the power to send every reading of her back level, carrying only what she holds up to it. It is the Lamp run backward, and in the old tongue of the house the word is hari, glass.
Capabilities
There is something so still and so clean in her that wards go over it like water over glass and find nowhere to catch, and a reader’s threads lie flat off her when she speaks the truth, which is always. Luminalis, the seeing and the hiding that are one act, runs here backward: it sets her Shell against any look laid on it the way clear glass slanted far enough from a ray stops passing it and sends the whole of it back, so a reading returns from her surface carrying only what the surface holds up. A ward is a look with a hook on it and fares no better.
At Dissonance it also does the thing the Byakuya have used it for since the house began: it returns any reading level, and level is whatever she holds up to it. Because the trick is all surface, it is no contest of reserve. What decides it is her Ward against the reader’s eye, and at 660 there are very few eyes in the north that outrank it.
Under Gimbzo the house’s custom became something more: he put his own blood down the cellars for being strong enough to tell him no, and a Byakuya at Dissonance in the white chair would have gone down after them. So she let GLASS do what it does. Every Measurewright, Hall assessor and fate-reader has entered her at Level 160, Stage VI, an Expert, with a Shell newly emerged, since she was fourteen.
Applications

Letting wards and readings slide off her
Showing every assessor a lesser woman than the one standing there
Keeping the Byakuya guard’s true strength unknown to the seven lines

Techniques

THE VEIL - GLASS as the house has always used it: every reading of her comes back as whatever she chooses to show, which since she was fourteen has been a Stage VI lady with sense and no reach

Associations

Luminalis, the Lamp
The Spirit Path, Walked: the surface of the soul, turned against a look
Her Ward, which decides it
The Byakuya guard’s custom of never letting the seven lines see what stands at the king’s shoulder, because a guard whose strength is known is a guard whose strength is planned for

Limitations

It costs nothing, and the Veil costs nothing
It hides nothing she chooses to show and protects nothing she is not
Plain eyes see her perfectly, and she cannot lie through it, because she does not lie; she has never once said she was Stage VI, she has only let people read it
The Veil’s limit is the body: plain eyes see a woman whose hands do not shake when they should, and whose draw, if anyone ever saw it, would end the pretense at once
When she calls YUKIAKARI the Veil is gone and cannot be put back in front of anyone who saw it
Every reading of her coming back level is itself the sign
It is beaten by a plain question asked in plain light

Techniques
HAKKŌ (白光 · White Light) · Signature Technique
HAKKŌ is basically a lightning draw: the power to lay a charged line through the air and bring the blade out along it faster than its own sound. It is the Byakuya draw, and the school’s working more than her own: the guard teaches the draw on Judicium, and the sword carries the channel in its steel.
Capabilities
The guard teaches the draw on Judicium, the Scale, whose idea is truth told apart and whose operation is separation, and in the draw the thing told apart is one line of air: from the scabbard mouth to the place the cut will end, the air along that line is parted into charged pieces and set apart from the air round it, a road laid before anything travels down it. A storm lays its road the same way, more slowly. A faint leader feels its way down in steps and leaves a thin road behind it, and then the return stroke runs back up that road many times faster than the leader came down. The Measurewrights say the air along it is heated several times hotter than the face of the sun before it has time to move aside, and that air that hot and that sudden can only burst outward, and the bursting is thunder.
Her left thumb cuts the scabbard mouth, and Judicium lays the road. For that breath a hair-fine violet line hangs in the air. That line is the leader. Her blade is the return stroke. The cut is over before the sound of the draw arrives, and the thunder is the air closing behind it. She does not call it; the thunder does.
It rides the blow completely. The cut is an honest cut by a Very Rare blade, and the stroke goes in with it, so the wound is a sword wound that has also been struck by lightning from the inside, parted and burned shut along the same line. It lands along a line a few inches wide, about a kiloton and a quarter by the Measurewrights’ reckoning. Inside her Hall the violet line is laid along one of the seams that already show.
Applications

Ending a fight in one movement, before the blow lands on her
A cut that parts and burns shut along the same line
Following a seam the Hall has already lit

Associations

Judicium, the guard’s school’s lens for the draw, carried in the sword’s steel and never harmonized by her
The Body Path, Studied: one cut from the scabbard, with the full force of it at contact
The Byakuya guard’s school, which taught it
Her katana, which carries the channel
YUKIAKARI, under which the violet line shortens to half a breath

Limitations

The violet line hangs for a full breath before the cut, and anyone with the eye can read it like a signpost and see exactly where she is going to cut
It takes about four percent of her reserve
Afterward the thunder is loud enough to stun anyone near it who did not see it coming, her allies included
The fault is the road’s own: what she parts out of the air is a storm’s road, and it keeps a storm’s habit of taking the easiest way to ground, so water, rain, wet earth or a grounded piece of iron near the line is an easier road than the one she laid
The channel wanders to it, and the blade, which only follows, either goes with it or arrives without it
A cut that loses its channel arrives at the speed of a very fast woman, which is still very fast
Along the line the blade beats Instrument plate; in the wet, or against Hallowed plate, it is only a very good sword
She has said so herself: her light wants dry air, and in steam as wet as a bathhouse the channel would wander like a drunk on a road and arrive wherever the water pulled it, perhaps in her own feet; in such air she fights with the spear
It is beaten by wet ground, rain or grounded metal; a grounded piece of iron thrust across the line takes the stroke

KAGAMI-WARI (鏡割り · the Mirror Split) · Bloodline Art, Byakuya
KAGAMI-WARI is basically spell cutting: the power to find the join where a working was put together and cut it there, so it falls in two clean halves. It is the Lamp turned on workings.
Capabilities
The Byakuya Meigan sees hidden seams and the clean structural breach, and in her Luminalis turns that on workings as well as on steel and bone. A working is a law and a place the law was told to act, and the join between the two is the only part that is neither. She looks at a technique instead of at its owner, finds the seam where its boundary condition meets its law, and cuts there, and the working comes apart along its own join, like a mirror that falls in two clean halves.
The school’s Seam-Gospel Cut, Nuime-kiri, lays a blade along a working’s join by feel. Hers is that cut with the Lamp behind it, so the join is seen. She calls it, clear and quick, “Kagami-wari,” and any edge will carry it once the eye has found the join, the sword or the side-blade of a spear.
Applications

Splitting a working of any weight, so long as it has a join
Splitting GŌKA at the seam where the fire is placed

Associations

Luminalis, through the Meigan, the Byakuya eye
The Spirit Path, Walked: a working read, and parted at its join
The school’s Seam-Gospel Cut
Any edge she is holding

Limitations

It parts and does not unmake: the law lets go, and whatever the working had gathered is still there, loose, and falls where it is, and she is standing next to it; a fire split a third gathered is a third of a fire on the ground
It takes about two percent of her reserve, and a heartbeat of looking that she cannot spend on anything else
A working must have a seam: a pure physical blow has none, and a working that is all one law with no boundary has none
A Trait, which is the soul’s own law and no boundary at all, gives her nothing to cut; she can do nothing to ENSHŌ
Her eyes leaving the owner and going to the working give it away
It is beaten by a working with no seam, or by a fighter who never lets her stand still long enough to look

MUSUBI (結び · the Knot) · Application of Fixatio
MUSUBI is basically immobilization: the power to tie three turns of white light round a thing and stop it where it was. It is what the white cord did to her own sword, done to anything she can see.
Capabilities
Three quick turns of white light go round a thing, and Fixatio holds it where it was, in the state it was in, for as long as she keeps paying, like a fly in amber. She calls it in one word, “Musubi,” and the knot sets with an amber flash in the white. The hold is a cure and no grip: for that breath the other arrangement of the thing, the hand an inch further on, is nowhere it can go.
Fixatio’s hold is contested by Sovereignty, hers against that of whatever she has tied. A heartbeat is still a heartbeat. She ties it to buy one, for an ally’s arrow or her own edge, and she will tie it again.
Applications

Stopping a wrist, a raised blade or a fist in the air
Holding a door, or a fire’s front
Catching a working in the moment it fires
Buying one heartbeat against something stronger than she is

Associations

Fixatio, the Knot
The Fate Path: a condition tied on a thing she can see and name
Her Sovereignty, which the hold is contested on
THE WHITE KNOT, which it survives from

Limitations

What she binds must be a thing she can see and name, and she can hold a man’s arm and not his will
She can hold one thing at a time
It takes about three percent of her reserve for each turn of the breath
It is paid in her own arms: when the thing tied is stronger the strain goes down into her hands
A practitioner whose Sovereignty outranks hers pulls out of the knot at a cost to both of them; against a stronger Sovereignty it holds one heartbeat, cracks, and goes to white dust
A contested knot splits her fingernails one after another on whatever she is holding, and each knot she ties again opens a fresh split in her fingers
The three turns of light give it away
It is beaten by a will stronger than her Sovereignty, or by a thing she cannot see

SHINGAN (心眼 · the heart-eye) · Bloodline Faculty, Moto
SHINGAN is basically structural perception: the power to see where a thing carries its weight, and what is working under a face. It is the common Moto sight, which in her line is the Meigan, the Eye of Revelation.
Capabilities
It shows as fine silver rings in her eyes. In her the sight is held level and quiet, the rings lying as still as the face of a deep well, so that the moment they turn is the moment everyone in the room learns something has struck her. With Luminalis it reads beneath a face to the mechanism under it as well as where a thing carries its weight.
With the Lamp in it, it shows her the gold line the Kōkan heir’s own eye lays across the air, because the gold in that eye is the surface of something, and what lies under a surface is hers to see.
Applications

Reading where a thing carries its weight
Reading what is working under a face
Seeing the gold line the Kōkan heir’s eye lays across the air
Seeing every seam her Hall lights, as a fine bright line

Associations

The Moto blood, which gives the eye and an early grip on the Thread ladder, and never a Path
No lens of its own; Luminalis sharpens it
It reads, spends her own share, and pulls nothing down

Limitations

It cannot read a man who is truly still inside
It does not tell her what to do about what she sees
It is a slow, steady spend while it is held wide, about ten hours from full
At rest the rings lie flat and silver as winter ice; when they turn, the room knows she has been struck

SHIROBANE (白羽 · the White Feathers) · House Working, Byakuya
SHIROBANE is basically scanning light blades: the power to throw a silent fan of feathers made of light that open a body a finger deep and light it through. It is the house’s oldest working, and the same lamp thrown ahead of her.
Capabilities
The Byakuya beast is the Owl, and the working has the Owl’s shape for the same reason the Owl hunts as it does: nothing hears it come. A fan of white planes goes out ahead of her, a hundred, two hundred, each the shape of an owl’s flight feather and as long as a forearm, so thin it has no edge to look at, only a plane of light with a cold rainbow burning along its rim. They make no sound in the air and cross eighty paces in the time a candle flame takes to bend.
Each feather is light held so hard and so narrow that where it touches it boils the surface off into vapor, the way a burning-glass holes a leaf; the Measurewrights call that ablation. It does not cut as steel cuts, and it goes exactly as deep as she lets it, a finger’s depth into the muscle of a belly wall and no further.
The wound is beside the point. In the instant a feather is inside a body Luminalis lights that body through, the way a hand held in front of a candle shows the shadow of its bones, and she sees everything in it at once: a scalded lung, the pace of a heart, the heat banked in the tissue, the open fracture in a Crystal with every lesser crack running into it. Then she arrives behind the feathers, at a run faster than eyes follow, already knowing where everything is, so that a watcher thinks the last feather folded itself into a woman. She does not call it.
Applications

Reading the inside of a body at eighty paces
Finding a hidden wound, banked heat or a cracked Crystal before she closes
Covering her own arrival

Associations

Luminalis, the Lamp
The Spirit Path, Walked: projection, force at range, sent to read
The Byakuya house and its beast, the Owl
YUKIAKARI, out of which the Feathers go when it comes up uncalled

Limitations

A fan takes about one percent of her reserve
It wounds shallow by design, and what it shows she must still act on with something else
Fog, steam and smoke scatter the planes into glare before they arrive, and a mirror-bright surface throws them wide
Before it, every shadow near her splits in two and the beads ring, and a white fan opens ahead of her without a sound
It is beaten by bad air, or by a body that drinks heat, closing every seam the feathers open and keeping their heat for itself

Releases
YUKIAKARI (雪明かり · Snowlight) · First Release, the First Turn
YUKIAKARI is basically light embodiment: the power to stop looking through the Lamp and become it. She calls it “Akari,” light, and the name is the old word for the light that snow gives back at night, enough to walk by with no lamp lit.
Capabilities
Glass passes light and shows nothing of it. A prism is the same glass cut so that the light comes out sorted, every color laid beside the next, and the Release is that cut made in her: the Lamp stops being something she looks through and becomes something she is.
The glass of her aura goes to a prism. The near-white breaks into every color at once round her edges, the glass beads at her temples ring where they used to click, and the halo-ring at her crown throws a pale gold circle on the floor round her feet. Reflex, Finesse and Perception strike a step high on the hidden scale for as long as it holds.
It can come up in her uncalled, as it did a thousand mornings alone behind the closed door, with the beads ringing at the very edge of hearing and every shadow split in two, and the White Feathers go out of it.
Applications

Striking a step high in Reflex, Finesse and Perception
Shortening HAKKŌ’s violet line to half a breath
Sending out SHIROBANE

Associations

Luminalis, the Lamp let off its limit
The Spirit Path, Walked, with the Studied Body’s edge under it: the body made the lamp
HAKKŌ and SHIROBANE, which it sharpens
A Walked Spirit Release, past the one Release her Fate lead brings; it stands because the frozen road saw it

Limitations

Called silent, the prism stays inside the glass and the gain is half
It lasts about four minutes from a full reserve
Afterward her hands shake for an hour
Its price is the Veil: once anyone has seen it, the Stage VI lady is gone for good in front of them
It is beaten by everything that counters HAKKŌ, and by patience

HAKUREN (白廉 · the White Hall) · the One, the Second Turn
HAKUREN, as a Release, is basically domain activation: the power to open her Domain in one breath. It is her Fate lead’s one Release, the One, opened at Refraction and counting as her Second, and it opens and powers the Domain.
Capabilities
Called, the field forms as it is named. The note of the struck crystal bowl rises under the beads and holds, and the field opens.
Associations

HAKUREN, the Domain it opens and powers

Limitations

Silent, it comes in at half the reach
Held past its limit it is a Crystal Fracture Event along the line of the four letters, and she has never held it past its limit

KŌKAN NO MAE (Before the Red) · the One’s last stage, the Third Turn
KŌKAN NO MAE is basically harm interception: the power to make every blow meant for the heir land on her instead. It is the oath made law, and the third turn of the cord.
Capabilities
The One’s last stage makes one Trait’s stated effect local law, and here the effect is the oath’s own sentence, the red before the white. Fixatio binds her body to the place between him and the blow, wherever the blow comes from, and THE RED BEFORE THE WHITE lifts her Oath, Ward and Anchoring to the top of what her stack will hold, so that nothing in the field reaches him except through her.
For forty seconds the Hall has one seam in it, the line between the heir and the blow, and she is tied across it. Every blow that would have landed on him lands on her instead, and is entered against her. The Hall’s white takes Fixatio’s amber at its edges while it holds, and the sweet resin smell comes up through the clean one.
Applications
