Keeping the Kōkan heir untouched by anything in the field
Lifting her Oath, Ward and Anchoring to the top of her stack

Associations

Fixatio, on the house’s oath
The Fate Path, Mastered: a binding made local law inside the Hall
THE RED BEFORE THE WHITE, whose stated effect it makes law, and that effect alone
HAKUREN, the Hall it must be called inside

Limitations

It can be called only with the Kōkan heir behind her, inside her White Hall
It lasts about forty seconds from a full reserve
The price is plain, and she said it at nine: what would have killed him is owed by her, and if it is enough, it is paid
Fixatio’s own failure is the price too, since a binding placed stays placed: she cannot step out from in front of a blow she would rather dodge, and the guard who was built never to be hit takes every one
Its limit is the oath’s own: it guards him from outside, and it has nothing to say if the knife is in his own hand
It is beaten by making her choose between him and his good, or by outlasting forty seconds

Domain
HAKUREN (白廉 · the White Hall) · Domain
HAKUREN is basically a revealing territory: the power to make a hundred and fifty meters of ground where nothing has a shadow and nothing has an inside she cannot see. It is the Lamp at its largest: where her eye finds one seam, the Hall shows every seam to everyone.
Capabilities
The One, counting as her Second, opens it in one breath, with Luminalis as the law of the ground. Every surface is lit from all sides at once with a clean near-white light that throws no shade. Veils, Letheveil concealments and Tenebra darks come apart in it like fog in a lamp. Every seam in every working, every weld in every blade, every place a body is carrying a wound it has hidden, shows to her Shingan as a fine bright line, and to her allies as a faint one. A lie spoken inside the field leaves the speaker’s mouth with a visible tremor in the light round it, because Luminalis shows the mechanism under a face, and a lie is a mechanism.
The school’s Glass Cathedral Sight, Hari no Dō, makes one room transparent to one reader for a breath. This is that art grown into a place and held. Called, it forms as it is named, on the note of the struck bowl, and the first thing anyone inside notices is their own feet, standing on a floor with no shadow under them. Like every Domain it is a claim laid on the ground and pulls no thread. The characters of its name say white and without stain, and the north has always heard a hall in it.
It adds no force to any blow and moves nothing. It only takes away the dark, and in a fight between people who rely on being misread, that is enough.
Applications

Stripping veils, concealments and darks from a whole field
Showing every seam, weld and hidden wound to her and her allies
Making a lie shake the light round the mouth that told it
Laying HAKKŌ’s violet line along a seam already lit
Giving KŌKAN NO MAE the ground it is called on

Associations

Luminalis, the Lamp
The Fate Path, Mastered: a claim on conditions, authored in the Core
The One, counting as her Second, which opens and powers it
The school’s Glass Cathedral Sight, grown into a place
Her Shingan, which reads what it lights

Limitations

It reaches about a hundred and fifty meters, and lasts about two and a half minutes from a full reserve
It adds no force to any blow and moves nothing
The law is total: light does not sort friend from enemy, and neither does the Hall; she cannot hide in it either, and it shows her allies’ secrets to her enemies as plainly as theirs to her
Its weak side is its Dominion, a mean of 145.71 with a Sovereignty of 195: a practitioner of her Stage with stronger Sovereignty contests the ground and dims the field from its edge
A Domain that is itself made of light, or a heat bright enough to drown it, washes it out
It is beaten by a stronger Sovereignty dimming it from the edge, by a brighter light or a great heat to drown it, or by fighting her with nothing hidden

characters/ability-accounts/larkin-gedge.title: Larkin Gedge — Abilities in full
characters/ability-accounts/larkin-gedge.content:
Card: Larkin Gedge
Techniques
HALVES! · Synergia, with Parkin Gedge
HALVES! is basically twin synchronization: the power to feel his brother’s sword as surely as his own hand, so the two of them can cut one wolf from both sides at once without looking, and it has nowhere to duck. Larkin shouts the name and counts each kill twice. Parkin calls it HALF AND HALF and says Halves sounds like a pie.
Capabilities
The thread is the whole art. A man knows where his own hand is with his eyes shut, because the muscles and joints report their place and their load to him without being asked. The scholars call that sense proprioception, the body’s knowledge of itself. The bond lends each twin a share of the other’s. Larkin feels where Parkin’s edge is, how fast it is moving and when it bites, the way two sawyers on one cross-cut saw feel each other down the blade and never need to look up. So they cut blind. A wolf that gets inside one man’s sword has only ducked one edge; with two edges crossing in it from two sides in the same instant, whichever way it goes off the one, it goes into the other.
The brothers are harmonized with Benediction, the Grace, whose law is that a bond freely given is weighed by the world as a real thing. Kit Quarrel’s word for it is “the blessing kind, that keeps no count.”
What anyone watching sees first is the charge. The twins put their shoulder blades together, both coats thicken to the red-gold of a loaf crust as they pull Aether (mana) up off the ground they stand on, and a thread of the same color comes up between their shoulders and pulls taut, with a soft low chord under it, a click as it catches, and a smell of new bread and church incense. About two parts in five of what each brother spends reaches the work, and the rest goes off them as warmth, which is why the ditch smells like an oven mouth.
Applications

Cutting blind off his brother’s edge, back to back
Cutting high while his brother cuts low through the same body in the same instant, so that it comes apart in two pieces that go on kicking
Going in at the head to make a thing look while his brother cuts from behind, “one before and one behind, as is the custom of the house”

Associations

Benediction, the Grace, a Wellspring of Fate whose Titan is Florwyn
His Path is not given; the Form is a Strike, and it lands through the body
Parkin Gedge, his twin and Resonant Pair, with whom he came by it living
Two plain hangers off the same smith’s bench

Limitations

Benediction has no primary glyph to set its limit, so the limit is the bond’s own measure: the thread is a sword’s reach long and no longer, and past that it snaps and they are two ordinary swordsmen with matching hangers
It is paid by the pair: both coats thin at once and they draw one breath together, every time, so neither can spare the other, and a twin who is winded winds his brother
It is no working thrown at an enemy and it does nothing to the wolf by itself; it rides two plain sword cuts, and all the damage is steel
It is two edges on one target
Its named failure is displacement, which the Measurewrights call competitive inhibition: a bond holds only until something one brother holds dearer takes its place, and the thread goes without either of them feeling it, until the blind cut comes and there is no second edge in the wolf; twenty-five years of the oatcake joke have not managed it yet
Its tell is the twins going back to back with the red-gold thread taut
It is beaten by parting them past a sword’s reach, by coming at one of them from where the other cannot turn, or by giving them more bodies than two edges can cross in
No reserve figure has been read for him

characters/ability-accounts/lorn-stark-—.title: Lorn Stark — Abilities in full
characters/ability-accounts/lorn-stark-—.content:
Card: Lorn Stark — The Sword
WHERE IT ENDS
WHERE IT ENDS is basically boundary manipulation: the power to decide where a thing ends, and to hold that line with cold. He scratches a line in the snow, swears to hold it, and whatever crosses it freezes. It is his signature art, and his Traits, his techniques and his Release are that one idea done at a different size.
Capabilities
House Stark defines where things end and begin. The blood decides where the warmth ends. The scratch in the snow decides where the road ends. The oath decides where he ends, which is nowhere short of the thing he swore to. The walk keeps him on his own side of all three. The Release is the same border drawn all the way round him and held until it breaks him.
The cold is the house’s inheritance and no Wellspring, so it has no Wellspring’s idea, no glyph and no Titan behind it. It has one rule of its own, which is that the Stark blood moves heat out and never in, and that rule is the house’s old decision worn in the body: the blood decides where the warmth ends, and it ends at a Stark. A house needs a fire and an icehouse needs a deep hole, and a Stark’s body is the hole. The air, the timber, the snow and the men inside a few paces of him give up their warmth to him, it passes down through his trunk and legs without stopping to warm him, and it leaves through his heels into the earth, which is big enough to take the heat of a whole army and not notice. The Measurewrights who have been allowed near one call it a heat pump made of a man, a thing that carries warmth from where it is to where it is wanted and pays for the carrying; they can say to a degree how much it carries, and not one word about why the blood does it.
When he puts the cold somewhere on purpose, into a blade or along a line, he drives it out through the Shell, the body-side layer of the soul, down the arm and into the steel. The small walked Fate in him does the one other thing it knows: his Attraction Layer, the soul’s own share of Fate, says on which side of a mark a thing stands.
Applications

Deciding where the warmth ends, where the road ends and where he ends
Putting the cold into a blade or along a line on purpose
Holding a border, an oath or a man past the point where another would let go

Techniques

STARK RIME - the blood, which decides where the warmth ends
A LINE IN THE SNOW - the scratch, which decides where the road ends
BY THE SKY THAT COVERS US - the oath, which decides where he ends
THE BREAKING COLD - the cold sent through a bind into another man’s steel
THE STARK WALK - the walk, which keeps him on his own side of all three
DOWNHILL TO THE FIRE - the cold leaning toward a great heat
FROSTFALL - the same border drawn all the way round him

Associations

The Stark cold, an inheritance older than the Moto and older than the Starks’ own records, which works outside the Wellsprings and which the Starks do not discuss with outsiders
The Body Path, mastered, carries the cold, the blade and the feet; the Fate Path he walks carries the line and the oath
House Stark
The Stark sword, his bonded weapon, a plain northern longsword with a wolf’s head cut into the pommel
His father’s axe rides across his back and has never been bonded to anyone but Ulf
He has no Domain yet

Limitations

He cannot let go: what he has sworn to hold he holds past sense, after holding it has stopped making sense, which is Rigidity
Breaking an oath sworn by the sky is his Shear Break condition
When FROSTFALL falls, all the cold he was holding comes home into him at once
A little under half of what he spends reaches the world, which is his yield, and the share that does not is paid in the body, showing as the shake in his shoulders and the left side of his jaw
It is beaten by heat and by keeping him calm, by going round the ends of the line, by carrying bronze, copper or a warm blade, by making him hurry, or by setting two of his oaths against each other

Traits
STARK RIME · Inherited Trait
STARK RIME is basically heat absorption: the power to draw the warmth out of everything near him and send it into the ground. It is the cold in the Stark blood, and it never stops.
Capabilities
Heat leaves everything near him the way it leaves a house with the door open in winter. The air within a few paces of him drops, and the heat goes down through his body and out through his heels into the ground, which is why the Starks walk the way they walk. What anyone can see is the frost. The water that is always in the air settles on anything cold enough as white rime, so timber silvers near him, the bear-fur on his shoulders goes pale at the tips, snow freezes hard and squeaks under his boots, and his own breath, which should stand white in front of his face like every other man’s, has had the water taken out of it before it can fog.
It runs harder under feeling. When his jaw tightens on the left side, the frost spreads.
Applications

Chilling the air, the timber, the snow and the men within a few paces of him
Feeding the cold that his line, his blade and his Release all use

Associations

The Stark cold, the house’s inheritance and no Wellspring
The Body Path
The Stark walk, which keeps the heels on the ground where the heat goes out

Limitations

It moves heat and cannot make it: on frozen ground or in deep winter it has little to take, and a man already as cold as the snow gives it nothing
Against a great heat it is a bucket against a fire
The heat has to have somewhere to go: when the ground under his heels is itself inside the fire, he is only carrying heat from the air into the earth, and it comes straight back
Its named failure is the full sink: nowhere left to put the warmth, and the frost stops where it stands
It costs nothing he notices; he has never been warm in his life and does not miss it
Its tell is that his breath stops steaming and his beard whitens
Heat beats it: a hot room, a furnace, a fire-worker
Keeping him steady beats it, since a Stark who is not angry is only a cold man
A far stronger presence does the same work as a fire, driving his frost back toward his own boots before a blow is struck

A LINE IN THE SNOW · Primary Trait
A LINE IN THE SNOW is basically barrier generation: the power to scratch a line in the ground and make it a border of cold. House Stark defines where things end and begin, and his soul did that before he ever drew a sword.
Capabilities
He draws the point of his blade through the ground, snow or earth or a stone floor. Once it is drawn, his Attraction Layer takes the scratch as a border and holds it, and the Stark rime gathers along the mark into a low white wall of cold, a hand high and as long as the stroke.
The wall is low because it does not need to be tall. Cold air is heavy and lies along the ground like water in a ditch, and what crosses the line toward what he guards wades into it feet first: the leather stiffens, the wet on the sole freezes to the rime, the fingers on a hilt lose their feeling, and a chest that takes a breath of it closes for a moment the way it does when a man is thrown into a winter river. Nothing in it stops a body. It makes the first step over the line the worst footing and the slowest hand that man will have all day, and Lorn is standing on the far side with a sword.
Applications

Guarding a person or a stretch of road behind a line
Taking the footing, the fingers and the breath of whoever crosses toward what he guards
Running twice as long under FROSTFALL, or closing into a ring

Associations

The Fate Path he walks, which claims the border, with the Body’s cold laid along it
The Stark cold
The sword, whose point draws it

Limitations

It takes about two percent of his reserve to draw, and a little to hold
He must stand on his side of it: the claim is that this ground is his and that ground is not, and a man who steps over his own border has unsaid it, so it is only a scratch in the snow
Its length is one stroke of the arm and a step, a few yards, never a wall round a city
It needs a whole breath to set, half to draw and the rest to plant his feet and bring the point down
Against a fighter who can cross eighty paces inside that breath it is never drawn at all
Its tell is the point of the sword dragging through the ground
It is beaten by going round the ends, or by coming at him from the side the line does not face

BY THE SKY THAT COVERS US · Secondary Trait
BY THE SKY THAT COVERS US is basically oath empowerment: the power to swear a thing and become unable to let it go. His father took him onto the wall-walk in the dark and told him all of it in twelve sentences, made him swear by the sky that covers us to carry it until it could be carried by someone with a better right, and then rode south to the Kurenai blade. Lorn carried it.
Capabilities
When he swears by the sky, with his right fist pressed once, hard, to his breastbone, the terms are written where his own soul can read them, no witness is needed, and the oath sets in him like frost in a crack. The oath gives him no strength. It takes a question away. A frightened man’s arm opens because some part of him is still deciding whether to hold on, and pain and fear are the arguments for letting go. Once Lorn has sworn, that is settled, and the arguments have nobody to speak to. So while he is keeping it, fear does not reach him, pain arrives late, as news, and the arm that holds what he swore to hold does not open.
On the frozen road he swore it with no hand free for the fist, both arms locked round a king with two broken ribs who was trying to throw him: by the sky that covers us, by his father’s death and his honor. The arms did not open, and the oath is still owed.
Applications

Shutting fear out and making pain arrive late
Holding what he swore to hold with an arm that does not open
Carrying what his father gave him until someone with a better right can take it

Associations

The Fate Path he walks: a vow is small Fate and spends his own share
No lens; his Oath prices it
His father, who swore him to the first one
His oath to the red chair and to the man in it

Limitations

It takes no reserve: nothing to swear, and everything to keep
The price shows on him at once: he goes stiller and plainer, and he can no more do the thing he swore against than put his hand through a wall
It holds what he said and nothing else, and he chooses his words like a man choosing footing on ice
It breaks by its own terms the moment he breaks it
Its tell is the right fist pressed once, hard, to the breastbone
The counter is the oldest one in the north: set two of his oaths against each other, so that keeping one breaks the other, and he stops between them like a cart with a wheel in each rut

Techniques
THE BREAKING COLD · Signature Technique
THE BREAKING COLD is basically brittleness inducement: the power to chill another man’s steel through a bind until the next hard blow shatters it. It is his signature technique, drilled, and learned by living it.
Capabilities
The working is only the Stark cold sent through a bind; what breaks the blade is an old habit of iron that every northern smith knows by hand. Iron and ordinary steel are tough when warm and brittle when cold enough, and the change comes all at once, inside a few degrees, at a point the Measurewrights call the ductile-to-brittle transition. Above it a struck blade bends, rings and springs back, because the metal can still give a little inside itself. Below it the metal cannot give, the whole blow goes into the first flaw it finds, and the flaw runs, the way a horseshoe left out in the hard frost will snap where in summer it would only have bent.
He needs the bind for it, steel laid on steel, because cold has to travel through metal and metal carries it a great deal faster than air does. The rime goes down his blade and into the other man’s, frost-flowers open across the enemy’s steel from the place the two blades touch, and for the next few breaths that sword, axe-head or stretch of mail is glass waiting for a hammer. It rides a blow twice. The bind sets it and the cut that follows breaks it, so the same exchange holds an ordinary sword stroke and a ruined weapon.
Applications

Breaking an enemy’s sword or axe-head
Making a stretch of mail brittle before the cut lands on it

Associations

The Stark cold
The Body Path
His own sword, one of the few nickel-rich steels that never go brittle in the cold, which is why it cost what it cost

Limitations

It takes about five percent of his reserve
It works only on iron and ordinary steel; bronze, copper and the few fine steels that never go brittle in the cold take no harm from it at all
The frost has to cross the bind before the blades part
Its failure is plain: the wrong metal, or a bind broken before the frost has crossed, and the cold spreads into the air for nothing with a twentieth of his reserve gone after it
Its tell is frost-flowers blooming on the other man’s blade
Before the fight, carry bronze, copper or a warm blade
During it, disengage and let the steel warm before striking with it again; a blade that survived its chill is as good as it was
A swordsman who will not bind with him, who slips, voids and cuts at the hands, never gives it a road

THE STARK WALK · House Art, Stark
THE STARK WALK is basically stance mastery: the power to stand and move so that nothing can tip him. There is no working in it and it is the oldest thing he has; he has trained it every day since he was six.
Capabilities
Heavy, even, unhurried, the weight going straight down through both heels, the knees soft, the hands still at the sides, and nothing ever lifted that does not have to be. It is how the Starks cross their own halls and how they cross a battlefield, and it is a fighting stance. A man standing that way has his weight low and between his feet, so a shoulder, a hooked ankle or a thrown elbow has nothing to tip.
It is also the road the cold leaves by. The heels are where the heat goes out, and a Stark who keeps both of them on the ground keeps the door open, which is why the house teaches the walk before it teaches the sword.
Applications

Keeping his line against a shoulder, a trip or a thrown elbow
Drawing the sword without changing his feet
Holding a man who is fighting to be let go
Keeping the heels down so the cold has its road out

Associations

House Stark, which teaches it, and mastered in him
The Body Path, with no lens and no working
STARK RIME, which leaves by the heels

Limitations

It takes no reserve
Anyone can see it: heavy, even, unhurried, weight down through the heels
It is beaten by making him hurry, because a Stark who runs has stopped walking it and is only a cold man with a sword

DOWNHILL TO THE FIRE · Technique
DOWNHILL TO THE FIRE is basically heat detection: the power to feel where a great heat is standing before anyone has seen it. He had no word for it and his father had not left him one.
Capabilities
Heat runs toward cold, and he is the coldest thing on any road, so a great heat anywhere near him pulls at the whole of his cold from one side. He feels it as a lean, the way a man wading feels which way the river is going. A furnace of a man standing behind a tree at eighty paces drags his frost toward the tree, and the rime on the side of his beard that faces it melts as fast as it forms and runs.
Applications

Knowing where a fire-worker or a great heat is standing, out of sight
Feeling such a heat from a quarter mile and placing it at eighty to ninety paces

Associations

The Stark cold, used as a sense
The Body Path
Held, and learned by living it

Limitations

It takes no reserve
It tells him where a fire is and nothing else: not who, not how strong, not whether it means harm
He does not read people and cannot sense a soul, and with his Gnosis as empty as it is, the body is the only instrument he has
It needs a heat far above the day’s, and one source; a camp of cookfires or a smithy drowns it
Its tell is the lopsided beard, where the rime will not form on the side that faces the heat, and the frost round his boots creeping one way
It is beaten by standing among other fires, or by being no warmer than the wood

Releases
FROSTFALL · First Release
FROSTFALL is basically a frost form: the power to run the Stark cold at flood through his own body and hold it there. It is his First Release, open from Stage IV, which the north calls the White Sky, and he calls it low: “the sky covers us.”
Capabilities
The same road runs at flood. Heat is pulled in from every side and driven down through him and out by the heels at the full of the rime’s strength, far faster than the blood does it by itself. The road is his own body, and a road carrying that much gets colder than living flesh should ever be. For as long as the Release lasts the Charge packed in his Shell holds that cold out in his skin, his father’s mail and his blade and keeps it off his heart. So his breath stops steaming, his beard and the fur of his collar go white with rime, a skin of clear ice runs over his father’s mail, and the snow in a ring round him turns to silver and creaks like a lake taking weight. A LINE IN THE SNOW runs twice as long.
The sword makes a second shape of it. With the point driven into the ground between his boots, both hands on the pommel and his head down, the line he would have drawn closes into a ring. The frost runs outward ten paces across, over whoever is lying or standing inside it, and the wet in the air above it falls as ice as fine as flour.
Applications

Striking with STARK RIME at the top of its Grade
Doubling the length of his line
Closing the line into a ring ten paces across to shelter whoever is inside
Keeping the air inside the ring only as hot as a summer noon inside a great fire’s field

Techniques

The ring - the point driven into the ground between his boots, both hands on the pommel, and the line closes round him ten paces across
Called silent - the rime stays on his hands and blade and goes no further

Associations

The Stark cold
The Body Path
The Stark sword, his bonded weapon, which carries FROSTFALL’s rime to its edge
His father’s mail, which the ice runs over

Limitations

It lasts about three minutes from a full reserve
Called silent it is weaker: the rime stays on his hands and blade
Inside a great fire’s field the ground is inside the fire, the heat has nowhere to go, and all the ring buys is minutes
It ends the way a held breath ends: the holding stops, everything he was keeping at arm’s length comes into him at once, a man who has never been warm in his life is cold for the first time, and he shakes and needs a fire
Heat beats it, as it beats the Trait
So does its own end: when it falls, the ground round him is ice

characters/ability-accounts/léonard-lamb.title: Léonard Lambert — Abilities in full
characters/ability-accounts/léonard-lamb.content:
Card: Léonard Lambert
COUNT TRUE
COUNT TRUE (Numera Vere, the house words in the Court’s Latin) is basically numerical precision: the power to have already counted you, your army and your next move, with a count that is never wrong. It is his signature art, and it is the two words on the Lambert banner, which his soul took for its law. Every ability below is that law working at a different size.
Capabilities
A true count is a count made before the thing happens, said out loud, and never softened. The Lamberts have sat at the Sea’s bench beside the cleric for as long as the Sea has had courts, counting what the testimony is about.
The blood counts a blow before it is thrown, the eye counts a field before it is fought, the list counts the men who gave a false number, and the sword pays out the answer. He calls nothing by a technique’s name. His call is the number, said politely, with a tap of the pommel for every thousand.
Applications

Counting a blow before it is thrown
Counting a field before it is fought
Counting the men who gave a false number
Telling a general his own numbers in front of his captains

Techniques

ONE BEFORE - the blood’s count of a blow before it is thrown
COUNT TRUE - the eye’s count of a field, said aloud
THE STRUCK LIST - the count of the men who gave a false number
THE SALLOWGATE ANSWER - the sword that pays out the answer

Associations

The Lambert inheritance and the house words are the lens; there is no Wellspring behind any of it
The Body Path does the Answer and carries the blood’s lean on his Reflex
The Spirit Path does the count and the list
The Lamberts’ seat at the Sea’s bench, beside the cleric

Limitations

The count judges the number and never the reason
The Answer takes about one and a half percent of his reserve each time
The rest costs no reserve and is paid in people, and there are four notches under his pommel to show it

Traits
ONE BEFORE · Inherited Trait
ONE BEFORE is basically intent perception: the power to start his answer a hair before the blow it answers. Across the south the blood’s gift is called the Lambert count, or the bench, and it is the thing in the Lambert blood the house does not discuss.
Capabilities
A great many Lamberts are born with Crystals that never wake and fight anyway, reading a blow before it is thrown with no faculty to read it with, so that a spectator calls it luck and a practitioner calls it impossible. Léonard woke, and the old gift woke with him. Every answer he gives begins before the delivery it answers, by a margin so slight it looks like chance, and men he has fought swear he struck first. While he is facing a blow with a will behind it, his Reflex reads a step high on the hidden scale.
The Measurewrights (the Guild’s scholars of measurement) have an account, which the house has never confirmed. A blow with a will behind it is decided before it is thrown. The body makes ready first: the weight settles on the driving foot, the breath sets, the shoulder loads, and all of that begins a good part of a heartbeat before the hand moves, which is what fighting men mean when they say a blow was telegraphed. Under the body, the deciding itself comes earlier still. A trained eye reads the shoulder. The scholars say the Lambert blood reads the deciding, the will at the moment it commits, which is why an unwoken Lambert with no trained faculty can do it at all, and why the south calls the gift the bench that reads a blow before the shoulder commits to it.
Lamberts who carry the gift tell it the other way round: the count sets the shoulder’s first commitment against ten thousand blows it has seen before. Both accounts are told at Sallowgate, and the house confirms neither.
Applications

Answering a blow before it is thrown
Putting the Sallowgate Answer in place so early that it looks like the first stroke
Reading a lie told knowingly, since it has a will behind it

Associations

The Lambert blood, an inheritance of the house and no Wellspring
The Body Path, as a lean on his Reflex
THE SALLOWGATE ANSWER, which it puts ahead of the blow

Limitations

It reads intent, and nothing else
It is slower against a thing with no will in it: a falling wall, a beast in a panic, a working that runs by itself
Where nobody decided anything there is nothing to read early, and he is left with only his ordinary quickness
It costs nothing, because nothing is made or thrown, and he no more spends reserve on it than a man spends reserve on hearing
Its tell is that he moves a hair before you do
A blow with no intent behind it beats it

COUNT TRUE · Primary Trait
COUNT TRUE is basically calculation mastery: the power to look at a field and know its number, men and horses and remounts and the days of grain behind them. It is the house words, become his soul’s law.
Capabilities
He knows the number of any field he can see, and when it matters he says it out loud, in front of everyone, and does not soften it. A field is a set of sums that have to close. So many men eat so much bread a day, so many horses so much fodder, a wagon carries a known load and a road passes a known number of wagons between dawn and dark, and every figure in a return leans on three others. A liar changes one figure and leaves the others standing, and the sum stops closing. Most men cannot hold enough columns at once to feel that.
Léonard’s soul keeps all of them, which is what his Retention is for, and reads where they are going, which is what his Forecast is for. So while he is counting, no lie told about the field gets past him. His Analysis and Forecast read a step high on the hidden scale, and a false return feels wrong in his hand like a cased weight, the hollowed and plugged kind a cheating merchant keeps for his scales, which looks right and lifts wrong.
It is a Trait of his own soul with no Wellspring behind it, a reading on the Spirit side, of what a report means and whether it is true.
Applications

Saying a field’s number aloud, never rounded, with one tap of the pommel for every thousand
Catching a false return
Telling how long an army can last on the grain behind it

Associations

The Spirit Path, as a reading
His Retention and his Forecast
The house words, and the bench-house at Sallowgate where he learned to count beside the clerks

Limitations

Its limit is sight: he counts what he can see and what he is told
A field he cannot see or a report never made is a hole in the sum, and a sum with a hole in it he will not call a count
It has no purchase at all on the men and the grain themselves
It costs nothing
Its tell is the saying: he gives the number aloud and taps the pommel
A field he cannot see beats it: night, fog, a reverse slope, a column that never came onto the roll

THE STRUCK LIST · Secondary Trait
THE STRUCK LIST is basically interrogation intuition: the power to ask for a count twice, so that a man who lies the second time knows exactly what he is doing. It formed the night he struck his own cousin from the house.
Capabilities
A Lambert who gives a false count is struck from the house, and the house keeps the list. Léonard has struck four names in his time, and one of them was his cousin, whom he loved, and who lied about two hundred sacks of grain to keep a village fed through a bad winter. Since then, when a man reports to him, he asks for the count twice, and the second asking carries the weight of the list.
A first answer can be habit, pride, hope or plain bad arithmetic, and a man can give it without ever deciding to lie. The second question takes that away. The man has now been told the number matters, by someone whose own cousin is on the list, and whatever he says next he has chosen.
The house clerks add that a lie told knowingly has a will behind it, and will is the one thing the Lambert blood has always been able to read.
Applications

Getting a true count out of a man who reports to him
Turning a careless wrong number into a chosen one

Associations

The Spirit Path, as a reading
The house list of struck names, and the four notches on the underside of his pommel
The Lambert blood, which reads the will behind a knowing lie

Limitations

It judges the number and not the reason
A true reason wrapped around a false number is still a false number, and the list has no column for mercy
It takes no reserve
Its tell is the second asking, in the same courteous voice, with his thumb on the underside of the pommel where the four notches are
A man who gives him a true count, however bad, beats it, because there is then nothing on him for the list to weigh

Techniques
THE SALLOWGATE ANSWER · House Art, Lambert · Signature
THE SALLOWGATE ANSWER is basically counter mastery: the power to turn his blade before yours has left its line, take it on the flat a hand from your guard, and ride down it into the wrist, the elbow or the throat. It is the Lambert counter-cut, and every child at Sallowgate, woken or not, learns it by this name on a wooden copy of the house sword’s balance.
Capabilities
It is one movement with no flourish. The visible charge is small and it is always there: the wrist turns, the gray blade rolls a quarter in his hand, and the pale gold of his aura draws down off his shoulders and lies along the steel as one thin white line.
The place it meets you is the mechanism. A swung sword turns about the hand that holds it, so the point travels fast and far while the steel beside the guard has barely begun to move. An answer that starts early enough can meet the blade there, a hand from the hilt, where it is still slow and has almost no force in it yet, and from there the wrist is a hand’s width away and the elbow and the throat lie on the same line. Any Lambert child can do it against a slow cut. In him, with ONE BEFORE and Glory’s Reflex behind it, the answer arrives so early that men he has fought swear he struck first.
The spending rides the cut. He pulls Aether (mana) up out of the ground he stands on, packs it raw in his Shell (the body-side layer of the soul) as Charge, and the Shell lays it along the edge as the same coat of aura that covers his body, drawn to one place. So two things land together: the sword’s own cut, placed where the harness opens, and the coat on the edge, which is what lets a plain gray blade bite a worked guard.
Applications

Taking an attacker’s wrist, elbow or throat off his own blow
Biting a worked guard with a plain gray blade

Associations

The Body Path, as a strike
Sallowgate, where it is taught, and where he has it Mastered
ONE BEFORE and Glory’s Reflex, which put it ahead of the blow
The house sword, balanced close to the guard for the turn of the wrist the Answer needs

Limitations

It is an answer: he has to be asked first, and a man who will not attack him gives him nothing to answer
Each Answer takes about one and a half percent of his reserve, about 66 Answers from full
About two thirds of what he spends reaches the steel, and the rest leaves him as heat, which is why in the cold he smokes like a horse
Its tell is the blade turning in his hand before yours leaves its line
To beat it, feint with the whole body, so that the intent he reads is false, and then strike with no thought at all
A real decision to throw a false blow reads to the blood as a real blow, the Answer is paid out against it, and the stroke that follows comes off drilled habit with no fresh deciding in it for him to read

characters/ability-accounts/mark-stark-—.title: Mark Stark — Abilities in full
characters/ability-accounts/mark-stark-—.content:
Card: Mark Stark
KEPT HOLD
KEPT HOLD is basically sheer tenacity: the power to keep hold, whatever has hold of him. It is a Trait-art, one idea, and he got it on the Vessant road, where a cub bit through his shield and took his forearm to the bone, raked his belly and his face and his good arm, and he kept hold of the short sword the whole time.
Capabilities
His soul learned one thing first: whatever has him, the hand does not open. Everything else he has is that one lesson said again in a different part of him. The hand holds the sword, the talking holds the fear, the knees hold the ground under the thing that is killing him, and the cold holds the blade in the wound.
Applications

Holding the sword, the fear, the ground under the thing that is killing him, and the blade in the wound, each with a different part of him

Techniques

KEPT HOLD - the Primary Trait: the hand that will not open
THAT WAS THE SMALL ONE - the Secondary Trait: the talking that keeps fear out of his hands
STARK RIME - the Inherited Trait: the Stark cold, which holds the blade in the wound
UNDER AND HOLD ON! - the Signature Technique: on his knees under the thing, the blade in to the hilt, held until it dies

Associations

The Body Path, in the Form of a Strike
The Stark cold, the house’s inheritance and no Wellspring, is the lens the art works through
The Vessant road and the cub, where it was learned
His aura is the Stark cold, thin and bright, a pale gray with a coppery shimmer at its edge like frost on a rust-red leaf

Limitations

Hurt, he screams, cries and complains the whole time, and the hand stays shut

Traits
KEPT HOLD · Primary Trait
KEPT HOLD is basically unbreakable grip: the power to keep a weapon in his hand against anything short of breaking the hand. It is the first thing his soul learned, and it gives the art its name.
Capabilities
A hand closes by muscles that sit in the forearm and pull the fingers shut through cords running over the wrist, and an ordinary frightened hand opens because pain and shock tell those muscles to let go. KEPT HOLD is his soul refusing to pass that order along. The muscles stay drawn tight, the way a cramp stays, for as long as there is a weapon in the hand, and no wrench, twist or blow on the blade gets it out of his fingers.
While he holds on, his Fortitude reads a step high on the hidden scale: the whole body takes its cue from the hand and is harder to put down.
Applications

Keeping the sword through a wrench, a twist or a blow on the blade
Being a step harder to put down for as long as he grips

Associations

His Shell, the body-side layer of the soul, which keeps it as a law without being asked
The short sword he held on the Vessant road, and his brother’s long sword, on which it has already set his knuckles

Limitations

It holds the sword, not the man: he can be knocked down holding it, dragged holding it, shaken like a rat holding it
A thing a step or two stronger than he is simply throws man and sword together
It costs nothing, because nothing is being made or thrown
Its tell is the knuckles of the sword hand, which go white on the hilt and stay white
Its counter follows from how a hand is built: take the hand, not the blade
Break the fingers, cut the cords in the forearm, or fold the wrist hard down toward the palm, which slackens those cords so that even a locked fist has nothing left to pull with

THAT WAS THE SMALL ONE · Secondary Trait
THAT WAS THE SMALL ONE is basically fear suppression: the power to keep fear out of his hands for as long as he keeps talking. He talks when he is frightened, a steady stream of it under his breath, and the talking keeps his feet under him.
Capabilities
A head can only attend to so much at once, and a mouth that is busy making words uses up the part of it that would otherwise be rehearsing what the teeth are about to do. A man talking also has to breathe out long and even to do it, and a long even breath slows the heart and steadies the fingers. So while he mutters, fear does not reach his hands.
That is why his brother’s “Aye” mattered. Rob said it once and the muttering stopped with his feet still under him, because Rob was there to answer for him.
Applications

Giving ground on fast feet, talking, with steady hands
Holding off the shakes, the scream and the tears until the fight is done

Associations

His brother Rob, who answered it

Limitations

The fear is held off, never spent: the moment the words stop, everything he has been holding off arrives at once, the shakes, the scream, the tears
It takes nothing from his reserve
Its tell is the steady stream of words under his breath
It is beaten by making him stop: wind him, strike the throat or the jaw, or say the one thing he cannot answer
With Rob dead there is nobody to say “Aye”, and the grief has done what no enemy managed and made him quiet

STARK RIME · Inherited Trait
STARK RIME is basically cold manipulation: the power to move heat out of a thing and down into the ground. The cold in the Stark blood is an inheritance of the house and no Wellspring, and in Mark it runs thin.
Capabilities
It does one thing, the one rule the Stark blood has, which is that it moves heat out and never in. In him it shows as frost on the fur of his collar when he is angry or afraid, and the heat going down through his heels into the ground. When he sets it on purpose he pulls Aether (mana) up out of the ground he is kneeling on, packs it raw in his Shell as Charge, and sets the rime through the sword arm. About a third of what he spends reaches the world, which is his yield, and the rest is paid in the body as a shudder through the shoulders.
It rides the blow, and from there the world’s own old habits do the rest. Warmth always runs from the warm thing to the cold one, and steel carries it far more readily than flesh does, something like a hundred times by the Measurewrights’ reckoning, so a cold blade buried to the hilt is a road, and the warmth of the wound walks out along it, up his arm, down through him and into the ground. Two things follow. Wet flesh freezes fast to cold metal, the way a tongue sticks to a pump handle in January, so the blade cannot be thrashed loose. And cold muscle is slow, weak muscle, so the thing on the end of the sword loses its strength from the wound outward while he keeps his.
Applications

Freezing a buried blade fast in the wound
Taking the strength out of whatever is on the end of the sword, from the wound outward

Associations

The Stark blood, the house’s inheritance
The sword, which is the road the heat leaves by
UNDER AND HOLD ON!, the blow it rides

Limitations

The cold moves heat and cannot make any, so on ground already frozen hard it has little to take
Against a real fire it is a bucket against a furnace
About two thirds of what he spends on it is lost
Its tells are frost on the fur at his collar, frost creeping white up the fuller from the wound, and his breath no longer steaming
It is beaten by heat, and by calm: a Stark who is not angry or afraid is only a cold man

Techniques
UNDER AND HOLD ON! · Signature Technique
UNDER AND HOLD ON! is basically a pinning strike: the power to get underneath a thing and hold a blade in it until it dies. It is the third move of KEPT HOLD, and the Lanternless still call it the Pin.
Capabilities
The visible charge is the drop. He stops giving ground, the muttering quickens, and he goes to his knees inside the reach of whatever is on him, where its weight is over him and its jaws or its arms have already gone past. The blade is driven up behind the foreleg or under the arm, where a beast’s hide is thinnest and a man’s mail gaps, in to the hilt, and he leans on the pommel with all his weight, his face a hand’s width from its eyes. Then he holds it there, sobbing if he has to, while it dies.
All of KEPT HOLD is in it: the hand holds the sword, the talking holds the fear, the knees hold the ground under the thing that is killing him, and the cold, set through the sword arm, holds the blade in the wound.
Applications

Killing a beast from behind the foreleg
Killing a man through the gap in his mail under the arm
He did it on the road one-handed, with the other arm hanging open to the bone and the cub’s claws working at his chest

Associations

KEPT HOLD, THAT WAS THE SMALL ONE and STARK RIME, all used at once
Rob, roaring at him to hold it and not let go, which is where the call comes from
He learned it by living through it: nobody taught him this
The short sword, now a long dagger, that he held behind the cub’s foreleg to the hilt

Limitations

He has to be under the thing to do it, and being under the thing is how he got his arm torn open
Setting the rime through the arm and holding takes about five percent of his reserve
Its tell is that he stops giving ground, the muttering quickens, and he goes to his knees inside the reach
It is beaten by not letting him get underneath: keep him at the long end of a spear, stay off him once he is down, or be something with no belly to get under

characters/ability-accounts/maud-corwen-.title: Maud Corwen — Abilities in full
characters/ability-accounts/maud-corwen-.content:
Card: Maud Corwen
THE WARDEN’S KEY
THE WARDEN’S KEY is basically ley line manipulation: the power to open and shut the ground’s supply of Aether to everyone standing on it. It is the house’s Hours in the hand of the Warden, and her own soul has grown around it until the soul’s name for her is the ring itself.
Capabilities
A practitioner pulls Aether from the world around her, and where she stands decides how fast she fills. A worked pool has a bronze ring at its lip, the ferrule, and whoever holds the ring decides who gets how much and when. Everyone else in the world treats that as plumbing. Maud holds the key to every ring on the chain from the Wellheads to the southern sea, and on the Hotwell she does not need the key.
The idea is Solfatara’s: pressure let out forever and never saved. The Wellheads have been venting since before the empire, and her soul vents with them, steadily, so that she stands in a fight the way a hot spring stands in a field. Its operation is sublimation, what presses given off as fume and never stored. Phreatis lies under it, the Waters of Memory: the pools remember everyone who has bathed in them, and she reads what they remember the way a keeper reads the tundish.
Closing a ring takes nothing from anyone. A closed Core takes no one’s reserve; it stops the refill, and nothing happens to you until you need more, and you always find out late. Anyone who has been truly dangerous in a long fight has been dangerous because they were filling as fast as they spent. On Maud’s ground, they were filling because she let them.
The flaw is the Fume’s. A head of Aether does not go away when the gate shuts. Interrupt the release and the pressure finds its way out through whatever is weakest, and when she shuts a ring by hand the weakest thing is usually her. Phreatis has its own: deep water does not ask what is sinking into it, and the pools remember the false as readily as the true. The house reads the forks, and the forks ring true.
Applications

Ending a sect’s siege of the Cask Yards by turning a key
Selling an hour on the book to the highest bidder
Fighting a long fight on her own ground against anyone at all
Passing a warning from Brightwater to the sea faster than a horse

Techniques

SOAKED - raised in the fat
THE HUM - every ring on the chain, felt like a pulse
THE BOOK - names that fill as if they owned the place
NEVER DRINKS - the Tongue turned inside out
SLACK WATER! - one terrace gone lean in ten breaths
ON THE HOUSE! - the ring thrown wide for one breath
READ THE TERMS! - the keeper’s Command
CASK! - a circle of fat ground, carried
THE KEPT POOL - nothing fills here but by the book

Associations

Solfatara, the Fume, deep: pressure let out and never saved
Phreatis, the Waters of Memory, governing: the pools remember
The Guild lease, which is the authority; the key, which is the instrument
The Body Path carries it, with the keeper’s drift into the shallow end of Fate

Limitations

Leased ground with a ring on it, and nowhere else; ten miles from a ring she is what her Stage says
A closed ring stops the refill and takes nothing; a man who arrives full and finishes fast never notices her
The pressure behind every closing rises, and is owed, and something breeds in a ring kept shut too long
Deadwater kicks back through the key, and her left ear is already half gone
The whole of it stands on a piece of wax nobody can find

Traits
SOAKED · Inherited Trait
SOAKED is basically enhanced recovery on home ground: raised in the pools from birth, she fills far above her Stage on rich ground, and her Regeneration and Filtration run high. Every Corwen raised in the fat has it. On lean or ordinary ground the gift stops, and every Corwen in a foreign war has written home to say the air there is thin.
THE HUM · Inherited Trait
THE HUM is basically network awareness: she feels every ring on the chain the way she feels her own pulse, and passes turnings and warnings down the assay forks faster than a horse. Off the ground the silence is a physical thing, and she does not sleep.
THE BOOK · Primary Trait
THE BOOK is basically selective empowerment: the power to make a named person fill on her ground as if they owned it.
Capabilities
An hour sold to a name: a sitter on the book fills as if she owned the place, and anyone else on the terrace gets a trickle. Any keeper of ten years can keep the book at her own lip. The Warden can enter a name at any lip on the whole chain by speaking it into the forks, and the pool hums a note higher when she does.
Limitations

Leased ground with a ring on it
Cost: a name entered is a name owed, and she keeps every hour she has ever given away
Counter: step off her ground, or buy your own cask

NEVER DRINKS · Secondary Trait
NEVER DRINKS is basically contaminant detection: the power to tell by smell alone which pool water came from and whether it has been cut. The house’s old Tongue tasted the water. She gave up tasting at fourteen and has never drunk from the pools since, and what the Tongue would have told her she has learned to take off the steam instead.
Limitations

She has given up the Tongue, and everything it would tell her that the forks do not
Tell: she lifts a cup and sets it down full

Techniques
SLACK WATER! · Signature Technique
SLACK WATER! is basically energy cutoff: the power to turn one terrace lean in ten breaths. It is the house’s Deadwater, taken by hand.
Capabilities
“Time, ladies and gentlemen, please,” in the voice of someone closing a public house, and a quarter-turn of the key with the ring in reach. The ground under one terrace goes lean in ten breaths. Nobody on it refills. She gives the warning every time, because the house does, and the ten breaths are the only chance anyone gets.
Limitations

Ten breaths’ warning, given every time
Cost: about 4% of her reserve, and the kick back through the key as a scald up the arm and a hum to the bone
Counter: finish the fight in ten breaths

ON THE HOUSE! · Technique
ON THE HOUSE! is basically energy surge: the ring thrown wide for one breath. Everyone on the book fills, every guard’s coat flares blue, and the pool behind her jumps as the head drops.
Limitations

One breath; anything standing in the pool is scalded
Cost: about 2% of her reserve

READ THE TERMS! · Technique
READ THE TERMS! is basically contractual command: a keeper’s Command with the key raised. Anyone on the book feels the line of their terms on their window in the middle of whatever they are doing, and the line says what they owe her. It is a poor moment for it.
Limitations

Only those on the book
Cost: about 1% of her reserve
Counter: never buy an hour from a Corwen

CASK! · Technique
CASK! is basically portable terrain: a sealed cask of Wellhead water stove in underfoot, and for a minute a circle a few paces across is fat ground, and she fights in it.
Limitations

A minute, a circle, one cask
Counter: let it run out

Releases
KINGFISHER! · First Release
KINGFISHER! is basically body enhancement: the house’s First Release, blue steam off the skin. Her Harmonics and Vitality read a step high on the hidden scale. The steam shows exactly where she is.

Cost: about 18,000 EU a second; on her ground she refills faster than that

HOTWELL! · Second Release
HOTWELL! is basically domain activation: the power to open THE KEPT POOL. With KINGFISHER! under it, her Harmonics and Vitality stand two steps over her line.

Cost: about 30,000 EU a second; with KINGFISHER! under it, 48,000
It fills the cap with the First

DEADWATER! · Third Release
DEADWATER! is basically energy nullification: the power to become the ring. The call is “Deadwater.”
Capabilities
She stops being the keeper of the ring and becomes it. Every pool within her reach closes through her body at once, and the head of pressure that has nowhere to go goes into her. For as long as she holds it, nobody near her refills but by her, and her Harmonics and Resilience read two steps high on the hidden scale. The hum stops for a mile, and people look round for it.
Limitations

The pressure rises behind her the whole time, and when she lets go it comes out through whatever in her is weakest
Cost: about 60,000 EU a second, and the back-pressure, which no one counts in EU
Counter: outlast her

Domain
THE KEPT POOL · Domain
THE KEPT POOL is basically resource monopoly: the power to make a place answer to her book.
Capabilities
Its law: nothing fills here but by the book. The ground goes wet and steaming under everyone’s boots, the hum comes up, and no one draws a breath of Aether from it that she has not entered. Those she has entered fill as if they owned the place. When she lets it go, the pressure behind it lets go too, and the pool jumps.
Limitations

The head rises the whole time it is open; held too long, something begins to breed in it
Counter: a Domain that brings its own supply, or a man with a bottled Draft and a short plan

characters/ability-accounts/muken-moto-—.title: Muken Moto — Abilities in full
characters/ability-accounts/muken-moto-—.content:
Card: Muken Moto
THE SPLINTERED WORK
THE SPLINTERED WORK is basically shatterpoint mastery: the power to see where anything is ready to break, and to finish the job. It is his signature, the one idea his Trait, his Works, his Releases and his Domain each express in their own way, said in northern Common with the Kōkan’s old words beside it.
Capabilities
A salt cutter reads a face for where it will give before he sets the pick, and Fractura, the Crack, runs that habit through his Perception. Fractura’s idea is that everything has a place where it will go, and its operation is separation: a thing is parted along the one place where it was always going to part. Nothing fails at its full strength; a thing fails at a flaw it already had, and a soul that has become that idea sees the flaw the way a cutter sees the soft seam in a face. The gold lines he sees over walls, bodies and formations are every place where a thing is ready to go, and Judicium, the Scale, whose idea is truth told apart, ranks them worst first. Smiths and masons, and the Measurewrights after them, call it stress concentration, and will tell you that the strain at the tip of a crack is many times what the sound stone beside it carries, and the sharper the tip, the worse; their figure is good, and they have no idea why a soul can see the tip.
Every made thing has a note as well, the pitch it rings at when struck, and a thing that is ready to break already sounds it: a cracked thing has two notes, the steady one of the sound part and a sour wavering one from the crack. He finishes the job by giving the thing its own ending in time with that note, each push adding to the last, until it parts at the place where it was always going to part. The strength that breaks the thing is the thing’s own, and Muken only gives it the way. The scholars call the note a natural frequency and the finishing resonance, and the comparison every Kharven child knows is a swing that goes higher when it is pushed in time; it is a good comparison, and it says nothing about why the crack answers him.
The Works of Hataraki are how his blood takes hold of this. They are no spells. Each is one inherited grip on one job of Fate, and the blood gives the grip and nothing else. He uses them the way most of his house fights: the grip finds the thing and names it (this is dead, this is whole, this is crossing, this is too much), and the work itself is done by his body and his blade. It rides a blow plainly. The Eye picks the place, the edge goes into it with everything his arm has, and the note goes in behind the edge, so the cut does its own harm and then the crack runs on from the cut.
Applications

Reading where a wall, a body, a line of men, a road, a promise or a war will give
Ending what is already dead without harming what stands next to it
Running the worst flaw in one chosen thing
Standing under a load by giving it a road to the ground
Closing a wound from the mending side, by its living edges
Giving him one chance in one place against a higher Stage

Techniques

SEAM-SIGHT - the principle as sight, always on
DEBT RECOGNITION - the same ranking, worst first, turned on the people in the room
SHINGAN - the Moto eye, SEAM-SIGHT held open
DEAD NOTE! - a dead crack’s sour note held through one long breath until the dead thing comes apart
THE WAY SHE DID IT - the knowledge from the mending side, the edges of a wound held on their living note until they close
OPEN HAND - the grip on a soul’s thread, held or let go
JIKAN NO SHIGOTO - a quiet Work that follows a cause back a knot at a time
CHISHIKI NO SHIGOTO - a quiet Work that hears what a man hums under his face
DIDN’T CRACK! - the same knowledge turned round, a load given a road through him to the ground
THE WHOLE HAND - all six grips closing together, priced as all six
FURE! - the blade as a tuning fork on one target, the way a singer can break a glass by holding its note
EVERY ROPE IN THE CITY - the same ring with no choosing in it, every note at once

Associations

Fractura finds the flaw and does the breaking; Judicium, the Scale, ranks the flaws; Petralon, the Foundation Stone, carries a load down
The Body Path does the work, through his body and blade; Fate is where each Work’s grip takes hold
The Kōkan blood gives the grip on the Works of Hataraki, and Faisal taught him six of them in the Plane of Fate
Tsugigane, his bonded sword, carries HIBI’s note and, in the silver thread of its join, his sister’s
The Kharven breath, which every Work and the release start on
He says every name low and plain; the marks on the names are how the north repeats them

Limitations

He can work only at a seam that is already there; a whole thing gives him nothing to see and nothing to hold
He stands at Knotwright, Fate IV, the fourth rung of his Fate Mastery; the hall where the table was cleared saw him at Weaver, an overreach, once, at a price, and no Moto has ever found the pull light
His Dominion Fate wins the contest and never lowers the price, so he cannot afford to force a Work on anything that pushes back
Dead things, willing wounds and loads on his own bones do not push back, which keeps the small uses small; reaching for something further from likely, the price climbs like a wall
About a fourteenth of every spend burns in his Shell’s furnace instead of reaching the thing: the heat behind the left eye, the tremor in the sword hand, the bell in his back teeth
His Eye will not switch off at the supper table, and he sees where everyone he loves will break
Each time he forces it the gold seam widens a thread and does not close
Breaking the oath he swore by his honor, that no Moto marches on Zettari land under his rule, is his Shear Break condition
Anyone watching sees it coming: the Kharven breath, in through the nose until the ribs ache, and the gold seam in the left iris widening
His aura’s gray goes nearly black while its seams brighten to forge-gold, and lamps and cups shiver before anything breaks
Against a higher Stage it gives him one chance in one place, because the strength that breaks the thing is the thing’s own
It is countered by bringing him nothing already flawed, by damping the note with cold, noise or a flat hand, by taking the ground away from DIDN’T CRACK, or by reaching him before the breath is out
Under strain it fails in Fractura’s own manner, which the Measurewrights call self-inspection: the bearer is shown his own flaws first, and a blade held too long on another thing’s note finds its own crack
Driven by rage it fails the other way, as runaway crazing, ending what was rotten and then what stood near the rot, and it does not stop by itself

Traits
SEAM-SIGHT · Primary Trait
SEAM-SIGHT is basically weakness detection: the power to see where anything is carrying its weight and where it will give. It is his Primary Trait, always on, and THE SPLINTERED WORK starts from it.
Capabilities
Before he ever knew it had a name he read a salt face for the place it would give before he set the pick, and his soul still does that before it tries anything else. Within about fifty paces he sees where a made thing, a body or a line of men is carrying its weight, and where that weight has gathered in a crack, as fine gold lines laid over the world like crazing in old glaze. He sees them without trying, and his own worst flaw is always the one he sees first.
It reads more than stone. A man’s locked loads show as colored bands, the way the colors run in a sheet of stressed glass held up to the sky. It shows where a road, a promise or a war would give. It can read every stance an opponent might take in the next breath, as a field of seams so thick it looks like light.
Applications

Finding a locked arm, or a knee that takes all the load
Finding a wall built new over an old frost-seam
Finding the feud running down the middle of a clan wedge
Reading where a road, a promise or a war would give
Reading every stance an opponent might take in the next breath

Associations

Fractura, read through the Body Path by the eye his blood gave him
Judicium ranks what it shows, worst flaw first
The cutter’s habit from the salt face, lived and never taught
Held open it is SHINGAN

Limitations

It reads only load and fault, so a thing truly whole, freshly forged or simply soft gives him nothing
It shows where a man will break, never what the man means
It reaches about fifty paces
It costs nothing he notices at rest, and a slow heat behind the left eye under strain
It does not switch off, and it has run hot since the war and will not rest, which is Resonance Fatigue
The heat and the widening gold seam in his left iris give it away
It can be blinded: when Fate collects, the Eye fills with blood and sees nothing
It is countered by offering nothing flawed, or by moving faster than a fifty-pace read can follow

THE UNWRITTEN NAME · Inherited Trait, the Kōkan blood
THE UNWRITTEN NAME is basically nameless existence: the power to go unfound by anything that looks a man up by his name. It is blood and no working, and it belongs to the red line and not to THE SPLINTERED WORK.
Capabilities
No book in the world has his name in it. The Kōkan wrote their name in a mark no register in the inner world can read, and Muken carries that blood without the mark ever having been entered against him. Every Nalūn seal-token, every Moto fate-read and every working that finds a person by the house written over them looks at him and finds a page with no ink on it. Ulf Stark’s token went cold and silent in his palm, and Shigure Tenrai’s fate-rings flickered and slid off him on the stair.
It has another side. A grip nobody ever wrote down is a grip nobody can call in, so the Kōkan hold on the Works is neither loan nor gift.
Applications

Staying unread by fate-sight, token-reads and name-workings
Wearing THE WHOLE HAND over it like a hand over a lamp, so his thread runs smooth where he stands and nothing there can find a seam in him until he lets the mask go
Keeping the Kōkan hold on the Works where nobody can call it in

Associations

The Kōkan blood, the red line of the Moto
It has no Path, no Lens and no Form
THE WHOLE HAND, which can be laid over it as a mask

Limitations

It hides him only from things that read by name and lineage; plain eyes, a blade and a good guess see him as well as anyone
It costs nothing in Essence, he cannot turn it off, and it does not grow
No token will ever hum for him, and no house seal will bind under his name until the Kōkan mark is set on it by hand
Tokens going dead in his hand give him away
It is countered by fighting him with your eyes open and your fate-sight shut

DEBT RECOGNITION · Secondary Trait
DEBT RECOGNITION is basically threat identification: the power to feel who in the room means him harm and who wants something from him. It is his Secondary Trait, left by the shore.
Capabilities
It formed in the three days on the Seat road after the shore, when every man he looked at was either bringing his sister back or keeping her from him. Judicium, the Scale, marks the people within about sixty paces who mean him or his harm, and the people who want something from him. He feels it the way a nose marks smoke: a pressure in the Eye, ranked worst first, and his head turns before they move.
It is strongest against intent that is clear and loud, and it goes quiet against a man who truly wants nothing. It marked Amelia Greymane as a solid, quiet weight, and that is all it could tell him.
Applications

Marking the people who mean him or his harm, worst first
Marking the people who want something from him

Associations

Judicium, the Scale, reads it
It lands through the Attraction Layer
Lived, never taught

Limitations

It has a reach of about sixty paces and no more, and a man waiting outside it is outside the Eye as well
It marks appetite as readily as malice, and a king who reads everyone at his table as a debt stops sitting at tables
It is hardening into reading every face as an account, which is Rigidity
It takes a little of his reserve while it runs hot, and almost nothing when he is calm
His head turning toward a threat a moment before the threat moves gives it away
It is countered by wanting nothing and standing very still, or by waiting outside sixty paces

STONES ON A CAIRN · Passive Trait
STONES ON A CAIRN is basically influential presence: the power to make a room stop and listen when he means what he says. It is a Passive Trait, left by the cairn on the ridge.
Capabilities
Since the cairn his voice comes lower and slower when he means it, each word set on the last like stones laid one on another, and the Attraction in it carries. Cups tremble, lamps on their chains swing all together, and people who were talking stop. Where there are no lamps the room still answers: frost on the walls trembles all together when he draws breath to speak, and the pillars hum back.
Kiyome Byakuya heard it in the death-house and thought it the first true Moto voice she had heard in her life.
Associations

It lands through the Attraction Layer, on his voice, as a claim at its smallest
Lived, never taught

Limitations

It rides his voice and his conviction, and does nothing when he does not mean what he says
It carries as far as a hall carries a low voice, and dies in a battle’s noise
It costs nothing
The lamps give it away
It is countered by noise and by distance

Techniques
SHINGAN (心眼 · Shingan, the heart-eye) · Bloodline Faculty, Moto
SHINGAN is basically structural sight: the power to read where everything is carrying its weight. It is the common Moto eye, and in him it is SEAM-SIGHT held open.
Capabilities
It woke on the Foot’s stair. In Muken it came with something the other lines do not have: a hairline seam of gold running out from the amber fleck low in his left iris. Shigure named it on the spot: any Moto brat can see where a wall wants to fall, and the gold in it is Kōkan. The seam is the first of the Kamigan, the crown eye that takes what all the other eyes see and ranks it.
The seam has torn wider since, and the crown eye has shown itself. A vow tore the seam and left a line of blood down his cheek, and the gold has come into both eyes. With Bara’s knowledge in him and the boy gone out of the body, both eyes have burned one even gold from lid to lid with no seam, ring or pupil, and Naiser Yukari had no name for it but Kamigan. Under THE WHOLE HAND both irises craze gold from edge to edge and bleed. When Fate collects, the gold goes out and both eyes go red through iris and white together, the red of the line of the red chair.
Applications

Reading load and fault in matter, bodies and formations

Associations

The Moto blood gives the eye, and the Kōkan gold in it opens the road to the Kamigan
Fractura, read through the Body Path
SEAM-SIGHT, the Trait it holds open

Limitations

It cannot resolve intent, a lie, or anything with no structure
Held open it takes a little under eight percent of his reserve a minute, some eleven and a half minutes from full to Starvation
It is heat behind the eye for as long as it is held
Forced past its depth, the seam widens by a thread and never closes
The gold seam gives it away
It is countered by giving it nothing flawed, or nothing it can see

DEAD NOTE! (破滅の業 · Hametsu no Gō, the Work of Ruins) · Bloodline Art, Hataraki
DEAD NOTE is basically resonant destruction: the power to end what is already dead. It is one of the six Works of Hataraki, and the one his blood leans to. Not to be confused with FURE, which uses the blade to ring one chosen thing at its worst flaw.
Capabilities
The Work of Ruins is his blood’s grip on one job of Fate, the ending of what has already begun to end, and Fractura does the breaking through his body. A dead crack, with the rot already through it, rings sour and wavering against the steady note of the sound stone around it: the thing is already telling the world where it will go. Muken finds that sour note with the Eye, takes it in the Kharven breath and holds it through one long breath and nothing else. The thing’s own readiness to end does the rest, until the dead thing comes apart along its own fault.
Nothing sound beside it is touched. The strength that breaks the thing is the thing’s own, which is why it takes so little from him and why it finds only what was already dying.
It can touch a living man, inside his oath, where a death done to him was never finished, because that crack is already dead. The ending that runs it is all the target’s own, whatever his Stage.
Applications

Bringing down rotten rope, timber and stonework without harming what stands next to it
Ending the lying ward-stone over the Seat’s gatehouse from half a mile away
Finishing a death that was begun and never completed, in a living man

Associations

The Kōkan grip on the Works of Hataraki, taught by Faisal in the Plane of Fate
Fate is where the grip takes hold, and Fractura does the breaking through his body
SEAM-SIGHT finds the note, and the Kharven breath carries it
His Dominion Fate is set against the target’s Persistence and Continuity, and a dead thing cannot meet it

Limitations

It works only on what is already dead, and he has sworn by his honor to crack nothing else
A rope’s worth of rot takes about two percent of his reserve; a thing held at a distance takes a fifth or more
The breath gives it away: in through the nose until the ribs ache, out through the mouth until nothing is left
Noise, damping, cold or a hand laid flat on the struck thing breaks the note
Bringing him nothing already dead leaves it nothing to end
Driven by rage it ends what was rotten and then what stood near the rot, and it does not stop by itself

THE WAY SHE DID IT (純潔の業 · Junketsu no Gō, the Work of Purity) · Bloodline Art, Hataraki
THE WAY SHE DID IT is basically healing: the power to close a wound by listening to its living edges. It is one of the six Works of Hataraki, and the breaker’s knowledge from the mending side.
Capabilities
Purity establishes a thing in its proper shape and holds it there. He learned it by learning to look at the edges of a wound and never the wound, the way his sister did. He lays his palm flat over the hurt, says nothing, listens for the living edges, and holds their note until they close along the shape they already had. The closing is done by the living flesh itself.
It can run without being called, along a shape already laid round him. A harness laced in the old order is a shape, and the Work finds the shape in the cords and runs along it, so the plates press broken ribs together and a greave draws a kneecap round and holds it like a splint.
Purity has an Obsession face, which purges whatever does not fit the shape. That is the Shirogane way.
Applications

Knitting his own broken ribs, the cut across his side, his forearm and his palm
Shutting a long fresh cut clean, without hiding the scar
Pressing broken ribs together and splinting a kneecap through a harness laced in the old order

Associations

The Kōkan grip on the Works of Hataraki, taught by Faisal
Fate is where the grip takes hold, and the living flesh does the closing
His sister, whose way of looking at a wound it is

Limitations

It works only on what is living and willing, and Faisal forbade him to do it to a man who has not asked
Old harm the body has already set crooked it will not touch, because the proper shape is now the crooked one: the wrist from the stamping floor, the shin from the Veyrath ditch, his knuckles
A fresh wound takes about five percent of his reserve and a quiet minute
The flat palm and the silence give it away
It is countered by hurting him faster than he can listen

OPEN HAND (精霊の業 · Seirei no Gō, the Work of Spirit) · Bloodline Art, Hataraki
OPEN HAND is basically soul anchoring: the power to feel a soul’s thread, and hold it or let it go. It is one of the six Works of Hataraki, the Work of what lies between life and death.
Capabilities
He can feel a soul’s thread where it runs, and hold it, or open his hand and let it pass. He held his sister’s on the road out without knowing he was doing it. In the Plane of Fate he let her go, and wept for the first time since he was nine.
It finds a living thread even in a dead hall: a bond to the dead, burned nearly through and still there.
Applications

Holding a soul’s thread on the crossing between living and dead
Letting a thread pass
Finding the one living bond in a dead place

Associations

The Kōkan grip on the Works of Hataraki, taught by Faisal
Fate is where the grip takes hold, on the crossing between living and dead

Limitations

It needs a thread that is still there to hold
It cannot call back a thread that has gone, nor keep one that will not stay
It costs little in Essence, and a great deal otherwise
His closed hand gives it away
It is countered by distance and time

JIKAN NO SHIGOTO (時間の仕事 · the Work of Temporality) · Bloodline Art, Hataraki
JIKAN NO SHIGOTO is basically retrocognition: the power to follow a cause back, a knot at a time. It is one of the six Works of Hataraki, and a quiet one.
Capabilities
Temporality is the Work of cause and consequence. Holding one thread, he can follow it back along what made it, a knot at a time. He followed his sister’s death back that way to the Shirogane’s thousand-year wound of standing second. He uses it only to follow.
Applications

Tracing a death back along what caused it

Associations

The Kōkan grip on the Works of Hataraki, taught by Faisal
Fate is where the grip takes hold
THE WHOLE HAND, which can read past a knot this Work stops at

Limitations

It shows causes and changes none
A long thread takes long hours
Each knot takes about one percent of his reserve, and leaves a heavy head
A knot where the cause has gone dark, or has been hidden, stops it every time
It is countered by a thread too tangled to follow before the moment passes

CHISHIKI NO SHIGOTO (知識の仕事 · the Work of Knowledge) · Bloodline Art, Hataraki
CHISHIKI NO SHIGOTO is basically emotion detection: the power to hear what a man is humming under his face. It is one of the six Works of Hataraki, and a quiet one.
Capabilities
Knowledge reveals what a thing is. He hears what a man is humming under his face: fear, grief, appetite. He uses it only to hear.
Associations

The Kōkan grip on the Works of Hataraki, taught by Faisal
Fate is where the grip takes hold

Limitations

It reveals and does not act: it will tell him Kagenori Tenrai is grieving without telling him what to do about it
Each reading takes about one percent of his reserve
His head tipping as if listening gives it away
It is countered by a man who has gone quiet inside

DIDN’T CRACK! (仕事の壁 · Shigoto no Kabe, the Work of Bearing Load) on BARANSU NO SHIGOTO (バランスの仕事 · the Work of Balance) · Bloodline Art, Hataraki, and its Application
DIDN’T CRACK is basically force redirection: the power to stand under a load and send it into the ground. Balance is one of the six Works of Hataraki, and the wall, Bearing Load, is what he makes of it.
Capabilities
It is the breaker’s knowledge turned round. A cutter who can see where a load gathers can see the road it wants to take, and a load need not stop in him if he gives it a road to the ground. Petralon, the Foundation Stone, whose idea is the foundation, to become what other things stand on, carries it down through bone and stance as a sound pillar carries a roof. He learned it kneeling beside Faisal under the Lawbell’s weight.
Applications
