Carrying even a seven-Stage Pressure through him into the ground
Standing in front of something that means to come down on everyone behind him

Techniques

BARANSU NO SHIGOTO - the Work under it: a load passes through him and goes down into the ground
SHIGOTO NO KABE - the wall: he plants both feet, Balance takes the blow through his bones into the earth, and he does not move

Associations

The Kōkan grip on the Works of Hataraki, taught by Faisal
Fate is where the grip takes hold, and his body does the carrying through Petralon

Limitations

It needs ground under him that will take the load; airborne, braced on ice, or on a floor that will not take it, the weight has nowhere to go
Against a load that comes from every side at once, or from below, it has no path
A floor that holds only what its owner lets it hold gives the load nowhere to go, and every blow stops in his body
Balance takes about three percent of his reserve to open, and a slow bleed while held
The wall takes about four percent to set and a steady drain to hold, some eight and a half minutes from full
It cracks his bones a little every time, which shows as hairline cracks down both forearms from wrist to elbow
Whatever he sends down the ground has to keep, and enough loads open a hollow under the stone until the hill goes out from under him
He kneels, or plants both feet and stops moving, and that gives it away
It is countered by taking the ground out from under him, making him move, or hitting him from where the ground is not

THE WHOLE HAND (全体性の働き · Zentai-sei no Hataraki, the Work of Totality) · Bloodline Art, Hataraki; the Kōkan’s own
THE WHOLE HAND is basically destiny perception: the power to close every Work on one thread at once and read the thing whole. It is the crown of the other Works and the Kōkan’s own, tied to the Kamigan.
Capabilities
Each Work is a grip on one job: what is failing, what ought to stand, what is crossing, what is due, what a thing is, what is overdone. A hand can close only one way at a time, which is why every Moto who ever lived held one grip well and the rest by rote. Totality is the hand itself. All six close on the same thread together, and the thread is read whole: what it is, what it is due, where it fails and where it holds, what it carries and where it is crossing to. A thing seen that way has no surprises left in it and needs no predicting, and he has stopped trying to read Fate ahead of itself, as the rest of his house does and buries its children for.
He sits inside the run of things and sees where each action goes down into its consequence, smooth where it is smooth and broken where it meets a fault. A complete thing can also be stepped into, the way a man steps into a river at the place where the water slides past itself in layers with no eddies in it. The scholars call that laminar flow: smooth water carries a stone without tumbling it.
It first came uncalled. The one bell in his teeth split into seven notes, the six Works and over them a seventh he had never heard, which gathered the rest into one chord, and everything in front of him went to glaze: every crack already in the air, the ground and the man, shown all at once as one total thing he can hold. Now he calls it low and plain, the way a man says grace over a bowl: “Zentai-sei no Hataraki.”
Applications

Reading a thread whole, past a dark knot that stops JIKAN NO SHIGOTO
Watching where a working sent across hundreds of miles of sky will run out of consequence, so that it ends there without his lifting a hand
Finding his own thread, where he is and where he is due, and letting the flow carry his place in the world down the smooth part and through a pocket left open in the Veil
Laying it over himself and THE UNWRITTEN NAME as a mask
Keeping it closed in the left hand for the length of a fight, holding a thousand mended threads steady while the right hand stays on the sword

Techniques

SPLIT AND RESOLVE - two words on one short falling cut with Tsugigane: “Split” is Ruins, every crack in the thing running at once, and “Resolve” is Purity, every piece sent to its proper end
SPLIT AND RESOLVE, how it works - a thing heated and quenched for centuries has one place where the whole of it is waiting to go, as a glassman’s drop laughs at a hammer on its bulb and goes to powder if the thin tail is snapped; he finds that place and cuts there
SPLIT AND RESOLVE, what it leaves - the thing shatters from the cut outward into pieces no bigger than rice grains, and the world keeps the line of that cut, still called Tsugigane’s Resolve, so a later cut can fall on it

Associations

The Kōkan blood, with the other Works in hand
Faisal withheld it and never taught it, until Muken could stand before seven lines, a dozen Banner Houses and a Zettari prince and want every one of them to stay exactly what they are and still be one thing together; then it came by itself
The Kamigan, the crown eye
Every move of UNLIMITED WORKS OF FATE is THE WHOLE HAND closed on one purpose

Limitations

It follows cause down into consequence, so a thing whose arriving has been cut loose from its going gives the hand nothing to close on, and he does not see it come
The step through the Veil needs an opening already there; a Body walker cannot step through the Soul Plane as a Yukari does, so this is the long way
It is priced as all six Works at once, far above what his rung of Fate Mastery, Fate IV, can pay for, and it is paid in blood from both eyes and the nose and in bells that go from ringing to aching
With the reserve short it goes through the floor of his reserve into his own substance, a debt the Crystal does not refill
The charge shows: the Kharven breath, held, then the left iris crazing gold like an old cup, then the right, then heat, pressure and a thin line of blood from each eye
His aura does not spread but draws in tight round the body, more seam than stone, six notes sound in his teeth as one chord, and the gravel under him beds lower
When Fate calls the debt in it stops like a mill stopping, six bells gone to one low note under the stone
Its Obsession face is the hunger to gather everything into one hand; his father reached for it, and that was what the cellars were
That is no longer only a warning: with the red in his eyes and the rules twisted in his fist he has felt his own mouth and jaw set into his father’s, the year before the cellars, and not stopped
It is countered by putting the result ahead of its cause, by breaking his hold while both hands are full, or by being so whole that the reading finds nothing to use

UNLIMITED WORKS OF FATE · Legendary art, Bara’s own, given as knowledge; counted in Acts
UNLIMITED WORKS OF FATE is basically fate manipulation on credit: the power to do every one of the first god’s jobs at once, and the bill always comes. It is a legendary art, Bara’s own, given to him as knowledge and not as a blessing, and its moves all run on the one idea below.
Capabilities
Bara wrote the Works before time to keep the world running. In the Plane of Fate Bara laughed, called the boy the White Wolf and the scavenger of Fate, a man who could see the flaws in any possibility and pick it clean, touched his forehead, and gave him the knowledge of his Ultimate Techniques. It is knowledge and no blessing, so nothing pays for it but him.
He opens it himself: every Work he has, all at once, with no limit set on what they are for except the one he sets as he names the move. That is the name, and he chose it alone, knowing Yusif would have laughed. Each move is THE WHOLE HAND closed on one purpose, so the charge is the same breath and the same crazed gold, and he speaks the name of the art aloud before the name of the move.
Several moves lean on roots. They come down from where the Plane of Fate leans closest and go into stone like roots into wet soil, and they take a standing load into ground far deeper than one man. They also fill him, and not by drawing. Purity knows the proper shape of his reserve, which is full, Balance knows what went out of it and where, and the roots make his Crystal the place the flow of Fate wants to go, so it comes in by itself. Foresters say a tree does the same, that it does not suck water up but packs its root with what it has gathered until the water outside cannot stay outside and pushes in, and they call it root pressure; it is a good comparison and a forester’s word, and it is not the reason.
Applications

Cutting a man whose skin seals wounds by drinking the force of a blow
Calling in the claim on a person’s past
Lifting a seal that has been pressed on a soul
Mending a person’s broken threads, and tying body back to spirit
Catching a collapse and setting it into a floor, a wall and a stair
Carrying a standing load into the ground through the roots
Refilling his reserve through the roots, to about 95 percent, on account

Techniques

CLEAVE - a cut with no force in it at all, falling on the line of an old cut because the world keeps the mark of a cut; a skin that seals wounds by drinking a blow’s force as heat has nothing to drink, and bleeds like any man’s
CLEAVE, as a real stroke - the rising diagonal from the hip with Tsugigane, which treats the body, the Shell, the Core and the layer where a soul’s share of fate is tied as the next thing along one line, the way a good cut goes through a bundle of bamboo, the mat behind it and the post behind that
CLEAVE, what it leaves - a seam into the Plane of Fate, the color of nothing, and whatever energy touches the seam is taken out of the world, chaos and order alike; he says it low, and the last of a set he shouts
NADI - one committed stroke allowed to run down every line it might have taken, ten seams, twenty, five hundred, and then closed back into the one; Temporality knows the cut is due, Knowledge knows what it is, and Balance lays its weight along every other course the motion could have run
FIRST ACT: INFINITE CLEAVE - the space round him curves and it cuts along every road the target could take, so every step away from him lands nearer, and a fist thrown straight down a bent road passes a hand’s width wide
INFINITE REACH - the world folds toward one target like cloth toward a pin, and a gold blade no longer than a forearm, the shape of the cutter’s chisel he carried at eight, comes down the grain of every seam in every stance the target might take, including the ones it has not chosen yet
SABA NO ROSA - the Reckoning of Roses: the sky grows roots, each rose a deposit and each thorn an unpaid debt, and the claim on a person’s past is called in a deposit at a time, the past staying true while the present grip on it thins like a spoon of salt in a river
CLEANSE - the roots go white, and a seal pressed on a soul lifts in flakes and spreads along them across the whole Plane until it is everywhere and therefore nowhere, like a drop of ink in a still lake
FUSION - gold thread off his fingers splices every broken strand of a person end to end, the cutters’ long splice, thicker at the mend and stronger there than anywhere else; it wakes the threads they never knew they had, and ties body back to spirit
WEAVE, then RESOLVE - Ruin lets the dead rubble fall, Purity holds the whole things in their shape, Balance turns each weight sideways to brace the next, and everything falling is knotted over and under its neighbor into a net; the second word pulls the net hard into a floor, a wall and a stair, the way a wet rope goes hard when the knot is pulled tight

Associations

Bara, the First Epoch, who gave it with a touch on the forehead in the Plane of Fate
THE WHOLE HAND, which every move is, and the six Works under it
Tsugigane, which puts a smith’s edge into CLEAVE
NADI is the old readers’ word for a channel, and SABA NO ROSA has its own page among the spells
INFINITE CLEAVE is the Stannvaard philosophers’ saying, that a thrown stone tries every road at once and goes by the one that costs least, made into a blade
He calls it “Unlimited Fate Works”

Limitations

It runs on credit: every share is entered against his name in Fate, and nothing comes down out of Fate that Fate does not mark
The bill always comes, and it has come once already and taken the Eye
When Fate collects it takes everything below a quarter of his reserve, the floor under it and the place under the floor, with blood from both eyes, the nose and the ears, his hearing muffled and the Eye blind
The gold seam in his eye tears a thread wider with every share
Every use runs on the gift or on borrowed sap, and none of it on his own rung
A move that leans on the roots dies with the roots: cut above the ground, they hang gray and the sap stops where it stood
Fire that has stopped telling fuel from air will eat the roots, though there is always more root
Used out of the body, paid by the gift, he comes back vomiting blood, his aura’s gold dim as brass, his teeth chattering
A crossing and FUSION together took him down to about 40 percent of his reserve, with blood from eyes and nose and the left knee loose; WEAVE costs more than FUSION
NADI at five hundred seams takes him past the half and past the quarter in one stroke with nothing refilling
SABA NO ROSA costs half a percent of his full reserve a rose
A thing that has bitten off its own thread has no knot for CLEAVE to part, and a thing with nothing tied gives it none either
He names the art aloud before every move, so it is heard coming
It is countered by owing nothing and carrying no old cut, by cutting the roots above the ground or taking the ground away, or by breaking his hold before the mends set

Releases
FURE! (ひび · Hibi, the Hairline) · First Release
FURE is basically shattering: the power to ring one thing at its own note until its worst crack runs. It is his First Release, which the north calls the Crack, and Tsugigane, his bonded sword, carries it.
Capabilities
He calls “Fure,” shake, the word the Kōkan used before it was taken from the line in the cellars at Halcrest, and Faisal gave it back. On the call the blade begins to ring at the natural note of one thing before him, a single blade, a bone, a plate of armor, an iron hand, and holds it there. Fractura and the Eye find that thing’s worst flaw, the place where it was always going to part, and the held note keeps telling the thing where it will go until the crack runs there on its own. The blade is the tuning fork, the way a singer can break a glass by holding its note, which is the comparison the north makes.
One target, one crack. Called silent, the blade only hums and the crack runs slow. The bond carries the call: torn from his hand and lying paces away, Tsugigane still rings on “Fure.”
Applications

Breaking a single blade, a bone, a plate of armor or an iron hand
Passing over a crack in plain sight to take a hidden one, such as a cold shut, a seam where the metal never fused in the casting
Ringing Tsugigane from paces away, out of his hand

Associations

Fractura, through the Body Path, as a strike
SEAM-SIGHT finds the flaw, and the Kharven breath comes before the call
Tsugigane carries HIBI’s note and, in the silver thread of its join, his sister’s
The word a blade of his house answers to while it sleeps is Asami

Limitations

It needs a flaw; something whole gives it nothing
It needs a blade to carry the note
A blade held on a note too long finds its own crack
It takes about eight percent of his reserve to wake and a fast drain to hold, a little under two minutes from full
The cost shows as heat behind the eyes and a tremor in the sword hand that grows with each new note he tunes to
The Kharven breath before it gives it away
It is countered by killing the note with cold, padding or a hand flat on the struck steel, by changing what he must read before he can hold one pitch, or by bringing nothing flawed

EVERY ROPE IN THE CITY (ひび割れ · Hibiware, the Crazing) · Second Release
EVERY ROPE IN THE CITY is basically a destructive field: the power to ring everything around him at once and find every hairline flaw in it. It is his Second Release. It woke once, it has never been called, and Faisal has forbidden it.
Capabilities
The single crack becomes a web. The blade rings at the note of everything around him at once, and the rings go out, felt in the long bones and the back teeth, finding every hairline flaw in whatever they pass. It is FURE’s ring with no choosing in it, every note at once, and that is the whole danger.
It woke once, out of him, in the rage after his sister, and crazed the snow of the Foot’s yard and the ends of the woodpile. Faisal named it, and forbade it until he can do to every rope in a city what he did to one rope and leave every sound one standing. He re-closed the crazed snow by holding its note, which is the only thing about it he has mastered.
It presses up under him and he refuses it. He can let it rise as far as his throat and set it down the way a cutter sets down a full load at the top of the fourth gallery, carefully, so it does not spill. A third waking lies under it, and Faisal will not speak of it.
Associations

Fractura, through the Body Path, as a field of the same ring
FURE, the same ring on one target
His Domain, which this release opens and pays for
Faisal, who named it and whose condition gives it its name

Limitations

Faisal’s word has not been lifted
The reserve is there now, but called in grief it would fracture the Crystal along its grief
With no choosing in it, it would crack everyone he loves along their flaws
He is the counter: his oath, and Faisal’s word
From outside it is countered as FURE is, and by distance from everything he loves

characters/ability-accounts/naiser-yukar.title: Naiser Yukari — Abilities in full
characters/ability-accounts/naiser-yukar.content:
Card: Naiser Yukari
THE RECORD OF BOTH HOUSES
THE RECORD OF BOTH HOUSES (両家の記録 · Ryōke no Kiroku) is basically record manipulation: the power to read what is already there, enter it, and make the entry hold. Whatever you say or owe near him goes into the book, and what is in the book comes true. It is his signature art, and his Traits, his techniques, his Releases and his Domain are this one idea done at a different size.
Capabilities
A house record does three things to a promise. It reads it, it writes it down, and after that it will not let the promise be anything other than what was written. His soul does those three things to people, to ground, to smoke, to wounds and to himself, and his two bloods are the two clerks who do the work. Two pendulum clocks hung on one beam fall into the same swing over a night, each nudging the other through the wood. The scholars call it entrainment, and the old clockmakers who found it could not stop it. His Crystal is the beam. The Yukari half, Ashura’s sight in his father’s line, sees every Aether thread in a room as a line. The Lambert half, his mother’s ledger, forecasts a blow from the shoulder’s first commitment by setting it against every blow it has ever counted. While the two swing together the sight gives the count something to count and the count tells the sight which thread matters. This part has no Wellspring behind it. It is inheritance and labor.
Three lenses shape the rest. Like any practitioner he pulls Aether (mana, in the common word) out of the ground he stands on, refines it in the Soul Crystal into Essence (spiritual energy), and drives it out through the Shell. He is a Spirit fighter with a Walked Body, so the Core authors everything and most of it lands on souls and on meaning, with enough left in the hands to carry a cut. Anamnesis, the Remembering, is the idea that everything keeps its past, and its operation is separation: the past a thing has kept is parted from it and read, as the residue is parted from the vessel that held it. A soul that has become that idea can touch a thing and read it, so under it a soul’s lineage, a stone’s history and a bone’s first shape are all pages. It reads and it never writes. The Measurewrights compare it to fired clay, which keeps the dose of its kiln and gives it back as light when it is heated again; their instruments can read the dose, and none of them has ever read a lineage. Fixatio, the Knot, is the lens that enters. Its idea is commitment, and its operation is coagulation: what is bound is set past melting, because the way back has stopped existing. A line set into the ground holds without him, a sentence set into smoke stands in still air, and a declaration made in his hearing sets with the padding fallen away, because a commitment takes only what was truly meant. The Measurewrights call it a thermoset cure, a resin whose cross-links leave no other shape to go back to, and their tables of cure times are the best in the four quarters. Ascensio, the Ladder of Ascent, is the idea of the ladder, the whole height climbed by steps with no single step large enough to break you, and its operation is distillation, the same work passed up again and again by degrees. It is how six Stages came to him quietly. The Measurewrights draw it as an inclined plane.
On a blow, the art rides inside the cut and never replaces it. The count chooses the line and the sight chooses the instant, the cut is real steel through real tissue, placed to the finger’s width, and the sum of what each man spent is known to him before the blade is clear.
Applications

Reading a blow before it is thrown, and tracking several fighters at once
Making oaths, truces and offers bind at the strength they were spoken
Showing a lie where the other man can see it
Bringing up everything unsettled in an opponent’s blood at once
Closing ground to anyone who has not decided what he is
Holding his own wounds at what was read
Striking the account of every exchange, and leaving the moment the sum turns
Calling every promise ever entered in the hall due at once

Techniques

TWIN-BLOOD HARMONY - the two bloods keeping one count, the clerks themselves
THE ENTERED WORD - what is said near him sets
THE BREATH’S CONTINUANCE - Ashura’s blood, which slows ruin and clears his senses
KAGE NO KEIFU - the record read out of another man
YUKARI NO MON - the record entered into ground, as a line
RYŌKE NO KATA - both bloods at full swing for one exchange, closed by SEISAN
KEMURI NO HAN - a sentence entered into smoke
NULL-LIGHT - the house’s instrument, as far as he carries it
MIZU NO UTSUWA, MIMAMORI, SENGAKI, YOMIAGE, KIZU-YOMI, MUSAN, IMI, MITSU NO MA - the moves found on the Aerne ridge, each called once
THE TWIN MANTLE - the First Release, the two halves of him shown at once
THE CORRIDOR BETWEEN HALLS - the Second Release and the Domain, the record given a floor
THE RECORD OPENS - the Second Release’s last stage, the whole archive read aloud at once

Associations

Anamnesis, the Remembering, reads the record a thing keeps of its own making
Fixatio, the Knot, enters what is read and holds it
Ascensio, the Ladder of Ascent, laid his Stages over a long road
The Spirit Path does the work, on souls and on meaning, and the Walked Body carries the cut
The Yukari blood gives the sight and the Lambert blood gives the count, and neither has a Wellspring behind it
The unnamed longblade, his bonded weapon, narrow and severe, carried more as punctuation than ornament
He does not shout any of it: a name is said once, low, in the house’s old Japonic, usually round the leaf, and the room goes quiet enough to hear it

Limitations

It reads and enters only what is already there: what was said, what is owed, what a thing was made as
The labor of keeping the two bloods agreed, the Equilibrium Tax, is charged against every great working he does
The book’s own price: his word sets too, the mistaken ones included, and people stand near him the way they stand near a record being written
What he binds stays bound, including mistakes; Fixatio’s named failure is over-cure, a rigidity that cannot bend even to save him
Ascensio’s failure is the debt: a ladder makes the height bearable and never makes it lower, every step is still owed, and he arrives everywhere owing the difference; at Stage XII he owes six
About a ninth of what he calls strays, and it comes off him as plain warmth at the fingertips, on the cord of the hilt or the paper of the leaf
Under a load too big to carry clean the heat shows in the thread-marks, which light silver, go violet at the edges, and redden the skin over them
Each of his arts costs a fixed share and lands entire; at full output he would empty in about 71 seconds, and nobody has ever seen him open at full
The charge always shows: his breath and heartbeat fall into one count, the two low notes of his aura drift together until they are one with a long hall’s echo under them, and the air round him dims as if somebody had gone down a corridor turning the lamps low, the gray of him going black-violet at the edges like black silk drawn over a blade
Smaller workings add their own sign: the shadow stretching for KAGE NO KEIFU, the dimmed line for the Gate, the smoke standing still for the Verdict, a small dry click as Fixatio sets
Against a higher Stage it thins in a known order: the forecast goes first, because a stronger fighter does things the ledger has never counted
THE ENTERED WORD and the Verdict keep working there, since they run on what is said and not on rank, and the Corridor still asks its question, though a soul far above him answers it and walks through at a cost
What he has left then is the hall’s doors, the account, and the choice to leave when the sum turns
It is beaten by saying nothing and swearing nothing, by driving his two bloods apart with ugly formless pressure or with grief, by hitting early before he settles, or by simply outlasting the form

Traits
TWIN-BLOOD HARMONY (双血調和 · Sōketsu Chōwa) · Primary Trait
TWIN-BLOOD HARMONY is basically bloodline synchronization: the power to have two inheritances keep one count, so that he is never where the blow goes and every cut of his arrives like something already decided. It is the two clerks of the art themselves.
Capabilities
Two inheritances that share one soul either tear it or learn to keep one count, and his learned. The Yukari current, Ashura’s sight in his father’s line, is wide and deep and always reaching for every thread in the room. The Lambert blood from his mother is exact and counting, the blood that reads a blow before it is thrown. They pulled against each other through his childhood, and then over years, through the beam of his own Crystal, they began to answer, the way two pendulum clocks hung on one beam fall into the same swing over a night, each nudging the other through the wood.
It is labor and inheritance, with no Wellspring behind it: the two bloods hold each other in his Core, and his Crystal is the beam they hang from. The Measurewrights call it entrainment and say coupled swings lock together through any shared medium; the yard says only that the clocks agree. The count sharpens the sight and the sight gives the count something to count. The count can read an attack worst first and answer it with breath alone, in for six and out for six. The count lays the next minute out in columns and the sight lays it out in threads, and he can read a whole field from both at once. His window names the state in plain words, AGREED at a hair’s width, then ONE COUNT.
Applications

Moving before a blow lands, so the opponent sees only a man who is never where the strike goes
Tracking several fighters at once and knowing which of them is committed
Never being surrounded by a crowd
Seeing where one duelist’s next line runs
Reading a whole field from the count and the sight together

Techniques

The Clocks Agree (同調 · Dōchō) - while the two swing together every action arrives less like a choice than an inevitability, and Finesse, Economy and Penetration run a step above what the numbers read
The Count Reads (算読 · Sandoku) - the Lambert half reads a blow before it is thrown by comparing the shoulder’s first commitment against thousands of earlier ones
The Sight Holds (糸視 · Itomi) - the Yukari half sees every Aether thread in the room, each person’s current as a line

Associations

The two inheritances, Yukari sight and Lambert count, with no Wellspring behind them
The Spirit Path reads, and the Walked Body’s hands land it
It scales with his Coherence and his Gnosis, and is bound to his two bloods agreeing
RYŌKE NO KATA and THE TWIN MANTLE, which are this Trait at full swing

Limitations

It is passive and constant and costs nothing to keep, which is why it is also the thing an opponent attacks
The forecast is made from old blows: it is accurate until the opponent does something no one has done, and blind to a blow nobody has thrown before
When the bloods disagree it fails all at once
Its failure is Rigidity: he will not lean toward either blood even when leaning would save him

THE ENTERED WORD is basically declaration binding: the power to make a thing said near him come out plainer than it was meant, and then set so it cannot be taken back. Capabilities
Fixatio is commitment, and what it binds stays bound because the way back has stopped existing. His soul has lived inside that idea so long that it reaches past him into what is said in his hearing: near him, declarations set. Reality listens a little harder when he decides what something is. The Measurewrights call it a thermoset cure, cross-links that leave no other shape to go back to.
A commitment takes only what was truly meant. The padding a lie needs does not set and falls away, so a boast spoken within twenty paces of him comes out as the bare thing under it, and a true threat is entered whole. When his reserve reaches nothing, soul sickness sets in under four parts in a hundred, and the plain matter of his hands begins to lift away in bloodless gray flecks while the soul inside stands whole. He has held that pipe shut all his life, and opening it on purpose is the last thing he would choose.

NULL-LIGHT (無光 · Mukō) · Bloodline Instrument, as far as he carries it
NULL-LIGHT is basically supreme observation: the power to know a thing so completely that it has no shadow left, and a thing that well known cannot be changed behind his back. It is the Yukari house’s instrument, Ashura’s own way of seeing, under the law to be known is to be held, and what he keeps of it is a fragment.

It gives no fire and moves no pebble. Its whole work is on souls, on workings and on what a thing is.
Laid along an edge, the fragment is the mirror of whatever law it meets: it knows the working whole, and a working known whole is held to its own opposite and lies down along the plane of the blade, so the steel goes through plain air at its own speed. The scholars draw it as a hump sent down a rope from each end, one flicked up and one flicked down, which leave the rope flat where they meet, and call it destructive interference.

THE CORRIDOR BETWEEN HALLS (狭間の廊 · Hazama no Rō) · Domain
THE CORRIDOR BETWEEN HALLS is basically a judgment territory: the power to make the ground round him a hall where everything you owe gets heavier, and where anyone without enough self cannot arrive. It is the record given a floor, and it formed round him at Emanation without being called.
Capabilities
Space round him behaves like a place between houses, between vows, between names. Those caught in his strongest pressure report a corridor between ancestral halls, judged by both and owned by neither. It stands up as a double row of square cedar posts gone red-brown and resin-dark, the posts of the Enclave’s long hall and of the Lambert bench-house at Sallowgate laid one over the other, with a door of cedar at one end and a door of iron-bound oak at the other, and the smell of old paper under the cedar smoke.
A threshold belongs to the houses on either side of it and never to the one standing in it, and the only question it asks is by whose leave. That is the law of the whole Domain: Fixatio commits the ground to the judgment of both houses, and the measure the judgment takes is a self. “Enough self” is the cutoff. A fighter who has decided what he is goes down the hall like a bell’s low note. One who has not is below cutoff, and below cutoff a thing does not slow down in the hall; it fails to arrive, so his force, his speed and his workings die a pace past the line. The scholars have their own account of it, a waveguide, a passage that carries only the modes it was built for and lets everything below its cutoff fade in the first paces, and they are right about how far the fading reaches and never about why a self is what it measures.
It reads the relations a rival law is made of, one thread at a time, and each thread that has no self behind it fades from the far end toward the near. With nothing left to spend, it can form again uncalled: the dimness goes out from two paces to six, the pillars stand up, and a hand that pushes to shut it with no leave from either house dies below cutoff. He calls himself a threshold that asks. The space that formed where the two bloods meet is the narrowest place in him, and it is where the Domain grew.
Applications

Killing the force, speed and workings of anyone who crosses without enough self
Reading what every person inside owes, and laying that weight on them
Fading a rival law thread by thread
Giving THE RECORD OPENS the hall it is called in
Giving NULL-LIGHT a length to run down

Techniques

The Threshold (敷居 · Shikii) - anyone crossing the line without enough force of self feels it as resistance in body and spirit at once, as if entering a doctrine that has already judged them unready, and the blow dies in the first pace past it
The Two Benches (両席 · Ryōseki) - the corridor is judged from both ends, the Yukari hall and the Lambert bench; every grievance, debt and unresolved inheritance a person carries is read, and the heavier the account, the heavier the air on them
The Length (廊の長 · Rō no Naga) - a hall and no field, about two hundred paces, with two doors, one at each end
THE CORRIDOR: SHIKII (敷居 · the Threshold) - called inside it, the dimmed line sets into a black sill under one man, the Two Benches read his whole account at once, and the pull his nature was built on is asked what it is and can crack like glaze on a pot plunged cold

Associations

Fixatio, with Anamnesis reading the accounts
The Spirit Path: a judgment on souls authored in the Core, landing through a small use of the Studied Fate as a claim on the ground
His Attraction Layer, which carries territorial durability and is why the Corridor forms round him without being called
YUKARI NO MON, whose fixed home it is
The Second Release, which calls it

Limitations

Its radius stays short, about two hundred paces
It costs what a Domain of his rank costs and is held for minutes; begun inside another’s Domain it costs three times as much to start
A fighter above cutoff walks through, at a cost
The Two Benches tell him what a person owes and never what they will do
A guest may leave by either door
It is only as sound as the judgment of both houses, and a man who has settled with both is below nothing
A line of dimmed air, then pillars appearing in the dark at the corridor’s edges, and the two notes of his aura becoming a long hall’s echo, show it coming
It is beaten by crossing with enough self, or by walking out by a door

characters/ability-accounts/ned-chapman-.title: Ned Chapman — Abilities in full
characters/ability-accounts/ned-chapman-.content:
Card: Ned Chapman
Techniques
GUESSING WHOSE IT WAS · the knack, a skill on his sheet, Adept
GUESSING WHOSE IT WAS is basically psychometry: the power to hold a used thing for a minute and have his hands learn how its last owner held it. It is a knack he cannot name and nobody has explained. He is unwoken and has no Trait slot, so his sheet lists it as a trade skill, and the name is the sheet’s own, which he first saw as a boy and has never stopped finding funny.
Capabilities
Half of it is the trade and needs no knack. A used thing keeps a record of how it was used whether or not anybody ever reads it. Brass and latten wear a grain at a time where skin rides them, as a step wears where feet fall. An edge keeps the lie of the hone’s strokes, and a stem bent once and bent back keeps a frosted look where the metal was worked. An appraiser reads that with his eyes and thumb, and Ned is a good one.
The knack starts where the eyes stop. The wear is the track of one body’s habit, the same motion made ten thousand times until the hand does it without being asked. What comes to him in the minute is that habit itself, laid into his own hands and forearms: the grip, the angle of the wrist, the tucked elbow, the stroke the thing knew best and the one time it was loaded hardest. It gives a how and never a how hard. The steel remembers the shape of the cut and does not remember the arm that drove it, so a dead trooper’s falling stroke in a peddler’s hand is exact and could not go through a loaf.
To anyone watching it is a buyer’s look and nothing else. He turns the thing up to the light and lays his thumb where the last thumb lay: the worn seat on a spoon’s knop, the blunt of a blade above the cross, a buckler’s grip bar. His fist closes, his breath holds, and his eyes go to the middle distance for the length of a slow minute. In his head there is a dry riffle and a faint smell of old paper and attic dust, and both are his alone. No light comes on his hands and no color into the air, because an unwoken man has none to show.
In a fight he has no Essence, so nothing rides the blow but the borrowed shape, and the shape is the arms’ alone. On the Furlong the messer’s dead owner gave him a twitch out of a bind that split Hob Stile’s scalp and stopped on the bone, because the placing was a veteran’s and the force was a walking man’s. On the Hem road Alan Thwaite’s spear gave him a levy’s short hard thrust from the right hip while his own hips stayed square, so the wolf read his shoulders and the point skidded.
Why it is slow is his own reckoning, worked out from the outside the way he works out a price. Every soul has a hard bright knot under the breastbone that the woken pull the world’s own magic (Aether, mana in plain speech) through and turn into their own. His has sealed over like a well with a stone on it, and Kemp’s finger named it Capped. A capped soul still seeps, he thinks, and the knack runs on the seep. A seep fills a cup slowly, which is why a read takes a minute. That is a chapman’s guess built from tongs and cartwheels. It is unconfirmed, and no Measurewright has looked at him.
Applications

Learning a thing’s last owner: the hand, the height, the reach, how long and how carefully it was used, whether it bit flesh, how the last hand left it, and its hardest load
Proving goods false, as with forty “came-home” bucklers at Tollgarth, proved a week from the forge and aged in cow’s piss
Borrowing a dead owner’s grip, guard and best stroke for a fight
Reading his father’s purse in the loft
Reading the deserter’s messer, whose owner’s low guard he calls the Boar
Reading Alan Thwaite’s levy spear: five musters in a file, the short hard thrust from the right hip off the back foot, the head always coming round to the left shoulder after, and the hardest load a great weight (a horse, he thinks) stopped on the set spear

Techniques

THE SLOW MINUTE - skin on a used thing, turned to the light like any buyer pricing it, and in a minute he has the hand, the height, the reach, the years and the care, whether it bit flesh, its hardest load, and how the last hand left it; never called aloud, and to the whole bridge it is a chapman making up his mind
THE BORROWED HOLD - his hands settle into the dead owner’s grip and guard and keep the shape a quarter of an hour, perfectly drawn and with nothing behind it; a picture of a cut, he calls it

Associations

No Path, no Wellspring and no Form: he is unwoken and Capped, and the sheet cannot see the knack’s root
The appraiser’s trade, which reads wear by eye and thumb and supplies the why from nine years of pricing dead men’s goods
The same trade gives him what else he has in a fight: taking a length with the staff and reading it at the ell notch (forty-five inches), which his father taught him at nine; the measuring slide (Staff, Initiate); and setting a spear’s butt, which needs no force (Spear, Novice)
On the Hem’s hard crown his hobnails slid, the butt skated and the lugless head let the bitch come up the shaft
The crier’s voice: he read two wolves’ shared light as two dealers working a farmer and cried it, and crying boots at the wolves backed one off
A dark, quiet loft or an empty field at dusk makes a read loud and clean

Limitations

It gives only what a hand did, so there is never a name, a face or a thought in it, and the why of anything is his own inference
It gives a how and never a how hard: the borrowed stroke lands at his own force, which is Swordwork F and Spear F
He has no reserve, no Essence and no light to show
A read costs a slow minute, and most of a second minute in a thick crowd
By the fourth read on a dead men’s morning there is a first ache behind his eyes, and a headache by dusk; two loud reads in a day bring the ache early
Its tell is skin on the thing for a slow minute with his eyes going far, and then a quarter of an hour of the dead owner’s hold in his hands: a scullion’s flat scouring grip on a buckler, a left-handed man’s two fingers into the mouth of a purse, a horseman’s high guard on a saber
A trained eye across the yard has nothing else to read but a peddler holding a thing a little oddly
Only one hand’s story comes at a time, the hand that held the thing the way his own holds it, so a thing with many owners gives him the one his grip happens to match
The record has to be there to be read: fire wipes it, which he has only as Measurewrights’ hearsay, and scouring or a long soak leaves motions and loads and little else
Cloth between skin and thing stops it dead, which is why he bound Bett’s grip through a rag
A thick crowd on the ground he stands on muddies a read like a voice heard through a wall
A fighter who closes inside the minute beats it
It fails in its own way, and no Wellspring’s: the hold is somebody else’s whole habit, the bad half with the good, set on a body with the wrong feet under it, and it will not be argued with for a quarter of an hour
On the Hem road the dead man’s drilled head-turn to the left shoulder came with the thrust and took his eyes off the bitch at the worst moment
A shock can knock the hold out of the arm for a breath, and then it takes the arm back
A loud read leaves a habit behind for a day or two; the messer’s left his right thumb hooking for a nail
A thing held to the end reads that way too, and the hold clenches on it, so he has to open his fingers one at a time
Some things he will not read: he will not hold Tizz’s Long Arm to price it, and at Kemp’s he made no read at all, his hand going toward a yard-iron and coming back

characters/ability-accounts/parkin-gedge.title: Parkin Gedge — Abilities in full
characters/ability-accounts/parkin-gedge.content:
Card: Parkin Gedge
Techniques
HALF AND HALF · Synergia, with Larkin Gedge
HALF AND HALF is basically twin synchronization: the power to feel his brother’s sword as surely as his own hand, so the two of them can cut one target from both sides without looking. His brother cuts high, he cuts low, and neither of them looks. Larkin shouts it as HALVES! and is told that Halves sounds like a pie.
Capabilities
A man knows where his own hand is with his eyes shut, because muscle and joint report their place and their load to him unasked. The scholars call that sense proprioception, the body’s knowledge of itself. The bond lends each twin a share of the other’s. Parkin feels where Larkin’s edge is, how fast it travels and the instant it bites or misses, the way two sawyers on one cross-cut saw feel each other down the blade, so he never has to turn his head.
The brothers are harmonized with Benediction, the Grace, whose law is that a bond freely given is weighed by the world as a real thing. Kit Quarrel’s word for it is “the blessing kind, that keeps no count,” which is a fine joke on the one man in the company who counts everything. On the body, Benediction also lends the one blessed a real steadiness in the hands and the footing, which is why a man cutting blind in a dry ditch at dusk does not flinch or shorten the stroke.
His half is the low line, and the low line is the one that kills. A four-footed beast gets out from under a sword by dropping its head and shoulders and driving in beneath the cut, where any one man’s blade has already gone past; that is exactly where Parkin’s edge is already traveling from the other side, flat and low, under the chest and behind the forelegs. Whichever way the wolf goes off the one edge, it goes onto the other.
The charge is there for anyone to read. The twins set their shoulder blades together, both coats thicken to the red-gold of a loaf crust as they pull Aether (mana) up off the ground under their boots, and a thread of the same color rises between their shoulders and catches taut, with a soft low chord under it and a smell of new bread and church incense. About two parts in five of what each brother spends reaches the work, and the rest leaves them as warmth.
Applications

Cutting blind off his brother’s edge, back to back
Taking a wolf apart in two pieces, high and low in the same instant
Finishing from behind while his brother goes in at the head to make the thing look

Techniques

HALF AND HALF - back to back with the thread pulled bright as wire, Larkin cuts high at the head and Parkin, turning behind him blind, cuts low under the chest of the same wolf in the same instant; or Larkin goes in at the head to make it look and Parkin, behind it, brings one short cut down across the back of the neck to the spine; Parkin counts it as one wolf either way

Associations

Benediction, the Grace, a Wellspring of Fate whose Titan is Florwyn
His Path is not given; the Form is a Strike, and it lands through the body
Larkin Gedge, his twin and Resonant Pair, with whom he came by it living
Two plain hangers off the same smith’s bench

Limitations

Benediction carries no primary glyph, so the limit is the bond’s own measure: the thread is a sword’s reach long, and past that it snaps and they are two men with matching hangers
It is charged to both: both coats thin at once and the pair draw one breath together, every time, so neither brother can carry the other, and a winded twin winds his twin
It throws nothing at an enemy and does nothing to the wolf by itself; it rides two plain sword cuts, and every wound is steel
It is two edges on one target
Its named failure is competitive inhibition, which is displacement: the bond holds until something one brother holds dearer takes its place, and it goes silently, unfelt, until the blind cut comes and there is no second edge in the wolf
Its tell is the twins back to back with the thread taut
It is beaten by parting them past a sword’s reach, by coming at one from where the other cannot turn, or by sending more bodies than two edges can cross in
No reserve figure has been read for him

characters/ability-accounts/raizan-tenra.title: Raizan Tenrai Moto — Abilities in full
characters/ability-accounts/raizan-tenra.content:
Card: Raizan Tenrai Moto · The Doom Breaker
THE LAST THREAD (終の糸 · Tsui no Ito) · Signature art
THE LAST THREAD is basically unnoticeability: the power to find the gap where nobody is looking, and be in it. He only moves when you are not looking, and he knows the morning you die. The art is named for the needle, and the north uses the one name for both. His Traits, his techniques, his Releases and his Domain are all that one act done at a different size.
Capabilities
Everything has a gap. A man’s eyes have gaps, and BETWEEN BLINKS crosses a room in them. A room has a floor of small noise, and HUSH keeps him under it. A man’s next hours have a gap, one narrow moment when every way he might live thins at once, and THE ONE STRAND finds it. A skull has a gap a finger wide where it meets the neck, and ONE NEEDLE goes up through it. A step has a gap, the place the foot was never going to reach, and the Kingstep stands there. The First Release closes every gap he might have missed, and the Second makes a field forty yards across in which nothing unlikely is allowed to happen at all.
The art runs on three lenses and an eye. Tenebra, the Hidden Shadow, is the idea of going unseen, and its operation is separation: the soul is parted from the world’s notice and kept quieter than everything around it, so his Shell drinks the light, sound and Essence that reach it and turns the little that escapes away from the watcher. The Measurewrights call it the noise floor, and say a thing cannot be found when what it sends back falls below the background of whatever is looking; they are right about how quiet he is, and the old question of what he is hiding from was never theirs. Oneirion, the Dream, is dream as a place: every way a man could go is laid out in the space of what can be thought, where no soul has an address in a room, and the Tenrai doom-sight is read on that map, which the scholars call a configuration space. Ignivale, the Spark, is the smallest beginning that pays for itself, and it closes the gap between deciding and doing until the hand has left before the shoulder has told anyone. Over all three sits the Tengan, which has no lens and needs none: it times the eyes, ranks the futures and shows the foot where to go.
It all rides one blow. He does not trade: there is no second movement in him, and he never trained one. The minute finds the moment, the eyes’ gap carries him to the nape, the breath stops, and the needle goes in with the Spark behind it, so that the read, the crossing and the thrust arrive as one thing and the wound is all a physician will find. When the blow cannot be had he does not strike at all, and what is left is the feet: the Kingstep keeps him where the answer is not, and the Forcing Stone makes a standing man move. About twenty-four parts in twenty-five of what he spends reach the world, which is his yield. The share that falls short is paid in his Core as hollowing, the Spirit’s own coin, and whatever of it would show on another fighter as glare and noise is swallowed by the Tenebra coat with everything else, and it stays swallowed until he lets the coat go.
Applications

Reaching a guarded man unseen and killing him with one thrust
Leaving a wound the physicians will miss
Leading a stronger fighter by the nose without once being struck
Working in bedchambers, rafters and ruins, the dark, quiet, Aether-thin ground the art is made for

Techniques

BETWEEN BLINKS - crossing a room in the gaps when eyes are blind
THE ONE STRAND - finding the one moment a man can be killed
TENGAN - the Tenrai eye the whole art runs on
HUSH - staying quieter than the room he stands in
ONE NEEDLE - the single thrust at the nape
FORCING STONE - a flicked go stone that must be answered
KINGSTEP OF THE WINNING THREAD - the foot set where the other man was about to step
RUINOUS COINFALL - one small chance tipped at the moment it matters
KAMIKAKUSHI - the First Release, the hush laid over every sense in the field
HITSUZEN - the Second Release and the Domain, forty yards where the likeliest thing happens

Associations

Tenebra, the Hidden Shadow, the idea of going unseen
Oneirion, the Dream, the map the doom-sight is read on
Ignivale, the Spark, which puts the hand in motion before the shoulder
The Tengan, the Tenrai blood’s eye, over all three
The Last Thread, the needle the art is named for
His aura, a black-violet so faint that it reads as the shadow of something else, which takes Oneirion’s lavender at its edges while he reads

Limitations

He has not slept a full night since he was twenty, and every doom he breaks brings his own last morning a year nearer
There is one blow in it and no second movement; when the blow cannot be had he does not strike at all
A packed hall or another fighter’s Domain starves it
The charge is small and always there for anyone who knows it: a whole room blinks at once before he crosses, he watches for a full minute before he breaks a doom, his breath stops for three heartbeats before the needle, and small things fall when the Coinfall is set
The shadows near him deepen and the lamps seem to burn a little lower
Against a higher Stage it thins from the top down: a doom that a stronger power holds will not open for him, and the Domain serves the likelier man, so against a fighter above him he keeps it shut
HUSH, the Kingstep and the ground still work there, and they can let a man of seventy-seven lead a fighter two Stages over him by the nose
It is beaten by many eyes or none, a sense that does not blink, a stiff collar at the nape, standing still, and owning nothing loose; deny him the minute and he will not work at all
Tenebra fails where its idea does, since a soul hides only from what it has thought of, which the Measurewrights call aspect dependence: the coat is shaped against the angles he expects, and from the one he did not plan for he is brighter than anyone in the room; held too long it saturates, and everything it swallowed comes out at once
Oneirion fails by projection error, a read that was true on the map and lands nowhere in the room, which is what a held doom or a man in the middle of a real choice does to him
Ignivale fails by preignition, the hand that fires on a feeling before he has chosen, and it is the reason the needle stays in the sleeve until the breath has stopped
The Trait risks he carries: he does not sleep, which is Resonance Fatigue; he will not work blind even when it would save him, which is Rigidity; and breaking a doom without watching first is his Shear Break condition

Traits
BETWEEN BLINKS (瞬き · Mabataki) · Primary Trait
BETWEEN BLINKS is basically blind spot movement: the power to cross a room only in the moments when nobody’s eyes can see. It is the art used on eyes.
Capabilities
The eye is blind while it moves. Every time a man’s gaze jumps from one point to the next, a dozen times a breath, his brain stops taking in what he sees for that tenth of a breath and paints over the gap with what was there before, and every time he blinks the world goes dark for longer, and he never notices either. Scholars call the blind jump saccadic masking: the eye cannot see while it sweeps, so the mind cuts the smear out and fills the gap with the picture from before.
Raizan moves only in those gaps. The Tengan times every pair of eyes in a room, their jumps and their blinks, and his body crosses the floor in the spaces where nobody is looking, so that he is seen standing by the door and then seen standing by the bed and never seen walking between. A one-eyed man has more gaps on his dead side, and paints over all of them. The same reading works on bodies as on eyes: in a running crowd he walks through the gaps between people.
Applications

Crossing a watched room without being seen walking
Coming up on a one-eyed man from his dead side
Walking through a running crowd so that the crowd is always between him and whoever hunts him and never once in his own way

Associations

Tenebra is its lens, under the Tengan’s timing
The Spirit Path does the reading, with a studied Body’s feet

Limitations

Its limit is the number of eyes: one man’s gaps are many, three men’s gaps overlap less, and in a crowded hall the moments when every eye is blind at once are rare, short and far apart
It does nothing against a sense that does not blink: a beastkin’s nose, a hound’s ears, a blind fighter’s hearing
A fighter who reads heat can find him in a room hotter than his body, where an old man’s body is the one shape colder than the air; in the cold among a crowd of warm townsfolk the same sense loses him
It is constant and nearly costless, about half a percent of his reserve a minute while he is crossing ground
For anyone who knows it, a whole room blinking at once is the warning
It is beaten by many eyes or none: surround the target with watchers who look in different directions, or put the guard out of the light and let him listen

THE ONE STRAND (運命割り · Unmei-wari) · Secondary Trait
THE ONE STRAND is basically death foresight: the power to find the single moment when a man can be killed, and strike into it. The house and the Hall still call it Doom-Breaking, and it came of the first doom he broke.
Capabilities
The Tenrai read a man’s doom: the knot of all the ways his next hours could go, drawn tight round the likeliest. Raizan reads it and breaks it. He watches a target for a full minute without blinking himself, and in the knot he finds the one strand where the man dies, and the single moment when every other strand thins at once, when the guard’s eyes are on the door, the mail has ridden up, the dog has gone out, the luck has run.
That moment is real and very narrow: every way the man might live, laid out on Oneirion’s map in the space of what can be thought, thins at once to one strand for a breath. The Measurewrights liken it to the still point between two waves that cancel, crest meeting trough so that the water does not move, and call it destructive interference; it is a good picture, and they cannot say why a man’s likelihoods should behave like water. He strikes into it, and the knot collapses onto that strand. He has broken a great many. He can see the morning now, quite clearly.
The read is made on Oneirion’s map through the Core and pulls nothing down from Fate. What it spends is his own share, the way a vow does, which is why the price is taken out of his own mornings and why it is so much cheaper in reserve than a true pull. It works by putting an ordinary blow into a moment that was already there, so it moves nothing that had no way of happening.
Applications

Killing a man the Tengan said could not die that year
Choosing the moment for ONE NEEDLE
Reading how a bound man will answer, which is what FORCING STONE is thrown on

Associations

Oneirion is its lens
The Spirit Path makes the read, with the walked Fate Path’s small share behind it
Dominion Fate, which his Fate Path opened, is its gate
A cigarette often burns down for a clock while he watches; one lasts a little over a minute

Limitations

It needs the minute of watching, close enough to read, and he will not work without it
It cannot find the death-strand in a man whose futures are truly open, a man in the middle of a real choice
It cannot read a doom that a stronger fate-sight is already holding; a Kōkan Kamigan ranks above a Tenrai Tengan, and under that eye his reading blurs
It costs about eight percent of his reserve
It also costs something he cannot get back: every doom he breaks, the Tengan shows him his own last morning a little closer, as if a year of his own futures went into the gap with the other man’s
The tell is the watching itself: a full minute on one man, unblinking, the spokes of the Tengan turning in his irises
It is beaten by being unpredictable, by standing beside someone whose eye is stronger, or by never giving him the minute

TENGAN (Eye of Fate) · Inherited Trait
TENGAN is basically probability perception: the power to see which way things are likely to go. It is the Tenrai line’s sight, the Tenrai branch of the Moto heart-eye, and the eye the whole art runs on.
Capabilities
It shows probability pressure, convergence, and the near-future paths of bodies and blades as lines of light that lean the way things are likely to go. In him it is fifty years sharper than in any Tenrai alive. It has no lens. It spends his own share and pulls nothing down.
Applications

Timing every pair of eyes in a room for BETWEEN BLINKS
Ranking a man’s futures for THE ONE STRAND
Showing the foot where to go for the Kingstep
Telling him beforehand which man is the likelier, before he opens the Domain

Associations

The Tenrai blood
No lens

Limitations

It shows pressure and direction and never the hour
It shows likelihood: what will probably happen, and anything genuinely improbable surprises him like anyone else
It shows him what is likely to happen to himself as plainly as to anyone, and when there is nowhere better to step he pays the likely price
It costs nothing to keep open and it is always open, so he has not slept a full night since he was twenty
The spokes in his irises show it
It is beaten by a ward that returns or blurs a reading, Oblivara’s or a Tenebra veil of one’s own, or by the plain unlikely act

HUSH (静寂 · Shijima) · Passive Trait
HUSH is basically presence concealment: the power to be quieter than the room he stands in. It is the art used on a room’s noise.
Capabilities
Tenebra parts him from the room’s notice and keeps him quieter than it: his footfalls absorbed, his scent thin, his Essence quieter than the lamps. Dogs do not bark at him; horses do not shy.
It hides the record as well as the man. A Reigan that reads the count of the dead in a chest found in his a gray quiet, a Tenrai of the Hall with a count of none, and in a town of carters and fishwives his chest read exactly like theirs. Tenebra thins in a crowd, but a veiled chest among two hundred empty ones needs no shadow.
Applications

Passing dogs, horses and guards without notice
Hiding the count of his dead from an eye that reads souls
Passing for one of the townsfolk in a crowd

Associations

Tenebra is its lens
The Spirit Path lays the hush over what he is, with a studied Body’s small share for footfall and scent

Limitations

Its limit is Tenebra’s own failure: it is shaped against the angles he expects, and from the one he did not plan for he is as bright as anyone, brighter, a figure suddenly sharp in the corner of a mirror or the eye of a second watcher behind the first
It costs nothing, and it is always on
Its tell is that dogs do not bark
It is beaten by the one angle he did not plan for

Techniques
ONE NEEDLE (一本針 · Ippon-bari) · Signature Technique
ONE NEEDLE is basically a one-hit kill: the power to end a man with a single thrust where the skull meets the neck. It is the art used on a skull, and the reason the north’s lords have worn high collars for fifty years.
Capabilities
A single thrust with the Last Thread, a needle-blade the length of a hand, up through the soft gap between the base of the skull and the first bone of the neck, the atlas, into the brainstem. The brainstem is the stalk that joins brain to spine and keeps breath and heartbeat going, so a point that reaches it stops both at once. Death is instant and almost bloodless, a single bead of blood at the nape for the physicians to miss.
Under it is the oldest habit of points: a thumb pushed against mail does nothing, and the same push behind a point finer than a surgeon’s needle is more than a steel ring or a plate of bone can bear. The force behind it is small, and the point is so fine that at its tip it goes through mail rings and leather and bone as if they were cloth; the Measurewrights call it pressure, force divided by the area it lands on. Ignivale, the spark that closes the gap between wanting and doing, puts the thrust in the hand before the shoulder has moved. He does not raise his voice for it.
Applications

Killing through mail rings, leather and bone at the nape
Killing so cleanly that a physician finds nothing

Associations

Ignivale is its lens
A studied Body Path gives the one honest thrust, aimed by the Spirit read
The Last Thread carries it
Mastered, in the Tenrai war-schools and fifty years of contracts

Limitations

It needs the nape bare or soft: a stiff high collar of boiled leather, a mail gorget at the back of the neck, or a back to a wall denies it
The steel is a limit too: a point that fine holds almost no heat of its own, and pushed through air at forge heat it passes the color where its temper lives and goes soft, so that on bone a hair above the gap it goes in a thumb’s depth and curls
It costs about 0.4 percent of his reserve, almost all of it spent keeping the point perfectly true
His breath stops for three heartbeats before the thrust
Before, guard the nape with a stiff high collar or a mail gorget
During, a turn of the head a finger’s breadth sends the needle off the gap and into bone, where it skids
After, he is an old man with an empty hand standing behind you, and he has never once been there long

FORCING STONE (利かし · Kikashi) · Technique
FORCING STONE is basically provocation: the power to make a standing man move, with a pebble. Kikashi is the go player’s word for a move that must be answered.
Capabilities
It is a go stone, slate or shell, flicked from the thumb at a cheekbone, a temple, the point of the jaw, with about enough behind it to crack a walnut. There is no working in it. He throws it only at a fighter whose answer he has already read: a man bound by law, vow, temper or pride to answer whatever lands on him.
The stone lands, the answer comes, and a man who has been made to move has somewhere to step to, so the Kingstep works again on a fighter who had beaten it by standing still. Each stone is a step and a palmful is a road, every answer passing through the air where an old man had just been.
Applications

Breaking a fighter out of standing still
Leading a stronger fighter across ground, a stone at a time

Associations

No lens and no working; the stone is aimed by the minute’s read
The Kingstep, which it opens the way for
His traveling go set, slate and shell

Limitations

It takes no reserve at all
Its price is that every stone is a blow landed and every answer is a real one, thrown with everything the other fighter has at a body one honest blow would kill
Against a fighter who banks what he is dealt, each stone is a coin in the other man’s purse
A hand going to the go stones gives it away
It is beaten by owing a pebble nothing: a fighter free to ignore it stands still, and the old man is out of moves

KINGSTEP OF THE WINNING THREAD (王歩 · Ōho) · School Art, Tenrai
KINGSTEP OF THE WINNING THREAD is basically predictive evasion: the power to put his foot where the other fighter was about to step. It is the Tenrai movement form, taught in the Tenrai war-schools, and the art used on a step.
Capabilities
The Tengan shows where an opponent will step, and the Kingstep puts the foot there first. In his feet it is one pace back and one to the right, the right heel carried off the floor even when he sits, and the foot comes down where nothing is going to be.
Applications

Keeping an old body out of the way of every blow
Standing where the answer is not

Associations

No lens, the Tengan alone
The Spirit Path for the read, a studied Body for the foot
A Tenrai school art, mastered

Limitations

It needs the other fighter to move: a blow, a rush, a step, anything with somewhere to go
It costs nothing beyond the open eye
Its tell is that his steps land where the other man’s next step would have gone
Standing still beats it, because that leaves nowhere to step to, and every Kurenai child is taught that answer at the same table as the oath

RUINOUS COINFALL (銭落とし · Zeni-otoshi) · School Art, Tenrai
RUINOUS COINFALL is basically probability manipulation: the power to tip one small chance at the moment it most matters. It is a Tenrai school art, and the one thing in his kit that reaches above his own share.
Capabilities
The lamp that falls, the coin that rolls, the latch that slips. It is a true pull on Fate, and at Fate II it brings down one thread for one thing that was already on its way: a latch already worn, a lamp already badly hung.
Applications

Slipping a worn latch
Dropping a badly hung lamp

Associations

The walked Fate Path, and Dominion Fate as its gate
Tenrai blood and fifty years of tipping small chances, with no Work behind it; blood without a Work is no grip, so his Fate stops at II
No lens stated

Limitations

It moves nothing sound
A single lean takes about half his reserve and has to be set beforehand, which is why he has used it rarely and why it never passed Drilled
Small things falling in the room give it away
It is beaten by owning nothing loose

Releases
KAMIKAKUSHI (神隠し · Spirited Away) · First Release
KAMIKAKUSHI is basically imperceptibility: the power to drop out of every sense in the field at once. It is the old word for a person the gods have taken, who is there and then is not, and the folk call it the Vanishing.
Capabilities
His aura drops below sight altogether, HUSH and BETWEEN BLINKS go as far as his Spirit III will carry them, and for as long as it holds there are no gaps he cannot use and no angle he forgot: even the second watcher sees nothing.
As a Spirit release it changes the reach of the line he already casts. The hush that lay over one old man is laid over every sense in the field at once, so that body heat, scent and footfall sink into the room’s own, and BETWEEN BLINKS can run on a hundred pairs of eyes and find in all their overlapping darks one gap wide enough to step through.
Applications

Crossing a hall full of watchers
Beating the second watcher and the angle he forgot

Techniques

Called - a single soft word in the old court tongue, for the full rise
Silent - weaker; it leaves his shadow behind for a heartbeat when he moves

Associations

Tenebra, at the top of what HUSH can do
The Last Thread carries its hush; taken from him, the First Release still hides him, but the needle that was the point of hiding is gone

Limitations

It lasts about four minutes from full
Everything the hush has is spent hiding the body, and nothing is left over the record: while it holds, a soul-reading eye at a finger’s distance reads his chest plainly, every killing in it
It hides him from watchers, never from what he owes: a working tagged to his own soul finds him wherever he stands
A hand laid flat on him breaks it
When it ends, the coat lets go of everything it swallowed at once, which is Tenebra’s saturation; he is spent and shaking, an old man again, and the shake is the window

HITSUZEN (必然 · Inevitability) · Second Release
HITSUZEN the Release is basically domain creation: the power to open his Domain and keep it standing. It opens and powers the Domain.
Capabilities
The held note is silence, deeper than the room’s. Called, it is one quiet word and the field forms as it is named.
Techniques

Called - one quiet word, and the field forms as it is named, out to forty yards
Silent - the field comes in at half the reach

Associations

A Spirit Release, the lead Path’s Second; because he walks Fate, the Domain it opens makes a Fate claim
The Domain of the same name, which it opens and powers

Limitations

Silent, it gives half the reach
What it opens is blind to whose side the odds are on

Domain
HITSUZEN (必然 · Inevitability) · Domain
HITSUZEN is basically luck negation: the power to make the likeliest thing happen every time, for everyone inside the line. It is his one idea at its largest: where BETWEEN BLINKS uses the gap nobody watches, the Domain leaves no gaps at all.
Capabilities
Opened by the Second Release out to forty yards, it presses every future in the field toward the most probable one: no lucky dodge, no blade that turns on a buckle by chance, no miracle. Whatever the odds favor, the odds deliver.
Called in the old court tongue, no louder than his speaking voice, it forms as it is named. Nothing in the room changes to the eye, and the held note is a silence deeper than the room’s. Like every Domain it is a claim laid on the ground and pulls no thread: it adds no force to anything and moves nothing that had no way of happening. It only strips the long chances out, the way a long night of dice would look if no throw ever ran against the odds.
Applications

Stripping the lucky dodge, the turned blade and the miracle out of a fight he is already likelier to win

Associations

Oneirion is its lens
Opened by a Spirit Second Release, its claim made on Fate because he walks Fate: a claim on conditions, authored in the Core, with Dominion Fate as its gate
The Second Release, which opens and powers it
The Tengan, which tells him beforehand which man is the likelier, the only reason he has ever dared open it

Limitations

It serves him only while he is the likelier man
It is blind to whose side the odds are on, and it makes a stronger enemy surer of winning
Its upkeep is paid at his Core’s rate, and it lasts about two minutes from a full reserve
It reaches forty yards, and half that when opened silent
It is beaten by being the likelier side outright, by stepping out of the forty yards, or by making one truly free choice inside it, an act no reading could have leaned toward, which the field cannot press because it has no weight to press

characters/ability-accounts/rob-stark-—-.title: Rob Stark — Abilities in full
characters/ability-accounts/rob-stark-—-.content:
Card: Rob Stark
HE’S ALL OF OURS
HE’S ALL OF OURS is basically guardianship: the power to be standing in front of whoever he has claimed as his. It is a Trait-art, one idea, and he had it before he had anything else, because his soul stood guard before it did anything else.
Capabilities
Two winters in the Lanternless he stood where the Sarge could not see behind himself, and fetched him for Ulf, and locked the door and stood outside it, and when Ulf asked if the boy was one of his, Rob said he was all of theirs. Everything he has is that one sentence said again in a different part of him. The claim puts his body in front of his people, the quiet keeps his pain from frightening them, the cold nails his boots to the ground in front of them, and the Wall is all three done at once over somebody who has fallen.
Applications

Putting his body in front of his people
Keeping his pain from frightening them
Nailing his boots to the ground in front of them

Techniques

HE’S ALL OF OURS - the Primary Trait: the claim, and the step across that needs no choosing
DIDN’T SCREAM - the Secondary Trait: pain that reaches him late and is shown only when he chooses
STARK RIME - the Inherited Trait: the Stark cold, which sets his boots to the ground
THE WALL OF ONE! - the Signature Technique: the body planted over whoever is down, feet frozen to one line

Associations

The Body Path, in the Form of a Shape
The Stark cold, the house’s inheritance and no Wellspring, is the lens the art works through
The Sarge, the Sarge’s sister and a boy who could not hold his own spear, the ones the company knew he had claimed
His aura is the Stark cold, a gray with frost at its edges that whitens his beard when he is angry

Limitations

He has one body, and it cannot be in front of two people who are standing apart
Whatever was meant for his people lands on him

Traits
HE’S ALL OF OURS · Primary Trait
HE’S ALL OF OURS is basically protective instinct: the power to be between his people and a blow before he has thought about it. Claiming is a thing he decides, slowly, and he does not undecide it.
Capabilities
While someone he has claimed is in reach, his Fortitude and Reflex read a step high on the hidden scale and his body is between them and the blow before he has thought about it. That last part is the real trick, and it is an ordinary one made into law. A man who has to choose what to do about a spear takes a good deal longer than a man who flinches, because the flinch never goes up to the part of the head that weighs things; it goes in at the eye and straight out at the legs. His Shell (the body-side layer of the soul) has taken the choosing out of it: for his own people the step across is a flinch.
The quarter of his practice he has spent studying Fate opens no gate and gives him one small use, which is this: a claim is a bond, and he knows without looking where the ones he has claimed are standing.
Applications

Stepping in front of a blow meant for one of his
Being a step harder to put down and a step quicker while one of his is in reach
Knowing without looking where his people are standing

Associations

His Shell, which has made the step a flinch
Fate, studied for a quarter of his practice, which gives the sense of where his people are and nothing more
Two winters a pace behind the Sarge, where standing over someone was learned

Limitations

Reach: he can guard only what he can step across, one long stride of a big man
He cannot be in front of two people who are standing apart
It takes nothing from his reserve, because nothing is being made or thrown; whatever was meant for them lands on him
Its tell is where he stands: a pace behind and to the left of the one he has claimed, on the side a right-handed man cannot see or cover
It is beaten by getting past whoever he is guarding first, or by making him pick: go for two of his at once and he has one body

DIDN’T SCREAM · Secondary Trait
DIDN’T SCREAM is basically pain suppression: the power to feel a wound late and choose when to show it. The cub bit him above the knee on the Vessant road and he did not scream; Yukazuri opened the rotten bite on a wagon tailboard with spirit and a knife, and he bit a strap and did not make a sound.
Capabilities
A hard fight does a little of this for anyone. Fear and effort make the body dull its own hurts for a while, which the surgeons call hypoalgesia, less pain from the same wound, and it is why a soldier finds the cut after the fighting. In Rob the soul holds that door shut on purpose and for longer, so that on the road the leg was bleeding into his boot and he had not yet noticed. A bite to the bone gets a groan through shut teeth and another swing of the axe.
Applications

Keeping on hitting through a wound and noticing the blood later
Keeping his pain from frightening the people behind him

Associations

Yukazuri Moto, the little surgeon, who opened the bite and later closed the cut on his leg
HE’S ALL OF OURS, since it holds only while he has somebody to stand in front of

Limitations

It holds the voice, not the body: the leg still goes bad, the lung still fills, and a wound he has not felt is a wound he has not bound
It needs him braced for it: fighting, it holds; lying still and safe with nobody to stand in front of, it lets go
At the Foot, when she closed the cut on his leg, he screamed at her and cursed her and then slept, and he never forgave himself the scream
It costs nothing
Its tell is the jaw: teeth shut on a strap, or on nothing, and a long grinding groan where another man would yell
Nobody found a counter to it in a fight, and he kept it to the end

STARK RIME · Inherited Trait
STARK RIME is basically cold manipulation: the power to move heat out of himself and down into the ground. The cold in the Stark blood is an inheritance of the house and no Wellspring, and in Rob it runs plain and strong.
Capabilities
It does one thing, the one rule the Stark blood has, which is that it moves heat out and never in. In him it shows as frost in his beard when he is angry, and the heat going down through his heels into the ground. When he sets it on purpose he pulls Aether (mana) up out of the ground he is standing on, packs it raw in his Shell as Charge, and sets the rime down through his legs. Two parts in five of what he spends reaches the world, which is his yield, and the rest is paid in the body as the hard breathing through his nose that is the only sound he makes.
What the rime does is the oldest thing frost does to a fence post. Wet ground that freezes turns from mud to something near mortar, and whatever is standing in it when it freezes is set there.
Applications

Freezing the damp under his soles and in the cracks between the stones to the leather of his boots
Sending the heat he pours out through his heels down into the ground

Associations

The Stark blood, the house’s inheritance
THE WALL OF ONE!, the stance it sets

Limitations
