Heat always runs from the warm thing to the cold one, and the cold cannot make any
On ground already frozen iron-hard there is no wet left for it to set and it grips less
Against a real fire it is a bucket against a furnace
Three parts in five of what he spends on it are lost
Its tell is frost in his beard
It is beaten by heat, and by calm: a Stark who is not angry is only a cold man

Techniques
THE WALL OF ONE! · Signature Technique
THE WALL OF ONE! is basically immovability: the power to plant himself over someone who has fallen so that nothing gets through him while he stands. It is the third move of HE’S ALL OF OURS, and it was the last thing he did.
Capabilities
He steps across, not aside: the big body planted over whoever is down, axe up, limewood shield up. The visible charge is the step itself and what the ground does under it, as he sets the rime down through his legs.
A man who is knocked over is nearly always a man whose feet went first. With his feet set, a blow on the shield has nowhere to push him: it goes down through the arm, the hips and the long bones of the legs into ground that will not give, and the heat he is pouring out through his heels goes down the same road. A shield wall works because each man is braced by the men at his shoulders; he has nobody at his shoulders, so he is braced by the ground.
Applications

Holding one line over a fallen man
Taking a blow on the shield without giving a step

Associations

HE’S ALL OF OURS, DIDN’T SCREAM and STARK RIME, all three done at once
The bearded axe and the limewood shield, which are what he fights with when someone is down behind him
He came by it living
The boy with the red ears, whom he stepped across

Limitations

A wall faces one way: his feet are frozen to the line he chose, and it holds one line against one blade at a time
To turn he has to break his own frost first
Setting the rime and holding the stance takes about five percent of his reserve, and it holds as long as he does
Its tells are the step across, his breath no longer steaming, his beard going white, and frost running out from his boot soles across the snow or the cobbles in a pale ring a stride wide
It is beaten by more than one blade, or by one from the side he is not facing: low, under the right arm, where the mail gaps at the armpit and the shield is not

characters/ability-accounts/shōki-kurena.title: Shōki Kurenai Moto — Abilities in full
characters/ability-accounts/shōki-kurena.content:
Card: Shōki Kurenai Moto · The Sin of Wrath
THE BOOK THAT WILL NOT CLOSE
THE BOOK THAT WILL NOT CLOSE (未済の帳 · Misai no Chō) is basically revenge empowerment: the power to keep everything done to him as fire with the doer’s name on it, and to pay every bit of it back. It is his signature art, and his Traits, techniques, releases and Domain are this one idea at different sizes. The eye it reads by is the Kurenai blood’s and the closing stroke is the Moto house’s; everything else is his.
Capabilities
A headsman closes the register. That was his whole trade for twenty-two years: the verdict kills, the hand ends it, and the book shuts on the name. At the block the Hall made him the thing the book was shut on, and his soul answered with the one sentence it has held ever since, that what is done to him is never finished. The art is that sentence worked out at every size. A blow is an entry, so he takes it in. An entry has an author, so he keeps it under a name. A debtor has a record, so he reads it. An account comes due, so he pays it into the body of whoever owes it. The ink never dries, so heat leaks off him day and night. That is the whole ladder: the idea, the transformed body, the world obeying it.
It starts where every practitioner starts. He pulls Aether (mana, in the common word) out of the ground he stands on, packs it raw in his Shell as Charge, shapes it there by his Wellsprings’ lenses and drives it out unrefined, the Body’s way. His Shell is the corrupted kind the ladder-keepers call Rot-Born, which amplifies every working and corrodes a little with each one. Of everything he spends, seventy-one parts in a hundred reach the thing he means them for, which is his yield. The other twenty-nine burn in the furnace of his Shell and leave him as heat, which is poor for a Grandmaster, and that share is no side matter: it is the oven he lives in, and at full output the Measurewrights reckon it in terawatts.
Four Wellsprings shape it, and each does one job. Tarturon, the Fire of Reckoning, is the payment: the idea of reckoning, a fire that burns on what is owed and that nothing can smother once it is lit, so the same touch burns a butcher to the bone and only scorches a child. Exuroth, the Trial Flame, is the trial by fire, burned and plunged and burned again, and three centuries of it have set his Shell hard enough to carry loads that would shatter another vessel. Vantabriel, the Night, is the keeping, the night that puts nothing down: what strikes him does not fade. Ignivale, the Spark, is the smallest beginning that pays for itself, so in him the gap between wanting and burning is a hair wide. It rides a blow plainly, and both damages are real. The cuff is nine kilograms of black iron on the end of an arm that strikes at the top of what a body can deliver, and that lands first, as bone and crater. The fire goes in with it: Tarturon seeds the fire in whatever the iron touched, the count sets how hot it burns, and the account pours in after if he chooses to spend it.
Applications

Taking a blow as heat, and sealing the wound it opens
Keeping each blow under the name of whoever threw it, and paying it back to that one person
Counting the killings a person carries, and burning them by that count
Setting a fire inside a body or its kit that needs no air
Breaking steel, stone or bone with two touches and a blow
Closing a fight inside an oven that no heat can leave

Techniques

ENSHŌ - the entry: a blow that lands is taken in as heat
ONNEN - the keeping: the heat is banked under the name of whoever dealt it
TSUMI-YOMI - the reading: the count of a debtor’s killings
SHŌNETSU - the ink that never dries: the heat that leaks off him day and night
HAKANASHI - the sentence itself, the two Traits fused into one law
GŌKA - the payment, made by the fist into the body of whoever owes it
YAKI-IRE - the quench, in his palm, on someone else’s steel
SENTENCE OF SEVERANCE - the Moto house’s closing stroke
THE HELL FIRE - the kept heat of the Register standing up as fire
TATAMI-ABI - the whole oven folded down to one point
SHAKUNETSU - the First Release, the open book worn as a skin
ABI - the Second Release and the Domain, a field where nothing spent is allowed to leave
ENMA-CHŌ - the Third Release, the Hall itself on the morning of the sentence, with him holding the pen

Associations

Tarturon, the Fire of Reckoning, a Wellspring of Fate, is the payment
Exuroth, the Trial Flame, is the quench and the temper
Vantabriel, the Night, taken at the block, is the keeping, and gives his aura its black-violet rim
Ignivale, the Spark, is the low barrier between wanting and burning
The Body Path does the work; his Walked Fate Path carries the name on each debt, the weight the fire burns by, and the Domain’s claim
The Kurenai blood gives the eye, which has no Wellspring
The Moto house gives the closing stroke
The Hall Irons, his bonded weapon, which are also what he hits with
The headsman’s trade, twenty-two years of closing the register

Limitations

He can put nothing down: the fever never breaks, he does not sleep a full night, he cannot forgive, and a long fight he does not finish cooks him from the inside
Twenty-nine parts in a hundred of every spend burn in his Shell’s furnace and leave him as heat
Hot ground fills him faster and cold, wet ground slower, and his Rot-Born Shell corrodes a little with every working
Anyone who knows it sees the charge: at rest the air shimmers and frost dies in a ring around him, and when he means it he breathes in like a bellows, the Covenant Scar flares black-violet through his shirt and the Hall Irons go from blue-black to white
The amber-red of his aura brightens to an overdriven filament with its dark rim thickening on the side of whoever owes him most, and the roar of a blast furnace stands under everything he does, with iron ringing in it
It is beaten by cold and water, by harm that carries no force, by a chest with no killing in it, by one small blow from the side to drag him off his target, or by a crew that loads the bank past its quarter line on purpose
Tarturon fails as runaway: a reckoning has no end it can recognize, every burning adds to what is owed, and his anger has the same shape, so a heavy enough record fires him before he has chosen and he wastes himself on the first butcher in the room
Exuroth fails as quench cracking, the Measurewrights’ name for a trial that cannot tell an ordeal from a ruin: burned and plunged for three centuries without rest, he is loaded like a drop of tempered glass, and cold water on hot skin shatters the glaze
Vantabriel fails as saturation: the night keeps everything and puts none of it down, the bank holds a quarter of his reserve above his maximum, and past that line the excess goes into the soul that holds it
Ignivale fails as preignition, the working that goes off on a feeling

Traits
He carries three Trait risks. Resonance Fatigue is the fever after every fight, days long. Rigidity is absolute, every blow answered. His Shear Break condition is one sustained outward look, Asami, held.
ENSHŌ (炎症 · Inflammation) · Primary Trait
ENSHŌ is basically kinetic absorption: the power to take a blow as heat instead of as harm. He was the hot child of a cold line, and his soul did this before it ever tried; it is older than any of his Wellsprings.
Capabilities
A blow is an entry, and his soul took every entry in long before it learned the word: what lands on him is kept, and nothing of it is given back. So a blow neither rebounds nor tears. The whole of it stops in the tissue under it and becomes heat, the way a dead-blow hammer, filled with loose shot, swallows its own recoil. The Measurewrights measure how much of a collision comes back as bounce and call it restitution, a dropped ball of glass returning nearly all of it and a ball of wet clay none; they say his Shell drives it toward nothing, call what is left a perfectly inelastic collision, and point out that a struck anvil warms. Their figure for the heat is good, and they have no idea why a soul should refuse to give a blow back.
The spot flushes, swells, burns and hurts, the four old signs of inflammation all at once, and the heat cauterizes the wound as it opens, so a cut that would bleed a man white closes in a hiss. The heat stays in him and does not radiate, and Exuroth’s trial-hardened Shell and his Tolerance let him carry it. Vantabriel then keeps it and the Reigan signs it.
Applications

Walking into a blow, letting it land, and being hotter than he was
Closing a cut as it opens
Swallowing the heat YAKI-IRE’s second touch pulls out of a thing
Feeding the grudge bank

Associations

The Body Path, shaping what strikes him
His own soul’s first habit, carried on Exuroth’s trial-hardened Shell
His Tolerance, which lets him hold the heat
ONNEN, which keeps what it swallows
SHAKUNETSU, under which it strikes as hard as his Body IV will carry it, and ENMA-CHŌ, inside which it becomes local law

Limitations

It acts only on harm that arrives as force or heat; cold, poison, starvation of air, soul-work and Nihiloth negation pass straight through it
It banks the force of a blow and cannot bank its timing, so a palm timed to the beat of his heart can stop it; Ignivale firing into his own chest starts it again
Whatever does not strike as force goes past it entirely: a note can open the old crack at his nape along the line of the block, and a cut that carries no weight gives it nothing to drink
Its cost is thermal debt, as the Measurewrights call it: everything he keeps is owed back out, and if he cannot spend it or vent it, it leaves through the nearest organ, so a long fight he does not finish cooks him from inside, and he drinks like a horse after every one
It shows: struck flesh glows cherry-red and steams, and his blood hisses where another man’s would run
Cold beats it: water, ice and saturated cold ground pull the banked heat out of the struck tissue faster than the Trait can hold it
A fighter who never trades blows and bleeds him by attrition with things that carry no force gives it nothing to eat
Running water is the worst of it: the skin of steam that lets water ride on a very hot surface holds until the current tears it away, then the flood boils against him and pulls the tissue heat out, the glaze of his First Release shatters, and he bleeds without a hiss

ONNEN (怨念 · Grudge) · Secondary Trait
ONNEN is basically damage banking: the power to keep every blow he swallows under the name of whoever threw it, and to pay it back to that one person, all at once. It was forged at the block.
Capabilities
What ENSHŌ swallows, ONNEN keeps. Vantabriel is the night that keeps, enduring by carrying everything that was lost with none of it put down, and its operation is coagulation: what is taken is fixed in the soul and never given back. In him nothing is ever put down. The Measurewrights call it hysteresis, a thing whose present state is the sum of its past, as iron stays magnetized when the lodestone is gone, and they time how long such a thing takes to let go; in him it never does. So the heat does not decay, and his Reigan tags each portion with the soul that dealt it, which makes the bank a ledger of who owes what. It is always on and it never forgets; every insult that lands as force is entered.
He can spend a portion only against its author, where Tarturon burns it by the moral weight of the debt and it burns with the force of the original blow returned. The bank sits in Vantabriel’s keeping and not in his flesh, so cold that takes every bit of heat his tissue holds leaves the blows entered in the bank untouched. The name on a portion is a bond, and a bond finds its owner: a man hidden from every eye is found by the rim of the aura leaning toward him, because he can hide from watchers and not from what he owes.
Applications

Holding up to a quarter of his maximum reserve above that maximum, 82,663,922 EU
Pouring a debtor’s whole account into GŌKA
Finding a hidden man by the lean of the aura’s rim
Banking from every hostile act in the field inside ABI, regardless of whom it struck
Fueling THE HELL FIRE, which burns on what the man in front of him owes

Associations

Vantabriel, the Night, for the keeping, and Tarturon for the spending
The Body Path for the heat kept, with his Walked Fate Path’s share for the name on it
The Reigan, which signs each portion
ENSHŌ, which fills it

Limitations

A portion can be spent only against the one who dealt it
A full bank is fever: it runs him at a heat that would kill a man and makes him sleepless
Past a quarter the excess has nowhere to go but into the structure holding it, which is a Crystal Fracture Event
It shows as the black-violet rim of his aura thickening toward whoever has hurt him
Give him nothing to bank: strike from range with harm he cannot turn to heat, or never strike him at all
Or overfeed him on purpose, several fighters loading him with more than he can spend, until the bank saturates and the overflow cracks his own lattice; it works, and until it works every blow is a coin in his purse
A Catharsis or Lethegraal practitioner who can lay hands on him can hurry the bank into settling and drain it, which he will kill to prevent

TSUMI-YOMI (罪読み · Sin-Reading) · Inherited Trait
TSUMI-YOMI is basically sin detection: the power to look at a breastbone and count everyone that person has ever killed. It is the Kurenai branch of the Moto heart-eye, the Reigan, hardened in him into a Trait.
Capabilities
The Kurenai Reigan reads curse anatomy and soul structure, and in the line’s headsmen it reads the record every killing leaves in the Attraction Layer, scar on scar, the way fired clay keeps the dose it has absorbed. He cannot look at a chest without counting what it holds, and the count is the moral weight his Tarturon fire burns by. A target with a long record takes GŌKA at full; a target who has never killed takes it at its base and no more.
The count comes to him as a number and he says it aloud, and calls the person by it. He can read a count out one entry at a time, with the place and the year of each. He reads by sight of the chest, and his heat-sense is a separate thing that the eye does not need.
Applications

Setting how hot his fire burns on a given person
Reading a count aloud, entry by entry, with the place and the year of each
Giving SENTENCE OF SEVERANCE its judgment, already made

Associations

The Kurenai blood’s inheritance, with no Wellspring; the blood gives the eye and a grip on the Work, and never a Path
It reads the Attraction Layer and pulls nothing down
Tarturon, which burns by the count
Ignivale, whose low barrier lets a heavy count fire him

Limitations

It reads only what has been done, never what is about to be done, and it reads the dead as nothing
He cannot stop reading, and a record heavy enough fires his heat before he chooses, which is how he wastes himself on the first butcher in a room while the real threat walks behind him
It shows as ring-lines and red capillary light in the left eye, with his gaze on the breastbone
A soul with no killing in it leaves him counting nothing and burning at base
So does any ward that returns or quiets a reading, Oblivara’s retroreflection or a Tenebra veil
A Tenebra hush holds only while its holder spends it on the record; spent on hiding the body instead, the record comes through plain

SHŌNETSU (焦熱 · Scorching Heat) · Passive Trait
SHŌNETSU is basically heat radiation: the power, which he cannot switch off, to make any place he stands into a forge. The Hell of Scorching Heat is where he lives, carried with him.
Capabilities
It is his furnace burning in the open and his bank’s leakage together, with no lens of its own. At rest he sheds as much heat as a smithy forge in full blast, so snow will not lie within ten yards of him, frost melts off the ground he crosses, iron in a room with him grows too hot to hold bare, and the untrained sweat, then sicken, then go down with heat-stroke inside the hour. Fighting at full output twenty-nine parts in a hundred of everything he spends burn off him, terawatts in the burst by the Measurewrights’ reckoning, and the yard turns to an oven, the air shimmering, wood scorching black, stone spalling.
It has a worse face. Let go on purpose and without flame, the heat goes out of him as a bruise-colored haze with the rage riding in it, and in every body it reaches the blood answers it the way blood answers a wound, everywhere at once: a fever that will not break, flesh swelling and burning, glaze-crack lines rising on the skin, the body’s own defense turned on the body. It goes from house to house; a Kharven border village on the western shield died of it, all but one girl in the last house past the bridge and a white-eared dog.
Applications

Turning a room into a forge and a yard into an oven
Sensing who is near by their warmth
Killing without flame, house by house

Techniques

Heat-sense - he feels warm bodies the way other men see lamps, and in a room hot as a kiln a veiled body shows as the one shape colder than the air; a warm crowd blinds it
The fever-storm - the physicians’ name for the heat let go on purpose as a bruise-colored haze, which turns every body it reaches against itself

Associations

The Body Path, unshaped
No lens of its own: it is the furnace of all four Wellsprings, burning in the open, and the leakage of the bank

Limitations

It costs him concealment and company: he cannot hide from anyone who can feel heat, he cannot be near anything he wants to keep, and he cannot be silent the way the Kurenai walk
It shows wherever he goes: snow will not lie within ten yards of him
A warm crowd blinds the heat-sense
Distance beats the forge and the fever-storm alike, and so does cold, wet ground that drinks the heat
Practitioners with Tolerance or Abython’s equalization stand in it unharmed
A fight on a frozen lake or in a winter river runs on terms he hates

HAKANASHI (墓無し · The Unburied) · Compound Trait, ENSHŌ and ONNEN
HAKANASHI is basically unfinishable existence: the power, and the curse, that nothing done to him can be finished, his death included. It is ENSHŌ and ONNEN fused into one law.
Capabilities
At the block he went into Asami and looked inward instead of out, the Shallow-Seen Unburied the Moto scholars refused to name, and then, at Gisei, he burned the bond to his wife for the fuel to break the irons. The two Traits fused into one law in that moment, the sentence he held as she died: what is done to me is never finished. Under that law ENSHŌ and ONNEN no longer switch off, Obsession Force has the whole of him, and the Crystal’s Overgrowth has made his body the shape of the law, which is why the Church files a Moto beside the First Eon’s demons.
The law reaches further than blows. A death is a thing done to him, so it cannot finish: the Hall could not execute him, thirteen Kurenai could not, and a blade he turns on himself is a blow he must answer first, which has ended every attempt. A lost limb is unfinished too. A stump driven into the floor of his own Register is rebuilt by the kept heat from the bud outward, the way a salamander regrows a leg.
Applications

Answering every blow that lands
Outliving execution, thirteen Kurenai, and his own hand
Regrowing a lost limb from kept heat, inside his Register

Associations

His Walked Fate Path, binding two Body Traits
No Wellspring: it is the law of his own Core, held by Obsession Force
ENSHŌ and ONNEN, which it keeps from ever switching off
ENMA-CHŌ, whose floor the stump is driven into

Limitations

It is the Rigidity Effect at its absolute: he must answer every blow that lands, from anyone, before he does anything else
He cannot forgive anything, because forgiveness would discharge the whole bank at once into his own structure
Regrowing a limb costs the last of his reserve, a spike of fever and a lung filling with blood
It shows in that he answers every blow
That rigidity is the counter: a fighter who lands something small on him from the side pulls his answer off whoever he was killing, and a crew can drag him by the nose across a field this way while his clock runs
The law can shear: true Asami looks outward, and anything that could turn his eyes outward and hold them there long enough would leave the Unburied nothing to grip

Techniques
GŌKA (業火 · Karmic Fire) · Signature Technique
GŌKA is basically sin burning: the power to set a fire inside whatever his fist touches that burns without air, on the weight of the target’s own dead. It is the payment, the account coming due.
Capabilities
He breathes in like a bellows, the Covenant Scar on his chest flares black-violet, the Hall Irons go white, and he puts a fist on the target. On contact Tarturon seeds a fire in the struck body or kit, and it is the fire of reckoning: it burns on what is owed, the soul’s own calcination turned outward, and a fire that burns on a debt asks nothing of the air. It burns at about two and a half thousand degrees under water or under sand and cannot be smothered, since water only turns to steam and bursts, and because every burning adds to what is owed it runs away until the fuel is gone. The Measurewrights liken it to a smith’s thermite, a metal and a metal’s rust ground together so the powder holds both the fuel and the air, and they are right about the heat and wrong about why it will not go out.
Against a target with a long record read by TSUMI-YOMI he may pour that target’s whole ONNEN account into the same blow, as high as his Stage lets any working of his climb. Poured in whole, on a long count with a full account behind it, it boils a man’s blood in every vessel he has. Against a soul with no killing in it, it runs at base and nothing more. At base it lands at SS, a blow the Measurewrights put at about six and a half kilotons, and with a full bank behind it near twenty-one.
Applications

Burning a body or its kit from the inside, under water or sand
Paying a debtor’s whole account back in one blow
Boiling a man’s blood on a long count

Associations

Tarturon, the Fire of Reckoning
The Body Path, by contact, with his Walked Fate Path’s share for the weight it burns by
TSUMI-YOMI, which sets the count, and ONNEN, which holds the account
YAKI-IRE, whose second touch can drink its heat home again

Limitations

It needs contact; the fire is placed, never thrown
The bellows breath needs a sound chest and a clear beat: with a lung torn and a forehead in his face, a full Karmic Fire goes into the floor
At base it costs about twelve percent of his reserve
Past the reserve it costs the rage itself: the bank spent is gone, and for one turn after he is cooler and slower than he can stand
The bellows breath, the flaring scar and the white irons are a full beat of warning
Before it lands, stepping out of reach or putting anything in the way that he will hit first spends the working on the wrong thing
While it burns, the fire lives in what was struck, so shedding the struck pauldron or cutting out the burning flesh ends it, ugly as that is
Afterward, the cool turn that follows is the window, and every crew that has ever hurt him took it there
The fuel is the price paid in, and the working has a seam where the fire meets the law that tells it where to go; a working that looks at a technique instead of its owner can find that seam while the fire is still gathering and split it
Split that way, what falls away goes up as steam, the Measurewrights’ tons where their kilotons were owed, because the full price was never paid

YAKI-IRE (焼入れ · Quench) · Signature Technique
YAKI-IRE is basically thermal shock inducement: the power to heat a thing with one touch, drink the heat back out with a second, and break what is left with a third. The name is the swordsmith’s word for the moment the blade goes into the water.
Capabilities
His first touch drives heat into one spot of steel, iron, stone or bone until steel glows cherry-red above its change point. His second touch on the same spot pulls the heat back out through his palm in an instant, ENSHŌ swallowing it. It is Exuroth’s trial by fire laid on someone else’s steel, burned and plunged with no rest between, and the thing comes out the way the trial’s flaw says it must: hard, brittle and split along the lines of its ordeal. Every swordsmith knows the steel side of it: steel cooled too fast to settle goes hard as a file and as easy to snap, and a slow reheat gives the toughness back. Stone and bone go the same way, the outside shrinking faster than the inside when it is chilled in an instant, and the difference tearing it; the Measurewrights call the hard steel martensite and the tearing thermal shock. The third blow shatters what the first two prepared. On bone it runs the same: a forearm heated through old hairline cracks and quenched crazes like glaze and breaks under a chop.
The second touch will drink any heat, his own fire’s included. Laid on a man already burning with GŌKA, it draws the Karmic Fire’s heat back through the palm as fast as the other hand pours it in, so the fire stays inside the man instead of bursting outward and its warmth comes home to him, burning a man’s sins for warmth. Lift the hand and the fire leaves through the man all at once.
Applications

Breaking steel plate and mail, stone or bone
Holding Karmic Fire inside a man and drinking its warmth
Refunding a little heat to the bank with each cycle

Associations

Exuroth, the Trial Flame, whose trial by fire it is
The Body Path, shaping, riding a strike
ENSHŌ, which swallows the heat on the second touch
The Hall Irons, which beat steel plate and mail once it has had its two touches

Limitations

It does nothing to wood, leather, cloth, soft flesh or ductile metal: copper comes out of a quench softer and not harder, which the Akagane copper line has known for a thousand years
Each cycle costs one and a half percent of his reserve
It shows as a cherry-red handprint that goes black with a hiss on the second touch
Never let him touch the same place twice
Temper the struck piece by heating it gently before the second touch, which restores its toughness
Or fight him in copper, bronze and leather
Running cold water turns the art on its owner, quenching his own glazed skin until it shatters

SENTENCE OF SEVERANCE · House Art, Moto
SENTENCE OF SEVERANCE is basically judgment striking: the power to bring one cut down with the whole weight of a judgment already made. It is the Moto house’s concluding principle, taught, with no Wellspring.
Capabilities
Every Moto uses it on a target already revealed. He uses it on everyone, because TSUMI-YOMI has already judged them. It is a stroke and wants an edge, and for three centuries his edge has been his hands. Give him an edge, even one taken off a guard as he throws her down, and the headsman’s grip finds it at once: one cut, falling, with the whole of the judgment in it.
Applications

Closing on anyone he has counted, which is everyone
Putting a headsman’s stroke through any edge that comes to hand

Associations

The Moto house’s inheritance
TSUMI-YOMI, the reading it falls on
The headsman’s grip

Limitations

It wants an edge, and his hands have had to serve
The stare comes first and gives it away
A target his reading cannot see gives it nothing to fall under

THE HELL FIRE · Technique
THE HELL FIRE is basically stored-heat eruption: the power to stamp, split the floor of his Register, and stand its kept heat up as a wall of fire that needs no air. It is the Third Release doing by the acre what GŌKA does by the fist.
Capabilities
Inside ENMA-CHŌ the edge lets no heat out, so everything ever spent in the kept morning is still there, lying in the black polish of the floor like coals under ash. A stamp opens a seam in that floor and three centuries of kept heat stand up through it as a sheet or a ring of Tarturon fire, white-orange at the root, ember-orange in the body, black-violet along its crown, carrying its own breath and wanting no air.
Applications

Raising a sheet or a ring of fire across the hall
Opening the same seams for himself, to feed a wound

Associations

Tarturon, fed from what ENMA-CHŌ has kept
The Body Path, shaping
ONNEN, whose portion it burns on

Limitations

It works only inside his own Register and only against a soul he holds an account for
It spends only what is already banked or kept: it burns on what the man in front of him owes, so using it spends that man’s ONNEN portion and leaves him cooler for it
The stamp and the seam show it coming
Go through it fast, which is a flash burn and not a charring
Have given him nothing to spend, bring cold, or stay out of his Register

TATAMI-ABI (畳み阿鼻 · Abi Folded) · Technique
TATAMI-ABI is basically heat concentration: the power to haul his whole Domain in through the Irons and squeeze the oven down to one point at the tip of whatever he is holding. It is what he does with ABI when it is about to fall.
Capabilities
When ABI is about to fall, the kept heat is supposed to leave at once as a blast. He folds it instead. The Hall Irons carry part of the boundary, so he hauls the wall in by his wrists, and heat that cannot cross a wall has to go where the wall drives it: toward the one door left open, the Irons, the way a bellows squeezed shut sends every breath it holds out through the nozzle. The wood behind the shrinking dome goes cold and its fires go out.
Everything the oven held pours into him and down whatever is in his hand, and there the Work of Ruins, alone in him since the block and bent by Obsession toward ending whatever it is pointed at, presses it into a single point, hot past violet, that ends what enters it. The air screams going in, and an eye that reads flaws finds none in it.
Applications

Throwing the point as a spear
Driving it point-down into the ground so that its heat pays for the opening of ENMA-CHŌ, and the Third Release opens like a book from its spine without waiting on his reserve

Associations

Tarturon, bent by Hametsu no Gō, the Work of Ruins
The Body Path for the heat, his Walked Fate Path for the Work that points it
ABI, whose heat it is, and the Hall Irons, the door it goes through
It needs his Dominion and the Irons on his wrists

Limitations

It spends only what the Domain has already kept, and the whole Domain is spent to make it
It shows on the arm that holds it
It is unmistakable: a red dome drawing in toward his wrists like glass back into a blowpipe, with frost following it and the wood going cold
Be gone before the point is made
Or break an Iron, or get the Irons off him, since they are the door the heat goes through

Releases
The Hall Irons are his bonded weapon. They carry the First Release’s heat and part of ABI’s boundary; taken off him, the boundary of his Domain falls inward a third of its radius.
SHAKUNETSU (灼熱 · White Heat) · First Release
SHAKUNETSU is basically ember embodiment: the power to stand as fired glaze with ember light in every crack. It is the open book worn as a skin, and the north calls it the Burning.
Capabilities
At Stage XI the First Release no longer needs calling; it is how he stands, and it never ends while he is awake. His skin crazes like glaze on fired pots, ember light in every crack across the forearms and the chest, the hair lifts white off his skull, the chain stubs on the Irons glow, and ENSHŌ strikes as hard as his Body IV will carry it. Released silently it is simply him. Called aloud, “Shakunetsu!”, at the start of a fight he means to win, it flares to his full color and roars.
As a Body release it changes the body, and after three centuries on the slab in the Pit it found a new face. Called in that face, his right hand splits along the knuckles into black scale edged in violet light, the palm folds into two jaws, the fingers become long teeth white-hot at the points, and where the wrist had been there is a furnace throat: a dragon’s mouth on the end of his arm, the old crown beast of the Moto, which no Kurenai was ever permitted to wear.
Applications

Raising ENSHŌ as far as his Body IV will carry it
Pouring heat from the maw as a wave
Letting the same heat out slowly, through every crack of the glaze at once, when something stops him moving fast

Associations

A Body release
The Hall Irons, which carry its heat
ENSHŌ, which it lifts

Limitations

It takes about half a percent of his reserve a minute, under what he recovers at rest
The glaze is fired skin and breaks like it: a quench shatters it, and banked heat fires it shut again
Everything that counters ENSHŌ counters it
It never stops, so he is never fresh, and his fever is always running

ABI (阿鼻 · Without Interval) · Second Release
ABI the release is basically domain opening: the power to stand the oven up with one word. It is a field where nothing spent is allowed to leave.
Capabilities
Called, it is one word in the old court tongue, “Abi!”, and the dome stands as it is said. Its standing note is the blast furnace with its doors thrown open, and the field is the color of a kiln’s mouth. It opens and powers the Domain of the same name, in one turn.
Applications

Opening and powering the Domain

Associations

The Domain ABI, which it opens
The Hall Irons, which carry part of the boundary

Limitations

Held past its limit it is a Crystal Fracture Event along the old line of the block
Afterward he runs Overgrown until he has slept, and he does not sleep well

ENMA-CHŌ (閻魔帳 · Enma’s Register) · Third Release
ENMA-CHŌ is basically law imposition: the power to keep the morning of his sentence open as a place, and to set his own law over the world’s inside it. It is the Hall itself with him holding the pen.
Capabilities
Enma is the judge of the dead in the old stories, and his register is the book in which every deed is written. Called aloud, shouted in the court tongue, “Enma-chō!”, the field shows what it is: the Hall of Verdicts on the morning of the sentence, kept open. Kiln light stands in the windows and does not move, the floor is black polish, the seven chairs are empty, and the block is there with its stain. The field takes Vantabriel’s black-violet at its edges, and its deep note sounds under the furnace. Anyone inside is standing in his one morning, and an eye that reads flaws hears every line of the hall ring with the same dead note as the crack at his nape.
Its law is his, set over the world’s. Inside it ENSHŌ becomes local law two steps over its base for that effect alone, so no blow lands on him as force at all: all of it arrives as heat and is banked. A floor pushes back on whatever stands on it exactly as hard as it is pushed; that is one of the world’s oldest habits, and the only reason anything stands. In the Register the floor keeps that bargain only for what he allows, so it carries a man’s weight and will not take a blow handed down into it, and every technique that sheds force into the ground stops in its user’s body.
Its far edge is already folded, so where something else has breached that edge he can bend the fold onto the breach and throw a man out of the hall through it, back into the world.
Applications

Taking every blow as heat to be entered
Stopping any technique that sheds force into the ground
Reading a count aloud, entry by entry, and taking a price for each
Holding THE HELL FIRE in its floor
Throwing a man out of the hall through a breach
Opening on borrowed heat, which TATAMI-ABI’s can pay for

Associations

Vantabriel, whose black-violet stands at its edges
ENSHŌ, made local law
THE HELL FIRE and TATAMI-ABI
HAKANASHI, which regrows a limb from its floor
The Hall Irons

Limitations

It lasts about fifty seconds from a full reserve
Its limit is the bank: everything poured into him goes toward the quarter-reserve saturation line, and a crew that loads him deliberately past it inside ENMA-CHŌ cracks his Crystal with their own blows
Cold, poison, soul-work and Nihiloth negation pass through it as they pass through the Trait
Throwing a man out costs that man’s whole account and another third of the hall
It shrinks as it is hurt: one Iron broken on a flaw in its casting drops the boundary inward a third, and the light of the kept morning moves

Domain
ABI (阿鼻 · Without Interval) · Domain
ABI the Domain is basically heat trapping: the power to close a hundred and fifty meters of ground into an oven that no heat can leave, his own included. The deepest of the hells is the one without a pause.
Capabilities
His Domain is his doctrine laid on the ground as its law: nothing spent is allowed to leave. The Second Release opens it in one turn, out to a hundred and fifty meters, and inside the field heat cannot cross the boundary by any road. The Measurewrights call such a wall adiabatic and quote the oldest law in their book, that nothing spent is lost and only goes somewhere; here the ground has taken his doctrine for its own, and there is nowhere for it to go. So every working spent inside, what his furnace burns, what his enemies’ workings shed, every blow’s heat, stays in and the temperature only climbs, second by second.
A dome that size holds some seven million cubic meters of air, and at fighting output the air inside climbs a few degrees every second, so that the unwoken go dry-skinned, then confused, then into seizure. Wet ground makes it worse, since steam stops sweat from cooling anyone.
Applications

Cooking everyone inside a little more each second
Filling the grudge bank from every hostile act inside, regardless of whom it struck
Softening thickened air the way warmth loosens pitch, so he can move again
Drawing the whole field in by his wrists instead of letting it fall, which is TATAMI-ABI

Associations

Tarturon over Exuroth
Opened by a Body Second Release, its claim laid on the ground through his Walked Fate Path, with a Body Path’s law of heat inside it
His Dominion, with his Path gate holding Sovereignty under 276
The Second Release, which opens and powers it
The Hall Irons, which carry part of the boundary

Limitations

It is a crude Domain on a Dominion of 1,595: bodies can walk out across the boundary even though heat cannot
The law is symmetric: his own heat stays too, so a long Domain cooks him past his Tolerance as surely as anyone
It lasts two minutes and forty seconds from a full reserve
When it falls the stored heat leaves all at once as a blast from the boundary inward and outward
With the Irons taken off him the boundary falls inward a third of its radius
Walk out across the edge
Contest the ground with stronger Sovereignty and Gravity, as any practitioner of his Stage with both can, eroding the field from its edge
Or be heat-proofed or Abython-equalized and outlast two minutes forty in the oven, waiting for the field to fall on its owner

characters/ability-accounts/sodoku-moto-.title: Sodoku Moto — Abilities in full
characters/ability-accounts/sodoku-moto-.content:
Card: Sodoku Moto
AKAI ITO (赤い糸), the Red Thread
AKAI ITO is basically Threads of Fate Manipulation: the power to make the threads of fate visible as red string, and to tie them together or cut them apart. It is his signature, the one idea his Traits, his moves and his blade each express in their own way.
Capabilities
There is an old saying in the south that two people meant to meet are tied at the little finger by a red thread nobody can see, and that the thread may tangle and stretch but never breaks. Sodoku’s soul has taken that saying for its law. The idea he works by is the oldest idea any marriage-broker or peacemaker ever lived on: whatever has truly met stays met. Its operation is conjunction, two things joined into one and the joining set down where the world can weigh it. A soul that has become that idea stops seeing people and things as separate; it sees the threads between them first, the way a weaver looking at cloth sees the warp before the pattern. When he calls the art, the threads come out of hiding as fine red strings in the air of the room, and for as long as he holds it, everyone there can see what he sees.
What reaches the world is Attraction Force, the binding principle under every vow, every lineage and every Domain, the thing that lets one presence acknowledge another and keeps that acknowledgment true. Sodoku’s blessing lets him lay his hands on it more freely than his blood alone would allow. He can tie two threads, and then the two things they belong to must meet: a blade and a throat, an arrow and its mark, a lost man and the road home. He can loosen a knot, and two things meant to meet miss each other by a hair. And because a fighter’s allies, his Domain and his own Wellspring are all held to him by the same force, Sodoku can cut those threads too, and a man who had friends, ground and power a moment before stands alone in the world.
The glyph’s limit is the road. He can only tie what already has a way to meet. Two things with nothing between them, no road, no reason, no chance, cannot be knotted, because Fate moves only what already has a way of happening. The flaw follows from the idea: a knot has two ends, and he is always holding one. Everything he ties runs a thread through his own soul, and everything he cuts is cut a little in him as well. Its contrary is Obsession Force, recognition gone to possession, which is his own brother’s road; and a soul severed from everything, which gives him nothing to tie.
Applications

Making a blow, an arrow or a meeting arrive where it must
Making a blow meant for him or his miss by a hair
Drawing a whole field’s threads to one crossing
Tying an enemy’s fate to a single ending
Cutting an enemy away from allies, ground and power
Feeling across any distance whether someone he loves is in danger
Reading every bond in a room, who is tied to whom and how hard

Techniques

EN-MUSUBI - the principle as sight and instinct, always on
INOCHIZUNA - every bond he holds become a lifeline, waking when one of them is in danger
THE UNCLOSED REACH - his blessing, the cap lifted off his reach
THE KATANA - the blade he carries, and the road the art rides into a fight
DEAI - his blade tied to a target’s thread
SURECHIGAI - a knot loosened so a blow misses
TSUJI - every thread on the field drawn to one crossing
MUSUBIME - an enemy’s fate tied to one ending
HANARE - one bond cut
HITORI - every ally in reach cut away
KODOKU - cut from everything

Associations

Benediction, the Grace, makes a bond freely given weigh as a real thing, so the knots he ties for those who love him hold hardest; Coagula, the Mending, brings scattered things back to one table
The Fate Path does the tying and cutting through the Attraction Layer; the Spirit half lets him read the souls on the ends of the threads
The Kōkan blood opened his Fate early, and his blessing, a grip, lifts its cap
His brother Sonzai is the contrary he loves; Tenma spreads along the threads he ties
His father’s beads, jade and iron, are in his hand whenever he pulls

Limitations

He can tie only what already has a road between it; a meeting with no way to happen cannot be knotted
He is one end of every thread he touches, so anyone who reads fate well reads everything he holds, and can pull on him through it
He feels every bond he cuts, and cutting someone he is tied to cuts him too
At Fate I, 0.60 to 0.70 of what he spends on a real pull arrives, and every pull ties a knot, and the knot comes due as luck turned against him, in a strap that snaps or a plan that fails for no reason anyone can find
The tell: his father’s beads come into his hand, the three ring-lines of his eye tighten, the air round his hands warms, and the red threads show themselves a breath before he moves
His aura is the warm red-gold of the Grace, with a gray-amber seam of the Mending under it
It is countered by a soul with no bonds, by a severing art that cuts the thread before he ties it, by possession that refuses to let a thread be read, and by reaching him before the threads show
Under strain it fails the way a weaver’s loom fails, by tangling: he ties more than he meant, and two things he wanted apart find themselves knotted together

Traits
EN-MUSUBI (縁結び), the Tying of Fates · Primary Trait
EN-MUSUBI is basically Node Manipulation: the power to see where things are going to meet, and to tie, tighten or untie those meetings. It is his Primary Trait, always on, and AKAI ITO starts from it.
Capabilities
Sodoku sees the world as threads of fate crossing each other, and wherever two cross there is a knot, a node: a sword and a throat, a cart and a bridge, two people who are going to meet at a gate. He sees those knots before anyone else does. He can pull two fates together so they meet, tie a knot so tight the meeting cannot be avoided, or slip one loose so two things miss each other by a hair. He never forces anything; he only ties what already has a road between it, so the world never feels pushed. It simply seems to have been going that way all along, which is why they call him the Author of Fate.
Applications

Knowing which door someone will come through, and being there
Arranging that two people meet, or never quite do
Tightening the knot between his blade and an opening
Seeing a betrayal coming as two threads drawing together that should not

Associations

Coagula, the Mending, whose old habit is scattered things coming back to the same table
His Dominion Fate and Gnosis Perception, the two Sub-Stats he leans on hardest

Limitations

Always one end of the knot; when a bond he tied breaks, he feels it go
It reads only the threads; what a person chooses on the end of one is still their own

INOCHIZUNA (命綱), the Lifeline · Secondary Trait
INOCHIZUNA is basically Bond Empowerment: the power to grow stronger whenever someone he is tied to is in danger. It woke the night Mizuyi was taken, when her thread went south pulled tight and he felt every inch of it go.
Capabilities
Every bond he holds is a lifeline. When someone on the end of one is threatened, he feels their thread at any distance: which way it runs, whether it is fraying, whether they are hurt or afraid. While they are in danger his body and his power rise to meet it, faster, harder to stop, his knots pulling tighter. The more people he stands for, the stronger he gets.
Applications

Following a captive’s thread across a country
Fighting above himself with his family behind him
Knowing the moment a loved one is hurt, and roughly where

Associations

Benediction, the Grace, which makes the lifelines of those who love him run strongest
His Harmonics Axis and Empathy, where bonds are held

Limitations

The line runs both ways: their fear and pain come to him through it
If someone on the end of a lifeline dies, he feels that too
It wakes only under real danger to someone he is truly tied to

THE UNCLOSED REACH · Blessing
THE UNCLOSED REACH is basically Limitless Potential, given: the power to keep climbing the ladder of Fate past where his blood would stop him.
Capabilities
The Moto blood opens Fate early and, with no Work behind it, stops it at the second rung. Sodoku was born with the cap lifted, as far as his Stage allows and never past it. On his window it reads as the giver wrote it:
[Blessing: The Unclosed Reach]
[Your reach upon what binds will never close.]

Limitations

A blessing can lie, because the giver wrote the line
It lifts the ceiling and nothing else; every rung is still climbed, and every pull still paid for

Techniques
THE KATANA · Blade (all swords)
THE KATANA is basically Swordsmanship: Sodoku can use any blade, and he fights with the katana.
Capabilities
He was taught the sword in the yard at Kharven-Seat like every Kōkan child, and he fights with a katana in the house’s way: a long two-handed draw, an even, unhurried guard, and a cut that comes out of the draw itself. He moves before he decides to, which on a sword reads as a blade already moving when the other man’s foot is still in the air. The sword is the road his art rides. He does not need a heavy cut, because DEAI has already decided that the cut arrives; he needs only a clean one, and he keeps it clean. He handles a straight sword, a saber or a long knife well enough to win with them, but the katana is the blade his hands go to.
Associations

DEAI ties the edge to the opening before the cut leaves the scabbard
His Dexterity Finesse and Reflex, and his father’s way of keeping the edge off the scabbard wood

Limitations

He is a boy of thirteen with a boy’s arms; a grown swordsman can beat his guard by weight
His art places the cut; it does not make the cut heavier

DEAI (出会い), the Meeting · Move of AKAI ITO
He ties his blade to a target’s thread, and the cut has to arrive. Dodging only changes where it lands. Its limit is the road: a target with no way to be reached, behind a wall that will not open, cannot be met. Its price is a small knot, which comes due within days.
SURECHIGAI (すれ違い), Passing By · Move of AKAI ITO
He loosens the knot between an attack and its target, and the blow misses by a hair. It works on what is aimed at him or at anyone he is tied to. A blow that was never going to miss by much, a wide swing or a falling roof, cannot be slipped far enough.
TSUJI (辻), the Crossroads · Move of AKAI ITO
He pulls every thread on the field to one point. Enemies collide, and arrows meet arrows in the air. It is a large pull for a boy of his rung, and it leaves a knot he will be paying off for a season.
MUSUBIME (結び目), the Final Knot · Move of AKAI ITO
He ties an enemy’s whole fate to one ending, so every move they make leads back to it. It is the move his brothers’ arts land on: Sonzai’s calamity cannot miss a man tied to one spot.
HANARE (離れ), Apart · Move of AKAI ITO
He cuts one bond, and an ally cannot reach them: a shield-man stumbles, a messenger takes the wrong road, a Resonant partner loses the other’s rhythm.
HITORI (一人), Alone · Move of AKAI ITO
He cuts every ally in reach, and help always arrives too late. He feels each cut, and if any of those allies were his own, he loses them too.
KODOKU (孤独), Solitude · Finisher of AKAI ITO
He cuts them off from everything, their own power included. Their Domain collapses, their Wellspring goes silent, and they stand in the world as if nothing has ever known them. It is the one he cannot take back: nothing cut this way comes back to the one who lost it.

characters/ability-accounts/sonzai-moto-.title: Sonzai Moto — Abilities in full
characters/ability-accounts/sonzai-moto-.content:
Card: Sonzai Moto
TATARIGAMI (祟り神), the Calamity God
TATARIGAMI is basically Misfortune Embodiment: the power to become calamity itself for whoever wronged him. It is his signature, the one idea his Traits, his moves and his body each express in their own way.
Capabilities
In the old stories a tatarigami is an angry spirit that brings disaster on whoever offended it, and the offerings people leave are meant to keep it from remembering them. Sonzai’s soul has taken that spirit’s law for its own. The idea he works by is one every feud in the world has lived on: a wrong that is never forgiven is never finished. Its operation is calcination, the soul burning on what it believes it is owed until nothing is left of the debt but the debtor. He remembers every wrong ever done to him, perfectly, and every one of them goes on burning.
What reaches the world is Obsession Force, a way of gripping Thread by force that any Fate soul may take up, and no exception to the rule. Where Attraction recognizes and lets go, Obsession takes hold and will not, and its knots run heavier. A Fate Path worker pulls a thread down for one working and lets it go, and pays for it afterward in a knot of bad luck. Sonzai pulls the thread and never lets it go, and he holds the knot so hard that it falls on the man he hates instead of on himself. When he calls the art, his grudge rises over its target as a red omen, and the world begins to turn against them. Beams crack over their head, the ground goes bad under their feet, their horse balks, their sword slips in a dry hand, and their luck runs out and keeps running out. None of it looks like magic; it looks like the worst day of someone’s life, over and over, until they break.
It breaks the oldest rule of his house. The Moto read a thing’s job and enforce it, and the Work of Ruin closes only on what is already failing. Sonzai reads nothing. His grudge makes a thing ready to fall, and then it falls. The glyph’s limit is the wrong itself: it takes hold only where a real wrong was done to him or his, and it can be held fully on only one target at a time. The flaw follows from the idea: what he will not let go of, he cannot put down, so if he ever forgives, or his target dies before he is finished, every held knot comes home to him at once. Its contrary is release, the soul that lets a thing go; and his brother’s recognition, the bond his obsession cannot eat.
Applications

Turning a man’s luck against him until he breaks
Bringing a roof, a beam or a banner down on one person in a crowd
Souring a hall’s ground, wells and footing under its master
Keeping on toward a target through wounds that should drop him
Turning a pinned blow into a blast on the Body side

Techniques

TATARI - the principle as instinct, always on: wrongs remembered, and misfortune leaning toward the one who did them
ONNEN - the grudge as a body that will not stop while its target lives
CATACLYSM ON THE BODY - a blow given a wall at the enemy’s back goes over into a blast
KYŌCHŌ - the target marked, and everything after it going wrong
FALLING SKY - everything above the target coming down
SOURED GROUND - the earth under the target turning on them
HYAKUSAI - every misfortune at once

Associations

Tarturon, the Fire of Reckoning, power that rises with what he believes is owed and draws the odds up the line toward the one man it is owed by; Cataclysm, the Blast, on the Body side
The Fate Path holds the thread; the Body half carries him to the target and hits
The Kōkan blood gave him the grip on Ruin, and he grips it the wrong way
His brother Sodoku ties the knot that TATARIGAMI comes down on
The white rose on his armor, which reddens as the grudge grows

Limitations

It needs a real wrong; hatred cannot be faked, and an invented grievance gives it nothing to hold
One target at a time; a second grudge splits the hold and both go weak
His knots are the heaviest in the house, because a thread held past its working leaves a heavier knot than a clean one
The calamity does not care who is standing next to the target, and allies close to it take the falling beam too
If he forgives, or the target dies before he is done, every held knot comes home to him at once
The more he uses it, the narrower his world grows: other bonds weaken, and the one person he hates fills more of it
The tell: the white rose reddens petal by petal, his aura flares white-orange at its edges, and the target starts seeing red birds on the sill
His aura is the hot amber-red of the Fire of Reckoning, which never banks down to embers
It is countered by forgiveness that the target can earn or force, by a Work of Purity that washes the omen off, by cutting his hold on the thread, and by Sodoku, who can loosen the knot it lands on
Under strain it fails the way a fire with no stopping condition fails: it keeps burning after the target, through whatever is nearest

Traits
TATARI (祟り), the Calamity · Primary Trait
TATARI is basically Calamity Manipulation: the power to make misfortune hunt down whoever wronged him. It is his Primary Trait, always on, and TATARIGAMI starts from it.
Capabilities
Sonzai never forgives and never forgets. Every wrong done to him goes into his memory and stays there, and the longer he holds it, the stronger it grows. Most people who pull on fate pay a debt for it afterward as bad luck coming back on them. Sonzai holds that debt so hard that it lands on the person he hates instead. Straps snap on them, roofs fall on them, horses throw them, wells go sour in their halls, and nothing anyone does can explain why.
Applications

Small calamities on small wrongs, the boy who pushed him on the stair falling down it
The slow ruin of a great enemy across months

Associations

Tarturon, the Fire of Reckoning
His Dominion Fate and Gnosis Retention, which keeps every wrong

Limitations

A real wrong, one target at a time
If he lets go, it all comes home to him

ONNEN (怨念), the Deep Grudge · Secondary Trait
ONNEN is basically Revenge Empowerment: the power to keep going for as long as the person who wronged him is still alive. It woke the night Mizuyi was taken, when Cozbi Mahuo said “let the games begin” and Sonzai decided he would never let it go.
Capabilities
While his target lives, Sonzai cannot be stopped. He ignores pain, does not tire, and gets back up from wounds that should have dropped him, because his soul will not let his body quit before the debt is paid. The calamity hunts his enemy, and Sonzai keeps walking toward them through anything in the way.
Applications

Walking through a wound to finish a fight
Days on the road without sleep, toward one man

Associations

His Vitality Threshold and Resilience Persistence, already the highest things on his sheet

Limitations

When the target is dead or out of reach, it lets go all at once, and every ignored wound and every unslept night arrives together
Without someone to hold on to, he may not get back up

Techniques
CATACLYSM ON THE BODY · Wellspring working
On the Body side, Cataclysm, the Blast, changes what his blows do. Given confinement behind the target, a set stance or a wall at the enemy’s back, a blow stops being a push and goes over all at once into a blast that crosses the target faster than they can flinch. He uses it with the red-hafted weapon and with his hands alike. Its limit is the confinement: in open air his blows are only blows.
KYŌCHŌ (凶兆), Ill Omen · Move of TATARIGAMI
He marks the target. They begin to see signs everywhere, a red bird on the sill, a crack in their cup, their name misspoken, and everything that happens to them from then on goes wrong. The mark holds as long as the grudge does.
FALLING SKY · Move of TATARIGAMI
Everything above the target comes down at once: beams, banners, stone, the roof itself. Whoever stands beside the target is under the same roof.
SOURED GROUND · Move of TATARIGAMI
The earth under them turns against them. Footing gives, wells go bad, and the floor of their own hall will not hold them.
HYAKUSAI (百災), the Hundred Misfortunes · Finisher of TATARIGAMI
Every bad thing that could happen to them happens at the same moment. It is the largest knot he can hold, and if he lets go of it before it is spent, it falls on him instead.

characters/ability-accounts/tenma-moto-—.title: Tenma Moto — Abilities in full
characters/ability-accounts/tenma-moto-—.content:
Card: Tenma Moto
NAGASHI-BINA (流し雛), the Floating Dolls
NAGASHI-BINA is basically Sympathetic Magic: the power to tie a person to a paper doll, so that whatever happens to the doll happens to them. It is his signature, the one idea his Traits and his dolls each express in their own way. Tenma does not fight with his hands at all; the dolls do the fighting.
Capabilities
In the old country, families fold small paper dolls and rub them against their bodies to draw their impurities into the paper, then set the dolls afloat on a river to carry everything away. The idea Tenma works by is older than the rite: things that have touched go on touching. A lock of a man’s hair, his name spoken over a folded shape, a drop of his blood on paper, and the thing becomes a door to him. Its operation is distillation: what one tuned vessel holds rises out of it and comes down in the other, with nothing poured between them.
What reaches the world runs on both his Traits. Through KEGARE, anything he puts into a doll spreads into the person tied to it: a wound, a sickness, a curse, sleep, fear. Through KAESHI, a doll can take what was meant for someone he loves and send it back along the thread to whoever did it. He folds them small and white from plain paper, and the moment one is tied, a thread runs between doll and person that only he can see. On the field he looks like a twelve-year-old playing with paper. People laugh until the first doll tears.
The glyph’s limit is the tie: a doll works only on someone it has been truly tied to, by a touch, a hair, blood or a true name, and a person he has never touched and cannot name is out of its reach. The flaw follows from the idea: what touches goes on touching both ways, so every doll is tied to him as well as to its target, and everything it carries passes through his hands first. Its contrary is purity, the Work that washes a thing back to what it ought to be; and severance, the cut that leaves nothing for a thread to run along.
Applications

Hurting a man by hurting the doll tied to him
Drawing a wound, poison or curse out of someone he loves and sending it elsewhere
Taking a killing blow on a doll instead of a brother
Putting a whole guard to sleep through one doll tied to their captain
Laying a slow curse with a straw doll and iron nails

Techniques

KEGARE - the principle as instinct, always on: whatever he carries spreads
KAESHI - whatever is done to him goes home to whoever did it
KATASHIRO - a doll tied to a person
NAGASHI - a wound or curse drawn out into a doll and sent away
MIGAWARI - a doll taking a killing blow in someone’s place
WARA NINGYŌ - the straw doll and the nails

Associations

Mortalis, the Black Gate, gives KEGARE its death-touch; Transference, the Give-and-Take, is the road his dolls’ threads run along
The Fate Path holds the ties; the Spirit half reads the soul on the other end
The Kōkan blood gives him Hataraki, and he carries it further than the house meant it to go
Sodoku ties the threads and Tenma spreads along them
The red hood, and paper always between his fingers

Limitations

He does not fight with his hands, and his body is a child’s; a man who reaches him before a doll is folded can kill him
A doll needs a true tie: a touch, a hair, blood or a true name
Every doll is tied to him too; if a doll is burned before he is done with it, whatever it held comes back to him
Whatever he spreads passes through him first, and he carries a little of every sickness he has ever started
At Fate I, 0.60 to 0.70 of a real pull arrives, and every pull ties a knot
The tell: paper in his fingers, a doll folding itself faster than hands should fold, and a thin violet thread in his black-red aura running off toward someone
His aura is the venous black-red of the Black Gate, the color of blood that has stopped hurrying
It is countered by fire, by purity, by a severing that leaves no thread, and by getting to him before he folds
Under strain it fails as contagion does, by spreading where he did not send it, to whoever is nearest the doll, the target, or himself

Traits
KEGARE (穢れ), the Defilement · Primary Trait
KEGARE is basically Ontopathogenesis: the power to infect what a thing is, so that whatever he carries spreads from one thing to the next like a sickness. It is his Primary Trait, always on, and NAGASHI-BINA runs on it.
Capabilities
In the old belief, kegare is the impurity that clings to anyone who touches death and passes to whoever touches them. Tenma’s soul works the same way. Everything is tied to everything else by fine threads of fate, and he can send whatever he holds along them: a wound, rot, frost, fire or poison, or health and strength; a working, a curse or a blessing; fear, sleep, courage or an oath’s hold. One touch starts it, and from there it travels through touch, bonds and shared ground. At its extreme it stops being something a person has and becomes what they are: a man becomes stone, a curse becomes who someone is, a Domain turns to rot from the inside.
Applications

Spreading one soldier’s courage down a whole line
Spreading one enemy’s wound to every man beside him
Rot through a wall from a single touched stone

Associations

Mortalis, the Black Gate; Transference, the Give-and-Take
His Harmonics Synergy and Projection, and his Vitality Filtration, which lets him carry what he spreads

Limitations

He is always the first one infected
It travels only where there is a connection; a soul cut off from everything cannot catch it
The Work of Purity washes it out
Which Hataraki Work it grows from is not known

KAESHI (返し), the Return · Secondary Trait
KAESHI is basically Damage Reflection: the power to send whatever is done to him back to whoever did it.
Capabilities
Tenma’s soul is woven into everything around him, and KAESHI turns that around: when someone hurts him, the hurt follows its own thread home. Cut him and the cut opens on the swordsman, in the same place. Poison him and the poisoner sickens. Curse him and the curse goes back to whoever laid it. It wakes while he is under attack, and it is strongest when the attack is meant to kill.
Applications

Making any attack on him cost the attacker the same wound
Turning MIGAWARI’s torn doll into a blow sent home

Associations

His Resilience Fortification and Continuity, which keep a curse from staying in him

Limitations

He feels all of it first, in full
A blow strong enough to kill him outright still kills him, and then kills the one who struck it

Techniques
KATASHIRO (形代), the Effigy · Move of NAGASHI-BINA
He folds a doll and ties it to a person, by a touch, a hair, a drop of blood or their name spoken over it. From then on, what happens to the doll happens to them. A doll keeps its tie until it is burned, drowned or torn through, or until he unties it.
NAGASHI (流し), the Floating Away · Move of NAGASHI-BINA
He pulls a wound or a curse out of someone into a doll and sets it loose, sending it to whoever he chooses. It is the healing side of his art, and the cruel side, in one fold.
MIGAWARI (身代わり), the Stand-In · Move of NAGASHI-BINA
A doll tied to someone he loves takes a killing blow for them. The doll tears, and through KAESHI the blow goes home to whoever struck it. He can keep only a few of these tied at once, and his brothers each carry one.
WARA NINGYŌ (藁人形), the Straw Doll · Finisher of NAGASHI-BINA
It comes from the old curse ritual of nailing a straw doll to a shrine tree in the darkest hour of the night. He nails one, and the person tied to it feels every nail. It is slow and certain, and it is the one thing he does that his mother has asked him never to do in the house.

characters/ability-accounts/tetsugen-aka.title: Tetsugen Akagane — Abilities in full
characters/ability-accounts/tetsugen-aka.content:
Card: Tetsugen Akagane
THE COPPER DRUM
THE COPPER DRUM (銅の鼓 · Akagane no Tsuzumi) is basically heartbeat manipulation: the power to take hold of a beat and keep it. He has held his own heart at twenty-five for forty years, and every heart near him beats when he says. It is his signature art, worked in the Akagane Blood and Heart Arts, and his Traits, techniques, Releases and Domain are all this one idea done at a different size.
Capabilities
He took hold of his own heart first, and kept it at one hour for forty years. With a hand on a man he takes hold of that man’s heart or his blood. With an arrow he takes hold of it at sixty paces, to listen. Released, he stops keeping his own hour and lets the true beat out; released again, the beat becomes a field and every heart in it takes his step; and at the last he keeps or does not keep one named heart. That is the whole ladder: the idea, the transformed body, the world obeying it. The two readings that sit beside it, the long read of what another man would do and the ledger of every heart he ever fed, are the same habit turned on minds and on debts. He puts his own heart in the other man’s place, and he keeps count.
It runs on two lenses. Anima Spirare, the Soul’s Breath, which his house calls the Breath of the Living, is the idea of the breath of the whole: a body that remembers being whole and answers a small hurt with everything it has, exactly where the hurt says. Its operation is fermentation, the whole body quickened round one small signal, and a soul that has taken the idea into its Shell carries that quickening in its own blood and can lend it to another body’s. The Measurewrights explain it by the clotting of blood, a cascade in which each woken factor wakes many of the next, and their figure for how large an answer a small signal draws is good; they have no idea why the body remembers being whole. The Akagane turned the idea from the wound to the heart. A heart is a muscle that fires itself: a small knot of tissue at its top sets the pace, a wave of current runs down through the muscle, the muscle clenches, and for a moment afterward it cannot fire again while it resets. That beat is a small signal that commands a whole body, which is exactly the kind of signal the Breath of the Living answers, so a man who has harmonized with it can listen to the signal, hold it, hurry it, or drown it. Verdantia, the Green, is the idea of growth without end, a self with no final size, the tissue that stays young because it never stops being made, and in him it does one job: it holds the body round the heart to the hour the beat was taken.
He reads Body IV, the rung of law, and still works by contact, the habit of the rung he learned on, which is why almost everything he does needs his hand on the thing: the palm on the breastbone, the hand flat on the chest, the thumb on the vein, the copper head in the flesh. Only the Domain lets go of that, because inside a Domain the field itself is the hand. It all rides one blow, and the blow is a clinch. He lets the first strike come and takes it on a folded forearm, clamps the striking arm against his own ribs, and lays the palm on. Then the same hand is already on the chest for the Warrant, or the thumb is already at the throat for the Blood Road.
Applications

Keeping his own body, and the outward face of his Crystal, at the hour he took the copper chair
Stopping, holding or keeping another man’s heart with a hand on him
Moving the blood in a body he has his thumb on
Listening to one heart from across a field, once an arrow has bitten
Setting the beat of every heart in a field
Reading what another man will do, and keeping count of every heart he ever fed

Techniques

THE COPPER HEART - his own heart held at one hour, and his body and Crystal face with it
IN HIS PLACE - the same habit turned on minds: what he would do in the other man’s place
THE SENNEN BOOKS - the same habit turned on debts: the heartbeat of everyone his granaries fed
AKA-TE - a palm on the breastbone in the one instant that breaks a heart’s rhythm
HEART-WARRANT - a flat hand that holds a heart still, or keeps a failing one going
KETSURO - a thumb on a vein that sends the blood where he wants it
KITSUNE-YA - an arrow whose bite lets him hear that heart at range
TOSHI-GAERI - the First Release: he lets go of the hour and the true beat comes out
KODŌ - the Second Release and the Domain: the beat becomes a field
SHINZŌ-DOME - the Third Release: one named heart, stopped by the field’s law

Associations

Anima Spirare, the Soul’s Breath, his governing Wellspring, gives him the heart’s own current: what the Akagane keep and what they can stop
Verdantia, the Green, holds the body’s renewal at the hour it was taken
The Body Path holds the heart and the blood, and the Spirit Path, which he walks, holds the long read and the books
The Akagane Blood and Heart Arts, learned at his grandfather’s hands
He bonds no weapon; the horn-handled knife is for meat
Living ground feeds him: both Wellsprings favor living biomass, temperate air and the nearness of blood, so a granary town, a full hall, a wood or a battlefield serves him well

Limitations

The art has purchase on living blood and a beating heart and on nothing else, so the dead and the made are outside it
Almost all of it needs his hand, his thumb or his arrow on the target; only the Domain lets go of that
It never stops charging him: about a hundredth of his reserve every hour of his life, asleep or awake, and every large use is paid in years that come into the body and stay
About a fifth of what he spends never reaches the world, which is his yield, and burns in the furnace of his Shell as blood-heat: a flush under the pale skin, palms hot enough to feel through a coat, and, when he is pushing, the snow round his feet melting pink
Sterile ground, extreme cold and soil already drained of Essence starve him; a frozen field is the poorest footing he can have, and he lost the worst day of his youth on the ice under the Grey Teeth
The charge is always readable, and at rest it is the slow copper pulse in his aura keeping time with his heart
As his reserve falls it shows: at half the copper pulse slows, at a quarter gray comes in at his temples and lines at his eyes, and at a tenth sixty-one years begin to arrive
Against a higher Stage the art thins at the grip and holds at the timing: a stronger Sovereignty contests the field at its edge and in its owner’s own chest, a stronger Hemostasis pushes the hand off the heart and holds its own blood where it is, and a heart held still or run ragged by its owner’s own art gives him no window
It is beaten by starving him or catching him asleep, by keeping his hands and his arrows off your skin, by giving him a heart he cannot read, a body in great heat or a thing with no heart at all, or by striking the drum, since the field beats to his own heart and falls when it is struck
Anima Spirare fails by its own flaw: the whole answers a small hurt with everything it has and cannot answer with less, so held past his reserve in the field or on the Blood Road, with no sense left of where, his own blood starts answering every heart he is holding, clots where nothing is cut, and leaves him with blue lips, a white face and nothing left to close the wound that matters; the Measurewrights call it disseminated activation
Pushed to the end, that is a Crystal Fracture Event along the Sennen road, and his own heart stops with the field
Verdantia fails by its own flaw, a self with no final size that goes on growing when nothing feeds it, which the Measurewrights call etiolation: starved, drugged or knocked senseless, the hold on the hour goes thin and the years come in at once, and the longer the lapse the more of them stay
THE COPPER HEART has run without rest for most of his life, which is Resonance Fatigue
Letting the hold lapse long enough that the years stay is his Shear Break condition
His Longevity stands at 725, past the fracture line, and the hold is now the thing keeping the Crystal in one piece

Traits
THE COPPER HEART (銅の心 · Akagane no Kokoro) · Inherited Trait
THE COPPER HEART is basically suspended aging: the power to keep his own heart, body and Crystal at one chosen hour. It is the Akagane keeping of a heart, turned on himself the year he took the copper chair.
Capabilities
Anima Spirare holds his heart to the beat it had that year, and Verdantia holds the body round it to the hour the beat was taken: the hair black, the face smooth, the eyes clear, the hands quick. He looks twenty-five, and has for most of his life; the seven lines have watched him sit the copper chair forty years without aging, and do not ask. It keeps the body and never what has been done to it. The scars on his hands stayed, and so did every year of what he did, which he carries like an old man and is tired like one.
A Crystal is a body too, so the same hold keeps the outward face of his Crystal at the density it had that year. That is the Veil. Every assessor who has read him since has read a Stage VII Refraction practitioner at Level 190, and been right about the face and wrong about everything under it. He kept it there because Gimbzo burned whatever in the north was strong enough to say no to him, the Akagane granaries at Hiroe among it, and a Fox who looks harmless lives to sit in council.
Applications

Keeping a sixty-one-year-old body at twenty-five
Holding off bleeding, wounds and aging
Passing for a Stage far below his own
Keeping his own heart beating through SHINZŌ-DOME, when it stops with the other

Techniques

THE VEIL - the same hold laid over his Crystal, so that it reads as Refraction; it costs nothing more

Associations

Anima Spirare for the beat, Verdantia for the hour
The Body Path, which he has mastered
Inherited with the Akagane blood and its Blood and Heart Arts
TOSHI-GAERI, which is this hold let go on purpose

Limitations

Its limit is the reserve: starved, drugged or knocked senseless, the hold slips, and the years he has been keeping off come into him at once, gray into the hair, lines into the face and a sixty-one-year-old heart laboring in a young man’s chest, until he can take hold again
The longer it lapses the more of the years stay, and with them the Veil goes, and anyone looking sees all of it at once
It costs about one percent of his reserve an hour, every hour, asleep or awake, for as long as he lives
The slow copper pulse in his aura keeps time with his heart, which no young man’s aura does, and that gives it away
He has called TOSHI-GAERI in front of witnesses, and the Veil is gone for everyone on the Kessen road who looked
It is beaten by starving him, or catching him asleep

IN HIS PLACE · Primary Trait
IN HIS PLACE is basically behavior prediction: the power to know what a man will do by asking what he himself would do in that man’s place. It is the art’s habit turned on minds.
