Capabilities
His soul reads a field by asking what it would do if it were the other man, and it is very rarely wrong. He says so out loud. Forecast and Analysis turn forty years of provisioning, levies and ledgers into the long read. The Keld were bought, with no tithe, seed grain and no Moto boot on their snow, because that is what he would have offered in Karogane’s place; Karogane would not need to win, only to walk out between the lines and shout.
Applications

Reading what an enemy commander will do before he does it
Working out what a bought man was offered

Associations

The Spirit Path, which he walks
No Wellspring: forty years of ledgers and the long read

Limitations

Its limit is himself: he reads every enemy as a man like him, and a man who would not do what Tetsugen would do, for better or worse, is invisible to it
Old Harald Keld moved four hundred riders through a whiteout so close to his column that he heard their horses blowing, in the second year of the war, and he never found out how
The Sin of Wrath is not buying anything, and Tetsugen cannot stand in a furnace
It costs nothing
The phrase gives it away: “That’s what I’d have offered, in his place”
It is beaten by an enemy who is not him, one who would not do what he would

THE SENNEN BOOKS · Secondary Trait
THE SENNEN BOOKS is basically life-sign tracking: the power to feel the heartbeat of everyone who ever ate from an Akagane granary, wherever they are. It formed at Dissonance along the Sennen road, and it is the art’s habit turned on debts.
Capabilities
He signed for every sack that fed the columns, in his own hand, with his own seal, knowing what they would do, and Anima Spirare entered every heart that ate from his granaries the way the books entered every sack. He can feel, faintly, at any distance, the heartbeat of anyone who was ever fed from an Akagane store, and whether it is steady, and when it stops: three hundred Starks at the woodpile; the Kurogane tenants, forty-one of them stopped; a Zettari border town that ate Akagane grain the winter before the columns came.
Applications

Knowing where the people he fed are, and how their hearts are beating
Feeling each one stop

Associations

Anima Spirare, through the Spirit Path
The Sennen road, the open fracture in his Core that left it

Limitations

It is a ledger and no reach: it tells him where those hearts are and how they are beating and lets him do nothing to them at range
It keeps him awake, and it costs nothing he can put down
His scarred hands turn palm up, as if there were writing on them
It cuts the other way too: a reader who counts a man’s dead finds every one of these hearts stacked in his chest, thousands of them, and anything that burns by the weight of what a man has done will go for him before anyone else in the room
It has nothing on a man who never ate his bread, who owes him nothing and was never fed by him

Techniques
AKA-TE (赤手 · Aka-te, the Red Hand) · Signature Technique
AKA-TE is basically fibrillation inducement: the power to stop a heart with an open palm, by landing it in the one instant of a heartbeat when a touch breaks the rhythm. It is the plainest piece of the art and the deadliest.
Capabilities
In every heartbeat there is a window, a few hundredths of a second while the heart’s lower chambers reset their charge for the next stroke. A blow over the heart inside that window, and only inside it, throws the whole rhythm into a quivering fibrillation: every fiber of the muscle firing on its own, none together, a heart that shakes and pumps nothing. Physicians call it commotio cordis, the agitation of the heart, and it is what kills a boy struck in the chest by a ball. It bruises nothing and breaks nothing, which is why it leaves no mark, and left alone it is death inside three minutes.
The Akagane have known about the window for a thousand years. Tetsugen steps into the clinch, goes quiet, feels the other man’s heart through his own with Anima Spirare, counts it, and puts his open palm on the breastbone in the window, every time, with the Breath of the Living behind it to hold the quiver once it starts. He says the name very low. Both harms are real and separate: the palm lands hard enough to bruise a breastbone or crack one, a blow the Measurewrights reckon at about a terajoule, and the timing stops the heart under it whether the breastbone breaks or not.
Applications

Dropping a man where he stands, with no mark on him
Stopping a heart whose skin banks every blow struck at it as heat, since the blow needs almost no force
Striking a frightened or furious heart more easily: at two hundred beats a minute the window comes round three times a second
Finishing a count that a Fox Arrow has already started, without needing the clinch to begin it

Associations

Anima Spirare, through the Body Path: the palm aimed by a listening heart
Clinch fighting, from the Akagane yard and his grandfather
KITSUNE-YA, which lets him start counting from range
HEART-WARRANT and KETSURO, which the same hand is already placed for

Limitations

Its limit is the rhythm: a heart he cannot catch, too fast, too irregular, or held still by its owner’s own art, gives him no window
A sternum armored in worked plate takes the blow and passes no shock to the heart
He must be close and listening first, and the strike is a palm, which can be caught
It takes about one percent of his reserve
The tell is the quiet before: he steps into the clinch and goes quiet, listening
Afterward the man’s own Hemostasis and his friends’ hands can shock the heart back into time if they are quick and know how; a spark of the target’s own lens firing inside the breastbone does it, the same thing a surgeon’s fist does
It is beaten by a heart he cannot read, one whose rhythm he cannot catch

HEART-WARRANT (the Akagane warrant) · School Art, the Blood and Heart Arts
HEART-WARRANT is basically heartbeat suspension: the power to hold a heart still between one beat and the next with a flat hand, or to keep a failing one going. The Akagane can keep a heart, and they can stop one, and this is the school art that does both.
Capabilities
With his open hand flat on a man’s chest, Anima Spirare finds the heart’s current and holds it still: no wave of current, no stroke, and a brain that gets no blood for six seconds goes dark and drops its body. A man whose heart is held for six seconds falls, and for three minutes does not get up. The same hand, gentler, keeps a failing heart beating, and that was its first use and its oldest. Inside KODŌ he needs no hand.
It is the art the Hall thinks of first when a lord is found dead with his heart stopped and no mark on him, which is how a needle in the nape was once laid at the copper line’s door.
Applications

Dropping a man in six seconds without wounding him
Keeping a failing heart beating
Holding a heart from across the field, inside KODŌ

Associations

Anima Spirare, through the Body Path
Taught, in the Akagane Blood and Heart Arts
SHINZŌ-DOME, which is this warrant read by the field

Limitations

It is fought by the target’s own Hemostasis and heart-ward: a strong practitioner whose blood is his own can push the hand off his heart, at a cost
It takes about three percent of his reserve to take hold and 25,000 EU a second to keep it, more than an hour from full
The tell is the open hand coming up flat, the way he lays it on his own chest when he swears, with the rings taken off first
It is beaten by never letting him touch you

KETSURO (血路 · Ketsuro, the Blood Road) · Application of Anima Spirare
KETSURO is basically blood manipulation: the power to send the blood in a body where he wants it, with a thumb on a vein. It is what the Copper Heart does with his own blood, done to someone else.
Capabilities
It works on the vessels and not the pump. He narrows them from inside to shut a bleed, pushes the blood away from a wound until it can be stitched, or keeps a crushed limb’s flesh alive for the hour it takes to reach a surgeon. Or he drives it, raising the pressure in every small vessel of a man’s eyes and brain and lungs at once until their walls give. In the old speech the word also means a way cut out through an enemy’s lines, and the Akagane surgeons who named it meant both.
Applications

Shutting a bleed from the inside
Starving a wound of blood until it can be stitched
Keeping a crushed limb alive on the way to a surgeon
Bursting the small vessels of the eyes, brain and lungs together

Associations

Anima Spirare, through the Body Path
Lived, and drilled as a surgeon’s art of the Akagane
KITSUNE-YA, which is this thumb sent out on an arrow

Limitations

It needs contact: his thumb must be on skin over a vein
A man whose Hemostasis outranks his reach holds his own blood where it is
It takes about one percent of his reserve to open and about 30,000 EU a second to hold
The tell is his thumb finding a vein, at the wrist or the throat
Held past his reserve it fails by the Breath’s own flaw, the whole answering everywhere at once, his own blood clotting where nothing is cut
It is beaten by keeping his hands off you

KITSUNE-YA (狐矢 · Kitsune-ya, the Fox Arrow) · Application of Anima Spirare, the war-bow of the copper line
KITSUNE-YA is basically heartbeat tagging: the power to mark a body with an arrow and hear its heart from across a field afterward. The Fox is the first of the Akagane beasts, and this is the house’s hunting art.
Capabilities
He draws the tall bow below its center, and his aura gathers round the copper broadhead in the shape of a fox’s mouth, red-bronze, bright arterial red at the lip, the long narrow jaws open and every tooth a needle of light. Where the head goes in, the jaws close on the blood and hold, and they go on holding after the shaft is pulled out, burned off or melted in the hand. The bite is Anima Spirare seated in living blood, and from it his listening runs up the veins to the chest, so that he hears that heart at any range on the field and can count it. By the time he closes he has already been counting it for half a minute.
It is contact made at range: KETSURO’s thumb and AKA-TE’s quiet, done from sixty paces. The arrow itself is an ordinary arrow with a soft head. It holes flesh, tendon and leather, folds like tin on worked plate or a hardened breastbone, and bites anyway if it breaks skin. The shafts are copper for one customer, but soft copper serves the art too, since the head folds and stays where a steel one would pass through.
Applications

Hearing and counting one heart at any range on the field
Starting the Red Hand’s count before he has closed
Hitting the knee and the neck at sixty paces

Associations

Anima Spirare; the Body Path for the shaft and the Spirit Path for the listening
Taught, in the Akagane yard
The war-bow of the copper line and the copper shafts

Limitations

It needs blood: a thing with none gives the fox nothing to hold
A man whose Hemostasis outranks his reach can push the listening out of his veins as he would push off the hand
Each shaft takes about half of one percent of his reserve, and the bite then holds for nothing
It is seen and heard coming: the mouth round the arrowhead, and a shaft that screams in the air and flies warm as blood, so anything with a sense for heat knows
The soft head fails against plate
It is beaten by letting it miss and never catching it, because catching it is touching it

SHINGAN (心眼 · Shingan, the heart-eye) · Bloodline Faculty, Moto
SHINGAN is basically load perception: the power to see where a thing carries its weight. It is the common Moto sight, inherited with the blood, and it does not run on THE COPPER DRUM.
Capabilities
The eye reads load, and men by their load. In him it is the long weighing look, the look of a man looking at a horse he has been told is unbreakable.
Applications

Weighing a thing, or a man, by where the load sits in it

Associations

The Moto blood’s eye, with no Wellspring behind it and no Path

Limitations

It does not read a man with nothing to weigh
Held wide it draws about 3,000 EU a second
The long weighing look gives it away

Releases
TOSHI-GAERI (年返り · Toshi-gaeri, the Years Returned) · First Release
TOSHI-GAERI is basically limiter removal: the power to let go of the hour he has kept and fight as what he really is. The word is “Kaese,” give it back.
Capabilities
The face the Copper Heart has held over his Crystal for forty years falls away, and the Sovereign density under it comes up all at once through the copper. The slow pulse in his aura becomes a drum, the red-bronze goes red as fresh blood in a basin, the smell comes off him, copper and something sweet like the air after a thunderstorm, and the room feels a Stage it did not know was in it.
With it the years come. The black curls go iron gray from the temples back all at once, as if frost had run through them, a soldier’s furrows come in at the gold eyes and the mouth, the knuckles knot, and the snow round his feet goes pink. For as long as the Release holds he fights as what he is, sixty-one, at Dissonance, with Hemostasis, Regeneration and Grapple striking a step high.
Applications

Fighting at his true Stage
Raising Hemostasis, Regeneration and Grapple a step
Called silent, a smaller rise: the face slips only a little and the gain is half

Associations

Anima Spirare and Verdantia, let go, through the Body Path
THE COPPER HEART, whose hold it drops
KODŌ, which opens on the released pulse

Limitations

Some of the years stay: for every minute he holds it, about a year comes into the body for good when he takes hold again, and a man who has kept himself at twenty-five for forty years has done the sum
It lasts about four minutes from full
It ends the Veil for whoever sees it: whoever sees it has seen him
It is beaten by time

KODŌ (鼓動 · Kodō, the Heartbeat) · Second Release
KODŌ the Second Release is basically field projection: the power to turn the drum in his aura into a field. It opens the Domain of the same name.
Capabilities
Released, the slow copper pulse in his aura has become a drum, and the Second Release opens the field on it. He is usually on one knee with his good hand flat on his own chest when he says the word, and the field comes up from the ground, copper-red at its edges, felt through the soles and the backs of the teeth before it is heard.
Applications

Opening and powering KODŌ the Domain
Making the ground SHINZŌ-DOME needs

Associations

Anima Spirare, through the Body Path
TOSHI-GAERI, whose drum it takes up

Limitations

Held past its limit it is a Crystal Fracture Event along the Sennen road, and his own heart stops with it

SHINZŌ-DOME (心臓止め · Shinzō-dome, the Heart Stopped) · Third Release
SHINZŌ-DOME is basically death by decree: the power to stop one named heart by the law of the field, with no hand on it. It is the Akagane warrant read by KODŌ.
Capabilities
Inside KODŌ he names one heart, aloud, the way the Akagane warrant is read, and that heart stops between one beat and the next, and stays stopped. HEART-WARRANT can be pushed off by a strong man’s blood. This cannot, because inside the field the heart’s beat is his to keep or not to keep, and it stops by law and not by force.
His own heart stops with the other for as long as he holds it, kept by the Copper Heart alone. That is the only reason he can do it at all.
Applications

Killing one named enemy anywhere inside the field
Stopping a heart whose owner’s blood would push off the hand

Associations

Anima Spirare, through the Body Path, by the field’s law
KODŌ, which it can only be called inside
HEART-WARRANT, which it is at Domain size
THE COPPER HEART, which keeps him alive through it

Limitations

One heart, inside the field, named aloud, and it cannot be called twice in one field
It takes a quarter of his reserve at once
His own heart is still for as long as he holds it, and every second of that puts years on him that stay
A Sovereignty stronger than his holds against it, and so does an Oath and Integrity that will not let the body go
A body with no heart gives it nothing
It is beaten by killing him in the seconds his own heart is still

Domain
KODŌ (鼓動 · Kodō, the Heartbeat) · Domain
KODŌ the Domain is basically heartbeat synchronization: the power to make every heart within about a hundred and twenty meters beat to his. It is Anima Spirare at Domain-law, and the one piece of the art that needs no hand.
Capabilities
It is the Breath of the Living with the ground for its body. Inside the field his doctrine is the ground’s law, and the field answers every heart in it as one whole body answers a hurt, with his own heart for the signal: Anima Spirare lays his beat under every heart, and each one takes it, the way men marching fall into step with a drum without choosing to. He sets the tempo. The Measurewrights call it entrainment, one rhythm pulling its neighbors into step, and they can time it to the beat; they cannot say why a heart that has never met him keeps his.
His allies’ hearts he steadies, holds and keeps. A steadied heart pumps evenly through shock and blood loss and does not race itself to death in heat or terror, so a man run through stays on his feet and a man bleeding out goes on bleeding slowly enough to be carried. His enemies’ he slows, a beat at a time, until too little blood reaches the brain, the sight grays and the knees go, which is how a field of men falls down without a mark on them. It lays a second field inside whatever field already stands, and a heart galloping in heat or fear stumbles once and catches his step.
Applications

Keeping wounded allies on their feet and alive long enough to be carried
Dropping a field of enemies without a mark on them
Calming a heart that is racing itself to death
Using HEART-WARRANT without a hand, and calling SHINZŌ-DOME

Associations

Anima Spirare, through the Body Path: the Shell’s hold laid over a field
The Second Release, which opens it

Limitations

The price is the drum itself: the field beats to his own heart, and anything that strikes his heart, or startles it, or stops it, collapses the field at once
Every heart he holds slowed is a weight on his own, which he feels as an old man feels stairs, and the gray at his temples goes white while he holds them
It holds about two minutes from full
A practitioner of his Stage with stronger Sovereignty or Hemostasis contests it at the edge and in his own chest
The dead and the made have no heart to hold
A body running a high fever, or standing in great heat, races its own heart harder than he can slow it
It holds the heart and nothing else: in an oven it keeps a man’s heart from racing itself to death and does nothing for his brain, which cooks first
Held past his reserve his own blood starts answering every heart he is holding, and pushed to the end his own heart stops with the field
It is beaten by contesting it, by striking the drum, or by bringing something with no heart

characters/ability-accounts/thibault-le-.title: Thibault Le Lambert — Abilities in full
characters/ability-accounts/thibault-le-.content:
Card: Thibault Le Lambert
LA RÉPONSE BLANCHE
LA RÉPONSE BLANCHE (the White Answer; Responsio Alba in the Court’s Latin) is basically preemptive counter: the power to answer an attack before it has been decided, with one cut that arrives exactly where it was meant. Every ability below is that one answer at a different size.
Capabilities
Every Lambert child at Sallowgate learns the Answer, the counter-cut that turns in the hand before your blade has left its line. Nobody in the house is taught to attack, because the Answer has to be asked first. Thibault is the Lamberts’ Answer carried to Emanation, where a Trait stops being something a soul does and becomes the law of the ground around it. Near him your will is counted the moment it forms, before your breath has set or your shoulder loaded, and the answer leaves his low guard on that count. By the time your body has begun to obey you, the cut is already in your throat.
The idea is a reply that comes before the question. Its operation is Aurevane’s sublimation: the answer is raised clear of everything that would cloud it, so it arrives meaning exactly what your blow meant, returned. Nothing in it starts with him. That is why the eyes of the great lines never saw him coming. The Moto Shingan, the Zettari Everlasting Eye and the Yukari Ketsumyōgan all read what a man is about to do, and what Thibault is about to do is decided by the man looking at him. A seer who looks into his next move sees his own blow coming back.
The price comes from the same idea, and it came due at Refraction, the first time his answer moved before the question. A man who answers everything before it is asked has lost the power to ask. He cannot petition, propose or pray, and he has not asked anyone anything in thirteen years. The Veil-Saints had ordained him at twenty, and a priest who cannot ask cannot pray.
The Measurewrights have their own account, which the house confirms no more than it confirms theirs for Léonard. In their reckoning the deciding comes before the body’s readiness by a good part of a heartbeat, the Lambert blood reads the deciding, and a Stage XII Shell at a yield of 1.00 loses almost nothing between the deciding and the cut. One of them timed it at Alabaster with a water clock and entered the margin as a fifth of a heartbeat. Thibault told him it was a seventh, and the clock was slow.
Applications

Killing a duelist before his first blow has been decided
Killing a seer through the eye that reads him
Breaking a charge by answering the first tenth of it
Ending a brawl before the first punch lands

Techniques

CROC BLANC! - the single cut he is named for
À L’ŒIL! - the cut that answers a reading
LA DÎME! - the answer to a field
AVANT LA QUESTION - the Trait that counts a will as it forms
LE RÉPONS - the Domain where every question is answered

Associations

Aurevane, the True Light, governing: what he sends arrives exactly as meant, and the light does not flatter
Judicium, the Scale, deep: the true will told apart from the feint wrapped around it
The Lambert inheritance, the Computus in the blood, and the Sallowgate Answer taught on a wooden sword
The Body Path carries all of it

Limitations

An answer needs a question. A man who means no harm to him or to anyone in his charge, or a thing with no will in it, gives the art nothing to answer
The mule, the falling wall, the dead man’s trap, the panicked horse and the working that runs by itself all reach him as they would reach any man of his Stage, and his body is a Lambert’s
Aurevane’s light shows him plainly, so he is the easiest man on any field to find, and every crossbow on the wall knows where to look
Pushed too far, the glare goes out through his eyes and burns the road it leaves by; the eyes go first
He cannot begin anything that asks: a question, a petition, a prayer

Traits
ONE BEFORE · Inherited Trait
ONE BEFORE is basically intent perception: the power to start his answer a hair before the blow it answers. It is the house’s own Trait, the Computus in the body, the same in him as in Léonard and in every woken Lambert.
Capabilities
His answer begins before the delivery it answers, by a margin so slight that a spectator calls it luck. Against a blow with a will behind it, his Reflex reads a step higher than the slate says. It costs nothing, since nothing is made or thrown, and it cannot be sensed, because it comes from no working.
Applications

Moving a hair before every blow
Reading the shoulder, the breath and the foot in the order a body cannot hide

Associations

The Lambert blood; no Wellspring
The Body Path

Limitations

It reads a will and nothing else, and is slower against anything with no will in it
It tells him what a body is about to do and makes him no faster
Tell: he moves a hair before you do
Counter: a blow with no intent behind it

AVANT LA QUESTION (Before the Question) · Primary Trait
AVANT LA QUESTION is basically intent precognition: the power to count a will the moment it forms, before the body has begun to obey it. ONE BEFORE reads the shoulder; this reads the deciding.
Capabilities
It woke at Refraction, the first time his answer moved before the question, and at Emanation, where a soul’s Traits become the law of the ground around it, it became the Lambert count made law. Within about thirty paces of him, any will turned on him or on anyone in his charge is counted as it forms, whether or not the man has begun to move, and whether or not he has told himself yet. It is what lets the White Answer move before it is asked.
It reads the true will and not the show. A feint with the whole body is still a man deciding to feint, and Judicium parts the feint from the will beneath it, so the answer goes to the intent and never to the performance. The house’s oldest counter, to feint with the whole body and then strike with no thought, works on Léonard and does not work on him, because the decision to feint is itself a will turned on him, and he answers that before the thoughtless blow can follow it. It reaches past him to anyone in his charge: a will turned on the men he stands over is turned on him, as far as the blood is concerned.
Applications

Counting every will in a room that is turned on him
Telling a real threat from a bluff before the bluff is finished
Knowing which of the men around a table has decided

Associations

The Lambert inheritance, made law by Emanation
Aurevane, which shows the true thing plainly, and Judicium, which tells it apart
The Body Path

Limitations

A will must form. He cannot read what nobody means
It reads the will turned on him and not the man behind it: a hired blade’s will is read, and the man who paid for it is not
Price: it took from him the power to ask, at Refraction. He cannot begin a question, a petition or a prayer
Tell: his eyes go pale and still and settle on the place on you where the decision will come out
Counter: the mule, the falling wall, the dead man’s trap, the working that runs by itself, and the man who truly comes to him with nothing in his hands

LA DERNIÈRE ONCTION (the Last Unction) · Secondary Trait
LA DERNIÈRE ONCTION is basically soul guiding: the power to send the men he kills across the Veil whole. It formed in the Rimward plague years, when he was a Veil-Saint, and it stayed when the Court cut his name from the roll.
Capabilities
The passage of the dead on the Sea’s ground has not gone right since the working that drowned the low country, and the Veil-Saints are paid to sit with the dying so the soul crosses without fragmenting. Thibault still says the commendation, in the old Latin, over every man he kills, with two fingers on the brow before the body is cold: Proficiscere, anima, go forth, soul. It is a command and not a petition, which is why he can still say it. The South knows what follows, and it is half of why the White Fang’s name is said the way it is: his dead do not walk.
The idea is Thaloré’s dissolution, a feeling let down through the whole soul to its true depth, where the soul takes the shape of what holds it. For the length of the crossing what holds the dead man is Thibault. The soul goes across in his shape, whole and closed, with no loose edge for a ghost to rise from, a dying curse to ride out on, or an art that feeds on the dead to take hold of.
Applications

Ending a fight with no haunting after it
Denying a necromancer or a soul-eater the men he has killed
Sitting with the dying of Rimward, who still send for him

Associations

Thaloré, the Heavy Heart, the ground of the Sounding Walk
The Spirit Path, a Stage behind the Body
The Veil-Saints of Rimward

Limitations

Only the men he kills himself, and only if he speaks the commendation before the body is cold
Cost: about a tenth of one percent of his reserve for each soul, and the soul’s full weight for the length of the crossing. A bad death presses on the Core, and if his footing gives under a heavy one, the weight goes down through him instead of across
Tell: Proficiscere, anima under his breath, and two fingers on the dead man’s brow
Counter: a soul taken before he can reach it, or ground and Domains that hold the dead

Techniques
CROC BLANC! (White Fang!) · Signature Technique
CROC BLANC! is basically preemptive strike: the power to kill a man with one cut before he has decided to strike. It is the cut he is named for.
Capabilities
When your will to strike him forms, the cut has already left the low guard. It rises along the line your blow would have taken and goes into the throat, or the wrist, or wherever on you the decision was going to come out. Aurevane puts every ounce of it on the span of skin it was meant for, so the cut is an S-Grade edge on a target the width of a finger. The men who have watched it describe one white flash, seen and gone, like a fang in a dark mouth, and that is where the name came from.
Applications

The end of a duel
The end of an assassin
The end of anyone who decides

Associations

Aurevane, the Sallowgate Answer, AMEN
The Body Path

Limitations

One man, one will, one cut. It does not answer a second man in the same heartbeat
Cost: about seven tenths of one percent of his reserve, near 4.4 million EU, spent in under a second; about a hundred and forty from full
Tell: the white flash, one clean high tone, and nothing before it
Counter: a blow with no will in it, such as the mule, the trap or a bolt loosed on a timed order; or a Fate fighter who removes what the cut depends on before it leaves the guard

À L’ŒIL! (To the Eye!) · Technique
À L’ŒIL! is basically perception counter: the power to answer a seer’s reading with a cut into the eye that read him. It is how the White Fang killed the great lines’ seers.
Capabilities
To the blood, a reading is a will turned on him, because a reading is a question. He answers it. A seer who looks into his next move sees only his own blow coming back, and while he is still looking, the point of AMEN goes into the eye that read him. The Shingan, the Everlasting Eye and the Ketsumyōgan all read what is coming, and what was coming was the answer to their reading.
Applications

Killing a seer at a blade’s reach
Blinding a reader who would not die of it
Teaching a whole army’s scouts not to look at him

Associations

Aurevane and Judicium
The Body Path

Limitations

Only an eye that reads him, and only within the reach of the blade or a step
Cost: about four tenths of one percent of his reserve, near 2.5 million EU
Tell: he meets the reader’s eye before the reader has finished looking
Counter: look away; send someone else to read him; read him from out of reach

LA DÎME! (The Tithe!) · Technique
LA DÎME! is basically mass counter: the power to answer the first tenth of a charge before the rest of it has finished deciding.
Capabilities
A tithe is the tenth the Church takes of everything, and he takes it of a charge. Against a rush or a volley he answers the wills turned on him in the order they formed, until a tenth of them have fallen, all inside one long breath of about six seconds. The other nine of every ten are left standing to see it. Most charges have stopped by then.
Applications

Breaking a charge with its own front rank
Breaking a volley by killing the archers who had decided first

Associations

Aurevane
The Body Path

Limitations

A tenth and no more; the rest are left alive
Cost: about six percent of his reserve, near 38 million EU, over one long breath; rarely used twice in a fight
Tell: he says “la dîme” quietly, as a priest says it at the collection
Counter: men who do not mean it, conscripts driven from behind, and crossbows loosed on a timed order, with no will in the loosing

Releases
BLANC DE NEIGE (Snow-White) · First Release
BLANC DE NEIGE is basically light-clad enhancement: the power to bring his aura up hard and white over the skin and read faster than he already does. The call is “Blanc.”
Capabilities
The white of his hair goes hard and lit from the roots outward, like frost on a pane at dawn, and the aura comes up close on the skin, hard-edged, with no soft part anywhere on it. His Reflex and Forecast read a step higher while it holds. Called silently, it rises less and lasts longer.
Applications

Holding the Stair against a crowd that has all decided
A duel with a Grandmaster who reads as fast as he does

Associations

Aurevane, which he touched on the snow above the shelf at Stage IV and took for good at Stage VIII
The Body Path; AMEN carries none of it

Limitations

Cost: about 1.2 million EU a second, near nine minutes from a full reserve
The light shows him to every crossbow on the wall
Counter: Tenebra, fog, any room caged in iron

LA CHAIRE (the Pulpit) · Second Release
LA CHAIRE is basically domain activation: the power to open his Domain. The call is “En chaire.”
Capabilities
A ring and a triangle of hard light stand behind his head like the halos the Court paints on its saints, AMEN’s edge goes white, and LE RÉPONS opens around him. At Refraction it only lit the Domain’s seed; from Transcendence it opens the whole of it. With the First Release under it, it carries him two steps over his sustainable line.
Applications

Opening LE RÉPONS

Associations

Aurevane; AMEN, whose edge whitens
The Body Path

Limitations

Cost: about 2.6 million EU a second; with the First under it, 3.8 million, near two minutes and three quarters from a full reserve
Tell: the halo behind his head
Counter: anything that breaks his Domain

LA MÂCHOIRE (the Jaw) · Third Release
LA MÂCHOIRE is basically total counter: the power to answer every will turned on him within a sword’s reach from two sides at once. The call is “La mâchoire.”
Capabilities
The white closes round him in the shape of a jaw, and AMEN’s edge is the lower teeth. Inside its reach a will turned on him is answered by the blade and by the light together. It fills the two-step cap by itself. It is on record three times.
Applications

A ring of Zettari who have all decided at once
A room where every man in it means it

Associations

Aurevane and Judicium
The Body Path; AMEN carries the lower teeth

Limitations

Cost: about 4 million EU a second, near two and a half minutes from a full reserve
It leaves no room in the cap for anything else
Tell: the light takes the shape of teeth
Counter: a man who comes in with no will at all, or a blow from outside the jaw’s reach

Domain
LE RÉPONS (the Responsory · Responsorium) · Domain
LE RÉPONS is basically answer domain: the power to make a place where every question raised is answered, and he is the answer. A responsory is the part of the liturgy where the cantor calls and the choir replies, and he named it for that.
Capabilities
LA CHAIRE opens it, and at Emanation it holds itself once open. The ground inside goes white, as the Walk goes wet under a true oath, and the light in the place comes from no lamp. Inside it, no will turned on him or on anyone in his charge goes uncounted at any distance, and no blow struck in anger reaches anyone before his answer reaches the striker. On open ground it runs about a hundred paces across.
Applications

Holding a gate, a hall or a stair
Ending a riot without drawing
Fighting more men than LA DÎME can answer

Associations

Aurevane
The Body Path; the Second Release opens it

Limitations

A will must form inside it; a working that runs by itself passes through
Counter: another Domain with a law that refuses his, a Fate claim on the ground, or a Zenith

characters/ability-accounts/tizz-copperw.title: Tizz Copperwick — Abilities in full
characters/ability-accounts/tizz-copperw.content:
Card: Tizz Copperwick
Techniques
THE LONG ARM, MARK FOUR · Signature art, a Tinker Goblin’s Spliced Runes
THE LONG ARM, MARK FOUR is basically ratcheted strength: the power to win ground one click at a time and never lose any of it. She built a ratchet into her own elbow, and she cut the idea into herself at fifteen with a mirror and a hot needle: a goblin’s temper comes in beats, so build a thing that keeps each beat. She has no Traits of her own; what she has by blood is her people’s.
Capabilities
Tinker Goblins are souls with more pressure in them than the frame can hold, and their people’s answer is the Spliced Rune, a line of marks cut into one limb that gives the pressure a road to run on. Hers begin in a copper socket at the left shoulder, cut close and fine as a page of writing, and run on out of the metal into her own skin as pale blue scars up her neck, so that nobody can say where she ends and the arm begins. Everything the arm does is her Essence sent down those marks, with a ratchet at the elbow deciding what is kept. Essence is spiritual energy: the ground’s raw Aether, which carters call mana, after the Crystal behind her breastbone has set her own color in it.
A ratchet is a toothed wheel with a small iron finger, the pawl, riding on it. The wheel may turn one way, and the moment it tries to turn back the pawl drops behind a tooth and stops it. She drives her Essence down the runes in beats, like a heart, and each beat is a pulse of blue that buys one tooth while the pawl keeps it. Between beats the load rests on the pawl, the arm rests on the load, and she rests. The arm adds no strength; it only keeps her from losing ground. That is how a goblin of three foot five lifts the four-ton outer grille of her gate by the inch and never holds it. The gate helps, because the Copperwicks built it to: the grille hangs against a counterweight a hair under four ton, so all anyone lifts is the hair, about ten stone, and the drag of a dozen chains in their wheels, and the windlass crank is as long as a man’s arm, which trades distance for force the way any lever does.
Anyone watching can read it coming. She sets her boots wide, closes the copper fingers on the work one by one, and winds the brass key in her elbow three full turns with her burned hand, until the pawl sits quivering at the top of its wheel. Then her eyes light, every window at once, bright enough to throw her shadow behind her, and she breathes in long. The breath is the pull: the air round her goes thin and cold and the dust on the floor stirs toward her boots. The whole arm lights from the shoulder down in hard blue lines like the leading of a church window with the sun behind it, and her colors come up close on her like a second coat.
Less than half the pull reaches the crank, and that share is her yield. The rest burns in the arm as heat, the way a rope run fast through a fist burns the fist, and the copper shows it honestly. Hot copper grows a skin of tarnish, thicker the hotter it gets, and light coming back through a skin that thin is colored by how thick it is, as oil is on a puddle, so the copper tempers straw to purple-blue, sliding from the elbow and the knuckles toward her shoulder as the beats go on. With no load on the arm a small beat has nothing to turn, so all of it arrives as heat at the end of the line, which is how the thumb melts wax.
The arm is also her temper’s safety valve, by Ned’s inference: the runes carry her temper out of her as well as into the arm. A Tinker Goblin who loses her temper can go off all at once and take the room along, which scholars call Emotional Detonation and Tollgarth calls a reason to keep buckets by the door. The arm is a place to put it, a crank she can turn it into, one tooth at a time.
Applications

Lifting the four-ton outer grille of her own gate, a finger’s breadth of grille to a tooth
Melting sealing wax with the copper thumb and signing it in the same touch, since the ball of the thumb is cut flat and engraved
Letting her temper out as a spin and not as a blast

Techniques

BY THE INCH! - boots planted, the copper hand shut on the work, and the arm turns a tooth at a beat with a pulse of blue down the runes, the pawl keeping every tooth
THAT’S A DEED! - one short turn of the key and the copper thumb goes dull red from nail to knuckle; on wax it is the Queen’s seal, and nobody has yet asked what it is on a hand
MIND YOUR TEMPER - every window of her eyes goes dark, the key goes back one full turn against the ratchet, the pawl lifts and the wheel runs down; she does not shout this one

Associations

The Spliced Runes of the Tinker Goblins, her people’s craft and her own cutting, in the Form of a Make
The made left arm itself: black enamel over copper, a saucer-sized ratchet wheel with its iron pawl at the elbow and a brass wind-key standing out of the joint; it is built into her shoulder and is no bonded weapon
By her own word the arm is “Rare, if it’s anything”, and it has never been put on a beam
The Tollgarth gate, counterweighted by the Copperwicks so that it can be lifted this way
Her seal, a candle with a crown on its flame; nobody steals the Queen of Tollgarth’s seal without taking the Queen of Tollgarth’s arm
Her colors are the clean hot blue at the root of a solder flame, close to the skin, with a smell of hot metal, burned vitriol and scorched paper
The Tinker temper, which is her people’s by blood and is the arm’s fuel
Her Stage and Path are not given

Limitations

The wheel’s own: it cannot move a thing by less than one tooth or faster than one beat, and it goes one way only until the key is turned back
By the wheel’s own law it is slow, a tooth to a breath and three turns of a key first, so it is beaten by being finished before she is wound
Lift the pawl and everything it has kept runs back at once
Poor ground starves it: at a crowded gate, in a town where every goblin has been pulling at the same hills since sunup, the breath has to run very long before she has her fill
Less than half the pull reaches the work, and the rest is heat: after the copper tempers, the black enamel blisters and smokes, her sweat hisses where it drops on her own wrist, she breathes a breath to a tooth, and her colors thin until the coat shows through them
The room answers the heat too: the far wall wavers through the blue as a road wavers in summer, the smell of scorched paper and burned vitriol comes off her in a wave, and every little spring bell in the tower rings faintly by itself
Copper that has gone blue and enamel that has blistered are an arm run past what it was built for
The fuel is her temper, which is the thing she has to mind to see forty; by her own count she has seven years in her only if she minds it, and she says she never does
BY THE INCH! shows as blue pulses down the runes and a tooth of the elbow ratchet at each beat
THAT’S A DEED! shows as one short turn of the key and blue in the neck scars for no longer than a breath, with her own breath coming short the once, as if she had run up a stair; it is one thumb on a short arm, and the way to beat it is to stay off the end of it
MIND YOUR TEMPER has to be reached in time, and a valve can fill faster than a hand can reach the key; no counter is wanted, since everybody in the room is hoping it works
When the temper is filling the air goes tight, the smells sharpen, the rune scars light thin blue and the key turns by itself, and all Tollgarth knows the answer: two paces back and a bucket chain

characters/ability-accounts/ulf-stark-—-.title: Ulf Stark — Abilities in full
characters/ability-accounts/ulf-stark-—-.content:
Card: Ulf Stark
AND THEN WE GIVE SOME MORE
AND THEN WE GIVE SOME MORE is basically charity embodiment: the power to give away everything he’s got, and to always know who can carry it. It is his signature art, and it is one idea that the house had before he did. A Stark gives, and every ability below is that giving in a different part of him.
Capabilities
The cold in the blood is the first of it: a Stark’s body hands its heat down into the ground and keeps none back. The rest is that same habit grown up into a lord. He looks at a man to learn what can be handed to him, he hands it over, and the handing-over is the only time in his day that he is not afraid.
The Winter Road is the house giving its riders to the snow so that the north does not have to give its villages to the Tenrai. He has put the whole art in one sentence himself, and says it to anyone under forty: that’s just the way this life is, lad, we give, and we give, and then we give some more.
Applications

Learning what can be handed to a man before handing it over
Giving up his brother, his riders, his granaries, his house and his neck
Handing the heat of everything near him down into the ground
Giving the house’s riders to the snow in place of the north’s villages

Techniques

THE MAKING OF A GENERAL - the look that tells him who can carry what
WE GIVE - the giving itself, and the steady hand that comes with it
STARK RIME - the cold in the blood, a body that keeps no heat back
THE WINTER ROAD - the house’s way of war, paid for in riders

Associations

The Body Path, Mastered, does the cold, the sword and the road
His Walked Fate carries the look and the giving, with a little Studied Spirit in the look
The Stark cold, the house’s inheritance and no Wellspring, is the lens for the rime
The look and the giving are his own soul’s habits, and the Winter Road is a taught craft of war

Limitations

It only goes one way: nothing is promised back
The last thing on the list is his neck

Traits
THE MAKING OF A GENERAL · Primary Trait
THE MAKING OF A GENERAL is basically potential detection: the power to take one long look at a man and know what that man can carry and how far. It is the look his signature art runs on, and it is very seldom wrong.
Capabilities
The look is forty winters of picking roads, become a law of his soul. A road is a question about load: how much weight, on what footing, for how many days, before something gives. He learned to answer it for timber bridges and river ice and tired horses, and somewhere in those winters his Crystal (the soul itself, which grows around whatever a person does most) stopped telling the difference between a road and a man. His soul reads a man the way it reads ground.
So he reads a man’s bearing, the way the weight sits, the way he goes quiet before he moves, what a room does when he walks into it, and he comes away knowing what that man will hold up under. Then he says, “Ah. So there he is.” It works best with the man under load, which is why he does not trust a look across a table when he can arrange a road instead.
He has seen two men in his life with what the boy has, and one of them is dead and the other is sitting in this chair. He rode beside Gimbzo for two summers, and knew that weight again on a sixteen-year-old sitting on a stool.
Applications

Learning what can be handed to a man before it is handed over
Feeling the great ones at ten paces
Testing a man by arranging a hard road and counting the wagons that come out

Associations

His Walked Fate, landing through a little Studied Spirit as a reading; a small use that opens no gate
Forty winters of picking roads
Gimbzo, the first weight of that kind he knew

Limitations

It reads what a man can carry, not what he will choose
Those two summers are the proof: he read what Gimbzo could carry, and he was right, and it told him nothing about what the man would do with it
It costs nothing, because nothing is made or thrown: it is a read, and it runs on his eyes and his years
Its tell is the long look, the pale eyes going over a man the way they go over a ford, the black iron ring turning in the beard-braid under his thumb, and then the line
A man who shows him nothing beats it: stand still, keep your hands quiet, carry nothing in front of him, and never take the road he offers

WE GIVE · Secondary Trait
WE GIVE is basically fear immunity: the power to be beyond the reach of fear for as long as he is giving something away. It formed the day Torvald’s head came back with a note.
Capabilities
He gives: his brother, his riders, his granaries, his house, his neck. While he is giving, fear does not reach him and his hands do not shake. He rode south to the Kurenai blade at an easy walk.
Fear is the body guarding what it still has to lose. It tightens the chest, quickens the heart and sets the fine shake in the fingers, all to make a man hold on harder to the thing in danger. WE GIVE takes away the thing fear is holding on to. When he has decided a thing is given, his soul closes the account on it before the body has heard, and a body with nothing left to guard has no reason to shake.
It is kin to a vow, which is small Fate and anyone’s to make, and his Walked Fate is why his holds so cleanly. He swore the whole house of Stark to a tokenless boy before witnesses and before the Sky, with his maimed hand flat on his chest, and the hand lay still.
Applications

Riding south to the Kurenai blade at an easy walk
Swearing away the whole house with a still hand
Handing over riders, granaries and harness without flinching

Associations

His Walked Fate, as a binding
Torvald Stark, his brother, whose death formed it
The vow, which is small Fate and anyone’s to make

Limitations

It is all one way; nobody promises the Starks anything back, not the Sky, not the lines, not the people they give it for
It works only on what is his: he cannot give away another man’s life and feel nothing
The boys younger than sixteen he lets lie their way into the vanguard are a weight the Trait does not lift
It steadies the hand and adds no step
It costs everything, and he does not count it
Its tell is a sentence and never a gesture: by the time he says “That’s just the way this life is, lad,” the giving is done and his hands are already quiet
What beats it is something he would not give, and nobody has found it
The nearest anyone came was Wystan Greymane, who talked him into keeping one thing back, the boy’s own name, and Ulf sat on it like a man selling a horse with a cracked hoof under a blanket

STARK RIME · Inherited Trait
STARK RIME is basically heat transferal: the power to move the warmth out of everything near him and send it down through his heels into the ground. It is the cold in the Stark blood at Glory’s clarity, an inheritance of the house and no Wellspring.
Capabilities
It does one thing, the one rule the Stark blood has, which is that it moves heat out and never in. Warmth runs from the warm thing to the cold one, as it always has, and a Stark’s body is a road for it, in at the skin and the hands and out through the soles into the ground, which can take more of it than any man can give. That is why the Starks walk the way they walk. For yards round him timber silvers, snow stiffens and squeaks, his breath stops steaming, and the fur of his wolf-hood goes white. Rime is what the damp in the air does when it meets something that cold: it freezes straight onto the fur and the steel in white needles. It runs harder under feeling.
At rest it spends nothing. To drive it he pulls Aether (mana) up out of the ground he stands on, packs it raw in his Shell (the body-side layer of the soul) as Charge, and sends it out through the Shell. A little over three fifths of what he spends reaches the world, which is his yield, and the rest goes as a deep groan in the frozen ground under his boots. At his rung a Body fighter commands matter as an object, so the rime bites hardest on what his hands are on. That is Marchstone. Steel carries warmth far more readily than flesh does, something like a hundred times by the Measurewrights’ reckoning, so when he sets the cold through the cross the broad double fuller runs white from the hilt to the point in a breath.
That climb is the visible charge, and it rides the blow. The edge does a great sword’s work on harness and bone, and the cold goes in behind it, the warmth of the wound walking out along the blade, up his arms and down through him. Chilled muscle is slow, weak muscle, and wet flesh freezes fast to cold steel, so the man on the end of the cut loses the limb’s strength from the wound outward and finds the blade hard to shake loose.
Applications

Setting the cold through Marchstone so it goes in behind the cut
Taking the strength out of a wounded limb and freezing the blade fast in it
Hardening snow as hard as a floor for yards round him
Stiffening a crust for the Winter Road’s horses and setting slush over river ice

Associations

The Stark cold, the house’s inheritance, with no Wellspring behind it
The Body Path, shaping and striking
Marchstone, the Warlord’s great sword, which it bites hardest on
The Stark walk, the weight straight down through the heels

Limitations

It moves heat and cannot make it
On ground already frozen to the bottom there is little left for it to take
Against a real fire it is a bucket against a furnace
At rest it takes no reserve; driven, a little over three fifths of what he spends reaches the world and the rest is lost into the ground
Pushed past what his body can pass along, the cold stops in him on the way down: white fingers first, then a slow, stupid hand on the cross, which a man two fingers short cannot afford
Its tell is that his breath stops steaming and the wolf-fur goes white, and anyone facing him can watch the white climb the fuller
Heat and calm beat it: a brazier at your back, a warm blade, and nothing said about his brother

Techniques
THE WINTER ROAD · House Art, Stark · Signature
THE WINTER ROAD is basically winter warfare: the power to move riders through the snow while the other side sits by the fire, and to come out of the white from the side nobody was watching. It is a taught school art of the house and every Stark captain rides it; his is the one the north measures against Old Harald Keld’s, and finds second.
Capabilities
It is a craft of war before it is anything else, and the craft is sound on its own. An army in winter is tied to its roads, its roofs and its fires. Its wagons cannot leave the packed track, its men cannot sleep away from a hearth, and every fire it lights can be seen for miles and counted.
A Stark column carries no wagons. It is light, each rider has his own days of food on his back, the rest is waiting in caches laid along scouted routes in autumn, and the men are turned through warm halls in shifts so that no one company stays out long enough for the cold to start taking fingers. They go for the other side’s cook-fires and fodder, never for his walls, and a garrison that has lost its supper two nights running will come out and fight on ground the Starks chose.
The Stark rime makes the cold an ally. Where a Stark lord rides at the head of a column, wet snow stiffens into a crust that bears a horse, and slush over river ice sets hard for the few yards his cold reaches, so the house crosses where a southern scout has written “no crossing.”
Applications

Arriving from somewhere nobody was watching
Burning cook-fires and fodder until a garrison comes out to fight
Crossing rivers and snowfields a southern scout has marked impassable
Holding the passes, as the Starks held them against the Zettari for forty years

Associations

House Stark, which teaches it to every captain
His father, and Old Harald Keld’s example, the only man who ever did it better
STARK RIME, which hardens the crust and the river ice
The Body Path, for the road

Limitations

The thaw stops it: in mud the caches flood, the crust rots, and the tracks show black for anyone to follow
In a thaw a light column with no wagons is just a small army a long way from home
It takes nothing from his reserve and is paid in riders, not by the lord: frostbite, lost horses, boys who sat down in the snow to rest
It has no tell: he has already moved before you knew he was coming
A fire, a thaw and a scout who does not sleep beat it
A garrison that stays warm, fed and behind its wall cannot be starved out by the weather
One waking man on the right ridge undoes a month of marching

characters/ability-accounts/vaashuuk-sno.title: Vaashuuk Snorr-Khal — Abilities in full
characters/ability-accounts/vaashuuk-sno.content:
Card: Vaashuuk Snorr-Khal · The Sin of Sloth
NOTHIN’ GETS DONE
NOTHIN’ GETS DONE (Vaross · Dok-Snorr, striking-at, asleep) is basically viscosity manipulation: the power to make the world go thick as tar, so that the harder you swing the slower you go and nothing anybody starts near him ever gets finished. It is his signature art, and his Traits, techniques, Releases and Domain are all this one idea: things stop before they are done.
Capabilities
The Sleep Crown he slept on for a year is Hypnather, the idea of change that comes only at rest, the soul setting itself in order in the dark while nothing is asked of it, and its operation is coagulation: left at rest, a thing slowly sets into an order it never had time to reach. A year asleep on its Core set his Crystal that way, never finished, always settling, and he does to a room what it did to him. His claim lays the air down to rest, and air at rest thickens and goes on thickening, like a sleeper sinking, until it has stopped flowing for any purpose that matters. It sets like a glass. The Measurewrights call the settling structural relaxation and say he drives the air toward the glass transition; they have good figures for how thick, and no idea why a goblin’s nap does it. The pitch in the philosophers’ funnel at Stannvaard is the picture he uses himself: it is flowing, and it drops once every ten winters.
Rest will not be hurried, and that is why the thickness stiffens under a blow. A slow hand asks little of the rested air and passes; a fast one asks to be let through at once, which is the one thing rest refuses, so the glass barely resists a slow hand and fights a fast one harder the harder it comes. Stir cornflour into water and a slow spoon passes through soup while a punch lands on a brick; the scholars call that shear thickening, and the glass behaves the same way. He never strikes anyone, and he does not need to. The blow that does not land goes somewhere, and where it goes is back up the arm that threw it. That is how the art rides a blow: the other fighter supplies the blow, and the glass returns it.
He moves through all of it at his ordinary amble because of Abython, the Abyssal Pulse, the idea of peace with the abyss, whose operation is dissolution: the soul’s difference from what surrounds it is loosed into it until nothing is left between them. A fish in a river feels no current, because it is carried at the river’s own pace; he has made his peace with his own thick air in the same way, keeps nothing of himself set against it, and so it does not drag on him. The charge is the yawn, and nobody has ever missed it. His jaw cracks, his eyes screw shut, one claw goes politely over his mouth, and the drowsy lavender round him thickens and goes level like a bath filling. He pulls Aether up out of whatever ground he happens to be lying over, the Crystal refines it into Essence, and the claim goes out through his Attraction Layer with almost nothing lost on the way.
Applications

Slowing everything that moves through a stretch of air
Turning a fast blow back on the one who threw it
Setting air hard as a pane, a plug or a bed
Undoing motion, ending heat, and stopping anything new from starting
Running his own body slow and cheap
Staying off every slate, since his fields only stand and wait

Techniques

TORPOR - the glass turned on his own body: he runs as slow and cheap as a dormouse in winter
DOK - the fracture under all of it: nothing he does is ever finished
DROWSE - the leak: everyone near him yawns
TAR TIME - the yawn that thickens a sphere of air
THE SNOOZE-GLASS DROP - one TAR TIME banked in a glass bubble, opened with no yawn
THE CHAISE - a slab of glassed air he lies on
THE WAITER’S WAVE - a hand that sets one piece of the glass harder: a pane, a plug, a slab
THE INFINITE DO-OVER - the field rocked back and forth so every motion comes home
PLAN B - the Crown forced, so pieces of the field stop all the way down
FEATHERBED - THE CHAISE grown large: the bed, and TORPOR at its deepest
THE LIE-IN - the One, his only Release, which counts as his Second, and the Domain: nothing new can start

Associations

Hypnather, the Sleep Crown, a Spirit Wellspring he was baptized in at its Core, makes the glass
Abython, the Abyssal Pulse, a Wild Wellspring, matches him to his own thick air
Nyxial, the Nocturne Flame, a Spirit Wellspring, holds heat for him
The Fate Path, which he has mastered, lays the fields; the Spirit Path, which he walks, turns the Crown on minds and on his own Crystal
Self-taught by sleeping on a Wellspring
He bonds no weapon and does not carry anything heavy; the Snooze-Glass rides at his shoulder
He does not shout these. Shouting is work. A name comes out of him on the back end of a yawn, in Vaross or in Common, whichever is less effort, and he raises his voice only to heckle and to complain

Limitations

His fields do not kill. They stand in the road and wait, and whatever dies in them is finished by its own speed or by somebody else’s hand
He cannot finish anything, his own kills, oaths and loves included, and he cannot start anything fast
Every working that wakes him properly costs him the only thing he values, which is lying still
The yawn is the tell, and DROWSE carries it ahead of the working, so every jaw in fifty paces has caught it by the time the air begins to change
About six parts in a hundred of what he spends never reach the world, and on a Fate soul that share ties a knot; his are too small for him to notice
Each piece fails in its own way: a dropped field lets go of everything it held in the same instant, with him standing in the middle of it; a fire held against under Nyxial comes back out of him all at once; and TORPOR lasts only as long as the Crystal holds him there
Against a higher Stage the art fails from the outside in: a stronger Sovereignty takes the Domain back hall by hall, a working that cancels a law the air is carrying cuts a path through TAR TIME, a glyph of unmaking shatters a pane from the inside, and a judge who reads what a soul has decided it is finds in him nothing to read
He has never trained an eye for anything fast, and he will not see it
He has no other Release: the Fate road gives a soul the One and no more
It is beaten by hitting him before the yawn; after it, by coming slow and breathing slow, running hot, turning one way, counting the Snooze-Glass, staying between the pieces of PLAN B, walking out of the Lie-In, or cornering him until he has to finish something
A judge who reads what a soul has decided it is can rule on the hole: it can crack his hold on the Sleep Crown and part the tether between his Crystal and its Wellspring in one cut, and then the Crystal leaves him and TORPOR’s long low pressure lets go like a diver hauled up too fast

Traits
TORPOR (Vaross · Snaal) · Primary Trait
TORPOR is basically hibernation: the power to idle his body and his Crystal at a floor most creatures reach only in winter sleep. It is the Sleep Crown turned on himself.
Capabilities
A dormouse in winter drops its heart to a few beats a minute and burns almost nothing, and he lives there. Everything in him runs slow and cheap: poisons and venoms work through him at a crawl, bleeding is sluggish because there is so little pressure behind it, his reserve barely moves when he is not using it, and when he sleeps under Hypnather he recovers three times as fast as he would awake. His blood is dark as plum wine and comes slowly, welling in a cut and hanging there in a fat bead, and he mends at the same sleeping pace: a cut hand draws to a pink seam in an afternoon.
It is a held state, a body kept at low pressure by the Crystal the way a diver is kept by the weight of the sea.
Applications

Slowing poison and venom to a crawl
Barely bleeding from a wound
Refilling his reserve three times as fast asleep
Spending almost nothing at rest

Associations

Hypnather, through the Spirit Path, written on his own Crystal
FEATHERBED, which takes it as deep as his Fate II will carry it

Limitations

It all rests on the Crystal’s hold: every wound he takes clots and pinches at a sleeping heart’s pace only for as long as the Crystal holds him there
A body kept at a low pressure for ninety years has never learned to bear an ordinary one
He wakes slowly: from a cold start his reactions lag, his thinking is foggy for a few breaths, and he could not run if he wanted to
A torpid animal is the easiest kill in the forest for anything quick, and he is the same
The tell is that he never hurries, even when he should
It is beaten by speed and surprise: hit him early, hard and fast, before he has yawned and before he is awake, and the whole sheet is a slow, soft goblin in a big coat

DOK (Vaross · Striking-At) · Secondary Trait
DOK is basically perpetual incompletion: the power to never have finished anything, so that nothing can be pinned on him. It belongs to no Wellspring. It is a fracture in his Attraction Layer, the layer of the Crystal that holds a soul’s share of fate.
Capabilities
In Vaross a doubled consonant marks a finished act: dok is to strike at, dokk is to have struck. Vaashuuk lives in the undoubled form. When the bellows-gang died he had done nothing, and the Plane of Fate wrote that down as exactly what it was. The fracture was written the night he lay down and let the roof come, and it is held open by an Obsession Force with nothing to grip. Since then nothing he does ever closes. His acts stay open in the Attraction Layer, and any working that needs a completed act to anchor to slides off him like rain off oiled cloth.
It is also the wall round his whole art. Whatever dies in one of his fields is, on his slate, nothing at all.
Applications

Showing a soul-reading no killing, because he has never completed one; the Kurenai eye read his chest and found a clean slate
Giving an oath-binding no oath to grip, because Oath 1 holds nothing
Leaving a grudge nothing banked against him, because he has never landed a blow that finished; the Wrath’s grudge had no blow of his to burn by
Leaving a working that sets a spoken promise no end to find; a Yukari smoke-working neither bent his promise nor set it

Associations

The Fate Path, with no Wellspring: a fracture feature of his own Attraction Layer, held by Obsession Force
The one grip his soul won for itself, lying in the coal-store, with no blood and no blessing behind it
The cave-in at the bellows-gang, which left an act open for good, and every act after it
THE WAITER’S WAVE, whose squash it stops half-set

Limitations

The price is total: he cannot finish anything either. He cannot complete a kill even when he wants to; he cannot keep a promise, finish a task or hold a love to its end, and every job he is given has to be the kind that someone else finishes
It shows in a fight as a hand that stops: a slab he begins to set on a chest goes half hard and will go no further, while he frowns at his own palm
Every verb he speaks is unfinished, and near a working that sets true speech the padding fell off his boast and what was left was “I’ll just start.”
A judge who reads what a soul has decided it is finds the same hole from the other side, and a hole can be ruled on
It is beaten by making him finish something: corner him with no way out but to strike to completion, or bind him to a deal he must close to survive, and the moment the act closes the Trait goes thin and every reading, oath and grudge that slid off him sticks at once

DROWSE (Heavy Air) · Passive Trait
DROWSE is basically sleep inducement: the power to make everything near him drowsy without trying. Hypnather leaks off him the way heat leaks off a stove.
Capabilities
Within about ten yards of him people yawn, eyelids grow heavy, attention drifts and reactions slow by a hair. Flames lean low and burn smaller, dust settles faster, a stirred cup stops swirling sooner, and an untrained guard on a long watch near him will be asleep inside the hour. It travels wherever his glass does, a seam in a wall included. It carries the yawn before the working arrives.
Applications

Stealing a beat between seeing and cutting, with one caught yawn
Putting a guard on a long watch to sleep
Reaching through a wall by a seam

Associations

Hypnather; the Fate Path for the reach, and the Spirit Path for what it does to a mind
It is unshaped, a leak and no working

Limitations

It costs nothing and he cannot switch it off, which makes him terrible company at parties and useless as a sentry
Everyone near him yawning is the tell
It is beaten by anything that wakes the body: noise, pain, cold water, a stimulant, or a practitioner whose Ignivale or whose plain fury keeps the fire lit

Techniques
TAR TIME · Signature Technique
TAR TIME is basically motion slowing: the power to thicken a sphere of air until everything moving through it crawls. It is the art at its plainest.
Capabilities
He yawns, enormously, and the air inside a sphere forty yards across, out to a hundred and twenty when he bothers, lies down to rest and starts to set. Everything that has to travel through space slows with the air: steam, smoke, a fire’s spread, a thrown weapon, a working’s flight, and the salts that carry a signal down a nerve, so a body inside it thinks at its own pace and moves at the field’s. Rest will not be hurried, so a slow push passes almost freely and the faster the blow, the thicker the world it meets. A bird flung at his face like a spear folded its own neck against the air a hand from his nose.
A small one needs only a small yawn, and can glass the air round a single fist and leave the arm hanging there mid-haul. The field also keeps what falls in it. Blood, thrown clods, breath and rice-mist hang where they stopped. He walks through it at his ordinary amble, because Abython equalizes him to it.
Applications

Slowing a thrown spear to a walk
Stopping steam, smoke and the spread of fire
Slowing a working in flight
Catching one fist in the air
Giving THE WAITER’S WAVE and THE INFINITE DO-OVER the glass they work in

Associations

Hypnather, with Abython for his own passage
The Fate Path for the field and its reach
THE SNOOZE-GLASS DROP, which is one of these banked overnight

Limitations

The glass is rest laid on whatever travels through it, and heat is restlessness, the one thing in a thing that will not lie down, so heat is untouched and keeps building, and a rest that is stirred goes soft; the Measurewrights say the glass slows motion through space and never the shaking of a thing’s smallest pieces where they stand, which is what they take heat to be
When he drops it, everything held in it comes loose at once, and he is standing in the middle of it
It takes 0.3 percent of his reserve a second and holds 5 minutes 33 seconds from full
The tell is the big yawn, long, loud and obvious, and then the air going glossy and steam ceasing to rise
What hangs in the field tells a watcher exactly how far the glass reaches, and anyone out of the forty yards when the yawn ends is outside it
A working that cancels a law the air is carrying, as the Yukari Null-Light does, cuts a path of plain air through it no wider than the blade, and a blow can come down that path at its own speed
It is beaten by moving slowly, which the field barely resists, by running hot, because heat will not lie down and thins it fast, or by stepping out of the radius

THE SNOOZE-GLASS DROP · Signature Technique
THE SNOOZE-GLASS DROP is basically stored casting: the power to bank one whole TAR TIME in a glass bubble and open it later with no yawn. It is the one way he has found to skip the yawn.
Capabilities
Overnight, while he sleeps, he lets a full TAR TIME’s worth of glassed air settle into the brass-banded glass bubble that floats at his shoulder, held ready. He drops the bubble and the field opens around him with no yawn and no warning. A fresh field is whole and cold, and it closes any hot channel that has been bored through the old one.
Applications

Opening a field on an enemy who was waiting for the yawn
Closing a hot channel bored through the old field
Catching a fighter already at full speed inside a thinned patch, who meets the new glass at exactly the speed she brought

Associations

Hypnather, through the Fate Path, banked in the glass overnight
The Snooze-Glass, a made thing he did not make
TAR TIME, which is what it holds

Limitations

It needs the Snooze-Glass
It takes four percent of his reserve, and it is one charge; the bubble needs a full night’s sleep to refill
After it he is back to yawning like everybody else
The tell is the bubble dimming as it falls
It is beaten by counting it: if it has dropped once today, it will not drop again

THE CHAISE · Technique
THE CHAISE is basically levitation: the power to lie down on nothing and drift wherever he leans. He spends most of his life on it.
Capabilities
He sets a slab of air under himself into glass and lies on it, held afloat by Abython, the same peace with the air that lets him walk through his own field. It carries him wherever he leans, at a walk. When he rolls off it, it sags into a puddle of clear syrup and is gone.
Applications

Travel without standing up
A bed anywhere

Associations

Hypnather for the slab, Abython for the float, through the Fate Path
FEATHERBED, which is this grown large and called aloud

Limitations

It holds his weight and nothing much more
Any real heat makes it sag and drip like toffee left in the sun
It costs so little it barely counts, a fraction of a percent of his reserve an hour
The tell is that he is lying on nothing
It is beaten by heating it until it drips

THE WAITER’S WAVE · Technique
THE WAITER’S WAVE is basically air solidification: the power to set one small piece of the glass harder with a lazy hand. It is a second claim made inside a standing TAR TIME.
Capabilities
He lifts his good hand off his knee, palm out, like a waiter waving away a plate, and a yard of the glass in front of it sets clear and hard as a window with no frame, the light running round its edges in a thin bright line. The pane rings when struck like a wine glass flicked with a finger, and whatever hits it meets it at exactly the speed it brought. A boy who charged one broke his nose and brow on it.
The plug is subtler and crueler. A breath is a thing that has to travel, down the long branching pipe of the throat into the chest, and the air a hand’s breadth from a mouth, laid down as thick as pitch, is rest that will not be hurried. A whole heaving chest cannot draw it: the harder the chest heaves the harder the rest refuses it, and the less comes down. The Measurewrights say the push a pipe needs rises in strict proportion to the thickness of what goes down it.
Techniques

The pane - a flat palm lifted, and a yard of glass sets hard as a window in front of a face
The plug - one claw closed slowly into the palm, like a man pinching out a candle, and the air at a mouth goes toward pitch
The squash - the palm laid flat an inch off a breastbone, beginning a slab that would stop the ribs rising; it has never been finished

Associations

Hypnather, through the Fate Path
TAR TIME, which it needs standing
DOK, which stops the squash

Limitations

It needs a standing TAR TIME, and is paid inside it
The tell is the hand, and it is a slow hand
The plug stiffens only as fast as the breath pulls on it, so a fighter who breathes slowly, in for six and out for six, breathes straight through
Heat breaks a pane, and so does a working that unmakes or cancels the glass at the touch; a glyph of unmaking shatters one from the inside
The squash has been begun at least twice and has always stopped half-set, because pressing a rib cage flat would be a finished act and DOK does not permit him one
It is beaten by coming slower than the glass stiffens

THE INFINITE DO-OVER · Technique
THE INFINITE DO-OVER is basically motion reversal: the power to make every back-and-forth motion in his field undo itself on the way home. It is the only thing he works at.
Capabilities
He does not yawn. The hum that sits under him all day goes quick, a steady beat like a man working a bellows handle, and the lavender round him swells and shrinks with it. He takes the glass that is still his past pitch, into a rest so deep that nothing in it keeps any going of its own: a thing moves exactly as far as it is pushed and no further, so if the push is undone the motion undoes itself, all the way back to the start. The Measurewrights say nothing in it has any momentum left. The Stannvaard philosophers show it with three drops of dye in corn syrup between two glass cylinders, smeared away to nothing by four turns of the inner cylinder and gathered back into three round drops by four turns the other way.
He sets his whole field rocking in time with his hum, one way and back, and every motion that goes out and returns is undone on the return stroke. He alone moves on.
Applications

A pike strikes and unstrikes the same air
A breath goes out and comes back
A rising girl rises and sinks
A line of fire runs out and is drawn home

Associations

Hypnather, through the Fate Path
TAR TIME, which it needs standing
Bellows-work, the skill from the bellows-gang that he swore he would never use again, and which is in the hum

Limitations

Only back-and-forth motion is caught: a thing that keeps turning one way, a spinning blade, a burning auger boring forward on its own twist, is never brought back, because its motion has no return in it
Anything turning one way goes through and takes the loops apart behind it
Heat is restlessness and goes where it likes, and no rocking can gather it home again
It is the hardest he has ever worked: the reserve goes in long pulls, his wounds bleed faster with every stroke, and sweat stands on his brow
The tell is the missing yawn, the hum gone quick as a bellows stroke, and the sweat
It is beaten by anything that turns one way, and by heat

PLAN B · Technique
PLAN B is basically absolute stillness: the power to stop pieces of the world all the way down, so that fire poured into them simply ends. It is the other yawn, and it is what happens when he forces the Crown instead of resting on it.
Capabilities
He puts two claws in his mouth and yawns again, slowly, and the yawn goes on and on with the corners of his mouth drawn back past his cheeks, and the look over the claws is not lazy at all. The Sleep Crown’s change comes only at rest, and a soul cannot say when it is finished. He hurries it anyway, with what he calls a little spark of enthusiasm, and patches of the field arrive all at once at the stillness rest only ever approaches: in those pieces the rest goes all the way down, so even the restlessness inside a thing where it stands lies down, and heat is that restlessness. Inside a piece nothing stirs, so nothing is hot and nothing is cold. The Measurewrights say the shaking of a thing’s smallest parts has stopped there.
Behind the stillness stands Nyxial, the Nocturne Flame, the idea of the even flame, a self that holds its level whatever is poured into it. The pieces take the fire and he carries it, and Nyxial’s flaw is that a level held against a load keeps everything it refused to feel, so it comes out of him when the load lifts. Hypnather’s named failure is interrupted relaxation, a rest broken before it has finished, which locks the thing worse ordered than before, and PLAN B is that failure used on purpose. That is why the stillness never comes as one whole. It comes scattered and malformed, in faceted pockets sealed off from each other along flat planes whose angles do not agree, with plain air between them.
Applications

Ending fire: poured in, it has nothing to stir and ends there, the way water ends at the bottom of a well
Putting out a Domain built on trapped heat, in holes from its edge inward
Hanging a falling drop of molten stone as a dull black bead, or a tongue of fire as a twisted violet sculpture
Holding a hand caught in a piece, which is there and cannot be felt or moved

Associations

Hypnather, forced, over Nyxial
