The Fate Path for the reach, with the Spirit Path forcing the Crown
It is also called the second yawn

Limitations

It comes in scattered pieces he does not place, with plain air between
The planes cut through steam, stone and light alike, and whatever solid thing they pass through breaks along them like a frozen lake along its cracks, so they break the ground and drop him along with everyone else
The fire he carries comes out of him all at once when the working lifts
It hurts him as much as it hurts anyone: he goes gray round the mouth, sweats, shakes, and is spent after
It wants a little spark of enthusiasm or it does not take
The tell is two claws in his mouth and a yawn that does not end
It is beaten by staying in the plain air between the pieces, and it empties him

FEATHERBED (the Lie-Down) · Technique
FEATHERBED is basically deep rest: the power to sink into a bed of glassed air where poison, bleeding and tiredness all but stop in him. It is THE CHAISE grown large and called aloud.
Capabilities
His eyes go fully heavy-lidded, the lavender shimmer thickens into a slow halo of hanging droplets, and the air under him gels into a long clear bed that carries him wherever he drifts, at a walk. TORPOR strikes as deep as his Fate II will carry it.
Applications

All but stopping poison, bleeding and fatigue in him
Riding out a week without spending down
Silent, it is only the bed; called, he sinks into it with a sigh and the whole of it blooms

Associations

Hypnather, with Abython’s float
The Fate Path for the bed, the Spirit Path for what it does in him
TORPOR, which it deepens

Limitations

It sips about 0.2 percent of his reserve a minute, under his recovery, and he can hold it for a week
Its counter is TORPOR’s: inside FEATHERBED he is at his slowest to wake

Releases
THE LIE-IN · the One
THE LIE-IN, the One, is basically domain opening: the power to open and pay for his Domain. It has no other use.
Capabilities
The held note is that slow ringing pane of glass, and the field the lavender of a sleepless dawn. It opens the Domain in one long yawn.
Applications

Opening and powering THE LIE-IN the Domain

Associations

Hypnather, through the Fate Path

Limitations

It holds 3 minutes 20 seconds from full
Held past its limit it is a Crystal Fracture Event, which would be the first hard thing that ever happened to his Crystal
Afterward he runs Overgrown until he sleeps, and he sleeps at once

Domain
THE LIE-IN (Vaross · Thaal-Snorr) · Domain
THE LIE-IN the Domain is basically beginning suppression: the power to make everything new, within a hundred and fifty yards, cost three times as much to start. It is the same law as the glass, laid on beginnings.
Capabilities
It is the Sleep Crown laid on beginnings. To begin, a thing has first to get up out of rest, and a thing that runs hot is already half up: a damp log on a cold hearth only smokes, and a coal from a hot fire lights whatever it is laid on. The Domain is a claim laid on the ground, on what has to be so before anything can begin, and what it says is that everything in it lies deeper and must climb three times as far to get up. The Measurewrights call it a raised activation barrier. He calls it sing-song and half asleep, the Vaross first and then the Common.
What is already moving keeps its pace, slowly, and anything that wants to begin has to climb three times as far. The law makes no exception for what he would rather spare, since he does not aim it. Its cruelest reach is one he has never aimed: a heart begins every beat from nothing and a chest begins every breath, and a body with no reserve left to pay the raised price stutters on both.
Applications

A fresh working costs three times its price to light
A fire already burning sinks to embers, and a new one will not catch; a fox-fire will not catch in it
A nerve fires late
A blade swung from stillness starts as if through mud
A dying heart, which has to begin every beat again from nothing, climbs the hill late and weaker each time

Associations

Hypnather, through the Fate Path
The One, the Fate road’s only Release, which counts as the Second and opens and powers it
His Sovereignty of 300, which holds it

Limitations

The same rise is charged to him: he cannot start anything quickly in it either, and he never does
It burns about half a percent of his reserve every second it stands, 3 minutes 20 seconds from full
A working already running when it opens keeps running, and so does anything already in motion
It is beaten by heat: the claim makes everything climb three times as far before it can begin, and a thing that runs hot is already half up, so a fighter who runs hot enough lights anyway, and a Domain held against a furnace burns through his reserve fast
A stronger Sovereignty contests it from its edge and takes the ground back hall by hall
Bodies can simply walk out of it, slowly

characters/ability-accounts/wolstan-kemp.title: Wolstan Kemp — Abilities in full
characters/ability-accounts/wolstan-kemp.content:
Card: Wolstan Kemp
Techniques
GOING ONCE! GOING TWICE! GONE! · Signature Art
GOING ONCE! GOING TWICE! GONE! is basically resonance striking: the power to load a thing with its own shiver until it cannot hold, and then finish it on a plane he chose before he began. It is named in plain Midmarch English for a roup-crier’s three calls. He sells the post three times, and on the third it is gone. He has no Traits; what the yard has seen is one art and twenty years of selling it over his own flags.
Capabilities
It is an auction, and he means every part of the word. A lot is put up, the bids are taken in order, each bid stands on the book until the next one tops it, and the hammer falls once. The art does the same thing to a body of wood or iron.
The charge is open and slow and anyone can read it. He rolls his sleeves, left and then right, plants his feet wide on the flags with the right a little behind and the knees soft, and settles his whole bulk onto the stone like a laden wagon onto its axles. He looks at the thing he means to break and finds the flaw in it before he touches it; on the yard’s pell that was the drying check across the crown, the crack oak opens along its rays as it seasons. He lays his left hand flat on it, almost gently, and breathes in, and his crown comes down on the yard. As Ned saw it, he seems to drink the yard, pulling up through his boots the raw stuff of the ground (Aether to the scholars, mana to the carters), and the flags go pale and dry. It is packed raw in his Shell, the body-side layer of the soul, and pushed out through his skin into his hands, where it shows as beaten copper climbing from the fingertips. By his own mouth more than half of what he puts in reaches the target, near two parts in three on a good day.
Then the three calls, and each one is a bid. They are three short palm-heel pushes from the hips, each at the instant the post’s shiver comes back to him, and a bid once called stands on the book: each push stays in the wood until the next one tops it, and none of them is allowed to lapse. Every solid thing has a pace it swings at when it is struck, the bell-founders’ note, and a push given at that pace adds to the swing already there; it is how the Minster ringers get a tenor bell that weighs as much as an ox up from dead still with small pulls on a rope, each taken at the top of the swing. No bell-ringer could do it to oak, because oak swallows its own ring and goes dead in a heartbeat. This is the woken half of the art. His copper sheathes the post and keeps each push in the wood like money on account, so oak that should go dead keeps ringing, the shiver running down to the socket and back to the crown and losing nothing on the way, because a bid on the book does not lapse. The Measurewrights call the pace the natural frequency, the adding resonance and the swallowing damping, the rubbing inside the wood that turns a shiver to a little warmth; their sums for a bell are good, and they cannot say why a man’s copper should keep oak from going dead. The second call therefore comes down on the whole of the first, and the post stops shivering and starts to sway, its crown moving like a mast and the check in its end-grain yawning and shutting with every swing.
The third call is the edge of the right hand held stiff as a froe. A froe is the cleaving blade a cooper sets in the end of a log to split staves, and it works because wood is strong along its grain and weak between its rays. The hand does the froe’s work at the one instant the swing has already pulled that weak plane open as wide as it will go, so the blow has only to finish what the post is doing to itself. It is the auction’s rule and nothing stranger: three small pushes, none of which could mark the oak, add up to a break because none of them was allowed to die.
Applications

Riving the yard’s pell, twenty years in its socket, from top to bottom
Breaking a thing along a flaw he found before he touched it
By his own boast it works on a man (“You want to know what I pay on a man, you’ll have to hire me”), though nobody has seen that

Techniques

GOING ONCE! - a short palm-heel push from the hips, the kind a man gives a stuck door, and a ring of copper runs round the struck thing and sheathes it top to bottom while it starts to shiver
GOING TWICE! - the same push in the same place at the instant the shiver comes back to his hand, so it lands on top of the first and the thing begins to sing and sway
GONE! - the right hand brought down edge-on, the copper run together into one bright line, along the plane he picked before he began, at the top of the swing, and the thing rives top to bottom

Associations

No Wellspring is named for it; the smell of a bell-founder’s yard is all Ned has to go on
The Body Path, in the Form of a Strike
He came by it living, in a dead king’s tourney ring and twenty years of his own yard
Reading the grain, his habit of finding the flaw in a post, a blade or a man before he touches it
His colors are beaten copper-orange, like a new copper pan held to a fire, with a heat-haze over them and a smell of hot pennies
The yard cries his calls with him like a crowd at a roup
No Release has been shown; if he has one he did not spend it on a post

Limitations

A bid called is a debt: once called, it is on the book, and he may not withdraw it
Whatever he has banked in the thing by the second call has to go somewhere, and if the third call does not spend it down the plane he chose, it comes back up the hand that is still on the wood
So he cannot stop at twice; by Bett’s account he broke his wrist so at twenty-six
It has no single-blow form, and the calls are three, never one or two
He needs both pushes banked in the same thing, and his left hand on it to feel the shiver come back
What does not reach the wood burns in his Shell’s furnace and comes off him as heat: scalp streaming and steaming, face red, breath hard for two or three breaths
Riving the pell split the edge of his right hand from the little finger to the wrist
Where he stands matters: on rich ground with nobody else on it the breath would be short, and in a crowded yard, with forty people pulling on the same stone, it runs long, which gives anyone watching more time
On a man it would want two touches landed in time on the same body before the third could do anything at all, and a man does not stand still in a socket the way a pell does; that is the yard’s guess and Bett’s, and it has not been tested
Its tell is the three calls, with the copper gathering to one bright line on the right hand by the third, and the second call’s ring louder than the first by more than twice
It is beaten by getting between the calls: moving, breaking his touch or striking him after the second call turns his own stored swing on his arm
The long breath before the first call is the other opening, longest on crowded or poor ground

characters/ability-accounts/wystan-greym.title: Wystan Greymane — Abilities in full
characters/ability-accounts/wystan-greym.content:
Card: Wystan Greymane
KEEPERS OF THE WALL
KEEPERS OF THE WALL is basically impassability: the power to be a wall, a thing that stands between, so that nothing gets past him, not a blow and not a secret, and when he finally moves he only needs to once. The name is northern Common, the house’s own words. It is his signature art, a Trait-art with the Greymane release, and it was the house’s idea before it was his.
Capabilities
A Greymane is a wall, and a wall is a thing that stands between. His children carry the same idea with younger knees. In him it has had sixty-one years to finish, and it has gone past the shield into everything else he does. The body is a wall against a blow. The stillness is a wall against being read. The silence is a wall against a question. The release is the same body made into the thing itself, one piece from boss to heel.
He has said the whole of it once, quietly, to his son, in the gatehouse at the Foot: we stand on the ridge so that nobody behind us has to.
Applications

Standing between a blow and the people behind him
Giving an opponent nothing to read
Keeping what is not his to tell

Techniques

KEEPERS OF THE WALL - the Trait of the same name, the body as a wall against a blow
STILL, THEN FAST - the stillness, a wall against being read
LATER, ULF - the silence, a wall against a question
SETTING THE STONE - the release, the same body made into the thing itself

Associations

The Body Path, mastered, carries the wall, the stillness and the release; the Fate Path he walks carries the silence, kept the way an oath is kept
Fixatio is the lens of the release; no lens is written for the wall and the stillness, which are the house’s raising and his own soul’s habit
House Greymane of the Ridgewall
The house expects that a Greymane’s Domain, if one of them ever lives to it, will be the ridge

Limitations

A wall faces one way and stays where it is: everything he has is paid for in not stepping, not turning and not telling

Traits
KEEPERS OF THE WALL · Primary Trait
KEEPERS OF THE WALL is basically guardianship: the power to hold a line with someone behind it and not be moved back a step. The Greymane soul stands on a wall looking west for something that might come, and his did that before it did anything else.
Capabilities
The body’s part is plain bracing, and any shield-man can be taught it. A blow moves a man by getting his weight outside his feet, and a man keeps his weight inside them by standing staggered and low with the shield seated against the shoulder, so that the push runs through bone into the ground and the ground pushes back exactly as hard, which every shield-man knows in his legs and the Measurewrights write down as their law that every push is met by an equal one.
What undoes a braced man is very seldom the blow. It is the flinch, the small backward start the body makes on its own to get away from what is coming, which lifts the heels and unloads the stance a heartbeat before the hit. This Trait is his soul refusing the flinch. The Shell, the body-side layer of the soul, holds the brace through the instant when a body would break it. While he holds a line with someone behind it, his Anchoring and Fortitude read one step high and nothing that reaches him moves him back.
Applications

Holding a line or a post with people behind it
Taking a blow without giving a step

Associations

The Body Path, with no lens written for it
The house’s raising and his own soul’s habit
The old sun, the round Greymane shield, seated against his shoulder

Limitations

It holds only while there is somebody behind him to hold it for, because that is the only reason his soul has ever accepted for standing still under a blow
It faces one way: a wall guards what is behind it and nothing else
With nobody behind him the step is gone and he is a strong old man with a good shield
A blow from the flank or the rear meets no wall at all
It costs nothing, since nothing is made or thrown
Its tell is that his eyes go west, or to whatever he has been set to face, before they come to the man in front of him, because he is checking the post before he checks the threat
It is beaten by coming at what he is not guarding: go round, split him from the people he is covering, or put a second threat on the far side of them and make him choose

STILL, THEN FAST · Secondary Trait
STILL, THEN FAST is basically counter-striking: the power to stand so still that there is nothing to read, and then make one move quicker than he has any right to. It is the Ridgewall stillness: he has a way of not moving at all and then moving very fast.
Capabilities
Two true things about bodies are doing the work. The first is that a moving fighter is a readable one. Every strike is announced by something smaller that comes before it, a shift of weight, a dip of the shoulder, a breath taken, and a trained eye answers the announcement and not the blow. A man who is truly still announces nothing, so there is no early warning to answer. The second is about choosing. A man who has to pick among several answers is slower than a man who has only one ready, and each choice added costs him time; the scholars who measure such things call the quick kind a simple reaction and the slow kind a choice reaction. Standing there, Wystan has already chosen.
He has one answer loaded, the way a crossbow is spanned and latched: the muscles of hip and shoulder drawn tight against each other and held, the fleece-lined scabbard keeping the blade loose, and nothing left to decide except when. The latch is the stillness, and his soul holds it without a tremor for as long as he likes. While he is still, his Reflex winds up behind it, and the first thing he does out of stillness comes one step quicker than his card. When the other man commits, the latch goes, and the whole wound-up body arrives at once, which is why old Stormfold men who have watched it a dozen times cannot say which hand moved first.
Applications

Answering the other man’s first move with the sword along the line he has just opened
Showing an opponent nothing to read
Striking from a planted body after the release is set

Associations

The Body Path, with no lens written for it
The Ridgewall sword and its scabbard, whose throat is lined in waxed fleece
SETTING THE STONE, which it answers out of

Limitations

It is one move, once
After the first, he is only an old man of sixty-one with a sword
Winding it again takes real stillness, a few breaths of it, which nobody close enough to hit him will give him
It takes no reserve
Its tell is that he stops moving altogether
Never be the first to move: a patient man wastes it
A longer weapon can make him come forward out of it
A false start he believes spends it as surely as a true one

LATER, ULF · Secondary Trait
LATER, ULF is basically secret keeping: the power to hold a silence that nothing gets out of him. He saw the gold seam in the boy’s eye from a hand’s width away in the yard at the Foot, and his face set like ground taking the frost, and he said “later.”
Capabilities
A secret gets out of an ordinary man through his body long before it gets out through his mouth: the eyes go to the person it concerns, the face answers a question before the tongue can lie, and the wish to be rid of the weight does the rest. LATER, ULF closes those roads. His face sets, his voice goes back to an old soldier’s ordinary voice giving orders about gates and stables and a count, and his eyes do not return to the thing he saw. One word, and the thing he is keeping is as far out of reach as if the ridge stood in front of it.
It is kin to a vow, which is small Fate and anyone’s to make, and his walked Fate is why his holds so cleanly. It pulls no thread and makes nothing happen. It only keeps what he already holds.
Applications

Keeping what he saw from his face, his voice and his eyes
He swore his own son to the same silence on the ridge, by the woodpile, with a cup going sour in his hand

Associations

The Fate Path he walks, kept the way an oath is kept
The same habit that keeps the wall: he keeps a silence the way he keeps a wall

Limitations

It takes no reserve; what it costs is what keeping costs: he carried the boy’s name south with him and never got to say it
A silence cannot defend itself except by staying silent
He cannot explain, argue or lie his way round a question, because he does not lie; he can only decline it
A declined question tells a sharp listener that there is something there
Its tell is the word itself: “Later.”
Ask him in front of the one he is keeping it from; he will walk to the window instead, and the walk is an answer of a kind

Releases
SETTING THE STONE · First Release, Greymane
SETTING THE STONE is basically immovability: the power to lock every joint in his body into one post that stands on the ground. It is the Greymane release, called aloud as “Stonefast,” low and level, taught on the Ridgewall as every Greymane is taught it, and his is Mastered.
Capabilities
Like any Body fighter he pulls Aether, mana in the common word, up out of the ground he stands on, packs it raw in his Shell as Charge, and drives it out through the Shell. Fixatio, the Knot, is the lens, and its idea is commitment: what is bound stays bound, because the way back has stopped existing. Its operation is coagulation, the setting of a thing past melting. Some stuffs can be melted and shaped again as often as you like, the way wax can. Others set once: boiled linseed oil dried hard on a shield’s face, lacquer, a raw hide tanned into leather, which will char before they flow, and every Greymane yard reaches for them as the comparison. Laid through his Shell, the house’s lens sets whatever it is laid on the same way, and what it holds stays held because the way back is no longer there to be reached. The Measurewrights say the long strands of a cured stuff have been bridged to one another all through, cross-linked in their word; their account of a shield’s face is good, and they cannot say why a man’s elbow should take the same cure.
A joint is the opposite of a cured thing. It exists to let two bones change their angle, and a body made of joints is a chain: lean on a chain and it folds at every link. That folding is how a blow gets into a man, each joint giving a little, the shield driven back into the arm, the arm into the shoulder, the hips turned, the heels lifted. When he calls the release, Fixatio sets each joint in the line, wrist, elbow, shoulder, spine, hip, knee and ankle, for as long as the feet stay where they are, and the chain becomes a post. A post under a push does one thing: it carries the push along its own length as squeeze, end to end, into whatever it stands on. So the weight of the blow goes down through him into the ground, the ground pushes back, and nothing in between is allowed to fold.
It rides a blow the plain way. The real hit lands on the old sun, on steel over ash, and the shield takes the dent, as sixty years of dents on its face will tell you. The working is what happens behind the shield: the arm that should have been driven back is not, and the man who struck feels his own blow come back up his weapon as if he had hit the gatehouse. At his rung a Body fighter commands matter as an object, what the hand is on, and the object here is himself and the shield on his arm; it is the smallest and oldest kind of command there is.
Applications

Taking a blow on the shield without the arm being driven back
Sending the striker’s own blow back up his weapon
Freeing the sword arm from a planted body, so the one answer of STILL, THEN FAST goes out along whatever line the striker has just opened: the wall first, and then very fast

Associations

Fixatio, the Knot, the house’s lens, carried in its drill and never harmonized by him, so it fires at the away rate
The Body Path, mastered
The old sun, which takes the real hit
House Greymane: his son and daughter call the same word, and the Stormfold says theirs are good and his is the one the others are measured against

Limitations

It takes about four percent of his reserve to set, some twenty-five settings from a full reserve, and it holds for as long as he does not move his feet
A little over three fifths of what he spends reaches the world, which is his yield; the rest burns in the Shell’s furnace, as warmth in the locked joints and as the one long low note people hear from very close
The feet are its limit: set, he cannot step
The charge is fair warning to anyone who has been told what to look for: the long breath out through his nose, the heels going down, the drifting dust and snow dropping straight to the ground in a ring round his feet, the old sun seeming to take the light, the dull gold edge of his aura ceasing to move and hardening like a bead of resin, a sweet resin smell that turns sharp, and one small sound from somewhere in him like a latch going home
Against a higher Stage it thins from the ground up: Fixatio holds the column and does not make the ground under it any stronger than it is, and a blow well over what the footing can bear breaks the footing, after which there is nothing for the post to stand on
The cure holds the man, never the footing: the post stands by its weight on the ground and the grip of his heels
The counters are the ones the house teaches its children to fear. Pull him, and a column built to be squeezed has nothing to say to a pull
Lift him, and there is no ground under the post
Or fight him on ice, where the heels have no grip and the whole locked man slides like a dropped statue
The lens fails from its own idea’s flaw: commitment cannot tell a true binding from a mistaken one, and a cured thing cannot bend, even to save itself; the Measurewrights call it irreversibility and the trade calls it over-cure
A set Greymane cannot ride a blow, roll with it or give an inch to bleed it off, so whatever exceeds the column does not stagger him. It cracks him, at whichever joint was a hair off the line when he called it, because Fixatio sets a wrong closing as firmly as a right one
Held too long, the cure lingers after the release has ended, and he comes off a long stand with hips and knees that take half a morning to remember they are joints; at sixty-one that bill is longer every winter

characters/ability-accounts/ylva-stark-—.title: Ylva Stark — Abilities in full
characters/ability-accounts/ylva-stark-—.content:
Card: Ylva Stark
THE WHITE ROAD
THE WHITE ROAD is basically path manipulation: the power to open a way in front of her and freeze it shut behind. She is a Stark and a Hallenfeld at once, the house that decides where things end and the house that keeps every road open, and the art is the two of them in one girl on a horse.
Capabilities
The Stark cold draws the warmth out of everything near its bearer and drives it into the ground. In her father it goes down through his heels and stands up along a scratch in the snow as a wall: this ground is mine, and that ground is not. In Ylva it runs forward. It goes out ahead of her along whatever road she is on, the way water runs downhill, and lies down on the ground in a white lane, and the lane tells her the road: hard where it will bear, thin where it won’t, broken where something warm crossed in the last hour.
What her father claims standing still, she claims riding away. She drags the point of her sword behind her at the gallop, and the road closes in a line of rime across it, and the horses that follow go down. It is Lorn’s line turned to run, and it carries his limit backward. He has to stand on his side of his line, because a man who steps over his own border has unsaid it. She has to keep moving away from hers, because a girl who stops on a road she has shut has said it was never shut.
The price is the house’s. The cold moves heat and cannot make it, and against a great fire it is a bucket. And when she spends too much, it comes home into her, as it came home into her father in the cedar wood.
Applications

Bringing a courier string home through a blizzard
Losing a pursuit on any road she has ridden once
Knowing who passed on a road in the last hour
Getting a horse across ice

Techniques

STARK RIME - the cold in the blood, running forward
WHERE IT BEARS - the road read in rime
SHUT THE ROAD! - the line drawn at the gallop
FROST-SHOD - a horse that grips ice
WHITE ROAD! - the First Release, a quarter mile of swept ice

Associations

The Stark cold, the house’s inheritance, no Wellspring
The Hallenfeld roads, which are no gift of the blood and every gift of the upbringing
The Body Path carries all of it

Limitations

She has to keep moving; if she stops, the road she shut opens
It goes where the road goes: no open water, no drop, no trackless ground
Heat answers it, and a warm wet road at midsummer tells her very little
A body made to be gone, and no good at all at being caught

Traits
STARK RIME · Inherited Trait
STARK RIME is basically cold aura: the power to draw the warmth out of everything near her. Every Stark carries it. Her breath stops steaming and the fur on her mantle frosts, and in her the cold leans forward, along the ground.
Limitations

It moves heat and cannot make it
Tell: her breath stops steaming
Counter: heat; a hot room; a fire-worker

WHERE IT BEARS · Primary Trait
WHERE IT BEARS is basically terrain reading: the power to read a road’s condition in the rime she lays on it.
Capabilities
Her mother taught her to read a road by eye, and the Hallenfeld shorthand to write it down. Her cold does it by itself. The rime runs ahead of her a quarter mile and settles hard and white on ground that will bear a horse, thin and gray on ground that won’t, and broken in prints where something warm crossed in the last hour. She reads ambushes off it by the warm patches where men have been lying.
Limitations

It reads the ground and nothing on it
Cost: almost nothing; a little reserve a mile
Tell: a white line running out in front of her horse
Counter: a hot day; or a road nobody has ever traveled

Techniques
SHUT THE ROAD! · Signature Technique
SHUT THE ROAD! is basically barrier creation in motion: the power to close a road behind her.
Capabilities
At the gallop she lets the point of her sword trail on the ground behind her, and a white plume comes up off it, and the road freezes shut across its width in a line of rime that takes the legs out from under any horse that crosses it. She built it the spring after she woke, by herself, out of watching her father.
Limitations

It holds only while she keeps riding away from it; if she stops or turns, it thaws in a breath
Cost: about 8% of her reserve, near 2,800 EU
Tell: the sword-point trailing white
Counter: outride her, or ride round, off the road

FROST-SHOD · Technique
FROST-SHOD is basically traction enhancement: the power to make her horse grip ice. Her cold goes down the reins and into the hooves, and the horse goes over a frozen ford like a cat along a wall.
Limitations

One horse, her own, under her
Cost: a little reserve a minute
Counter: heat; a horse that is frightened of her

Releases
WHITE ROAD! · First Release
WHITE ROAD! is basically path creation: the power to lay a quarter mile of true ice ahead of her. The call is “White road!”
Capabilities
A lane of hard white rime shoots out in front of her, flat and true as a swept floor over whatever the road was, ruts and mud and broken stone, and her horse runs on it without a slip. Her Celerity and Reflex read a step high, and nothing in her passes the roof of her Stage. It is the thing the couriers named her for.
Limitations

It goes where the road goes; no open water, no drop
Cost: about 200 EU a second, near 3 minutes from a full reserve
Counter: heat, or a road that ends

characters/ability-accounts/yukazuri-mot.title: Yukazuri Moto — Abilities in full
characters/ability-accounts/yukazuri-mot.content:
Card: Yukazuri Moto
HOLD STILL
HOLD STILL is basically tranquility inducement: the power to make a body hold still, and to hear in the quiet exactly what is wrong with it. It is the surgeon’s art, said in northern Common, and three of her Traits are this one idea. The name is her own two words, the ones every man she ever sewed heard first.
Capabilities
All three pieces are one act at three sizes: make it hold still, listen, and take only what is dead. STILL WATER stills the room. THE HUM listens to what the stillness leaves audible. WHERE IT’S DEAD stills her own hands and face and puts the listening to work on a wound.
It rides no blow, because there is no blow in her. It rides the needle. The room comes down first, so the man lies still; the ear goes to him second, so she knows what he is not saying; the hands go in third, and by then the three are one movement that takes less time than it takes him to finish swearing at her.
She did not design any of it. It grew around the work, the way her Crystal did, and it is the reason a girl of thirteen with a reserve a grown practitioner would laugh at ran the surgeons’ line of an army.
Applications

Getting a wounded man to lie still for the needle
Knowing what he is not saying before the hands go in
Taking the dead part of a wound and nothing else

Techniques

STILL WATER - stills the room
THE HUM - listens to what the stillness leaves audible
WHERE IT’S DEAD - stills her own hands and face and puts the listening to work on a wound

Associations

Somnalis, the Hush, and Anamnesis, the Remembering, which she has never harmonized
The Spirit Path carries the gift that hears, and the Body Path, studied, carries her hands
The field surgeon’s trade
THE MARK is the red line’s and not the art’s
She has no named technique, no Release and no Domain; the nearest she came to a Domain was a surgeons’ tent where everyone breathed slower

Limitations

It has never been pointed at anyone: its three pieces are Traits and not techniques, and nothing in it is called, charged or aimed
It is aimed at nobody, so anyone with a blade can simply walk up to her
It costs almost nothing in reserve. The price is the art’s own: it only works beside the dying, so she has to be where they are
Whatever she shut away to keep her hands steady comes due in the hours when she is not working
The visible charge is small and a room learns it fast: she comes close, her own out-breath goes long and slow, the frost-pale of her aura takes a faint rose, and the tin comes out of the apron pocket before she has said a word
It is beaten by noise and fear louder than she is, by a man who has decided, and by a shut mouth and a low, even breath
Each piece fails in its own way

Traits
STILL WATER · Passive Trait
STILL WATER is basically a calming aura: the power to slow the breath and the pulse of everyone within a few paces of her. It is always on, and her brother stopped noticing it years ago.
Capabilities
A frightened body breathes high and short, up under the collarbone, and a body breathing like that keeps itself frightened. The heart quickens on every in-breath and eases on every out-breath, a swing the scholars call respiratory sinus arrhythmia, and the long nerve that does the easing they call the vagus, so a man taking quick gulps of air never reaches the part of the breath that would slow him. Breath is also the one such rhythm a person can be led in, and people fall into step with a slower breather beside them without noticing they have. That is the plain half, and any calm surgeon has a little of it.
The other half is Somnalis, folk name the Hush. Somnalis is the Wellspring of the near branches, the law that what has not happened yet already has weight and can be held as a spread instead of a single answer, and its bearers are souls at ease in not knowing. Panic is the opposite condition: a body that has picked the worst branch out of the spread and is already living in it. What runs off her into the air within a few paces is that ease, laid through her Core onto the souls nearest. Under it the frightened body lets go of the one doom it had settled on, the breath comes down from the collarbone to the belly, the pulse follows the breath, and the shaking stops.
Applications

Quieting a shouting yard when the salve tin comes out of the apron
Getting a man who was thrashing to lie down for the needle
Calming a whole room when her fingers are on the wound, which is when it is strongest
It works on anyone, friend or prisoner or dog, and on her brother most of all, who felt it through a door before he had turned to see her and never once in his life wondered why

Associations

Somnalis, the Hush, at first contact, met at the Veyrath ditch
The lens met her where it pools, on ground where many plans cross and every one could still go either way: two hundred men in a ditch, each of whom might live or might not
The Spirit Path, laid through the Core on the souls nearest

Limitations

Its reach is a few paces
The lens’s own limit, the one the scholars write as Return, brings a body back toward its own rest and no lower: it cannot put a man under and it cannot slow a heart past resting
It cannot stop a bleed, only the panic over the bleed, which matters because a panicking man pumps himself empty faster
A man who has decided is not running too fast, so there is nothing in him for it to return; a hall full of men who have already decided is the place it does least
It costs almost nothing, a share of her reserve too small to feel and less than she recovers standing still, and it never stops
Something over a third of what she spends arrives as that work; the rest goes off as the pale light almost nobody sees and a slight coolness in the air about her
Its tell is everyone near her breathing slower
Noise and terror louder than she is beat it
Somnalis fails by ensemble collapse, the spread taken for a single answer: if she ever told a man he would be fine, she would be choosing one branch for him out loud, the ease would turn false on the spot, and his body would know it before he did
So she never says it. She says to hold still, which is true on every branch

THE HUM · Primary Trait
THE HUM is basically psychometry by ear: the power to hear the record a thing or a person is carrying. It is Anamnesis leaking through her Perception, a gift she was born with, before she has a name for it.
Capabilities
Everything keeps its past, and that is the whole idea of Anamnesis, the Remembering: a fired pot holds every dose it has taken since the kiln, and a body, a soul and a sworn thing keep theirs the same way. Its operation is separation, the kept past parted from the thing that kept it and read, and the Measurewrights’ favorite example is basalt, which they say holds the direction of the field it cooled in. In her it comes as sound. She bends her ear to a thing the way she bends over a man’s chest and closes her eyes for it, and when they open they have gone very dark, the blue nearly black.
So a seal-token that sits under a house’s name has a note she can hear across a yard at night, like bees in a wall, a sealed one has a shape she can feel like a coin in a pocket, and a man’s decision is on him before he opens his mouth. She does not have to touch the thing. Under it sits the plain trade skill that any good surgeon has and she has to a rare degree: where the breath sits, what a thumb does on a table edge.
Applications

Hearing every token in a post hum, all the way across a yard at night
Reading her brother’s dead Stark token: not broken, not dead, only looking straight at him and unable to see anyone there
Reading the Stark token in his closed fist as sealed, a good seal, old wall and bright light
Hearing a man decide
Hearing a lie in the breath, high and short, right up under the collarbone

Associations

Anamnesis, never harmonized, a leak through her Perception
The Spirit Path
Her Perception and Empathy, which price it
The surgeon’s habit of reading breath

Limitations

A record is all it is: it hears what has been laid down and nothing that has not
It hears and does not act
What she hears she then has to reason out like anyone else: it took her three days of listening to a post full of tokens to work out that they were listening for a house name, and that she and her brother had none one could find
It costs nothing she notices
Its tell is her head bent to listen
A man who keeps his mouth shut and his breath low and even has laid nothing down for her to hear, so the counter is to say nothing and breathe evenly
Anamnesis fails by thermal resetting, a careless reader wiping the record in the act of taking it; it has never happened to her because she has never pulled, only listened, and a trained hand grabbing at what she hears would risk it

WHERE IT’S DEAD · Secondary Trait
WHERE IT’S DEAD is basically surgical precision: the power to find exactly where the living part of a wound stops, with hands that do not shake. It formed at the Veyrath ditch at twelve, two hundred men on her knees.
Capabilities
A wound heals from tissue that is alive, and dead tissue left in it feeds the rot that kills the man a week later; cut too far and he loses what he could have kept. The whole craft, which the scholars call debridement, is finding the line, and the line shows at the edges: living flesh has color, bleeds bright when touched and draws back from the knife, and dead flesh does none of the three. Her rule for it is this: you don’t cut what you can sew; you don’t sew what has to come off; you look; you find where it’s dead; you take that, and nothing else; and then you close what’s left, and let it live.
That rule is no Wellspring’s. It is a break in her Core from the Veyrath ditch that healed into a tool. While there is work in front of her, the fear is shut behind it, her hands are steady, her face does nothing at all, which is what it does when she is frightened, and everything she is goes into the look.
Applications

Taking the dead part of a wound and nothing else, and closing what is left
Keeping her hands steady and her face blank while she works
It became the first lesson of her brother’s Work of Ruins, and the law of the oath he swore before the Seat

Associations

A healed break in her Core, with no Wellspring under it
The Body Path, studied, for the hands, under a Spirit Path’s look
Plain field surgery: the cut and the stitch are no working

Limitations

It takes no reserve
It holds only while there is work in front of her, and it steadies her for a wound and for nothing else
It has no say over what happens to her when her hands are tied
Its tell is the stillness, the hands gone steady and the face gone blank at the same moment, which the people who know her read as the sign that it is bad
She pays afterward, in the hours when she is not working, and she does not show that either
It is beaten by taking the work away from her
The Core’s rule fails when the work stops: what it was holding back arrives in the hours afterward, all at once, and she lets nobody see it

THE MARK · Inherited Trait
THE MARK is basically bloodline marking: the power to write the red line’s name true, in the one hand the registers cannot read. It is blood and no working, and it stands apart from HOLD STILL because it belongs to the red line and not to the surgeon.
Capabilities
The Kōkan mark is a long down-stroke, a hook, a crossing and a small closed loop like a knot in a rope, a little like a closed eye. Her brother’s hand could never draw it. Hers always drew it true, on frost, in camp dirt, on the bottom of her salve tin, in her own blood on her palm to steady her hands. At eleven she drew it in spilled lamp oil on the stamping floor and it burned blue for a moment before the oil went out.
It is the red line’s name, and in her it answers. It does nothing but tell the truth about whose she is, which she did not know until her brother told her, and she answered, “so that’s whose it was.”
Applications

Telling the truth about whose she is
Steadying her hands, drawn in her own blood on her palm
Held up on her palm in her own blood in the yard of the Foot, it put six hundred people on their knees without a word from her

Associations

The Kōkan blood, the red line
No Wellspring, no Path and no Lens; it is a name, drawn by hand
Her brother, who told her whose it was

Limitations

It costs nothing: it spends nothing and pulls nothing down
It only speaks to people who can already read it, and those people lie about what they saw
A Zettari surveyor at the Marrow went white when she drew it on his frosted window, wiped it off with his sleeve and lied to her about it, with his breath gone short and high under the collarbone
Its tell is the hand: four strokes, the same every time, on frost or tin or skin
That same silence is what beats it: a register that will not enter it and a clerk who will not say its name

characters/ability-accounts/yusif-stark-.title: Yusif Stark — Abilities in full
characters/ability-accounts/yusif-stark-.content:
Card: Yusif Stark
THE DOG THAT DOESN’T BARK
THE DOG THAT DOESN’T BARK is basically presence concealment: the power to never let anything show, not the cut before it lands, not the cold, and not the secret. It is his signature art, one idea, and it is in the line about his cold: he keeps it the way a man keeps a dog that does not bark. Each ability below is that same quiet in a different part of him: the feet, the edge, the mouth and the blood.
Capabilities
A Stark is supposed to be seen coming. The snow stiffens, the timber silvers, the breath of everyone in the room shows, and the house likes it that way, because a border that announces itself gets crossed less often. Yusif took the announcement out of everything he had. His cold stops at his hands. His sword gives no notice. His face gives none. The one thing he knew that mattered, he kept behind his teeth for sixteen years and died with it there.
A barking dog tells you where it is and how frightened it is; the one that says nothing is the one that has already decided.
Applications

Cutting with no notice given
Keeping the Stark cold from announcing him
Keeping his face empty
Keeping one secret for sixteen years, to the death

Techniques

LET YOUR FEET DO IT - the quiet in the feet, a body that fights before the head decides
THE THING NOBODY WROTE DOWN - the quiet in the mouth, one promise kept
STARK RIME - the quiet in the blood, the cold held to his hands and blade
THE LONG CLEAN LINE - the quiet in the edge, one cut with nothing shown first

Associations

The Body Path, Mastered, does the feet, the line and the cold
His Walked Fate holds the thing kept; nothing is routed through his Studied Spirit
The Stark cold, the house’s inheritance and no Wellspring, is the lens for the rime and the edge
The feet are drill made into law, and the thing kept is his own sworn word

Limitations

Every clean line chills his own steel toward breaking
The thing he keeps can never speak up for him

Traits
LET YOUR FEET DO IT · Primary Trait
LET YOUR FEET DO IT is basically muscle memory combat: the power to fight below thought, the body moving before the mind decides. “You’re thinking. Stop thinking. Let your feet do it.” He lived it, and it is what he put into a salt-cutter’s boy with an ash stick from the age of eight.
Capabilities
The plain account is the one any drill-yard knows: a thing done ten thousand times stops needing the head. The scholars call it automaticity, which only means the body has the whole movement stored and runs it without asking, the way a man walks downstairs in the dark. It is faster than choosing, because choosing takes time and the stored movement takes none.
It is also quieter. Nearly every warning a fighter gives, the glance at the target, the shoulder that turns a hair early, the breath caught before the swing, is the mind getting ready and the body leaking it. Fencing masters call that leak a tell, and a blow that carries one is said to be telegraphed. Take the deciding out and the leak goes with it, so there is no moment of making up his mind for anyone to see.
In Yusif this stopped being a habit and became a law of his Shell (the body-side layer of the soul, the part that turns what is inside a person into force in the world). While it runs, his Reflex reads a step high and his cuts come without a tell. The boy’s body still moves before he decides, every time.
Applications

Answering a blow faster than choosing allows
Cutting with no warning on the cut
Teaching it, until a child’s feet stop asking the head

Associations

The Body Path, as a strike, through the Shell
Drill made into law
The Kharven breath, in through the nose until the ribs ache and out through the mouth until nothing is left
The boy he taught with an ash stick

Limitations

It answers what the body has met before
A fight that needs a new idea needs the mind back, and the instant the mind comes back, the step and the silence both go
It costs nothing, because nothing is being made or thrown
It has no tell, and that is the point
What anyone watching sees before it starts is the one piece of ritual he allowed himself, the breath, and then a face with nobody at home in it
A fight he has to think his way through beats it: ground he has never stood on, a weapon nobody has shown him, a question asked in the middle of the exchange
Scholars call that the centipede’s trouble, after the creature that walked perfectly until somebody asked it which leg went first

THE THING NOBODY WROTE DOWN · Secondary Trait
THE THING NOBODY WROTE DOWN is basically interrogation immunity: the power to keep one unwritten promise so that neither fear nor pain gets a word of it out of him. It formed the morning after the cellars, when he quit Gimbzo and never rode with him again.
Capabilities
A contract is not the paper; it is the thing both sides know that nobody wrote down, and he kept one for sixteen years: the boy’s blood, his mother’s road, the name. This is the Fate he walks, and it is small Fate, the kind anyone can make: a vow, with terms, that the soul itself holds him to.
Nobody witnessed it and it needed nobody. His sheet carried the line where only he could read it. A kept vow is a bond, and a bond that is fed every day for sixteen years sets hard. What it does for him is narrow and absolute: while he keeps it nothing gets it out of him, not fear and not pain.
Applications

Keeping the boy’s blood, his mother’s road and the name behind his teeth
Holding his silence under fear and under pain

Associations

His Walked Fate, as a binding
His own sworn word, kept sixteen years
The morning after the cellars

Limitations

Its limit is the keeping: it is a silence, and a silence cannot defend itself except by staying silent
It cannot argue, cannot explain him to his own house, cannot tell his nephew why he rode away
It could not ask anybody for help on the road where he died
It takes no reserve, and it buys him no step
Its tell is that he says nothing at all, and when the question comes close his hand goes flat on the nearest child’s head, or would
To beat it, ask him in front of the one he is keeping it from
He will walk away rather than lie to the boy, and a man who has to walk away has been moved

STARK RIME · Inherited Trait
STARK RIME is basically personal cold: the power to carry the Stark cold on a short lead, as frost on his knuckles and along his blade and no further. It is an inheritance of the house and no Wellspring, and his nephew’s whitens a whole yard.
Capabilities
The cold in the Stark blood does one thing: it moves heat out, from the warm thing to the cold one, through him and down through his heels into the earth, which can take more than any man can give. Near a Stark, heat leaves everything, timber silvers and snow stiffens.
In him it ran quiet, a rime on the hands and the blade and no further, the way a man keeps a dog that does not bark. Holding it that close is harder than letting it run. The cold wants out the way water wants downhill, and a Stark who is angry or afraid whitens the room without meaning to. Yusif’s never got past his wrists in front of two children in all the seasons he came down, and that tells you what he was like inside.
Applications

A thread of cold along the edge in THE LONG CLEAN LINE
Frost on his own knuckles thick enough that a wound he has taken does not show in his hands
Standing in a room without whitening it

Associations

The Stark cold, the house’s inheritance, with no Wellspring behind it
The Body Path, as a shaping
THE LONG CLEAN LINE, which it runs along
Ulf Stark, his nephew, who lets the same cold run

Limitations

The cold moves heat and cannot make any
Where everything around him is already frozen hard it has little heat to take
Against a real fire it loses
At rest it takes no reserve
Its tell is that his breath stops steaming
Heat and calm beat it

Techniques
THE LONG CLEAN LINE · Signature Technique
THE LONG CLEAN LINE is basically sharpness manipulation: the power to put the whole of him behind one cut along one line, with nothing wasted and nothing shown first, and then it is over. He lived his way to it and has it Mastered. The boy has it now, and nobody alive calls it by this name but him.
Capabilities
The visible charge is small and it is all there is: the rime on the flat of the blade draws in toward the edge, a white thread running from the cross to the point, and his back heel settles. Then the body goes in order. The hips turn first, the shoulders follow, the arms come last, and each joins while the one before is still moving, so that the speeds add and the edge arrives carrying all of them. A carter cracking a whip is doing the same thing with leather.
Along that same line he sends the working. He pulls Aether (mana) up through his heels out of the ground he stands on, packs it raw in his Shell as Charge, and puts the whole of it, the coat a practitioner ordinarily wears spread thin over body and blade, into the last finger’s width of the edge for the length of one stroke. At his rung a Body fighter commands matter as an object, which means the thing his hand is on does as it is told, and what he tells the sword is to be an edge and nothing else.
That is why the cut does not ask the steel. The market blade is only a ruler laid down for the line to follow. What parts the harness is the Charge along it, B-Grade on the edge from a man whose hands read a mean of 125.
Applications

Parting worked harness that stops the plain steel of a market sword
Ending an exchange in one stroke

Associations

The Body Path, as a strike
STARK RIME, a thread of it along the edge
LET YOUR FEET DO IT, which takes the warning off the cut
The road sword, a plain market blade he has never bonded

Limitations

It is one cut, and a man who sees the line can step off it
There is no second stroke folded inside the first
Each cut takes about two percent of his reserve
A little over three fifths of what he spends gets to the edge, which is his yield, and the share that burns in his Shell comes off as cold, because he is a Stark and that is the shape his furnace takes
The cold goes into the nearest thing, which is the sword, and steel chilled hard enough stops bending and starts cracking; smiths call the point where it turns the brittle change, and a blade on the wrong side of it breaks like a pane
Every clean line leaves his sword a little nearer to glass, which is the true price of the art and the reason he wears through a blade every couple of years and leaves the old one with a farrier
A blade that has had too many winters of it may be the thing that gives
Its tell is one cut, no flourish, with the white thread on the edge and the back heel settling before it
To beat it, do not be where the line ends: break the measure as the heel sets, or crowd him so close the hips have no room to turn

I. Identity

II. Soul Architecture

III. Wellspring Harmonizations

Oblation (Fate) · the Offering Flame; what is given up returns as force, never one grain more. Every boundary he moves is paid here.
Fixatio (Medium) · a line he draws sets and stays set.
Luminalis (Medium) · the line between what is seen and what is there; sees edges, hides the ones he wants hidden.
Mortalis (Medium) · thresholds and completion; sees a boundary through to its proper end.
Nihiloth (Wild) · the boundary between something and nothing; for his last art only, and seldom.
Forms: Scriptia · Harmonia.

IV–V. Stats
Pool: Levels 1–100 1,200 + 101–200 1,500 + 201–300 1,800 + 301–400 2,100 + 401–480 1,920 + Thresholds I–XIII 9,100 = 17,620 points on Sub-Stats.



























































PrimaryTotalMeanSignature Sub-StatsDominion3,500500Sovereignty 1,150 · Radius 900 · Sense 600 · Gravity 400 (divided by seven; Throne outside)Gnosis3,600450Analysis 950 · Fluency 800 · Perception 700 · Retention 500Resilience3,000375Ward 1,100 · Integrity 700 · Continuity 500Tempering2,400300Maturity 800 · Clarity 700 · Coherence 500Harmonics2,200275Axis 800 · Attunement 500 · Synergy 450Dexterity1,200150Economy 450 · Finesse 400Ardency1,000125Compression 400 · Penetration 350Vitality72090Threshold 220 · Constitution 180 · Regeneration 150
Skills: Boundary-reading Archmaster · Vaeloric script Archmaster · Spiritual law Archmaster · Governance Expert · Small talk Apprentice.
VI. Physical Force
Vitality 720, Ardency 1,000: thin in the body like every Valorin. He stops talking and starts drawing.
VII. Aether Flow
Essence through a surveyed lattice; every boundary moved is paid through Oblation at exact par. Domain upkeep about 1.6 million EU a second.
VIII. Traits
Lineage (Valorin Family page): Scripted Soul Lattice · Primordial Scriptia · Harmonic Translation Engine · Living Spell Memory · Arcane Vessel Sovereignty · the Cistern of Unspoken Lines · Scribed Flesh · the Inner Grimoire · Errata · the Distributed Soul.
His own (each feeds his boundary arts):

The Surveyor’s Eye Feeds every boundary art. Sees boundaries: of bodies, wards, claims, Domains, and between what a soul owns and what it only holds. Cannot move what he has not seen. Chaos and the undefined show nothing.
Consideration Feeds every boundary art and the Last Line. No boundary moves without a price; he always knows it exactly and pays it from what is truly his, returned as force at par. Cannot spend another’s claim; every payment leaves a hollow open until the bargain closes.
The Headmaster’s Bounds Feeds Terminus and the Walled Garden. Every ward, wall, door and boundary-stone of Vaeloris and the Scriptorium is written to his name; there, lines obey him first and cost a fraction. Abroad he pays full price.
Threshold-Walker Feeds Inter Est and Limen Apertum. Stands on the line between two states and belongs to neither for a breath. Fails when a working fills both sides at once.

IX. Domain
Hortus Conclusus, the Walled Garden · complete Principality Domain. About 12 km natural; the whole valley of Vaeloris on his own ground. Upkeep about 1.6 million EU/s; collapses at about 14% reserve, a little over half an hour from full. “Inside, every line is mine: what is in and what is out, what is owned and what is only held, what may cross and what may not.” Ruled silver lines cover everything; every edge shows. Behaviors: Partition · The Gate · Title Shown · The Price Board · Confinement · Restored Edges. A greater sovereignty contests it line by line; chaos walks through its walls.
X. Techniques
Boundary Manipulation. Everything is held by where it ends; he draws, moves, opens, closes, joins and restores those lines in Valorin Scriptia. No boundary moves without consideration.

Terminus, the Drawn Line · a boundary nothing crosses without his leave, in space or in concept; holds by his Sovereignty; price rises with what it holds back.
Divisio, the Line Through · parts a thing along a drawn line: a wall, a ward, a fused working, a curse from its host. Through a living body: trusted least, used last. Lines through greater claims do not take.
Confinium, the Shared Border · overlaps two boundaries into one; both must be his or consent.
Limen Apertum, the Opened Threshold · a door where a wall was; between his marked boundary-stones, here and there share one threshold. Only between marked stones.
Lex Finium, the Law of Limits · sets a working a limit: not beyond this line. Greater sovereignty pushes it back.
Inter Est, Between · on the line between two states, belonging to neither, for a breath.
Restitutio Finium, the Borders Restored · puts a broken boundary back: a breached ward, a torn Veil seam, a soul’s edge after possession. Restores the line, not what passed through.
Ultima Linea, the Last Line (Nihiloth) · draws the boundary between something and nothing beneath a thing and lets it fall to the far side. Oblation demands exactly what is unmade, and both times he has drawn it, the price was memory, which in a Valorin is the architecture of the soul.

First, at twenty-four: something nameless was beginning to be in a hollow under the staff gardens. He unmade it before it finished. Price: every memory of his own childhood before the age of nine. He knows his early years only as Malex tells them.
Second, the night Rheana died: her soul sickness could not be cut from her while she lived, because in a living soul the sickness and its edge were the same line. Price: every memory of his sister’s last year. He cannot remember her dying; Malex remembers for both of them.
Sworn never to draw it under a person. Archon and Titan boundaries are not his; symmetric null.
Limits: metaphysical, not absolute: he cannot redraw his own boundaries or raise his own limits. Chaos has no edges. Greater claims push back. Overpaying ends in cavitation.



XI. Spirit Axes

Sienna Valorin his wife, Lyria’s mother; in a magical hibernation. He visits every evening after the Scriptorium closes; the line around her room is the one he walks first.
Lyria Valorin daughter, 12; the boundary he would pay any price to hold. She has grown up with her mother asleep.
Malex Valorin older brother and best colleague; a healthy brotherhood: they disagree about everything, drink together on the bad nights, and stand behind each other in every room that matters. Malex remembers two things Dhaerin paid away: his childhood, and Rheana’s last year.
Rheana Valorin younger sister, Xhem’s mother; died of a soul sickness; both brothers mourn her.
Xhem Valorin nephew, Rheana’s son; now teaching at the Scriptorium under him.
Vaeloris his village, written to his name.

XII. Resistances
Possession, intrusion, soul-edits: very high (Ward 1,100; surveyed soul). Spatial attacks and folds: high. Structured magic: high. Weak to chaos and the nameless and to dream logic. Deepest danger: overpaying (cavitation); two hollows are already held open. Counters: formless or ever-changing attacks, greater sovereignty, distance from his marked thresholds, being made to choose whose boundary to hold.
XIII. Physical Description
Six foot two, the tallest of the three siblings; broad-shouldered and straight-backed, like a surveyor who walks his own lines. Warm Kushian brown skin a shade darker than Malex’s; thick white Valorin hair, medium-length, worn loose and a little tousled, falling around his ears as if he has just pushed it back with one hand and forgotten it; a short white beard and mustache, a little rough at the edges. Pale royal violet eyes, the same as his brother’s and his nephew’s; ruled lines cross his irises when he reads a boundary. His face rests in a faint, amused half-smile, as if he has already worked out the price of whatever you are about to ask. Lattice markings in straight ruled lines along hands, forearms and collarbones. A deep violet headmaster’s robe edged in silver, properly closed, and the leader’s chain of iron keys and brass rulers. Smells of cedar, sealing wax, chalk dust and cold iron. People tend to stop where he stands.
XIV. Psychology
Core wound: he leads a village written to his name and could not keep a line around his own sister; in a living soul, the soul sickness and its edge were the same line. His wife sleeps behind a line he cannot open. Flaw: he prices everything, including what should not have a price; fair, and hard to love. Desire: keep Vaeloris, the Scriptorium, Lyria and Xhem safe; a school where nobody pays more than they owe. Voice: measured, formal, exact; he finishes every sentence he starts. Calls Malex’s work vandalism with footnotes; Malex calls his accounting.
XV. Equipment
The Chain of Vaeloris · leader’s chain; each brass ruler is cut from a village boundary-stone and is a marked threshold, so Vaeloris is always one step away. The Measuring Rod · black iron surveyor’s rod with silver rule marks; draws his lines. The Ledger of Prices · bonded grimoire recording every price he has paid; two pages sealed in black wax record the prices of the Last Line, not the memories.
XVI. Temperance Record
I first glyph a straight line · II lattice writes in ruled lines · III the schoolroom door nobody opened for three days · IV first line drawn through a working · V every line keeps someone out · VI chose to pay his own prices · VII first Limen Apertum · VIII the Walled Garden opens · IX Oblation keeps his books · X a line across all Three Planes · XI Rheana’s death to a soul sickness, and the second Last Line: a price he did not choose, and one he did · XII the ground of Vaeloris knows his lines · XIII surveyed soul stabilizes, Domain matures · XIV not reached.
XVII. Fracture Log

Rheana’s death (Soul · Fate) · mourned.
The Last Line, twice (Fate · Lattice) · paid: his childhood before nine, and his sister’s last year; two hollows Oblation keeps open.
Sienna’s hibernation (Soul · Fate) · ongoing.
The headship (Fate) · ongoing; the weight of a village written to his name.

characters/volume-i-—-character-cards/do.title: Dougou Zettari
characters/volume-i-—-character-cards/do.content:
The Iron Bison · He Whose Stillness Is the Warning
As of sixteen years after the Division of the Worlds.
I. Identity
Full Name: Dougou Ozumu Zettari
Alias: The Iron Bison · Little Bison (Malakar’s name for him) · Baba (to his children)
Race / Lineage: Human · Zettari, the Path-Born Sovereigns of Aegor; royal line of Kushara · Vessel of the Titan Atla’zon, the World-Binder
Faction / Rank: Sovereign of Kushara. Every house of Kushara has sworn fealty to him.
Status: Alive
Family: Father Shaka-Al Zettari (dead; gone into the Paths). Wife Naevra Yukari, sister of Naiser Yukari. Five children: Ma’Kovu (15), Rashani (14), Rengai (12), Zuberi (10), Ayaka (8).
Heir: Zuberi, his fourth son, whom he calls Dawn Guard. The three elder brothers declined the heirship; Zuberi embraced it.
Current Location: The Sovereign House, Kushara Crownlands, rebuilt to his own design for his family
Origin: Born the vessel of Atla’zon, who bears the law of gravity and the burden of order. The Titan’s pressure has sat in his body since birth; the Iron Bison is the seal that lets a human frame hold it.
Catalyst Event: The Akar Road. He hung in Malakar’s chains and watched his father beaten to death, then was left alive on purpose. The Paths took him in while he was dying, healed him and sent him back.
II. Soul Architecture
Stat line: Stage VI Glory · Expert (Faceted), at the Division of the Worlds · Level not known · State: sealed by the Iron Bison · Class not known · Body primary, Fate secondary, Mastery not known · Lenses: home + 6, with Atla’zon’s Strain outside the Sixty
Temperance Stage: Stage VI · Glory · Expert, at the Division of the Worlds.
Level: not known
Path: Body, primary. Fate, secondary, as in all the royal Zettari
Crystal: Zettari three-layer Crystal; Faceted by its Stage at the Division; Mastery not known
Crystal State: Sealed by the Iron Bison. All seven seals burst at the Sevenfold Release; how far they have been rebuilt in sixteen years is not known.
Standing with the Paths: Path-Acknowledged. One of the very few Zettari to walk the Paths and return alive
III. Wellspring Harmonizations

Fixatio Primary. The seal.
Anima Spirare Engine. The harder the sealed body pulls, the more readily the soul provides.
Coagulatio Densifier. Compressed Essence laid down in layers.
Chthonica Column. Roots the axis crown to root.
Phreatis Circulation. All seven chambers breathing as one.
Monolithion Support. The monument body.
Terranova Support. Living foundation, recovery under load.
Atla’zon’s Strain The core. A Titan’s power, not one of the Sixty. Titanic compression and world-binding pressure seated in a human body; the reason the seal was necessary in the first place.

IV–V. Stats
All values not known. Leans follow the Zettari lineage and the Iron Bison.



























































PrimaryLeanSignature Sub-StatsWeak pointsVitality+++++Fortitude · Absorption · Tolerance · ThresholdnoneResilience+++++Integrity · Continuity · Fortification · PersistencenoneDominion++++Gravity · Sovereignty · RadiusnoneArdency+++Compression · Density · Penetrationprojects almost nothing outwardGnosis+++Perception · Analysis · Forecastreads structure, struggles with the structurelessTempering+++Maturity · Clarity · YieldnoneDexterity++Economy · FinesseFeint · EvasionHarmonics+Stability · Axisthe Attraction Layer does almost nothing in his art
VI. Physical Force
Figures not known. Feats known: stopped a falling dome with his body in the plaza at Kushara; killed eleven hundred of fifteen hundred demonic N’Kharu on the Akar Road; ran across the sky to the Aerne mouth on claimed air; struck Malakar two hundred miles with one Black-Heart Bison Break; with the Three Halls lent to him, emptied all seven chambers through one fist and obliterated Malakar’s body. Sixteen years on: stands in a ring with one hand behind his back while his two eldest, both master swordsmen, fail to touch him.
VII. Aether Flow
A sealed vessel. External leak near nil by design, so Essence-readers take him for dormant or untrained. Internal cycling not known.
VIII. Traits

Vessel of Atla’zon He carries the World-Binder’s pressure-law in a human body.
Sealed-World Physiology Essence and feeling convert to stored weight instead of radiating.
True Everlasting Eyes Pale silver-gray eyes ringed in gold since the Paths. Reads the script of the world, the Wellspring a person draws on, and the threads between people. Read of Intent: feels the will to strike a breath before the strike. Limit: needs structure to read.
Fault-Sight (Brow Chamber) Reads strain, footing, breath and the weak seam in a body or a wall.
Load-Bearing Will Takes another’s Load onto his own body and carries it into the ground.
Sovereign Footing Ground he stands on is harder to take from him.
Wellspring Sovereignty Reads Wellsprings at a glance. Whether the Spring Arts have opened to him in sixteen years is not known.

IX. Domain
Not known. At the Division he had none, only its seed, a pressure the house calls the Ground That Confesses: near him movement grows expensive and weak structures show their strain.
X. Techniques
Elite master of the Zettari arts. Sixteen years of rule and practice have made him the standard his house measures itself against.
Matla (three of the Nine Practices at the Division). Form, the First: makes and changes matter. Anti-Form: the unbinding of substance. Dominion, the Fifth: Material Jurisdiction. Paid under the Law of Weight. Any Practice gained since is not known.
Njia ya Uzito, the Way of Weight. Mtiririko wa Kimya (the Silent Flow), the Breaking Palm, the Sarmad Fracture.
The Iron Bison (his version: the Iron Tree).

Nanatsu no Fūin · Sevenfold Seal. Closes the whole vessel. About fifteen in a hundred of full reserve. Cannot be held while a chamber vents.
The seven branches · Iron Fist, Kick, Elbow, Knee, Shoulder, Head, Step. Three to ten in a hundred each. Contact and a grounded stance.
Kokushin Gyūha · Black-Heart Bison Break. The apex: one sealed chamber into one point of contact. About eight in a hundred.
Ozumu no Katachi · Form of Accumulated Crush.
Juuretsu · Binding Weight.
Tetsu no Arashi · the Iron Bison’s Charge.
Kokushin Shissō · Black-Heart Stampede. Every chamber emptied into the legs at once.
Nanatsu no Kaihō · Sevenfold Release. All seven chambers into one point of contact. Done once, against Malakar, with the Three Halls in his spine.
Shinsei Tetsugyū · True Iron Bison, the apex state. Whether he has reached it is not known.

Borrowed, not his: Mitsu no Ma, the Three Halls, lent by Naiser Yukari and Muken Moto at the Division and returned after the blow.
XI. Spirit Axes

Naevra Yukari (wife) An alliance marriage neither chose, made real under the baobab. Carried north with the Inner World at the Division; with him in Kushara now, mother of his five children.
Ma’Kovu (son, 15) The eldest. Origin Eye, power over Names, master of the single katana. Favors his father.
Rashani (son, 14) Origin Eye, power over Origins, master of two katana. Favors his father.
Rengai (son, 12) His mother’s eyes and face, his father’s wrath in a fight. Training in every Zettari art. May join his elder brothers’ sessions at thirteen.
Zuberi (son, 10) Dawn Guard. His heir. The most Zettari of the children.
Ayaka (daughter, 8) The image of her mother. He spoils her. She wants to be a fighter.
Shaka-Al Zettari (father) Killed by Malakar on the Akar Road. His body turned to sand and went into the Paths.
Revari (kinsman) Last of the eastern branch line. Hanged on the gate of the Sovereign House.
Naiser Yukari (brother-in-law) Lent him the soul strand at the Division.
Muken Moto Dougou killed his father, Gimbzo Kōkan Moto, at seventeen. Muken swore to fight him when the snow went, no armies. What became of that oath in sixteen years is not known.
Malakar The enemy. Obliterated at the Division and stopped, not dead. Kushara was retaken from his forces.
Atla’zon The Titan whose burden he carries.
Theluji, Seraph Their standing sixteen years on is not known.
The Paths Healed him, opened his eyes, trained him in Dominion.

XII. Resistances
Structural / Impact: Very high while sealed.
Reading and detection: Very high; a sealed body emits nothing.
Root disruption: Low. Lost footing or a blow through an open Root drains the column into the ground.
Void and anti-recognition fields: Low.
Contamination: Low.
Emotional breach: Lowest. Love, grief and kinship flood the Heart chamber, and he now has a wife and five children.
Known Counters: Take the ground away, strike the open vent, contaminate the loop, or reach him.
XIII. Physical Description
Height / Build: Six foot nine. Monolithic, load-bearing.
Skin: Dark brown. Eyes: Pale silver-gray, pupils ringed in gold. Hair: Long, heavy black locs with gold cuffs, gray now at the temples.
Scars: Slash scars across the chest; a round scar at the center of the chest from Malakar, closed by the Paths. An old break in the jaw that clicks when he smiles.
Dress for war: An open black-and-gold royal warrior’s robe, bare chest beneath.
The House-Bound Dress: A blend of Zettari and Yukari clothing. Long dark haori-style coat worn open; wide hakama-style trousers and plain cloth shoes (Yukari). Black and gold (Zettari). High collar closed with Yukari bond-knots in Zettari gold thread. A thick braided rope belt with two tassels: his Cord of Becoming braided the Yukari way from a gold strand and a silver-white one, knotted for what he has paid, with five bright beads for his five children. Fighting wraps at the wrists.
XIV. Psychology
Core Wound: He was a sealed vessel before he was old enough to choose to be one. Then he watched his father die while he hung in chains, and was left alive on purpose.
Flaw: Turns every feeling into stored weight and calls it mastery.
Desire: To keep what he rebuilt: his house, his family and Kushara. To be ready the day Malakar comes back.
Strength: Patience, doctrine over impulse, violence that accumulates. Carries other people’s weight unasked.
As a father: Strict about the rules of the yard, never raises his voice, and is soft on his daughter. Six people get past the seal now.
Foils: Muken Moto; Malakar.
Voice: Quiet, severe, patient. Few words, plain ones. “Death will have me when it earns me.” To his sons: “Language.” “Again.”
XV. Equipment
None. His body is the only implement he trusts. He wears his Cord of Becoming as a belt.
XVI. Temperance Record
I–IV: not itemized.
V · Splintering: held through the war and the fall of Kushara.
VI · Glory: crossed on the Akar Road, mid-battle.
Since: not known.
XVII. Fracture Log

Birth. Seeded as Atla’zon’s vessel.
The war. Kills Gimbzo Kōkan Moto at seventeen.
The Akar Road. Kills eleven hundred demonic N’Kharu; Malakar chains him, kills his father and blows a hole through his chest.
The Paths. Healed; True Everlasting Eyes; two months of Dominion.
The burial. Kills Tariq-Nal, the Sin of Pride.
The Trident. Saves Naevra from Malakar’s beam.
The Division of the Worlds. His fist meets Malakar’s above the Aerne and the one land breaks into four. With the Three Halls he obliterates Malakar, who is stopped and not dead.
The sixteen years. Takes the Kushara Crownlands back from Malakar’s forces. Makes every house swear fealty and becomes Sovereign. Rebuilds the Zettari homeland to his own design. Has five children with Naevra and names Zuberi his heir.

Squares at the hour the ledger wants and not the hour the person needs, so he is hard on debtors who needed grace. Reads every kindness, thanks or favor as a bill, and so is lonely among people who love him.DesireThe road open once more, so he can walk the last load up himself, hear “delivered” in the reeve’s own mouth, and shelve the token.StrengthExactness other people can build on. Hiromi Mahuo
Heir of the Vermilion Dynasty · Paragon of Irath, the Archon of Dominion
I. Identity
Full Name: Hiromi Mahuo
Pronunciation: hee-ROH-mee mah-HOO-oh
Age: 17
Race / Lineage: Human · the Mahuo line, through his mother Saeju, rightful heir of the Vermilion Dynasty
Faction: House Mahuo by blood; raised in the Cedar Enclave by Naiser Yukari, the Lord of the Cedars, who seats him on the Zettari bench among his own household.
Epithet: Paragon of Irath. In the south they say the ground he stands on is already his.
Status: Alive
Family: Mother Saeju Mahuo, killed when a roof came down on her in the war; uncle Cozbi Mahuo, Head of House Mahuo, who kept him for three years after the war; Naiser Yukari, who raised him; Senna Yukari, Naiser’s daughter, who sets his collar straight like a sister.
