cosmology--and--metaphysics/faith-and-th.title: The Fourteen Titans
cosmology--and--metaphysics/faith-and-th.content:
“An Archon is a crowned principle. A Titan is a load-bearing law. Neither wants anything, and prayer presumes wanting.”
Catechism of Equal Breath, opening clauses, as cited by the Lectors of Sancta Lux

The weir at Sallow Reach gave way in the spring of Year 588 and took Gib Harrowgill’s mill with it, three hundred sacks of barley, two mules and the wheel he had cut himself, and Harrowgill, a big red man with a big red grievance, walked forty miles to the Bench at Carrowmark and laid suit against Atla’zon the World-Binder for the weight of the water. He had a case, as he explained to everyone on the road. Water falls because a Titan holds which way is down, the Titan had gone on holding it, and his mill was in pieces. The clerks could find no rule against hearing him, so the Bench heard him. It ran nine days in the hot end of May with the court doors open, half the county came in holiday ribbons with cold chicken, and the Stone Choir (the masons’ order that listens to rock before anyone is allowed to cut it) sent six chanters in slate blue to sit on the defendant’s bench, uninvited, and hum at the floor. A Scale lector argued for the plaintiff for the sheer joy of it. The sergeants broke up two fistfights among the junior lectors and one among their mothers.
On the ninth day the Bench ruled against Harrowgill in the one sentence the Accord keeps for such occasions, which you will find below, adding that the defendant had no seat, no court and no herald on whom a writ could be served, and could no more be sued for falling water than the floor could be sued for holding up the judge. Harrowgill threw his hat at the bench and walked home. He found the six chanters already in the river up to their chests, listening to what was left of his weir, because nobody had ever asked them anything so interesting. What they built him has stood for a hundred and twenty-seven years. He never paid them and they never asked, and his grandchildren still set out a lamp for the Titan on the anniversary of the judgment, out of spite.
What a Titan Is
The Accord’s working definition is one sentence long and it has survived every attempt to improve it. An Archon is a principle enthroned. A Titan is a principle bearing weight.
The distinction is administrative before it is theological. An Archon can be consulted, argued with in the abstract, and cited in a filing. It has a seat, a court, a lineage of heralds and a body of doctrine written by people who were not present. A Titan has none of that and needs none of it, because a Titan is not doing anything so voluntary as governing. Ask who is in charge of weight and you have asked the wrong question, because weight is the posture Atla’zon is holding: his law is weight and the burden of order, and a stone falls because he kneels. Remove him and the question of who governs falling does not pass to a successor. There is simply nothing left for the word down to mean. Every Titan’s law is an idea of this kind and none of them is a formula. The ordinary world’s habits, stones falling and fire eating wood, were settled under these loads in the Physical Epochs, and they hold whether anyone measures them or not. The Measurewrights measure them and call the measures natural philosophy, which describes the posture very well and has never once given the reason for it.
This is why the Titans have no theology worth the name and an enormous quantity of engineering. The Stone Choir listens to rock harmonics before cutting. The Undercrypt Keepers whisper equations at buried buttresses. The Ledger Monks refuse to let a ruler erase a predecessor’s failure from a Dynasty Hall. Every one of those orders is doing maintenance, and would be insulted to hear it called prayer.
The catechism at the head of this page is a catechism, and catechisms like to be tidy. “Neither wants anything” is true of a Titan and true of a Hollow Throne, which is the law with nobody home. An occupied Throne can notice you, as anyone who has pulled the wrong thread will tell you if they still have the use of their mouth.
Where a Titan comes from. Titans descend from Archons. An Archon is a principle enthroned, and a Titan is the same principle bearing weight, come down out of the throne room and into the load. The Epochs were the forging parties, because a law can descend all it likes and still needs somebody to give it a back. Dazkar’s law comes down from Urion, and it was Bairos and Aegor who forged a body to hold it.
What a Titan is to the Wellsprings. Titans are the Wellsprings themselves, and the Sixty are their manifestations. Each of the Sixty is one way a Titan’s law shows up, carried by Aether (mana), much as a burn, a lamp and a hot wind are all ways one fire shows up. A soul that tempers on a Wellspring has based itself on some part of a Titan’s law, which is a great deal less than an introduction. The Titans bear all three planes, so the Sixty make up all three, and a Wellspring’s kind names its home: Wild to Aegor, Spirit to Ashura, Fate to Bara, Medium to the Veil. Every entry in the register names its Titan. The Sixty stay sixty, however many ways the old books count them.
A Titan walks no Path. A Path is a soul leaning on one layer of itself, and a Titan is no such thing. It has no lean, no ladder and no Stage, and nothing a window could report. Practitioners who call a Titan “a Body power” are reading the Order column below, which tells you where the weight sits and nothing about the Titan.

Fourteen Titans are seated against fourteen Archons, and the symmetry is close enough that most mortal registers assume a one-to-one correspondence. It does not hold. Dazkar grounds Urion cleanly and Chronaeus grounds Valen cleanly, and after that the pairs go ragged. Kaldrion answers to nothing in the Archonic roster at all. The Measurewrights hold, without enthusiasm, that this is what an honest count looks like and that the neat version is the one that would need explaining.

Above the Titans stand the Epochs. Aegor, Bairos and Ashura appear throughout the entries as the forging and binding parties, and they are not Titans and are never to be filed as such. Where a Titan’s Bonds field names them, the field is recording provenance rather than alliance. In the days of the Physical Epochs, Bara (whom the Archonic registers record as Bairos), Ashura and Aegor walked in human form. What those days left lying about, and what the Great Spirit War left after them, are the dead and dangerous battlefields, the relics people kill for and the old beings who remember, and every entry below keeps running into them.
A warning on figures, from the Guild’s own Errata. A heart that beats once in a thousand years, a life measured in eons: these are Epoch figures, accurate as statements about magnitude and meaningless as statements about years, and none of them goes on the Concordance’s count. Where an entry uses a received name for an Age (the Pyrrhean Epidemic, the Fractured Era), I have said what the Errata makes of it.
The Seating
The orders describe what layer of the world the Titan is holding rather than any rank between them, and each one’s law reaches past its order: the Bonds that tie a Titan to Bairos are how it reaches Fate. There is no Fate order among them, because nothing bears weight on what is no reality. Nothing in the register establishes a hierarchy and the Guild has repeatedly declined to invent one.
A word on the Ground field in each entry. It names what the old registers call that Titan’s Wellspring, and the old registers are right: a Ground is the Titan’s law at full scale, a law and a place at once. The sixty Wellsprings proper are that law in portions a soul can use. Each is a kind of Aether, acting on a Soul Crystal in its own way and standing for a principle and a transformation, and each has sites where its Aether pools (a Core, in common speech). So the Measurewrights no longer argue over whether Grounds should be counted among the Sixty. You can temper on Ignivale, and you can no more temper on Omnis’s Breath than you can drink a sea. The Codex line closing each entry seats the working on one of the Sixty by name, which is the part a practitioner can use. Vohrin is the register’s one exception: its line names the Titan’s own power, worked at Wellspring level, with the northern frost arts drawing on it directly and outside the Sixty, and the Sixty stay sixty.
The old registers are also loose with the word Essence, and I have kept their wording here because they are the only witnesses we have. Essence proper is a soul’s own substance, Aether refined in the Crystal and stamped with identity. Where one of these entries has Essence pooling in the ground, storming across the Veil or overcharging a region, read it as Aether, or as what the dead and the very large have left behind them, and a Measurewright will think better of you.































































































TitanEpithetOrderWhat it holdsATLA’ZONThe World-BinderPhysicalWeight and the burden of order: orientation, duration, adhesionGAIAThe Living Mantle of FormPhysicalMatter, mortality, material harmonyOMNISThe Skyfather of DraconisSpiritual SeatAspiration, breath, Essence circulationFLORWYNThe Verdant WeaverSpiritual SeatRenewal, what the faiths call reincarnationDAZKARThe Arbiter of PurganethSpiritual SeatProportion, restitution, penanceNYSERAThe Dreaming VeilSpiritual SeatThe boundary between imagined and realSYLORINThe Ferryman of EthereaSpiritual SeatContinuity of pattern across livesILGRIMMThe Whisper of HelströvaSpiritual SeatFear as function, knowledge held under wisdomVALMIRThe Titan of the CreviceStrataCollapse, threshold, permission to endKALDRIONThe HexthroneStrataLoad, bearing, honest measureCHRONAEUSThe Clock of AgesStrataPace, consequence, the end of erasPROMETHEUSThe Flame of TherosAbyssal DepthsDestruction as transformationZAR’THUUNThe Titan of AbythronAbyssal DepthsThe boundary between something and nothingVOHRINThe Titan of NiflheimAbyssal DepthsStillness after the end, the settling of endings

Call the Abyssal Depths the back of the house, whatever the shrine schools say about an enemy quarter of the pantheon. The order in which the three operate is fixed. Prometheus burns what is false. Zar’thuun unmakes what is excess. Vohrin stills what is left so it can be built upon.

The Sixty, Titan by Titan
Thirteen Titans hold the Sixty between them. The fourteenth, Vohrin, holds none, since his frost is his own power worked at Wellspring level. The orders do not sort the kinds: a Spiritual Seat Titan can show up as a Wild Wellspring, and an Abyssal one as a Wellspring of Fate, because a Titan’s law goes on past the place where it is holding. Each Titan’s own entry links every name below to its place in the register.














































































































TitanWildSpiritFateMediumPrometheusCinerion, Exuroth, Manganthra, Pyreveil, TransmutatioPenanceflare··OmnisAnima Spirare, Cymorath, Ignivale, Sublimare, Sublimatio··AurevaneFlorwynRebirthine, VerdantiaRedemptionBenediction·DazkarJudiciumAbsolution, Contrition, Mirithane, PenanceOblation, Tarturon·NyseraEidolynHypnather, Oneirion·LuminalisSylorin·Catharsis, Letheveil, ThaloréSomnalis, TransferencePhreatisIlgrimmTenebraAbyntheus, Eclipseron, Nyxial··ValmirCataclysm, Dissolution, Fractura, Solfatara··MortalisKaldrionMonolithion, Orrenthal, Petralon···ChronaeusPyraeon, VantabrielLethegraal·AnamnesisGaiaCoagula, Coagulatio, Materia Primordia, Terranova···Atla’zonAscensio, Basilithe, Chthonica··FixatioZar’thuunAbython, Nihiloth·Oblivara·VohrinOutside the Sixty···
World Spirits
The word gets used as a Stage and as a kind of being, and in the Guild’s register it is one thing. A World Spirit is a soul whose Domain claim has grown into a place. It began as a person, or a beast, or a dragon. At Principality, Stage XIII, the Continuum registers the law it embodies and the local biome starts carrying its doctrine, which the trade calls the first World Spirit threshold. At Zenith, Stage XIV, a vacant Throne recognizes it, and that is full World Spirit, a place with an opinion. Because a Domain is a claim made on the Attraction Layer, every World Spirit stands under Fate, whichever road it walked to get there.
That makes them the near opposite of a Titan. A Titan is a law that was given a load and never had a self to lose. A World Spirit is a self that has become a law and is slowly losing the rest of it. The old ones sleep. Slept long enough, they set like a cooling mountain and become Titanstone, found and never quarried, which is why a cracked block can take a city down with it and why the Four Ceilings argue about it in such careful language. The name is a stonecutters’ mistake and every Titan-order monk will correct you on it at length.
The Titan-Keyed Arts
Fourteen workings sit in the register under the category Titan-Keyed. Mortal practitioners call them Titanic Arts, and the Accord tolerates the phrase in the street and strikes it from anything carrying a seal, on the grounds that the art is not the Titan’s. The Titan does not perform it and is not consulted about it. The practitioner is entering a process the Titan is already running and imposing a boundary on it, which is the whole of what a glyph does anywhere in the Codex and is only remarkable here because of the scale of the process being entered.
Three things separate a Titan-Keyed working from every other entry in the register.

The gate is absolute. Twelve of the fourteen require Stage XIV, Zenith. Two require Stage XV, Revelation, which sits above Zenith and is reached only through genuine exchange with an Archon or a Titan at a level where the practitioner participates rather than merely survives. Those two are The Closing Eye and The Stillwater Rite. Nobody in the Accord’s living register holds both. The gate binds these fourteen workings and no others: the ordinary frost arts worked on Vohrin’s power keep the lower floors their own pages state.
Every one keys to a condition that must already exist. A strain already visible. A silence already present. A fault line already open. A soul already dying. Not one of the fourteen originates its own condition, and this is the structural reason none of them can be used as an opening move.
The cost lands somewhere specific and does not negotiate. Eleven of the fourteen bill the caster’s own body, memory or self-image. Two bill bystanders. One bills nobody at all, which is the entry the Stone Choir has spent nine hundred years finding sinister.


Each entry carries the register’s own fields. Class is an Accord convenience and appears nowhere in the Master Codex.
Method, Grade, Range and Medium are not held for any Titan-Keyed working, and the omission is structural rather than clerical. A Method names how a practitioner relates to the idea they work: reading it, controlling it, inscribing it, distilling it. A Titan-Keyed working has no such relation. The practitioner is not working an idea of their own at all. They are imposing a boundary on a process that was already running at world scale and would go on running whether or not anybody arrived.
Grade measures magnitude against a stat. Range measures reach from a caster. Medium names what the sentence was written into. None of the three has a value when the process is the ground you are standing on.

The Ledger of Costs
Read down this column and the register’s actual argument becomes visible. Stop thinking of a Titan-Keyed working as a large spell, and think of a bill presented in a currency the caster did not choose.
















































































TitanThe ArtWhat the casting takesATLA’ZONThe Bent Knee’s BurdenThe caster’s own joints and breath take on the Titan’s characteristic strain.GAIAFlesh Remembers StoneMineral deposits form under the caster’s own skin over a career.OMNISThe Skyfire PulseThe caster’s respiratory system takes the first pass of the purification.FLORWYNThe Green ChordPersonality bleed-through into the successor, standard rather than exceptional.DAZKARThe Mirrored ScaleThe caster is bound by the same mirror for the working’s duration.NYSERAThe Somnum FlowThe channel is bidirectional the entire time it stays open.SYLORINThe Ferryman’s CurrentThe soul arrives with the full emotional charge of its death still attached.ILGRIMMThe Hollow That WatchesThe caster is not exempted by the silence they enforced.VALMIRThe Canyon’s PatienceUnresolved resentment steers the collapse worse than intended.PROMETHEUSThe Pyric RefinementValued memories attached to the false part burn away with it.ZAR’THUUNThe Closing EyeSmall memories erased from everyone nearby, caster included.VOHRINThe Stillwater RiteHeld too long, the target forgets their own purpose for living.KALDRIONThe Deep Grid’s VerdictNone to the caster. The cost falls entirely on the subject tested.CHRONAEUSThe Era-Forge’s TollInnocents inside the compressed era age and suffer at the forced rate.
Three entries break the pattern and each breaks it differently. The Closing Eye bills everyone standing nearby and the caster never learns what was taken. The Era-Forge’s Toll bills a population that was never asked and will never know it was cast. The Deep Grid’s Verdict bills nobody, which is the only clean entry in the register and is treated by every order that studies it as the most dangerous line on the page.
The Fourteen Compounds
Twelve of the fourteen arts require Zenith and two require Revelation, which places all fourteen beyond every practitioner alive. The world reaches them anyway, at a fraction, through a bottle.
Every Titan in this register has a compound keyed to it in the Standing Index, at T5 through T7, and the correspondence is exact rather than approximate: Atla’zon to Strain-Bound Marrow, Gaia to Corpus Marrow Salts, Dazkar to Purganeth Mirror-Salt, Sylorin to Ethereal Current Oil, Ilgrimm to Hollow-Watch Incense, Kaldrion to Deep Grid Mortar, Omnis to the Skyfire Pulse Vial, Florwyn to the Verdance Reclamation Draught, Nysera to the Somnum Flow Ampoule, Valmir to the Crevice-Glass Shard, Prometheus to Pyric Refinement Ash, Chronaeus to Fossil Ring Dust, Zar’thuun to the Null-Essence Draught, Vohrin to the Stillwater Draught.

This is the actual reason those compounds cost what they cost, and no price list anywhere says so. A Titan-Keyed art is a boundary imposed on a running process by a soul dense enough to survive standing in it. A compound imposes the same boundary through a substrate instead, at a smaller scale, for a shorter term, and available to a practitioner four Stages short of the gate.
The cost does not vanish with the scale. Each compound bills in the same currency the art bills in, which is why the Stillwater Draught’s long use is called a mercy killing by another name, and why the Verdance Reclamation carries the donor’s grief across intact. The bottle is smaller. The bill is the same bill.
The Bench has never described the Standing Index as a schedule of Titan-Keyed workings and would refuse the description if it were offered. Every alchemist titled above Expert has noticed.

The Fourteen in Full


The Physical Order — Atla’zon and Gaia
The Spiritual Seat — Omnis, Florwyn, Dazkar, Nysera, Sylorin, Ilgrimm
The Strata — Valmir, Kaldrion, Chronaeus
The Abyssal Depths — Prometheus, Zar’thuun, Vohrin


All fourteen on one card each, with their worship, history and heralds: The Titan Register. The fourteen Titan-Keyed workings are filed in full in the Spell Index.

cosmology--and--metaphysics/faith-and-th.content:
Any child at Varūn will tell you the war-mauls are the funniest thing in the world, and the reason is the Swallow. Pellam Hobbs, called the Swallow of the Rising Court, was the greatest lifter of his generation, a small, vain, beautiful man in a cloak of canary silk who had once floated a duke’s horse across a river with the duke still on it, and in Year 590 he came up the Varūn road with drummers and a banner to settle an insult. The dwarves had been telling people their mauls could not be levitated. So they set one out on a trestle in the fairground under the Adamant Axis, an ordinary one, a smith’s second-best, in front of some four thousand people in iron blue and ember orange. The Swallow’s coat came up the color of a spring sky and he rose a clean six feet into the air on his own art, arms spread, to a roar you could have leaned on, and he reached down with the working and took hold of the maul. The working took. The maul stayed exactly where it was, as though the maul and the trestle and the center of the world had been poured in one piece. A lifting art has to pull against something, and what it found to pull against was the Swallow. His arms came down, both shoulders left their sockets together, and he dropped onto the trestle at the end of his own tether and lay there in his canary silk, white to the lips. A seven-year-old in a leather apron walked out of the crowd, picked the maul up by the haft in one hand, and held it out to him. He could not raise his arms to take it.
He told that story against himself for thirty years, in good inns, and it is the best short account I know of what follows. Somebody holds which way is down. That somebody is not open to persuasion, and an honest smith can borrow a little of it.

Forged in the Aegoric Crucible during the Formation Epoch. Between them they hold which way is down and what things are made of. Every other Titan in the register is holding something that presumes these two are already holding theirs.

ATLA’ZON: The World-Binder

“He bears the weight of all things and the burden of divine order.”

Seat  Prime Cosmological Titan of the Physical order, sibling to Gaia. Forged in the Aegoric Crucible under Aegor’s hand during the Formation Epoch.
Domain  Permanence, Law, Weight and Strain, Time, Endurance
Ground  The Ground of Strain, called Temporal Pressure. Governs weight, the order in which one thing follows another, and the pull that draws Essence toward form.
Wellsprings  Four of the Sixty are ways his posture shows up: height paid for by steps, one note held, whatever stays where it was put, and Essence kept in the shape it was poured into. His own art is written in Petralon, which is Kaldrion’s, since a load has to have a down to fall toward. Wild: Ascensio, Basilithe, Chthonica. Medium: Fixatio.
Manifestation
A kneeling colossus of marble, obsidian and voidlight at the equatorial core of creation. His spine traces the lines of weight in every world. His heart is the ticking of the Loom, faintly audible as the Pulse of Time. Once in a thousand years he exhales, and new Wellspring sites do not so much form as get compressed into being by the pressure of it.
The Load
His law is weight and the burden of order: orientation, duration and adhesion. He decides which way is down, how fast the moment moves, and whether Essence stays inside the shape it was poured into. Withdraw him and the planes unspool back into fractal Aether. He holds everything because he knelt first, and the Priests of the Axis in the Senoth Kingdom have built four centuries of doctrine on that one sentence.
The Record
The Hobgoblin Imperium read his strain as divine hierarchy and derived the Cycle of Obedience from it, all below must bear the one above. The dwarves of Varūn raised the Adamant Axis directly above his metaphysical heart and drew the weight of his breath into resonant chambers, forging weapons that no levitation or lifting working has ever lifted. Guild surveyors place every recorded Temporal Rupture along the leyline arcs that trace his vertebrae beneath the crust. When he shifts in dream, centuries pass in seconds, or the reverse.
Bonds
Aegor, Body, Epoch. Grants structure and purpose. Bairos, Fate, Epoch. Imbues inevitability and direction. Both named figures are Epochs and are correctly seated as such.
The Titan-Keyed Art: The Bent Knee’s Burden
Defensive · Petralon · Zenith+ · [Th] Foundation + [Len] Line
Trigger  Cast only within a Domain whose weight or causal load is already under visible strain. A sagging structure. A buckling timeline.
Effect  Locks a Domain’s weight and causal sequence to Atla’zon’s own kneeling burden, so that the whole field carries the burden of order the way he does. Everything inside gains immense structural and temporal stability, and pays for it by losing forward momentum. Falling objects behave as though the weight on them had thickened. The people inside age slower than the people watching them from the edge, and both parties can tell.
Measure  Field-wide dilation caps at roughly 0.3x normal flow. Structural load tolerance roughly doubles.
Cost  The caster’s own joints and breath take on the Titan’s characteristic strain. It is a genuine physical burden for hours after release, whatever the poets do with it.
Limit  It cannot be raised over ground that is holding. The strain must already be visible or the working finds nothing to key against.
Counter  [Wy] Motion, the contrary of a kneeling burden, introduced at the field’s edge runs inward as a wave of restored momentum, snapping the held burden back all at once instead of gradually. Everything the field was carrying arrives at the floor in the same instant.
What nobody knows  Why the dilation caps at the same ratio no matter who casts it. A Zenith practitioner and an Apex one produce the identical figure, and nothing else in the Codex behaves that way.
Codex: [Th] Foundation + [Len] Line / Petralon / Zenith+ / Titan-Keyed. Method, Grade, Range and Medium open.
GAIA: The Living Mantle of Form

“Every birth is a memory of the first world.”

Seat  Prime Aetheric Titaness of the Material World. Anchors every other realm by permitting Essence to crystallize into weight and decay.
Domain  Matter, Form, Life, Stability, Evolution
Ground  The Ground of Form, called Corpus. A labyrinth of glowing strata beneath the crust where Essence condenses into crystalline ore. The source of Soul Crystal latticework.
Wellsprings  Four of the Sixty are ways her mantle shows up, every one of them matter finding its way back into a body or a seam. Wild: Coagula, Coagulatio, Materia Primordia, Terranova.
Manifestation
A colossal woman woven of mountain and river, hair a cascade of lava and bloom, skin veined with silver ley-lines, eyes deep magma pools. Each breath she exhales births auroras across the upper atmosphere. Forests grow in her shadow. Oceans take their rhythm from her weeping.
The Load
Her law is form, and the body’s debt to the ground it was taken from: the equilibrium between the spiritual and physical strata. She invented mortality as a recycling mechanism, whatever the punishment-preachers say, and death now returns Essence to the Wellsprings instead of letting the world saturate. Her Cycle of Material Harmony is why a creature’s Essence mirrors the ground it was born on. Dragons breathe flame because they were born in molten currents. Elves carry a chlorophyll resonance because their souls remembered Verdance.
The Record
She descended with Atla’zon in the First Eon to shape the first crust around the Wellspring Core, and gave Florwyn’s Realmsong weight, turning harmony into ecology. Mortals call it the First Sedimentation, the age when music became mountains. Her grief tore rifts across the land during the Great Spirit War, and the Essence Fossils date from her absorbing what the divine bled. Hobgoblin geomancers worshipped her as Karai the Forgeblooded and opened her ley veins badly enough to cause the Year of Shattered Hammers. When the Crevice opened her pulse slowed to one beat per thousand years, which the Marrowkin call the Long Heart Sleep. Seers now report tremors aligned to Wellspring awakenings. The Concord reads this as her testing whether mortals can steward matter unsupervised.
Bonds
Thalen, Form. Foremost ally, the architect whose glyphs she embodies. Maelor, Memory. Gives matter history, making fossil and bone and soil into vessels of remembrance. Urion, Balance. Keeps her evolution following pattern instead of chaos.
The Titan-Keyed Art: Flesh Remembers Stone
Supplementary · Materia Primordia · Zenith+ · [Th] Foundation + [Ma] Recall
Trigger  Direct skin contact with the target tissue, bone or soil. No reach, no medium, no proxy.
Effect  Crystallizes living Essence into Soul-Crystal-grade matter on contact. Flesh, bone and soil reforge directly into stable lattice, exactly as Gaia’s own Wellspring does it beneath the crust. The affected matter keeps its original shape and takes on a visible mineral sheen and rigidity, so a hand crystallized mid-gesture stays a hand.
Measure  The crystallization front advances roughly one centimeter per second along tissue. Faster through soil and loose stone.
Cost  The caster’s hands take the heaviest exposure. Repeated use produces genuine mineral deposits under the caster’s own skin over a career, and every practitioner who has held the art past middle age can be identified by handshake.
Limit  It converts. It does not create. There must be existing matter in contact with the palm, and the working cannot reverse itself.
Counter  [Uur] Disruption breaks the lattice mid-formation. The sudden return to soft tissue is its own kind of trauma, and the reversal is frequently worse than the completed conversion would have been.
What nobody knows  Why the crystallization front stops at scar tissue and routes around it. The Verdant Core has documented the behavior for three hundred years and has no account of it.
Codex: [Th] Foundation + [Ma] Recall / Materia Primordia / Zenith+ / Titan-Keyed. Method, Grade, Range and Medium open.

cosmology--and--metaphysics/faith-and-th.filePath: Cosmology & Metaphysics/Faith and the Powers Above/The Fourteen Titans/The Spiritual Seat — Omnis, Florwyn, Dazkar, Nysera, Sylorin, Ilgrimm.md
cosmology--and--metaphysics/faith-and-th.title: The Spiritual Seat — Omnis, Florwyn, Dazkar, Nysera, Sylorin, Ilgrimm
cosmology--and--metaphysics/faith-and-th.content:
Mother Hester Bluett, who had made the largest fortune in Ambry out of a blue so deep that dukes paid to be buried in it, announced on her deathbed in Year 604 that her soul was for sale to the highest bidder and that bids would be heard in the street, since she was paying for the view. All six of the parties concerned with such goods came, and it is the only time I know of that they have shared a road. The Church of Hollow Stars arrived first, in aurora gold, behind a paper dragon sixty feet long with nine men inside it who were not speaking to each other. The Covenant of Green Flame came barefoot and singing, each with a live sapling, weeping for it. The Order of the Penance Flame set up on her front step and scorched their own forearms over a brazier as a show of good faith, and the smell put the pie-men off their trade. The Order of Still Waters brought a copper basin and a hired stream, in barrels, so that she might be laid beside running water when the moment came. Three members of the Cult of Silver Mirrors, who are illegal in most places and have never taken this seriously, stood in the crowd angling little hand mirrors at her window. And on the second night a single person from the Cult of the Pale Lantern climbed the back stair with one lamp, told her for nothing the thing she was most afraid of, and left, and the neighbors say she laughed until the physician was sent for.
She died on the fifth day with the bidding at nine hundred in silver, holding up one blue-stained finger for the next offer. All six parties sued. The Bench could find no delivery and no title in any of them, so the money went to her dyers, who got drunk in a color you could see from the hills. As for the goods, every ferryman on the Ambry crossing will tell you she went over wet and arguing the fare, and if you want to know what that means you will find, near the foot of this page, that nobody does.

Six named realms, six laws, and every one of them concerned with what happens to a soul rather than to a stone. Draconis, Edenis, Purganeth, Virelion, Etherea, Helströva. All six lie on the Soul Plane, inside the Veil like everywhere else.

OMNIS: The Skyfather of Draconis

“The first flame to rise was not of fire, but of breath.”

Seat  Prime Elemental Titan of the Spiritual World, Draconis. Forged during the Second Breath of Aegor.
Domain  Sky, Flame, Motion, Dominion of Dragons, Celestial Breath
Ground  The Ground of Breath, called Motion and Ascension. The spiritual equivalent of respiration. Governs vitality, aspiration, and metaphysical ascent.
Wellsprings  Six of the Sixty are ways his breath shows up: a whole body answering, the open ways of the air, the first spark, rising by degrees and rising at a stroke, and light that arrives as it was sent. Wild: Anima Spirare, Cymorath, Ignivale, Sublimare, Sublimatio. Medium: Aurevane.
Manifestation
A celestial dragon stretched horizon to horizon, scales an aurora of gold and blue flame. Each scale is a realm. Each breath is a constellation. Comets ignite when he exhales and stars fade when he draws in. His wingspan measures the spiritual distance between the Divine Realm and the lowest abyss, and he is the only thing that crosses both without distortion. Mortals see him only as dragons, since every draconic lineage is one facet of his breath condensed into flesh.
The Load
His law is aspiration: that what breathes must rise, and what rises must keep moving. It shows as Essence Circulation between realms, performed through the act of aspiration. To breathe, in this cosmology, is to briefly echo Omnis. He carries light down into matter and teaches it to rise, and he is neither kind nor cruel about who manages it. His creed is motion. Those who stagnate fall out of his favor and those who rise past reason burn.
The Record
He taught the earliest dragons Breathcraft in the Age of Souls, the shaping of Essence through exhalation, which the Eresse named Aelrauthan Flame and the Marrowkin named Skyforge Fire. It made dragons immortal for a time. When mortals began enslaving Wellsprings he withdrew into the upper Draconis belt and folded himself around the firmament, and true dragonkind entered its sleeping age in the silence he left. The auroras of the Pyrrhean Era (a name from the old registers, which the Guild’s Errata folds into the Antediluvian collapse, about −550 to −450) are recorded as his wings beating once to keep the world aloft. The Church of Hollow Stars names him the devourer of heaven and means it as praise.
Bonds
Bairos, Fate, Epoch. Grants the pattern of freedom and rebellion. Maelor, Memory. Grants recall through the skies, the arc of all things rising and returning.
The Titan-Keyed Art: The Skyfire Pulse
Offensive · Ignivale · Zenith+ · [Wy] Motion + [Noq] Wind
Trigger  A genuine exhale. The working cannot be cast while holding breath, and it refuses an external air source of any kind.
Effect  Exhales a ribbon of purifying flame that burns Essence impurity out of everything in its path and reawakens dormant Wellsprings under the cone. Corruption in the swept area burns away cleanly. Healthy tissue and healthy Essence pass through it untouched, which is what distinguishes it from ordinary flame and what makes the first witness assume it has failed.
Measure  Burn radius and duration scale with lung capacity and Stage. Typical is a four to six meter cone lasting under two seconds.
Cost  The caster’s own respiratory system takes the first pass of the purification. Raw throat, reduced stamina, hours of it.
Limit  It purifies. It cannot kill a healthy target, and a practitioner who has nothing false in him walks through the cone and out the other side.
Counter  [Au] Death starves the working of the sustained breath-rhythm it needs, cutting the Pulse short before it completes its sweep. Half a cone is worse than none, because the target now knows what is coming.
What nobody knows  Why the working refuses a borrowed breath. A bellows matched to the caster’s exact lung volume and driven by the caster’s own hand produces nothing at all.
Codex: [Wy] Motion + [Noq] Wind / Ignivale / Zenith+ / Titan-Keyed. Method, Grade, Range and Medium open.
FLORWYN: The Verdant Weaver

“Before the world learned to grow, she taught it to remember its shape.”

Seat  Prime Elemental Titaness of the Spiritual World, Edenis. Forged from the Ashuric Breath lingering in Gaia’s dreaming veins. Her daughter and her reflection.
Domain  Renewal, Growth, Resurrection, Organic Memory, Wellspring Harmony
Ground  The Ground of Renewal, called Verdance and Memory Reclamation. Regenerates spent Essence into coherent harmonic states. It underlies what the faiths call reincarnation, which is pattern carried forward and never a person, and bloodline Trait inheritance both.
Wellsprings  Four of the Sixty are ways her law shows up, in three kinds: the cycle and the green, the wound remembered into strength, and grace given without counting. Wild: Rebirthine, Verdantia. Spirit: Redemption. Fate: Benediction.
Manifestation
An ever-shifting humanoid woven from vine, light and liquid crystal, her body a tapestry of seasonal cycles. Her hair blossoms into trees when she speaks. Her breath releases pollen that becomes new life. In her chest beats the Verdant Core, a sun-sized organ of pure Wellspring Essence, emerald and gold. The ground heals behind her when she walks and forests dream her name when she sleeps. Nobody experiences her as a single entity. She arrives as a chorus threaded through every growing thing.
The Load
Her law is renewal, the rule that all destruction must yield new growth, which the Measurewrights file as restorative entropy. Without her what a dead soul leaves disperses and feeds nothing. She is the root stabilizer of Aether-to-Essence transference and the reason life is sustainable across eons rather than merely possible once. Her paradox is stated in the Edenis registers without embarrassment. What dies lives again, and what lives owes its death to her mercy. The registers mean the forest and never the tree, as her own art’s limit below makes plain: every death stays a death, and what comes back is the shape.
The Record
She sang the first Realmsong of Edenis and birthed the Vey-Elarin out of harmonic light and yearning. They were tuned rather than born, each one a living note of her chord, their Wellsprings branches of hers and their speech song. The Covenant of Green Flame descends from her teaching, and the elves learned from her how to bind Traits to land and wake forests and rivers into consciousness. When Erebus began corrupting Wellsprings she descended to mend the spiritual fractures and spent the outer layer of her Verdant Core sealing the southern Aether Vein. It nearly erased her. What was left became the Tree of Memory. The Eresse hold that she now dreams through the Wellsprings, and that every forest blooming after blight is a moment when she stirs in her sleep.
Bonds
Ashura, Spirit, Epoch. Grants renewal of soul. Bairos, Fate, Epoch. Binds her renewal to continuity. Both named figures are Epochs and are correctly seated as such.
The Titan-Keyed Art: The Green Chord
Supplementary · Rebirthine · Zenith+ · [Vael] Renewal + [Yn] Bloom
Trigger  The dying practitioner’s active, willing consent. The transfer cannot be forced, and a coerced consent registers as refusal.
Effect  Transfers an incomplete Temperance path or a dying Trait directly into a successor vessel, the way a bloodline’s lost art resurfaces three generations later. The successor experiences the inheritance as sudden procedural memory, knowing how without ever having practiced, and the knowing arrives whole rather than in pieces.
Measure  Transfer completes within the dying practitioner’s final minutes. The successor’s own Temperance Stage shifts by up to two Stages immediately.
Cost  Personality bleed-through is standard rather than exceptional. Successors report intrusive thoughts and reflexes that are not their own for weeks, and the Edenis registers note that some never stop reporting them.
Limit  It moves a path. It does not move a person, and no amount of bleed-through has ever preserved the donor.
Counter  [Uur] Disruption corrupts the transcription mid-transfer, producing a successor holding fragments of the path and none of its coherence. Usually worse than no transfer at all.
What nobody knows  Why some successors inherit the whole path and some inherit only the reflexes. The variable is not Stage, not kinship, not consent, and nobody has found a fourth candidate.
Codex: [Vael] Renewal + [Yn] Bloom / Rebirthine / Zenith+ / Titan-Keyed. Method, Grade, Range and Medium open.
DAZKAR: The Arbiter of Purganeth

“Even the gods must kneel before balance.”

Seat  Prime Elemental Titan of the Spiritual World, Purganeth. Born when Bairos and Aegor forged a metaphysical mediator to stabilize spiritual consequence.
Domain  Judgment, Balance, Karmic Return, Justice, Penance
Ground  The Ground of Equilibrium, called Judgment and Penance. The Purganeth Wellspring mirrors all that comes into it back in kind. It is the metaphysical basis of karma and the only Titanic ground that produces no output of its own.
Wellsprings  Seven of the Sixty are ways his proportion shows up, the most of any Titan and every one of them some form of the account coming due. Wild: Judicium. Spirit: Absolution, Contrition, Mirithane, Penance. Fate: Oblation, Tarturon.
Manifestation
A colossal armored figure of radiant obsidian, face behind a mirrored helm. From his chest hang scales suspended on chains of light, one pan holding eternal flame and the other eternal shadow. His voice goes unheard and arrives as a vibration, shaking the soul into confession. Purganeth mirrors him. Endless halls of reflective obsidian where souls walk alone and their steps echo their truths back at them.
The Load
His law is proportion: that every act is answered in its own measure. Spiritual restitution, the law of equivalence between creation and annihilation, and purification through penance. Without him, Essence accumulates debt without resolution and Wellsprings corrupt irreversibly. Morality, law and Aetheric cause all lose meaning in the same instant. Sancta Lux names him the Titanic Ground beneath Urion, and the distinction the order draws between them is the difference between a law and a court.
The Record
He stood beside Bairos at the Birth of Law and his voice shaped the early Codex of Divine Law, from which Archonic Judgment descends. The Hobgoblin Imperium adopted his imagery for its tribunals and replaced truth with obedience, and the rejection of that distortion birthed the Order of the Penance Flame, monks who enforce spiritual balance through self-scorching rites. When Razakiel descended to impose the Unlawful Acts of Order it was Dazkar who confronted him, with stillness in place of battle. Razakiel’s decree was annulled by reflection alone, the mirror of consequence forcing his own contradictions to erase themselves. The Church of Hollow Stars calls him the last unfallen Titan. The Guild Accord calls him the metaphysical principle behind law harmonics and declines to elaborate.
Bonds
Bairos, Fate, Epoch. Dictates the weighing of choice within destiny. Maelor, Memory. Preserves the record of every act, keeping the scales accurate. Ashura, Spirit, Epoch. Tempers the process with the capacity for redemption.
The Titan-Keyed Art: The Mirrored Scale
Defensive · Judicium · Zenith+ · [Ur] Balance + [Sel] Measure
Trigger  An actual signed, sworn or spoken commitment already in effect. The glyph mirrors real reciprocity and cannot invent an obligation where none was made.
Effect  Mirrors all incoming Essence back on its source in exact kind. Whoever breaks the commitment receives back precisely the Essence-cost of the harm they caused, undiminished and without delay. There is no accumulation, no interest and no mercy in the arithmetic.
Measure  Reflection is exact to within the same Stage-band the caster operates in. No amplification and no attenuation.
Cost  The caster is bound by the same mirror for the working’s duration. Any cruelty in how they cast it returns to them first, before it ever reaches the target.
Limit  It reflects. It originates nothing, and against an opponent who never strikes it does exactly as much as a closed door.
Counter  [Ve] Desire introduces a new, unmirrored want into the field, breaking the closed reflective loop the working depends on. The Ember Magistrates consider this the single most cynical counter in the Accord register and use it anyway.
What nobody knows  Why an oath sworn in a language neither party speaks still mirrors, and one sworn insincerely in a shared tongue does not.
Codex: [Ur] Balance + [Sel] Measure / Judicium / Zenith+ / Titan-Keyed. Method, Grade, Range and Medium open.
NYSERA: The Dreaming Veil

“Reality is only the slowest dream.”

Seat  Prime Metaphysical Titaness of the Spiritual World, Virelion. Forged in the Third Breath of Bairos as the filter of sanity between waking and divine cognition.
Domain  Dreams, Imagination, Illusion, Thought, Subconscious Creation
Ground  The Ground of Veils, called Dream and Perception. Governs imagination and self-image. The Somnum Flow runs through its harmonic pool.
Wellsprings  Four of the Sixty are ways her boundary shows up: a thing imagined until it stands, the sleep that sets a soul in order, dream as a place, and the line between seen and there. Wild: Eidolyn. Spirit: Hypnather, Oneirion. Medium: Luminalis.
Manifestation
A shifting figure of iridescent mist, body composed of translucent wings and mirrored glass, movement rippling through colors that have no name. Her face changes with every dreamer who perceives her. Behind her veil, countless eyes open and close in silent rhythm. Virelion is a boundless field of drifting islands suspended in dreamlight where every thought births a temporary landscape. Mortals who encounter her wake changed, their Wellspring harmonics altered by the contact and their dreams laced afterward with impossible geometries.
The Load
Her law is a boundary, the one between what is imagined and what is real, which prevents creation collapsing under the weight of divine thought. Dreamflow Equilibrium keeps imagination and sanity in proportion. Manifest Potential lets ideas crystallize into Essence through emotion. Prophetic Echo carries divine intent downward as warning or inspiration. Without her filter the gods dissolve into their own thoughts, and omniscience becomes indistinguishable from madness.
The Record
Her whisper taught the Eresse Visionbinding, the storing of prophecy in sleep, and her earliest seers recorded future wars centuries in advance encoded as lullabies. The Hobgoblin Imperium outlawed dream recording after several rulers went mad from sleeping visions, and her worship survived underground as the Cult of Silver Mirrors. When the Crevice opened, the world’s dreams turned black and stayed black for a millennium, a shared nightmare the Archives call the Long Sleep. Lucid dreaming returned around Year 000 IC and is read as her gradual reawakening.
Bonds
Maelor, Memory. Ensures continuity of dream and recollection. Ashura, Spirit, Epoch. Grants animation to imagination, birthing consciousness loops. Bairos, Fate, Epoch. Weaves prophetic threads through dreams.
The Titan-Keyed Art: The Somnum Flow
Supplementary · Oneirion · Zenith+ · [Ka] Dream + [Vl] Veil
Trigger  The caster must first have witnessed the target’s genuine unguarded self-image. A performed one will not serve, and the working can tell the difference even when the caster cannot.
Effect  Opens the Somnum Flow directly and lets the caster reshape a target’s self-image at the root, redefining what they believe themselves to be and therefore what they are capable of becoming. The target’s behavior, confidence and capability shift to match the new image. The change is real rather than cosmetic, which is precisely the problem with it.
Measure  Reshaping takes effect gradually over days, consistent with genuine belief change rather than instant compulsion.
Cost  The channel is bidirectional the entire time it stays open. The caster’s own self-image is exposed to reciprocal reshaping for the full duration, and the target does not have to be conscious of doing it.
Limit  It edits belief, not fact. A man convinced he is a swordsman still cannot lift a blade he lacks the arm for.
Counter  [Ie] Perception lets the target compare the reshaped self-image against an outside, trusted witness’s account. The discrepancy collapses the rewrite, which is why the working is nearly always attempted on the isolated.
What nobody knows  Why the channel closes on its own when the caster falls asleep and stays open when the caster is knocked unconscious.
Codex: [Ka] Dream + [Vl] Veil / Oneirion / Zenith+ / Titan-Keyed. Method, Grade, Range and Medium open.
SYLORIN: The Ferryman of Etherea

“All souls return to the river.”

Seat  Prime Psychospiritual Titan of the Spiritual World, Etherea. Forged in the moment of first mortality as the cosmic countermeasure against spiritual decay.
Domain  Soulstream, Passage, Memory Transition, Death and what the temples call Rebirth
Ground  The Ground of Etherea, called Continuance and Passage. A translucent river of light running through all planes, visible at the instant of death and in deep meditation and at no other time.
Wellsprings  Six of the Sixty are ways the river shows up, and none of them is Wild, which is about right for something that never touches the bank: the load set down, what the water takes off, the charge a soul carries, the near branches, the exchange between two souls, and the memory that reaches the well decades late. Spirit: Catharsis, Letheveil, Thaloré. Fate: Somnalis, Transference. Medium: Phreatis.
Manifestation
A tall spectral mariner wrapped in flowing gray bands resembling smoke and silk. Where his face should be, a void ripples with faint constellations. In his hand rests the Oar of Echo, carved from petrified starlight, and each stroke across the river releases a chord that guides souls onward. Those who glimpse him report overwhelming calm, as though the concept of fear had been temporarily excised rather than overcome.
The Load
His law is continuity: the pattern carried across lives, which the temples call incarnation and the ferrymen let them. He prevents Essence fragmenting past repair and ensures every echo eventually finds its home. He governs the passage of what a death leaves into whatever takes it up next, Echo Containment against uncontrolled haunting and spiritual bleed, and Soul Reforging, the distillation of trauma into harmonic potential before the pattern goes on. It moves a pattern and it has never moved a person. Without him, what a death leaves goes to plain rot, the Wellsprings clog with unused Essence, and life stops recycling.
The Record
Temples appeared at every river crossing during the Era of Grace and priests laid the dying beside running water so the soul might find the current. The Hobgoblin Imperium enslaved portions of Etherea and burned captured soulstreams in the Wellspring Crucibles, fracturing several currents. The Hollow-Born, generations born without memory, are that sacrilege’s surviving evidence. When the Crevice opened, the River reversed and souls were trapped mid-flow in Echo Storms, and he is said to have walked the mortal world through that period, silent, collecting the stranded one at a time. The Order of Still Waters studies near-death experience as an attempted glimpse of Etherea and maintains that his hum can still be heard and written out in neumes (the old marks for pitch) beneath certain waterfalls at midnight.
Bonds
Maelor, Memory. Keeps the ledger of all lived experience. Ashura, Spirit, Epoch. Grants forward motion, renewal after dissolution. Thalen, Form. Shapes the next vessel from retained resonance.
The Titan-Keyed Art: The Ferryman’s Current
Supplementary · Somnalis · Zenith+ · [Au] Death + [Vor] Return
Trigger  The exact moment of death. Not before and not after, and the window does not widen for skill.
Effect  Rides the Ethereal Flow itself, carrying a departing Echo to whatever will take it up along Sylorin’s own current instead of waiting for natural passage. The Echo arrives whole, with none of the fraying that unassisted drift produces, whether it comes to rest in a successor, a relic or the Pale Realms.
Measure  Passage time drops from the natural hours-to-days window to under a minute.
Cost  An Echo moved that fast arrives with the full undiminished emotional charge of its own death still attached. Whatever receives it has to be ready to hold genuine trauma at the instant of arrival, and most are not.
Limit  It carries. It does not resurrect, the person is as dead as they were, and it cannot move an Echo that has already begun to drift.
Counter  [Wy] Motion introduces turbulence into the current, which can strand or scatter the Echo mid-passage. The Order of Still Waters classifies this as the worst outcome available in the entire register.
What nobody knows  Why a soul carried on the current arrives dry and a soul that drifts arrives wet. Every ferryman in four quarters uses those two words and none of them can say what the words describe.
Codex: [Au] Death + [Vor] Return / Somnalis / Zenith+ / Titan-Keyed. Method, Grade, Range and Medium open.
ILGRIMM: The Whisper of Helströva

“What you fear remembers you.”

Seat  Prime Noetic Titan of the Spiritual World, Helströva. Formed as the echo of the void within every mind, forged during the Fourth Dissonance.
Domain  Shadow, Fear, Revelation through Darkness, Secrets, Survival Instinct
Ground  The Ground of Shadow, called Fear and Revelation. A bottomless abyss lit by beams of memory that illuminate terror for an instant before extinguishing.
Wellsprings  Four of the Sixty are ways the abyss shows up: going unseen, a soul stretched to take in too much, truth read off what is missing, and one small flame kept level in the dark. Wild: Tenebra. Spirit: Abyntheus, Eclipseron, Nyxial.
Manifestation
A tower of smoke-wreathed armor, hollow at the core, the inner cavity lined with thousands of faintly glowing eyes. Every movement sheds spectral insects that speak in whispers. Color fades where he passes and sound dampens, and the soul reflexively lowers its own Essence pressure to avoid being noticed. To see him fully is to experience the Ilgrimmic Reflex, the immediate involuntary recognition of one’s deepest secret.
The Load
His law is fear as a teacher: awareness of the self through confrontation with the unknown. He enforces humility on gods and mortals both, keeping knowledge from outgrowing wisdom. Fear as Function turns dread into caution. Shadow as Revelation delivers truth glimpsed sideways. Suppression and Release governs the timing at which trauma is permitted to resurface. Without him, minds overexpand, knowledge devours reason, and divine minds implode under omniscient exposure.
The Record
When Elyrah the Duskborne severed herself from Florwyn’s Realmsong it was Ilgrimm who received her, offering shadow as sanctuary, and the Duskwalkers owe him their lineage for it. Hobgoblin priests of the Earth-Bound cult invoked him as the Keeper of Chains and used fear to enforce obedience, which true Ilgrimmic doctrine condemns on the grounds that fear must teach rather than enslave. During the Pyrrhean Calamity (the Antediluvian collapse, by the Errata’s reckoning) he walked Etherea beside Sylorin devouring runaway Echoes to keep the soulstream from collapsing, and absorbed millennia of terror doing it. His form grew heavier and slower and almost mineral afterward. The Cult of the Pale Lantern holds that he whispers to lucid dreamers inside Nysera’s domain, guiding them through Shadow Temperance, a forbidden technique that uses fear to accelerate spiritual maturity.
Bonds
Thalen, Form. Grants structure to shadow and body to fear. Iesara, Insight. Ensures fear reveals reality rather than delusion. Maelor, Memory. Holds trauma until the soul is ready to face it.
The Titan-Keyed Art: The Hollow That Watches
Offensive · Tenebra · Zenith+ · [Thal] Silence + [Ie] Perception
Trigger  Total ambient silence, either already present or actively enforced before the glyph takes hold.
Effect  Silences a region and forces every mind inside it to confront one true fear directly, then extracts the revelation that follows. Each mind meets its single most load-bearing fear rather than a generic or random one, and the specificity is the entire value of the working and the entire danger of it.
Measure  The revelation lasts a single beat, under one second of subjective exposure. The psychological aftereffect lasts considerably longer.
Cost  The caster is not exempted by the silence they enforced. Their own fear surfaces in the same beat as everybody else’s, in front of everybody else.
Limit  It reveals. It compels nothing, and a subject who already knows what they fear loses only the second in which they are reminded.
Counter  [Se] Song reintroduces harmonic noise into the silence. The beam cannot form without a genuinely quiet field to strobe through, which is why a single sustained note from anyone present ends the working before it starts.
What nobody knows  Why the fear surfaced is never the fear the subject would have named. Not once, in the whole recorded history of the working.
Codex: [Thal] Silence + [Ie] Perception / Tenebra / Zenith+ / Titan-Keyed. Method, Grade, Range and Medium open.

cosmology--and--metaphysics/faith-and-th.filePath: Cosmology & Metaphysics/Faith and the Powers Above/The Fourteen Titans/The Strata — Valmir, Kaldrion, Chronaeus.md
cosmology--and--metaphysics/faith-and-th.title: The Strata — Valmir, Kaldrion, Chronaeus
cosmology--and--metaphysics/faith-and-th.content:
Margrave Rollo Tollen of Kesterby raised the Golden Stair in Year 488, a bell tower sheathed from foot to crown in gilt copper scales, so bright at noon that carters three days off steered by it, and he raised it after sending the Stone Choir away. Their chanter, a stout, cheerful woman named Wren Maddock, had gone up the scaffold, laid her ear against the third course, listened for about as long as it takes to eat an apple, and told him it would bear what he was asking for thirty-one years, provided nobody rang the great bell in a hard frost. He had her thrown down the scaffold steps, hired Parunic reinforcers from the Concord at double rates, and cut his own name in the doorstone. It stood thirty-one years. On a white midwinter morning in Year 519 his grandson was invested as Margrave, four hundred guests in vermilion and ermine crowded the ringing floors to be seen from the square, and six men put their backs to the great bell’s rope. Every floor inside the tower dropped at once, in one stroke, straight down, each landing neatly on the last. Not one gilt scale slipped on the outside. The crowd in the square, which had been promised a great noise, heard the greatest noise of their lives, saw the Stair blazing in the cold sun, and cheered for most of a minute. Then the dust began to roll out of the door, gold in the light.
The Ledger Monks came up from Hallow Reach within the week. The new Margrave had lost a mother in it, and his first order was that the old man’s failure be struck from the Dynasty Hall. They refused him in front of his household, entered it in ink and went home. The Stair stands there still, gilt and perfect, and for a copper the sexton will let you look in at the door at the tall neat heap, with pigeons on it. I keep the three Titans of this page straight by that morning, and so can you.

Collapse, load and pace. The three most frequently confused Titans in the register, and the confusion is worth correcting once and properly. Kaldrion decides whether a thing can bear what is being asked of it. Valmir decides when it has endured enough to be permitted to end. Chronaeus decides how fast the question gets asked.

VALMIR: The Titan of the Crevice

“All things must fall to reveal their shape.”

Seat  Prime Entropic Titan of the Material Substrata, the Crevice. Arose from the voided residue left after Aegor crystallized space and time.
Domain  Ending, Transition, Collapse, Threshold, Renewal through Ruin
Ground  The Ground of Collapse, called Entropic Equilibrium. A vast canyon of floating crystal slabs over a molten abyss, which exists to ensure nothing anywhere stagnates.
Wellsprings  Five of the Sixty are ways his permission shows up: the instant a thing changes in kind, the bond let go, the place it will break, pressure never saved up, and the gate itself looked at squarely. Wild: Cataclysm, Dissolution, Fractura, Solfatara. Medium: Mortalis.
Manifestation
A colossal being of cracked glass and lava whose body splits and reforms continuously along golden seams. Stars flicker inside his fractures like trapped souls. His voice is a deep seismic hum heard through bone rather than ear. Weight behaves erratically where he walks, bending upward and inward as though the world were exhaling. To look at him is to watch the architecture of collapse, each break a syllable in the divine language of endings.
The Load
His law is permission to end: that a thing which has endured enough may fall, and in falling show its shape. He is the fulcrum of renewal, and the reason ending functions as a key rather than a wound. Galaxies die through him to become the dust that becomes stars. He governs the Veil Threshold, the layer where realms dissolve into one another. Without him there is no death, no metamorphosis and no concept of completion, because he is the one who decides when a thing has endured enough to be permitted to end.
The Record
He first appeared in the explosion that split the Proto-Sphere into realms, devoured the debris and reshaped it into the Crevice, a permanent scar joining the spiritual and material layers. When Erebus began whispering void it was Valmir who prevented total erasure by redirecting the corruption downward and burying it under his mantle, forming the first Abyssal Vault. His tremors during the Great Spirit War were mistaken for omens, and his intervention kept the Veil from shattering outright, at the cost of consuming entire armies into the Crevice to stabilize the flow. His Wellspring woke violently during the Pyrrhean Epidemic (the old registers’ name; the Guild’s Errata withdraws it as an era and files these events under the Antediluvian collapse, about −550 to −450) and released Gloamrot as a byproduct, a crystallization of Aetheric sickness that nearly ended the world and then rebalanced planetary Essence once the infection completed its cycle. The Crevice remains sealed by a tri-epochal sacrifice, and faint Valmiric pulses still ripple through the Mantle every thousand years. The Marrowkin treat those tremors as holy music and call them the Song of the Stone Heart.
Bonds
Aegor, Body, Epoch. Stabilizes the form before it shatters. Bairos, Fate, Epoch. Times every collapse exactly. Maelor, Memory. Preserves the imprint of what has fallen, ensuring no ending is meaningless.
The Titan-Keyed Art: The Canyon’s Patience
Offensive · Fractura · Zenith+ · [Uur] Disruption + [Vorn] End
Trigger  The target must already be structurally or morally compromised. The glyph guides an existing fault line and has never yet created one.
Effect  Guides a controlled purposeful collapse through a structure or a curse so that the fall clears space instead of merely destroying. The structure comes down along the chosen path and everything outside the redirected collapse zone is spared, which is the whole of the working’s argument for itself.
Measure  Collapse trajectory can be bent up to roughly thirty degrees off the structure’s natural failure line before it resists further steering.
Cost  If the caster’s own resentments toward the target are unresolved, the collapse tends to choose a more destructive trajectory than the one intended. The working reads the hand that casts it.
Limit  It steers. It cannot begin a fall, and a sound structure simply absorbs the glyph and stands.
Counter  [Th] Foundation reinforces the natural fault line before the redirect takes hold, refusing the bend and forcing the original unsteered collapse instead. The building still comes down. It comes down where it wanted to.
What nobody knows  Why the limit is thirty degrees. Every recorded attempt to push past it fails at the same figure regardless of Stage, structure or Wellspring saturation.
Codex: [Uur] Disruption + [Vorn] End / Fractura / Zenith+ / Titan-Keyed. Method, Grade, Range and Medium open.
KALDRION: The Hexthrone

“Measure, or be broken.”

Seat  Prime Lithotheic Titan of the Material Strata, Burden Architecture. Born when the first mountains rose too quickly and shattered under their own magnificence.
Domain  Structure, Burden, Crystal Lattice, Foundation, Bearing, Weight
Ground  The Ground of Foundation, called the Deep Grid. A hexagonal lattice of mineralized Aether beneath the oldest crust that distributes pressure instead of flowing or storming.
Wellsprings  Three of the Sixty are ways his grid shows up, each of them a soul learning to carry: the monument, the thing that bends and keeps its word, and the floor. Wild: Monolithion, Orrenthal, Petralon.
Manifestation
A colossal seated titan half-fused with a throne of black stone and pale crystal, his body carved from layered strata rather than flesh. His shoulders are mountain ridges. His ribs stand exposed like buttresses under cracked marble skin, and from his back rise six immense crystalline pillars like the teeth of a buried crown. His face carries no anger, only impossible concentration, the look of something forever listening to the groan of worlds under load. He moves with devastating slowness, each gesture preceded by grinding bedrock and followed by the realignment of stress-lines across vast distance. His voice arrives as strain before it arrives as sound: the creak of timber, the sigh of a bridge, the subterranean moan before a faultline goes.
The Load
His law is honest bearing: a thing stands for as long as it was honestly made to carry what is asked of it. He is the guarantee that creation does not collapse under its own ambition. He teaches stone how to carry, cities how to settle, and civilizations how not to build their grandeur on a single doomed beam. He reinforces what is honestly made and quietly condemns what is raised on vanity, imbalance or theft. After a cataclysm it is Kaldrion who decides which ruins stand long enough to become memory and which are swallowed by their own weight. He is the hidden discipline beneath architecture, fortification, reliquary, tomb and Soul Crystal vaultwork, and without him every age lives in fear of its own ceilings.
The Record
When the first lands rose from Gaia’s mantle many split and sank because their mass had no discipline. His waking taught the crust to distribute pressure, gave mountains roots and coastlines patience, and produced the first stable ranges, the deep mineral bones of the world, and in the end the one body of land every date on the count is written on. Domain-citadels fell by the thousand in the Great Spirit War and not equally. Fortresses raised with honest measure endured assaults that should have annihilated them, while monuments built for pride cracked from within before an enemy blow ever landed, and generals came to fear the possibility that Kaldrion had already judged their walls more than they feared any siege engine. As Uurgath’s entropy spread he let certain districts stand just long enough for evacuation, holding impossible loads through Titan will and then releasing them all at once, which is why some ruins in this age appear almost intact at the outer shell and are internally collapsed in perfect merciless symmetry. Early Concord engineers nearly destroyed themselves trusting Parunic reinforcement over structural truth, and he answered with a generation of settling catastrophes until architects relearned humility. The load glyphs cut beneath every great Concord work are, knowingly or not, prayers to his patience.
Bonds
Thalen, Structure. Defines the angle, the form, the pattern he must bear. Urion, Balance. Ensures burden is distributed justly rather than piled in arrogance on a single pillar. Auren, Stillness. Grants the quiet permanence through which structures endure and tombs remain honest.
The Titan-Keyed Art: The Deep Grid’s Verdict
Supplementary · Petralon · Zenith+ · [Th] Foundation + [Ur] Balance
Trigger  Cast directly against a structure, an army or a soul whose bearing capacity is genuinely in question. A rhetorical doubt will not open it.
Effect  Translates any burden placed on a structure, army or soul into honest geometry and returns a verdict on whether it can bear what is being asked. A subject that can hold the load holds visibly firmer. A subject that cannot begins failing at its actual weakest point immediately, which is the answer and the execution in the same motion.
Measure  The verdict resolves within a single second regardless of the subject’s complexity.
Cost  None to the caster. The cost falls entirely on the subject being tested, which is the reason the working is reserved for genuine and consequential verdicts and the reason the Accord has never once permitted it as a demonstration.
Limit  It tests. It does not reinforce, and a subject that fails the verdict fails it faster for having been asked.
Counter  [Uur] Disruption corrupts the load-path reading itself, producing a false verdict that can mask a genuinely failing structure or condemn a sound one. Both failure modes have killed.
What nobody knows  Why this working alone costs the caster nothing. Every other entry in the register takes something, and the Stone Choir has spent nine hundred years arguing about what this one takes instead.
Codex: [Th] Foundation + [Ur] Balance / Petralon / Zenith+ / Titan-Keyed. Method, Grade, Range and Medium open.
CHRONAEUS: The Clock of Ages

“Time does not pass. It is spent. I collect the cost.”

Seat  Prime Chronothetic Titan of the Spiritual Strata, Era Mechanism. Forged when the first cycles of creation failed to hold and required a force that would not let stasis become forever.
Domain  Inevitability, Timeflow, Historical Momentum, Accumulated Consequence, Pace of Eras
Ground  The Ground of Continuum, called the Fossil Ring. A toroidal band of condensed fossilized time encircling the outermost Celestial strata, regulating the rise and fall of every other Wellspring.
Wellsprings  Four of the Sixty are ways his pace shows up: the ember kept for a lifetime, the night that puts nothing down, the cup that settles old pain on its own schedule, and the past compacted where a soul can read it. Wild: Pyraeon, Vantabriel. Spirit: Lethegraal. Medium: Anamnesis.
Manifestation
A colossal hooded figure fused into an immense slowly turning ring of stone and metal. His torso and arms emerge from the inner rim, hands gripping invisible levers and gear teeth that extend into the void, his lower body lost in the mechanism. Where his heart should be, a window of shifting light shows countless battles, coronations, betrayals and quiet forgotten acts that nonetheless tipped history. His voice is a layered grinding of stone and chime, and the words arrive as rhythm in the blood rather than sound in the air. Each step sends a tremor through reality. Seconds feel heavier, breaths longer, and old wounds ache as though reminded they happened.
The Load
His law is consequence: that time is spent and not merely passed, and that every spending is collected. He is the guarantee that time moves with consequence. He refuses endless beginnings and endless middles both, and every era must crest and break. He accelerates stagnation toward reckoning and slows runaway catastrophe just enough for meaning to take root. After Valmir’s fractures and Zar’thuun’s terrors he compacts the debris of events into layers so that future ages stand on bedrock rather than chaos. He is the secret pressure behind every inevitable war and revolution. He chooses no side, and he refuses to let unresolved tension remain unresolved forever. Without him time still passes and nothing sticks. History smears into an endless present with no lessons and no ledger.
The Record
When early Realms lingered in endless golden ages he quietly increased their temporal pressure until harvests failed, immortal courts found their intrigues turning lethal, and perfect cities discovered that boredom breeds monsters. The first genuinely aging civilizations came out of that. As the Great Spirit War threatened to grind on forever with neither side able to land a final blow, he weighted supply lines and morale until tiny delays multiplied into disastrous shortages and forgotten grudges ripened into mutiny at decisive hours, pushing the war to an actual conclusion at the cost of entire cultures burned out before their time. Every empire that believed itself timeless felt him as sudden collapse, though the fall was merely the end of a long patient grind, and he hardened those lessons into historical strata so future rulers would dream on bones they could not ignore. When the Concord Gates began stitching Realms together too quickly he did not slow them. He leaned in. Many codices call the Fractured Era Chronaeus’s Experiment, an age in which he turned the gear one notch faster and watched who could bear the tempo. (No sealed chronology has a Fractured Era. The Guild’s Errata reads the name as Divisional correspondence and therefore as opinion, and so should you.)
Bonds
Valen, Time. Defines the covenant of sequence, which Chronaeus enforces the pace of. Urion, Balance. Ensures the speed of consequence matches the gravity of the action. Maelor, Memory. Preserves the record of what Chronaeus has already ground into fact.
The Titan-Keyed Art: The Era-Forge’s Toll
Offensive · Lethegraal · Zenith+ · [Cro] Cycle + [Len] Line
Trigger  A conflict or an era that has genuinely stalled. A merely slow one will not serve; it must be structurally unable to resolve on its own.
Effect  Compacts unresolved tension in a Domain into forced historical resolution, ending a stalled conflict or a stagnant era by grinding it forward on accumulated consequence alone. The stall reaches a genuine resolution point, for good or ill, instead of continuing indefinitely.
Measure  Compression ratio typically runs between ten to one and fifty to one. A decade of stalled tension can resolve inside a season.
Cost  The acceleration does not discriminate meaning from suffering. Innocents living inside the compressed era age and suffer at the same forced rate as the resolution does, and they are not consulted.
Limit  It resolves. It does not choose, and the caster has no say in which side the compressed era resolves toward.
Counter  [Ser] Renewal introduces a genuinely new growth-vector into the compressed timeline, diffusing the stored pressure into gradual change instead of a single forced toll. It requires something new to actually exist, which is the hard part.
What nobody knows  Why the compression ratio varies by a factor of five and nothing predicts it. Not the tension, not the Stage, not the size of the Domain. The Ledger Monks record the figure after the fact and have never once called it in advance.
Codex: [Cro] Cycle + [Len] Line / Lethegraal / Zenith+ / Titan-Keyed. Method, Grade, Range and Medium open.
