cosmology--and--metaphysics/faith-and-th.title: The Titan Register
cosmology--and--metaphysics/faith-and-th.content:
The fourteen Titans as the Master Codex files them
One card to each Titan: epithets, domain, law, manifestation, glyphs and Wellsprings, signature working, edict, its constructive and corrupt expressions, its bonds, its history, its cults and its heralds. The long account of each is on its seat’s page under The Fourteen Titans.
















































































TitanSeatDomainAtla’zonThe Physical OrderPermanence, Law, Gravitational Strain, Time, EnduranceGaiaThe Physical OrderMatter, Form, Life, Stability, EvolutionOmnisThe Spiritual SeatSky, Flame, Motion, Dominion of Dragons, Celestial BreathFlorwynThe Spiritual SeatRenewal, Growth, Resurrection, Organic Memory, Wellspring HarmonyDazkarThe Spiritual SeatJudgment, Balance, Karmic Return, Justice, PenanceNyseraThe Spiritual SeatDreams, Imagination, Illusion, Thought, Subconscious CreationSylorinThe Spiritual SeatSoulstream, Passage, Memory Transition, Death and RebirthIlgrimmThe Spiritual SeatShadow, Fear, Revelation through Darkness, Secrets, Survival InstinctValmirThe StrataEntropy, Transition, Collapse, Threshold, Renewal through RuinPrometheusThe Abyssal DepthsFire, Destruction, Transmutation, Enlightenment through PainZar’thuunThe Abyssal DepthsVoid, Cosmic Dread, Silence, Non-Existence, Reflection through TerrorVohrinThe Abyssal DepthsOblivion, Frost, Stasis, Memory Erosion, Eternal SleepKaldrionThe StrataStructure, Burden, Crystal Lattice, Foundation, Bearing, WeightChronaeusThe StrataInevitability, Timeflow, Historical Momentum, Accumulated Consequence, Pace of Eras
Atla’zon
The World-Binder









































DomainPermanence, Law, Gravitational Strain, Time, EnduranceDesignationPrime Cosmological Titan (First of the Physical Three; sibling to Gaia and Oureia). Forged in the Aegoric Crucible under Aegor’s hand during the Formation Epoch.Lawweight and the burden of order: orientation, duration and adhesion.Celestial formAtla’zon’s visible form is incomprehensibly vast — a colossus of marble, obsidian, and voidlight, eternally kneeling at the equatorial core of creation. His spine forms the gravitational lines of all worlds. His shoulders are the balance between creation and collapse. His heart is the ticking of the cosmic Loom, heard faintly as the Pulse of Time. Every thousand years, when he exhales, new Wellsprings form — not born, but compressed into being by the force of his breath.Glyphs[Th] Foundation + [Len] LineWellspringsWellspring of Strain (Temporal Pressure) — governs gravity, linear causality, and the force that pulls Essence toward form.Signature workingThe Bent Knee’s BurdenFull accountThe Physical Order — Atla’zon and Gaia

“He bears the law of gravity and the burden of divine order.”

Constructive expression. Atla’zon is not merely a holder of worlds — he is the axis by which the Veil turns. He determines orientation: defining up, down, and gravity’s bias. He determines duration: the speed of time’s flow. He determines stability: ensuring Essence adheres to form and does not drift into chaos. Without him, the planes would unspool into their original fractal Aether. Every star, mountain, or heartbeat is bound to his posture.
Corrupt expression and cost. The caster’s own joints and breath take on Atla’zon’s characteristic strain — genuine physical burden, not metaphor, for hours after release.
Bonds and alignments. Aegor (Body, Epoch) — grants structure and purpose. Bairos (Fate, Epoch) — imbues inevitability and direction. (No Archon-tier mismatch here — both named figures are Epochs, correctly used.)
Historical influence. Age of Dominion: The Hobgoblin Imperium misinterpreted Atla’zon’s strain as divine hierarchy. Their doctrine, the Cycle of Obedience, was based on the myth that “All below must bear the one above,” echoing his kneel. Age of Nations: The dwarves of Varūn constructed the Adamant Axis, a fortress aligned directly above the Titan’s metaphysical heart. Their Axis Forges used resonant chambers to draw gravity harmonics from his breath, allowing the crafting of weapons immune to levitation or anti-gravity Aether. Voyager Era: Guild scholars note that Temporal Ruptures — anomalies where time fractures — occur along the leyline arcs that trace his vertebrae beneath the crust. When Atla’zon shifts slightly in dream, centuries pass in seconds or vice versa.
Cults and worship. Atla’zon symbolizes the paradox of servitude and supremacy: He holds everything because he bowed first. His chains, forged by Aegor and blessed by Bairos, are the Chains of Continuance — metaphysical ligatures preventing the planes from scattering into silence. The Priests of the Axis in the Senoth Kingdom teach that: “Atla’zon’s burden is proof that submission can become strength, and endurance, divinity.” He is depicted as a kneeling titan whose hands cradle a sphere of stars — his wrists bound by molten runes of law.
Gaia
The Living Mantle of Form









































DomainMatter, Form, Life, Stability, EvolutionDesignationPrime Aetheric Titan of the Material World — anchors all other realms by letting Essence crystallize into weight and decay.Lawform, and the body’s debt to the ground it was taken from: the equilibrium between the spiritual and physical strata.Celestial formWhen perceived in divine sight, Gaia appears as a colossal woman woven of mountain and river, her hair a flowing cascade of lava and bloom. Her skin is veined with silver ley-lines; her eyes are deep magma pools. Each breath she exhales births auroras across the world’s upper atmosphere. In her shadow bloom forests; from her tears, oceans find their rhythm.Glyphs[Th] Foundation + [Ma] RecallWellspringsWellspring of Form (Corpus) — a labyrinth of glowing strata beneath the crust where Essence condenses into crystalline ore, source of Soul Crystal latticework.Signature workingFlesh Remembers StoneFull accountThe Physical Order — Atla’zon and Gaia

“Every birth is a memory of the first world.”

Constructive expression. Gaia maintains structural equilibrium between the spiritual and physical strata of the cosmos. She invented mortality—not as punishment, but as a mechanism for renewal. Through her, death recycles Essence back into Wellsprings, preventing universal saturation. She also forged the Cycle of Material Harmony, ensuring that every creature’s Essence mirrors its environment. Thus, dragons breathe flame because they were born in molten currents; elves carry chlorophyll resonance because their souls remembered Verdance.
Corrupt expression and cost. Caster’s hands take the heaviest exposure; repeated use produces genuine mineral deposits under the caster’s own skin over a career.
Bonds and alignments. Thalen (Form) — foremost ally; the architect whose glyphs she embodies. Maelor (Memory) — gives matter history, making fossils, bones, and soil into vessels of remembrance. Urion (Balance) — stabilizes her evolution, ensuring growth follows pattern and not chaos.
Historical influence. First Eon: Gaia descended from the Divine Realm with Atlas to shape the first crust around the Wellspring Core. She granted Florwyn’s Realmsong weight—turning harmony into ecology. Mortals call this the First Sedimentation, when music became mountains. Great Spirit War: Gaia’s sorrow split continents. When the divine bled, she absorbed their essence to heal the world’s shell, creating the first Essence Fossils, living relics that hum with residual godlight. Age of Dominion: Hobgoblin geomancers worshiped her as Karai the Forgeblooded, mistress of tectonic harmony. Their misuse of her ley veins caused magma storms and the Year of Shattered Hammers. Pyrrhean Epidemic: As the Crevice opened, Gaia fought to hold the mantle together against Valmir’s aetheric suction. Her pulse slowed to one beat every thousand years—what the Dwarves call the Long Heart Sleep. Imperial Calendar: The Mantle stirs again. Seers report tremors aligned with Wellspring awakenings, implying Gaia is “breathing” anew. The Concord interprets this as her testing whether mortals can steward matter without divine interference.
Cults and worship. Symbols: The Spiral Shell: representing evolution through compression. The Split Seed: life and death sharing a single vessel. The Fourfold Leaf: matter’s four expressions—solid, liquid, gas, and Essence. Cults: The Verdant Core: worshipers who merge biological study and alchemy, treating dissection as devotion. The Terral Mothers: silent order of geomancers who walk barefoot across continents, claiming each step “reminds the world it is alive.”
Omnis
The Skyfather of Draconis









































DomainSky, Flame, Motion, Dominion of Dragons, Celestial BreathDesignationPrime Elemental Titan of the Spiritual World (Draconis) — forged during the Second Breath of Aegor.Lawaspiration: that what breathes must rise, and what rises must keep moving.Celestial formOmnis manifests as a celestial dragon stretching from horizon to horizon, his scales a shifting aurora of gold and blue flame. Each scale is a realm — each breath, a constellation. When he exhales, comets ignite; when he inhales, stars fade. His wingspan measures the spiritual distance between the Divine Realm and the lowest abyss — he alone traverses both without distortion. Mortals see his presence only as dragons, for every draconic lineage is a mirrored facet of his breath condensed into flesh.Glyphs[Wy] Motion + [Noq] WindWellspringsWellspring of Breath (Motion & Ascension) — the spiritual equivalent of respiration; governs vitality, aspiration, and metaphysical ascent.Signature workingThe Skyfire PulseFull accountThe Spiritual Seat — Omnis, Florwyn, Dazkar, Nysera, Sylorin, Ilgrimm

“The first flame to rise was not of fire, but of breath.”

Constructive expression. Omnis is the conduit between divine radiance and mortal will. He carries light into matter, teaching it to rise. In metaphysical function, he ensures Essence Circulation between realms through the act of aspiration — breath as metaphysical exchange. To breathe, in the cosmology of WOTR, is to briefly echo Omnis.
Corrupt expression and cost. The caster’s own respiratory system takes the first pass of the purification, leaving a raw throat and reduced stamina for hours.
Bonds and alignments. Bairos (Fate, Epoch) — grants the pattern of freedom and rebellion. Maelor (Memory) — grants recall through the skies, the arc of all things rising and returning.
Historical influence. Age of Souls (First Eon): Omnis taught the earliest dragons Breathcraft — the shaping of Essence through exhalation. The elves called it Aelrauthan Flame, the dwarves called it Skyforge Fire. It was through this art that dragons became immortal for a time. Age of Dominion: When mortals began to enslave Wellsprings, Omnis withdrew into the upper Draconis belt, folding himself around the firmament. His silence caused the decline of true dragonkind — their “sleeping age.” Pyrrhean Era: It is said that Omnis’ sigh weakened the Crevice’s growth. The auroras seen during that age were his wings beating once to keep the world aloft.
Cults and worship. Omnis represents aspiration, freedom, and the cycle of return. He is neither benevolent nor cruel — his creed is motion. Those who stagnate fall from his grace; those who rise beyond reason burn. He is depicted as: A dragon swallowing its own tail — the breath that reclaims itself. A spiral of wings circling a burning sun — symbolizing continuity. Among the Church of Hollow Stars, as the devourer of heaven.

The Verdant Weaver

“Before the world learned to grow, she taught it to remember its shape.”

Constructive expression. Florwyn governs renewal, the rule that all destruction must yield new growth (the Measurewrights’ restorative entropy). Without her, the death of a soul would result in permanent dispersal; she ensures reformation. She maintains the harmonic continuity of organic Wellsprings, ensuring the balance of birth and decay remains intact. In cosmological terms, she is the root stabilizer of Aether-to-Essence transference, making life sustainable across eons.
Corrupt expression and cost. Personality bleed-through is standard, not exceptional; successors report intrusive thoughts and reflexes not their own for weeks afterward.
Bonds and alignments. Ashura (Spirit, Epoch) — grants renewal of soul. Bairos (Fate, Epoch) — binds her renewal to continuity. (No Archon-tier mismatch here — both named figures are Epochs, correctly used.)
Historical influence. First Eon (Birth of the Elves): Florwyn sang the first Realmsong of Edenis, birthing the Vey-Elarin (the Elves) directly from harmonic light and yearning. They were not born, but tuned — each one a living note of her chord. Their Wellsprings were branches of hers; their speech was song. Era of Verdance: The Covenant of Green Flame — the Elves’ earliest communion with Wellsprings — originated from Florwyn’s own teachings. She taught them how to bind Traits to land, awakening forests and rivers as conscious entities. Great Spirit War: When Erebus’ void began corrupting Wellsprings, Florwyn descended from Edenis to mend the spiritual fractures. Her intervention was brief but pivotal — she sacrificed her Verdant Core’s outer layer to seal the rift in the southern Aether Vein. The act nearly erased her, leaving behind what would become the Tree of Memory — a fragment of her soul. Imperial Calendar (Current Age): The Elves claim she now dreams through the Wellsprings. Every act of regrowth, every spontaneous forest blooming after blight, is considered a moment when Florwyn stirs in her sleep.
Cults and worship. Florwyn symbolizes forgiveness through continuity. She does not deny decay — she redeems it. Her paradox: what dies, lives again; what lives, owes its death to her mercy. Common symbols: The Spiral Bloom: A flower curling inward then outward, denoting rebirth. The Green Flame: Sacred fire of renewal — used by druids and Verdant magi in resurrection rites. The Singing Root: A relic that hums her frequency when planted in sacred soil. Her followers whisper: “She weaves through rot, never fearing it — for she is the thread that outlasts all endings.”

DomainStructure, Burden, Crystal Lattice, Foundation, Bearing, WeightDesignationPrime Lithotheic Titan of the Material Strata (Burden Architecture) — born when the first mountains rose too quickly and shattered under their own magnificence.Lawhonest bearing: a thing stands for as long as it was honestly made to carry what is asked of it.Celestial formKaldrion appears as a colossal, seated titan half-fused with a throne of black stone and pale crystal, his body carved from layered strata rather than flesh. His shoulders are mountain ridges, his ribs exposed like buttresses beneath cracked marble skin, and from his back rise six immense crystalline pillars like the teeth of a buried crown. His face bears no anger, only impossible concentration—the look of something forever listening to the groan of worlds under load. When he moves, it is with devastating slowness, each gesture preceded by the sound of grinding bedrock and followed by the realignment of stress-lines across vast distances. His voice is heard as strain before sound: the creak of timber, the sigh of a bridge, the subterranean moan before a faultline breaks.Glyphs[Th] Foundation + [Ur] BalanceWellspringsWellspring of Foundation (The Deep Grid) — a hexagonal lattice of mineralized Aether beneath the oldest crust that distributes pressure rather than flowing or storming.Signature workingThe Deep Grid’s VerdictFull accountThe Strata — Valmir, Kaldrion, Chronaeus

“Measure, or be broken.”

Constructive expression. Kaldrion ensures that creation does not collapse beneath its own ambition. He teaches stone how to carry, cities how to settle, and civilizations how not to build their grandeur atop a single doomed beam. He reinforces what is honestly made and quietly condemns what is built on vanity, imbalance, or theft. After cataclysms, it is Kaldrion who determines which ruins remain standing long enough to become memory and which are swallowed by their own weight. He is the hidden discipline beneath architecture, fortification, reliquaries, tombs, and Soul Crystal vaultwork. Without Kaldrion, all works of permanence would become temporary, and every age would live in fear of its own ceilings.
Corrupt expression and cost. None to the caster directly — the cost falls entirely on the target being tested, which is why this working is reserved for genuine, consequential verdicts.
Bonds and alignments. Thalen (Structure) — defines the angle, the form, the pattern he must bear. Urion (Balance) — ensures burden is distributed justly, not piled in arrogance upon a single pillar. Auren (Stillness) — grants the quiet permanence through which structures endure and tombs remain honest. (Already correct as written — unchanged.)
Historical influence. First Eons: When the first continents rose from Gaia’s mantle, many split and sank because their own mass had no discipline. Kaldrion’s awakening taught the crust to distribute pressure, giving mountains roots and coastlines patience. From him came the first stable ranges and the deep mineral bones of the world. Great Spirit Wars: During the Great Spirit Wars, fortresses and Domain-citadels fell by the thousands, but not all equally. Those raised with honest measure endured assaults that should have annihilated them, while towering monuments built for pride cracked from within before enemy blows even landed. Generals came to fear not merely siege engines, but the possibility that Kaldrion had judged their walls unworthy. Withering Era: As Uurgath’s entropy spread, whole cities should have folded into rubble overnight. Kaldrion chose instead to let some districts stand just long enough for evacuation, holding impossible loads through sheer Titan will before releasing them all at once into dust. This is why certain ruins in the modern age appear almost intact at their outer shell, yet are internally collapsed in perfect, merciless symmetry. Concord Age: The early Concord engineers nearly destroyed themselves by trusting Parunic reinforcement over structural truth. Kaldrion answered with a generation of “settling catastrophes,” forcing towers, bridges, and aerial citadels to sag, crack, or implode until architects relearned humility. The modern load glyph systems used beneath Concord megastructures are all, knowingly or not, prayers to his patience.
Cults and worship. Symbols: The Six-Pillar Crown: endurance through balanced support. The Load Line: the hidden path every burden must travel. The Cracked Beam: warning against vanity in design. Cults: The Stone Choir: masons, geomancers, and architects who listen to rock harmonics before they ever cut or place stone. The Undercrypt Keepers: engineers entombed beneath ancient strongholds, tending buried buttresses and whispering equations into the earth so structures do not forget their purpose. The Burden Votaries: ascetics who wear increasing weights on their bodies through life, believing one must feel pressure to build mercy into the world.
Chronaeus
The Clock of Ages









































DomainInevitability, Timeflow, Historical Momentum, Accumulated Consequence, Pace of ErasDesignationPrime Chronothetic Titan of the Spiritual Strata (Era Mechanism) — forged when the first cycles of creation failed to hold and required a force that would not let stasis become forever.Lawconsequence: that time is spent and not merely passed, and that every spending is collected.Celestial formChronaeus appears as a colossal, hooded figure fused into an immense, slowly turning ring of stone and metal. His torso and arms emerge from the inner rim, hands gripping invisible levers and teeth of gears that extend into the void; his lower body is lost in the mechanism. Where his heart should be, a window of shifting light reveals scenes from countless battles, coronations, betrayals, and quiet, forgotten acts that nonetheless tipped history. His voice is a layered grinding of stone and chime, as if multiple bells and millstones speak at once; words arrive as rhythms in the blood more than sound in the air. Each step he takes sends a tremor through reality—seconds feel heavier, breaths longer, and old wounds ache as if reminded they happened.Glyphs[Cro] Cycle + [Len] LineWellspringsWellspring of Continuum (The Fossil Ring) — a toroidal band of condensed, fossilized time encircling the outermost Celestial strata, regulating the rise and fall of other Wellsprings.Signature workingThe Era-Forge’s TollFull accountThe Strata — Valmir, Kaldrion, Chronaeus

“Time does not pass. It is spent. I collect the cost.”

Constructive expression. Chronaeus ensures that time moves with consequence. He refuses both endless beginnings and endless middles; every era must crest and break. He accelerates stagnation toward reckoning and slows runaway catastrophe just enough for meaning to take root. After Valmir’s fractures and Zarthuun’s terrors, he compacts the debris of events into layers, so future ages stand atop bedrock rather than chaos. He is the secret pressure behind “inevitable” wars and revolutions: not in choosing sides, but in refusing to let unresolved tensions remain unresolved forever. Without Chronaeus, time would still pass—but nothing would stick. History would smear into an endless present with no lessons and no ledger.
Corrupt expression and cost. The acceleration doesn’t discriminate meaning from suffering; innocents living through the compressed era age and suffer at the same forced rate as the resolution itself.
Bonds and alignments. Valen (Time) — defines the covenant of sequence; Chronaeus enforces its pace. Urion (Balance) — ensures that the speed of consequence matches the gravity of action. Maelor (Memory) — preserves the record of what Chronaeus has already ground into fact. (Already correct as written — unchanged.)
Historical influence. First Eons: When early Realms lingered in endless golden ages, refusing to evolve, Chronaeus quietly increased their temporal pressure. Harvests began to fail, immortal courts found their intrigues turning lethal, and “perfect” cities discovered that boredom breeds monsters. From this, the first true aging civilizations emerged. Great Spirit Wars: As the Great Spirit Wars threatened to grind on forever, with neither side capable of delivering a final blow, Chronaeus weighted supply lines and morale. Tiny delays multiplied into disastrous shortages; forgotten grudges ripened into mutinies at decisive hours. His unseen hand pushed the conflict to actual conclusion instead of endless attrition, at the cost of entire cultures burned out before their time. Era of Dominion: Across the Age of Dominion, every empire that believed itself timeless felt his pressure as “sudden” collapse—though for Chronaeus, the fall was merely the end of a long, patient grind. He hardened the lessons of these collapses into historical strata—conquests written into law, uprisings carved into legend—so that future rulers dreamed on bones they could not ignore. Fractured Era Onset: When the Concord Gates began to stitch Realms together too quickly, Chronaeus did not slow them; he leaned in. Political systems strained and broke under the speed of change, forcing a new equilibrium to emerge rather than allowing ancient orders to parasitize a new age. The Fractured Era is, in many codices, called “Chronaeus’s Experiment”—an age where he turned the gear one notch faster and watched who could bear the tempo.
Cults and worship. Symbols: The Cracked Hourglass: a reminder that no measure of time is truly safe from breaking. The Fossil Spiral: history layered, not erased. The Iron Pendulum: the inexorable swing between peace and conflict. Cults: The Gearbound: ascetic historians who chain weighted pendulums to their wrists, feeling every recorded event as extra drag on their bodies. They believe that writing history should hurt. The Ledger Monks: keepers of Dynasty Halls where every rise and fall is carved line by line; they refuse to let revisionist rulers erase their predecessors’ failures. The Shardwalkers: mystics who meditate beside battlefields and ruins, listening for “echo-clicks” of unrealized futures, which they then inscribe as warnings in hidden chronicle vaults.

cosmology--and--metaphysics/from-omnara-.title: From Omnara to a Blow
cosmology--and--metaphysics/from-omnara-.content:
Account for this fist. Begin at the beginning.
The Guild of Measurewrights, second seal examination, the only question on the paper

On a hot blue Thursday in the eel season, at the crown of Ambrel Bridge, with the market in full cry and the river running gold under the arches, a toll collector named Fitch told an eel-seller named Tam Hobday that her barrow now counted as a wagon. Tam was fifty-one, wide as a door, in scarlet stockings and a leather apron, and she had been pushing that barrow over that bridge since before Fitch’s father met his mother. She set the handles down. She breathed in through her nose until the apron creaked, and an ember-orange coat came up off her shoulders, steady as a banked forge, and every eel in the barrow turned to face the other way. It ran down her right arm and stayed there. “Toll This!” said Tam Hobday, and she hit him on the point of the jaw. He left through the back wall of his painted booth with a good part of the booth, in a spray of green planks and copper pennies and three of his teeth, and he went into the river forty feet down with his hair on fire. The bridge cheered until the pigeons left.
An examiner of the Guild happened to be eating a pie at the next stall. He went back up to the hall that afternoon, wiped the board, and wrote the question at the head of this page, and it has been the whole of the second seal paper ever since. Candidates get three hours. Most of them start with the fist and work up, and they run out of time somewhere around the hips.
What follows is the model answer, with the order kept and my own remarks let in. It walks the whole chain from the first thing there was down to Fitch’s jaw, one step at a time, for anyone who has never opened these shelves. Where the world’s own word has a plainer cousin in foreign books I give both. Every step ends at the page that goes deeper, and the table at the foot has the lot on one sheet.
1. Omnara
Before anything there was everything, with no parts in it. Omnara is the old archivists’ name for that state, the Apeiron, the undivided source. It had no sequence or weight or awareness, because those are parts. Every law, every god and every soul that would ever be was in there as potential, with nothing yet to tell them apart.
For Tam: her fist has a knuckle end and a wrist end, and it happens before his jaw breaks. None of that was possible yet.
Go deeper: Omnara and the Division.
2. The Division and the three who rose
Omnara split, and no surviving record says why. Three currents came out of it, and three planes rose from the currents, and from each plane rose a being the registers call an Epoch. The nearest foreign words are primordial and god, and both undersell it.

























PlaneWhat it isWho rose from itThe Physical PlanePhysical reality under Aegor: matter, body and the world’s settled habits, every event and mountain rangeAegor, the Stone-FatherThe Soul PlaneSpiritual Reality: souls, the dead, what a thing meansAshura, the Breath Between WorldsThe Plane of FateEvery possibility, idea and concept, what has to be so before anything can happen: the law and construction of the worldBara, also written Bairos, the Weaver Eternal
The first two are the lower realities, and a person lives in both at once. Fate stands above them and is no reality at all. “Plane” is a courtesy, like calling a very old and dangerous man “sir”.
For Tam: her arm is on the Physical Plane, the woman deciding to use it is on the Soul Plane, and the fact that a blow can land at all is up above both of them.
Go deeper: The Three Epochs.
3. The Veil
Where one plane’s law meets another’s there has to be a border, and that border is the Veil. Think of a wineskin with a pleat stitched down the middle. The skin wraps both lower realities, and every realm anybody has ever named is somewhere inside it. The pleat, the inner fold, runs between Physical and Soul, thick in some places and thin in others, and it is what a crossing crosses. The skin’s outer face is where the lower realities meet Fate, so a thread pulled down from Fate comes in through there.
For Tam: the fold is close enough that one woman can be on both sides of it without noticing, which is the ordinary condition of being alive.
Go deeper: The Veil, which has the map of the realms.
4. The Works and the Archons
Inside the Plane of Fate, before there was a before, Bara wrote the seven Works: the first grammar, the bare functions by which anything ends, stands, passes, unfolds, is known, is balanced or is whole. Out of the tension among the three Epochs came the fourteen Archons, and an Archon is a Work crowned, a law with somebody on the throne. The closest foreign phrase is concept given a god: Order, Chaos, Form, Time, Memory, Death and the rest. A Hollow Throne is the same law with nobody home, and it runs on regardless.
Most if not all of the Archons are Sovereign on all three planes. Bara stands above them, so they are the most powerful things that still act up there, which is a smaller claim than the shrines make of it.
For Tam: a jaw can break because Ruin is a function, and the jaw stays broken in the right order because Time has an owner.
Go deeper: The Fourteen Archons, and Hataraki for the Works themselves.
5. The Titans
Titans descend from Archons. An Archon is a principle enthroned, and a Titan is the same principle bearing weight, come down out of the throne room and into the load, with an Epoch to forge it a back. There are fourteen. Atla’zon holds weight and the burden of order, which is which way is down, Gaia holds what things are made of, Valmir holds permission to end. Foreign books say world-bearer or primordial titan, and for once the foreign books are close.
A Titan has no Stage and no ladder and walks no Path, and it does not hear you. Its near opposite is a World Spirit, a soul whose claim on the world has grown into a place, and that started out as somebody.
All of this makes a tidy order of authority, and the Guild asks for it on the paper. Fate and the Works stand over everything. Under them run Titanic Law, Archonic Law and Wellspring Law, which are three domains of authority and not three ranks. Everything anyone has ever done with power takes its permission from one of the three, and all three rest on Fate.
For Tam: Prometheus, who holds destruction as transformation, has never heard of her, and she is about to use him.
Go deeper: The Fourteen Titans.
6. The Sixty Wellsprings
Titans are the Wellsprings themselves, and the Sixty are their manifestations: each is one way a Titan’s law shows up, small enough for a soul to live with. A burn, a lamp and a hot wind are all ways one fire shows up, and Prometheus shows up six ways on the register. Foreign books say affinity or element, and a Wellspring is bigger than either. It is a governing idea that changes how a soul uses its power, a lens laid over magic that was already potent.
Each has a kind, which names its home: Wild (thirty-three) to Aegor, Spirit (fifteen) to Ashura, Fate (six) to Bara, Medium (six) to the Veil, at home on all three. A kind is a home and never a lock. Places where one pools are Wellspring sites, or Cores in common speech, and people kill for them.
For Tam: she has lived for thirty years with Pyreveil, the Fire of Renewal, Wild, deep ember-orange. Whatever it touches it burns down so that something can stand up in its place. She came to it after the first barrow burned.
Go deeper: The Sixty Wellsprings.
7. Aether
The Division left offcuts. Aether is the world’s own substance, the part of Omnara nobody used, and every foreign book in the world calls it mana. Because it was never divided it still holds every possibility and has no nature of its own, so it will carry any idea: the same medium burns in one valley and grieves in the next. That is how a Wellspring reaches anybody.
Only a body can pull it in. The medium is endless, and any one stretch of ground’s supply is not, so where you stand matters. Fighters say fat ground and lean ground, and will walk you half a league to get onto the one they like.
For Tam: a stone bridge over a warm river at midday, with a market’s worth of lamps and frying pans on it, is decent ground for a fire-lens. She has been pulling from it for thirty years and it has never asked for a toll.
Go deeper: the end of Omnara and the Division, and Two Sets of Books.
8. The soul
All three Epochs had a hand in a soul, so it has three layers. The Soul Crystal is the soul, and the scholars mean that literally.





























LayerGiven byWhere it sitsWhat it doesAether ShellAegor’s groundThe Physical WorldKnows and works matter, force and heatEssence CoreAshura’s breathThe Soul PlaneHolds identity, memory and Traits, and authors everything the soul doesAttraction LayerBara’s threadReaching toward FateA soul’s own share of what could be
Everyone has all three, the people who never wake included, and so do beasts, though a beast’s Shell stays sealed until evolution or a Level threshold cracks it. This Core has no relation to a Core on a map, whatever they tell you in the taverns. About one person in ten wakes their Crystal, nearly always as a child, and the rest live out their lives with a little sheet and a sleeping soul.
For Tam: she woke at eleven, gutting eels, and put the knife through the bench.
Go deeper: The Three Epochs and How Magic Works.
9. Essence, and the Charge
Here the chain forks for the first time, over what a soul does with Aether once it is in. Older model answers sent everybody down one road, and the Guild now fails the candidate who does.
Pull Aether into a woken Crystal and refine it, and it takes the stamp of whoever refined it. From then on it is Essence, which foreign books call spiritual energy. It is the soul’s stamped blood, a little more of you than there was, and it is held in the Core. That is the Spirit road, and spending Essence is spending yourself: below a tenth the Core itself begins to fray, names and memory first.
Pull Aether in and leave it raw, packed in the Shell as it came, and it is the Charge. That is the Body road. The Charge has nobody’s stamp on it, so spending it is spending the world, and what the spender pays is the body’s price for handling it: heat, torn fiber, recoil. Below a tenth the Shell starts taking its Charge out of the flesh.
The third road stores nothing. A Fate worker pulls a thread down for the one working and pays from the soul’s own share, and step 13 has the bill.
Whichever fills it, the store you hold is your reserve, one figure on the card, and it is measured, spent and watched like money. A soul on two roads holds a share of each, and the two never trade back. The unwoken hold a trickle of Essence they cannot spend and no Charge at all, since the Shell is sealed. A fight Draft follows the road of whoever drinks it: Core stock arrives unstamped and the crash that follows is the stamping, and a hitter’s Salt goes down like a swallowed burn and leaves cramps and fever.
For Tam: she refines next to nothing. The coat is Ambrel Bridge’s own Aether, packed raw and burning in Pyreveil’s shape. What anyone who has stood near her in a temper would know blind is the way she wears it.
Go deeper: The Essence Ledger.
10. The climb
A soul grows by being melted down and rebuilt. That is tempering, and each rebuilding toward the next of the sixteen Stages (a cultivation realm, in foreign books) needs its Catalyst, the one deed that Stage asks, met in a crisis or a long seclusion or handed over in a bought Draft, and enough Level to hold the Stage once it opens. A lived breakthrough passes the Great Work in the soul’s own Path: it is broken down, purified, woken and fixed, the nigredo, albedo, citrinitas and rubedo of the benches, and a Body soul goes through all four in the flesh. A person tempers on a Wellspring, and that lens shapes what they spend, reaching double its effect after years of mastery at home. The lens tempered on longest sets the color of their aura. Level is separate, and moves by everything hard and real the soul has done, danger overcome above all. Along the way a soul lays down Traits, standing laws formed by what it survived.
The harmonization that ties a soul to a lens happens in three places, said once. The lock happens at the Shell, where Aether enters. The tie is held on the Layer. The lens shapes what the lead layer works: raw Aether in the Shell for a Body fighter, Essence in the Core for a Spirit fighter, the claim on the Layer for a Fate fighter.
For Tam: she is at Stage VI, Glory, reached the hard way across two floods and a fire. At Glory the soul first offers a named class, and hers offered her Barrow Queen, and she told it what it could do with that and then took it.
Go deeper: How Power Grows, The Sixteen Stages, and The Ladder and the Draft.
11. The Path
Every soul has all three layers, and a Path is the one it has learned to lean on, hardened by repetition until it stops being a choice. There are three roads, and each ends under the Epoch who gave that layer.





































PathLeans onSpendsWorks onForeign books sayFar endBodyAether ShellThe Charge: raw AetherMatter, force, heat, the blowPhysical enhancement, then matter manipulationMatlaSpiritEssence CoreEssenceSouls, the dead, what a thing meansSoul manipulation, conceptual attackNull-LightFateAttraction LayerThread, pulled and never heldOdds, prerequisites, bonds, oathsFate and probability manipulationHataraki
Fighters call the three styles Aether Manipulation, Essence Manipulation and Thread Manipulation, and for once the common names are exact. No road is the better one, and each has a clear loss against the others. Each road also has its Mastery, one rung from I to V and then Ω, read from Glory up: a card says Body IV or Spirit III, and each road’s own people keep an older word for the rung. A Mastery rung sets the yield (η), how much of each spend reaches the world, as a distillation has its yield. Stage sets how high Mastery can go and the soul’s Level places it under that ceiling. Fate climbs the same way, and stops at the second rung for anyone without a Work of their blood or a blessing to grip it, which is nearly everyone.
For Tam: Body, Mastered (her one road, walked as far as her Stage goes), because she has never in her life wanted anything to happen from a distance. Body I, Muridic as the river towns still say it, the first rung: she commands matter as an object, it takes a good deal of noise to do it, and something over a third of what she spends never reaches the fist.
Go deeper: The Three Paths and Classes and Mastery.
12. The blow
Now we can hit him. Here is that half second, in order.

She draws in. The breath is the visible charge, and anyone can read it. Aether comes up out of the bridge and the warm air into her body.
It is packed. Hers is the Body road, so nothing is refined. The Aether goes into the Shell raw, as the Charge, and Pyreveil lays its idea over it right there. Her Core decides and her Shell does the work.
It goes out through the Shell, the layer she leans on and the only door into matter anyone has, and shows as a coat of her own aura, the skin of power called reinforcement. She gathers the whole coat into her right arm, so one place goes up a step on the hidden scale the Measurewrights read stats on (the F to EX letters they give beasts and blades, and never say of a person) and all the rest of her drops to bare skin. Fitch could have killed her with a bread knife in that moment, had it occurred to him.
The call. “Toll This!” is a technique name, for her purposes, and shouting it buys a surge for the beat it takes. It is also the loudest tell in the Quarter.
The body does its work. The left heel plants on the crown of the bridge, her hips turn, the shoulder comes through last, and all that weight goes along a straight line into the point of the jaw. On the Body Path the full force bonus lands at contact, which is why she had to walk up to him.
Both things hit. The fist breaks the jawbone at the hinge, and that half is plain bone and plain leverage, the same as any drunk in any tavern. The other half is the lens. Pyreveil’s idea is the fire that burns a thing down so that something can stand up in its place, and thirty years of it have made her Shell a furnace that thinks that way. On this road the idea lives in the tissue, so the Charge goes in with the knuckles as burning, and the world gives way exactly as far as her soul has truly been changed, and not a hair further. Once the fire is in him the world’s old habits take over, because fire set in hair goes on eating hair after she has stopped thinking about it. That is why his hair was on fire, and why it was still on fire in the river for about as long as his hair lasted. A glyph, had she known one, would have set a boundary on that law and told it where to stop. She has never known one.
The furnace. The third or more that never reached the fist was the Shell burning, because the Shell is a furnace that never goes cold, and it came off her as glare and roar and heat, as a Shell’s burning always does. Every eel turned away for the same reason. A hitter burns loud and hot, and mastery burns quiet. The Measurewrights book that third as waste heat, and on their ledger it is.
The price. Some of her reserve is gone, the knuckles are split, and the breath is short. She has spent the bridge and not herself, and the bill is the body’s: a hitter who goes on like this runs red, wet and steaming long before she runs strange. Her window, which is the soul reporting its numbers to its owner and nobody else, has it all down:

[TOLL THIS: landed, jaw.]
[Reserve: 71% ▓▓▓▓▓▓▓░░░]
[Hit: right knuckles split. Vitality 97%]

That is the whole of the machinery. Every other blow in these shelves is this one with different numbers, and One Exchange, Annotated takes a real bout through it line by line.
A fighter who keeps going climbs further: a Release is a full transformation of what the lead layer does, and a Domain (a reality marble, in foreign books) is a claim made on the Attraction Layer that makes a stretch of the world run on the fighter’s terms. Tam has a Release she does not know about, and the river towns would prefer that it stayed that way.
Go deeper: Release Forms and Domains.
13. The same fist on the other two roads
The examiner gives a bonus mark for this. Everything from Omnara to step 8 is the same for all three roads, they part at step 9 over what is done with the Aether, and here is where the parting shows.

























RoadThe routeThe lost shareBodyAether drawn in, packed raw in the Shell as the Charge, shaped there by the lens, driven out through the ShellHeat, the Shell’s furnace burningSpiritAether drawn in, refined in the Crystal into Essence, stamped, spent through the CoreA hollowing in the Core, and never heatFateA thread pulled down through the Attraction Layer, paid from the soul’s own shareA knot, which the world collects later
On the Spirit Path she does not need to walk up. The working is authored in the Core and spent there, in Essence, reads Spirit Mastery, and carries the author’s say on what a thing is. A Spirit master at Stage VI standing at the far end of the bridge could write across the booth until the whole structure forgot what a toll was for, or throw the working straight at Fitch, and his jaw would be perfectly fine and he would be unable to remember why he was standing there. What that master could not do from the far end is put him through the wall. Thrown Spirit force lands on souls and marks no matter, and anyone who wants a booth moved moves it through their own Shell, at whatever their Body Mastery will bear. The room would show almost nothing, and the master would not even be warm: the lost share is paid in the Core, in a color gone flat and a word that will not come. No armor covers a soul, and a hitter who reaches that master ends the discussion.
On the Fate Path nobody hits anyone. Fitch’s stool has a worn leg, the booth has an old nail, and the wind is off the river. A true pull moves what the thing depends on, comes down through the Veil’s outer face as Thread, and reads Fate Mastery on top of everything. Low down it is one lean on the odds, which may cost half the reserve and leaves the puller bleeding from the nose across the street, and it often fails. Landed or failed it leaves a knot, and the world collects within days: the puller’s own stool, or a friend’s. It also moves only what already has a way of happening, so a well-kept booth with a sound stool stands.
Go deeper: the routes and the round of who beats whom on The Three Paths, and The Tell and the Knot for what a pull leaves behind.
14. The two books
The Guild records every working twice. The physical account says what happened to matter in the room, and a clerk with no soul to speak of can take it with a fork and a water clock. The stratal account says which Wellspring’s idea governed the soul, what the Aether was doing, and what the Crystal paid. Both have to close.
Only the Shell’s price is heat, because only the Shell is a furnace. Loss through the Core or the Layer is paid in that layer, and the blood and the shaking are the report of that payment. A nosebleed is a receipt and not a leak, and that goes on the paper too.
For Tam: Fitch, the booth, the pennies and the river are the physical book. The reserve, the lens and the thirty years are the other one. Her lost third went through the Shell, so it is in the physical book as heat, and the eels will vouch for it. They balance.
Go deeper: Two Sets of Books.
15. And back again
What three hands put together goes back three ways. When a Crystal comes apart, the Core goes to Echo, which leaves for the Soul Plane within hours. The Shell goes to residue, which takes nine days to leave through the body and repays the Wellspring. The Layer goes to Name, filed in the Archive and never released. A person’s Path sets which of the three is heaviest: Body dead leave their Charge in the residue and are what the renderers race for, Spirit dead haunt, and Fate dead leave vows still binding. The unlensed feed the ground they lie in. Pattern may come round again in a bloodline, and a person never does. Every death stays permanent.
For Tam: she died in her bed at eighty-three with her boots on, against medical advice. The family sat with her until the room changed, as every family does, then took it in shifts with two hired spears and a very large dog for the nine days, because a Body master’s corpse is worth more than the street it lies on, and she had told them to. What she owed went back to Pyreveil, which is one way Prometheus shows up, whose law came down from a throne the registers still argue over, which is a Work that Bara wrote in the plane that rose from what Omnara stopped being. Fitch’s successor charges barrows at the handcart rate. There is a small painted sign to that effect at the crown of Ambrel Bridge, in orange, and a burnt place on the coping where nobody has ever got round to replacing the stone.
Go deeper: The Crossing.
The Chain on One Sheet

cosmology--and--metaphysics/the-making-o.title: Omnara and the Division
cosmology--and--metaphysics/the-making-o.content:
“The Apeiron does not remember the Division, for it was not conscious in any way the post-Division cosmos would recognize. To remember requires sequence. Omnara contained all sequences simultaneously, and therefore remembered nothing, and therefore forgot nothing, and therefore was everything that memory and forgetting would later describe.”
Lattice of Names, Fragment Zero

On the morning of the spring equinox, three hundred singers of the Sect of the One Note climbed the green hill above Ossery in robes of cloth-of-gold, with some four thousand people behind them carrying picnics, to sing the world back to where it started. Their abbess, Iseult Lisle, had spent thirty years on the theory: a chord holding every pitch at once, in which no voice could be told from any other, would be the Apeiron itself made audible, and whoever stood inside it would know what the cosmos knew before it had parts. At sunrise she brought her hand down. Three hundred coats came up at once, ember and teal and arterial red and every other hue the sect had recruited, and as the chord closed the colors ran together up the hillside into a white that no Wellspring owns and nobody present could look at. The noise had no pitch at all. People a mile off said it was like standing inside every bell foundry in the world. Glass broke in three parishes, the cows in the low meadow dropped their calves early, the river at Ossery stood up in small square waves, and thirty-seven of the singers never heard another thing as long as they lived. It lasted until they ran out of breath, which was a little under a minute. The Guild’s observer, eating an onion on the far slope with wool in his ears, entered the event as a complete success at producing noise, and added that a totality does not contain partitions and that the abbess had used three hundred of them to build it.
They were wrong in a very grand way, and I love them for it. Every school that has ever gone looking for what came before the first thing has been wrong in some way, and here is what they were all looking for.
Omnara: The Apeiron
The Formless Totality · The Womb Before Naming
Before causality drew its first breath, before weight existed to anchor thought, before awareness discovered itself in the dark between uncounted infinities, there was Omnara.
Omnara is the name given by the earliest Parunic archivists to the state of absolute undifferentiated unity that preceded all existence. The word itself is borrowed from the Proto-Parunic root omn, meaning “completeness without boundary,” and ara, meaning “womb” or “the place from which emergence is permitted.” Together, Omnara translates roughly as The Womb of All Completion, a title the archivists used with visible reluctance, aware that naming the unnameable was itself a kind of transgression.

The archivists refuse Omnara the name of being and the name of force alike. Omnara was the condition of totality before totality required compartments.

Every law that would later govern reality, every Archon that would later embody a principle, every Wellspring that would later pool in the ground of the world and turn a Crystal to its own nature, every soul that would later struggle toward Temperance, all of it existed within Omnara as potential without partition. Fate was not yet separate from Body. Spirit had no boundary against Matter. Attraction and Obsession were the same current flowing in a direction that did not yet exist.
To call Omnara a god would be to diminish it by suggesting it had intention prior to the mechanisms of intention. To call it a place would be to impose space upon something that predated the geometry of placement. Omnara simply was, and within that was lay everything the cosmos would ever become, compressed into a singularity of undifferentiated meaning.
The Division
The Division is the cosmological event that ended the Apeiron and birthed the tripartite architecture of existence. No surviving record describes why it occurred. The oldest fragments treat it as an inevitability encoded within Omnara’s own totality, with no choice anywhere in it: a unity that contains all possibilities must eventually contain the possibility of its own separation.
The Measurewrights, who cannot leave anything alone, have an account of their own. Take a pail of very still water on a very cold night, they say, and it can sink well past freezing and stay liquid, perfectly even, with no reason in it to become one thing rather than another, until a single nudge sets the whole pail to ice along the lines the water’s own nature allows. They call this the Pail, and they say totality was the pail. The archivists answer that a pail implies a shelf and a nudge implies a neighbor. Neither side has ever given an inch, and the record says nothing either way.
From Omnara’s singularity, three primal currents unfurled, each carrying a distinct axis of what existence would require to function as a coherent system.
The Three Currents

























CurrentWhat it carriedWhat rose from itThe First CurrentThe architecture of sequence, causality, and the permission for events to unfold in ordered relation to one another. This current became Attraction Force in its rawest form: the capacity for one thing to recognize another across the void of uncreated space.The Plane of FateThe Second CurrentSubstance, mass, endurance, and the debt of physical consequence. It compacted potential into weight, turning the infinite into the finite, the imagined into the endured.The Physical PlaneThe Third CurrentAwareness, empathy, the recursive spark that allows thought to discover itself thinking. It breathed will into matter and choice into destiny.The Soul Plane
Two Realities, and What Stands Above Them
The three planes are not three of a kind, and no stair runs between them. The Physical Plane is physical reality under the epoch Aegor, who rose from its current: matter, body and the world’s settled habits, where truth becomes event, ruin and mountain range. Those habits were settled in the Physical Epochs and have never been overturned, by any working, at any Stage. The Soul Plane is Spiritual Reality, the stratum through which abstract law becomes a soul’s felt truth, and Ashura rose from its current. Those two are the lower realities, pressed so close against each other that a person lives in both at once, and neither stands over the other. The Plane of Fate, from which Bara rose, is above them, and it is no reality in any careful sense. It is everything that flows, every possibility, idea and concept, anything that can happen in the two below before it has, the lattice all of it hangs from and the law and construction of the world, and “plane” is a courtesy.

      
      
      
      
      
      through the Veil's outer facethrough the Veil's outer facethe Veil's inner foldPLANE OF FATE:above, and norealitypossibility, before it iswornthe law and constructionof the worldSOUL PLANE:Spiritual Realityfelt truthPHYSICAL PLANE:Physical Realitymatter, body, settledhabits

“Reality is the shape that possibility chooses to wear for a little while. The Plane of Fate is the wardrobe.”
Fragment of the Lattice of Names
Wherever distinct planar laws border each other, a transition zone must exist. That transition zone is the Veil, a structural necessity generated by the three-plane cosmology rather than a fourth plane in its own right. It is the skin of the lower realities: both of them lie inside it, its inner fold runs between them, and its outer face is where they meet Fate. The Veil has the whole account.

Students will meet an older picture of all this, because every field surveyor still carries it. “Depth, the nested plane model. Fate deepest, Soul between, Physical at the surface. A Well is not a hole in the ground. It is a place where the surface has thinned enough that the middle layer reaches through.” It is a good rule for the job it does. It gives the order in which a Well opens to somebody standing on one with a rope around their waist: the ground first, the soul’s country next, and last of all the thing that makes no sense down there. It says nothing about where that thing stands, and the word deepest has been misleading students for as long as there have been students. Fate is what the other two depend on. It is above them, and a surveyor who reaches it from below has only come at it from the one side a surveyor can.
Bara rose from the First Current and wrote the Works of Hataraki inside that plane before there was a before to write them in. The Fourteen Archons came out of the tension among the three who rose from these currents, and what came was those Works crowned: a law with somebody on the throne. Most if not all of them are Sovereign on all three planes, and on the Plane of Fate they are the laws as well as the powers, with Uurgath and Urion unparalleled there among the rest because what they are cannot be conceived. Bara stands above every one of them. They are the most powerful things that still act up there, which is a smaller claim than it sounds. The Titans descend from the Archons in their turn, and everything else on these shelves comes down from there.
What the Division Left Over
A cut leaves offcuts, as any dyer at Wenlock Cross will tell you, and the most useful thing in the world turns out to be the part of Omnara nobody used.
Aether (the rest of the world’s books call it mana) is the world’s own substance, what remains of Omnara undivided. The three currents carried off sequence, substance and awareness, and what they left behind still holds every possibility with no partition in it. That is why it can carry any idea. A single medium burns in one valley and grieves in the next because it has no nature of its own to get in the way, and Aegor compacted it into the first strata of matter for the same reason a mason likes clean sand.
Only a body can pull it. An Echo cannot, a thought cannot, and a soul with its body left behind in a chair goes on spending what it walked in with. The medium is endless, and any one ground’s supply is not, since a stretch of country fills at its own rate and can be drawn down faster than it fills. Fighters call the two ends fat ground and lean ground, and the Measurewrights have a table.
That ground is a sore subject. An auditor of the Guild once set the shortfall described in The Crossing, what the rendering houses take from the Wellsprings in transit, beside the seventy-year rate of the Withering, and observed that the two columns looked very much like one question. She was told that two columns that look alike are two columns. The Guild cannot prove otherwise, and I notice that it still has her figures.
The Wellsprings did not come out of Aether. They ride in it. The Sixty come from the Archons by way of the Titans: Titans are the Wellsprings themselves, and each of the Sixty is one way a Titan’s law shows up, carried by this medium that will carry anything.
The soul came last and owes all three who rose. The Three Epochs says who gave it what, and From Omnara to a Blow walks the whole road from this page down to somebody’s fist.

cosmology--and--metaphysics/the-making-o.content:
Every puppet booth at every fair in the four quarters does the Making of the World in under ten minutes, with three painted socks and a stick, and the Guild of Measurewrights, which has spent centuries on the same subject, has never drawn half the crowd.
How the world came to be: the Division, the three Epochs, the Veil around the lower realities, and the Crossing that takes a soul apart again.


Omnara and the Division
The Three Epochs
The Veil
The Crossing

cosmology--and--metaphysics/the-making-o.title: The Three Epochs
cosmology--and--metaphysics/the-making-o.content:
High on Kessel Tor there is a hollow in a basalt face, broad as a threshing floor and whorled from edge to edge, and every child in the district will tell you that it is the print of Aegor’s thumb, left where he leaned to get his breath in the days he walked in human form. The Masons of Kessel and the Quarrymen of Stane fought for fifty-two years over the right to cut it. Each midsummer they met on the slope in their colors, ochre sashes against scarlet, first with mallets and then, as the prices of a chip of the Thumb went up among relic-buyers, with hired fighters from the sects down the valley, while the villages sold them beer. It ended on the day a hired man called Wat Greathand, of a good Stage and a bigger opinion, drove his amber-coated fist into the deepest whorl to settle the argument in front of three hundred witnesses. His coat went out. The basalt came up his arm to the shoulder faster than he could shout, with no heat in it and no pain he ever complained of, and he stood there nailed to the mountain for sixteen years, fed by both guilds, cheerful to the end and very good on the subject of guild politics. He is still there, and the arm has since been joined by the rest of him, and people tie ribbons on him for luck with heavy lifting. Neither guild has touched the Thumb since. A Guild surveyor measured it, reported that the whorls match no hand or tool known to him, and declined with some force to say how old it is.
Things like that are why people get careful about the three beings on this page. In the days of the Physical Epochs, Bara, Ashura and Aegor walked in human form, and what is left of those days lies about the world as dead and dangerous battlefields, relics people kill for, and old beings who remember. What they were before they ever put on a body is the rest of this entry.

From the Division’s three currents arose three Primordial Epochs, each one a sovereign intelligence crystallized from the raw law of a single plane. The mortal word god fits them badly: they are the principles that make godhood possible, the load-bearing grammar beneath every subsequent expression of divine, mortal, and metaphysical power. The word Epoch does two jobs, and the registers use both: it names these three beings, and it names the long stretch of the world each of them shaped.


      
      
      
      
      
      THE DIVISIONBAIROS (Bara)The Weaver EternalPlane of FateAEGOR (Aegoron)The Stone-FatherPhysical PlaneASHURA (Ashuraya)The Breath Between WorldsSoul PlaneWrites meaningBuilds formRemembers whyTHE TRIUNE SYNTHESIS
I. Bairos, the Weaver Eternal





















True NameBara (in the mortal tongue)PlaneThe Plane of FateAspectCausality, Probability, Inevitability, SequenceEpoch formsThread · Line · Sequence · Knot
Bairos is the first Epoch, the consciousness that allowed the act of “before” and “after” to exist. Before Bairos, reality was simultaneity, an infinite compression of acts without order. He stretched the first thread across that chaos, creating distance between causes and effects, and thus gave birth to Time itself.
He dwells within the Loom of Stars, a construct visible only from the Astral Fold (the old books’ name for the Veil’s outer face), a lattice of golden filaments intersecting at impossible angles and connecting every living soul to the pulse of its consequence. It is what the Parun lattice looks like from above: the Archons read that lattice from their fourteen stations, every glyph is a path traced across it, and the Moto read it by sight delegated from the Loom itself. What will happen he leaves to happen. What he defines is why things can happen at all, and all choices occur within the mathematical curvature of his web.

Bairos authored the Seven Works of Hataraki within the Plane of Fate before measured time: the primal functions of Ruin, Purity, Spirit, Temporality, Knowledge, Balance, and Totality. These Works are the operative laws by which existence acts, divides, endures, unravels, and completes itself. Even time is merely one Work within the larger architecture he laid.
In every mortal tradition that names him at all he is Bara, and the oral sources use the short name where the archives use the long one.
“I am not your destiny. I am the floor it walks upon.”

The forms listed against each Epoch on this page are the old registers’ names for how that Epoch writes. None of them is a glyph. They are unattested in the Index, they are read from no Archon’s station, and nobody can cut one. Where a word turns up in the Index as well, as Knot does under Maelor and Form under Thalen, a station has read a little of the same thing from below.
A careful reader will set that line beside the rest of this shelf, which puts his plane above the other two, and ask how a thing above you can also be your floor. Law can. It sits over the judge and under the house at the same time, and the Plane of Fate is the law and construction of the world.
II. Aegor, the Stone-Father





















True NameAegoron (in the Adamant Tongue)PlaneThe Physical PlaneAspectMatter, Mass, Endurance, Structure, ConsequenceEpoch formsForm · Body · Anvil · Weight
Aegor is the hand that gives weight to thought. If Bairos wrote causality, Aegor made it heavy enough to stay. He is the body of the cosmos, the density that anchors divine law to physical reality. Where Bairos’s threads stretched infinite, Aegor struck the hammer that pinned them in place.
His domain is the Adamant Vault, an endless cavern beneath all Realms where reality’s structure hums. Every object in existence casts a metaphysical echo there: stars as mountains, thoughts as motes of dust, bodies as sculpted strata. Within it sleep the Four Pillars, titanic oxen carved from living basalt whose hooves pulse with heartbeat rhythm, upholding the cosmic crust of matter itself.
Aegor compacted Aether into the first strata of matter, and with it made the fall of a stone, the press of the deep and the weight of mortality. Those are the world’s settled habits, fixed in the Physical Epochs: matter and body behave as they do because he set them so, the Measurewrights measure them and call the measures natural philosophy, and no working since has overturned one.

The Three Laws of Aegor · the Covenant of Weight, the Anvil and the Spark, and the Pillar and the Root. Together they ensure that nothing may exist freely, that endurance validates existence, and that every form survives by its unseen foundation.
“Ideas are smoke until struck upon my anvil.”

III. Ashura, the Breath Between Worlds





















True NameAshuraya (in the Celestial Proto-Tongue)PlaneThe Soul PlaneAspectConsciousness, Emotion, Transcendence, Memory of SelfEpoch formsFlame · Spirit · Dream · Awakening
Ashura, final of the Three Epochs, is the spark that made awareness possible. Where Bairos wrote the pattern and Aegor forged its vessel, Ashura entered the clay and taught it to dream. Her essence is both warmth and motion: the unquantifiable impulse that turns observation into empathy. She is the first breath drawn by existence. Every soul, mortal, divine, or Archonic, is a micro-inhalation of her will, a reflection of the first whisper that parted silence from knowing.
Her domain, the Empyreal (the old books say Empyreal Veil, though it is a country inside the Veil like every other realm, and on the Soul Plane), lies between dream and Aether, a sea of soft-burning auroras where memory becomes visible. Within its tides drift innumerable Soul-Echoes: reflections of all who have ever lived, flickering like candlelight upon an infinite wind. When she manifests, perception folds inward; every observer sees the image most needed for peace.

“When all light dies, close your eyes: you will see me there, still burning.”

The Triune Synthesis

The Triune Synthesis binds all three Epochs into one equation of being.
Bairos writes meaning. Aegor builds form. Ashura remembers why.

The registers call the three Epochs the three Realities, and every careful Measurewright winces at that and then does it anyway. Aegor’s is Physical Reality and Ashura’s is Spiritual Reality, and these are the lower realities, where things are. What Bairos stands over is above them both and cannot honestly be called a reality at all. It is everything that flows: every possibility, every idea, every concept, anything and everything that can happen in the two below, and it is the law and construction of the world itself. That is what a soul is reaching for on each of the three Paths: the Body Path into what Aegor built, the Spirit Path into what Ashura remembers, the Fate Path up toward what Bairos stands over and wrote his Works inside. The reach upward is the hardest of the three and buys no rank over the others, as anyone who has lost a straight exchange to a Body fighter can tell you, provided they lived.
What Each of Them Gave a Soul
A soul is a thing all three had a hand in, and it has three layers because there were three hands. Every soul has all of them, the unwoken and the beasts included, though a beast’s Shell is sealed until evolution or a Level threshold cracks it.





























LayerWhoseWhere it comes fromWhat it doesAether ShellAegor’sHis ground: the same stratum Gaia keeps as Corpus, the source of Soul Crystal latticeworkSits in the Physical World. Knows and works matter, force and heatEssence CoreAshura’sHer breath: every soul is a micro-inhalation of her willSits on the Soul Plane. Holds identity, memory and Traits, and authors everything the soul doesAttraction LayerBara’sHis thread: one filament of the Loom, tying a soul to the pulse of its consequenceReaches toward Fate. A soul’s own share of what could be
A Path is the layer a soul has learned to lean on, which is why each road ends under the Epoch who gave that layer. Each Epoch’s line keeps an eye and an instrument for that far end: the Zettari have the Everlasting Eye and Matla, the Yukari have the Ketsumyōgan and Null-Light, and the Moto have the Shingan and the Works of Hataraki.
Essence (spiritual energy, if you read foreign books) is the soul’s stamped blood: Aether drawn in by the body, refined in the Crystal and stamped with identity, so that a full reserve is a good deal of you in one place. The unwoken hold a trickle of it that they cannot spend. Below a tenth of reserve the Core begins to fray, names and memory first, and that is what fighters mean by spending themselves. A fight Draft’s Essence arrives unstamped, and the crash that follows it is the stamping.
How It Comes Apart
What three hands put together goes back three ways. The Core goes to Echo, the Shell to residue through the body, and the Layer to Name. The Crossing gives the sequence and the law: the Echo leaves within hours for the Soul Plane, the residue takes nine days to diffuse through the corpse, and the Name is filed in the Archive and never released. A Crystal can be cut from the body inside those nine days, and rendering houses are built near battlefields for that reason.
The Path sets the heaviest product. A soul that leaned on one layer for a lifetime leaves most of itself in what that layer becomes.

Body dead are what the renderers race for. A Body master’s residue is the richest stock in the trade, and there is a reason the guards at his wake are armed and the family is counting days.
Spirit dead haunt. Their Echoes are heavy and clear, they do not settle quickly, and nobody buys a Spirit master’s house for a generation.
Fate dead leave vows still binding. The Name goes to the Archive and whatever was tied to it stays tied. A dead Moto swore a bridge on the Tobi would never carry a Shirogane, and the Shirogane still go round.

The residue goes to the lens the soul tempered on longest, and it pays back that Wellspring. The unlensed, which is most of the world, feed the ground they lie in, and a good graveyard grows good beans.
Rebirth moves pattern and never a person. Bloodlines repeat, Traits resurface three generations on, and an Echo set into a successor gives the successor a dead woman’s reflexes and her grief, and all of the faiths have fine words for this. The woman is still dead. Every death stays permanent, and no road on the Veil’s short roll has ever brought one home.
Where They Are Now
Nobody with a seal on their work will say. They walked in human form in the days of the Physical Epochs, and Ashura kept a house and raised children at it. A blessing is still sometimes traced to one of them, the Crevice is sealed by what the registers call a tri-epochal sacrifice, and Ashura is the Soul Plane in some sense careful people decline to define, since a seam has been forced in her and a man is holding it shut. The working answer is that they act very rarely, as the Archons do, and that it shakes the world when they do. From Omnara to a Blow shows where all of this lands.

Read next: The Fourteen Archons, for the crowned Works; Hataraki, Matla and Null-Light, for the three instruments; From Omnara to a Blow, for the whole chain.
