cosmology--and--metaphysics/the-making-o.title: The Veil
cosmology--and--metaphysics/the-making-o.content:
The Veil is a condition with no address: the state of being between planes, the moment of transition where the ordinary separation between matter, soul, and fate becomes navigable.

When the grain factor Bardolph Mowle of Salt Cross buried his wife, he hired a Veil-thread singer named Merrin Two-Bodies to fetch him her last word, and he held the wake on the green above the Salt Cross plague pits, where three thousand had gone into the lime in a single summer and the ground ran Thin (a place where the fold between the Physical and the Soul Plane wears close). He paid for a striped pavilion, forty musicians and a table of roast swans with their feathers put back on, and he invited the county, because he wanted it witnessed. Merrin sat down in a gilded chair with a cup in her hand, sang her thread until her coat ran black-violet at the edges, and crossed. Her body stayed behind in the chair, upright and smiling slightly, while the band played and the swans went round. A crossing runs under a minute at the threshold’s edge, and she was gone for four. At the fifth, Mowle’s nephew, who was young and well into the wine, took her by the shoulder and shook her to see if she was shamming.
A crossing cannot be aborted fast. She came back too hard and too shallow, and something came with her: a split in the air above the swan table, tall as a barn door, deep violet along its lips, with a color at its center on which no two witnesses have ever agreed. That was a rupture, a channel struck clean through the Veil, and it stayed struck. Out of it, down onto the good linen, condensed the unresolved content of three thousand plague dead, in the shape of Echo Beasts (what crosses a rupture and sets on this side like a precipitate), each with the character of what formed it and none of its mind, big as carts and bent double, wet in the lungs, and very frightened. The nephew died first, and a third of the band. Four Concordia practitioners rode in from the Guild hall at Ambrel through the night in their sea-blue cloaks, and they sang in relays for three days to re-insulate the channel, and two of them went home to bed for a month. Merrin lived, with more Soul Drift counted against her in one afternoon than most of her trade collect in a career. She went back in the next spring, on the advice of a school I will come to below, and Mowle never did get the word. Measurewrights have argued for sixty years over whether the shake struck the channel or the pits were going regardless, and the argument has the great merit of being unwinnable.
In the bracket towns a crossing is called stepping out, a Thick zone is a wall, and someone who has done too much of it has gone thin. A Guild roll says what follows, and every clause of it is in that afternoon.
What the Veil Is
Everyone calls it a wall, and everyone is thinking of the part they have bumped into. The Veil is the skin of the lower realities. The Physical Plane and the Soul Plane both lie inside it, and every realm anyone has ever named is a region inside it. It has no address because there is nowhere it is not: it is everywhere, and thinner in some places.
Picture a wineskin with a pleat stitched down the middle, so that one skin makes two chambers. Wine in either chamber is still inside the skin, and a person can press a finger against the pleat from one side and feel a good deal of what is on the other. That gives the two surfaces that matter.

The inner fold is the pleat, running between the Physical and the Soul Plane. It is what a crossing crosses, it is thick or thin by the place, and everything below about Thin zones, ruptures and Drift (the loosening a soul takes from each crossing) is an account of this one surface.
The outer face is the skin itself, where the lower realities meet Fate. Nothing is on the far side of it but what both sides depend on, which is why nobody has mapped it and why “beyond the Veil” means something quite different in the mouth of a thread singer and a Moto. A thread pulled down from Fate comes in through the outer face, and the old books call that surface the Astral Fold.

The Plane of Fate is therefore outside the skin, if it is anywhere, and the Measurewrights who say “perhaps” at this point have earned it. The Titans bear what is inside and carry a law out to the edge of it, and a Wellspring whose kind is Medium is one at home on the skin itself, which is why it is at home on all three.
Where the realms sit
A realm is a region inside the Veil, on one plane or across the fold. People write as though these were separate worlds because the way to them is long, and they are about as separate as the cellar and the attic.























































RegionWhere it liesWhoseThe waking world (the Grand World and its Four Quarters)PhysicalAegor’s, held up by Atla’zon and GaiaThe Adamant VaultPhysical, under all of itAegor’s ownDraconis, Edenis, Purganeth, Virelion, Etherea, HelströvaSoul Plane: the six realms of the Spiritual Seat. Etherea’s river runs on through the fold and downOne Titan eachThe EmpyrealSoul Plane, where the Soul-Echoes driftAshura’sThe Pale RealmsSoul Plane, the shallows just past the fold, where Echoes settleAuren keeps the thresholdThe CreviceAcross the inner fold, a permanent scar joining the two sidesValmirTheros, Abythron, NiflheimThe deep end of both sides, under the Crevice, felt in rock and in soul alikeThe Abyssal DepthsUtopia (Highspire, Midreach, Lowmere)Soul Plane, hard against the outer face, which is why its law reads so much like a contractThe Celestial HostThe SandsThe Zettari’s plane, which their own texts call the Sands. They place it themselves, and the Guild has no surveyThe Zettari
The Loom of Stars is on no such list, being what the whole lattice looks like from the outer face. Nor is Fate, which has no regions, and “plane” is a courtesy.
Cosmological Classification
Summary card

Effect A practitioner perceives the Physical and Soul Planes at once, crosses briefly into the threshold of the inner fold, works there at length, or at the top carries others across.
Cost Essence priced by the ground: a Baseline crossing is 2 percent of full reserve, a Thin zone half to 1 percent, a Thick zone 5 to 20 percent. Every crossing also adds Soul Drift, which never comes back.
Limit No controlled operation below Refraction. The crossing art gives no entry into the Soul Plane or Plane of Fate, only the threshold, and it leaves the body behind every time; the rare road that takes the body is at the foot of this page. Nobody seals a significant rupture alone.
Counter Thick ground or a city; Silence, wards and anti-Harmonia fields; harm to the unattended body, since a crossing cannot be aborted fast.
What nobody knows Whether the soul of a Moto who worked the deep layers still drifts between the Veil’s folds after his death, as the tradition about him claims.

Codex line

Path Spirit, with the Fate and Body gates below.
Lens Transference, the Living Exchange (primary); Anamnesis and Oneirion (secondary); Somnalis, Eidolyn, Tenebra and Mortalis for particular operations.
Form Sing, the Harmonia trade, for Bifold Perception and crossings; rupture containment is Concordia work.
Skill Thread-singing, with the chain held internally from Refraction.
Stage floor Refraction
Figure required Harmonics at the hidden scale’s A for Bifold Perception; S for crossings; SS for sustained liminal work; SSS for carrying others.
Path gate Fate Path for Projection past the hidden scale’s C and Synergy past its S; Body Path for Tempering Yield past its C.

FOW line

Governing Primary Harmonics (Synergy, Projection), with Tempering (Conversion, Tempering Yield) secondary.
Stage floor Refraction for Bifold Perception, Transcendence for short crossings, Invocation for sustained Bifold, Realization for sustained liminal work, Emanation for carrying others.
Figure required on the hidden scale, A for Bifold, S for crossings and sustained Bifold, SS for sustained liminal work, SSS for carrying.
Path gate Fate at Ascension and Glory for Projection past the scale’s C and A; Fate at Splintering for Synergy past its S; Body at Ascension for Tempering Yield past its C.
Resonant Pair None

Origin
Origin · Sylorin, the Ferryman of Etherea, governs the Ethereal Flow that runs through the Veil, and Aetherica literature names the Veil the Spiritual Stratum. The first known method of Veil-thread weaving was developed through song.
Practitioners · A Moto said to have worked the deep Veil layers to fracture spiritual continuity across battlefields; the Veil-thread singers; the Bound Watchers at the outer edge of the Astral Fold, who sit in judgment over oaths and Temperance rites; the Veil Pilgrims, who never fully returned.
The lens

The idea Correspondence: two things alike enough and near enough pass to one another, and nothing is coerced. A crossing is a soul tuned so close to the far side of the fold that for a minute it is like enough to be there. Transference lends the exchange, Anamnesis the place’s memory of itself, Oneirion the grammar of a room that is also a dream.
Thickness How much of a place refuses to be like the far side: dense matter, close-set wards, Silence, a city’s noise. A thick crossing costs what it does because the soul has to make itself like something that is not like it, and there is no moderately hard way to do that.
The price Drift is the price the idea sets. Every time a soul makes itself like the far side a little of that likeness stays and never comes back, and enough of it and the Physical Plane stops being home.
The flaw A likeness forced instead of found. A rupture is a correspondence struck by force through the fold, and a forced likeness does not close of its own accord. It is put out by taking away what feeds it, never by pushing harder, and until then the far side’s unresolved content comes through it and sets on this side as Echo Beasts.

The Measurewrights’ account
The guild’s natural philosophy of the Veil follows, as their theory. Their figures are good and the table below runs on them; they have never once said why.

Phenomenon The Veil is a condition with no address: the membrane where one plane’s law softens into another’s. Crossing its inner fold is evanescent coupling, a wave leaking through a barrier it cannot travel in and resuming on the far side if the barrier is thin enough. Where its outer face touches the Plane of Fate, which stands above both lower realities and is no reality, what lies past it is less a far side than the thing both sides depend on.
Law Transmission falls exponentially with thickness, T ≈ e^(−2κd); ruptures follow dielectric breakdown (an insulator failing into a self-sustaining channel); Drift follows per-cycle fatigue, damage summed per crossing until it reaches one.
Limit Thickness is a property of the place, not the practitioner, and cost rises by e^(2κΔd): there is no moderately hard crossing.
Terrain Thin zones gather near Wellspring sites (Cores, in common speech), worn ritual sites and mass-death sites; Thick comes from dense material, close-set wards, Silence, or a city’s noise drowning the Soul Plane’s deeper frequencies.

Rupture (a Veil rupture: a channel struck through the Veil, not a Shell Rupture or Rupture Event) · A struck channel runs at a far lower field than it took to strike and stays struck until re-insulated: it is put out by removing its current or cooling it, never by pushing harder.
Echo Beasts · Unresolved spiritual content crosses a rupture and condenses on the Physical side like a precipitate, keeping the character of what formed it and none of its mind.
Energy · Coupling moves what is already present; the practitioner pays for the match, priced by thickness. A rupture was paid for once by whatever struck it and has run free since; containment is the expense.






























QuantityWorkingResultTransmissione^(−2κd)exponential in barrier thicknessExtra thickness Δdcost × e^(2κΔd)a multiplier, not a modifierDriftΣ nᵢ/Nᵢ over crossingsthe Pilgrim arrives when the sum reaches oneRupture channelsustaining field ≪ striking fieldstays open until re-insulated
Metaphysics

Aether The Veil is the Aether stratum’s own geography. A Thin zone is Residue, carries ambient Resonance, and deafens Harmonists; ambient noise inverts saturation, so Thick zones protect mortals, while a rupture risks a Crystal Fracture Event for anyone standing in it.
Wellspring Transference, the Living Exchange, primary: two Crystals in tune and near exchange Essence along a gradient, with coupling falling off sharply with distance; it strengthens Harmonics Synergy, Projection and Tempering Conversion.
Wellspring Anamnesis, the Wellspring of Remembrance: objects store their history readably; it reads a location’s Mnemata, sharper and more erasive in Thin zones.
Wellspring Oneirion, the Wellspring of Dream: a working acts on the manifold, not the room; it is Bifold Perception’s second grammar.
Secondary Somnalis, Eidolyn, Tenebra and Mortalis attach to particular operations.
Inherited failures Transference gives toward whoever has less and never asks who is giving, so it empties the practitioner into a depleted ally and couples every stabilized spirit back to them; Anamnesis’s reading writes itself over what it came to read and erases it; Oneirion’s working, true in the space of what can be thought, lands nowhere when it comes down into a room. The Measurewrights call these reverse coupling, thermal resetting and projection error. Any of them can be induced from outside.
Theory The Residue Position: Thin zones, Mnemata, Echo Beasts and Drift are all residue. Correspondence governs lawful passage: two things alike and near enough, nothing coerced.
Essence All three layers radiate through the medium: the Shell’s Resonant Tone, the Core’s emotional frequency, the Attraction Layer’s recognition hum; the Attraction Layer is the oscillator and dissolves in transit. The Crystal looks Faceted from Splintering through Refraction, Fire from Transcendence through Realization, and Flawless at Dissonance and Emanation.
School An instrument-makers’ school reads the Veil as a stationary medium, so Drift is a displacement one can navigate back from; it maps Thin zones superbly, but its remedy, go back in, is another cycle, and it graduates Veil Pilgrims.

Mechanism

Glyph Passage (Auren) as the boundary that moves, laid under Frequency (Selhar) for the tuning the crossing needs.
Boundary Where the practitioner’s operation is resident moves, never the barrier: the body stays on the Physical Plane while awareness, Essence circulation and Crystal operation shift into the threshold.
Effect Two renderings of one room at once: surfaces and light, with frequency, emotional density, temporal depth and relational topology over them. Buildings carry their history, people their Trait haloes, ground its grief and prayer.
Gates None below Refraction but exposure: passive unease for all, involuntary sensitivity at Splintering (B). Bifold at Refraction (A), short crossings at Transcendence (S), sustained Bifold at Invocation (S), sustained liminal work at Realization (SS), carrying others at Emanation (SSS).
Containment A significant rupture cannot be sealed by one practitioner at any Stage or Temperance; it takes Concordia-level practice re-insulating the channel by sustained harmonic projection.
Drift Each crossing couples the far side back to the practitioner and loosens their anchorage by an increment that never returns; the Physical Plane grows less convincing, then stops being home.
Drift Scale Loosened (0 to 24 points), no outward sign; Thinned (25 to 49), bodily sensation dulls; Unmoored (50 to 74), the Veil feels realer than the body; Adrift (75 to 99), returns come slow and incomplete; Veil Pilgrim at 100.
Failure Field fault: a Thin zone brings contamination, memory bleed and involuntary Bifold; a Thick zone costs exponentially more and muddies readings; at a rupture the planes collide, with no interface between them.
Structural Drift is a structural fault paid in installments; the Veil Pilgrim, patient enough to guide the lost and too thin to remember wanting a body, is the fault completing.
Bleed The Shell’s furnace burns off what does not arrive, as heat and light: 30 to 40 percent at Refraction, 20 to 30 at Transcendence to Realization, 10 to 15 at Emanation, around a body that is not moving.

Essence
Practitioner · Bifold: Refraction, Expert, 51,800 to 961,000 EU, yield (η) 0.60 to 0.70. Crossings: Transcendence to Realization, Master, 9.90 × 10⁵ to 1.84 × 10⁷ EU, yield 0.70 to 0.80. Carrying: Emanation, Grandmaster, 1.89 × 10⁷ to 3.51 × 10⁸ EU, yield 0.85 to 0.90.
Paths · Projection needs Fate at Ascension to pass C (else a containment share carries no weight) and at Glory to pass A for reach; Synergy needs Fate at Splintering to pass S; Tempering Yield needs Body at Ascension to pass C, or reserve refills slowly.



































OperationThin ZoneBaselineThick ZoneShort crossing, in and back0.5 to 1% of reserve2%5 to 20%, past that unaffordableBifold held, per turn0.1%0.25%1%, readings muddyCarrying one other1 to 2%4%10 to 40%Rupture containment, per practitioner per turnnone1%none



































Drift SourceWorkingResultShort crossing, under a minutedepth: threshold edge1 pointEach further minute residentduration: ten turns+1 pointSustained liminal entry (Realization)depth: deep in the threshold3 points, then +1 a minuteCarryingcarrier and carried eachthe full amountReserve covers, Baseline crossings90% ÷ 2%45; about 4 in a Thick city
Cost · Essence priced by terrain, exponentially; and Soul Drift, a second currency no reserve pays and no yield reaches, set by depth and duration and never recovered.
Duration · A short crossing is under a minute, under ten six-second turns; Bifold and containment are held turn by turn; Drift is permanent.
Counterplay

Tell A practitioner visibly handling two perceptual grammars at once; on a crossing, an unattended body exactly where it was. Drift has no tell at any one crossing; only the count of entries reads it. A rupture’s tell is Echo Beasts.
Limits No controlled operation below Refraction; no solo rupture sealing; for the crossing art, no entry into the Soul Plane or Plane of Fate, only the threshold, and the body left behind every time; cost set by where the practitioner stands.
Fails against Thick ground or a city; Silence, wards and anti-Harmonia fields; harm to the unattended body, since a crossing cannot be aborted fast; repeated lawful reasons to cross, each one counted in Drift.
Carried Anyone ever carried through a crossing is already counting Drift, told or not; a soulguard cannot decline a soul.
Look up The Veil entry’s Access and Perception gates and Thin, Thick and Rupture structure; the Drift scale; Transference’s Failure on its own entry in the Sixty; the Silence Realm register; records of how often a practitioner has gone in.

The Bodily Road
Everything above is the crossing art, and the crossing art leaves the body in the chair. The world is wider than the art. The planes can be entered by the living, in the flesh, rarely and at a high price, and the Guild keeps a short roll of those who did it beside a much longer one of those who set out.
Ysolde Carrow is the entry every clerk knows. She was a thread singer of Realization standing with a coat of plum and silver and the highest fee in the Rose Coils, and in 668 a grain widow paid her nine hundred gold to go down to the bottom of a Whirlpool and fetch back a drowned son, in person, since a word was no use to her. Six men held the rope. It went slack in the fourth hour. Carrow walked up the stair eleven months later by the hall’s book and eighty-eight minutes later by her own count, in the same coat, holding the cut end, at ninety-one points of Drift on a scale that stops at a hundred. She has not tasted salt since, and she cannot say which hand she writes with. She gave back the nine hundred. The son is still where he was, because the dead stay dead, and no one on either roll has ever brought one home by this road.
Three roads are on the roll.

Thin ground at its worst. A mass-death site or a worn ritual ground where the wall has come so close that a whole person can be pushed through it, on a rare night, at a place nobody has learned to choose.
The bottom of a deep dungeon. The Deeps of an old dungeon thin the Veil and the Heart thins it further, so whoever has killed their way that far stands nearer another plane than any singer in a gilded chair. The Well’s law holds the door, and what guards the Heart generally stands in it.
A high-Stage art. A handful of arts, taught in no hall, carry the body where the crossing art carries only the awareness. The roll credits them to people at Emanation and above, the floor for carrying others, and it lists each one by owner and by what became of the owner.

Why it costs what it costs. It is the same likeness on a far worse account. A whole body, with all its weight and the Crystal seated in it, is a great deal more to make like the far side than an awareness and a shift of Essence, and the Measurewrights put it as transmission falling exponentially with what has to pass. Nobody has ever found this to be a harder crossing. It is a different order of expense, and no reserve makes it cheap. All three roads run through the inner fold. The outer face has a shorter heading on the roll and very few names under it, since a body past that surface has nothing to stand on.
The price.





























What it takesHow it landsReserveThe way in spends as a Thick crossing at its worst, and there is no Aether a body can pull on the far side, since the medium may be everywhere but a body draws it in through its standing in the Physical World, and there it has none. You have what you walked in withDriftA body on the far side counts as sustained liminal entry from the first step: 3 points, then 1 a minute, and it never comes back. Ninety-seven minutes makes a Veil Pilgrim, with no chair to come back toThe clockThe far side keeps its own hours. A traveler may come home to a dead spouse, a sold house and an arrears noticeThe bodyFlesh has no standing on the Soul Plane, where what a thing is counts as where it stands, or on the Plane of Fate, which stands above both realities and is not one itself, and where the odds are the ground. Something is always left there, and the window does not always say whatThe neighborsA body going through a wall strains it. A traveler can strike a rupture on the way out or on the way home, and the Echo Beasts are a bill the nearest town pays

Who holds what across the four quarters, what each wants, and where a stranger first runs into them.
A stranger who walks into a market town in any year of this age can be fined by one power, hanged by a second, hired by a third and cheered from a bridge by a fourth before the noon bell, and a fair number have been.
Most ground in the Dark Ages is ruled three times over. A crown or great house holds the land, the levy and the right to hang. A chartered company (a sworn partnership of merchants licensed by a crown, its backers holding shares in its ventures) holds the trade. The guilds hold the hunters, the makers, the dealers and the license, and most of them have signed on to the Guild Accord, a coalition of many kinds of guild across many nations, which buys its members a shared rank, contracts that bind in any court it keeps, and passage on the road. It holds no land and swears it keeps no army, and its courts are faster than anyone’s. Under and around all of it run the sects, with their colors and their brackets. Every power below wants some share of the same five things: Wells (sites where one kind of Aether pools, mostly in dungeons, and where practitioners fill fast), materials, markets, routes and the hunting trade.

Ranks

The guilds of the Accord share nine titles, the same in every hall: Initiate, Apprentice, Journeyman, Adept, Expert, Master, Grandmaster, Archmaster and Paragon. A title grades trust in a trade and is earned by commissions: a merchant may deal up to it, a craftsman make up to it, an adventurer take bounties up to the Grade it allows. They are the same nine words as the ranks of the soul’s Stages, in two worlds: fighting guilds also ask the title’s own rank in Stage, so only their titles also tell you how dangerous someone is, while a trade asks none. A Master smith may be an Apprentice by Stage, and a Grandmaster merchant may not be able to throw a punch. It travels as a silver token, and a forged token is a great crime.
Inside a company, membership runs apprentice, freeman and liveryman, with a Master, Wardens and a self-appointing Court above them. That is your standing at the company’s own table, and the token is your standing with strangers.
Crews are rated in the board’s seal colors (green, blue, gold and obsidian) and chalked on each hall’s Wall. The Accord keeps a Roll, heralds cry their own, bookies keep odds, and every realm and sect has its own list. They all disagree, and getting on one makes you a target.
Sects, schools and teaching houses (the sects, the Aetherion Academy, the lineage halls, and the Moto, Mahuo, Yukari and Zettari houses) rank by discipleship: outer disciples, inner disciples, core disciples and the elders above them. A disciple rises by ranking contests and the elders’ word. Rank opens the school’s guarded secrets and its stores, and it demands duty in return. A disciple who leaves with the school’s methods is hunted for what they know. At Aetherion the contest is open: Class X holds the top seats and Class S wants them.
Academy credentials are what a disciple carries out under the Accord’s charter: Scholar, then Licentiate (the license to practice for hire, and the one that matters), Master, Doctor and Chair.
Sancta Lux ranks by what a member may do with a reading: Attestant witnesses, Measurewright reads, Lector finds, Arbiter sentences, with fewer than thirty Archpaladins (those who sentence at the largest scale) above them.

factions,-bloodlines--and--institutions/.content:
Two systems of legitimacy occupy the same ground and neither can abolish the other. The Crown holds the land, the law, the levy, and the right to hang, legitimate by descent. The Accord holds the assay, the rank, the credit, the writ, and the arrays, legitimate by measurement.
Neither side says this out loud. Both sides have costed it.
“Balance before Dominion.” Carved into every Guild Hall gate across every realm.


In Year 706 the Reeve of Wick Cross hanged a Guild Adept in her blue-sealed sash for a killing done with a working, and the Accord sent no soldiers. Inside the month no weight in that shire could be proved, no factor would take its bills, and the Midsummer fair pitched on the far bank of the river, in a blaze of pennants plainly visible from the gibbet. The Reeve stood it until harvest. Then he cut her down with his own hands, paid a fine to the last copper in open market, kept the right to hang, and went home believing he had won, and so did they.
The Argument This Section Is About
Every institution in the four quarters is an answer to one question: on what grounds does anyone get to say what happens.
THREE GROUNDS OF AUTHORITYOn what grounds does anyone get to say what happens?BY MEASUREMENTTHE GUILD ACCORDthe coil reads a soul in undera minute, and the reading ishonest
      
      
      BY DESCENTTHE ARCHAIC BLOODLINESMoto · Zettari · Yukari,the three lines descendedfrom the Epochs themselvesBY ATTRIBUTIONTHE BENCH OFATTRIBUTIONwho did this, and by whatwarrantThe Accord does not need to depose a king. It needs only to stop taking his bills.A crown passes to a body. Rank does not.

























InstitutionIts claimIts vulnerabilityThe Guild AccordLegitimacy by measurement. It recognizes no bloodline, honors rank in every member polity, and issues the only portable legal identity most people will ever holdIt is a bureaucracy that compresses what it administers, and it has a sixth Division whose existence the public Codex does not acknowledgeThe archaic bloodlinesLegitimacy by descent, and the descent is meant literally: three of them trace to the three Epochs directlyA crown passes to a body. A kingdom whose heir assays weak has a strategic problem no amount of ancestry solvesThe third partiesSancta Lux, the Bench of Attribution, and the Zettari of the Sands each claim an authority that answers to neither crown nor coilBeing answerable to no one is only an advantage until somebody asks who audits you
The Registers





















RegisterVoiceThe Concord CodexStatutory and liturgical at once. Articles numbered, laws named, every section closing on an engraving with a date attached. It is a legal instrument that believes it is scripture, and it is not entirely wrongThe bloodline codicesInheritance documents. Written by lineages about themselves, for their own descendants, with the specific unreliability that impliesRestricted Article XIIThe Black Concord’s own record, which exists to be burned. If this record is read, you were meant to
Entries
The Guild Accord carries the structure of authority, the Commission framework, and the culture of duty, with seven pages beneath it: the Tiered Path, Merit and Severance, the Black Concord, the Gate Network, the Military Divisions, the Citadel, and the Practitioner Problem.
Sancta Lux is the order that does not worship and says so in the first line of its own catechism. The Bench of Attribution is the most consequential body in the four quarters and the only one with no seat on the Concord Council.
The Archaic Bloodlines carries the Moto, the Zettari with the Sands beneath them, the Yukari, and the Agamalu: three Epochs, three inheritances, and a fourth house that inherited the harder portion.
The Powers of the Dark Ages sets the crowns, the great houses, the orders, the guilds, the sects and the chartered companies side by side: what each wants, what it holds, how it fights, who it is set against, and where the three layers of rule meet and quarrel.
Authority by measurement, descent and attribution


The Guild Accord
The Bench of Attribution
The Archaic Bloodlines


Authority by doctrine
Two bodies claim a warrant that answers to neither crown nor coil, and they are in open doctrinal conflict with each other.
Sancta Lux is the order that does not worship and says so in the first line of its own catechism. Sōhai, the Moto True High Religion, holds that consulting one reference exclusively for four millennia is a devotion whether or not anyone kneels, and calls the Scale the largest Singling in the history of the Realms.

Read the two together or neither. The charge and the answer are both recorded on the Sōhai page, in the order’s own words, because the argument is genuine and neither side is being stupid.
No arbitration exists, and none can, because the only body with standing to arbitrate is one of the two parties.



Sancta Lux
Sōhai — The Whole Bow
The Eight Great Houses of Kushara
The Ten Great Houses of Drakyssia
The Banner Houses of Kharven
The Void Vanguard
The Articles of the Accord, and the Kinds of Polity



The law, in articles. The Articles of the Accord, and the Kinds of Polity gives the actual text: twenty-eight numbered articles across six titles, each with its register name, its plain name, and its penalty.
The Accord is a jurisdiction, not a sovereign. It holds no territory, keeps no army, and cannot hang anybody. Its sanction is exclusion, and its power is that its courts are faster and more predictable than anything else on the road. The dusty foot, a traveler’s plea heard and determined before the market closes, is the single rule that built the whole system.
Article XV is the one to know: the speaking is not licensed and the Accord has never found a way to license it, because a spoken working has no author in its own grammar. The Bench spent four hundred years trying to place a mouth at a scene and then legislated around it. Liability falls on whoever paid.
The second half sets out the seven forms of polity the Accord has to reach across, from the composite monarchy of the Concord to Marrowhold’s oligarchic republic, the Mandate’s standing decree, the Keth-Gorrum’s sealed war-moot, Iampu’s rotating crown, the Echo Elf confederation and Eresse’s calendrical principality. And Kharven, which sits outside the typology entirely and never asked the Accord for an instrument until the first circle was signed in its own lower hall.
Companion piece. The Guild Accord in the Dark Ages, under the Guild Accord page, covers the institution rather than its law: where its reach actually ends, the Divisions as rivals, the politics of the High Concordant, the company and academy structures, and the great offices. It also supersedes the old Accord register: no Lattice-stones, no sigils hung in the air, no floating numbers.

The old blood and the great houses: who holds the land, the seats and the inheritance.
At the Kessen horse fair three heralds in three sets of colors once reached the same plank bridge in the same moment, each with his house’s precedence in his mouth, and by the time the matter had been settled with staves the plank was in the river and a Yan stud-master was renting out places on the bank. Everything on this shelf is that argument at a larger size: who goes first, who says so, and who is selling seats.


The Archaic Bloodlines
The Houses of the Inner World every house of the northern shield and what belongs to it alone.
The Banner Houses of Kharven Six houses beneath the Ashen Crown, each holding territory, troops, and the conditional loyalty that is the north’s only currency.
The Southern Warlords Seven houses of the Inner World’s south, below the Moto border and beyond any crown: Yukari, Mahuo, Lambert of the Holy Sea, Yan, Ryu, Corwen and Marrick.
The Eight Great Houses of Kushara The Sovereign House and the Seven Pillars beneath the Kusharan Throne. Old World continental order.
The Ten Great Houses of Drakyssia Vaer’Kharath, “The Ten Wings Beneath the Throne.” Outer World imperial order.

factions,-bloodlines--and--institutions/.content:
Bara wrote meaning. Aegor built form. Ashura remembered why.
The Moto carry the Scribe’s mandate. The Zettari carry the Smith’s endurance. The Yukari carry the Breath’s own blood.
Thread, Weight, Breath. Purpose, Form, Meaning. Three Epochs. Three bloodlines. Three ways of holding reality together.

Tessaly Wray was a junior Measurewright, nine years out of her indentures and frightened of nobody, when she hired a wool hall at Kessen ford in the wet spring of 533, hung it with Accord blue, and announced at a silver a seat that she would put the old blood under a brass assay coil in front of witnesses and settle the matter. Six hundred people came, some of them with lunch. A Byakuya lady in near-white sat down first, and the coil gave her Stage to the rung and Level to the mark, clean as a butcher’s scale, and of the thing looking out of her eyes it gave nothing whatever. A Yukari cousin in black with silver at the cuffs sat down next, and the coil did exactly the same, and while it did he told the coil’s maker, from the chair, in a mild voice, which of its windings had been cut by a man in debt, and to whom. The hall came apart with joy. Wray’s report ran to six lines. The Accord sealed it, fined her the seat money and took her post, and she went off to keep bees and tell the story to anyone who bought her a drink, which is how I have it.
Every roll in the world is built to pretend that afternoon never happened. Here is why it did.
What a Bloodline Gives
A bloodline gives four things and never a Path. A Path is recognized off how a person has lived, and no quantity of ancestors has ever lived anything on your behalf.

























What it givesWhat that meansAn eyeA way of seeing that the blood carries and no school can teachA gripA hold on one road. An Epoch line’s grip reads the first rung of [[The Magic System/The Soul and the Climb/How Power GrowsA stat leanWhat comes easily, shown on the sheet under race and lineageLens affinitiesThe Wellsprings the blood takes to, which go easier and lock nobody out of the rest
A Path figure on a lineage page is a lean of the untrained soul, what such a child tends to do with a free afternoon. It never sets Mastered or Walked.
The Three Epoch Lines
Three of the old lines have an Epoch behind them, one to each road, and those three carry something more: an instrument, written by the Epoch and held in pieces. Each is the far end of its road, and everyone else climbs the same ladder without it.





















































The MotoThe ZettariThe YukariEpoch and roadBara, FateAegor, BodyAshura, SpiritThe eyeThe [[Factions, Bloodlines & Institutions/Houses and Bloodlines/The Archaic Bloodlines/The Moto Bloodline/The Moto BloodlineShingan]]The Everlasting Eye, up to the [[Factions, Bloodlines & Institutions/Houses and Bloodlines/The Archaic Bloodlines/The Zettari/The ZettariThe instrumentHataraki: seven Works, one truly heldMatla: nine Practices, one normalNull-Light: seven Regards, one normal, two rareIts lawFate is laborTo exist is to bearTo be known is to be heldThe gripA Work held: Fate early, its ceiling the Stage’s. The blood without a Work stops at Fate IIMatla: Body early and cleanNull-Light: Spirit early. The eye’s edits are pulls and are read on Fate, and the house keeps both roadsThe climbA lean, a lean held, a prerequisite, a fieldObject, contact, recognition, law, systemHears, is answered, reads wholly, holds, holds manyThe priceBlood, a share of an Essence reserve and a knot on every pull, and a corruption vector on every WorkLoad carried in the body, and a Failure Vector on every PracticeThe Long Look, the Threadburn in the eye, and a knot on every edit
So a Moto of Ruin may lead on the Body road, a Zettari may be a scholar and a Yukari may hit people, and each of them still has what the blood gave. A great many of them do exactly that.
The instruments by rung
Each piece of an instrument opens at a rung of Mastery on the instrument’s own road, wherever the holder leads: Hataraki reads Fate, Matla reads Body and Null-Light reads Spirit. The rung is the door and not the piece. A holder has only the pieces they have found, and reaching a rung hands them nothing they have not already closed a hand on. The Works by rung are set out on Hataraki and the Practices on Matla.
The Regards of Null-Light keep their own numerals, and under the reckoning the numerals turn out to be the rungs themselves: the first five Regards sit on Spirit I to V, the forbidden one on the Inverted mark, and the last on Ω, which is Ashura’s.

It is whole at III, where a Confessor reads a soul entireJōshi, the Fixed RegardSpirit IIAn Answerer is answered: the thing looked at gives back what it is, and the look can hold it there while the looker stays still. Only on a Spirit rung marked Inverted, from III Inverted upNull without Light, recognition taken back. Its reach is its rung’s: a soul’s name at III, a ward’s purpose at IV, a formed Domain’s law at V. The house teaches two pairs on these rungs. Mushō and Ninshiki are one act in two tenses, at I and at V, and Jōshi and Ruten are one look in two rhythms, at II and III, so a physician of the house who runs a wound forward and stops it at the hour she chooses needs Spirit III. Like the Moto and the Zettari, a Yukari holding the instrument reads Spirit I from Ascension, years before Glory, which is how a child of the house can hear the dead long before anyone else’s road is read.
The Triune Equation

      
      
      
      mortal manifestation in human formforged in the Sands from his own substanceborn to her her own children and chosen kinBARA · FIRST EPOCHauthored the Works beforechronologyAEGOR · SECOND EPOCHbuilt form, weight, thePhysical PlaneASHURA YUKARI ·THIRD EPOCHthe Breath, awareness, theSoul Plane awakenedTHE MOTOBara and MizukiTHE LOOM · administrationTHE ZETTARIAegor → Shaka-Al → theroyal lineTHE ANVIL · sovereigntyTHE YUKARIAshura → Senri → thepresent houseTHE THRESHOLD ·recognition





























LineInheritanceHow the connection was madeThe cost it carriesThe MotoThe Shingan and Hataraki. Lawful perception and lawful functionChosen. Bara selected them, marked them, and delegated authority within the same cosmic periodEvery Work carries a corruption vector, and the house’s own founder warned that nothing becomes more monstrous, more quickly, than a righteous fool with correct metaphysicsThe ZettariThe Everlasting Eyes and Physical Plane authority. The body as the first throneForged. The Epoch shaped their bodies and their mandate from his own substanceTheir bodies reach combat maturity faster than their emotional architecture. Their greatest risk is not weakness. It is becoming powerful before they become wiseThe YukariThe Ketsumyōgan, Ashura’s own sight in a mortal body, and Null-Light, her instrument. Thread-sight across all three planes, and a thing known and heldBorn. Ashura walked the waking world as Ashura Yukari, kept a house and bore children; the family is exactly as old as the Third EpochThe Threadburn, because a mortal Crystal was never built to carry an Epoch’s sight; and the Immortal Cross, a test the family keeps and no Yukari born can pass
What the Three Have in Common
None of them is a noble house. All three predate every crown currently sitting, and all three hold an inheritance that a crown cannot confer and a coil cannot fully measure. This is the specific fact that makes them politically dangerous: the Accord’s whole legitimacy rests on measurement recognizing no bloodline, and these are the bloodlines the measurement cannot fully account for.

And all three inheritances are perceptual before they are martial. The Shingan determines what layer of reality the bearer can see. The Everlasting Eyes reveal where the body, soul and Aether system can be broken. The Ketsumyōgan reads the connective tissue between planes.
Three archaic bloodlines, and each of them is an eye and an instrument. The eye tells the bearer what is there. The instrument decides what may be done about it, and an Epoch wrote it.

The Quarrel That Has Never Closed
The oldest inter-house tension in mortal history is between the Moto and the Yukari, and it is as old as Ashura’s first children.

The Moto see the threads as property. The Loom is theirs. Bara delegated it. Their administrative mandate gives them jurisdiction over the Plane of Fate’s architecture, and that jurisdiction extends to the perception of it.
No one should see the threads except those authorized to see them, and authorization flows from Bara through the Moto and nowhere else.
The Yukari see the threads as reality. The connective tissue of everything that exists, which their mother came into the world to set moving.
To claim ownership of the threads is, in the Yukari tradition, like claiming ownership of gravity: a statement that reveals more about the claimant’s need for control than about the nature of the thing being claimed.
The Moto fear the Yukari the way a chancery fears a witness it cannot swear in: such a witness could never overthrow the chancery and has no wish to, and she can see what the chancery is doing, and the seeing itself is an uncontrollable form of power. That the witness is an Epoch’s own family makes it worse.

The Zettari sit outside that quarrel entirely. Their response to the Yukari has been consistent across every era: not friendship, not alliance: respect, in the Zettari sense. The acknowledgment that another being’s function is lawful, useful, and complementary to one’s own, and that the being who performs it deserves to be left alone to perform it.

When a Zettari meets a Yukari, the response is typically a nod. Not a bow. Not a salute. A nod.

The Lines With No Epoch Behind Them
The other old houses have the same four slots and no instrument. Whatever they have done with their blood, they did themselves, and they will tell you so. The Yuno have the keeper’s eye for an interval, and hold the sacred and the speaking in one line. The Valorin have no Crystal at all to speak of, a soul that grew as written pathways, which reads on the Paths and on Mastery the same way. The Mahuo are written two ways and known to this office chiefly by what they have signed.

factions,-bloodlines--and--institutions/.content:
Two notaries of Haeseong once went to law over this spelling and kept it up for a whole winter, at a copper a day in fees, and when the bench ruled for both of them they split the costs and a very bad supper.
The line is written two ways, and both are correct. Mahou is the line as an institution, the lineage the Zettari–Mahou Accord recognizes and binds; Mahuo is the surname a person of that line bears, which is why the Accord can name Ara Min Mahuo, of the Mahou line, in a single breath.
Overview





































TypeArchaic summoning bloodline · fallen imperial house of the South · the Keepers of Death, by their own claimOriginBreath Hollow, the rice valley above Sum-gol, older than the Moto crownFounderWonsum Mahuo, a village breath-counter, by the house’s account; Daeju Mahuo for the empireSeatSum-gol, the throne vacant; the Post-House in the old imperial mewsAnchorsThe Breath · the Roll · the Sum-gol PostSignatureThe Answering (응답 · Eungdap): what has answered a Mahuo once answers the blood more cheaply ever after, and the debt goes down the blood with itMaximCall, and It Answers
Up in Breath Hollow, in the dry summer of 688, a woman named Yeon-ju Mahuo was still drying her radishes the way her mother had. She was eighty-one and owned one good cooking pot. Every morning for seventy years she had stood on her step, breathed out, and called a storm, a bound weather-spirit of the middle tiers called Danbi (단비), the word for rain that comes exactly when wanted. It came down the valley about the size of a barn, shook a cupful over the kale, took the bowl of rice she left on the step, and went home. In her girlhood the calling had put her to bed for a day. By then it cost her about what a sneeze costs. That summer a Moto column came up the terrace road under a vermilion banner, four hundred men protecting the Mahuo from somebody, and its quartermaster explained that he would be requisitioning the rice. She said he would have to speak to the weather. Then she breathed out on her step, as she did every morning, and Danbi arrived with seventy years of breakfasts behind it and an old friend’s opinion of the man. Nobody in the valley got wet. The quartermaster was found in the next province, and the banner was returned to Sum-gol by a heron-fisher, who asked for a fee.
She died two winters later. Danbi came to the funeral and sat over the hollow for nine days without raining, which frightened people badly, until her granddaughter, seven years old, went out on the step with a bowl and breathed out the way she had seen it done. It came as if it had never been away. The child did not know that she had inherited a grandmother’s good standing with a storm, and with it a grandmother’s bowl of rice, every morning, for life, and that if she ever missed one she would be answering for seventy years of them. They still leave a bowl on every step in Breath Hollow, sixty roofs now, and if you ask why, they tell you it is manners.
That is the whole house in one old woman, and the empire was only ever the large form of what Yeon-ju did with her radishes. They call things from across the Veil, the skin between the lower realities, and the things come, and it gets easier every time. What they hold that everyone needs was once a throne and is now a road: every letter between the north and the Yukari valleys goes through the olive coats of the Sum-gol Post, and since the Soul Plane broke and the South’s dead began to drift, the same coats will lay a haunting for a fee. Their name was carried at the front of other people’s armies until there was little left but the carrying. What they want, in the plain words of the table at the Cedar Enclave, is their own name back off other people’s banners.
Origin of the House
The valley has always said that breath goes out of a person and stays there, spread thin, and it counts breath before it counts coin. The oldest entry in the teaching house is a ledger of oxen, kept by a woman called Wonsum, who noticed that a beast she had counted through a bad night would come to her voice in the morning when it came to nobody else’s, that this was true of her daughter’s voice as well, and that it held good for several things in the hills that were not oxen. Everything after that is scholarship. Her descendants wrote it down, sealed their first great compact (a bargain with a power that owns its own soul) with the White Stag they call the Baengnok, and about the year 300 a Daeju Mahuo came down the terraces with the Stag at his shoulder and a large number of guests, and the South found that it had an emperor.
You know how that ended: the Calling of 602, the Stag walking out by the East Gate, three more generations as kings, and then the long war, which three houses fought under the excuse of protecting them. Today the line stands in pieces, and the pieces disagree. The head of the house is Cozbi Mahuo, twenty-five, Master of the Post and the man the Zettari–Mahou Accord condemns by name. The Kwon cadet branch gave the Accord its drafter, Kwon Mu-jin, called the Teacher, and lost generations ago the knack of hosting souls; it calls by request form instead. His sister Ara Min Mahuo, the Healer, is the name most of the world puts on the lawful line. The Aperture branch at Yeol-gol keeps the household pattern of Obrenkael, the Mule, under a standing objection.
The House on the Crystal
A Soul Crystal is the soul itself, in three layers: the Aether Shell on the outside, where Aether (mana) enters and force goes out; the Essence Core at the center, where it is refined into Essence (spiritual energy) and stamped with who you are; and the Attraction Layer, a soul’s own share of Fate. The Mahuo run them unevenly.

























LayerPlaneThe Mahuo formAether ShellPhysicalThin and undistinguished. Most Mahuo read a low rung here all their lives and leave the heavy lifting to their guestsEssence CoreSoulTheir strength. Early to hear, slow to fray, and used from childhood on oxen, grandmothers and the deadAttraction LayerFateClean, which is all. It is where a compact is addressed, and what a Mahuo writes there spends their own share and pulls nothing down
Path. A Path is the layer a soul has learned to lean on, recognized from how it lives, and no blood ever gave one. Mahuo children tend toward the Spirit Path with a long second road into Fate’s shallow end, since a summons reads the Shell for the crossing, the Core for what the thing is, and the Layer for who it recognizes.
The grip. The Mahuo’s grip is on the Spirit road. No coil reads Mastery before Glory, Stage VI, theirs included, but the grip sits in the body long before that as the Trait below, so a child of the line hears souls years before any coil can number why. From Glory their Spirit Mastery is read from Level under the Stage’s ceiling, as over everybody. They have no eye and no grip on Fate: without a Work or a blessing Fate stops at the second rung, most of the house never reads it at all, and a Mahuo who has held to her compacts for decades may read Fate I.





























Spirit rung, and the road’s own word for itTypical MahuoI · ListenerA teenager in Breath Hollow, who knows who is on the household rollII · AnswererA Post rider who can lay a small haunting; the first real compactIII · ConfessorPhysicians of the line, reading a soul whole by its breathingIV · ShepherdElders who hold the dead still long enough to ask them thingsV · FerrymanThe head of the house, at an age that has made a great many scholars write to each other
The Answering — 응답 · Eungdap
What it is. Every summoner knows that a thing called once is easier to call twice. In ordinary hands that is a small saving, and it belongs to the one who earned it. In the Mahuo it runs as blood does: each answer makes the next come quicker and cheaper, on a curve no other summoner’s will follow, and it is filed under the family. A child can come into a compact her grandmother paid down.
How it works, in plain words. A Mahuo calls on the out-breath, and the calling is an address, a name sent out with an offer. Nothing is dragged anywhere. A summons by recognition can be refused, which is why the art can be learned in a yard at all. Where others leave the reply at that, the house current, the Wellspring Anima Spirare, teaches the soul a different habit. Blood is the scholars’ picture of it. Each grain of the red part of the blood takes up its first breath of air grudgingly, and every breath it has already taken makes the next go on easier, so it loads faster the more it carries. The Mahuo Core does that with recognition. The first answer is expensive. The second has a place to land. By the fiftieth the thing has almost no distance left to cross. And since Essence is stamped with identity, and a family’s stamps run close, a called thing that has known the mother will know the daughter when she breathes out, as a dog knows a voice in the next room.
The forms.






























FormKoreanWhat it isFirst Call첫 부름 · Cheot BureumThe full price, the long breath and the real chance of no. A seal in the house color opens on the thing’s brow if it agreesCalling Back되부름 · DoebureumA compact called again. The price falls with each answering, and what the thing is owed starts to be kept by habitThe House Roll가문 명부 · Gamun MyeongbuInheritance. A compact entered on the family’s list passes to a recognized descendant, with all its savings and all its arrearsThe Morning Bowl아침 그릇 · Achim GeureutThe old compacts, answered so often they come almost before the breath is out, for nearly nothing. A lifetime’s work, or several lifetimes’
What it costs. The words run both ways, and everyone in the valley knows it. A called thing is paid in what it wants, and the great ones want things that cost. Inherit the compact and you inherit the bill. Mahuo children are read their debts along with their sums, and the Seven Debts of Sum-gol, cousins whose grandfather gave them all the generation-syllable Chae, are the valley’s oldest joke because they are also its truest. Anything on the roll has standing. It can come to the door without being called, and ask.
Its limit. The Answering saves on the call and adds nothing to the thing that answers. A sealed compact runs on the creature’s own Essence, so it is as strong as the creature and no stronger, and a house with a small roll is a house with a small roll. It needs a name that still means something, too. Recognition is a two-sided thing, and a compact written to run while the realm answers ends when it stops. Nobody living has the great roll of the empire. Scavengers in painted hoods come up out of the Answering Vaults under the Palace square with reports of a host standing in rows, waiting for a voice they would know.
Who beats it. Reach the caller: a bound will tests its leash, and a fighter who strikes at the holder’s resolve instead of the beast has found the real weak point. Exhaust the creature, since its reserve is what is paying. Get a better contract onto it, which the rolls call theft and the yards call Tuesday. And do not mistake the Answering for what the Accord condemns. An answer is given. A soul taken from someone who was never asked, folded into a thread and spent, is conscription, the crime with the house’s name on it, and the Accord’s whole written code exists to tell the two apart in a form a soldier can read.
Physical Appearance and Dress
There is no Mahuo face to speak of, three centuries of imperial marriages having seen to that, though black hair that goes green in lamplight runs in the main line and a long ear turns up in the eastern households. They are slight, narrow in the chest, and famous for their breathing, slow and very even, so that nervous people find themselves falling into it. Elders of the old school can be told by the small lines at the corners of the mouth, from a lifetime of breathing out through it. Voices run warm and carrying, and a Mahuo at table is always the host, whoever is paying.
Vermilion and white are the house colors. Sum-gol wears vermilion still, a sash or a rag or a dyed hat, because the cinnabar is local and cheap. The Post wears olive. A rider has an olive wool coat and a short curved hwando saber across the shoulders, a bag of salt at the belt and brass leg-tubes for the crows. An elder of Breath Hollow goes in undyed hemp with a soul-breath physician’s red cord at the wrist. At fifty paces the thing to look for is a person walking quite alone with too much room around them. A poor cousin has one good cup, gray-green, from the old Sum-gol kilns, and will turn its small vermilion glaze-mark to face you before she pours.
Lineage Traits
[Trait] The Long Breath — Hearing Before Glory
The grip, as it sits in the body. A Mahuo child’s Core takes to souls before it takes to anything else.

Works at its base from childhood, long before Glory; from Glory it reads at the soul’s Spirit Mastery, up to what the Stage allows.
Hears a soul in another’s breathing: fear, lies, the first days of a wasting sickness. Sum-gol sells this as diagnosis and lineage-reading.
Sensing, called nunchi, comes easily and rudely, and every grandmother in the line has it.

A nursemaid in the Hollow teaches a child to count the ox’s breathing before she teaches it the copper.
[Trait] The Blood’s Own Answer — Anima Spirare in the Line

The body answers a small hurt with all it has: bleeding stops fast and sickness is met early.
A trained Mahuo can lend this to another by touch, which is most of what the Healer’s school is, and it sits very ill with the Accord’s enemies that the line’s lawful art is mostly nursing.
Under strain it fails as the cascade fails, running everywhere at once.

They are the only house whose healers and whose monsters use the same breath.
[Trait] Blood Knows Blood — The Reading of the Roll

A Mahuo can see, a little, what another Mahuo has called: seals, threads, the shape of a compact.
A descendant knows when something on the family roll has moved, though not always what.
It works in both directions, and no Mahuo has ever kept a summons from a sufficiently stubborn relative.

Hiding a guest from your mother has never once worked in Sum-gol.

Wellspring compatibility
A Wellspring is a type of Aether and the idea a soul tempers itself on. It is a lens and locks nobody out of the rest.






























TierWellspringsWhyNaturalAnima Spirare, Mortalis, AnamnesisThe breath, the gate and the memory. The first two are contraries, and the house has tempered on both by custom for centuries, at a price it does not put in the prospectusEasyEidolyn, Benediction, Fixatio, TransferenceShaping a guest, a bond freely given, a binding that stays, a road between two soulsWorkableVerdantia, Phreatis, Oblation, Catharsis, AbsolutionLiving and watery work. Catharsis and Absolution are Spirit Wellsprings, and give a Mahuo no fire, only what a grief or a haunting can be made to set downAgainst the grainNihiloth, Vantabriel, PyraeonNothing there answers
On the Stages





























StagesHow a Mahuo readsI to III · Murmuring to AscensionBreath counted, the roll learned, a small echo of an ancestor that comes for a breath and goesIV to VI · Flourishing to GloryFirst Release, cheotjjae puri, “the first untying.” A vessel shaped and an identity lent; the first small compact, and a class name at Glory, often about a job or a debtVII to IX · Refraction to InvocationSecond Release, duljjae puri. Standing forms, a real roster and a seat on the Post’s roadX to XII · Realization to EmanationStable calling, then sustained autonomous summons, the gates the whole trade uses. The Spirit road has no third untying; the old word for one, setjjae puri, is kept for the Second Release grown whole, and said rarely. Kwon Hae-ryu of Yeol-gol stands at Realization, and the house once had a hall full of elders hereXIII and upWhere the great ones of the old line brought bestiaries to the square. One living Mahuo stands here
Doctrine and Arts
The Host. A Mahuo at war does not fight; a Mahuo gives a party at which you are killed. The doctrine is to arrive with enough room, lay the field like a table, and bring the guest who suits the company. Riders stay on the horse, draw a ring, and let the salt argue. Sum-gol salt, poured in a closed ring and named aloud, gives a called thing a door it must ask at, and that holds off the lesser drift for about as long as a rider needs.















































MoveTongueMeaningWhat it doesBulleora!불러라”Call!”The plain summons, on the out-breath, with a compact’s name in it. The name comes first and the thing a beat afterSogeum Gori!소금 고리”Salt Ring!”A ring of stamped salt thrown around a body or a door. Lesser spirits and the drifting dead stop at itSum Segi숨 세기”Counting Breath”Said softly. Reads a soul by its breathing: its fear, its hurt, how long it hasPi-Ui Daedap!피의 대답”The Blood’s Answer!”A touch that sends a body’s whole defense to one wound. It closes a torn artery in a breath, and overdone it opens the gumsDoebureum!되부름”Call Back!”Dismisses a guest and has it answer again elsewhere on the field a beat later, so a thing can be somewhere new at the price of an old friend’s patienceMyeongbu Pyeolchyeora!명부 펼쳐라”Open the Roll!”Every compact the caller holds, at once, on one breath. Done perhaps three times in the empire’s history, and the bills went on arriving for a generation
Culture
They speak Sum-gol’s Korean-registered tongue, with given names of a generation-syllable and a personal one, the family name before or after as it falls, and syllables drawn from breath, ledger and care. A release is an untying, the same word as the old rites that untie a grief. Their ranks run outer disciple to elder, as any teaching house.

The First Count. At three, a child sits up one night with the oldest ox in the village and counts its breathing to dawn. If it comes to the child’s voice in the morning, the teaching house opens a page.
The Reading of Arrears. On the eve of the first compact, an elder reads the candidate everything the family owes: what, to whom, since when. It has been known to take three days. Some walk out, and the house lets them.
The Turned Cup. Anything called, from a beast to a thing with no face, is offered a cup before it is asked for anything, the mark turned toward it. Those who skip this, the valley says, are the ones who get eaten.
The Untying. Mahuo burial law alone in the four quarters does not require the family to keep the body. The breath has already gone to the valley. Family members sit with the dying and take over the compacts one by one, aloud, until none is left in the room with nowhere to go.

Who they marry, fight and owe. They married the South for three centuries and are related to everyone who is not speaking to them. The Accord proposes a marriage with the Zettari Sovereign that is entirely the Healer’s to refuse. Lord Naiser Yukari has offered the throne back, and it has been declined with very good manners. House Ryu holds the old revenue and sends a letter. Sum-gol’s commoners have rent cheap enough to live in a duke’s kitchen, the oldest law in the South, and a sealed bag no one may rob. Couriers are paid when the Post can pay, and they stay anyway, for reasons a good many people would like to know.
Limitations and Soul-Costs
[Curse] The Roll Reads Both Ways — Call, and It Answers
Everything a Mahuo has on the roll has standing. A compact missed comes to collect, by its own terms, and what comes may not be small. A newborn of the line can owe a power that was old when the empire was young.
[Curse] Two Lenses, One Gate — The Contrary in the Blood
A body refusing the gate and a soul walking toward it make a poor marriage. Mahuo who push Anima Spirare fail by disseminated activation, the cascade running everywhere until they bleed from the gums, nose and eyes. Those who push Mortalis fail by Equilibration, cooling a little toward the boundary with every working. Elders of the line are often both, and they keep their rooms warm.
[Curse] The Thin House — Nobody to Inherit
Sixty roofs, a school with more benches than pupils. A compact with no recognized heir does not end. It just stops being answered from this side, and everything owed goes on being owed. Somewhere in the iron hills there is a Stag. The house has a young head and very few children, and a great many things out there remember the name.
How They Stand Against the Three Paths
Body. The old nightmare. A hitter who gets through the guests finds a slight person in a good coat, and a spear does not care what you mean. Every Mahuo rider therefore knows exactly how far away a charging man is, and how long the out-breath takes.
Spirit. Their own ground, and the most dangerous of their enemies. A Spirit fighter can read the compact, find the clause the charter forgot, or wound the Core that holds the leash. The trained ear finds the seams in anything built from borrowed souls.
Fate. Slow, and it hurts. They have no answer of their own to a true pull, and a Fate user can move what an answer depends on: the name that arrives late, the seal that fails to open. They beat it by reaching the hand on the thread, since a called thing is often standing nearer than the caller’s enemy expects.
Final Definition
The Mahuo are the family that made the world answer, and they went on making it answer until it noticed that the question could be turned around. What remains is a road, sixty roofs, some very old debts, and every morning a bowl of rice on a step in Breath Hollow, because you do not leave the weather waiting. Northerners ask what a summoning line does with its arts when it has no hall left to call them into. The answer in the valley is the one it has always been.
Call, and it answers. Then it asks what you owe.
