The target is not just held; their ability to reorganize is takenSarmad FractureInfinite BreakA finisher at the central junction through which force or Shell pressure is distributed. Infinite means not limitless force but cascading failure that keeps going after the blow, each broken line passing its load to the nextAsili Flow-Blade—An ocular-guided construct laid along visible Aether channels. Lower forms cut Essence pathways without cutting flesh; advanced forms can sever summoning links and Fate-recognized routesRuqya Collapse—Turns instability already inside an Essence structure (contradiction, overcharge, contamination, poor purity) against itself. Against a stable, flawless system it has almost nothing to work withN’gala Fang Pulse—Compressed Aether bursts woven into close combinations, each pressing a different weakness so the opponent cannot rebuild one stable defensive rhythmKumi-na-Mbili SealTwelvefold StillnessTwelve sequences, one hundred and forty-four strikes on joints, Aether routes, movement initiators, Essence junctions and pressure points. Its aim is enforced stillness, not deathDawam Soul-Still Art—Heavily restricted. Interferes with recovery, Soul recognition, Fate continuity, regeneration and adaptive circulation. Because it can sever recovery from identity, ethical use is limited to beings whose regeneration makes ordinary containment impossibleUzito wa MwishoThe Final WeightA royal finishing art. The Zettari strikes while still carrying the Load of their last Matla working, and the Law of Weight passes that Load into the target instead of the ground. Only the Load actually borne can be given; a bearer who tries to give more than they carried breaks first
Sanaa za Chemchemi — The Spring Arts
Taught only to royal and high-blood Zettari from Stage VIII who hold the Current Practice (Material Energetics, once called the Essence Practice) or the Dominion Practice (Material Jurisdiction), and who have at least the Everlasting Eye. The three arts build on one another: a spring must be shut off before it can be seized, and seized many times before it can become your own.
Kuzima Chemchemi — Shutting Off the Spring
A contact art, usually landed through Kiganja cha Kuvunja or the Nuruq Point-Seal. The Zettari strikes the junction where the target’s Wellspring Aether enters their Shell and switches it off. Their Shell stops answering that Wellspring at all. The lens goes dark: the target’s Wellspring techniques fail, and anything mid-cast collapses back into unshaped power, Charge or Essence by the road the target walks. The bearer chooses, at the moment of the strike, whether the shut-off is temporary or permanent.

One Wellspring per strike. A target with several harmonizations needs several strikes.
Temporary. Lasts as long as the bearer chooses, up to a limit set by the Stage gap and their Dominion: a few breaths against an equal, a whole fight against someone two Stages lower, days or weeks against the far weaker. The bearer carries the shut-off lens’s weight the whole time, and can switch it back on at will.
Permanent. The junction is not held closed; it is broken for good, and the target never draws on that Wellspring again. It needs the True Everlasting Eye to see the full harmonization route, a target at or below the bearer’s Stage, and a clean strike. The Load is paid all at once instead of over time: days of Charge Starvation, and a new Zettari pattern recording what was taken. Only the Zettari who did it can restore it, or an Origin-Eye bearer’s Baqaa.
Counters. A higher-Stage target throws off a temporary shut-off quickly and cannot be permanently shut off at all. The road a soul walks is no shelter: every soul’s harmonization locks at the Shell, where Aether enters, so a Spirit or Fate soul is shut off at the same junction as a Body one. What such a soul keeps is the Essence it had already refined before the strike, which still carries the old stamp and can be spent until it runs out. Blessings, Domain law and Archon-scale authority sit above the art. A Wellspring the target was born harmonized to can be shut off temporarily, but only a Path-Acknowledged Sovereign can shut it off for good.

Kutwaa Chemchemi — Seizing the Spring
A shut-off spring’s Aether is still in the air, still drawn toward the soul that called it. The Zettari reaches into that current and routes it through their own Shell instead.

The bearer can work the seized Wellspring for as long as the shut-off holds and its Aether is present; a permanently shut-off spring can be seized only once, for that fight.
Better than its owner. With the lineage’s exceptional Lattice Conductivity and Continuum Retention, a seized Wellspring usually expresses more cleanly and more forcefully in Zettari hands than in the hands that called it. Against a bearer of a lower Body Mastery, the difference is brutal.
The lens without the years. Raw output can exceed the original. The owner’s lived depth (their quirks, their decades of mastery, their school’s named techniques) does not come with it.
The bill comes too. A Wellspring charges in its own coin, and a seized one charges whoever is using it. Seize Pyreveil, and the heat still has to leave by your own hands.
Limits. One seized Wellspring at a time below Stage XI; two from Dissonance on. Springs of another kind cost more of the reserve. Dream-dominant, nameless and structureless springs are dangerous to seize: they give the Zettari Shell nothing to hold, and can leak into the bearer’s own lens.

Kubadili Chemchemi — Turning the Spring
A rite, not a combat art. The Zettari changes the Wellspring their soul is tempered on: their native lens.

Where and how. At a Wellspring Core, on a Path pilgrimage, or at a Stone Witness site, across days of fasting, Essence Communion and the Breath of Kushara. It cannot be done in battle.
When. From Stage IX (Invocation), when Wellsprings begin to recognize the bearer instead of merely being drawn on.
Which spring. One the Zettari is already harmonized with, or one they have seized through Kutwaa Chemchemi often enough that their Shell knows its law.
What carries over. Hereditary bodily memory softens the turn. A Zettari keeps up to half the old lens’s earned maturity if the new Wellspring shares its kind, and about a quarter if it does not. The rest must be lived again.
The cost. The old law is pulled out of Shell, Core and Attraction Layer at once, and the Load lands on the body: weeks of weakness, a new Zettari pattern marking the turning, and an Ink Rite to recognize it.
Once per Stage. A Zettari who turns their spring too often becomes no one’s lens, and every Wellspring treats them as a stranger.

VIII. How the Inheritance Fits Together
Five systems make one Zettari:

The Path-Forged Body carries physical consequence.
The Soul Crystal preserves Essence, identity and spiritual architecture.
The Everlasting Ocular Inheritance perceives the physical and metaphysical structure of the problem.
Matla provides Aegoric authority over the law of matter being addressed.
The Paths decide how much of that authority this person can actually carry.

The Eye ascends Everlasting → True Everlasting → Origin. The Practices stand side by side: Form, Anti-Form, Time, Space, Dominion, Current, Void, Reality, Totality. Neither ladder replaces the other. The Eye tells the bearer what is there. Matla decides which law can be addressed. The body decides whether the result can be survived. And Aegor asks one question after all of them have acted: what carries what happens next?
Final Lineage Definition
The Zettari are a Path-Born sovereign human lineage descended from Aegor’s covenant with physical existence. Their bodies are extraordinarily dense; their Soul Crystals evolved for extreme physical translation; their Fate architecture binds them to ancestry and sovereignty; and their eyes climb from the Everlasting Eye to the True Everlasting Eye and, once in an age, to the Origin Eye.
Their supreme inheritance is Matla, the Instrument of the Paths. They are not rulers of all physical reality. They are a lineage with the right, under enough recognition and enough burden, to argue with the laws by which physical reality stays standing.
Their strongest warriors break bodies. Their sovereigns make territory acknowledge them. Their Matla bearers lay hands on Matter, Anti-Matter, sequence, interval, jurisdiction, material energetics, absence, actuality and whole material systems. And once in an age, the bloodline produces an Eye that looks past everything a thing has become and asks the question even Matla reaches only after analysis: where did you begin?
“The body is the first throne. The blood is the first oath. The ancestor does not die while the living still stand.”
Beneath it, in the oldest Path halls, where only the royal dead and the recognized living may read, another line is carved:
“Everything that stands began somewhere. Everything that begins must bear the weight of becoming.”

factions,-bloodlines--and--institutions/.filePath: Factions, Bloodlines & Institutions/Houses and Bloodlines/The Banner Houses of Kharven.md
factions,-bloodlines--and--institutions/.title: The Banner Houses of Kharven
factions,-bloodlines--and--institutions/.content:
Six houses around the Seat, each holding land, troops, and the conditional loyalty that is the north’s only currency. Lands and houses, all six, and never kingdoms.
Nobody at Hollenmark has forgiven the pie. When a Stark daughter married a Thornwall in the hard winter of 592, House Ashmore sent the gift the whole north still talks about: a raised game pie six feet across, its crust glazed gold and painted with all six banners in the proper colors, with a bushel measure baked inside it in case anybody had forgotten who kept the granaries. A Hallenfeld courier captain brought it up the March road on a sledge, six hours ahead of the day he had promised, and was unbearable about it. A Greymane sat guard on it all night in the firelit hall, because no one had told him to stop. In the morning a Keld elder come for the bride’s side tasted the crust and remarked that it would have made a decent meal for one, and the bride’s Dire Icebear, which had been let into the hall out of plain fear, walked over and ate the remainder, along with the measure, the banners and most of the table, while the Thornwall groom priced the damage aloud and the bride laughed until she had to sit down. The Ashmore envoy, soft-voiced and clean-handed, said nothing whatever. That year Hollenmark’s grain allocation came in short by exactly one bushel, and the Starks have sent an empty pie dish to Ashbury every midwinter since.
That is the north in one meal, and the rest of this page is the ledger behind it.

Two hands on this page. The seats, lands, charges and tempers below stand as this shelf stands them, in Year 715, the twenty-fifth of the Dark Ages, when the six are old. What comes after runs past that seal, and the little of it set down here is in the later hand that also annotates the Concordance of Ages, marked Later hand where it begins. Read those lines as weather coming over the ridge.

How the years run
The houses are far older than the crown that binds them, and older copies of this page have muddled which came first, so here it is in order.
Before. The Banner Houses carry northern names because their roots predate the Moto arrival by centuries. Kharven-Seat stands on its rock already. The Kōkan sit the red chair for a long time, with Thornwall as their forester and the others about their business, until the Tenrai take the rock three hundred years before this seal. The north’s old count speaks of Seven Warlords, names six houses, and declines to discuss it.
Year 715, the page’s morning. The forty-year war has just stopped. The red chair has stood empty all forty of those years. There is no sovereign to swear to, so no Banner Oath is running, and the houses answer under the old summons law to the seven lines in the Hall of Verdicts, which in practice means Tenrai silver, Tenrai factors and a Tenrai toll-post on the Kessen road. Each house is on its own land with its own lord, and each is working out what it is owed.
Later hand: within a few winters of the seal the Seat has a king again, and the Northern Empire of Whitemere is built out of the kingdom. The six go into it as they stand, holding their own lands. That is his story, and it is told elsewhere.
1. House Stark
Realm: The Cobalt March of Hollenmark
Seat: Hollenmark, eastern highlands, toward the Ring
Territory: The Ironwood March and eastern frontier
Identity: Borders. House Stark defines where things end and begin.
Lord in 715: Ulf Stark, Lord of Hollenmark, Master of the eastern March, one of the Seven Warlords
The Starks carry an ice-aspected bloodline inheritance that predates the Moto and operates outside the standard Wellspring framework: a cold radiating from body and blood, intensifying under emotional pressure, silvering timber and stiffening snow in a radius around the bearer. The inheritance is northern, no part of the Moto, older than the kingdom and older than the Starks’ own records, and the Starks do not discuss its origins with outsiders because the origins are Stark business and the Starks keep their business behind their borders.
Their mount tradition is the Dire Icebear, an enormous polar ursid whose white fur carries a permanent frost dusting and whose temperament is exactly what the name implies. Nobody has ever domesticated an Icebear; the arrangement is a partnership. A Stark rides one because the bear has decided to permit it, and the permission is withdrawn the moment the rider stops being worth carrying, and the withdrawal is not gentle.
The full codex: House Stark.
2. House Greymane
Realm: The Slate Ridge of Stormfold
Seat: The Ridgewall, western highlands
Territory: The Stormfold
Identity: The shield. House Greymane holds the western border.
Title: The Shieldwarden, always, regardless of the lord’s given name
Words: The Ridge Does Not Move
The north’s defensive architecture in human form. Their seat is a fortress built into the ridgeline separating Kharven from Undaar-Keth, and they have held it, in their own words, since before there was a north to hold it for. The words describe the house, which has never once found them inspiring.
Greymane culture is military to the point of institutional. Children are raised to see themselves as components of a defensive structure rather than individuals with personal ambitions; the ones who reject the framing leave, and the ones who stay become the most reliable garrison troops in the Inner World. The Shieldwarden is addressed by title rather than name because the function matters more than the person, and the house has internalized this deeply enough that the personal name of the current Shieldwarden is known within the family and almost nowhere else.
The full codex: House Greymane.
3. House Ashmore
Realm: The Golden Hollow of Ashbury
Seat: Ashbury, southern lowlands, where the Kessen, the Marrow and the salt road meet
Territory: The Greenhollow
Identity: The breadbasket. House Ashmore feeds the north.
Lord in 715: Edric Ashmore, Lord of the Ashmore Marches
The least martial house in a martial kingdom and the most quietly dangerous. Their power is grain. Their leverage is the specific kind that comes from controlling what everyone else needs to survive the winter, and the Ashmores have never lost a negotiation with anyone who was hungry, which in the north means they have never lost a negotiation.
The house governs through a steward’s competence rather than personal combat capability: soft voice, clean hands, and the danger that comes from knowing exactly how many bushels each Banner House needs to survive December and being willing to adjust the allocation on political grounds. The Ashmores do not threaten. Threats are for houses whose leverage requires explanation. Ashmore leverage explains itself every time the temperature drops. Oaths in the Hollow are sworn with the hand flat on the junction stone below Ashbury, and the Hollow believes the stone holds them.
The full codex: House Ashmore.
4. House Thornwall
Realm: The Scarlet Wood of Thornhaven
Seat: Thornhaven, northern Ironwood March
Territory: The Thornwood, the ironwood stands, and the corridor to Marrowhold
Identity: Timber and trade. House Thornwall bridges the north and the Marrowkin.
Ruler in 715: Hisae Thornwall, the Lady of Thornwall
Merchant-warriors, comfortable with commerce in a way most northern houses find slightly undignified and the Thornwalls consider essential. Their wealth comes from the ironwood stands the Marrowkin import for tool handles and ward-frames, and their function as the Marrowhold-facing house gives them an outsized voice in the north’s trade. They read cargo rolls the way other houses read battle reports, and consider the ability to predict a supply shortage six months out a more valuable military skill than the ability to hold a shield wall, on the grounds that the shield wall is useless if the men behind it are starving.
When the Ore Council of Marrowhold cuts grain supply but keeps sending inscription stock, the Thornwalls notice first, because they have tracked the holds’ trade behavior for generations and know the difference between a shortage and a message. Their standing reading of the Ore Council’s supply decisions is that they are political rather than logistical: the Marrowkin are comfortable with an armed frontier buffer and uncomfortable with an independent one, and the grain cut is a statement about the limits of northern autonomy rather than a reflection of the holds’ capacity. The reading is correct. The Thornwalls are almost always correct about trade, which is why the other houses find them slightly irritating.
The full codex: House Thornwall.
5. House Keld
Realm: The Aurora Reach of the Keld
Seat: None fixed. Seasonal camps on the Polar Reach, the greatest being the Whalebone Gather.
Territory: The tundra beyond the treeline
Identity: Survival. House Keld exists where existence is the primary occupation.
In 715: Old Harald leads the fires, and his grandson is coming up behind him fast
The smallest house, the hardest people, and the most conditionally loyal. They live beyond the treeline in conditions that would kill members of any other house inside a week and that the Keld consider baseline. A Keld fighter raised on the Polar Reach has already survived conditions that would kill the enemy before the fighting started, and the fighting itself is an afterthought beside the surviving. They swear to a person, never to a letter or a house, and only to one who comes out onto the tundra and sits at their fires.
The full codex: House Keld.
6. House Hallenfeld
Realm: The Painted Rivers of Hallenfeld
Seat: Hallenfeld, the river junction
Territory: The river valleys and trade corridors between Kharven-Seat and the eastern provinces
Identity: Movement. House Hallenfeld controls roads, rivers, and communication.
In 715: Ilse Hallenfeld, Mistress of the Hallenfeld counting-house
The north’s nervous system. They hold the junction where the three principal roads meet: the eastern route toward the March and the corridor to Marrowhold, the northern route toward the Polar Reach, and the southern route down to Ashbury and the Center. Whoever holds that junction controls the speed at which the north can respond to anything.
The Hallenfelds have no glamour and produce no legendary warriors or political masterminds. They produce quartermasters, road engineers, courier captains, and the category of administrator who understands that a message delivered six hours faster can save a thousand lives and treats the six hours as a problem worth solving with the intensity other houses bring to swordwork.
The full codex: House Hallenfeld.
The Six at a Glance






















































HouseRealmSeatHoldsIn 715StarkThe Cobalt March of HollenmarkHollenmarkThe eastern March, the bordersUlf Stark’s. Short on sons, long on grudgesGreymaneThe Slate Ridge of StormfoldThe RidgewallThe western wall against Undaar-KethThe Shieldwarden’sAshmoreThe Golden Hollow of AshburyAshburyGrain, the GreenhollowEdric Ashmore’s, on Tenrai roads and Tenrai silverThornwallThe Scarlet Wood of ThornhavenThornhavenIronwood, the corridor to MarrowholdThe Lady’s, under Tenrai factorsKeldThe Aurora Reach of the KeldNone. Polar Reach campsThe tundra beyond the treelineOld Harald’s firesHallenfeldThe Painted Rivers of HallenfeldHallenfeld junctionRoads, rivers, couriersIlse Hallenfeld’s ledger

factions,-bloodlines--and--institutions/.filePath: Factions, Bloodlines & Institutions/Houses and Bloodlines/The Central Warlords.md
factions,-bloodlines--and--institutions/.title: The Central Warlords
factions,-bloodlines--and--institutions/.content:
Four houses of the Inner World’s center, wedged between the North and the South, none of them human, each content that you have to look them up
Quartermaster-General Tancred Hasketh of the second Aldwater League was the best-prepared man ever to march across the center, and in the spring of 709 he said so. He had paid the councils of the salt cities for the road. He had paid the Accord at Sealhall for the seals, and three separate petty kings of the Midmarch for three separate bridges, all of which turned out to be the same bridge. He had nine thousand men in orange, a wagon train a day long, four hundred licensed Beastkin porters on the Verath contract, and a ledger bound in red, and on the morning of the eleventh day he came out of his tent into a bright gold camp and found four things waiting for him on his folding table, none of which had been there when he went to bed.
The first was a basket of pears, with a note in a beautiful hand on birch bark, inviting him to go round. The second was an account from a surgeon he had never engaged, in rose ink, listing the names of the eleven men in his host who would be dead of the flux by the end of the month, the well they had drunk from, the price of the cure, and a line noting that his grandfather had camped in the same field and made the same mistake. The third fell out of a perfectly empty blue sky as he was reading it and stuck in the table, an arrow fletched with a gray feather, carrying a slip of paper that read Rain Thursday, heavy, you are in a floodplain, four silver. The fourth was no message at all. His ledger’s Beastkin page was gone, sliced out with a very clean edge, and four hundred porters and their pack-beasts had left in the night without waking one sentry, and on the ledger’s open spine lay a single sawn piece of iron, stamped with a thumb. He held all four up in front of his captains, the morning sun coming through the orange tent-silk and turning his face the color of a bad peach, and he bellowed, with nine thousand men listening, “Who in the name of hell are these people?”
Nobody could tell him. The Marrick sergeant who had been his guide said he believed there were four of them, and could name three. He went round by the second week, the rain arrived on Thursday, and he paid every one of those bills. He died an old man still unable to name the fourth, and that was the way all four of them preferred it.
The north counts its Banner Houses, and every soldier knows the words. The south has its seven, with a table and a chair kept empty, and every merchant knows the prices. Ask a northerner about the Central Warlords and you will get a shrug, a song that gets the details wrong, or a very good story about a pear. I have seen a man win a tidy sum in a Kharven tavern for naming three, and the bookie paid out on the spot, with no danger of anyone ever taking the fourth leg of the bet. The roads run through the salt cities and the Accord’s seal-towns and the bridges of the Hundred Crowns, and the armies follow those roads, and so do the heralds, with the minstrels close after. The four Warlords live off to the side of all of that, around the rim of the Scourge of Hell, in a mire, up a cliff, behind a posted price and under no name at all.
Each of them, for reasons of its own, likes it. A people the Accord would classify as stock has very little to gain from fame. The great powers march through the center every generation and take note of whatever they can name, so whatever they can name, they burn, tax or marry. The salt cities and the petty kings have paid for being on the map for as long as there have been maps. The four have spent a good many centuries staying off it, and they have discovered that an army with no idea you exist will walk into your country without a scout out.

The central rule. A Banner House of the north serves for as long as the Crown serves. A Southern Warlord serves nobody and has a price for everything. A Central Warlord would rather you had not heard of it, and will send you a bill on the morning you find out. The Moss Court’s bill is in pears. The Scalebond’s is itemized. The Caelwards charge for the weather. House Nobody has already been paid.

1. The Moss Court
People: Verdant Orcs
Seat: Mosk-Vaal, grown into the roots of the great tree
Territory: The Moonlight Forest of Mosk-Vaal, the glowing wetlands of the low center, with Rootgate, Glowwater, Ghurash Hollow, the Blooming Mire and Totemdeep
Identity: The ground. What marches through the Moonlight Forest stays there and comes up in the spring.
Current head: The Mire-Mother, Ssaaleth the Long Breath, chosen by the largest working spoken on one breath
Words: We Will Keep It For You
Colors: Moss-green and moth-white
A nation of wetland orcs who treat death as a phase, and who cannot leave. More than two days from swamp or kin a Verdant Orc begins to wither, and so the Court has never in its long history taken a yard of anyone’s land. It has simply kept every army that tried to use its causeway, in rows, and sold the fruit. To a passing general this is the safest neighbor in the world up to the moment he decides to save eleven days.
The full codex: The Moss Court.
2. House Scalebond
People: Serpentkin
Seat: Coilspire Den, under the statue of the man they kept
Territory: The Rose Coils of Coilspire, the rose-stone hills with Stoneglass Hollow and Bothhands, and a disputed claim on the Pale Fang Archipelago
Identity: The record. They remember everything anyone has tried to forget, and they treat and poison both armies.
Current head: The Remembrancer, Zsovrath Oda-riss, for the Standing Record
Words: It Has Been Tried
Colors: Rose and gold
A country of gold-scaled scholars and surgeons, with a stair and a posted price. Every commander of means has a Scalebond at his bedside and has made his peace with the fact that the other side has one too. They take no side and forget nothing, and their testimony is admitted everywhere it can be afforded and treated as anecdotal by the Accord, which then asks them for the answer. The great powers know of them mainly as a surgeon’s fee, which is the least frightening way to know them.
The full codex: House Scalebond.
3. House Caelward
People: Avian Kin
Seat: Caelspire, on the twin crags, keeping the summit pool and the bridge
Territory: The Violet Peaks of Caelspire, a range of rival schools, with Windstair and Highroost
Identity: The height. No army has ever taken the high stairs, and most have not been noticed trying.
Current head: The Warden of the High Stair, Vessaly Caelward, called Nobody’s Landing
Words: Step Off
Colors: Violet and white
A house that keeps order among a dozen schools run like football clubs, and that has never been the strongest on its own mountain. It holds the hoists, the Core’s hours and the court of the Drop, and it sells the wind to whoever pays. Half the battles of the center have been timed off a Windstair almanac by someone who has never heard the name of the people who wrote it. The Peaks consider this a healthy arrangement, and their real enemy is whichever club beat them on Saturday.
The full codex: House Caelward.
4. House Nobody
People: Catkin, Wolfkin and Bearkin runaways
Seat: Brokencollar, at the foot of the Heap
Territory: The Russet Crown of the Unpapered, the forest of permanent autumn on the Concord’s flank, with Shadowed Ridge, Nightveil Hollow, Greyfang Crossing and the Glade of the Slumbering Root
Identity: The refusal. A kingdom the Accord will not recognize, whose whole safety depends on a form it filled out wrong.
Current head: The Queen of Nobody, Sefa Tuen-zhiv, while the town allows it
Words: Ashe, which is “I remain”
Colors: Russet and gold
This is usually the one the man in the tavern forgets, and I have met people in that forest who bought a round on hearing so. Anonymity for the others is a preference. For House Nobody it is the law of the land: it keeps no list, because a list can be stolen, and the people on it can be found. A correction to the Accord’s roll of 668 has been pending for nearly fifty years, since it must be served upon the party concerned.
The full codex: House Nobody.
The Table Nobody Called
The Southern Warlords have a table and the north has a Crown. The center has neither, and nothing in it binds any of the four to the others. The one time all four are known to have sat in a room was the winter of 612, at Bothhands, in the long ward, when a sickness was going through the armies and the Mire-Mother’s rot-wives, the Scalebond surgeons, a Caelward wind-reader and an old Bearkin from the Glade who had just come in with a cart found themselves over the same bed. They settled the matter of the sickness. They also came to one understanding, by all accounts without anyone proposing it, which is that none of them would ever point a marching army at any of the others. It has held for a hundred years, mainly on the strength of none of them being able to prove when it was agreed, apart from the Scalebond, who are not saying.
What the center wants, in one line each:

























HouseWantsMoss CourtThe salt kept sealed, the board obeyed, and a good cropScalebondThe record complete, the exemption renewed, and everyone’s accounts keptCaelwardThe stair uncut, the Core’s hours kept, and the Peaks left to their own quarrelsNobodyThe correction never served, the Long Way open, and every last pen gate off its pins
The Center and Everyone Else
The Accord. The Sealed Charter of the Concord is the one neighbor all four must answer. Its Beastkin Classification Provision makes stock of three of them on any day it chooses, and the fourth has no entry at all. Its clerks count everything in the center except the people who live there, and all four Warlords owe their obscurity, in part, to the fact that a people the Accord refuses to write down is also a people no one else can look up.
The other center. The Amber Cities of Nalūn and the Hundred Crowns of the Midmarch are the part of the center that anyone has heard of, and they take the marching. The salt councils pay both sides and owe neither. The petty kings change sides each decade. The four Warlords sell to them all, and regard them, kindly, as the people who stand in the road.
The North. Kharven’s Banner Houses buy Scalebond surgeons, Windstair almanacs and Vantry pears, and most of them could not tell you where any of it comes from. A clerk of the Hall of Verdicts at Kharven-Seat has lately sent inquiries. They are the first northern letters ever to spell all four names correctly, and all four houses have taken note of that with a good deal more alarm than they showed at any army.
The South. The great Dynasty of Sum-gol, when it held the whole South, sent its summoners and tax-collectors as far as the Rose Coils and no further, and the Coils will give you the date. Its breaking-up has left a generation of southern powers with their minds on each other. The Yan sell horses to anyone who can get a horse up a cliff, and the Marrick companies know the Moonlight Forest well enough to take their contracts’ end dates into account.

In a later hand, in the margin: The Northern Empire of Whitemere, in the years of its making, came down through the center by the roads like everyone before it, and it met the councils, the seal-clerks and the kings. Somebody in the Stack had at last read the right pages. Its columns were fed and guided and told about the rain, and few of the men in them ever knew how much of that was bought, or from whom. I have seen the ledgers, and the fourth column is blank.



On the record.
From the Guild’s rolls: the Verdant Orcs and their settlements, Spoor-Melds, Soul-Trees and the Swamp hand; the Serpentkin, Coilspire Den, Stoneglass Hollow and the Pale Fang claim; the Avian Kin as a single line in a table, which is all the Guild ever troubled to write; the Catkin, Wolfkin and Bearkin, their towns and their rites; the Labor Provision and its prices.
From hearsay, and the Guild would like that noted: every seat, head, word and color above; every date of a battle; the Heap; the Table Nobody Called.
Open. Whether there are really four. The Marrick sergeants say three and a rumor.



The Southern Warlords
The Banner Houses of Kharven

factions,-bloodlines--and--institutions/.filePath: Factions, Bloodlines & Institutions/Houses and Bloodlines/The Eight Great Houses of Kushara.md
factions,-bloodlines--and--institutions/.title: The Eight Great Houses of Kushara
factions,-bloodlines--and--institutions/.content:
The Sovereign House and the Seven Pillars beneath the Kusharan Throne. Old World continental order.
The Structure
The Old World is too large, too old and too geographically various to be governed by Kusharan officials alone. Deserts, rainforests, savannas, riftlands, river basins, mineral plateaus and southern seas each require rulers who know the land well enough to act without waiting weeks on instruction from the Crownlands.
The continental order beneath Dawn Guard is therefore built around eight houses. They are not equal. At their head stands House Zettari, holding the continental throne. Beneath it stand the Seven Pillars, each bearing one structure the Old World cannot do without: armies, gold, food, medicine, strategic minerals, maritime trade, northern water.
Several of the Seven ruled independent kingdoms, confederacies, tribal territories, mining domains, river cities or merchant states before incorporation. Dawn Guard did not destroy those identities. He bound them into a system.

Seven pillars hold the continent. The Zettari Crown decides what they hold together.

1. House Zettari — The Sovereign House
Seat: Kushara · Territory: The Kusharan Crownlands · Epithet: The Sovereign House
Additional titles: House of the Living Throne · Blood of the Crownlands · Keepers of Kushara
Continental duty: Sovereignty, continental law, supreme defense, inter-house arbitration, Royal Roads, Path stewardship
Greatest asset: The strongest sovereign bloodline and military lineage in the Old World
House Zettari is not merely the family currently occupying the throne. It is the political, martial, ancestral and metaphysical foundation the modern Old World is organised around, reaching backward past Dawn Guard’s consolidation into Material Aspect Sovereignty, the Everlasting Eyes, the Paths, ancestral recognition and the rites of Kushara.
The other houses possess something the continent requires. House Zettari possesses the authority that makes those things a system rather than seven competing regional powers.
Its territory covers the Crownlands surrounding the River Kesh: high savanna, fertile valleys, ancient plateaus, royal estates, military grounds, Ancestral Halls, Path-recognised sites and the city of Kushara itself. Its wealth is considerable and its military strength greater, but neither is the foundation. The foundation is sovereignty — power understood as the ability to make a claim survive contradiction. Material Aspect doctrine concerning Form, Essence, Space, Existence and localised Sequence shapes Zettari law as much as Zettari combat, deeply enough that non-Zettari administrators describe continental law in vocabulary borrowed from it.
The Sovereign Line. Dawn Guard — Zuberi Zettari — is sovereign head of the house and ruler of Kushara, with authority reaching across nearly every recognised political territory of the Old World. Supremacy does not mean local rulers have been replaced by Zettari governors; that would make the continent weaker. The sovereign house sits above the regional houses as arbiter, military guarantor, continental judge and final authority when one region’s interests threaten another’s.
The throne is expected to intervene when two Great Houses reach an unresolved dispute, a regional ruler violates continental compact, a major Royal Road becomes unsafe, invasion threatens multiple territories, Wellspring catastrophe exceeds regional capacity, trade restrictions threaten stability, one house attempts to monopolise resources essential to another, or a crisis concerns the Old World as a whole.
The Zettari military. N’Kharu can field far more ordinary soldiers. This does not make N’Kharu stronger. N’Kharu provides mass; Zettari provides supremacy. Zettari forces are considerably smaller — professional warriors, royal guards, Zettari Ken practitioners, Material Aspect specialists, sovereign bloodline combatants — operating at levels ordinary levy formations cannot reproduce. The Kusharan Royal Host forms the permanent core surrounding the throne: Crownland infantry, palace guards, reconnaissance, royal engineers, river forces, mounted companies, specialists sworn to the sovereign rather than a provincial lord.
In continental war Kushara does not replace the forces of the Seven. It becomes the command spine binding them.
The Paths. The Crownlands hold the strongest known stable Path recognition in the Old World, where ancestral rites, sovereign blood, family cords, historical standing, Material recognition and ancient ground intersect. The Paths are neither a public resource nor a private family privilege; they are an ancestral jurisdiction whose misuse could endanger things considerably older than the throne. House Zettari protects Path-sensitive sites, ancestral sanctuaries, sovereign burial grounds and the locations where the boundary between Kushara and the ancestral plane becomes unusually responsive.

The Seven keep the Old World alive. Zettari keeps it one.

2. House N’Kharu — The Thousand Spears
Seat: Khar’Mbara · Territory: The M’Bala Great Savannas and southern Kharu Belt
Continental duty: Armies, cavalry, migration-road security, central defense
Greatest asset: The largest bannermen host in the Old World
The military giant among the Pillars. Its grasslands are among the most populous in the Old World, holding farming towns, pastoral communities, warrior clans, fortified settlements, royal estates and old provincial families. The openness of the M’Bala permits rapid mustering and long-distance mounted movement.
At full continental levy N’Kharu can call approximately forty thousand bannermen — not forty thousand standing soldiers, but household warriors, cavalry retainers, regional companies, hunters, scouts, village militias and provincial troops bound to answer the banners.
Its permanent professionals are the Red Spear Companies, who patrol the Twelve Migration Roads, break bandit confederacies, protect settlements from large predators, escort royal messengers, manage dangerous herd movements and reinforce wherever the central territories require it. N’Kharu cavalry is among the finest conventional mounted force on the continent; their savanna coursers combine endurance, speed, heat tolerance and the ability to cross difficult seasonal terrain.
Its position west and southwest of the Crownlands is also a vast defensive buffer. Any hostile force approaching Kushara through the central continent must first contend with territories that raise armies faster than nearly anywhere else.

Zettari wins the battle that decides the war. N’Kharu makes certain there is still an army afterward.

3. House Vokari — Keepers of the Golden Vein
Seat: Vorak-Tel · Territory: The Auric Plateau and eastern Golden Back
Continental duty: Precious metals, treasury support, deep mining, mineral law
Greatest asset: The richest gold mines in the Old World
Where N’Kharu provides bodies, Vokari provides the wealth that sustains them. Beyond gold, its domains yield platinum, silver, cobalt, manganese, diamonds, Harmonic ore, chromium and occasional star-metal fragments. The Golden Veins are not one mine but an interconnected mineral system running beneath multiple valleys and canyon formations.
Vokari extraction law treats mining as a form of spiritual surgery. Seams intersect buried Wellspring currents, Memory Stone, ancient ruins and Three-Plane alignments, so reckless extraction damages more than geology. Vokari surveyors have abandoned mines worth fortunes because going deeper would destabilise something beneath them.
Vokari wealth underwrites sovereign coinage, military procurement, continental infrastructure, emergency reserves, ceremonial gold, royal construction, Zettari regalia, ancestral restoration and high-level magical instruments. The house maintains the Deep Surveyors, the continent’s finest specialists in identifying buried Wellspring activity, geological anomalies, ancient structures and dangerous mineral formations.

N’Kharu raises the army. Vokari keeps it paid.

4. House Malani — The Hands Beneath the Bowl
Seat: Malara-Nahal · Territory: The Golden Floodplain, Sundi Basin, central Nahal valleys
Continental duty: Agriculture, irrigation, river management, famine prevention
Greatest asset: The largest food-production network in the Old World
Malani governs the resource every throne eventually discovers matters more than gold. Its lands follow the Nahal River System across floodplains, wetland farms, island communities, livestock regions, fisheries, irrigation districts, orchards and grain valleys. Its power is measured not by how its soldiers look but by how long a region survives when the rains fail.
The house keeps the Flood Calendar, an archive combining rainfall, sediment, mountain snowmelt, water color, Wellspring behavior, animal migration, river depth and centuries of flood records. Malani engineers use reservoirs, spill channels, gates, canals, flood fields and artificial wetlands to turn destructive river expansion into agricultural renewal.
Malani barges carry grain, fish, preserved meat, fruit, oils, livestock, river salt, medicinal reeds and emergency drinking water toward the capital continuously, and royal strategic granaries are maintained with Malani assistance. When M’Bala dries, when Zamaran storms destroy crops, when northern settlements lose harvests, Malani reserves are redirected under sovereign command.

Crowns rule men. Malani decides whether those men eat.

5. House Obaru — Wardens of the Living Green
Seat: Obar-Kele · Territory: Nyoka Rainsea and western Cloudwall foothills
Continental duty: Medicine, rare plants, timber, rainforest roads, ecological stewardship
Greatest asset: The greatest medicinal and biological resource network in the Old World
Obaru borders rarely follow straight lines. Jurisdiction follows rivers, groves, canopy roads, ancestral territories, settlements, living boundary trees and recognised forest corridors through the Nyoka Rainsea.
Its wealth is biological: medicinal compounds, poisons, rare fibers, resins, fungi, spirit amber, Memory bark, bloodwood and living materials that cannot be reliably cultivated elsewhere. Obaru healers and naturalists keep enormous archives recording which substances heal, poison, preserve, sedate, regenerate, stabilise Essence, or turn dangerous in combination.
Kushara draws anti-venoms, medicinal resins, battlefield drugs, restorative fungi, rare herbs, surgical compounds, Memory bark, spirit amber, bloodwood and specialised healing fibers from these territories, along with extremely durable tropical timber for major architecture and weapon construction. Obaru patrols maintain canopy roads, regulate harvests, protect sacred groves, manage dangerous fauna, monitor disease, recover travelers and investigate biological Wellspring corruption.

When armor breaks and blood follows, Obaru becomes the stronger shield.

6. House N’Yari — The House Beneath the Mountain
Seat: Yarath-Kel · Territory: The Great Akar Rift, Broken Spine, southern Orunthal approaches
Continental duty: Strategic minerals, eastern defense, geothermal engineering, Rift crossings
Greatest asset: The greatest concentration of rare magical minerals under one regional authority
N’Yari occupies land that appears determined to kill anyone attempting to govern it: volcanic valleys, fault systems, high escarpments, geothermal basins, cliff settlements, mountain passes and portions of the Broken Spine.
Its deposits include Riftstone, gravity ore, geothermal crystal, diamonds, rubies, sapphires, silver, obsidian, black salt, rare-earth metals and volatile Aetheric compounds. Vokari controls the greater concentration of financial wealth; N’Yari controls materials advanced civilisation cannot easily substitute — high-level construction, magical devices, military engineering, specialised wards, bridges, Rift Lifts and experimental spatial mechanisms.
Its troops specialise in mountain warfare, cliff operations, volcanic hazard, aerial predators and fortified passes. Its engineers make the eastern continent traversable at all: lifts, bridges, stairs, mountain shelters, geothermal stations, hazard beacons and warning systems for volcanic or Wellspring activity.

Vokari finds value beneath the earth. N’Yari finds what should never have been possible.

7. House Jomari — Lords of the Open Water
Seat: Jomaraz · Territory: Zamara Gulf, Nine-Mouth Delta approaches, southwestern coast
Continental duty: Navy, ports, foreign commerce, shipbuilding, coastal defense
Greatest asset: The largest fleet in the Old World
Jomari authority stretches across the Painted Harbors, the Sapphire Shelf, important islands, major coastal cities, naval fortresses and portions of the Nine-Mouth Delta. It maintains the Gulf Fleet, the largest maritime force on the continent, defending shipping lanes, suppressing piracy, escorting merchants, hunting dangerous sea creatures, transporting troops and monitoring foreign naval movement.
Jomari shipwrights combine tropical hardwood, ironwood, Tide crystal, metal reinforcement and foreign technique into some of the finest ships built outside dedicated maritime civilisations. Diplomats, imported technology, distant goods, overseas intelligence, foreign merchants and visitors pass through Jomari harbors before moving inland, and the house keeps vessels reserved for sovereign deployment.

Kushara commands the land roads. Jomari keeps the horizon open.

8. House Zembari — Keepers of the Hidden Water
Seat: Zembar-Kesh · Territory: Zafaran Expanse, Blackglass frontier, northern caravan routes
Continental duty: Desert commerce, aquifers, intelligence, northern frontier security
Greatest asset: The largest caravan and deep-water network in the Old World
Zembari governs a land where a castle may matter less than a well. Its holdings stretch across oasis cities, subterranean reservoirs, caravan fortresses, sandstone settlements, buried cisterns, salt roads, aquifers and ancient hydraulic routes. Individual holdings may stand hundreds of miles apart; what binds them is the Hidden Water Network, whose true extent is known only to trusted navigators, senior Zembari officials, certain caravan masters and the throne. Control of that network is control over which armies, merchants, pilgrims and migrations cross the Zafaran interior alive.
Its caravans carry salt, copper, desert glass, Sunstone, fire opal, Wellspring amber, spices, livestock, relics and information toward the heartland. Its merchants form one of the throne’s best informal intelligence systems. Armies see armies. Caravans see everything else.
Its riders maintain wells, rescue caravans, map migrating dunes, monitor Essence storms, track Dune Leviathan activity, reopen buried routes and keep traffic moving around the Blackglass Basin.

Gold buys water everywhere else. In Zafaran, water decides whether gold reaches anywhere.

The Eight Continental Duties



























































Great HousePositionContinental FunctionGreatest Strategic AssetZettariSovereign HouseContinental rule, supreme defense, arbitrationStrongest bloodline and the Kusharan throneN’KharuPillar HouseArmies and central defenseLargest bannermen levyVokariPillar HouseTreasury and precious metalsRichest gold minesMalaniPillar HouseAgriculture and river managementLargest food networkObaruPillar HouseMedicine and rainforest stewardshipGreatest medicinal resourcesN’YariPillar HouseStrategic minerals and Rift engineeringRare magical materialsJomariPillar HouseNavy and foreign tradeLargest fleet and portsZembariPillar HouseDesert routes and intelligenceNorthern aquifers and caravan network
The Balance of the Eight
Zettari supremacy does not make the others unnecessary. Dawn Guard’s system does almost the opposite: he wants them powerful. A weak N’Kharu cannot defend M’Bala. A weak Malani cannot answer famine. A weak Jomari cannot hold the coast. A weak N’Yari cannot maintain the Rift. A weak Zembari loses the north.
The objective is not to prevent strength. It is to make strength interdependent. N’Kharu armies require Malani food, Vokari coin, N’Yari material, Obaru medicine, Zembari intelligence and Jomari shipping. Vokari requires roads, labor, protection, food and markets. Malani requires military protection and transport. Obaru requires trade infrastructure. N’Yari requires food and commercial access. Jomari requires inland cargo, timber, ore and grain. Zembari requires manufactured goods and southern agriculture. And all seven require an authority capable of settling the disputes that inevitably follow.
The Council of Seven Pillars
Each Pillar House keeps a permanent representative in Kushara. Their rulers are not expected to abandon their territories for court; Dawn Guard considers a regional ruler who spends more time flattering the sovereign than governing his people to be failing at the reason he holds authority. Stewardship comes first. But when Kushara calls formally, the Seven answer.
House Zettari is not counted among the Seven, because the sovereign does not sit as one pillar among the structures holding up his own throne. House Zettari presides.
The Council advises on matters spanning several regions: continental taxation, resource shortage, major mobilisation, inter-house dispute, infrastructure, foreign trade, Wellspring emergency, and problems too large for one house. The Seven may disagree, argue, and tell Dawn Guard that a proposed action is foolish, economically destructive, militarily premature, culturally dangerous or impossible to implement. Competent disagreement is expected. What they may not do is mistake consultation for shared sovereignty.
Once a formal continental decision is rendered, the Pillars execute it unless the order violates one of the foundational compacts under which their local sovereignty was recognised. This is neither conventional feudalism nor a federation of equals. It is regional sovereignty beneath continental sovereignty. Malani water law remains Malani law. N’Yari mountain law remains N’Yari law. Vokari retains authority over its mines; N’Kharu retains its martial customs and regional banners.
Dawn Guard’s doctrine reduces to two principles: unity does not require sameness, and sovereignty carries responsibility in both directions. The Seven owe Kushara loyalty. Kushara owes the Seven protection, judgment, restraint, and a reason for that loyalty to remain worth holding.

See also: The Zettari · The Zettari–Mahou Accord · The Paths.

factions,-bloodlines--and--institutions/.filePath: Factions, Bloodlines & Institutions/Houses and Bloodlines/The Houses of the Inner World/House Ashmore.md
factions,-bloodlines--and--institutions/.title: House Ashmore
factions,-bloodlines--and--institutions/.content:
Overview





































TypeBanner House of Kharven · Grain Lords · Stewards of the GreenhollowOriginThe first tithe barn at Ashbury, which is older than the first lord who claimed itFounderGodric the Reeve, a steward who stayed on after the family he stewarded for had eaten itselfSeatAshbury, on the Golden HollowAnchorsThe tithe barns · the allocation · the split tally · the junction stoneSignatureThe Count of Mouths: an Ashmore can feel every mouth that has eaten Ashmore bread, and how long until it is hungry. The street calls it Which SackMaxim”Everyone in the north always pays Ashmore in the end.” It is carved nowhere, and it does not need to be
In the bad autumn of 633 the Host of the Nine Crowns came up over the Kessen ford, twelve thousand spears out of the Midmarch in every color the Hundred Crowns have ever fought over, to take the harvest of the Greenhollow. The Ashmore Line was somewhere else. On the fourth morning the Host drew up on the stubble of Sheafton Field, under a tall gold sky with the great teal roof of the tithe barn standing behind the stooks, and a single horse came out to meet it at a walk.
Lady Aldith Ashmore was a spare woman of fifty in a brown dress, with clean hands. She stopped a bowshot off the front rank, sat on a folding stool and took an onion out of her pocket. She peeled it, in no hurry, and ate it, in front of twelve thousand men who had marched eleven days on short commons. Then she looked along the line the way you look along a shelf, and remarked in the soft voice that carries in the Hollow that the left wing had four days and the right had three, and that the Yan horse had started on their own oats on Tuesday. She got up and let it go.
What went across that field was Pressure, the plain weight of a stronger soul, as every lord in the north can lay it on a room. It landed as the second week of the Thin Weeks (the starving end of winter), in the stomach, all at once. They heard it at Sheafton, half a mile off: the whole Host’s bellies turning over together. A captain of the Yellows was seen with his glove in his mouth. All along the front rank great bearded pikemen sat down in the stubble and wept for their mothers’ bread, by name and by loaf, and a Stage VII duke, whom it hardly touched, stood in his stirrups shouting at a host that could no longer hear anything but its own insides.
The barn doors opened behind her. The carts came out, each with a clerk and a bundle of notched sticks, and every man who took a loaf had a stick split in front of him, one half for the barn and one for him. By sundown the Host had stopped being an army and turned into a very large number of customers. There are households in the Midmarch paying it off today.
Lady Aldith never finished another meal. That is the part the Hollow leaves out when it tells the story.
House Ashmore is the least martial house in a martial kingdom and the most quietly dangerous. They hold every sack between the Greenhollow and the treeline, and they know how many bushels each Banner House needs to survive December. The north assumes this comes from good clerks, and they have the best in the world. The clerks are not how Lady Aldith knew about the oats.
Origin of the House
The house counts from Godric the Reeve, steward to a family nobody bothers to name, who kept the tally through a famine that killed his masters, and by the end of it everyone left in the upper Hollow owed him their next year. In a valley of plenty he found he could no longer sit down to dinner in comfort, because he knew where the dinner had come from and who had not had it. His descendants have made a dynasty of that discomfort.
The House on the Crystal

























LayerPlaneThe Ashmore formAether ShellPhysicalOrdinary, well fed in the commons and strangely lean in the lord’s line. Fit for a saddle and not much elseEssence CoreSoulPatient. It weighs for as long as it needs toAttraction LayerFateThe working part. It carries thousands of tiny ties, each one a bargain so small nobody noticed making it, and it looks to a trained eye like a seed-head in the wind
Path. The soul leans Body for a lord who means to ride and Fate for the bonds and the Pressure, heavier on Fate than any other Banner House: Edric reads Body V Mastered, Fate IV Walked 40%, Spirit Studied 10%. Ladders. Aether climbs. Thread stays at Ø, because a Fate road’s Range, Pressure, presence and bonds work at any rung, and that is all the Count is. Grip. None. Things come to them in the Thin Weeks.
The Count of Mouths
In a breath: every sack under the boar carries a grain of Ashmore’s own soul, so everyone who eats it goes on Ashmore’s books, and an Ashmore can feel the whole hungry north as you feel your own stomach.
How it works. Essence is Aether refined in the Crystal and stamped with identity, and the stamp can be small. Every sack out of a barn takes a lead seal from an iron die on the steward’s belt, in a line of Ashmore hands since Godric, and the die presses in a very little of whoever swung it. The tally stick does the rest: one stick split down its length, half to the barn and half to the farmer, a real bargain freely entered. Whoever eats from that sack has taken a share of a bargain, and a bargain is a tie on the Layer, the same kind of thing as a vow. Each tie is as thin as anything can be and fades within a season of the last mouthful. Ashmore grain feeds most of the north, so there are a great many.
That is why a sack under the boar sells a tenth higher in a famine, and why the marches are thick with forged seals. A forged seal is a blind spot, and when Edric has a forger’s sacks weighed in the market square he is finding out where he cannot see.
The forms















































FormWhoWhat it doesWhat it costsThe StackAny Ashmore from wakingLooking at a person or a household, you know how long until they are hungryDinner parties are difficultWhich SackAny Ashmore, by touchWhether the bread came from an Ashmore barn, and which one. The Hollow’s favorite punchline, and the answer is always the one you already gave themYou also know whose it should have beenThe CountWhoever holds the Corn HallThe ties together, felt whole, thinnest where people are running out. The allocation’s real source, and it knows where a host is by what it has started eatingThe Hunger, belowThe Thin WeeksStage IV and upPressure, weighted by Stage gap as all Pressure is, shaped as hunger. It lands hardest on the worst-fed and scarcely touches a man who has just eatenA tenth of the reserve across a field, and it feeds the Hunger for a weekHarvest HomeStage VI and upThe reverse. A company on Ashmore bread feels the best meal of their lives under the ribs for the length of a chargeThey come down hungrierStack-CountDomain, Stage VIII at leastInside it, what is not entered does not feed you: fight Drafts (battle potions that refill the reserve) arrive as water, and rest fills nothingThe caster must be paid up too. Two have held it, and both died thin
What it costs: the Hunger. A tie goes both ways. Whoever holds the Count carries a share of the wanting at the far end of every thread, and food does not touch it. That is why the lords of the fattest country in the north are tall and spare, and why Edric at forty looks like his own clerk. It is also the truth of a habit the north takes for a bargaining trick: an Ashmore will not eat or drink at a table where he is weighing a bargain, because a cup taken is a tie entered on someone else’s books. Edric looks at an offer for as long as it takes the wine to go cold, and he would very much like to drink it.
Its limit. It reads hunger and nothing else. It gives no thoughts and no orders, and no tie has ever moved a man’s arm. It stops at the last sealed sack, so on the Reach, which runs on seal fat and buys grain third after iron and salt, it finds a few thin lines and a lot of white.
Who beats it. Feed your people, which is the whole answer to The Thin Weeks and any sergeant can do it. Buy elsewhere, or bring your own seal. A Stage gap works as it does against any Pressure. A Weaver moving the weather on the harvest will hurt them more than any army. And there is what Hayato Amagiri did: he drew new roads on a map, where grain could go up indigo at no price, with a Yukari witness counting sacks at each end, so that the north could eat without going on anybody’s books. Edric looked at that map until the wine went cold and swore to the one thing that could end him. He has looked faintly amazed ever since.
Physical Appearance and Dress
Stature and coloring. The commons are plump by northern standards and reminded of it. The ruling line is tall and spare, with black or brown hair, long pale faces and a level mouth. Marks. The die callus on the right palm. Voice. Very quiet. “And Ashmore?”
The look at fifty paces. In the hall, the plainest person at any table where they own the bread: black wool with a turned collar, a brown coat edged in pale tape, and the iron die on the belt. The Silver Boar at Edric’s throat, a Rare clasp cast from the first purse of Tenrai silver the house took, is a receipt he wore to every table with a factor at it. In the field the show is the color: bright russet, picked so that anyone across five miles of snow can tell whose horse is coming, on big southern horses at about fifty gold each. Edric has priced Wallbiter plate twice against what the same money buys in seed. The poor cousin has a clean russet scarf, a tally-bundle and an onion.
Lineage Traits
[Trait] The Weighing — Nothing Moves Them, Then Nothing Stops Them

An Ashmore considering a thing cannot be pushed, by bribe or threat, and once it is decided the house commits entirely. Edric’s Untouched Wine is the finished version. Someone who needs an answer before the wine is poured gets none.

Bargain with them in a hurry if you can. Few have managed to arrange it.
[Trait] Hand on Stone — What the Junction Holds

Ashmore oaths are sworn hand flat on the black upright below Ashbury, older than the house, on ground that favors old bargains, and the Oath sets like the stone. It holds one promise cleanly, and two grind.

A promise from an Ashmore is hard to get and impossible to return.
[Trait] Full Weight — The Honest Sack

What they sell is what they say it is, since the tie carries a false measure back as a sour note. Short-weighting takes real intent, as Hollenmark found by one bushel in 592.

That one bushel was an act of war, and everyone involved knows it.
System Metrics



























































PrimaryLeanSignature Sub-StatsWhyVitalityModerateFortitude, ToleranceHunger is good trainingArdencyModeratePenetrationMostly purchasedGnosisHighForecast, AnalysisJanuary, in AugustDexterityModerateEconomyIn the saddle, without wasteHarmonicsLow to ModerateEmpathyIt has not made them kindResilienceModerate to HighOathNobody moves a promise on the stoneTemperingLowYieldThey store and do not refineDominionExceptionalCommand, Pressure, SenseThe one Primary they truly spend on
Wellspring compatibility.

Strongest: Oblation, the bargain at exact par, which favors old bargain-stones like their own. Verdantia, the green pulse, with a worked Well under Barleyford in the Malt Deeps.
Workable: Transference for the few who push the tie, Rebirthine, which is farming, and Terranova for parish reeves.
Against the grain: Benediction, the gift with no count, Oblation’s contrary and a standing Ashmore horror.


























StagesHow they readI to IIIThe Stack, Which Sack, and counting on sticks before lettersIV to VThe Count and The Thin Weeks. First Release: an aura of brown and russet rolling ahead of a horseVIGlory. Harvest Home. Class names run to Tallyman and ReeveVII and upSecond Release, then Stack-Count
Doctrine and Arts
Everything the Hollow needs killed is arranged by contract, usually by not sending someone their grain. When that fails there is the Line: five or six hundred big southern horses in a long ragged charge, lords’ sons in the saddle, coming down on a flank like a landslide of money. It buckled the Keld south flank at the Skeldmere.

























MoveWhat it doesThe Ashmore LineHouse art. It needs a field it can take at speed, and its counter is pikes, setThe Thin WeeksCalled in the soft voiceWhich Sack?The question, asked across a table or a battlefield. It has made generals check their supplyShort MeasureOne man’s tie, pulled on for a breath in melee: he feels empty and his arm is suddenly a long way off. It does nothing to a man who ate elsewhere
Culture
Language. Hollow Common, unhurried, with an unnerving number of idioms about what you have eaten.
Rites.

Sack Day. First market after harvest, rent in coin and a sack, every stick checked against its half.
Stack-Count. The allocation read in the Corn Hall, which has ended more friendships than adultery. The holder fasts through the reading.
The First Stick. A child of the house splits her first tally at six with a farmer’s child, and the two keep the halves for life.
Harvest Home. A week of dancing in the empty barns and Stage brackets on the stubble under the moon, with bad luck to win the first night.
The Receipt. Every midwinter, a very polite one to Hollenmark for an empty pie dish.

Marriage, feud and debt. They marry anyone, with care, as a form of bookkeeping. Thornwall has billed them for clearing the Malt Deeps since the 540s, and Hallenfeld carries their grain under mutual loathing. Ulf Stark said before the war that they would sell to whoever stood at the gate with silver when the snow came, and Edric considered it a fair summary. They took Tenrai silver for twenty years and came over at the Skeldmere.
What the commons get. Fresh bread every day, the only commons in the north to have it, for a tenth to the barn and a day a week to the manor. A clerk knows without asking that the widow on the end strip has nine days of barley left, and whether she gets a tenth off depends on the clerk. In 684 the hedge-workers walked out and there were no pears for two years, the only time anyone has seen an Ashmore surprised.
Limitations and Soul-Costs
[Curse] Never Finished a Meal — What Lady Aldith Ate

Every mouth on the books is a little more hunger for the one holding them, and a great famine can kill a grain lord in a barn full of wheat, with a physician looking on.

Her last entry in the Corn Hall’s book, in a hand you could barely read, was a query about the price of onions.
[Curse] Free Bread — The One Thing They Cannot Count

A gift with no price leaves no stick. Grain handed out at the cart-tail by someone who wants nothing makes a hole in the Count, and a fed people who owe nobody are a people they cannot find.

“He told me my grain could go up the indigo at no price at all,” Edric is reported to have said. “Then I said yes. I would like someone to explain that to me.”
How They Stand Against the Three Paths
Body. A well-fed hitter does not care, so they arrange never to meet him until his wagons have been late for a week. Spirit. A strong one reads the tie straight off them, finds the Hunger behind it, and has a very interesting lever. Fate. Their true rivals. Move a harvest or a frost, and it runs through the Count like a crack through a plate.
Final Definition
House Ashmore keeps the north alive and has never let it forget. They are quiet people with clean hands, hungry all the time on account of everyone else’s dinner, and they stopped twelve thousand men with an onion. They will send you a bill and you will pay, because the only thing worse than owing an Ashmore is having nothing for them to count.
“Which sack?”
