factions,-bloodlines--and--institutions/.title: House Nobody
factions,-bloodlines--and--institutions/.content:
TypeA kingdom of runaways · Catkin, Wolfkin, Bearkin and whoever else arrives · one of the four Central Warlords, unrecognizedOriginThe last days of the Third Eon, when the first runaways came through and the Bearkin declined to move. The law dates from the Assessor’s return of 668 ICFounderNobodySeatBrokencollar, at the foot of the Heap, in the Russet Crown of the UnpaperedAnchorsThe Heap · the Assessor’s return · the witness (ndoto) · the Long Way · the refusal of writingSignatureUnserved: what has no name on it cannot be addressed, and they have all sworn their names awayMaximAshe, “I remain”
The Hearing of the Bell was held at Goodmorrow on the salt road in the autumn of 694, in a tithe barn hung with Accord blue, because a licensed returner named Bart Cray had finally caught someone. He had lost eleven men and forty good collars on the eaves of the Russet Forest that season, and he had a small Catkin called Tiss, in a coat of six colors with a stripe of red dye down her nose, chained to a post. The Accord had sent an examining clerk, and Cray had paid out of his own pocket for a truth-bell from Alabaster, worked to ring true on an oath and crack on a lie, the sort that has hanged bishops. A Scalebond notary sat in to witness. The whole town came, with pies. Tiss was sworn, and she swore very readily, and the clerk asked her who had cut the collars. “Nobody cut them,” she said. The bell rang clear as a morning. He asked who had killed Cray’s men. “Nobody killed them,” she said, and it rang again, sweet and full, and somebody at the back began to laugh. He asked who had taught her to answer so. He asked who her king was, who was hiding the runaways, who had stolen the mules. It rang true at every answer, and by the mules the whole barn was chanting it along with her and beating on the benches, and the bell, a holy object of great age, was ringing without being asked. The clerk turned in despair to the notary, who was gold-scaled and in a very good coat, and who said only that she found the proceeding clarifying.
There was nothing to hold her on. They struck off the chain, and that was when the barn went quiet, because a small gray man had got up from the third bench with a folded paper, walking toward her with a pleasant expression and holding it out. “This is yours, miss, I think,” he said. Tiss put both her hands behind her back. She went out of that barn backward with her hands clasped behind her, and the gray man followed her at a walking pace, smiling, for nine leagues. They say at Greyfang that she went into the ford backward, and that her witness carried her the rest of the way, not touching her hands.
Who They Are
There is no blood in this house, and that is the entire idea of it. House Nobody is anyone who has arrived and spoken. They want the correction never served, the Long Way open, and every last pen gate off its pins. What they hold that everyone needs is forged papers, knife-hands, Bearkin lintels and the plain example of a hole in the law of the world, about the width of one person, that has stayed open for nearly fifty years.
An old line passes on an eye, a grip on one of the soul’s roads, a lean in the stats and an easy road to certain Wellsprings. The Crown’s answer to the obvious question is painted on a wall at Nightveil Hollow, with a drawing.

























What a House givesHouse NobodyThe eyeNobody’sThe gripNobody has oneThe stat leanWhatever you walked in withLens affinitiesAsk your mother, if you can find her
What passes down instead is one sentence, a witness, and a joke with a very sharp edge.
Origin of the House
The people are older than the name. For centuries what they had was a forest, a heap of cut iron at the foot of a stolen fortress, and a rite: a person who arrives speaks her soul-name aloud at the Heap, and whoever is nearest answers Ashe. The fox-spirits call this the Name-Keeping, and the first of them through the Long Way left it behind as the only thing she had to pay with.
Then, in the autumn of 668, Provision Assessor Pell Wickham set up his table in the old sorting yard, and four thousand one hundred people gave their name and their owner as Nobody. He swore to record what was declared, and he sealed it under the Accord’s green seal. What neither he nor the town understood until much later was that an Accord seal is a real oath, sworn by an institution that has spent centuries making sure its seals bear load, and that an oath is small Fate.
The House on the Crystal
The Soul Crystal is the soul, refining Aether (mana) into Essence (spiritual energy). The Attraction Layer is the part that faces Fate, and a person’s Name sits there. Each person keeps the layers of her own people, and the house adds one strange feature to the third.





























LayerCatkinWolfkinBearkinAether ShellThe lie: no aura worth seeing. A reservoir of stored feeling, burst through one stepThe pelt: the Shell runs with the moon and with the packThe weather: vast, slow and not your businessEssence CoreHolds the reservoir and counts it before any actPartly lives in the others. A Wolfkin alone goes “too quiet for too long”Old-growth heavy. Cannot take in a wall that is not thereAttraction LayerIn all three, for anyone who has spoken at the Heap: the Name is held by a witness and no longer reads on the sheet
Path lean. All three peoples lean Body, then Spirit, as a tendency of the untrained soul, and Body is the road most of them read. Fate is the surprise. Without a Work or a blessing it stops at its second rung like anyone’s, and a very old runaway who has kept her Ashe for forty years and walked the road reads Touched, its first. The longest-kept vows reach Drawn, and stop. There are a few hundred of them, and they sit at the long tables with chestnut bread and look like anybody. Classes. Nobody’s Dog at Glory, the first offer. Off the Roll and Nobody Owns This for those who live.
Unserved
A writ, a curse, a brand, a summons or a blessing is a sentence with a name in it. Theirs is blank, by sworn and sealed record of the Guild Accord, and the Accord cannot fix it without admitting a seal can lie.
What it is. Fate reaches along terms: a condition, a prerequisite, a named party. A collar-seal that drops a runaway to her knees at ten leagues, a family curse, a contract’s penalty clause and a summoner’s call all carry a slot for the party concerned. Those who have spoken at the Heap have sworn away what goes in it. They pull no thread to do this. They have made one vow, I remain, and I own nothing written, which spends a soul’s own small share of fate, on top of a clerical error sealed under the most heavily trusted oath in the world. The harder the Accord swears by its own seals, the better it holds.
On the window, the soul’s private report of itself:
[Name: Nobody]
[Owed by: nobody]
[To be served upon: nobody]
[Witness: 1]










































FormFromWhat it doesWhat it costsThe BitAnyoneA collar-bit, sawn neck-iron stamped with a thumb, good for a day’s work. Held in the teeth, it makes a name impossible to call for one breath, and rusts through. Left on an enemy’s table it is a receipt: the House has already been paidA day’s work. Hoard forty and your window reads [Owed: 40 days] and the rest of this page stops applying to youAsheAnyone, at the HeapThe rite. You speak your soul-name, and whoever is nearest answers. You are Nobody now, and that person is your witness for lifeEverything you held on paper. Every deed, title, guild rank, inheritance and debt owed you is goneNobody Home!Stage IV or so, shoutedSets the vow against one incoming addressed working. Brand, seal, curse or summons arrives, finds no party, and falls off the skin like a wet letterA share of reserve and a nosebleed, against anything of real strength. Contest of Resilience Oath and Persistence against whoever sent itNon Est!Stage VIA writ’s old return, “he is not found.” What failed to be delivered goes back to the sender, with the sender’s name on it, and most senders have written their own name very clearlyA heavy bite of reserve. Spoken wrong, it finds the witness insteadNobody Did ItAny sworn NobodyTestimony. Under any oath or truth-bell the sworn truth of a deed is that nobody did it, and it reads true. It hides a name and no other factLose the Ashe and you lie under oath with every answer you have ever given
Domain: Nobody’s Land. A Domain is the territory where a high-Stage practitioner’s own law holds, opened by a Second Release from Stage VIII, and every Domain is a claim on the ground. This one claims there are no claims. Law: nothing here is anyone’s. A knight’s bonded blade stops knowing him, a summoner’s contract lapses and the thing he summoned turns round to look at him, and a sworn company becomes a number of men standing near each other. It takes no power from a fist or a Stage gap, it blanks the holder’s own witness bond with the rest, and it has one famous fault: the holder may never say mine. Fights inside it become an extraordinary shouting match.
The Russet Crown. Somebody has to answer for the muster, and all three of the Crown’s powers (to speak to outsiders, to call the muster, to be blamed) require a party. Whoever wears the rusted band is the one soul in the house with a slot on her, and every working aimed at the Queen of Nobody finds its way to her neck. A Guild Appraisal of the band reads Common Grade, Unique Rarity. Sefa Tuen-zhiv has held it eleven years.
What it costs. It costs exactly what it says. Nobody owes you. A contract binds in neither direction, so they take payment in advance and in coin. You inherit nothing, and hold no land, Guild title or sealed rank. No blessing lands, and bonded gear will not bond. And when you die the Layer goes to Name, as everyone’s does, and yours goes to one person.
Its limit. It stops what is addressed and never what is aimed. A sword needs no paperwork, and “that one, in the coat” has killed a good many of them. Pressure, called the old man here, lands on anyone with knees. A raid by men who do not care about the fee is simply a raid.
Who beats it.

Serve her. The Accord’s correction needs only to be delivered. Put it in a Nobody’s hand, have her take it, and [Name: restored]: every old writ with her name on it comes due that minute. Sealhall keeps a small corps of process-servers, polite and very hard to frighten, who have wrapped papers around pies and love letters. No child in Brokencollar will take a thing from a stranger’s hand, and a correct Nobody takes a parcel off a table with her elbow.
Get her name. A soul-name spoken aloud, with one witness to swear to it, fills the slot long enough for one working to land. Only her ndoto knows it, and her ndoto can be caught. This is why the Scalebond’s list of Harrowgate names, at the posted price, keeps the Queen awake.
Move what it depends on. A real Fate user needs no name, and one lean on the odds makes a strap give. It is ruinously hard and it works.
Fight her. Light for a Catkin, a Lupine alone past a few days or under a Lunar Inversion, and for a Bearkin, go around.

Physical Appearance and Dress
They look like everyone the Accord ever sold: slim pretty Catkin with a second conversation running under the first, dense Wolfkin with kin-cut palms shown open, enormous Bearkin in fir-green wool with a chair they brought themselves. Nearly all of them have a pale band at the neck where the fur has grown in wrong, and they do not cover it.
You can tell how long someone has been free by how loud they are: fur dyed in bars, stripes and handprints, a coat of nineteen colors if you can get it. None of their gear is bonded and all of it was someone else’s. A Nightveil knife-hand wears three Rare pieces off three dead returners, guild marks filed down and her own thumb stamped over them, and she will tell you who she had each from. A new arrival wears a sack and a neck-sore and is the most honored person at the table.
Lineage Traits
The first three are the lineages’ own. The last is the house’s.
[Trait] The Reservoir — Before You Decided (Catkin)

Feeling is stored in muscle and goes off as force through one precise step.
The Emotional Covenant: before an important act, she stands still and counts up what she is carrying.

Nobody in Brokencollar interrupts a Catkin standing still in a doorway.
[Trait] The Pack-Soul — One Gait (Wolfkin)

Enough of them close together think as one, bound palm to cut palm under a full moon.
A Howl sings the dead into the local lines of the earth.

A Wolfkin can tell you how your brother is, by the weight of him, for a fee.
[Trait] Weight-Bound — Some Things Should Stay (Bearkin)

A Bearkin tethers her soul to one mountain or glade and feels what it feels.
Earthen Domains root in the geology and persist through her absence.

They take hits that would end engagements for others, and do not track it.
[Trait] The Witness Line — The Only Family Tree

A witness answers for you for life, and you may answer for others. You know one name above you and however many below.
That chain of people, each holding one or two names, is the house’s whole genealogy, and it exists in no single head.

A child born here is nobody’s until she first answers Ashe for someone else, usually at about nine, usually crying.
System Metrics




































































PrimaryCatkinWolfkinBearkinSignature Sub-StatsVitality−++++++Fortitude · AbsorptionArdency+++++++Alacrity · CompressionGnosis− −− −−Perception · RetentionDexterity+++++++− − −Celerity · Reflex · FeintHarmonics+++++++Synergy · AttunementResilience−+++++Oath · Persistence · HardeningTempering+−−ClarityDominion+−+Sovereignty · Gravity
Every sworn Nobody leans a little further on Resilience Oath and Persistence as the years go on. It is the one lean that comes from the house.

























TierWellspringsCatkinSomnalis · Tenebra · Ignivale. Aurevane and Luminalis are the enemyWolfkinVerdantia · Luminalis · Anima Spirare. Judicium and Fixatio are the enemyBearkinMonolithion · Verdantia · Basilithe. Oneirion, Eidolyn and Hypnather are the enemyThe houseCatharsis (the load set down), Transference (the witness), Penance (going back for the others). Oblivara, the keeping of a name in many hands, is taught as a warning
Doctrine and Arts
The muster is called by Howl. The Catkin go first and you do not see them, then the Wolfkin, and then you turn to retreat to the ford, and there in the ford is a very large Bearkin in an apron.



































MoveWhoWhat it doesBefore You Decided!CatkinThe reservoir goes off through one precise step, and the knife was already in you when you thought about parryingNine-Howl Run!WolfkinA whole pack in one gait, and the distance you were relying on stops existingThe Mountain Has Thought About ItBearkin, slowlyA lifetime of patience finally exhausted, in one blow, some years after you started the argumentWho’s Your King?Anyone, shouted at a sworn levyThe oldest joke in the center. It has no power of any kind, and it starts a good many routsEnumeratedNightveil knife-handsYour ledger’s page sliced out in the night, very clean, and one bit on the spine
Culture
Language. Purrspeech, Moontongue and Urganic Growlscript on every bridge. Nothing is written in the country, and forgers are its most respected artists because they write for export. To keep a list of names here is the one crime for which the town will hang you without a hearing.
Rites.

The Tongs. The Underhill Forge cuts any collar free, on any day. The only price is that you hold the tongs for the next one.
The Bad Day. Someone stops on a bridge and stands shaking at a sound. Nobody remarks on it. Somebody comes and stands next to them, and in a while they go on.
The Saying Over. At a witness’s deathbed she speaks aloud every name she holds, once, to someone she has chosen. It is the only act of inheritance in the country, and it is why people are careful who they sit with.
The Feast of the Assessor. Every autumn, in the sorting yard, a child in a paper hat sits at a table and asks the town its name. The hat is the only paper in the country and is burned at the end.

Who they marry, feud with and owe. They marry whoever they like and no one records it. Midmarch kings who offer the Queen a marriage are always surprised by the reply. No Scalebond is served a drink at the Heap. Some schools of the Violet Peaks run their high roads for love, and the Moss Court keeps a small garden of their dead.
What commoners get. A year and a day free, then one day in seven to the common work, then nothing else ever. It is the only country in the world where the poorest person at the table can tell the Queen she is wrong, and the Queen must then be blamed.
Limitations and Soul-Costs
[Curse] The Second Death — When the Witness Goes
You exist in the record of one head. Below a tenth of reserve a Core begins to fray, names first, and for a Nobody there is no file to read it back from. There are old people on the walkways of Brokencollar who no longer know what they were called, and they answer to Nobody with a great deal of dignity.
[Curse] Owed by Nobody — No Way to Get Ahead
The house can accumulate nothing. Every generation pays its entire income down the Long Way at seventeen gold marks a head and starts again with chestnut bread. The Accord’s accountants have calculated when this ends, and they are in no hurry.
[Curse] Take Nothing From a Stranger — The Habit
They cannot be handed a cup or a child, or a bandage in a fight, without a flinch that good enemies have learned to read. Lovers pass things by setting them down.
How They Stand Against the Three Paths
Body. The ordinary way they die, since a plain sword reads no paper. Spirit. A soul-reader can go past the blank slot and read the name off the Core, and a good one is the most dangerous thing a returner can hire. Fate. Most of Fate’s cheap tricks slide off, and a real pull does not care what you are called. They console themselves that nobody who can do it would work for a returner.
Final Definition
House Nobody is what is left when you take everything a House is and cut it off with a saw: no blood, no land, no paper, no name, nothing passed down but a chair, a witness, and the right answer to a clerk. It costs every one of them whatever they might otherwise have had, and they held a month-long feast about it.
Who’s your king?
Ashe.

factions,-bloodlines--and--institutions/.filePath: Factions, Bloodlines & Institutions/Houses and Bloodlines/The Houses of the Inner World/House Ryu.md
factions,-bloodlines--and--institutions/.title: House Ryu
factions,-bloodlines--and--institutions/.content:
Overview





































TypeAdmiralty house of the Dynasty of Sum-gol · second family of the old empire · keepers of the salt fleetOriginThe Thousand Moorings, the warm coast east of the Holy SeaFounderRyu Bo-gyeong, first Admiral of the Vermilion fleet, by the booksSeatHaeseong, the sea-fortress at the mouth of the salt roadAnchorsThe Two Tides · the books headed held for the Throne · the salt roadSignatureThe Holding (보관 · Bogwan): whatever comes to a Ryu and is not asked for, she may hold, and when the tide turns it pays back twiceMaximThe Tide Pays Twice
He called the Ryu, who sent a superb letter. It is the best-known line of correspondence in the South, and you can buy it on a tea towel at Geumpo. On the first day of autumn in 602, while the rest of the Empire was failing to answer the Emperor Rokju from the square at Sum-gol, a Ryu courier in sea-green silk came up the Balcony stair with a lacquer tube, and read it aloud, as custom required. It took about as long as a good meal. It opens by recalling, with tears, the first voyage of the Vermilion fleet. It lists every ship, by name and tonnage, as a thing belonging absolutely to the Throne. It expresses a grief that no words could equal at the thought of the Emperor’s present difficulties. It gives the state of the tides, which were unfavorable, and it says of the Thousand Moorings that they remain, as they have always remained, in the hand of Your Majesty, which is at present at some distance. Rokju Mahuo, who had just lost an empire and a stag, is said to have listened to the end with an expression of real gratitude, and to have asked whether the fleet would be coming, and it was only when the courier bowed and started down the stair that anyone at all noticed that the letter had not said.
Nobody has ever found a sentence in it that says no. Scholars have tried for a hundred years. The Ryu have sent another each autumn since, and the coast copies them out in a fair hand for the pleasure of the prose. The ships, the harbor dues and the salt fleet all stayed at Haeseong, with no one left to send the revenue to. The Ryu left the Mahuo’s wealth exactly where it sat, and simply stopped forwarding it, and the South has never settled whether that is theft. Those are the family’s own words, more or less, and they would like it noted that the Mahuo have never asked.
Everything that comes into the Inner World by water comes through this house, by their own account, and the account is close to the truth. They hold the harbor dues, the salt tolls and wreck-right on the whole coast. What they want is Sum-gol left empty, the salt road open, and the harbor dues uncontested. Admiral-Lord Ryu Ha-eun sat at the Cedar Enclave and heard Lord Naiser promise to restore the Mahuo royal line, and smiled, and asked a very good question about harbor dues. It is worth knowing why it was such a good question, and that is what the rest of this page is for.
Origin of the House
The Mahou were valley people, and when they came down to the sea they needed somebody who knew which way it went. The family that told them were pilots and salt-carriers at the mouth of the Moorings, Ryu by name, and about the year 300 the first Emperor gave a Ryu Bo-gyeong the fleet he had just won, on terms that have been the whole of the house’s law ever since. It reads, in the Admiralty’s oldest book, that the ships are held for the Throne, that the Admiral shall keep them and use them as his own, and that on the Throne’s asking they shall be rendered, with the increase. It was an ordinary form of words for a steward, and by the time anyone read it carefully the fleet had been ten generations in one family.
The Ryu did not leave at the Calling. They keep the Dynasty’s old governor’s palace on the next rise from their own fortress, swept and aired, with nobody in it. The counting-rooms keep the entire sum in a separate set of books under the heading held for the Throne, correct to the copper and growing, and the last small remittance, which paid the Post’s eastern stations, stopped in the summer. They will show you the heading.
The House on the Crystal
A Soul Crystal is the soul itself, in three layers: the Aether Shell, where Aether (mana) comes in and force goes out; the Essence Core, where it is refined into Essence (spiritual energy); and the Attraction Layer, a soul’s own share of Fate.

























LayerPlaneThe Ryu formAether ShellPhysicalElastic and well kept. Taught from childhood to let a shock run through rather than stop it, and the whole family’s art sits hereEssence CoreSoulSound and rather quiet, and good with figuresAttraction LayerFateNothing to brag of. Their Holding is a kept word, and it spends the soul’s own share and pulls down no thread
Path. They lean to the Body Path: sailors, boarders and fighting-platform officers, with the Admiralty’s clerks taking a slow second road on the Spirit side for the books. A Ryu who talks about Fate is usually selling something.
The grip. A small one, by long habit and the sea, on the Body road. A Ryu child in the fleet has the knack of its first rung, what the fleet calls Muridic, by Flourishing, Stage IV, a couple of Stages before Glory, when any coil can first read Mastery: it shows on the deck and in the hands until Glory reads it as Body I. The Stage ceilings stand exactly as they do for everyone. The house has no eye, and Fate goes unwalked. Most Ryu read Body II, Harmonic, and no higher, and that serves very well.

























Body rung, and the fleet’s wordTypical RyuI · MuridicA midshipman at fifteen, who can hold one thrown punch and has been sick from itII · HarmonicA boarding officer in copper-scaled harness, the backbone of the fleetIII · ResonantShip’s captains, and a Holding that runs across a whole crew in lineIV · LuminousThe Admiral-Lord’s own rank, and rare. Matter by law, with the sea as the matter
The Holding — 보관 · Bogwan
What it is. The family’s one great idea, and it works at every scale from a slap to a treasury. What comes in and is not claimed may be held. The holder gets the use of it while it is held. Then the tide turns and it goes out again, and it goes out double.
How it works, in plain words. Anybody can stop a blow, and it hurts. A Ryu learns on a heaving deck not to stop it. The force of a hit comes into the Shell and, instead of going to break a rib, is sent round: spread through the coat of reinforcement as a long slow swell, the way a shock goes into a bay and starts it rocking. Every bay has a natural rhythm, and scholars say that is why the tide runs so high in some narrow inlets: the water is sloshing at its own time, and each push from the sea comes exactly when it will add to the slosh. A held blow rocks in the Shell at the holder’s own rhythm, a few breaths long in a young officer and much longer in an old one. She feels it as a tide in the chest. The copper at her throat, which every Ryu wears, sweats green along the edges where the Essence is running. It is the fight’s best tell, and the old ones are proud of their verdigris.
On its turn, the swell goes out, through a fist, a boathook or the deck, and that is the part the Admiralty teaches last. A push in time with a swing adds to the swing. She adds her own Essence at the top of the swell and the whole thing comes out at twice what came in. The tide pays twice, and the second payment comes out of her reserve. Nothing is free. All she has bought is a blow she did not have to take now, and one that lands at the moment she picks, inside the limits of the tide.
The forms.









































FormKoreanMeaningWhat it isRipple잔물결 · Janmulgyeol”Small waves”A single light blow held for a breath and paid back. Taught with a slap, at twelveFlood밀물 · Milmul”Flood tide”One real strike, held through two or three breaths. Everyone in a boarding party can do this oneNeap조금 · Jogeum”Neap tide”A holding let out low and slow over minutes instead of all at once, at half the pay. It saves a life, and costs the fightSpring Tide사리 · Sari”Spring tide”Several blows stacked on one swell and paid in one. The whole account comes due at once, and the holder had better have the reserveTidal Wave해일 · Haeil”Tidal wave”At the Luminous rung: not a blow but a ship’s way, a wave, the weight of a ramming junk, held by an Admiral standing at the bow with a line of officers coat to coat behind her
The great form. It works the same way on paper, and this is the part scholars argue about. Under Ryu law a thing that has come to them and has not been asked for may be entered as held, and as long as it is acknowledged every year in proper form, it is lawfully held and the holder has the use of it. The superb letter is the acknowledgment. It has to be sent, and it has to be true, and every Ryu word in it is a small vow, a line on the signer’s own window (the soul’s private report of its numbers). Every year the signer swears that all of this is the Throne’s. And by the oldest clause in the Admiralty’s first book, when the true owner comes and asks in person, it is rendered on that day, with the increase. The clerks have always read that as double.
So every fleet in those harbors is sitting on the largest unpaid account in the South. The money that should have gone to Sum-gol has mostly become ships. Now you see why the harbor dues were a very good question, and why a house that would sooner lose an arm than raise an army has been watching a young man in an olive coat with such close attention.
What it costs. A held account has to be paid. If the reserve is not there when the swell comes round, she defaults, and a default goes out through her: the whole sum, as it would have been, plus what it has gathered, inside the chest. It looks like a fighter who was winning falling over with her nose and ears running. Hold too much too often and the Shell stops settling. Old admirals shake on the turn of the tide, twice a day, and their sons take the wheel.
Its limit. It holds force and nothing else. It works on a blow, a wave or a ram. A slow crush has no impulse to send round, a grapple gives nothing to swing, and a working that goes past the Shell does not touch it. It has to be paid inside its tide, and she can only keep so much rocking at once. Below Spring Tide, one account is all most people can run. Above a certain blow it simply fails, and you have hit a sailor very hard.
Who beats it. Stop hitting her, as the best of the Ryu’s enemies learn to do, and the swell comes round with nowhere useful to go, and she has spent the second payment on the air. Grapple. Use a Spirit art. Or do what the Bad Weather school of the outer Moorings teaches its children: ask. A blow stamped with Essence is still yours, and it knows your voice. Hit a Ryu, and shout for it back, dollyeojwo!, and the account falls due on the spot, out of her rhythm, at a bad moment. It pays you, certainly, but it pays her too, and on the wrong beat half of it stays inside. You have to survive being paid. Plenty of people have thought it over and decided to shout anyway.
Physical Appearance and Dress
Harbor people, thick in the leg and easy in the knee, sunburned to the color of old teak, with salt-cracked hands and a roll to the walk they cannot quite lose on a paved road. Ha-eun is fifty-three, stout and merry, at sea since she was eleven, and the fleet would follow her onto the Sawbacks. They have loud, rolling voices, made to go down the length of a ship in wind, and they laugh with the whole chest. It is said a Haeseong child cannot sleep in the dark.
Sea-green and copper are the colors. Officers wear green silk on the quay and copper-scaled harness on the platform, each scale on its own rivet so it can move with the swell. Copper at the throat is the family’s mark, a plain hammered collar in the poor branches and a worked gorget in the rich. It is left to go green on purpose. A clean bright collar means a new officer. A collar that is sea-green to the clasp means someone has held a great deal and paid it all, and that is the look at fifty paces, and it is the flex. A poor cousin has a loop of copper wire at the neck, tarry cotton and a cook’s temper, and his wire is green too, since he works harder than you do.
Lineage Traits
[Trait] Sea Legs — The Shock Runs Through

Taught, and early. Absorption and Economy run high: the deck moves and the Ryu stays with it.
A Ryu knocked sprawling is a Ryu whose feet are in the right place when she gets up.
Ashore on flat stone they lose a small part of it, and they will complain about the ground.

Their first duel is on a barge. So is their last.
[Trait] Green at the Throat — A Readable Account

A held blow shows in the collar, in the breath, and in how she stands.
Other Ryu can read each other’s accounts across a deck, and call out who has what, and when it falls due. A boarding party is a running argument in numbers.
So can anyone who knows the signs, which is why so many of them have learned to bluff.

A sharp opponent counts the green. A sharper one counts how much she wants you to.
[Trait] The Superb Letter — Courtesy as a Weapon

Fluency and Command, trained on paper. Every Ryu child can write a letter of perfect obedience that gives nothing at all, and it holds up in court.
It is a skill and not a working, and it has moved more silver than any fleet.

“With the greatest respect” is the most dangerous phrase on the coast. The Tide Court has ruled on it twice.
System Metrics

Wellspring compatibility
A Wellspring is one of the sixty types of Aether and the idea a soul tempers itself on. It is a lens and locks nobody out of the rest.






























TierWellspringsWhyNaturalAbython, TransferenceMatching the pressure in place of fighting it, and what one holds, another can use. The Admiralty’s twoEasyOrrenthal, Cymorath, PhreatisMetal that bends under load and keeps its word, the open ways of the wind, and what comes back long afterWorkableOblation, Basilithe, DissolutionThe Gold Mouth’s giving-up, the clean crystal of the Galleries, and salt in water. Oblation is a Wellspring of Fate, the bargain and not the fire, and the smugglers who take it up do not retireAgainst the grainPyraeon, Exuroth, VantabrielA fire-lens on a ship is a bad neighbor. The fleet has stories
On the Stages

























StagesHow a Ryu readsI to III · Murmuring to AscensionSea legs, a first coat, and a lot of being slappedIV to VI · Flourishing to GloryMuridic early, Ripple and Flood, First Release as a green shine over the shoulders and a much longer tide. Class names to do with the job, at GloryVII to IX · Refraction to InvocationSecond Release and Spring Tide. A Domain from VIII is a harbor, and everything in it paysX and up · RealizationTidal Wave, at the Luminous rung. Old admirals who are hard to kill, and shake
Doctrine and Arts
Windward, then rowers. At sea, a Ryu line takes the wind, lets the current do the work and shoots the rowers first. Ashore, the salt road is held by toll-forts every thirty miles and they hire Marrick for anything larger, and they have never fought a land battle they could avoid by raising a price. Hand to hand, the doctrine is to invite a hit you can afford and then be standing in the right place at the turn.















































MoveTongueMeaningWhat it doesBogwan!보관”Held!”Called on the hit. She takes it through the Shell, in a swell, and the copper starts to sweatDu Beon!두 번”Twice!”The turn. The held blow goes out at double, through whatever she is holdingSseolmul!썰물”Ebb Tide!”She gives ground on purpose and draws the opponent’s weight on after her, off his balance, and into the FloodSari!사리”Spring Tide!”Everything on the book, one blow, at the top of the swell. Named for the highest water of the month, and you should not stand on the beachNo Kkeokgi!노 꺾기”Break the Oars!”The marine crossbow drill: rowers first, then the steersman, then discuss termsBissage!비싸게”Dearly!”A boarder’s trick from the Bad Weather school, by way of the Admiralty. She drops the Holding on purpose to take a cut on the arm, because you have overreached
Culture
They speak the coast’s Korean-registered tongue, with a family name first and given names of two parts. Harbor-mothers run the sampans, and thousands live on the water, paying mooring-fee by the lunar month.

The First Letter. At twelve, a Ryu child writes a letter of apology to someone in the family for a thing they do not intend to give back. It is read at table and scored.
The Turn. At each of the day’s two tides the books close, in every house and on every ship, and the family says what is held and what is owing. Sailors do it in a sentence. Children do it with sweets.
Lantern Night. That is every night, since 671, when Deok-sun the net-widow hung a paper lantern on a boathook. The Ryu fined the town for the use of the fishing line, and the town still pays the fine, in mackerel, every year on the day. Both sides enjoy it.
The Drowned Shrine. Each village has one. A crew’s wages left on the book are entered as held, and paid to the widow at double if she comes to the counting-room and asks in person. The Admiralty is quite strict about the in person. Widows come down on the tide in their hundreds, in good clothes, with a sister to hold the baby.

Who they marry, fight and owe. They marry captains, and now and then a Geumpo pilot, when the two guilds can spare a truce from their two-hundredth year of cold war. They dispute the salt toll with the Yan and everything else with Rimward, whose Lambert tariff books are the only ones in the South that match theirs. They owe the Throne. Sailors get a share of the voyage, a place on a good ship and a seat at the Tide Court, with a harbor-mother beside the bench to say who is lying, and what they get in the end is what they can come and ask for.
Limitations and Soul-Costs
[Curse] The Asking — Everything Held Can Be Called
The Holding is worthless if the owner never comes, and it is ruinous if the owner does. Anyone with a true claim can walk in, in person, and ask. In a fight that takes a shout, and in the counting-rooms a very long walk up the Long Mole, in olive. Every year the sum grows, and so does the double of it. No Ryu has ever been sure what happens to a fleet if the house defaults.
[Curse] Default — The Whole Sum, Inside
A swell with no second payment behind it goes out through the holder. Fighters die this way in a good fight they were winning, in front of their crew, and the crew reads the collar afterward and can say to the copper what she was short.
[Curse] Nothing Freely Given — A Family That Cannot Make a Gift
In every word of a Ryu’s life, something is held and something is owed, and they are very bad at the other thing. Love letters from this coast are the most beautiful in the South, and no one receiving one has ever been sure of their position.
How They Stand Against the Three Paths
Body. Their ground, as long as the enemy keeps hitting. A good Body fighter works this out in about three exchanges and starts grappling instead, and a Ryu in a clinch on dry land has a difficult afternoon.
Spirit. Their terror. A working that goes past the Shell finds nothing there to send round, and a Spirit fighter can stand at range and simply wait. They answer with crossbows, and by making sure they are on a ship.
Fate. It moves what a tide depends on: a slipped footing on the turn, a late breath. And a sufficiently bad-tempered Fate user can look at that first book, with that clause in it, and ask himself what holds it up.
Final Definition
House Ryu is the most loyal family in the South, and they will show you the paperwork. They have kept an emperor’s ships in perfect order for a century after the emperor, wearing the proof green at their throats, and every autumn they write to say so. The Mahuo have never asked. Everyone on the coast knows what they would be owed if they did, and the lanterns go up every night regardless, across the water, in a city that cannot sleep in the dark.
The tide pays twice. It pays whoever is standing there.

factions,-bloodlines--and--institutions/.content:
TypeSerpentkin house · physicians, poisoners and notaries · one of the four Central WarlordsOriginThe Dissolution Period of the Second Eon, near the Scorchline WellspringsFounderZseraxil the Coil, ancient guardian of the Anamnesis site called Ancestral Echoes, by spiritual descentSeatCoilspire Den, in the Rose Coils, under the statue of the man they keptAnchorsThe Coiling Memory · the Standing Record · Chronos-Vision · the posted priceSignatureBoth Hands (Zsenn-riss, “the hand that remembers”)MaximIt Has Been Tried
Marshal Quillon Aske was the most wounded man in the center, and he dined out on it. For thirty years he had a set speech for the second bottle, in which he took off his coat in front of the ladies and walked the table through his own body: the Threeways knee, the three ribs from Marl Bridge, the ax at Sedgeford that had opened him from the collarbone to the nipple and that he liked people to touch. In the winter of 688, flush from a good war, he disputed his surgeon’s fee. It was a small sum. She was a narrow person in a coat of plum brocade named Zsevette Ir-riss, who had attended him for nineteen years, and she came to his victory dinner at Kingsbridge with the account in her head, and asked very civilly if she might take his hand. Nobody thought anything of it. They were all quite drunk, and the hall was hung with so many captured banners that the servants had to duck.
“The eleventh of March, 661,” she said. “Threeways, the left knee. Eleven silver.” The left knee went. It bent the way it had bent at Threeways, with no one near it, under a man who had not stood on it wrong in twenty-seven years, and he sat down hard among the sweetmeats with a noise I am told the back tables mistook for a toast. “Marl Bridge, the spring of 664. Nineteen silver, with the fever.” Three ribs stove in under a clean silk shirt. He was still trying to get his breath when she mentioned Sedgeford, and at that point a very large man who had faced everything the Hundred Crowns could send began screaming for his purse, in front of the ladies, because he could see his shirt opening. She stopped there. She had the other hand on him by then, and his body was told, in the same dry voice, that it was this morning, and everything closed. She stayed to dress the sprain. He paid promptly for the rest of his life and never took his coat off at dinner again, and his son Hew, who had never been hurt in any way, and who went on to be a very bad general, was the only member of that family she could not have touched.
Every commander of means has a Scalebond at his bedside and knows the other side has one too. He tends not to think through what it means that she has read every wound he ever took, and has them all by date.
They want the record complete, the scholar-class exemption renewed and everyone’s accounts kept. What they hold that everyone needs is the best surgeons in the world, the best poisons, the only antidotes to the best poisons, and a living memory of what you did. The house has never once agreed to forget anything. It holds that a thing with a price cut into the stair is no secret, and that distinction has got a good many people killed.
Origin of the House
When the realms collapsed in the Dissolution Period, memory-essence came off them in sheets and etched itself into scaled bodies shaped to resist its erosion, and Serpentkin hold that the patience of Zseraxil the Coil runs in them. House Scalebond as a body came later, when the elders of the Rose Coils found the same families asking the same questions every two hundred years and began charging.
The surgery came from the ford. The first long ward at Bothhands was a shed, and it was there that an old notary, reading a dying man’s scars for the sake of his will, discovered that the scars read back. The town took its name from what she did next, with each hand in turn.
The House on the Crystal
The Soul Crystal is the soul, the organ that refines Aether (mana) into Essence (spiritual energy). It has three layers: the Shell toward the world, the Core toward what a thing is, and the Attraction Layer toward Fate. In the Serpentkin all three run through one strange fact, which is that memory lays down as structure. An old Crystal, read with enough skill, looks like sedimentary rock.

























LayerHow it runs in themWhat showsAether ShellKeyed to temperature and kept thin. They call the aura coat the entry and keep it pale goldComfortable at either thermal extreme, dull in betweenEssence CoreHolds the layers, each a period of a life compacted into the substrate. The great elders stop consulting their own memory and begin consulting the world’sA faded violet behind the gold when a layer is openedAttraction LayerA very long list of names, kept without trying. Territories they have practiced in become living archivesTheir word carries oddly far in a court
Path lean. Spirit, then Fate, with almost no Body, as a tendency of the untrained soul, and the hands have to be good all the same. The eye. Chronos-Vision, on waking: past Aetheric events still standing in physical space, the last man’s footwork in the air beside you. It reads and moves nothing. The grip. A slow one on the Fate road, by time alone and never by a Work. Their Fate is read from Level like anyone’s and stops at the second rung: a Scalebond of two centuries reads Touched without having tried, a very old one Drawn, the cap never lifts, and they do not pull. On the rungs. Spirit is the road they climb: stair-wives are Listeners (I), army surgeons Answerers (II), long-ward physicians and memory-weavers Confessors (III), and the eldest of the Record Shepherds (IV), stalled at Realization and content.
Both Hands
Your body remembers everything that ever happened to it, and a Scalebond can remind it: your oldest wound with the left hand, this morning’s health with the right, at the posted price.
How it works. Flesh keeps its accounts. Bone knits thick at an old break, a scar pulls for life, and the blood that has met a sickness once keeps a standing guard against it. The physicians of the long ward call this last the anamnestic response: the second meeting is answered faster and harder than the first, which is why a man who survives the pox never catches it twice, and why a second bee sting can kill someone the first one only annoyed. Anamnesis, the Medium Wellspring of remembrance, teaches a soul that everything keeps its past, and a Serpentkin who tempers on it in the flesh can walk her Essence along that record by skin contact and find the day she wants. She then makes the tissue do again what it did then. The strength of it is the patient’s own. A wound recalled comes from inside, so armor is no use, and the Aether Shell, which is built to stop things arriving from outside, has no one to stop. In the other direction, a fresh injury is told it is still the morning, and for as long as the tissue’s record of this morning is strong, the wound closes.















































FormFromWhat it doesPosted atKeeping AccountsStage IA fingertip on a scar gives the date, the weapon, and how the last man with that wound diedTwo coppersThe TwingeStage IIIOne old hurt at a quarter of its force, for an hourA silver, and you will want a receiptThe Reminder (left hand)Stage VIOne old wound at full force. A healed break breaks again along the same line and a healed fever comes back for its second visitBy the woundThe Recall (right hand)Stage VIA wound under a day old closes, as far as the flesh recalls being whole. A severed hand, held on inside the hour, may takeBy the wound, and double for the second side of a warBoth HandsStage VIIIThe two at once. A surgeon holds a body between what it was and what it is, for interrogation, for a very hard amputation, or so that a man can be reminded of a thing many timesNot posted. AskThe Full AccountElders of the Record, Stage VIII and pastEvery entry in a body, read back at once, in order, aloudSee below
The Full Account is performed about once a century, both hands, skin to skin, with the door shut. Gorvaine the Unanswered, who wrestled a dragon, a serpent and a beast and raised a statue to say so, was brought up the great stair at the end of his conquest by a series of small accurate notes about his family, seeking a physician. The Reading of Gorvaine is performed on the plaza each year with the exact manner of his death, and it takes four hours, because he had a very long career, and children climb on him afterward. The reader who did it first lay still for eleven years, and every wound of that body is a layer in her Crystal for good.
Poison, the second hand’s cousin. A Scalebond compound is rarely one dose. The first cup, the introduction, does nothing a soldier would notice except teach the blood to recognize it, and the second, perhaps from a different cask a month later, is answered by the man’s own body at full fury. Widow’s Rose works so, and the antidote they sell you is often a third cup.
What it costs. What she touches, she keeps. Every wound read back lays down in her own Crystal as a layer, an old physician carries a whole war from the inside, and that is the true reason so many stall at Stage VIII: Transcendence means restructuring, and there is too much in there she cannot bring herself to lose. The patient pays too. A wound recalled to health is filed and owes the body a hunger and a weight within the week, and it stays easier to reopen for anyone who has the date.
Its limit. Skin on skin, which is why a surgeon’s first request is that you take off your gauntlet and why a duelist comes in on a short coiled strike. Only what this body has actually lived, and no stronger than it was, and the patient has by definition survived it once. It takes a breath to find each entry. It does nothing to the dead.
Who beats it. A body with nothing written in it: sheltered young heirs are close to immune, and easy to kill by other means. Letheveil or Absolution, which take an old wound’s memory or its charge away. Negation, since the glyphs Uur and No leave a gap in a Serpentkin’s filing logic and she stands for a moment at a loss. Long measure, a good gauntlet, a mild spring day. And the answer every student of the Coils learns first: do something to her that has never been done before in the recorded history of the art.
Domain: It Has Been Tried. A Domain is the territory where a high-Stage practitioner’s own law holds, opened by a Second Release from Stage VIII. Theirs is passive: the past is present. Every technique used inside is entered as it fires, and its second use meets a holder who has already read it. It compels nothing, and a stranger with something new walks through it like weather.
Physical Appearance and Dress
They are long and narrow, unhurried in every joint, with fine gold scale from brow to heel. The eyes are slitted and do not blink when they read you. The hands are what people remember: long, dry, perfectly steady and cold to the touch on any battlefield. Their voices are soft, exact and dated.
At fifty paces it is the coat. The Accord’s exemption must be renewed in person in a good coat, so they have made the coat the house’s flag: rose and gold brocade over bare scale, cut long and close, a notary’s seal on a chain, a slit at the wrist so the hand comes out clean. A good surgeon’s case is Very Rare work from a Den maker whose mark she will show you whether or not you asked. A poor cousin’s coat has been turned twice, and he will tell you which grandmother’s it was. Their gauntlets lace on the inside of the wrist so they can come off in one motion.
Lineage Traits
[Trait] The Coiling Memory — Sediment in the Soul

Memory imprints accumulate as structural layers in the Crystal and do not degrade.
They can harmonize with the residue of Wellspring states that no longer exist, and they do fine work at damaged sites because they remember what a site used to be.
The layers feed glyph-chains passively, so a Ma-Zo-En chain (Memory, Echo, Lattice) stays live for a century.

The young are told it is like learning you have always known a very long song.
[Trait] Chronos-Vision — The Last Man Beside You

After-images of prior Aetheric events stand in the air for those who can see them.
It reads a body against everyone who has ever stood where it is standing, and that read gets better with age.
At high Stages it reaches the world’s memory, and the seer loses track of her century.

“When did you say that was?” is a point of grammar and it is also the most feared question in the center.
[Trait] Both Extremes — The Unwelcoming Corridor

Aetheric sync holds them comfortable in great heat and great cold alike. Solfatara and the Titan Vohrin’s cold ground are both workable.
One great meal a fortnight, and a hot room and a cold room with a short corridor between at the temperature everyone else likes.

A mild spring day in a shaded field is the nearest thing they have to a natural enemy.
System Metrics

TierWellspringsPrimaryAnamnesis · MirithaneSecondaryPhreatis · Somnalis · Solfatara · Manganthra (a poison and its cure in one arm) · JudiciumDifficultLetheveil · Lethegraal · Nihiloth · Cataclysm, and anything whose law is that the record ends
Doctrine and Arts
The doctrine fits on the stair: know how it went last time, charge for it and sit down. A Scalebond fighter talks throughout, telling you what you are about to do and when you last did it. A name gets said once, clearly, in Common, and then it happens to you.






























MoveMeaningWhat it doesAs Previously (Zsa-Veth)“The same again”A coiled strike with the exact force that settled this same fight two hundred years ago, read off the place and repeated by her own shouldersWhen Did You Say That Was (Ess-Oda Riss)The questionA Coilspeech working on one spoken claim. Every assertion in the tongue must carry when it is true, and the speaker’s own Core gets snagged on the tense of a lieAn Introduction (Riss-Ani)The first cupA scratch, and nothing else for a monthEntered (Zsenn)“Noted”A fingertip on the wrist in the clinch, and one old wound comes back in the hand holding the sword
Culture
Language. Coilspeech, in which a statement that does not say where it sits in time is incomplete. Soul-names run in two parts, and foreigners get a sealed copy of everything as a courtesy.
Rites.

The Coil-Rite. The young meditate in an Anamnesis zone until the Crystal takes its first deep layer, holding the shape of the lineage and no one person’s recollection.
The First Reminder. No one may lay the left hand on a patient until she has done it to herself, with the worst thing that has ever happened to her body, in front of her teacher, who then waits a little while before using the right.
The Reading of Gorvaine. Yearly, on the plaza, on the statue’s steps. Bookies do not take bets on how long it runs, because the Record has the time.

Who they marry, feud with and owe. They marry inside the Coils, by a process closely resembling a merger of archives. The Concord is the standing fight. The Peaks owe an old fine over a bird. No Scalebond is served a drink at the Heap in Brokencollar, because the Record’s list of everyone who ever passed through a Harrowgate pen is for sale. They honor Zsalla Underscale, who was theirs and spoke for the pen-breakers, and see no contradiction in this.
What commoners get. The same bed in the same ward at the same posted price, in no particular order. A dyer and a duke wait side by side at Bothhands, and their full accounts are kept alike.
Limitations and Soul-Costs
[Curse] The Crystal That Will Not Let Go — The Stall at Transcendence
Stage VIII demands genuine change and the Crystal is built to preserve. Most great Scalebond stay there for centuries, regarding the matter as settled by the evidence.
[Curse] Nothing Filed Away — The Physician’s Sediment
Old surgeons wake with other men’s limps, and a bad campaign leaves a young one unable to eat at the fortnight. They have no word for the condition, because in their language to forget it would be tampering.
[Curse] The Category Error — What Has Not Been Done
Clean negation leaves a gap where a backlash ought to be, and a truly novel situation sends her cautious at exactly the moment she needs to move. They lose to amateurs more often than they will tell you, and they can give you the dates.
How They Stand Against the Three Paths
Body. A strong fighter with reach never lets the hands arrive, and has a lifetime of wounds he has survived. Spirit. A skimmer with Letheveil erases what they are made of, yet the Core is where they are strongest. Fate. They read a thread on contact and do not pull, and one lean on the odds, a gauntlet that will not come unlaced, sends the whole patient art past him.
Final Definition
House Scalebond is the people who took the body at its word. They sit at every bedside with your whole history in their cold hands, they will mend you or end you for the same posted price, and they will tell you, once, clearly, that it has been tried. They hold no grudge against you, and they will keep an exact record of any you have earned.
It has been tried.
And cut at the bottom of the great stair, where you will read it on your way down: Your account remains open.
