Perception one step up (Gnosis, the stat of reading and noticing) for about ten minutes: the twitch before a feint, the smell of a working being readiedPoured I to VISenses flood. While it runs, a flash or a loud noise hits twice as hard. After, a splitting headache, and light and noise hurt for hoursThe band: 4 copper at I, 1½ silver at III, 3½ gold at VIEnvironmentalEquilibrium DraughtSteadies the Shell and damps panic. Hands stop shaking and output stops tracking fear, for about an hour. Drunk before duelsPoured I to VOver-damping. While it runs the drinker cannot reach a peak Resonance (the surge a fighter hits when everything aligns). Used for years, feeling itself goes flatThe band: 4 copper at I, 1½ silver at III, 13½ silver at VMaterial-SourcedGrace Fall DraughtHolds a fall. A drop that would break a leg arrives as a hard bruise, so a fighter can leap off a wall into a fightPoured I to VIThe late reckoning. Every fall held inside one dose’s window is stored, not spent. When the window closes, the sum arrives togetherThe band: 4 copper at I, 1½ silver at III, 3½ gold at VISyntheticVeyric SparkwineLowers the cost of starting a working. The refill, by road. What refills a reserve depends on what the reserve is. A Body fighter holds Charge, raw Aether (mana) packed in the Shell, and the refill made for it is a fight Salt: a Salt fraction poured for the belt, which goes down like a burn and leaves a crash of cramps and fever. A Spirit fighter holds Essence (spiritual energy), and the refill made for it is poured Core stock, with the stamping crash and a little of the beast besides. A Fate fighter drinks the same Core stock, because a Fate reserve is Essence too and the Thread is never stored. Nobody pours a fight Draft for the Fate road, and a barber’s curl (below) refills nothing. The Vein Cordial in the table is the plain mineral article any road can drink, at the price in stalled recovery it names.
Two old names. The guilds once called any dry mineral Draft a salt, which is how Windglass and Hillcarry came by the word on their old seals. Since the benches began pouring Salt fractions for the Shell, a counter that says Salt means that and nothing else, and the two older articles are sold as Windglass Snuff and Hillcarry Powder. Neither has ever packed a Shell.
Everyday Drafts

Advancement Drafts
An advancement Draft can supply the floor (the Level a Crystal must reach before it can hold the next Stage, which the Bench calls the hold) and a seed (a borrowed law the Crystal can rebuild itself around). The four rows below stop there, and a practitioner who has not met their Catalyst (the one deed each Stage demands before it will open) can drink the whole case of them and stay where they are, and if they drink their Level past the top of their rank with no Catalyst coming, the pressure that builds in them is Residual Strain, which shows in the room and can crack the Crystal. The bottle that supplies the Catalyst is the breakthrough Draft, further down. These four sell at the licensed counter at the Index price below; on the street they are fought over like treasure and change hands at three to ten times it.













































NameWhat it doesStage gradeThe crash / side effectPriceSource typeHillcarry Powder (old seals read Hillcarry Salts)Raises the Crystal’s clarity and yield across a season. Brings a Welling practitioner to the Ascension floor in a third of the timeIINone at the ration dose. The Guild is careful to state the ration dose1.2 silver a ration doseMaterial-SourcedAscension RationCarries a practitioner to the Flourishing floor (Stage IV) reliably. It does not stop the fracture. It decides where the fracture runsVWhere the fracture runs is the product and the risk at once. Gray-trade Drafts













































NameWhat it doesStage gradeThe crash / side effectPriceSource typeLadder DustPushes a practitioner’s stats above what their Crystal can hold, without a Catalyst. The numbers climb, and for a few weeks it looks like a breakthroughPoured II to VIIICompounding fracture. The Crystal cracks faster each week until the stat collapses or the Threshold is forced through crisis, and whatever fear or hunger was in the Crystal at that moment is built into what comes outTwice the band of the grade above: 3 silver for grade II, 7 gold for grade VSyntheticSpawnbloodBlood rendered from Well-spawn (creatures born out of a Well) by unlicensed houses. A savage surge of strength and reserve, graded by the depth of the Well it came fromII to IXThe Well comes with it. Cravings, dreams of the Well, a stain of its color in the aura. Used long enough, the drinker cannot tell which wants are their ownHalf the band: 18 copper at III, 1¾ gold at VI, 45 gold at IXCreature-SourcedThreshold Reversal DraughtStruck from the Index and illegal everywhere. Sold as Vein Cordial, Red Seal or any clear fight Draft, under a forged sealClaims any gradeDoes nothing, which a fighter learns mid-fight. Some batches are cut with quicksilver or lead and kill slowlyA little under the real thingSynthetic, in name
Essence Drafts and the bought Stage
Everything above works on the belt. This part works on the ladder, and it is why a rich man’s son is stronger than you at nineteen.
Tempering melts the Soul Crystal down and rebuilds each layer. Every pass tempers each layer in its own coin: the Shell packs tighter and holds more raw Charge, the Core’s Essence is refined and made stronger, and the Layer’s claim firms. The body comes out of it gaining Traits. A practitioner can do this on rich ground for years, or by hard fighting, or at speed on a course of Essence Drafts, and most of those are rendered from monster cores. A monster’s core is in a way its Soul Crystal, worth more the stronger the monster, and a hall’s whole year turns on what its crews bring up (the prices are in Monster Cores). A course runs a dose every few days up to the melt. Level climbs on the window (the soul reporting its numbers to its owner, unseen by anyone else) afterward, and a poor neighbor who did it on the hill gets the same lines in four times the years.













































NameWhat it doesStage gradeThe crash / side effectPriceSource typeEssence Draft (core lot)Rendered from a monster’s core and taken as a course. Feeds tempering directly: Essence refines, the body gains, Level climbs. The bottle carries the beast’s Grade on the sealPoured I to X, by the strength of the coreIdentity Contamination. The beast’s appetites and habits come with it, a little per dose, and an Essence Core that takes in enough can no longer say which convictions are its own. Serious houses keep a tally of doses, and every other house keeps a story about someone who growlsFive times the band a dose: 20 copper at I, 22½ silver at IV, 50 gold at VII, 450 gold at IX, 1,350 gold at XCreature-SourcedVein EssenceThe same feeding off high-density minerals. About half the effect per dose, with no stranger in itPoured I to VIINone worth the name, which is why cautious families and the Lamp-Wardens’ daughters take it, and why they are overtakenTwice the band a dose: 8 copper at I, 9 silver at IV, 20 gold at VIIMaterial-SourcedHarmonizing DraughtLocks the Shell to one named Wellspring, with the Attraction Layer holding the tie, the same result as a sitting at its Core or a school’s rite. It lands small, as any new harmonization does, and only years of mastery at the Wellspring’s home Path bring it up to double, half again at most away from itPoured III to VIIIThe ground’s stamp. The drinker takes the Well’s habits with its law: dreams of it, a color at the edge of the aura, a taste for going backFifty times the band: 75 silver at III, 175 gold at VI, 1,500 gold at VIIIEnvironmentalWaking DraftOpens a sealed Crystal in someone who has never woken, with no teacher and no seven years of study. The window opens out with Essence and Stage I, and no class yet. The rich buy it for their children, and commoners sell themselves into guild debt for itUnwoken onlyIt often kills or warps the child. The Crystal goes to the melt with nothing trained around it, and whatever it was feeling at that moment is built into what comes out. A rich family’s physician stands by the bed, and that is all the rich family gets for the extra money60 to 120 goldCreature-Sourced
The raw core. A core can be swallowed or broken raw, with no alchemist’s fee, and it gives everything at once. Most who try it die, and a good share of the rest come out wrong. The few who come out whole are why it keeps happening, and a commoner standing in a lord’s county with a big core in his fist and nothing left to lose is the most frightening sight that lord will ever see.
Stock, layer and lens
A buyer who asks what grade a bottle is has asked half the question. Tempering melts each layer of the soul and rebuilds it around the Wellspring that soul has based itself on (its lens, as The Three Paths has it), so two more things decide what a course does: what the stock ran on, and which layer it reaches.
The lens: matching stock tempers cleanly. Every stone ran on a Wellspring, and an honest seal says which. A Pyreveil duelist on a course of Pyreveil stock melts cleanly, because what goes in already agrees with what her soul is built around. Foreign stock tempers just as far and leaves more behind, adding carry over and above what the washings left: the same Pyreveil duelist on a Greater Wolf course (a Transference stone) comes out as strong, and rather fonder of her company than she was. Stock from one of her own lens’s Contraries fights the melt all the way down, and a serious house will refuse to pour it for her. This is why a sworn company buys wolf and a sect with a house Wellspring keeps its own hunting ground.
The layer: Sulfur, Salt and Mercury. The bench’s three principles (see Alchemetrica) answer to the three layers, and the Parting can split a lot along them.

































StockPrincipleReachesWhere it comes fromWho wants itCore stockSulfurThe Essence Core: identity, Traits, reserveAny monster’s stone, which is mostly Core; a Spirit monster’s stone is richest in it. A plain course is thisEveryone, and Spirit Path fighters above allSalt fractionSaltThe Aether Shell: what it can take in and drive outThe white ash of a stone’s Parting, poured apart at extra cost, heaviest by far from a Body monster’s stone, whose packed Charge set into it in life, and Vein Essence, which is mineral Salt from end to end and so has no stranger in itBody Path fighters, and anyone whose Shell has fallen behind a run of plain coursesShaved LayerMercuryThe Attraction LayerAlmost no lawful source. An ordinary beast’s Layer never thickens and is not in the stone; only the rarest monster, one that has learned to turn luck on its hunters, grows a thin skin of Layer on its stone, and no bench can tell that skin from Layer shaved off a dead practitioner’s Crystal by a dresser, so both trade in the same back roomsThe black market, and Alchemarchs at the end of their lives
The black-market Fate reagent. Dressers sell the shavings in twists of waxed paper, and the street calls them barber’s curl. A curl moves no rung, because Fate Mastery is not for sale: it climbs with Level like any road, and stops at the second rung for anyone without a Work of their blood or a blessing to lift it. What it gives is a season of having more share of fate than you were born with, in which your vows bite harder, your luck goes strange and strangers keep meeting you. It also carries the dead owner’s bonds, and a good many drinkers have been surprised by a creditor. It is the worst of the Grade IV crime in the smallest parcel, and it is the only stock from which a Fate Essence Draft has ever been poured.
What the bottle does not buy. A course feeds the melt and lifts Level, slowly and with a stranger in every dose, and a breakthrough bottle opens a ceiling. Mastery, the rung at which a soul works its own road, has its top set by the Stage and is read from the Level lived under it. So the heir who has bought his way to Stage VII on bottled Catalysts, faster than his Level could follow, is Overgrown: his power spills, lamps lean toward him, his Mastery reads low and no Release will come, until his Level reaches what the Stage holds. He has no Path, either, since a Path is the layer a soul has learned to lean on and nothing about learning to lean comes in a bottle. He is the person on the sheet with the very high numbers, about to find out what they are for.
Buying a Stage
A breakthrough Draft supplies the Catalyst in liquid form. The Crystal goes to the melt on schedule and the Stage is real, on every instrument, for good. A bought Stage opens the door and no more. It has no Release (the named, staged power-up a fighter calls aloud) until one is found and mastered by fighting, and no Level comes with it, since Level moves by hard and real work done, danger overcome above all. A buyer whose Level sits under the bought Stage’s hold stands Overgrown until it catches up. Sects teach what money cannot buy, which is why dukes’ sons still scrub floors at mountain gates. On the sheet it reads as high ceilings and a thin skill column, and anyone who has worked a bracket can see it from the rope.
The bottle is poured for the road. Each Stage asks one thing of a soul, and each road meets it in its own way, so a breakthrough Draft is made for the layer the buyer leans on. A Body buyer’s is Salt-based, poured from Body stones and vein stock, and it works on the Shell and the flesh. A Spirit buyer’s is poured on Core stock and works on the self. A Fate buyer’s needs the Layer reagent, which has almost no lawful source, so it is the dearest of the three by a long way and the most criminal. A soul on two roads buys for the road it leads on. The prices below are the Body and Spirit article at the licensed counter, and a Fate bottle is quoted in a back room, if at all.







































































Carries you toStageThe Stage bought outright, course and bottleWho is buyingIIWelling20 goldA prosperous shopkeeper, once, with a loanIIIAscension60 goldMerchants and country gentry, for the eldestIVFlourishing180 goldMerchant families, one child at a timeVSplintering540 goldRich guild halls, for a hand they have stakedVIGlory1,600 goldGreat houses. A clerk’s working life, the first truly ruinous price on the ladderVIIRefraction5,000 goldGreat houses, for an heirVIIITranscendence15,000 goldCrowns and great sectsIXInvocation45,000 goldCrowns, and rarelyXRealization135,000 gold, on the rare occasion one is pricedNobody buys these. They are given as dowries and held as hostagesXI and upNo shelf and no priceA vault, a grave, or the belly of an ambitious second son
The price is about five hundred times the band for the Stage it carries you to, threefold a Stage like everything else on this page (What Things Cost has the same rows). The twelve-dose course is about an eighth of it and the bottle is the rest, and on the street it all runs three to ten times that. From VI up the stock is Crystal Draw and the seed is a stranger’s law, with everything that means. The wealthy are stronger because they are wealthy, the great houses hoard the top Drafts, and the poor rise by dungeon luck, guild patronage and blessings. A blessing can turn the same key, and a great giver spends almost nothing to do it.
The two at the top
The Dead Man’s Cordial. A Crystal cut from a dead practitioner and rendered makes the strongest Draft of all. It sells as a monster-core lot at several times the price, its buyers do not ask, and it is the worst crime in every realm and the most profitable. A clerk who says the name at a counter is either a fool or an Enforcement man.
The Fate Essence Draft. A Master Work, which is to say a piece that does what its Grade and material should not be able to, made once at the end of a lifetime, always Unique or Mythic, and named. It bends the Plane of Fate (the control of Attraction Force and Obsession Force, and of what the odds are allowed to do) for whoever drinks it, it is extremely hard to make, and there is no price. Its account is in Alchemetrica and Master Works.
Counterfeits
Counterfeits are common and sometimes deadly. Chalkwater is the cheapest. Worse are the real Drafts sold a grade high (a grade-II Cordial with a grade-IV seal, which does too little) and the real Drafts sold a grade low (which does too much and puts the buyer in the street with a scalded Shell). Spoiled stock relabeled with a fresh date is the most common killer of all.

Check the seal, tilt the sediment, smell the cork, and buy from someone you can find again. Licensed stock carries an excise stamp and the pourer’s mark. Neither proves the bottle. Both prove there is a ledger, and a ledger is somebody to hang.

Where they are sold

The kept cities (those whose lamps, wards and warm stones are kept by hired crafts) buy anything: corner apothecaries for the everyday Drafts, licensed houses for the fight and advancement stock, and smugglers in every port for the rest. The trade is licensed, taxed at the gate and smuggled around the tax.
The hunting towns render where the crews come up. Any town with a dungeon on it has a rendering house by the hall, and an Essence Draft bought there costs a third less and has been nearer the beast.
The north trades in kind. A belt of Drafts travels where a wall cannot, so the north ranks the pouring above the cutting, and a vial is paid for in salt, meat, fuel or a season’s labor owed.
The East buys through its sects (the schools and great houses). A disciple draws Drafts against rank and duty; an outsider buys through a sect’s factor, at a sect’s price, or not at all.


Read next: The Ladder and the Draft, for advancement and tempering; Monster Cores, for the stock; Stacking and Spending, for the crash and the cap.
