materials,-alchemy--and--trade/alchemy/t.content:
A Concordant Treatise on Lawful Alchemy, Cacodaemonic Drift, Wellspring Injury, and the Civil Management of Metaphysical Error
They buried Odger Marrable twice, and the first funeral is still the best party Hartle Ferry has ever thrown.
He had been master of the dyers’ company for twenty-eight years. Marrable Red was his, the red that ran the river the color of a split pomegranate every market day and sold as far as Urbis, and he had kept the recipe in his head his whole life out of plain spite and taken it with him. So in the spring of 661 IC his three daughters paid sixty gold to a licensed spagyrist (an alchemist who parts a medicine into its principles and puts them back together) named Damaris Corbie to go and get it. She spent nine weeks in his dye house among his vats and his aprons, working Anamnesis (the Wellspring, one of the sixty governing ideas that shape how a soul uses Aether, that reads the record a thing keeps of its own past) off the residue of forty years, and Mortalis (the Wellspring of passage and the lawful withdrawal of presence) over the body. The town turned out for the procession in company colors, saffron and woad and weld-green, with shawms in front and a cart of free ale behind. At the graveside, with the company treasurer halfway into a eulogy nobody was listening to, Odger Marrable sat up on the bier in his best scarlet gown, complained about the ale, corrected the treasurer’s figures for the year of the flood, named the man his eldest daughter had been climbing out of a window to meet, and dictated the Red to the first clerk who could find a pen. Four hundred people went out of their minds with joy. They carried him home on their shoulders and they carried Damaris Corbie behind him, her aura standing up over Dyers’ Row in long black-violet streamers where the whole street could admire it.
Within the year the company had seated him as master again, a magistrate had taken his signature on a lease, and Corbie had a hall with her name over the door and commissions from three counties. Then came the third summer. Every plum on the Ferry ripened in a week and set no stone that would grow. Dyers who had never met woke from the same dream of the same vat. Dogs would not cross his threshold and the swallows quit the roofs of Dyers’ Row. The Red came out of the vat the color of liver and came off on the skin. And Odger told the story of the abbot’s horse at every dinner, word for word, with the same pause in the same place, and wept when someone pointed this out, because he believed himself whole. When the Accord’s party of four came up the river, Corbie met them at her door and explained the elegance of what she had done, with diagrams and real delight, and later she told her tribunal that reality had not yet understood her. Hartle Ferry buried Odger Marrable for the second time that autumn, at his daughters’ expense, with the same shawms. He asked them not to, in his own voice, all the way to the hole. Nobody has made that red since, and there is still no plum worth eating on the Ferry.
I have carried this book for twenty-two years, and the afternoon I would have you remember is the first one, the ale and the shoulders and the daughters weeping with happiness, because nobody on Dyers’ Row that day was a fool. Every sign was there to be read on the morning of the procession and every one of them is listed below. The Guild issued these pages for whoever has to stand at the graveside with a full cart of ale behind them and say so out loud.

Issued in the style of a Guild Accord doctrinal manuscript for use by magistrates, monastic instructors, licensed spagyrists, battlefield adjudicators, archivists, infirmary-supervisors, relic wardens, and all officers entrusted with the distinction between difficult craft and forbidden transformation.
A civilization that practices alchemy yet lacks a language for its inversions will eventually mistake catastrophe for genius.
This book exists to prevent that stupidity.

The Thesis
All true alchemy participates in the Sevenfold Great Work. Each of the seven stages possesses a lawful expression and a corrupt inversion, and these inversions repeat. They are spiritual and procedural deviations that a trained eye can name in advance, and nothing about them is random. The alchemist, the laboratory, the patient, the institution, and the surrounding territory all record those deviations.

The earlier a corruption is named, the less blood, memory, soil, and sky must be spent correcting it.

The older Hermetic masters wrote in symbols, aphorisms, and witness-testimony, and their language remains indispensable. Yet states, infirmaries, monasteries, and war colleges require an additional grammar: distinctions, thresholds, procedures, signs of contamination, and lawful responses. Heresiology is that grammar.
An eccentric is welcome at this table. The concern is with drift, and with the point at which curiosity ceases to illuminate and begins to consume.
Alchemy in Its Lawful Estate
Alchemy differs from ordinary craft in that it alters significance as well as shape. A lawful alchemical act changes what a thing can mean inside the lattice of reality. A tincture ceases to be a mixture and becomes a carrier of directed correction. An ash ceases to be waste and becomes the readable memory of what was burned away.
The reason this can be done at all is the reason it can go so badly. A Wellspring is an alchemical and a spiritual transformation, and a concept: the governing idea that transforms how a soul uses Aether, as well as a source of power to pull from. There are sixty, fixed and counted, and each is a type of the Aether practitioners pull from the world around them, affecting the Soul Crystal (literally the soul) in its own way. One law works in the vessel and in the one who tends it. A Measurewright (the Guild’s certified assessor of practitioners and workings) reads Judicium as a physical law, a bench reads it as the discernment that parts a charge, and a confessor reads it as what discernment does to a soul that survives it, and each of the three professions considers the other two amateurs. For this treatise all three readings are evidence, because a fault in any one of them turns up in the others.
All serious alchemy operates simultaneously in four theaters.

Material vessels, reagents, temperatures, distillation, ash, salts, vapors, coagulates.
Glyphic inscribed order, naming, containment sequence, lawful syntax.
Aetheric which of the sixty Aethers is at work, resonance, saturation, contamination, ambient field response.
Moral motive, cost-bearing, truthfulness of intent, relation between practitioner and process.

Any system that describes only the first theater is chemistry. Any system that ignores the fourth theater is already in danger.
The Great Work
Calcination · Dissolution · Separation · Conjunction · Fermentation · Distillation · Coagulation.
In the lawful art, these are disciplines imposed upon both matter and maker, and only then procedural phases.

What burns in the vessel burns in the practitioner. What refuses to dissolve in the alembic often refuses to dissolve in the ego. What is falsely joined in compound is often falsely joined in motive.

The Great Work is therefore a method and a judgment.
Six of the seven stages draw on a Wellspring’s law, and the seventh runs on something the soul already carries. This is why a stage perverted counts as an injury: the practitioner has been lying in a language the world is obliged to answer in.





















































Stage of the WorkThe bench’s wordThe law it draws onWhat that law does to the soulCalcinationThe BurningCinerion, the Ash Veil: strong dry heat drives off what is volatile and leaves what is fixedTemperance (the climb of a soul from Stage to Stage) through aftermathDissolutionThe TakingDissolution, the Unbinding Stream: cohesion unraveled into the menstruumTemperance through unbinding, the soul dissolving what no longer serves its architecture (the confessors’ reading)SeparationThe PartingJudicium, the Wellspring of Truth: discernment, the parts told apart and taken apartTemperance through discernment: order, measure and consequenceConjunctionThe WeddingNo Wellspring of its own. It runs on Attraction, how reality, memory and people bind to a soul, and a Conjunction corrupted injures Attraction itself—FermentationThe Rot through the FeedingRebirthine, the Cycle Eternal: breakdown pays for growthTemperance through loss, destruction treated as the first step of reconstruction (the confessors’ reading)DistillationThe stillSublimare, the Rising Breath: parting by boiling point, the spirit risen and returnedTemperance through ascentCoagulationThe SettingCoagulatio, the Returning Stone: a charge sets round one grain, and the grain grows on after the hand is goneTemperance through settling, the scattered self finding its seed (the confessors’ reading)
Calcination and Distillation are bench operations and no soul harmonizes with either as such. A soul harmonizes with Cinerion or Sublimare, and the bench borrows from them.
The three estates
Lawful · transparent in cost, properly anchored, proportionate to the practitioner’s station, and capable of review by peers or superiors.
Liminal · not yet forbidden, but presenting unresolved uncertainty concerning residue, Wellspring strain, psychological displacement, or contamination.
Forbidden · proceeds by concealment, coercive substitution of cost, counterfeit identity, unlawful resurrection claims, synthetic law bypass, or persistent violation of environmental and soul integrity.
The Seven Cacodaemonic Corruptions
Cacodaemonic is the Accord’s word for a stage of the Work that has gone over to its own inversion. On the docks they say a man has gone to the mirror and leave it there. An investigator needs seven words where the docks need one, because each of the seven has a different cure, and the cure for one will feed another.
Calcination Perverted · The Corruption of Conviction
Lawful calcination burns away vanity, inherited falsehood, and the crust of self-certainty. It leaves the practitioner poorer in illusion and richer in humility.

Perverted calcination burns away doubt instead. The practitioner emerges sealed, with nothing clarified. The fire that should have made them corrigible makes them unanswerable.
Such a soul has lost the sentence I may be wrong. What it says in that sentence’s place is: reality has not yet understood me.


Signs Inability to revise theory after contradictory results. Increasingly punitive treatment of assistants, patients, or critics. Reclassification of failed experiments as misunderstood successes. Ritual language of inevitability, chosenness, singular genius, or historical exemption. Hardened resonance: the aura feels dry, angular, and non-responsive to moral appeal.
Common expressions Mortalis practitioners insisting an impression-body (a body shaped to carry a dead person’s trace, which knows their names and is someone else) is the deceased whole person. State alchemists weaponizing purification rites as moral justification for mass erasure. Teachers who turn initiation into obedience cults.
Danger Conviction-corrupted alchemists are often brilliant. They will destroy ten true observations rather than surrender one false certainty.
Corrective Contradiction must be imposed from outside. Peer review, adversarial review, witness-audits, and in severe cases supervised ritual silence. A conviction-corrupted practitioner should never be left alone with a theory they have begun to love more than truth.

Dissolution Perverted · The Corruption of Submission
Lawful dissolution softens the self into relation with a greater law. The practitioner learns permeability without annihilation.
Perverted dissolution occurs when the practitioner dissolves into another will in place of Wellspring truth: a patron, teacher, order, monarch, lover, dead ideal, or institution. This is the corruption of talent without boundary.
Signs · Research produced under visible reluctance yet defended with exhausted loyalty. Habitual use of I had no choice, it was necessary, or someone would have done it anyway. Emotional flattening after acts that should have provoked moral protest. Substitution of access, approval, or belonging for judgment.
Common expressions · The gifted assistant writing what the master wished written. The court scholar engineering taboo procedures in exchange for archive access. The medical savant rationalizing increasingly invasive protocols because the purse is noble, sacred, or politically untouchable.

Danger. Submission-corrupted alchemists become instruments for stronger corruptions in others.
They are how monstrous work acquires clean handwriting.

Corrective · Remove the practitioner from the commanding field. Break patronage, isolate influence, restore deliberative selfhood, and require a written account of what they believed they were surrendering. Without recovered boundary, no higher correction is stable.
Separation Perverted · The Corruption of Non-Commitment
Lawful separation distinguishes the essential from the accidental. It should culminate in judgment and action.
Perverted separation produces a spectator soul: clear-sighted, verbally precise, ethically evasive. The practitioner sees exactly what is wrong and then exempts themselves from consequence by retreating into analysis.
Signs · Perfect diagnosis, absent intervention. Accumulation of notes in place of decisions. Fascination with moral structure coupled to refusal of moral burden. Repeated postponement under the guise of nuance, complexity, or future inquiry. Aura behavior of cool detachment, often mistaken for wisdom.
Common expressions · The archivist who knows a manuscript is dangerous and shelves it without alert. The teacher who recognizes drift in a student and says nothing because the scene is not yet unbearable. The investigator who documents a coming catastrophe more carefully than they obstruct it.

Danger. Non-commitment allows every other corruption to ripen.
Whole regions are lost less often to ignorance than to lucid cowardice.

Corrective · Decision under witness. Once separation has occurred, action must follow. If it does not, the stage has inverted. All practitioners trained in advanced theory should be bound by intervention thresholds, because private conscience alone has a long record of waiting until after lunch.
Conjunction Perverted · The Corruption of Instrumental Union
Lawful conjunction marries what has been truthfully separated.
Perverted conjunction joins things for utility rather than truth. The practitioner ceases to ask whether two elements belong together and asks only whether the union produces power, access, leverage, continuity, pleasure, or political advantage. Conjunction has no Wellspring of its own and runs on Attraction, so this is the one corruption that injures the binding itself, and the people bound by it.
Signs · Forced soul-pairings, coerced bindings, unauthorized grafts. Reagents that only stabilize through suffering, fear, or domination. Relationships treated as metaphysical infrastructure rather than covenant. Research language that calls persons anchors, keys, or fuel vectors. Hybrid compounds whose stability is maintained through continuous suppression.
Common expressions · Counterfeit resurrections assembled from grief, trace, and desire. Marriage of Wellspring signatures without compatible moral or glyphic mediation. Dynastic blood-alchemy that treats lineages as breeding stock for lawful effect.
Instrumental union is the polite face of desecration. It produces useful results quickly, which is why courts, armies, and panicked physicians are especially vulnerable to it.
Every conjunction above minor grade must answer three questions before sanction.
What is being joined?
By what right are they joined?
Who bears the cost if the union refuses the joining?
If the answer to the third question is “someone absent, powerless, dead, or unnamed,” the conjunction is already heretical.
The three questions are also the Grade IV questions (Grade IV being carry rendered from anything that bore a Soul Crystal, a monster’s core being the lawful article and a person’s Crystal the worst crime in every realm), and the register does not ask them. What is joined: a borrowed law and a living Crystal. By what right: an Attribution (the entry by which the Bench, the register’s court, names a product’s source) that names the class and is silent on the source. Who bears the cost if the union refuses the joining: the donor, who is by definition dead, and the recipient, who was not told whose law they were seated to. A course of Essence Drafts (Drafts rendered from monster cores to feed tempering) puts the question a dose at a time, and a breakthrough Draft, which supplies the Catalyst in liquid form and sells the buyer a Stage, puts it all at once.
Every Threshold product (a Draft that carries a soul through the melt between Stages by giving it a seed it did not grow) above T5 (the fifth item Tier) answers the third question with an absent, powerless, dead and unnamed party. The Bench has ruled on all of them. The Bench was never asked this question.
Fermentation Perverted · The Corruption of Catastrophic Germination
Lawful fermentation permits breakdown so that truer life may arise. It is rot in service to transformation.
Perverted fermentation begins to value the rot itself. Crisis becomes laboratory. Ruin becomes methodology. The practitioner starts preserving instability because instability is productive.
Signs · Deliberate prolongation of dangerous states for data yield. Phraseology that romanticizes collapse, plague, grief, war, or mania as generative necessities. Experimental sites where improvement for a few coincides with cumulative contamination for many. Fascination with civil emergencies as research windows. Aetheric weather around the laboratory becoming erratic, feverish, fecund in wrong ways.
Common expressions · Regional activations of a Wellspring site (a place where one type of Aether pools, called a Core in common speech once it is worked) justified by the useful works they complete. Battlefield alchemy that studies trauma as an energy multiplier. Infirmaries that tolerate low-level soul-splintering because the success rate remains politically impressive.

Danger. This corruption is beloved by reformers, visionaries, and progress cults.
It creates the obscene condition in which real good is visibly accomplished by methods that quietly poison the future.
Corrective: no yielded benefit excuses ambient corruption. If the work cannot survive review by timescales longer than triumph, it is not lawful fermentation.

Distillation Perverted · The Corruption of Sanitized Truth
Lawful distillation refines. Perverted distillation strips away context, pain, and moral texture until only technique remains. It is the corruption by which horror becomes procedure and the dead are translated into elegant diagrams.
Signs · Perfectly clean theory built on filthy practice. Reports with exceptional precision and astonishingly absent human cost. Reduction of persons to residue classes without accompanying ethical commentary. Archival habits that privilege reproducibility over reality. Tendency to speak of unbearable acts in tranquil, antiseptic language.
Common expressions · Necromantic manuals whose warnings survive only as footnotes. Medical notes that preserve dosage and erase despair. State dossiers that classify districts as acceptable loss-fields for the sake of doctrinal clarity.

Danger. Sanitized truth is difficult to resist because it sounds sane.
It is often the stage by which a civilization teaches itself to admire the shape of an atrocity.
Corrective: every distillate must be accompanied by provenance, burden, casualty, and contamination record. Where human cost has been removed from the page, the page is suspect. The cleaner the manuscript, the more aggressively it should be interrogated.

Coagulation Perverted · The Corruption of Tyrannous Finality
Lawful coagulation gives durable form to what has been rightly transformed. Perverted coagulation mistakes interim form for absolute completion. It ossifies doctrine, enthrones one method as universal law, and punishes any further refinement as treason.
Signs · Claims that a process, creed, state formula, or salvific compound has ended debate. Demand for obedience to fixed procedure despite altered conditions. Crystallized institutions that convert living law into dead command. Relics, compounds, or state rites that require continuous denial of contrary evidence to remain stable. Soul-pattern of terrible stillness, often felt as oppressive inevitability.
Common expressions · A throne’s purification decrees made permanent after emergency use. Schools that canonize provisional findings into sacred orthodoxy. Practitioners who identify their own perfected state with reality itself.

Danger. Tyrannous finality is how corruption acquires architecture.
Every other inversion can still be argued with. This one builds walls, seals libraries, and calls its fear peace.
Corrective: revision rites at fixed intervals. Any doctrine, formula, relic, or institutional procedure that cannot survive periodic contradiction is embalmed, and stability is the wrong word for it.

Signs by Which Corruption Is Known


Soul signs · the soul records corruption before the hand does
Investigators should privilege resonance reading over testimony where the two diverge. Resonance reading is the Guild’s name for the famous shared art of sensing, the trained read of another person’s Essence (a soul’s own refined share of Aether). The crowds at a Stage bracket (a tournament ladder) call it the nose, a Moto lord kehai, the Marrowkin sounding a man, as a rock face is sounded for a bad seam, and every one of those peoples will tell you the others are doing it wrong. It holds up in a hearing under any of those names.
Tonal hardening under contradiction · sympathetic over-compliance with dominant fields · split between declared belief and actual pulse-pattern · hollow over-coherence, especially after Mortalis or Anamnesis work · oscillation between euphoria and vacancy following apparently successful procedures · memory bleed, dream intrusion, involuntary recurrence imagery · attraction-layer (the part of the Crystal that binds reality, memory and people to the soul) misalignment causing pathological fixation, obsession, or artificial aversion


Bodily signs · the body invents nothing and reports everything
Metallic scent in sweat after non-metallurgic work · ash under fingernails that does not correspond to any burned reagent in the room · nosebleeds coinciding with successful concealment of results · delayed hand tremor after patient contact · mirrored bruising across sternum or wrists after bond work · atypical pupil dilation during glyph recitation · persistent cold patches, especially over the heart and lower throat


Laboratory signs · a laboratory tells the truth the practitioner refuses
Recurrent hairline fractures in vessels used by one specific operator · sigils that “correct themselves” into darker variants over time · soot fall patterns inconsistent with local airflow · residues clustering in the shapes of names, ribs, roots, spirals, or open mouths · repeated spoilage of control compounds near certain benches · instruments sounding a low steady note when no operation is active · notes rewritten in the margins by the same hand in a distinct moral register


Environmental signs · realms and districts begin to remember prolonged error
Discoloration or behavioral irregularity at a Wellspring site · dream convergence among unrelated residents · agricultural inversions, such as premature ripening followed by sterility · local time-slippage, repetition, stalled echoes, or lost intervals · weather taking on ritual rhythm around a single workshop · birds refusing roofs, children reporting the same impossible figure, dogs barking at empty thresholds · celestial or astronomical irregularities following sustained high-order activation


Institutional signs · corruption at civic scale is marked less by smoke than by paperwork
Rising use of sealed exemptions without peer review · concentration of authority in one “indispensable” practitioner · reduction of witness requirements during crisis · disappearance of dissenting notes from archives · relabeling of casualties as acceptable metaphysical attrition · creation of euphemistic categories to avoid the word heresy
When institutions stop naming what they fear, the heresiarch is usually already inside the walls.


Wellsprings Most Frequently Injured
A word on the word. The Sixty are fixed and no hand has ever laid one on or shut one off, so a Measurewright will tell you that a law cannot be hurt and that what this chapter calls injury is a damaged site and a great many damaged Crystals. The confessors will tell you that a principle lied about is a principle wounded, and that the Measurewright should try sleeping near one. The Accord wrote “injury” so that both parties could sign, and the two have been correcting each other’s drafts ever since. What everyone agrees on is what you will find when you get there: a site where that Aether pools gone wrong, and people who took it in gone wrong the same way.



































WellspringCommon corruptionsDoctrineMortalis dissolution, threshold, completion, the lawful withdrawal of presence. It governs passage and keeps nobody in storage. At the bench it is read as the Blacking, the charge gone black in the RotCounterfeit resurrection claims · impression-body confusion · grief-powered commissions · substitution of resemblance for personhoodThe dead may leave traces. The trace is not the soul. Any practitioner who refuses this distinction after demonstration should be placed under Conviction review immediatelyAnamnesis preserves charged records of lived commitment, and more than mere memory. At the bench it is read as the fired pot’s testimony, the residue that says everything a vessel has heldActivation of old traces for practical use · extraction of unfinished work from the dead without context-restoration · regional saturation through repeated retrieval · conflation of remembered purpose with lawful permissionA trace may complete a decision. It does not grant ownership of the dead to the living. The older the trace, the more carefully its completion must be mediatedJudicium order, measure, and consequence. At the bench it is the law Separation draws on, the parts told apart and taken apartMoralization of extermination · transformation of review into domination · reclassification of cruelty as cleansingLaw without mercy becomes burnished sadism. Mercy without law becomes indulgent chaos. Judicium injury is most visible where either side is used to excuse the other’s absenceCatharsis release, purgation, true clearing. At the bench it is read as purgation, the matter giving up its burden in the change of state itselfCompulsory confession rites used as fuel extraction · emotional stripping mistaken for healing · public absolution systems that erase accountability instead of transmuting itNothing is purified by being merely emptied. If what is removed has not been rightly transformed, it returns elsewhere, often in a more venomous formTenebra and allied shadow Wellsprings at the bench, read as the cover-name, the recipe written to hideOften blamed too quickly. Not every hidden process is shadow-corrupted. Yet concealment culture, identity erosion, and oblivion hunger commonly recruit themThe presence of shadow is no proof of heresy. The use of shadow to erase cost, witness, or responsibility often is
Grades of Offense



































GradeWhat it isResponseI · Negligent IrregularityErrors of handling, notation, calibration, containment, or overreach without evidence of concealment or repeated driftCensure, retraining, supervised practice, restitutionII · Liminal DriftPattern of misjudgment, weak boundary, unreviewed innovation, unstable residue, or minor Wellspring strain. Not yet knowingly heretical, but the work has entered dangerous weatherTemporary suspension, field audit, soul-read, laboratory cleansing, mandatory reviewIII · Cacodaemonic InversionOne or more of the Seven Corruptions is visibly active in procedure, motive, and resultConfiscation of work, formal tribunal, warded confinement, supervised correction where possible, proscription if notIV · Heresiarchic PracticeA practitioner teaches, exports, codifies, or politically shields corrupt procedure while understanding its nature sufficiently to know betterBroad interdiction, associate review, archive purge or sealing, coordinated enforcement across jurisdictionsV · Mechanica TrespassThe work bypasses soul-law, lawful glyphic order, or Wellspring integrity through synthetic, counterfeit, or anti-lattice means. At this level the issue has passed alchemical corruption and become civilizational breach. The doctrinal line here is one of kind, where the others are lines of degree. Grades I through IV describe workings that ran lawfully and ended, however badly. A Mechanica working (forbidden working that takes power without lawful consent) cannot end. Sealing closes an operation against the warrant that opened it, and a working with no Authorization has no warrant to close against, so the boundary it opened stays open after the practitioner has gone home. Every other grade leaves a practitioner to be corrected. This one leaves ground that cannot be. A Crystal cut from a dead practitioner to be rendered is filed here and hanged, in every realm, under whichever warrant is waved over itImmediate highest-grade containment, relic seizure, memory quarantine, external review by Accord high authority, erasure of propagation chains where lawful
Nearly everything that crosses a magistrate’s table is Grade I, and most of Grade I is small and human: a hedge-worker (a village’s jobbing worker of small charms) who charged a well charm past what the well could hold, a stall-holder’s fever tincture that was mostly plum, a lamp-warden (a hired keeper of street lamps) whose boy cut a stolen glyph into his mother’s stove. They pay a fine, they complain about the fine, and they are back at work by the market. Grade IV goes the other way. The name is cried by heralds at every market cross in the jurisdiction, the bounty goes up on doors in hand-copied bills, and the minstrels have the verses wrong by the next market, which has on two occasions helped the accused escape.
Investigation and Response

First Entry Protocol. No suspected site is to be entered by a single investigator. The minimum lawful party is four: one resonance-reader, one glyph-scrivener, one material examiner, and one witness-officer or adjudicator.
No assumption of innocence or guilt shall excuse documentation.

On interviewing the practitioner · The first interview should not begin with accusation. Corrupted alchemists are most revealing when invited to explain the elegance of what they have done. Investigators should note what the practitioner refuses to name, who they blame for cost, whether success is defined by truth, efficacy, acclaim, or necessity, and whether contradiction produces grief, anger, or contempt.
On the seizure of texts and relics · Every text must be copied before sealing if safe to do so. Destruction of evidence is laziness wearing moral perfume. Classified as: preservable under ward · preservable under redaction · transmissible only by excerpt · seal-only · destruction-lawful under emergency decree.
Quarantine · Personal (the practitioner isolated from assistants, patrons, and active instruments) · Laboratory (site sealed, residue mapped, ambient field monitored) · District (imposed where Wellspring injury or civic spread is probable).

Where possible, correction outranks execution. The purpose of law is the restoration of intelligible order, and theatrical violence has never yet restored any.
Permitted correctives: supervised contradiction rites · silence fasts · witness-confession under resonance reading · guided dissolution with independent anchor · ethical re-education attached to technical review · removal from patronage structures · long-term service in cleansing and reconstruction.
Execution becomes lawful only where the practitioner remains actively contagious in doctrine or metaphysical effect, and where lesser restraints have failed or are impossible.

Historical Cases for Instruction
I · The Hall of the Unquestioned King · A ruler hardened in private certainty became the living image of Calcination Perverted. His governance was cruel and, worse, metaphysically sealed against contradiction. The intervention took force, and it took more than force: it reintroduced correspondence between his conduct and his own soul-account. Instruction: some political tyrannies are alchemical pathologies embodied in governance. Heresiology is therefore a civic science as well as a laboratory one.
II · The Compelled Author and the Necromantic Manuscript · A talented writer, pulled by access and manipulated through need, produced a technically brilliant but spiritually dangerous architecture for post-Mortalic reconstruction. The warning survived as a footnote. Instruction: a footnote may preserve conscience, but it does not neutralize a weaponized text.
III · The Eastern Commission of Grief · A dead woman’s likeness was reconstructed with terrible fidelity. She spoke, knew names, and believed herself whole enough to console the living. The mourner received something real and something not identical to what he had lost. Instruction: resemblance is not identity. Consolation is not proof. Grief is the patron most likely to mistake precision for resurrection.
IV · The Genesio Activation Sequence · Old traces activated in pursuit of unfinished good. Works were completed. Benefits were undeniable. So too were the accumulating distortions in the pressure of the local Wellspring site and in celestial correspondence. Instruction: Fermentation Perverted often arrives crowned with achievements.
V · The Drift of Tempus · Astronomical deviation followed repeated pressure upon a regional metaphysical field. The sky registered what the operators called tolerable deviation. Instruction: the realm answers what the scholar asks of it, whether or not the scholar understands the scale of the question.
Duties, and the Vows

Monasteries Teach the Great Work as discipline before technique. An unformed soul armed with advanced method is an invitation to elegant catastrophe.
Infirmaries No healing protocol may be judged solely by immediate survival. Memory integrity, soul coherence, dream stability, and delayed contamination must be part of every successful outcome.
Academies To teach transmutation without inversion is to educate disaster.
States Centralizing all high-order alchemy in one patriotic genius buys a future tribunal, and it is sold to you as efficiency.
Archives Redaction is guided survivability, and it should never be mistaken for concealment. Dangerous texts should remain legible to the qualified, and romantic erasure for the sake of the unqualified protects nobody.

The Vows. Let every licensed practitioner swear, before witness and vessel:
I will not call resemblance identity.
I will not join what I would not answer for.
I will not borrow cost from the voiceless.
I will not make crisis my preferred laboratory.
I will not cleanse my notes of blood that was necessary to their truth.
I will not call what is provisional final.
I will submit my greatest work to contradiction before I submit it to power.
These vows make review possible, and nobody has yet been made a saint by them.
What the Vows are, mechanically
The Concordant register calls them an oath. The Standing Index would call them Votia (working bought with a vow), and both are correct.
A vow is small Fate (the Plane that governs Attraction Force, Obsession Force and what reality is obliged to allow), and anyone may make one. It declares a permanent restriction, the Essence Core (the Crystal’s inner layer, holding identity, memory and Traits) adopts it as a standing law, and the swearer’s window (the soul reporting its numbers to its owner, unseen by anyone else) shows the terms from then on. Tempering Coherence, the Sub-Stat, measures the alignment between a practitioner’s stated law and their lived behavior, and Coherence is the structural prerequisite for Threshold eligibility. A licensed practitioner who keeps these seven is therefore buying Coherence with conduct, which is why the orders and the poor swear more of them than the great houses do.

And a vow broken is a Shear Break, and it lands at once. The Core has been running a law the practitioner has now denied, and the law does not negotiate its own withdrawal.
Which changes what the Vows are for. They were framed as a discipline and they function as an instrument. A sworn practitioner in drift is producing a falling Coherence reading before they have concealed anything, altered a note, or lied to a single investigator. The soul signs precede the hand because the vow is what the soul is failing at.
The investigator’s practical consequence: ask which vows the practitioner swore and to whom, and read the Coherence before the interview rather than after. Corrupted practitioners are most revealing when invited to explain the elegance of what they have done. They are most legible before they open their mouths.

Final Admonition
Ambition can be tutored. The oldest error in alchemy is the belief that success exempts the practitioner from interpretation.

A result is never self-explanatory. Every result must answer the old questions.
What did it cost. Who paid. What law was obeyed. What law was bent.
What part of the practitioner became easier to live with after the act. What part became harder to see.

When those questions stop being asked, the work grows no freer and becomes invisible to itself. That is the hour in which corruption flowers quickest.
Darkness in alchemy can be honest, because some vessels must be blackened before they can carry light. Severity can be honest, because some truths require incision. Concealment can be honest as well, because some things must be warded until the world is less stupid.

Yet when alchemy begins to love opacity, force, certainty, usefulness, and finality more than truth, it leaves the Great Work and enters its mirror.
The mirror is always polished. The mirror is always persuasive. The mirror usually produces results.
The mirror is where realms go to forget what they have done.

Appendix I · Quick Diagnostic Table





























































CorruptionLawful stageFalse promiseCommon excusePrimary civic riskConvictionCalcinationPerfect certainty”I alone understand”Purifying tyrannySubmissionDissolutionBelonging through obedience”I had no choice”Weaponized talentNon-CommitmentSeparationInnocence through distance”It is complicated”Preventable catastropheInstrumental UnionConjunctionPower through joining”The result justifies it”Desecrative synthesisCatastrophic GerminationFermentationGood born from ruin”Look at what it accomplished”Regional corruptionSanitized TruthDistillationClean theory without burden”I am only recording facts”Administrative atrocityTyrannous FinalityCoagulationPeace through fixed form”The matter is settled”Institutional ossification
Appendix II · Field questions for investigators
What stage did the practitioner believe they were in? Which corruption best explains the motive, not only the method? Where has cost been displaced? Who benefits immediately? Who pays later? What in the environment has begun to remember the act? Is the work being hidden, romanticized, bureaucratized, or canonized? If repeated for ten years, what would this do to the district, the institution, and the sky?
Appendix III · Marginal maxim

Better an interrupted experiment than a perfected lie.
Better a sealed archive than a celebrated plague.
Better a wounded conscience than a stainless report built over the dead.
For the lawful alchemist may fail and remain lawful.


Read next: Alchemetrica, for the lawful work; Mechanica, for the worst of it; The Sixty Wellsprings, for what the drift is drifting from.

materials,-alchemy--and--trade/alchemy/t.title: The Real Alchemy
materials,-alchemy--and--trade/alchemy/t.content:
What the laboratory did, from the fourteenth century to the end of the nineteenth, with the figures the sources give. An out-of-world reference page.
In 1810 the British warship HMS Triumph, at Cadiz with a cargo of mercury aboard, sprang the worst kind of leak there is. The metal got loose below decks. Within three weeks the men’s gums had swelled and their mouths were running with spit, and about two hundred of the 587 aboard fell ill. The animals aboard died. Coins and watches came up silvered, the ship’s small change plated by the air everyone was breathing, and you could have drawn the disease on a plan of the berths: the men under the forecastle got off with sore gums, and of those who berthed below, the midshipmen came off lightest, because their duties kept them on deck. Nobody smelled a thing, because mercury vapor has no smell. Most of the salivated men were back aboard after sixteen to twenty-seven days ashore, to a ship poisoned with a metal the physicians of the age were prescribing by the ounce.
That is the real trade, and nothing anyone has invented for it is louder. Isaac Newton and his assistant sat up on alternate nights for six weeks every spring and six more every autumn, feeding a fire that scarcely went out, and when his dated experiments stopped he stood, by his own plan, at least ten steps short of the stone. Herman Boerhaave distilled the same mercury five hundred times, broke retorts along the way, and got no gold for it. In 1658, with antimony ninety-two years under the ban of the Paris Faculty of Medicine, the physician Vallot gave Louis XIV emetic wine at Calais and the king got up cured, after which the Parlement of Paris needed eight more years to lift the ban. An Edinburgh chemist named Stewart broke a vessel of fuming nitric acid in 1863, within hours he and his assistant could hardly breathe, and both of them died. And in a modern laboratory, working from a recipe in George Starkey’s notebook, Lawrence Principe came in one morning and found a metallic tree standing in his sealed flask.
Every one of those figures is in the entries below, with its source and its fault. They are here so that a WOTR bench can be as filthy and as dangerous as the real one, and louder, because on a WOTR bench the principles the real alchemists only believed in are true.
Alchemy on the page rests on three sources, read in order. The Alchemical Index says what exists. Alchemetrica says what the discipline believes. This page says what the real trade did at the bench. The operations were genuine laboratory procedure. The furnaces were tended for weeks, sometimes months. The vessels were luted with dung and clay, and the cover-names were written to hide. Anything invented about process, apparatus or reagent behavior is checked here before it reaches the page. Every entry gives the real practice with its figures and its sources, then the way it failed, then one or two lines on where WOTR already carries it. Where WOTR has no counterpart, the entry says so, and whatever is built there is WOTR’s own.
Reading the entries. Figures are as the sources give them. Metric conversions are standard arithmetic. A claim confirmed from one source only is marked (single source). Sources are named by author and year and listed in full at the foot of the page. The In WOTR lines speak of the bench of the Dark Ages, the age that opens in 690 IC, where everything built and carried stays medieval. The modern figures are here so the reader knows what the bench is really doing, and a Measurewright (the Guild’s certified assessor) or a high-Stage practitioner may know them through the Aether, but nobody in that world can buy the instrument that reads them.
The Bench and the Sixty
The real alchemists were wrong about the world and right about the bench. WOTR keeps their bench and makes them right about the world, and that is the one large difference between every entry below and the page you would write from it.
The law. A Wellspring is an alchemical and a spiritual transformation, and a concept. It can be seen as a source of power to pull from, and it is more the governing idea that transforms how a soul uses Aether, a lens on magic already potent. There are sixty, fixed and counted. Practitioners pull Aether, the raw stuff of magic, from the environment around them, and each Wellspring is also a type of Aether, affecting the Soul Crystal (literally the soul) in its own way. What the Crystal refines from them is Essence, the share of Aether a soul holds and spends. A Wellspring’s effect reaches double only with years of mastery at its home Path, and half again at most away from it. So a Wellspring does in WOTR what Sulfur, Mercury and the stages of the Great Work were only supposed to do at the real bench: one law runs in the fire, in the vessel and in the person tending them. A Wellspring also has sites where its Aether pools, which common speech calls Cores, mostly in dungeons, and that is ground and its keepers, a separate matter. The physics on each entry is how WOTR’s scholars explain it. Each entry in The Sixty Wellsprings carries an Alchemy line for what it stands for at the bench and a Spirit line for what it does to the soul, and this page follows those lines.
This also leaves an old fight in a state neither side would enjoy. Newman and Principe, below, read alchemy’s images as chemistry in code, against Jung’s reading of them as the soul’s projections, and in the real record the chemists have the better of it. In WOTR the furnace and the soul run on one law, so the chemist and the confessor go on arguing over every deathbed and both of them are reading something that is there.
Bench apprentices in the Four Quarters learn the seven stages of the Work as a counting chant for the bellows, in the Work’s own order:

Burn it, drown it, part it, wed it,
rot it, raise it, set it, dread it.

The eighth verb is their own addition, and the masters have stopped correcting it.
What has standing at the Bench. The Bench of Attribution is the court that keeps the trade’s register, and it files what it can prove. Six Wellsprings are at once Wellspring, cosmic principle and named operation, and four more lend their law to a stage of the Work.













































































This page’s entryThe bench’s wordWellspringWhat it lendsCalcinationThe BurningCinerion, the Ash VeilStage of the Work. Strong dry heat drives off what is volatile and leaves what is fixedSolutionThe TakingDissolution, the Unbinding StreamNamed operation and stage of the Work. Cohesion unraveled into the menstruum (the dissolving liquid)SeparationThe PartingJudicium, the Wellspring of TruthStage of the Work. Discernment: the parts told apart and taken apartPutrefaction and digestion, FermentationThe Rot through the FeedingRebirthine, the Cycle EternalStage of the Work. Breakdown pays for growthConjunctionThe WeddingNone of its ownStage of the Work. It runs on Attraction (how reality, memory and people bind to a soul), and a Conjunction corrupted injures Attraction itselfDistillationDistillationSublimare, the Rising BreathStage of the Work. Parting by boiling point, the spirit risen and returnedSublimationThe RisingSublimatio, the Ascending BreathNamed operation. Elevates without passing through the states betweenCoagulation and congelationThe SettingCoagulatio, the Returning StoneNamed operation and stage of the Work. Gathers what is dispersed round a seed and sets itFixationThe SealingFixatio, the Binding FlameNamed operation. Anchors and sealsNo entry—Transmutatio, the Law of ChangeNamed operation. Re-expresses a thing in another basis, nothing created or lostNo entry—Materia Primordia, the First SubstanceNamed operation. Re-lattices one Essence into another of its own forms
The last two have no entry below because no real bench ever did what they do, though Boerhaave gave it five hundred tries. Calcination and Distillation are bench operations and no soul harmonizes with either as such: a soul harmonizes with Cinerion or Sublimare, and the bench borrows from them.
What the trade says about the rest. The other Wellsprings have no operation filed under their name at the Bench. Every working alchemist has an opinion anyway, and the register of the Sixty gives those opinions marked as the trade’s reading, open to a fight. A WOTR workshop should be having that fight. These are the ones that touch this page.














































































































This page’s entryWellspringThe trade’s readingThe tria prima: SulfurPyreveilThe Sulfur principle at full heat: a fire that stays resident in the body it burnsThe tria prima: MercuryCymorathVolatile Mercury: the spirit that finds its own road up the neck of the stillThe tria prima: SaltPetralonSalt in its fixed office: the foundation that bears the whole vessel and never risesThe degrees of fireIgnivale, AscensioThe first degree, the smallest heat that goes on to pay for itself; and one heat reached by steps, where a fool reaches it at a stroke and loses the glassReading heat by colorPenanceflareThe fire that reports itselfThe water bathNyxialThe Still Bath: self-limiting at the boil, whatever the fire below it doesThe dung bathAnima SpirareThe quickening: the steady blood-warmth of the Bed, in which a charge stays aliveThe athanorPyraeonThe Long Furnace’s fire: slow heat kept for months, with the charge never once flaringThe philosophical eggSomnalis, HypnatherThe sealed egg before it turns; and the Standing, in which nothing may be done and the thing goes on ordering itself in the darkLuteChthonicaThe humble seal: it holds because it touches everythingThe blackingMortalisThe charge gone black in the Rot, at the point where a matter stops holding itself togetherCibationVerdantiaThe Feeding: growth given a little at a time and never all at onceThe metal treeTerranovaThe metal tree in the still flask: a mass that mends by growingThe assay’s blickMirithaneThe flash on the assay button that shows the metal exactly as it isThe assay poundBasilitheThe Standard: the one fixed measure every other weight is read againstThe caput mortuumEclipseronThe dead head read: what stayed behind in the retort tells you what left itThe burst vesselCataclysm, SolfataraThe moment a burning charge stops burning and becomes a blast; and the vessel that breathes, fume let off without end so the charge never burstsThe doseContritionA poison survived at its measure, and the body keeps the receiptCover-namesTenebraThe recipe written to hideThe Emerald TabletAbyntheusThe Emerald Principle at the bench, as above, so below: the great scale read off the small vessel
The two bills. Alchemetrica says that what burns in the crucible burns in the one who tends it, and in WOTR that is architecture. A bench worker pays twice. The real bill is all here, in the mercury and the arsenic and the nitrous fume, and it is the same in both worlds. The second bill runs through the Soul Crystal, on the Spirit line of whatever Wellspring the work has been running under, and its law, its signs and its inquisitors are in The Heresiology of Alchemy.
The Operations
Calcination
The practice. A solid was held at strong heat in open air, in a pan, a crucible or a reverberatory, until it fell to a calx. Lemery calcined tin in a wide unglazed earthen pan over a great fire for thirty-six hours, stirring now and then. The same tin in a crucible took four days. The pan spread the metal thin (Lemery 1686). Gold cemented between layers of a salt paste took ten to twelve hours of violent heat, and a red powder fixed on gold leaf took three days in the reverberatory (Newman 2019). Lavoisier held four ounces of mercury just under its boil for twelve days in 1777. Red specks showed on the second day. At the end he had about forty-five grains of red calx, and the air in the vessel had lost about a sixth of its volume (Lavoisier 1777).
The fault. Calcination is slow and its yield is small. The result follows how long the fire was kept, far more than how fierce it was. A calx also changes as it burns: Lemery found that longer calcination of red precipitate lightened it and made it milder.
In WOTR. Alchemetrica’s Burning runs four hours to three days (The Twelve Turnings; Time, and What It Costs). Real calcinations ran from thirty-six hours (Lemery’s tin in a pan) and four days (the same tin in a crucible) to Lavoisier’s twelve days, past the Burning’s upper figure. The law under the Burning is Cinerion’s. The Burning’s smell of hot stone and scorched bone, and the fume not to be breathed, match Lemery’s bench.
Solution
The practice. A solid was taken into a liquid, the menstruum. Newton’s standing routine dissolved his matter in aqua fortis with stibnite and sal ammoniac over heat, then decanted and filtered the liquor and boiled it dry. A heavy calx usually stayed undissolved at the bottom (Newman 2019). Lemery soaked corrosive sublimate in spirit of wine, cold, for six or seven hours. He noted that iron would not go into plain water if it were boiled a month, and went readily once the water carried tartar (Lemery 1686).
The fault. The menstruum decides everything. The wrong one leaves the matter untouched, and an impure stock dissolves into something the worker did not expect.
In WOTR. Alchemetrica’s Taking is the Turning where a workshop learns its stock was not what the seller said. The historical bench met impure stock at the same step. The Taking is the bench’s Dissolution, and Dissolution is at once a Wellspring, a named operation and a stage of the Work.
Separation
The practice. The bench parted what the solution had mixed. It decanted clear liquor off a settled sediment, filtered through a cone of brown paper, precipitated, and washed the precipitate until the washings ran clean. That washing was called edulcoration (Lemery 1686; Newman 2019). Lixiviation drew the fixed salt of a plant. The residue left after distilling was calcined in open fire until the black soot burned off it, and the salt was leached out of the ash with water (Lemery 1686). Precipitation could be slow: Lemery’s silver Tree of Diana, a cold metallic precipitation, stood still in its matrass “in some convenient place” for forty days (Lemery 1686).
The fault. Every step loses matter. Paper holds liquor, washings carry salts away, and a careless decant takes the sediment with it.
In WOTR. Alchemetrica’s Parting is filtration and decanting, slow and unglamorous, where most of a journeyman’s early years are spent. The historical parting was as slow, and it lost matter at every step. The law it draws on is Judicium, discernment, which is why a good parting hand and a good liar-catcher are sometimes the same person.
Putrefaction and digestion
The practice. Matter was sealed in a vessel and held at a steady low heat until it went black and “rotted” (Lemery 1686; Newman 2019). The times are among the best recorded figures in the trade.








































CaseTimeSourceDe natura rerum (1537, attributed to Paracelsus), a charge in the venter equinus40 days, then 40 weeks of feedingWikipedia, “Homunculus”, after NewmanTreatise copied by Newton, the mixture in the philosophical eggblack by day 30, then white, then redNewman 2019Newton’s Praxis, a plan never carried outgreen liquid at day 30, black powder at day 40Newman 2019Philalethes, as read by Newmanthe “doves” rise at about three weeksNewman 2019Lemery, a tincture in horse dung in a double vessela fortnightLemery 1686Fatio’s account of an adept’s medicine, 1690s7 months through 4 putrefactionsNewman 2019
The fault. A sealed digestion gives no reading but its color. The worker waits weeks for a black that may be rot or may be ruin, and the heat under it wanders.
In WOTR. Alchemetrica’s Rot runs three to four and a half turns (six to nine weeks) in the Bed, unopened, and goes black. Real putrefactions reached black in thirty to forty days and ran longer schemes by the month, so the Rot sits on the recorded range. The Alftian Codex’s ferment took three turns in warm dung, forty-two days at fourteen days to the turn, which lands on the real forty-day digestion. The law from the Rot to the Feeding is Rebirthine’s, breakdown paying for growth, and the trade reads the black itself as Mortalis.
Fermentation
The practice. Lemery defined fermentation as a boiling-up raised by spirits forcing their way out of a body, which changes its nature. Fruit, honey, berries, seeds, leaves and flowers could be set to ferment like wine. Dry matter was beaten, wetted, and given a little yeast to hasten it. Distilling the ferment gave a burning spirit (Lemery 1686).
The fault. A ferment runs on its own clock and its own heat. It can foam over, sour, or stall, and a sealed ferment builds gas.
In WOTR. The Alftian Codex draws Furveus’s Mercury as the spirit from the ferment, which is Lemery’s route. The Codex’s seven stages of the Work (Volume the Second) place Fermentation fifth, and the stage draws on Rebirthine.
Distillation
The practice. Heat raised vapor from the charge. The cold of the head or the neck brought it back down as liquid, drop by drop, into a receiver. Lemery distilled balm in a copper still with a tinned head, its joint luted with wet bladder. The fire was of the second degree. He kept it between the second and third degree, because too low a fire would not raise the volatile part. Too high, and the water tasted burned. The trade called that empyreuma. The drops were to come slowly, one after another (Lemery 1686).
The fault. Distillation separates by heat alone, and heat is a blunt blade. Everything volatile at that heat comes over together, and a hot fire scorches the charge.
In WOTR. Alchemetrica’s Distillation separates a signal from noise, and without a Direction glyph it separates every signature present. Lemery’s still had the same failing with no glyph to help it. The law Distillation draws on is Sublimare’s, the spirit risen and returned, and the trade reads the spirit that finds its own road up the neck as Cymorath.
The strong waters
The practice. The bench made its own acids by distillation, and the recipes are exact.

Aqua fortis (nitric acid), literally “strong water.” Lemery charged a luted retort with saltpetre, white-calcined vitriol and dried clay, thirty-two ounces of each, and left a third of the retort empty. He warmed it by degrees. When red clouds passed into the receiver he held that degree fifteen or sixteen hours, then pushed the fire to its extremity until the clouds turned white (Lemery 1686). Assayers used it to part silver from gold (Wikipedia, “Nitric acid”).
Aqua regia (“royal water”). It was first made by dissolving sal ammoniac in aqua fortis, a method in pseudo-Geber’s De inventione veritatis of about 1300. It dissolves gold (Wikipedia, “Aqua regia”) (single source).
Sal ammoniac (ammonium chloride). It is a white crystal raised by sublimation, used as a flux and as the salt that turns aqua fortis into aqua regia (Wikipedia, “Aqua regia”; Newman 2019).
Oil of vitriol (sulfuric acid). Eighteen or twenty hours was not enough. The oil came over only after three days of continuous distilling. Lemery ran one retort of German vitriol three days and three nights. In his remarks on aqua fortis he adds that a fire kept five days and nights would still leave the receiver full of fume (Lemery 1686).
Spirit of salt (hydrochloric acid). Glauber made it from common salt and oil of vitriol. Its by-product, Glauber’s salt, is dated to his discovery about 1625 in one account and to his published process in De natura salium of 1658 in another, and the date is disputed (Wikipedia, “Johann Rudolf Glauber”; Ahonen, DSB).
The fault. Every one of these is made hot and delivered as fume. The luting has to hold for a day or three, and the receiver fills with the thing that kills.

In WOTR. Alchemetrica’s Menstrua carry all five. Strongwater is aqua fortis, down to the saltpetre and vitriol, the day of graduated heat, the red-orange fume, and gold left untouched. Kingswater is aqua regia, Ghostsalt is sal ammoniac, Blackstone Oil is oil of vitriol with its three days, and Salt-spirit is spirit of salt. Copper “eaten alive by Strongwater in under an hour” has no period figure behind it. Real rates turned on the acid’s strength and the metal’s thickness.
Cohobation
The practice. The distillate was poured back on the residue in the vessel and distilled again, over and over, “to open Bodies, or to Volatilize the Spirits” (Lemery 1686; Wikipedia, “Cohobation”). It differs from circulation because the liquor is drawn off each time. Newton digested spirit of wine on a sublimed salt twenty-four hours, then distilled it seven times or more (Newman 2019). Boerhaave carried repetition to its limit. He distilled the same mercury five hundred times, 448 of them in one series, lost weight to broken retorts and cleaning, and got no transmutation (Boerhaave 1730s).
The fault. Modern chemistry finds cohobation does nothing that holding the charge at heat for the same time would not do (Wikipedia, “Cohobation”). Each pass also costs matter and risks the glass.
In WOTR. No counterpart. Alchemetrica names no repeated-return distillation, and the Standing Index’s nine recrystallizations under witness are a different operation.
Circulation
The practice. In a pelican or a sealed double vessel, heat drove vapor up and the cold of the arms brought it back into the charge, without the liquor ever being drawn off. The aim was to refine a spirit or to open a hard body (Lemery 1686; Brunschwig 1500). Rupescissa’s quintessence was wine distilled repeatedly and then circulated in a closed glass for “a long period,” and period recipes rarely give a time (Stewart 2013). In the adept’s menstruum Fatio described, five pounds of matter gave four and a half in the receiver, which stood several days in a cold place before its vapors settled (Newman 2019).
The fault. A closed circulation cannot be tasted, measured or corrected. A crack in the arm ends it, and so does a fire that falters.
In WOTR. Alchemetrica’s circulation in the Returner runs turns or months, the vessel never opened. The Alftian Codex runs Furveus’s spirit in the Returner for most of a month. Both sit inside the recorded order of time.
Sublimation
The practice. A volatile solid was driven up by heat and caught as a solid on the cold upper walls or in the head. For corrosive sublimate, Lemery’s matrass poured red nitrous vapor from its mouth for at least three hours, and the earthy residue at the bottom weighed twenty-eight ounces (Lemery 1686). The Treatise Newton copied sublimed on a mild fire for three days. It left a caput mortuum at the bottom, a cinnabar in the middle and a white sublimate at the top. The product was mixed and sublimed again two or three more times. Newton graded his own sublimations from a candle, to a sand bath, to the naked fire on a fire shovel, to be sure all that could rise had risen (Newman 2019).
The fault. Sublimation leaves a residue and layers its product. A single pass is rarely clean, so the real trade sublimed again and again.
In WOTR. Alchemetrica’s Rising collects on the cold walls of the Riser, and what failed to rise is lost. There is no partial Sublimation. What did not rise stays as a fused mass broken out with a chisel. The historical bench sublimed partially and repeatedly, and its unrisen residue is the period counterpart of that fused mass. Canon names no sublimation outside the Sublimatio operation, whose law elevates a thing without passing through the states between, with no stage at which the working can be inspected or corrected.
Coagulation, congelation and fixation
The practice. Coagulation gave a liquid a body by evaporating it or by mixing two liquors. Congelation was letting a melt set (Lemery 1686). Fixation made a volatile thing stand the fire. Boerhaave took the fire acting through the glass for the cause that fixed his mercury powder. When he then held that powder red-hot for four hours in a retort coated with sand and clay, most of it came over as running mercury, and of seventeen ounces of mercury worked in all, fifteen grains stayed fixed (Boerhaave 1730s).
The fault. A thing “fixed” by one fire may rise again under a hotter one. The word named a result at a stated heat, and the heat was rarely stated.
In WOTR. Alchemetrica’s Coagulation mirrors Coagulatio, and its Setting is the Turning where process becomes object. Lemery’s and Boerhaave’s operations are the physical register those entries name. Coagulatio and Fixatio are both among the six Wellsprings that are also named operations: every Sealing chain on the bench runs under Fixatio’s law, and the Bench files a Fixatio Draft as a Coagulation.
Conjunction
The practice. At the bench, conjunction was the joining of prepared matters in one vessel. Gold was amalgamated with a prepared mercury, or the “Secret’s” ferment went into its menstruum, four ounces to one, between two matrasses sealed mouth to mouth with lute in a sand bath (Newman 2019). The vessel was then sealed and digested for weeks. Principe, working from a recipe in Starkey’s notebook, put the prepared mercury and gold, worked to a buttery lump, into a sealed flask in a heated sand bath, and one morning found a metallic tree grown in it. The report gives no elapsed time (Conniff 2014).
The fault. The danger was pressure in sealed glass. Newton’s notes record his egg-glass breaking when volatile vitriolic salts rose during a digestion (Spargo 2005).
In WOTR. Alchemetrica’s Wedding is fast and decisive, and the Alftian Codex’s Furveus pours the principles in one movement with an Aperture glyph at the neck to let pressure out. Recombination at the historical bench, of metals or of plant principles, was a slow sealed digestion (Lemery: days to a fortnight in dung). The fast Wedding is WOTR’s own. The period danger at the joining was pressure in sealed glass, which is what the Aperture answers. Canon’s own danger at the Wedding is Rupture. Conjunction is the one stage with no Wellspring of its own: it runs on Attraction, and a Conjunction corrupted injures Attraction itself, which the Heresiology treats as the Corruption of Instrumental Union.
Cementation, cupellation and parting
The practice. These were the assayer’s operations. Cementation packed gold plate in layers with a salt paste and held it at violent heat ten to twelve hours to purge its base metals (Lemery 1686). Cupellation needs a porous cup of bone ash. Lead oxide melts at 888 °C and soaks into the cup, leaving the silver or gold bead on top, in a furnace at about 960 to 1,000 °C under an oxidizing draft (Wikipedia, “Cupellation”). The stibnite parting, first set out in the German assaying booklets of the early sixteenth century, drew silver and base metals into sulfides and left the gold (Craddock 2000). The excavated laboratory at Oberstockstall, in Lower Austria, held about three hundred triangular crucibles and about forty scorifiers. It held between sixty and a hundred bone-ash cupels, by differing counts (Martinón-Torres and Rehren).
The fault. Each parting carried a little gold away with it. Cupellation also breathed lead fume into the room.
In WOTR. Alchemetrica’s Reading is the assay before any working, and Weight, Measure and the Standard sets the assay pound so a bead’s mass reads directly as fineness. The Working Vocabulary names the cupel, scorification, litharge, the button and the blick as the assay’s trade words, and Alchemetrica keeps Kingswater at every parting bench. The trade reads the blick as Mirithane. Cementation has no counterpart.
The order of the operations
The practice. No two authors agreed on the list. George Ripley’s Compound of Alchymy (1471) gave twelve gates: calcination, solution, separation, conjunction, putrefaction, congelation, cibation, sublimation, fermentation, exaltation, multiplication and projection (Wikipedia, “Magnum opus”; Newman 1996). Samuel Norton in the sixteenth century gave fourteen (Wikipedia, “Magnum opus”). The seven-stage list that runs from calcination to coagulation circulates in modern writing on spiritual alchemy. No early modern source for that order has been traced.
The fault. A list of operations in a book was a teaching order, and often a cover. It omitted steps and repeated others under new names.
In WOTR. Alchemetrica’s Twelve Turnings echo Ripley’s twelve in number, with cibation as the Feeding. The Alftian Codex’s seven stages of the Work are WOTR’s own list and need no real warrant, and they carry a weight the real lists never could: six of the seven draw on a Wellspring’s law.
The stone
The practice. Every long list of operations pointed at a finished thing. Ripley’s twelve gates close on multiplication and projection (Wikipedia, “Magnum opus”; Newman 1996), and the end of the road was a stone or medicine that a small measure of would carry its virtue into a great deal else. The real record of pursuit is the rest of this page: Newton’s fires, stopped by his own plan at least ten steps short (Newman 2019), and Boerhaave’s five hundred distillations of one mercury with no gold at the end of them (Boerhaave 1730s).
The fault. Nobody on these sources made it. The claims that survive are claims.
In WOTR. The stone has a counterpart, and it works. A Master Work is a piece that does what its Grade and material should not be able to, made once at the end of a lifetime, always Unique or Mythic, and named, and the bench’s own are Drafts. The great one is the Fate Essence Draft, which bottles a share of the Plane of Fate, the control of Attraction Force and Obsession Force and of what the odds are allowed to do. Its account is in Alchemetrica, under Master Works of the Bench. Its real kin is the stone’s reputation: extremely hard, very coveted, the prize of a lifetime, and the reason a great house will pay for decades of a fire nobody may let go out. The real trade’s goal was gold, and WOTR’s money runs the other way. Most of what a WOTR house actually pours is Essence Drafts from monster cores, for which the real bench has no counterpart at all.
The Apparatus and the Fire
The degrees of fire
The practice. Lemery counted four degrees of fire by fuel, not by number (Lemery 1686):

the first, two or three lit coals, the gentlest;
the second, three or four coals, the vessel sensibly warm but bearable under a hand for a while;
the third, enough fire to boil a pot of five or six quarts of water;
the fourth, coals and wood together, the fiercest.
Sand, iron filings and ash made graded beds, each with degrees of its own, and ash was the mildest because it holds little heat. The reverberatory ran hotter than any of them. A “wheel fire” ringed a crucible with live coals for fusion. The Treatise Newton copied set a water-bath digestion at a heat “which you can hardly bear to touch” (Newman 2019).

The fault. A degree measured in coals depends on the coal, the draft and the furnace. Two workshops following one recipe ran two different fires.
In WOTR. Alchemetrica’s Heat says every alchemist judges temperature by flame color, the sound of the charge, and a hand held where a hand should not go. That is Lemery’s method. The conclusion that a written formula never reproduces the product follows from the period practice too. The trade reads the first degree as Ignivale and the climb by degrees as Ascensio, and a practitioner harmonized to either will tell you that he can feel the difference between your third degree and your fourth, and may be right.
Reading heat by color
The practice. Solids begin to glow a dull red at about 450 to 475 °C in a darkened room (Darling 1911). The color tables disagree with each other:
