materials,-alchemy--and--trade/index.title: Materials, Alchemy & Trade
materials,-alchemy--and--trade/index.content:
Mad Dunna Quillon ran Bloodsilver past the harbor searchers of three kingdoms for seventeen years by packing it inside hollowed bars of Chainsalt, because Chainsalt (a bedded salt that refuses Essence, the refined power a practitioner holds and spends) gives an assay fork nothing to ring against, and the fork is what a searcher carries. She was caught by a cook. Off the southern serpentine coast, with the whole crew of the Bold Annis singing under green lanterns, he cracked a salt bar over the stew pot and a slug of bright metal dropped into the fish. He pocketed it, as any cook would. Within the month it had eaten through the pocket, the purse and a good part of his thigh, and he limped up the first quay of the first port he saw and begged the first searcher there to arrest him. They hanged Dunna in a yellow dress at the Accord’s expense, before the largest crowd that harbor has ever held, and she is said to have asked who paid for the rope and what it was graded.

Three registers, one economy. The Ledger says what the world is made of. The Standing Index says what may lawfully be made from it. Hide, Horn and Bone says what was alive first.
A material that scores high on both earns a harder word than good: strategic, and the Accord keeps a register of who owns the seams.
The money runs on cores. A monster’s core is in a way its Soul Crystal, worth more the stronger the monster, and it renders into the Essence Drafts every practitioner with a purse takes to temper. Hunting halls live on it, the great houses hoard the top of it, and the worst crime in every realm is passing off a dead practitioner’s Crystal as one. The Common Drafts has the bottles, and Hide, Horn and Bone has the price at the door.

The Twin Rating

BEARING is what a material does under load. Compression, tension, shear, thermal cycling, abrasion.
Measured on the press. It has nothing whatsoever to do with Essence.
HOLDING is what a material does under Essence. How much it retains, how long, how cleanly it releases, and whether an inscription stays legible to the Continuum (the order of the world that reads a working and answers it) over years rather than weeks.
Measured on the coil (the great brass assay instrument; a practitioner stands inside it to be read, and a sample sits where the practitioner would).

The two do not track each other. Forge-Iron bears magnificently and holds nothing. Gloomhide is spiritually inert and physically superb. Mireclay holds a totem for one night and cannot hold a roof for one hour. A material’s tier says what it can hold; a finished piece also carries a Grade for its power and a Rarity for its scarcity, and those belong to Grade and Rarity.
Resonance names the Wellspring or Wellsprings a substrate is naturally sympathetic to (the Wellsprings are the sixty alchemical and spiritual transformations, each the governing idea that shapes how a soul uses Aether and each a type of Aether as well). Kind names the plane that Wellspring is at home on: Wild, Spirit, Fate or Medium. Domain is the Measurewrights’ column: the branch of natural philosophy their guild files the Wellspring’s behavior under, beneath the Parunic dressing (Parun being the glyph-tongue a working is written in), recorded so that a thermal refractory is not ordered for an electrical duty by a clerk who never went underground. It is often right about how much a substrate will take and never about why; the why is the Wellspring’s idea, and its Operation is on the Sixty. Virtue stands beside all three: matter has virtues, not properties, and a material’s virtue decides which workings it holds well and how it fails. Stone remembers, salt fixes, gold will not corrupt, quicksilver will not keep a shape.

Blank cells in those three columns mean the Ledger is silent, not that the material is inert. An Engraver (the craftsman who cuts a working into a substrate) who fights his substrate pays for it in the lifespan of the inscription.

The Three Registers

      
      
      
      entry, striking, attribution, reservationrules onTHE GROUNDfour quarters, T0 to T9THE MASTER MATERIALLEDGER87 attested materialswhat the world is made ofHIDE, HORN AND BONE20 creature materialswhat was alive firstTHE STANDING INDEX45 entered formulaswhat may lawfully be madeTHE BENCH OFATTRIBUTION

























RegisterCompiled fromWhat it settlesThe Master Material LedgerThe Measurewrights’ survey, the standing Accord T0–T9 list, the coin volume, the Four Ceilings technology history, and the Master Codex alchemical tabEvery material attested anywhere: building stone, structural metal, armor and weapon stock, fabric and thread, Holding substrate, precious metals, and the alchemical formula indexThe Standing IndexThe Bench’s own register, with Provenance Grade, Fidelity and Carry on every rowWhat is lawful in commerce. Nothing in the alchemical economy exists commercially until it is enteredHide, Horn and BoneThe creature-material addendumThe organic input side, from the commonest worked bone in the four quarters to the skeleton of a confirmed World Spirit
What Reading These Registers Teaches
The registers are dry by construction and the pattern only shows at scale.

The world’s whole high-temperature capability rests on two ores in two places. Blacktooth wolfram out of the western tin districts and Ashfast chromite off the southern serpentine belt. The Logistics Division has flagged the dependency in every annual report for nineteen years and nothing has changed.

The most important materials are the dull ones. Chainsalt refuses Essence so completely that every gasket and isolation collar in every serious array (a working laid out in glyph and substrate to run in place) is cut from it. Drawcord Sinew is the best cordage below silk and nobody has ever written a song about it. Gray Standing Chalk is deliberately characterless, and an apprentice who cannot make a circle work with it has made a bad circle.
And the register’s most consequential column is the one about where things came from. The Three Marks run from Grade I Vein Draw, taken straight off a Wellspring site by array and carrying nothing, to Class VI Archonic Residue, which is not rendered but found, and has no origin the instrument can locate.

Between them sits Grade IV, Crystal Draw, rendered from something that carried a Soul Crystal. The lawful article is a monster’s core, and the arithmetic has never balanced, because the surplus was cut from the dead.

Entries
The reading order. Thirteen documents. The path runs from the ground upward: what the world is made of, what was alive first, how it is worked, what may lawfully be sold, who rules on it, what it is worth, and who does the work.

1 · The Bearing and the Holding the ground itself, and what Essence actually did to the trades. Read this first. It is the only document that explains why the world looks the way it does, and everything below assumes it.
2 · The Master Material Ledger the Tier Scale, the Hazard Register, the unlocatable sources, and the Grade IV shortfall.
3 · The Material Index, T0–T4 the ground, the bulk supply, the first instrument grades.
4 · The Material Index, T5–T9 what requires a forge-array, a rite, or a corpse, and what lies past that.
5 · Hide, Horn and Bone what was alive first, the twentieth entry, what a kill makes and what a core is worth.
6 · Alchemetrica the practitioner’s codex. What the work is, what the bench costs the body, the core on the bench and the Master Works.
7 · The Alchemical Index the sixty-one attested formulas, each with its analogue, its mechanism and its failure.
8 · The Heresiology of Alchemy the doctrinal counterpart. Seven lawful stages, seven inversions, and the grammar a civilization needs so it does not mistake catastrophe for genius.
9 · The Standing Index the Bench’s own register. Forty-five entries, the three marks, and the lawful sources of Grade IV, with the monster core first among them. Its shelf-mates The Common Drafts and Prepared Tags are what the counter actually sells.
10 · The Bench of Attribution entry, striking, attribution and reservation, and the one instrument the procedure has never required.
11 · Value, Coin and Trade what any of it is worth, in two ledgers that meet at one number.
12 · The Works and Days who does the work, sorted by what the instrument can see.
13 · The Apparatus of the Age what they carry while doing it. The tallow candle before the Aethersteel plate.

On the two counts. The Master Material Ledger carries sixty-one attested formulas in its Alchemical Index. The Standing Index carries forty-five entries. These are different registers and the numbers are not in conflict: one records what the trade knows, the other records what the trade was willing to surrender to the Bench.
The groupings below are the filing. The order above is the path.
I · The ground and the registers
What the world is made of. The two Material Indices and the Alchemical Index sit beneath the Ledger.


The Master Material Ledger
The Standing Index
Hide, Horn and Bone


II · The bench
How the work is done, what it costs the body, and how a civilization names the ways it goes wrong.


Alchemetrica
The Heresiology of Alchemy
The Common Drafts
Prepared Tags


III · The body that rules on it, and the money
Filed elsewhere in the wiki and reached from here, because nothing in this section is settled without them.
The Bench of Attribution
The Material Index · T0–T4
The Bearing and the Holding
Value, Coin and Trade
IV · The hands that use it
The registers say what the world is made of. These two say who touches it, with what, and what it does to them.
The Works and Days sorts the whole population by what the instrument can see: three floors, and the register begins with the third because they are the majority, and any account of the world’s work that begins with the practitioners is describing the exception and calling it the rule.
The Apparatus of the Age is its equipment appendix: the tallow candle before the Aethersteel plate, because the candle appears in more scenes than any weapon.


The Works and Days — Occupations, Trades and Technology
The Apparatus of the Age — Equipment and Material Culture



The Works and Days says plainly what it leaves out, food and cuisine, music, ground-level justice, domestic life and courtship, which is most of what people call the folk world. That register is the closest thing to a foundation for them that exists.



Weight, Measure and the Standard



What a pound is, and who never accepted it. Weight, Measure and the Standard underpins the assay, the proof-mark and the Bench, none of which work without standard weights.
Everything is built on a counted seed, which is also the flaw, since the Accord’s grain is a Western seed. Two parallel systems: market weight at sixteen ounces for bulk and assay weight at twelve for anything the Bench touches, with the assay pound scaled so a bead reads directly as fineness. Weights carry verification stamps and a false one is struck with a six-point mark across them, and struck weights still in circulation are the most reliable indicator of how far the Accord’s reach actually extends.
Two things worth having in any market scene. A cased weight is a bronze shell filled with lead and gives a dull note instead of ringing, so every market searcher taps before he does anything else. And the whole grain trade turns on one word, level or heaped, which makes the strike-board the most political object in the market.



The Real Alchemy



Read beside this. The Sixty Wellsprings for what a material’s Resonance and Kind mean, The Three Paths for the three layers a Draft feeds and a harness does or does not cover, and Classes and the Three Ladders for what a bought Stage does not buy.

Read next: The Working Trades, for the crafts these materials feed; The Ladder and the Draft, for what the Drafts are for.

materials,-alchemy--and--trade/materials.title: Hide, Horn and Bone
materials,-alchemy--and--trade/materials.content:
The creature-material register · hide, horn, claw, bone, sinew, gut, blood, organ, scale, quill and shell, and the core that pays for all of it.

Everything in this register was alive once. Some of it has not been told.
Chalked over the door of a Dorrosfenn rendering house, and repainted by the owners whenever it wears off

Bettany Quarrie’s wedding feast at Sarrow Cross ran three nights, and the wine town talked of nothing else for forty years. Her father, a vintner who had come into money and wanted the valley to know it, built a great hall for the purpose, hung its beams in saffron and kingfisher blue, set a whole ox turning, and hired the pipers of two parishes who detested each other. What he had mentioned to nobody was the loft, where he kept the most expensive thing he had ever bought: two hundred fathoms of Tidedrawn Cable, leviathan tendon a hand’s width across, taken on speculation against a siege that never came, and stored coiled, twelve days’ haul from salt water, by a man who had read the price and not the row. It had spent five weeks working its way across the floorboards toward the river. On the third night, halfway through the second pipers’ set, it reached the north gable and kept going.
The gable went out in one piece. The cable came down through the roof tree over the heads of the dancers like a black river with an appointment, its tail fouled around the king post, and a hand’s width of that cable holds a ship, so the hall went with it. The whole north end of the building walked eleven paces down the hill toward the Sarrow at about the pace of a plow ox, beams shrieking, carrying the high table along on its floor and leaving two pipers, an uncle and the ox underneath. Bettany Quarrie stayed in her chair with a cup in her fist and her yellow skirts full of roof, and shouted down the length of the wreck for somebody to bring more wine. The minstrels have her riding the cable to the river with a sword in her hand, and in the longer versions out to sea. It reached the water on the ninth day and has lain there since, by every account perfectly content, and the town charges to see it.
The trade’s word for what was in that loft is carry (what a creature’s life leaves in the material rendered out of it). It is graded on every row below, by Provenance Grade (the mark of where a stock came from), and any factor in the four quarters will sell it to you by the pound without once telling you what it is. I will.

What carry actually is, stated once. Every entry below is graded for it and the register has never said what it does.
A Threshold (the breakthrough that remakes a practitioner’s Soul Crystal) is a melt, and a melt cools into order only around structures that survived the heat. A lived one passes the Great Work in its Path’s own terms, nigredo, albedo, citrinitas and rubedo: broken down, purified, woken and fixed. In a Soul Crystal those structures are Traits, which are laws the bearer survived into existence. Carry is a seed: a law that something else survived into existence, still attached to the material it was rendered out of.
So a high-carry creature material used in Threshold work does more than work harder. It grows a region of the recipient’s new lattice around a law that was never theirs. The appetite in Ripper Talon is a hunting law a predator lived long enough to make true. The pull in Tidedrawn Cable is a law about deep water. Neither of them is a metaphor and neither of them stops.
Grade III carry is appetite-shaped and can be lived with. Grade IV is identity-shaped, and identity-shaped carry is what Identity Contamination is a description of: a Core (here the Essence Core inside the Crystal) that has absorbed enough borrowed law to stop being able to say cleanly which convictions are its own. This register is that supply chain. It has never been written down as one.

The Core
A monster’s core is in a way its Soul Crystal. Inside a creature’s chest the Essence Core (the seat of its nature) hardens over its life into a fist of glassy stuff in its own color, and it is worth more the stronger the monster. Monsters gain Levels by killing, each other included, evolve at their own thresholds, and are posted by Grade, E to EX, on the Commission’s board (see The Bestiary); the core table below is keyed to that Grade, and the materials further down carry the Accord ledger’s own material tier, T0 to T9, as every substance in The Master Material Ledger does. A core is the lawful Crystal Draw of The Standing Index, and an alchemist renders it into Essence Drafts used for tempering. A Well-spawn carries one under the mask, so a hunter may be paid twice on one kill: the hall on the mask, the rendering house on the core. Anything banished down its Well takes the core along.
A core keeps far longer than anything else on the carcass, which is why crews run for the hall with the mask and walk home with the core inside their shirts. What follows is the price at a rendering house’s door, for a clean core with a hall’s chit. A house pays between a third and a half of what the core will fetch poured.

































































Beast’s GradeStage it servesPrice at the doorWhat that buysEI3 to 5 silverA laborer’s week, from something that had been at the henhouseDII12 to 18 silverAbout a laborer’s month, for a boy with a spadeCIII3 to 6 goldA soldier’s half-year, and a crew’s first good nightBIV8 to 15 goldMost of a laborer’s year. A village remembers who brought it homeAV to VII, and the coil tells you which30 to 300 goldThe bottom buys two horses and the top a clerk’s four yearsSVIII to X800 to 8,000 goldMore than the crew’s home village will see in a generationSS, a wyrmXI and XII20,000 gold and upA fortune anywhere there is a crucible, a song, and every lord in the region asking who you areXXIII and XIVBy private treaty, and a war afterwardA crown’s ransomEXXV and XVINot entered
Any core renders about a dozen doses at its own grade (What Things Cost carries the same rows, and Monster Cores the whole trade).
A wyrm core is the one the crews mean when they say a fortune. A good earth wyrm’s fetches 20,000 gold at the door of any rendering house with a crucible big enough, a good deal more for an old one with a name and a bounty, and the bill on the rim-town doors of the Scourge of Hell pays on top of that. Do not confuse any of this with a Core in the street’s sense, a place where a Wellspring pools, and be careful which one you promise a factor.

Swallowed raw, a core gives everything at once. Most die and a good share come out wrong. A Crystal cut from a dead practitioner reads the same on the coil, makes the strongest Draft of all, and is the worst crime in every realm and the most profitable. A rendering house can spot a human Crystal on the bench if it cares to look, and the houses that care are the ones still solvent after a hanging. Ask for the chit. Ask for the beast’s name. Then ask yourself why the price is good.

What a Kill Makes
Monster parts make gear, and most of what a fighter wears that is worth stealing was walking around once. A piece carries a Grade for power, on the same letters the Commission posts beasts by, and a Rarity for scarcity: Common, Uncommon, Rare, Very Rare, Legendary, Mythic, Unique. Its material sets the most Grade it can hold, by the rows below and Grade and Rarity; the smith’s title caps the Grade she may make, and the merchant’s title caps the Rarity he may sell. The Accord’s old stamps (Marked, Proofed, Tempered, Instrument, Hallowed, Storied, Found, Numinous, Proscribed) still go on the mark. An Appraisal skill and an assay instrument read a piece, and a good forger beats a weak appraiser. Only bonded gear grows.













































PartBecomesWhat the buyer is paying forHide, scale, plateArmor backing, coats, brigandine facing, a cloak with a reputationWhatever the beast shrugged off, and whatever it never learned to fearHorn, claw, fangSpearheads, blade facing, arrow and bolt heads, knife hiltsEdge, and off a B-Grade beast or better a little of the appetiteBoneHafts, grips, ward-tokens, marrow for the renderStiffness, and something to cut a rune intoSinew, gutBowstrings, crossbow cord, harness, suturePull. The best cordage in the world is on the inside of somethingGlands, bladders, bloodCharges, Drafts, quenchesA short clock and a high priceThe mask of a Well-spawnHall pay, while it holds its color; a gray shard over the door afterwardA clerk’s signatureThe coreEssence DraftsEverything above, several times over
A piece from a famous beast takes its name and goes on being talked about. A hunter in a coat of Aunt Teeth’s plum-colored hide is buying a drink, a fight or both in every town on the moor.
Hide, Scale and Plate



































MaterialSourceResonance · Kind · DomainWhat it isFellstag Winterpelt T2 · Bearing · NorthFellstag herds, taken in the cold months onlyVohrin · Titan-touched · ThermodynamicsExcellent insulation; turns a glancing cut and nothing more. The cold teams’ single most important piece of equipment and the reason the winter trade exists at all. The pelt rots fast above freezing and cannot be worked in summerMarshcoat Hide T3 · Bearing · SouthAmbush predators of the Dorrosfenn basinsThaloré · Spirit · Fluid DynamicsSheds water completely; supple when wet. Carries a stillness rather than an appetite. Nothing spoils inside a Marshcoat bag. Sealwright teams pay whatever is asked. Cracks in dry heat and will not recoverSlatecoil Skin T4 · Bearing · EastIroncoil kin from the deep Braqth galleriesPetralon · Wild · MechanicsLayered scale spreading a crushing blow across a wide area. Inert by construction. Brigandine facing and array-house aprons. The mundane cousin of Coilhide and better at the one thing Coilhide does. A thrust goes between the scalesSlatescale T4 · Bearing · EastShed plates, gathered rather than takenPetralon · Wild · MechanicsExcellent against cutting, poor against crushing: the plates transmit what they do not stop. Gathered rather than taken, which puts it outside the runner trade entirely and into the hands of children
Horn, Claw, Bone and Shell















































MaterialSourceResonance · Kind · DomainWhat it isFellstag Crown T3 · Holding · NorthShed annually; taken from the ground rather than the beastAnamnesis · Medium · Abstract/EntropicTakes and holds an inscription cleanly. Household ward-tokens and parish witness seals. Shed rather than taken, which is why northern parishes will use it for witness work and will not use Knellhide. A wet crown loses its inscription inside a seasonRipper Talon T4 · Bearing · EastApex canopy predators, eastern cloud forestAnima Spirare · Wild · BiochemistryHolds an edge better than bronze and worse than steel. Grade III carry, appetite-shaped, pursuit-set. A blade faced with Ripper Talon is difficult to disengage from and the difficulty is not mechanicalRunner’s Ivory T3 · Bearing · SouthGrazing megafauna, southern plainsMaterial ScienceDense, workable, takes a fine polish. Handles, buttons, inlay, instrument keys. Nothing much fails it. It simply is not very good at anything. Included because ninety percent of the bone trade by weight is this and no codex has ever mentioned itMarrowglass T5 · Holding · WestLong bones of Tempered beasts, vitrified in the renderMortalis · Medium · BiochemistryRetains a Grade IV-adjacent carry from a beast that grew a Crystal. Threshold work and Spirit Axis attestation stock. A Tempered beast is not a person and the Bench has ruled so eleven times. The rulings are re-litigated annually. Fails to impact, and to Scribe’s Wash, which lifts the inscription and the value together. What the eleven rulings are actually about. A Tempered beast grew a Crystal, and a Crystal that reached a Threshold seated Traits, and a Trait is a law the bearer survived into existence. Marrowglass therefore seeds a human melt with a beast’s law: a hunting law, a cold law, a law about the dark under a gallery. Whether that constitutes personhood is the question the Bench answers annually and the question nobody in the trade is actually asking. The buyers want to know what the law wasDeepshell Nacre T5 · Bearing · SouthDeep-shelf molluscs, dredgedFixatio · Medium · Material ScienceLayered and tough; spreads impact through delamination. Takes a Fixatio seal unusually well. The standard lining of every reagent case in the four quarters and the reason sealed stock arrives at grade. Sustained heat separates the layers and the seal goes with themWorldspine T9 · Bearing · unconfirmedSkeletal structure of a confirmed World Spirit. One attested recoveryVantabriel · Wild · Boundary PhysicsBearing beyond assessment: the Measurewrights’ instrument reports no upper bound and the report is not believed. The material does not hold Essence so much as decline to be separated from it. Never worked. Nothing tested against it has marked it. Entered, held, not authorized
Sinew, Gut and Cordage





























MaterialSourceResonance · Kind · DomainWhat it isDrawcord Sinew T2 · Bearing · all quartersBack and leg sinew, any large grazing stockMechanicsSuperb tensile strength; the best cordage available below silk. Bowstrings, lashings, surgical ligature. Used by everyone, everywhere, constantly. The most useful material in the ledger and the least glamorous. Loses half its strength wet and recovers it on dryingGutstring T3 · Holding · all quartersCleaned intestine, sheep or goat, scraped and twistedBasilithe · Wild · Material ScienceModest Holding but unusually clean. Takes a resonance and holds pitch. Instrument strings, harmonic apparatus, surgical suture. The overlap between the instrument trade and the surgical trade is not a coincidence and both buy from the same manTidedrawn Cable T5 · Bearing · SouthDeep-water leviathan tendon, taken at seaThaloré · Spirit · Fluid DynamicsA hand’s width holds a ship. Low but directional Holding: the carry pulls, continuously, toward deep water. Ship rigging, Gate-margin anchoring, siege haulage. Cannot be stored coiled inland. It works itself toward water and fouls. Every warehouse reports the same thing and the Measurewrights have measured it and have not explained it
Blood and Organ















































MaterialSourceResonance · Kind · DomainWhat it isField Draw T1 · Holding · all quartersBled at the kill into a sealed vesselAnima Spirare · Wild · BiochemistryBase stock for Grade III rendering. The single largest input by volume into the reagent economy and the one with the shortest clock. Every child in the four quarters skips rope to some version of the Stuff Rhyme: iron for the soldier, salt for the stew, silver for the oath and the oath for you; bone for the bishop, hide for the lord, and who was the marrow in the Margrave’s sword? The last line has cost more than one hedge-school dame her post, and it remains the most accurate thing ever written about the material trade.
What the world is made of, tier by tier, and what was alive first.


The Master Material Ledger Consolidated substrate register · T0 through T9 · all four quarters
Hide, Horn and Bone The creature-material register · hide, horn, claw, bone, sinew, gut, blood, organ, scale, quill and shell, what a kill makes, and what a core is worth.

The 61 attested formulas of the Master Codex, as made at the bench
The Alchemical Index gives each formula’s Measurewrights’ account and its failure. This page is the bench copy: what goes in, how it is made, what it does, what it risks, and how it works by its Wellspring’s idea. The two are read together, and they are filed in the same tiers.

































TierFormulasT2 · Apprentice WorkEquilibrium Draught, Veilthread Salve, Echo-Bloom IncenseT3 · Trade StandardVeilstone Tincture, Null-Salt, Tide-Silt Compress, Cinder-Salt Glyph Wash, Lantern Resin, Veyric Sparkwine, Stillgate Ash, Choirglass Phials, Verdant Overgrowth Seeds, Null-Resonance Buffer, Vector Piercing Draught, Aperture Wound Ichor, Grace Fall DraughtT4 · ProfessionalPyraeon Bloom Oil, Verdant Suture Paste, Judic Flame Wax, Granite-Bone Binding Mortar, Architect’s Ink, Chronal Sandglass Dust, Dominion Brand Oil, Vaststep Chalk, Gravetide Ink, Ashfang Venom Vial, Edgetruth Whetstone Oil, Beastheart Serum, Slag-Iron Caustic, Excision Bloodletting Needles, Null-Edge Paste, Ignis Barb Oil, Will-Break Fumigant, Thunderclap Bracer ChargeT5 · ExpertObsidian Epoch Resin, Forge-Tempered Essence Ink, Dreamstone Shard Flask, Stasisline Needles, Strain-Bound Marrow, Corpus Marrow Salts, Purganeth Mirror-Salt, Ethereal Current Oil, Hollow-Watch Incense, Deep Grid Mortar, Thundercrack Grenade, Gravewell Shackle Coating, Rupture Powder, Frostthrone Lance Balm, Command Brand Iron, Sever-Bond Twine, Obsidian Fang PoisonT6 · MasterAnamnesis Draught, Skyfire Pulse Vial, Verdance Reclamation Draught, Somnum Flow Ampoule, Crevice-Glass Shard, Pyric Refinement Ash, Fossil Ring Dust, Pressure Burst CapsuleT7 · GrandmasterNull-Essence Draught, Stillwater Draught
T2 · Apprentice Work
Equilibrium Draught
Liquid Tonic · T2 · Ur, Me

















WellspringJudicium (Wild)OperationSeparation
Ingredients. Distilled Wellspring water, scale-seed, balanced salt-pair
Method. Brew on twin flames under Eq Equivalence; bottle in mirrored glass.
Effect. Temporarily steadies emotions and Aether output, resisting panic and surges.
Risk. Long-term reliance flattens affect; harder to reach peak emotional Resonance.
How it works.

The idea. Truth told apart. Discernment that knows what a thing is made of, and whether it is lying, from the mark it cannot help leaving.
The operation. Separation. A thing is parted from what it claims to be, the true told apart from the false by the mark it cannot help leaving.
In the maker. Ur, Me fix what it may do, and the bench work keeps the separation going until the maker’s hold on the idea sets in the matter, so it does: temporarily steadies emotions and Aether output, resisting panic and surges.
Price. The maker’s reserve at the bench; the Risk line is the taker’s price.
Flaw. Discernment tells everything apart and cannot choose to leave anything untold. Off guard, every object in view reports what it is made of at once, and the reader loses the power to put any of it first. Pushed past the point where a reading only reads, telling a thing apart becomes taking it apart: the read starts to pass judgment, which can turn away force or at the very top end a life, and since it has no way to look at one thing only, it takes the reader’s own memory in the same stroke.
The Measurewrights’ line. Emission and absorption spectroscopy.

Veilthread Salve
Topical Ointment · T2 · Vl, Ka

















WellspringOneirion (Spirit)OperationSublimation
Ingredients. Spider-silk, dream-pollen, veilleaf oil
Method. Cold-fold under Ka Dream until sheen turns opalescent.
Effect. Smearing on skin masks small areas from scrying and low-grade true-sight for a scene.
Risk. Prolonged use disassociates the wearer; weak boundary between self and dream.
How it works.

The idea. Dream as a place. Work done in the space of what can be thought, reaching a soul where no line of sight runs, because no soul was ever in the room.
The operation. Sublimation. The working is lifted off every bench into the space of what can be thought, and comes down again in a soul.
In the maker. Vl, Ka fix what it may do, and the bench work keeps the sublimation going until the maker’s hold on the idea sets in the matter, so it does: Smearing on skin masks small areas from scrying and low-grade true-sight for a scene.
Price. The maker’s reserve at the bench; the Risk line is the taker’s price.
Flaw. A dream is a place with no ground under it, and nothing done there knows where it is in a room. A working that was true in the space of what can be thought lands nowhere in particular when it has to come down into a real one.
The Measurewrights’ line. Configuration space.

Echo-Bloom Incense
Incense · T2 · Ae, Yn





















WellspringOneirion (Spirit)Second WellspringVerdantiaOperationSublimation
Ingredients. Echo-petals, resin, thread of hair from intended focus
Method. Rolled while Rv Reverie is softly intoned.
Effect. Burned, it draws out memory-echoes of a place, making them semi-visible to observers.
Risk. Overexposure traps users in nostalgic feedback and emotional loops.
How it works.

The idea. Dream as a place. Work done in the space of what can be thought, reaching a soul where no line of sight runs, because no soul was ever in the room. Verdantia’s idea is folded in (growth without end, a self with no final size, which feeds on simply being out in the world. It comes through accumulation rather than rupture, one good day on top of another).
The operation. Sublimation. The working is lifted off every bench into the space of what can be thought, and comes down again in a soul.
In the maker. Ae, Yn fix what it may do, and the bench work keeps the sublimation going until the maker’s hold on the idea sets in the matter, so it does: burned, it draws out memory-echoes of a place, making them semi-visible to observers.
Price. The maker’s reserve at the bench; the Risk line is the taker’s price.
Flaw. A dream is a place with no ground under it, and nothing done there knows where it is in a room. A working that was true in the space of what can be thought lands nowhere in particular when it has to come down into a real one.
The Measurewrights’ line. Configuration space.

T3 · Trade Standard
Veilstone Tincture
Liquid Reagent · T3 · [Vl] Veil + [El] Life

















WellspringOneirion (Spirit)OperationSublimation
Ingredients. Crushed dreamstone; silver morning dew; echo-moth wing ash
Method. Cold-press under crescent moon; seal in obsidian vial with [DmSl] Dream-Seal
Effect. Renders user’s Essence signature invisible to basic Aetheric detection for 6 hours; dreamwalker-safe formula
Risk. Overdose causes permanent echo-bleed; user perceives waking life as a dream
How it works.

The idea. Dream as a place. Work done in the space of what can be thought, reaching a soul where no line of sight runs, because no soul was ever in the room.
The operation. Sublimation. The working is lifted off every bench into the space of what can be thought, and comes down again in a soul.
In the maker. [Vl] Veil + [El] Life fix what it may do, and the bench work keeps the sublimation going until the maker’s hold on the idea sets in the matter, so it does: Renders user’s Essence signature invisible to basic Aetheric detection for 6 hours; dreamwalker-safe formula.
Price. The maker’s reserve at the bench; the Risk line is the taker’s price.
Flaw. A dream is a place with no ground under it, and nothing done there knows where it is in a room. A working that was true in the space of what can be thought lands nowhere in particular when it has to come down into a real one.
The Measurewrights’ line. Configuration space.

Notes. Commonly used by Varn archivists and Nysera-aligned scouts
Null-Salt
Powder / Anti-Reagent · T3 · [Nul] Null + [Vn] Void

















WellspringNihiloth (Wild)OperationDissolution
Ingredients. Refined void-crystal dust; Vaun-charged salt (harvested in full eclipse); ground [Thru] Hollow glyph-stone
Method. Grind under total silence; store in lead-sealed vial never touched by fire
Effect. Sprinkled on an active glyph array to cancel it instantly; one vial = one array; does not discriminate friendly/hostile
Risk. Contact with living Essence causes Null-bleed; mild but cumulative on prolonged exposure
How it works.

The idea. The hollow law. Power by negation: the rule itself unmade, and what stands in the gap.
The operation. Dissolution. The rule itself is loosed until nothing of it is left, and the gap is left standing where it was.
In the maker. [Nul] Null + [Vn] Void fix what it may do, and the bench work keeps the dissolution going until the maker’s hold on the idea sets in the matter, so it does: Sprinkled on an active glyph array to cancel it instantly; one vial = one array; does not discriminate friendly/hostile.
Price. The maker’s reserve at the bench; the Risk line is the taker’s price.
Flaw. A rule unmade is unmade for everyone, and the idea has no way to spare its maker. Everything the practitioner brought inside is subject to the same gap, including the parts of themselves they were relying on.
The Measurewrights’ line. Destructive interference and the null field.

Notes. Standard kit for Accord glyph-breakers and Counter-Weavers
Tide-Silt Compress
Battlefield Compress · T3 · [Let] Tide + [Drn] Drain





















WellspringAbyntheus (Spirit)Second WellspringPhreatisOperationSublimation
Ingredients. Deep-ocean salt-mud from Lethis-adjacent Wellspring; pale-tide kelp; Drain-glyph mineral
Method. Pack raw; activate with tide-current pulse from caster before application
Effect. Draws excess Essence from overloaded wounds; stabilizes Splintering-stage overcharge; slows bleeding at Hermetic and physical layers
Risk. If Essence drain exceeds injury level, draws vitality
How it works.

The idea. Vastness. The great scale read off the small vessel, a mortal soul stretched to take in things far too large for it. Phreatis’s idea is folded in (memory as deep water, what is lived sinks in, is built into you, and comes back long after the weather has changed).
The operation. Sublimation. The small soul is raised toward the great scale and brought back down still holding it.
In the maker. [Let] Tide + [Drn] Drain fix what it may do, and the bench work keeps the sublimation going until the maker’s hold on the idea sets in the matter, so it does: draws excess Essence from overloaded wounds; stabilizes Splintering-stage overcharge; slows bleeding at Hermetic and physical layers.
Price. The maker’s reserve at the bench; the Risk line is the taker’s price.
Flaw. The small vessel can hold the great scale only while it still knows it is small. Stretched too long between the near end and the far one, the soul loses its sense of how the two fit together, and what comes back to it is noise the practitioner is nonetheless convinced is a signal.
The Measurewrights’ line. Very-long-wavelength propagation and interferometry.

Notes. Used by Accord field-medics in coastal or deep-realm engagements
Cinder-Salt Glyph Wash
Cleansing Compound · T3 · [Cin] Cinder + [Xr] Excision





















WellspringPyraeon (Wild)Second WellspringCatharsisOperationDistillation
Ingredients. Pyreth cinder-salt; distilled sunwater; ember-bark shavings
Method. Dissolve in sunwater at dawn; allow to cool; apply to glyph arrays to purge corruption
Effect. Burns out corrupted glyph threads without destroying the underlying inscription framework; safe for Domain markers
Risk. Overuse strips beneficial enchantments alongside rot
How it works.

The idea. The ember that stays lit. Power that gives up its flare and keeps its heat for a lifetime. Catharsis’s idea is folded in (letting go, a load set down so completely that the setting down spends it, and the soul comes out on the other side lighter and changed).
The operation. Distillation. A low fire kept under the vessel for months and years, never let flare, until what is wanted comes over drop by drop for a lifetime.
In the maker. [Cin] Cinder + [Xr] Excision fix what it may do, and the bench work keeps the distillation going until the maker’s hold on the idea sets in the matter, so it does: burns out corrupted glyph threads without destroying the underlying inscription framework; safe for Domain markers.
Price. The maker’s reserve at the bench; the Risk line is the taker’s price.
Flaw. The ember stays lit, and nothing in the idea knows how to put it out. When the practitioner lets the working go it goes on smoldering where they cannot see it, eating reserve and tissue for hours after they believed it ended.
The Measurewrights’ line. Smoldering combustion.

Notes. Standard Accord purification kit; issued to field chaplains
Lantern Resin
Solid Resin · T3 · Ma, Ae





















WellspringAnamnesis (Medium)Second WellspringOneirionOperationSeparation
Ingredients. Echo-sap, powdered memory-glass, silver-thread dust
Method. Slow-cure in darkness with Rv Reverie etched into mold.
Effect. Stores a clean replay of one scene when broken and held.
Risk. Overloaded scenes blur into symbolic nonsense; risk of misreading Echoes.
How it works.

The idea. Remembrance. Everything keeps its past, and a soul under this lens can touch a thing and read it. Oneirion’s idea is folded in (dream as a place, work done in the space of what can be thought, reaching a soul where no line of sight runs, because no soul was ever in the room).
The operation. Separation. The past a thing has kept is parted from it and read, as the residue is parted from the vessel that held it.
In the maker. Ma, Ae fix what it may do, and the bench work keeps the separation going until the maker’s hold on the idea sets in the matter, so it does: stores a clean replay of one scene when broken and held.
Price. The maker’s reserve at the bench; the Risk line is the taker’s price.
Flaw. Everything keeps its past, and the reading becomes part of that past the moment it is made. A careless hand laid on the record writes itself over what it came to read, so a careless practitioner erases the record in the act of taking it.
The Measurewrights’ line. Remanent magnetization and thermoluminescent dosimetry.

Veyric Sparkwine
Alchemical Wine · T3 · Ve, Ra





















WellspringIgnivale (Wild)Second WellspringExurothOperationCalcination
Ingredients. Bloodfruit, ember-grapes, cinder-sugar
Method. Ferment in sealed casks inscribed with Desire runes.
Effect. Boosts creativity and battle-lust; minor Essence regen spike.
Risk. Addictive; users may chase the Spark to self-destructive extremes.
How it works.

The idea. The spark. The smallest beginning that goes on to pay for itself, so that the gap between wanting a thing and doing it closes to almost nothing. Exuroth’s idea is folded in (the trial by fire, power comes only through ordeal, plunged and reheated and plunged again, until the soul holds a hardness no gentle road could have given it).
The operation. Calcination. One point of fire is set to the work at the first degree, and the burning is left to pay its own way.
In the maker. Ve, Ra fix what it may do, and the bench work keeps the calcination going until the maker’s hold on the idea sets in the matter, so it does: Boosts creativity and battle-lust; minor Essence regen spike.
Price. The maker’s reserve at the bench; the Risk line is the taker’s price.
Flaw. With the gap between wanting and doing closed, the soul has no moment left in which to decide. Any stray feeling in the room is beginning enough, and the working fires without the practitioner having decided to fire it.
The Measurewrights’ line. Minimum ignition energy and the activation barrier.

Stillgate Ash
Powder Reagent · T3 · Au, Sil

















WellspringMortalis (Medium)OperationDissolution
Ingredients. Bone-ash, river-silt, cooled funeral-flame soot
Method. Grind under Ps Passage and Rt Return; store dry.
Effect. Sprinkled in a circle, calms restless dead and seals minor hauntings.
Risk. Misuse around living beings induces emotional numbness and sleep-paralysis dreams.
How it works.

The idea. The black gate. Ending looked at squarely and understood as a passage with its own law, by a soul that has stopped fearing it and has started, a little, to cool.
The operation. Dissolution. A thing’s hold on what it is gets loosed, lawfully and in order, until it comes apart at its proper end.
In the maker. Au, Sil fix what it may do, and the bench work keeps the dissolution going until the maker’s hold on the idea sets in the matter, so it does: Sprinkled in a circle, calms restless dead and seals minor hauntings.
Price. The maker’s reserve at the bench; the Risk line is the taker’s price.
Flaw. A soul that has stopped fearing the gate has also stopped holding out against it, and the fear was part of what kept it on this side. Stay near the ending long enough and the worker drifts toward it, cooling a little at a time without noticing.
The Measurewrights’ line. The non-equilibrium steady state, and the thermodynamic boundary of its collapse.

Choirglass Phials
Alchemical Glass · T3 · Se, Chw

















WellspringThaloré (Spirit)OperationDissolution
Ingredients. Song-sand, echo-quartz, tuning-fork shavings
Method. Melt with Se Song sung during the entire smelting.
Effect. Liquids stored within harmonize; stacked phials can amplify supportive chants or mantras.
Risk. Discordant voices near them can shatter the glass explosively.
How it works.

The idea. Depth of feeling. Emotion given its true weight in the soul, so that a grief can press on every soul in a whole room. A soul under this lens takes the shape of what holds it, and is likelier than most to fall into Synergia (Crystals briefly sharing one working) and Echo Bonds.
The operation. Dissolution. A feeling is let down through the whole soul to its true depth, and the soul takes the shape of what holds it.
In the maker. Se, Chw fix what it may do, and the bench work keeps the dissolution going until the maker’s hold on the idea sets in the matter, so it does: Liquids stored within harmonize; stacked phials can amplify supportive chants or mantras.
Price. The maker’s reserve at the bench; the Risk line is the taker’s price.
Flaw. A feeling given its true weight weighs on the one who feels it as surely as on the room, and the idea does not choose which way it presses. A Thaloré practitioner whose own inner support fails is crushed under the weight they were laying on everyone else.
The Measurewrights’ line. Hydrostatic pressure.

Verdant Overgrowth Seeds
Seed-Reagent · T3 · El, Yn

















WellspringVerdantia (Wild)OperationFermentation
Ingredients. Bloom-Root kernels, verdant Wellspring dew, fertile loam
Method. Encased in Vael Renewal sigil and sun-baked one full cycle.
Effect. Thrown or planted, creates rapid thickets/roots that reshape terrain.
Risk. Can overrun allies and structures; hard to prune without Blight-grade counteragents.
How it works.

The idea. Growth without end. A self with no final size, which feeds on simply being out in the world. It comes through accumulation rather than rupture, one good day on top of another.
The operation. Fermentation. The soul is fed a little at a time from the world it stands in, and grows on that feeding without end.
In the maker. El, Yn fix what it may do, and the bench work keeps the fermentation going until the maker’s hold on the idea sets in the matter, so it does: thrown or planted, creates rapid thickets/roots that reshape terrain.
Price. The maker’s reserve at the bench; the Risk line is the taker’s price.
Flaw. A self with no final size cannot stop growing, even when the world has stopped feeding it. Shut away from the open air it grows on anyway, all length and no substance, until it cannot hold itself up.
The Measurewrights’ line. Carbon fixation and indeterminate meristematic growth.

Null-Resonance Buffer
Suspension · T3 · Nl (Null), Ar Accord





















WellspringNihiloth (Wild)Second WellspringThaloréOperationDissolution
Ingredients. Null-salt trace, harmonized water, choirstone dust
Method. Agitated with low-frequency humming to keep stable.
Effect. Drinking grants brief resistance to Null-fields disrupting your own spells.
Risk. If used near strong Choirs, the buffer “sings apart,” stunning the drinker.
How it works.

The idea. The hollow law. Power by negation: the rule itself unmade, and what stands in the gap. Thaloré’s idea is folded in (depth of feeling, emotion given its true weight in the soul, so that a grief can press on every soul in a whole room. A soul under this lens takes the shape of what holds it, and is likelier than most to fall into Synergia (Crystals briefly sharing one working) and Echo Bonds).
The operation. Dissolution. The rule itself is loosed until nothing of it is left, and the gap is left standing where it was.
In the maker. Nl (Null), Ar Accord fix what it may do, and the bench work keeps the dissolution going until the maker’s hold on the idea sets in the matter, so it does: Drinking grants brief resistance to Null-fields disrupting your own spells.
Price. The maker’s reserve at the bench; the Risk line is the taker’s price.
Flaw. A rule unmade is unmade for everyone, and the idea has no way to spare its maker. Everything the practitioner brought inside is subject to the same gap, including the parts of themselves they were relying on.
The Measurewrights’ line. Destructive interference and the null field.

Vector Piercing Draught
Alchemical Oil · T3 · [Vt] Vector + [Wy] Motion





















WellspringIgnivale (Wild)Second WellspringCataclysmOperationCalcination
Ingredients. Distilled Ignivale spark-oil; Cataclysm storm-dust; fletching wax
Method. Work the oil into arrow fletching and shaft in the direction of intended flight only; against the grain ruins the batch
Effect. Arrows and bolts treated fly true past wind and hold momentum through soft cover, punching cleanly through padded and mail armor tiers that would otherwise deflect a standard shaft
Risk. A shaft fired against its own treated grain can double back on release, embedding in the archer’s own draw hand
How it works.

The idea. The spark. The smallest beginning that goes on to pay for itself, so that the gap between wanting a thing and doing it closes to almost nothing. Cataclysm’s idea is folded in (upheaval, the moment a fire stops being a fire and becomes a blast, a change in kind as well as size, and the soul that has learned to call that moment).
The operation. Calcination. One point of fire is set to the work at the first degree, and the burning is left to pay its own way.
In the maker. [Vt] Vector + [Wy] Motion fix what it may do, and the bench work keeps the calcination going until the maker’s hold on the idea sets in the matter, so it does: Arrows and bolts treated fly true past wind and hold momentum through soft cover, punching cleanly through padded and mail armor tiers that would otherwise deflect a standard shaft.
Price. The maker’s reserve at the bench; the Risk line is the taker’s price.
Flaw. With the gap between wanting and doing closed, the soul has no moment left in which to decide. Any stray feeling in the room is beginning enough, and the working fires without the practitioner having decided to fire it.
The Measurewrights’ line. Minimum ignition energy and the activation barrier.

Notes. Standard Guild Accord army-issue for siege archer corps
Aperture Wound Ichor
Battlefield Compress · T3 · [Ap] Aperture + [El] Life





















WellspringPhreatis (Medium)Second WellspringVerdantiaOperationDissolution
Ingredients. Phreatis tide-ichor; crushed elderwood sap; boiled compress-linen
Method. Soak the linen in tide-ichor and sap at body-heat, never boiling, and apply directly to an open wound within the first minute of injury
Effect. Holds a wound open at a controlled width rather than sealing it, letting poison, infection, or foreign Essence drain freely for as long as the compress stays wet, at the cost of ordinary blood loss continuing unchecked
Risk. Left on too long, the wound forgets how to close on its own and requires a second alchemical intervention to seal
How it works.

The idea. Memory as deep water. What is lived sinks in, is built into you, and comes back long after the weather has changed. Verdantia’s idea is folded in (growth without end, a self with no final size, which feeds on simply being out in the world. It comes through accumulation rather than rupture, one good day on top of another).
The operation. Dissolution. What is lived is taken down into the deep water and held there in solution, to be given back whole long after.
In the maker. [Ap] Aperture + [El] Life fix what it may do, and the bench work keeps the dissolution going until the maker’s hold on the idea sets in the matter, so it does: holds a wound open at a controlled width rather than sealing it, letting poison, infection, or foreign Essence drain freely for as long as the compress stays wet, at the cost of ordinary blood loss continuing unchecked.
Price. The maker’s reserve at the bench; the Risk line is the taker’s price.
Flaw. Deep water does not ask what is sinking into it. Whatever is lived goes down and is built in, and nothing can be fished back out of it later on its own, so a falsified memory comes back up as readily as a true one.
The Measurewrights’ line. Long-term potentiation on the one reading.

Notes. Battlefield medics’ answer to venom and Essence-corruption wounds where sealing the wound seals the poison in with it
Grace Fall Draught
Liquid Tonic · T3 · [Grs] Grace + [Vor] Return





















WellspringAbsolution (Spirit)Second WellspringSomnalisOperationSeparation
Ingredients. Absolution dew gathered only at a fall from height that didn’t kill the gatherer; Somnalis return-salt; clarified honey
Method. Distill the dew over low heat until it thickens, then cut with return-salt at the exact temperature the honey stops steaming
Effect. For the duration, a fall the drinker takes redistributes its own momentum through the body rather than concentrating at the point of landing, turning what would be a broken leg into a hard bruise
Risk. The redistribution has to go somewhere; repeated falls in a single dose’s window compound the deferred damage into one late, catastrophic reckoning
How it works.

The idea. Forgiveness. A soul’s history stays and its shape stays, and the old poison stored in them is let out. Somnalis’s idea is folded in (living among what might be, the near possibilities of the Plane of Fate held in view at once, each with its odds on it, and a soul at ease in the not knowing).
The operation. Separation. The old poison is parted from the history that stored it, and the history is left whole.

Ingredients. Obsidian-glacier dust; void-ash; rendered fang-oil from a cold-blooded predator
Method. Grind the obsidian dust and void-ash together under moving water, never still, until the mixture stops reflecting light entirely
Effect. Introduced to the bloodstream, numbs sensation outward from the wound in a slow creeping void rather than causing pain, so the victim often doesn’t register the severity of the injury until well past the point of safe intervention
Risk. Handled bare-handed, numbs the poisoner’s own fingers first, a warning sign as often ignored as heeded
How it works.

The idea. Freedom in the air. The world read as a set of open ways, so that moving becomes a matter of noticing which way is already open. Nihiloth’s idea is folded in (the hollow law, power by negation: the rule itself unmade, and what stands in the gap).
The operation. Sublimation. The soul is made volatile, so that it rises and goes by whatever way already lies open.
In the maker. [ObsG] Obsidian-Glacier + [Vn] Void fix what it may do, and the bench work keeps the sublimation going until the maker’s hold on the idea sets in the matter, so it does: introduced to the bloodstream, numbs sensation outward from the wound in a slow creeping void rather than causing pain, so the victim often doesn’t register the severity of the injury until well past the point of safe intervention.
Price. The maker’s reserve at the bench; the Risk line is the taker’s price.
Flaw. Freedom in the air goes by whatever way is already open, and it has no say in which way that is. Lean on it too long and the practitioner follows the open way instead of the intended line, and arrives somewhere efficient that is not where they meant to be.
The Measurewrights’ line. Vector fields and the Lorentz force.

Notes. The signature poison of Cymorath contract-killers, prized because the victim frequently keeps fighting past when they should have stopped
T6 · Master
Anamnesis Draught
Memory Catalyst · T6 · [AnMa] Anamnesis + [Mn] Mnemonic





















WellspringAnamnesis (Medium)Second WellspringEidolynOperationSeparation
Ingredients. Dreamstone powder; memory-glyph water (filtered through [Ar] Archive inscription); Titan-blood derivative (trace)
Method. Dissolve at dusk; bind with [Ne] Thread glyph etched in silver; must be consumed before sunrise
Effect. Unlocks all suppressed or sealed memories across Temperance stages; used in Dream Oath ceremonies
Risk. Total recall without preparation causes soul-fracture; requires a Weave-Keeper to hold the memory net
How it works.

The idea. Remembrance. Everything keeps its past, and a soul under this lens can touch a thing and read it. Eidolyn’s idea is folded in (the shaping mind, a thing imagined so hard that it stands up and has to answer for itself).
The operation. Separation. The past a thing has kept is parted from it and read, as the residue is parted from the vessel that held it.
In the maker. [AnMa] Anamnesis + [Mn] Mnemonic fix what it may do, and the bench work keeps the separation going until the maker’s hold on the idea sets in the matter, so it does: Unlocks all suppressed or sealed memories across Temperance stages; used in Dream Oath ceremonies.
Price. The maker’s reserve at the bench; the Risk line is the taker’s price.
Flaw. Everything keeps its past, and the reading becomes part of that past the moment it is made. A careless hand laid on the record writes itself over what it came to read, so a careless practitioner erases the record in the act of taking it.
The Measurewrights’ line. Remanent magnetization and thermoluminescent dosimetry.

Notes. Sacred to Varn Dream-Forged Dwarves; restricted by Vault-Thane Rhovar Embermind
Skyfire Pulse Vial
Volatile Reagent · T6 · [Wy] Motion + [Ra] Flame





















WellspringIgnivale (Wild)OperationCalcinationTitanOmnis
Ingredients. Condensed plasma drawn during an actual Skyfire Pulse event; dragon-scale ash; distilled cloud-water
Method. Must be bottled within one hour of a Pulse or the charge disperses
Effect. Uncorked, releases a controlled burn that purges Essence impurities from a wound or ward without harming healthy tissue.
Risk. Extremely rare and unstable; a bottled Pulse left uncorked too long detonates outward instead of burning clean.
How it works.

The idea. The spark. The smallest beginning that goes on to pay for itself, so that the gap between wanting a thing and doing it closes to almost nothing.
The operation. Calcination. One point of fire is set to the work at the first degree, and the burning is left to pay its own way.
In the maker. [Wy] Motion + [Ra] Flame fix what it may do, and the bench work keeps the calcination going until the maker’s hold on the idea sets in the matter, so it does: uncorked, releases a controlled burn that purges Essence impurities from a wound or ward without harming healthy tissue.
Price. The maker’s reserve at the bench; the Risk line is the taker’s price.
Flaw. With the gap between wanting and doing closed, the soul has no moment left in which to decide. Any stray feeling in the room is beginning enough, and the working fires without the practitioner having decided to fire it.
The Measurewrights’ line. Minimum ignition energy and the activation barrier.

Notes. Prized by dragonkind physicians; nearly extinct since the “sleeping age.”
Verdance Reclamation Draught
Liquid Tonic · T6 · [Vael] Renewal + [Ma] Recall





















WellspringRebirthine (Wild)OperationFermentationTitanFlorwyn
Ingredients. Root-sap from a grove that has died and regrown at least three times; ash from the same grove’s first death
Method. Brewed across a full Temperance-stage transition (weeks to months)
Effect. Transfers an incomplete Temperance path from a dying practitioner into a chosen successor.
Risk. Inheritance is not selective; the successor may also inherit grief, trauma, or unfinished obsessions along with the path.
How it works.

The idea. The cycle. Loss taken as the first step of the next building, what is broken down paying for what comes up.
The operation. Fermentation. What is broken down is let rot so that what comes up next can feed on it.
In the maker. [Vael] Renewal + [Ma] Recall fix what it may do, and the bench work keeps the fermentation going until the maker’s hold on the idea sets in the matter, so it does: transfers an incomplete Temperance path from a dying practitioner into a chosen successor.
Price. The maker’s reserve at the bench; the Risk line is the taker’s price.
Flaw. The cycle pays for every building with a loss, and with nothing outside to break down it breaks down the worker. It eats structure faster than it rebuilds, and it does not recognize the point at which there is nothing left to spend.
The Measurewrights’ line. Apoptosis and autophagy.

Notes. The alchemical basis of Florwyn’s “Cycle of Green Flame.”
Somnum Flow Ampoule
Sealed Vapor · T6 · [Ka] Dream + [Vl] Veil





















WellspringOneirion (Spirit)OperationSublimationTitanNysera
Ingredients. Condensed vapor from the Somnum Flow’s harmonic pool; dreamstone dust; a lock of the intended subject’s hair
Method. Sealed unopened for a full lunar cycle before use
Effect. Released near a sleeping subject, lets a trained dreamwalker enter their self-image directly rather than merely observing their dreams.
Risk. The dreamwalker’s own self-image is equally exposed and malleable for the ampoule’s duration.
How it works.

The idea. Dream as a place. Work done in the space of what can be thought, reaching a soul where no line of sight runs, because no soul was ever in the room.
The operation. Sublimation. The working is lifted off every bench into the space of what can be thought, and comes down again in a soul.
In the maker. [Ka] Dream + [Vl] Veil fix what it may do, and the bench work keeps the sublimation going until the maker’s hold on the idea sets in the matter, so it does: released near a sleeping subject, lets a trained dreamwalker enter their self-image directly rather than merely observing their dreams.
Price. The maker’s reserve at the bench; the Risk line is the taker’s price.
Flaw. A dream is a place with no ground under it, and nothing done there knows where it is in a room. A working that was true in the space of what can be thought lands nowhere in particular when it has to come down into a real one.
The Measurewrights’ line. Configuration space.

Notes. Restricted; classified alongside Anamnesis Draught by Vault-Thane Rhovar Embermind.
Crevice-Glass Shard
Solid Reagent · T6 · [Uur] Disruption + [Vorn] End





















WellspringFractura (Wild)OperationSeparationTitanValmir
Ingredients. Floating crystal slabs harvested directly from the Wellspring of Collapse, cooled under total silence
Method. Must be cut, never broken, or the stored collapse triggers early
Effect. Embedded in a structure or wound slated for controlled demolition or amputation, guarantees a clean, purposeful failure rather than a chaotic one.
Risk. Cutting it wrong releases the collapse instantly and indiscriminately.
How it works.

The idea. The breaking point. Everything has a place where it will go, and this lens shows it to you, in bridges, in friends and in your own left wrist.
The operation. Separation. A thing is parted along the one place where it was always going to part.
In the maker. [Uur] Disruption + [Vorn] End fix what it may do, and the bench work keeps the separation going until the maker’s hold on the idea sets in the matter, so it does: Embedded in a structure or wound slated for controlled demolition or amputation, guarantees a clean, purposeful failure rather than a chaotic one.
Price. The maker’s reserve at the bench; the Risk line is the taker’s price.
Flaw. The lens shows where everything will go, and it cannot leave its bearer out of everything. Under strain a Fractura practitioner reads their own breaking points with perfect clarity, at the worst possible moment.
The Measurewrights’ line. Linear elastic fracture mechanics.

Notes. Favored by siege-breakers and battlefield surgeons alike.
Pyric Refinement Ash
Powder Catalyst · T6 · [Ra] Flame + [Asa] Creation





















WellspringExuroth (Wild)OperationCalcinationTitanPrometheus
Ingredients. Ash from the Pyric Heart’s outermost cooled crust; a fragment of something the alchemist genuinely regrets
Method. Burned once, at full honesty, or the ash refuses to form
Effect. Applied to a soul fragment or corrupted Trait, burns away what is false or unworthy, leaving only what deserves to persist.
Risk. The process cannot distinguish sentiment from falsehood; it burns cleanly, but not kindly.
How it works.

The idea. The trial by fire. Power comes only through ordeal, plunged and reheated and plunged again, until the soul holds a hardness no gentle road could have given it.
The operation. Calcination. The soul is burned, plunged and burned again, until only the hardness that lives through the fire is left.
In the maker. [Ra] Flame + [Asa] Creation fix what it may do, and the bench work keeps the calcination going until the maker’s hold on the idea sets in the matter, so it does: applied to a soul fragment or corrupted Trait, burns away what is false or unworthy, leaving only what deserves to persist.
Price. The maker’s reserve at the bench; the Risk line is the taker’s price.
Flaw. The trial gives hardness only to a soul that lives through it, and the idea cannot tell an ordeal from a ruin. Plunge again too soon, without the rest between, and the soul comes out hard, brittle and split along the lines of its own trials.
The Measurewrights’ line. Quench and temper.

Notes. The alchemical seed of Prometheus’s own myth, “he who burns the false.”
Fossil Ring Dust
Powder Catalyst · T6 · [Cro] Cycle + [Len] Line





















WellspringLethegraal (Spirit)OperationDissolutionTitanChronaeus
Ingredients. Fossilized ‘dead seconds’ harvested from the Fossil Ring, ground fine; star-salt
Method. Sealed in twin ampoules; must never be opened simultaneously
Effect. Sprinkled on a stalled conflict or stagnant era, accelerates it toward its historical resolution, for good or ill.
Risk. Repeated use on the same Domain draws Chronaeus’s direct attention, and his attention is never gentle.
How it works.

The idea. The cup. Time’s mercy hurried along: old pain settles on its own schedule, and no hand chooses what falls.
The operation. Dissolution. Old pain is loosened into the soul on its own schedule until nothing of it is left but plain structure that holds weight.
In the maker. [Cro] Cycle + [Len] Line fix what it may do, and the bench work keeps the dissolution going until the maker’s hold on the idea sets in the matter, so it does: Sprinkled on a stalled conflict or stagnant era, accelerates it toward its historical resolution, for good or ill.
Price. The maker’s reserve at the bench; the Risk line is the taker’s price.
Flaw. The cup can hurry time’s mercy and cannot choose where the settling stops, because no hand chooses what falls. Hurry it too far and the old pain does not come to rest but swings past it on every cycle, and the practitioner rocks back and forth rather than settling.
The Measurewrights’ line. Relaxation time.

Notes. Blamed for several suspiciously “short centuries” in the historical record.
Pressure Burst Capsule
Combat Alchemical · T6 · [Prc] Pressure + [Clp] Collapse





















WellspringSublimare (Wild)Second WellspringFracturaOperationDistillation
Ingredients. Sublimare pressure-glass; rupture-quartz shavings; sealed vacuum-wax
Method. Blow the glass thin enough to hum under a fingernail’s tap, pack the shaving core, and seal the vacuum before the glass cools past clarity
Effect. On impact the capsule collapses inward before rebounding outward in a single violent pulse, a fist-sized void that punches dents through plate and ceramic alike without the wide blast radius of a Thundercrack
Risk. Capsules blown even slightly too thick fail to collapse at all and simply shatter as glass; too thin and they collapse in the maker’s own hand
How it works.

The idea. Purification by rising. What is light goes up, what remains is purer, and the soul goes on refining itself toward one clear thing. Fractura’s idea is folded in (the breaking point, everything has a place where it will go, and this lens shows it to you, in bridges, in friends and in your own left wrist).
The operation. Distillation. What is light in the soul is driven up and parted from what stays, and what stays is purer each time.
In the maker. [Prc] Pressure + [Clp] Collapse fix what it may do, and the bench work keeps the distillation going until the maker’s hold on the idea sets in the matter, so it does: on impact the capsule collapses inward before rebounding outward in a single violent pulse, a fist-sized void that punches dents through plate and ceramic alike without the wide blast radius of a Thundercrack.
Price. The maker’s reserve at the bench; the Risk line is the taker’s price.
Flaw. Rising parts only what rises differently, and some faults rise exactly as the soul does. Refining against one never ends: the practitioner runs the column indefinitely against something that goes up with every breath of them and will not be left behind.
The Measurewrights’ line. Fractional distillation.

Notes. Prized by duelists against heavily armored opponents where a wide-area weapon would be disqualifying
T7 · Grandmaster
Null-Essence Draught
Inverted Reagent · T7 · [Thru] Hollow + [Au] Death





















WellspringNihiloth (Wild)OperationDissolutionTitanZar’thuun
Ingredients. Absorbed starlight from the rings around the Wellspring of Dread; void-salt; a name willingly forgotten
Method. Brewed in absolute dark; must never be named while brewing
Effect. Absorbs overaccumulated Essence from a person, place, or artifact into null-space, cleansing overcharge without violence.
Risk. Absorbs small memories from everyone nearby along with the excess Essence; the mercy and the erasure are the same act.
How it works.

The idea. The hollow law. Power by negation: the rule itself unmade, and what stands in the gap.
The operation. Dissolution. The rule itself is loosed until nothing of it is left, and the gap is left standing where it was.
In the maker. [Thru] Hollow + [Au] Death fix what it may do, and the bench work keeps the dissolution going until the maker’s hold on the idea sets in the matter, so it does: absorbs overaccumulated Essence from a person, place, or artifact into null-space, cleansing overcharge without violence.
Price. The maker’s reserve at the bench; the Risk line is the taker’s price.
Flaw. A rule unmade is unmade for everyone, and the idea has no way to spare its maker. Everything the practitioner brought inside is subject to the same gap, including the parts of themselves they were relying on.
The Measurewrights’ line. Destructive interference and the null field.

Notes. Considered psychological warfare by the Accord ethics board when used on the living.
Stillwater Draught
Frozen Tonic · T7 · [Vor] Return + [Cro] Cycle





















WellspringCymorath (Wild)OperationSublimationTitanVohrin
Ingredients. Water drawn from the Stillwater Core itself, motionless and perfectly reflective, never allowed to move again once drawn
Method. Transported without a single ripple or the effect fails
Effect. Holds a wound, curse, or dying practitioner in perfect stasis, neither worsening nor healing, until deliberately released.
Risk. Held too long, the subject forgets their own purpose for living, per Vohrin’s law.
How it works.

The idea. Freedom in the air. The world read as a set of open ways, so that moving becomes a matter of noticing which way is already open.
The operation. Sublimation. The soul is made volatile, so that it rises and goes by whatever way already lies open.
In the maker. [Vor] Return + [Cro] Cycle fix what it may do, and the bench work keeps the sublimation going until the maker’s hold on the idea sets in the matter, so it does: holds a wound, curse, or dying practitioner in perfect stasis, neither worsening nor healing, until deliberately released.
Price. The maker’s reserve at the bench; the Risk line is the taker’s price.
Flaw. Freedom in the air goes by whatever way is already open, and it has no say in which way that is. Lean on it too long and the practitioner follows the open way instead of the intended line, and arrives somewhere efficient that is not where they meant to be.
The Measurewrights’ line. Vector fields and the Lorentz force.

Notes. Last-resort battlefield stabilizer; overuse is considered a mercy killing by another name.
