races--and--peoples/the-peoples/draconic.title: Draconic Kind — The Dragons of Drakyssia
races--and--peoples/the-peoples/draconic.content:
Draconic Kind





















TypeMajor Race · Spiritual-Biological Race FamilyOriginThe ancient flame-realms, long before the rise of the Draconic Empire of DrakyssiaSpiritual lineageThe primordial flameborn creation of the Titan Omnis, later diversified through draconic evolution, Crystal mutation, Dragon Bond culture and regional adaptation
Draconic Kind is the family name for every dragon people of the burning south: from the near-extinct Salamanders at its root to the Bonded Mortals who share a dragon’s soul. Their Essence does not express as simple elemental affinity. It carries breath, scale, wing, instinct, territory and ancestry as structural qualities, so that a dragon’s fire is never just fire; it is its bloodline and its claim to the ground.
Soul Architecture
Path. Draconic Kind lean overwhelmingly on the Body Path: scale density, breath organs, wing-force, physical dominance and long-lived biological architecture. The Spirit Path rises in the Dragon Bond, the ancient dragons, Hydra and Western Dragons, and the ritual castes. The Fate Path shows in the Bond, ancestral reverence, egg rites, territorial oaths and sovereign bloodlines.
Body Mastery. Read from Level, and unread below Glory: I (Muridic) at Glory, II (Harmonic) at Refraction and III (Resonant) at Transcendence for most mature dragons. Lesser draconic beings settle at I–II; greater dragons, Hydra Dragons, Western Dragons and truebloods, who pass Transcendence, regularly reach III (Resonant) and, from Realization, IV (Luminous), and the few who climb to Emanation reach V (Radiant). A rare ancient, Salamander, Dragon-Salamander Mutant or Dragon Sovereign candidate may come to hold its rung Inverted under extreme pressure.
Crystal’s look. Clouded through Faceted and Fire for common mature dragons; ancient dragons, Hydra Dragons and Mutants can reach Flawless. Draconic Crystals most often fracture at breath awakening, territory recognition, first Bond contact, the first alpha challenge, and the egg-protection crisis.
Temperance
Dragons climb fast early, through physical pressure, territorial conflict, flight mastery and breath awakening. They stall when instinct overpowers doctrine.





















StageWhat it looks like in a dragonV · SplinteringCommon during first dominance challengesVIII · TranscendenceArrives when territory, Bond or bloodline becomes worth more than survival aloneXI · DissonanceHoard madness, territorial obsession, Bond corruption, alpha collapse, or ancestral identity overload
Typical ceiling: Stage VI–VIII, by subspecies. Hits like a beast of Grade: B–A for most mature draconic races; SS for the greater subspecies; EX for ancient exceptional branches.
Stats
A Primary is the sum of its eight Sub-Stats, and the card keeps the total. The family lean below shapes which Sub-Stats come easily; each subspecies adjusts it.



























































PrimaryLeanSignature Sub-StatsWeak pointsVitality++++Fortitude · Constitution · Tolerance—Ardency+++Flux · Cascade · Density—Dominion+++Gravity · Radius · Sovereignty—Harmonics++Axis · StabilityEmpathy outside the broodResilience++Persistence · FortificationWard, unless Void-adaptedTempering++Maturity · YieldClarity, when instinct runs hotDexterity+Celerity in flightEvasion and Feint in the heavy breedsGnosisVaries—Fluency in non-scholarly breeds; Western Dragons and Wyrms run far higher
Metaphysical Identity
Wellsprings:





















































WellspringWhat it does for a dragonSolfataraVolcanic flame, molten pressure, heat endurancePyraeonThe ember that stays lit; the current of the Ember Crown at Kra’VorrakCataclysmDestructive dragonfire and battlefield devastationMonolithionScale density, fortress bodies, draconic anchoringChthonicaAncient earth, caves, catacombs, deep nestsMateria PrimordiaPhysical supremacy and the law of draconic massAnima SpirareLife-breath, the Dragon Bond, egg ritesTransferenceBond synchronization and dragon-rider resonanceJudiciumAlpha verdict, sovereign legitimacy, bloodline judgmentFixatioScale hardening, lair stabilization, defensive nestsLuminalisRare noble dragons: oath-light and ancestral recognition
Parun glyphs. Draconic chains favor breath, blood, wing, flame, scale, oath and territory: [Ra] Flame, [Leth] Blood, [Th] Foundation, [RenB] Boundary, [Vo] Voice, [Ma] Recall and [Lei] Binding. Glyphs of absolute silence, anti-birth or anti-bond often backlash.
Traits wake as breath mutations, scale authority, territorial pressure, ancestral memory, wing-force distortion, alpha dominance or Bond resonance. Overgrowth risks: runaway scale expansion, breath-organ rupture, hoard fixation, and instinct-dominance, where the dragon becomes more beast than person.
Domains appear as skies, volcanic fields, ancient nests, treasure caverns, storm territories, blood-red horizons or battlefield pressure zones. Their laws turn on territory, dominance, ancestry, the protection of eggs, sky-right and bloodline legitimacy.
Culture & World
Customs: egg rites, Dragon Bond rituals, ancestor-flame ceremonies, alpha challenges, sky dances, brood protection, battle songs, scale offerings, blood-pool blessings, territorial oaths. Languages: Ancient Draconic, regional Drakyssian dialects, battle-roar command codes, the emotional speech of rider and dragon.
Realms: Kra’Vorrak and the Ember Crown, the Dragon Catacombs, Avo’Kara Sanctum, Dova’Ruun Fortress, the Black Scale Ranges, the Wyrmdeep Cities, the Iron Roosts, the Ember Vaults, the Drakhalis Throne Spire.
Relations. Drakyssia respects strength, bloodline legitimacy, military value and sacred bonds. It sees weak states as future territory, but does not always destroy the cultures it conquers. Humans and Elves may be conquered, allied, married into secondary houses, or bonded. No non-draconic civilization is treated as an equal without overwhelming military, divine or ancestral legitimacy, which is why the Dreadvalis Empire to the north, with its veils, its cold and its grain, is the only power the dragons deal with as a peer.
Historical role. Draconic Kind are ancient embodied sovereignty: the right of wing, scale, flame and blood to shape territory. In the Dragon Empire arc they become a civilization of conquest, ritual, family, bloodline preservation and imperial expansion.
Famous figures: Dova’Kan, Avo’Kan, Gorgi, Mesha, Kain Drakhalis, Scylla, General Vorkesh.
Advantages: massive bodies, long lifespans, breath weapons, scale defense, flight, Bond compatibility, crushing Dominion, strong inheritance. Limitations: instinct overload, territorial obsession, Bond grief, egg-loss trauma, little subtlety in many branches, vulnerability to anti-draconic conceptual weapons, and bloodline decline among the ancient flameborn.
Salamanders — The Primordial Flameborn





















TypeMajor Race · Primordial · Near-ExtinctOriginThe primordial flame-realms, before organized DrakyssiaSpiritual lineageThe first flameborn creation of the Titan Omnis
Salamander Essence is not ordinary fire. It is ancient living flame given body, pressure, endurance and memory. Salamanders are the sacred root of Drakyssian flame authority, and they are dying out.
Soul Architecture
Path. Overwhelmingly Body: immense bodies, heat-proof flesh, breath, flame organs and old-world physical supremacy. Their Spirit shows in ancestral fire-memory and sacred bloodline inheritance.
Body Mastery. III (Resonant) to IV (Luminous), and V (Radiant) for the ancient leaders who climb to Emanation; rare ancients come to hold their rung Inverted under apocalyptic pressure. Even young Salamanders hold higher baseline coherence than lesser dragons.
Crystal’s look. Faceted through Fire and Flawless. Their Crystals are old, heavy and saturated with inheritance. Common fractures: the first volcanic awakening, the first territory oath, the bloodline reproduction crisis, and ancient memory overload.
Temperance
Inherited flame density carries them through Stages I–VI fast. They stall around VIII–IX, when instinct, ancestry and identity become hard to tell apart. At XI · Dissonance, the danger is Primordial Flame Regression: the Salamander stops thinking as an individual and acts as ancient fire wearing flesh.
Typical ceiling: Stage IX–XI; ancient leaders higher. Hits like a beast of Grade: SS–SSS; exceptional ancients EX.
Stats



























































PrimaryLeanSignature Sub-StatsWeak pointsVitality+++++Tolerance · Fortitude · Constitution—Ardency+++++Flux · Depth · Cascade—Resilience++++Persistence · FortificationWard against Void erasureTempering++++Maturity · Yield—Dominion++++Gravity · Sovereignty—Harmonics+++Axis · Stability—Gnosis+Retention (ancestral)FluencyDexterity−—Evasion · Feint · Finesse
Metaphysical Identity
Wellsprings: Solfatara, Pyraeon, Cataclysm, Materia Primordia, Monolithion, Chthonica, Judicium, Anima Spirare. Wellsprings of absolute cold, Void erasure or anti-life silence can destabilize a Salamander body if they get past its Tolerance.
Glyphs: [Ra] Flame, [Leth] Blood, [Th] Foundation, [Ma] Recall, [Vo] Voice, [Cro] Cycle. They resonate with glyphs of flame, origin, blood, breath, mountain and old kingship. [Ra] + [Leth] + [Cro] is the Salamander signature: the fire in the blood comes round again.
Traits: primordial breath, volcanic body reinforcement, living flame blood, heat immunity, territorial pressure, ancestral flame-memory. Overgrowth: runaway body heat, molten organ stress, regression into fire-instinct.
Domains: volcanic worlds, burning mountains, red skies, magma seas, ancient flame temples. Their laws declare that fire is origin, that heat is memory, or that only what endures flame deserves form.
Culture & World
Customs: bloodline preservation, flame-inheritance rites, volcanic nesting, mate-selection rituals, ancient memory recitations, sacred reproduction law. Languages: Ancient Draconic, the Primordial Flame Tongue. Realms: the ancient flame-realms, Zyraxia, the sacred territories of Drakyssia, the volcanic highlands around the Ember Crown.
Relations. Revered by dragons, feared by lesser races, and politically central to Drakyssia, because Salamander blood is rare and getting rarer.
Historical role. Salamanders are the sacred root of Drakyssian flame authority. Their decline drives Dova’Kan and Avo’Kan’s concern over marriage, heirs, succession and the preservation of the line.
Famous figures: Dova’Kan, Avo’Kan, Scylla, the last ancient Salamanders of Zyraxia.
Advantages: extreme fire resistance, immense physical power, ancient inheritance, long life, terrifying breath. Limitations: near-extinction, difficult reproduction, a heavy inheritance burden, and the risk of regression into primordial instinct.
Dragon-Salamander Mutants — Humanoid-Locked Apex Dragons





















TypeHybrid · Mutant · Apex Draconic BloodlineOriginA rare compression mutation between dragon blood and Salamander inheritanceSpiritual lineageThe flameborn line of the Titan Omnis, through unstable draconic hybridization
Their Essence is compressed, not expansive: enormous dragon potential forced into a humanoid or semi-humanoid frame. They are the living bridge between dragon sovereignty and humanoid imperial rule, and the most politically watched beings in Drakyssia.
Soul Architecture
Path. Mostly Body (compressed draconic musculature, heat-proof organs, scale-pattern reinforcement), with a strong Spirit side through the Bond, draconic language and ancestral flame-memory, and a real Fate lean through bloodline destiny and sovereign pressure.
Body Mastery. III (Resonant) to IV (Luminous), and V (Radiant) for the exceptional founders and sovereigns who climb to Emanation, some of whom approach the Inverted mark. Their Aether often flares to a Radiant’s pitch in battle, because the humanoid body works as a compression chamber.
Crystal’s look. Faceted through Fire and Flawless. Their fractures come when the body cannot hold the dragon: breath-channel rupture, scale overgrowth, or rejection of the humanoid frame.
Temperance
They climb through combat pressure and bloodline awakening. At V · Splintering, the body often has to decide whether it is dragon, Salamander or something new. At XI · Dissonance comes Humanoid Shell Rejection: the dragon-self tries to exceed the form the body allows.
Typical ceiling: Stage VIII–X; exceptional founders beyond. Hits like a beast of Grade: S–SSS; rarely EX.
Stats



























































PrimaryLeanSignature Sub-StatsWeak pointsVitality+++++Tolerance · Fortitude—Ardency+++++Compression · Depth · Flux—Dominion++++Sovereignty · Gravity—Harmonics+++Axis · Synergy—Resilience+++Integrity · PersistenceIdentity hardening against form-collapseTempering+++MaturityClarity during mutation crisesGnosis++Analysis · Cognition—Dexterity++Finesse · GrappleFeint · Evasion
Metaphysical Identity
Wellsprings: Solfatara, Cataclysm, Materia Primordia, Anima Spirare, Transference, Judicium, Fixatio, Monolithion.
Glyphs: [Ra] Flame, [Th] Foundation, [Vo] Voice, [Leth] Blood, [Lei] Binding, [Ur] Balance. Glyphs of body, flame, command, breath and bond run strong; anti-form glyphs such as [Thru] Hollow can trigger shell rejection.
Traits: Dragon Force manipulation, dragon command, breath compression, scale awakening, roar authority, Dragon Tongue command. Overgrowth: scale-burn, breath-organ rupture, partial regression to beast.
Domains: draconic warfields, blackened skies, territorial pressure, throne-like flame courts. Their laws turn on compressed dragonhood, the right of conquest, or bloodline survival.
Culture & World
Customs. Sacred and politically dangerous. Their marriages, heirs, bonds and succession are tightly controlled by Drakyssian law. Languages: Ancient Draconic, Imperial Drakyssian. Realms: Kra’Vorrak, the Drakhalis Throne Spire, Avo’Kara Sanctum, Dova’Ruun Fortress.
Relations. Revered by dragons, feared by humans and Elves, and watched closely by the Blood Purity Adjudicators.
Famous figures: Dova’Kan, Avo’Kan, Vaeryx, Kain Drakhalis.
Advantages: humanoid precision with dragon-scale power, high intelligence, terrifying breath, political legitimacy. Limitations: cannot always take full dragon form; reproduction is difficult; mutation instability can cause catastrophic Dissonance.
Trueblood Dragons — The Ancient Full Dragons





















TypeMajor Race · Draconic Apex SpeciesOriginAncient dragon evolution from primordial flame and sky-lineageSpiritual lineageDraconic descent from the Titan Omnis, later diversified by realm, climate and Crystal expression
Truebloods are the mythic backbone of Drakyssia: the great winged dragons of the old stories, whose bodies, breath and memory carry the empire’s military power and its ancestral legitimacy.
Soul Architecture
Path. Body above all (scale, breath, flight, territorial authority), with long memory giving a real Spirit side.
Body Mastery. III (Resonant) to IV (Luminous); ancients exposed to realm fractures or catastrophic wars may come to hold their rung Inverted.
Crystal’s look. Faceted through Fire and Flawless. Fractures usually come with the first flight, the first breath, the first territory claim and the first brood defense.
Temperance
Strong early acceleration through physical growth. Stages VII–VIII often arrive when the dragon claims a territory or forms a major Bond. At XI · Dissonance: territory madness, hoard-identity fusion, or ancestral roar collapse.
Typical ceiling: Stage VIII–X. Hits like a beast of Grade: A–S; ancient alphas SS.
Stats



























































PrimaryLeanSignature Sub-StatsWeak pointsVitality+++++Fortitude · Constitution · Tolerance—Ardency++++Flux · Depth · Cascade—Dominion++++Radius · Gravity · Sovereignty—Resilience+++Persistence · Fortification—Harmonics++Axis · Stability—Tempering++Yield · Maturity—Gnosis+RetentionFluency outside the scholar linesDexterity·Celerity in the airFeint · Finesse
Metaphysical Identity
Wellsprings: Solfatara, Pyraeon, Cataclysm, Monolithion, Chthonica, Materia Primordia, Anima Spirare, Judicium.
Glyphs: [Ra] Flame, [Noq] Wind, [RenB] Boundary, [Vo] Voice, [Leth] Blood, [Ma] Recall.
Traits: breath mutations, territorial dominance, scale hardening, sky command, wing-force manipulation, the ancestral roar.
Domains: skies, mountains, treasure caverns, volcanic horizons, ancient nesting grounds.
Culture & World
Customs: territory claims, brood protection, hoard symbolism, aerial rites, ancestor roars, Dragon Bond selection. Languages: Ancient Draconic and the regional dragon dialects. Realms: Kra’Vorrak, the Black Scale Ranges, the Dragon Catacombs, the high sanctuaries of the Drakhal Spine.
Relations. Dominant within Drakyssia: nobles, soldiers, scholars and sovereign candidates.
Famous figures: Gorgi, the high trueblood alphas, the imperial dragon nobility.
Advantages: great size, breath, flight, scale defense, territorial Dominion. Limitations: pride, hoard fixation, egg grief, vulnerability to anti-dragon law.
Modern Dragons — The Drakyssian Majority





















TypeMajor Race · Draconic SpeciesOriginLater descendants of the ancient dragons, adapted into Drakyssian civilizationSpiritual lineageOmnis-rooted descent, diluted and diversified over generations
Modern Dragons are the empire’s everyday dragons: soldiers, scholars, workers, hatchery defenders and bonded partners. More socially woven into Drakyssia than the ancient truebloods, they trade raw ceiling for reliability.
Soul Architecture
Path. Body first, but with a stronger Spirit and Fate side than truebloods, drawn from military service, Bond culture and civic ancestry.
Body Mastery. I (Muridic) at Glory, their common ceiling; II (Harmonic) at Refraction; III (Resonant) only for those who reach Transcendence. Most never reach trueblood ceilings without exceptional pressure.
Crystal’s look. Clouded through Faceted and Fire. Fractures come with military selection, first breath use, a first failed Bond attempt, or a first brood crisis.
Temperance
Steady rather than explosive. VI · Glory is a common mature ceiling; reaching VIII · Transcendence takes exceptional Bond, war or bloodline pressure.
Typical ceiling: Stage VI–VIII. Hits like a beast of Grade: B–A.
Stats



























































PrimaryLeanSignature Sub-StatsWeak pointsVitality+++Constitution · Fortitude—Ardency++Depth · FluxBreath varies widely between linesHarmonics++Axis · Synergy—Resilience++PersistenceWardTempering++Yield—Dominion++GravityThroneGnosis+Fluency · Retention—Dexterity+Celerity · EconomyFeint
Metaphysical Identity
Wellsprings: Solfatara, Cataclysm, Anima Spirare, Transference, Fixatio, Monolithion.
Glyphs: [Ra] Flame, [Noq] Wind, [Lei] Binding, [Ur] Balance.
Traits: specialized breath, military coordination, Bond receptivity, scale resistance, pack-flight synergy.
Domains: smaller, built on unit loyalty, nest protection, flight lanes or family territory.
Culture & World
Customs: military academies, hatchery rites, ancestor festivals, breath trials, Bond trials. Languages: Drakyssian, with Ancient Draconic for ceremony. Realms: Kra’Vorrak, the Iron Roosts, the cities around the Wyrmdeep, the military hatcheries.
Relations. The majority of Drakyssia’s civic and military dragon population.
Famous figures: the empire’s many dragon nobles and military officers.
Advantages: reliable growth, fit for civilization, breath diversity, Bond compatibility. Limitations: lower ceilings than the ancients; vulnerable to stronger alpha pressure.
Western Dragons — The Scholar-Nobility





















TypeMajor Race · Noble Draconic SubspeciesOriginHigh-altitude lines of the Drakhal Spine, adapted to scholarship, law, architecture and strategic war theorySpiritual lineageOmnis-rooted descent, refined through noble bloodlines
Western Dragons turned Drakyssia from a beast empire into a military civilization with law, memory and continuity. They balance physical power with thought, law, memory and the ethics of the Bond.
Soul Architecture
Path. The rare dragons who lean as much on the Spirit Path as the Body: law, memory, strategy and Bond intelligence alongside scale and breath. Their Fate side shows in noble legitimacy and oath-law.
Body Mastery. III (Resonant) to IV (Luminous). Scholar-nobles often reach IV (Luminous) through disciplined study rather than battlefield pressure.
Crystal’s look. Faceted through Fire and Flawless. Their fractures come from intellectual arrogance, contradictions between oath and law, ancestral memory strain, or failed Bond ethics.
Temperance
They climb through education, oath-law, strategic warfare and Bond theory, and stall when pride stops them adapting. At XI · Dissonance, the danger is Law Hoarding: knowledge becomes possession instead of wisdom.
Typical ceiling: Stage VIII–X. Hits like a beast of Grade: SS–SSS.
Stats



























































PrimaryLeanSignature Sub-StatsWeak pointsVitality++++Fortitude · Constitution—Gnosis++++Analysis · Retention · Cognition · Forecast—Ardency+++Depth · CompressionOverchannel, beside a SalamanderHarmonics+++Attunement · Axis—Dominion+++Radius · Sovereignty—Resilience++Integrity · Continuity—Tempering++Clarity · Maturity—Dexterity+EconomyCelerity, beside a Wyvern
Metaphysical Identity
Wellsprings: Judicium, Luminalis, Anamnesis, Solfatara, Cataclysm, Transference, Materia Primordia.
Glyphs: [Flm] Judic Flame, [Ra] Flame, [Ma] Recall, [Mn] Mnemonic, [Ora] Truth, [Lei] Binding. [Flm] + [Ora] is the Western signature: the fire that burns only what is false.
Traits: law-breath, memory scales, strategic foresight, architectural Domain sense, oath-fire.
Domains: sky-courts, archives of flame, floating citadels, ceremonial battlefields. Their laws concern order, ancestry, judgment, and war as doctrine.
Culture & World
Customs: debate circles, war colleges, ancestral libraries, architecture rites, Bond ethics, law recitation. Languages: Ancient Draconic, High Drakyssian, legal Parunic. Realms: Kra’Vorrak, Avo’Kara Sanctum, the Drakhalis Throne Spire, the high scholar-roosts of the Spine.
Relations. Diplomats, historians, lawkeepers, high officers and noble scholars. Most of Drakyssia’s treaties with the Dreadvalis north were drafted in Western claws.
Famous figures: Gorgi, the noble Western scholars, the imperial flight-marshals.
Advantages: intelligence, noble legitimacy, strong breath, flight, a gift for law-Domains. Limitations: pride, intellectual rigidity, less raw ferocity than Wyverns or Salamanders.
Hydra Dragons — The Many-Souled Ritual Guardians





















TypeMajor Race · Multi-Soul Draconic SubspeciesOriginAn ancient ritual mutation of dragon bloodlines into multi-headed soul structuresSpiritual lineageOmnis-rooted descent, altered by ancestral ritual and Crystal plurality
A Hydra Dragon is many souls in one body. Each head may carry its own Wellspring lens, Crystal tone, personality and breath. Their bodies are massive, but what makes them unique is the coordination of many wills as one.
Soul Architecture
Path. Body and Spirit almost evenly: physically enormous, but defined by multi-soul coordination.
Body Mastery. III (Resonant) to IV (Luminous). Ancient Hydras may come to hold their rung Inverted if their many Crystal structures harmonize instead of fighting.
Crystal’s look. Faceted through Fire and Flawless. Their fractures come from head-disagreement, conflicts between soul-axes, grief splitting, and one head outgrowing the others.
Temperance
They advance unevenly; one head may reach a threshold long before the rest. V · Splintering is common. At XI · Dissonance comes the Head Sovereignty War, each head fighting to become the true self.
Typical ceiling: Stage VIII–X; rarely XI and beyond. Hits like a beast of Grade: SSS; rarely EX.
Stats



























































PrimaryLeanSignature Sub-StatsWeak pointsHarmonics+++++Axis · Synergy · AttunementStability, when the heads disagreeVitality+++++Hemostasis · Fortitude · Regeneration—Ardency++++Cascade · Flux—Gnosis+++Acuity · Analysis (when unified)—Resilience+++Continuity · PersistenceIntegrity, under internal conflictDominion+++Sovereignty · Radius—Tempering++YieldClarity during internal conflictDexterity·Simultaneous action across the headsFinesse
Metaphysical Identity
Wellsprings: Anima Spirare, Transference, Judicium, Cataclysm, Solfatara, Benediction, Luminalis, Chthonica, and each head’s own.
Glyphs: [Lei] Binding, [Oc] Oculus (sight shared between heads), [Ur] Balance, [Ra] Flame, [Vo] Voice, [Cro] Cycle. Mesha’s threefold-breath chain, [Ra] + [Lei] + [Ur], binds three breaths into one balanced release.
Traits: multi-breath release, shared mind, independent casting by each head, layered perception, multi-axis Bond reinforcement.
Domains: threefold temples, multi-voiced skies, mirrored pools, ritual nests. Their laws turn on many wills acting as one, protection, and shared breath.
Culture & World
Customs: ritual guardianship, egg protection, temple watch, multi-voice chanting, sacred debate between heads. Languages: Ancient Draconic, multi-throat ritual chant. Realms: the Hydra sanctums, the Dragon Catacombs, the sacred nests, Avo’Kara Sanctum.
Relations. Highly respected as ritual guardians and living weapons; their Bonds are held to be spiritually profound.
Famous figures: Mesha, Saloris, the ancient Hydra guardians.
Advantages: many heads, many breaths, strong Bond architecture, redundancy, ritual power. Limitations: internal disagreement, multi-soul Dissonance, personality fracture, hard-won Tempering.
Wyverns — The Aerial Military Class





















TypeMajor Race · Draconic Subspecies · Military Beast-RaceOriginA sky-adapted draconic branch bred and trained for speed, war and aerial dominanceSpiritual lineageOmnis-rooted descent, refined by military breeding and harsh skies
Wyverns are Drakyssia’s aerial cavalry and rapid strike force: speed, wing-force, pack discipline and predatory instinct. They obey the dragons they recognize as higher in the hierarchy, and very little else.
Soul Architecture
Path. Overwhelmingly Body: speed, wing-force, aerial pack discipline, instinct.
Body Mastery. I (Muridic) at Glory to II (Harmonic) at Refraction; those who pass Transcendence reach III (Resonant), and the elite military Wyverns that battlefield pressure carries to Realization may reach IV (Luminous).
Crystal’s look. Clouded through Faceted and Fire. Fractures come with the first military imprint, rider rejection, alpha contests or wing-injury trauma.
Temperance
Fast early progress through flight trials and combat. They may stall at VI · Glory if instinct stays stronger than doctrine. XI · Dissonance is rare but takes the form of Sky Frenzy: the Wyvern attacks anything that violates its flight territory.
Typical ceiling: Stage VI–VIII. Hits like a beast of Grade: B–A; elite alphas S.
Stats



























































PrimaryLeanSignature Sub-StatsWeak pointsDexterity+++++Celerity · Reflex · EvasionGrappleVitality++ConstitutionFortitude, beside the heavier dragonsArdency++Alacrity · Flux—Harmonics++Synergy · Axis—Dominion++Radius—Resilience+Persistence—Tempering+Yield—Gnosis−VigilanceCognition · Fluency
Metaphysical Identity
Wellsprings: Aurevane, Cymorath, Cataclysm, Solfatara, Anima Spirare, Transference.
Glyphs: [Noq] Wind, [Ra] Flame, [Lei] Binding, [Vo] Voice. [Noq] + [Ra] is the dive-strike: wind that carries fire.
Traits: wing-force blades, dive acceleration, storm breath, rider sync, formation instinct, the alpha screech.
Domains: rare; when they appear, storm corridors, hunting skies, wind tunnels, aerial kill-zones.
Culture & World
Customs: flight trials, rider imprinting, spearhost formations, alpha contests, sky-patrol rites. Languages: draconic command cries, rider signals, simplified Ancient Draconic. Realms: the Iron Roosts, the military hatcheries, the high cliffs of the Spine, the wild skies over the Rainsea.
Relations. The heart of Drakyssia’s imperial air force.
Famous figures: General Vorkesh’s Wyvern; the Primal Wyvern Alpha of the North.
Advantages: speed, air superiority, formation combat, rider compatibility. Limitations: a vulnerable underbelly, less durability than true dragons, instinctive frenzy under stress, and half-blindness under the northern veils.
Drakes — The Wingless Fortress Dragons





















TypeMajor Race · Draconic Subspecies · Siege-ClassOriginAn earthbound branch adapted for defense, siege warfare and ground dominanceSpiritual lineageOmnis-rooted descent shaped by stone, pressure and military breeding
Drakes break walls, carry siege engines, hold gates and anchor ground campaigns. They are almost entirely body: armor, weight, impact and the resonance of the earth under their feet.
Soul Architecture
Path. Very nearly pure Body.
Body Mastery. Unread below Glory, which most Drakes never pass; I (Muridic) at Glory. Exceptional war Drakes of Refraction clarify into II (Harmonic), and the rare one past Transcendence into III (Resonant).
Crystal’s look. Clouded through Faceted. Drakes with a Fire Crystal exist but are uncommon. Fractures come from forced siege imprinting, excessive armor growth or earth-channel overload.
Temperance
They climb through physical strain, wall-breaking, siege defense and battlefield survival, and usually stall around Stages IV–VI, where instinct and body density outweigh higher doctrine.
Typical ceiling: Stage IV–VI; exceptional war Drakes VII and beyond. Hits like a beast of Grade: C–B; elite A.
Stats



























































PrimaryLeanSignature Sub-StatsWeak pointsVitality+++++Fortitude · Absorption · Tolerance · Threshold—Resilience++Fortification · Persistence—Dominion++Gravity · Radius—Ardency+DensityLittle breath; earth Essence insteadHarmonics+Stability—Tempering+Yield—Gnosis−−—Fluency · CognitionDexterity−−—Evasion · Celerity · Feint
Metaphysical Identity
Wellsprings: Monolithion, Chthonica, Materia Primordia, Fixatio, Solfatara, Coagulatio, Petralon.
Glyphs: [Grt] Granite, [Th] Foundation, [Ur] Balance, [RenB] Boundary. [Grt] + [Th] is the Drake wall: stone that remembers it was a mountain.
Traits: fortress hide, earth tremor, wall-breaking charge, ground rooting, siege endurance.
Domains: rare; stone bastions, pressure fields, cracked earth, immovable territory.
Culture & World
Customs: siege training, fortress guarding, wall rituals, earth feeding, military harnessing. Languages: Low Draconic, command roars, military signals. Realms: the Drake Wall, the siege yards, the fortress cities, the Dragonstone campaigns.
Relations. Living siege engines and defensive beasts for Drakyssia’s armies.
Famous figures: Avo’Kan’s Drake mount during the western campaign.
Advantages: extreme durability, siege power, earth resonance, loyalty. Limitations: no flight, little subtlety, low speed, vulnerable to mobility.
Wyrms — The Subterranean Oracles and Earthwardens





















TypeMajor Race · Draconic Subspecies · Subterranean Spiritual RaceOriginAn ancient burrowing branch shaped by caves, memory and underground Essence currentsSpiritual lineageOmnis-rooted descent adapted to Chthonica and deep-earth resonance
Wyrms are not just burrowers. They are earth-listeners, memory-readers, tunnel-makers and subterranean oracles, and they give Drakyssia its underground logistics, its prophecy and its command of terrain.
Soul Architecture
Path. The most Spirit-leaning of the dragons, with Body close behind and a real Fate side through prophecy and burial memory.
Body Mastery. I (Muridic) to II (Harmonic) at Refraction; III (Resonant) past Transcendence; ancient oracles who reach Realization may hold IV (Luminous).
Crystal’s look. Clouded through Faceted and Fire. Fractures come with the first deep-earth hearing, prophetic overload, tunnel-collapse trauma, or contact with ancestral burials.
Temperance
They grow through depth, patience and long memory, and can stall when their sense of the underground currents becomes too vast. At XI · Dissonance, the danger is the Buried Self: the Wyrm forgets the surface and identifies only with the memory of the earth.
Typical ceiling: Stage VII–IX. Hits like a beast of Grade: A; ancient oracles S.
Stats



























































PrimaryLeanSignature Sub-StatsWeak pointsGnosis++++Forecast · Analysis · Retention · Perception—Harmonics++++Attunement · Stability—Vitality+++Constitution · Tolerance—Dominion+++Sense · Gravity—Resilience++Continuity · Persistence—Tempering++Maturity · Clarity—Ardency++Density · PenetrationCascadeDexterity−—Celerity · Evasion above ground
Metaphysical Identity
Wellsprings: Chthonica, Monolithion, Anamnesis, Materia Primordia, Phreatis, Fixatio, Judicium.
Glyphs: [Grt] Granite, [Ma] Recall, [Mn] Mnemonic, [Oc] Oculus, [Th] Foundation, [Ur] Balance. [Grt] + [Ma] lets a Wyrm read what a stone remembers.
Traits: earth-memory, tunnel sense, subterranean prophecy, mineral shaping, building underground trade routes, speaking with the buried.
Domains: endless tunnels, underground rivers, fossil cathedrals, memory-stone labyrinths.
Culture & World
Customs: oracle councils, tunnel ceremonies, earthward oaths, burial-memory rites, underground road-building. Languages: Deep Draconic, tunnel-hum resonance, Ancient Draconic. Realms: the Wyrmdeep Cities, the lava tubes of the Black Mother, the underground trade routes, the Dragonstone tunnels, the roots of the Spine.
Relations. Engineers, oracles, earthwardens and road-builders for Drakyssia.
Famous figures: the Wyrmdeep elders, the imperial tunnel-builders.
Advantages: cartography, deep-earth movement, memory, prophecy, underground construction. Limitations: weak in open sky; vulnerable to sound-based tunnel disruption and to anything that severs them from the earth.
Dragonkin — The Mortal-Draconic Blooded





















TypeHybrid · Major Imperial RaceOriginMortal bloodlines carrying draconic inheritance through ancient unions, ritual infusion, or long life inside Dragon Bond societySpiritual lineageOmnis-rooted dragon blood, stabilized in humanoid bodies
Dragonkin are the empire’s elite infantry, captains, ritual guards and ground commanders, and the bridge between Drakyssia’s humanoid peoples and its full dragons. They are fiercely loyal to the Dragon Sovereign.
Soul Architecture
Path. Body first (humanoid technique on draconic biology), with Spirit through military discipline and dragon speech and Fate through imperial loyalty and captain’s oaths.
Body Mastery. Unread below Glory; I (Muridic) at Glory to II (Harmonic) at Refraction, III (Resonant) for those who pass Transcendence; elite captains who climb to Realization through war pressure, Bond proximity or noble blood can reach IV (Luminous).
Crystal’s look. Clouded through Faceted and Fire. Fractures come with scale awakening, breath failure, first exposure to dragon command, or the bloodline rejecting them.
Temperance
They progress well through training and war, and stall when mortal identity and draconic inheritance pull against each other. XI · Dissonance is rare, but can show as Bloodline Supremacy Fever or Scale Overgrowth.
Typical ceiling: Stage VI–VIII; elites IX and beyond. Hits like a beast of Grade: C–A; elite captains S.
Stats



























































PrimaryLeanSignature Sub-StatsWeak pointsVitality++Tolerance · Constitution—Dexterity++Finesse · Economy—Harmonics++Synergy · Axis—Ardency++FluxCascadeResilience++IntegrityWardTempering++MaturityClarity during awakeningsDominion++Sovereignty (captains)ThroneGnosis+Acuity—
Metaphysical Identity
Wellsprings: Anima Spirare, Transference, Solfatara, Cataclysm, Fixatio, Judicium.
Glyphs: [Ra] Flame, [Leth] Blood, [Vo] Voice, [Ur] Balance, [Flm] Judic Flame.
Traits: scale patches, heat resistance, flashes of dragon-eye, command receptivity, claw growth, breath sparks, Dragon Force channeled through weapons.
Domains: uncommon; battlefield formations, oath-circles, shield walls, flame banners.
Culture & World
Customs: military service, captain’s oaths, scale markings, bloodline trials, dragon-speech training, ritual loyalty to the Dragon Sovereign. Languages: Drakyssian, Ancient Draconic military phrases. Realms: Kra’Vorrak, the military barracks, the Dragonstone garrisons, the Iron Roosts, and the fortresses of the Twilight March facing north.
Relations. The bridge between the humanoid peoples and the full dragons; deeply loyal to Drakyssia.
Famous figures: Avo’Kan’s Dragonkin captain and his fifteen soldiers in the Dragonstone campaign.
Advantages: strong bodies, weapon skill, command discipline, draconic resistance. Limitations: bloodline instability, weaker than true dragons, susceptible to stronger draconic hierarchy pressure.
Bonded Mortals — The Dragon-Bonded





















TypeOther · Spiritual Bond-State · Cross-Racial ClassificationOriginThe sacred Dragon Bond ritual, or natural mutual recognition between a mortal and a dragonSpiritual lineageThe Dragon Bond doctrine of Drakyssia: communion through a shard of Soul Crystal shared between dragon and mortal
A Bonded Mortal is not a race but a state: a mortal of any people whose soul is joined to a dragon’s through a living Axis. They are the diplomatic and spiritual bridge between Draconic Kind and everyone else. They keep their original lens, and take on the color of their dragon’s.
Soul Architecture
Path. The Bond pulls them toward the Spirit Path, because it creates a living Axis between two souls, and deepens their Fate layer through shared fate, oath and emotional recognition. Their original Body lean remains.
Body Mastery. Unread below Glory; after the Bond stabilizes, I (Muridic) at Glory to II (Harmonic) at Refraction, III (Resonant) for those who pass Transcendence; exceptional bonded champions whom dragon resonance carries to Realization may reach IV (Luminous).
Crystal’s look. Clouded through Faceted and Fire. Fractures come with shard integration, the first shared pain, injury to the dragon, forced Bond corruption, and the dragon’s death.
Temperance
They often surge right after bonding, then stall while integrating the shard. At V · Splintering the mortal may lose track of which instincts are theirs and which are the dragon’s. At XI · Dissonance comes Bond Eclipse: the mortal can no longer tell their will from their dragon’s.
Typical ceiling: Stage VI–VIII; exceptional riders IX and beyond. Hits like a beast of Grade: C–A; elite bonded riders S.
Stats



























































PrimaryLeanSignature Sub-StatsWeak pointsHarmonics+++++Axis · Synergy · EmpathyThe Bond Axis is their defining advantageArdency++Flux · Alacrity—Tempering++YieldClarity during shard overloadGnosis++Perception · ForecastShared senses sharpen bothVitality++Tolerance—Dexterity++Evasion · Reflex—Resilience++IntegrityWard, while the Bond is immatureDominion++SovereigntyCommand weight borrowed from the dragon
Metaphysical Identity
Wellsprings: Transference, Anima Spirare, Judicium, Solfatara, Cataclysm, and their dragon’s own.
Glyphs: [Lei] Binding, [Oc] Oculus, [Vo] Voice, [Ur] Balance, [Ra] Flame. [Lei] + [Oc] is the rider’s first lesson: see what your dragon sees.
Traits: shared senses, borrowed dragon strength, a partial scale aura, rider-breath techniques, emotional command, crisis synchronization.
Domains: shared skyfields, twin-heart flames, rider-and-dragon battle circles, oath-bound territories.
Culture & World
Customs: Bond trials, permission to enter the Catacombs, mutual oath recitation, dragon-chosen legitimacy, and shame laws around a dragon’s death. Languages: their own tongue, Drakyssian, Bond-emotion speech, Ancient Draconic commands. Realms: the Dragon Catacombs, the Aetherrider Corps, Kra’Vorrak, the Bond-rider academies.
Relations. Revered if naturally bonded, shamed if the Bond was forced, and politically useful as bridges between Drakyssia and the peoples it conquers.
Famous figures: the Drakyssian Aetherriders, bonded champions, the mortal-dragon heroes still to come.
Advantages: shared power, dragon senses, rapid growth, an emotional Axis, aerial combat. Limitations: Bond grief, the shame of a dragon’s death, incomplete forced Bonds, identity bleed.

Read beside this. The Geography of the Outer World, for the land; The Ten Great Houses of Drakyssia, for the House system; The Draconic Lineage, for the wild lines that share these names.

races--and--peoples/the-peoples/the-ashk.title: The Ashkaru
races--and--peoples/the-peoples/the-ashk.content:
“Bairos did not name them what they were. He named them what they were for. Ask what changed.”
margin note, unsigned, found in the Ledger of the Stone Choir’s deep archive

A peddler called Clem Pennywhistle sold Abbot Aldhelm Mereth of Saltmere a paperweight in the spring of 588 IC: a lump of gray-blue stone the size of a child’s head, smooth as a river cobble, shaped a little too much like a jaw, dug out of a dead battlefield up on the Marrow Fells, and his for four silver and a cheese. The abbot set it on the scriptorium table to hold down the charters. Inside a month the copyists of Saltmere had stopped making mistakes. Slipped lines came back in the night, in a hand none of them owned, in ink as red as a cut. Misnumbered columns put themselves right. The monks rang the bells, roasted an ox and told the whole valley, and pilgrims came with their family registers under their arms and paid in gold to leave them on that table overnight.
Then the stone reached the land charter, which said the abbey ran to the river. The boundary stones said otherwise, as the abbey had been hoping nobody would notice for two hundred years. On Midsummer morning the boundary stones stood in the river, and Sir Aldous Wrenfield’s best orchard, in full pink blossom, stood on abbey land, with his steward up one of the trees, screaming. Wrenfield sued. The abbey won, on the plain ground that every document in the case agreed. And in the same week the infirmary roll, in which some long-dead brother had entered the abbot as having lost two fingers to frostbite, came to the top of the pile, and Abbot Mereth woke with eight fingers and no wound, and a neat seam of darker stone where the two had been. They got it stopped at last with a cuff of plain gold, beaten around it by a goldsmith named Hanne Lund on the guess of a Measurewright named Ysolde Carrow, who could never afterward explain why she had guessed gold. Three later Measurewrights have called the Saltmere stone a dead reading-head, a clever fraud and a mass hysteria. All three declined to borrow it.
Whichever of them is right, here is what the stone was supposed to be a piece of.
Origin
The Ashkaru predate the Planar Separation. They were authored by Bairos, the Scribe, the First Epoch, in the period before the Plane of Soul, the Plane of Fate, and the Material Plane divided into the three-layered architecture the entire magic system now runs on. They were not the first thing Bairos made. They were the last thing he made before making became unnecessary, because the deep text he was writing finished itself once they existed to read it.
The Accord’s register has no entry for them. The Stone Choir’s deep archive holds a single margin note. The Ledger Monks decline to comment and have never explained why, which is the loudest thing the Ledger Monks have ever done.
The Moto are Bara’s children, the First Epoch given human form, the primordial authority made inheritable through Mizuki’s dynastic architecture. The Ashkaru are the older work. Bairos’s instruments before Bara existed. A sibling line to the Moto in the way that a chisel is a sibling to the carpenter’s son: made by the same hand, made first, made for a different kind of labor.
The Deep Text
Before the Planes separated, reality’s grammar was unified. Meaning, structure, and substance had not yet been sorted into three layers. They were a single continuous text, and that text could be read and rewritten by anything equipped to perceive it at the structural level.
The Ashkaru were that equipment.
Interpretation was never the job. The job was transcription and correction: reading the state of the deep text, identifying inconsistencies in its grammar, and rewriting the passage so the inconsistency resolved. Bairos did not trust the deep text to maintain itself. He built instruments that maintained it for him, and he made the instruments alive because dead tools cannot exercise judgment about which inconsistency matters.
This is the foundational fact about the Ashkaru that decides everything else: they were built to edit reality’s source document, and they were given judgment so the edits would be good. The judgment is what made them people. It is also what made Kinjiki possible.
Biology
Mortal anatomists who use the word “body” here are being polite. What the Ashkaru have is a reading architecture that happens to be alive.
The Executor. The central torso: bilateral, muscular, superficially humanoid in its symmetry. This is the part of the Ashkaru that acts on what has been read. Hands, a jaw, a chest cavity dense enough to house the organs that sustain the whole structure. A careless observer takes the torso for the core of the creature. It is the pen, and the core is everything radiating from it.
The Threads. Six serpentine appendages, muscular and scaled, each terminating in an independent head with its own jaw, its own sensory apparatus, and its own rudimentary cognition. These are the parallel reading threads. Each head processes a different strand of input simultaneously. In the pre-Planar period, each strand corresponded to a different layer of the deep text. After the Separation, the six threads lost their native material and began reading whatever was available, which is why an Ashkaru’s perceptive range is so broad and so difficult for any current-system instrument to classify. Assay forks have been known to give up.
The Hide. Dense, mineral-adjacent, the gray-blue of deep basalt, closer to quartzite under compression than to skin over muscle. It does not scar in the conventional sense. Damage is filled by the body’s own crystalline substrate, leaving seams of slightly darker material that a geologist would recognize as veining in metamorphic rock.
The Ears. Elongated, pointed, angled outward. Directional sensing organs, with no decoration about them. They predate any elven morphology and are not related to it, a point on which elves have written at some length.
No Hair. The Ashkaru produce no keratin structures of any kind. The body’s surface is uniform and smooth, interrupted only by the gold sealing hardware and the crystalline veining of old wounds.
Scale. Larger than human. The executor torso stands roughly seven feet at the shoulder before the threads are accounted for. With all six threads extended, the Ashkaru’s total silhouette fills a space most mortal practitioners would classify as environmental.
The Planar Separation and Its Consequence
When the three Planes divided, the deep text ceased to be a single readable document. Its grammar fragmented across three layers: what can be so on the Plane of Fate, meaning on the Plane of Soul, substance on the Material Plane. The unified transcription the Ashkaru were built for became mechanically impossible.
They did not die and they did not degrade. They simply had nothing left to do.
The Soul Crystal system (the organ in which a practitioner refines the Aether of the world into Essence), which emerged from the Plane of Soul’s architecture, was never designed for them. It was fitted afterward, the way you would bolt a saddle onto something that was never a horse. The Ashkaru can operate within the current magic system. They pull Aether and spend Essence like anyone. Their Soul Crystals function. Their Wellspring harmonizations (the sixty types of Aether, and the bond a practitioner forms with one) register. But the works underneath are older than the system classifying them, and the fit is imperfect in ways that no amount of refinement will correct. Call the imperfection a difference of era, and do not waste a career trying to mend it.
The Void Affinity
Every Ashkaru who has been classified under the current system registers on the void end of the Sixty, the Wellsprings of entropy and undoing. This is a post-hoc label. A human practitioner harmonizes with Dissolution or Nihiloth by long work and at some risk. The Ashkaru are what those Wellsprings describe, in the same way that a river is what the word “current” describes. The word came after.
The specific Wellsprings that map to Ashkaru native function:
Dissolution. Unbinding: what no longer serves is allowed to come apart on its own. The Measurewrights call it the entropy of mixing, the preference toward the unbound state. In an Ashkaru, this is the reading thread’s ability to take apart what it perceives. Perception and disassembly are the same action.
Nihiloth. The hollow law, the rule itself unmade and the gap left standing (destructive interference and the null field, in the Measurewrights’ terms). An Ashkaru’s Domain (the territory in which a high-Stage practitioner’s own law holds) imposes nothing. It cancels the law already present. Inside remains the absence of a rule, which is the exact condition the deep text requires to be readable.
Vantabriel. The night that keeps, carrying everything that was lost with none of it put down (near-total absorption and hysteresis, to the Measurewrights). What strikes the Ashkaru is kept rather than reflected. The Crystal’s condition is a function of everything it has ever absorbed. For a being built to read without being read, this is native camouflage: a deep-text scribe that broadcast its own signal would corrupt its own readings.
Oblivara. Keeping your name, a self written down so many times that it cannot be erased (error-correcting redundancy, the Measurewrights say). The Ashkaru identity is redundantly encoded against erasure. For a being designed to edit reality’s source document, being editable in return would have been a structural flaw.
The Sealing Hardware
The gold bands visible in Kinjiki’s configuration are self-imposed control architecture. Each serpent thread, left unsupervised, reverts to its original function: it reads what it perceives, and if the reading reveals an inconsistency, it begins correcting. At Stage XIV, where the Domain and the body are indistinguishable, an unsupervised thread perceives more than a room. It perceives the room’s structural grammar, and it edits.
The bands interrupt the correction cycle without interrupting the reading. They are restraints in the precise sense, suppressing a function and leaving the power where it was. Each gold cuff is a stop set between perception and action, the way a pawl stops a windlass from running back. The chains connecting them distribute the load across the full thread architecture so that no single band bears the entire interruption.
Removing a band does not make Kinjiki stronger. It makes one of his threads autonomous: a parallel reader with its own judgment and no governor, doing to its surroundings what it was built to do to the deep text.
The Distant World
The Ashkaru homeworld has not been named. It exists in the wider cosmology as one of the worlds Bairos touched before the Separation, a place where the deep text was particularly dense, where reality’s grammar required constant maintenance, and where the instruments built to maintain it were given permanent residence.
After the Separation, the world continued. The Ashkaru continued. Their purpose did not. What a race of living editorial instruments does when the document closes is the question their entire post-Separation history answers, and the answer is far from uniform. Some maintained. Some adapted. Some, like Kinjiki, looked at the new arrangement and decided it was a draft.
Known Ashkaru
Kinjiki, The Inversion. Level 500. Stage XIV, Zenith, an Archmaster. The only Ashkaru confirmed present in the current narrative theater. See character entry.

Read next: The Three Paths, for what a lean means; The Sixty Wellsprings, for what their harmonizations are.

races--and--peoples/the-peoples/the-beas.title: The Beastkin and Demihuman Peoples
races--and--peoples/the-peoples/the-beas.content:
Races · Soul Architecture · Languages · Cultures · The Social Reality

Beastkin are a category the Guild Accord inherited and then legislated. The Accord will tell you it invented them, as a kindness.

At the Harrowgate Fair in the summer of 603 IC, under the cherry and cream banners of the horse lines, a Bearkin smith named Orsa Underhill came down from the hills to buy charcoal and took a wrong turn behind the farriers. There were sixty-three people in Cob Rennick’s pens that week, Catkin and Lupine for the most part, and a licensed notice on the post. A Lupine girl of about eleven looked at Orsa through the bars and said nothing at all. Orsa put down her charcoal money, took the pen gate in both hands, lifted it off its hinge-pins, leaned it tidily against the fence, and stood in the gap.
She stood there for three days. Rennick’s hired bravos, three coated men of the Red Bar school in their red and white, broke a dozen ash staves on her by the first noon, and a brawler of real standing, sent for from the next town at some expense, broke his right hand on her jaw while the crowd bought sausage and climbed the farriers’ roofs to see. She never raised a fist. She held her stance with the blood drying black on her apron and her aura the dark green of old fir, and she held it the way her people hold a mountain, and on the second day a Scalebond advocate named Zsalla Underscale walked up in a good coat, citing precedents from memory all the way back to the Second Eon, and began to argue before the Fair Court that a gate was a question of law. On the second night a Catkin pickpocket called Tansy Nightfinger, who had no interest in law, went through the wall of Rennick’s counting tent and came out with every paper he owned. The licensed and documented qualifier, it turned out, cut both ways. With his license and his bills of title in the river, Rennick could not show lawful claim to a single soul in those pens, and on the third morning sixty-three people walked out past Orsa Underhill, between the banners, with the whole fair watching and the minstrels already working on the second verse.
The Court fined her for the gate. A hat went around and paid it twice. Within the year Rennick had papers again, and nineteen of the sixty-three had been caught on the roads and sold, the girl among them, and the Provision reads today exactly as it read that morning. The pens at Harrowgate have had two gates since. Here is the law they hang on, and here are the people it was written about.
What Beastkin Are
The living peoples who fall under this designation (Catkin, Lupine, Bearkin, Fox-Spirit, Serpentkin, and several dozen smaller lineages) share no common origin event, no common spiritual ancestor, and no common metaphysical architecture. What they share is the external feature the Accord used to group them: the presence of non-human biological characteristics alongside functional Aetheric architecture, which is to say a working Soul Crystal, the organ that refines the Aether of the world into Essence.
The formal category exists to solve an administrative problem: what to do with peoples who are too structured to be classified as Spirit Entities, too distinct to be absorbed into the Human taxonomy, and too varied to be given individual lineage recognition. The Third Eon solution was the Beastkin Classification Provision, which created a unified legal category and then subdivided it into free-status, bonded-status, and labor-stock classifications on criteria that the Accord’s own practitioners consider inconsistently applied.

“Those aren’t people, boy. Those are labor stock. Licensed and documented under the Verath Township Labor Provision.”
Darvo, Verath Township. Seventeen gold marks per head. Less than a horse.

The Labor Provision
The Provision classifies beastkin who cannot demonstrate free-holder status through guild membership, a sealed indenture of service, or bloodline recognition as available for labor contracts.

In practice this means a beastkin without current sealed papers can be purchased, held in licensed pens, and sold at Accord-adjacent fairs and markets without the transaction constituting a crime under Accord law in most territories.
Read the licensed and documented qualifier closely, because it protects nobody. It is the mechanism by which the transaction is made legal.
The world has two categories for beastkin: victim or animal. Neither category contains the word person. The Accord wrote that policy down, in a good clear hand, on purpose.

The Beastkin Family



























































LineageUntrained lean · Known forDefinitive StatAccord StatusFeline · CatkinBody, then Spirit · Kinetic ReservoirDexterityContested: often “skilled labor”Lupine · WolfkinBody, then Spirit · Pack-SoulHarmonicsContested: “wild beastkin” provisionUrsine · BearkinBody, then Spirit · Geological EnduranceVitalityGenerally free-status where documentedFox-Spirit · MishiroSpirit, then Fate · Aetheric NoseHarmonicsContested: Spirit-adjacent exemption arguableSerpentkin · ScalebondSpirit, then Fate · Coiling MemoryGnosisScholar-class exemption availableAvian KinBody, then Spirit · Current-ReadingDexterityVariable by territoryAquatic KinSpirit, then Body · Depth-Pressure ResonanceResilienceLargely unclassified: maritime gapChimeric-BornNo fixed lean · Variable ConductorVariableNo coherent policy
The Demihuman Peoples
Demihumans occupy a distinct category: defined by dual-lineage inheritance rather than by non-human biological features.

The distinction matters legally. Demihumans are generally accorded default free-status pending investigation of lineage claims, whereas beastkin default to labor-stock status pending documentation of free-holder status.
This distinction produces meaningfully different lives for the people it classifies.

A note on the columns below, which are the Guild’s measure of what a lineage adds to or takes from a practitioner. Vitality counts for wounds, Ardency for output and the punch through worked armor, Gnosis for knowledge and the read, Dexterity for measure and reaction, Harmonics for attunement and the pull of Aether from the ground, Resilience for what a working does to the Crystal, Tempering for control and how long a working can be pushed, and Dominion for spatial authority and Pressure. An Untrained lean is the tilt a lineage gives the three layers of a soul before anyone has trained it, and it never sets Mastered or Walked (The Three Paths). A Wellspring is one of the sixty types of Aether, each working on the Crystal in its own way. A glyph is a unit of Parunic, the script that writes boundaries onto laws, and a Domain is the territory in which a high-Stage practitioner’s own law holds.
Half-Elves · The Third Path
Emerged during the Harmonial Twilight when Elves and Humans shared Wellspring territories. Born from the spiritual overlap of Elven soul-depth and Human glyph flexibility, not fully either, genuinely both, navigating the friction between two Crystal architectures that were not designed to occupy the same body.
Untrained lean · Spirit 55% / Body 30% / Fate 15%. Both sides of the blood at once, Elven reach and Human adaptability. High conductivity, internal friction as the structural cost.


















































StatModNoteVitality−05Lighter than full-human baseline; not as resilient as Elven longevity architecture. AdequateArdency+10Human adaptive output combined with Elven Inscription yield (η)Gnosis+15Partial Parunic Fluency inheritance. Above human baseline; below Eressean ceilingDexterity+10Elven flow-state influence on movement. Economy elevatedHarmonics+20Dual resonance: both Elven Attunement and Human emotive Harmonics active simultaneously. Fidelity sometimes inconsistent due to internal frictionResilience+05Modest. Spiritual Friction creates specific vulnerability to Ur/Ae glyph misfireTempering+10Clean routing from Elven inheritance; Human adaptive processing adds flexibilityDominion+10Partial Elven Domain Stability inheritance. Domain formation achievable and more stable than full-human baseline

Spiritual Friction: −20% yield for Ur (Balance) and Ae (Order) glyphs; under strain (hurried, or below a quarter of reserve) those glyphs misfire and crack the caster’s Crystal a little.
Rootlessness: neither Elven nor Human communities fully accept them without active negotiation. The political cost of existing between categories is ongoing.

Wellsprings · Aurevane through Elven inheritance. Somnalis through Florwynic lineage trace. Human-compatible Wellsprings fully accessible. Anamnesis occasionally accessible. No Wellspring is fully closed; none is fully native.
Culture · The Harmonic Quarter communities in Altherion and border territories, loud, polyglot, and the best place on the river for a meal you will have to explain to both your families. Often the informal diplomatic bridge between Elven and Human institutions, a function assigned to them rather than chosen by them, with predictable consequences for how they feel about performing it.
Half-Orcs · The Unchained
Born from the intersection of Orcish Stone-Blood and Human glyph-flexibility during the Great Concord Splintering. Anyone who takes them for the weakest expression of either lineage tends to learn better at close quarters. They are a third expression: Stone-Blood’s kinetic inheritance running through a human body that has the glyph-processing capacity the pure Orcish lineage lacks.
Untrained lean · Body 60% / Spirit 30% / Fate 10%. Stone-Blood provides the kinetic expression; Human inheritance provides the structural processing capacity that allows it to be directed rather than just released.


















































StatModNoteVitality+15Stone-Blood mineral deposits and human constitution combined. Below pure Ironblood ceiling, significantly above human baselineArdency+20Kinetic inheritance expressed through human-scale Essence architecture: high relative to body size compared to pure Ironblood, lower in absolute termsGnosis−10Logic-Void influence present but attenuated, since the Human inheritance partially compensates. Perception unaffectedDexterity+05Adequate. Stone-Blood’s mass-over-precision tendency present but the human frame moderates itHarmonics−05Below baseline. Orcish communal resonance architecture is absent without full Stone-Blood saturationResilience+15Stone-Blood Clotting partially present. Hardening and Scarring elevatedTempering−05Overflow elevated: they push past sustainable output the way Ironblood does, but their human Crystal architecture survives it betterDominion+05Sub-bass resonance partial field. Territorial instinct present at reduced expression
Wellsprings · Monolithion partial, accessible without full Ironblood resonance. Solfatara and Exuroth accessible. Human-standard fully accessible. Benediction and Absolution are accessible, which distinguishes them from pure Ironblood and is a significant practical advantage.

Palischuk, the City of the Unchained: a half-Orc mercenary city-state, all banners, contracts and arguments, and the only city I know where a recruiting sergeant is expected to bid. Deep distrust of pure-blood institutions of both lineages. Independent mercenary culture that functions as a practical rather than ideological identity:
They are free because neither side will fully claim them, and they have decided that freedom is the better deal.

Chimeric-Born
Produced through high-level magical grafting, alchemical transmutation, or Soul-Forge processes. Most are crafted, and few are born. Second-generation Chimerics can reproduce through volatile magical inheritance. Their lineage is a fractured mosaic (Fleshshapers, Ascendant Alchemists, failed divine imitations), and some trace partial lineage to primordial beasts whose Essence was harvested.
Untrained lean · Variable, with no fixed distribution. Their souls function as Variable Conductors, capable of containing and channeling contradictory Wellspring qualities simultaneously. This produces unstable or morphic glyph behavior as the structural cost.
No fixed stat modifier set: each has a unique distribution dependent on component lineages. Three universal markers only: Adaptability (resistance to environmental Essence stress), Morphic Instability (variable reliability of complex technique execution), and Binding Scar (the permanent inscription required to prevent physical and spiritual unraveling).

Binding Scars are mandatory. Removal or damage risks catastrophic Crystal and physical dissolution.
Metabolic Tax: maintaining multiple active Traits drains life force. More than four simultaneous active Traits costs 5% of reserve per turn, and at Starvation it draws on the flesh.
The Variable Conductor architecture can channel contradictory Wellspring types simultaneously, which should be impossible and is. The cost is that neither harmonization is clean.

The most politically isolated of the demihuman categories: the Accord has no coherent policy on Chimeric-Born because their existence defies consistent classification. Some receive grudging tolerance through Alchemarch guild protections; most navigate through the same unofficial channels as other unbonded beastkin.
Languages
Beastkin languages are not related to each other in the way human language families share roots. They developed independently, in different ecological and metaphysical contexts, and share structural features only where those features reflect shared soul-architecture rather than shared origin.
What they do share is physicality. Beastkin languages consistently encode more sensory and physical information than human languages encode, and consistently encode less temporal abstraction.
Purrspeech · Catkin
Tonal click-language carried in Catkin vocal cord resonance. Non-Catkin cannot replicate most phonemes without significant modification to their Harmonics architecture.
Purrspeech conveys emotional state through harmonic overlay alongside literal content: a statement said with one emotional register carries a different meaning from the same statement said with another. Outsiders describe conversations in Purrspeech as seeming to contain a second conversation running underneath the first one, which is accurate, and is usually about them.
Moontongue · Lupine
Resonant, multi-tonal, carrying a predatory growl even in neutral speech. Kinpulse runs underneath Moontongue as an emotional channel: pack members receive the emotional context of statements even when the literal content is in a language they do not share.
Moontongue has the highest information density per phoneme of any beastkin language. A six-syllable statement can contain content requiring three sentences in Common to approximate.
Urganic Growlscript · Bearkin
Slow, tonal-rooted, dense. An Urganic conversation contains more information per syllable than most languages contain per sentence, because Urganic phonemes carry geological metaphor as grammatical structure. Every statement implicitly describes both the thing stated and its relationship to enduring reality. Ordering breakfast takes a while.
Urganic is the language in which the Siege of the Seventh Fold memorial tradition is maintained. There is no shorter way to say what it says.
Seraphi-Adjacent · Fox-Spirit / Mishiro
The Mishiro lineage’s tonal whisper-tongue, distinct from pure Seraphi-Tongue. Structured around the nose’s filing architecture: statements carry implicit scent-context, and the most precise expression in the language is a short phrase that means “and I smelled this was true.”
No external documentation of this language exists. The Accord’s linguistic archive has three partial records, all clearly incomplete, none sourced to practitioners who were actually invited to learn it.
Coilspeech · Serpentkin
Patterned tonal language in which temporal context is grammatically mandatory. Every statement includes the speaker’s assessment of when the statement is true in relation to what came before. A statement without temporal anchoring is grammatically incomplete in the same way a sentence without a subject is incomplete in Common.
External practitioners describe this as every conversation having an additional dimension: you are told what is true, and you are told where it sits in the sequence of what has been and what will be.


“The world has two categories for beastkin: victim or animal. Neither category allows for the possibility that I am standing here because I chose to stand here.”
Yoko Mishiro



The Five Beastkin Lineages



Read next: The Three Paths, for what a lean means and never sets; The Trait System, for how a lineage’s powers work; The Tongues of the Realms, for how they sound.
