races--and--peoples/the-peoples/the-beas.title: The Five Beastkin Lineages
races--and--peoples/the-peoples/the-beas.content:
Soul architecture, stat frameworks, metaphysical identity, culture, and historical record for the five documented major lineages.
The Merry Alderman was a fat yellow coasting cog out of Altherion with a cargo of oranges and palm oil, and she went onto the Gannet Rocks in the spring gale of 619 IC with five beastkin in her crew, and the deposition is the best thing in the port archive. The cook, a fox-spirit the crew called Ginger, had come up on deck two hours before the strike to tell the master she could smell old wrecks to leeward, a great many of them, and he had told her to see to the soup. When the hull opened, the Catkin topman Nessa Quickstep came off the mast and was on the first rock before the spar finished falling, and she crossed the black gaps between the rocks with a line in her teeth, appearing a stride ahead of where she had just been, without anyone seeing her get there. The four Tovey brothers, Lupine deckhands, went into the surf together with that line and swam it in one stroke, four bodies keeping one time, while burst jars turned the sea around them the color of a sunrise and ten thousand oranges came bobbing up through it on the swell.
Down in the flooding hold the ship’s carpenter, an old Bearkin named Brannoch, had put his back under the cracked keel-beam, and there he stayed, with the water at his chest and the whole hull working on his spine, for the six hours it took thirty-four people to climb out over him. Somebody had to go down at dawn and tell him he could stop. Out on the rock the purser, a Scalebond notary named Zsevrin, sat with the rain running off his scales and observed that the Bishop’s Daughter had struck here on the same tide two hundred and twelve years earlier, and that the people who went left along the ledge had lived and the people who went right had not, and he said this once, clearly, to anyone who wished to consider it. The master went right, with the strongbox. Young Wil Tovey, torn off the line in the dark and thrown up alone on the far stack, was found at sundown sitting quite still with nothing wrong with him, and told his brothers he had been too quiet for too long, and they carried him home between them.
Then came the salvage court at Altherion, which divided the crew’s share as the sea-law required. Brannoch and Zsevrin were paid. Under the Labor Provision the cook, the topman and the four brothers could show no free-holder papers, and the clerk therefore entered them on the roll with the oranges, as recovered cargo, value to the owner. Zsevrin sealed the record himself, and it is his hand that notes in the margin that he found the ruling clarifying.
Five people, one bad night, and five entirely different souls doing the only thing each of them was built to do. Here are the builds.
On terms. The stat columns are the Guild’s measure of what a lineage adds to or takes from a practitioner: Vitality for wounds, Ardency for output and the punch through worked armor, Gnosis for knowledge and the read, Dexterity for measure and reaction, Harmonics for attunement and the pull of Aether from the ground, Resilience for what a working does to the Crystal, Tempering for control and how long a working can be pushed, Dominion for spatial authority and Pressure. An Untrained lean is the tilt a lineage gives the three layers of a soul before anyone has trained it, and it never sets Mastered or Walked (The Three Paths). Body Mastery sets how much of what a practitioner pulls reaches a working that lands through the Shell. A Wellspring is one of the sixty types of Aether, each working on the Soul Crystal in its own way. A glyph is a unit of Parunic, the script that writes boundaries onto laws. A Trait is a power bound into the soul, and a Domain is the territory in which a high-Stage practitioner’s own law holds. Dissonance is what a soul does when a Stage breaks it instead of raising it.
Feline: Catkin
Shadow-Leap Stalkers · Emotive Kinetics
Descended from the ancient Clawbound Accord formed during the Watcher’s Eclipse. When the celestial lattice first fractured, spirit-leopards and desert nomads fused beneath a period of absolute darkness, trading permanent physical stability for a soul-lattice optimized entirely for reflex and shadow-walking. They are built for the moment between moments.
Spiritual lineage · Nyzara, the Silent Pad. Archonic guardian of foresight and emotional poise, whose heirs inherit her mastery of the blink-space between physical actions and her ability to weaponize stillness before movement.
Soul architecture
In the blood · Their souls function as Kinetic Reservoirs: raw emotion stored in muscle memory, released as Aetheric force through physical acceleration. Where most practitioners channel Aether deliberately, they embody it, and then they move.
Untrained lean · Body 62% / Spirit 38%. Their Aura lays no claim to the space around it. It is the absence of spatial presence, the way a room changes when something very fast has just passed through it.
Body Mastery · unread below Glory; I through IV standard above it, by Stage and Level; V (Radiant) for senior shadow-walkers with sustained Somnalis resonance. Their Body rung tends to read lower than their practical capability because burst, precise, contained output does not saturate ambient Aether the way volume-heavy practitioners do. Assay forks have cost a lot of people a lot of money over this.

Primary fracture point at Stage V Splintering. The emotional reservoir architecture resists the soul cracking open that the Stage requires. Catkin who pass Stage V cleanly tend to pass it violently, and emerge with elevated Domain formation instincts they weren’t expecting.
Stage VII Refraction stall: the Stage requires the soul to perceive itself from outside, which the emotional architecture resists. Catkin at Stage VII frequently mistake the external self-perception for external threat and respond accordingly.
Dissonance expression: the emotional reservoir detonates. A single overwhelming release of accumulated stored emotion that either transforms the practitioner or dissolves them. Survivors describe it as finally feeling something they had been storing for years, all at once.

Stat framework


















































StatModExpressionVitality−15They are built to not be where the force lands, and absorbing it was never the plan. Metabolic Burn: cannot sustain high Ardency output without caloric costArdency+15Emotion-linked kinetic burst. Spike output, with little sustained behind it. Stored emotion released as force in single precise momentsGnosis−20Linear logic structurally suppressed. Perception and Acuity unaffected: the suppression is in building logical chains from what they perceive, and the perceiving itself is untouchedDexterity+25Definitive stat. Shadow-walking is Dexterity at its purest: the ability to be not-there when the attack arrives and there when the response doesHarmonics+15Emotional resonance and shadow-frequency attunement. Chord suppressed: communal harmonics are not their architectureResilience−10Fragile under sustained pressure. Designed for short violent exchanges, not attritionTempering+10Clean kinetic routing. They do not overchannel; the reservoir architecture naturally regulates expenditureDominion+10Shadow-space territory assertion. Sovereignty in darkness contexts above baseline
Sub-stat notes · Celerity and Burst are definitive, the highest single-movement speed of any beastkin lineage. Ardency Alacrity elevated: the emotional reservoir fires faster than deliberate Ardency routing. Resilience Nullity above average: take away the Aether and they still have claws. Harmonics Chord consistently floors. Do not build a team around one. They are a precision instrument. Gnosis Sapience flooring does not suppress tactical intelligence: they make the right call through pattern recognition rather than reasoning, and they are usually faster.
Metaphysical identity
Wellsprings · Somnalis primary: shadow-walking is a Somnalis expression made physical; the blink-space between moments is Somnalis territory. Tenebra strong secondary. Ignivale accessible, the moment of emotional ignition that converts reservoir to output. Aurevane and Luminalis suppressed, −30% all stats in Radiant Domains: their architecture is built around the space between light sources, and light itself is no friend of it.
Glyphs · Strong: Wy Motion, Fi Passion, El Illusion, Sa Silence. Rejected: Ko Order, Ky Structure. These require the linear Gnosis chains the architecture suppresses, and contact produces feedback rather than working.
Traits · Awakening clusters around kinetic enhancement and shadow expression: movement blurs, after-images that persist slightly too long, the first involuntary shadow-step, appearing two feet from where the practitioner was standing with no visible transit. Ascension moves through speed → shadow-embodiment → absence. At high stages, senior practitioners stop walking through shadow and become temporarily indistinguishable from it.
Overgrowth risk · Reservoir saturation. A Catkin who stores too much Aetheric emotion without releasing it develops overflow: involuntary emotional detonations, technique misfires, Stage V risk elevated to acute.

Domain law. Shadow Domains. Light deepens rather than extinguishes: every shadow in the territory has depth, a quality of there being more room in the dark than the architecture should allow. Entities inside experience elevated reaction-time pressure: their own Dexterity feels slightly slower, as if the Domain is running faster than they are.
Governing principle: the moment before movement as sovereign law. Within the territory, Catkin have first-action authority over any exchange. No technique is involved. The Domain is expressing the practitioner’s nature as the ground’s own law.

Culture and record
The Clawbound Trial · A rite in which the young practitioner must shadow-walk through territory their clan elder has anchored with Tenebra-resonance. Speed will not save them: the test is whether the practitioner can read the shadow-map the elder has written and follow it without detection. Both emerge with a permanent bond marker in their Harmonics architecture. The bond is always mutual; the elder accepts a burden too.
The Emotional Covenant · Before significant action, Catkin formally acknowledge the reservoir they are bringing to the event. Nobody prays. It is closer to inventory. The warrior stands still, catalogs what they are carrying emotionally, and decides consciously whether the reservoir is ready or should be managed first. They are the only known culture to treat pre-combat emotional assessment as a formal discipline.
Settlements · Shadowed Ridge · the Dusk Quarter of Altherion · Nightveil Hollow. Characterized by being difficult to locate from the outside and immediately obvious to navigate once inside, built around the shadow map residents carry rather than around visible landmarks.
Relations · Lupine: deep kinship, the oldest beastkin alliance; agility and pack-force are complementary architectures, and the kinship holds across sharply divergent cultural practice. Humans: complex. Catkin are among the most frequently enslaved lineages because their physical features are considered aesthetically appealing by human buyers, and this history shapes every cross-species interaction in ways neither party consistently acknowledges. Hobgoblins: professional respect; practitioners describe the pairing as “the most uncomfortable military alliance that consistently wins engagements.”
Historical role · The Clawbound Accord’s original function was assassination and deep infiltration; the shadow-walking architecture made them the Concord’s preferred covert operatives during the Spirit War. Current Catkin communities hold no parades for this history. They acknowledge it, the way you acknowledge something that happened and that you cannot pretend didn’t.
Known figure · Saiya, active, Scourge of Hell mercenary operations.
Lupine: Wolfkin
Pack-Soul Beastkin · Lunar Strikers
Born from the Great Hunt Pact during the First Moonfall, when wild spirits and mortals fused beneath a blood eclipse. Call them wolves who became people and you will have it wrong. They are the pact itself, given a body that runs on both.
Spiritual lineage · Fenraal, the Lunar Stalker, whose moonbound clarity and Pack-Soul allow individual Lupine to function as a singular metaphysical organism at sufficient proximity. Cooperation is the least of it. At Pack-Soul depth, they think together.
Soul architecture
In the blood · Their souls oscillate with the lunar cycle, and the Core answers by reflex, triggering Aetheric bursts through physical reflex rather than cognitive calculation. They feel the technique happen before they decide to use it.
Untrained lean · Body 60% / Spirit 40%. Among those who walk the Spirit Path, it is distributed across the pack as a shared architecture, and no one Lupine holds all of it.

Isolation Decay produces Crystal compression rather than fracture, a slow fading that reads as emotional shutdown before it reads as spiritual damage. Lupine who have been isolated long enough describe feeling “too quiet for too long.” The recovery requires pack proximity, and no physician can substitute.
Acute fracture risk at Stage V if isolated. Splintering requires the soul to crack open to become larger, and the Lupine soul architecture is communal, resisting individual expansion. In isolation, Stage V tends to produce collapse rather than growth.
Stage VII stall: the soul needs to perceive itself from outside, but a Lupine’s self is partly constituted by their pack. Perceiving the self requires first separating the individual architecture from the shared one, which the Crystal resists.

Stat framework


















































StatModExpressionVitality+10Dense physique sustained by pack-bond. Depresses under Isolation DecayArdency+15Pack-amplified burst. Kinpulse synchronicity amplifies output proportionally per bonded ally within rangeGnosis−20Linear logic suppressed. Perception elevated: Aetheric-scent tracking reads spiritual residues at 48-hour range. They do not calculate. They knowDexterity+20Explosive speed. The digitigrade posture concentrates kinetic mass at the launch point; highest travel speed of any beastkin in pack-sprint configurationHarmonics+25Definitive stat. The entire Lupine power architecture runs through Harmonics. In full pack formation, Chord value exceeds any individual practitioner’s ratingResilience+10Pack-buffering. Isolation Decay as the structural counter: away from pack 6+ hours, all Resilience sub-stats decline at −5% per 2-hour interval, capping at −40%Tempering−10Instinctual rather than refined. They cannot overchannel by choice, since the output is reflexive. They do not waste output because they cannot plan it; they produce exactly what the moment calls forDominion−05Communal rather than individually sovereign. The exception: in Alpha-Binding formation, collective Dominion exceeds any individual member’s ceiling, the pack as a Dominion unit
Sub-stat notes · Harmonics Chord in full pack formation approaches ceilings individual practitioners across all races typically cannot reach without Domain-stage development. Attunement is tuned for 48-hour spiritual residue detection rather than ambient field reading. Pack-sprint Celerity exceeds individual peak because the Pack-Soul synchronizes gait patterns, eliminating timing variance. Resilience Integrity degrades under isolation with no damage to the Crystal at all, because the Crystal is not a closed system for Lupine: it is designed to be partly constituted by pack-proximity.
Metaphysical identity
Wellsprings · Verdantia primary: life as continuous communal process, pack as ecosystem. Luminalis, moonlight being the light that hides, primary secondary: their power expression genuinely varies with lunar phase. Anima Spirare accessible through bond-formation overlap. Somnalis accessible at full-moon peak, for dream-pack communion during Howls of Mourning. Judicium and Fixatio suppressed: the reactive architecture reads structured stillness as threat rather than discipline.
Glyphs · Strong: Ye Unity (the Pack-Soul’s primary phoneme), Ka Cycle, Va Moment, Ma Memory. Backlash: Ko Order, Al Edge. Structure and boundary phonemes produce the Aetheric equivalent of a wall appearing inside a field that was never designed to contain one.
Kinpulse falls outside the formal glyph-chain systems. It is emotional Aether transmission without phonemic structure. Experienced practitioners can translate Kinpulse states into approximate glyph expressions, but the translation always loses something.
Overgrowth risk · Bloodmoon Corruption. During Lunar Inversions the oscillating soul-lattice destabilizes and high-stage Lupine can enter Involuntary Berserk states in which complex glyph-casting fails but raw physical output spikes catastrophically.

Domain law. Pack-Hunt Domains. The territory’s spatial geometry becomes a hunt-field: distance between predator and prey within the Domain is subject to Kinpulse law. Entities trying to create separation from a pack inside the Domain find the separation collapsing; the hunt-geometry reasserts.
Governing principle: the distance you think exists between you and us is not the distance that exists.

Culture and record
Kinbinding · Pack members cut their palms and press them together under a full moon, creating a permanent Aetheric tether. The tether carries no words, and it does not transmit thoughts. It transmits weight: the sense of another soul’s presence, its state, its direction. The closest thing Lupine culture has to a sacred act, and treated as one.
Howls of Mourning · A communal vocal ritual recording the life-echoes of the fallen into local ley-lines. The pack’s history is encoded in the land. Walking through old Lupine territory, practitioners with sufficient Attunement hear faint resonances in the ground, with neither words nor images in them: the emotional signature of lives that were lived here.
Alpha-Binding · Linking individual Soul Crystals to a single Alpha’s Crystal architecture, creating a collective metaphysical organism. The Alpha accepts responsibility for the pack’s coherence in exchange for the pack’s amplified output. Call that leadership and a Lupine will correct you: it is load-bearing.
Settlements · Lumis Village · Greyfang Crossing · the Shrine of Nine Howls. Positioned relative to ley-line nodes and lunar sight-lines rather than resource proximity. The strategic logic of their positioning is not immediately legible to other races.
Relations · Elves: deep distrust rooted in the First Betrayal, a historical event in which Elven Accord operatives used Lupine pack-bond architecture against them during a treaty negotiation. The details are in the Lupine oral tradition and not in any Accord archive. Humans: the most frequently hunted beastkin lineage where the Labor Provision permits wild beastkin clearance; their speed makes them difficult to capture, and their Isolation Decay makes extended pursuit more effective than it should be.
Historical role · The Moonwake Accord. Lupine packs guarded collapsing Wellspring sites during the Verdant Siege, allowing the Western Realms to stabilize. They received formal recognition from the Concord. Formal Accord membership did not come with it. The distinction was understood.
Ursine: Bearkin
Living Fortifications · Mountain-Anchored
Formed during the Age of Glacial Memory when the Titan of Endurance drew mountain-spirits into mortal flesh during a confluence of Monolithion and Verdantia eruptions. People expected a warrior race. They got a people who understand load-bearing.
Spiritual lineage · Orruvak, the Unmoved Mountain, a being who watched civilizations build and collapse across the hillside it occupied and never once considered that the appropriate response to either was to move. Bearkin carry this as a constitutional truth: some things should stay.
Soul architecture
In the blood · The specific weight of things that refuse to end. Their souls are old-growth heavy.
Untrained lean · Body 70% / Spirit 30%. The Spirit side shows through environmental attunement and the Stillness Trial discipline: the spiritual practice of holding while everything around you fails is both a combat technique and a soul architecture.

Crystal fracture pattern · Subtle-Blindness amplification. The Crystal resists abstract and illusory architecture so fundamentally that exposure to high-tier Illusion or Dream workings produces confusion fractures, a specific Crystal disorientation with no physical damage in it.
They cannot be tricked into reaching for a wall that isn’t there, because their Crystal does not process “wall that isn’t there” as a possible category.

Progression · Slow, thorough, through all stages. No rapid acceleration. No sudden fractures. Each transition takes roughly one and a half times the species average, because the Crystal is denser and requires more Essence pressure to restructure, and weakness has nothing to do with it. Stall potential at Stage VI Glory, whose burning-bright expression conflicts with a constitutional preference for not broadcasting. Dissonance expression: Geological Stall. The Crystal enters absolute stillness that can last years, where another people’s would shatter. Bearkin Dissonance survivors are indistinguishable from sleep to outside observation. They are not asleep.
Stat framework


















































StatModExpressionVitality+30Dominant stat. The most physically durable beastkin lineage. They take hits that would end engagements for other practitioners and continue. They do this without tracking itArdency+20Raw rather than refined. Their output is massive and approximate. When a Bearkin technique lands, the surrounding architecture knows about itGnosis−15Deliberate thinkers, not fast ones. Retention elevated: what a Bearkin has learned, they have learned permanentlyDexterity−20Reaction Lag: −40% Evasion, cannot react to high-speed or airborne technique windows. They do not dodge. They endure. These are not equivalent responses but they produce equivalent survival outcomes at different scalesHarmonics+10Nature attunement, narrow in range and deep. They read Verdantia, Monolithion, and Terra-aspected nodes with exceptional clarityResilience+25Near-ceiling. The thing that absorbs pressure without fracturing becomes structurally better than the thing that never had toTempering−10Overwhelming but not precise. Overflow elevated through constitutionally large capacity. Output lands, but not always exactly where intendedDominion+10Territory sovereignty through Weight-Binding. Their Domain roots into local geology and persists through their absence with greater stability than other lineage Domains
Sub-stat notes · Fortitude and Ossification are definitive; the Siege of the Seventh Fold’s three-day hold is the canonical demonstration. Resilience Hardening elevates through sustained pressure producing Crystal densification: Bearkin who have been under pressure longer are harder, and no weaker for it. Ardency Detonation expresses as a patience finally exhausted, a mountain deciding the valley below it has needed rearranging. Dexterity Evasion floors consistently: the design intent is to make damage insufficient, and avoiding it never entered the plan.
Metaphysical identity
Wellsprings · Monolithion primary, native. Verdantia strong secondary, the living system’s version of the mountain’s permanence. Basilithe accessible. Oneirion, Eidolyn and Hypnather rejected: Subtle-Blindness; contact produces confusion fractures.
Glyphs · Strong: Ir Endurance, Tar Weight, Ka Cycle, Ky Structure. Their glyph-chains are the most materially stable in any beastkin tradition: Ir-Tar-Ky chains persist without maintenance for decades. The Bearkin are the only beastkin lineage whose inscribed workings outlast the practitioner who made them without Aetheric renewal. Backlash: El Illusion, No Negation. Their soul is too grounded for negation.
Overgrowth risk · Weight-Lock. Over-investment in Vitality and Resilience Traits can develop Crystal density so extreme that Aetheric flexibility is suppressed, leaving a person capable of surviving almost anything and unable to do almost anything.

Domain law. Earthen Domains. The territory becomes materially denser, invisibly, physically and Aetherically. Objects weigh more. Force requirements increase. High-speed techniques require more Essence inside the Domain than outside it.
Governing principle: mass as sovereign law. Things should stay where they are. Kinetic disruption costs more. Defensive endurance costs less.

Culture and record
Stillness Trials · Meditative duels where two Bearkin stand within a collapsing Domain or under sustained pressure; the first to break their stance loses. Physical endurance decides very little. The question is whether the practitioner can hold their Crystal’s architecture coherent while everything around them is telling the Crystal that change is warranted. The winners are not always the strongest Bearkin. They are always the most settled ones.
Weight-Binding · Tethering the soul to a specific mountain or glade, creating a permanent Aetheric anchor. Weight-Bound Bearkin pull Aether from bonded territory within range and refine it to Essence as other practitioners do, and develop responsibility for that territory’s Aetheric health. What the mountain feels, they feel. They do not describe this as a burden.
Settlements · Korr Orvun · Glade of the Slumbering Root · Ulg-Vorakar. Among the oldest continuously occupied locations in the world, the same sites in many cases since the Age of Glacial Memory. The architecture is stone and has outlasted the practitioners who built it.
Relations · Marrowkin: honor-bound kinship; forge-culture and endurance-culture share enough foundational philosophy that cooperation is natural rather than negotiated. Lupine: protective regard: Lupine move; Bearkin stay, and neither lineage pretends the complementarity is accidental. Humans: their size reads as threatening to those who have not spent time with them. They are the most dangerous-looking and least aggressive of the major beastkin lineages, which creates consistent mismatches in initial encounter framing.

The Siege of the Seventh Fold. Bearkin held the final line for three days while the Domain around them collapsed, allowing other races to escape. The hold required sustained Stillness Trial discipline at Stage V+ from every participant. None survived intact.
The surviving Bearkin lineages consider this the defining event in their historical record and the reason the Accord’s treatment of them is an ongoing institutional insult.
Annually, Bearkin communities observe a three-day silence in memory. They call the silence recognition, and they will not have it called grief.

Fox-Spirit: Mishiro-Kin
Spirit-Adjacent Beastkin · Aetheric Nose
First Eon origin that the Guild Accord’s taxonomy system has never cleanly handled. Fox-spirit beastkin predate the formal beastkin classification and sit at the border where the Fae taxonomy also has a partial claim. The Mishiro lineage has been in contested classification since the First Eon, when the earliest practitioners demonstrated Somnalis attunement at birth that no formal harmonization ritual could account for.
Every tavern from the Salt Road to the sea calls trained sensing the nose (the Guild says sensing, the Moto kehai), and Mishiro-kin find this very funny. The rest of the continent is talking in metaphor. They are not.
Spiritual lineage · Classified under beastkin taxonomy for Accord purposes. True lineage: Somnalis-adjacent Fae of unknown direct ancestor. The Mishiro family maintains that the answer to who made your people is “we were always here,” which is not a satisfying answer to archivists and is probably correct.
Soul architecture
In the blood · Warmth, the specific quality of choosing openness as a position, and a tidal memory of felt things. Their souls are permeable in a way that other beastkin souls are not: they receive environmental Aether rather than just projecting into it.
Untrained lean · Spirit 78% / Fate 18% / Body 4%. Do not look for a combat lineage here.

Fox-spirit Crystal fracture is rare and typically associated with sustained olfactory overload: exposure to extreme Aetheric event residue without adequate processing time. The Crystal’s porosity, which makes the nose function, also makes it vulnerable to saturation. Practitioners in high-Aether environments need periodic Somnalis-integration sleep to process accumulated intake.
Stage III is the stage most affected by captivity and environmental suppression. Fox-spirit Crystal requires conditions of reasonable safety, or the kind of danger that pushes outward. Inward-pressing danger, meaning captivity, sustained threat, isolation from sensory richness, stalls Stage III at the threshold.

Stat framework


















































StatModExpressionVitality−05Light frames. Filtration elevated: their body chemistry handles organic and environmental toxins efficientlyArdency−10Not a combat output lineage. They are not going to out-fight things. The nose tells them where things are so other people can deal with themGnosis+15Olfactory intelligence. They read situations with unusual accuracy because the nose provides information at a layer most practitioners cannot accessDexterity+15They move without announcing themselves: no trained stealth, only the ingrained habit of a people who learned early that taking up less space was a survival techniqueHarmonics+35ANOMALOUS. Attunement, Memory, and Confluence at the level of a Master in a body that otherwise reads Adept at best. The nose predates training, captivity, circumstance, and everything else. It is what they are before they are anything elseResilience+05Modest. Crystal porosity means standard Aetheric assault is slightly less efficient: the Crystal absorbs and processes rather than resisting sharplyTempering+10Clean, minimal-overhead output. They don’t overchannel because they never had enough volume to develop overchannel as a habitDominion−05Bond-based sovereignty, with little interest in territory. Anima Spirare architecture builds spatial authority around significant relationships rather than around occupied ground
Sub-stat notes · Harmonics Memory is elevated alongside Attunement: they read current Aetheric state against an archive of historical states. A Fox-Spirit in a space where something significant happened can smell the event’s residue with enough detail to reconstruct rough sequence. And a unique architecture: bond depth converts to Dominion Confluence, creating spatial authority around significant others rather than around territory.
Metaphysical identity
Wellsprings · Somnalis native: opens without harmonization ritual. It is their home frequency; they dream with resolution and accuracy that formal practitioners require decades of work to approach. Anima Spirare develops in sustained relationships: the architecture of choosing to remain beside someone builds this Wellspring access naturally over time. Verdantia accessible via lineage. Manganthra peripheral: changes chosen or survived leave traces.
Glyphs · Strong: Ma Memory (the nose’s deepest phoneme; every Fox-Spirit technique is Ma-authorized), Zo Echo, Sa Silence, Ye Unity. Backlash: Uur Disruption, Fi Passion. These produce metabolic spike, sharp input overload that temporarily saturates the olfactory architecture.

Their glyph expression is ambient, with nothing inscriptive about it. Fox-Spirit workings look less like formal technique and more like the world cooperating.
The practitioner forces nothing; they remind the environment of what it already was.

Traits · Awakening brings the nose’s first Aetheric layer becoming consciously distinguishable from biological scent, and fox-fire, a minor ambient cold-amber luminescence, palm-sized, three to five minutes at Stage III. At Stage V, fox-fire becomes significantly less minor. The Stage V crack-open expands what it can do, moving it from ambient light into directed Aetheric expression.
Overgrowth risk · Olfactory saturation in high-Aether events. Processing failures express as temporal confusion: the practitioner loses sequence, unsure whether they are smelling the current state of a space or its state from hours ago.

Domain law. Memory Domains, rare, Stage VI+. The territory holds recent Aetheric events as accessible residue: footstep patterns persist visibly, voice-echoes hang in the air, significant emotional events leave readable impressions on surfaces. The Domain judges nothing it records, and it records everything.
Governing principle: the present moment is transparent, and its history is visible to those who know how to look. Within the territory, deception leaves residue. No formal proceeding will admit that residue as evidence. It is information that cannot be unfelt.

Culture and record

The Name-Keeping Fox-spirit beastkin place significant weight on names as the last thing that cannot be physically removed. The practice of speaking one’s name aloud in the presence of a witness when circumstances have taken everything else is documented in Mishiro oral tradition as the act of remaining.
The Waiting Fox-spirit patience has nothing passive in it. It is the accumulated practice of a people who have learned to hold their position and their perception long enough for the world to reveal what it actually is. The fox waits. The thing-that-seems-to-be eventually reveals itself as what-it-is. Most fox-spirit wisdom traditions begin here and build outward.
Bond tending Significant relationships have literal Aetheric consequences. Practitioners tend their significant bonds the way they tend their nose: regularly, with attention, without forcing the process.
Settlements Nomadic-adjacent, driven by Wellspring quality and Somnalis accessibility. Mishiro communities are small and mobile, a pattern that predates the Labor Provision and has continued regardless of it.


Fox-spirit beastkin appear in the formal historical record almost exclusively in Labor Provision documentation, as property rather than as actors. This is an accurate reflection of how the Accord’s record was compiled, and a poor one of what actually occurred.
The Mishiro lineage’s actual historical record exists in oral tradition and in the nose’s archive, in the Aetheric memory of territory that remembers what happened there. It is not accessible to the formal historical apparatus. This may be intentional.

Known figure · Yoko Mishiro, active, traveling with Sodoku and Emira Moto.
Serpentkin: Scalebond
Ancestral Memory-Bearers · Coil-Pattern Holders
Second Eon, Dissolution Period. Formed near the Scorchline Wellsprings when memory-essence from collapsing realms etched itself into scaled biological bodies specifically shaped for metaphysical erosion resistance. They did not evolve into their function. Their function was the condition of their creation.
Spiritual lineage · Zseraxil the Coil, ancient guardian of the Anamnesis site called Ancestral Echoes. Their lineage grants native connection to the Coiling Memory of the world: the principle that nothing is truly gone, that the echo of a thing persists in the Aetheric record longer than the thing itself.
Soul architecture
In the blood · The mirror before anything. Their souls function as Aetheric mirrors, capable of reflecting and storing complex historical data within the Core. What they touch, they remember. What they remember, they can use.
Untrained lean · Spirit 65% / Fate 25% / Body 10%. The Fate side shows through historical Domain formation: territories where Serpentkin have practiced become living archives.

Their Crystal is architecturally unusual: memory imprints accumulate as structural layers rather than as stored data. An old Serpentkin Crystal, viewed with sufficient Gnosis, looks like sedimentary rock, each layer a period of their life, compacted into the substrate.
Stall potential at Stage VIII. Transcendence requires genuine change, and the Coiling Memory architecture is oriented toward preservation. The Crystal resists restructuring because it contains too much it doesn’t want to lose.

Stat framework


















































StatModExpressionVitality+10Resilient scaled biology. Temperature regulation via Aetheric sync provides survival advantage in extreme environmentsArdency+10Memory-laced output. When a strike draws on the Coiling Memory of how a similar strike resolved, Penetration and Depth amplifyGnosis+25Definitive stat. Chronos-Vision, ancestral memory access, pattern recognition across historical data. They can read how a situation resembles situations they have memory of, producing uncanny tactical accuracy against historical opponentsDexterity+15Coiled-strike precision. Their strike windows are short and precise in the way that things optimized for a specific function become precise through durationHarmonics+20Memory-frequency resonance near ceiling. They can harmonize with the residue of Wellspring states that no longer exist in present formResilience+10Scale hardening and environmental adaptation. Anchoring to historically significant territory elevated through the Coiling Memory bondTempering+15Precise routing through memory channels. Latency elevated: they hold technique output until the optimal moment with the patience of a practitioner who has seen the moment come beforeDominion−10Inward-focused memory architecture suppresses spatial authority. Their Domain expression, when it forms, is passive rather than asserted
Sub-stat notes · Gnosis Retention is definitive: accumulated Crystal-layer memory that does not degrade, an archive growing continuously from birth. Harmonics Memory is elevated above most races’ maximum, making them uniquely effective at Wellspring work in damaged zones: they remember what the Wellspring site was before it was damaged. Against truly novel situations they are more cautious than other races, because novelty has less precedent to cross-reference. And Dexterity Finesse: a Serpentkin does not hit harder than necessary, because “harder than necessary” wastes the Coiling Memory’s evidence of what sufficient force looks like.
Metaphysical identity
Wellsprings · Anamnesis primary: recovered memory, historical resonance, temporal depth. Mirithane strong secondary. Somnalis accessible, used for Coiling Memory integration work. Solfatara accessible through temperature-sync architecture, and the Titan Vohrin’s cold ground workable through opposite-temperature regulation: both thermal extremes available, moderate temperatures actually their weakest environmental range.
Glyphs · Strong: Ma Memory, Zo Echo, Ka Cycle, En Lattice, Len Line. Their glyph chains are among the most temporally stable in the Continuum: Ma-Zo-En chains persist without degradation because the Crystal substrate feeds them passive Essence from its accumulated memory layers.
Backlash · Uur Disruption, No Negation. The Coiling Memory cannot process negation of pattern: the architecture is built on preservation, and negation workings produce a category error where backlash would be, a gap in the Crystal’s filing logic where the working should have landed.
Traits · Awakening brings Chronos-Vision (seeing after-images of prior Aetheric events in physical space), the first memory-layer deposition, and scale-resonance at significant historical sites. Ascension moves through personal memory → ancestral memory → Coiling Memory access. At high stages, Serpentkin stop accessing their own memory and start accessing the world’s.

Domain law. Memory Domains: passive accumulation of event residue. The territory becomes a living archive. At Stage VII+, the Domain can be queried intentionally: what happened here, in what sequence, by whom.
Governing principle: the past is present. What occurred in the territory is part of the territory’s current Aetheric composition. The law is passive and passes no judgment.

Culture and record
The Coil-Rite · A coming-of-age ritual in which the young practitioner meditates within an Anamnesis Wellspring zone, allowing the Crystal to receive its first deep memory-layer deposit. The layer contains the combined Aetheric signature of the lineage’s history: pattern-memory, the shape of what the lineage is, with no one individual’s recollection in it.
Memory-weaving · Practitioners can share Crystal layers with willing recipients through sustained physical contact and synchronized breathing. The recipient receives the emotional and Aetheric texture of the shared period and none of the content. Used for historical transmission and for grief processing.
Settlements · Coilspire Den · Stoneglass Hollow · the Pale Fang Archipelago (disputed). Positioned at historically significant sites: Wellspring ruins, event-dense ley-line intersections, anywhere the Coiling Memory is accessible.
Relations · Marrowkin: mutual respect grounded in shared commitment to preservation, material preservation and Aetheric preservation as parallel projects. Elves: scholarly cooperation, productive and slightly territorial. Humans: viewed as people who do not understand what is being lost when they destroy things, with no contempt in it: a patient, ongoing observation of a civilization that consistently fails to consult available historical data before repeating documented mistakes.

The Dissolution Period’s surviving historical record is partially the Serpentkin’s contribution: their Crystal-layer memory of events that no formal archive preserved.
The Accord’s historical division treats this data as anecdotal because its source is living memory rather than inscribed record.
The Serpentkin find this classification clarifying.

Moves, Costume and What Everyone Says









































LineageThe moveThe lookWhat they say about the othersCatkinBefore You Decided: the reservoir goes off through one precise step, and the knife was already in you when you thought about parryingDark, close-cut, bells only as an insult”A Lupine cannot go to the privy alone”LupineNine-Howl Run: the whole pack in one gait, and the distance you were relying on stops existingTooth-strung cords, kin-cut palms shown open, always a brother somewhere”A Catkin will tell you she was never there, and for once you should believe her”BearkinThe Mountain Has Thought About It: a lifetime of patience finally exhausted, in one blow, some years after you started the argumentLeather aprons, fir-green wool, a chair they brought themselves”A fox will tell you what you had for dinner and leave you to fight it”Fox-SpiritAnd I Smelled This Was True: no blow at all, only fox-fire on the one spot you lied about, in front of everyoneAmber and gray-green, light travel clothes, someone else’s cloak”A Scalebond has been wrong before, and can give you the date”SerpentkinAs Previously: a coiled strike with the exact force that settled this same fight two hundred years ago, against someone who fought like youGood coats over bare scale, a notary’s seal, cold hands”A Bearkin is the only person who is older than my grudge”
Each lineage also has a word for the aura coat (the visible coat of a fighter’s own color), and the words start fights: Catkin call it the lie, since the skill is in not showing one; Lupine say the pelt and ask whose; Bearkin call it the weather and do not understand why you are worrying about yours.

Read next: The Three Paths, for what the untrained lean means; The Trait System, for how a lineage power is held.

Five Theologies of a Single Song · Revised Codex

“She sang one note. We have spent every Eon since arguing about how it should be sung back.”
Marginal note, provenance disputed across all five surviving elven archives

When the old bargewoman Ilarenth Sweetwater died at Alder Landing in the fall of 544 IC, she left kin in all five branches, and all five came to bury her, which is the sort of mistake a person only gets to make once. The Eressean arrived first, forty of them in sun-gold and white on a barge with a water clock aboard, carrying the correct rite in the correct order and a surveyor to check the grave. The Varrisak came out of the red autumn woods on the third day, painted and barefoot, informed the Eressean that the correct rite had stopped listening some time ago, and set about dreaming her a new one on the riverbank at the top of their lungs. On the fifth day a Drow Debt-Keeper in midnight blue stepped off the ferry and read out, to the whole landing, everything Ilarenth had owed to every stretch of river she had ever worked, which took until dark and included a heron. The Eladrin cousins walked in from the north with frost in their braids, packed her in river ice to hold her, and stood in silence for four days, which the landing found restful and the Eressean took as an insult. The Echo Elves then asked to see the will, and declined to let anything proceed until every mourner could recite its terms back without variation.
There were nineteen days of it. Songs were sung at one another across the water, and on the eleventh night the singing turned to knives and then to something worse, gold light and green light and black going up from the two banks while the whole town watched from the roofs with their dinners. A Varrisak grove-singer lost an eye. An Eressean rite-officer lost his temper in public, for the first time in three hundred years, and his family still does not speak of it. In all five archives Ilarenth Sweetwater has a grave at Alder Landing, and in all five it is somewhere else. The ferryman says she is under the pear tree and that he dug it himself.
Everyone at that landing loved her, and everyone there was keeping faith with the same mother and the same song. Here is the song.
The Origin, Briefly
Florwyn sang the Realmsong of Edenis and the Vey-Elarin were tuned into being as living notes of that chord. For the whole of the First Eon they were one people, the High Empire of Eresse, bound less by law than by the Kinship Doctrine: the land is a relative, not a resource, and everything else follows from how seriously that is taken.

The Great Spirit War against the Erebus incursion left that unity standing against every force thrown at it. What broke it was a question, asked under maximum pressure: what did the Doctrine actually mean? Five different, sincere, mutually incompatible answers came back.

The Theology of the Split



































BranchThe answerWhat it holdsEresseanOrder as DevotionThe Doctrine is honored through exact repetition: the same calendar, the same rite, in the same order, forever, because a promise kept carelessly is not a promise. Structure is what reverence looks like sustained across centuries, and they will not hear it called the oppositeVarrisakDream as TruthThe Doctrine is honored by being re-lived, and repeating it does not count. A rite performed identically to last year is a rite that has stopped listening. The land changes; the song describing it must be re-dreamed fresh each generation or it becomes a lie wearing the shape of a memoryDrowDebt as MemoryThe Doctrine is honored by carrying what others cannot bear to carry. Every taking creates an obligation, and someone must go into the places too corrupted, too costly, or too dangerous for anyone else to tally what is owed there and make sure it is eventually paidEladrinSilence as EnduranceAn Eressean daughter-people who carried Order-as-Devotion into the harshest northern theater and found that repetition alone could not survive the cold. What replaced it: the surest form of devotion, in a place this unforgiving, is knowing exactly when to stop insisting and simply endureEcho ElvesCovenant as MemoryA second Eressean daughter-people, splitting off through political conviction rather than catastrophe: that any agreement, including the Realmsong itself, is only as good as the exactness with which its terms are remembered and consented to by every party, and a flawed memory of a promise is the same thing as a broken one

The Duskwalker Schism is what happens when the first three of these answers meet each other for the first time and discover they cannot be reconciled.
The Ice-Voice Conflict and the Celestial Accord refusal are what happens when the first of those three turns out not to be able to hold all of its own children either.

A note on the tables below. The stat columns are the Guild’s measure of what a people’s soul architecture adds to or takes from a practitioner: Vitality for wounds, Ardency for output and the punch through worked armor, Gnosis for knowledge and the read, Dexterity for measure and reaction, Harmonics for attunement and the pull of Aether from the ground, Resilience for what a working does to the Crystal, Tempering for control and how long a working can be pushed, Dominion for spatial authority and Pressure. A Domain is the territory in which a high-Stage practitioner’s own law holds, and a glyph or phoneme is a unit of Parunic, the script that writes boundaries onto laws. The elves will tell you the Guild’s measure misses the point. It does, and it also predicts who wins.
Eressean: The Grand Principality of Eresse
The branch that answered the Great Spirit War by tightening. Where the High Empire’s Wheel of Given Seasons was a shared, informal rhythm, the Eressean formalized it into Parunic ritual law, fixed rite, and the crystalline court culture the wider world now associates with elves generally: white stone, sun-gold thread, nine-tiered barges and a sense that you have come in at the wrong moment.
From the Eressean’s own perspective this betrays nothing of the Kinship Doctrine. It is the Doctrine taken with maximum seriousness: if the land is owed a promise, the promise should be kept in exactly the same words, exactly the same order, every single time, because a people who improvise their reverence are a people already halfway to abandoning it.

Visitors take Velthaeir, the Floating Archive-City, for a monument to Eressean vanity. It is a monument to Eressean terror of forgetting anything correctly.

Its seat is Vaelmarr, where the Sunroot Court, Saeloria’s court, sits and votes; Velthaeir keeps the record apart from it, entering everything and giving out nothing. The whole of it, and every daughter-branch below, stands on the elven old-ground of the New World, the Eastern Rise, the older of its two grounds, and nowhere in the Old World.
Cultural traits

Calendrical governance No significant Sunroot-descended decision is made outside its properly appointed ceremonial window; urgency is treated the way the High Empire once treated haste in harvest. Several wars have been lost this way, on schedule.
Kiva-descended council architecture Formal deliberation chambers, built partly below grade, where Council of Bloom elders debate through fixed ceremonial roles rather than open argument.
Clan-lineage record over personal record An Eressean’s standing is legible primarily through which lineage-line and rite-office they hold, less through individual achievement.
Florwyndic Songscript Ritual, directive-force writing reserved for law and consecration, distinct from the Common tongue used for ordinary speech.

Soul architecture and stats


















































StatModExpressionVitality−15Lighter skeletal structure; Longevity sub-stat exceptionally elevated. They break cleanly rather than decayArdency+10Economy over force; +25% yield (η) on Ma/Ur/Ie phoneme chainsGnosis+25Definitive stat. Parunic Fluency reads glyphs as ancestral language, not learned systemDexterity+10Grace read as inevitability rather than speedHarmonics+20Domain Stability: the most stable Domains of any documented lineageResilience+10Structured soul resists conventional damage; Emotional Rigidity: Fear and Rage go past their Resilience and wound the Core directlyTempering+15Cleanest Essence routing of any surface elf; minimal overheadDominion+20Domain Expansion doubled; presence stabilizes Aetheric drift passively
Relations
Eressean regard Varrisak as a fragile, mourning kinship, a people who had the same chance at order and chose to let it go feral. They regard Drow with the particular discomfort of watching a sibling live out the version of the choice they themselves were most afraid of making.

They founded the Eladrin and lost the argument with the Celestial-Accord dissenters who became the Echo Elves, and both losses are treated, in low voices at very good dinners, as evidence the Eressean have never fully resolved: that Order as Devotion produces extraordinary stability and, eventually, children who leave it.

Varrisak: Wood Elves of the Sylvaar Wandering
Where the Eressean answered the war by fixing the rite, the Varrisak answered it by refusing to let any rite calcify at all. Descended from the Sylvaar Wanderers who remained bound to the Primeval Forests through the Duskwalker Schism, Varrisak practice centers on the vision, a personal, unrepeatable encounter with the forest’s own spirits, sought deliberately and never scripted twice the same way, that renews a person’s standing with the land far more than any fixed calendar could.
Their seasonal movement through forest territory has nothing of homelessness in it. It rests on the belief that staying too long in one place lets a person start mistaking their own habits for the forest’s actual will.
Cultural traits

The Dream-Fast A Varrisak seeking guidance withdraws alone into old growth and fasts until a vision arrives. No two accounts of the practice are recorded identically, which the Varrisak consider proof the practice works.
Kin-bonded clan identity Organized around a bonded animal or plant-kin rather than bloodline alone, cutting across biological family lines.
Dream Groves Old-growth root-networks carrying generations of practitioner Crystal-inclusion, functioning as a literal, structured Aetheric archive, with no metaphor about it.
Oral transmission only The Varrisak have no equivalent to Florwyndic Songscript by choice. A law that can be written down can be followed without being understood, which they consider worse than no law at all.

Soul architecture and stats


















































StatModExpressionVitality+05Distributed resilience rather than raw density: damage spreads across a bonded territory the way it spreads across an ecosystem, rather than a single bodyArdency−05Output is depth, not volume; a Varrisak spends less because their Essence is rarely fully separate from the forest supplying itGnosis+15Ecological and historical memory at extraordinary depth within bonded territory; shallow outside itDexterity+05Certainty over speed: Economy high, Celerity middlingHarmonics+30Definitive stat. Fate-Path-heavy resonance; in bonded territory a Varrisak’s Harmonics are read as the forest’s ownResilience+20Damage distributes across bonded territory rather than localizing, so a deeply rooted Varrisak is genuinely harder to finish than to merely woundTempering+05Efficient through depth rather than discipline; Coherence is high specifically because behavior, Path, and Crystal have never been asked to disagreeDominion+25Territory-as-self Domain law, the most literal of any elven lineage; in the most bonded cases, simply how far the forest currently breathes
Relations
Varrisak describe Eressean as crystalline arrogance in search of a vessel and mean it with real grief rather than contempt. The Sylvaar Rebellion Schism is, from the Varrisak side, the moment a shared people definitively stopped being able to dream the same forest together.
Their relationship with Drow is fraught but genuinely functional: Drow handle deep corruption, Varrisak tend surface regrowth, and the partnership survives specifically because neither theology asks the other to become itself.
Drow: Shadow-Custodians of Rovann
Drow theology begins from the same Kinship Doctrine as everyone else and reaches an entirely different conclusion: that a debt owed to the land does not vanish because the site where it was incurred has become too corrupted, too dangerous, or too shameful for anyone else to enter. Someone has to go in anyway, tally exactly what is owed, and hold that ledger open until it can be paid.
Standing among Drow is built through what has been given away and accounted for, and hoarding earns nobody anything. When the Duskwalkers offered a path into the underside of Realmsong during the Schism, the Drow’s ancestors were the branch whose theology already told them someone had to walk into the dark and keep the books.

The tragedy is that the ledger they were keeping eventually kept them.

Cultural traits

Clan-crest identity Lineage marked through a bonded crest-form (an animal, a natural feature, a Voidthorn-adjacent phenomenon in the more corrupted enclaves) worked into architecture, regalia, and formal address.
The Debt-Keeper lineages A rotating collective responsible for the precise tally of what is owed to which ruined or quarantined site, and by whom.
Redistribution over accumulation Standing is built by what a person has formally given away to settle a debt, and what they retain counts for nothing.
Shadow-Veil notation A closed writing system readable only by Drow practitioners, used specifically to record what happened at sites the rest of the world has agreed to forget.

Soul architecture
In the blood · Debt, the obligation an ending creates, a long way from nihilism, and the authority of having stood in the dark and mapped it.
Untrained lean · Spirit 60% / Fate 30% / Body 10%, the strongest lean toward Fate of any elven lineage, and the structural source of their unusual reach and Domain authority. (An untrained lean is the tilt of the three layers of a soul before anyone has trained them, and it never sets Mastered or Walked.)
Advantages

Shadow Parallax passive three-layer Aetheric perception, physical, Aetheric, and Veil-sheen simultaneously.
Fracture-channel architecture Crystal fractures functioning as efficient shadow-frequency routing rather than pure damage.
Drow Veil sensitivity past events leave readable impressions across their Domain territory, an involuntary archive.
Nullity function in Essence-hostile environments where other practitioners shut down entirely.

Limitations
Inherited Crystal fractures: the lineage begins with compromised architecture; learning to route power through the fracture rather than around it is the central Drow developmental challenge.
Social trust penalty (−10): an institutional role as recorder of unpaid debts and manager of acknowledged harms does not generate warmth, and the Drow have made a kind of peace with that.
Erebus-contact risk: the same access that makes them effective can, pursued too far, produce Crystal inversion.
Relations
Eresseans see Drow as living proof of elven failure. Drow consider the Eressean archive of the Schism period incomplete because the Eresseans have never found a way to ask the Drow, directly, for what they know. Both sides are, in the historical record’s own words, still waiting for the other to acknowledge the gap.
Rovann functions less as a capital than as the largest single concentration of Debt-Keeper lineages in one place, and its government, a Twilight Matriarch advised by the Council of Whispered Blades, is best understood as the administrative apparatus of an extremely old, extremely precise accounting practice with very good knives.
Eladrin: The Seasonal Courts of Iampu
Eressean daughters who took Order as Devotion into the northern theater and discovered that fixed rite alone could not survive the cold. What replaced it, gradually, was a second theology built on top of the first: that true devotion sometimes means surrendering the will to insist at all, and yielding entirely to season, silence, and collective endurance.
This produced the Kingdom of Iampu’s defining feature, a Crown that rotates with the solstices and equinoxes rather than passing by bloodline, since no single will, however devoted, is trusted to outlast an entire winter’s judgment alone.

The Ice-Voice Conflict, in this reading, had nothing random about it. It was the moment an entire generation’s collective silence-as-endurance tipped over into total Stasis, threatening to freeze the whole regional lattice solid, and had to be answered by a silencing whose exact method the Eladrin themselves have never fully recovered.

Cultural traits

The Seasonal Crown Leadership rotates formally to a new monarch at each solstice and equinox, per the Treaty of Four Courts.
Silence as high courtesy Prolonged, deliberate silence during negotiation is read as strength and patience rather than evasion. Queen Seralyth’s unbroken silence during negotiations is the Court’s own gold standard of statecraft.
Frost as preservation The Eladrin’s core reframing of an Eressean anxiety: what the Order-as-Devotion branch fears losing, the Eladrin believe cold simply holds in trust until it is needed again. They would have you know that it is not death, and their fruit in midwinter is excellent.
The Frost Council Elemental enchanters and climate-diviners advising whichever Court currently holds the Crown, providing the one continuous institutional thread across every seasonal transfer of power.

Limitations

Brittle Soul: Chaos and Vibration attacks deal +25% damage; cannot wield fire or passion-aligned glyphs.
Trait Lock: Stasis Shock on Aether-zero causes three-turn complete immobilization; Crystal freezes at Fire tier without active challenge.
Inertia: Dexterity Burst and Celerity floor. Initiating motion from stillness requires overcoming their own architecture: the literal cost of a theology built on yielding to season rather than asserting against it.

Relations
Eladrin maintain closer cultural ties to distant Eressean cousins than either branch advertises openly, and treat the relationship with the caution of two people who both know exactly how the last serious disagreement between their theologies nearly ended. They hold their Winter and Spring Courts’ seasonal handoffs as the clearest surviving proof that Order as Devotion and Silence as Endurance can, occasionally, still agree on something.
Echo Elves: The Longhouse Accord
The second Eressean daughter-people, and the only elven branch produced by conviction rather than geography or catastrophe.
When the post-Spirit-War Celestial Accord was drafted, a faction of Eressean jurists objected to what they called its flawed memory-logic, and had no quarrel with its goals: clauses whose exact meaning depended on interpretation rather than precise, mutually memorized wording.

The discipline they developed: no agreement is considered binding until every signatory can recite its full terms back without variation. A practice that makes Echo Elf diplomacy exhaustingly slow and, by their own account, the only kind of peace that has never once needed to be refought.

Cultural traits

The Recitation No Echo Elf treaty, internal or external, takes effect until all parties recite its full terms identically in open session. The law requires it, and they will wait.
Confederated rather than crowned No monarch. Decisions binding the whole body require consensus across every represented lineage-house.
Compulsive restatement as a documented speech pattern Echo Elves in ordinary conversation frequently restate an agreed fact exactly once more before moving on, a diplomatic habit so ingrained it has become a linguistic signature, the echoing Zo phonemes.
The Longhouse Accord The founding covenant among the original dissenting lineage-houses, kept as the living model for how the Echo Elves later helped shape Altherion’s River Crown Council, whose coalition-of-elected-representatives structure owes more to Echo Elf political philosophy than Altherion’s official histories tend to credit.

Relations
The Celestial Accord refusal remains, in the Eressean political body’s own words, a wound that has not fully healed. The Echo Elves were not wrong, exactly, and that is the trouble: their walking away proved the Order-as-Devotion theology could produce a faction devoted enough to its own logic to reject the parent society’s biggest diplomatic achievement outright.
Warm, functional relations with Altherion’s multi-racial republic, whose confederated governance already resembles the model the Echo Elves live by. Cool, formal relations with the Grand Principality of Eresse, who have never entirely forgiven the walking away and have never entirely disagreed with the reasoning behind it either.
Moves, Costume and What Everyone Says
The bracket crowds of Altherion know the five branches on sight and bet accordingly. Each has the move people pay to see, and each has a name for the aura coat (the visible coat of a fighter’s own color) that doubles as an accusation: the Eressean Vael-aurë, the kept light, which must never flicker; the Varrisak say it should flicker, and call theirs the leaf; the Drow keep theirs so low that the Guild’s word for it in Rovann is unpaid.









































BranchThe moveThe lookWhat they say about the othersEresseanVael Sereth, the Ninth Stillness: a Domain laid down so stable that a thrown spear finishes its arc politely and on timeSun-gold on white, a rite-office badge, not a hair out of order”Varrisak cannot tell you what they believed last year, and that is their theology”VarrisakForest Answers: the ground, the roots and the crows all arrive first, and the elf turns up to take the creditBark-paint, moss-green, bare feet, a different story each time you ask”An Eressean prays with a ruler”DrowAccount Rendered: the Fracture-channel pays out through the crack in their own Crystal, and the shadow they send you has your name on itMidnight blue, crest-silver, a very small notebook”We have your family’s figures, if you would like them”EladrinWinter Keeps It: they stand. They go on standing. You have now been frozen for some timeFrost-blue and pearl, breath that does not fogA long look, and they will consider this a replyEcho ElvesSay It Back: a Vow Clause called across the measure, and if you agreed to its terms in your pride, you are now bound by themLonghouse braids, a clause-cord knotted at the belt”Eressean keep their word, up to the part they forgot. Eressean keep their word, up to the part they forgot”


“Five children remembering one mother’s voice, each one certain the others have gotten the tune wrong.”
Attributed to a Sunroot-era elegy, author lost to all five archives equally



The High Empire of Eresse
