races--and--peoples/the-tongues-of-the-r.title: Common — The Tongue With No Distinctions
races--and--peoples/the-tongues-of-the-r.content:
The tongue the story is told in. The Tongues of the Realms governs, with one exception noted below.

Kha-Vaross. The weightless tongue.
What the Mandate calls it, and it is no compliment

In a good spring on the Long Quay, Sibby Tamm, a rope-seller of the southern ports in a yellow headscarf, sold one boatload of saffron to three separate buyers in a single afternoon, in Common, to their faces, with a crowd around her eating whelks. All three believed they owned it. All three went to law at Sealhall with advocates and their best furs, and the chancery sat a full week over her exact words. It found that she had said she would see them right, that she meant to have it there by the tenth, that a man could do worse, and that nobody would regret it, and that nowhere in any of this had she told anybody anything. The court said so with visible regret and let her go, and nobody has yet explained whose saffron it was.
That is the tongue this whole archive is written in. Keep one hand on your purse while you read it.
Why This One Gets a Document
These shelves give a tongue its own grammar when a reader will meet it untranslated. Common fails that test completely, because Common is the page. Everything on these shelves is already in it.
It earns an entry for a different reason. Its central feature is alive in every conversation anyone in the four quarters has, and getting it wrong flattens a speaker’s class, origin and education into nothing. The other grammars exist so that a foreign line lands. This one exists so that an ordinary line does.
I. What Common Is
A Concord human vernacular that took Accord Latin as its prestige layer and then absorbed loans from everyone it traded with, fought, garrisoned, or was garrisoned by.
The result is a language with two words for nearly everything: a short plain one from the vernacular core and a long formal one from the Latin overlay, sitting side by side, meaning approximately the same thing and placing the speaker completely.













































PlainLatinateaskinquirecutengravespeakinvokethe pouringDraftcraft, Ars Vasispayremitholdretainbreakviolatethe writingthe inscriptiona moutha speaker
Neither column is more correct. Which one a character reaches for is characterization before it is information, and a character who crosses between the columns mid-sentence is doing something: reaching up, condescending, or being caught out.
II. The Hole
Every tongue in this archive is built around something it makes impossible. Old Vaross cannot let a quality float free of the thing it describes. Eressean cannot state a possession without naming who stood for it. The Tally-Tongue has no future tense. Accord Latin’s invocation register has no first person.
Common forces nothing.
A speaker of Common is never obliged to say whether a claim was witnessed, whether an act was recorded, whether a promise was sworn, or whether the quality he just used belongs to anyone in particular. Every distinction the other tongues make compulsory, Common makes optional, and a speaker who wants to leave all of them open can do so in a perfectly ordinary sentence that nobody will query.
This is why it spread and why every other people distrusts it.
It is the only tongue in the four quarters in which it is comfortable to say something without committing to anything. Merchants negotiate in Common because a negotiation in Eressean concedes standing with every possessive, and a negotiation in Marrowkin forces a man to swear or admit he has not begun. Common lets both parties talk for three hours and leave with nothing conceded, which is what a negotiation is for.
And it is why Accord instruments are not written in Common. Common cannot bind. The chancery has said so in as many words, four times, across four revisions of the formulary.
The future tense
The feature every other people finds scandalous and every Concord speaker finds unremarkable.

I will pay you on the tenth.

A Marrowkin hearing that translated has heard a man produce an entire verb form for a thing he has not undertaken. There is no equivalent in the Tally-Tongue, and the constructions a Marrowkin reaches for to render it come out as either an oath or an admission that nothing has begun. The Marrowkin name for Common is Kielnur, the unentered tongue, and the Kegshard position is that a language with a future tense is a language built for people who intend to be believed without being bound.
The Eressean name is Aureth, the unwitnessing, and it is the same complaint from the other direction.
III. Phonology
Large, tolerant and inconsistent, because it absorbed four sound systems and discarded none of them.
The stress is a passport. Common has no regular stress rule, and decay had no part in that. Each stratum kept the stress it arrived with, so a word’s pattern reports which war, treaty or trade route brought it.









































StratumStressShapeExampleVernacular coreinitialshort, closed, one or two syllableshold, bar, stackVaross loansinitialheavy onsets, clusteredcadre, drack, thrumMarrowkin loansinitialdoubled consonants, long vowelstally, cask, olletEressean loansnever finalopen, liquid, ending in a vowel or nasalseth, thair, lithLatin loanspenultimatethree and four syllables, -ion, -ate, -oryregister, attestation, formulary
A clerk who says reGISter trained in the chancery. One who says REGister learned the word at a gate. Both are correct, and a room full of clerks hears the difference in one syllable and does not mention it.
IV. The Strata
The vernacular core. Short, closed, monosyllabic. Body, weather, labor, kinship, violence, food. The oldest layer and the least changed, because nothing about carrying a load or burying a parent has needed a new word.
The Latin overlay. Law, contract, examination, craft, administration, medicine, measurement. Arrived with the Accord and arrived from above. Nearly every abstraction in Common is Latin, which is why a speaker reaching for a general idea sounds educated whether he is or not, and why a speaker who wants to sound plain has to work at it.
Vaross loans came through garrison and war. Cadre, from kaadre, a garrison settlement, now a body of men held together by their officers. Drack, from drakh, the ground moving under a standing thing, now the first moment of a rout and the specific noise a line makes as it goes. Thrum, from thruum, a decree read aloud, now the sound of a crowd receiving news. Soldiers’ words that civilians adopted, all three keeping their clusters.
Marrowkin loans came through trade and the vaults. Tally, from tallu, the record. Cask, from kaas. Nick, from nikka, an angle, now a cut made at one. Ollet, from ollut, a brew come to age, now any strong ale and specifically one you did not brew yourself.
Eressean loans came through court and calendar, the smallest stratum and the highest status. Seth, from saeth, an appointed window: at seth is on time, off seth is late in a way that is somebody’s fault. Thair, from thaer, a records room. Lith, from lyth, silence, borrowed together with the Eladrin practice, meaning a deliberate pause held in negotiation, which Concord negotiators attempt and almost always break first.
There is no word for magic. Common refused one. It names the crafts by the labor: the work, the speaking, the writing, the cutting, the pouring, the singing. The Latin column exists for examiners and the plain column for everyone else, and a man who says magic has listened to too many minstrels and is about to be corrected by somebody who has not.
The street has its own words for the rest. Where a Guild roll says reinforcement, Pressure and sensing, a bracket crowd in Common says the shine, the weight and the nose, and every region has a further set it thinks is better. Ordinary fighters talk that way and scholars keep the real terms. The quarrel is laid out in Part Six of The Color of Essence.
V. Registers
Plain. Vernacular core, short sentences, Latin only where no plain word exists. What is spoken everywhere by nearly everyone.
High. The Latin column, longer periods, subordination borrowed wholesale from chancery syntax. Court, guild, examination, sermon, and any letter a man wants taken seriously. The tell is not vocabulary alone. High Common holds its main verb until late, which the vernacular core never does.
Cant. Dock, road and market argot, and the one register in which the Latin overlay is inverted. A Latin word used in cant is used mockingly, so remit in a dockside mouth means to be robbed and attest means to lie for a friend. Cant borrows heavily from Vaross and almost nothing from Eressean, which reports exactly who has been on the docks.
VI. Dialects
By quarter, and the differences are lexical and prosodic rather than grammatical.
Western. The Concord standard, because the chancery schools are there. Latin stratum heaviest, vowels short. Heard elsewhere as clipped and pleased with itself.
Northern. Heaviest Marrowkin loading, first-syllable stress generalized even onto Latin words. Slow. Reads as blunt to a westerner and honest to a northerner.
Eastern. Heaviest Eressean loading, calendar vocabulary in ordinary use, the lith actually practiced rather than attempted. An easterner who goes quiet in an argument has said something. A westerner reads it as having run out of words.
Southern and the ports. Cant closest to the surface, largest loan intake, fastest change. Almost every new word in Common in the last century entered through a port and was in respectable Western use within thirty years, while everybody denied where it came from.
VII. Script
An alphabet of twenty-four letters, and this is the reason Common won.
Songscript is a score and needs a musician. Marrowkin runes need an angle-set and a hand trained to it. Vaross tally-notation needs a blade and a board, and a document is an object that can be split with an axe. Common is written with ink on anything, in a hand a clerk’s son learns in a season, by somebody with no craft, no guild, no seven years and no master.
Literacy in Common is cheap. Literacy in every other written tongue in the four quarters is an apprenticeship. That single fact has done more to spread Common than the Accord, the Concord, and every army either has fielded.
It is not one of the Fourteen Hands and does nothing on its own. Words written in it are inert. Every other script in this archive acts on the world by existing, which is why the peoples who own those scripts regard the Common alphabet as a convenience rather than a writing system, and why Common speakers regard that judgment as the reason those peoples cannot get a letter to a village.
VIII. Speaking It Badly
Everyone speaks Common badly and nobody is corrected, which is unique among these tongues and has nothing to do with generosity. There is no prestige standard a foreigner is expected to reach, because Common’s speakers have never organized around one, because there is no guild, no chancery and no order with jurisdiction over it. A Marrowkin with forty years of blunt, article-dropping Common is understood, served and cheated in it as fluently as anyone else.
Goblinoid speakers drop articles, since Vaross has none, and stack compounds where Common wants an adjective, producing the flat noun-heavy speech Concord readers mistake for stupidity and which is a speaker refusing to let a quality float free of the thing it describes.
Marrowkin speakers state the copula every time, mark acts as recorded or not, and will not express an intention without swearing to it, so their Common reads as pedantic and evasive by turns. He is using the only distinctions he has.
Eressean speakers name their witnesses unprompted, over-specify provenance, and issue schedules instead of orders, which reads as aristocratic or paranoid depending on the listener.
Concord speakers of everything else carry the reverse habit and it is the worst of the four. Having a tongue that forces no distinctions, they assume none of the others do either. They translate my name into Eressean with the validated possessive and claim ownership of things they have merely been shown. They address Marrowkin by oath-names in the weak grade. They reach for a future tense in the Tally-Tongue and land in the oath form. Four Concord trade delegations have sworn by accident. None of them found out for a season.
IX. Sample Texts
The same statement, three registers.

Plain. He cut the ward himself and it held.
High. The inscription was engraved by his own hand and has been attested to hold.
Cant. He nicked it himself, and it’s still nicked.

A gate exchange, Northern.

“Tally?”
“Paid at the last one.”
“Tally, or you’re stood here till one comes.”

The Latin behind that is Solutum et transitum, in registro relatum. The corporal has never seen it written and says tally because a Marrowkin trader taught the word to a garrison two hundred years ago.
A refusal, Eastern.

“So we’re agreed.”
A lith, held.
”…Are we agreed?”

The easterner has answered. The westerner has now asked twice and conceded the room.
Notes
The names other peoples use. Kha-Vaross, the weightless tongue, from kha, that which has no load-bearing capacity, and vaross, the tongue that carries law. Both roots are old and the compound is the Mandate’s own joke: a tongue that carries nothing. Kielnur, the unentered tongue, Tally-Tongue, from -nur, the completed but unrecorded act. Aureth, the unwitnessing, Eressean, from ureth, the office of standing witness, with the privative. Three peoples arrived independently at the same complaint, which Concord scholars note with some pride and no reflection.


Accent — Placement, Prestige and the Shibboleth

races--and--peoples/the-tongues-of-the-r.title: Eressean and Varrisak — The Tongue of the Vey-Elarin
races--and--peoples/the-tongues-of-the-r.content:
A grammar of the elven tongue and its schism. The Tongues of the Realms governs.

“She sang one note. We have spent every Eon since arguing about how it should be sung back.”

Ruvaen of the Sylvaaren was taken up for poaching a white stag in a Sunroot preserve, and the jurists of Velthaeir, in their green and silver under the gold lamps, asked him his name. He gave it in the form his people use, -ieur, held and self-witnessed. The bench ruled that the form was ungrammatical, that an ungrammatical answer has not been given, and that a man who has not stated his name can be neither charged with a stag nor released from the charge. So every morning for thirty-one years they brought him up and asked, and every morning he answered in the same clear tenor, and the court recorded that he had said nothing. Eressean children play it on the cellar stairs, one as the bench and one as the poacher, and the minstrels of three quarters have the tune wrong. He died in that cell with the stag long eaten, and both branches count the case as a victory.
One language, two branches, and the disagreement between them is grammatical before it is legal. Eressean and Varrisak share phonology, most morphology and nearly all of the lexicon. They differ on one affix, and that affix decides who lawfully holds a name.
I. Attestation
The Velthaeir holdings. The Floating Archive-City is the largest body of record in any elven tongue and the least representative, because everything in it was entered in the sealed register by people whose profession was entering things in the sealed register. Velthaeir preserves how Eressean law was written across four Eons and almost nothing of how anyone spoke.
The rite calendars. Every Sunroot-descended house keeps its ceremonial windows in fixed wording, recopied without variation, and the recopying is itself a rite. These are the deepest attestation available for the archaic layer, and they are the reason the high register has not drifted measurably since the Spirit War. A phrase in a calendar is a phrase nobody has been permitted to improve.
The Dream Groves. Varrisak transmission is oral by doctrine, and the Groves are the only archive: old-growth root-networks carrying generations of practitioner Crystal-inclusion. What is held there is the experience of having heard a thing said, with no text anywhere in it, which the Varrisak consider a superior record and which is unreadable to any Eressean philologist who has tried.
The Accord’s compilations. Adequate on phonology, useless on the witness system, because the compilers took the validated and contingent possessives for a politeness distinction and glossed both as my. Every Concord treaty with an elven signatory drafted before the fourth century contains at least one clause that says something nobody at the table intended.
What is lost. The Vey-Elarin tongue as it stood before the five theologies. Both surviving branches claim to be the conservative one and both are demonstrably wrong, since each preserves archaisms the other has lost.
II. Phonology
Open, liquid, and light. Where Old Vaross builds heavy onsets and closes syllables hard, Eressean does neither, and a speaker moving between the two tongues sounds to both audiences as though they are performing an accent on purpose.













































LabialDentalAlveolarPalatalVelarStopsp, bt, dk, gFricativesf, vths, shhNasalsmnnyLiquidsl, ry
r is a light alveolar tap, never trilled and never syllabic. This is the first thing that separates an elven speaker from a goblinoid one, and the two peoples find each other’s r comic for opposite reasons.
There are no aspirates, no uvulars, and no geminates. A doubled consonant in the orthography, as in Rovann or Varrisak, marks the preceding vowel as short and is not itself lengthened.
Vowels. Five simple: a e i o u. Four diphthongs: ae ei ie ao. Vowel length is not phonemic. Vowel pitch is, and that is Section III.
Syllable shape. Onsets are single consonants or nothing. Words may and often do begin with a vowel: Eresse, Elarin, Iampu, Altherion. This is categorically forbidden in Vaross and permitted without comment here, which is why the two languages have almost no loanwords in either direction despite six centuries of adjacency.
Codas. A word ends in a vowel, a liquid, a nasal, or th. Nothing else. Velthaeir, Sylvaar, Rovann, Seralyth, Eresse. A word ending in a stop is not an Eressean word, and the language has a productive suffix, -ak, whose entire function is to mark something as foreign. That suffix is the origin of the name Varrisak, and the Varrisak know it.
III. Prosody
Pitch, not duration and not volume. The Vey-Elarin were tuned into being as notes of a chord, and the language kept the mechanism.
Every lexical word carries one of three contours across its stressed syllable.

























ContourWrittenFunctionLevelunmarkedstatement, the neutral registerRisingú in citationthe incomplete, the pending, the not-yet-validatedFallingù in citationthe settled, the closed, the witnessed
Contour is never written in running text and never written in Songscript prose, because a reader who needs it marked is a reader who should not be reading that document. It is written only in teaching grammars and in Accord compilations, which is one of several reasons Accord compilations are held in contempt.
The pitch does grammatical work. A falling contour on a possessive can validate a claim that the affix left contingent, and a rising contour can withdraw one that the affix granted. An Eressean jurist reading a deposition aloud in court is performing an act with legal weight, and a jurist who reads a rising contour where the text expects a falling one has said something actionable. Depositions are therefore read by two jurists in alternation and the second exists to catch the first.
Volume carries nothing at all, exactly as in Vaross, and for an unrelated reason. Vaross reserves volume for signaling across water. Eressean reserves it for song, and using a singing mechanism for speech is a category error that reads as either drunk or blasphemous depending on the room.
IV. Morphology
Roots
Roots are disyllabic and open: elar, vey, thaer, sylva, marin. A monosyllabic root is archaic, and the closed set of them is the oldest identifiable layer in the language.
The three canon particles
Three roots do more work than any others and are the phoneme chains an Eressean practitioner routes Essence through most efficiently.
ma: to hold, to have in hand, without any claim about right.
ur: to witness, to stand for, to have been present and be answerable for it.
ie: the grant, the giving-over, the transfer itself.
Every institution in Eressean law is built out of those three and nothing else, which is why the language’s legal vocabulary is so shallow and its legal reasoning so deep.
There is no unwitnessed possessive
The central fact of the language. A speaker cannot say my name without also saying, in the same word, whether the holding was witnessed. There is no neutral form. Silence on the question is not available.




















FormSuffixMeaningValidated-urenheld, and the assembly stood for the holdingContingent-amaheld, and nobody stood for it

elaruren: my name, and the witnesses were assembled and compensated
elarama: the name I am holding, and you are entitled to ask by what right

Both are perfectly grammatical. Only one is a claim. An Eressean who is asked their name and answers in -ama has said something enormous and entirely polite, and everyone in the room has heard it.
The Varrisak third form. -ieur, from ie and ur together: the grant and the witness collapsed into one act. It means held, and the holding witnessed itself. Varrisak doctrine is that a vision sought alone in old growth is a valid witnessing, because the forest was present and the forest is a relative rather than a resource, and a relative who was present has witnessed.
Eressean grammarians do not consider -ieur wrong. They consider it ungrammatical, which is worse, and the distinction matters: a wrong claim can be corrected, and an ungrammatical one has not been made. Four Eons of mutual illegitimacy proceed from that affix. Both sides are arguing in good faith and neither has ever conceded a syllable.
Other affixes








































AffixFunctionExample-incollective, the gathered kinvey, kin → Vey-Elarin, the kin of the note-engenitive, of, belonging to the estate ofthaeren, of the archive-ethoffice, the rite-role rather than the personuren → ureth, the office of standing witness-aerthe high, the raised, the floatingthaer → Velthaeir, the raised archive-akforeign, outside the formVarrisak, those outside the form-iththe small, and neutrally soelarith, a short name, a by-name
Note that -ith is neutral here and contemptuous in Vaross. Goblinoid and elven speakers have gone to war over less.
Verbs, and the window
Eressean has no imperative. There is no verbal form that orders an action. Politeness has nothing to do with it. The calendar does: an act has an appointed window, and to command is to name the window, after which the act follows because the window has opened.

Sae-ureth. The witnessing-office window stands open.
Stand witness. Now.

A speaker who wants something done says when it is due. A speaker with no authority to open a window cannot issue an order at all, in any register, using any construction, and Eressean political life is largely the study of who may open which window.
The verb accordingly marks not time but whether the act fell inside its window.

















MarkerMeaning-saein-window; done at its appointed time-loout-of-window; done in haste, in emergency, or in error

iesae: the transfer was made in its season
ielo: the transfer was made outside its season

-lo is not past tense and is not a judgment, formally. In practice a chain of -lo verbs in a deposition is how an Eressean advocate destroys a witness without ever calling them a liar.
Varrisak has no window marking and never developed it. In its place is an obligatory evidential: -ven seen, -dhae dreamed, -tor told by another. A Varrisak cannot report an event without stating how they came to it, and the dreamed evidential outranks the seen one, which Eressean speakers find so difficult that most simply stop translating at that point.
V. Syntax
Verb-initial in the high register. The act is named before the actors, because the rite is the subject of the sentence and the participants are its instruments.

Ie-sae Vey-Elarin thaeruren. Granted-in-season, the kin, the witnessed archive.

Subject-first in common speech. The colloquial register moves the subject forward and is understood by the high register to be lazy rather than wrong.
The witness slot is obligatory and final. Any clause making a claim ends by naming who stood for it. A clause that ends without one is complete and has claimed nothing, and Eressean speakers use bare clauses deliberately when they wish to say a thing without owning it. This is the single most common construction in Eressean diplomacy and the single most misread one in Concord transcripts.
No copula, and for the opposite reason to Vaross. Vaross omits it because identity is not asserted. Eressean omits it because identity is sung rather than stated, and a bare juxtaposition is understood to be quoting the Realmsong. Vey elar is the kin, the note, and it makes neither a metaphor nor a claim, being a citation.
VI. The Semantic Architecture
One. Ma against ur. To hold against to be answerable for holding. Every object, office, name, territory and debt in elven thought is sorted by whether anyone stood for it. There is no third category and no way to decline the question.
Two. Sae against lo. In its season against out of it. This is the Eressean model of virtue and it is not about outcome. An act performed correctly out of its window is worse than an act performed badly within one, and the Eressean will say so under oath.
Three. Elar. The note, and by extension the name, and by extension the person. There is no separate word for identity. There is elar, and a person’s elar can be held, granted, witnessed, vacated, or held contingently by somebody the assembly has not stood for, and all of those are things that happen to a note in a chord rather than things that happen to a self. A vacant name is a silence in a chord, and an Eressean hearing one described will hear the gap rather than the person.
VII. Registers
Common Eressean. Subject-first, contours flattened toward level, the witness suffix reduced to -ren and -ma. What is spoken in a Velthaeir kitchen. Fully mutually intelligible with Varrisak common speech, which both branches find embarrassing.
Ureth Eressean, the witnessing register. Court and deposition. Verb-initial, full contours realized, witness slot never omitted, -lo used surgically. Read aloud in alternation by paired jurists.
Elareth, the sung register. Rite and consecration. Not spoken at all. Every word carries its contour as pitch in the literal sense, the text is Songscript, and a rite performed in the wrong key has not been performed. This is the register the calendars preserve and the reason the archaic layer has not moved.
VIII. Dialects
Eressean. The standard by its own account. Contours fully realized, morphology conservative, -uren obligatory.
Varrisak. Faster, flatter contours, the evidential system in place of the window, and -ieur everywhere. Retains an imperative that Eressean lost, or invented one, depending on which philologist is asked. Oral only, by doctrine.
Eladrin. The northern courts made the pause a morpheme. A measured silence of a counted length functions as a particle, and the count is the meaning: a four-count is assent, a nine-count is a refusal that will not be argued, and a silence held past a nine-count has moved out of language and into judgment. Queen Seralyth’s unbroken silence through an entire negotiation is taught in the Winter Court as the highest sentence ever constructed in the dialect. Concord envoys transcribe these exchanges as having had nothing said in them.
Echo Elf. The restatement is grammatical rather than stylistic. An agreed fact takes the clitic zo and is repeated once, exactly, and an agreement that has not been zo-restated by every party has not been entered. The doubled zo phonemes are audible from across a room and are the reason Echo Elf negotiation takes as long as it does and has never once needed refighting.
Drow. Conservative in morphology, radical in script. Speech is close to archaic Eressean, with the witness suffixes intact and the window system reduced to a debt-marker: an obligation is either sae, still inside the term in which it may be paid, or lo, past it. Under pressure, Eressean structure surfaces in a Drow speaker’s grammar, and a Drow scribe who lets that happen in front of a witness has revealed something about their lineage they would rather not have.
IX. Script
Florwyndic Songscript, one of the Fourteen Hands, and the only writing system any elven branch acknowledges.
Each glyph carries two components: the segmental body, which records the consonants and vowels, and the contour rail, a line above the body recording the pitch. A Songscript text is therefore a score. It records how the thing must be sung and leaves what was said to look after itself, and a text without its rail has become a different kind of document entirely, a thing that can be read and cannot be performed.
Songscript is reserved for law and consecration. Ordinary Eressean correspondence is written in a Concord hand, and every Eressean feels mildly compromised about this and does it anyway.
The Varrisak have no script and want none. A law that can be written down can be followed without being understood, which they hold to be worse than no law at all. The Dream Groves are the archive and the archive is alive, and the Varrisak position is that Eresse mistook a filing system for a memory four Eons ago and has been arguing from a transcript ever since.
Drow Shadow-Veil notation is a closed system, readable only by Drow practitioners, used to record what happened at sites the rest of the world has agreed to forget. It is not a hand of Parun and does not pretend to be.
X. Lexicon
Name, note and person. elar, note, name, person. elarith, a by-name. elareth, the sung register. vey, kin, relative. Vey-Elarin, the kin of the note.
Holding and witness. ma, to hold. ur, to witness. ureth, the witnessing office. ie, the grant. -uren, validated. -ama, contingent. -ieur, self-witnessed, Varrisak only.
Season and window. sae, in season. lo, out of season. saeth, an appointed window. saethen, of the calendar.
Archive and place. thaer, the kept thing, archive. -aer, raised, floating. Velthaeir, the raised archive. vel, high. ann, beneath. Rovann, the place beneath.
Forest and depth. sylva, growing ground. aar, old, deep. Sylvaar, the old growth. dhae, the dream. -dhae, dreamed evidential. ven, seen. tor, told.
Cold and silence. seral, the held season, winter. lyth, silence. Seralyth, winter-silence.
Function words. zo, the restatement clitic, Echo Elf. -ak, foreign, outside the form. -in, collective. -en, genitive. -eth, office.
XI. Sample Texts
The oldest surviving formula, Elareth register.

Elar iesae. Elar uren. Vey-Elarin ureth.
The note, granted in season. The note, witnessed. The kin, standing in the office of witness.
The name passes at its appointed hour. The name is witnessed. The kin stand for it.

From a Velthaeir deposition, Ureth register.

Ielo. Ielo. Elarama vey-en.
Granted out of season. Granted out of season. A contingently held name, of that kin.
He was given it twice, both times outside the window, and what he is holding is not yet his.

A Varrisak reply, recorded by an Eressean who considered it unanswerable.

Elarieur. Sylvaar ven-dhae. Sylvaar ur.
Self-witnessed name. The old growth, seen-and-dreamed. The old growth, witness.
I hold my name and the forest stood for it. You were not asked because you were not there.

Echo Elf assent.

Ie-sae. Zo ie-sae. Uren zo.
Granted in season. Restated: granted in season. Witnessed, restated.

A proverb both branches claim.

Ma-ama, lyth. Ma-uren, elar.
Held unwitnessed, silence. Held witnessed, a note.
What nobody stood for makes no sound in the chord.

XII. Speaking It Badly
Concord speakers cannot hear the contours at all, and their flat delivery renders every claim they make legally void in an Eressean court without their ever learning why. They also default to the validated -uren on everything, since it sounds more respectful, and thereby claim ownership of items, offices and people they have merely been shown.
Goblinoid speakers trill the r, close their syllables, and reach instinctively for an imperative that does not exist, producing window-statements with no authority behind them. A Vaross speaker in an Eressean chamber is a man repeatedly announcing that the hour has come, to a room that knows perfectly well he cannot open it.
Marrowkin speakers handle the phonology well and the witness system badly, because Tally-Tongue oath-names put the answerability in the name itself rather than in an affix, so a Marrowkin speaking Eressean under-marks constantly. They are heard as evasive when they are being, by their own lights, redundant.
Eressean speakers of Common over-specify provenance, name their witnesses unprompted, and produce sentences that read to Concord ears as either aristocratic or paranoid. They also refuse to give orders and issue schedules instead, which has cost at least two joint campaigns their opening week.
Notes on Names
On Varrisak against Vassirak. Both are Eressean coinages and neither is an endonym. Vassirak is the older, from vassir, to go out without a return date, and it fell out of use because it concedes that leaving was a journey. Varrisak replaced it, from varris, to be unfixed, and it concedes nothing. Varrisak is the current form and Vassirak is archaic, which means a character who uses Vassirak is either very old, quoting a very old document, or making a point. The Varrisak call themselves Sylvaaren, the old growth’s own, and have never once used either name for themselves in a document they wrote.

races--and--peoples/the-tongues-of-the-r.title: Old Vaross — The Goblinoid Tongue
races--and--peoples/the-tongues-of-the-r.content:
A grammar of the goblinoid tongue. The Tongues of the Realms governs.
Sir Hamon Manningtree of the Concord rode to the Salt Ford parley in scarlet with a peacock crest, shouted for an hour across the water at a hobgoblin kaan (an officer) named Grakk Thurnen, and watched the man’s voice sink and his words slow, until Sir Hamon, who had been told all his life that a quiet enemy is a beaten one, turned grinning to his trumpeters and told them to sound the victory. The last word Thurnen spoke was durraak, a thousand years and feel the length of it, held for as long as one breath could hold it with the whole ford listening, and the spears came up out of the reeds before the vowel had finished. The crest is in the Keth-Gorrum’s timber archive to this day, nailed to the board that records the parley. The board’s entry runs to one word, with so many crossing cuts that the stem looks like a comb.
What the kaan did with that vowel is the load-bearing fact of this tongue. The rest of it follows, and the Accord’s grammars still get half of the rest wrong.
I. Attestation
Three bodies of record and none of them disinterested.
The Keth-Gorrum registers. Moot record of the Hobgoblin Expanse, continuous since the settlement, held in the Vaross the moot uses for its own proceedings. Voluminous, procedurally obsessive, and useless for anything colloquial, because nothing colloquial was ever entered.
The Mandate’s decree archive. Every active decree read daily at every district garrison for the entire history of Undaar-Keth, and every one of them written down. This is where the modern spoken language is best preserved, because a decree is written to be read aloud to people who must understand it, which is the only formal register in the four quarters under continuous pressure to stay comprehensible.
The Accord’s grammars. Compiled by philologists at Altherion across four decades. Excellent phonology. Confident and repeatedly wrong on semantics, because the compilers translated nakh and brakh as take and carry and never worked out that the pair is one concept split in half. Half the errors downstream in Concord scholarship come out of that single decision.
What is lost. Everything before the Scattering. The goblinoid peoples crossed the water carrying what could be carried, and a language’s older layer is not a thing you can carry. What survives of pre-Scattering Vaross is a closed set of roots preserved inside compounds nobody can decompose any more, and the Expanse’s philologists treat those the way other cultures treat relics.
II. Phonology





















































LabialDentalAlveolarVelarUvularStops, voicelessptkqStops, voicedbdgFricativesf, vths, shkh, ghNasalsmnngLiquidsl, r
r is an alveolar trill and is the language’s signature sound. It occurs syllabically, without a vowel, and this is the single most distinctive feature of Vaross to an outside ear. Grr is one syllable and contains no vowel at all. Concord speakers universally fail this and insert a vowel, which is the first thing that marks them.
kh and gh are true fricatives and never aspirated stops. q is uvular and occurs only in a handful of pre-Scattering roots, which is how philologists identify them.
Vowels. Five: a e i o u. Length is phonemic and is written doubled.



































ShortLongContrastaaakan, a hand set to a task. kaan, an officer.eeerareiiirareooogor, to weigh. goor, to be found wanting under weighing.uuuvashum, an opening. vashuum, a thing that opens where it should not.
Clusters. Heavy onsets are the rule, not the exception. Permitted initially: gr kr thr vr dr shk str vl kh gh thn. Permitted finally: kk rr nn tt rk sk ld and geminates generally.
Geminates are meaningful. A doubled consonant marks a completed or bounded action against an ongoing one. Dok, to strike at. Dokk, to have struck. This is why the strike-root in names is always geminate: Dokk-Vraal, the one who went out having struck, and Dokkan, of the completed strike.
Forbidden. No vowel-initial words. No final voiced stops. No sequence of three vowels. A word that breaks any of these is a loan and every Vaross speaker hears it as one instantly.
III. Prosody
Weight-timed, not stress-timed and not syllable-timed. A heavy syllable takes roughly twice the duration of a light one, and this is absolute. It is why Vaross spoken by a native sounds slow to Concord ears, and why Concord speakers of Vaross sound to natives as though they are gabbling through the important parts.
A syllable is heavy if it contains a long vowel, a geminate, a syllabic r, or a final cluster.
Emphasis is duration. Never volume.
This is the load-bearing prosodic fact and it is a cultural one. Volume in goblinoid usage is a signaling function, for shouting across water or a working floor, and carries no emotional content whatsoever. A goblinoid who raises his voice in an argument is understood to have lost control of the situation and is treated accordingly.
To emphasize, a speaker holds the vowel. In writing this is marked by doubling beyond the lexical length, so a word already long can go longer.

durrak: a thousand-count of years
durraak: a thousand-count of years, and I want you to feel the length of it

A Vaross speaker in a rage gets quieter and slower. Every Concord officer who has misread that has misread it exactly once.
IV. Morphology
Roots
Roots are monosyllabic, heavy, and carry a concept rather than a part of speech. Vorruk belongs to no part of speech. It is the concept of ground that tried to move and was stopped, and what it does in a sentence is determined by what is attached to it.
Derivational suffixes













































SuffixFunctionExample-ukthe resulting state of a force appliedvor, to shift → vorruk, ground that tried to move and was stopped-umthe gathered, the collectivegorr, weight → gorrum, an assembly-an, -engenitive; of; son or daughter ofDokkan, of the strike. Vreshen, of Vresh-akpertaining to the business ofthruum, a decree → Thruumak, of the reading-implural and possessive bothokk, we → okkim, ours. kha-ur → kha-urrim, humans-aalthe long form; augmentativeketh, a seal → Kethaal, the great seal. Also the Bugbear dialect marker-ithdiminutive, and always contemptuouskaan, an officer → kaanith, a jumped-up officer
Verbs
A bare root is an imperative. This is why Crimson Order speech under stress reads as a stack of nouns to an outsider: the subjects have dropped and what remains is roots.

Vrekh. Hold.
Rukh. Stand.

-aan is the directional, meaning toward or against, and it is the closest thing Vaross has to a finite verb. vashk-, to open → vashkaan, breaches against. nakh-, to take without bearing the cost → nakhaan, reaches for.
-akh is the completive. brakhakh okk, we have borne it, and it is finished.
skaal is the negative auxiliary and always stands last in its clause. It negates the whole clause and takes no subject, which is why refusals in a decree arrive with nobody in them. Skaal vashk. There shall be no breaching.
nurr is standalone refusal. Using it to a superior is a formal act with consequences, and rudeness does not come into it.
Compounding
Elements join with a hyphen and the second element governs. Gorr-Keth is a seal of the mantle-weight kind. Keth-Gorr is a weight of the sealed kind. Reversing a compound is a real and common insult in moot debate.
There are no adjectives
The most important fact in the language. A quality cannot float. It must be compounded onto a noun, which means every descriptive statement is an assertion about a specific thing.

shkarr, unshaped force → shkarr-kha-ur, a human made of unshaped force

There is no way to say savage in Old Vaross. There is only a way to say made of unshaped force, attached to somebody, in front of witnesses. Every Vaross insult is therefore a factual accusation, and a speaker asked to soften a description will restructure the entire sentence rather than reach for a milder adjective, because there are none to reach for.
V. Syntax
Neutral order is verb-final. Subject, object, verb.

Okk vorruk vrekh. We the stopped-ground hold.

Under stress the verb fronts. This is the Ironblood tell and it is involuntary. An Ironblood speaker who has begun to front his verbs has stopped choosing his words, and every hobgoblin in the room knows it.

Vrekh okk vorruk. Hold, we, the stopped ground.

A Crimson Order officer trained out of it will front only under extremity, and a hobgoblin who hears an Order officer do it will treat the situation as considerably worse than the officer has said it is.
No copula. Okk keth is we the seal, and it does the work of we are the seal without asserting anything about identity, which is why Vaross legal statements are difficult to challenge and why Accord clerks hate them.
VI. The Semantic Architecture
Three distinctions the language forces on every speaker.
Nakh against brakh. Nakh is to take without bearing the cost of taking. Brakh is to bear the cost. Every transaction, conquest, inheritance, gift and theft in goblinoid thought sorts into one or the other, and there is no neutral third verb. A goblinoid cannot describe an acquisition without also stating whether it was paid for.
Gorr against kha. Gorr is mantle-weight, what absorbs and does not move. Kha is the weightless, what has no load-bearing capacity. This pair is the goblinoid model of worth, and it is why humans are kha-urrim, and why the insult is not about strength.
Khal. Held, as a wound holds after stitching. There is no word in Vaross for healed. The nearest is khal, and it means the closing held, and it carries the wound in it permanently. Vorruk-Khal is the Expanse’s own name for itself, and it is an admission no goblinoid has ever been able to translate into Common without the Common version sounding either braver or sadder than the original.
VII. Registers
Common Vaross. The street. Compounds shortened, geminates lenited, the directional -aan reduced to -an. What is spoken in Kaadre-Six.
Thruum Vaross, the decree register. Clauses ordered by operational priority. Subjects present at the opening and dropped progressively. Full lexical length observed on every word. It exists to be read aloud to people who must act on it, and it is the reason the language has not drifted in six centuries.
Kethaal Vaross, the sealed register. The moot and legal layer, full of pre-Scattering roots nobody can decompose, and deliberately so. A Keth-Gorrum ruling is written in a register that requires an interpreter, and the interpreters are a profession, and the profession is hereditary.
VIII. Dialects
Hobgoblin. The standard. Vowels held to full length. Grr-Vashuum with the second syllable long, because the breaking was not quick.
Ironblood. Shorter vowels throughout, heavier consonantal attack, verb-fronting under far less pressure. Grr-Vashuum with the second syllable clipped. The two pronunciations of that one word are the whole political history of the goblinoid peoples in four syllables, and both peoples know it.
Gorr-Vaross, the Bugbear dialect. Marked by the -aal extension applied far beyond its augmentative function, producing the long-vowelled register outsiders find eerie. Vesh-Undaal rather than Vesh-Undar. Slower even by Vaross standards.
Goblin. Rapid, heavily contracted, with the syllabic r often lost. Held in contempt by every other dialect and demonstrably the most innovative, since almost every new coinage in the Expanse in the last century entered through it.
IX. Script
Tally-notation, cut rather than written.
The pre-Scattering script did not cross the water. What the goblinoid peoples rebuilt was a notation designed to be cut into wood, stone and bone with a single blade, because that is what could be done on ships and on volcanic rock with no ink and no hides.
Every character is a vertical stem with cuts to one or both sides. Consonants are cuts to the right, vowels are cuts to the left, and length is marked by a cut that crosses the stem entirely. The rank compound on Vresk Dokkan’s shoulder plate is four cuts and a crossbar and can be read at forty paces by anyone in the Mandate.
The consequence. Vaross is a language in which writing is a physical act performed on an object, and a Vaross document is therefore an object rather than a page. A decree is a board. A ruling is a post. The Keth-Gorrum’s archive is a room full of timber, every entry in it can be destroyed with an axe, this has happened, and the Expanse’s law has a hole in it where the year 411 used to be.
X. Lexicon
Force and violence. grr-, a force event, kinetic and percussive. dokk, the strike, completed. dok, to strike at. vashk-, to open, to breach. vashuum, a thing that opens where it should not. shkarr, unshaped force. drakh, fear, the ground moving under a standing thing.
Weight and worth. gorr, mantle-weight. goor, found wanting under weighing. kha, the weightless. kha-ur, a weightless one. kha-urrim, humans. brakh-, to bear the cost. nakh-, to take without bearing it. gor-, to weigh.
Ground and holding. vor-, to shift. vorruk, ground that tried to move and was stopped. vrekh-, to hold a line. rukh-, to stand. khal, held after stitching. vesh, a shelf or tier. undaar, the standing thing, that which does not fall.
Binding and law. keth, seal, binding. kethaal, the great seal. thruum, a decree read aloud. gorrum, an assembly. kaan, an officer. kaanith, a jumped-up officer. vaross, the tongue that carries law.
Persons and pronouns. okk, we. okkim, ours. ghrim, they. ghrimin, theirs. thaal, the elder. vraal, the one who went out.
Time and place. durrak, a thousand-count of years. mokk, the hearth-stone, home. ashfold, a district of the Mandate. kaadre, a garrison settlement.
Function words. skaal, shall not, clause-final. nurr, no, standalone refusal. -aan, toward, against. -akh, completive.
Pre-Scattering roots, undecomposable. qeth-, quum, qarr. All three appear only inside compounds, all three contain the uvular, and the Expanse’s philologists have four competing accounts of what any of them meant.
XI. Sample Texts
A proverb.

Brakhakh, keth. Nakhakh, vashuum.
Borne-and-finished, a seal. Taken-and-finished, a thing that opens where it should not.
What you paid for holds. What you took will open under you.

A moot formula, Kethaal register.

Keth-Gorrum gorrumakh. Vaross keth. Qeth-thruum rukhaan.
The gathered weight of the sealed assembly is gathered. The word is sealed. The old-decree stands toward.
The moot is seated. The word is sealed. The standing law is in force.

From the Third Ashfold Decree.
Ghrim shkarr okkim vashkaan. Ghrim drakh okkim nakhaan.
They unshaped-force ours open-toward. They fear ours take-toward.
They want savagery out of us. They come for our fear and mean to take it.
Durraak. Durraak. Brakhaan okk.
A-thousand-years-held. A-thousand-years-held. Bear-toward, we.
A thousand years. A thousand years. And we bore it.
Skaal vashk. Skaal drakh. Skaal nakh ghrim.
Shall-not breach. Shall-not fear. Shall-not take, they.
XII. Speaking It Badly
Concord speakers insert a vowel into syllabic r, producing gurr for grr, which is the single most reliable marker and is audible in the first word. They also emphasize by volume, which reads to a goblinoid audience as a man announcing that he has lost the argument.
Marrowkin speakers do well on the clusters and fail on vowel length, because Tally-Tongue gradation trains the ear to hear consonants as the carriers of meaning. A Marrowkin speaking Vaross produces grammatically flawless sentences with every emphasis in the wrong place.
Eressean speakers overuse the genitive, because Eressean cannot express possession without naming a witness, and a court Eressean reaching for that structure in Vaross generates of-of-of chains that Vaross speakers find both incomprehensible and hilarious.
Goblinoid speakers of Common drop articles, since Vaross has none, and reach for compounds where Common wants an adjective, producing the flat noun-stacked speech Concord readers mistake for stupidity and that is in fact a speaker refusing to let a quality float free of the thing it describes.
A note on Undaar-Keth and Undaar-Gorr. Under the compounding rule the second element governs, so Undaar-Keth is a seal of the standing kind and Undaar-Gorr is a mantle-weight of the standing kind. They are two different places, or one place renamed by somebody making a claim, and never spelling variants of one name.

races--and--peoples/the-tongues-of-the-r.content:
One of the better grammars on this shelf was paid for by an Altherion salt merchant who had just learned, in open court and in front of his wife, that he had sworn himself to a Marrowkin brewery for life.
The constructed languages of the Realms, each with its own grammar.


Common — The Tongue With No Distinctions The tongue the story is told in. The Tongues of the Realms governs, with one exception noted below.
Accord Latin — The Formulary and the Two Spoken Registers A formula set and a register guide. The Tongues of the Realms governs.
Eressean and Varrisak — The Tongue of the Vey-Elarin A grammar of the elven tongue and its schism. The Tongues of the Realms governs.
The Tally-Tongue of the Marrowkin A grammar of the tongue of the holds. The Tongues of the Realms governs.
Old Vaross — The Goblinoid Tongue A grammar of the goblinoid tongue. The Tongues of the Realms governs.

races--and--peoples/the-tongues-of-the-r.title: The Tally-Tongue of the Marrowkin
races--and--peoples/the-tongues-of-the-r.content:
A grammar of the tongue of the holds, Tallukieli in its own words and Runic Dawi on the older rolls. The Tongues of the Realms governs.

“A Marrowkin will tell you what he has done and what he has undertaken. Ask him what he will do and watch him reach for a word that is not there.”

They buried the brewmaster Ulvi Rautekk Sarnan at Kegshard with a thousand in the grand hall, the red and copper banners let down from the galleries and every cask in the lower vault tapped in his honor, and his oldest friend Tappo got up to give the reading with his mouth full of funeral pork. He reached the oath-name, the pork went the wrong way, and the close of it stayed in his throat. Raute. One grade down, in front of the widow, the whole hold and the Oath-Breakers’ wall. He had time to turn purple. The widow reached him first, with a cask bung, and after her it was everybody, for three days, with anvils in it by the second. When it ended fourteen Marrowkin had broken bones and the hold-clerks sat down to do what the law required, which was enter the entire affair in a wording that scanned. The line is in the Tally. It has the pork in it, in the strong position, and metricians come from Barkstone to admire it.
A people who will break a friend’s nose over one consonant have a grammar worth reading.
I. Attestation
The Tally. Every hold keeps one, and nobody should mistake it for a chronicle. It is a list of completed lawful acts and of everything taken from the Body, entered in fixed wording, with the entering itself a lawful act that gets entered. Six thousand years of it exist by its own count and almost none of it is narrative. What the Tally preserves is the exact phrasing in which a thing counts as done, and that phrasing has not been permitted to move.
The Kegshard oath-record. Cask-Oaths carved into fermentation barrels, held as long as the brew lives, with the accumulated tallies stored since the Second Eon. This is the best attestation of the oath register anywhere, because a Cask-Oath is inscribed once and cannot be recopied without ending the brew. Every barrel is a text nobody has been able to edit.
The Oath-Breakers’ wall. Kegshard Hold’s grand hall carries the public record of those who broke Cask-Oaths, and its entries are the only body of Marrowkin text written about people rather than acts. Philologists value it disproportionately, since it is the sole archive where a name is repeatedly written in the weak grade, which is otherwise never done on purpose.
The bills of sale. Every piece of the Body sold, read aloud and copied in two columns, one for the hold and one for the buyer, closing on the Return Clause. Tens of thousands survive in the chests of the people who bought them, unread, and they are the best evidence anyone has for how the clerks’ meter moved between one century and the next.
The Nine-Anvil inscriptions. Varun work, in Old High Runic, predating the Rite of Bound Geometry. These carry a different resonance from the modern hand and a noticeably older grammar, and the Varun position is that Old High Runic is not an ancestor of the spoken tongue at all but a parallel access to the Lattice, which no other lineage accepts and none has managed to disprove.
The Accord’s compilations. Better here than on any other tongue, because gradation is audible and the Accord’s philologists at Altherion were good phoneticians. Their semantic work is the usual disaster: they recorded the absence of a future tense as a curiosity of style.
The Old World cognates
The Accord’s philologists read the relationship with Old Vaross into the record at Altherion four decades ago and were expelled from both the Keth-Gorrum and the Ore Council in the same season. The evidence sits where relatedness always survives, in the low numerals and the body-part roots.








































SenseTally-TongueOld Varossoneyktukktwokahtkaddthreekolmkholmhandkadukanweight, load bornekurrgorrto stand, to not falluntarundaar
Both peoples have read the table. Neither has commented.
II. Phonology















































LabialDentalAlveolarVelarStopsptkFricativesvthshNasalsmnngLiquidsl, rGlidej
There are no voiced stops. b, d and g appear only in Concord transcription of Marrowkin names and are, to a Marrowkin ear, simply the same consonants spoken by somebody who is not paying attention. Borin is Porin. Kegshard is Kekshart. The holds have stopped correcting it.
Vowels. Eight, in two harmony classes.















FrontBackNeutralä, ö, ya, o, ue, i
Vowel harmony is absolute. A word draws its vowels from one class only, and every suffix has two shapes to match. This is the constraint that governs naming, and Section IV is where it becomes a political instrument. It also means the plain Common word rib-bone has no equivalent: kylki, rib, is front and luu, bone, is back, so the two cannot join, and the holds say kylki alone and let you work it out.
Length is phonemic and written doubled: kur, a load. kuur, the bearing of a load across time.
Clusters. Permitted initially, unlike most Finnic-shaped tongues, and this is held to be the strongest single argument for the Old World relationship. kr-, thr-, st-, vr-, tn-.
The under-note. Generations in the bone have given the speakers a second tone, an octave or so below the voiced word, sounding from the chest wall on every stressed syllable. It carries no grammar. It does carry through stone, which is why a clerk’s reading can be followed on the far side of a gallery wall, and why a Marrowkin who has been taught Common by a human still sounds to other Marrowkin as if he were speaking from inside a barrel, and sounds to the human as if the floor agreed with him. Foreign speakers cannot produce it and are not expected to, and its absence marks them from the first word.
III. Prosody
First-syllable stress, without exception. Stress never moves, which means it carries no information and is never used for emphasis. A Marrowkin cannot stress a word to make a point.
Emphasis is gradation, and Section IV explains the mechanism. What matters prosodically is that the emphatic device is a consonant rather than a pitch or a duration. Old Vaross holds the vowel. Eressean bends the pitch. The Tally-Tongue hardens the consonant, and all three peoples find the other two mechanisms slightly indecent.
Mathematical Cadence. Formal speech runs in fixed metrical feet, and the count is not decorative. A statement entered into the Tally must scan, and a statement that does not scan has not been entered, whatever it says. Hold-clerks are trained metricians before they are trained anything else, and a petitioner who cannot scan their own claim hires one who can. Outside practitioners describe hearing the cadence as hearing the grammar of the universe. Marrowkin describe it as the difference between a statement and a record.
IV. Morphology
Consonant gradation
The signature of the language and the load-bearing fact in it. A stem consonant alternates between a strong grade and a weak grade depending on the syllable that follows it.

































StrongWeakkkkppptttk∅pvtth

thrukka, the hold, in the strong grade
thrukan, of the hold, weak grade under the genitive suffix

Gradation is invisible as a rule and unmistakable as texture. A Marrowkin hears the grade before they hear the word.
Names, and what gradation does to them
A full name has four slots: a given name, an oath-name in the second place, a line in the genitive, and a cut-name. Before the given name a child has only a shift-name, the birth-shift and a count, Second-Shift Four, and nobody thinks this is unkind.
The given name is a two-element compound from a fixed inventory, conferred at the First Entry around the seventh year, on the same day the child takes a smear of marrow on bread and has its opening debt entered. The first element is traditionally a word of the Body or the gallery (hiil-, ember; ver-, blood; rin-, breast; sol-, collar; kyl-, rib; os-, a share cut); the second a word of the work (-run, -rin, -tar, -mo, -ja, -ri, -ppu). Clerks can no longer agree on what half the elements mean, and families fight over the rare ones.
The line is a hearth-line or a parent in the genitive: Sarnan, Vanhanan, Kreisan. A Marrowkin who has moved holds keeps it.
The cut-name is earned. It gives the largest single thing its bearer ever took from the Body, in plain words and usually in the speaker’s own language: Sixty Tuns, Half a Rib, Thimble. It is not graded, is never a compliment and never an insult, is used by everyone, and goes on the roll of the dead. Older bynames of deed survive from the deep halls and the five Reach branches, among them Straightedge and Sevenhoop, and the Reach still prefer them.
The oath-name is the one that matters. It is conferred at oath-taking, and two rules govern it, both structural rather than ceremonial.
One. The oath-name must harmonize with the given name. Vowel harmony is absolute, and a compound that mixes classes cannot be spoken. This means not every oath can be sworn by every Marrowkin, because not every oath-name will harmonize with the name a person already carries. Holds keep harmony tables. Marriages have been arranged around them. A young Marrowkin with a back-class given name is on a shorter list of possible oaths from the day they are named, and everybody involved knows it.
Two. The oath-name is spoken in the strong grade for as long as the oath stands.

Ilmo Torvekk Kreisan: the oath held
Ilmo Torve Kreisan: the oath broken

One consonant. Every Marrowkin in the room hears it, in the first syllable of the second name, before that name has finished, and there is no way to say it that conceals it. Losing an oath-name and breaking the oath are structurally the same event, and nobody hands it down as a punishment, because the Crystal registers the gap between stated intent and actual behavior without waiting to be told, and the language registers it the same way in the same instant.
A Marrowkin introducing themselves to a stranger is submitting to an audit, every time, in public, in one word.
Other affixes













































AffixFunctionExample-an / -ängenitive, of, from the hold ofthrukan, of the hold-ur / -yragent, one who doeskurrur, one who bears the load-ta / -täthe completed act, enteredkurta, a bearing that is in the Tally-nur / -nyrthe completed act, unenteredkurnur, a bearing nobody recorded-me / -mithe undertaken, under oathkurme, a bearing sworn to-us / -ysthe made thing, the artifactthrus, a cut inscription-lo / -löthe unbegunkurlo, a bearing not yet begun
There is no future tense
The second load-bearing fact. There is no verb form that says I will. The language offers three constructions and none of them is a prediction.

kurta: I bore it and it is in the Tally
kurme: I have undertaken it under oath
kurlo: it is unbegun

A Marrowkin asked whether they will do a thing answers in the oath form or the unbegun form. There is no third option and no softer one. To say kurme is to have sworn, with everything that follows, and to say kurlo is to have said nothing at all except that the thing has not started.
This is why Marrowhold’s commercial reliability is what it is, and why its diplomacy is so difficult for everyone else. A Concord envoy who wants an assurance is asking a Marrowkin to either take an oath or admit they have not begun. There is no available sentence in which a Marrowkin expresses a firm intention that is not yet binding, and every Marrowkin has spent their life not needing one.
The one place the tongue reaches past the present is the Return Clause, and it does so without a future: Lainuran palaute on, the Lender’s return stands, an existing fact about an event that has not happened. Clerks consider this the most frightening line in the grammar and read it in the same voice as the price.
V. Syntax
Verb-final, subject-initial. Neutral order is subject, object, verb, the same shape as Old Vaross and one of the quieter arguments for the shared ancestor.

Porin thrus kurta. Porin the inscription bore-and-entered.

The doer stands at the front and is obligatory. Every act in the formal register opens on the name of whoever did it. There is no passive, no impersonal and no way to say that mistakes were made. A statement with no doer in it does not scan and has not been said, and the holds’ own explanation is the plainest thing in the grammar: when the Body asks, someone has to answer.
The Tally slot is final and obligatory in the formal register. Any statement of an act ends by marking whether it is entered. A clause left in -nur is a clause admitting the act happened and was never recorded, which in a hold is a heavier admission than most confessions. So every sentence that matters runs from a person to a verdict, and a trained ear hears the doer and waits for the slot. A sentence built in Common, with nobody at the front of it, goes past a hold-clerk like a gap in a wall.
Word order does not move under stress. It cannot, because gradation is doing the emphatic work and stress is fixed. Marrowkin under extreme pressure produce syntactically identical sentences to Marrowkin at rest, with different consonants, which is why other peoples consistently misread their agitation and why they consistently misread everybody else’s.
There is a copula and it is used constantly. on, invariant. Vaross omits it, Eressean omits it, and Marrowkin state it explicitly in every predicate, which both neighbors find laborious and which the holds regard as the only honest way to assert that a thing is the case.
VI. The Semantic Architecture
One. Entered against unentered. -ta against -nur. Every act is either in the Tally or outside it, and the distinction is not about importance. An unentered act is no lesser for it, only unowned, and a hold cannot be asked to stand behind it.
Two. Undertaken against unbegun. -me against -lo, with nothing between. This is the hole the language builds its ethics in.
Three. Strong against weak. Gradation is a grammatical process and simultaneously the entire status system. The language never describes a person’s standing. It pronounces it, every time their name is said, by whoever is saying it, including their enemies. There is no polite grade and no way to grant one as a courtesy.
Four. Owed. velka, the debt to the Body, takes no plural and no possessive. Each person’s share is reckoned, and in the grammar there is one debt, and it belongs to nobody in particular until a doer is placed in front of it.
VII. Registers
Out-Tally. External use, for trade and for Concord contact, called Common Dawi on the older rolls. Gradation preserved, Mathematical Cadence dropped, the doer and the Tally slot optional. This is the only register in which a Marrowkin can leave an act unmarked without saying something, and it is the reason a great deal of the holds’ business with outsiders is conducted in it.
The Tally-Tongue, the Barkstone dialect. The working language of the holds. Full gradation, full harmony, Tally slot obligatory, cadence in formal contexts. Every phoneme carries material-world resonance, which is the Cask Line’s own account of why their brewing chants work.
Oath register. Cask-Oath inscriptions and hold-oaths. Fixed wording, strict meter, and a fourth register at Kegshard that is not publicly documented and about which the maintainers have never been successfully asked.
Old Alchemic Song. The tonal register of the brewing chants, sung at a pitch that works the liquor.
Old High Runic. Sacred inscription, predating the Rite of Bound Geometry, carrying a different resonance and an older grammar in which gradation is not yet regular. Read by Varun rune-forgers and by nobody else with confidence.
VIII. Dialects
Barkstone. The standard. Slow, heavily graded, with the longest vowels of any dialect.
Varun, the High Line register. Mathematical Cadence extended out of the formal register into ordinary speech, so that Varun speak in meter continuously. Other Marrowkin find this exhausting and slightly self-satisfied. The Varun are unaware of the impression and would not adjust if they were.
Low Tally, the Hollow dialect. Deepkin. The hollow vocal quality has a physical cause: sound stops carrying resonance in a Deepkin throat, so the fricatives lose their friction, the under-note goes altogether and the whole inventory shifts toward nasals and stops. Gradation survives and is the only reliable way to read a Deepkin’s standing, since the rest of the phonology has flattened.
Rib-knock. A tapped code on bone and stone, learned by every child in the Ring before letters, carrying the Tally register at walking pace through a mile of rib. A doubled knock is the strong grade, so a name knocked along a gallery carries its oath with it. Forge Guard officers use it in battle. Shift-mates use it to warn each other about the foreman.
Mirror-Sign. A full manual language with its own grammar, neither dialect nor code, used wherever vocal speech would leave an Aetheric signature or acoustic evidence, which for Deepkin is most contexts. It has no gradation, and this is the single most discussed fact about it in the holds: Mirror-Sign is the only language of the people in which a broken oath does not announce itself. Deepkin do not consider this a defect. Every other lineage does.
IX. Script
Cut runes, geometric, one of the Fourteen Hands.
Every character is constructed from straight strokes at fixed angles, and the angles are the meaning rather than the shape being the meaning. A rune cut at the wrong angle is a different rune, or no rune, and it does nothing, which makes the word misspelling far too kind.
Gradation is written. The strong grade takes a doubled stroke and the weak grade a single one, which means a name carved into stone or bone carries its oath-status permanently and visibly. A hold’s roll of the dead can be read for oath-breaking at a glance, from across the chamber, forever.
The Rite of Bound Geometry fixed the angle set. Old High Runic predates it and uses angles the modern hand does not permit, which is why old inscriptions read as slightly askew to a modern eye and why the Varun insist they are not askew at all but correctly aligned to something the Rite stopped describing.
The Soul-Rune practice puts the same script on the body, cut into the ridges of the rise. An elder’s body is a reading of their life, and the entries are in the Tally register, and they accumulate, and they cannot be revised.
X. Lexicon
Weight and bearing. kurr, a load. kuur, the bearing of a load across time. kurrur, one who bears. untar, to stand, to not fall. thruk, a hold, a stronghold, and the act of holding.
Oath and tally. kurme, the undertaken. tallu, the record. tallut, an entry. vann, an oath-name. vannus, the conferring of one. kreis, a hearth-line, a lineage.
The Body. luu, bone. ytin, marrow. kylki, rib. rintaluu, breastbone. solisluu, collarbone. veri, blood. hehkuveri, the glow-blood. lainur, the Lender. velka, the debt. palaute, the return. luuthruk, bone-hold, the realm. ytinkreis, the people’s own name for themselves.
Cutting and making. thrus, a cut inscription. thrusur, one who cuts. nikka, an angle. nikkat, the fixed angle-set. raut, worked iron. rautus, a made thing of iron. hiillos, an ember.
Brewing and time. ollu, the brew. ollut, a brew that has come to age. kaas, the cask. kaasme, a Cask-Oath. ikke, the cycle, the turn of a process.
Depth and silence. sylv, the deep working. hollu, the hollow, the emptied. hollut, one whose voice has stopped carrying. mirr, the hand-sign.
Function words. on, the copula. ei, not. ykt kaht kolm, one two three.
XI. Sample Texts
A Tally entry, formal cadence.

Porin Kurrekk Vanhanan thrus kurta. Nikkat on. Tallut on.
Porin, oath-name in the strong grade, of Vanhan, the inscription bore-and-entered. The angle-set stands. The entry stands.
Porin son of Vanhan, oath standing, made the inscription and it is recorded. The angles are true. The entry holds.

The close of a bill of sale.

Lainuran palaute on. Tallut on.
Of-the-Lender the return stands. The entry stands.
Returnable on the Lender’s demand. It is written down.

The oldest surviving Cask-Oath opening.

Ollu elää, kaasme elää. Ollu kuolee, ei kaasme kuole.
The brew lives, the oath lives. The brew dies, the oath does not die.
While it ages, I am bound. When it is gone, I am still bound.

The second clause is grammatically unusual and every child is taught why: the negative ei takes the oath out of the cycle entirely, so the Cask-Oath outlives its own cask. Whether the barrel in Kegshard’s deepest vault is being maintained for the brew’s sake or because nobody wants to test that line is not discussed.
From the Oath-Breakers' wall.

Ilmo Torve Kreisan. Kurnur. Kurnur. Kurnur.
Ilmo, oath-name in the weak grade, of the hearth-line. Unentered. Unentered. Unentered.
He is named without his oath, and three things he did were never recorded.

The wall never states the offense. It states the grade and the count of unentered acts, and the holds consider that sufficient.
A refusal.

Kurlo. Ei kurme.
Unbegun. Not undertaken.
No. And do not ask me for the other word.

XII. Speaking It Badly
Concord speakers voice the stops, producing Borin for Porin and Kegshard for Kekshart, and they treat gradation as free variation, which means they call Marrowkin by their oath-names in the weak grade constantly and without noticing. The holds have stopped taking offense and have not stopped hearing it. Concord speakers also reach for a future tense that does not exist, and their attempts to construct one land in the oath form, which is how at least four trade delegations have accidentally sworn. They drop the doer as well, out of a lifetime’s politeness, and leave sentences that a clerk simply does not write down.
Goblinoid speakers manage the clusters easily and destroy the harmony, since Vaross has none, producing words that mix classes and are simply unpronounceable rather than merely wrong. They also emphasize by holding the vowel, which in a language with phonemic length changes the word.
Eressean speakers do the harmony well, the gradation adequately, and the tense system not at all, because the Eressean window system marks whether an act was timely and the Tally-Tongue marks whether it was sworn, and the two do not map. An Eressean speaking it produces beautifully scanning statements about seasons in a language that does not care what season it was.
Marrowkin speakers of Common state the copula every time, name the doer every time, mark every act as entered or unentered, and refuse to express intention without swearing, so their Common reads as pedantic, over-precise and evasive in turn. The speaker is using the only distinctions they have, in a voice with a floor under it.
Notes on the Sources
On Lattice Tongue. Varun sources describe Lattice Tongue as foundational Parunic access rather than a language of the people, and it is treated that way here. It belongs with the Descent of Parun, not with this grammar. The Varun claim that Old High Runic is a parallel access to the Lattice rather than an ancestor of the spoken tongue is recorded as their position and is not adopted, since no other lineage accepts it and the numeral cognates point the other way.
