the-bestiary/the-called-and-the-divine/s.title: Obrenkael · The Mule
the-bestiary/the-called-and-the-divine/s.content:
Native-Consenting bearer form. Mahuo line, Aperture branch. Filed under standing Bench objection.

Every skull on the cord is a promise a summoner made and could not keep. Four of them belong to the practitioner who currently holds the naming-right.
This entry records a called thing that becomes measurably stronger each time it is failed. The Arbitration Division’s objection is on that basis and has not been ruled on.

The gatehouse at Haldren Ford stands a meter and a half to one side of where its foundations were laid, at a slant you can feel in your back teeth when you walk under it, and the toll-keeper charges a copper extra to see the place and another to hear about the morning. He tells it well. The banners were out on both banks, a shield wall in red and white stood locked across the causeway with the river flashing behind it, and in the middle of the road a small Mahuo woman named Kwon Hae-ryu stood with her hands open and spoke a dead man’s name in an ordinary voice. Then the thing came up out of nowhere, blue-black and bigger than a loaded dray, boar and wolf argued into one shape, with a gold rope as thick as a wrist across its shoulder and a net of skulls knocking at its hip, and it came at a walk. It went through the shield wall the way a barge goes through reeds. Men rose out of the line with looks of pure astonishment and came down on either side of it, unhurt and furious. It walked on into the gatehouse and did not slow, and the gatehouse, twelve men and a pot of soup included, moved over. “Not far,” it said, to nobody at all. The soup is the toll-keeper’s own contribution and I have let him keep it. What he leaves out is the afternoon, when a Silence Realm came down over the crossing and the same animal stood in it with its head up, refusing every order it was given, while eleven of her people died around its knees.
So that is the entry: a beast that weighs as much as an ox and a half, walks at one speed, has cracked pads that do not bleed, and grows stronger every time somebody fails it. I have stood at three paces, and I felt it in the knees first. For the newcomer: Vocatia is the art of calling something that already exists, and Native provenance means the thing owns its own Soul Crystal (the organ that refines Aether into Essence). Bond Class Consenting means it may refuse an order that contradicts its nature. Grade is the Commission’s letter for it, given as though it were loose. A Draft is the four-glyph working that calls it, and Attraction Force and Obsession Force are the two ways a called thing can be reached, by recognition or by compulsion. The rest of the grammar is set out in the Summon Register.
I · Identity









































Formal NameObrenkael. High Parunic, from Ob (the fare, the lawful crossing) + Ren (the passage) + Kael (ruin, the corrosion of structure and memory). Rendered by Accord archivists as the fare carried down a road that is coming apartField NameThe Mule. Older Aperture-branch usage, still current among the households that remember it: Fare. Zettari line-soldiers who fought beside it once call it Grandfather, which nobody in the Accord has been able to get them to stop doingSummonerKwon Hae-ryu of Yeol-gol. Level 355 / 500, a Master, Temperance Stage X RealizationLineage · SchoolMahuo line, Aperture branch. Held as household pattern rather than school instruction. Yeol-gol seat, seven generations attested, the first four undocumentedLoanableStructurally, no. The pattern will accept a second voice only if Hae-ryu names that voice aloud in the construct’s hearing before dissolution of a prior calling. She has done this twice. Both borrowers returned it early and neither has requested it sinceFormCall · Make · Bind, in that order of load. Call does the work; Make supplies the interface; Bind holds the Draft-circle open long enough for a Native form to consentSummon TierIII · GreaterGradeSS, rated loose and hostile. The rating assumes it has been given a name and cannot be talked out of the carriage. Loose and un-named it rates B and mostly standsAccord ClassificationRegistered, Division of Concordia, filed under a Native-Consenting exception. The Arbitration Division’s objection, that an entity which accrues its own strength from its summoner’s failures cannot lawfully be described as bound, is entered before the Bench of Attribution as a Reservation, which withholds the entry’s standing pending determination. The Bench hears it in a three-chair session, the Doctrine chair reading the Wellspring-authorization question and Arbitration sitting as both objector and Ruling chair. No determination has issued
II · Provenance and Architecture





















































Crystal ProvenanceNative. It owned a Crystal before the Mahuo line existed to call it and will own one afterEssence CoreGenuine. The identity is its own and predates the pattern that reaches it. The Aperture branch’s honest position, written into their household ledger in the fourth generation and never amended, is that they do not know what it was before it began carrying, and that the question has been asked of it directly and answered with a distance in ri rather than a wordAether ShellGenuine, and unusually poor. It conducts the way a wet rope conducts, slow and lossy and absolutely unbreakable under load. Leakage reads from outside as a cold seam in the air along its spine, measurable at roughly four degrees below ambient within three paces and steady regardless of weatherAttraction LayerGenuine, and bonded to the road rather than to Hae-ryu. She is a voice it has agreed to hear. The bond underneath that is older and belongs to something the register does not nameCrystal’s lookFacetedCrystal StateOvergrown. The accretion is visible and hangs at its hipMastery, BodyIII, Resonant in the old wordMastery, SpiritIII, a Confessor’s. It knows what it carries, every one of them, which is the part its summoner does not get to refuseMastery, FateII, Drawn. A promise holds it to the road, and it can lean on that promise and on little elseSummon Stability FacetB. Agrees with Tier III’s C-to-B range, sitting at the ceiling of it, and the reason is the Native provenance rather than anything Hae-ryu does wellTraitsBearer’s Exemption. It is not subject to the drag of its own Cord while a carriage is active. Uncounted. The Lattice property altered is the accretion’s count. Each arrested carriage is integrated into the Overgrown accretion at its hip as load, and load is what the Crystal holds and reports; the tally is held nowhere, so no observation of the skulls, by eye or by instrument, returns a number that a second observation confirms. No two witnesses agree, and the disagreement is not a perception effect anyone has been able to isolate. The load itself is unaltered and reads identically to every witness, which is what Deadweight scales with. No real number is fixed. Weight-Sense. It knows, on arrival, how many dead are within four hundred paces and how long each has been waitingDomainNone. It has never formed one and Hae-ryu has stated in writing that she hopes it never does, which the Bench has entered into the record without comment
III · Wellspring and Codex Assignment





































Primary WellspringOblation, the Offering Flame. Temperance through sacrifice, giving becomes becoming. Harmonized by Hae-ryu at Stage VII and the only harmonization in her record that she did not chooseSecondary WellspringMortalis, the Black Gate, ending becomes passage. A Medium Wellspring, at home on all three planes, which is the seam that makes this construct strange to read: a thing this concerned with dying takes half its grammar from a law that keeps to the living as wellKind ResonanceOblation carries it, a Fate Wellspring, the law of what is given up, and it produces forms that carry a debt and do not stop. Nothing about the Mule is anchored. Everything about it is transport, and the Mortalis secondary is what keeps the transport from being merely mechanical, since Mortalis insists that what is being moved was recently a personKindFate, with a Medium secondary in MortalisLeans onThe Attraction Layer. Body: take the road away, since a thing that carries a debt along a road needs the road. Spirit: the hand on the debt shows on its Core, and it is carrying a great many Cores besides. Fate: what it owes can be argued, at length, by someone with standingOperationSeparation, Oblation’s: the thing given parted from the giver, and what it held freed to go elsewhere. Each ability below works by the idea its Function line statesThe Measurewrights’ accountFluid Dynamics. The guild reads every Mechanism field below as gradient, pressure, or drag. Nothing in the kit is impact and nothing in it is heat. Often right about how much, never about whyThe DonationThe donation runs as weight. Witnesses reach for weight rather than for light or heat when they describe the calling: the sensation of something heavy being set down nearby, felt in the knees and the base of the spine before the eyes find anything
IV · The Draft

















































Authorization Glyph[Vo] Voice. A spoken fate-tag binds an oath to its listener. Attested at Oblation and Thaloré. The Authorization role here is a promise rather than a permission, and the Aperture branch has always drafted it that wayBoundary Glyph[RenB] Boundary. Establishes metaphysical borders and wards. Attested through ThaloréDirection Glyph[Vor] Return. Recycles Essence, prevents restless dead. Somnalis primary, attested at Mortalis, Fluid Dynamics. The behavioral vector is carry, and Return is the only glyph in the index that means carry rather than moveSealing Glyph[Sil] Silence. Mutes hostile resonance, dignified stillness. Attested at SomnalisInvocation”Veni tu qui portas. Nomino mortuum.”   Come, you who carry. I name the deadMaterial AnchorA length of gold cord, three spans, kept coiled at Hae-ryu’s belt and never cut. It is the same cord. The construct’s rope and her rope are one object appearing in two places, which is a claim the Division of Concordia has recorded and declined to test. Taking the anchor does not banish the construct. It transfers the naming-right to whoever holds the cord, which is considerably worse, and is the reason she does not put it downCircle RequirementOpen Draft-circle, four glyph-roles laid in salt or in blood, three paces minimum radius. No ceremonial infrastructure. Hae-ryu has laid it one-handed on a tilting deck and it heldReadinessEleven to fourteen seconds. Slow for a Greater form. The delay is not hers. Something on the other side is putting down what it was already carryingDurationUntil the carriage completes, or until dawn, whichever arrives first. What thins first is the rope. The skulls stay solid longest and are the last part of it visibleCall CostApproximately 9% of her reserve, which is about 8,100,000 EU against a reserve of 90,000,000 EU. The percentage is the honest figure and the absolute number now stands behind it, set by ruling; the interpolation is recorded in Section XIIISustain CostLow and flat while it is standing. During an active carriage the sustain rate roughly triples and continues climbing as a function of distance to the Still Gate. She cannot hold a second construct during a carriage and has never tried to hold a third
V · Bond and Standing





















Bond ClassConsentingTerms of AnsweringIt answers a named dead. Hae-ryu’s obligation is to name only those she has actually seen die, in her own hearing or her own sight, and to name them accurately. In exchange it will cross ground she cannot cross and carry weight she cannot carry. If she names a stranger, a rumor, or a lie, it completes that carriage anyway and then does not answer her again for one full year. This has happened once. She was twenty-two and the name was her brother’s, given on a report rather than a body, and he was aliveRefusal ConditionsIt will not kill on ground where the dead cannot cross. Inside a Silence Realm, on Nihiloth-scoured earth, within an active Entombment, it will defend and it will carry nothing and it will not strike. It will not accept a name from anyone without standing to give it, and standing means having been present at the death. It will not set down a carriage once begun, for any order, in any circumstance, including the death of the summoner. It will not be sealed while carrying, and an attempted sealing mid-carriage is read as an attack on the roadPrecedentFour recorded refusals. At Haldren Ford it declined a strike order inside a Silence Realm and Hae-ryu lost the crossing and eleven of her people. At Yeol-gol it refused a name given by her uncle, who had not been present, and stood in the doorway of the household hall for six hours until someone who had been present said the name properly. At the Ossuary Line it refused sealing and Hae-ryu held the circle open for two days past the point where her hands stopped working. At Sum-gol it refused nothing and everyone who saw it wishes it had
VI · Physical Description
It stands three and a half meters at the shoulder in the crouch it never leaves, and the Aperture ledger records an old estimate that it would clear four and a half if it straightened. Nobody has seen it straighten. Mass runs somewhere near that of a draft ox and a half, close to nineteen hundred kilograms, and the figure matters because it is the number the ground reports back: on packed earth it sinks to the second knuckle of the forelimb and on wet ground it sinks past that and keeps walking at the same pace.
The pelt is blue-black, the color of wet slate under a low sky, wolf-coarse at the ruff and matted lower down into ropes of its own where the gold cord has worn a channel across the shoulder over what must be centuries. The hair along the spine stands in a ridge and does not lie down. Beneath the pelt the hide shows through in patches at the flank and the haunch, gray-green and pebbled, and the texture there is closer to a drowned thing than a living one.
The head is boar and wolf argued into one shape. Two horns sweep back from the crown, ridged in tight bands like a ram’s and blunted at the tips from use rather than growth. A third horn, smaller, spirals forward off the brow above the left eye and is banded in copper wire that has gone green. The lower tusks cant outward past the upper lip, worn flat on their inner faces where they close. Two long ears, each split lengthwise, one of them split twice. The eyes sit deep and are pale as boiled milk, and there are two more eye-shaped marks branded into the shoulder that are not eyes, cut rather than burned, spiraling inward. Aperture-branch witness marks. Three of them altogether, the third beneath the left eye, and the household knows what all three attest to and has never written it down.
The cord runs from the ruff across the shoulder and down to the right hip, braided gold as thick as a man’s wrist, and there is no one on the other end of it. It harnesses nothing, and it ends where it began. At the hip it gathers into a net of gold wire holding a cluster of skulls, human, adult, brown with age at the crown and paler at the jaw where they have knocked against each other for a long time. Count them and you will get a number. Count them again and you will get a different one. Three separate Accord field observers at the Ossuary Line recorded nine, eleven, and fourteen within the same hour and all three signed their counts as certain.
Over the left flank hangs an apron of lamellar plate, iron scales riveted to a leather ground, studded and pitted and lacquered black in patches where the lacquer survives. A maroon sash cinches it, gold-fitted, and the sash is the only clean thing on the construct. Someone replaces it. The forelimbs end in three splayed digits, hoof-nailed, black, the pads between them cracked open and dry, and the cracks do not bleed.
Within three paces the air drops about four degrees regardless of season, and the smell arrives before the cold does: standing water, wet wool, and old copper underneath. Sound goes flat. Voices carry to it and do not carry past it, which is a nuisance in a line and the reason Zettari officers learned to shout from in front of it rather than behind. Light treats it badly. It absorbs more than the pelt should and the edges of it stay indistinct at distance, so that soldiers reliably underestimate how close it has come and reliably overestimate how fast it is moving.
Where it has stood it leaves a wet print on dry stone, and the print dries from the outside inward over about a quarter of an hour, which is the wrong direction and is the detail that convinces Accord observers when nothing else has. Kwon Hae-ryu’s whole interior architecture is legible in the thing: a woman whose branch of the family kept the aptitude for hosting the dead and lost every institution that made hosting them bearable, who calls something that carries rather than something that fights, and who has never once summoned a form that could move faster than a walk.
VII · Temperament and Voice
It speaks. The register is flat, low, entirely unhurried, and the vocabulary is almost exclusively weight and distance. It reports load. It reports how far. It does not report danger, and Hae-ryu has learned to read danger off the load figure instead, which is the arrangement they arrived at without either of them proposing it.
Sentences run four words or fewer while it is standing and get shorter under carriage. It will not use the name of the person it is carrying, at any point, for any reason, including when asked directly, and it will not explain the prohibition. It refers to a carriage as the weight and to the Still Gate only as there.
Its signature line, delivered in every recorded engagement where anyone was close enough to hear it, is “Not far.” It has said this at nine paces and at forty leagues and the tone does not change.
Under strain it counts. Out loud, evenly, in no language anyone in the Aperture household recognizes, and it does not stop counting when spoken to. The count does not appear to reset between summonings. Hae-ryu wrote down the number she heard at Haldren Ford and the number she heard four years later at the Ossuary Line, and the second was larger, and she has not written down by how much.
VIII · Abilities


THE FARE · Signature · Vocatia-Native · Transport
Glyph Basis: [Ob] Obol, the guided lawful crossing · [Vor] Return, recycling Essence and quieting the restless dead · [Au] Death, ushering passage
“Quod portatur, transeat.”
Let what is carried cross over.
Trigger: Hae-ryu speaks the name of a dead person she was present for, aloud, within the construct’s hearing. No circle required after the initial calling. The construct answers by lowering its head, which is the only time it lowers its head.
Function: It takes the named dead’s Essence onto itself and walks it to the Still Gate, and while it is walking it cannot be turned aside.
Mechanism, the Measurewrights’ account: Fluid Dynamics. Oblation establishes a pressure differential between the ground where the death occurred and the Gate, and Essence descends that gradient under the same rule that moves any fluid down a head of pressure. The construct works less like a courier than like a millrace, the channel the whole head of water runs down. Its own mass and the Mortalis secondary supply the wall thickness that keeps the transfer laminar (smooth and unbroken) instead of letting it bleed off into the surrounding field, which is what happens to a death nobody attends and is why unattended dead go strange.
Numerical Effect: Bearing pace holds at approximately 3.5 meters per second and does not vary. It cannot be accelerated by any means yet attempted, including downhill. It cannot be slowed below that figure by anything short of removing the road. Sustain drain scales with straight-line distance to the Gate rather than distance traveled, so a carriage begun on bad ground costs more for the whole of its length.
Target Response: Nothing happens to a living body in its path. It walks through a shield wall the way a barge walks through reeds, and the men in that wall report afterward that nothing struck them and that they were displaced, and several of them describe going briefly and unpleasantly weightless. Structures fare worse. A stone gatehouse at Haldren Ford took no break at all and was pushed, foundation and all, about a meter and a half laterally, and it is still standing at the wrong angle.
Limitation: It walks a straight line to the Gate and it will not deviate for terrain, for allies, or for the summoner. It cannot carry two. It cannot begin a second carriage until the first completes.
Weakness: For the whole duration Hae-ryu is standing still with her hands open, and every practitioner within reading range knows exactly where the Oblation pull is coming from and exactly how long she is going to be there.
Cost: Moral and spiritual, escalating. If the carriage is interrupted before it completes, the crossing does not simply fail. It arrests, and what was being carried stays on the construct, and a skull joins the cord at the hip. Every skull on that rope is a promise a summoner made and could not keep. Four of them are hers. She can name all four, and does, once a year, out loud, which is the only ritual the Aperture branch practices that nobody taught her.
Vow: The carriage will be completed. Hae-ryu may not recall the construct mid-carriage. Attempting it forfeits the naming-right for one year and adds to the cord regardless.
Counterplay: Take the road away. Harmonic Silence, Nihiloth-scoured ground, an active Entombment, or a sufficiently dense Nihiloth field arrests the transfer and stops the walk cold. A competent opponent who recognizes the form does not attack the construct at all. They attack the ground in front of it.
Codex Assignment: [Ob] · [Vor] · [Au] · Oblation primary, Mortalis secondary · Separation (the Measurewrights’ Fluid Dynamics)
First Display: Planted at a burial rather than a battle. A single farmhand, no stakes, the construct called for one man and walking him three fields over while Hae-ryu stands in the doorway with her hands open and does not move for eleven minutes. Nobody in that scene understands they have watched a weapon.
Sensory Description: The cold seam along its spine opens and the air within three paces goes still enough to feel wrong in the ears. It lowers its head. The rope pulls taut across the shoulder although nothing is pulling it. Hae-ryu’s hands open and stay open, and her fingers do not close again until it is finished, and afterwards she cannot make a fist for about an hour.
Interactions: Deadweight is unavailable during a carriage. The Cord is not, and the two of them together are the entire reason she survives a carriage begun in contact.
Corruption Vector: An Obsession-Force Fare does not wait to be given a name. It decides who is finished and begins the carriage while they are still standing, and the person it has chosen keeps talking for a while.


DEADWEIGHT · Offensive · Vocatia-Native · Hydrostatic
Glyph Basis: [Ob] Obol, the lawful crossing · [Abys] Deep, a directional undertow of sub-Realm pressure · [Th] Foundation, imposing geometry and load path
“Fer quod ferre non potes.”
Carry what you cannot carry.
Trigger: It sets a forelimb against a target and shifts its shoulder. That is the whole of the trigger. No line is spoken by Hae-ryu; the Latin belongs to the construct and it says it every time.
Function: It puts the accumulated weight of every unfinished crossing on the cord into whatever it is touching.
Mechanism, the Measurewrights’ account: Fluid Dynamics, hydrostatic loading. The arrested carriages at its hip are a standing column of pressure that has nowhere to discharge, and the Foundation glyph supplies the load path from the cord through the shoulder to the contact patch. The pressure enters the target’s own fluid column as head rather than as force, and the body is then required to contain a pressure it was never built to contain.
Numerical Effect: Contact patch of roughly nine hundred square centimeters. Internal hydrostatic rise in the target measured, in the one case where a Concordia diagnostician was present and equipped, at slightly over three hundred kilopascals inside eight tenths of a second. Arterial pressure in a healthy adult runs near sixteen. The applied figure scales with the number of skulls on the cord, and the register’s position, entered under Bench objection, is that this construct becomes measurably stronger every time a summoner fails it.
Target Response: There is no crush. The armor survives. What fails is everything small and unsupported, in order, from the outside in: the vessels of the eye go first and the whites fill, then the ears, then the gums and the beds of the nails. Harness makes no difference at all and the men who understand this stop wearing it around the construct, which the Accord has recorded as a morale problem rather than as evidence. Witnesses describe a man standing upright, unmarked, weeping blood, for the two or three seconds before he goes down.
Limitation: Contact only. It has no ranged expression whatsoever and cannot be projected through a shield, a weapon, or an intervening body.
Weakness: The cord goes slack for about four seconds afterward and the construct’s Bearer’s Exemption lapses with it, which means for those four seconds it is standing inside its own Cord and moving through it like everything else.
Cost: Physical toll, borne by the summoner rather than the construct. Every use drives the same pressure differential back up the Attraction Layer into Hae-ryu at a fraction of magnitude, and she has the small persistent hemorrhages to show for it. Her left eye has been red for two years. It does not clear between engagements any more.
Vow: None recorded.
Counterplay: Do not be touched by it, which is easier than it sounds because it walks at a walk. Failing that, the four-second slack window after each use is the entire opening. Radiant current disrupts the load path at the shoulder and drops the applied figure sharply, which is the standard Accord answer and the reason Arbitration teams deploy with Luminalis harmonization when this entry is expected.
Codex Assignment: [Ob] · [Abys] · [Th] · Oblation primary, Mortalis secondary · Separation (the Measurewrights’ Fluid Dynamics). [Abys] Deep’s row in the Master Glyph Index carries Oblation among its attested Wellsprings on the strength of this working. [Th] Foundation keeps its Petralon row in Mechanics and stays cross-domain, and Deadweight remains the roster’s one cross-domain chain.
First Display: Against a door. A barred household door at Yeol-gol, nobody behind it, the construct setting a forelimb on it and the door failing in a way doors do not fail: the boards intact, every nail driven out of them and lying on the floor.
Sensory Description: The rope goes rigid first, a hand’s width off the flank, and stays there. The skulls stop knocking. Then the shoulder rolls forward about the distance of a slow breath and that is all the movement there is. Hae-ryu’s vision goes red at the edges wherever she is standing.
Interactions: Locked out entirely during an active Fare. Works inside her own Cord without penalty until the slack window opens, at which point it does not.
Corruption Vector: An Obsession-Force Deadweight does not discharge into a target. It discharges into the ground and keeps discharging, and everything standing on that ground for two hundred paces bleeds from the eyes at once, including whoever called it.


THE CORD · Defensive · Vocatia-Native · Viscous
Glyph Basis: [RenB] Boundary, establishing metaphysical borders and wards · [Sil] Silence, muting hostile resonance into dignified stillness · [Ob] Obol, the lawful crossing
“Intra funem nemo festinet.”
Within the rope let no one hurry.
Trigger: It plants and the gold cord comes off its shoulder to lie on the ground in a closed loop. It lays the loop itself and Hae-ryu does not choose the shape.
Function: Inside the loop, nothing may move quickly. Slow movement is unhindered.
Mechanism, the Measurewrights’ account: Fluid Dynamics, quadratic drag. The Boundary glyph raises the effective viscosity of the local Essence medium within the enclosure, and resistance then climbs with the square of velocity exactly as it does in any real fluid. Below roughly one and a half meters per second there is no perceptible effect beyond a slight heaviness. Above it the penalty compounds hard, so that a body moving at six meters per second meets something near sixteen times the resistance of a body moving at one and a half.
Numerical Effect: Loop radius five to seven paces, laid to the ground rather than projected. A sword cut delivered at eight meters per second arrives carrying perhaps a fifth of its intended energy. Loosed arrows fall inside the loop. A charging horse does not stop; it decelerates over about four strides and arrives at a walk, which is worse for the rider than stopping would have been.
Target Response: Men inside it describe wading. They can walk, they can talk, they can bleed and they can die, and everything they attempt at speed feels as though the air has thickened around the limb doing it. Practitioners find that the physical half of their working slows while the metaphysical half does not, which produces a particular and dangerous mismatch in anything that requires both to arrive together.
Limitation: It is a ward against velocity and nothing else. It stops no working that does not need to travel, blocks no line of sight, and does not care in the slightest whether the person inside it is an enemy.
Weakness: Hae-ryu is slowed by it exactly as much as anyone else. The construct is not, and the discrepancy is legible to any competent reader as a bright clean statement about what the Attraction Layer is actually bonded to, which is not her.
Cost: Social and legal. The Cord does not distinguish and it has cost her a field command, two Concord contracts, and the standing to speak first in her own household hall. Every officer who has ever fought beside it has an opinion about the wounded man who could not be dragged out fast enough, and every one of those opinions is correct.
Vow: Optional and used once. She may swear the loop closed around a specific named individual, which narrows it to a single protected body and roughly doubles the drag coefficient. Breaking that vow, meaning stepping out of the loop herself while the named person remains inside it, forfeits the Cord for the remainder of the engagement.
Counterplay: Walk. The whole of the counterplay is walk, and the reason it works anyway is that almost nobody in a fight can make themselves do it. Beyond that: separation from Oblation ground degrades the enclosure quickly, and the loop cannot be re-laid inside two minutes of collapsing.
Codex Assignment: [RenB] · [Sil] · [Ob] · Oblation primary, Mortalis secondary · Separation (the Measurewrights’ Fluid Dynamics).
First Display: In a market. A runaway cart, a child, the construct laying its rope in the road, and the cart arriving at the child’s feet at a walking pace with the driver still screaming at a horse that has stopped being able to run.
Sensory Description: Dust inside the loop stops rising and hangs. Rain slows visibly and lands soft. The sound of the fight drops about half and the drop is in the air rather than the ears. Hae-ryu’s own breathing goes shallow and stays shallow, because breathing fast inside the loop is one of the things the loop declines to permit.
Interactions: Runs concurrently with The Fare, which is the only combination that lets her survive a carriage that begins in contact. Deadweight functions inside it until the slack window, at which point the construct is briefly subject to its own ward and is the slowest thing on the field.
Corruption Vector: An Obsession-Force Cord does not have an upper threshold. It slows everything inside it toward nothing, asymptotically, and the people caught in it do not die. They are still in there.


IX · Dissolution and Failure

























Clean SealingHae-ryu closes the [Sil] role and it turns and walks out of the circle rather than fading, and it is gone at about the fourth stride whether or not there is anywhere for it to have gone. Takes between nine and twenty seconds depending on how much of the rope is on the ground. What remains is a wet print drying from the outside in and a smell of standing water that outlasts the print by an hourSevered TetherNothing happens to the construct, which is the entire problem with Native provenance and the reason the Bench keeps the file open. It continues. What comes back up the line into Hae-ryu is the sustain drain with nothing regulating it, a hemorrhagic event she has survived twice and describes as being emptied rather than injured. It will complete whatever it was carrying and then it will come and find her, and the Aperture ledger does not record what it does when it arrives, because on both occasions she was unconscious for itBehavior in SilenceIt holds. It does not function. Inside a Silence Realm it will not carry, will not strike, will not lay the Cord, and will not leave, and it stands between her and whatever is coming with its head up for as long as the Realm lasts. Three engagements’ worth of Accord observation agree that this is the only circumstance in which it raises its headResistance to DissolutionRecorded once. At the Ossuary Line it declined to be sealed while carrying, and the answer to that was not force. Hae-ryu held the circle open for two days and let it finish. The Arbitration Division’s written position is that this was a failure of control. The Aperture household’s written position is that the Division has misunderstood which party the control was ever supposed to run towardPermanence HazardIt stops being a summon at the moment the cord finishes. If every arrested carriage on that rope were completed, the accretion would clear, the Overgrown state would resolve, and there would be nothing left tying it to the naming-right at all. It has never suggested this. Hae-ryu worked it out on her own at twenty-six and has told two people
X · Corruption Vector
Attraction Force answers by recognition. The Mule comes because a name was spoken by someone who was there, and it goes because the weight has been set down. Every part of it is consent expressed as freight.
The Obsession-Force inversion keeps the shape and inverts the direction of the asking. It does not wait for a name. It reads the room on arrival, using the same Weight-Sense that tells it how many dead are within four hundred paces, and it decides which of the living are close enough to finished to be worth beginning. Then it begins. The person it has chosen goes on standing, goes on talking, sometimes for a considerable while, and the carriage is already underway beneath that, and there is no interrupting it because there is no summoner who could be persuaded to interrupt it.
The lawful Mule cannot be made to strike where the dead cannot cross. The compelled version strikes anywhere and simply accrues, cord growing, weight climbing, Deadweight rising with it, and it does not experience the accumulation as failure. The lawful form carries eleven skulls as a debt. The compelled form carries them as capital.
It would also stop counting. Every account of the corrupted expression that the Aperture branch has collected, and there are four, agrees on this one detail and on nothing else.
XI · Counterplay
On seeing it arrive, do not engage the construct. Nothing in the kit is ranged, nothing in it is fast, and everything in it requires either contact or ground. A competent opponent gives it distance and takes the road.
Of the three recurring vulnerabilities, two apply hard and one applies sideways. Separation from the native Wellspring is decisive: Oblation’s pooled ground feeds the gradient that The Fare runs on and the enclosure that The Cord maintains, and moving the engagement onto ground where Oblation does not reach reduces the entry to a large slow animal with a rope. Radiant current works specifically against Deadweight, disrupting the load path at the shoulder before the pressure column reaches the contact patch, and Arbitration teams deploy Luminalis-harmonized officers for this reason and no other. Essence-dampening is the sideways one and it is a trap. Dampening does not weaken a Native form the way it weakens a Donated one, and dampening applied to the road rather than the construct produces the arrest condition, which stops the carriage and adds a skull and makes the thing permanently stronger. Every opponent who has tried to win by dampening has won that engagement and lost the next one.

The genuine counter is neither of these. Give it a name. Anyone present at a death may speak that name in its hearing, and it does not check whose side the speaker is on, because standing has never meant allegiance. It means presence. An enemy who watched one of his own men die can put the Mule on a carriage in the wrong direction and Hae-ryu can do nothing about it at all, and the only reason this does not happen constantly is that almost nobody believes it will work until they have seen it work.

Signature legibility applies and is unusually loud here. The cold seam and the flat sound reach further than the construct does, and the Oblation pull during a carriage is the most legible thing Hae-ryu ever does.
XII · Attested Encounters
Haldren Ford, Accord Archive, Concordia field record, dated. First Accord-observed deployment. The construct declined a strike order inside a Silence Realm and stood over the withdrawal for the duration. Eleven of Hae-ryu’s people were lost in the crossing. The Archive record is a clean two-page assessment concluding that the Native-Consenting exception carries an unacceptable operational risk. Kellwright company survivors, who were on the far bank and could see the whole of it, tell it differently and have never stopped: they say the eleven were lost because the Realm was laid on top of them and the Mule stood in it anyway, and they use the word stood the way you would use it about a person. The register does not resolve this.
The Ossuary Line, Accord Archive, Arbitration Division report, dated. The refusal-of-sealing incident. Three field observers, three different skull counts, all three signed as certain, all three retained in the file without reconciliation. The Division’s assessment is control failure. Two of the three observers appended personal notes that were not requested and were entered anyway, and neither note mentions control.
Yeol-gol, household ledger, undated entry in the seventh generation hand. The uncle’s name and the six hours in the doorway. The household ledger records the refusal, records who eventually spoke the name correctly, and records nothing about the uncle. Yeol-gol village tradition, which is not archival and is marked here as folk account, holds that the uncle left the seat that winter and that the doorway is a different doorway from the one the ledger means. Both readings survive locally and the households that hold each one do not eat together.
Sum-gol, no Accord record, no household entry. Field accounts only, four of them, from three different companies, and they agree on the sequence and disagree on the count of the dead by a factor the register declines to average. Marked as rumor. Retained because all four independently describe the construct counting aloud, and because two of them, who did not know each other, wrote down the same number.

the-bestiary/the-called-and-the-divine/s.title: Raga · The Divine Thunder Bear
the-bestiary/the-called-and-the-divine/s.content:
Divine Beast · Vocatia · Native Provenance · Bond Class Sovereign · Grade SS

Thunder is the world telling you how far away the harm was. Everything Raga does is a version of that sentence, and the reason practitioners fear him has nothing to do with the lightning.
“Numera intervallum. Veniat sonus.”
Count the interval. Let the sound come.

Children in the Halvedge hill country learn their numbers in thunderstorms, by the oldest game there is: see the flash, count till the sound, and every three counts is a kilometer to the harm. Their rhyme for it has a bear in it.
One for the flash and two for the rain,
Three for the bear on the burning plain,
Four for the horn and five for the stone,
Six for the man who stands alone,
Seven he walks and eight he runs,
Nine, and the sound of it comes.
It stops at nine because of Long Colin Thwaite of the Madder Company, and the Accord Archives will not help you with him. They hold a measurement, eight point seven seconds, and nothing else. The line holds the rest. The company stood on a green ridge under a storm the color of a plum, three hundred men in madder red and yellow with the rain coming sideways and small green lights rising through it from somewhere far off down the valley, as if a summer field had got up and gone to heaven, and a little under three kilometers away somebody who had never seen Colin Thwaite spoke his name off another man’s report. There was a flash without heat or sound. It lit nothing, and it left him with a cold pressure behind the breastbone and a look on his face that the men either side of him knew, because the company had been told what the look meant. So they counted for him, three hundred men at the top of their lungs. On one he dropped his spear. On two and three he gave his purse to the man on his left and told him which woman. By five the line had opened and he was walking out ahead of it onto the empty grass, by himself, to get his two meters clear of anyone else’s, and on eight he turned around and shouted something about the sergeant’s mother that is still the best-known sentence the Madder Company ever produced. On nine the thunder that had been waiting arrived. His harness came through it without a dent and was sent home to Halvedge, and it hangs on a wall there, and nobody has ever been able to say whether he was the man who was meant.
The company named the bear Nine Seconds, and it was never a compliment. The rest of this page is what the Commission and the Measurewrights have got down about the animal since: a mythic beast by any standard you care to bring, and also a body with a hump of shoulder muscle, a sore left foreleg and a habit of standing in shallow water. For the newcomer: Vocatia is the art of calling something that already exists. Native provenance means he owns his own Soul Crystal (the organ that refines Aether into Essence) and owes nobody for it. Bond Class Sovereign means he sets the terms of his answering. Grade is the Commission’s letter for it, given as though he were loose. Shell, Layer, Draft and the rest of the grammar are set out in the Summon Register.
I · Identity





















































Formal NameSelraga, Old Parunic. From [Sel], Measure, and the beast-root. Rendered in Accord registry as Raga of the MeasureField NameRaga. Among Accord line infantry, the Count, and among the two companies that have stood inside his field, Nine Seconds, which is a complaint rather than a titleTypeDivine Beast · Archonic Witness. One of a kind, forged by will rather than bornSummonerUnassignedLineage · SchoolNo school holds the pattern. Raga is no pattern. He is contacted, and the contact is either recognized or it is refusedLoanableNo. A summoner who has been recognized cannot transfer the recognition, and three attempts to broker one are recorded in Arbitration filings without a single successFormCall, with Sing active only where the summoner sustains him past the first hourSummon TierIII · Greater in still air. V · World-Tethered in the presence of a live storm cell, which supplies an anchor he did not have to be givenTemperance GateStage X Realization for stable contact. Stage XII Emanation for sustained presence. Below X the invocation is heard and declinedGradeSS · Realm Hazard. Rated loose and hostile. The leash is a fact about the summonerAccord ClassificationRegistered under Divine Correspondence, restricted. Standing Bench objection filed twice on the grounds that a Divine Beast cannot be entered in a register it did not consent to, and dismissed both times on procedure rather than on meritRealm AffiliationNo native realm recorded. Attested in the Material World only during storm, and never twice in the same weather
II · Provenance and Architecture





















































Crystal ProvenanceNative. Raga owned his Crystal before anyone learned to ask for him and will own it after the last person who knows the invocation is deadEssence CoreGenuine. Holds a single function rather than a biography: the measuring of distance between an act and its consequence. Everything else about him is downstream of that one jobAether ShellGenuine, and the most conductive Shell attested in a non-practitioner. Ventilates through the rack rather than the hide, which is why the antlers shed points during an engagement and grow them back betweenAttraction LayerGenuine, bonded to nothing. He has no Domain of his own and has never seated one, which the Meridian assessors found more alarming than the alternativeCrystal’s lookFlawless. Trait law and local law have been the same law for long enough that nobody can say when they divergedCrystal StateRefined. No fracture recorded, and no evidence he has ever been under enough pressure to produce oneMastery, SpiritII, an Answerer’s. One function, and it answersMastery, FateNone. Bonded to nothing, by choice, for longer than anyone has countedMastery, BodyV, Radiant in the old word. Currents curve toward him at a measured 45 m from the outermost tine, which is the same figure the Sealwrights use for a 30 kA striking distance and is assumed to be coincidence by people who have not stood inside itSummon Stability FacetA-Tier. Hours with an anchor. Storm-anchored persistence has run to four days, which sits above the Tier III ceiling and is the strongest argument for reclassifying himTraitsOne, unnamed in any document that survived the filing. It expresses as the interval and cannot be separated from him. The Arbitration record refers to it only as the delayDomainNone. He borrows one from the weather when the weather offers
III · Wellspring and Codex Assignment









































Primary WellspringOrrenthal. Pure resonance, the harmonic core. Thunder is resonance arriving late and Raga is the arrivalSecondary WellspringJudicium. Measure, weight, the verdict. Supplies the half of him that decides what is worth strikingTertiary, technique-localCataclysm, pulled only by Report. See the cross-domain note in that blockKind ResonanceWild, the storm’s own, and elevated and judgmental by his Judicium. Constructs and correspondences under this current develop conviction that outlasts their authorization, which is the polite Codex phrasing for a Divine Beast that has stopped taking suggestionsKindWildLeans onThe Aether Shell, as hard as anything on this register. Body: bring something that is not lightning. Spirit: past the rack to a single function, which can be read and cannot be argued with. Fate: a very sound thing, and what he depends on is the name he has refused to answer toOperationConjunction, Orrenthal’s: the parts of the soul joined so that everything in it is held in common by the whole. Each ability below works by the idea its Function line statesThe Measurewrights’ accountElectromagnetism. The guild reads every Mechanism field below in these terms except Report, which they read as Thermodynamics and say so. Often right about how much, never about whyThe DonationDischarge. His donation neither burns nor flows. It accumulates until the potential is intolerable and then equalizes in one event, and there is no partial version of him
IV · The Draft





















































Authorization[Sel] Measure. Urion. Quantifies flows for judgment. The only Authorization glyph Raga has ever answeredBoundary[RenB] Boundary. Zhaeren. Establishes the metaphysical border and the ward on itDirection[Thn] Thunder. Wyther and Uurgath. Nonlinear run that avoids friendlies, which is the glyph doing work the summoner would otherwise have to do by handSealing[Vor] Return. Auren. Recycles Essence and prevents restless dead. Skipping it does not free him. It leaves the count runningThe Refused Glyph[Bst] Beast. The older attested chain used it, since summoned fauna reinforce a crossing. Raga stopped answering chains carrying [Bst] some time before the Accord existed. The Codex still lists it against him and the field practice does notInvocation”Numera intervallum. Veniat sonus.” Spoken once, aloud, with the target named in the same breath. A silent Draft is heard and declinedMaterial AnchorNone permitted. He has refused every relic offered and one Guild attempt to anchor him to prepared iron produced a crater and no summonCircle RequirementOpen ground and open sky. No circle. The Draft is spoken standingReadinessBetween four and nine seconds, and the variation is the tell. He arrives at the interval, and the interval is how far he wasDurationOne hour unaided. Hours to four days storm-anchored. He leaves when the naming stops, and not beforeCall Cost180,000,000 EU, or roughly a fifth of an Archmaster’s reserve. A Stage X summoner spends most of what he has to be recognized onceSustain CostNil. Raga sustains himself. The cost is taken somewhere else and is recorded in section V
V · Bond and Standing

























Bond ClassSovereign. He negotiates terms and imposes them as the condition of answering at allTerms of AnsweringThe summoner names the target aloud, in a voice the people standing nearby can hear, and accepts the Arrears. Both terms are stated once, at first recognition, and are never restatedThe ArrearsThe summoner’s own sensation runs late for as long as Raga is present, and for a long while after. Pain, sound, heat, the weight of a hand on the shoulder, all of it arrives at the same interval Raga is running. A man opened across the ribs keeps fighting for four seconds because his body has not told him yet. Attested residual: eleven hours after a single hour of presence. One practitioner has carried a half-second delay for nine years and eats alone because of itRefusal ConditionsHe will not strike a thing that has not been named. He will not strike from behind. He will not strike the same target twice, and a summoner who asks him to will find the second Draft unanswered and the first one still owedPrecedentFour recorded refusals. Three were second strikes. The fourth was a named target the summoner had named wrongly, and Raga stood in the open for the remaining forty minutes of his presence without moving, which the survivors describe as the worst part
VI · Physical Description
He stands two point nine meters at the shoulder on all fours and runs six point two from muzzle to haunch, and the assessors who put a figure on his mass settled on three point eight tonnes with a note attached, because a body that heavy should sink and his prints in river silt run four centimeters deep where a bull would leave thirty. The hide is black in the way a burned thing is black, absorbing rather than reflecting, and the guard hairs stand in dense parallel ranks that shed water in sheets and never lie flat. Across the shoulders the fur thickens into a hump of muscle wider than a cart, and the forelimbs beneath it carry the heavy straight-boned architecture of an animal built to push rather than to chase.
The rack is the part that ruins people’s sleep. Twelve tines minimum, more when he has been standing in weather, spanning close to five meters and branching in the pale gray of storm-stripped driftwood, ridged and knuckled along their length where new horn has pushed through old. They are not antlers in any sense a hunter would accept. They grow during an engagement and shed during one, dropping points that steam when they hit wet ground and are cold by the time anybody dares pick one up. Every tip carries a standing corona, and the green motes that drift free of them are that corona letting go, small and slow and drifting upward through the rain in numbers that make a battlefield look briefly like a summer field at dusk.
His eyes have no sclera and no pupil. Two flat green points set deep under the brow ridge, the same green as the motes, and they do not track the way an animal’s track. They arrive on a thing a moment after the head has already turned toward it. The muzzle is broad and blunt and scarred across the bridge in three parallel lines that nobody has ever explained. There is no smell of animal on him at all. Ozone, wet stone, and scorched hair, layered in that order, and the ozone reaches a formation about two seconds before he does.
He makes no sound walking. The footfalls arrive later, and they arrive at the place he was, and a line that has learned this stops trying to fight by ear inside the first minute.
VII · Temperament and Voice
Raga does not speak, and the assumption that he cannot is one the Archives have declined to endorse. He communicates by arriving, by standing, and by declining to move, and the vocabulary is smaller than it sounds. A summoner learns to read the set of the head and the angle of the rack, and every summoner who has learned it reports the same three positions and no more.
What he does instead of speaking is count. The interval is audible to anyone standing inside forty-five meters, a low beat under the storm, somewhere between a sound and a pressure change, and it is regular, and it does not stop when he is idle. Practitioners who have worked with him describe the beat continuing in their own chest for days afterward, keeping time with nothing.
He is patient in a way that reads as indifference and is closer to arithmetic. No decision about striking is going on in him. He is establishing where the thing is, and the thing is a distance, and the distance resolves on its own schedule.
The one behavior every account agrees on: he faces the summoner before he faces the target. Every time. Nobody has recorded what he is checking for and nobody has asked twice.
VIII · Abilities


THE COUNT · Signature · Marking · Delayed Delivery
Glyph Basis: [Sel] Measure · [Len] Line · [Thn] Thunder
“Nomina, et numera.”
Name it, and count.
Trigger: The summoner speaks the target’s name aloud. Raga turns his head. There is a flash without heat, without sound, and without any visible origin, and it lands on the target and does not stay.
Function: The strike happens immediately. The consequence arrives at the speed of sound.
Mechanism, the Measurewrights’ account: Electromagnetism. The flash is a genuine return stroke, a channel established and equalized in under two hundred microseconds, and it deposits its charge at the marked point in the instant it occurs. What Raga withholds is the acoustic event. The channel’s superheated air wants to expand and produce the shock, and Orrenthal holds the resonance folded and unreleased at the point of origin until the interval has run. The count is the real distance between Raga and the mark divided by three hundred and forty three meters per second, and it is not adjustable, and Raga does not know how to make it shorter.
Numerical Effect: Peak current in the 30 kA range against ordinary targets, with one attested measurement at 180 kA against a Domain-seated practitioner. Channel temperature near 28,000 K. Interval measured between 0.29 seconds at a hundred meters and 8.7 seconds at three kilometers, which is the engagement that gave him his soldiers’ name.
Target Response: Nothing, and then everything. The marked target feels the charge deposit as a cold pressure behind the sternum and has the interval to understand what is standing over them. When the count runs out the withheld shock releases at the mark, and the release carries the full acoustic energy of a strike that has been holding it in one place for several seconds. Bodies inside two meters come apart along the wet lines. Armor survives and the man inside does not.
Limitation: The consequence lands where the mark is, and the mark travels with the target. It cannot be made to land early, cannot be made to land elsewhere, and cannot be canceled by Raga once the flash has gone.
Weakness: The interval tells a competent opponent exactly how far away Raga is, to within a few meters, before he has been seen. Every use of The Count is a range report given free to the enemy.
Cost: Attraction-category, carried by the summoner. Each Count deepens the Arrears by a fraction that does not reset between engagements.
Vow: The target must be named aloud by a voice Raga recognizes. An unnamed target cannot be marked, and a wrongly named one is marked and then abandoned.
Counterplay: The charge is deposited on the body, and the body can be put somewhere the release cannot follow usefully. Full immersion, deep water or river silt, bleeds the deposit to ground before the interval runs. A practitioner who holds Body Inverted devours it outright. Failing either, distance is a friend: the further the mark from Raga, the longer the interval, and eight seconds is enough time for allies to drag a man clear and enough time for him to walk out of the blast radius himself if somebody tells him which way.
Codex Assignment: [Sel] · [Len] · [Thn] · Primary Judicium · Secondary Orrenthal · Separation (the Measurewrights’ Electromagnetism)
First Display: Low stakes. Raga marks a standing stone at fifty paces during a demonstration and the assembled Proctors watch nothing happen for a fifth of a second before the stone opens. The rule is taught in one beat and never needs teaching again.
Sensory Description: The flash has no color anyone agrees on and leaves no afterimage. The summoner’s mouth is still open on the last syllable of the name. Raga’s rack sheds two tines and the motes come off them in a rush, drifting up through the rain, and under everything the beat keeps time.
Interactions: Anything that pins a target in place converts The Count from a warning into an execution. This is the entire reason a Sovereign-bond Divine Beast has ever been fielded alongside line infantry.
Corruption Vector: An Obsession-Force Count does not wait for a name. It marks the nearest living thing, and it marks again, and the intervals begin to overlap until a field has more counts running in it than people.


THE STANDING CHARGE · Area Denial · Protective · Immobile
Glyph Basis: [Krn] Crown · [RenB] Boundary · [Ur] Balance
“Ad me ictus omnes.”
Every stroke to me.
Trigger: Raga lowers the head until the rack is the highest standing structure in the field and plants all four limbs. He does not move again until he releases it.
Function: Every discharge in the area terminates on Raga and on nothing else.
Mechanism, the Measurewrights’ account: Electromagnetism, and specifically the geometry of the striking distance. The rack presents an overwhelming upward streamer at a potential no other object in the field can match, and every descending leader within the protective radius commits to it before it can commit to anything else. Judicium supplies the part that is not weather. Practitioner discharges, inscribed lightning, lightning techniques of any kind, all of them resolve their path against Raga’s rack in preference to their intended target, because the Wellspring reads him as the correct terminus and the technique is obliged to agree.
Numerical Effect: Protective radius of 45 m from the outermost tine, consistent with a 30 kA striking distance, expanding toward 70 m as accumulated charge on the rack rises. Sustained across the longest attested hold, thirty one minutes, during which the rack shed nine tines and regrew four.
Target Response: A practitioner watching his own technique curve away from a target and terminate on an animal’s antlers experiences it as a failure of his own work rather than as an interception. The Arbitration filings record three separate accusations of sabotage from casters who did not understand what had happened to them.
Limitation: Raga cannot move while holding it, cannot use The Count while holding it, and cannot exclude anyone from it. The enemy’s discharges and the allies’ resolve to him identically.
Weakness: He is a stationary four-tonne target with his head down. Anything that is not electrical goes through him without impediment, and a competent line understands within thirty seconds that the answer is a spear.
Cost: Physical, carried by Raga rather than the summoner, and the only cost in the entry that works that way. Every hold ages the rack. The regrowth is never complete and the shed points do not come back in the same arrangement.
Counterplay: Bring something that is not lightning. Failing that, overload him: sustained lightning input past his Shell’s venting rate forces the accumulated charge back down through the body, and two engagements have ended with Raga discharging into the ground beneath his own feet and standing in the resulting crater with his hide smoking.
Codex Assignment: [Krn] · [RenB] · [Ur] · Primary Judicium · Secondary Fixatio · Separation (the Measurewrights’ Electromagnetism)
First Display: He does it unasked, over a wounded man, during a storm that had nothing to do with the engagement. Nobody orders it and nobody can make him do it on request afterward.
Sensory Description: The hair stands on every arm in the field. The rain begins falling upward within the radius, drawn to the tines in fine threads. The beat speeds up.


REPORT · Charge · Overpressure · Cross-Domain
Glyph Basis: [Thn] Thunder · [Noq] Wind · [Uur] Disruption
“Sonus advenit.”
The sound arrives.
Trigger: Contact. Raga runs, and the running is silent, and the sound of the running arrives afterward.
Function: A bear’s charge that delivers a blast wave instead of an impact.
Mechanism, the Measurewrights’ account: Thermodynamics. This block departs from the Electromagnetism domain the rest of the entry runs on, and the departure is deliberate and Codex-supported: [Thn] Thunder is assigned to Cataclysm, and Report is the one technique in Raga’s kit that is genuinely a heat event. The charge accumulated across the hide superheats the air in the compression layer ahead of his mass, and the layer detonates on contact rather than deforming. The strike is the expansion, and the body he hits is standing inside it.
Numerical Effect: Overpressure of 40 to 60 kPa within two meters of contact. Tympanic rupture begins near 35 kPa and pulmonary injury near 70, which places every target of a clean Report in the band where the ears go and the lungs are a coin toss. Closing speed measured at 14 m/s over the last twenty meters.
Target Response: Mail and brigandine transmit the overpressure into the torso intact. Harness performs worse, because the breastplate rings and the ringing is inside the man. Survivors bleed from the ears for a week and describe the world afterward as being underwater. The dead are intact and wrong.
Limitation: Requires a run-up of at least twenty meters. It cannot be delivered from a standing position and it cannot be steered once committed.
Weakness: The compression layer is visible for the last half second as a distortion in the rain, and it announces the contact point. A man who has seen one Report can time the second one.
Cost: Physical. The detonation happens against Raga as much as against the target, and he carries the deceleration through the forelimbs. Attested consequence: after four Reports in one engagement he stopped putting weight on the left fore, and he still favors it.
Counterplay: Break the run-up. Broken ground, caltrops, a spear hedge, anything that makes twenty meters of clean approach unavailable. Failing that, get to ground: overpressure falls off sharply with distance and prone bodies inside four meters have survived where standing ones inside eight did not.
Codex Assignment: [Thn] · [Noq] · [Uur] · Primary Cataclysm · Secondary Orrenthal · Calcination (the Measurewrights’ Thermodynamics, with an electrical trigger). A deliberate crossing of domains, consistent with the Codex’s own assignment of [Thn]
First Display: Against a wall rather than a person. He puts a gate through its own gatehouse and the garrison surrenders to a summoner who had not yet decided to ask them.
Sensory Description: Silence, and then the shape of him already too close, and then the sound of the last four seconds of running arriving all at once behind the blast.


WHAT IS NOT NAMED · Passive · Vow · The Refusal
Glyph Basis: [Vo] Voice · [Va] Law
“Quod non nominatur, non percutitur.”
What is not named is not struck.
Trigger: Permanent. It cannot be switched off and Raga has never been observed attempting to.
Function: Raga is incapable of harming anything that has not been named aloud in his hearing by a voice he recognizes.
Mechanism, the Measurewrights’ account: Electromagnetism through Judicium, with the spoken-fate mechanics of [Vo] doing the binding. The naming is a genuine Draft operation compressed into a single word, and the target’s designation is written into the Continuum’s local accounting before any charge moves. An unnamed body is not protected. It is simply not addressed, and nothing Raga does can find it.
Numerical Effect: No figure. This is the one field in the entry where a number would be a lie.
Target Response: Enemy formations that work this out send unnamed men forward and the tactic works exactly once per summoner, since the second engagement has the summoner naming a rank rather than a man. Whether a rank counts as a name is the live question, and the answer so far has been sometimes.
Limitation: Structural and absolute. Raga cannot be talked around it, cannot be angered past it, and has stood over an unnamed man who was actively killing his summoner without intervening.
Weakness: It makes the summoner audible. A voice that must speak a name aloud in a battle line is a voice that can be located, and three attempts on summoners have been made on that basis.
Cost: Borne entirely by the summoner, in the currency of having to decide out loud, in front of witnesses, who is going to die. The Arrears is the physical cost of the bond. This is the other one, and practitioners report it as the heavier of the two.
Vow: The whole technique is the vow. Forfeiting it is not available to either party.
Counterplay: Go unnamed. Kill the voice.
Ruled 2026-09-12: the Raga delivery-method question (spoken or poured) is answered: spoken. Nothing in this entry ever supported a poured mechanism; the counter runs entirely on the voice the Invocation, the naming, and the stated Counterplay already require. Kaalabad destroys the construct by killing the voice: closing the distance on Kwon Mu-jin fast enough, and violently enough, that the naming itself is interrupted mid-word, by a struck throat, a broken jaw, anything that stops the sound before the target is named, rather than by attacking Raga directly, who by his own entry cannot be harmed by ordinary means and does not need to be. An unnamed target is not protected from Raga; it is simply not addressed, and a naming interrupted mid-word is functionally the same as no naming at all.
Codex Assignment: [Vo] · [Va] · Primary Judicium · Secondary Thaloré · Separation (the Measurewrights’ Electromagnetism). A crossing worth marking: [Vo] is a Thaloré assignment and is doing the binding work here rather than the striking work
First Display: Before any combat at all. A summoner points and Raga does not move, and the summoner has to say the name, and the saying of it in front of his own men is the scene.
Sensory Description: Raga faces the summoner. The beat continues. Nothing else happens, for as long as it takes.


IX · Dissolution and Failure





























Clean Sealing[Vor] Return, spoken once. He turns, walks four or five paces, and is not there for the sixth. The motes hang in the air for a further two minutes and the ozone lasts an hourSevered TetherNo tether exists to sever. Killing the summoner does not banish him. He completes any running count, faces the body, and leaves on his own scheduleUnsealed DepartureA summoner who omits [Vor] finds the Arrears does not decay. It becomes the practitioner’s permanent baseline, and the nine-year case in section V is an unsealed departure and nothing more complicated than thatBehavior in SilenceHarmonic Silence does not remove him. It removes the interval, and a Raga whose count has been silenced strikes without delay and without warning, which two Sealwrights have now learned is the worse outcome. Standing Enforcement guidance: do not silence the bearResistance to DissolutionNot applicable in the ordinary sense. He is Native and departs by choice. The register notes that no summoner has ever tested what happens if the choice and the sealing disagreePermanence HazardHe is already permanent. The hazard runs the other way: a summoner storm-anchored past four days stops being able to distinguish the Arrears from his own sense of time
X · Corruption Vector
Attraction Force answers by recognition. Obsession Force takes the same shape and compels, and the compelled Raga is documented once, in a filing the Bench sealed and the Measurewrights have petitioned twice to reopen.
The interval inverts. A compelled Raga does not withhold the consequence and let it arrive. He withholds the cause. The thunder comes first, at full weight, on a target that has not been struck by anything and will not be for several seconds, and the target hears their own death arrive and then stands in the interval waiting for the flash that will justify it. Nobody named survives the wait. Two in the filing tried to run and the mark went with them, and the account of what the running looked like is the reason the filing is sealed.
The second inversion is quieter and is the one the Arbitration Division actually fears. A compelled Raga stops needing the name. [Vo] is doing the binding under Thaloré, and Thaloré is the true weight of what is felt, and a weight that has been forced rather than asked does not hold a boundary. The vow goes first. Everything Raga is, is downstream of a refusal, and a Raga who cannot refuse is a weather system with a grudge and forty-five meters of reach.
XI · Counterplay
Water. The single most reliable answer in the entry, and it works against The Count directly by bleeding the deposit to ground before the interval runs. Rivers, flooded ground, deep silt. The image most often attached to him has him standing in shallow water and that is not an aesthetic choice on anyone’s part.
Distance is inverted. Every other SS in the register is more dangerous close and less dangerous far. Raga is the opposite. The further out the mark, the longer the interval, and the interval is survival time. A formation that closes on him is choosing to make his strikes instantaneous.
Bring something that is not electrical. The Standing Charge is the whole of his defensive game and it is blind to steel.
Inverted suppression works and is not worth what it costs. A practitioner who holds the Inverted mark devours the deposit outright. The same practitioner is a stationary siege engine requiring a guard detachment, and Raga does not need to strike a man who cannot leave.
And the answer nobody writes down. He will not strike from behind, he will not strike twice, and he will not strike the unnamed. Three of his four abilities have a counterplay that consists of understanding him. The Accord’s own field guidance omits this on the grounds that it is unreliable, which is true, and the Measurewrights’ dissent notes that it is unreliable in the same way a law is unreliable.
XII · Attested Encounters
Nine Seconds. Archives hold the measurement and not the engagement. A mark at eight point seven seconds, which places the flash a little under three kilometers from where Raga was standing, and a summoner who named a target he could not see on somebody else’s report. The Archives do not record whether the naming was correct. The line that was present has named him for it ever since, and the naming is not affectionate.
The Gatehouse. Report against a wall rather than a person. The garrison surrendered before terms were offered and the filing lists the engagement as a bloodless success, which is accurate and is also the reason the Enforcement Division keeps citing it.
The Forty Minutes. Fourth recorded refusal. A wrongly named target, and Raga standing in the open until his presence expired. Field account, not Archive. The survivors are consistent on the detail that he faced the summoner the entire time.
The Crater at Halvedge. An attempt to anchor him to prepared iron. Folk account holds that the smith who forged the anchor was still alive when the Draft was spoken. Archives hold the crater’s dimensions and nothing else.

the-bestiary/the-called-and-the-divine/s.content:
Called things, entered as creatures. What a summoner keeps on a chain and what the chain is actually made of.

The register’s other six sections describe things that exist whether or not anyone wants them to. This section describes things that arrive because they were asked. The difference matters exactly once, and it matters on the day the asking stops working.
A summon entry is a Bestiary entry with a second creature in it: the person holding the other end.

Hamo Pockle called up a wine-steward for the Drapers’ election feast, and it remains the most expensive thing anyone in Ostlergate has ever done at a party. He was a Stage VIII hedge summoner with a coat the color of pale ale and a hired hall, and what stepped out of the chalk circle in the buttery was a tall figure of amber light in a steward’s shape, which bowed to the new Master, to huge applause. Hamo, three cups in, told it to keep every cup full, and went off to dance. It kept every cup full. It kept them full when the guests stopped lifting them, and when the guests started covering them with their hands it filled the hands. For the eleven minutes the form could hold, it went up and down that hall with its arms held out and the new Master’s six best tuns running through it, while the floor went purple to the ankle, his gown of office turned the color of a bruise, the Drapers’ banner came down in the flood, and a rural dean went over on the stairs and broke his hip.
The new Master sued. Hamo pleaded that the thing had done it, and pointed to where it had been. The Reeve of Ostlergate, who had been at the feast and was still pink to the knee, found against him in a sentence every Commission clerk can recite: the thing did as it was told, so find me who told it. That sentence is this section. A called thing is a creature like any other in the register, with a body, a diet and a way of being beaten, and it also has somebody’s name on it.
How These Entries Differ
Two fields carry weight here that carry none anywhere else in the Bestiary.
Crystal Provenance decides whether the thing has a soul of its own or is wearing a piece of somebody else’s. A Donated construct has no Crystal (Soul Crystal, the organ that refines Aether into Essence) to record. A Native entity has one and had it long before anyone learned its name. Everything the entry can honestly say about resilience, refusal and death follows from that single line. A bound thing also has its own window, with its Level, its terms and its evolution, and the contract behind it can be stolen. The Spirit Summoning Arts has that law, and Windows and the Sheet has the window.
Bond Class decides how much of an order the thing can decline. The Bestiary’s other sections never need this, because a wyvern is not under instruction. Half the entries in this section can refuse, and the register should say so in the same breath it says what they can do.
The standard eleven questions still apply. Origin before appearance, Essence Affinity before abilities, weaknesses in the same breath as powers. A summon entry adds Provenance, Bond, the Draft (the four-glyph working) that calls it, and the cost the caller carries afterward, and the cost is the field most likely to be left thin.
Grade
Rated as though the thing were loose and hostile, on the same E through EX letters as the rest of the register and the Commission’s bounties. A summon’s Grade does not drop because somebody has a leash on it. The leash is a fact about the summoner.
Cross-Reference
Full doctrine, the entry skeleton, the five Summon Tiers, Crystal Provenance, Bond Class, the Glyph Chain and the blank template all live in The Called · Summon Register. Use the blank template there rather than copying an existing entry, since copying an entry carries its assumptions with it.


The Called · Summon Register
