It can be a sustained, weeks-long contest of presence, each creature occupying the boundary and waiting for the other to concede, and the Rimegaunt clans have been known to sit up on a ridge and watch one for the entertainment.
Bonded Droval extend their territorial instinct to include their rider, treating that individual as part of their own being. This bond is the most dangerous thing about them in a military context, because a bonded Droval whose rider is threatened abandons every tactical calculation the species is known for and operates on the single remaining directive: protect the territory. What arrives at that point has stopped calculating, and the armies that have met it describe a cataclysm with a face.
Essence Architecture
Droval do not cast spells, invoke Wellsprings, or refine Essence through a Soul Crystal in the way practitioners do, because the Shell that work would have to leave by is sealed, as every beast’s is until something cracks it (see What Has a Soul). They have a soul and a stone behind the breastbone like any wild thing. What they possess beyond that is older, simpler and more concentrated: a bloodline permanently saturated with the resonance of Vohrin’s cold that has been breeding true for millennia.
Their Essence expression is entirely passive and environmental. Their presence lowers ambient temperature. Their proximity suppresses natural sound through Harmonic resonance. Their vocalizations carry a sub-audible component that produces instinctive dread in nearby creatures. No mind control and no working is involved, only a primal terror sharpened by Wellspring resonance until it operates below conscious thought and above the threshold of physiological response. The body reacts before the mind identifies the threat. Heart rate rises, sweat comes, fine motor control degrades. At its root the terror is thermoregulatory: the body recognizing, at the deepest level of its survival, that the thing nearby is the cold itself, which is what the body evolved to flee.
Titan Droval intensify every passive effect to catastrophic levels. A Titan’s presence freezes standing water, cracks exposed stone, disrupts weaker fire-aligned manifestations, and produces the ice-crystal orbiting phenomenon that makes a Titan identifiable at distance. The Titan’s Harmonic output is sufficient to suppress the morale of trained military formations and to destabilize the Essence coherence of practitioners below Stage IV.
Abilities & Powers
Standard Droval

























Frost-Cloak HideSnow and ice accumulate naturally across the pelt, granting near-perfect camouflage in tundra, blizzard, and glacier terrain. A resting Droval is functionally invisible to the eye. A hunter’s bare hand held out for warmth does no better, because the fur keeps a surface temperature identical to the surrounding iceAurora HowlA low, owl-like roar that carries through snowfields and frozen valleys. Audible component: shakes morale, panics lesser beasts and mounts. Sub-audible component: Harmonic resonance suppresses ambient sound and replaces it with the specific stillness that the body takes for dread. Dual-frequency, and the part you cannot hear is the part that does the harmGlacier PounceAn explosive launch from absolute stillness covering up to thirty meters in a single bound. The pounce is delivered at maximum velocity with the full mass behind it. Impact force at the landing point exceeds what most structural reinforcement is rated to absorb. Hours of stillness are spent in a single moment of maximum violenceWinter’s EnduranceExceptional resilience to cold, hunger, fatigue, and storm conditions. A Droval can survive weeks without feeding, months without shelter, and indefinitely without warmth, which the species does not require. The endurance is metabolic: Winter-saturated biology processes ambient Aetheric energy as a supplemental source of food, reducing dependence on preySilent TreadPaw structure (wide, padded, cartilage-backed) combined with Harmonic resonance produces near-silent movement at any speed across any frozen surface. A charging Droval is quieter than a walking human. This is the most terrifying ability in the standard kit, because the prey’s first sign of the Droval’s presence is the Droval’s arrival
War-Bred & Elder Droval

















Rime AuraBodies radiate cold intensely enough to frost armor, numb exposed flesh, and weaken lesser fire effects at close range. The aura is a 5–10m passive field that degrades enemy equipment and physiology through sustained thermal extraction. Extended proximity produces hypothermia symptoms in unprotected combatantsPermafrost SlamStriking the ground with sufficient force sends cracking waves through frozen terrain, disrupting enemy formations and destabilizing footing in a 20m radius. The crack pattern follows the ice’s natural fault geometry, exploiting existing structural weaknesses, which beats brute force because it lets the terrain do the damageBattle Bond InstinctBonded Droval react to a rider’s movement or intent with near-preternatural precision, functioning as an extension of the rider. The bond operates through the Winter resonance shared between the Droval’s biology and the rider’s Essence field, and it runs on heat rather than telepathy: the rider’s intentions produce tiny shifts in the warmth of their body, and the Droval reads the shifts the way it reads everything, through the cold
Titan Droval
Titan Droval are ancient threshold-crossed entities whose Winter saturation has become metaphysical. Each Titan develops distinct and individualized powers based on age, terrain, lineage, and Wellspring exposure. No two are exactly alike, and this variance is what allows the upper end of the species to rise into bounties of Grade SS and X, and in the most extreme cases EX.





























Blizzard SovereignThe Titan generates a localized weather dominion, bringing snow, wind, and killing cold across a massive radius. The dominion is real weather and no construct, and a Measurewright’s storm-glass and wind-vane read the Titan’s presence as an actual storm systemPermafrost DominionGround beneath the Titan’s passage freezes solid to a depth of several meters. Structures and terrain remain altered long after the Titan leaves. The alteration is geological rather than Aetheric: the ground stays frozen because its temperature was genuinely reduced, with no effect left running to dispelCrystalline EnduranceThe hide hardens into frost-mineral armor that deflects conventional steel, arrows, bolts and most non-Essence-infused attacks. The armor is the fur itself, partially crystallized into a translucent mineral-ice composite that carries the hardness of stone and the flexibility of cartilageAurora CascadeThe Titan’s howl becomes a resonance wave capable of shattering morale, disrupting military formations, and physically damaging structures of ice or stone through harmonic destabilization. The wave is visible: the air shimmers with the aurora-like distortion that Winter Harmonic resonance produces at high amplitudeDeep Winter PulseRare high-tier Titans release a catastrophic wave of Winter essence that flash-freezes a battlefield. The pulse is a single-use event that requires hours of accumulation. The flash-freeze is indiscriminate, total, and permanent until external heat is appliedTrait VarianceIndividual Titans may manifest unique powers: ice-mist concealment, spirit-sight, anti-flame aura suppression, glacial regeneration, the ability to sleep for decades and awaken stronger. No two Titan Droval are identical, which makes each one a regional event rather than a species specimen
Grade by Classification













































ClassificationGradeAssessmentJuvenile / WoundedDManageable by experienced frontier hunters. Still lethal to the unpreparedHealthy Wild AdultC to BStandard megafaunal threat. Requires coordinated response from trained hunters. Solo practitioners below a Journeyman should not engageWar-Bred (mounted)B to AArmored and paired with an experienced Winter Eladrin rider. Combined threat exceeds either component. Cavalry formations at this Grade are among the most terrifying battlefield forces in winter terrainElder AlphaA to SHeightened Essence mutation or battlefield history. Requires Experts or dedicated military responseTitan (low)SSMay destroy elite warbands or devastate fortified frontier settlements. No longer a beast encounter. A regional military eventTitan (high)XCan alter terrain, freeze rivers, scatter armies, and reshape local climate. Requires Masters of Stage IX and up, or strategic withdrawalTitan (apex)EXCalamity-class entity. Presence alone reshapes climate, breaks military campaigns, and forces regional evacuation. Historical encounters are measured in settlements abandoned rather than battles fought. Do not engage. Relocate
A word on the bills. Lords and jarls of the far north post Droval bounties with some regularity, mostly young lords, and the crews who know the shelf read the Grade before the sum. The Rimegaunt clans will guide a party for pay as far as the last cairn and no farther, and will quote you the price for bringing back your banners.
Weaknesses
Droval are creatures of deep cold, and while dominant in their native environment, they suffer outside it.
Thermal vulnerability. Intense heat, dry climates, volcanic terrain, and prolonged exposure to strong fire-aspected Essence sap their strength and destabilize their Winter resonance. In hot regions, their endurance drops sharply, their passive cold field weakens, and their frost-based adaptations become liabilities. A Droval forced to operate in temperate-to-warm conditions is running on a timer, and the timer is the speed at which its Winter saturation dissipates.
Size limitations. Tight corridors, unstable floors, marshes, thin ice, and enclosed town streets deny them the space needed for full movement and pouncing force. A Droval in a hallway is still a creature the size of a longhouse, but it cannot pounce, cannot maneuver, and cannot make an ally of the terrain.
Bond exploitation. Bonded Droval can be manipulated by threatening their rider, cubs, or den range. They often abandon optimal tactics in favor of direct protection, and a commander who has read this far knows what to do with that. A bonded Droval whose rider is threatened behaves like a mother whose child is in danger, the most dangerous thing in the world and also the easiest to predict.
Titan margin. Titan Droval possess the same basic weaknesses on a much narrower margin. Only high-tier fire Essence, major hot Wild sites, fire-aspected Masters, or elite coordinated multi-practitioner opposition can reliably exploit Titan weaknesses. Below that threshold, the weaknesses are theoretical.
Cultural Significance
To the northern polar peoples, Droval mean wildly different things depending on one’s relationship with the shelf. Some communities see them as sacred guardians of the old ice and leave offerings at suspected den sites: carved bone and rendered fat, the tribute of people who have decided that living beside the apex predator requires its permission, and who ask for it the only way they can. Others consider slaying one the ultimate mark of warrior prestige, though such hunts usually end in the specific category of disaster that produces legends about why the hunt should not have been attempted.
To military cultures, Droval cavalry formations are one of the most terrifying battlefield forces in winter terrain. The combination of stealth (Silent Tread), shock (Glacier Pounce), area denial (Rime Aura), and a howl that works below the threshold of conscious fear makes Droval cavalry the thing commanders plan around rather than against, since no one has reliably developed a counter to a Droval charge in blizzard conditions.
Titan Droval stand outside ordinary cultural categories entirely. They are viewed as living omens, ancient powers, or the direct will of Winter made flesh. Entire communities flee at rumors of one stirring. Frost cults and northern mystics sometimes seek them out in the hope of worship, alliance, or control. The worship occasionally succeeds, the alliance rarely does, and the control never has. People survive in the same territory as a Titan Droval, on the Titan’s terms, for as long as it allows.
The Arctic Lion Encounter

Recent Event: The Polar Shelf, Present Day
During the Kokan expedition’s march toward Kharven, two Titan-class Droval emerged from the shelf ice and approached the column. Rather than attacking, the Titans performed a Winter recognition assessment, identifying the Arctic Lion’s Verdict Plate and Vohrin-integrated Essence field as a kindred Winter authority.
The first Titan locked on Sodoku Moto. The second locked on Sonzai Moto. The encounter did not produce violence. It produced the specific gesture the bestiary classifies as territorial acknowledgment between Winter authorities of comparable resonance: the head-lower, the sustained eye-hold, and the waiting.
The encounter’s resolution is ongoing. The Titans have not departed. They have not attacked. They are waiting. And the waiting is the thing the species does better than any other thing.



“A standard Droval encounter is a survival problem. A war-bred Droval encounter is a military problem. A Titan Droval encounter is a weather event, and weather has heard every argument you know. Get under something or be elsewhere, and leave the opinions to the weather.”
Frontier Bestiary, Northern Polar Shelf Addendum

the-bestiary/the-wild/natural-beasts/gre.title: Greater Wolf
the-bestiary/the-wild/natural-beasts/gre.content:
The reeve of Ebbe’s Fold posted two silver a pelt one hard winter, on the church door, in his best hand. By the thaw the pack had taken all nine hunters who answered that bill, one at a time and each on the way home, and had not touched a single sheep, and the reeve went out and took the bill down himself and left a side of mutton where the door faced the trees.

Vael’kar, Shadow Howl, in Old Sylvaar. The Silver Fang among frontier hunters.

Natural Beast, Apex Predator · Grade C, Moderate Threat · Transference, with a minor Anamnesis resonance tied to pack lineage · native to the dense forests and mountain borderlands of the Innerworld, with roaming packs ranging into the Outer World
Leans on · the Layer, by Transference, Fate, and the Pack Bond is what it does with it. Body: stand sound, stand together and kill the alpha pair, and a pack is some large wolves. Spirit: the Essence signals pass soul to soul, and a Listener can hear the flank before it comes. Fate: cut the bond and lose a week. Most of a pack’s own Fate is the reason it found you.
Greater Wolves are natural-born hunters, evolved from mortal wolf stock but heavily shaped by Transference’s Aether, which granted them heightened intelligence, endurance, and pack coordination. Their line traces to the primal forests of the Innerworld and Material World borderlands, where Wellspring energy runs richest through the wilds.
Larger and more muscular than ordinary wolves, with dense fur ranging from silver-gray to deep charcoal, often mottled with patches of white or black. Their eyes gleam intelligent amber or icy blue, and their movement is fluid and predatory. Some packs bear faint Essence markings that glow subtly during a hunt.
Highly social and cooperative, Greater Wolves rely on coordinated pack tactics and relentless pursuit. Packs are tightly knit, governed by alpha pairs, and communicate through howl patterns, body language, and Essence signals. They defend territory and young fiercely, challenging rival packs and even humanoid hunters who press too far into their range.


Abilities

Coordinated Hunt flanks, traps, and exhausts prey.
Essence Howl disorients or weakens foes and can summon pack members across great distance.
Enhanced Senses: smell, hearing, and night vision amplified by Wellspring resonance.
Pack Bond, a shared Essence link that speeds coordination and passes information between members.



Weaknesses
Vulnerable when separated from the pack, or during full-moon shifts when their Essence flux fluctuates. Reluctant to engage heavily armored foes without support. Sensitive to Essence-disrupting magic and scent-blocking wards.


The Silverfang Hunts of the Innerworld recount fierce battles between Greater Wolf packs and Concord scouts, and packs have been known to ally with sylvan rangers or druidic circles to defend sacred groves. Forest tribes respect and sometimes worship them as symbols of unity, strength, and the wild’s relentless spirit; a few hunters seek to tame or bond with them as companions, though such efforts are rare and perilous.

the-bestiary/the-wild/natural-beasts/ind.title: Natural Beasts
the-bestiary/the-wild/natural-beasts/ind.content:
Eight entries · creatures that were born rather than made, however large they got
The Worshipful Farriers of Highmere held that a hippogrif’s hind hooves were horse and therefore theirs. The Falconers’ Mews held that a beast with an eagle’s head was a hawk and therefore theirs. The Saddlers wanted a fee off both, and the quarrel was four generations old when it came to blows in the cathedral square on the morning of the great muster, with the guild banners up, the gilded war-birds in their line and half the county cracking walnuts on the steps. Master Farrier Joss Anvilhand, in a coat the color of a horseshoe coming out of the fire, had hold of the near hind leg of a charger called Bright Sibyl. Mistress Falconer Ede Rushlight had hold of the other end, with a hood. Sibyl had been standing six hours in the sun with nothing to eat. She took Master Anvilhand’s right arm off at the elbow with one sweep of the talon, went up over the cathedral with a falconer’s banner in her beak and two saddlers hanging from her girth, dropped the saddlers on the bishop’s roof, and did not come back. She founded a wild line on the crags above Highmere that the muster has been trying to buy back ever since. The guilds still argue over which of them she belonged to, with staves, on muster day.
A natural beast may be the size of a longhouse and glow like a saint, and it was still born of a mother, it still eats, and it has its own view of your arrangements. Wellspring Aether has soaked into these lines over the generations and made them larger, stranger and harder to kill, which is the only reason a working person would know their names.
Goliath

Tharvak, Mountain’s Fury, in Old Parunic. Brakkar, Stonebreaker, in the Innerworld dialect.

Natural Beast, Giantkin · Grade A, Extreme Threat · Chthonica, with a strong Anamnesis resonance tied to ancestral lineage · the Innerworld's high ranges
Leans on · the Shell, by Chthonica, Wild, with Anamnesis holding the ancestors. Body: its knees, and a lot of friends. Spirit: past the stone to a very long memory, which is also how to be left alone. Fate: a rockfall needs a slope, and the giant needs you to be on it.
A rare race of colossal humanoids born from the primal forces of Gaia’s mountains. Their ancestors were sculpted by elemental titans to guard ancient mountain passes and Wellspring sites, and over millennia they developed the size and endurance to live where nothing else could.
Towering, often exceeding three and a half meters, with stone-gray or earthen skin textured like granite. Coarse dark hair streaked with mineral glints. Eyes glowing faintly amber or moss green. Rugged angular features marked with ancient tribal tattoos in natural pigment or Essence ink.
Stoic and territorial, wary of outsiders and not inherently hostile. They live in small close-knit clans where strength and endurance dictate status, and maintain ancient traditions bound to the mountains and Wellspring sites they protect.
Stoneform hardens the skin to near-rock toughness. Mountain’s Endurance grants resistance to cold, altitude and fatigue. Earthquake Stomp creates localized tremors. Wellspring Channeling enhances physical strikes and raises simple stone constructs.
Less effective in dense forest or swamp. Slow to recover from magical or elemental exhaustion. Vulnerable to attacks targeting joints or unprotected limbs.

During the Mountain Wars goliath clans sided variably, some joining Concord forces to defend Wellspring sites, others rebelling in defense of ancestral land. At the Siege of Vellsorea Peak a goliath chieftain held a mountain pass against overwhelming numbers for weeks.
Among mountainfolk and Marrowkin clans they are respected as primal guardians and ancestral kin.

Cyclops

Gorath, One-Eyed Terror, in Old Parunic. Stonebreaker among mountain tribes.

Natural Beast, Giantkin · Grade A, Extreme Threat · Monolithion and Chthonica · rugged ranges, deep caves, and Wellspring caverns
Leans on · the Shell, by Monolithion and Chthonica, both Wild. Body: the blind side. Spirit: one eye and one idea, read at a distance. Fate: it depends on the depth it can judge, and its footing in the cave it knows.
Colossal humanoids born from primal Wellspring forces and ancient elemental titans. Legend says they were crafted as the first guardians of mountain Wellspring sites, forged from stone and spirit to withstand the ravages of the ages.
Towering, with a single large eye centered in the forehead. Skin resembling rough stone, cracked and mottled with ancient runes. Thick powerful limbs wielding massive clubs or boulders.
Solitary and territorial. Often slow-witted, and their cunning in combat and mastery of stone weapons make them deadly regardless. They occasionally serve as mercenaries or guardians for powerful sorcerers.
Stone Crushing Strength shatters shields and walls. Piercing Gaze focuses Essence to blind or intimidate. Mountain Stomp. Regenerative Resilience, sustained by Wellspring essence.

Limited peripheral vision due to the single eye. Vulnerable to ranged attacks exploiting the blind spot. Slow movement and reaction beside smaller foes.

The Siege of Grimestone Peak recounts a cyclops battling Concord forces for weeks to hold a pass crucial to Wellspring control. Tribal legend speaks of the Stone-Eye, who guarded sacred Wellspring sites until a hero killed him.
Minotaur

Tharnok, Horned Fury, in Old Parunic. The Mazebreaker among frontier clans.

Natural Beast, Labyrinth Guardian · Grade A, Extreme Threat · Petralon, with Monolithion · underground labyrinthine domains and ancient ruins
Leans on · the Shell, by Petralon and Monolithion, both Wild. Body: a charge cannot turn, so make it try. Spirit: past the hide to a guardian who has been told one thing. Fate: a labyrinth is a set of conditions, and a pulled thread can make a wrong turn right, at a price.
Descendants of mortal beastkin and ancient Wellspring-infused lineages, born to guard sacred labyrinths and Wellspring sanctuaries. Their origin is tied to the convergence of Petralon and Monolithion deep within the Material World’s underground realms.
Massive humanoid beasts with bull-like heads and horns, muscular torsos, thick hides. Skin often mottled with stone-like texture; eyes glowing deep amber or earthen. Many bear tribal tattoos or Wellspring runes etched into hide or armor.
Labyrinth Mastery grants exceptional spatial awareness and tracking within complex terrain. Horn Charge shatters shields. Earthshaker Stomp cracks ground. Resilient Hide resists both physical and magical damage.
Vulnerable to magic disrupting Earth Essence flow. Less agile in open or flat terrain. And their territorial instincts can be exploited for ambush, which is the standard Concord approach.
The Siege of the Hollow Maze recounts minotaurs defending Wellspring relics against Concord forces. Many explorers have vanished within labyrinths rumored to be cursed by minotaur guardians. Some subterranean clans worship them as ancestral protectors.
Sea Serpent

Tethyrath, Ocean’s Coil, in Old Mariner’s Cant. Myr’galar, Wave Devourer, in Abyssal Tongue.

Natural Beast, Aquatic Colossus · Grade S, Domain Threat · Thaloré, some variants Abyntheus or Nihiloth · the deep seas and coastal waters of the Material World
Leans on · the Core, by Thaloré, Spirit, or Abyntheus in some lines, and its bulk does the rest. Body: a harpoon and a shallow bay. Spirit: a grief the size of a coast, and a brave hand can lay a line on it. Fate: it follows what it has always followed, so move the mackerel.
Ancient leviathanic creatures born from the confluence of Thaloré’s Aether and the deep ocean’s primal forces. Many scholars hold them among the first true giants to emerge in the Material World’s oceans, apex predators and keepers of the deep’s mysteries. Their presence is linked to the health of Wellspring sites near oceanic ley lines.
Enormous serpentine bodies in smooth overlapping scales from deep blue to sea green and slate gray. Eyes glowing faintly with watery light. Elongated heads with rows of sharp backward-curving teeth; long fins and frilled gills line their sides.
Predatory and territorial. They patrol vast stretches of ocean, generally avoiding human contact but fiercely defending nesting grounds. Mostly solitary, though some have been observed forming loose pods during migration.
Tidal Surge capsizes vessels. Waterform liquefies parts of the body temporarily to slip through tight spaces or escape bindings. Sonar Roar stuns and communicates across leagues. Regenerative Scales heal rapidly and resist corrosion.
Vulnerable to fire-based attacks and to a Guild craftsman’s bursting fire-pots, when they burst at the right end of the ship. Less agile in shallow, narrow water. Sensitive to sudden Essence disruptions that disturb the Aether of a water Wellspring site.
The Storming of Crestport details a sea serpent wrecking a fleet attempting to blockade a Crevice port. Coastal legend speaks of the Coil of the Forgotten Depths, which guided lost sailors to watery graves.
Greater Wolf

Vael’kar, Shadow Howl, in Old Sylvaar. The Silver Fang among frontier hunters.

Natural Beast, Apex Predator · Grade C, Moderate Threat · Transference, with a minor Anamnesis resonance tied to pack lineage · the dense forests and mountain borderlands of the Innerworld
Leans on · the Layer, by Transference, Fate, and the Pack Bond is what it does with it. Body: stand sound, stand together and kill the alpha pair, and a pack is some large wolves. Spirit: the Essence signals pass soul to soul, and a Listener can hear the flank before it comes. Fate: cut the bond and lose a week. Most of a pack’s own Fate is the reason it found you.
Evolved from mortal wolf stock and heavily influenced by Transference’s Aether, which granted heightened intelligence, endurance and pack coordination.
Larger and more muscular than typical wolves, dense fur from silver-gray to deep charcoal. Eyes gleaming intelligent amber or icy blue. Some packs bear faint Essence markings that glow subtly during hunts.
Highly social and cooperative. Packs are tightly-knit under alpha pairs, and communicate through howl patterns, body language, and Essence signals. They defend territory and young fiercely.
Coordinated Hunt flanks, traps and exhausts prey. Essence Howl disorients and summons pack members across great distance. Enhanced Senses amplified by Wellspring resonance. Pack Bond: a shared Essence link permitting rapid information transfer between members.

Vulnerable when separated from pack, and during full moon shifts when their Essence flux fluctuates. Reluctant to engage heavily armored foes without support. Sensitive to Essence-disrupting magic and scent-blocking wards.

The Silverfang Hunts recount fierce battles between Greater Wolf packs and Concord scouts. Packs have allied with sylvan rangers and druidic circles to defend sacred groves. Forest tribes respect and sometimes worship them as symbols of unity and the wild’s relentless spirit.
Neiman Lion

Rael’thor, King of the Savannah, in Old Parunic. Sunmaw among desert tribes.

Natural Beast, Apex Predator · Grade B, High Threat · Pyraeon, with a minor Aurevane influence · the desert savannahs and grasslands of the Old and Outer Worlds
Leans on · the Shell, by Pyraeon, Wild, with Aurevane in the mane. Body: it holds the ground it stands on, so fight it elsewhere. Spirit: the Core is a pride’s, and a pride remembers. Fate: its stunning roar needs open air and an audience.
Evolved from mortal lion stock, uniquely adapted to harsh desert and savannah, and infused with Pyraeon’s Essence granting enhanced strength, endurance, and a mystical aura that commands respect and fear.
Golden tawny fur shimmering faintly under sunlight. Manes glow subtly with Wellspring energy, sometimes appearing as haloes of light. Eyes blaze amber or fiery gold. Scars and battle marks are common among pride leaders.
Regal and fiercely territorial: noble hunters and protectors of their prides, with complex social structures under dominant males who guard territory and lead hunts.
Solar Roar stuns prey and rallies allies. Essence Prowess. Sunlit Aura bolsters allies and intimidates foes. Savannah Stalk grants exceptional stealth and tracking in harsh environments.
Vulnerable to Essence disruptions interfering with their solar resonance. Less effective in dense forest or mountain. Dependent on pride cooperation: lone lions are markedly more vulnerable.
The Battle of Searing Dunes recounts Neiman pride leaders defending Wellspring oases from poachers and Crevice-spawn. Tribal elders tell of the Sunmaw’s Blessing, a rare cub believed to bring prosperity. Their manes are prized in ceremonial garb.
Sasquatch

Grav’thar, the Hidden Giant, in Old Parunic. Wildershadow among frontier tribes.

Natural Beast, Forest Colossus · Grade C, Moderate Threat · Verdantia, with Anamnesis and deep ties to primal forest Essence · the dense woodlands of the Material World
Leans on · the Shell, by Verdantia, Wild, with Anamnesis in the old stands. Body: catching it is the whole difficulty. Spirit: it can be read, and it would rather you left food. Fate: scent, wind and the woodsman’s habits are what it hunts by.
Enormous elusive humanoids, mortal-born but heavily influenced by Verdantia and Anamnesis. They have roamed ancient forests since the First Eon, serving as protectors of sacred groves and ancient Wellspring sites, blending with nature through subtle Essence manipulation.
Massive ape-like humanoids covered in thick dark fur mottled with moss and lichen. Standing over three meters with broad shoulders and powerful limbs. Eyes gleaming with a soft greenish Essence glow, and their movement is surprisingly silent for their size.
Reclusive and wary. Mostly solitary or in small family groups. Herbivorous, and fiercely protective when provoked.
Essence Camouflage masks scent and presence. Primal Roar stuns and communicates across distance. Nature’s Grasp manipulates plant life to entangle. Wellspring Regeneration heals rapidly near sacred groves.
Slow outside forest. Sensitive to Essence disruption magic that breaks the camouflage. Vulnerable to fire and ranged attack.
Tales of the Silent Guardians of Velthaeir describe Sasquatches protecting ancient Wellspring groves from poachers and dark forces. Concord scouts occasionally report mysterious forest giants aiding sylvan patrols during incursions.
Hippogrif

Aelthar, Sky Charger, in Old Parunic. The Stormwing among frontier riders.

Hybrid Beast, Aerial Mount · Grade B, High Threat · Cymorath, with Transference and a trace of Anamnesis · high peaks, open skies and enchanted forests
Leans on · the Shell, by Cymorath, Wild, with Transference’s Fate in a broken-in mount. Body: a good net, or a good rider. Spirit: its nerves can be read and calmed by anyone who has spent a season in a mews. Fate: the bond with a rider is real and can be pulled, which is why stables insure against it.
Noble hybrids born of majestic equine stock and fierce avian predators, forged through Cymorath’s Aether, which blesses their lineage. They have served as mounts to knights, sorcerers and warriors since the Harmonial Age.
The body of a powerful horse with the wings, head and talons of a great eagle. Plumage shining gold, bronze or silver. Eyes gleaming with sharp intelligence and keen perception.
Proud, intelligent, fiercely loyal to chosen riders, territorial and protective of nests and offspring. They form strong bonds with those who earn their trust.
Aerial Supremacy. Talons of the Storm rend armor and flesh alike. Windborne Roar disorients enemies and bolsters allies. Essence Bond shares Wellspring Essence with the rider, enhancing coordination and resilience.
Vulnerable when grounded or separated from riders. Sensitive to Essence-disrupting magic targeting the bond or the flight. And they require vast territories and Wellspring-rich nesting sites to thrive, which is why the elite wings of cavalry are as small as they are.
The Skyward Charge chronicles legendary hippogrif riders breaking enemy sieges. Several Concord orders maintain elite hippogrif cavalry, renowned for getting anywhere first.


Droval — The Frost-Howler
Neiman Lion
Greater Wolf



Read next: Monster Cores, for what a beast’s stone is and does; The Sixteen Stages, for the scale a beast shares with you; The Bestiary, for the rest of the register.

the-bestiary/the-wild/natural-beasts/nei.title: Neiman Lion
the-bestiary/the-wild/natural-beasts/nei.content:
A chief of the dune tribes once took his people’s chair in a robe trimmed with a Neiman mane, and at noon on the day of the gathering the trim lit up like a lamp in front of all nine clans. By dusk the dead lion’s pride had come forty leagues across the sand and sat down in a golden ring around the chief’s tent, in perfect courtesy, and on the third day the chief walked out in his shirt and handed back the robe.
Natural Beast, Apex Predator · Grade B, High Threat · Pyraeon, with a minor Aurevane influence · native to the desert savannahs and grasslands of the Old World and the Outer World, especially near sun-drenched Wellspring sites
Leans on · the Shell, by Pyraeon, Wild, with Aurevane in the mane. Body: it holds the ground it stands on, so fight it elsewhere. Spirit: the Core is a pride’s, and a pride remembers. Fate: its stunning roar needs open air and an audience.
The Neiman Lion is a majestic predator evolved from mortal lion stock, adapted to the harsh deserts and savannahs of the Old and Outer Worlds. Pyraeon’s Essence runs through the line, granting enhanced strength, endurance, and a mystical aura that commands respect and fear; a Neiman Lion reigns over its territory, hunting alone or in small prides.
A large feline with golden tawny fur that shimmers faintly under sunlight. Its mane glows subtly with Wellspring energy, sometimes reading as a halo of light, and its eyes blaze amber or fiery gold. Its movement blends grace with raw power, and scars and battle marks are common among pride leaders.
Regal and fiercely territorial, Neiman Lions are both hunters and protectors of their prides, with dominant males guarding territory and leading hunts under a complex social order. Their presence inspires awe and terror in equal measure among other creatures and the local tribes who share their ground.


Abilities

Solar Roar stuns prey and rallies allies with a roar imbued with Solar Essence.
Essence Prowess heightens speed, strength, and endurance through Wellspring resonance.
Sunlit Aura bolsters allies and intimidates foes.
Savannah Stalk grants exceptional stealth and tracking suited to harsh terrain.



Weaknesses
Vulnerable to Essence disruptions that interfere with solar resonance. Less effective in dense forest or mountain terrain. Dependent on pride cooperation; a lone lion is markedly more vulnerable.


The Battle of Searing Dunes recounts Neiman pride leaders defending Wellspring oases from poachers and Crevice-spawn incursions, and tribal elders still tell of the Sunmaw’s Blessing, a rare cub believed to bring prosperity. Desert cultures revere the Neiman Lion as a symbol of power and vitality; its mane is prized in ceremonial garb, and its spirit is invoked in rites for courage and protection.

the-bestiary/the-wild/spirit-beasts.title: Spirit Beasts
the-bestiary/the-wild/spirit-beasts.content:
Eleven entries · creatures formed from Wellspring resonance rather than born of flesh
Brother Cuthwin Tace had a choir of forty, a very patient abbot and a theory, which was that a siren’s song could be beaten by a better one, in four parts, properly pitched. He put it to the test in high summer aboard the cog Pious Alys, bound through the Wailing Reefs with a hold full of the dyers’ guild’s saffron and his singers lined up along the rail in new scarlet, and for the first mile he was right. The sirens came up on the rocks with their hair moving like weed and listened, courteous as a paying audience, through the whole of the first verse and the second. On the third they took up the tenor line and gave it back a shade sweeter. The choir went over the side in order of voice, smiling, basses last, with Brother Cuthwin still beating time, and the Pious Alys opened on the reef with nobody at the steering oar. The saffron went into the sea, and for nine days the whole bay ran as gold as a coronation. The coast has held a festival there ever since. On clear nights the fishermen swear the rocks still sing that hymn in four parts, with Cuthwin’s own ornament in the last bar, which he never wrote down.
Mark what the creature did. It listened, learned the tune and kept it. A Spirit Beast was formed from the resonance of a Wellspring (one of the sixty kinds of Aether, the stuff a practitioner pulls from the world around him) rather than born of flesh, and it comes with a mind, a memory and opinions of its own. Most of them can be bargained with, some can be befriended, and the hunting halls will tell you that a bill posted on one is a bill posted on its whole herd, flock or reef. I would read the entries below as if each of them could read you back.
Unicorn

Elessae, the Moon’s First Hoof, in High Parunic. Thal’wyn, Horned Dawn, in Old Sylvaar.

Spirit Beast · Grade B, High Threat · Benediction, with a minor Somnalis affinity via Nysera · native to Edenis
Leans on · the Layer, by Benediction and Somnalis, both Fate. Body: a sound fighter gives its blessings nothing to work on, and whatever it wears can be killed if it can be caught, which is the sacrilege the valleys remember. Spirit: its calming and its Horn of Binding are pulled by a soul and show on the Core before they land. Fate: a contest over who owes whom, and it has been owed for longer.
Spirit-born from Benediction’s resonance during the Harmonial Age. Said to be the first beings Florwyn dreamed into being when she envisioned peace between mortal and spirit realms. Rare herds persist in secluded Material World forests where Benediction sites surface.
Equine and slender. Coats shimmer under moonlight in pure white, silver, pale gold or rare midnight blue. Horns long and spiraled, glowing when they channel. Eyes luminescent gold or pale blue; elders bear star-flecked irises. Their manes move as though in a breeze that is not there.
They travel in loose herds of four to six under an elder mare called a Moonkeeper, and vanish into dream-light trails during migration. Highly intelligent, cautious, and not inherently aggressive, but they defend Wellspring sites from corruption fiercely, and will ally with mortal defenders where trust is earned.


Abilities

Harmonic Healing · purifies Essence corruption, mends wounds, calms emotional unrest
Moonveil Step · short-range teleportation through dreamlight, leaving an aurora shimmer
Wellspring Guard · speed and magic resistance greatly amplified within reach of a Wellspring site
Horn of Binding · channels a Conjunction of Ma Memory + Ur Balance to seal a corrupted being temporarily



Weaknesses
Cannot survive heavily corrupted or void-aspected zones; prolonged exposure sickens them Trust is hard to earn: hostility meets immediate evasion or overwhelming defense Horn shattering removes most of their magical ability, and is considered sacrilege in many cultures



During the Withering Age several herds guarded Wellspring sites that kept whole forest realms from falling. The Siege of Moonveil Grove records a single Moonkeeper halting a Crevice-born horror for three days until Concord forces arrived.
Among the Sylvaar they are Florwyn’s first promise made flesh. In human kingdoms, purity and incorruptible truth. In Abyss-touched cultures they are omens of destruction, because their arrival heralds the cleansing of corrupted land, and the land in question is yours.

Griffon

Gryphael, Sky-Claw, in High Parunic. Talaruk, Lion of the Wind, in Old Iampu.

Spirit Beast · Grade A, Extreme Threat · Cymorath, secondary Transference resonance when bonded · native to Draconis and Caelum
Leans on · the Shell, by Cymorath, Wild. Body: drag it to the ground and keep it there. Spirit: past the feathers to a mind that holds one idea, the nest. Fate: a dive depends on the wind, the ledge and the nest staying put.
Shaped in the early Harmonial Age where Transference and Cymorath Aethers intertwined. Many hold that Omnis himself molded the first griffons as aerial guardians of the floating citadels.
Forequarters of a great eagle fused seamlessly into the hindquarters of a lion. Plumage reflects Wellspring alignment: white and silver for skybound flocks, bronze and gold for sun-favored lineages, storm-gray for tempest dwellers. Talons strong enough to pierce tempered steel.
Predatory but not needlessly aggressive, and fiercely territorial over nesting cliffs and Wellspring-fed aeries. They mate for life; bonded pairs defend a chosen roost until death. They ally with mortal riders who pass their trials of worthiness.


Abilities

Aerial Supremacy · extreme maneuverability in high wind; dives above 200 kph
Sonic Cry · a screech that disrupts Essence concentration and shatters brittle material
Wellspring Bond · increased stamina and magic resistance defending bonded territory or rider
Sky Rend · a dive capable of breaking siege engines or large beasts in one strike



Weaknesses

Poor endurance in prolonged ground combat Vulnerable to nets, entangling magic, and attacks on wing membranes Will abandon combat to protect nests or mates



At the Battle of Skychain Pass, twelve storm griffons routed a Crevice-born wyvern swarm before it reached the fortress gates. The High Aerie Riders of Foraye maintain griffon bonds running back seven centuries. In Draconis they are loyalty and sovereignty and appear throughout royal heraldry; in the frontier kingdoms, taming one is the ultimate mark of a sky knight.
Raiju

Voh’thir, Storm’s Howl, in Old Sylvaar. The Thunder Beast in Material World folklore.

Spirit Beast, Elemental Predator · Grade A, Extreme Threat · Cymorath, with a minor Orrenthal strain · Draconis and Caelum peaks
Leans on · the Shell, by Cymorath, Wild. Body: a low roof and wet footing. Spirit: the Static Cloak stops workings on the skin and has no say about the Core behind it. Fate: the Lightning Leap needs its trail, and a trail needs dry air.
Born from the fusion of Cymorath and Orrenthal Aethers. Legend says they were first formed by Nysera’s breath during a cataclysmic lightning storm that tore through the ancient forests of Edenis.
A lithe quadruped between wolf and great cat, cloaked in crackling blue-white fur that arcs with static. Eyes glow bright violet. Long whip-like tails and sharp talons ending in glowing tips.
Wild, unpredictable, fiercely territorial. They hunt in small packs and alone in storm season. Their howls are said to summon lightning and their presence foreshadows violent weather. They show a playful cunning, stunning prey with sudden bursts before closing.


Abilities

Stormcall Howl · summons localized lightning strikes and electric storms
Electric Surge · bursts through fur and talons to stun
Static Cloak · a crackling field that disrupts magic and shocks attackers
Lightning Leap · closes distance instantly on a trail of electricity



Weaknesses
Vulnerable in enclosed spaces where mobility is limited Water dampens their static and can cause unpredictable feedback Excessive cold temporarily suppresses their lightning


During the Storm of Wailing Peaks a Raiju pack destroyed a Concord scouting expedition, and the region carries a long-term magical storm curse as a result. Shamanic tribes invoke them as spirits of vengeance and renewal and offer tribute before hunting seasons. Some warrior orders attempt to bond with them and ride them into battle. Others fear them as nature’s unbridled fury.
Harpy

Skrial, Storm Wing, in Old Parunic. Tal’kira, Screech of the Hunt, in Outer World dialect.

Spirit Beast, Aerial Predator · Grade B, High Threat · Cymorath, with Luminalis sharpening sense and speed · Caelum and Draconis
Leans on · the Shell, by Cymorath, Wild, with Luminalis in the eye. Body: nets and a tight formation. Spirit: a flock’s cunning is shallow and easily read. Fate: an ambush depends on the caravan being where it was said to be.
Spirit-born from the raw winds, shaped by the violent intersection of Cymorath and Luminalis Aethers. Long held as harbingers of storm and misfortune.
Raptor and humanoid fused: feathered wings and arms, hooked beaks, eyes glowing faintly with Wellspring energy. Plumage from storm-gray to sunlit bronze, mottled with streaks of elemental energy crackling along the feathers.

Aggressive and territorial. They hunt in small flocks, using piercing cries and aerial agility to disorient prey before tearing it apart.
And they are cunning enough for rudimentary communication, which they use to mimic voices and lure travelers into traps. Concord scouts have reported harpies imitating patrol members to lead them into crevices.

Sonic Screech shatters fragile material and disrupts Essence concentration. Wind Blade generates slicing gusts from talon strikes. Aerial Acrobatics and Mimicry complete the set.
Vulnerable to grounded combatants and heavy armor, sensitive to loud disorienting noise that breaks their coordination, and their wings are delicate and susceptible to targeted attack.
The Screeching of the Wind Pass records a flock’s ambush that cost several trade caravans. In Draconis and Caelum they are feared and revered as wild spirits of storm and vengeance; frontier tribes use harpy feathers as talismans, and others conduct rites to appease them during storm season.
Psy-Apes

M’thak, Mindclaw, in Innerworld dialects. The Thoughtshard Primates among arcane scholars.

Spirit-Hybrid Beast, Psychic Primate · Grade B, High Threat · Oneirion and Eidolyn · the Innerworld's central jungles
Leans on · the Core, by Oneirion, Spirit, with Eidolyn building the rest. Body: a spear does not care what you dream, and an ape that is reached goes down like an ape. Spirit: a straight contest of minds against a troop. Fate: the troop survives by being right about you, and one spoiled read will do.
Mortal-born primates whose Essence became deeply intertwined with Oneirion and Eidolyn Aethers. The fusion granted psychic capability, elevated intelligence, and subtle manipulation of nearby minds. They evolved where Wellspring Aether lies thick beneath the canopy.
Larger than typical apes, sleek dark fur with faint iridescent highlights. Eyes glow soft violet or pale blue, and subtle markings along their limbs resemble glyphic tattoos.

They live in complex social groups with hierarchies determined by psychic dominance, communicating through a blend of vocalization and telepathic pulse, and coordinating hunts and defense with uncanny efficiency.

Telepathic Link shares thought and emotion across the group. Psychic Strike disrupts mental focus. Dream Veil creates illusion and mental barrier. Wellspring Empathy senses Essence flux and emotional state.
Vulnerable to Essence-dampening wards and counter-psychic magic. Physically weaker than brute beasts. And psychic overload can collapse group cohesion outright.
The Mindshade Jungles Campaign details ambushes on Concord patrols using psychic illusion to mask approach. Several arcane researchers have vanished investigating their territories. Innerworld tribes regard them as guardians of sacred Wellspring sites.
Dryads

Lioraen, Forest Spirits, in the Sylvaar tongues. Verdant Whisperers among frontier woodfolk.

Spirit-Beast, Nature Guardian · Grade C, Moderate Threat · Verdantia, with Anamnesis in the oldest groves · the deep forests of the Innerworld and Material World
Leans on · the Shell, by Verdantia, Wild, and the grove’s memory by Anamnesis in the oldest stands. Body: an axe, and the war that follows. Spirit: past the bark to what the grove remembers, which is also where a bargain begins. Fate: a grove depends on its water and on what people have promised it.
Spirits born from Verdantia’s Aether intertwined with ancient forest Essence. They embody the living soul of the oldest trees, and their existence is tied to sacred groves: their power ebbs and flows with the health of their forest.
Slender humanoid figures with bark-like skin, leaf-green eyes, hair resembling flowing vines. Their limbs shift subtly between wood and flesh, and their movement echoes rustling leaves.
Peaceful and nurturing and fiercely protective. They tend flora and fauna, heal, and hold the balance of their groves; threatened, they unleash nature magic and summon forest creatures. They aid travelers they judge respectful.
Verdant Growth entangles and builds barriers. Healing Touch mends wounds and cures poison. Nature’s Call summons woodland creatures and elemental vines. Forest Camouflage makes them nearly invisible among trees.
Vulnerable outside forested or Wellspring-rich ground, susceptible to fire and Essence-dampening magic, and physically fragile beside other spirit-beasts.
The Siege of Elderbark Grove records Dryads defending their sanctuary against Crevice-spawn. Concord rangers routinely seek their aid navigating perilous forest realms.
Bai Ze

Zhal’rei, the Enlightened One, in Old Parunic. The Oracle Beast among sages.

Spirit-Beast, Guardian of Knowledge · Grade B, High Threat · Anamnesis and Oneirion, with Judicium for the clear reading · Innerworld sanctuaries
Leans on · the Core, by Anamnesis, Medium, and Oneirion, Spirit, with Judicium for the clear reading. Body: it is physically fragile and will leave long before you arrive. Spirit: it reads you first and better. Fate: it knows what is, and what has a way of happening is a different question. Nobody who has met one recommends any of this.

Emerged during the Harmonial Age as a guide for mortals, gifted with profound wisdom and the perception of hidden truth. It roams sacred groves and ancient libraries, aiding seekers of knowledge or guarding esoteric Wellspring sites.
A majestic quadruped with multiple eyes arrayed across head and shoulders, each glowing softly. Fur a shimmering blend of pale gold and silver; a form combining lion, ox and dragon. Elegant horns curl from its crown and ethereal runes shimmer along its flanks.

Calm, enigmatic, benevolent. A patient guardian, offering cryptic guidance and riddles to those it judges worthy. It avoids conflict and will fiercely protect sacred Wellspring sites and ancient knowledge from desecration.
Omniscient Gaze peers into past, present and potential futures. Essence Insight reads the Aether of a site and metaphysical signatures. Protective Aura wards against corruption and hostility. Mystic Speech communicates telepathically, in riddle or vision.
Physically fragile. Vulnerable to Essence disruption that clouds its perception. Rare and elusive, and deliberately hidden, to avoid exploitation.

Ancient texts recount the Bai Ze aiding the early Concord founders with divine wisdom, shaping treaties and Wellspring stewardship. Scholars today seek it to unlock lost knowledge or avert metaphysical disaster. Its sightings are held as omens of profound change.

Siren

Liora, Song Weaver, in Old Parunic. The Sea’s Temptress among sailors.

Spirit-Beast, Enchanting Predator · Grade B, High Threat · Somnalis and Thaloré, with Transference amplifying the enchantment · coastal waters, mist-shrouded islands, underwater grottoes
Leans on · the Layer, by Somnalis and Transference, both Fate, with Thaloré giving the song its weight. Body: wax, rope and a steady hand on the oar, and then it is an animal on a rock. Spirit: a Listener hears the hand on the tune before the crew goes over the side. Fate: cut what the song has tied, at about what it cost to tie.
Ethereal beings born from the fusion of Thaloré and Somnalis Aethers, embodying the hypnotic power of the sea and the allure of dreams. Legend says they arise from the restless souls of lost sailors and oceanic spirits bound by ancient magic.
Beautiful humanoid forms, hair shifting like seaweed, skin shimmering with reflected moonlight. Eyes glowing soft blue. Some display webbed fingers or scaled patches.
Seductive and cunning. They lure sailors to treacherous reefs or drown them outright. They prefer to avoid direct conflict and can summon oceanic creatures and shape water to defend themselves.
Siren’s Song charms, disorients, incapacitates. Water Manipulation controls tide, current and aquatic life. Mist Veil obscures. Ocean’s Grasp restrains and strikes with tendrils of water.
Vulnerable to sound-dampening wards and Essence disruptors, markedly less effective on land, and susceptible to bright light and holy Essence.
The Wailing Reefs Incident attributes numerous wrecks to siren lures. Coastal communities hold festivals to appease them and protect their fishermen, which is not framed locally as superstition.
Tanuki

Mokuri, Trickster Spirit, in Old Parunic. The Forest Jester among frontier folk.

Spirit-Beast, Trickster Shapeshifter · Grade D, Minor Threat · Eidolyn and Oneirion · dense forests, mystical groves, hidden Wellspring sites
Leans on · the Shell by Eidolyn, Wild, and the Core by Oneirion, Spirit. Body: pin the shape and it stops being clever. Spirit: a Read sees the leaf under the coin. Fate: a trick depends on being believed, and a sound purse does not believe it.
Born from the blend of Eidolyn and Oneirion Aethers, embodying playful cunning and shape-shifting magic. Rooted in ancient forest lore, they delight in mischief, illusion, and testing the wits of travelers and sorcerers alike. Their true forms are rare to witness, as they prefer ever-changing guises.
Small, fox-like or raccoon-like, with large expressive eyes and bushy tails often tipped in glowing essence light. Their forms shimmer and flicker, sometimes sporting additional tails or strange appendages that are not there.
Shape-shifting into humanoid or animal forms. Illusion Weaving. Essence Mimicry of voices, sounds and magical signatures. Spirit Mischief, causing minor disruptions in the Aether of a Wellspring site and in ambient magic.
Vulnerable to Essence detection and truth-binding magic. Their physical forms are fragile and illusory, and direct attacks disrupt the transformation. They avoid conflict and flee threats.
Folklore of the Laughing Grove tells of Tanuki leading lost hunters safely out of enchanted woods, or into deeper danger. Many arcane practitioners regard them as mischievous but valuable informants.
Pegasus

Aeloria, Sky Wanderer, in Old Parunic. The Starhoof among frontier riders.

Spirit-Beast, Celestial Mount · Grade B, High Threat · Aurevane, with Benediction · high peaks, sacred groves, celestial realms
Leans on · Medium, by Aurevane, leaning toward the Shell in flight and with Benediction’s Fate on anyone it has chosen. Body: the wing and the tether. Spirit: it answers to being asked, and that is the road people mean when they tell the story. Fate: a chosen rider’s bond is the thing that can be pulled, and whoever pulls it will be hunted.
Noble celestial horses born from the purest Aurevane and Benediction Aethers. Legend places their emergence in the Harmonial Age as messengers and guardians of the divine realms, embodying freedom, purity and swift flight.
Gleaming white coats, large feathered wings shimmering with radiant light, eyes glowing with serene wisdom. Their hooves leave faint trails of stardust.
Noble, intelligent, fiercely loyal. They bond deeply with a chosen rider.
Celestial Flight · unmatched aerial speed and agility. Radiant Aura · a calming light that heals allies and wards off darkness. Essence Bond · shares Wellspring Essence with the rider, enhancing the vitality and senses of both. Divine Charge.
Vulnerable to Essence-disrupting magic and dark curses. Sensitive to pollution or corruption at Wellspring sites. Require pure Wellspring environments to maintain strength.
The Skyward Crusades recount Pegasus-mounted knights breaking enemy lines and carrying vital messages. Several orders maintain sacred herds for war and ceremony.
Phoenix

Ignara, Flameborn, in Old Parunic. The Eternal Ember in the Innerworld.

Spirit-Beast, Elemental Flame · Grade SS, Realm Hazard · Pyreveil, with Rebirthine · volcanic peaks, sacred flame groves, radiant Wellspring sites
Leans on · the Shell, by Pyreveil and Rebirthine, both Wild. Body: a hitter can kill it, once, at great cost, and then there are the ashes. Spirit: in the ash there is nothing but the Core, the one hour a Spirit hand has it alone. Fate: the rebirth depends on the sanctuary it is bound to, and sanctuaries can be made to fail.
Born from the purest Pyreveil and Rebirthine Aethers, embodying cycles of destruction and renewal. Said to arise from the ashes of its own death. Revered as a divine omen and protector of sacred Wellspring sites.
A massive bird, plumage of blazing red, gold and orange, radiating light and warmth. Eyes glowing with intense fire, feathers shimmering as if aflame. Its flight leaves trails of embers.
Noble, majestic, fiercely protective. It intervenes to purge corruption and restore a Wellspring site to balance.


Abilities

Rebirth Flame · immolates itself to ashes and is reborn, restoring vitality
Radiant Burst · waves of purifying fire that cleanse corruption and heal allies
Essence Beacon · amplifies Wellspring energy, empowering nearby creatures and sites
Flame Talons · scorching strikes capable of melting armor and flesh



Weaknesses

Vulnerable during the rebirth cycle, when it exists only as ashes Susceptible to water and Essence-dampening magic
Bound to Wellspring sanctuaries, which limits its range




The Ashes of Renewal chronicles the Phoenix’s intervention during the Great Spirit War, turning the tide by cleansing corrupted Wellspring sites.
Pilgrims journey to witness a rebirth. It is a sacred event in many cultures and it is the only window in which the creature can be killed.


Read next: The Sixty Wellsprings, for the Wellsprings these formed from; The Three Paths, for what can touch them; The Bestiary, for the rest of the register.

the-bestiary/the-wild/the-draconic-linea.title: The Draconic Lineage
the-bestiary/the-wild/the-draconic-linea.content:
Four entries · the sky-serpent path, and the two branches that left it
Tobin Sark stole a glyph-stone the size of a fist out of the lair of an earth wyrm nobody had troubled to name, sold it in the salt towns for a very good price, heard what was following it, bought it back for a much better one, and ran for twenty-six years. The wyrm came after him at about the pace of a glacier in a bad mood, a long ochre hill with a crest of stone spines going through the country in a straight line, and six towns on the salt road still have a street that runs crooked where it passed. Lords posted bills on it. Crews in their colors went out with banners and came home quieter with their hats in their hands. The towns stopped running, after a while, and took to selling buns along the route. It found him at last in a rented room above a bakery, an old man of eighty with the stone under his chamber pot, and it lifted off the roof at dawn, put in a head the size of a river barge with its long whiskers feeling over the rafters, took the stone out from under the pot with a delicacy that surprised the baker, and went home. Tobin lived six more years and always said he had never slept so well. The baker sent the bill for the roof to the wyrm, care of the Concord, and the Concord has it on file.
That is a wyrm being patient. The rest of this entry explains why you should prefer it to the alternatives.

All four descend from Omnis’ first sky-breath. Two of them no longer do so honestly.
The Hydra is a wyrm bloodline fractured by void-tainted Wellsprings. The Voidwyrm is draconic blood crossed with raw Crevice essence. Draconic cultures regard both as tragic: reminders of what happens when a draconic soul fractures beyond repair.
A word on the names. This page enters the wild and corrupted lines. The peoples of Drakyssia who carry the same words, the Hydra Dragons of its sanctums, the Wyrms of the Wyrmdeep and the bred Wyverns of the Iron Roosts, are civilized branches with their own account in Draconic Kind, which also holds the Salamanders, the first flameborn of Omnis. They share descent with what follows and should not be mistaken for it, least of all by a hunter.

Wyrm

Vyrrhos, Ancient Serpent of Sky and Stone, in Draconic. Serpenta Magna in Old Parunic.

Draconic Lineage · Grade SS, Realm Hazard · Chthonica or Cymorath by subspecies, rare Orrenthal lines out of Caelum · native to Draconis, in the highland roots of the floating isles
Leans on · the Shell, by Chthonica or Cymorath, both Wild. Body: the scale gaps, a precise blow, and a very long day. Spirit: past the hide to a Core that is old, sure and hard to surprise, so bring a Confessor and not a student. Fate: a wyrm is about the soundest thing in the world, and the one thread on it is a blood-oath it has sworn.
Among the oldest draconic forms and direct descendants of Omnis’ first sky-breath. Wingless, moving with serpentine grace across earth and sky through Wellspring resonance alone.

Many scholars hold that wyrms were the trial form before Omnis perfected winged dragons. Wyrms themselves reject this as myth. They claim to be purer, and closer to the source.

Long, limbless or short-limbed bodies armored in thick plate-like scales. Coloration reflects Wellspring alignment: ochre, bronze and stone-gray for earth wyrms; pale silver, sky-blue and cloud-white for air. Eyes glow faintly with glyph-light when channeling. Horn crests or jagged stone-like spines run the length of the back, and the head is crowned with elaborate whiskers that read atmospheric and Essence shift.
Territorial, solitary, and thinkers as much as hunters. They lair where Wellspring Aether pools along geomantic lines in the rock and feed on that Aether rather than on prey alone. Slow to anger, and once provoked they pursue relentlessly, sometimes for decades. They leave gold where it lies and collect objects with long resonance: ancient stones, glyph-bound artifacts, the bones of legendary beasts.


Abilities

Essence Glide · flight without wings; movement through stone as if through water
Geomantic Breath · earth wyrms release a pulverizing shockwave of stone and sand, air wyrms slicing wind or vacuum implosion
Wellspring Guard · their presence
stabilizes the local Aether. They are living anchors in high-Essence zones
Resonance Sense · detects ley-line and Wellspring disturbance across vast distance



Weaknesses
Extremely large bodies make confined spaces a disadvantage Extended separation from their preferred Wellspring type weakens them Vulnerable to precise high-penetration strikes at the jointed scale gaps


During the First Concord War the Earth Wyrm Kallessyr the Stone Maw collapsed an entire pass to halt an advancing army of abyssal constructs. The Air Wyrm Thyrrin Cloudrend survives in Outer World seafarer legend as the storm serpent that swallowed ships whole without ever touching the sea.

In Draconis they are honored as elders of the sky-serpent path: advisors to younger dragons and occasional arbiters in draconic disputes.
In the Material World they are unstoppable disasters, or mountain guardians, depending on the district. Some Innerworld mining clans make blood-oaths with wyrms to secure safe passage beneath their territories.

Wyvern

Vyreth, Storm Talon, in Draconic. Vryssal, Winged Fang, in Old Parunic.

Draconic Lineage, Winged Reptile · Grade S, Domain Threat · Cymorath and Orrenthal, some bloodlines Pyraeon · Caelum and Draconis, with isolated Outer World populations
Leans on · the Shell, by Cymorath and Orrenthal, both Wild, some lines Pyraeon. Body: it has no forelimbs, and a wing on the ground stays there. Spirit: a young one’s cunning is a pack’s, and it does not expect to be read. Fate: its ambush needs the storm it came in on.
Descendants of ancient draconic stock forged in the tempestuous storms of Caelum’s skies. Lacking forelimbs, they rely entirely on wings and hind legs. Their evolution is tied to the volatile Cymorath and Orrenthal sites of the high peaks, and they inhabit storm-battered peaks and tempestuous archipelagos.
Large reptilian body with a barbed tail. Scales from storm-gray to fiery red by lineage. Sharp crests and serrated horns; eyes glow with lightning intensity during a charge. Razor claws on the hind legs and a venomous bite.
Pack hunters when young, solitary apex predators as adults. Cunning, swift, ambush-reliant, and fiercely protective of nesting sites near Cymorath ground.
Storm Dive creates sonic booms and shockwaves. Venomous Bite injects a paralyzing neurotoxin. Electric Surge channels storm energy into bolts and static fields. Wing Gust knocks enemies prone and breaks formations.
Vulnerable when grounded or molting. Susceptible to cold and water magic that disrupts their storm resonance. And packs fracture under prolonged coordinated assault.
The Tempest Siege of Eldric Pass details wyvern packs harrying Concord supply lines until elite air hunters broke the assault. They feature heavily in Outer World smuggler folklore as guardians of hidden Wellspring caches, and some mountain clans worship them as elemental spirits while others hunt them for the scales, which are used in storm-forged weapons.
Hydra

Hyrathos, the Many-Mawed Doom, in Draconic. Serpentis Multicauda in Old Parunic.

Draconic Lineage, Aberrant Offshoot · Grade X, Cataclysmic Entity · Nihiloth over Pyraeon, Manganthra or Cymorath, by pre-corruption lineage · Crevice-scarred border zones
Leans on · the Shell, by Nihiloth over its old lineage, all Wild. Body: all the heads, inside the window, with fire behind the blade. Spirit: many heads and one Core, in the trunk, and every song about a hydra is wrong on this point. Fate: the regrowth depends on nothing stopping it, and a cautery set up in advance is cheaper than a thread.

A draconic bloodline corrupted by void-tainted Wellsprings during the First Crevice Incursion.
Originally a strain of earth-bound wyrms. Their essence became unstable and split their core consciousness into multiple semi-independent heads, each manifesting its own elemental or corrupted breath.
In some abyssal regions they are bred deliberately as living siege weapons.

Massive, scaled and heavily muscled, with three to nine heads depending on age and Essence exposure. Each head bears unique horn patterns and scale colors tied to its own attunement. Four massive legs, a powerful tail, armored plate from neck to tail-tip. Eyes burn with feral, individual intelligence in each head.
Highly aggressive, driven by constant hunger due to unstable Essence metabolism. Ambush predators using marsh, cave and river delta. Each head exhibits partial autonomy, which makes the attack pattern unpredictable.


Abilities

Multi-Element Breath · multiple breath attacks simultaneously, each of different elemental or corrupted nature
Regeneration · regrows heads and limbs within hours,
and a severed head may sprout two in its place unless cauterized or destroyed by Essence-based means
Coordinated Strike · independent heads make conventional defensive formation nearly useless
Abyssal Endurance · highly resistant to fatigue, poison, and most elemental attack



Weaknesses
Regeneration halts under cauterization by fire or high-intensity Essence disruption Severing all heads within a narrow window kills it, and the window is dangerously short Slower on open ground. Excels in water and dense terrain


The Siege of Lornhaven saw a six-headed storm hydra destroy three Concord watchtowers in a single night before massed trebuchets and a wing of griffon riders brought it down. In the Abyssal Depths, the Nine-Maw of Zar’thuun remains an active and growing threat.
Among draconic cultures these void-fractured hydras are tragic abominations, and the Hydra Dragons of Drakyssia, whose heads were joined by ritual, are quick to say so. To abyssal warlords they are symbols of unstoppable consumption.
Voidwyrm

Xal’tharix, the Rift Serpent, in Abyssal Tongue. Nihilcoil in Outer World dialects.

Draconic Lineage, Aberrant Voidspawn · Grade X, Cataclysmic Entity · Nihiloth and Vantabriel, with fractured Transference residues that flicker sporadically · Abythron, Niflheim, and Outer World crevice zones
Leans on · the Shell, by Nihiloth and Vantabriel, both Wild, with a flicker of Transference’s Fate where the old Layer is failing. Body: it does not read as mass where you think it is, so wait for what it has to do to strike. Spirit: what is left of the Core is mostly hunger, which makes it readable and no easier to hold. Fate: those fractured Transference residues are the only handle on it, and they do not belong to anything sane.
Born from the darkest rifts between realms, twisted offspring of corrupted draconic blood and raw Crevice essence. Bound to the fissures where void and reality blur. Their presence causes unnatural distortion and unsettling whispers in the minds of those nearby.
Sleek and sinuous, scales that seem to absorb light, appearing as shifting void-black with star-like flecks scattered across the body. Eyes glow eerie purple. Tendrils and barbs pulse with unstable Essence. When they move, reality ripples around them, bending as if space itself resists their form.
Highly predatory and elusive. They hunt from shadow and strike in unpredictable bursts. They target Essence-rich beings preferentially, feeding off spiritual energy as much as physical sustenance.
Void Ripple distorts space locally, fracturing enemy coordination. Essence Drain leaches Wellspring energy from foes to heal or amplify. Shadowstep teleports through the folds of the Crevice. Mind Shatter emits psychic waves causing hallucination, fear and temporary madness.
Vulnerable to concentrated Harmonic Essence attacks that restore balance. Their spatial distortions require recovery after use, creating brief openings. And they are bound to crevice zones: prolonged absence weakens them.

The Fracturing of Dorrosfenn was blamed on a pack tearing through the border crevices, causing widespread Essence contamination.
Outer World records detail hunters who tracked a solitary Voidwyrm for months before their minds fractured.
Some sects worship them as agents of inevitable entropy. Others seek to banish them forever.


Read next: The Sixty Wellsprings, for what fractured them; Monster Cores, for why anyone goes near one; The Bestiary, for the rest of the register.

the-bestiary/the-wild/index.title: The Wild
the-bestiary/the-wild/index.content:
Creatures that belong to the world: beasts of the land, beasts of spirit, and the dragon line.
At any autumn fair you can buy griffon feathers by the dozen, dragons’ teeth by the jar and a lock of unicorn mane from a man with very fast legs. One in a hundred of them is real, and that one got somebody killed. Here is what the other end of it looks like.


Natural Beasts Eight entries · creatures that were born rather than made, however large they got
Spirit Beasts Eleven entries · creatures formed from Wellspring resonance rather than born of flesh
The Draconic Lineage Four entries · the sky-serpent path, and the two branches that left it



Read next: The Bestiary, for how the register reads; The Sixty Wellsprings, for the Affinity each entry names; Monster Cores, for what the stone is worth.

the-magic-system/first-steps/index.title: First Steps
the-magic-system/first-steps/index.content:
At the Lammas fair in Harrow Cross a goose-plucker named Tib Oakshott climbed onto a cider barrel and bet a fairground brawler his whole year’s feathers that he could name every part of the man’s art out loud, blow by blow, while it was being thrown at him. He lost a tooth and most of one ear and won four sacks of silver, and the Guild has been writing to him ever since. I cannot promise you the silver. I can promise you the names, and the numbers your own soul will show you in a window (its report to you, in your own tongue, which nobody else can see).
The newcomer’s road. Read these five first, in this order, and everything after them will make sense. This shelf opens the one reading order on The Magic System page, and Start Here keeps the short routes.


Magic on One Page The whole system on one screen, for a guest with five minutes: Aether, the Crystal’s three layers, the three Paths and what each spends, Wellsprings, Stages, stats and windows, the ladders and gear.
How Magic Works The whole system in brief, for a newcomer: the soul and its windows, the three Paths and what each one spends (Charge, Essence or Thread), Wellsprings as lenses, Traits, skills and their ranks, classes and Mastery, Stages for sale, monster cores and dungeons, guild titles, gear, Fate and blessings.
The Measures at a Glance Every number a practitioner, a monster or a piece of gear is read by, what it decides, and one fighter read on all of them, window included.
One Exchange, Annotated A single exchange between two fighters, with every rule that decided it marked and each fighter’s windows shown as a worked example.
The Core Vocabulary The words. The first three pages explain each one as it comes; this is where they are kept, and it stays open beside everything after.


Five pages from the next shelves answer the questions a newcomer asks first, usually the morning after a first bout. Take them as the need comes.


The Three Paths What each road works, where it is held, what the lost share becomes and what it costs, and how to tell a hitter from a thrower by the way they tire.
Tier Grade, Bands & the Aether Shell Its section on the three routes, Charge, Essence and Thread, and why a soul still has one reserve and one number.
Soul Wounds and the Menders Why your armor did not help, what you have lost, and what it costs to have it closed.
The Tell and the Knot How to see a pull on a thread coming, how long you have, and what the world takes back from the puller afterward.
Releases and Domains by Path What a Release and a Domain do on each of the three roads.


Next shelf: The Foundations. Back to The Magic System.
