With the relevant Dexterity entries at 51 and up the practitioner can read a crossbow bolt loosed across a room and slip it, if they see the loose. At 176 and up they can stand in a volley of bolts and arrows without significant reactive disadvantage. Every missile carries a fixed threat Grade by its kind, sling stone, hunting arrow, war-bow shaft, crossbow bolt or ballista bolt, a worked missile taking its maker’s Grade instead, and the catcher’s speed meets it on the same scale. A bolt stays the cheap thing that can kill a high-Stage fighter in a room, which is why veterans sit with their backs to walls. At 276 and up movement generates significant environmental effects, heat buildup from air friction, pressure waves, surface disruption, without deliberate technique activation. At 401 and up the air itself becomes a weapon; characters whose Resilience stands below 401 sustain structural damage simply from proximity to such a practitioner moving at full speed. At 551 and up biological neural processes are insufficient and Essence-mediated sensory routing becomes the primary perceptual mechanism, and the practitioner’s passage through space at full speed is perceived as instantaneous by anyone below 401. Dodging a full-speed attack at 726 or more requires Reaction Speed of the same step at minimum to even register the attack as having occurred. Below 726 nobody can perceive, let alone react to, full speed at 951 and up. Movement at 1,201 and up generates relativistic effects that interact with the surrounding Aether field and can cause localized temporal distortion as a byproduct rather than an intention. Movement at 1,501 and up is not faster travel between two points; it is Essence-mediated spatial restructuring where distance is subject to Domain authority.
Zenith, Stage XIV: Immeasurable Speed classification applies at full expression. The practitioner does not move through space. In the limit case, they exist in all relevant positions simultaneously until they choose otherwise.
Part Seven — Individual Stat Gates
Every Sub-Stat carries a Path Alignment requirement. Certain subs cannot exceed a given figure without demonstrated Path commitment. Path commitment is not declared. It is recognized by the Crystal based on behavioral pattern, the consistent routing of Essence through a specific plane’s logic over time.
Where a gate below names a component of a Sub-Stat, the inscription and glyph-chain durability under Density, the gravitational component under Tolerance, and the rest, the gate caps only that component. Part Twelve’s Merge Ledger folded those components into the entries that carry them, but the gate still reads the part it names: a sheet without the named Path commitment runs that component capped at the gate’s figure, or without it, while the rest of the Sub-Stat runs at full. A healer without Body Path heals fully and cannot reinforce.
A character who has fought exclusively through Body Path mechanics from Initiate to Master has genuine Body Path alignment regardless of what they claim. A character who has occasionally used Spirit techniques while routing primarily through physical expression will find Spirit-aligned Sub-Stats quietly resisting advancement beyond 175 until the actual pattern of Soul Crystal use reflects commitment.
The gates below are written for one Path. A soul on one Path opens them at the Stage written. A soul on two Paths opens the gates of the Path behind a Stage late until that Path is mastered. A soul on three opens every gate two Stages late, and the highest steps (726 and up) stay shut. The highest Stage whose gates a Path has opened is its Path Stage on the card, and Mastered means it equals the soul’s Stage, read again at each Threshold. Studying a Path, which anyone may do, opens no gates at all. A gate asks for the road and never for a Mastery rung: Fate gates open from Stage II though Fate Mastery is not read before Glory, and a Fate Path fighter clears them on Range, presence, bonds and oaths without ever having pulled a thread.
Older registers list Attraction as a road of its own. They were looking at the shallow end of Fate, and an Attraction gate in an old table is a Fate gate at the same Stage and figure. Obsession Force satisfies a Fate gate the same way clean Attraction Force does, every corrupted practitioner in the four quarters included.
Vitality Gates
Fortitude requires Body Path at Stage III to exceed 175, and Stage IV to exceed 275, the higher gate covering the bone and connective-tissue density it absorbed. Absorption requires Body Path at Stage III to exceed 175. Constitution requires Body Path at Stage II to exceed 100. Hemostasis open. Regeneration open, though reinforcement of healed tissue requires Body Path at Stage V to exceed 275. Filtration open. Tolerance open, except that its Aether-dead component requires Fate Path at Stage VII to exceed 550 and its gravitational component requires Fate Path at Stage VI to exceed 400, both being more Domain-anchored than physical. Threshold requires Body Path at Stage IV to exceed 275.
Ardency Gates
Flux open to any Path, with scaling character determined by dominant Path expression. Alacrity requires Spirit Path at Stage III to exceed 175. Depth requires Fate Path at Stage IV to exceed 275, and Stage VI to exceed 400 where two Wellspring qualities are held in one working. Penetration requires Body Path at Stage III to exceed 175. Compression open to any Path, scaling exponentially with Temperance Stage rather than Path commitment; concealment of a working’s signature requires Fate Path at Stage VII to exceed 550. Cascade requires Fate Path at Stage IV to exceed 275 for spread, Spirit Path at Stage V to exceed 550 for range. Overchannel open, carrying inherent Overflow risk above 100 and Backlash risk above 175, with no Path providing structural protection; recovery of rebound as usable output requires Body Path at Stage V to exceed 275. Density requires Body Path at Stage IV to exceed 275, with inscription and glyph-chain durability requiring Spirit Path at Stage III to exceed 175.
The concealment gate, as it is read now. The line under Compression above is the old one, and the assay houses have since split it by road. Compression is the Body fighter’s mastery stat, the measure of how cleanly raw Aether is worked unrefined in the Shell, and working quietly is simply what a high Compression is: a Body Path hand hides the signature of a working through Compression itself, at whatever figure the stat has reached, and no Fate gate is asked of it. The Fate Path gate at Stage VII to exceed 550 stands for one thing only, hiding a pull or a claim, which is done on the Attraction Layer and by nobody who has not walked that road.
Gnosis Gates
Perception open. Acuity requires Spirit Path at Stage III to exceed 175. Forecast requires Fate Path at Stage V to exceed 550. Fluency requires Spirit Path at Stage II to exceed 100 and Stage III to exceed 175, with its Command Weight component requiring Fate Path at Stage III to exceed 175. Retention requires Spirit Path at Stage II to exceed 100, and Stage VI to exceed 400 for the number of complete workings held loaded. Analysis open, though diagnosis of external fields and living beings requires Spirit Path at Stage IV to exceed 275. Cognition open, though resistance to glamour and psychic misdirection requires Spirit Path at Stage IV to exceed 275. Vigilance open.
Dexterity Gates
Celerity requires Body Path at Stage II to exceed 100, and Stage IV to exceed 275 for standing acceleration. Reflex open. Finesse open to any Path, though redirecting incoming force by timed contact requires Body Path at Stage III to exceed 175. Economy requires Body Path at Stage III to exceed 175. Evasion open to any Path. Grapple requires Body Path at Stage III to exceed 175. Feint requires Spirit Path at Stage IV to exceed 275, with suppression of kinetic noise and Aura spill requiring Fate Path at Stage V to exceed 550. Sequence requires Spirit Path at Stage VI to exceed 400, and Body Path at Stage V to exceed 400 for simultaneous action across separate limbs.
Harmonics Gates
Attunement requires Fate Path at Stage II to exceed 100, with retention of previously encountered frequencies requiring Spirit Path at Stage III to exceed 175. Projection requires Fate Path at Stage III to exceed 175 for field weight and Stage VI to exceed 400 for reach. Breadth requires Fate Path at Stage IV to exceed 275, and Stage V to exceed 400 where several Wellsprings are layered inside one working. Stability open, though holding resonance in Wellspring-absent ground requires Fate Path at Stage VII to exceed 550. Empathy requires Fate Path at Stage III to exceed 175. Synergy requires Fate Path at Stage V to exceed 550 for ambient amplification and Stage VI to exceed 400 for allied amplification. Axis requires Fate Path at Stage IV to exceed 275. Suppression requires Spirit Path at Stage V to exceed 400.
Attunement, as it is read now. The Fate gate on Attunement above is no longer asked. Attunement is open to any Path at any Stage, since every soul that takes a lens has to attune to it and the lock is made at the Shell where Aether enters; the Spirit gate on retention stands as written. Every other Fate gate in these tables stands, Empathy and Breadth here and Radius, Sovereignty and Gravity under Dominion among them. They are read against Fate Path Stage, which climbs with the soul’s own Stage like the Stage of any Path. Fate Mastery climbs with Level like the others and stops at II without a grip, a Work of a bloodline or a blessing, and no gate asks for a rung.
Resilience Gates
Integrity open, though the conversion of prior fractures into reinforcement requires Body Path at Stage V to exceed 275. Ward requires Spirit Path at Stage III to exceed 175, with defense of the character’s own Domain requiring Fate Path at Stage VIII to exceed 725. Persistence requires Fate Path at Stage VII to exceed 550, and Stage VIII to exceed 725 against Oblivion-class pressure. Anchoring open, though resistance to memory erasure and false implantation requires Spirit Path at Stage III to exceed 175. Fortification requires Body Path at Stage IV to exceed 275; resistance to self-generated blowback is open. Hardening requires Body Path at Stage III to exceed 175; passive rejection of contamination is open. Oath requires Fate Path at Stage IV to exceed 275. Continuity requires Fate Path at Stage VI to exceed 400 against spatial displacement and Stage VII to exceed 550 against causal disruption.
Tempering Gates
Clarity requires Spirit Path at Stage III to exceed 175, with resistance to Overgrowth requiring Body Path at Stage IV to exceed 275. Overflow open, with inherent structural risk above 275. Maturity open, and is the primary Sub-Stat consulted by the Crystal when evaluating Threshold readiness; its transition-recognition component requires Spirit Path at Stage IV to exceed 275, its fracture-metabolism component Spirit Path at Stage V to exceed 400, and its bloodline component Fate Path at Stage VI to exceed 400. Coherence (how closely a soul’s chosen Path matches how it actually works) open, and functions as the structural prerequisite for Temperance Threshold eligibility. Tempering Yield requires Body Path at Stage III to exceed 175; ambient conversion and generation latency are open. Ceiling requires Fate Path at Stage VIII to exceed 725. Capacity requires Fate Path at Stage V to exceed 400. Longevity open.
Dominion Gates
Radius requires Fate Path at Stage V to exceed 400, Stage VI to exceed 400 for partial projection outward, and Stage VII to exceed 550 for boundary expansion speed. Sovereignty requires Fate Path at Stage VI to exceed 400, and Stage IX to exceed 950 where the imposed law encodes abstract conceptual truths. Sense requires Spirit Path at Stage III to exceed 175 for topology and higher-order phenomena, Spirit Path at Stage IV to exceed 275 for Archon-tier pressures, and Fate Path at Stage VIII to exceed 725 for passive detection of spatial tears. Gravity requires Fate Path at Stage V to exceed 400, for the law’s structural weight and for holding territory in hostile Realm environments. Pressure requires Fate Path at Stage VI to exceed 400. Command requires Fate Path at Stage VIII to exceed 725. Fate requires Fate Path at Stage VII to exceed 550. Throne requires Fate Path at Stage XIII minimum and cannot be advanced below 1,201. Its ceiling is Absolute, the only Sub-Stat in the system with no practical upper boundary on this side of Apotheosis, and it is excluded from the Dominion total for that reason.
Part Eight — Temperance Threshold Events
Thresholds are not achieved by accumulating enough experience. They are triggered by two factors: the soul’s Level must be able to hold the next Stage, a quantitative floor (the hold table is in Part One); and a Catalyst Condition must have been met, a specific quality of experience the Crystal requires before it will authorize the transition, or else the Catalyst must be supplied from outside.
A character can be quantitatively eligible for months of in-world time and never pass a Threshold because the Catalyst has not occurred. The road to the Catalyst differs: some meet it in crisis, some work toward it in seclusion, some are driven to it by tribulation, and most by a mixture of the three.
The fourth road is money. A Draft or a blessing can supply the Catalyst for any Stage, and it simply works, so Stages can be bought, and the wealthy are stronger because they are wealthy. The great houses hoard the top Drafts. The poor rise by dungeon luck, guild patronage and blessings, and a blessing may carry a person further than any of those, since it grants a power out of their natural reach, even in Level. A bought Stage opens the door and no more. The ceiling lifts, and nothing the events below would have taught comes with it. If Level is short of the Stage’s hold, the Crystal sits Overgrown, spilling power and reading low, until living fills it. Level, Mastery and every Release must still be lived, each Release with its own Catalyst, and sects teach what money cannot buy: Releases, Domains, techniques, skills and the rites for their Wellspring. Veterans will tell you they can feel a bought Stage inside two exchanges, and they say so at the top of their lungs, usually to the person who bought it.
Stage I counts as a Threshold worth 100 points. Every practitioner starts with it. The events below are the transitions as a soul lives them, and each grants the Stage number multiplied by 100 on the terms of Part Three, whichever way the Catalyst arrived.
I to II, Welling. First genuine contact with a Wellspring’s Aether under personal pressure, not observed, not instructed, but touched and survived.
II to III, Ascension. First technique developed independently from instruction, built from the character’s own understanding of their Essence rather than received doctrine.
III to IV, Flourishing. Formation of the first genuine Spirit Axis, a bond with another soul that carries mechanical weight in the Harmonics system.
IV to V, Splintering. Surviving contact with an entity or force more than two full steps above the character’s current ceiling. Not defeating it, surviving it. The Crystal fractures along emotional lines.
V to VI, Glory. The self burns bright and is noticed. Willingly accepting genuine soul-cost to preserve something the character values above their own structural integrity. The peak of the inner phase.
VI to VII, Refraction. Dual sight. The soul sees itself from outside. First Domain seed activation, however fragile or small: a one-time flicker of the person’s own Trait at the Threshold, which needs no Release. The Second Release, open from this Stage on the Body and Spirit roads, or Fate’s One, which opens here and counts as its Second, is what later lets a seed be called and held. Projected fields become coherent.
VII to VIII, Transcendence. The world is read as symbol. Resolving a core internal contradiction documented in the Soul Crystal’s fracture record, a wound carried as structural damage and consciously processed into architecture. From this Stage a true Domain can be grown by living and called aloud.
VIII to IX, Invocation. Calling on Wellsprings, Titans, or Archonic law as co-authors of expression. The practitioner’s Domain throws a first flicker of a Realm capable of holding other Domains, once, at the Threshold, on the same terms as the seed. The Body road’s Third Release opens at this Stage. The Realm itself is the far end of the climb and every road reaches it by its own door, late: Body through the Third, Spirit through its Second grown whole, Fate through the One. Each door opens no earlier than Realization: the Body’s asks another’s world carried, and not let fall; the Spirit’s, another’s whole meaning held inside your own, and both left true; Fate’s, a claim others stand on, kept for them (How Power Grows gives the three Realms).
IX to X, Realization. Truth as lived consequence. The world answers back. Pacts, artifacts and law imprint on terrain. The Domain becomes a reality the Continuum must accommodate.
X to XI, Dissonance. Deliberately entering contact with a force or truth capable of ending the character’s existence and remaining coherent long enough to choose how they meet it. Power and identity clash. The Crystal fractures or breaks through.
XI to XII, Emanation. Emerging from Dissonance with a Soul Crystal denser and cleaner than before entry. The fractures must have become features. The practitioner radiates outward. Traits become local law. Passive miracles leak.
XII to XIII, Principality. Achieving Domain coherence sufficient for the Continuum to formally register a law the character embodies. A local force of nature. First World Spirit threshold. Biomes carry doctrine.
XIII to XIV, Zenith. The character’s accumulated doctrine becomes recognizable to a Hollow Throne (the empty seat of a dead Archon). The Throne resonates with them. The transition is not a breakthrough. It is recognition, and a Throne must recognize a buyer too, so here money buys the attempt and not the seat. Full World Spirit. Reality acclimates to the character. Story becomes law.
XIV to XV, Revelation. Genuine exchange with an Archon or Titan at a level where the character is a participant rather than a witness or a casualty. The first step of the Apotheosis approach.
XV to XVI, Apex. Holding a Principle in the Soul Crystal without fracturing, even momentarily, even imperfectly. Apex is perpetual. It is the state of a soul pressing against what it has not yet become.
Part Nine — Cross-Stat Harmonic Bonuses
When specific Sub-Stats from different Primary Stats reach the same step on the hidden scale simultaneously, the Soul Crystal registers a Harmonic Convergence. These Resonant Pairs generate passive structural bonuses neither stat could produce in isolation.

Part Ten — Stagnation and Diminishing Returns
The System has two structural enemies: grinding and stagnation. Both are penalized in the architecture of the Crystal itself.
Grinding is countered by the Crystal Adaptation Rule. Any threat or stimulus type engaged more than five times without meaningful variation to the character’s technique or the threat’s composition is reclassified internally as Familiar. Familiar stimuli yield ten percent of their original XP value, permanently, for that character. The only way to restore value is to approach it with a genuinely novel technique or under genuinely novel conditions the Crystal registers as a different category of experience.
Stagnation is countered by Residual Strain accumulation. Every fifty levels’ worth of XP accrued past the top of the rank’s group (Part One: 100 below Expert, 200 below Master, 300 below Grandmaster, 400 below Archmaster, 500 below Paragon) without passing the required Temperance Threshold imposes a five percent penalty to all XP gains and a two percent increase to all Overchannel and Backlash risk values. This pressure builds continuously.
It dissolves entirely the moment the Threshold is passed. On dissolution the character receives a Strain Release Bonus equal to thirty percent of all XP accumulated during the stagnation period, delivered as a single Resonant Surge. The System is not punishing patience. It is representing the physical truth of a soul carrying the weight of what it has already earned but not yet integrated. That weight has texture. That texture eventually becomes pain. And then, when the character meets the Catalyst Condition or can afford someone who bottled it, it becomes power.
Read next: Part Eleven. The account in words is The Three Paths, for the gates, and The Sixteen Stages, for the Catalysts.

the-magic-system/fracture-of-worlds-—-th.content:
The Continuum does not distinguish between the fist and the meteor. It measures the pressure that arrives, and it measures what survives.
Two women took the Hwangsan Gate in one afternoon, and the Southern houses are still fighting about which of them did it. The Seo women, an aunt and her niece, hired out as a pair, Hye-rin with a sword and Bo-ra with her fists, in matching persimmon coats, the same figure against both their names on the Guild roll, and a strike that graded A on the wall-reckoners’ table. Bo-ra went first. She set her heel in a cart rut, her aura flared the orange of her coat from the shoulder down, and she punched the curtain wall.
Forty paces of masonry came down in a wave of yellow dust with the garrison still standing on it, and a Measurewright watching from the siege line got a mouthful of it. Hye-rin strolled through the dust, told her niece she had missed a bit, and drew one line through the iron portcullis and the oak doors behind it, so clean that the halves stood a moment longer and the gate captain was still shouting orders when the top half slid. The minstrels gave the day to the sword. The sutlers in the camp paid on the fist. Bo-ra’s arm had come back with the wall’s answer in it, the wrist and both bones of the forearm, a month in splints, because every push is pushed back and the Charge only pays part of that bill. And the Measurewright, spitting grit, worked the whole thing out in charcoal on a wagon board and announced that the two blows had carried the same energy within a rounding error, whereupon both women tried to hit him.
That wagon board is this page.
What Force of Hand Is
Force of Hand, which the older registers call Physical Force, is the umbrella measure of every destructive, resistive or manipulative output a character can bring to bear on matter, by bodily action, by reinforced technique, or by a working driven out through the Shell. Five facets: Strike Force, the EU a single attack delivers; Durability, the capacity to absorb, deflect or endure what comes in without structural failure; Lifting Strength, sustained force applied against weight or structural resistance; Range, the spatial envelope across which force stays whole; and Aura Pressure, the passive force a character’s presence exerts on their surroundings.
Every Grade on this page reads off EU delivered, which is the EU spent times the yield (η), the share of what is spent that reaches the world, as a distillation has its yield. The thresholds are the ones the trade has always used. The Measurewrights reckon them in joules, newtons and tons of TNT besides, at one EU to the megajoule, and their columns stand beside each table as the guild’s conversion: often right about how much, and never the reading. Older copies of this Part say yield for a blow’s whole energy; the word now belongs to η alone, and this Part says output or EU delivered where it means the blow.
Force of Hand is not separate from Aetheric power. It is its most immediate showing. Every soul works under what the Measurewrights still call the Aether-Physics Fusion Rule, and what the benches put more plainly: a working changes the worker, and the world gives way as far as that soul is truly changed, without overturning any of the habits the world settled in the Physical Epochs. Stone keeps its strength, a fist still has to meet the wall, and the wall still answers. When a practitioner punches through a castle wall, the wall breaks because the fist carried more than masonry was ever made to bear, and the Measurewright will say the kinetic energy concentrated in the fist exceeded the tensile and compressive strength of the masonry, which is right about how much. That the blow was driven by the Charge, raw Aether packed in the Shell, rather than by muscle alone changes nothing about what the stone does once it is struck. The Continuum measures what arrived. It does not ask where it came from.
A note on the word Essence in this Part. The older copies call the engine of every blow Essence. A Body Path fighter refines nothing: what the Shell holds and drives out is the Charge, shaped there by the lens, and its lost share burns in the Shell’s furnace as heat. Force that breaks matter leaves by the Shell whoever sends it, because the Shell is the only door into matter, so a soul on another road who wants a wall down pays for it through their own Shell at their own Body Mastery. Where a line below says Essence of a blow, read the reserve. Every figure stands as written.
What does differentiate is delivery mechanism. A punch delivers force through physical contact across a finite impact area. A Sage Art (a working fed by the Wellspring Aether pooled in the ground underfoot) technique delivers force through Aetheric projection across a volumetric zone. A Domain-grade expression delivers force through ground that has taken the practitioner’s own law in place of the world’s. The EU delivered may be identical. The tactical application is not.
The Dual-Law Requirement
Every expression of Force of Hand must satisfy two criteria at once.
True to the world’s habits. The blow must have a source, a line, a point of application and a measurable force. Weight, momentum, inertia and leverage go on applying to the striker and to the thing struck even when the drive is the Charge rather than muscle, because the world gives way to a changed soul without dropping its habits. A punch the guild reckons at three giganewtons still comes back up the arm that threw it, taken by reinforced bone density and Vitality-governed tendon architecture. A thrown boulder still flies the way thrown boulders fly.
Aetherically coherent. The Soul Crystal must structurally support the output. A character whose Ardency Sub-Stats have not reached the step required for a given output experiences Overchannel (forcing more output than the Crystal can safely sustain) events, Backlash, or outright technique collapse when attempting it. The body may be capable of the motion. The Crystal may not be capable of the cost.
The benchmarks below therefore represent the structurally sustainable ceiling. Characters can exceed them through Overchannel or crisis, and an Overchannel counts toward the boost cap, two steps on the hidden scale, like any other self-boost. The cost is Crystal Fracture risk, Residual Strain, and potential permanent Sub-Stat degradation.
Strike Force
Strike Force is the EU a single attack delivers. The Measurewrights reckon it two ways besides, in newtons for the peak contact force at the moment of impact and in joules for the whole of what arrived, and both of their readings matter, because steel and bone keep the world’s habits. A sword thrust concentrates little into an extremely small contact area, producing high local pressure and deep penetration. A body slam spreads an enormous blow across a broad contact zone, producing catastrophic structural damage without penetration. The Continuum records both.

The Somatic-Aetheric Split. In a blow grading Hollow or F, Strike Force is predominantly somatic. By E the ratio is roughly sixty percent Aetheric, forty percent somatic. From C up the somatic contribution is structurally negligible: the body is the delivery frame, the reserve is the engine. By the time a fighter’s blows grade S the body has been so thoroughly rebuilt by saturation that the distinction between muscle and Aether ceases to be anatomically meaningful. The practitioner’s bicep does not contract harder. Their Shell packs the Charge into the limb’s contact zone so densely that the guild reckons the force in giganewtons, because the furnace in the Shell is doing the work and the muscle is only the frame it works through.
The Focused-Yield Principle, as the trade still names it from the days when yield meant a blow’s whole energy. Strike Force measures what is delivered, the EU spent times the yield, never the whole of the reserve expended. A practitioner whose strike grades A, with Ardency Compression a step higher, can focus their output into a contact area smaller than a coin, producing local pressures orders of magnitude above the rest of their reckoning. This is why a sword cut grading A bisects materials a blunt strike of the same Grade only cracks. The EU delivered is identical. The pressure distribution, which is a matter of steel and stone, is not.
Lifting Strength
Lifting Strength is a continuous output metric: how much mass can be held motionless against gravity, or how much structural resistance overcome through sustained application rather than impact.
Governed primarily by Vitality, particularly Fortitude and Constitution, with secondary contribution from Tempering Yield, which determines how much of what the body spends it can hold as sustained effort. Body Path practitioners receive a multiplicative bonus at all Grades because they work through the Shell, the one door into matter, where weight is the world’s own habit and nothing has to be translated.

Durability
Durability is the total EU of destruction a character can absorb, deflect, distribute or endure without structural failure of body, Aether Shell or Soul Crystal. It is a composite of four layered systems.
Layer One: Physical Hardness. Raw material resistance of the body: bone density, muscle fiber tensile strength, skin cohesion, organ integrity as enhanced by Essence saturation. The last line of defense. Governed by Vitality, particularly Constitution, Fortitude and Regeneration.
Layer Two: Aether Shell Shielding. The active Essence field surrounding every woken practitioner, buffering between incoming force and the body, worn as a coat of the practitioner’s own aura. Density governed by Resilience, particularly Integrity, Hardening and Fortification. Held evenly, the Shell absorbs and redistributes what comes in across its entire surface before residual force reaches the body, and a Shell rated at five million EU (5 TJ by the guild’s conversion) absorbs that much across all concurrent attacks before anything reaches flesh. It can be thickened where a blow is expected, at the price of leaving the rest thin, and reading where it went is half of reading the fighter. It is held, not owned: asleep, drugged or taken by surprise, a practitioner keeps the passive hardness of Layer One and loses this layer entirely. “Essence field” is the older wording. As it is read now, the coat that buffers a body is a Shell coat, raw Aether held in the Shell at its wearer’s Body Mastery, whichever road the wearer leads on. A Spirit coat is Essence and wards the soul, not the hide, and a Fate coat is the claim worn as presence, which carries Pressure and settles a room and absorbs nothing in this column.
Layer Three: Technique-Active Defenses. Wards, barriers, Domain-grade exclusion fields actively maintained or deployed. Not included in baseline benchmarks because they are technique-dependent and Essence-costly. A Fixatio-anchored (anchored on Fixatio, the Wellspring of binding) barrier with a fifty-million-EU ceiling (50 TJ as the guild reckons it) adds that on top of baseline, but costs Essence to maintain and can be shattered independently.
Layer Four: Domain Resistance. From Stage VIII, practitioners with active Domains gain a layer derived from Domain coherence. Within their own Domain, local law favors their survival. Not quantified in EU, because it absorbs nothing. It is ground holding another law than the attacker’s, and it degrades the coherence of incoming attacks, cutting their yield before they reach the Shell.
An aside on Layer Two, because it is the most famous art in the world and the most quarreled over. Every culture learned it, and none will use another’s word. On a Guild roll it is Aether Shell Shielding, and in most mouths it is the coat. The Moto say matoi, the wearing, and hold that a coat anyone can see is badly worn. A Kharven rider calls it the hide, and thinks the Moto are showing off by hiding it. The Mahuo say gabot, armor, and teach it before they let a student touch a sword. The lineage halls say hùtǐ, guarding the body, and keep a commentary older than any living elder on how thick is vulgar. The figures below apply to all of them, which no school has ever been pleased to hear.

Why a bolt still kills. The ceilings above read the whole stack with the coat up and the blow seen. Take the coat away, by sleep, by drugging or by surprise, and Layer One stands alone, and Layer One is no line on this table. It turns a fist, a thrown stone and a glancing edge, more surely the higher the Vitality, and it buys time from a bad hit, since saturated flesh closes and saturated bone holds. But a point concentrates what it carries. A steel-bowed arbalest’s bolt of about 440 J, stopped inside five centimeters, pushes about 8,800 newtons, and on a square millimeter of point that is near nine gigapascals, well past any bone. So a bolt nobody saw coming goes into a high-Stage fighter as it goes into anyone, and the throat, the eye and the roof of the mouth have the least to say about it. A bolt seen is a contest on the scale: every missile carries a fixed threat Grade by its kind (sling stone, hunting arrow, war-bow shaft, crossbow bolt, ballista bolt), a worked missile taking its maker’s Grade instead, and the target’s speed meets it on the same scale before the coat does.
The Asymmetry Principle. Durability ceilings are deliberately lower than Strike Force ceilings at every Grade. This is architecture, not oversight. A world where every character could perfectly tank every attack from their own rank would produce stagnation, endless exchanges with no consequence. The offset ensures a committed, well-placed strike from a peer produces meaningful damage if it lands cleanly. Technique, positioning, timing and tactical intelligence exist precisely because raw Durability is not sufficient to ignore raw Strike Force from a peer.
The ratio varies. At F through D on the guard’s Grade, Durability sits at roughly seventy to eighty percent of Strike Force output, so a clean peer hit penetrates but is not catastrophic. At A through S, the ratio narrows to sixty to seventy percent, reflecting denser Shell architecture but also more lethal focused technique. At SSS and above it widens again to roughly fifty percent, because the gap in EU between a clean hit and survival is so vast that the Crystal’s priority shifts from absorption to avoidance, Domain manipulation and reality-grade countermeasures.
Range and Force Coherence
Every expression of force has a coherence envelope: the maximum distance from the body at which it keeps its full destructive output. Beyond that, it degrades, at a rate set by delivery mechanism.
Contact Force has zero range beyond the point of contact. A punch delivers its full output at the knuckle surface and nowhere else. The shock of it can carry through air and stone and extend the effective damage radius, as any blow’s shock does, but it thins as it spreads, losing roughly seventy-five percent of its force per doubling of distance from impact, which the Measurewrights write as the inverse square law.
Projected Force degrades according to the practitioner’s Ardency Cascade Sub-Stat and the Wellspring used. A tightly gathered Coagulatio-based (shaped through Coagulatio, a Wellspring that gathers and densifies) force lance keeps ninety percent of its output across its full effective range. A broadly dispersed Pyreveil-based (shaped through Pyreveil, a fire Wellspring) detonation wave keeps only forty percent of its peak at the edge of its blast radius. Range benchmarks below are the maximum distance at which at least fifty percent of peak Strike Force is delivered. Projected force that breaks matter is a Shell working at any distance and reads Body Mastery, whether it comes from a high Body fighter, a Sage on Wild ground or anyone else. A Spirit worker’s thrown force keeps the same range column and lands on souls only.

Range Without Force
Not every reach is a strike. A practitioner also has to name a thing before he can set a limit on it, hold a limit at a distance from his own body, and keep a volume of ground under his own law rather than somebody else’s. Those three reaches are not the range above and are not governed by it. A working that expresses no force is not bound by the coherence envelope of one that does. They have their own ladder, and it keys to Grade the same way.
Addressing range is the greatest distance at which a practitioner can name a thing precisely enough to impose a boundary on it. Anchor reach is the greatest distance between the boundary he sets and the practitioner, or the ink, blood, voice or hand that anchors him. Authority radius is the radius inside which his own law is the operating law: a Domain’s edge, a ward’s jurisdiction, a Seal’s writ.
The three are one field read at three thresholds, and the thresholds differ by a hundredfold each. A boundary must stand a hundredfold above the background to be imposed at all. The background itself is where a law stops being the operating one. A name is narrow and coherent, so it is read a hundredfold beneath the background, the way a faint tone is picked out of a loud room by somebody who knows which note to listen for. A presence carries less the further it has to carry, and by the Measurewrights’ rule, that a field’s strength falls with the square of distance, each hundredfold step in threshold is a tenfold step in radius. Anchor reach, authority radius and addressing range stand as one to ten to a hundred. The middle rung is the Passive Pressure Field of the table above, which is precisely the distance at which a practitioner’s field still stands above ordinary ground.

Ground changes all three together.
