The square root is the Measurewrights’ rule of thumb, and it has not yet been wrong about how much. That is about ten times further on Aether-thin ground, an eighteenth at Active Concentration (ground near a Wellspring site, thick with Aether), a thousandth at a Veil-Thin Nexus, and about a five-millionth inside a Wellspring Core (a site where a Wellspring’s Aether pools, in common speech, mostly found at the heart of a dungeon). Residue still ringing counts in the same sum, which is why fought-over ground is short ground for hours afterwards. The ground a practitioner would choose for output is the worst ground he could choose for reach, and every veteran knows one of those two facts.
One measure runs the other way, for one road. A Fate Path fighter lives on Range and on the radius of his Domain, and rich Aetheric ground crowds both by the root rule above exactly as it crowds anyone’s. Thread Weight, the measure of how much has been decided on a piece of ground, extends them: on heavy ground his Range and his Domain’s radius run longer than the Density alone allows. The two are read together, and a battlefield that is both rich and heavy takes with one hand and gives with the other (The Three Grounds).
A working target is ten times easier to name. Anything standing a hundredfold above the background is addressed at ten times the range, and anything performing a working at all stands there. Suppression is the same fact run backwards, and it is paid for continuously rather than once.
Below Refraction the anchor is not the body. A working below Stage VII needs voice, hand, ink or blood, and anchor reach is measured from the anchor rather than from the man. This is the whole commercial case for a drawn circle and an inscribed wall. They move the origin to where the boundary is needed, and a good one is worth more than a step on the scale.
The crossover. Projected force range and addressing range cross at the B row. Below it a practitioner can name what he cannot hit. From there upward he can hit what he cannot name, and every doctrine of scouting, spotting and signal lives in that gap.
The failure modes, which are not gentle. Past addressing range a name does not single its target out. Two men are one address, and the working lands on both of them or on the wrong one. Past anchor reach the boundary sets and slips. Past authority radius nothing of the practitioner’s is operating at all, and a Seal sworn on authority he does not hold there closes anyway, with the difference deducted from the speaker.
Aura Pressure as Force of Hand
Aura Pressure is the passive force a character’s metaphysical presence exerts on everything in proximity. Not a technique. Not activated or deactivated. The ambient consequence of a Soul Crystal existing at a given density within a given Temperance Stage. It increases monotonically with Temperance advancement and Dominion, and cannot be reduced below baseline without active suppression.
Between the woken it is read on the Stage gap, with Dominion deciding inside the gap. It shows in the room first: smoke, frost, lamp flames, animals. Then it reaches the bodies. One Stage up bends attention. Two brings sweat and nausea, and the lower party’s Aether Shell begins consuming Essence to resist the ambient load. Three or more drops people, and the Shell of anyone still standing takes passive structural damage simply by being present. A gap of a whole Crystal look changes the weather.
The unwoken take it by the fighter’s rank, because they have no Stage to set against it.
From an Initiate or an Apprentice, Aura Pressure is perceptual rather than physical. The unwoken feel dread, instinctive deference, mild sensory distortion. Psychological and spiritual, no measurable physical force.
From a Journeyman, weight enters the room and measurable physical effects begin. Air density increases within the field. Loose objects vibrate. Surfaces crack under sustained exposure. The ground compresses. Effects scale with the gap between the practitioner’s Pressure and whatever is absorbing it.
From an Expert an unwoken body stops being able to stand under it. An Expert standing within ten meters of a porter exerts a pressure the guild reckons as several hundred kilograms of distributed weight. The porter’s knees bend and their breathing compresses. From a Master whose Pressure has climbed high, the effects on the ground become geological. Stone cracks. Water compresses. Air becomes optically dense. Footsteps leave indentations not from body mass but because Aura pressure exceeds the soil’s load-bearing capacity.
Governed primarily by Dominion, through its Pressure Sub-Stat, with Harmonics Projection setting how far the field carries. Body Path Aura is physically heavier but spatially compact. Fate Path Aura is lighter per square meter but extends across far larger volumes. Spirit Path Aura is perceptually intense, targeting cognition and emotional stability rather than physical structure, and exerts less raw gravitational-analogue force.
An aura’s look comes in layers: the Wellspring a soul has tempered on longest sets the base color, clouded and smoky at the low Stages and clearing as the Stage rises, any others add texture and sound, and a class or a big Trait adds a shape. Pressure is felt in the room first, in the lamps and the knees and the dog going under the table, and then the window reports it to the owner of the knees: [Pressure: heavy, above your Stage]. A stronger Gnosis Perception reads a weaker Resilience Ward. Everything else is an estimate said aloud, and people can hide their pressure or fake it, which has won more tavern brawls than it has lost and ended a few fakers very quickly.
Everyone knows this art and nobody agrees on its manners. A Guild examiner writes Pressure. A southern tavern says a man is leaning on the room, and a Kharven soldier calls it the low sky and thinks hiding it is a kind of lie. The Moto say atsu and consider leaking it indoors an insult to the host. Mahuo halls say nureum, the pressing-down, and the lineage halls wēiyā, which they will tell you is a matter of virtue and which feels the same on the knees. The Marrowkin enter it in the Tally as a load, and argue about who should pay for it.
Path Modifiers to Force of Hand
Path modifiers apply after Temperance and the step are calculated. The magnitude widens with distance from the Physical Plane. Because they come after, they never move a blow’s Grade and never count on the boost cap, and the same goes for a Wellspring’s lens.
Body Path. Direct multiplicative bonus to Strike Force, Durability and Lifting Strength, from +5% at early Temperance Stages to +20% at Stage XII and above. The shortest road and the most immediately reliable. Body Path practitioners at equivalent figures and Stage consistently out-hit, out-tank and out-lift their counterparts by margins that widen with advancement. Trade-off: reduced bonuses to Range and Aura Pressure, so low down they must close distance to leverage the advantage. Those figures are the force table only. High on the Path a Body fighter commands matter by recognition and by law, and their reach grows as far as there is matter to read, still needing existing substance and paying in recoil through body and Crystal.
Spirit Path. Moderate bonus to Strike Force delivered through projection, +5% to +25%, but no bonus and in some configurations a slight penalty to physically delivered Strike Force. They hit hardest at range, and projected force retains coherence across greater distances. That projected force is force on souls and on souls only: it knocks a soul out of true, lays dread on a mind or wounds a Core, it is spent in Essence through the Core, and it marks no matter. The bonus is read in the table’s own units as a measure of what arrives, and it is answered by Resilience Integrity and Anchoring, never by the Durability column. A Spirit worker who wants a stone moved moves it through their own Shell, as a Body working at their own Body Mastery and with no bonus from this line. Durability bonus negligible, replaced by enhanced precision in defensive technique deployment. They survive through correct response rather than raw absorption.
Fate Path. Smallest direct bonus to Strike Force and Durability, largest bonus to Range, Aura Pressure, and the interaction between Force of Hand and Domain authority. Less raw contact damage than a Body Path counterpart at the same figures, but projected force degrades less over distance, Aura extends across larger volumes, and their Domain amplifies all Force of Hand expressions within its territory by a factor scaling with Dominion Radius and Gravity: +10% while the lower of the two stands below 401, +25% from 401, +40% from 551, inside the line only. Once those two stand at 401 and up the compound Domain-amplified advantage can exceed Body Path’s raw output advantage, but only within their own Domain. Outside it, Body Path remains king. These Range, Aura and Domain figures are what a Fate fighter lives on from day to day. A real pull of Fate adds nothing to any figure here: a guard slips or a strap gives, and an ordinary cut at an ordinary EU rating lands where it had no business landing, at a ruinous cost in reserve and often not at all, and landed or failed the pull leaves a knot the world collects from the puller afterward. The far end of the Path, where the true Fate Arts live, works on what has to be so before a blow can land, and its gates are permissions rather than output, as The Three Paths sets out.
Two and three Paths. These bonuses are written for a soul on one Path with a clean seat. A fighter on two Paths takes three-quarters of each Path’s bonus, and a fighter on three takes half of each, for life: time closes the gap in the gates and never this one. So the Body Path’s +20% at Stage XII is +15% on two Paths and +10% on three, and the rest of the table follows the same way, the Fate Domain’s amplification included.
What this table does not say. This Part measures force, so the Body Path looks its best on it, the way a mason looks his best in a quarry. A Spirit working that goes past the Shell is never read against the Durability column, since armor and Durability do not cover the soul, and a Fate fighter who has spoiled the footing never has to stand in front of the Strike column at all. None of the three is the better road, and The Three Paths sets out how each beats each.
Force Interaction Rules
The Differential. The single most decisive factor. A strike a full Grade above the guard it meets wins a direct exchange without meaningful contest; the gap in what arrives is too large for technique or positioning to overcome. Two Grades above is one-sided destruction. Three Grades above means the one receiving it is not participating in a fight. They are experiencing an event.
Within-Step Resolution. Inside the same step, exchanges resolve by technique quality, tactical intelligence, positioning and Sub-Stat architecture. A character at 275 delivers about forty-four times the EU of a character at 176, and by the guild’s reckoning roughly five times the peak force in newtons. Both strikes grade B. The differential is real and significant but not automatically decisive, because technique architecture, Wellspring affinity and Path bonuses can compress or invert the raw stat advantage.
The Sharp-Blunt Asymmetry. A swordsman whose cut grades F, delivering 0.2 MN through an edge contacting roughly one square millimeter produces local pressure of 200 GPa, exceeding the compressive strength of virtually all natural and most Essence-reinforced materials at that Grade. The same 0.2 MN through a fist contacting one hundred square centimeters produces 20 MPa, enough to crack stone but not bisect steel. The Continuum tracks EU delivered for the Grade comparison, and local pressure, which is a matter of edges and stone and the world’s old habits, for what the blow does to the material. The ratio is ten thousand to one at any force, which is why a swordsman’s B-Grade cut parts what a brawler’s B-Grade blow can only dent, and why the brawler shatters structures the swordsman can only slice.
Wellspring-Typed Damage. Force delivered through Wellspring-attuned technique carries that Wellspring’s signature. Pyreveil adds its burning. Fractura adds the breaking point a thing already carries. Vohrin, a Titan’s power worked at Wellspring level and no member of the Sixty, adds thermal extraction. These are not counted in the Strike Force benchmark because they are Wellspring-dependent, but they represent real additional damage that can push what arrives above the raw EU rating. The Path decides how it arrives and what it arrives on: the same Pyreveil burns flesh on contact from a Body Path fist, and thrown from a Spirit Path hand it burns what a soul means and holds and leaves the coat unscorched, so it adds nothing to an EU rating. A Spirit Wellspring adds no such damage on any Path, because it gives no fire and changes what the person can bear instead, and that shows on the Durability side of a fight if it shows here at all. A Fractura-enhanced strike targeting a pre-identified fault line in the target’s Aether Shell can produce Shell failure at outputs thirty to fifty percent below the Shell’s rated ceiling, because Fractura’s idea is that everything has a place where it will go, and a blow laid on a place already found asks the Shell to do only what it was always going to do. The Measurewrights say the strike applies force at the exact frequency and vector that maximizes structural degradation, and their thirty to fifty percent is right.
Force of Hand at the Boundaries
The Apotheosis Threshold. The Zenith rows in these tables sit beside the Grade ladder, not on it: each is keyed to a Stage, where every row above it is keyed to a stat range. At Zenith, Stage XIV, Force of Hand is no longer assessed by conventional metrics. Revelation, Stage XV, keeps its EX+ Grade label, but its force goes unmeasured in the same way; the EX+ row marks where the lettered ladder ends, not a figure a Revelation practitioner is measured by. A punch from a Zenith-level practitioner does not deliver a quantifiable number of EU. It delivers an event the local law must accommodate. Every rating on this page assumes a blow is a finite quantity meeting matter on the world’s old habits; a Zenith soul has become so wholly its own law that the ground under the blow takes that law as its own for as long as the blow lasts. The force is real. The meeting is no longer standard.
The Hollow Floor. Hollow-Grade output is indistinguishable from ordinary mortal capacity, below sixty joules by the guild’s reckoning, a normal human fist at under twelve and a half meters per second. The System tracks a soul here all the same: a sealed Crystal keeps a Level and a few trade skills on a small window, and only Essence, Mastery and a class wait on the Crystal opening.
Overchannel Spikes. The benchmarks above are sustainable output. Overchannel can temporarily spike Strike Force and Lifting Strength by two to five times the sustainable ceiling, depending on the Ardency Overchannel Sub-Stat and the character’s tolerance for Crystal Fracture risk. From the top of a Grade that lands inside the next Grade up on every row, so it reads as one step and spends one of the two the cap allows. Every Overchannel event deposits structural damage that must be healed through rest, alchemical treatment or Temperance advancement. A character who regularly Overchannels accumulates fracture density that eventually becomes permanent. Some fractures become architectural features. Most become liabilities.
Every EU was earned. The Measurewrights will tell you every newton has a name.
Read next: Part Twelve. For what a force figure leaves out, see The Three Paths and Counterplay.

the-magic-system/fracture-of-worlds-—-th.filePath: The Magic System/Fracture of Worlds — The Living System/IV. The Eight Primaries and the Sixty-Four Sub-Stats (Part Twelve).md
the-magic-system/fracture-of-worlds-—-th.title: IV. The Eight Primaries and the Sixty-Four Sub-Stats (Part Twelve)
the-magic-system/fracture-of-worlds-—-th.content:
The Crystal does not measure what you believe you are. It measures where the pressure went.
On Loaf Day at Ostler’s Cross the Guild read two wrestlers as the same Vitality to the point, and the fight hall, which believes the Guild when it suits the gate, billed it as the fairest match of the year. Bran Anvilchops had put his points into Fortitude and Absorption (two of the Sub-Stats, the finer measures beneath a Primary), and you could break a bench across him, as several had. Moll Thrice-Hanged had put the same total into Hemostasis, Regeneration and Filtration, and had earned her name in three different towns, the last of which still owes her a rope. In a ring of trampled clover under green and yellow bunting, with every carter on the East Road hollering, Bran caught her arm in the first minute and snapped it across his knee, and half the crowd paid out on the spot. Moll looked at the bone standing out of her sleeve, the color of a peeled almond, pushed it back with her other hand, and spat a mouthful of the wolfsbane somebody had put in her ale. By the time the ale-wives had made change the arm was knitting. Two hours in she had been broken nine times and he had not been broken at all, and he was slipping in his own blood from a split over the eye that would not close, gone pale under the sunburn, while she grinned at him with two teeth that had not been there when the bell rang. He dropped at sundown, undefeated in every particular but the last. Their registers still read the same. Ostler’s Cross now pays a clerk to copy Sub-Stats onto the door of the fight hall, and the Guild charges double for the reading.
A Primary Stat is the combined total of its eight Sub-Stats. Points are spent on Sub-Stats only; a Primary is never purchased and holds no value of its own. The Temperance ceiling and the Path gates bind the Sub-Stat. The Primary is the arithmetic afterward, and an assessor reads it off the mean of its eight, or of Dominion’s seven counted entries, set against the hidden scale. No letter is ever put on a person: a normal look at the owner’s window shows the eight Primaries with their totals; a Sub-Stat appears when it is used or when it moves, and the full set remains to study. Life spends most of the points, by what the person does, and a few are the owner’s to place at each Stage.
Primary Stats are the broad categories. Sub-Stats are the grain. Two characters at identical Primary totals can be radically different practitioners because their distributions tell different stories. One may have Vitality concentrated in Fortitude and Absorption, producing a frame that refuses to break but bleeds badly and heals slowly. Another may have the same total across Hemostasis, Regeneration and Filtration, producing a body that breaks readily, reconstructs itself and shrugs off poison. The Primary says they are equally durable. The Sub-Stats say they are durable in completely different ways.

Consolidated from one hundred and twenty to sixty-four. The original architecture carried fifteen Sub-Stats per Primary, of which a substantial share were restatements of each other under different names. Dominion Density and Dominion Stability both measured how hard the law is to break. Vitality Contuition and Vitality Filtration both measured poison resistance. Gnosis Sapience and Gnosis Fluency both measured Parunic (Parun, the written language of magical law) construction. Those duplicates are merged, and the merged entry carries the senior name.
Where an old name appears on an existing sheet, read it as the entry that absorbed it. Each entry below names, in italics, the old Sub-Stats it absorbed.

I. Vitality
The measured structural integrity of the physical vessel.
Vitality governs how the body resists, absorbs and persists against destructive forces across both physical and metaphysical vectors. It does not measure fighting capacity. It measures the capacity to remain a coherent physical organism while fighting capacity is expressed through other stats. A character with high Vitality and nothing else does not win fights. They survive them.

Fortitude Resistance to blunt trauma, impact force and structural breakdown, across bone, joint and connective tissue. Whether a strike folds the frame, snaps the limb or dislocates the shoulder. The first number consulted when a clean hit lands and the question is whether the recipient is still standing. Absorbs Ossification and Tenacity.
Absorption Capacity to dissipate incoming force laterally rather than receive the full transfer inward. Where Fortitude decides whether the body breaks, Absorption decides whether the body moves.
Constitution The raw pool of physical health, and resistance to attrition: exhaustion, oxygen deprivation, starvation, environmental grind over a long engagement. Why one fighter is still swinging ten minutes in while the other is breathing through their mouth. Absorbs Endurance.
Hemostasis Speed and stability of wound closure and blood retention. The difference between a wound that bleeds out in minutes and one that seals in seconds. Operates during combat, not after.
Regeneration Rate of physical restoration outside active combat, and the degree to which healed wounds come back structurally reinforced rather than weakened. Not a healing working; the body’s own reconstruction speed, and whether it learns. Absorbs Scarring.
Filtration Resistance to toxins, venoms, alchemical corrosives, corrupted Essence bleed and Aetheric contamination. The body’s capacity to recognize hostile intrusion at the cellular and Essence-lattice level and reject it before systemic degradation. Absorbs Contuition.
Tolerance Resistance to environmental vectors the body must simply refuse: extreme temperature, gravity distortion, spatial compression, Essence-induced weight amplification, and the absence of Aether in Wellspring-dead zones. A character with high Tolerance does not feel comfortable in a furnace. Their tissues refuse to denature at the rate physics demands. Absorbs Gravitas and Nullity.
Threshold The degree to which the body filters or suppresses pain signals during combat. High Threshold does not eliminate pain. It prevents pain from translating into functional degradation.

II. Ardency
The measured output potential of a soul through the layer in use: raw Aether through the Shell on the Body Path, Essence through the Core on the Spirit Path, Thread through the Attraction Layer on the Fate Path.
Ardency governs not what the body can do unaided, but what a soul can put out through the layer it leans on. The three roads spend three different things. A Body fighter’s Ardency is raw Aether (mana, in the plainer books), drawn in, packed unrefined in the Shell as the Charge, shaped there by the Wellspring’s lens and driven out through the Shell. A Spirit worker’s is Essence (spiritual energy), Aether refined and stamped in the Crystal and spent through the Core. A Fate puller’s is Thread, pulled down through the Attraction Layer and paid for out of the soul’s own share. The letter is read the same way on all three, and a soul that walks two roads uses the one Ardency for both. A practitioner with low Ardency and high Vitality is a wall. High Ardency and low Vitality is a trebuchet. What separates a weapon from a practitioner is having both.
Flux — Raw destructive and constructive output of active expressions. The damage ceiling. How much force the working carries when it arrives. Flux is the same number on every Path, but it does not do the same work on every job: the Mastery of the Path in use sets the yield (η, the share of a spend that arrives as effect, as a distillation has its yield). A Spirit master with a great Flux who turns it on matter works it through his Body Mastery, which on a road he has only studied reads two rungs behind and never past II, and gets that poor rung for his trouble, and most of that great Flux burns off in the Shell’s furnace as heat on his own skin. The Measurewrights’ way of putting it is that Flux says how much you can throw and Mastery says how much of it lands.
Alacrity — Casting speed, cooldown compression and reflexive casting window availability. The tempo axis.
Depth — How deeply the caster synchronizes with an active Wellspring, how unmistakably the working carries that Wellspring’s qualitative character, and whether two Wellspring qualities can be held in one expression without resonance conflict. Whether you are borrowing from a Wellspring or speaking its language. Absorbs Saturation and Duality.
Penetration — Capacity to pierce defensive fields, Soul Crystal wards, metaphysical barriers and worked armor, where a strike is read on this figure against the piece’s own Grade and proof; plain armor fights by its kind. High Flux with low Penetration hits like a padded wall.
Compression — On the Body Path, the mastery stat: how cleanly a fighter works Aether unrefined in the Shell. The Charge is raw, and raw Aether handled badly is loud and hot, the furnace roaring for little, so a Body fighter’s Compression is the difference between a blow thrown with steam pouring off the shoulders and the same blow thrown with a dry back. On the Spirit Path it keeps its old sense, the degree to which Essence is packed before release. Either way it buys the same three things: the same destruction for less cost and with less signature, since a compressed working is quieter in the Aether and harder to identify before it lands. Absorbs Radiance.
Cascade — Reach. How wide a working spreads when spread is intended, and how far it travels before attenuation degrades its structure. High Cascade covers battlefields. Low Cascade covers opponents. Absorbs Spectral.
Overchannel — Maximum temporary output achievable by pulling beyond sustainable thresholds, the minimum investment required for a significant destructive release, and how much of a failed or interrupted working’s rebound comes back as usable output rather than damage. How far past safe before the engine eats itself. Absorbs Detonation and Conversion.
Density — Structural weight and coherence of anything a working leaves standing: inscriptions, active glyph-chains, summoned constructs, bound spirits. Whether your ward outlasts the siege and whether your summon is a suggestion or a participant. Absorbs Inscription.
III. Gnosis
The architecture of the mind across both cognitive and metaphysical axes.
Gnosis is the stat of understanding. Not wisdom, which is a product of experience and Temperance, but the raw cognitive and perceptual machinery that lets a soul process what it encounters at the speed and resolution required to act. Whether they act correctly on what they see is a question for other stats.
Perception — Sensory acuity and Aetheric threat detection. Awareness of displacement, Veil distortion, concealed entities and incoming force vectors before they resolve, and accurate modeling of the surrounding geometry including distorted architecture and Domain interiors. Absorbs Cartography.
An aside, since this entry and Empathy and Sense are between them the famous art of sensing, known in every tavern and named differently in each. A Guild examiner splits it across the three. A Kharven soldier asks whether you can smell a man’s stack, by which he means how much the man is carrying. The Moto speak of kehai, the sign of someone there, and think it rude to read a guest before the tea. The Mahuo say nunchi, and the lineage halls shénshí, spirit-sense, with diagrams. Each school will prove to you that its way is the true one, and each has lost someone to a Feint. The one hard law under the quarrel is this: a stronger Gnosis Perception reads a weaker Resilience Ward. Everything else is an estimate said aloud, and people can hide it or fake it.

Acuity Tactical cognition and real-time processing of multi-vector combat environments. Positioning, sequence recognition, adaptive strategy, and the speed at which an unfamiliar pattern is internalized mid-fight. Absorbs Adaptation.
Forecast Combat sequence forecasting from kinetic, spatial and Aetheric pattern recognition. Tells you what is about to happen. Whether you can do anything about it is a Dexterity problem.
Fluency Precision and vocabulary depth in the Parunic inscription language, structural logic of glyph-chain construction, and sensitivity to Command Weight and spoken oath-structures as force rather than sound. The difference between a working that does what you meant and one that does what you said. Absorbs Sapience and Resonance.
Retention Clarity and accessibility of the Crystalline Memory structure under pressure, and the number of complete working structures held loaded in active cognitive memory without external inscription. Absorbs Memorium.
Analysis Reading Essence signatures, Crystal fractures, Wellspring composition and corruption grade from limited observational data, on contact or at proximity, and reading matter the same way: the load a beam is carrying, the grain of a blade, the flaw in a casting, what an ore or an alloy is made of. A Body fighter’s Analysis is how they know where a wall will go before they hit it, and a healed soul wound shows on it as a pale place in the Core. The diagnostic eye. Absorbs Diagnosis.
Cognition Capacity to engage law-level phenomena, Archonic expressions and higher-dimensional constructs without perceptual fragmentation, and resistance to glamours, false spatial constructs and psychic misdirection. Whether a Principle-level truth enlightens you or shatters you. Absorbs Warding.
Vigilance Passive detection of approaching Temperance ceilings, Essence overspend proximity and the warnings that precede Dissonance (the eleventh Stage, where power and identity clash) events. The stat that reads your own architecture rather than the room.

IV. Dexterity
The body’s capacity to occupy, vacate and redirect across spatial geometry with precision and efficiency.
Not how strong the body is; how correctly it uses the space it occupies. A high-Dexterity fighter does not hit harder. They hit where the opening is, arrive before the defense closes and leave before the counter launches.

Celerity Raw movement speed across physical and Aetheric displacement, and maximum acceleration over short distances from standing or braced. Travel and the first step’s lethality. Absorbs Burst.
Reflex Speed of involuntary response to sensory or Aetheric threat data. What moves the body before the mind has finished deciding.
Finesse Precision and accuracy of technique, with the empty hand and with an implement. Edge control, draw speed, footwork integration, and altering the path of incoming force through timed contact rather than absorption. What separates a person holding a sword from a swordsman. Absorbs Dexterity Acuity and Deflection.
Economy Maximum positional advantage from minimum motion, balance and orientation during non-grounded states, and the rate at which stance and positional integrity are restored after a miss or a hit. How long the vulnerability window lasts. Absorbs Equilibrium and Recovery.
Evasion Passive tendency to occupy positions that conflict with incoming attack vectors, separate from conscious reaction. The body drifts toward safety the way water finds the lowest point.
Grapple Close-range physical control, joint manipulation, leverage and transition speed. Dexterity at zero distance, where the arena is the opponent’s body.
Feint Depth and believability of deceptive movement, and suppression of kinetic noise, Aura spill and sound output. How many layers of false commitment before a genuine technique releases, and whether the approach was heard at all. Absorbs Silence.
Sequence Number of distinct technical actions executable within a single engagement window without mechanical degradation, including separate simultaneous actions with different limbs. How many clean strikes fit inside one breath. Absorbs Independence.

V. Harmonics
The degree to which a soul’s frequency coheres with the ambient metaphysical substrate and other living resonances.
Not charisma in the human sense, but the raw degree to which a soul’s frequency is legible to, compatible with and influential upon the frequencies around it. A character with high Harmonics does not necessarily speak well. They resonate well. The Continuum hears them more clearly than it hears others.

Attunement Affinity and synchronization strength with bound Wellsprings, retention of previously encountered frequencies for re-attunement without re-contact, and the clarity with which a working reflects the soul that authored it. Reduces the cost of drawing Aether in, increases maximum invocation depth. The difference between borrowing power and being trusted with it. Absorbs Memory and Fidelity.
Projection Weight, suppressive reach and range of the passive resonance field. How far the soul’s voice carries when it is not trying to speak. Your Aura arrives in the room before you do. Absorbs Harmonics Density.
Breadth Total number of Wellsprings maintainable in active harmonization simultaneously, and the capacity to hold several of them inside a single working as layered effect profiles. The difference between a note and a symphony. Absorbs Chord.
Stability Consistency of resonance output under environmental pressure, emotional volatility, hostile interference or Wellspring-absent ground, and the speed of re-establishing it after a break. Prevents Harmonic Drift. How long you are deaf to the Wellsprings after someone drowns out your note. Absorbs Recovery and Voidance.
Empathy Passive sensitivity to emotional and Essence states within Aura range. You feel the room change before anyone has spoken.
Synergy The degree to which ambient Wellspring activity feeds the character’s Harmonic state and the Harmonic field synchronizes with and amplifies allied resonances. You fight stronger on rich ground and allies hit harder standing near you. Absorbs Confluence.
Axis Structural integrity of established Spirit Axes; how much Essence flows across bonded relational connections. Bonds carrying metaphysical weight, not just emotional weight.
Suppression Consciously compressing or masking the resonance field to reduce detectability and conceal Temperance tier. The muffle on the soul’s bell, and a skill that tires the user for as long as it is held.

VI. Resilience
The structural coherence of the Soul Crystal against forces that target existence itself.
Where Vitality protects the body, Resilience protects the soul. Low on the scale the distinction barely matters, because most threats are physical. High on it it is the only thing that matters, because the threats that kill Masters are conceptual intrusions, reality-overwriting effects, Domain inversions and forces that target the right of a thing to continue existing.

Integrity The Crystal’s resistance to fracture, Dissonance collapse and catastrophic resonance failure under overspending or hostile pressure, and the degree to which prior fractures have been processed into structural reinforcement. The foundation every other Sub-Stat rests on. Wounds that become walls. Absorbs Scarring.
Ward Defense against law-breaking, reality-overwriting and Domain-erasure forces, including techniques aimed at collapsing, inverting or redirecting the character’s own Domain. What stands between a character and an effect that says they do not exist. Absorbs Severance.
Persistence Resistance to forced cessation, obliteration and conceptual erasure, and to Nospheric intrusion, Oblivion-class pressure and the corrosive qualities of inverted or annihilation-aspected Wellsprings. The soul’s refusal to stop being when something with sufficient authority tells it to. Absorbs Resilience Nullity.
Anchoring Resistance to dissolution, corruption, possession and the Mirage Identity threshold, and to memory erasure, false implantation and Anamnesis-hostile intrusion. Whether identity holds its shape and its continuity under pressure. Absorbs Coherence.
Fortification Compressing incoming hostile Essence and redirecting it through internal structure rather than absorbing it as damage, and resistance to self-generated blowback from Overchannel rebound and interrupted high-tier workings. Converting a wound, or a mistake, into something the Crystal can metabolize. Absorbs Insulation.
Hardening Resistance to hostile resonance imposition and forced re-attunement, and passive rejection of Erebus-class contamination, possession vectors and gradual metaphysical degradation. The Crystal’s refusal to vibrate at someone else’s frequency. Absorbs Immunity.
Oath Structural durability of active vows, contracts and Fate-anchor oaths under attempts to sever, invert or weaponize them.
Continuity Resistance to spatial displacement, forced dimensional transit and Domain-class intrusion, and to sequence disruption, localized timeline alteration and temporal dislocation targeting causal continuity. Absorbs Dimensional.

VII. Tempering
The potential axis. The measure of how far a soul can go and how cleanly it gets there.
Every other Primary measures what a character is right now. Tempering measures the structural quality of the vessel that will carry them to what they are next. High Tempering does not mean more power. It means a cleaner, deeper, more structurally sound container for whatever power is accumulated. The Primary is named for the act: to temper is to melt the Soul Crystal, which is the soul itself, down and rebuild each layer, refining Essence and making it stronger while the body gains Traits. These eight entries say how well the vessel takes that.

Clarity Structural cleanliness and internal density of the Crystal’s architecture. Governs output noise, precision degradation at high output, Essence waste, and resistance to Essence pressing outward into flesh and bone faster than Temperance can shape it. Low Clarity produces Overgrowth. Absorbs Tempering Compression and Resistance.
Overflow Maximum sustainable output before Backlash, Dissonance or Essence-burn triggers. The red line. Everything past it costs structural integrity.
Maturity Integration of prior stage trauma, resolution of internal contradictions, the speed at which fractures and failed transitions are metabolized into architecture rather than persistent damage, the rate at which transition conditions are recognized, and the efficiency with which bloodline traits and ancestral Geasa activate cleanly rather than ambush. The primary Sub-Stat consulted when evaluating Threshold readiness. Absorbs Acceleration, Processing and Inheritance.
Coherence Alignment between chosen Path and lived metaphysical behavior. Dissonance between stated Path and actual expression degrades Tempering efficiency. The structural prerequisite for Threshold eligibility. The Crystal’s internal honesty assay.
Tempering Yield Raw volume of Essence produced per Temperance Stage relative to universal baseline, the efficiency of converting ambient Wellspring activity into usable internal Essence, and the gap between generation and availability. On a Body-led soul read Charge for Essence throughout: the same figure says how fast the Shell packs raw Aether. Reload speed for the soul. Absorbs Conversion and Latency.
Ceiling Theoretical maximum Stage achievable given bloodline, Crystal architecture and Wellspring compatibility. Structural potential rather than current attainment.
Capacity Maximum number of Wellspring harmonizations the Crystal can hold without resonance conflict. The Crystal’s bandwidth for metaphysical languages.
Longevity Resistance to accelerated metaphysical aging and erosion from high-tier operation, dimensional pressure and extended exposure to absolute-scale forces. How long the soul remains structurally viable at the ceiling it has reached.

VIII. Dominion
The degree of structural command a soul exercises over local metaphysical law.
Low on the scale, Dominion is mild ambient influence, the instinctive way a strong presence bends conversations and adjusts posture. High on it, it is literal reality modification: the character’s inner law becoming local law, overriding the world’s ambient habits within their territory. Every Archon was, before they were an Archon, a soul whose Dominion reached the point where the Continuum stopped treating their will as a request and began treating it as legislation.
Radius — Active reach of the Domain when formed, the speed at which its boundary extends during active formation, and the capacity to push a partial expression outward as an influence field short of full formation. How far your word carries, how fast it gets there, and what it can do before it has committed. Absorbs Expansion and Dominion Projection.
Sovereignty — Control over local geometry, distance behavior and trajectory interference, and the maximum complexity of law imposable through the Domain. Whether the rules inside your territory are simple physical rules or encoded conceptual truths. Absorbs Reach.
Sense — Perceiving and interacting with higher-order phenomena: dimensional seams, conceptual laws, Archon-tier pressures, Veil fold proximity, Realm boundaries, and the passive detection of tears and unstable junctions in spatial fabric. Where the seams are and where reality is thin. Absorbs Dominion Acuity and Rift. Renamed from Acuity to end the collision with Gnosis Acuity.
Gravity — The structural weight of the Domain’s law and its resistance to collapse, hostile inversion or dissolution, in calm ground and in a hurricane. Your law is heavy. It does not move when someone pushes it, and it does not dissolve because the Realm is hostile. Absorbs Dominion Density and Dominion Anchoring. Renamed from Stability to end the collision with Harmonics Stability.
Pressure — Oppressive environmental weight generated by concentrated will. Passive suppression of weaker Aetheric expressions, resolving within Dominion range. The weight of your presence when you stop being polite about it.
Command — The degree to which spoken intent carries metaphysical authority, causing ambient Aether to reorganize, oaths to register with the Continuum, and subordinate spiritual entities to respond. The voice of sovereignty made audible.
Fate — Integration with the Plane of Fate, the control of Attraction Force and Obsession Force and of the workings of reality itself. Governs reach and stability of the Attraction Layer, how far a soul can bend probability, covenant-binding capacity, and the mechanical weight of sworn oaths and of the blessings a soul can give. How loudly the Continuum hears you when you make a promise, and how far it lets you rewrite what was going to happen. It is what pushes on the rare occasion a Fate fighter moves what a blow or a march depends on, and the target’s Persistence and Continuity are what push back.
Throne — Latent compatibility between accumulated doctrine and the Hollow Thrones of defunct Archons. Not a measure of power. A measure of destiny. Throne carries no Temperance ceiling and is excluded from the Dominion total and the Dominion mean, since its floor sits above every ceiling in the Stage table and including it would distort the Primary beyond use. Dominion’s mean is the total divided by seven. It is carried as its own line on the character sheet.

Read next: Parts Thirteen to Fifteen. For which road opens which Sub-Stat, see The Three Paths and the gate table.

the-magic-system/fracture-of-worlds-—-th.title: IX. The Essence Ledger (Part Twenty-Three)
the-magic-system/fracture-of-worlds-—-th.content:
The fire at Gull Strand took nine seconds, and a clerk had it on her slate before it started. Wu Jinbao of the Vermilion Lamp Hall, Stage III, twenty-two years old, in a gold sash and with teeth like a lord’s plate, stood up on a beached fishing smack at the Strand brackets and announced to the whole beach that he would hold his full output for one whole minute and let any comer try him while he did it. The heralds cried it, the odds went up on a board, and Marget Pinch, who kept tallies for the Strand’s net-menders and had never thrown a punch, asked the Measurewright (an assayer of souls and workings) in the judges’ box for two figures off Wu’s assay sheet, forty-two thousand and four thousand two hundred. She did a short sum and put her sister’s dowry on nine seconds.
He opened on the noon bell.
His aura went up scarlet and gold, a column of it, the prettiest thing anyone on that strand had ever seen, and three parts in five of what he spent came off him as raw heat. Every stick of timber within a hundred and twenty-seven meters took light together: booths, bunting, the judges’ box, the bookies’ board with the odds still chalked on it. People on the sea wall three hundred meters off were slapping at their own faces. Seventeen died of it, and for the rest of their lives some hundreds carried marks across the nose and cheeks that the Strand still calls Wu’s freckles. At nine seconds by the water clock the column stuttered and his color went thin as weak tea, and a net-mender called Big Ned, who had been standing in the shallows with an oar, waded up the burning beach and knocked him off the boat. The Hall paid for the fair, and Wu paid the Hall for thirty years. Marget Pinch bought four boats, and when anyone asked how she had known she told them she could divide.
Her sum is the first line of this Part. A reserve divided by a rate is the time to empty, nine tenths of that is the time to Starvation (the floor at a tenth of the reserve, where the Traits begin to flicker), and the heat is the Shell’s furnace burning everything the yield (η, the share of a spend that arrives as effect, as a distillation has its yield) lets go of, when the spend goes out through the Shell as Wu’s did. Every one of those figures can be had from a sheet, and any one of them can be used by whoever is standing across from the person it describes. Wu’s own window, for what it was worth, had shown him a bar and a percentage the whole nine seconds, [Reserve: 10%] at the last, because a window leaves EU, AU/s and yield to the assay sheet. Marget Pinch had the better numbers.

Four quantities run through every practitioner in the Continuum (the whole fabric of reality): a reserve in EU, a compression in EU/g, an output rate in AU/s, a yield η. The Grade ladder reads destruction in EU delivered, and the Measurewrights keep a second set of books in joules. This Part is the join. The guild reckons one Essence Unit at one megajoule, and that conversion is theirs, never the reading. What follows is what that buys on the ladder, what a reserve costs to spend, how long it lasts at full output, how fast it comes back, and what can be done about all of it from the other side of a fight.

The four quantities, and the fifth
EU (Essence Units) is the raw reserve: the total volume of usable power the Crystal (the Soul Crystal, which is the soul itself) holds at any moment. It is set by Level and capped by Temperance Stage (one of sixteen rungs of the soul’s refinement), and governed primarily by Tempering Yield. Maximum EU is the structural ceiling the Crystal refills to.
What an EU counts. The unit was named when the books held that every soul spent Essence. It now counts either of two things, at the same rate. On the Body Path it counts Charge: raw Aether packed in the Shell, never refined, shaped there by the lens and driven out through the Shell. On the Spirit Path it counts Essence: Aether refined in the Crystal and stamped with identity, the soul’s own substance, spent through the Core. A soul’s one figure is held mostly as the one or the other by its lead Path, a soul on both roads carries the split on its card (Charge 70% · Essence 30%), and the two never trade back. So a Spirit worker’s reserve is a quantity of the person, and for her this Part is the book kept on somebody spending themselves. A Body fighter’s reserve is a quantity of the world, held, and for him it is the book kept on what the handling costs a body. A Fate worker’s pull is priced in EU through Fate Mastery, though the Thread itself is never held. The arithmetic does not care which, and none of it has changed. A Measurewright will tell you the U ought to stand for something else now, and will go on writing EU. Tier Grade, Bands and the Aether Shell sets out the three routes.
Operating below ten percent EU produces Essence Starvation: reduced stat expression, Shell (the soul’s outer layer, which passes power out into the world) degradation, Trait (a belief hardened into a personal law of the soul) flickering.
Flux Density (EU/g) is the compression ratio, how much power is packed per unit of Crystal mass. Higher means greater output from the same reserve, and it is the same number on every Path. It is governed by Tempering Clarity and Ardency Compression, and it is what separates a practitioner who burns through their reserve in three techniques from one who fights for an hour on the same pool.
AU/s (Aether Units per second) is the output rate, how much of the reserve is spent into active expression per second at full output. It is governed by Ardency Flux, Ardency Alacrity and Tempering Yield, and it follows the formula AU/s = Flux Density × η.
Yield (η) is the share of a spend that arrives as intended effect; the Measurewrights’ older word for it is efficiency. At η 0.50 through the Shell, half of every expenditure burns in the Shell’s furnace as heat, with noise and structural bleed; the same share lost through the Core is paid in the Core as a hollowing and warms nothing, and through the Attraction Layer it stands as a knot. At η 0.90, ninety percent converts to clean output. It is the single most important variable in sustained combat, because for the same delivered effect it determines how long the reserve lasts. It is governed by the Mastery of the Path in use (Body, Spirit or Fate, one rung each, read from Level under the Stage’s ceiling), Tempering Clarity and Ardency Compression.
The fifth quantity is the one Part Eleven already measures, and it is the one that lets the other four be priced at all. Strike Force is the EU a single attack delivers, which the Measurewrights record besides in newtons for peak contact force and in joules for the whole of it. The Continuum keeps its books in what arrives; the guild keeps theirs in joules. The Ledger is not a new currency; it is the exchange rate between the two sets of books.
The direction of the conversion. EU is potential and AU is actual: what the Crystal holds against what leaves it. One AU is one EU leaving the reserve, across the Shell for a Body spend and through the Core for a Spirit one. The two are never the same number in practice, because one is the store, one is the flow, and the yield says how much of it crosses the boundary between them.

The Aristotelian reading, in-world. The Collegium tradition that descends from the old faculty of Causes reads the Ledger as the doctrine of potency and act: EU is what a Crystal is able to become, AU is what it has become, the yield is the fraction of the becoming that arrives. Their term for Essence Starvation is the exhausted potency, and their objection to the whole Aether-Flow apparatus is that it measures the act and infers the potency, which they hold is backwards. They are a school, not a mechanic. The numbers below are what happens; the Causes faculty is one of several arguments about what the numbers mean, carried the way the Four Theories are carried.

Reserve bands by Stage and by rank
The law of reserves
A reserve is set by Level and capped by Stage. Level sets it along a log-linear law; the strain lines of Part One, past which Level climbs only at the price of Residual Strain, mark where a Stage’s reserve stops being ordinary.
The law runs from waking. A sealed Crystal holds no Essence, so a commoner’s Level sits on the window and buys no reserve at all, and the day the Crystal opens the law takes up at whatever Level the life has reached. A bought Stage lifts the cap and leaves the reserve where Level put it: an heir who drinks through to Stage VII at Level 20 holds about 4,750 EU, his Crystal Overgrown, an eighth of a Stage III brawler’s 37,400 at Level 90, with the ceiling and the color and nothing underneath.
The law runs through three fixed reference points: a Stage VIII Master at Level 250 with 4,200,000 EU, a Stage XII Grandmaster at Level 378 with 180,000,000 EU, and a Stage XII Grandmaster at Level 430 with 850,000,000 EU. Between the first two the slope is 0.012750 decades per Level; between the second two it is 0.012964. The two segments agree to 1.7 percent, and across the whole span:
log₁₀ EU = 3.4202 + 0.012812 × Level. A reserve multiplies by ten every 78.1 Levels, and by about 19 across each hundred Levels.
A Stage X Realization practitioner at Level 355, fifty-five Levels into Residual Strain, holds 90,000,000 EU, within four percent of the 93,000,000 this law gives at that Level.

The Pythagorean reading, in-world. The Measurewrights’ (the assayers who measure souls and workings) old Harmonic faculty never accepted the Level axis and reads the same regularity as a ratio: each hundred Levels, which the faculty still calls a Band, multiplies the reserve by a fixed interval, so the five Bands are five octaves of one string and the Crystal is a monochord being stopped shorter. They tune their assay forks to intervals rather than to numbers and they are, in practice, no worse at it. A school, not a mechanic. The fork reads what the arithmetic above says it reads, and the Harmonic faculty’s error is in what they think it proves.

Part One sets the lines where Residual Strain begins: a soul at Stages I to IV whose Level passes 100 with no Catalyst to Stage V, at V to VII past 200, at VIII to X past 300, at XI and XII past 400, at XIII and XIV past 500. What AU/s is not
AU/s is a ceiling on the rate, not a duty cycle. No practitioner runs at their AU/s continuously, and sustained work runs at a fraction of it. The small practitioner’s broadcast suppression costs 390 EU, is a full-broadcast sympathetic suppression across twenty-five feet, and lasts eight seconds: 390 ÷ 8 = 48.75 AU/s, about a fifth of the ceiling. The ceiling is what the practitioner can do for a heartbeat; the fifth is what they do for eight seconds. Read a practitioner’s AU/s as the number that caps a burst, and read a working’s EU ÷ duration as the number that runs a scene.
Costs are a share of the reserve
A working is priced as a share of the reserve it spends from, and the shares are large enough that a real fight reaches the ten-percent floor. The small practitioner’s workings run 4.5 to 12.6 percent of the reserve apiece. The middle practitioner’s branches run 3.0 to 9.7 percent, and the apex strike 8.0. The large practitioner’s constructs run 5 to 15 percent. A real pull of Fate is priced the same way, through its Fate Mastery, and it is the worst of them: low down one lean on the odds can take a large share of the reserve and still fail, and landed or failed it leaves a knot on top of the share, a debt no reserve pays and the world collects later. A practitioner who commits to a fight spends in whole percents per exchange, and ten to twenty committed exchanges bring anyone to Starvation. The absolute size of the reserve decides how large each working is; the share decides how long the practitioner lasts, and the share is what a scene tracks.
The cost can be permanent. A working may forfeit a permanent portion of the practitioner’s own maximum reserve each time it is performed. Performed seven times, it takes seven portions that do not grow back, and the maximum reserve was higher before the first.
Flux Density and yield
The equation, read per working gram
AU/s = Flux Density × η. The equation governs: a practitioner’s output rate is their Flux Density multiplied by their yield.
AU/s is Essence per second and Flux Density is Essence per gram, so the equation is read per working gram per second: the gram of Crystal engaged at the working aperture in each second of output. The gram goes unwritten because it is always one. It is not the whole Crystal. A Crystal of nine kilograms of Crystal and slag that reads as one structure, at a Flux Density of 670 million EU/g and η 0.61, outputs 408,700,000 AU/s, passed through one gram of it at a time.
Where the heat goes, and why it cannot go through the body
This section and the next are the Shell’s, and so they are the Body Path’s bill and the bill of anyone else who sends a working into matter. The missing fraction of every expenditure through the Shell burns off as heat, noise and structural bleed, because the Shell is the athanor, the furnace that never goes cold, and what it does not drive into the work it burns. The Measurewrights’ account says the same in their own terms, and their list is right about how much. Their first law says the missing fraction cannot vanish; the second says it cannot come back as work; the Gouy–Stodola relation (Ẇlost = T₀ · Ṡgen) says it reappears as low-grade heat at the place the loss happened. Light and sound are ways out of that place, not alternatives to it, and each becomes heat where it is absorbed.
It cannot burn inside the body and be carried out. The Measurewrights prove it by Fourier’s law, q = −k∇T. The small practitioner’s 28.4 MW of furnace heat through 1.8 m² of skin is 15.8 MW/m²; across 3 mm of skin at k ≈ 0.4 W·m⁻¹·K⁻¹ that would need
ΔT = qL/k = 1.58 × 10⁷ × 0.003 / 0.4 = 1.2 × 10⁵ K.
across three millimeters, and that is the small practitioner. At the middle practitioner’s 39.0 MW it is 1.63 × 10⁵ K; at the large practitioner’s 204 GW it is 8.5 × 10⁸ K. Skin chars at about 200 °C.
So the furnace is not in the chest. The Soul Crystal is an aperture, the Shell is the furnace, and its heat burns at or outside the body’s surface. The body does not carry the heat of its own workings; the Shell does, and the Shell sheds it into the room. A practitioner at a yield above one is marked by exactly this: no furnace heat, aura warmth or harmonic noise leaks outward from them, which says that from everyone below one it does. Their aura still shows in its own color, and their strength can still be felt; it simply sheds nothing.
Only the Shell’s loss is heat. A spend through the Core loses its share in the Core, as a hollowing: a color gone flat, a cold, a slipped word, and at the end a name. A pull through the Attraction Layer leaves its lost share standing on the Layer as a knot. Neither warms the room by a degree, and the blood and the shaking that come with them are the report of the payment and carry none of it. The guild’s megajoules are the same megajoules, and the stratal book takes the whole debit. So the table below prices a hitter. A Spirit worker at full output lights no timber at any radius, and a cool, quiet aura may be a master of the Shell or may be a thrower spending herself, which is a different thing to be afraid of.

By the guild’s figures the large practitioner at full output burns at six and a half times the Sun’s surface temperature, as hot as a blue O-type star, and an ignition radius of 1.14 kilometers reaches their own army and the ground they stand on; they can be seen working from the next valley.
At the drain a working actually runs at, the tell is smaller and still there. The broadcast suppression at 48.75 AU/s and η 0.89 sheds 5.36 MW: a surface near 2,700 K, pain on bare skin to 14.6 m, timber catching at 5.8 m.
This is the tell, and it is also the cost. A practitioner at full output is a lamp, a furnace and a hazard to everyone within a stated radius, and the radius is on this table. A low-yield practitioner throws more heat and glare for the same work. A high-yield one sheds almost none: their aura still burns in its own color and brightens as they push, but it gives off no heat, which is why a cool, quiet aura is remarked on, and why one working in silence and in the cold should frighten an onlooker more, not less. The ladder of who is brighter than whom depends on (1 − η) × output and on nothing else. The tell does not end when the working does: scorched ground, a burned ring and a room still warm are the aftermath, and the aftermath is read like the working was.
Yield above one
Above 1.0 the Continuum recognizes the expression as law and supplements it with ambient flow; the environment becomes a co-author. A yield above one is real. The soul has become so wholly the law it works that the world joins the work, and what the room adds was never the worker’s to pay. The Measurewrights, who say it breaks none of their laws because the practitioner is not a closed system, compare it to a heat pump, a device they can reckon on a slate and nobody has ever built, delivering three to five times its input by moving energy it did not make.
The surplus is pulled from the Aether stratum, the room, not from the Crystal. Of every 1.05 delivered at η 1.05, 0.05 is pulled in. At 9,870 AU/s and η 1.05 that is 4.76% of the 10.36 GW delivered, 494 MW taken from the stratum around the practitioner, every second of full output, while their own Crystal pays only the 9,870 EU/s it would pay at η 1.00. Their reserve drains at the same rate as anyone’s with the same AU/s; what the high yield buys is delivered effect and a working that sheds nothing.
The room pays, and the room shows it. The stratum a practitioner above one pulls on is measurably depleted, and it stays thinner after the working ends; passive recovery in that ground runs slower (see “How fast it comes back, and on what it depends”), for them and for anyone else who stands in it. That is the tell and it is also the counter: starve the reservoir. Aether-dead ground, a depleted site or a Silence Realm (a place where the Aether is dead) leaves nothing to supplement the expression with, and the yield falls back below one by definition.
Essence Starvation and recovery
The threshold
Operating below ten percent EU produces Essence Starvation: reduced stat expression, Shell degradation, Trait flickering.
Ten percent of the reserve at each rank’s strain line, with the guild’s joules:



























































Rankreserve at the strain line, EUStarvation floor, EUin joulesInitiate50,3005,0305.03 GJApprentice50,3005,0305.03 GJJourneyman50,3005,0305.03 GJAdept50,3005,0305.03 GJExpert961,00096,10096.1 GJMaster1.84 × 10⁷1.84 × 10⁶1.84 TJGrandmaster3.51 × 10⁸3.51 × 10⁷35.1 TJArchmaster6.70 × 10⁹6.70 × 10⁸670 TJ
The floor is ten percent of the practitioner’s own maximum, not of the rank’s line; the table gives the floor of a soul standing at the line, and a Strained soul’s floor stands higher. The Grandmaster figure, 3.51 × 10⁷ EU (35.1 TJ and 8.39 kilotons to the guild), sits in SS on the spine, so what a Starved Grandmaster still holds, released at once, is an SS discharge.
A practitioner may keep a wider margin than the law does. One who maintains peak output only until the reserve drops below thirty percent keeps thirty as a personal operating margin; the law’s floor is ten.
What it costs
Traits come and go without pattern under Essence Starvation. A Trait is a standing bias maintained across the Shell, and a Shell below its working reserve cannot maintain a bias, so the law drops out and returns as the reserve moves. That is the Flicker.
Starvation has a direction, not only a line. A store doing the same work through a falling density loses yield: a millpond sinking behind its dam turns the wheel weaker, and a slackening bowstring throws the bolt shorter. So the yield falls as the reserve falls, and the lost share (1 − η) rises at exactly the moment the practitioner can least afford it. The Starved practitioner is brighter for the same work, sheds more, delivers less. Starvation does not begin at ten percent; it becomes visible there.
Each road runs dry in its own way. The shared tells stand for everyone: the breath shortens and the aura dims at half, tremor and thinning color at a quarter, the Flicker at a tenth. On top of them a Body fighter runs hot and then cracks, since the furnace burns more of every spend: haze on the skin at half, steam off the shoulders and cramps at a quarter, and below the floor the Shell draws its Charge out of the flesh and the skin splits in fine lines. A Spirit worker runs hollow, since the rising loss is paid in the Core: the colors near her go flat, then a cold and a slipped word, and below the floor names and memories go. A Fate worker runs unlucky: small luck curdles nearby, then things go wrong around her, then her own name sits wrong in other mouths, and at the very end the knots all come due at once. The Three Paths has the table.
The reserve clock is the clock a fight runs on. Because the heat burns at the Shell and is not carried by the body, a practitioner can spend down to the floor and past it, and a real fight does: at the shares of “Costs are a share of the reserve”, ten to twenty committed exchanges bring a practitioner to Starvation, and at full output the table in “The clock across the ladder” does it in turns.
How fast it comes back, and on what it depends
Recovery runs by three routes.
Passive Recovery is the baseline pull of ambient Aether without active effort, packed raw in the Shell as Charge or refined in the Crystal into Essence in the shares the soul’s Paths have set, governed by Tempering Yield and Harmonics Synergy. It is faster near active Wellspring veins, slower in depleted or hostile environments, and negligible in Silence Realms. Rich ground fills a Crystal faster and thin ground starves it.
Active Recovery is deliberate absorption through meditation, Wellspring communion or alchemical treatment. It is significantly faster, but requires the character to stop fighting and concentrate. An alchemical treatment quickens the pull from the ground and the Wellspring, and a fight Draft (a dose brewed for battle) pours power straight back into a reserve, taking its price in the crash that follows. The Draft follows the drinker’s road: Core stock feeds the Core with unstamped Essence and the crash is the stamping, and a Body fighter’s Salt packs raw Aether into the Shell and leaves cramps and fever.
Crisis Recovery is a surge triggered by a soul-cost event, a Threshold completion or a genuine emotional breakthrough during combat. It is not reliable and cannot be manufactured.
The rates:

































ConditionRatePassive recovery, at rest, in ordinary ground≈ 10% of maximum reserve per minute → 1% per turn → empty to full in 10 minutes → out of Starvation in ~1 minuteActive recovery (not fighting, concentrating)≈ 2 to 3 × passiveOn an active Wellspring veinfasterIn depleted or hostile groundslowerIn a Silence RealmnegligibleCrisis recoverycannot be planned for
Ten percent a minute is the same number as the Starvation floor, so one figure serves twice: a Starved practitioner is about one minute, ten turns, of rest from being out of Starvation. Long enough to be a decision in a fight, short enough not to end one, and slow enough that a siege still works: a percent a turn does not refill anybody mid-exchange.
Energy taken in
Energy a practitioner absorbs is banked in their own Crystal. Whatever reaches the Crystal from outside (a working turned and taken rather than blocked, a Wellspring drunk from, a discharge caught) enters the reserve at the same rate it leaves it: one EU banked for every EU’s worth taken in, which the guild books as a megajoule, as Charge in a Body fighter’s Shell and as Essence, once stamped, in a Spirit worker’s Core.
Absorption can overfill the Crystal. Recovery stops at maximum; absorption does not. A practitioner can be driven above their own maximum reserve by what they take in, and what they hold above it is reserve like any other, spent at the same rate and counted toward the same floor.
What Starvation is not
It is not unconsciousness and it is not a hit-point track. A Starved practitioner is still a person with a sword. What they have lost is the standing part of what they were: Traits that were law become weather, the Shell that was a wall becomes a sheet, stats read one Grade lower than they stand at full reserve. Below ten percent a practitioner suffers Essence Starvation, and a defender who can afford to spend nothing wins a long engagement against an attacker who cannot afford to spend nothing. Sieges are decided by this more often than by any working.
What the Ledger gives the other side of the fight
Every figure in this Part is a figure someone can use against the person it describes.
It costs something that hurts. Seven broadcast suppressions and the small practitioner is Starved; six heavy constructs and the large practitioner is (see “Worked, at three scales”). A committed exchange costs whole percents of a reserve (see “Costs are a share of the reserve”). A working that forfeits reserve leaves the maximum permanently smaller each time it is performed. The furnace’s heat is a burn radius around the practitioner’s own position (see “The tell, priced”).
It has stated limits. The Stage’s strain line prices the reserve (see “The bands”). Reserve ÷ AU/s caps the duration (see “The drain”). The Stage’s Sub-Stat ceiling caps the output (see “The spine: EU delivered → Grade → the rank that reaches it”). The AU/s a practitioner carries is a burst ceiling, not a duty cycle (see “What AU/s is not”).
Something beats it, and it is one of the four routes. Deny the field. Break the boundary. Break the body. Break the man. The Ledger arms the first and the third:

Deny the field (see “Yield above one”). A practitioner at a yield above 1.0 is pulling on the room. Aether-dead ground, a depleted site or a Silence Realm takes the supplement away and the yield falls below one by definition. The same ground slows or stops the refill (see “How fast it comes back, and on what it depends”).
Break the body (see “The clock across the ladder”). Most reserves empty in under two minutes at full drain. The whole column is a clock, and making an enemy spend is making the clock run. Starvation lowers every stat a step on the scale and makes the Traits flicker; the practitioner who has spent is the practitioner who can be broken.
It has a tell. Surface temperature, burn radius and the aftermath of scorched ground mark a practitioner whose furnace is burning (see “The tell, priced”). A thinned stratum marks one pulling above one (see “Yield above one”). The Flicker is visible before the practitioner admits to it (see “What it costs”), and a Starved practitioner burns brighter for the same work. Heat is the Shell’s tell. A Spirit worker running down goes flat, cold and forgetful, and a Fate worker’s bad luck arrives before she does.

Its numbers stay in band. Every reserve stands against its Stage’s band (see “Where a reserve sits against its band”), including those that sit under it and those that stand past the gate.
And it is findable. Part Four gives the Grade ladder. Part Five gives the Stage ceilings. Part One gives the hold table and the strain lines. Part Nineteen gives the yield and the Starvation floor. The Counterplay page gives the four routes. This Part joins them and adds nothing that cannot be derived from them with a calculator. Nobody has to be told the answer, and the answer is there for anyone who looks.
Read next: Part Twenty-Four. For what a spend looks like on the body, see Stacking and Spending.
