Nobody at the Saltgate Cod Fair had ever seen a line like it, because the bookies had never been asked to price a coin toss with fists. Sissel and Gunnild Scarbrow were twin sisters out of the Tar Street Bellows, a fire school with yellow-and-black colors and a song about its own bad manners, and they stood at the seventh of the sixteen Stages (the rungs of the soul’s refinement), both of them. The Guild’s Measurewright (an assayer of souls and workings) had read them that morning in front of a paying crowd and called out two sheets of Sub-Stats that matched to the last figure, and nobody thought to ask for their Levels. Even money, then, on the strangest card of the summer. Sissel went first, because Sissel always went first: she planted her boots, filled her chest and threw a fire the color of a ripe persimmon, a great roaring sheaf of it that came with a fistful of sparks and a stink of scorched hair and set the Chandlers’ Guild’s bunting alight twenty paces off. The crowd howled with joy. Gunnild answered from the hip with a thread of white flame no wider than a bootlace and no louder than a kettle, which crossed the ring without lighting anything at all until it reached the oak post behind her sister’s shoulder, and the post fell over in two pieces.
It took three exchanges. Sissel finished flat on her back in a smoking yellow shirt, short one tooth and the ends of both braids, laughing so hard the surgeon could not get a hand on her, while the Tar Street end sang the whole of the bad-manners song at her sister and everyone with money on her went looking for whoever had read those sheets. The sheets had been right. They gave what each sister could put forward. But Gunnild had spent the same years on the night furnaces and in the Ring’s worst brackets while her sister sang in the taverns, and her Level had run fifty ahead, and Level is what places a soul under its Stage’s ceiling. A third of what Sissel put forward had gone into bunting and noise on its way out of her, and Gunnild had lost about one part in five. On the Saltgate quays they call a clean delivery a clear throat and a leaking one a wet throat, and they will tell you which you have for the price of a drink. Each sister had known for years what her own window said, Bonfire Herald at Body I, a Muridic Shell as the quays say, for one, and Wick-Trimmer at Body II, a Harmonic Shell, for the other, and neither had thought it the bookies’ business. The Guild’s word for the whole of it is Mastery, and it opens this Part.
Part Seventeen — Mastery and the Class
“Power is not what you hold, but how cleanly you pass the infinite through the finite.”
The Class the Soul Is Offered
The soul offers a named class that fits how the person has lived. A gate-sergeant is offered one thing and the woman who robbed him another, and the name arrives in the window in the owner’s own tongue. A class is a name and never a number. The first offer comes at Glory, Stage VI, with the first rung of Mastery; Stages I through V are unclassed. It evolves each time the person’s lead Mastery rises, so the same Wick-Trimmer may come out a rung later under a name nobody else has ever been offered, and each evolution gives one move that fits it and a lean on where life spends the person’s stat points. The one wild concept stays the person’s own: the class is what the soul makes of a life, and the concept, soup or debt or doors, is what the person goes on to do with it. Crews squabble over class names and taverns rank them. Measurewrights will tell you for free that the offer proves the Continuum reads biography, and for a fee that it proves no such thing.
[Class: Wick-Trimmer]
[Body III]
[Gained: Clean Thread. A flame held to a bootlace's width keeps all its heat.]

What Mastery Measures
Temperance (the soul’s inner refinement, climbed in sixteen Stages) measures refinement of the Crystal. The Sub-Stats measure raw output magnitude. Mastery measures one thing only: how cleanly a soul works its road’s substance into the world, the Charge through the Shell on the Body Path, Essence through the Core on the Spirit Path, the claim through the Attraction Layer on the Fate Path. When the Core speaks, how much of what it says actually arrives?
There is one rung per Path, I to V and Ω, and the card writes it plainly: Body IV, Spirit III, Fate II. Mastery is never tracked. The Stage sets its ceiling and Level places the soul under that ceiling, so two souls at one Stage read differently because one has lived harder, which is the whole story of the Scarbrow twins. Two characters at identical stat values and Stage can have wildly different combat output if one reads Body III and the other Body I. The stats are the same. The delivery is not.
The old books kept three ladders here, Aether Class for the Shell, Essence Class for the Core and Thread Class for the Layer, each running Ø to Ω with a name to every rung. The names live on as what each road’s people call the rungs, and nobody official uses them. Scholars of a certain age still score a Shell by a sum they call the Aether Index, and it is a fine way to pass a winter, since nothing on any sheet has ever read it.
The Rungs





































































RungBody, matterSpirit, souls and meaningsFate, odds and conditionsYield (η)Folk names (Body / Spirit / Fate)unreadbelow Glorybelow Glorybelow Glorythe Stage’s own figure (below)noneIthe objecthearsa lean0.60–0.70Muridic / Listener / TouchedIIby contactis answereda lean, held0.75–0.85Harmonic / Answerer / DrawnIIIby recognitionreads whollya prerequisite0.90–0.95Resonant / Confessor / SpinnerIVby lawholdsa prerequisite, sureloss negligibleLuminous / Shepherd / KnotwrightVby law, wideholds manya field1.00 and aboveRadiant / Ferryman / WeaverΩthe whole systemall of itall of itno separate measurementAbsolute, on every road
I, the first rung. The awakening road, flickering with first resonance. On the Body road the Charge leaks unevenly into space; emotion distorts weather and mood; will echoes unpredictably. Roughly thirty to forty percent of every spend is lost, as heat through the Shell, as hollowing through the Core, as knot through the Layer.
II. The road begins to hold rhythm. Simple spellwork stabilizes. Wellspring (one of the sixty governing ideas that transform how a soul uses Aether) whispers find purchase. Bonds form without tearing the self. Fifteen to twenty-five percent loss.
III. The conductor. Power moves even in silence, and magic ceases to feel like performance and begins to feel like breathing. Dual-casting, Synergia (power born when several souls or forces resonate together) and complex techniques awaken naturally. Five to ten percent loss, and the first rung at which stat values translate into combat output at near-full fidelity.
IV. The lucid road. Wellsprings respond with minimal prompting, and the working mirrors the worker’s emotional and moral alignment with unnerving precision. On the Body road it is the first rung of law. Loss negligible.
V. The world-bending road. Aether bends toward the worker, currents curve around their presence, and they can stabilize Realmgates, hold Domains (a space where a soul’s inner law becomes local reality) against collapse and speak Parun (the tongue law is written in) motifs into matter. Output begins exceeding what the raw numbers suggest, because the road is amplifying rather than merely conducting.
Ω. The threshold. The layer dissolves as a distinct boundary, being and Continuum interpenetrate, and every fragment of the self conducts law with minimal deviation. Paragons only. Archons (the world’s fourteen great powers), Titans and World Spirits who have crossed the Apotheosis Threshold exist at this clarity, and stat output is no longer meaningful as a separate measurement.
Each Path’s Mastery sets the yield of workings through its own layer. The Core authors everything, and the layer the working lands through sets the rung: matter reads Body, a soul or a meaning reads Spirit, and a condition reads Fate. An art’s Path line picks the road. The Three Paths has the list by working and by trade.
The Ceiling and the Level
The Stage sets the ceiling, and Level places the soul under it. A bought Stage opens the ceiling and not the rung, and an Overgrown Crystal reads low until Level catches up.





































StageHighest rung on any roadI–VUnreadVI GloryIVII RefractionIIVIII Transcendence, IX InvocationIIIX Realization, XI DissonanceIVXII Emanation to XIV ZenithVXV Revelation, XVI ApexΩ
Under that ceiling the rung is read from Level: I from Glory’s hold at Level 115, II at 150, III at 215, IV at 260, V at 340, and Ω only at Paragon. The ceiling climbs a rung at a time so that the numeral means something at every height, and a soul fresh across a Stage reads a rung under its new ceiling until its Level grows into the Stage: a new Transcendent at 201 reads II and III at 215, a new Realization soul at 230 reads III and IV at 260, a new Emanation soul at 320 reads IV and V at 340. Mastery is read from Level for everyone, with no list of exceptions. A scene that shows someone working past their read rung shows an overreach, done once, in that moment, at a price, and never a rung held.
Two Paths. A Walked second Path runs a rung behind the lead until it is mastered, and a Studied road runs two behind and never past II. The card reads Body VIII Mastered, III · Spirit VII Walked 35%, II.
Fate and the grip. Fate Mastery climbs with Level like the others, and the Fate Path’s Stage rises with the soul’s Stage like the Stage of any Path, which is what the Fate gates are read against. But nobody grips Fate bare: without a grip, Fate stops at II. A grip is a Work of a bloodline or a blessing that grants one, and it lifts the ceiling to the Stage’s own and never past it. Blood without a Work, a cadet line of an Epoch’s house, still stops at II. An Epoch’s grip opens its road early: a Moto holding a Work, a Zettari holding Matla, a Yukari holding Null-Light reads rung I on that road from Ascension, Stage III, the one exception to “unread below Glory”. Fate’s yield is read on the same table as the other roads; its price is the knot, sized by how far the result sits from likely, and what a pull costs at each rung is set out in The Tell and the Knot. A pull on the low rungs still takes a huge share of the reserve, often fails, and leaves its knot either way.
Inverted. The old books gave each ladder a sixth rung, lateral rather than sequential: the Voidic Shell, the Hollow or Sin-Eater Core, the Severer’s Layer. It is no rung. It is a mark that any rung can carry, a feared and wrong way of working it, and the card writes it so: Spirit IV Inverted. The road reverses: instead of emitting it devours, remembers and reflects, channeling absence, silence and negation without erasing the self, and it interfaces most directly with Nihiloth, Vantabriel and the other Wellsprings of absence, and with Titanic depths. It is most often found in Split-Shell Entities and souls deep in those harmonizations. An Inverted rung reads the yield of its numeral, and its Ardency does not deal damage in the conventional sense. It removes things.
A window reads each road on one line, [Body IV · Spirit II]. The Crystal’s look of Part Twenty-One stays as the reading of what the stone has grown into. The full account is in Classes and Mastery.
How a Road Clears
Level places the rung, and Level comes by living; but how a soul lives shapes how clean a road runs inside its rung. Each kind of living removes interference: ego noise, denial, unprocessed fracture, clinging to false narratives. Each time the lead Mastery climbs, the named class evolves by how it has been lived, and the window shows the new name beside the new rung.
Temperance Refinement: gradual clarity through discipline and self-confrontation. The most common and safest road. The Core refines and the layer learns to match.
Wellspring Baptism: deep immersion in a Wellspring’s Aether where it pools, forcibly realigning the layer’s resonance. Potent, perilous, often irreversible.
Aether Forge Rites: Mechanica (forbidden working that takes power without lawful consent) and ritual that widen conductivity or restructure the Shell directly, sometimes at the cost of memory, autonomy or Essence stability.
Higher Resonance Infusion: alignment with Archonic principle, Titanic depth, or world-bearing law that rewrites the layer from above.
Variants and Anomalies
Rot-Born Conductors channel Aether through damaged or corrupted Shells. Output can be immense, but each working corrodes the lattice further. Every stat expression carries a hidden cost in Crystal integrity.
Synthetic Aetherics bear engineered or grafted Shells. They read cleaner than their Level allows and suffer accelerated decay, instability or identity drift for it. Their Mastery can outpace their Core’s actual Temperance by a dangerous margin.
Split-Shell Entities possess dual polarity, luminous and voidic channels braided through one soul. Capable of rare paradoxical feats, prone to fracture or self-annihilation. A Split-Shell soul may read the same rung clean and Inverted at once.
Interaction with the Stat System
A rung is a multiplier on stat expression for workings through that layer. Raw values determine ceiling. The rung determines how much of that ceiling translates into observable output.
A character whose Ardency Flux stands at 200 and who reads Body II produces roughly seventy-five to eighty-five percent of their theoretical maximum damage through the Shell. The same character at the same value reading Body V produces one hundred percent or more.
The interaction is not linear. II to III produces the largest single improvement in stat-to-output fidelity. The Inverted mark produces the most dramatic qualitative shift, from conventional force expression to inverted and negation-based expression. Ω produces output the stat system can no longer meaningfully track.
Part Eighteen — Paths, the Lens and the Kinds
“The element does not choose you. You temper yourself on it, and it remembers you.”
Older books sort souls by an inborn bias toward one element or another. The trade has given that up. Nobody is a fire soul: there are only people who have tempered themselves on a Wellspring of fire. What gives a blow its character is the Wellspring a soul has tempered on and the Path it comes out by, and both of those can be read off a life. Which Wellsprings sit easily with a soul follows from how each one’s kind sits with the Path. How a Primary Trait (a belief hardened into a personal law of the soul, the first and quietest of them) forms is a matter of origin, first imprint and the lived Path, by Part Twenty. Where a class is going is a matter of how the person has lived and how their lead Mastery rises, by Part Seventeen.
The Three Paths
A soul meets the world through three layers, and every soul has all three, the unwoken included. A Path is the layer a Crystal has learned to lean on. The full account is The Three Paths.





































PathPlaneLayerWhat it works onBuysCostsBodyThe Physical WorldAether ShellPhysical reality under Aegor, known and worked literally: matter, body and the world’s settled habitsStrike, Durability, Lifting, in full at contact; high up, authority over matter itselfRange and Aura Pressure. Must close until very high, and needs existing substance always. Pays in the bodySpiritThe Soul PlaneEssence CoreSpiritual reality: souls, spirits, the dead, what a thing meansForce at range on souls, through projection and inscription, and a say on what a thing is taken to beDurability, and any purchase on matter at range. Survives by being right. Pays in the selfFateThe Plane of FateAttraction LayerWhat has to be so before anything can happen, the law and construction of the worldRange, Aura Pressure, presence, bonds, oaths and Domain authority; rarely, the odds and prerequisites of a blow or a war; at the deadly far end, true Fate ArtsRaw output. A real pull is ruinously expensive, moves only what already has a way of happening, often fails, and leaves a knot either way. Loses a straight exchange. Pays in luck, later
The bracket crowds say hitter, thrower, talker and stayer, and anyone who has met the far ends of these roads says something else. Physical and Spiritual Reality are the two lower realities, under Aegor and Ashura. Fate, under Bara, is no reality at all, and “plane” is a courtesy: it is everything that flows, every possibility, idea and concept, anything that can happen in the other two.
Attraction Force and Obsession Force are what the Plane of Fate runs on, and the Attraction Layer is a soul’s own share of fate, so older registers that list Attraction as a road of its own were looking at the shallow end of Fate. An Attraction gate in an old table is a Fate gate at the same Stage and figure.
What is being routed. Each road spends a different thing. Aether (mana) is drawn in by the body, and nobody works it in the world without drawing it in first.

































PathWhat it worksWhere it is heldThe route outThe lost share becomesBodyRaw Aether, unrefinedThe Charge, packed in the ShellShaped in the Shell by the lens and driven out through the ShellHeat, the Shell’s furnace burningSpiritEssence (spiritual energy): Aether refined in the Crystal and stamped with identityThe CoreSpent through the CoreA hollowing in the Core, and never heatFateThread, pulled down from FateNot held: the reserve that pays for it is Essence, in the CoreDown through the Attraction Layer, paid from the soul’s own share, which is part of that reserveA knot, which the world collects later
The Essence Core is the center of identity and the Crystal is the soul, so Essence is the soul’s own substance, and spending it is spending yourself. That sentence belongs to the Spirit Path, and to vows, which spend the soul’s share. Spending Charge is spending the world, and the body pays for the handling. The Core authors on every road: on the Body Path it decides and the Shell does the work. And because the Shell is the only door into matter, a Spirit worker’s thrown force lands on souls (a soul knocked out of true, dread laid on a mind, a Core wounded) and marks no matter; one who wants a stone moved moves it through their own Shell, at their own Body Mastery.
One Path, Two or Three
A soul has one life’s time to spend. A Path on a card is Mastered, Walked (at least thirty percent of a person’s practice) or Studied. Anyone may study any Path, which gives knowledge and small uses and opens no gates. The percentages on a card are the record of time spent. Each road on a card also carries a Path Stage, the highest Stage whose gates that Path has opened. Mastered means Path Stage equals soul Stage, read again at each Threshold. The card reads Body VII Mastered · Fate VI Walked 35%. On Fate, practice is counted in vows kept and bonds held.















































One PathTwo PathsThree PathsTime to masterThe base timeAbout two and a half times that, for the pairAbout six times that, beyond a mortal spanGatesOpen at the Stage writtenThe Path behind opens a Stage late until it is masteredOpen two Stages late, and the highest steps (726 and up) stay shutForce modifierIn fullThree-quarters on each, for lifeHalf on eachMasteryRead from LevelThe road behind reads a rung behind until masteredThe roads behind read two behind, never past IIReleasesThe Path’s own countThe lead Path’s count; the Walked road flavors them and brings none of its ownThe lead Path’s countSeat (how the lattice sets at a Threshold)CleanRoughRough, with a high risk of a Dead Set
Time closes the gap in the gates and never the gap in the modifier. A two-Path fighter has real holes at times and breaks an opponent’s read of them. Three Paths is rare and looked down on by nearly everyone. Force modifiers and the lens apply after the step is read, so they never move a blow’s Grade and never count on the boost cap of two steps.
The Kinds of Wellspring
Every one of the Sixty has a kind, and the kind names its home plane. A kind is a qualifier and never a lock: any Path can use any Wellspring.
Wild (33) are at home in the Physical World: transformations of matter, things you can point at, which a practitioner shapes what they spend around. Spirit (15) are at home on the Soul Plane. They are purely spiritual, their ground looks ordinary, they usually do little or nothing to the physical world and they give a fighter no fire to throw, showing instead in what a person can bear, know, keep or let go. Wellsprings of Fate (6) are at home on the Plane of Fate and work on bonds, debts, names and odds; on their ground luck goes strange, oaths bite, and strangers keep meeting. Medium (6) are at home on all three. The sort itself is in Part Thirteen.
The Lens
A Wellspring is the lens a soul bases its tempering on, a lens on magic already potent, and it shapes what each Path spends: raw Aether in the Shell, Essence in the Core, the claim on the Layer, where the Thread pulled through the claim takes its shape. The idea stays and the target changes. Take Pyreveil, a Wild Wellspring. On the Body Path the heat lives in the tissue and the blow burns on contact, and what it burns is matter. On the Spirit Path it is thrown, and it burns what a soul means and holds, a grief, a grudge, an attachment, whatever in it is false, and leaves the coat unscorched. On the Fate Path it is a claim that burns its way through: it burns chances, what a thing could have been, and rivalries and oaths catch around the person who holds it. Absolution, a Spirit Wellspring, gives no fire on any of them: on the Body Path old injuries stop costing what they cost, at home it lets the old poison out of a soul, and on the Fate Path a held grudge can be let go, and the thing it was pulling on stops pulling.
At its home Path a Wellspring harmonizes cleanly and can even double its effect, starting small and reaching double only with years of mastery. Away from home it works in that layer’s terms, at lower-quality resonance and higher cost, and half again is the most anyone has got out of it. On two Paths the lens is read per working, by the layer the working goes out through. No stat points change hands either way. The number stays where it was, and the Body Path fighter on Pyreveil simply burns twice as much like herself, once the years have been put in. Young fighters who claim the doubling are generally claiming it to a bookie.
Wellspring, Path and the Stat System
Neither a Wellspring nor a Path adds stat points. They change the qualitative character of stat expression. Two characters with identical Ardency Flux at 450 produce radically different combat output if one has tempered on Pyreveil and the other on Nihiloth. The Pyreveil practitioner’s Flux burns, ruptures and catalyzes. The Nihiloth practitioner’s Flux ends, quiets and unmakes. The EU rating may be identical. The experience of being hit by either is not. The Path changes it again, since the same Flux may arrive by the fist, by a line thrown across a yard at the soul and at nothing else, or by way of a claim on the thing struck.
How a Wellspring’s kind sits with the Path determines compatibility, which determines which Sub-Stats receive qualitative enhancement through harmonization. A Body Path fighter harmonizing with Pyreveil receives stronger Ardency and Vitality enhancement than a Spirit Path fighter attempting the same. The Spirit Path fighter’s Crystal does not reject Pyreveil, but the lattice works harder to integrate it, producing lower-quality resonance at higher cost.
Harmonization
The lock happens at the Shell, where Aether enters. The tie is held on the Layer. The lens shapes what the lead layer works: raw Aether in the Shell for Body, Essence in the Core for Spirit, the claim on the Layer for Fate. A person’s base hue comes from the lens tempered on longest, and the rest add texture. What each Wellspring favors, hates and stands contrary to is on its entry in The Sixty Wellsprings.
Part Nineteen — Aether Flow and Essence Economy
“The soul does not cast from infinite reserves. It casts from what it has earned, compressed, and dared to spend.”
The Three Routes
The Part keeps its old name, and the name is now two-thirds of the matter. A reserve leaves a soul by one of three routes, and the figures below count the first two in one unit and price the third.





























RoutePath and layerWhat is spentThe lost share becomesChargeBody · Aether ShellRaw Aether, packed in the Shell unrefined, shaped there by the lens and driven out through the ShellHeat as the Shell’s furnace burns, with noise and structural bleedEssenceSpirit · Essence CoreAether refined in the Crystal, stamped, and spent through the CoreA hollowing in the Core, and never heatThreadFate · Attraction LayerA thread pulled down for one working, never held, paid from the soul’s own share, a part of the one reserve and held as EssenceA knot, which the world collects later
One reserve, one number: a Body-led soul holds most of its EU as Charge and a Spirit-led soul as Essence, a Fate-led soul holds Essence too, refining what it draws as a Spirit soul does and paying its pulls and its vows out of that, a soul on both holds a share of each (Charge 70% · Essence 30%), and the two never trade back. The Aether Shell sets the routes out at length and The Tell and the Knot has the third one’s bill.
The Resource System
EU (Essence Units): the raw reserve. Total volume of usable power the soul holds at any moment, Charge in the Shell and Essence in the Core counted as one figure; the unit kept its name when the Charge was let into it. Set by Level and capped by Stage (below), governed primarily by Tempering Yield. Maximum EU is the structural ceiling. Operating below ten percent EU produces Starvation (Essence Starvation in the older registers, a name now kept for the Spirit and Fate roads, whose reserve is Essence; a Body fighter’s is Charge Starvation): reduced stat expression, Shell degradation, Trait flickering. Then each road sends its own bill. A Body fighter’s Shell starts drawing its Charge out of the flesh, and the skin splits in fine lines. A Spirit worker’s Core frays, names first and then memory, since Essence is the soul’s own stamped substance. A Fate worker’s reserve is Essence as well, so her Core frays the same way, with the Fate tells on top: luck curdling, then her name sitting wrong in other mouths, and at the bottom every knot due at once.
Flux Density (EU/g): the compression ratio, how much power is packed per unit of Crystal mass. Higher means greater output from the same reserve, and it is the same number on every Path. Governed by Tempering Clarity and Ardency Compression. This separates a practitioner who burns through their reserve in three techniques from one who fights for an hour on the same pool.
AU/s (Aether Units per second): the output rate, how much of the reserve is spent into active expression per second at full output. Governed by Ardency Flux, Ardency Alacrity and Tempering Yield. Formula: AU/s = Flux Density × η.
Yield (η): the share of a spend that arrives as intended effect, as a distillation has its yield; the Measurewrights call it efficiency. At η 0.50 through the Shell, half of every expenditure burns in the Shell’s furnace as heat, with noise and structural bleed; the same figure through the Core is paid as hollowing, and through the Layer it stands as a knot. At η 0.90, ninety percent converts to clean output. A Spirit master’s great Flux turned on matter goes through a Shell he never trained, at his Body Mastery’s yield, and mostly burns off as heat on his own skin. The single most important variable in sustained combat, because for the same delivered effect it determines how long the reserve lasts. Governed by the Mastery of the Path in use, Tempering Clarity and Ardency Compression: the rung sets the band and the other two the place inside it. From Glory the rung sets it, Body Mastery through the Shell, Spirit Mastery through the Core and Fate Mastery for a pull, and souls below Glory, whose Mastery is unread, take their Stage’s typical figure below.
What the owner sees. None of these figures appears in a window. The window shows the reserve as a percentage and a bar, [Reserve: 41%], and leaves EU, AU/s and yield to the assay sheet and the slate. Body tells come first anyway: at half the breath shortens, at a quarter the color thins, at a tenth the Traits begin to stutter. Each road adds its own on top. A Body fighter runs hot and then cracks: heat-haze on the skin at half, steam and cramps at a quarter, the skin splitting in fine lines at a tenth. A Spirit worker runs hollow: the colors near them go flat, then a cold and a slipped word, then names and memories. A Fate worker runs unlucky: small luck curdles nearby, then things go wrong around them, then their own name sits wrong in other mouths. The Three Paths has the table.
The Turn, and What a Unit Is Worth
One combat turn is 6 seconds. Every duration the system states in combat turns is read through that figure: a working held three turns is held 18 seconds, a field that stands eight turns stands 48. The fourteen-day turn of older papers is another thing that shares the name.
One AU is one EU, and a rate is read in AU/s. Spent is AU/s, delivered is AU/s × η, and the difference burns in the Shell’s furnace as heat, with sound and structural bleed, when the spend went through the Shell. The Measurewrights reckon one EU at one megajoule, so by their conversion 1 AU/s is 1 MW. Through the Core the same difference is paid in the Core, unit for unit, and warms nothing; through the Layer it is owed as a knot. A reserve of E EU spent at R AU/s empties in E ÷ R seconds.
Yield counts twice, on purpose: once in AU/s, for how much the layer in use can move, and once in delivery, for what survives the trip. So at full output a higher yield empties the reserve faster, because the layer moves more, and for the same delivered effect it lasts longer, because less is lost on the way. Part Twenty-Three works the figures.
The EU Band by Temperance Stage
A reserve is set by Level and capped by Stage, by the law of reserves in Part Twenty-Three: log₁₀ EU = 3.4202 + 0.012812 × Level. A Stage’s practitioners usually stand in the hundred Levels where most of their rank lives, and that cluster read through the law is the Stage’s working band. The benchmark inside each band is its midpoint in decades, the geometric mean of floor and ceiling. The strain line is the reserve at the Level past which, with no Catalyst to the next Stage, Residual Strain builds (past 100 below Expert, 200 below Master, 300 below Grandmaster, 400 below Archmaster, 500 below Paragon). Level runs on past it, at a price; the working band is only typical.

The floor is not a floor. A reserve below its working band is a practitioner who built a precise instrument instead of a large one, and it is lawful at any Stage. Above Zenith the Level scale ends, and a Revelation or Apex reserve is known only to stand above the highest reserve the scale can hold.
The AU/s Progression
A reserve becomes a rate the moment a turn has a length. A Stage’s AU/s band is its working band spread across one turn, and the benchmark rate is the benchmark reserve spent inside a single turn. That is the plainest statement of what full output costs: open at your Stage’s benchmark rate and you have 6 seconds of it, and nothing after. Sustained work therefore runs far below the benchmark, and the ten percent Starvation floor is reachable inside one exchange by anyone who forgets it.

The table gives typical rates, not limits. A practitioner’s own output is Flux Density × η, and a sheet that sits off the table is a practitioner who built differently. The same bands rolled up by rank are in Part Twenty-Three.
Yield by Rank
The nine ranks are read here by Stage; a merchant’s title of the same name says nothing about his yield. Scholars once ran this table on the Tier of Standing, and before that on lettered Coherence Bands that stopped at Zenith. The figures below are the yield below Glory, where Mastery is unread, and only a field average above it, what a hall expects of a stranger before he is read. From Glory each Path’s Mastery sets the yield for its own layer, so a read rung overrides this table, and a card’s own figure governs its holder.

Techniques feel like shouting into wind.ApprenticeII Welling~0.35The leak is still the loudest thing about the practitioner.JourneymanIII Ascension~0.40Waste becomes predictable, which is the first thing that can be trained against.AdeptIV Flourishing~0.45The last rank at which more than half of every expenditure is lost.ExpertV–VII Splintering to Refraction0.60–0.70First genuine yield; the Crystal has learned to stop leaking. Dual sight at Refraction allows real-time observation and correction of waste.MasterVIII–X Transcendence to Realization0.70–0.80First true Domain, which provides a feedback loop recycling ambient bleed. Presence optimizes Aether flow in the vicinity.ArchmasterXIII–XIV Principality to Zenith0.95–1.2Biomes carry the practitioner’s doctrine. Above 1.0 the Continuum recognizes the expression as law and supplements it with ambient flow; the environment becomes a co-author.ParagonXV–XVI Revelation to Apexabove 1.2, unboundedNo upper figure is set. Yield at this rank is bounded only by what the Continuum will supplement.
Essence Recovery
Passive Recovery: the baseline drawing-in of ambient Aether without active effort, packed raw in the Shell as Charge or refined in the Crystal into Essence, in the shares the soul’s Paths have set. Governed by Tempering Yield and Harmonics Synergy. Faster near active Wellspring veins, slower in depleted or hostile environments, negligible in Silence Realms (places where the Aether is dead). Rich ground fills a Crystal faster and thin ground starves it, which is why the scholar’s Aetheric Density (how thickly a place is charged with Aether) is the first thing a veteran asks about a new town, usually in rougher words.
Active Recovery: deliberate absorption through meditation, Wellspring communion or alchemical treatment. Significantly faster, but requires the character to stop fighting and concentrate. An alchemical treatment quickens the draw from the ground and the Wellspring, and a fight Draft (a dose brewed for battle) pours power straight back into a reserve, taking its price in the crash that follows. It follows the drinker’s road. Core stock feeds the Core with Essence that arrives unstamped, and the crash is the stamping. A Body fighter’s Draft is a Salt, raw Aether that packs straight into the Shell, goes down like a swallowed burn and leaves cramps and fever. No Draft is brewed for the Fate road: a Fate worker’s reserve is Essence, so Core stock refills it. Governed by Harmonics Attunement and Tempering Yield.
Crisis Recovery: surges triggered by soul-cost events, Threshold completions or genuine emotional breakthroughs during combat. Not reliable and cannot be manufactured. The Crystal’s reward for genuine contact with consequence, the same principle underlying the XP system.
Read next: Parts Twenty to Twenty-Two. The account in words is Classes and Mastery, How Power Grows and The Three Paths.

the-magic-system/fracture-of-worlds-—-th.title: VIII. Traits, the Crystal's Look, Domains (Parts Twenty–Twenty-Two)
the-magic-system/fracture-of-worlds-—-th.content:
On the north road they still sing about Penny Thyra, and the song gets most of it wrong. Thyra Ketilsdottir kept the toll on the Ottermouth bridge for forty-one years at a penny a head, and somewhere in the second of those years, after a raider’s horse went over her and left her with a hip that told the weather, she came to believe with her whole body that nobody crosses without paying. The Guild roll calls what grew out of that a Trait (a belief hardened into a personal law of the soul). The carters called it Thyra’s rule and kept a penny ready. The Seven Bright Sabers of the Cinnabar Hall, inner disciples in vermilion silk with a bet riding on them in three towns, came up that road one harvest morning and declined. The first walked onto the planks with his chin up and stopped with one boot in the air, as though the morning had set around him. The second threw a slash of orange aura at the old woman in her hutch, and it got halfway across the river and fell into the water as a shower of hot sparks, having paid no more than he had. Then the toll-bell began to swing with nobody on the rope, its one flat note lifting every gull off the Ott, and the air over the whole bridge turned the brown-gold of old copper, thick as cold honey, with the rule standing in it as plainly as a hand against the chest: the flickering seed of a Domain, from a woman who had never fought anybody in her life and had told the assay house she was too busy to come in.
It held four minutes. In the fifth a fish-seller on the far bank shouted her name, her attention split, and the seed collapsed with a shockwave that took out the middle span and put all seven Sabers and Thyra herself into the Ott. They paid, every one of them, dripping, from the bank, seven pennies laid out on a wet stone, and three towns have not let the Cinnabar Hall forget it. She never raised it again. A soul gets that one flicker at the Threshold into Refraction, on its own Trait and with no Release behind it, and calling and holding a seed takes a Second Release, or the One on the Fate road, each of which has its own Catalyst to be met. Her own bill came out of the same idea. The rule had no exception in it, so she could not cross her own bridge without paying herself, out of one apron pocket into the other, and in the winter there was no penny in the house her daughter was buried on the far bank without her. The roll has a name for that as well, the Rigidity Effect. A street fighter will tell you a power grows in three sizes, the idea, the changed body and the world obeying it. This Part sets down the law of the idea, the Crystal that carries it, and the world.
Part Twenty — The Trait System
“Belief, once survived, becomes law.”
What Traits Are
A Trait is the crystallized law of a soul, the moment emotion, conviction and Temperance (the soul’s refinement, climbed in sixteen Stages) align so completely that the Continuum (the whole fabric of reality) begins responding to that belief as a rule. A Trait is not learned. It awakens when lived experience hardens into metaphysical truth, when the three layers of the Crystal (the Soul Crystal, which is the soul itself) stop merely holding a belief and begin running on it.
Every Trait forms when four harmonics fall into coherence: the Essence Core (the center of identity, and the emotional truth it holds), the Attraction Layer (the pattern of recognition bending toward that truth), the Aether Shell (the behavior of force born from that belief), and the Temperance Field (the refinement keeping the belief from collapsing under strain).
The Four Reflections
Primary Trait, the Innate Reflection. Formed from origin, first Temperance imprint and the lived Path (the layer of the Crystal a life has come to lean on). Instinct, disposition, natural affinity. A modest but constant boost in the aligned facet. Primary Traits answer what your soul does even before it tries.
Secondary Trait, the Tempered Reflection. Forged through trauma, revelation, sustained Wellspring (one of the sixty governing ideas that transform how a soul uses Aether, each with its own type of Aether and its own law) exposure, or a decisive moral or existential choice. Often conditional, activating under emotional or situational pressure. Strong boost while active, balanced by fatigue or emotional cost. Scar-tissue turned into weapon or shield.
Inherited Trait, the Lineage Reflection. Carried through bloodline, ancestral resonance, reincarnational echo, or pacts maintained across generations. Manifests as blessing, mutation, curse, or latent technique. Widely variable depending on lineage purity, Domain (a space where a soul’s inner law becomes local reality) alignment and Wellspring compatibility. History refusing to stay in the past.
Passive Trait, the Resonant Reflection. Stabilized over time through long-term emotional patterns, continuous Essence exposure, or deep habit etched into the Crystal. Always active. Shapes aura, posture, presence and ambient effects. Low to moderate but constant impact with little conscious cost. The atmosphere your soul carries wherever it goes.
Compound Traits: fusions of two or more Reflections into a single law. Often catalytic, risky or anomalous.
Higher-Imprint Traits: marked by Archons (the world’s fourteen great powers), Titans or World Spirit Realms. Exceed normal scaling and behave more like miniaturized Principles than personal talents.
Formation Process
Traits awaken during Resonance Events.
Resonance Trauma: survival under extreme pressure carves an unshakeable statement into the Essence Core. The Continuum begins treating that statement as reliable.
Wellspring Convergence: the soul harmonizes deeply with a Wellspring’s dialect. Its law writes into the Aether Shell.
Temperance Insight: revelation during meditation, crisis, battle or devotion. An inner conflict resolves so completely that the new equilibrium becomes law.
Ritual or Lineage Invocation: a Trait awakened intentionally through rites, pacts, oaths or ancestral activation.
Trait Scaling with Temperance



































RanksStagesBehaviorInitiate to AdeptI–IVPresent but volatile. Output low to modest, inconsistent, real risk of misfires and self-harm.ExpertV–VIStabilize into the soul’s baseline rhythm. Modest to meaningful output, reliable enough for training.Expert to MasterVII–VIIIInterface cleanly with Wellspring dialects. Significant output, semi-lawful, capable of shaping small environments.Master to GrandmasterIX–XIIField-state behavior. Major, consistently world-facing output. Reality bends locally wherever the bearer exerts will.ArchmasterXIII–XIVFuse with Domain Law. Output exceeds ordinary metrics. The Trait stops being an ability and becomes part of how reality must behave in that presence.
A Trait Reads at Mastery
The Stage sets what a Trait is permitted to be, and the bearer’s lead Mastery says how far it reaches inside that. A Trait has no level of its own and no number in the window, which shows it by name, [Thyra's Rule]. Below Glory, where Mastery is unread, a Trait works at its base; from Glory it reads at the Mastery of the soul’s lead Path, so it deepens as Level carries that rung up, and Release and Domain are the same Trait escalating. The Four Reflections stay what they are, and Mastery changes none of their laws or costs; the Rigidity Effect at a higher rung is the same bill at a higher price. Old rolls and older braggarts give Traits levels of their own (“Thyra’s Rule, Level 6”), and the assay houses stopped writing them that way. A technique shows no level either and takes a bigger name when it jumps, which happens when its skill gains a rank and a fight pushes it past its old limit.
Trait Evolution
Fusion (Compound Formation): two or more Traits merge into a single coherent law. Fewer, stronger principles. If the fused law contradicts the self, the collapse can be catastrophic.
Overgrowth: a Trait expands beyond the soul’s capacity to guide it, producing bodily mutation, Essence warping, environmental distortion or unintended Domain formation. The warning sign is a Trait that acts even when the bearer does not consciously will it.
Ascension: a Trait crosses the final threshold into Domain Law. Its behavior defines local physics. Space, memory, probability and emotion must negotiate with that law. The bearer’s presence becomes synonymous with a particular kind of reality.
Trait Costs and Risks
Resonance Fatigue: exhaustion, Essence depletion and slowed recovery from overuse.
The Rigidity Effect: emotional or behavioral inflexibility. The more absolute the Trait’s law, the less the soul can safely contradict it.
Shear Break: the Trait collapses, inverts, or turns against the bearer after they repeatedly deny the truth that birthed it. A single broken vow lands at once by its own terms and is no Shear Break until the denial repeats; see Vows and Oaths.
Alignment Benefits: compatible Wellsprings, Realms or Archonic Domains increase stability, reduce Essence cost and deepen expression.
Misalignment Penalties: working against one’s own law weakens effectiveness, increases backlash risk and accelerates lattice fatigue.
Part Twenty-One — The Crystal’s Look
“To refine the soul is not to polish it. It is to remove everything that was never truly part of the design.”
The Soul Crystal is literally the soul, and tempering melts it down and rebuilds each layer. What a reader sees in the stone is its look, the synthesis of all three layers at once. The look is how the stone looks and not a track of its own: it follows the Stage, and it is not a measure of Mastery, which is read per Path from Level. A Crystal can run ahead of or behind its Shell or Core, and the gap is itself diagnostic. A Stage held above its Level, bought or met early, shows in the look as the Overgrown State below until Level catches up. The scholars called the looks the Developmental Tiers, or the Soul Crystal Tiers, and kept them as a ladder. The three layers are the Aether Shell, which meets the Physical World; the Essence Core, which holds identity, memory and Traits on the Soul Plane; and the Attraction Layer, a soul’s own share of fate on the Plane of Fate. Every soul has all three, and a Path is the one its Crystal leans on. A pure alchemist works on a Crystal that never woke and reads Seed on the table below; the Accord title such an alchemist holds is earned at the bench and never read off the Crystal. The names are a jeweler’s, each for what a reader sees in the stone; the older name, which old books and songs still use, stands beside each, retired because Harmonic, Resonant and Radiant are also what the Body road’s people call its Mastery rungs. The old books also kept a Clear look between Faceted and Fire, for Refraction alone; it is not read now, and a Refraction Crystal is Faceted.





















































LookOld nameDescriptionCorresponds toSeedDormantSealed and silent. The Crystal exists but does not yet function as a metaphysical organ.The unwoken, pre-InitiateCloudedAwakenedOpened and circulating what its road holds: a Body-led Crystal packs Charge in the Shell, a Spirit-led or Fate-led one refines Essence in the Core. Traits can begin forming. The older registers have the Essence Core always activating first; as it is read now the first layer to activate is the lead layer, the one the soul’s Path leans on.Initiate to Adept (Temperance I–IV)FacetedHarmonic; late, Resonant or ClearThe three layers have found a recurring rhythm the Continuum can read consistently. Techniques stabilize; a second lens can be harmonized without tearing the lattice. A Clouded Crystal can harmonize as well, and many do, at a real risk of exactly that tear; from Faceted it is safe. By Refraction the Crystal self-conducts, power moves even in silence, and the resonance signature becomes a permanent feature of the Continuum’s local accounting.Expert (Temperance V–VII)FireRadiantThe Attraction Layer gains territorial durability. The first true Domain becomes possible. Existence begins exerting topological pressure on its surroundings.Master (Temperance VIII–X)FlawlessSovereignTrait law and Domain law begin to be the same law. No longer a container for power but a generator of local metaphysical conditions.Grandmaster (Temperance XI–XII)StarredCrystallized SoulSelf and law correspond with near-perfect precision. An exact instrument of identity. Thought carries causal weight.Archmaster (Temperance XIII–XIV)AbsoluteAbsoluteThe Crystal dissolves as a distinct boundary between self and Continuum. Being and law interpenetrate.Paragon (Temperance XV–XVI), the Apotheosis approach
Crystal States
Fractured: split by contradiction or strain. The Core leaks, the Shell destabilizes, the Layer weakens. Thought becomes difficult to trust. Can heal through Temperance advancement, alchemical treatment, or integration of the fracture into architectural feature, which is the Dissonance path.
Refined: balanced and coherent. Essence moves in rhythm, Aether conducts cleanly, Attraction Force binds without overreach. The standard healthy state.
Overgrown: swollen with more pressure than integrated. Power spills outward, lamps lean toward the bearer, emotions distort nearby space, the soul wounds its own surroundings. It is the state of any Crystal holding a Stage its Level cannot yet hold, whether the Stage was bought in a Draft, given in a blessing or met early by a prodigy: Mastery reads low and no Release will answer until Level reaches the Stage’s hold. The heir and the prodigy are the same case to the Crystal.
Part Twenty-Two — Domain Mechanics
“When belief holds, the world begins to answer.”
What a Domain Is
A Domain is a space where a character’s inner law becomes local reality: the moment the Attraction Layer claims territory on the Plane of Fate (which stands above the two lower realities, where all possibility rests and where Attraction and Obsession are controlled) and that claim reflects downward into physical and spiritual law. Inside a Domain, the ground takes the character’s doctrine as its own law, and it outranks the world’s ambient habits for as long as it is sustained. Because the claim is the Attraction Layer’s, a Domain belongs to Fate’s authority whichever Path its holder walks: the Fate Path has the most say inside one, and the Body Path fighter’s Domain is a Domain all the same. A Domain pulls no thread, and its upkeep reads the holder’s lead Mastery. A Body Path field rules matter, a Spirit Path field rules meanings and the room looks unchanged, and a Fate Path field rules conditions; the Fate gates on Radius, Sovereignty and Gravity are what cap a Body Path Domain’s figures at 400.
A Domain is grown before it is called, and it is no technique to be learned off a wall. The Stage grants it and a number never does, and the growing is done by living: Temperance, Dominion (the stat for presence and pressure on others) and the lead Path’s Mastery climb until the character’s soul has become heavy enough to dent reality, and reality has stopped resisting the dent. Once a soul has grown one, the Second Release, or the One on the Fate road, opens it and powers it, it is called aloud at the fighter’s choosing, and it forms as it is named; what nobody has ever done is call a Domain the soul has not grown.
Anyone at Stage VIII can have one, their own concept made real; the fuller account is on Domains. A bought Stage VIII opens that door and no more, and sects teach the road through it, which money cannot buy. A Release or a Domain fills the window with its name and what changed, and a timer bar drains. The boost cap of two steps on the hidden scale stands, the holder’s own Domain counting against it; only outside help goes past it.
[DOMAIN SEED: NOBODY CROSSES WITHOUT PAYING]
[Changed: the unpaid stop at the first plank. Force sent across pays what it carries.]
[Held: ██████░░░░]

Domain Formation Timeline
Stage VII, Refraction: seed activation. The first fragile, flickering territory. As the Catalyst into this Stage it is a one-time flicker of the person’s own Trait and needs no Release; the Second Release, open from here on the Body and Spirit roads, or the Fate road’s One, which opens here and counts as its Second, is what lets a seed be called and held. Lasts minutes rather than hours. Requires active concentration and collapses if attention fractures. The seed is the Attraction Layer’s first territorial claim.
Stage VIII, Transcendence: the Domain stabilizes. A piece of the lattice accepts the soul’s signature permanently. Holdable for hours; survives minor disruption. The first true Domain, grown by living and called aloud.
Stages IX–X, Invocation through Realization: the Domain consolidates toward a Realm capable of holding other Domains. The Catalyst into Stage IX is a first flicker of one, on the same terms as the seed. The Realm itself comes late, at the far end of the climb, and each road reaches it by its own door: Body through the Third Release, which opens at Invocation, Spirit through its Second grown whole, Fate through the One. Each door opens no earlier than Realization: the Body’s asks another’s world carried, and not let fall; the Spirit’s, another’s whole meaning held inside your own, and both left true; Fate’s, a claim others stand on, kept for them (How Power Grows gives the three Realms). Pacts, artifacts and law imprint on terrain. The Domain becomes a reality the Continuum must accommodate.
Stages XI–XII, Dissonance through Emanation: passive effects leak without active maintenance. Traits become local law. Mere presence alters metaphysical conditions. The Domain transitions from deliberate expression to ambient consequence of existing.
Stage XIII, Principality: the Continuum formally registers a law the character embodies. The Domain becomes a recognized structural feature of local reality. Biomes carry the character’s doctrine.
Stage XIV, Zenith: Domain and character become indistinguishable. Reality acclimates to the character rather than the character imposing on reality.
Common Domain Behaviors
Low-G / High-G: adjusted gravity. Governed by Dominion Sovereignty and the character’s relationship to physical law.
Hush / Silence: dampened energy transfer; sound, kinetic force or Essence propagation suppressed. Governed by Dominion Pressure and Harmonics Suppression.
Heat-Invert / Phase-Stabilize: thermal or state control; the Domain enforces a specific temperature or material phase. Governed by Wellspring alignment.
Vectoring: trajectory and reach modification; projectiles curve, distances distort, approach angles shift. Governed by Dominion Sovereignty and Dexterity Finesse.
Construct Sustain: summoned constructs maintained passively without the summoner’s concentration. Governed by Dominion Gravity and Ardency Density.
Inertial Dominion: motion and momentum obey the holder’s doctrine; moving objects arrested, redirected or accelerated. Governed by Dominion Sovereignty and Vitality Absorption.
Domain versus Domain
When two Domains overlap, the Continuum resolves the conflict through a hierarchy.
First, Temperance differential. A character two or more Stages above their opponent’s Domain simply overwrites it. The higher doctrine takes precedence.
Second, Dominion Sub-Stat comparison. Within the same Stage, or a Stage apart, the character with higher Sovereignty and Gravity holds their territory while the weaker Domain erodes, and a sharp read can flip it: find where the holder’s law is thin and the ground changes hands.
Third, Wellspring compatibility. Domains built from contrary Wellsprings produce interference patterns that degrade both. Domains from neighboring Wellsprings may coexist or reinforce each other.
Fourth, doctrine coherence. A Domain built from a deeply held, honestly lived truth is structurally denser than one built from adopted belief or forced cultivation. The Continuum measures Tempering Coherence and Tempering Maturity as the tiebreaker between otherwise equivalent Domains.
Domain Costs
Maintenance costs Essence continuously. The rate is governed by Dominion Radius (larger Domains cost more), Dominion Gravity (unstable Domains bleed faster), and environmental hostility (maintaining a Domain inside someone else’s costs significantly more).
A Domain collapses when EU drops below the minimum maintenance threshold, when concentration is shattered by sufficient force, or when a stronger Domain overwrites it. Collapse produces a Resonance Shockwave proportional to the Domain’s size and density, often dealing significant damage to everything within the former territory, including the character who lost it.
Read next: The Essence Ledger. The account in words is The Trait System, Release Forms and Domains.

the-magic-system/fracture-of-worlds-—-th.content:
The Wyvern of Anner Moss had killed forty carters and a magistrate’s mule before anyone troubled to read its row. The Reeve posted three hundred silver marks in hand-copied bills on every door in the hundred, the heralds cried it as far as the coast, and the Accord’s Commission (its licensed hunting contract, rated by danger) stamped the job an S bounty under a Gold Sigil, which the taverns of the hundred took as their cue to lay twenty to one against the Merry Gallows: fourteen hedge-hunters, one borrowed Sigil, and a cook named Bettris Two-Spoons, who had read nothing in her life but recipes and the Bestiary ladder. On that ladder a Wyvern throws a bolt the guild reckons at about a gigajoule, which is a fine way to lose a barn. It stands two rungs above that, on its reach and on the storm that feeds it, and the row says plainly that cold and water break a storm’s hold. So Bettris left the Moss alone. She drove a red brewer’s wagon full of screaming goats out onto the ice of Hob’s Tarn, four leagues from the crag where the thing kept its weather, with a stewpot strapped on her head, and she sat up there singing until it came.
The first bolt went violet through the wagon and took her left ear, four goats and a Gallows boy called Little Perkin. Then the crew on the far bank hauled on the ropes they had sawn through the ice all night, the floe tipped, and the whole Wyvern went shoulder-deep into black water with its sky unraveling above it, the violet running out of the clouds like dye out of a cheap shirt. It still killed five of them before the boar spears went in under the wing. The minstrels say she finished it with a ladle, and the ladle has its own song now and a shrine at Anner Moss that charges admission. The spear was hers, and the ladle was for afterward, and the whole plan cost a penny, which is what a copied row goes for at any Guild Hall door.

Every ladder in the Continuum (the whole fabric of reality) hangs on one spine: peak output in EU delivered (the EU spent times the yield, η, the share of a spend that reaches the world), read to a Grade (a letter rank of output, Hollow up to EX+), read to a rung from one to nine. The Essence Ledger sets the spine. Every joule, kilojoule, terajoule and ton of TNT on this page is the Measurewrights’ conversion of the same figure, at a megajoule to the EU, kept because the frontier has learned to talk in them and never the reading. This Part names the rungs for each kind of thing that can be measured on it (beasts, draughts, artifacts, summons, Domains (a space where a soul’s inner law becomes local reality), Wellspring (one of the sixty governing ideas that transform how a soul uses Aether, each with its own type of Aether and its own law) sites, weapons and armor) and says what each ladder adds that an output figure does not show. A rung is a fact anyone can look up. What it means in the room is for whoever is standing in it to work out.

The Bestiary ladder
A beast goes on the spine (the spine of the Essence Ledger) the way a practitioner does: by its peak output in EU delivered, its hardest blow, breath, dive or discharge. That figure finds the row, and the row is the rung. The Bestiary ladder gives the nine rungs the names the frontier already uses for them, and then adds the three things a beast has that an output figure does not show: how far its harm reaches, how hard it is to end, and what ground feeds it.
The rung says what the thing can break. The modifiers say how long you will be in the room with it, and whose room it is.
Monsters climb. They move and live across the whole Inner World, beasts and beast-like animals more widely still, and the Scourge of Hell is only the one area known for extremely dangerous ones. A monster gains Levels by killing and changes form at its own thresholds, and it stands on the same Stage and Level scale as a person, with a Path it leans on; unlike a person it carries its Grade openly, on every bill and in every tavern. A strong enough Gnosis reads it like anyone else, and a weak reader gets question marks in the window, [Wyvern · Level ??? · Grade ?], and is well advised to take the hint. Commissions grade monsters by bounty Grade, E up to EX, and a famous one earns a name, an epithet and a bounty, at about which point the odds boards take an interest.
The core and the parts. A monster’s core is in a way its Soul Crystal, worth more the stronger the monster. It is the lawful Crystal Draw of The Standing Index: an alchemist renders it into Essence Drafts used for tempering, with Creature-Sourced potency and the risk of Identity Contamination (the source’s nature coming through in the drinker). Swallowed raw it gives everything at once, and most who try die or come out wrong. Monster parts make gear. A stone and its parts are read from the beast’s own Stage and Level on the coil; the bounty Grade stays the shorthand for danger and price, and most beasts line up with it. A Crystal cut from a dead practitioner makes the strongest Draft of all, the worst crime in every realm and the most profitable, and it is why Grade IV of the Index has never balanced. Some of what is sold as monster core came out of people.

The guild reckons one EU at a megajoule, so their joule column is the EU ceiling times a million. S and SS meet edge to edge and both sit in March-bane, so no beast’s rung turns on the line between them.
Any rung kills a man. A crossbow bolt carries a few hundred joules. The ladder does not measure whether a creature can kill you. It measures what it can break when you are not the only thing in front of it.
Hearth-pest. Below 0.015 EU delivered, fifteen kilojoules to the guild. Its hardest blow is a man’s or a dog’s. A door holds against it, a householder with a spade answers it, and it is dangerous by being where somebody is rather than by what it does when it arrives. Vermin, the single walking corpse, the trickster in the hedge.
Field-bane. Up to 20.9 EU delivered, twenty-one megajoules to the guild, Wall level at the ceiling. It kills stock, breaks a fence, stoves in a door, puts a horse and rider down in one exchange. The great natural predators live here: the Greater Wolf’s run, the lion’s charge, the griffon’s dive, a grown Droval’s pounce across thirty meters. A Field-bane costs a fraction of an EU at the floor and twenty at the top.
Road-bane. Up to 1,046 EU delivered, a gigajoule to the guild. It closes a road: overturns a wagon, breaks a gate, capsizes a boat, brings down a bridge span or a small house. This is the Cyclops’s wall-breaking blow, the Goliath’s stomp, a hellhound’s breath across a camp. Its hardest working costs between 21 and 1,046 EU.
Hamlet-bane. Up to 46,024 EU delivered, forty-six gigajoules to the guild, Building to Large Building. A lightning strike lands here, and so does the petrifying gaze, because remaking a body into stone asks the whole of it to become something else, which the guild reckons on the order of a gigajoule for a grown man. What stands here can take down the buildings of a hamlet one at a time.
Town-bane. Up to 4.184 million EU delivered, four terajoules to the guild, City Block to Multi-City Block. The wyrm’s breath, the phoenix’s burst, the gorgon’s gaze swept across a battalion, the hydra’s heads all breathing at once. What stands here can empty a town in an afternoon if it is let.
March-bane. Up to 418 million EU delivered, four hundred terajoules and one to a hundred kilotons to the guild: Town to Large Town. A coast-shattering surge, a trench throwing up a sea, a Titan’s pulse flash-freezing a battlefield. This is the highest rung any creature in the register reaches by its own output. The Leviathan’s surge and the Kraken’s upheaval both sit here.
Realm-bane. Large Town to Small Country. No creature in the register stands here by output. Every creature that stands here stands on a Town-bane or March-bane output and the modifiers below.
World-bane. Country to Large Planet. No creature in the register stands here by output. The Voidwyrm, the Cerberus and the high Titan Droval stand here by standing, and the difference between those two words is the whole of this ladder.
Sky-eater. Brown Dwarf and beyond. No creature in the register reaches it by output. Those that stand here stand on a March-bane’s output with all three modifiers held, and the name is the frontier’s, not the Ledger’s.
What this ladder adds
The spine gives every ladder its own modifiers. The Bestiary’s are three, and each lifts the rung by one. A creature’s standing is its output rung plus the modifiers it holds: never more than three above its output, never past nine.
Reach. Its harm lands beyond the ground a party can hold. Lightning at three kilometers, a song across open water, a hunt that runs across realms on an Essence signature, harm that outlasts the creature’s presence: a storm curse on a valley, ground frozen meters deep after the Titan has gone, currents altered for a season. A creature with reach cannot be answered by standing still and holding a line, because the line is inside its range.
Persistence. It is hard to kill. It regenerates, returns, stores its life somewhere other than its body, or keeps fighting through wounds that end a body: the hydra’s heads, the phoenix’s ashes, the lich’s phylactery, the Goliath’s stoneform. Hard to hit does not lift the rung. A thing that phases, teleports, flies or vanishes into snow lengthens the fight and does not raise its ceiling; the first blow that lands on it lands on its rung. The Ledger prices what lands, not what misses.
The tie. It is fed by a Wellspring, a vein, a Crevice or a plane boundary: stronger at the site, weaker off it, and in the worst cases a living anchor of the site itself. The tie is the only modifier that can be taken away in the middle of a fight. Draw the creature off its ground, or deny the ground, and the rung the tie gave it is gone.
Workings that do not strike. A gaze, a song, a drain or a curse is read by the work it does to what it lands on. A body turned to stone is priced at remaking that body’s matter. A song that walks sailors onto a reef is priced at the tide that wrecks them. A death is not a quantity of work. A sting that kills, or a severed Essence thread, stands on the blow that carried it, and the difference between that blow and the body count is the Commission’s to price, not the Ledger’s.
Numbers are not a modifier. The Ledger reads the animal. A pack, a herd, a horde or a coven is a party’s problem and a Commission’s figure; it is never a rung.
The Bestiary’s own observation that almost everything bountied above S is a Wellspring event rather than an animal is what the ladder shows in figures. Nothing in the register reaches Realm-bane by output, and every creature the Ledger stands at seven or above holds the tie. The Lich holds it through the person it was.

The Leviathan and the Kraken show why a bounty Grade cannot simply be read off output. Both are bountied EX, and neither eats worlds. E is empty because nobody files it. A Hearth-pest is a householder’s matter. The rat in the grain store and the fox at the hens are E on the Commission’s scale and no Guild Hall has ever opened a Commission for one, so the register asks its eleven questions of nothing there. The rung exists; the paperwork does not.
D and C share the word Moderate because a crowd changes the word. D is Minor for one and Moderate for many: one walking corpse is a Hearth-pest with a grip, a battlefield of them is a Moderate Threat, and the Commission issues the same Grade for both because it sends the same rank to either. C is Moderate by itself. The Ledger reads the body in both cases and lets the Commission read the crowd.
Where the two differ, both stand. The Ledger never overrules a Commission; it enters its reading beside it. In the register as it stands the Ledger never reads above the Commission. Where it reads below, the Commission is pricing something the ladder does not: numbers, a rider, what a thing does to a place rather than a body, what it does loose, or a death without output. Those gaps are where a hunter can choose the fight the Ledger describes instead of the one the Commission does.

The Lich is read as a person first. Its output is what the necromancer’s hardest working delivered, placed on the spine like any practitioner’s, and the three modifiers stand on top of it. The Commission bounties every lich at EX. The Ledger enters a lich at nine only when the necromancer stood at Master before the phylactery; a lesser one who made the same bargain stands lower, and the Commission’s Grade is the Grade of the worst of them.
The Elemental is the one entry with no fixed rung, because it has no fixed size. It always holds the tie, since an Elemental is concentrated Wellspring energy and collapses when the site is spent. The small ones stand one rung above their output; the ones that reshape a landscape reach and stand two.
Summoned things are read loose, as the Commission reads them. The leash is a fact about the summoner. The Ledger’s rung is a fact about the beast.
What the rung tells a hunter
The output rung is what you must be able to survive: armor, ward and the stats behind them are chosen against it, and a guard a full Grade above a creature’s output wins the exchange the way it wins any exchange. The modifiers tell you where and how to fight. Persistence means bring the thing that ends it (fire for the hydra’s stumps, the phylactery before the lich, the ashes before the phoenix rises), and a creature that is only hard to hit needs patience, noise and mirrors, not a higher rank. Reach means close the distance or leave its ground, and Raga is the one entry where closing is the mistake. The tie is the best counter in the register: draw the thing off its Wellspring, deny it the site, or fight it where the vein is thin, and every rung the tie gave it is gone. And where the Commission’s bounty Grade sits above the Ledger’s standing, the Commission is pricing a pack, a rider, a place or a death. Break the pack, unseat the rider, change the ground, or refuse the death, and you are fighting the creature the Ledger describes.
The Drafts ladder
Alchemical works and Drafts, on the spine. Every Draft, salt, oil, powder and charge the trade produces is a working stabilized into a substance, and a substance holds a definite quantity of Essence. The ladder reads that quantity. A work is placed by the EU one dose holds, read on the spine like any other peak output, with the guild’s joules beside it at a megajoule to the unit. Two modifiers, Carry and Fidelity, then move it.
What is read is what the dose holds, not what arrives. The spine is read on the held figure at the constant, before anybody’s yield (η: the share of spent Essence that arrives as effect) touches it. What reaches the drinker is the held figure times the drinker’s own yield, and it is spent where the formula sends it: on the body, on the Shell (the soul’s outer layer, which passes power out into the world), or on the pressure a Crystal builds toward its next Threshold (the breakthrough that opens the next Stage), or, in a work made for it, on the Catalyst itself. Only a fight Draft refills a reserve. Otherwise a practitioner is refilled by rest, the ground and the Wellsprings, and an ordinary Draft drunk on an empty reserve mends the body and steadies the Shell and leaves the reserve as empty as it found it. A fight Draft, poured for the purpose, gives the reserve back at once and takes its price in the crash after.

Tincture. A work measured in thousandths of a unit. It cleans a cut, holds a fall, lights a room, and needs no circle and no understanding. The whole first rung together costs less than the smallest reserve carries in its lowest percent, which is why a household can own a shelf of it and never think of it as alchemy.
Tonic. A working day’s steadiness in a bottle, a lamp for a season, a thunderclap in a flask. A careless hand can ruin a Tonic without dying of it. This is the rung of the ration and the field kit.
Draught. The trade standard. A Draught holds enough to matter against a Welling reserve and to carry a Welling practitioner toward the Ascension floor across a course of doses. The bulk of what the four quarters drink for their Crystal is here.
Philter. A dose that holds a Journeyman’s whole working range in one vessel. This is the rung at which a Draft can carry a practitioner to a quantitative floor in one issue, and the rung at which it is sold against a term of service rather than a price.
Elixir. Threshold work in earnest. An Elixir holds as much as an Expert’s reserve spends in a long engagement and supports a Crystal through a reorganization. An Elixir can supply the floor and it can supply a seed, and a work made for the purpose, here or on a higher rung, can supply the Catalyst (the event that sets off a Stage breakthrough) as well. The Stage has then simply been bought, the door is open and no more, and the great houses hoard the top of this ladder for exactly that reason. The low Stages are bought smaller. Below Splintering a Threshold holds little, so a work made to supply its Catalyst stands on a Tonic, a Draught or a Philter, dear for its recipe rather than for what it holds, and a house child drinks through them on an allowance. A purse can buy the Catalyst for any Stage; at Zenith a Hollow Throne must still recognize the buyer, so money buys the attempt and not the seat.
Quintessence. A dose at the scale of a Master’s Domain. Works on this rung anchor, stabilize and hold at the size of a live, law-bearing field, and the question of what the dose was rendered from stops being hypothetical.
Magisterium. A work that enforces. It holds energy on the scale of a regional event, and what it does to a blade, a wound or a Domain behaves as a ruling rather than a reaction.
Panacea. Realm-scale. What a Panacea is laid into registers in the Continuum as terrain. Works on this rung are used a handful of times in the record, and what they are laid into outlasts whoever laid it.
Stone. The rung with no ceiling. It holds what a Paragon’s working holds, and the Stone is the rung the trade keeps open because the ladder required a top, not because the trade has filled it.
Master Works. The trade has its own: a Draft that does what its Grade and material should not be able to, made once at the end of a lifetime, always Unique or Mythic, and named. A Fate Essence Draft is one, bottling the manipulation of possibility itself, extremely hard to make and very coveted. Its rung is whatever its energy says, and that is the least interesting thing about it.
The modifiers

Carry: how much of the origin came with the dose. The origin rides in the energy and arrives with it.

The Index and the ladder
The Standing Index and the ladder are two readings of the same lot, and neither corrects the other. The Index ranks an entered lot from T1 to T9 by provenance and standing: its Provenance Grade, its rank gate, who may lawfully hold it and what the Bench is prepared to certify about it. The ladder ranks the same lot by the energy one dose holds. The Index prices provenance and standing. The ladder prices energy held.
The two agree most often through the middle of the trade, where a Threshold ration’s rank gate and its dose climb together. They part wherever the Index is pricing law, provenance or danger rather than what a dose holds. A lot can hold almost nothing and be reserved to Masters, because what it does is dangerous out of all proportion to what it holds; and a lot can hold a Domain’s worth and be entered one rank lower than its rung, because its Carry lifts it on the ladder and not in the ledger. A buyer reads the Index to learn who may hold a thing. A drinker, and anyone facing one, reads the rung to learn what it will do.

A lot that has never been drawn from has no rung. The ladder reads what a dose holds, and a residue that does not deplete, or has never been opened, offers no dose to read. Both stand on the Index and neither stands on the ladder, and that absence is the most honest line in either document.
A vessel that refills is not a dose. A phial that never runs dry is read on the Artifacts ladder, by what one pour discharges and how bound the vessel is to its bearer.
Counterplay
The rung says how much a dosed opponent took in, and none of it is reserve. A Philter or an Elixir drunk before a fight has gone into the body and the Shell, and the opponent’s reserve stands where it stood, spending at the same rate toward the same ten-percent floor. The answer is findable in the arithmetic, and it is the answer it was before the vial: make them spend it. A Draft supplies energy and it can supply a seed, so a practitioner on an ordinary dose is mended and steadied, holds no more to spend than they did, and is not a Stage higher than they were. One made to supply a Catalyst does leave them a Stage higher, and a Stage bought that week has no Release behind it, since a Release is found and mastered by fighting. Where the Carry is Heavy, the origin arrived with the energy, and the source’s own weaknesses, appetites and habits of mind are in the drinker now and can be found there. Where the Fidelity is C or worse, the dose did not do the same thing twice, and the part that went into the adjacent process is a tell.
The Artifacts ladder
Artifacts, on the spine. An artifact is a working given a body that outlasts the working. Some hold a store of their own, charge laid down against a later need. Most hold nothing and pass what their bearer spends through a glyph (a sigil written into a working) chain that shapes it. The ladder reads both the same way. An artifact is placed by the EU it stores or the EU one act of it discharges, whichever is greater, read on the spine like any other peak output, with the guild’s joules beside it at a megajoule to the unit. One modifier, how bound the thing is to its bearer, then decides whose rung it is.
Stored and discharged are read differently. A store is read as it stands: what the thing holds, in EU. A discharge is read as delivered, the EU spent times the yield of whoever spends it; where a record gives only the drain on the bearer, the drain is read at the constant and the rung is a ceiling. A drain given as a share of the bearer’s reserve is as large as the reserve makes it. The share decides how long the bearer lasts; the absolute size of the reserve decides how large each act is, and an artifact that asks a Master for five percent of a Master’s reserve is discharging on a Master’s scale.

Implement. A single act at the scale of a building. An Implement that stores its own charge is an Implement in any hand that can open it; one that only passes its bearer’s drain is an Implement because its bearer is.
