the-magic-system/practice-and-institutio.title: Blessings and Curses
the-magic-system/practice-and-institutio.content:
What a thumb grants, who can press one on you, what it costs them, how the line on your window lies, what the terms were, and who can take it off again

READ IT AGAIN.
Painted in red at eye height over the door of Wording Row at Waxgate, where the wording-men keep their stalls, and repainted every spring at the expense of the widows

Dickon Sedley sold mutton pies off a barrow on the great bridge at Kingsbridge, and at the spring fair of 661 he sold one to Dame Rohese Vaske, Stage XI, a very large woman in scarlet and gold who had been celebrating since Tuesday. She pronounced it the finest thing she had eaten in forty years. Then she pressed her thumb into the flour on his forehead and told him, with a great laugh and a wave at the river, that a man who could make that should never be beaten. It took about as long as a sneeze and cost her less than the pie. A print the color of hot brass came up on his skin and stayed there, and when Dickon looked at his window that night (the soul’s report of its own numbers, which only its owner can see), there was a new line under Baking and Gout.
[Dickon Sedley · Level 11]
[Baking: Journeyman · Haggling: Apprentice]
[Health: Gout, left foot]
[Blessing: Unbeaten]
[You will not be beaten.]

By midsummer he was in the Kingsbridge brackets in his apron with a rolling pin, because a man with that line owes it to himself, and the whole Midmarch came down to see it. He had never thrown a punch and he never learned. A Splintering champion of the Blue Herons tripped on her own ribbon and broke her collarbone on the rope. A lancer’s horse took a sudden dislike to the lance. In the semifinal a Stage VII duelist opened him from hip to armpit in front of nine thousand people, and Dickon stood there with the flour going red and his own side held shut in one hand, and the duelist’s heart stopped. Bookies quit the book, heralds cried him from every market cross on the Kessen road, and by autumn he was King of Little Tolland, which had been looking for one.
The terms arrived over the next thirty years. He could not lose at dice, so nobody would dice with him. He could not lose an argument, and his wife, who had been winning them for two decades, went home to her sister. He could not be beaten by a fever, so it stayed, unwon, for nineteen winters. The cut in his side never closed, since closing would have meant the cut had finished with him, and neither of them could finish. At eighty-one he got up every morning on a body that should have stopped nine separate times, because lying down was losing. His grandchildren petitioned Dame Rohese, who was still alive and in excellent color, and she did not remember the pie.
So in 692 they spent the treasury of Little Tolland on a letter north, and an old woman named Tokiwa Moto came down the Kessen road with two attendants and a bill. She stood him on the bridge, read the line aloud, and said one quiet sentence to it, and the brass print went out like a lamp. Dickon Sedley sat down. He asked for dice. He lost nine straight games to a child, at a copper a game, roaring with laughter and bleeding on the stones, and he was dead before the week was out, thoroughly beaten, in the best mood anyone had ever seen him.
Every clause of the law is in that story. This page takes them in order, and I would ask you to read it before you go near a shrine, or a duchess, or a pie.
At a Glance
What it is. A blessing grants a power out of a person’s natural reach, even in Level. Most run through the Plane of Fate, some do not. The street calls it a thumb, and a person who has one is thumbed.
How it looks. A line of its own on the window, and on the body a print or a stain in the giver’s color. In a practitioner’s aura (the visible coat of their own Essence, which is Aether refined in the soul) a thumb shows as a ribbon of somebody else’s hue at the edge, and anyone trained can spot it across a ring. A thumb on one of the unwoken, whose Soul Crystals never opened, usually shows as a mark on the skin, warm to the touch.
What it costs. The giver, almost nothing. The holder, whatever the terms were.
How it is beaten. Read the wording and fight what it leaves out. Failing that, a handful of bloodlines can take it off, and one of them is famous for it.
Example. Jory Tull, Stage III, a Green Sigil hunter, spends a season hauling water up a mountain for an old spirit who likes being carried to. It thumbs her, and her window now holds [Blessing: Cold Doesn't Mind You]. She walks through a cold gallery, a Titan-touched one, in her shirt, breaks masks her Stage has no business breaking, and sells them for a year’s wages. In the second winter she notices that she no longer feels the stove either, and that she has burned both hands to the bone without waking.
What One Can Grant
The law says out of a person’s natural reach, and the range is wider than most people dare ask for.


















































The grantWhat the window showsWhat usually goes unmentionedA rule about youOne flat sentence. [You will not drown.]Everything the sentence left out. This is the commonest kind and the most dangerousLevelThe number moves, and every reader will confirm it. A blessing is the one thing that can move Level without danger overcomeThe fighting that goes with those Levels is absent, and the body arrives ahead of its ownerA stat or severalA Primary (one of the Eight stats on the sheet) or a Sub-Stat jumpsIt is outside help, so it may lift a fighter past the two-step cap on self-boosts (see Stacking and Spending), and it adds no risk unless it was forced on the one receiving it. Whoever is holding it up can also let goA skill or a tongueA new rank on a trade or weapon skill, overnightSkills rise with use, and a skill that never rose has no habits under it. It works perfectly right up to the first surpriseA WellspringA harmonization with one of the sixty alchemical and spiritual transformations that shape how a soul uses Aether. It lands small, as any new one does, and years of mastery bring it upThe giver chose which oneA CatalystA Stage. The Catalyst is the one deed a Crystal demands before it will climb, and a thumb can supply it as a Draft can. A giver can hand over Level as well, or insteadA given Stage opens the door and no more. Held above the holder’s Level it stands Overgrown, spilling and reading low, until Level catches up, and it has no Release (a fighter’s staged power-up) until one is found and mastered by living its own CatalystWakingThe whole window opens, with Essence and Stage IThe Crystal woke to the giver’s knock and may answer to that knock for life. Measurewrights argue about this one, and the wise ones do it quietlyA grip on FateFate Mastery (how well a soul works the odds and conditions) let past the second rung, where everyone without a grip stops, up to the Stage’s own ceiling and never past it. Nothing else but a bloodline’s Work can manage itA grip is all it is. The holder still cannot reason out what they are holding, and the first pull can take most of a reserve and often fails. Whatever handed you the thread may be what it belongs to
Two things stand outside the list. Nothing a thumb gives is a vow: a vow is a person binding their own probability, small Fate that anyone can make, and its window shows the bargain and its terms in full because you wrote them. And a blessing does not reliably undo a death. The dead stay dead. A very great giver could in theory reverse one, a world-shaking event with a terrible price, and it comes back as a curse more often than not (see Cold Harrow, below).
Written and poured
The trade distinguishes two kinds, and the distinction pays for most of the wording-men’s lunches.
A written blessing goes through the Plane of Fate, the control of Attraction Force (the pull that makes a name, bond or vow take hold) and Obsession Force (the same pull when it refuses to let go), and through them of what the odds are allowed to do. It moves no strength to anyone, and it tells the world how things are going to fall around you. All spirits and all physical things have fates, so a writer has plenty to lean on. Most blessings are written, because writing is cheap, and a written line outlives its author unless the terms say otherwise.
A poured blessing skips Fate entirely. The giver hands over something real, a share of its own Essence or its own law, and the holder’s numbers rise because something was actually moved. It is honest in a way a written one seldom is, it costs more, and it tends to thin when the giver is far off and go out when the giver dies. Lords prefer this kind for their captains, and I invite you to think about why.
Who Can Give One
Anything spiritually stronger than you. The sum of the qualification is that the world listens to it first.















































GiverHow commonWhat they giveWhat they wantLesser spirits (of a ford, a hill, a Well’s edge, an old tree)Most of the blessings anyone meetsOne small rule within their own ground, often worded by something that has never met a personAttention, mostly. Offerings, a song, being carried to, somebody who remembers their nameSpirit Beasts and old things in dungeonsRare, and you have to survive the introductionA rule about the deep, a sense, a WellspringAn alliance. See Dungeons, where the advice is to be politeOld beings who remember (survivors of the Great Spirit War and the days when the Epochs walked)A handful in the worldAlmost anything, with terms written in a language that has lost its other speakersNobody who has gone looking has reported back in a form I would trustPeople of higher Temperance (a high-Stage practitioner, Temperance being the refining of the soul up the sixteen Stages)Most of what the powerful hand outStats, Levels, a Catalyst, a leashService, loyalty, a good jokeHigher spirits, World Spirits, TitansOnce or twice in a realm’s historyA people’s luck, a line’s nature, a kingdom’s riverTheir reasons are not on fileArchons and EpochsRarely, and it shakes the worldWhatever they meantWhen one acts, the survey maps are redrawn and the churches split. The Archives enter such events with a date and a long silence
For a person, the gap is what matters. In practice a giver needs at least three Stages over the one receiving, the same distance at which Pressure starts dropping people in the room. Under that the thumb will not hold past a night, and a good many sect elders have embarrassed themselves discovering this in front of a favorite student.
Consent is optional. A giver far enough above you needs no leave, and most great givers do not think to ask. A line can arrive while you sleep, while you are praying for something else, or because something passing through the valley liked your singing.
What a Giver Spends

The most insulting sentence in the Archives: a great giver spends almost nothing.

A written line pays for itself. A loaded die has no more strength in it than a fair one; the weight only settles which face comes up, and the throw was happening anyway. The stronger the soul, the more readily the Continuum (the standing order of the world, which measures every soul) takes its word, so at the top a thumb costs a sentence and at the very top it costs less than that.
A reader fresh from The Three Paths will object that Fate is the hardest road there is, that a real pull can empty a soul at Stage XII, and that I have just told him a woman did it with flour on her thumb. These are different acts. A pull reaches up and warps what the world has already arranged, out of the puller’s own hand and against the odds. A thumb sets a small weight on a page far below the writer, the holder’s own Attraction Layer, where the stronger soul’s word already carries, and it lets the throw fall. So the cheapness belongs to the gap and to nothing else. Narrow the gap and the bill climbs, as the table shows, and below the very top a line moves only what already has a way of happening. A heart can stop. A lancer’s horse can take a dislike to the lance.



































The gapWhat the giver feelsWhat it can carryThree or four StagesA hard morning. A real bite out of the reserve (the Essence a practitioner can spend), and a poured thumb may cost near half of it and a week in bedOne small rule, a skill, a stat held a step up for a seasonFive to eight StagesA good sneeze. The cost of lighting a coatA Level jump, a stat held up for years, a Catalyst for someone far belowMore than thatNothing they would notice, and they frequently do not noticeMost of the table above. Dame Rohese had eleven Stages on a pie man, and the pie was the larger expenseSpirits, on their own groundNothing, plus the pleasure of companyAs much as their ground holds. Off it they cannot hold muchArchons and EpochsNothing has been recordedThe cost lands on the world instead: on the weather, the Wells, the odds across a whole quarter. The bill goes to everyone else
It is that cheap, and every duke’s army is still not thumbed to the eyes, and the reasons make up the politics of the age. A thumb cannot be collected unless the terms say so, and writing terms that hold takes more care than most givers own. A fighter lifted past his natural reach is a rival you built by hand. A careless line can kill the holder or the giver’s whole plan, and the wording is on the giver’s head when it does. And every Moto in the north can read what you wrote. So thumbs are given sparingly and on a short rope, and they have become the most valuable thing a powerful person can hand out for free. Lords hold people they cannot out-fight through grain, land, debt and the Draft supply, and the thumb is the debt that sits on the sheet where its owner sees it every morning.
For the poor it is one of three roads, along with dungeon luck and guild patronage. People walk the shrine roads for years, leave offerings at every ford, haul water up mountains and sing to rocks, and it works often enough to keep the roads busy. Every shrine road has its false givers too, and a stranger with a good coat and a bright smile who presses your forehead for a silver mark is giving you a sore forehead.
The Line
The window tells the truth about the numbers. A blessing is a different matter, since the giver wrote the line, and the soul is only reading it back. A soul has no way of checking what somebody stronger has written on it, any more than a page can check a scribe.
How a line lies








































The methodThe lineWhat is actually happeningBy leaving things out[You will not drown.]True. It does not say who willBy flattery[Blessing: Beloved of the Hill]The hill will not let you leaveBy a false name[Blessing: Grace of the Saint of Sheafton]There is no saint, and the thing that signed her name has your addressBy a false number[Strike Force: A]B, and a thumb that makes the window read high until the fight in which it matters. Rare, because it takes a real writerBy changing later[Blessing: Favored]A line can be rewritten by whoever wrote it. It read differently yesterday, and the soul’s memory of yesterday may have been tidied tooBy saying nothing at allNo lineThe commonest curse in the Archives is the one that never showed. Assay, if you can afford it
This is separate from the other way a window can lie. A strong mind-worker, on the Wellsprings of memory, sleep and reflection, can make a window show false numbers or hide a line, and that is a violation with a cost, with Gnosis as the fair counter. A blessing’s lie has no such seam, because the line belongs there.
Reading one
Gnosis first, and it will mostly fail. A stronger Gnosis Perception reads a weaker Resilience Ward. A line wears the Ward of whoever wrote it, so nobody below the giver reads through it. Everyone else is estimating aloud.
Assay the holder. An assay reads what the soul is actually doing, and a line that says Ardency 2,400 on a soul the coil reads at 1,600 has told you something expensive. It says nothing about terms.
Test it, slowly, on something you can afford. Hold your breath in a bucket with a friend standing by before you trust the Tide-Mother.
Hire a wording-man. Every city with a court has a row of them, ex-advocates who read a line for a fee and tell you what it does not say. They are very good, and they have never once found the term that killed the client, and they will show you the clause in your contract that says so.
Ask what the giver eats. This is the oldest advice and still the best: learn what the giver wants, what it has done before, and what became of the last one.
In court. A court makes you swear to what your sheet shows, and lying under a proper oath costs you, because an oath is small Fate. A person who swears honestly to a line that lies is a question the lawyers have been fighting over for three hundred years, and the Waxgate assize has ruled both ways. The current reading is that you are bound to your own understanding of the words, which is why a wording-man will tell you never to read your line too closely before a hearing.
Terms and Fine Print
Every blessing has terms, which is the street’s word for what the line did not say. A vow shows its terms on the window. A blessing shows what the giver chose to show. These are the clauses the trade has learned to expect.













































The clauseWhat it doesThe usual signThe riderA thing you must keep doing: a shrine visited, a name kept, a meat not eatenYour numbers drop one morning and you cannot think whyThe collectionThe giver comes back for something. A service, a child’s first word, your Crystal at the endA polite visitor, decades later, who knows your mother’s nameThe heir clauseIt passes down, and the descendants never signed. This is how a lineage comes to carry a blessing, a mutation or a curse in its Inherited Traits (the laws a bloodline hands on)Everybody in one family has the same stain and the same bad luck with horsesThe exclusionNo other giver’s line will hold beside itThe second thumb will not take, or both go wrong togetherThe fenceIt only runs on the giver’s ground, or only off itYour great gift stops working forty miles from home, in a fightThe appetiteThe thing granted keeps growing past what you asked forYou wanted to be unafraid. You are now unable to beThe plain wordingThere is no trick. It does exactly what it says, forever, including when you wish it would stopDickon Sedley
When a blessing is a curse
A curse is often a blessing with terms you did not read, or a giver who does not care what you want. Nobody can tell at first, and some are both. The power on either side is the same power, written the same way and sitting on the same line, and most of the difference is how the holder feels about it at the time of asking. A few curses are laid on purpose, with malice and good penmanship. Far more are gifts from something that had never met a person, that found you charming, and that has since gone back to sleep.
Famous Thumbs
All of these are told in taverns and most of them are told wrong. The people are long dead, and their descendants have asked me not to go on about it.
Favor of the Tide-Mother. [You will not drown.] Sabra Haldane, a pilot on the bay at Alabaster, was thumbed by a sea spirit of the Drowned Parishes in 618 after a lifetime of leaving out fish. She went down with the Good Intent that autumn and walked up the harbor steps nine days later, breathing brine and in high spirits. Every captain on the coast wanted her aboard, and she made a great deal of money. By 640 she was the sole survivor of eleven wrecks. The line never said anything about her shipmates, and the Tide-Mother had been hungry for a long time and had worked out how to fish. The harbor board of Alabaster eventually paid her a pension to stay ashore, and she drew it for thirty years in a house with a very good view, watching the water with an expression nobody cared to interrupt.
The Road Remembers You. Piers Aldane, a courier on the salt road, got it from a milestone spirit for straightening its stone. He was never lost again, in fog, in the Scourge’s edge or blind drunk, and he carried the Bridgemarch mails for twenty years without one failure, in a yellow coat the whole road knew. The road remembered him for everyone. Anything hunting him, on any road, found the way as easily as he did. The bailiffs came first, then three wives, then something from the Verath Expanse that had once eaten his mule and had enjoyed it.
There Will Always Be an Averill at Sheafton. The Averills, a small and proud house of the Golden Hollow, were granted this by a hill they had built a very nice chapel on, and they had it carved over the door. It is entirely true. There has always been one. Exactly one. It took them three generations to see the pattern in the family tombs, since every heir who came of age did so in the same week the last one died, and no Averill who rode out of Sheafton ever arrived anywhere. The current Averill lives there still, in a beautiful house with gold trees all around it, and does not encourage visitors.
You Will Not Break. Captain Thorold Gatty bought this for the two hundred men of his free company from a hermit of Stage XIV, at the price of a sack of dried figs, before the fighting at Sorley Bridge in the autumn of 631. They did not break. They held when the Moot’s line collapsed on both sides of them, when the order to fall back came down, and when the order came a second time with a man running it. They stood in perfect dress under their green pennons and went on standing until none of them was alive, which took most of a day and an astonishing number of the enemy. They went into the trench at Sorley with the rest. The Long Barrow has been cleared sixty times since then, and what comes up out of it comes up in step, and the clearing crews will tell you that nobody has been close enough to ask what those windows say.
The Hills Are Listening. [Sing.] Something very large crossed the Slate Ridge one night in the 590s, heard a shepherd named Selwyn Hay at his evening song, and approved. His singing went to Paragon by morning, the top of the nine ranks, and the sound of it brought people weeping up the mountain from four valleys. He could not stop. He sang through meals and through the births of his children, he sang in his sleep, and he sang for sixty-one more years with a voice that never tired, and his wife learned to wear wax. The giver did not care what he wanted, and very probably never knew he wanted anything. Ridge shepherds still sing with their hands over their mouths.
The Undying Year. In Year 388 at Cold Harrow in the Long Fields, Annot Lorne’s husband died of a kicked-in chest, and she went up to the old stone on the hill and asked. Nobody knows what answered. He walked home that night with the bruise on him, and she wept for joy, and the whole village carried him round the green. Then nothing in the county died. No hen, no fly, no fever, no calf with a broken back, no man with his belly opened by a scythe. Wounds went on being wounds, and meat would not stop being alive on the hook, and the wheat stood and rotted and went on growing. It lasted nine months. There is an account of what the county smelled like by harvest and I will spare you. When the neighbors came with torches to burn the whole shire down, Annot Lorne went upstairs with a hay fork and did what she had to do to the man she had asked for. He was the first thing in that country to die in nine months, and everything else followed him before sunset. The Archives enter it as a rumor with a body count, and decline to say which giver acted. It is the reason for the line in every faith’s catechism about asking.
Taking One Off
There are four ways, and three of them are mostly unavailable.
The giver takes it back. Always possible, if the giver can be found, remembers, and can be persuaded, and each of those has defeated better people than you.
The giver dies. A poured thumb usually goes out with its giver, sometimes at a very bad moment. A written one usually does not, since the line is doing its own work by then, and killing a spirit to get out of its terms has a long and discouraging history.
A greater giver overwrites it. You now have a greater giver, and a new set of terms.
Hataraki. The Moto can do it, whoever gave it.
How Hataraki removes one
Hataraki is the Moto’s governing power, a real Fate Art, and it treats the world as a set of jobs. A blessing, to a Moto, is a job someone has assigned to the odds, and a job can be read, and a worker can be fired. There are few enough cases on the public record that the method is known mostly from what the holders report, and it runs in three motions.
The grips do not trade, so one Moto with one Work cannot do this alone: it takes two Works or two Moto, one to read and one to discharge.
The reading. The Work of Knowledge (Chishiki no Shigoto) reads the line for what it is, and for a moment the holder’s own window shows the whole of it, in plain words, usually for the first time. Everyone who has lived through this says it was the worst part.
[Blessing: Unbeaten]
[You will not be beaten.]
[Given in drink. Giver does not recall. No term.]

The naming. The remover states aloud what job this thing was given and by whom. Hataraki administers purpose, so it has to say what the purpose was, and this is why a Moto’s reading of your thumb is known across a battlefield as something to stop whatever you are doing and run from.
The discharge. A line that has become a false continuity, a thing going on past any good reason, falls to the Work of Ruins (Hametsu no Gō), which breaks only what is already hollow and does nothing at all to something sound. A line that sits in the soul as a stain goes under the Work of Purity (Junketsu no Gō), which makes a thing stand as it ought until the stain has nowhere to stay. A true gift, well held and fitted to its holder over decades, offers neither handle, and it takes longer, a matter of days, with the holder awake.
Taken back or taken off. The Moto keep the two apart. To take back is to return a line to its author, who feels it arrive, and that is a message. To remove is to end it where it stands.
What it costs. The Work presses the soul into a useful shape, and every Work carries a corruption vector, so that a Moto who has spent a long life firing the world’s gifts tends to grow very sure of what ought to be fired. The larger the giver, the heavier it runs. And a giver of any size knows when somebody has taken its pen away. The Moto themselves bill in obligations, and nobody has yet established what Little Tolland still owes.
What falls with it. Everything standing on the line comes down, at once.

























What the thumb heldWhen it comes offLevels and statsThey drop to what the person earned, and the body has to survive the differenceA given StageThe Crystal is left built to a shape it never earned and nothing holding it there. Most survive, and few fight againA rule that kept you aliveEverything it was holding off arrives. Dickon Sedley had thirty years of it waitingA heir clauseThe family’s stain lifts from the living, and only the living
It also works in a fight, which is the reason for the fear. A fighter who has built his whole life on the line in his window can lose it at the range of a raised voice, from someone he did not see come in. A few other bloodlines hold real Fate Arts, and what theirs can do to a thumb they have preferred to say for themselves.
What the Fate Path Can and Cannot Do
A Path is the layer of the Crystal a soul has learned to lean on, and there are three: Body, Spirit and Fate (see The Three Paths). The Fate Path leans on the Attraction Layer, and it is the hardest of them. It works on what has to be so before anything can happen, the law and construction of the world, and people fight and wage wars with it, though most of its walkers do their fighting with Range, Aura Pressure, presence and bonds. Its shallow water is bond, recognition and the kept word, and a midwife of forty years is standing in it without knowing. Far down it is recognized by what a soul refuses to let end, and people who have heard of Hataraki assume its walkers can do what the Moto do. Very few can, and the Path stays very hard all the way up. Some high-Stage masters reach real Fate Arts on it late, after decades of kept vows, and that is as much as most of them ever claim.
A written thumb is Fate work, whoever writes it, and it lands on the holder’s Attraction Layer, which every soul has. So a hitter who has never sworn anything can be thumbed as easily as a nun, and being thumbed puts nobody on the Path, any more than a loan makes you a banker. A giver who walks some other road, or none, is writing on the Plane of Fate with a borrowed hand, and this is one reason so many lines lie without anyone having meant them to.













































A Fate Path practitioner canA Fate Path practitioner cannotHold what should have ended. A vow past the point where it costs everything, a bond across a death, a claim for a century. This is the Path’s daily work, and the Crystal reads itBe made, at depth. No school can drill a deep one and no house can buy one. A Fate Essence Draft lends the touch, and it no more makes a Fate Path practitioner than a borrowed horse makes a cavalrymanFight with reach and weight. Range, Aura Pressure, presence and bonds are the Path’s everyday weapons: the room is heavy before they arrive, and everyone sworn to them fights betterWin a straight exchange. They take the smallest force bonus on the table, and outside a Domain the Body Path is king. Caught before a result arrives, a Fate fighter is an ordinary bodyPull a thread, on a rare day. A real pull moves what a blow depends on: a guard slips, a strap gives, and an ordinary cut is already there. Higher up it removes or assigns a prerequisite at a ruinous priceDo it cheaply, or surely. One lean on the odds can take a large share of the reserve and leave the body bleeding, it often fails, it shows a charge and a tell, and Dominion’s Fate Sub-Stat has to get past the target’s Persistence and ContinuityMove a field, once. Weather, supply, panic and the hour a column arrives, as a life’s masterwork at high Stage or a bloodline’s art. It may be done once in a war, and it may cost the person doing itMove what has no way of happening. A strap that is not wearing will not give, and a sound gate stands whoever pronounces collapse on itMake vows that weigh more. Anyone can bind their own probability. On this Path the binding bites harder, and a kept vow pays moreRemove someone else’s blessing. That is Hataraki’s. A master of the Path may read a weaker giver’s line, and may outlast it, and it stays on the sheetLean hardest on what they have a true claim on, their own vow, their own blood, a door they swore to keep. A claim gives Fate more to pull onDo what the Moto do, in nearly every case. Real Fate Arts are rare, mostly by bloodline, and considered incredibly overpowered. Nobody grips Fate bare, and the Works of Hataraki are that house’s inherited gripGive blessings more cleanly, at high Stage, because they know what the line is doing. A Fate Path giver writes the thumb the wording-men cannot faultReason their way in. Understanding is made of the thing it would be used against. A Measurewright can describe a thread for a lifetime and never lift oneSummon through Fate itself, in the rare few who have that art, without the limit a contract hasUndo a death. Nobody on the Path has done it, and those who tried with their whole lives are the people the Obsession Force passages of Fracture of Worlds are aboutAttach terms to an oath so that it holds without anyone present to enforce itLet go easily. The same grip that makes the Path makes Obsession Force its nearest neighbor. A Fate walker who will not release a thing becomes the thing that will not release
How a Measurewright Explains It
Magister Ysolde Corbet, of the Sealhall chair of Attraction, taught for thirty years that a blessing is a coupling. Attraction Force is a real term in the books, she said, as real as weight, and a stronger soul has a greater share of it in any place it has noticed. When such a soul takes note of you, your Attraction Layer (the Fate-Plane layer of the Crystal’s three, where the soul’s bonds are held) is pulled into step with its own, the way one clock on a wall will bring a second clock into its own swing through nothing more than the shared timber. A poured thumb is a true transfer, paid for in the giver’s Essence, and the books balance. A written thumb moves no energy at all, and only biases which of the things already possible comes to pass. She proposed to demonstrate this with dice before a full bench, using a blessed subject and a counted ten thousand throws.
The figures were superb. The subject rolled exactly as often as he should have, for nine thousand nine hundred throws, while her assistant’s ladder gave way, the tallow caught and the bench’s roof came down on the east side of the hall. The subject was not hurt, and when pressed he admitted that his line read [Nothing will prove it.] The Sealhall chair remains funded and argues its case from a different building. The Moto, asked to comment, said that the Magister had described the shadow of a job very accurately, and sent an invoice for the comment.
What They Call It


















































WhoThe wordThe argumentThe Guild Accord and its courtsA grant, a line, a third-party instrumentIt is a contract with an undisclosed party, and it ought to be registeredNorthern commons, crewsA thumb, thumbed; the termsLucky bastard. Read it againMotoKago (加護), divine protection; noroi (呪い) when it has gone badA thread laid on the Loom by a hand with no authority to lay it, in most cases. They would like you to know that they can see itMahuoGaho (가호)A gift, and every gift in the Dynasty is entered in the rolls with the date, and is taxedThe lineage hallsJiāchí (加持), the added supportA family asset. A thumb from an ancestor is added to the title, and the title gets longerKharven marketsA loan with no paperSomebody is carrying that on a ledger, and you are going to meet himThe MarrowkinA tally mark you did not cutIt goes in the book as owing, and the Tally keeps it as a debt against the bodyThe faithsGrace, favor, election, temptationEvery faith has its own answer to what the window is, and so to who may write on it. Real wars have come of this and more are on order
Read next: Vows and Oaths, for the line you wrote yourself.

the-magic-system/practice-and-institutio.title: Mechanica: Extraction Without Recognition
the-magic-system/practice-and-institutio.content:
Every other practice in the register asks. This one takes, and the difference is structural before anyone gets to the morals, and the Continuum (the whole lawful order of reality) records it in the ground.

January Street got its name honestly. For twenty-seven winters the roses along its gutters bloomed through the snow, fat and red and smelling of a June nobody else was having, and the whole tenement row sat with its windows open while the rest of the city froze, and strangers came from three towns to eat their dinner on its doorsteps. Then an Enforcement party in Division blue came down the cellar steps of the Ockley bakery with a warrant and two assay instruments, and found what the street had been keeping warm on: a thing of oak and copper the size of a mill wheel, going round and round in the dark, with one pipe of rose-colored light running out of the floor. The crowd was on them inside the hour, a thousand people with bakers’ peels and fire-irons. The serjeant lost an ear, and he stopped the wheel anyway. Every rose on January Street went black by morning, thirty-eight people froze before the thaw, and the old millwright who built it, Jonas Ockley, was found three towns away mending a sluice and could not see what the fuss was about. Walk there today. Nothing grows, your lamp burns the wrong way, and the roses’ smell comes up through the cobbles every January for no reason any Measurewright has been able to give.
The street never paid a copper for its roses. This page is about who did.
I. What It Actually Is
A lawful working imposes a boundary on a law that is already running, and the law does the work. The practitioner supplies the condition and pays for the privilege of setting it. Mechanica skips the condition.
An operator does not invoke a Wellspring (a governing idea that transforms how a soul uses Aether, in the scholars’ account one of sixty kinds of Aether with its own law), because invoking one requires Authorization (the glyph role naming a lawful channel) and Authorization is precisely what they do not have. They take finished output from a system that already did the conditioning, and route it. The law was conditioned by somebody else, or by a site, or by a thing that was alive at the time.
Which means Mechanica always has a donor. There is no such thing as an operator working alone, and every apparatus in the record has something on the other end of it.
II. The Three Practices
Extraction. Output taken from a Soul Crystal (the soul itself, which stores Essence and channels it outward) that is not the operator’s. The donor may be captive, purchased, dead, or unaware. This is the oldest form and the one the Statutes were written against, and its products are the most efficient in the register because a Crystal has already done the expensive part. It is also the plainest crime on the page. Essence is a soul’s own substance and the Core is the center of its identity, so what comes down the pipe is the donor, by the spoonful, and a donor who survives it is less of a person than went in.

Soul Splicing, Trait Collapse Engines, and the whole vocabulary the Accord uses in its prohibition schedules describe extraction and nothing else, which is why the schedules read as hysterical to anyone who has only encountered the second and third practices.

The butcher’s line. A monster’s core is in a way its Soul Crystal, and an alchemist who renders one into Essence Drafts is doing lawful work under the Standing Index, the Crystal Draw (draw being the bench’s old word for a lot taken off its source) every hunter’s hall lives on. A Crystal cut from a dead practitioner is the same procedure on a different table, the great crime, and it is why Grade IV on the Index has never balanced: every year more of it is sold than the lawful sources can yield, and the coil reads the two Drafts the same. The operator will tell you the donor was already dead. The law has never found that interesting.
Tapping. Output taken from a Wellspring site without the site’s participation. A lawful practitioner at a concentration harmonizes, which is a negotiation the current can decline. A tap does not ask. It opens a path from the vein into an apparatus and holds it open, and the site is pulled from without reciprocity until it stops giving. Nearly every tap on record sits on Wild ground, where there is heat and light to carry off. A Spirit-type site has no fire to give a pipe, and the few apparatus ever built to drain one were not built for anybody’s stair.

This is what produces a site running under Obsession Force (recognition curdled into taking). Priests call the corruption spiritual, and I will let them; a Measurewright calls it the physical consequence of sustained withdrawal against a current that was never consulted, and the site’s subsequent behavior toward visitors is the behavior of a system that has learned what people are for. Dungeons are alive and learning, whether or not they think, and scholars have stopped arguing about whether this one was taught.

Engine work. Built apparatus that performs extraction or tapping without a practitioner present. The operator’s skill is entirely in the construction, the device runs unattended, and this is the form that scales.

Engine work is why Mechanica is an economic problem as much as a criminal one. Extraction requires a monster. Tapping requires a monster with a workshop. An engine requires a competent millwright, a license he does not have, and a district that cannot afford a warden’s fee.
The Enforcement Division’s own figures, which it does not publish in this form, show that the overwhelming majority of Mechanica in the Concord is somebody’s heating.

III. Why It Leaves a Scar
The Four Glyph Roles are Authorization, Boundary, Direction and Sealing, and they are a sequence rather than a checklist. A working that never established Authorization cannot execute a lawful Sealing, because the Seal closes an operation against the warrant that opened it and there is no warrant to close against.
So a Mechanica working never ends. It is interrupted, abandoned, or exhausted, and the boundary it opened stays open.
Mechanica debt is the Continuum’s record of that unclosed operation. Nobody is punishing anybody and nothing is watching. An unsealed boundary is a persistent local condition, the field around it never returns to its prior state, and every subsequent working in that area is conditioned by a boundary nobody set deliberately and nobody can find.

Statute XXVI, Mechanica Irreversibility. The one damage in the register with no documented remediation. Concordia (the art of aligning many fields into one) can close a Hollowing (a region losing its capacity for lawful working) over years. Nothing closes an unsealed boundary, because closing requires a warrant and the whole point was that there was never one.

IV. What It Costs the Operator
Nothing, directly, and that is the entire problem.
Every lawful practice bills the practitioner. The speaking (a working cast live from the body) bills the body in the same scene. The cutting (a working inscribed in material) bills a season and a stone. The pouring (a working bottled as a Draft) bills provenance. Votia (working bought with a vow) bills the rest of a life. Mechanica bills the donor, the site, or the district, and the operator walks away with output they did not pay for.
This is the honest reason the Accord’s condemnation carries so little weight with the people who do it. A doctrine that says power must cost is being preached by the institution that sets the prices, and an operator heating a tenement off a tapped vein has a reply to that which nobody in the Division has ever answered in public.

The delayed bill. Operators are merely billed late. Sustained work in an unsealed field produces a documented syndrome: Shell clouding (the soul’s outer layer losing clarity) without corresponding output, Coherence (how closely a person’s stated Path matches how they live) falling with no change in conduct, and Traits that begin flickering in the absence of Essence Starvation (running below a tenth of reserve).
The Crystal is being conditioned by boundaries it did not set. The operator’s own architecture starts obeying the mess they are standing in. Renderers can identify a long-term engine man on the table by the state of the Shell alone, and several of them will not say so on a record.

V. Reading a Site That Has Been Worked
Residue that does not disperse. Ordinary Aetheric Residue thins on a schedule set by local density, toward a floor it never passes. Mechanica residue holds undiminished, because the operation that produced it never closed and is in some sense still producing it.
The pull that does not answer. A lawful practitioner at a tapped site finds Harmonics (the stat that governs pulling Aether from the environment) costs elevated for no visible reason. They are working against a gradient somebody else established and left running.
The wrong quiet. Dead ground would at least be honest. A worked site reads as ordinary ground with one thing missing, and most surveyors identify the absence about a minute after they should have.
Instruments disagree. The coil (the assay instrument a practitioner stands inside) reads a field; the assay fork reads a density; the two do not reconcile, and the discrepancy is the size of what is being taken. This is the only reliable detection method and it requires two instruments and someone who can be bothered to compare them.
VI. Enforcement, and Why It Fails
The Enforcement Division is real, funded, and armed, and it prosecutes extraction with genuine ferocity. It prosecutes tapping when the site belongs to somebody with standing. It does not meaningfully prosecute engine work, and corruption has little to do with the reasons.
An engine is a device in a cellar. Finding it requires the two-instrument comparison, performed on the right street, by a searcher who has a reason to be there. Removing it turns off a district’s heat in a month with a name. And the prosecution requires proving who built it, in a trade where the millwright is three towns away and the householder genuinely does not know what is under the floor.

The Division’s internal position, stated once in a report that was not circulated: enforcement against engine work is enforcement against poverty, performed with a warrant, by men who can see that perfectly well.

VII. The Part the Accord Does Not Discuss
The Concord’s chartered Cores, each of them a dungeon somebody cleared and now holds, are licensed, sealed and lawful, and their Authorization is held institutionally rather than personally. A householder warming her stair off a warden who fills at a chartered Core has never warranted anything in her life.
The Accord’s position is that the company holds the warrant and the work runs under it, which is coherent, and which is also the same structure as engine work with a license on top.

The distinction the Accord draws is that the chartered sites were harmonized with rather than tapped, at the founding, by practitioners named in the founding instruments. Several of those instruments are four hundred years old. Two are known to be forgeries. The Division that would investigate the third has been reorganized twice since the question was last asked in writing.

Nobody involved thinks they are damned. The householder is warm, and the neighbors call it “the warm” when they are cold and stolen work when they are angry. The millwright was paid. The Division man knows what turning it off does. All three have a reasonable position, and the ground goes on carrying the argument.
Read next: Reference and Craft, the last shelf, which you consult and do not read.

the-magic-system/practice-and-institutio.filePath: The Magic System/Practice and Institution/On Walking Into the Current — Wellspring Encounter and Recovery.md
the-magic-system/practice-and-institutio.title: On Walking Into the Current — Wellspring Encounter and Recovery
the-magic-system/practice-and-institutio.content:
A Field Register of Wellspring Encounter, Survival, and Recovery · Second Edition
Guild of Measurewrights, under the Hexagonal Oath, in concurrence with the Research & Archives Division and the Voyager-Era Survey Corps (Retired)

The current was always running. The question was never whether you would find it. The question was whether you would notice before it found you.
Voyager-era survey maxim, attributed to the third Chainward expedition

Surveyor-Major Osric Tallant of the Chainward service was explaining the correct way to pitch a tent, at Cold Kettle Hollow, in full sun, when a bolt of bottle-green lightning left his right hand in the middle of a sentence and took the top off a pine. He looked at the pine. He told the party it had been a demonstration. By nightfall he had given six more demonstrations, each larger than the last, the scorched trees smoking around the camp in a ring and his coat, which had been a respectable plum for twenty years, gone green to the shoulder, and he was happier than anyone had ever seen him, explaining at the top of his voice that a man at last understood his own gifts. His second, a clever young Magister, went forward to read the source, and that is the last the record has of her. It was the porter who ended it. Wat Nettle had carried the tent poles for nineteen seasons, he had noticed that the Major’s nose was bleeding and that the Major had not, and at dawn he knocked him down with a tent pole, tied him over a mule, and walked him out of the valley by voice, saying out loud at every step what was actually there: that’s a rock, sir, that’s a birch, that’s your own hand. Tallant lost two fingers and kept the harmonization. He mourned that valley for the rest of his life, and he wrote the preface to the first edition of this register, and he never once named the porter.

The Sixty Wellsprings, with their encounter types and density scale, are written for practitioners who understand the system and are approaching concentrations deliberately. Most Wellspring encounters in unmapped territory are not deliberate. They are accidents.
The surveyor steps across a threshold they did not see, and the first indication that they have entered a concentration is the concentration’s effect on their body or their mind or both.
This register is written for the accident.
A warning to the confident reader. Confidence is a Spirit-type early symptom. If you are reading this document and feel certain you would recognize the onset, you are describing exactly the state in which surveyors fail to recognize it.

A note on words, for the new reader. A Wellspring represents an alchemical and a spiritual transformation: it is the governing idea that changes how a soul uses Aether, a lens set on magic already potent, and the scholars’ account of it is sixty different types of Aether that affect the Soul Crystal (the soul itself) differently. A concentration is a place where one of them pools, thick enough to act on whoever is standing in it, and surveyors call the way it moves through such a place the current. Rich ground fills a practitioner faster, and this page is what happens when the ground is richer than you are. Most concentrations of any size have a dungeon around them or will shortly, and monsters move across the whole Inner World, so an encounter in the field rarely stays the only thing happening to you.
A harmonization caught by accident is as real as one got at a school’s rites, out of a Draft, from a blessing or by birth. It starts small, like any of them, and it reaches double only with years of mastery on its home Path, and half again at most away from it. Surveyors who come out convinced they have doubled overnight are running a Spirit-type symptom.
The Onset Profiles
What each encounter type does to the body in the first thirty seconds.
Wild-Type Onset
The body knows first. The feet report a surface that does not match what the eyes see. The weight of the pack shifts. A tool in the belt resonates at a frequency it should not carry. Metal tastes wrong against the teeth. The air pressure changes without altitude change. Sound arrives at the wrong speed, or does not arrive at all from directions where it should.

The Crystal is unaffected. Gnosis reads normally. The Shell is stable. This is the critical diagnostic: if your own internal architecture feels normal and the world feels wrong, the concentration is Wild-type.

Response time is generous. Wild-type onset is perceptible before it is dangerous, because the physical anomalies are legible to the untrained body. You do not need Gnosis training to notice that rocks are floating. You need functioning eyes and the willingness to believe what the eyes report.

The common failure is rationalization. The surveyor sees an anomaly and explains it away, because the human inclination when the ground behaves strangely is to assume the ground is normal and the perception is wrong.
In a Wild-type concentration the perception is correct and the ground is lying. Trust the body.

Stay anyway and the Crystal stops being unaffected. A Wild Wellspring is a thing in the world, and a soul that lingers beside it starts shaping its Essence around that thing, which is how a harmonization is caught here: slowly, with plenty of warning, and with everyone in the party able to see what you are becoming.
Spirit-Type Onset
The Crystal knows first, and the Crystal does not report to the conscious mind at the speed the conscious mind requires.
The first symptom is physiological, and it comes before anything you could call a perception. Thermal change in the hands or face with no external heat source. A sudden emotional shift, grief or elation or rage, that does not connect to any stimulus you can identify. An involuntary discharge, a technique half-forming in the Shell without the practitioner having decided to cast it. Nosebleed. The headache behind the eyes specific to Gnosis overload. The taste of your own Essence in the back of the throat, which most practitioners describe as metallic and which experienced surveyors describe as the taste of the Wellspring itself.

The landscape is unchanged. Trees are trees. Stone is stone. Sky is sky. Nothing in the environment is wrong. The instruments read normal.
You are the instrument that is reading wrong, and you frequently will not recognize this, because the Crystal’s activation feels, from the inside, like your own decision.
This is the critical danger. A Spirit-type concentration makes no attack. It authors.
The practitioner begins producing effects they believe are their own, because the Crystal is the origin of all their effects and the Crystal is the thing being activated.
The fire does not fall from the sky. The fire comes from the practitioner’s own Shell, and the practitioner, feeling the fire leave their body, concludes that they chose to produce it. A spiritual Wellspring has no fire to give. What leaves the Shell is the person’s own Essence, shaped by whatever they have already tempered on and driven out by a soul that is being changed.

Response time is narrow. The window between onset and commitment (the point at which the Crystal has been retuned enough that you can no longer distinguish your native architecture from the concentration’s influence) is measured in seconds at Active Concentration and is functionally zero at Veil-Thin and above.

The surveyor who hesitates during a Spirit-type onset to confirm their reading is the surveyor who has already been retuned.

The common failure is self-trust. By the time they suspect the effects are not their own, the effects have been running long enough that the distinction is no longer available to them. The Crystal that would make the distinction is the Crystal that has been compromised.
Fate-Type Onset
Nothing reports at all. The landscape looks normal and the instruments read normal. The feet agree with the eyes, Gnosis reads clean, the hands are the temperature they were, and there is no taste in the throat. The first thirty seconds of a Fate-type encounter are the most comfortable thirty seconds in this register.
What changes is how the week goes. Luck goes strange: a mule that has never gone lame goes lame on the one morning it matters, and the same man draws the short straw three times running. Oaths bite: a cook who swore at breakfast he would sooner lose a thumb than carry that kettle another league is short a thumb by the following noon, and nobody can quite say how. Strangers keep meeting: the peddler on the ridge turns out to be owed money by the guide’s brother, and the woman at the next ford knew the peddler. And the surveyor’s plans keep working out, in ways the surveyor did not plan.

Neither the body nor the Crystal’s working layers have anything to tell you, because this current works on the Attraction Layer, the part of a soul that holds its bonds, oaths, claims and odds.
The critical diagnostic is repetition. If your body feels normal, your Crystal feels normal, the world looks normal and you are on your third coincidence of the day, the concentration is Fate-type.
A Fate-type concentration makes no attack and authors nothing. It collects.

Response time is long and useless. You have days, sometimes weeks, and almost nobody spends them, because a strange run of luck is a story you tell at dinner and no one has ever withdrawn a survey over a good story.
The common failure is the lucky streak. The surveyor whose plans keep coming off is the last person in the party who wants to leave, and the debts come due after they have made camp on the strength of it. Stay anyway and what you carry out will not show as a new color in the Shell. It will show as a bond you did not have when you walked in, to someone you have not met yet.
Medium-Type Onset
Both report simultaneously, and neither report is trustworthy.
The stream is flowing the wrong direction and childhood memories are surfacing uninvited. The light is bending around a clearing and Gnosis is suddenly reading things it has never been able to read. The air pressure has dropped and the emotional state has shifted.

Both the environmental changes and the internal changes are real, and you cannot determine which is causing which, because both are being driven by one current that crosses the Veil threshold every cycle.
The stream flows wrong because the current is altering local law. The memories surface because the same current is activating the Crystal’s Anamnesis architecture.
Both are symptoms of one cause operating on two planes, and you have no instrument that reads both planes at once unless you are a Ketsumyōgan bearer or a Transference-trained Bifold Perception specialist.

A Medium current is at home on the Plane of Fate as well, so there is often a third report coming, days late, in the form described above.
Response time is the worst of the four. The body says the world is wrong. The Crystal says the body is wrong. Both are correct. The surveyor inside a Medium-type concentration at Active density has lost their reference frame, and restoring it requires an external observer standing outside the effect radius.
The common failure is confusion mistaken for illness. They sit down. They wait for the symptoms to pass. The symptoms do not pass, because they are harmonization in progress and no illness at all, and sitting down inside the concentration gives the current more time to complete the process.
The six Medium grounds
A Medium site runs one law, and that law works on the ground and on the delver’s Crystal along the same line. A site never mixes two. Each of the six reads this way:








































WellspringThe groundThe delverPhreatisWater runs the wrong way and pools where it should notMemory surfaces unasked, the way water rises in a wellLuminalisLight bends and sightlines lieGnosis over-reads and finds meaning that is not thereAnamnesisThe ground keeps its past and shows itThe delver’s own past wakes and crowds the presentFixatioWhat changes stops changing back: a bent door stays bent, a footprint staysBonds and habits set for good, including the ones formed inside the siteMortalisThe dying are held at the gate and cannot finishThe living drift toward the gateAurevaneNothing scatters: no shade, haze or fog, sightlines carry for miles, and every lamp and every coat is a beaconNothing can be held in: every intent leaves the delver exactly as meant and is read by everyone near, and the eyes, over-resolving, go first
The cost of standing in one is the Medium row of the Tier Ladders. The way out is the one above: an observer or an anchor outside the radius, which the law cannot reach, gives the delver a fixed point to read against.
The Exposure Curve
What happens after the first thirty seconds. You have not withdrawn. You are still inside.
Active Concentration · involuntary harmonization. See the encounter types and density scale in The Sixty Wellsprings for compatible and incompatible outcomes.
Veil-Thin Nexus · planar bleed.

Bifold Perception onset: the Soul Plane perceived simultaneously with the Physical. You have not been trained for this. Objects appear as structure and soul-signature at once; people as body and Crystal at once. The thinning is not selective, and Gnosis is not built for the volume.
Involuntary Soul Drift: your position on the Soul Plane dissociates from your position on the Physical. Practitioners describe it as being in two places at once while knowing that both places are real.
Echo Beast manifestation: the concentration’s consequence, rather than its product. Unprocessed grief, rage and trauma given temporary autonomous form by the inter-planar conditions the concentration has created.

Wellspring Core · law replacement.

A warning about the word. In common speech any worked site is a Core, meaning a dungeon somebody cleared and now holds, and porters will tell you cheerfully that they have sat beside a dozen. On this register a Wellspring Core means the innermost and densest class of concentration, and the two usages have killed people who heard the wrong one.
Everything inside the Core obeys the Wellspring’s law, including the surveyor, and their previous architecture persists only as a structural memory that the Core’s law is not interested in consulting.
Every surveyor recovered from Core exposure describes it identically: they felt no change happening to them. They felt like they had always been the thing the Core was making them.
The change was experienced as truth. The recovery, paradoxically, is experienced as loss.

Recovery Protocols
Wild-type · Withdraw. The body is reliable. Walk in the direction that feels most normal; anomalies decrease with distance from the core. When the ground behaves correctly and the tools stop resonating, you are out. Then run a standard Wellspring inventory: if a new harmonization has appeared, it was acquired during exposure.
Spirit-type · Withdrawal requires external assistance. The Crystal that would tell you which direction is safe is the Crystal that has been retuned. A Spirit-exposed surveyor self-navigating is navigating with a compass that has been re-magnetized.

The external observer talks the exposed surveyor out by voice, confirming each step against observable reality.
With no observer available: move in the direction that feels least comfortable, because the concentration produces comfort toward the core and discomfort toward the exit. This is unreliable. It is better than the alternative, which is staying.

Post-exit assessment requires a Gnosis specialist. The self-report cannot be trusted, because the Crystal that would produce the self-report has been altered. An external reader performs a full inventory and compares against the pre-deployment baseline.
Fate-type · Withdraw, and do not take leaving for being out. Distance ends the pull and does nothing about what has already been bound. Leave by the route that has been going badly, since the current favors the road toward its center. On the way out swear nothing, promise nothing and accept no gift, favor or courtesy you would have to repay.

The external reader works from the log and the baseline, and the question is simple: what does this person owe, and whom, that they did not owe at the gate? Anything on the list that did not come in with them came out of the ground.
A bond caught this way is a real bond, and it does not lift because the Guild has filed it. Some are paid off, some are outlived, and a few run on after the surveyor stops believing in them. This is normal. It is also why the older surveyors do not take lifts from strangers for a year afterward.

Medium-type · Treat as Spirit-type until proven otherwise. The unique complication is memory contamination: Phreatis or Anamnesis content can introduce memory material the surveyor experiences as their own. Post-exit they may report memories of events that did not happen to them, or fail to report events that did. Disentangling requires a Mnemata specialist and is frequently incomplete.
Core · Transference-assisted re-anchoring by a specialist outside the radius. Requires Stage IX or above; no field surveyor carries the training.

What the field surveyor needs to know: it works, and it is slow. The surveyor who comes back will describe it as losing something they valued. What they valued was the Core’s law, which felt, while they were inside it, more true than their own identity. They will mourn the law. This is normal. It is also temporary, provided the re-anchoring was performed competently.

The Unawakened in the Field
Everything above assumes the reader has a woken Crystal. Nine people in ten standing inside a concentration do not.
A survey party is a practitioner or two and eight other people. Porters, guides, mule-handlers, the cook. Settlements sit downwind of concentrations for generations without anyone in them ever being screened. A current does not check for a Crystal before it acts, and the register has been written for a decade as though it did.
An unwoken soul’s Shell is sealed and cannot phase-lock, so no harmonization occurs. This is the whole of the good news. The Essence Core is present, furnished, and fully exposed.
Wild-type. Identical in every respect, and the unawakened are frequently better at it. The body is the instrument, the instrument is unimpaired, and a porter has no Gnosis reading to argue with when the ground starts lying. Experienced survey leads have known for years that the man who says this is wrong first is usually the one carrying the tent poles, and the published curriculum does not mention it.
Spirit-type. The onset is physiological and it arrives on schedule. Thermal change in the hands, an emotional shift with no stimulus behind it, nosebleed, the taste in the back of the throat. What does not arrive is the involuntary discharge, because the sealed Shell cannot express it.

This is worse, and in one specific way. A practitioner in a Spirit-type onset vents. The load leaves through the Shell as a half-formed working, badly, expensively, and it leaves.
An unawakened soul has no exit. The current drives the Essence Core and the Essence Core has nowhere to put what it is being given. The load stays, and it goes on staying after the party has withdrawn and made camp and gone home.
The recorded presentation is a porter who was cheerful on the outbound leg and is never cheerful again. It reads as ordinary hardship and it is filed as ordinary hardship.

Fate-type. Identical, and this is the one current a sealed Shell does nothing about. Every soul has an Attraction Layer, the unwoken included, and a porter’s oaths are as good as a Magister’s. Nobody in the party will connect the thumb to the kettle. A village on Fate ground is a place with a reputation: marriages that arrange themselves, a family whose debts always find them, and a market where nobody has gone back on a handshake in living memory because of what happened to the last man.
Medium-type. Fully applicable and fully undocumented. Anamnesis and Phreatis content acts on the Essence Core, and the Essence Core is what an unawakened soul has. Memory contamination in an unawakened bearer is indistinguishable from confabulation to every physician who will ever examine them.
Long exposure. Residence at Active Concentration or above, sustained over seasons rather than hours, produces a Trait by Wellspring Convergence. It is real, it is lawful, it is heritable, and it is in a body nobody will screen. Villages downwind of a concentration produce a family that has been strange for six generations, and the strangeness is a Wellspring’s law running quietly in people who have no word for any of this.
Recovery. There is none written. Transference-assisted re-anchoring assumes a Shell to anchor. No protocol exists for an unawakened soul returned from a Wellspring Core, and the Guild has never commissioned one, because the recovery ledger records practitioners and the practitioners are the ones the Guild is liable for.

The hole in Protocol IV. Pre-deployment baselines are taken for team members with woken Crystals. Nobody has ever taken one for a porter.
Which means that for the entire Voyager Era there has been no instrument, anywhere, capable of establishing what a survey did to the people carrying it. Nobody conspired at this. It is a filing category that was never opened, and it has been doing the work of a conspiracy for a hundred and forty years.

Standing Field Protocols

















































#ProtocolIAssume Spirit-type until proven otherwise. The cost of treating a Wild site as Spirit is unnecessary caution. The cost of treating a Spirit site as Wild is a surveyor whose Crystal has been forcibly rewritten before they identified the perimeterIIMonitor the surveyor, not the landscape. A surveyor trained to watch the ground will miss Spirit-type and Medium-type onset. A surveyor trained to watch their own body will not. Neither of them will catch a Fate-type onset, which is what Protocol IX is forIIIDeploy in pairs with one member outside the estimated effect radius. The interior surveyor reports what they experience. The observer confirms or contradicts. The contradiction is the diagnosisIVCarry pre-deployment Crystal baselines for every team member. Without a baseline the assessor cannot distinguish native architecture from the concentration’s additions. Taken before entering unmapped territory, not after the first day’s marchVDo not carry Object Wellsprings into Site Wellsprings. A surveyor wearing a forged ward and stepping into an Active Concentration is asking two Wellspring laws to share a Shell that was built for oneVIWithdrawal is no retreat. Marking the perimeter from safe distance completes the survey. The Guild has buried enough surveyors who decided that the interior documentation could not waitVIIReport Medium-type sites as priority. A surveyor who identifies one and reports location, density and dominant Wellspring has done more for the survey than a surveyor who maps the interior of a Wild-type site that was going to be found anywayVIIIWatch the unawakened members of the party. They will not report onset, because they have no vocabulary for it and no reason to think it applies to them. A porter who stops talking is a reading. Baseline them before departure by any means available, even if it is only a note on how they wereIXKeep a dated written log on every site that reads normal: who was met, what was sworn, what fell out well and what fell out badly. A Fate-type site reads as nothing on every instrument and reads plainly on paper. Three coincidences in a day is a readingXSwear nothing on ground that has not been typed: no oaths, no wagers, no promises, no courtesies that could be taken for one. The oath sworn lightly on Fate-type ground is the one that holds
Read next: Mechanica, for the people who take from the current without asking.

the-magic-system/practice-and-institutio.title: Practice and Institution
the-magic-system/practice-and-institutio.content:
Who may practice, where their capacity came from, what their guild will trust them with, what money can and cannot buy them, how they are trained, and what the practice is set against.
Any stallholder in any market will sing you the school song she hates most, badly, with the words changed, and then charge you for the noodles. Practitioners are common and everybody has opinions. These pages are the machinery behind the opinions, set down by the archivists who keep having to explain them.


The Gate: Who May Learn Magic Why nearly everyone carries a Crystal, why about one in ten is taught to wake it, who holds the door on the rest of the lesson, what a purse does once you are through it, and why a Magister and a Natural cannot agree about the girl who burned the Bureau’s tent.
The Standing and the Title: Guild Titles as Trust The nine titles every guild shares, what each one lets a stranger hand you, and the two other names you carry.
Training and Sects Schools, disciple ranks, seclusion, the tournament ladder, and what a sect teaches that money cannot buy.
Blessings and Curses What a thumb grants, who can press one on you, how the line on your window lies, and who can take it off again.
Vows and Oaths Small Fate, anyone’s to make: what the window shows, what lands when you break one, what your own denial does after, and what you risk when a court hands you the book.
Who Pays for the Lamp: The Living Crafts The lamp-wardens, ward-cutters, hedge-workers and the keepers of cleared dungeons, who pays them, and who can refuse.
On Walking Into the Current — Wellspring Encounter and Recovery What happens to a body that meets a Wellspring without meaning to.
Mechanica: Extraction Without Recognition The practice everything above defines itself against.


Back to The Magic System. Next shelf: Reference and Craft.
