the-magic-system/reference-and-craft/the.title: The Practitioner's Field Manual — The Forge
the-magic-system/reference-and-craft/the.content:
Being a working register of what each kind of work can and cannot do, and the Forge by which Abilities and Techniques are built at speed

Craft Companion, the Seventh Guide
Governs how magic is written. Does not govern what magic is.
“Ask what he is permitted to do with the power he has, and what it takes out of him when he does. The size of it comes last.”

Oswin Crumb, baker of Karrowgate, a Journeyman, Stage III (third on the soul’s sixteen-step ladder), had a heat trade worth two copper an oven. He lit ovens. He had lit every oven on Dyers’ Lane for twenty-three years with the same small, smoky orange push from the same two fingers, and on the morning the bailiff’s men came about the arrears, three of them, in good boots, with his daughter’s name on their paper, he put those two fingers against the first man’s breastbone and did the same thing, with the same spoonful of Charge (raw Aether, packed in the Shell and never refined), all at once.
The shutters of Dyers’ Lane left their hinges in order, flour hung in the street like a snowfall going sideways, and a tray of rolls was found on the church roof. The bailiff’s men lay in the road with their eyebrows on and their boots shining and not one burn among them, and every one of them had drowned in his own lungs. Crumb himself never heard another word from anybody. A Measurewright (a sworn measurer of the Guild) walked in from the Assize before the dust had settled, ate one of the surviving rolls, and wrote on a slate, in a hand that got larger as she went: Same fuel. Same Charge. Entirely different corpse.
That slate is the Delivery Rate Law, below, and this manual is what the Guild’s compilers did about it. A word to whoever opens it: everything here is about how a working gets onto the page and earns its place there. I have kept the arguments in, because they are better than the conclusions.
The Two Layers
Nothing in the Continuum (the lawful fabric of reality) became more complicated. A second layer accumulated on top of the first, the two were carried as one thing, and the second layer is accounting.

















LayerWhat it isThe Generative LayerConcept → Affinity → Ability → Technique, seen through a Wellspring (the lens the soul has tempered on) and going out by a Path (the layer the Crystal leans on) in a [[The Magic System/Reference and Craft/FormsThe Accounting LayerStage and its rank, Level, the stat numbers, Mastery (one rung per road, read from Level under the Stage’s ceiling, each setting how much power survives the trip through its own layer), Class (the name a soul is offered at Glory), skills on the nine ranks, the Grades of gear and beasts, EU (Essence Units, the measure of a reserve), yield (η, the share of spent power that does its work, as a distillation has its yield). This settles what a practitioner can actually do and who wins. It answers how much. Load it before writing, never abandon it while writing, and put its numbers on the page only through a mouth, an instrument, a document, a private count or the bearer’s own window; its names may stand in any sentence

Both layers stay open. The generative layer decides what happens; the accounting layer decides whether it could have.
Every outcome should trace to a specific row, and the working notes should say which. What the reader receives is behavior and body, and the window right after it. What the numbers do is make sure the behavior was earned.

The Sheet, the Class and the Climb
The accounting layer as it looks from inside the person carrying it.
The window. The Soul Crystal is the soul and the Continuum measures it, so a window is the soul reporting its numbers to its owner, in their own tongue, unseen by anyone else. Write them often and in detail, fights included, for damage, skill gains and reserve. Each sits on the page as its own text block, following the blow it reports, and the prose around it stays body first. It shows numbers, ranks, percentages, bars and Level. EU, AU/s and yield stay in the notes.
[Reserve: 41%  ████░░░░░░]
[Cracked rib, left side. Breath short.]
[Skill risen: Haggling, Apprentice]

A called Release or Domain fills the window with its name and what changed, and a timer bar drains. Pressure is felt in the room first, and then the window reports it.






































































On the sheetHow it movesWhat to do with itEight Primaries, as totals, with no letter on a personLife spends most stat points by what the person does; a few are theirs to place at each StageThis is what a normal look shows. Ask what the life has been, and the spread followsSub-StatsAppear when used or when they moveThe full set remains to study. Show one the moment it mattersLevelAnything hard and real, danger overcome above all. Killing something stronger moves it more than a hundred weak kills. It holds a Stage open once the Catalyst is met, and places MasteryCrews argue over who got the kill. Write the argumentRace and lineageFixed, and on the lineThey shape base stats, what comes easily, and which classes and Wellsprings suitPathRecognized off how the person has lived, never picked: Body, Spirit or Fate, each standing as Mastered, Walked (three parts in ten of their practice or more) or StudiedAsk what they have spent the years on. Two Paths take about two and a half times as long at three-quarters of the force bonus each, and leave real holes at times; three take about six times as long, past a mortal span, and the world looks down on anyone tryingClassA name offered at Glory, with Mastery I, fitting how the person has lived. Evolves each time the lead Mastery risesEach evolution gives one move and a lean on where stat points go. It is a name, never a number. The one wild concept stays the person’s own; no class hands it outMasteryOne rung per road, I to V and Ω, read from Glory: Body for matter, Spirit for souls and meanings, Fate for odds and conditions. The Stage sets the ceiling and Level places the soul under itSets the yield for workings through its own layer, on one table, a read rung overriding the field average and a card’s own figure governing its holder. A Walked second road reads a rung behind until mastered, a Studied one two behind and capped at II. Fate stops at II without a grip, a bloodline’s Work or a blessing. The folk names (Muridic, Confessor, Knotwright and the rest) are the old ladders’ words, still saidSkills, on the nine ranks (Initiate, Apprentice, Journeyman, Adept, Expert, Master, Grandmaster, Archmaster, Paragon)Rise with use. A trade has no cap; a fighting skill never ranks above its owner’s own Stage rankDrafts, runes, tags and chants are skills. Anyone can pour; the cutting, tags, chants and spoken workings want a woken Crystal. A guild’s title says how far the hall trusts the skillTraits, with no levelWork at the lead road’s Mastery, and at their base below GloryThe Four Reflections and their laws are untouched; Release and Domain are the Trait escalatingTechniquesShow no level. Take a bigger name when they jumpA technique is a named thing done with a skill. The old name stays in useBlessingsTheir own line, written by the giverThe line can lie. A curse is often a blessing with terms nobody readVows and crew bondsA vow shows its bargain and terms; a real bond shows as a line, with the crew’s barsEarned in play, and a broken one shows at once
The climb and the purse. Drafts and blessings can supply a Catalyst, and Stages can simply be bought, so the wealthy are stronger because they are wealthy. The great houses hoard the top Drafts; the poor rise by dungeon luck, guild patronage and blessings. A bought Stage opens the door and no more: the soul stands Overgrown until Level catches up, a Release must still be found and mastered by living its own Catalyst, and sects teach what money cannot buy, Releases, Domains, techniques, skills and the rites for their Wellspring. When a character’s Stage is higher than their fighting, that gap is a scene.
Reading anyone else. A stronger Gnosis Perception reads a weaker Resilience Ward. Everything else is an estimate said aloud, and people can hide or fake it, which gives every fighter on the page a reason to lie about their numbers and every opponent a reason to test them.
The Rule for Invention Under Fire

Abilities are character architecture: a root idea the Crystal (the Soul Crystal, the soul itself, which works magic) has internalized over years. Cozbi is Antithesis. Krothar is Binding. Sodoku is Ruin.
These are never invented inside a scene. If a fight appears to require a new Ability, the fight is wrong, or the scene stops and the Ability is pitched properly.
Techniques are moves: a specific repeatable application within an Ability already established, a named thing done with a skill. These may be invented at speed, mid-scene, without stopping, provided they are built through the Forge and logged afterward.
Invent freely downward, never upward. A new Technique under a known Ability is craft. A new Ability under a known character is a decision about the whole person wearing a technique’s coat.

The Forge
Before the first step, the concept. A kit starts as one wild idea you can explain in a breath, soup, debt, doors, boredom, anything, so long as the character can push it somewhere terrifying. Character first, then the concept, and only then the lens, the Wellspring and the glyph that explain it and the Path it goes out by; the Sixty and the Glyphs stay fixed and the idea finds its place among them. A major character starts with three to five named moves and adds one when a fight or scene earns it. A fighter may invent and name a new move in the middle of a fight, and it stands from then on. The Forge below takes that idea and makes it hold.
Seven steps at the desk. Steps one through four are structural and cannot be skipped. Five through seven are what separate a technique from a special effect.





































StepWhat it demands1 · The ideaName it from what the idea actually does in the soul and the world, not from the feeling it evokes. A grief-working that rots a body works on flesh. A grief-working that removes the memory of a face works on mind. Name the bench operation it performs (calcination, dissolution, separation, conjunction, fermentation, distillation, coagulation or sublimation) and the flaw it cannot hold. This step is idea-first and it will offend intuition roughly a third of the time. Follow it anyway2 · VerbOne verb from that idea’s verb table. A technique that uses three verbs is three techniques badly stapled together3 · RatePush or shatter. This single decision determines what the corpse looks like and is the most underused instrument available4 · LimitationState what it structurally cannot do before stating what it does. A power invented before its constraint is a power looking for a constraint to justify it, and it reads bolted-on every time5 · CostFrom the Wheel, deliberately, checked against the character’s existing category; a big art’s price comes out of its own idea, on top of reserve and body tells. A cast where everything costs blood is a cast with one idea6 · CounterplayOne sentence naming what answers it: its contrary idea, a soul further refined in its own idea, ground that holds another idea, or a refusal of its claim. The answer may be out of reach, rare or none at all; the flaw its idea gives it stays7 · StampThe Codex line: glyph pair, primary Wellspring (the lens it comes through, in the Measurewrights’ account the type of Aether it pulls on), its kind and Titan, the Operation, the Form and the Stage; then Path and Gates. The Measurewrights’ phenomenon may follow, labeled as theirs. Thirty seconds. Never left unlinked
The three-line version
For use mid-scene, at speed, when a named character needs to do something in the next paragraph.

VERB. RATE. PRICE.
He does one operation from his idea, at a stated speed, and it takes something the reader can see out of him.
The stamp and the counterplay can be filled in at the end of the pass without damaging the prose. The price cannot be added retroactively, because a cost the reader never watched get exacted did not happen.
The gate the Forge does not list, because it stands outside the steps. A Signature Technique requires a matching Trait, and no amount of Stage, instruction or expenditure substitutes for one. The Trait is a structural prerequisite rather than an advantage: it is the law the working applies, and without it the technique has nothing to apply.
Which is the test for whether a signature has been invented honestly. Name the Trait it comes out of. If there isn’t one, what has been built is a good technique belonging to nobody in particular.

The Road It Leaves By
The stamp asks for a Path, and no other line on it changes the page so much.
A blow’s character comes from Wellspring and Path together. Every soul has the three layers, and a Path is the one its Crystal has learned to lean on, so ask which one a working goes out through before writing a word of it. A Wellspring is the lens a soul bases its tempering on, and it shapes what each road works, the idea staying put and the target changing: Pyreveil on the Body shapes raw Aether in the Shell and is heat living in the tissue, burning matter; on the Spirit it shapes Essence in the Core and burns what a soul means and holds, a grief, a grudge, an attachment, and leaves the coat unscorched; and on Fate it is a claim that burns its way through, and what it burns is chances. A Wellspring’s kind names its home and never locks it. At home the lens can reach double after years of mastery, and away from home it costs more and reaches half again at most. A Spirit Wellspring gives no fire on any road. Write what the person can bear, know, keep or let go.

























PathWrite it asThe limits a fight must honorBodyThe literal understanding and manipulation of physical reality. Low down it closes and hits. High up, by recognition and then by law, its reach runs as far as there is matter to read: armor too heavy to lift, a blade rusting in the handNeeds existing substance, has to close until very high, pays in recoil through bones and Crystal, and has no purchase on a soulSpiritEverything to do with spiritual reality: souls, spirits, the dead, what a thing means. Authored in the Core and thrown at range, past the Shell, where it lands on souls only: a soul knocked out of true, a dread laid on a mind, a Core woundedNeeds a soul or a meaning to work on, has no purchase on matter except through its own Shell at its own Body Mastery, has a fragile body, and dies out of positionFateDay to day, Range, Aura Pressure, presence and bonds. A real pull moves what a blow, a wall or a march depends on, with a visible charge and a tell, and lands as the ordinary blow it turned intoRuinously hard and slow to set, moves only what already has a way of happening, often fails, leaves a knot every time, and loses a straight exchange
Three roads spend three things, and the pull step of a working names its own road.

































PathWhat goes outThe lost shareWho paysHow it flags, on top of the shared tellsBodyRaw Aether: drawn in, packed in the Shell as the Charge, shaped there by the lens and driven out unrefinedHeat: the Shell’s furnace burningThe body: Shell strain, torn fiber, recoil. Spending Charge is spending the world, and the body pays for the handlingRuns hot and cracks: heat-haze, then steam and cramps, then skin splitting in fine linesSpiritEssence: drawn in, refined in the Crystal, stamped, spent through the CoreA hollowing in the Core, and never heatThe self: color, memory. Spending Essence is spending yourselfRuns hollow: flat colors, then a cold and a slipped word, then names and memoriesFateThread: pulled down through the Attraction Layer for the one working, paid from the soul’s own shareA knot, which the world collects laterLuck, afterward, on the puller or on what is hersRuns unlucky: small luck curdles, then things go wrong nearby, then their own name sits wrong in other mouths
The shared tells at half, a quarter and a tenth stand on every road, and these go on top of them. An art that throws fire, force or matter at range on a Spirit line alone is written wrong. Make it a Body-and-Spirit art, with the Body half doing the matter through the Shell, or let its Spirit half work on the souls in the blast, and keep its story, name, numbers and cost. Someone who walks both roads carries the split on the card. The routes and the tables of tiring are set out on The Three Paths.
Fate is never casual. A pull takes extreme effort at every Stage, it cannot be reasoned out or drilled in, and almost nobody can do it twice in a day, so a character who does has been written wrong or is about to pay for it. Moving a whole field is a life’s masterwork or a bloodline’s art, and the Works of Hataraki exist because nobody grips it bare. Every pull, landed or failed, leaves a knot, so the price of a pull is written twice: the share of the reserve now, and the knot on the ledger, due within days for a lean and within the arc for a removed prerequisite (The Tell and the Knot).
No road is the better one. Body beats Spirit by getting there, and Spirit beats Body by going past the Shell. Body beats Fate with force and soundness, and Fate beats Body through what closing depends on. Spirit beats Fate by reaching the hand on the thread, and Fate beats Spirit because Spirit survives by being right. Stage, ground and preparation decide which of these holds on the day, and a kit that reads as simply the superior road is a kit with no counterplay. The Three Paths has the full account.
The Delivery Rate Law
It generalizes across every kind of matter a working can touch as one rule and resolves the recurring problem of every escalation reading as simply larger. The rate is the worker’s to choose and the idea’s to carry; what the blow then does to bodies and walls is the world’s old habit, and the middle column gives the Measurewrights’ names for each.

Every working has a delivery rate. Rate decides whether the effect pushes or shatters. Magnitude does not.

The same reserve (Charge on the Body road, Essence on the Spirit), the same Wellspring, the same practitioner, delivered slow or delivered instantaneously, produce two entirely different injuries. This is the correct way to escalate a character without inflating a number, and it is available at every Stage from Murmuring upward.


















































Kind of workThe Measurewrights’ namesWhat the difference isHeatDeflagration ↔ detonationSubsonic pushes, throws men, takes hair and eyebrows and leaves survivors. Break the sound barrier and it stops being fire and becomes a pressure wave, and a pressure wave leaves the skin alone and delaminates the man, lungs first. Same fuel. Same Charge. Entirely different corpseLightningSustained arc ↔ single dischargeA held arc cuts and cauterizes and can be walked away from. One discharge dumps the differential in a millisecond, and the body answers with interruption before it has time for injury: the heart is an electrical organ and it does not argueForceSustained load ↔ impulseA slow load bends, buckles, collapses, and everyone inside gets to watch it happen and possibly leave. As impulse it exceeds the material’s ability to distribute stress and the material fails along its worst line, immediately, everywhere at onceDistanceGradual displacement ↔ instantaneous foldSlowly through compressed distance: nausea and a headache. Folded instantaneously, the shear at the boundary becomes the entire event, and shear does not care that the thing being sheared is a personMatterCreep ↔ brittle fractureSlow loading yields, sags, redistributes, visibly failing the whole time. Faster than it can redistribute and it goes from intact to particulate with nothing in between and no warning to anyone standing under itBiologyChronic ↔ acuteSlow is survivable, treatable, often invisible for weeks, which makes it the assassin’s road. Acute overwhelms every compensatory mechanism at once: the body skips gradual failure and goes in a cascade that takes four organs in nine minutesFluidFlood ↔ water hammerAt its own pace, a slow disaster people escape by climbing. Stop that column instantaneously and its momentum bursts pipe, stone, and vessel walls, and the vessel wall in question is frequently an arteryEntropy, Void, MindErosion ↔ erasureErosion is experienced as ordinary decline: forgetfulness, bad luck, a joint that aches. The difference: erosion leaves a man who knows something is wrong, and erasure leaves a man who does not
The Cost Wheel
Rotate deliberately across the cast and audit for collision.

The governing test is unchanged and it is severe: if the cost never touches the character when they are not using the power, it is a resource limit wearing a cost’s coat.














































CategoryStandingPhysical tollExhaustion, injury, aging, organ damage. Reliable. OverusedResource depletionThe weakest category available. Only a real cost if scarcity bites outside a fightCorruptionThe usual default for anything Wellspring-adjacent, which is precisely why it should not be the default hereSanityA large lever. SparinglyMemoryTrading recall for capability. Underused across the whole trade, and it fits the Anima Spirare register exactlyTimeCast duration, cooldown, or lifespan spentSocial and legalA hall that will not sign with you, Concord Seal, exile. Every guild on the Accord can refuse your coin and your contract, and that is doing almost no workEscalating dependencyThe addiction structure. The best long-arc dread engine available, because the reader can see the bill coming and cannot stop itRigidityThe newest category and the one nobody else is using. A technique repeated enough deepens the Trait it comes out of, and the Rigidity Effect scales with how absolute a law is. The practitioner keeps all his strength and becomes less able to contradict the thing he built his power on, in his life as well as in a fight. The cost is paid in what he can no longer be talked out of, and it is visible at a table long before it is visible in a duel
The road pays first. Before the wheel is turned, the Path has already named a cost. A Body working is paid in the body, which is the wheel’s physical toll and arrives as heat. A Spirit working is paid in the self, in color and memory, which is why Memory sits so well on that road. A Fate pull is paid in a knot, a debt that falls due later on the puller or on what is hers. The wheel’s category goes on top of the road’s bill and never in place of it.
The Vow Clause
Lives in Votia; sealed as Claustra.
A practitioner may bind a technique under a stated condition, sworn into the Lattice or into their own Crystal. The narrower the condition and the heavier the forfeiture, the greater the output.

“Against those who deserve it” buys nothing. “Only against the Zettari, and if I break it my Crystal shatters” is a vow.

Why it works. The Core adopts the restriction as a standing law, and Tempering Coherence measures the alignment between a practitioner’s stated law and their lived behavior. Coherence is the structural prerequisite for Threshold eligibility. A vow kept therefore buys Coherence with conduct instead of expenditure, which makes it the cheapest advancement mechanism in the world and the one that clusters among people who cannot afford Drafts. A vow is small Fate, a person binding their own probability, and anyone can make one: spoken, it shows in the window with the bargain and its terms, and what it buys counts toward the two-step cap on self-boosts. See Vows and Oaths.
Why it kills. A broken vow lands at once by its own terms and needs no witness. Repeated denial of the truth behind it makes a Shear Break. The Core has been running a law the bearer has now denied, and the law does not negotiate its own withdrawal. The orders treat a lapsed vow as a medical emergency and get to the disciplinary question later, if there is one.

The disclosure variant is the useful one. Stating a technique’s true mechanism aloud, in the target’s hearing, before use, surrenders every advantage of surprise and increases output accordingly.
This is the best structural justification for a villain’s monologue ever devised and the Continuum should take it.

What the clause buys is an answer to power creep. A character becomes dramatically stronger by narrowing rather than escalating.

A Stage XIV fighter has no use for a larger number. What would change him is a vow the reader can watch him keep.

The Two Tests Before Presenting
The Collapse Test · If two techniques under one Ability share a Limitation, a Cost, and a Counterplay, they are one technique with two names. Collapse them.
The Name Test · Does the name tell you something true about who is using it? It may be the idea itself, direct and unadorned, Ruin is Ruin, Gravity is Gravity, or it may be one big shouted phrase, or a signature’s title with its moves under it (Art: Move), in the fighter’s own tongue with the meaning landing in the same beat. Anyone may reach for a word like World, God, Fate or Infinite: the room laughs until it works. Goofy names can be truly lethal on anyone whose card fits. A name that could belong to any practitioner in the Continuum has failed.
What Each Kind of Work Cannot Do
What each kind of work governs, and, more usefully, what it categorically cannot do. Every line below is a habit the world settled in the Physical Epochs: a working changes the worker, and the world gives way as far as that soul is truly changed, and none of these habits is ever overturned. The lens changes how a working feels and what it charges, and it does not lift them. The wording is the Measurewrights’, who are right about how much.


















































Kind of workWhat it cannot doSignature costHeat and its absenceCannot create energy. Every degree added is a degree taken from somewhere, and the practitioner must name the source or become it. Cannot sustain combustion without an oxidizer: sealed rooms, deep water and the high thin air of the Reach are hostile ground for any firePhysical toll, sink-side. A thirty-year adept has hands that no longer sweat, corneas gone slightly opaque, and a resting body temperature nobody wants to shake hands withLightning the work of the differentialCannot arc across a gap it has not prepared. Useless against wood, ceramic, dry rope, ungirded stone, which is why the counter-lightning kit is boiled leather and fired clay and always has been. Falls off with the square of distance, so every lightning threat is a threat about closing rangeSanity-adjacent, sensory. The nervous system is the instrument, and instruments detune. Early signs read as brilliance: he answers before you finish, he notices everything, he has not slept and does not think that is strangeForce and motionCannot create momentum. Every push has an equal push on the practitioner, and the only question is which of his joints receives it. Resonance requires knowing the frequency, and knowing it requires time the fight may not givePhysical toll, reaction-side, and it is skeletal. Shoulders that come out of socket in cold weather. A spine that has been used as a bracing member for twenty years. Corruption is gravitational isolation: the early symptom is that people stop being able to stand near him comfortably and cannot say whyDistance and positionCannot fold to a place it has not measured, and the failure state for blind translocation is arriving somewhere occupied. Cannot move what it cannot fully bound, so a partial working takes a partial manTime and proprioception. Long before terminal dissociation, the practitioner reaches for a cup and misses by a hand’s width, and stops trusting stairsMatter and substanceCannot make matter. Conservation is absolute here and there are no exceptions, which is why a matter-worker on bare ice or open water is a man with opinions and no tools. Loses every exchange decided in under two seconds and wins every one that lasts a weekEscalating dependency, mineral. Petrification compulsion, terminating in mineralized flesh. It shows first in the nail beds and the whites of the eyes, the only corruption in the manual a physician can diagnose by lookingBiology and anatomyHealing eats mass, and the mass comes from the patient, the caster, or something the caster brought, and a healer who will not say which is a healer who is lying. Cannot restore what has lost its pattern; the dead stay dead, and the attempt to argue with that is the void’s crime and no healer’sMemory and metabolic debt. A healer at the end of a long campaign is a man who can name every wound he closed and not the wife he closed them to get home toFluid and pressureCannot act without a medium: deep vaults, sealed reliquaries and the dry Undaar deeps are deliberately hostile ground. Cannot hold a boundary indefinitely, because fluids want to mix and the working is always spending reserve to disagreeDissolution of boundaries, and it is the eeriest corruption in the register. The tell is grammatical and should be written that way: an adept who has gone too far starts saying we about himself, without noticing, and gets irritated when correctedEntropy, Void, MindCannot create. Every working of this kind is subtractive and there are no exceptions, the single most useful clarifying sentence in the manual. Cannot act on what has no pattern, so raw undifferentiated matter is nearly immune and a rock is a better shield against it than a wardExistential erosion, and it is reflexive: the practitioner pays in the same currency he spends. A man who erases memory loses memory. A man who nulls loses the ability to feel Aether at all in a widening radius around his own skin

Standing prohibition. Chronokinesis is Forbidden beyond Stage X. Chronoturgy is Forbidden outright.
The Accord’s enforcement of both is a plot instrument that has barely been used.

The Working Trades, for Whoever Writes Them
The workbench behind The Working Trades, which keeps the story and the trades themselves in the hall’s voice.
The Design Problem
A note from the compilers, standing outside the hall’s own voice, on where the tradition was taken from. It stays here because every lever below hangs off it.
The casting model as it stands is correct and complete. It is also, in its center of gravity, Eastern.
The five-step pipeline (Intent, Pattern, Essence Donation, Aether Formation, Attraction Anchoring; see The Disciplines) runs inside one practitioner, in real time, in a single continuous act of will. The most legible unit is the Technique: a named, repeatable thing a person does with their body and their reserve, at a stated cost. Every load-bearing question the system asks is a question about one soul’s interior.

That is the cultivation shape. It is the core of the system and it stays the core, and it is not what Tolkien, Martin, Clarke or Le Guin are doing; the trades below build their made things around it.

What the Western tradition does instead
Tolkien has made things where other books have spells. The power lives in objects made well by people who were what they were: the Rings, the Phial, mithril, lembas, the rope that unties itself. Galadriel’s correction to Sam is the whole thesis: mortals use one word for the Enemy’s deceits and for the craft of the Eldar, and the Elves do not have a word that separates art from enchantment at all. Nobody in Middle-earth casts. They make, and the making holds.
Martin has an economy of denial where other books have a system. Rare, foreign, unreliable, morally contaminating. Its price is paid in blood and in life, directly, with no reserve to spend first. The maesters have an institutional interest in insisting the subject is superstition, which is itself a plot engine, because they are wrong and they are also not entirely wrong.
Clarke gives the sharpest structural gift, and the trade is already most of the way to it. A scholarly tradition with a bibliography, a lost golden age, live controversies, and a hard social distinction between the theoretical magician who reads and would never dream of performing, and the practical magician who performs and is therefore vulgar.

The academies and research halls under the Guild Accord are four-fifths of the way to being that institution and do not yet know it.
And the deepest one: the trade’s own glyph system is already Western Renaissance occultism.
The Parun (the language of law every working is written in) lattice is Agrippa’s kamea method out of the Three Books, II.22, unaltered. That is the operative tradition of European ceremonial magic, lifted whole.
Which means the Four Glyph Roles are already the Solomonic operation, in order, and nobody has noticed.































Glyph RoleSolomonic operationWhat it doesAuthorizationThe conjuration and the citation of authorityNames by what right the operator actsBoundaryThe circle and the triangle of artFixes where the working may reachDirectionThe constraintCompels a specific outcomeSealingThe license to departCloses the operation and releases the power

The four roles are the boundary operation, in order, and the order is not decorative.
A glyph creates nothing. A Wellspring (the governing idea, alchemical and spiritual at once, that transforms how a soul uses Aether, and in the Measurewrights’ account one of sixty types of Aether with its own physical law) was already at work. Authorization says by what right a limit is set, Boundary sets it, Direction states which way the law is to run across it, and Sealing takes the limit back down.
Which is why Sealing is the role that kills people. Authorization, Boundary and Direction failing produce a working that goes wrong while the operator is still in the room. Sealing failing produces a working that does not stop, because the law goes on obeying itself after the operator’s attention has left the room. Every burned workshop in the Accord’s incident record is a Sealing failure and roughly a third of them are recorded as something else.
Nobody needs to import the Western frame into the trade. It only needs digging out.

The Five Levers
I · Let the guilds feud over rank. Real-time casting sits at the center by default, and the crowd adores it. In the halls, the made object and the prepared substance sit above the live caster, and the man the crowd came to see is told so at the door. Nothing in the system backs either side. That is a feud, and feuds are free, and they change everything about how the world reads.
II · Contest the word. Nobody calls it magic. Each trade carries an Accord name in liturgical Latin and a plain name in the common tongue, and which one a character reaches for places them by class before they have finished the sentence. This is the Norman and Anglo-Saxon doublet English actually runs on, and it is Tolkien’s method exactly.
III · Make the golden age real, lost, and officially denied. The best inscriptions in the world are all old. Some of them cannot be read. The Accord’s published position is that this is not the case.
IV · Make the filing political. The Forms, and every older sorting of magic before them, are an Accord publication before they are a law of the world. Documents serve the people who publish them. Somebody’s trade was reclassified as Mechanica on grounds that were political before they were metaphysical.
V · Move cost from the ledger to the page. EU (Essence Units, the measure of a reserve), Flux Density (how densely power packs into the Crystal) and yield (η, the share of spent power that does its work) remain the compilers’ business and unchanged, and even a person’s own window (the soul reporting its numbers to its owner, unseen by anyone else) shows only numbers, ranks, percentages, bars and Level. What a reader sees is the Cost Wheel: the years, the memory, the sanction, the debt, the man who knows what you bought.
Prose cues, trade by trade
The speaking. The speaker pays inside the same scene, visibly. Nosebleed, tremor, the hand that will not close, the four days of sleeping badly afterward. Somebody in the room reacts to the fact that a working was spoken aloud in company, because in some rooms that is an obscenity. Nobody polite says casting.
The cutting. Chisels, drift, tooling marks, the grain of the stone and where it fought the cut. Somebody’s hands. The apprentice who holds the light. A wall with three hands on it, two of them dead. Weather on an inscription. Somebody scraping a rune off a doorframe with a knife, badly, because the man who cut it is now an enemy. This is where the awe and the old grief get their material, and where the Tolkien register lives without a word of it needing to be stated.
Standing rule for prose: the wall is older than the war. Any standing inscription on the page should carry a date, an author, or a visible repair, and the repair should be worse than the original.
The pouring. Price, always. Weight and volume. What the vessel is made of and why that matters. Sediment. A seal, intact or broken. Somebody checking a seal. An excise stamp. The difference between what the label says and what is in the bottle, and the person who knows the difference and says nothing.
The singing, reference points. Finrod and Sauron singing at each other until one of them falls. Lúthien before the throne. The monastic office sung eight times a day for six hundred years by men who were replaced one at a time.
Which column a character speaks from is characterization before it is information. Bodily speaking is not a separate art and should never be written as one.
What This Changes on the Page
The default working in a quiet scene should be a cut or a bottle, or some petty art done by hand for a fee. A wall that holds. A bottle that was bought. A lamp-warden arguing about what you owe her. The speaking owns the fight: it is what a fighter shouts when the blades are out, and what anyone reaches for when out of time or out of options.
Every named practitioner has skills, and usually one trade they are known for, and that is characterization. Sodoku speaks because Sodoku fights. Somebody in Marrowhold cuts. Somebody in the Amber Cities pours and keeps two sets of books.
Cost is visible outside the working. The Engraver’s hands. The Drafter’s ledger. The speaker who is still shaking at supper.
The ranking is contested in dialogue. A character who calls the pouring mere cookery is expressing a live guild position and is entitled to be wrong loudly.
Elegy attaches to one named thing that is gone. An array under a particular gate that four generations have failed to reproduce, and the last man who could read its third layer, who died in the winter.
Settled Positions





































QuestionSettled positionI · Law V settled as a gateLaw V, the Law of Material Anchor, is a Stage gate rather than a universal. Below Stage VII, Refraction, a working requires voice, hand, ink or blood: an external anchor for the boundary. At Refraction the practitioner can hold the Crystal as an object of study, and the Glyph Roles compress into an internal chain that needs no material anchor at all. This is why internalized speaking reads as a mark of rank rather than a technique, and why a man who casts silently in a room has told everyone present his Stage without saying a numberII · Law III struckLaw III is struck from the register. It states that progression follows the fourteen Wellsprings. There are sixteen Stages and sixty Wellsprings and the two were never the same axis. It survives in-world as an error with a history: the fourteen it counted were the Archons, and a copyist’s conflation four hundred years old propagated into three generations of teaching texts before anyone checked. Older practitioners still teach it. They are wrong and they are extremely difficult to correctIII · The singingIt stands on its own terms, the medium-home of Harmonia, and answers to no guildIV · Whose trade is bestA feud, and the feud varies by culture, downstream of material conditions rather than taste. The Concord baseline ranks cutting first. The Marrowkin rank it first and hardest, since a hold is a permanent substrate and everything they own is inscribed. Kharven ranks pouring first: nothing in a camp that moves is permanent, a Draft travels in a belt, and the standing runework in the death-houses is imported work that no living Kharven hand can read, a fact the seat does not raise and the Accord does not stop mentioning. The speaking ranks highest in Kharven of anywhere in the Concord’s reach, because a soldier is not embarrassed by an art that works nowV · The lost golden ageThe Accord is mistaken, and has become invested in the mistake, which produces a worse institution than lying would. The recovery program is real, funded, sincere and structurally incapable of succeeding, because what was lost was a substrate condition that no longer obtains, and no quantity of technique gets it back. Four generations of honest men have failed at it and each has been promoted for the attempt. Somebody in the research halls has worked this out. They have not publishedVI · Scope of the doubletThe wider scope. Every trade term in the four quarters carries an Accord register name and a common-tongue name, and which one a character reaches for places them before they finish the sentenceVII · Standing InventoryEntered for Kharven. Household object: the doorframe, and whether it has been cut. Oath: by the hand that cut it. Proverb, fixed wording: “A cut wall keeps a promise longer than the man who made it.” Contempt terms carry over intact, a mouth, a cutter, a potboy, and potboy is the one that starts fights, because Kharven pours
The Blank Card
Copy, fill, log. Fields marked † are mandatory for anything that will later resolve a conflict.

Name · Ability / Root Idea · Path · Skill It Rides · Trigger † · Function † · Verb · Rate · Mechanism † · Operation † · Numerical Effect · Target Response · Limitation † · Weakness · Cost † · Vow · Counterplay † · Codex Stamp † · First Display † · Window Line · Sensory Description
Cross-reference. This card is the workbook form and carries more than any single scene will use. Mechanism is prose-legal and belongs on the page: the idea and its operation, what it does to the worker’s soul and how that reaches the world, the glyph’s limit, and the fault that falls out of the idea’s flaw. What stays in the workbook is the form itself, the Codex stamp, and the arithmetic.
An entry the reader sees runs: the name in caps with its native name and kind; a hook a child could repeat; the named moves, a line each; How it really works, the whole account by the lens (the idea, what it does to the soul, how that reaches the world, the glyph’s limit), with any science only as a comparison or a Measurewright’s line; one short Cost line and one short Counter line; and a Numbers block at the bottom for the exact figures. Effect, Cost, Limit and Counter all stay required, the Counter naming whatever answers it, out of reach or none included, plus one line of what nobody knows.

the-magic-system/reference-and-craft/the.title: The Working Vocabulary — Trade Jargon and Its Metaphysical Extensions
the-magic-system/reference-and-craft/the.content:
“Read every book in the Guild and you will still be caught by the first man who has burned his thumb on the thing.” Goody Sharrock, assay-mistress of Wick Cross

The man calling himself Journeyman Tobit Lamb lasted four months at the Wick Cross assay house. He had the Latin perfect. He had the licenses, the stained apron and a very good forged seal, and he had the Guild’s cupel ledgers halfway copied for whoever was paying him, and then one payday at the Gilded Ladle, with eighteen assayers around him and the third round on the table, somebody told the old story of the Abbot’s button and he laughed in the right place and said, “Aye, and then the flash.”
Every cup at the table stopped where it was.
No assayer on earth has ever called it the flash. Eighteen brass forks came up off the table. Lamb was a good deal stronger than anyone had been told, a Stage IV (fourth on the soul’s sixteen-step ladder) with arc-blue lightning crackling down both arms, and he put five of them through the front wall of the Gilded Ladle, in a shower of painted plaster and spilled small beer, while the whole of Assay Street came out to bet on it. He left by the roof, and he left his left ear and a season’s copying on the taproom floor, and Goody Sharrock (who had taken the ear, with a pair of cupel tongs) had it pickled and set on the shelf by the scales, where it has been shown to every apprentice since. Nobody there had been fooled by anything but his paper. The word caught him.
I collect these words the way other Measurewrights (the Guild’s sworn measurers) collect grudges, and this page is the collection.
Why This Exists
The canonical term list runs to four hundred and thirty-four entries and every one of them is machinery: Grades, Stages, Wellsprings, Sub-Stats, Crystal tiers. That vocabulary names the system, and it may stand on the page beside the effect it names, but it places nobody by trade or class.
What a scene actually needs is the other layer. What a lamp-warden calls a wick. What an assayer calls the flash. What a glasshouse calls a flaw. Those words do three things at once: they place a speaker by trade and class, they make the world feel worked rather than described, and they give the metaphysics somewhere to borrow from that is not the Codex.
The Method
Every entry below moves through the same three steps, and the third is where the world gets built.
One. Take it whole. The trade exists here, so the term exists unchanged. A wick is a wick. This costs nothing and buys texture immediately.
Two. Extend it. The trade’s word is applied to the metaphysical case by the people who work both, because that is how technical vocabulary actually spreads. Practitioners never coined a word for the moment a Crystal’s grade declares itself, because the assayer’s was lying there on the bench.
Three. Invert it. The word turns up in cant, meaning something adjacent and usually worse. This is the layer that makes a vocabulary feel lived in rather than compiled, and it ties directly to the doublet on the Common page.
The discipline that keeps this honest. The extended sense describes what happened. An assayer’s word for a flash is a word for a flash, and the word itself explains nothing about the Crystal. The explaining comes right after, complete, from a mouth or from the narration, and the word is what the speaker reached for first.
I. The Pull
Nobody who does it for a living talks about refining Aether. A practitioner hauls it in off the ground around them the way a boat hauls a net, and what becomes of the catch depends on the road: a Body fighter packs it raw in the Shell and drives it out unrefined, a Spirit worker has the Soul Crystal turn it into Essence and spends that through the Core, and a Fate fighter fills up like anyone and then reaches for something else entirely. The vocabulary was borrowed from everyone who ever took something out of the world by hand: bargemen and fishers, smiths at the bellows, miners on a seam, farmers arguing about soil. The daily crafts that live off it, lamp-wardens on their rounds, ward-cutters at their doorframes, hedge-workers at their hedges, add words of their own, because they are paid by the job and every one of those words has been shouted across a bill.















































































































































TermTrade senseMetaphysical extensionCantthe pullone heave on a line, the bargeman’s and the net-hauler’s unit of worktaking Aether in from the environment toward the Crystal; a long pull is a slow filling on poor grounda man’s pull is who will come when he sends for themthe haulwhat comes up in the netthe raw Aether of one pull, before the Shell has packed it or the Crystal refined ita short haul is a job that paid less than it costthe chargewhat a furnaceman loads for one melt: ore, flux and fuel, weighed inthe raw Aether a Body fighter keeps packed in the Shell, unrefined; a full charge is a full reserve on that roadshort-charged is sent to a job without what it neededbellowsthe leather lungs of a forgethe breath-work that sets the rhythm of a pull; every school teaches its own count and sings it at the othersall bellows is a loud man with no fire under himtuyerethe clay nozzle where the blast enters the firethe place in the body a school teaches you to feel the pull come in: the breastbone, the soles, the nape of the neck. Measurewrights say it makes no difference and the schools have broken each other’s windows over it for centuries—fat ground, lean groundfarmers’ words for soilrich and thin ground, which scholars call high and low Aetheric Density; fat ground fills you faster and lean ground starves youfat ground is any soft position; on lean ground is broke and still fightingseamthe run of ore a miner followsa line of rich ground running through poor; where a commander goes when he means to shrink somebody’s reacha good seam is a man’s main source of incomegleaninggathering what the reapers left in the fieldpulling the thin leavings of poor ground; where the unhoused and the unregistered work froma gleaner lives off other people’s scrapsbleddrained by the barber’s lancet or the butcher’s knifeground pulled empty by a long fight or a greedy crew, and slow to fillbled is squeezed dry by a creditorsaltingsalt worked into a field so that nothing will growground treated by hired hedge-workers so that Aether will not pool on it, usually the night before somebody else’s fightsalted is spoiled on purpose: a market, a witness, a marriagebankingheaping ash over a fire to hold it low till morningwhat a Core’s keepers do when they close a worked Wellspring site; it goes on recharging and nobody can pull from itbanked is shut out, ruined, out of the traderunning hota millwright’s phrase for an axle or a bearing gone short of greasea Body fighter flagging: heat-haze thick on the skin, steam off the shoulders, cramps, and at the last the skin splitting in fine linesrunning hot is spending faster than you earnhollowa founder’s and a cooper’s fault: a casting or a stave with a void inside the walla Spirit worker flagging: the colors near her gone flat, a cold with no weather in it, a word that will not come and then a namehollow is a man with the look of the thing and none of the insidethe knota hitch in a line, and the hard place in timber that turns the sawwhat every pull on a thread leaves owing, which the world collects later on the puller or on what is hersknotted is owing something that has not come due yet, and knowing itthe rounda watchman’s walk through the nightthe lamp-warden’s paid route, street by street and door by dooroff the round is on strike; a dark street is one that did not paytrimmingcutting a wick back so it burns cleanre-cutting the worn rune on a lamp, which is a warden’s whole livingtrimmed is overcharged, and every household believes it has beendead wicka wick still in the lamp with nothing left to burna runed lamp still stamped, still billed for, and giving nothing; common across any Withering-era districta dead wick is a man still on the books who does no worktallya notched stick split down its length, each party keeping half so neither can cheatthe job-stick between a ward-cutter and the client: how many cuts, what price, whose walla short tally is a robbery that leaves no damagepleachinghalf-cutting a hedge’s stems and weaving them over so they livethe hedge-worker’s trade of laying a small ward or charm through living growthpleached is cut halfway through and still on his feetmufflingwrapping a bell’s clapper in leather for a funerala coat or a Pressure held in so that it makes no show; tiring work, and everyone can tell you are doing itmuffled is deadened, kept quietsweatingwarming sealing wax over a lamp until the seal lifts wholea Guild seal opened and closed without tracesweating a seal is forging onetundisha funnel for filling a cask, set so the pour can be seenthe small brass funnel on every Drafter’s bench; the fitting whose entire purpose is that a short measure cannot be hiddenthe tundish is any arrangement designed to make a thing undeniable
The one to steal first is the tundish. It is a funnel whose only function is that somebody can see what is going into the cask. A fitting that exists to prevent concealment. In a world where every hall and crown wants its cut by the bottle, and a great many Drafters would prefer they did not know how much is being poured, the tundish is the object every argument in a Dark Ages street happens over.
II. The Assay
The fire assay is the trade that determines what a thing actually is by destroying part of it, and it has supplied practitioner diagnosis with most of its working vocabulary.
The real process: a sliver of the sample is wrapped in lead, sometimes pre-treated by scorification in lead foil, and heated in a porous cupel of bone ash inside a muffle furnace. The lead oxidizes to litharge, which the cupel absorbs, carrying the base metals with it. What is left is a bead, or button, of the precious metal. Parting in acid separates silver from gold, and comparing weights gives the fineness.













































































TermTrade senseMetaphysical extensionCantthe assaydestructive determination of true contentany procedure that establishes what a practitioner actually is, as against what they are registered asassayed is found outcupelthe porous bone-ash dish that drinks the leadthe diagnostic bench, and by extension the examiner’s roomin the cupel is under investigationlithargethe lead oxide that carries the base metal awaywhat an assay takes off a Crystal and what the practitioner is left short by afterward—scorificationpre-treatment before the assay properthe preliminary questioning before an examinationscorified is softened upthe buttonthe residue after cupellationwhat remains of a man’s capacity when everything unearned has been burned off; a bought Stage assays small, and its owner knows ita small button is a man with less to him than his reputationfinenessproportion of precious metal in the alloythe ratio of a practitioner’s real Coherence to their claimed standing—partingseparating two metals that alloyed togetherseparating a bloodline trait from a trained one; contested and rarely clean—proofthe mark struck on tested metal, armor, glassthe Guild proof-mark; a proofed working, a proofed breastplate, dented by a crossbow at the armorer’s doorproofed is vouched fortouchstonethe dark stone a sample is rubbed against for a rapid, non-destructive readany quick field test that gives an approximate answer without opening anythingthe touch is a rough estimateslag, scoriathe waste glass floating on the meltResidue after a working; what a workshop’s sweepers collectslag is an insult and needs no explanation: a man who came out slag took a Dead Setfeatheringworking the cupel carefully near the endhandling a diagnosis at the point it could still go wrong—
The blick
The single best word available and it is free.
As a cupellation completes, the last of the molten litharge runs across the surface of the bead and throws a rainbow play of color. The color dulls for an instant. Then there is a bright flash, called the blick, caused by the release of latent heat as the bead reaches its solidification point. The assayer watches for it because it is the moment the test finishes and the answer exists.
It transfers directly and it transfers without explaining anything.
The blick is the instant a Crystal’s real grade declares itself: the color running, the dull beat, the flash. Examiners watch for it. Practitioners dread it, because a man can lie about his Stage in every document he signs and cannot lie during the second the blick takes. There is a phrase for a career that ended in one, and there is a phrase for a man who has never sat for one.
And it is a scene first. What lands on the page is the color, the dulling, and the flash, and the assayer’s word for the flash is a word for a flash. Why the Crystal does that comes right after, in a Measurewright’s mouth or in the narration, and three Measurewrights will give you three accounts, two of them wrong and all of them loud.
III. The Glass
Glasshouse vocabulary supplies the language of Draft vessels, lens work, and the physical condition of a Soul Crystal, and it supplies it better than any other trade because glass has the same three properties: it is worked hot, it holds stress invisibly, and it fails at the flaw you did not see.































































































TermTrade senseMetaphysical extensionCantthe metalmolten glass, as glassmen call ita Crystal in a worked state—gatherthe mass of hot glass taken up on the roda pull taken and held before it is shapeda gather is a crowd about to become a problemmarverthe polished slab glass is rolled on, to shape it and to control its temperaturethe bench a Drafter works a vessel onmarvered is smoothed over, made presentablepontil, and the pontil scarthe rod that holds the work, and the mark left where it was broken offthe point at which a working was held during its making; readable afterward by anyone who knows to lookthe scar is the tell that gives a forger awayblanka cooled object still needing forminga working prepared but not finished; a Draft vessel not yet chargeda blank is a man with no craftannealingslow, controlled cooling that relieves invisible stresswhat a Crystal requires after a Threshold, and what most practitioners skimp—lehrthe long oven a piece travels through as it annealsthe enforced rest after an ascension, weeks long, deeply resentedin the lehr is laid up, out of actionseedfine bubbles left in the metalsmall permanent inclusions in a Crystal; common, mostly harmless, always noted—cordstriations from an unevenly mixed meltstructural striation across a Crystal, and the thing an examiner looks for before anything elsecorded is inconsistent, unreliablefritground glass applied to add colorfragments of a broken Crystal, and the trade in them, the cheap end of the worst crime in every realmfrit is powder, and buying frit is buying something that came off a corpseencasinga clear layer laid over a decorated core, which magnifies ita working laid over another to amplify it—fumingmetal vaporized over hot glass, depositing colorresidue laid down on a vessel by proximity to a working—flaringopening out the end of a tubewidening a channel past its intended bore—battledorethe flat wooden paddle used to true a basethe flat tool that levels a poured vessel—
Annealing is the concept with the most story in it. A piece that is cooled too fast looks perfect and carries stress it cannot show you, and it fails later, without warning, at the flaw nobody could see. That is a description of a practitioner who climbed a Stage and went straight back to work, and it does not require a single word of metaphysical explanation to land.
IV. Where the Contempt Lives
Every column above has a cant entry or is missing one, and the pattern is worth naming: the words that invert are the words that touch money, standing, or whether a man is any good. Banked. Trimmed. Slag. A small button. A blank. Corded. Assayed. Nobody has made a cant sense out of tuyere or battledore, because nobody has ever needed to insult a man by comparing him to one.
This is the same engine as the doublet on the Common page. The Latin column is what the examiner says. The trade column is what the tradesman says. The cant column is what is said about a man when he has left the room, and it is almost always drawn from the trade rather than the Latin, because contempt is specific and Latin is not.
Next Passes
Domains that would yield as well and have not been mined yet, in the order I would take them.
Bell-founding and acoustics, for the singing and every chanter who has leveled the skill. Bells are tuned on their partials, and a bell that will not come into tune is called false. A choir vocabulary built on strike note, hum, and falseness would give the chant the technical layer it currently lacks.
Quarrying and banker masonry, for rune-cutters. The bed, the grain, quarry sap, spalling, dressing, the reveal. A stone has a direction and a rune cut across it fails, which makes inscription a trade with real failure modes that anyone who has split a paving slab can follow.
Knacking and the rendering floor, for monster cores and the crews who bring them up. Everyone who has ever boiled a carcass down for tallow has words for what comes off the top and what stays in the pot, and the people rendering a core into a Draft have been borrowing them.
Surveying and the chain, for Domain radius, boundary disputes and the Bench.
Rope, rigging and cordage, for Attraction Force and bonds, which currently reach for a bank of metaphors with nothing under them.
Tanning and the blood trades, which already have a research document on the Guild’s shelves and have never been mined for vocabulary.
