the-magic-system/the-foundations/the-des.content:
A Speaker’s Grammar of Parun, with the Lexicon and the Spoken Hands
Compiled for the Guild Accord Division of Alchemetrica · companion volume to The Descent of Parun

Twenty-five cells · one constant · three lawful short sentences
“The Descent taught you fourteen ways to write it. This teaches you why almost nobody says it.”
Opening line of the Vaulted Ring recitation primer, unattributed.

When the east wall came down at Dunmere Gate, Sergeant Ebba Thorn was in the gatehouse with a spear butt coming at her mouth and the whole room full of burning thatch. She took the butt, spat two teeth across the floor and bellowed the field sentence, AT PEN MA RA, in the voice she used for mules: eight and twenty-one and thirteen and twenty-three, sixty-five, sealed.
The air of that room ran inward toward her, every lick of flame and rag of smoke hauled back off the door like a dog on a chain, and it stayed that way till first light while the garrison in their yellow coats came up the stair past her, cheering. Beside her stood a licensed Cant speaker in a very clean tabard, who needed something nobody had composed for him in advance, composed it, and came out three short of the sum. Nothing sealed it. It ran down the gatehouse stair and it is, the locals will tell you, still a bad stair. The sum is why Thorn’s name got a song and his got a footnote, and this volume is the sum.
What Is Actually Being Done
Parun has no mother tongue and no register below the legal one, and the reason is arithmetic rather than culture.
A spoken sentence is a path traced across the same lattice the written hands trace, performed with the mouth instead of the chisel. The sounds are the cells.

To speak the sentence is to walk the square out loud.
This produces a language that cannot be babbled, cannot be sung to a child, cannot be used to gossip, and cannot be spoken quickly by anyone who has not made the count automatic.
It can be shouted across a breach by a woman who has done it ten thousand times, and there are perhaps four hundred such people alive.

The count is a skill like any other: anyone with a woken Crystal can level it, it rises with use, and it shows as a Grade on the sheet. Sergeant Thorn never held a title in anything, and her soul has been telling her for years what her Parun stands at, which is more than the Vaulted Ring has ever done for her.
The Twenty-Five
Five vowels and twenty consonants, one to each cell, keyed to the cell's value and not to its position.

Every sound in the inventory is one a Marrowkin throat, an Eressean throat and a goblinoid throat can all produce, which was a design constraint before it was an observation.


































































































































































ValueSoundWrittenArticulation1aaopen front2eemid front3iiclose front4oomid back rounded5uuclose back rounded6ppvoiceless labial stop7ttvoiceless dental stop8kkvoiceless velar stop9bbvoiced labial stop10ddvoiced dental stop11ggvoiced velar stop12mmlabial nasal13nndental nasal, the still cell14ŋngvelar nasal15ssvoiceless sibilant16ʃshvoiceless post-alveolar sibilant17zzvoiced sibilant18ffvoiceless labial fricative19vvvoiced labial fricative20θthvoiceless dental fricative21hhglottal fricative22rralveolar trill23lllateral approximant24jypalatal approximant25wwlabiovelar approximant

Concord transliteration uses ng, sh and th as digraphs. A Parunist reading aloud is reading values, not letters, and will tell you the transliteration is a courtesy extended to people who cannot count.

The Lattice
The five-by-five kamea of Mars. Every row, every column and both diagonals total sixty-five.








































11247203412258161751321910181142223619215

Thirteen sits at the center and is the only cell that does not move under any of the fourteen Archonic stations.
Which is why the dental nasal appears in more Parun words than any other sound, and why a speaker who cannot produce it cannot speak the language at all.
The whole square totals three hundred and twenty-five. This number matters later and is best not reached.

The Three Laws
I · A sound may not repeat inside a word.
A traced path cannot revisit a cell it has already occupied. This caps a word at twenty-five sounds and makes reduplication structurally impossible.

It is the reason Parun has no lullabies, no chants, no drinking songs and no baby-talk. You cannot say a sound twice for comfort. The language has no mechanism for it. What the choirs do is another thing, held in resonance, and the singing has its own account.

II · The first sound declares the slot.
Values 1–5 open a Warrant. 6–11 a Ground. 12–17 a Vector. 18–25 a Seal.

A listener therefore knows a slot has been skipped before the speaker has finished the word, which in a discipline where a skipped slot means no working at the moment you needed one is the single most useful thing the language does.

III · The sentence must total sixty-five.
Add the values of every sound in all four words. A lawful sentence comes to sixty-five, or to a whole multiple of it. Nothing else seals.

This law binds the mouth and only the mouth. A spoken sentence has nothing else to close on. A cut one is closed by its sealing stroke and held by what it is cut into, and it answers to the Seal and the stone and not to the sum.
This is the entire difficulty and the entire reason the world writes Parun rather than speaking it, because a speaker composing live is performing mental arithmetic while making a legal claim under pressure, and the arithmetic is not forgiving.
The practical consequence: Parun is grotesquely rich in near-synonyms of differing value. A speaker does not choose a word because it is the right word. He chooses it because it is the right word that makes the sum close.

The Four Slots



































SlotThe role it fillsOpens onNamesWarrantAuthorizationvowels, 1–5who is speaking and by what standingGroundBoundarystops, 6–11what territory, body or interval the speech coversVectorDirectionnasals and sibilants, 12–17which way the working runsSealSealing18–25the condition on which it ends
The slots are the four roles of the working trades, in the mouth. Notice what is missing from all of them, including every sentence on this page: the Wellspring. Nobody says it. It is named by harmonization under the Warrant, read off the Attraction Layer of the soul behind the sentence, so at pen ma ra in Sergeant Thorn’s mouth and in a Pyreveil speaker’s are the same words doing different things. A written form from the Glyph Index can fill a slot where a plain word would, and the Index shows one in a sentence on each of the three Paths.

A Warrant that overstates standing does not fail loudly. It seals, and the difference between the standing claimed and the standing held is deducted from the speaker at the moment the Seal closes.
Practitioners who habitually over-warrant are identifiable across a room by their hands.

That deduction governs a Warrant spoken in Parun. Vocatia summons by recognition and keeps its own law: a summoner who claims a standing he lacks gets nothing.
A Warrant answers the question Irath’s station reads, by what right, and when two souls contest a working it is weighed as Dominion Fate (the soul’s weight in Fate). Those are three names for one idea on three shelves.
The Seal Levels



































LevelTotalCharacterSingle65Three lawful sentences exist. Every practitioner alive knows all threeDoubled130Where working Parun lives. Several hundred lawful sentences attestedThird195Interdictions, curses, foundations. Long enough that saying it is a commitmentFourth260Sixteen lawful sentences attested. Every one of them ends a bloodline or a buildingTotal325The whole square. No attested lexicon reaches it. The Accord’s position is that this is fortunate
The Three Single Seals
The first thing an apprentice learns, the last thing a dying practitioner can still hold, and the only Parun most working people ever speak aloud.

























SentenceReadingSumip tam ma raBy my own standing, over this stone under me, running inward toward me, ending at first light9+20+13+23ip pen ne feBy my own standing, over the air in this room, running outward from me, ending at full dark9+21+15+20at pen ma raSpoken in haste and under duress, over the air in this room, running inward, ending at first light8+21+13+23

The third is the field version. It exists because the first is unsayable by a man who is being hit.

What a Seal can reach
A Seal spends the speaker’s own share of fate. It sets a term, and it moves only what already has a way of happening. It never pulls a thread of Fate, so anyone may speak a Seal with Fate unread (no rung at all of the Mastery that measures a soul’s reach into Fate), and wolyeth may wait a hundred years on the last of a line without killing anybody.
A spoken term is carried by the speaker. The Seal sets it, the speaker’s own Layer anchors it for as long as it runs, and the speaker is the substrate that caps it, which is why first light is a long way off for a tired sergeant. See how long a working lasts.
A Fourth Seal needs a grip. A sentence that ends a bloodline or a building is past what any soul’s own share will buy, so it takes a grip on Fate, by blood or blessing, or a Warrant that carries one. A Warrant word grants nothing: it names a grip somebody holds. Said without one, the sum closes and the difference between standing claimed and standing held comes out of the speaker at the Seal, and most of the Ring’s register ends there.
Failure





























FaultWhat happensUnder the sumNothing sealed it. The working runs and does not stop. This is the fault that kills bystandersOver the sumIt seals early. The difference is taken out of the speaker, in the body, at the moment of closingSlot skippedNo seal, no working, no cost. The commonest fault and the only harmless one. The Valorin bank whole formulae this way, one word short, against the day they need themSlot misorderedSeals inverted. The Vector runs from the Ground into the Warrant, which means into the speakerSound repeatedThe path crosses itself. The word is simply not a word

The rule across every trade is the same. A slot left wholly empty does nothing, and a sentence that fires with a bad limit runs.
A practitioner who has been over the sum is legible afterward. Depending on where the count went wrong the deduction comes out of the hands, the hearing, the teeth or the years, and the Vaulted Ring keeps a register of which faults take which, compiled from people who survived them.

The Lexicon

Values are computed from the lattice and every entry has been checked against the First and Second Laws. A word whose value is not listed is not a word.

Warrants


























































































WordValueSenseat8by my own standing, spoken under duress or in hasteip9by my own standing, a practitioner speaking for himselfute14by the ground itself; no person warrants thisame15by the house that trained meena16by the dead, in the mouth of the livingoku17by a warrant I hold in writing and can produceeshi21by an office, not a person; spoken by whoever holds the chairiso22under Accord license, number unstateduza23by a debt owed to me and now calledanger39by a bloodline, named or unnamedisof40under Accord license, number appended after the clauseithun41by an oath sworn elsewhere and still standingoyeth50by a thing I made with my handsublash54by the consent of the one this coversefrom58by force, consent refused and the refusal notedelwar73by the sum itself; a clause that warrants only its own arithmetic
Grounds




































































































WordValueSensetam20this stone, this ground under the speakerpen21the air enclosed by this roombes26the speaker’s own bodypav26iron, workedbime26a threshold, doorway, gate or mouthdosh30what is written on the surface in questionganu30the interval between two named momentstir32iron, unworked, still in the oreputha32a wound, openkor34a body not the speaker’s, present and namedgith34fire already burning; never fire to be madekelo37a boundary, drawn or walkeddul38water, standing or heldkanvi44everything within the speaker’s reachtozer52a wound, closed and not healeddepithash58a lineage across generations; the widest lawful groundgolsher78a name, spoken aloud in the same breathbulyer85everything within sight and no further
Vectors





















































































WordValueSensema13inward, toward the speakerne15outward, from the speakerngat22through, and out the far sidenub27reversed; back along the path it camengide29sideways into an adjacent ground, unlawful without a second warrantmos31held still; a working that runs nowherezen32around; enclosing without touchingzoku34across, tangential, touching nothing it passessil41downward, with weightshor42upward, against weightshilo46divided unevenly, the speaker taking the remaindersekar48divided evenly among all namedmesuth54outward and returning; the only vector that closes itselfnashor56outward in every direction at oncesengalo59downward through every layer named, in order
Seals





















































































WordValueSensefe20ends at full darkra23ends at first lightlo27ends when the speaker stops speakingtheb31ends when the speaker dies, and not beforevin35ends when the ground is crossed by anyoneyad35ends when the debt named in the Warrant is repaidwok37ends when a second speaker says so; the surrendered sealvashe38ends when the thing named in the Ground is destroyedhus41ends when the speaker sleepslifo48ends when the sum is spoken back correctly by anotherryup57ends after one turn of a named glasshoyem63ends when the speaker is touched by the one it coversthurin63ends when it is countersigned in writingrakensho66does not end. Barred by the Accord and by every house that has onewolyeth98ends when the last of the lineage in the Ground is dead
The Spoken Hands
The same six pressures the Descent uses, transposed from hand to mouth. Speech produces far fewer varieties, because a mouth that cannot hold the count does not produce a dialect. It produces a people who write instead.





































VarietyCharacterRoot Parun the Counted SpeechThe reference variety. All twenty-five held distinct, the count carried silently, the sentence composed live. Taught at the Vaulted Ring and in three other places. A Root speaker can compose a Doubled Seal in the time it takes to draw breath, and this is the specific skill the Accord licenses Understood by every trained Parunist. Composed live by almost none of themThe Vaulted Cant Guild Accord · the memorized handWhat most licensed practitioners actually speak. Lawful sentences learned whole, by rote, in blocks of eleven, deployed without any count being performed at the time. It works, it is fast, and it fails absolutely the moment a situation requires a sentence nobody has pre-composed. Cant speakers are visibly the same people as Root speakers until the moment they are not, distinguishable only by asking for something newCold Parun Echo Elf · the counted-aloud handThe Echo Elves externalize the arithmetic. One sound to one beat, metronomic, the count audible in the rhythm rather than held in the head, exhausting to listen to and effectively immune to error. Their treaties sum correctly in the mouth and on the page and have never once needed renegotiation. They regard the second fact as sufficient answer to the first Corrected mid-sentence by any listener who is also countingInverted Parun Drow · the spoken cipherEvery sound replaced by its complement, twenty-six minus the value. An outsider follows easily, confidently, at speed, and understands wrongly. The arithmetic constrains it savagely: a complemented sentence only seals when its total sound-count is divisible by five, so a Drow speaker composes to a length before composing to a meaning. None of the three Single Seals is invertible: all three run to nine sounds. There is therefore no such thing as a small Drow working, which is a fact about their reputation usually attributed to temperamentMirror-Speech Deepkin · the hand that is not saidThey say every cell the word does not touch and leave the word itself unsaid, so the meaning is the silence in the middle of a great deal of noise. The sums hold always, because the complement of four words against the full square comes to nineteen sixty-fives without fail. The cost is length. A Deepkin sentence is nineteen times the sentence it means, which is why they correspond in Mirror-Sign and speak it only where a working must not be detected. Nothing was inscribed and nothing was said, so there is nothing for a ward to findSwamp Parun Verdant Orc · the unbroken handThe reed never lifts and neither does the breath. Four slots on one exhalation, no pause admitted anywhere, which makes lung capacity the hard limit on how large a working a Verdant speaker can attempt. A Third Seal spoken on one breath is a physical feat before it is anything else, and Verdant practitioners are built accordinglyGravetongue Ironblood · the hand that abandoned the countThe exception, and the reason it is the exception. Its meaning is not carried in the sounds and therefore not in the sums, which is why a transcription is inert. Whatever Gravetongue is doing, it is not walking the square, and the Ironblood have never claimed otherwise. The Vaulted Ring’s position is that Gravetongue is not Parun. The Ironblood position is that Parun is a way of counting and Gravetongue is a way of being made of something, and that the Accord’s confusion is its own affair
Worked Sentences













































SentenceLevelReadingip tam ma ra65Standing on his own warrant, over the stone beneath him, running inward, until dawnithun dul ma vashe130Under an oath sworn elsewhere and still standing, over held water, running inward, ending when the water is destroyedame bes sekar hus130By the house that trained her, over her own body, divided evenly among all named, ending when she sleepsat kelo ngat hoyem130In haste and under duress, over a boundary walked, through and out the far side, ending when she is touched by the one it coverseshi tam nashor wolyeth195By an office and not a person, over this ground, outward in every direction at once, ending when the last of the lineage here is deadisof golsher shilo theb195Under license with the number appended, over a name spoken in the same breath, divided unevenly with the remainder retained, ending when the speaker dies and not beforeelwar dosh sengalo wolyeth260Warranted by its own arithmetic, over what is written on this surface, downward through every layer named in order, ending when the last of the lineage is dead

The Fourth Seal above is the clause the Accord cites when it argues that licensing is not bureaucracy.
It warrants itself, which means no person is answerable for it, and it ends a line.
elwar names no grip, so whoever says it brings their own and declines to say whose. That is the Accord’s real objection.

Who Speaks It

















































PeopleStandingGuild AccordRoot and Cant. The Cant is the product; the Root is the licenseEcho ElvesCold Parun. The largest population of live composers in the worldDeepkinMirror-Speech, rarely, and never where it can be timedDrowInverted, fluently, and never below the Doubled SealVerdant OrcsSwamp Parun, limited by breathIronbloodGravetongue, which is not thisThe High LineAlmost none. They cut instead, and consider speech a hurried mediumEresseansRead universally, spoken under license only, and a private letter in Songscript is still the greater threatConcord humansThe Cant, by rote, badly, and the death rate reflects itThe MotoNeither Root nor Cant. The Kōkan Line administered the Loom (the Parun lattice seen from above) under delegated sight, and a delegated warrant is not by my own standing and is not by an office either. The lexicon has no Warrant word for what they hold, because a word’s value is a sum of cells and cells are what the Archons’ stations read, and Moto speakers open on a sound the Vaulted Ring records and does not assign a value to. The Ring’s working position is that the word exists and the value is unknown. The Moto have never been asked, and would not be answered if they were
Settled Positions





























QuestionSettled positionThe latticeMars at 5×5. Twenty-five phonemes, constant sixty-five. Venus at 7×7 would give forty-nine phonemes and a constant of a hundred and seventy-five, which no mouth carries. The lattice is not an aesthetic decision. It is the reason the language can be spoken at allThe three Single SealsFixed at three, permanently. The lexicon may grow; the Single Seal count does not. This is the Vaulted Ring’s oldest standing finding and the one piece of Parun scholarship nobody has ever attempted to overturn, because every practitioner alive learned all three as a child and none of them wants a fourthGravetongueNot Parun. It does not walk the square, its meaning is carried in a physical resonance rather than in sounds, and the inert transcriptions follow directly. Structurally it is a chant with no notation. The Vaulted Ring and the Ironblood are both correct and have been arguing past each other for six hundred yearsThe Total Seal, 325Not barred. Simply fatal, for a reason internal to the arithmetic. The whole square includes cell thirteen, the still cell, the one that does not move under any of the fourteen Archonic stations. A sentence using every cell therefore warrants under all fourteen at once, and no living person holds that standing. The difference between standing claimed and standing held is deducted at the Seal. At the Total the difference is everything the speaker is. The Accord’s position that no attested lexicon reaches 325 is fortunate is a polite way of saying the thing has killed everyone who got close, and the Ring’s register of over-sum deductions ends its list at the fourth level for that reasonMoto standingEntered in the table above. Their Warrant class is delegated sight, which the lexicon has no word for and no value for. A Work of Hataraki is a grip and never a glyph, so nothing they inherit will fill a slot, and the Index has [[The Magic System/The Foundations/The Master Glyph Index — 136 Attested Forms
Read next: the next shelf, The Soul and the Climb: what a soul carries, what advancement does to it, and how it reads from outside.

the-magic-system/the-foundations/the-des.title: The Descent of Parun — The Fourteen Hands
the-magic-system/the-foundations/the-des.content:
A Reader’s Grammar of the Written Tongues · compiled for the Guild Accord Division of Alchemetrica

Fourteen hands · one lattice · one root
“There is one script. There have always been fourteen ways to be wrong about that.”
Attributed to a Measurewright (a certified assessor of practitioners and workings) of the Vaulted Ring, name struck from the record.

Ambrose Pinchbeck, a Concord wine factor of good family, learned Barkstone Tally in one afternoon at the Cooper’s Fair, read four hundred cask ledgers by the evening, and bought what he took for forty-year pitch-oak at a price that made the Cask Line of the Long Rack go very quiet and very polite. The letters had said forty. The slant of the barbs had said four. He tapped the first cask in front of a paying crowd, and got a spray of young green beer that went up like a whale’s breath and hit the banner of his own house, and then the whole rack began to go, bung after bung blowing out across the yard, four hundred casks working in the summer heat, with the coopers singing the tally aloud in harmony and the foam running gold and stinking down Rack Street as far as the river. Pinchbeck was still paying for it nine years later. Every clerk in the Four Quarters knows the song, and hardly one of them can tell you which barb he misread, so here is the whole business from the root.
The Root and the Six Drivers
Nothing in this record is a separate invention. Every hand traces the same Parun (the root script of law that reality reads) path across the same lattice (the fixed grid every glyph is traced on, which from above is Bara’s Loom; the Glyph Index joins the two), and every difference between them is the residue of a decision that was never about writing at all.

































DriverWhat it does to the handThe toolA chisel makes straight segments. A punch makes points and no line at all. A knife on a stave cuts with the grain or splits it. A reed on wet bark cannot be lifted. Three of these produce scripts a scholar would not guess were relatedThe surfaceGranite holds a curve badly and holds a straight cut for four thousand years. Soft iron takes an impact and refuses a stroke. Wet bark bleeds. Living tissue grows, which is a problem no other surface posesThe speedA trade hand and a liturgical hand cannot be the same hand. Every script here that got faster did so by joining what had been separate, and every one of them was accused of dilution while doing itThe purposeLaw wants a hand that cannot be varied. Ritual wants a hand that cannot be casually produced. Correspondence wants a hand that can be produced at all. These pull in different directions and no culture has ever resolved them into one scriptThe prohibitionTwo hands were shaped mostly by what was refused. The Varrisak refused the rail. The Ironblood refused, and still refuse, to write Gravetongue down at allThe bodyOnly the Fleshshapers write on something that changes size. Their solution, nesting the same glyph at three scales, is the single most original piece of orthography in the world and is universally read by outsiders as scarring

Every plate renders the same five roots in every hand: BALANCE of Urion, MOTION of Wyther, RECALL of Maelor, DISRUPTION of Uurgath, and VASTNESS of Zhaeren. Read down the plates and the family resemblance surfaces on its own.

What a Hand Changes and What It Does Not
The question every apprentice asks in the second week, answered badly by most instructors.
A glyph creates nothing. The law of the Wellspring (one of the sixty governing ideas that change how a soul uses Aether, which is mana, each written down by scholars as a fixed law) was already running, and the glyph is a boundary set on it: it says where the law stops. The boundary is set by the traced path, and the path is the same path in all fourteen hands, because all fourteen trace one lattice. Where the limit lands is a separate question, settled by the layer of the soul the maker’s Essence (spiritual energy) leaves through and answered in the Index. The hand has no say in that.
So a hand does not change the working. A ward cut in Old High Runic and the same ward struck in Old Vaross impose the same condition on the same law and produce the same effect. This is why the Accord can enforce a writ across eleven hundred leagues and why a Chancery notary and a Cask Line cooper are arguing about the same instrument even when neither can read the other’s page.
What a hand changes is everything around the working.





























What the hand decidesWhyHow long the boundary can holdThe Seal sets the term and the substrate caps it. A boundary cannot persist longer than its substrate does. Granite outlives the mason. Wet bark outlives the afternoon. The hand and the surface are one decision and the ceiling on duration follows from itWho can find itMirror-Sign leaves no signature because nothing was inscribed to leave one. The boundary is real and the evidence of it is not, which is a legal problem rather than a metaphysical one and the Accord has never solved itWho can check itInverted Parunic is an attack on the reader rather than on the working. The outsider reads fluently, arrives at a boundary that was not set, and acts on a condition that does not existWhether it can be validated at allCold Parunic engineers ambiguity out so that two readers cannot set two boundaries from one page. Sylvaaric refuses the question. Both positions are coherent and they cannot share a treatyWhether it survives its own authorSkin-Records grow. The nested scales exist because a boundary written on something that changes size stops describing the same limit within a decade

Gravetongue is the exception that proves the rule, and it is not a hand at all. Every other entry here is rune-cutting: a boundary committed to substrate. Gravetongue carries its condition in a physical resonance produced by a body that knows what it is made from, which makes it a chant (a working carried by the voice) with no notation and explains the inert transcriptions completely. No chant is Parun, for that matter: a chant holds its condition in resonance, and its words carry a sentence only when someone trained in the writing of law has put one there.
A written Gravetongue phrase produces nothing because the writing was never where the boundary lived. The Crimson Order’s pulse-code works for the same reason: they kept the resonance and discarded the part that was never load-bearing.

Cutting a rune is a skill and a trade, and anyone with a woken Crystal can level it. It rises with use and shows as a Grade on the sheet, one line for each hand the cutter has really worked, and a guild’s title says how far she has gone in it and how large a job a stranger may trust her with. The Temple of Inscription and the Accord’s scribes have been telling each other for centuries that the other side does not count, and that is the whole of the rank in it.
Parun
The Lawful Root
Not a language in the sense that a mother sings to a child in it. It is the grammar the Continuum (the whole lawful order of reality) reads, and it has no register below the legal one.
A Parun sentence names who is speaking, what ground the speech covers, which way the working runs, and how it is to end, and it does this whether it is chalked on a barn door or held internally by an Archmagus who has not moved his hands.

Every hand that follows is Parun with one thing done to it. Change the tool, change the surface, change what the writing is for, and the same traced path comes out the other side unrecognizable to anyone but a scholar.
The scholars are the ones who insist all of this is one script. Nobody else believes them until it is shown side by side.

Legibility · Spoken, gestured, inscribed. No mother tongue anywhere.
The Fourteen Hands
The count is a librarian’s. It takes Parun itself as the first of fourteen and the thirteen below it as the rest, Gravetongue included by courtesy, since it has no hand to count. The hands are not one per Archon, whatever the lecture halls of the Vaulted Ring would like: the two fourteens share a number and no history.
Old High Runic
The High Line · the sacred hand
A chisel driven into granite will not make a curve. It makes a straight segment and then another one, and the mason’s wrist has eight bearings available to it and no more. Old High Runic is Lattice Tongue put through that constraint for four thousand years: every arc squared off, every terminal blocked, every glyph resolved onto the compass.

The Temple of Inscription runs seventy years on a single theorem cut in this hand, and the discipline is not the theorem. It is the cutting.
The High Line will tell you the hand is slow because truth is slow. What they will not tell you is that they have never found a way to make it faster and have stopped considering that a failure.

Legibility · Read by any trained Parunist. Cut correctly by almost no one.
Barkstone Tally
The Cask Line · the working hand · plate 03
A knife on a cask stave cuts with the grain or it splits the stave, so the Barkstone hand gave up on the second dimension entirely. The whole path collapses onto one stem and every turn in it becomes a barb cut off that stem: above it, below it, or straight across. It reads downward, the way a stave stands.

The trap is that the barb angles are not decoration. They carry duration, which in a brewing hand is the load-bearing quantity, and a Grand Brewmaster reading a forty-year cask ledger is reading time off the slant of the cuts.
Outsiders learn the letters in an afternoon and then misprice barrels for a decade.

Legibility · Learned in an afternoon. Read properly after a decade.
Mirror-Sign
Deepkin · the hand that is not there · plate 04, the Hollow
Everything else in this record is a stroke laid on a surface. Mirror-Sign is the surface laid around a stroke that was never made. The field is worked and the path is left bare, so what a reader follows is the absence, and the absence produces no Aetheric signature because nothing was ever inscribed to produce one.

This is why no ward in the world detects Deepkin correspondence and why no Concord auditor has ever successfully audited a Deepkin holding.
The High Line calls it a broken geometry. The Deepkin have not sent a reply, and the Mirror-Sign record of their position has never been translated for anyone outside the lineage.

Legibility · Read by fingertip and by reflection. Undetectable to Harmonics (the trained sense that reads Aether in the field).
Old Vaross
Ironblood · the ancestral hand · plate 05, the Wedge
A punch cannot draw a line. It can only strike a point and leave a wedge behind, so Old Vaross kept the nodes of the Parun path and lost every connecting stroke between them. What sits on the iron is a constellation of impacts, and the reader supplies the line that runs between them out of their own head.

Ironblood theology takes this as the correct arrangement rather than a limitation.
The First Impact did not draw anything either. It struck once and left the world to work out what shape the strike had been, and a people who read their own script by reconstructing the missing stroke are practicing that every time they open a war-oath.

Legibility · Read across every goblinoid people. Written now only in ritual.
Low Goblintongue
Za’tarch · the trade hand
Trade will not wait for a punch and a hammer. Somewhere in the Za’tarch markets a clerk shrank the wedges down to nail-marks and ran a single quick stroke between them, and what had been a constellation became a line again with the impacts still hanging off it.

Faster, and legible to a Verdant Orc and a Tinker and a Hobgoblin quartermaster alike, and every Ironblood elder alive considers it a thinned thing.
Gorrum Ashentusk writes in it deliberately and in front of them, which is a position taken rather than a convenience.

Legibility · The most widely read goblinoid hand. Universal in council.
Gravetongue
Ironblood · never written · plate 14, the Silent
Gravetongue has no hand and has refused every attempt to give it one. Transcriptions exist. They are inert. What is on the page produces nothing when read aloud by someone who was not there, because the meaning of a Gravetongue phrase is not carried in the phonemes but in a specific physical resonance produced by a body that knows what it is made from.
The Crimson Order stripped the chant element out and kept the three-beat rhythm as pulse-code, which works, and which Ironblood traditionalists regard as grave-robbery.

The empty frame on the plate is drawn from a Concord ethnographer’s field notes. He ruled the box, was refused, and filed it empty rather than fill it with an approximation.

Legibility · No script exists. The frame is what a scribe leaves behind.
Swamp Parunic
Verdant Orc · the flowing hand
Reed on wet bark bleeds. Lift the reed and the ink spreads into the fiber and eats the next stroke before you have made it, so the Verdant hand never lifts. One continuous line, every glyph joined to the next, terminals drawn long so the bleed has somewhere to go that does not matter.

Held near saturated ground, certain sequences in this hand have catalyzed Spoor-Meld states in readers who were not attempting one. Whether that is a property of the script or of the language it carries is disputed. The Verdant position is that the question is badly posed.

Legibility · Read with effort by other goblinoids. Written by few outsiders.
Florwyndic Songscript
Eressean · the binding hand · plate 08
The rail is drawn first. One unbroken horizontal stroke across the whole line, and every glyph after it hangs beneath that stroke rather than standing on a baseline.

The rail is the Authorization clause (the part of a working that names its lawful channel) for the entire sentence, which is why nothing written under a broken rail carries force, and why an Eressean scribe who lifts the pen mid-rail begins the page again.

The hand of law and consecration and nothing else. Ordinary correspondence uses a plain unrailed cursive that no one bothers to name.

A private letter written in Songscript is either a legal instrument or a threat, and the recipient is expected to know which before opening it.

Legibility · Read by every educated elf. Written only under license.
Sylvaaric
Varrisak · the unruled hand
The Varrisak took the Eressean forms and refused the rail. What is left runs as a single meandering line with the nodes swelled into blooms and small tendrils thrown off wherever the hand felt like throwing one. No two Varrisak scribes produce the same glyph twice and none of them regard this as a defect.

An Eressean jurist will tell you Sylvaaric cannot be a script because it cannot be validated. A Varrisak reading a hand they know will tell you they can identify the writer, the season and the mood from the tendrils alone, which is a great deal more information than a validated glyph carries.

Legibility · Read within the wandering. Illegible to Eressean eyes by design.
Inverted Parunic
Drow · the hand built to be misread
Every Drow glyph is its Parun ancestor mirrored, run right to left, with the opening and sealing terminals exchanged.

Opacity would be kinder. An outsider does not stall on Inverted Parunic.
They read it easily, confidently, at speed, and they arrive at a meaning that is not the one on the page.

The inversion is constructed rather than drifted, which means it is applied with a consistency no natural hand has ever managed. Its one failure mode is under pressure, when Eressean structure surfaces underneath, and a Drow scribe who lets that happen in front of a witness has done something they will not be forgiven for.
Legibility · Read fluently by any Parunist, and read wrong.
Cold Parunic
Echo Elf · the hand without a hand · plate 11
Quantizes the Parun path onto a fixed grid of cells. Every glyph occupies the same count of cells. No cursive form, no ligature, no personal hand, no flourish, and no permitted variation of any kind between one scribe and the next.

A treaty that can be written two ways can be recited two ways, and the Echo Elf position is that a peace which has to be interpreted will eventually have to be refought.
Their diplomacy is exhausting and their treaties have never once needed renegotiation. They regard the second fact as sufficient answer to the first.

Legibility · Read identically by everyone. That is the entire specification.
Skin-Records
Fleshshaper · the growing hand
A glyph cut into living tissue does not stay the size it was cut. The body grows, the scar migrates, and within a decade a single-scale inscription has stretched past legibility. Most of what a Fleshshaper cuts is record and carries no working; a cut that sets a live boundary in the flesh is a rare and dangerous high art, and its failures are buried quietly.
The answer is to cut the same glyph three times, nested inside itself at diminishing scale, so that when the outer form has distorted the middle one is still readable and the innermost has not begun to move.

An elder’s back is a stack of decades that can be read downward through the scales, and a Fleshshaper reading another Fleshshaper is reading age directly off the ratio between the rings.
Outside their own communities this is invariably mistaken for mutilation, and they have long since stopped correcting the mistake.

Legibility · Read by Fleshshapers. Read as disfigurement by everyone else.
Accord Chancery Hand
Guild Accord · the ruled hand
It did not descend from anything. Assembled by committee in the post-Calamity regulation era out of whatever fragments of the older hands could be made to sit inside a ruled band of fixed height, and then boxed, so that a writ issued in one kingdom could be read without dispute in another eleven hundred leagues away.

It is characterless on purpose. No lineage, no region, no hand, no mood, and every scribe trained in it produces output indistinguishable from every other.
Practitioners of the older hands describe it as a script with nothing behind it. Accord notaries consider this the highest compliment their office has ever received.

Legibility · Read by everyone from Marrowhold to Kharven. That is the product.
A Hand Outside the Count
The Valorin write Vaeloric Script, and it is a further hand in every sense the six drivers can measure. Its surface is the soul itself, a Scripted Soul Lattice that never crystallized, and it traces the same lattice as everything on this page, so nothing in this record is a separate invention even here. A soul with no Crystal still has the three faces of one, and when the Continuum reads a Valorin’s Authorization it reads the Attraction Layer of that written soul exactly as it reads anyone’s.
The odd things the house does are ordinary grammar on an odd surface. The lines in its Cistern are formulae left one word short, which is a skipped slot, and a skipped slot fires nothing and bills nothing, which is why a master can carry a lifetime of them and sleep soundly. Errata is an amendment to a sentence somebody else is already saying, so it adds no third form to the two that obstruct. Their writing on Fate stays Fate: they cannot read it, and can only write a sentence and wait to see whether it is recognized, which takes generations.
Who Reads What

Cross-legibility is not symmetrical and is not a function of how closely two hands are related. A Parunist can read Inverted Parunic fluently and will be wrong about all of it. A Concord clerk can read the Chancery Hand and nothing else. The practical map is narrower than the family tree suggests.

















































































HandRead without training byOpaque toParunTrained practitioners of every peopleThe unlettered, entirelyOld High RunicAny Parunist, slowlyNo one, but almost no one can cut itBarkstone TallyMarrowkin of all three lineagesOutsiders misread the barb angles, not the lettersMirror-SignDeepkin onlyEveryone, including Harmonics detectionOld VarossAll goblinoid peoplesOutsiders, who cannot supply the missing strokeLow GoblintongueGoblinoids, Accord traders, most Concord clerksFewGravetongueNo one. It has no scriptEveryone, by designSwamp ParunicVerdant Orcs; other goblinoids with effortMost non-goblinoidsFlorwyndic SongscriptEvery educated elfOutsiders read the glyphs and miss the rail’s forceSylvaaricVarrisak of the same wanderingEresseans, who deny it is a scriptInverted ParunicDrow, correctly; Parunists, incorrectlyNo one, which is the weaponCold ParunicAnyone taught the grid, identicallyNo one; ambiguity was engineered outSkin-RecordsFleshshapersEveryone, who read it as injuryAccord Chancery HandEssentially everyoneNo one, deliberately
The Method
Workbook. How the Division rules its plates, so that no form has to be drawn from nothing.

The lattice is the 5×5 kamea of Mars, constant 65. Each of the fourteen Archons reads that lattice from a different station: one of the eight dihedral symmetries plus a cyclic value-shift.
A glyph name reduces letter by letter to lattice cells, and the path traced between those cells is the glyph. Class and Wellspring are inflections laid on that path rather than redrawings of it.
No glyph is drawn by eye. Which means the method never runs out: name a new spell and its written form already exists in every one of the fourteen hands.
Any path can be traced, then, and what stays fixed is attestation: a hundred and thirty-six forms have a station’s reading on record, and a fresh trace has none. The Seven Works of Hataraki trace nothing at all, being grips on Fate and not paths on the lattice, and so they appear in no hand.



Load-bearing cross-reference. The Long Reading holds that the Moto ancestral seat’s own name is recorded in a glyph the Continuum cannot classify, one of the thirty unclassified forms in the Master Glyph Index. It is the oldest proper noun in the record and it is deliberately blank.

Read next: The Counted Speech, why almost nobody says it aloud. This page sits on the shelf called The Foundations.

the-magic-system/the-foundations/index.content:
What a working is, the laws it conditions, and the boundaries every working is written in.
Dob Threlkeld, hedge-worker of Cobb’s Wharf, once bet his mule that he could set a wet hay bale alight in a rainstorm, and he won, the whole bale going up at once with the rain still falling on it, and then lost the mule, the bale, the barn and his good name in three parishes when the fire went on keeping the habits fire has always kept after he had stopped looking at it. This shelf exists so that you can lose your mule for better reasons.


The Physical Account: Two Sets of Books What a working is, in two complete descriptions of every event: the soul’s, which is the lens and says why, and the Measurewrights’ physics, their own theory, often right about how much and never about why; and where the power actually comes from.
The Sixty Wellsprings The sixty alchemical and spiritual transformations, each a governing idea that changes how a soul uses Aether, a lens on magic already potent, each with its own operation at the bench and its own flaw, and each explained by the Measurewrights, in their own account, as a law of natural philosophy. Read the hub, then whichever kind you need.
The Master Glyph Index — 136 Attested Forms The limits set on those laws, where each one stops.
The Spell Index Every attested working, filed by shelf, with its glyphs, Wellspring, operation, cost and counter.
The Master Codex The canon workbook, sheet by sheet, and where each sheet lives on this wiki.
The Descent of Parun — The Fourteen Hands The fourteen ways of writing a boundary down, and what each one changes. Its child, The Counted Speech, is why almost nobody says it aloud.


This shelf is the second in The Magic System, after First Steps. Next shelf: The Soul and the Climb.

the-magic-system/the-foundations/the-mas.content:
The canon workbook of the system, sheet by sheet, and where each sheet lives on this wiki
The Master Codex is the reference workbook every count and name in the magic system is checked against: the Wellsprings, the powers, the Stages, the glyphs, the workings and the formulas, one sheet each. This edition reads every working by the alchemical lens, its idea and the operation that idea performs, and keeps the Measurewrights’ account beside it as their own reckoning. Most of its sheets are drawn from pages of this wiki, so the page is the fuller account and the sheet is the table. Facts in it are copied, never invented, and a blank cell means no source states it.

the-magic-system/the-foundations/the-mas.title: The Master Glyph Index — 136 Attested Forms
the-magic-system/the-foundations/the-mas.content:
All one hundred and thirty-six attested Parun (root script of law) forms, ordered by Archon (one of the fourteen great powers of cosmic law)
Every midwinter the Third Counter Society sits down to eel pie and too much brandy, and every midwinter someone climbs on the bench, roars that they have found a third form written to obstruct another form, and traces it on the table in spilled wine with the whole room howling. Then a sober apprentice runs the path across the lattice, and it comes out as Knot or Lock in a borrowed hat, and the claimant buys the brandy. Master Simeon Blackwell bought the brandy nine years running and stayed solvent only by marrying a vintner. The index below is what they are all failing to get round.
What a Glyph Does
The index is a filing system. This section is what the filed thing is.
A glyph creates nothing and carries no power. A Wellspring (one of the sixty governing ideas that change how a soul uses Aether, which is mana, each of the sixty being one way a Titan’s law shows up in the world) is the lens, and the glyph is where you tell it to stop. The Wellspring’s law was already running before anyone wrote anything, and it continues running afterward. A glyph limits what a Wellspring’s idea is doing, at the layer the working leaves through. That is raw Aether out of the Shell for a Body hand, Essence (spiritual energy) out of the Core for a Spirit one, and a pull through the Attraction Layer for a Fate one. The bench’s old phrase for this is a boundary condition, and it still serves: the glyph moves a limit, and the law does what it has always done on the far side of the new limit.
This is why practitioners are burned, crushed and drowned by their own workings with such regularity. The glyph ends. The law does not. Everything a working produces goes on obeying every rule it has ever obeyed, including the ones nobody at the bench thought about, and the correct instinct at any threshold is to ask what the law will keep doing after the intent stops.
The same path on each layer
Every soul meets the world through three layers, and a Path is the layer it has learned to lean on. The path traced across the lattice is the same whichever layer the working leaves through, and so is the kind of limit. Where the limit lands is what changes.





























The working leaves throughPathWhat the limit isWhat runs on past itThe Aether ShellBodyA limit in matter: how far, how hot, how much load, the idea stopping where the glyph says it stops. The figures the Measurewrights write on a Wellspring’s entry are best kept hereMatter, keeping every habit matter keepsThe Essence CoreSpiritWhat a thing is taken to be. Bai Lüxian’s hinges kept their iron and lost the idea of being hingesThe meaning, which goes on being said after anyone wants it saidThe Attraction LayerFateA term or a prerequisite, inside the soul’s own share of fate: what has to be so firstThe odds, leaning for as long as the term stands
A Wellspring’s kind names its home plane and changes the bill, as follows.

A Spirit Wellspring on the Body Path still gives no fire. Its limit falls on what the flesh can bear.
A Fate Wellspring limits a bond, a debt, a name or the odds on every Path, and the Measurewrights’ account in its entry is only their analogue, there to give them something to argue with.
A Wild Wellspring on the Fate Path limits a claim. Pyreveil on that road is a claim that burns its way through, and its glyph says whose oaths may catch and whose may not.
A Medium Wellspring is at home on all three.
Home or away changes the resonance and the cost, double the effect at home with years of mastery and half again at most away. Off home, efficiency (η, the share of the spend that arrives) falls, and that fall multiplies with the η of the ground and of the worker’s Mastery on the road in use; the lost share is paid in the Path’s own coin, as heat through the Shell, as hollowing in the Core, as a heavier knot on the Layer. It never changes the path.

Glyphica, the writing of law, sits most comfortably on the Core, and any Path may take it up: a Body cutter’s ward stops the bottle, and a Spirit cutter’s is taken for a wall. On every Path the Continuum (the whole lawful order of reality) reads Authorization off the Attraction Layer, because the tie of harmonization is held there, so every cutter has dealings with the shallow end of Fate whether they like it or not.

The three-part reading of any entry. The seated Wellspring and its kind say which law is being limited. The Meaning and Use say what kind of limit it is. The Path says where it lands. A technique is those three decisions and nothing else, and everything downstream is the law’s own behavior.

One form in one sentence on three Paths
A sentence in Parun has four slots: a Warrant (by what right), a Ground (over what), a Vector (which way) and a Seal (until when). A form from this index fills whichever slot its limit belongs to, and the plain words of the Lexicon fill the rest. The Wellspring is never written at all. It is named by harmonization under the Warrant, read off the soul that stands behind the sentence.
Take [Th] Foundation, seated on Petralon (Wild): Imposes geometry; reinforces boundaries and load paths. Three masons, each of whom has tempered on Petralon and built her own gate, cut the same sentence over the arch:

oyeth · [Th] · mos · theb
By a thing I made with my hands · Foundation · held still · ending when the maker dies, and not before






























Her PathWhat she has limitedWhat happens when the ram comesWhat the law goes on doingBody (Petralon at home)The load, through the Shell: it stays in the line of the stonesThe force goes down the jambs and into the footing, and the lintel does not shear. The gate holds until the footing goesIt keeps sending weight to the floor. The gate settles a finger a decade, and somebody’s grandchild digs out the thresholdSpirit (Petralon away)What the gate is taken to be, through the Core: it is taken for the wall it stands inA ghost, a summoned thing or a thrower reading the place finds no door. The men on the ram find a door, oak and iron, and break itIt goes on saying wall. Her own dead cannot find their way home through it, and the priest she pays to fix that cannot lift itFate (Petralon away)A term on her own share of fate: before this gate falls, it goes through meNo thread comes down. The ram’s axle gives, the crew’s relief is late, and the bad luck of the siege runs down through her and into the ground. She sinks a little each day of itA gate with a real way of falling still falls, and what the term could not hold comes out of her
None of the three masons needs any Fate Mastery at all. None of them has moved anything that did not already have a way of happening.
A glyph and a thread
A glyph and its Seal spend the soul’s own share of fate. They set terms, and they move only what already has a way of happening. They never pull. A thread of Fate is another order of thing: it comes down from above through the Veil’s outer face, taking hold of one is extreme effort at every Stage, and how well anyone can do it is read on Fate Mastery. No path on the lattice is a thread, which is why this register holds no form called Thread and never has. The filament of the Seraphic Thread Blessing is the common confusion. It has the name, and it is a bond between two souls, given its weight in the shallow water of the Plane of Fate.
Where a Meaning below says thread, it means a strand of memory, of rot or of a bond, and where it says fate-thread or fate-tag it means a sworn thing in that same shallow water. Three cases mark the edge.

A Seal that waits. wolyeth ends a working when the last of a lineage is dead. It kills nobody. It sets a term, and any speaker with no Fate Mastery at all can say it.
Knot on a sworn bond. [Knt] Knot is a glyph, a cut sign that ties one thing over another, and it is no kin to the knot a pull leaves behind, the debt the world collects later, though the benches have been confusing students with the two since the word was first used for both. [Knt] supersedes a bound fate-thread, and the bond is somebody’s, so it is a contest: Dominion Fate (the soul’s weight in Fate) against the target’s Persistence and Continuity. Nothing is pulled and the loser’s oath is still sworn, superseded and sore.
A Fourth Seal. A sentence at that level does not wait for a line to end. It ends the line, which is past what any soul’s own share will buy, so it needs a grip on Fate, or a Warrant that carries one.

The eleven with no form
Eleven of the Sixty appear in no row of this index, seated or attested: Pyreveil, Cinerion, Manganthra, Ascensio and Abython (Wild); Nyxial, Penance, Redemption and Contrition (Spirit); Tarturon (Fate); and Aurevane (Medium). They do not line up by kind, and none of them is on any Archon’s list of associated Wellsprings. No Archon reads these eleven directly, so they take the thirty kind-of-limit forms and no others. A seated form is a station’s reading of one law, and no station has read these. A kind of limit applies to any law at all, and that gives the blank thirty their work. So a Pyreveil cutter writes in [Hael] Flame or [RenB] Boundary, a Cinerion rune is cut in the same forms, and the Moon of a Hundred Noons, an Aurevane art, lays [RenB] Boundary across [On] Light. It also explains why the best-known lens in the trade has nothing of its own to show a student on the first day.
The Loom, the lattice and the stations
The lattice of this page is a fixed five-by-five grid, the kamea of Mars, and every form is a path across it. The Loom of Stars is what that lattice looks like from above. Bara wrote it, and from the Veil’s outer face it is golden filaments crossing at impossible angles, each one tied to the pulse of a consequence. A scholar who has seen only the page draws squares. They are the same object, and nobody has yet survived the comparison with enough composure to publish it.
The Archons read it from stations. Each of the fourteen holds one position, and each of the 136 forms is a reading taken from one of them, or from two where a Secondary Archon is named, which is why every row below has an owner. An Epoch has no station. Bara stands above the seats, and the forms the old registers list beside the Three Epochs are unattested here: they are read from no station, and nobody can cut one. Where the same word turns up below, as Knot does under Maelor, a station has read a little of the same thing from underneath.
A Work is a grip and never a glyph. The Seven Works of Hataraki are functions Bara wrote into the Plane of Fate, and a Work is an inherited way of taking hold of one. It traces no path, fills no slot and adds up to nothing. The Moto read by delegated sight, from the Loom, the Kōkan Line having administered it under leave from above the stations. That is why the Lexicon has no Warrant word for what they hold: a word’s value is a sum of cells, and cells are what the stations read. The Vaulted Ring writes down the sound a Moto speaker opens on and leaves the value blank.
By what right. Irath’s small station sees the part of the lattice that asks this, and holds Command and Dominion for it. The Warrant is a sentence’s answer to the same question, and Dominion Fate is how that answer is weighed when somebody contests it. The three go by different names on different shelves, and they are one idea.

Runes, tags, chants and how long a working lasts
The four roles of the working trades and the four slots of the Counted Speech are one list under two names. Authorization is the Warrant, Boundary the Ground, Direction the Vector and Sealing the Seal.
What a fault does. A slot left wholly empty does nothing: no seal, no working, no cost, which is why a Valorin can bank whole formulae one word short and sleep beside them. A sentence that fires with a bad limit runs. The Long Loaf of Mothwick had its Boundary begun and abandoned before the last strokes, and it rose for months. The Long Noon of Skelby had a seal cut by somebody’s nephew, and it burned for thirteen days. Only a sentence that has actually fired can hurt anyone, and those two fired.
What must add up. Only spoken Parun must sum to sixty-five or a multiple of it. In the mouth the sum is all that can close a sentence, since there is nothing else for it to rest on. A cut hand is closed by its sealing stroke and held by what it is cut into, and a cutter who wants to count anyway is welcome to.
How long. The Seal sets the term, the substrate caps it, and anchoring holds it. The term is whatever the Seal says: first light, the maker’s death, the debt repaid. The substrate is the most it can have: granite outlives the mason and wet bark outlives the afternoon, and a spoken sentence’s substrate is the speaker. Anchoring is the Attraction Layer claiming the working as a presence in the world, the last step of every working, and without it the form dissolves the moment attention lapses. A cut sentence is anchored once, at its closing, and the surface carries the claim from then on, which is how a ward outlives its cutter. A spoken one stays on the speaker’s own Layer for as long as its term runs. Most field speaking seals on attention because that is cheap. Sergeant Thorn’s sentence at Dunmere Gate held to first light because she carried it there, on her feet, all night. A sentence that never sealed has nothing holding it and nothing stopping it, and it drinks the Aether of the place the way an ambient tag does until the place runs out or someone cuts across the line.
Runes and tags. A rune is the whole sentence in a substrate, and it works on anyone who passes. A tag is a short sentence that waits for a thumb. Its Warrant closes at the firing, and the Layer read is the one behind that thumb, which is why only the woken can fire one.
Chants. A chant is not Parun. A sound may not repeat inside a Parun word, and a chant is mostly repetition. It sets its condition in resonance, as Gravetongue does, and it does the same four jobs in tone: who sings and by what right, how far the sound carries, which way it runs, and the decay when it stops. Its words carry a sentence only when Glyphica is present, as when a chorister who has the count sings over a cut ward, and then that sentence answers to the rules above.
Three notations, kept apart. A Lexicon word is a run of sounds with a value. A form in this index is a named path, and its bracket mark is a filing mark and no sound at all, so the Vector ma and [Ma] Recall have nothing to do with each other. The strings of syllables in older rune manuals are a third and drifted notation, and they cross-check against neither.
Why the Counter class holds only two
Knot and Lock are the only two forms in the index written to obstruct another form, and under the limit reading the scarcity stops being a curiosity.
A glyph cannot attack a law. Laws are not the sort of thing that can be opposed; the practitioner who tries is arguing with the tide and will lose on schedule. What a counter does instead is impose a limit that prevents another limit from being established, a condition on the conditioning rather than on the phenomenon.
There are two of them because there are two ways to do it. Knot entangles a path so it cannot be traced cleanly. Lock occupies a limit so no other limit can be set there. Every counter-working ever recorded is one of those two moves, and the four centuries of effort spent looking for a third have produced synonyms.
The Valorin’s Errata looks like a third to everyone who has had a working corrected in mid-air, and the Society has had it on the bench more than once. It obstructs nothing. A correction amends a sentence that is already being said, blunting or redirecting it, and the amended sentence fires. Chaos is the other thing people bring to the brandy. Uurgath holds eleven forms in this index, and all eleven are legible limits on how things come apart, Ruin and Rupture among them. True Chaos is what breaks the sum itself, which is why it has no form, and why Errata finds nothing there to correct.
Why thirty carry no tally
The unclassified thirty are seated on no Wellspring, and the standing recommendation has been to leave the blank alone. The limit reading gives a reason to, rather than merely a preference.
A seat names the law being limited. Fifteen of the unclassified are first-order Roots: Flame, Light, Passage, Boundary, Ruin, Vastness, Command, Dominion. None of these names a law. Each names a kind of limit, applicable to any law at all, which is precisely why the Codex (the Master Codex, the standing register of glyphs and Wellsprings) can classify a derivative of the thing and cannot classify the thing.

Whether that is an archival gap or a property of the Continuum remains unstated. The mechanism explains why the column is empty. It does not explain why the world is built so the column has to be.

Unseated does not mean unused. Thirteen of the thirty have attested Wellsprings all the same, Silence and Truth among the widest in the register.

Each of the 136 entries carries its Glyph, Name, Class, Primary Archon, Secondary Archon, Meaning & Use, seated Wellspring with its kind, and its reach: every Wellspring attested for it, sorted by kind.
Worked example. [Ur] Balance · Root · Urion · Stabilizes Essence gradients; equalizes opposing forces. · Seated on Judicium (Wild).

The Titans’ grounds. Fourteen names in the reach column stand outside the Sixty, three cells each: Breath, Collapse, Continuum, Dread, Equilibrium, Etherea, Finality, Form, Foundation, Oblivion, Renewal, Shadow, Strain and Veils. Titans descend from Archons, so a form read from an Archon’s station can serve a Titan’s ground, and these rows are where it has been seen to. They do not make the Sixty any larger.

Standing Note

Every technique entry in the register closes on a Codex assignment line. That line points here, and it names the Wellspring and its kind, the Path, the glyph, and the limit stated in that Path’s terms.
Assignment is decided after the concept and the idea, never before, and it is a filing decision rather than a generative one. If no form fits, the correct move is to say so in the same sitting, and not to bend the idea until it files.
Any path can be traced, and attestation is what is fixed. A new name reduces letter by letter to cells like any other, so the method never runs out, and a working may use the trace at the maker’s own risk. It is a sentence no station has been seen to read. It stays in that working’s own notes, and it does not enter this index.

Amendments
The 136 stay fixed, and a form’s attested lists can still grow at the edges when a working on file shows the reach. Each extension is entered here with its reason, so that a reader checking a Codex line finds it, and it is entered in the Codex’s own columns, since the Codex is what it amends.
[Abys] Deep · Oblation added. [Abys] Deep, a directional undertow of sub-Realm pressure, carried an Abyntheus row. Its attested reach now includes Oblation, taken on the pitch in Obrenkael · The Mule (Summoned and Bound), Deadweight, on the reasoning that a psychopomp’s road is a directional undertow of sub-Realm pressure and that Abyntheus and Oblation are both pressure-grammar Wellsprings under different Archons. Its primary Wellspring is unchanged. [Th] Foundation, drafted beside it in the same chain, is not amended.
In this index’s terms: [Abys] Deep stays seated on Abyntheus (Spirit), and its reach now includes Oblation (Fate).

Every attested working written in these forms is filed in the Spell Index.
