Absolution · The Cleansing Current

Folk name the Pardon (what carters, soldiers and the commons call it; each culture may add its own beside it).
The idea Forgiveness. A soul’s history stays and its shape stays, and the old poison stored in them is let out.
Kind Spirit
Titan Dazkar: restitution completed, the debt let go once proportion has been met.
Operation Separation: the old poison is parted from the history that stored it, and the history is left whole.
Hue Polished steel, bright and unclouded, because the poison has been let out and the shape that held it is left whole with nothing locked under the shine.
Ground Favors old pilgrim roads, shrines and the quiet ground of a feud settled; hates fresh battlefields and any ground under a live grudge. This says where its Aether pools and thins and no more: with nothing in the world for the ground to act on, it answers in a fight only to the ground’s own measures, Aetheric Density and, on ground like this, Echo Depth, which runs high here and cheapens a Spirit working.
Contrary Exuroth (the quench against the anneal); Tarturon (the debt held against the debt let go); Penance (the anneal against the hammer).
On the Body Old injuries stop costing what they cost: the knee keeps its scar and its bad angle and no longer charges the fighter for them. There is no fire and no glow, only a body that has stopped carrying its history.
On the Spirit At home it lets the old poison out of a soul, one’s own or a willing other’s. The memory and the shape it left stay exactly where they were, and what they had been leaking into everything else stops.
On Fate A debt or grudge can be let go and the thing it was pulling on stops pulling, and at the end of long confession a levied host held in the line by an old wrong may wake one morning with no very clear reason to charge. It takes all the holder’s strength to absolve what was never theirs to forgive, it fails more often than not and leaves a knot either way, some old grudge against the holder waking up elsewhere, and whether the men feel the line go slack or merely forget to form up is an old quarrel among confessors.
Spirit Temperance through forgiveness.
Alchemy The gentle reheat: the strain let out of worked metal and its shape left alone. (the trade’s reading)
Stat Effect Strengthens Tempering Clarity, Harmonics Attunement, Resilience Fortification. Old fractures lose their toxicity.
Glyph [Grs] Grace; attested on five more.
Failure Not every old hurt is poison: some of what a soul stores in its history is what holds it shut, and forgiveness, once it is running, cannot tell the two apart. Let out more than the poison and the soul loses the hold it had been quietly relying on to stay closed, and the old fractures it had carried safely open. The Measurewrights call it over-relaxation.

The Measurewrights’ account. This is the guild’s theory, often right about how much and never about why.
Analogue · Stress-relief annealing. Removal of residual stress without change of form.
Mechanism · A worked component, they say, carries locked-in stresses from its own manufacture, invisible, dimensionally irrelevant, and entirely capable of causing failure under a load the part should have carried, and heat treatment relaxes them while leaving the shape untouched. By their reckoning Absolution does exactly this to the old fractures in a soul: the history stays, the geometry stays, and the stored energy that made the history dangerous is released. Reports of it easing anything outside a soul, a cracked bell or an unwilling stranger, are rare and argued over. Where the released energy goes, their ledgers have never said.
Abyntheus · The Outer Pulse

Folk name the Vastness (what carters, soldiers and the commons call it; each culture may add its own beside it).
The idea Vastness. The great scale read off the small vessel, a mortal soul stretched to take in things far too large for it.
Kind Spirit
Titan Ilgrimm: the unknown met at a scale that keeps knowledge humble, and breaks those it does not humble.
Operation Sublimation: the small soul is raised toward the great scale and brought back down still holding it.
Hue Deep naval blue, slow-pulsing, the color of open sea and night sky, because the soul has been stretched over the great distance and keeps the slow time of things far too large to hurry.
Ground Favors high open ground, sea horizons and clear night sky; hates iron-caged interiors and deep shafts. This says where its Aether pools and thins and no more: with nothing in the world for the ground to act on, it fills a reserve from Aetheric Density like any other, and in a fight it answers to Echo Depth, the weight of memory a place holds.
Contrary Coagulatio (a soul stretched over the great distance against a soul settled round one grain).
On the Body It lends the arm nothing. It gives a frame that can stand under things too big to look at, so the fighter keeps their feet and their breakfast when a far higher Stage’s Pressure or the sky over a Well comes down on them.
On the Spirit The Core’s aperture widens past what a mortal head was built to hold, and a Principle or an Archon’s working becomes something the practitioner can read and, at some cost to their sanity, engage.
On Fate The holder feels very long ties, the bond laid down before they were born or the debt that runs to the far side of the world, and soldiers near them bear what others break under, having been made to feel how small one field is inside what is coming. A tug on one of those ties, which might lean a whole people’s old hatred on somebody’s border, is the labor of decades, and the longest threads are apt to belong to Archons and the great principles, who may look down to see who is pulling. The knot on a thread that long is sized to match.
Spirit Temperance through vastness.
Alchemy The Emerald Principle at the bench, as above, so below: the great scale read off the small vessel. (the trade’s reading)
Stat Effect Strengthens Dominion Sovereignty, Sense, Gnosis Cognition. The conceptual ceiling expands to engage Archon-tier and Principle-level phenomena.
Glyph [Ab] Abyss, [Abys] Deep, [Let] Tide; attested on three more.
Failure The small vessel can hold the great scale only while it still knows it is small. Stretched too long between the near end and the far one, the soul loses its sense of how the two fit together, and what comes back to it is noise the practitioner is nonetheless convinced is a signal. The Measurewrights call it baseline decoherence.

The Measurewrights’ account. This is the guild’s theory, often right about how much and never about why.
Analogue · Very-long-wavelength propagation and interferometry. Resolution from baseline, not aperture.
Mechanism · Long wavelengths, they explain, travel enormous distances, penetrate what shorter ones cannot, and carry the oldest signals in existence. Resolution at that scale comes from separating two small instruments by a continental baseline and reconciling their phase, and a larger instrument would not help. They hold that Abyntheus expands the conceptual aperture of the Essence Core by the same trick, letting a mortal Crystal engage phenomena whose scale should render them illegible. All of it happens in the soul. It throws nothing and moves nothing, and the reports of far-off bells heard and floors felt to tilt around an old Abyntheus master are argued over at every Measurewright’s dinner.
Catharsis · The Wellspring of Release

Folk name the Letting Go (what carters, soldiers and the commons call it; each culture may add its own beside it).
The idea Letting go. A load set down so completely that the setting down spends it, and the soul comes out on the other side lighter and changed.
Kind Spirit
Titan Sylorin: Soul Reforging, a load of trauma spent down in the change of state.
Operation Dissolution: the hard thing held in the soul is loosed into the change of state and is gone into it.
Hue Pale rose-gold, the flush of a face after the weeping is done, warm and spent.
Ground Favors bathhouses, hot springs and confessionals, where people have long come to set things down; hates barracks and courts, where nobody dares. This says where its Aether pools and thins and no more: with nothing in the world for the ground to act on, it answers in a fight only to the ground’s own measures, Aetheric Density and, on ground like this, Echo Depth, which runs high here and cheapens a Spirit working.
Contrary Pyraeon (keeping the heat for life against setting the load down); Vantabriel (setting it all down against carrying it all).
On the Body It gives a fighter nothing to throw. Terror, exhaustion and the shaking after a kill go out of the limbs in one long breath, and hands that could not close an hour ago close.
On the Spirit Grief and rage held in the Core are spent by the letting go of them and take the old order of the soul along, so the person who stands up afterward is calmer and honestly somewhat different from the one who sat down.
On Fate With everything the holder has, a bond or a load can be put down so completely that the line goes slack, and once in a long while a beaten company under such a captain sets down its terror all at once and stands up again with nothing left to rout from. Turned across a field it is rarer and stranger, the men opposite losing their hatred in the hour they needed it, and the holder comes out of it unable to say for a season what they themselves were fighting for, and is handed, later, a load that somebody else set down, which is the knot.
Spirit Temperance through letting go: release, purgation, true clearing. The Heresiology’s warning stands beside it, that nothing is purified by being merely emptied.
Alchemy Purgation: the matter gives up its burden in the change of state itself. (the trade’s reading)
Stat Effect Strengthens Harmonics Empathy, Tempering Maturity, Resilience Fortification. Emotional weight converts into structural clarity.
Glyph [Xr] Excision, [Sv] Sever; attested on three more.
Failure Nothing can be let go that has not first been admitted. A soul on this lens that will not say what it is carrying cannot set it down, so the load goes on gathering past the hour it should have gone, and when the admission finally comes it comes all at once and takes everything near it down with the load. The Measurewrights call it supercooling.

The Measurewrights’ account. This is the guild’s theory, often right about how much and never about why.
Analogue · Latent heat of phase change. Enthalpy absorbed at constant temperature.
Mechanism · Melting ice at zero degrees, they point out, absorbs three hundred and thirty-four joules per gram and the temperature does not move a fraction, the whole of it going into breaking the ordered structure. They read Catharsis as the Core doing the same with an emotional load: routing it into a change of state instead of into output, so that the pressure is spent in the change and the practitioner arrives calmer and differently made. The ice is a comparison and all of this happens in the soul: nothing outside the practitioner changes by a degree, unless you count the chill reported in a few confessionals, which the guild is still arguing about.
Contrition · The Broken Flame

Folk name the Hard Lesson (what carters, soldiers and the commons call it; each culture may add its own beside it).
The idea A failure owned. Only what a soul truly got wrong and truly survived turns into armor for it.
Kind Spirit
Titan Dazkar: karmic return taken up willingly, the thing done coming back as armor.
Operation Fermentation: a failure truly lived through is left to work in the soul until the poison of it turns into armor against itself.
Hue Dull red with a sting, because a failure owned is a wound kept, healed over and still smarting wherever it is touched.
Ground Favors plague graves, hospices and ground where a whole people failed and lived; hates sterile ground and places that have never been tried. This says where its Aether pools and thins and no more: with nothing in the world for the ground to act on, it answers in a fight only to the ground’s own measures, Aetheric Density and, on ground like this, Echo Depth, which runs high here and cheapens a Spirit working.
Contrary Lethegraal (no hand choosing what falls against a failure owned by name); Sublimatio (a failure kept as armor against a lower self left behind).
On the Body The body learns to bear what it has already failed against, and the tremor that took a fighter’s hand in their first rout does not come a second time, because the same fear met again is answered at once. A rehearsed failure teaches the flesh nothing, and neither does anyone else’s.
On the Spirit A real failure, owned without excuse, is written into the Core as a standing answer, so the deceit or the despair that broke a soul once finds it already armed. An excuse voids the record, and the Core knows an excuse when it has made one.
On Fate An admitted fault loses its hold, so a captain who has stood in front of her company and named her own rout has taken away a crack that a Fate fighter would have pried at, and the next oath sworn over it tends to keep. It has to be paid for by failing in earnest and surviving it, and such a person is famously hard to blackmail and seldom beaten the same way twice.
Spirit Temperance through acceptance. The confessors’ reading: a failure owned and survived.
Alchemy The dose: a poison survived at its measure, and the body keeps the receipt. (the trade’s reading)
Stat Effect Strengthens Tempering Maturity, Resilience Integrity. Past failures become structural reinforcement.
Glyph None attested in the Index (see Where the Registers Disagree on the hub).
Failure A failure owned becomes armor against that failure, and a soul that owns its failures too thoroughly stops telling the failure apart from itself. The armor spreads past what it was raised against, and the practitioner begins answering their own tissue as though it were the original insult. The Measurewrights call it autoimmunity.

The Measurewrights’ account. This is the guild’s theory, often right about how much and never about why.
Analogue · Immunological memory and hormesis. Sub-lethal exposure producing adaptive benefit.
Mechanism · A pathogen survived once, they note, is answered faster and harder the second time because the response was recorded, and a sub-lethal dose of a stressor frequently leaves an organism measurably more capable than it was. Their reading is that Contrition converts failure into that record. On their account the mechanism requires the failure to have been survived, and it requires it to have been genuine, because a rehearsed one produces no antibody. The record is kept in the soul, and reports of it reaching further, a body shrugging off the very poison its owner once confessed to, are few and argued over. How the Core tells a rehearsed failure from a real one is a question they answer by changing the subject.
Eclipseron · The Shadowed Star

Folk name the Absence (what carters, soldiers and the commons call it; each culture may add its own beside it).
The idea Reading what is missing. The shape of an absence taken as knowledge of the thing that cast it. This lens has the truest claim of the Sixty to reading what fails to be there. People call that darkness and are being romantic: it is a system described by its absences, which is a harder and less romantic thing than its practitioners generally admit.
Kind Spirit
Titan Ilgrimm: Shadow as Revelation, truth glimpsed sideways.
Operation Distillation: what was driven off is read from the dead head left behind in the retort, the absence drawn down into knowledge of the thing that cast it.
Hue Red-violet with a dark disc, because the lens is read by what is missing, and the disc is the absence at its center that tells the rest of the light what cast it.
Ground Favors Veil-thin zones, surveyed ground and the sites of old observatories; hates warp scarring, contested Domains and unmapped terrain. This says where its Aether pools and thins and no more: with nothing in the world for the ground to act on, it fills a reserve from Aetheric Density like any other, and in a fight it answers to Echo Depth, the weight of memory a place holds.
Contrary Aurevane (seeing the thing against reading the hole it leaves).
On the Body The body learns to bear what has been taken from it, with no fire or force added: a missing finger, a deaf ear or a dead leg stops throwing the fighter, whose limbs now know the exact shape of what is gone and work around it.
On the Spirit The practitioner reads a soul by what it withholds, and derives from the shape of a silence, or of a memory cut out with a clean edge, the thing that used to be there.
On Fate The holder reads the shape of what is missing, the oath left out of the contract or the column that ought to be on the ridge by now, and that reading takes nothing but a long sad habit. To act on it is the hard thing: after years of grief spent learning how, a company under this person can be made to close on the shape of its dead, so the gap torn in the line at noon never opens in the men beside it, and the holder carries the whole absence afterward, with a knot that falls due as one more gap, opened where they were not looking.
Spirit Temperance through eclipse.
Alchemy The dead head read: what stayed behind in the retort tells you what left it. (the trade’s reading)
Stat Effect Strengthens Gnosis Analysis, Harmonics Suppression, Dominion Sense. The practitioner reads reality by what is missing from it.
Glyph [Oth] Path, [Ph] Phase; attested on five more.
Failure An absence is knowledge only if something cast it, and the idea cannot tell a gap left by a thing from a gap that was always empty. A practitioner committed to reading what is missing will eventually construct an object out of a gap that had nothing behind it. The Measurewrights call it false transit.

The Measurewrights’ account. This is the guild’s theory, often right about how much and never about why.
Analogue · Occultation and transit photometry. The information carried by absorption lines.
Mechanism · A hidden planet, they say, is found by the dip in its star’s brightness long before anyone sees it, and a spectrum’s dark lines carry more composition data than its bright continuum. By their reckoning Eclipseron tunes the perception of the Essence Core to the negative: the practitioner reads what has been blocked, subtracted, or withheld in a soul, and derives from the shape of the absence the shape of the thing casting it. It casts no shadow and dims no lamp, and whether a master can read a sealed box the same way, from the hole it leaves in a room, is claimed by some and argued over by the rest.
Hypnather · The Sleep Crown

Folk name the Sleep Crown (what carters, soldiers and the commons call it; each culture may add its own beside it).
The idea The sleep crown. Change that comes only at rest, the soul setting itself in order in the dark while nothing is asked of it.
Kind Spirit
Titan Nysera: the sleep that passes under her veil, the soul setting itself in order where nothing real is asked of it.
Operation Distillation: the soul is passed through the dark again and again while it rests, each pass leaving its order a little purer than the last.
Hue Glassy violet, the clear still violet of a dark room at rest, because nothing stirs on the surface while the soul sets itself in order underneath.
Ground Favors darkness, silence, sickrooms and old dormitories; hates crowd density and any place with an alarm bell. This says where its Aether pools and thins and no more: with nothing in the world for the ground to act on, it answers in a fight only to the ground’s own measures, Aetheric Density and, on ground like this, Echo Depth, which runs high here and cheapens a Spirit working.
Contrary Ignivale (no gap between wanting and doing against change that comes only at rest); Tarturon (the soul at rest against a debt that will not let it lie down).
On the Body The body does its mending asleep and does it thoroughly, a single night’s rest doing the work of many, and none of it works while the eyes are open. Its fighters come to the field new every morning and are finished after a few nights without it.
On the Spirit At home the Core sets itself in order in the dark while nothing is asked of it, and the person who lay down is not quite the one who wakes. The rare art that lays that quiet on someone else in sight is really laying it on their soul, the sect masters say, with the body merely following, and nobody has settled the matter since the only witness is asleep.
On Fate A sleeper’s oaths hold and their enemies lose the thread of them, and a commander who will give up waking for it, sometimes for weeks, may see a camp rest when it ought to lie awake and a night attack come down the wrong valley, for a knot that falls due as a night’s rest the holder badly needed and does not get. The old rule against waking anyone under it is older than the Guild, because what stops partway sets worse than it began.
Spirit Temperance through rest.
Alchemy The Standing: nothing is done and nothing may be done, and the thing goes on ordering itself in the dark. (the trade’s reading)
Stat Effect Strengthens Vitality Regeneration on sleep cycles, Tempering Yield, Gnosis Retention. Recovery during rest becomes dramatically more efficient.
Glyph None primary. Attested on [Vel] Mind, [Vl] Veil, [AnMa] Anamnesis and [Ora] Truth.
Failure Change that comes only at rest belongs to the rest, and the soul has no say in when it is finished. Break it off partway, by waking or by force, and the order it was setting stops where it stood, worse ordered than before it began. The Measurewrights call it interrupted relaxation.

The Measurewrights’ account. This is the guild’s theory, often right about how much and never about why.
Analogue · Structural relaxation. Physical aging of a glass toward its equilibrium configuration.
Mechanism · A glass, by their account, is a liquid that stopped moving before it finished arranging itself, and left undisturbed it continues to relax toward the ordered state it never reached, slowly and only while quiescent. They say Hypnather grants the Crystal that behavior. The reorganization happens during genuine rest and cannot be forced by ordinary means, which is why, they say, Hypnather practitioners sleep like the dead and wake structurally different. A few arts do force it, pinning the quiet true on command in the practitioner or in a body held in sight, so that the target’s motion slows and its outline smooths as though sleep had come down all at once. On their figures the physics is nearly free and the Essence is not, and a relaxation forced is a relaxation that ends in the Failure above.
Lethegraal · The Cup of Forgetting

Folk name the Cup (what carters, soldiers and the commons call it; each culture may add its own beside it).
The idea The cup. Time’s mercy hurried along: old pain settles on its own schedule, and no hand chooses what falls.
The turn Accepting that something is over, and meaning it.
Kind Spirit
Titan Chronaeus: pace, every disturbance settled in its own time. His Era-Forge’s Toll is written in this Wellspring.
Operation Dissolution: old pain is loosened into the soul on its own schedule until nothing of it is left but plain structure that holds weight.
Hue Gray-violet, slow ebb, because old pain settling on its own schedule gives up its color the way a bruise does, a little each day and never by anyone’s choosing.
Ground Favors old battlefields grown over, ruins and quiet graveyards; hates saturated Aether, crowd density and fresh wounds. This says where its Aether pools and thins and no more: with nothing in the world for the ground to act on, it answers in a fight only to the ground’s own measures, Aetheric Density and, on ground like this, Echo Depth, which runs high here and cheapens a Spirit working.
Contrary Cataclysm (upheaval against settling on its own schedule); Penance (letting time take the old pain against going back to it on purpose); Contrition (no hand choosing what falls against a failure owned by name).
On the Body The same wounds close on the same schedule, and the terror stored in them drains early, so a man burned half to death can stand beside a cook fire by spring with no faster healing to show for it.
On the Spirit Under this cup the soul digests what it has been choking on, by its own clock and nobody’s choice, and old grief goes down into the Core as plain structure that holds weight. Physicians prescribe it for that reason, and nothing about it reaches anyone but the one holding the cup, unless you count the family who wonder why she has stopped crying.
On Fate Time wears bonds as well, and by pouring themselves out a holder can hurry it along, so the rage an enemy army carried out of its burned capital may have gone to mere complaint by the second week of the march. It is slow, draining work that nothing can aim, its knot least of all, and its holders have lost sieges to their own side’s forgiveness when a vow to die on the wall went slack on the morning it fell due.
Spirit Temperance through quiet. The confessors’ reading: time, old pain digested into neutral architecture.
Alchemy The settling: the charge left to come to rest on its own schedule, with no hand choosing what falls. (the trade’s reading)
Stat Effect Strengthens Tempering Maturity, Harmonics Stability. Trauma metabolizes faster. The Crystal digests old pain into neutral architecture.
Glyph [Cro] Cycle, [Len] Line, [StSl] Still-Sleep; attested on eight more.
Failure The cup can hurry time’s mercy and cannot choose where the settling stops, because no hand chooses what falls. Hurry it too far and the old pain does not come to rest but swings past it on every cycle, and the practitioner rocks back and forth rather than settling. The Measurewrights call it under-damping.

The Measurewrights’ account. This is the guild’s theory, often right about how much and never about why.
Analogue · Relaxation time. The characteristic constant with which a perturbed system returns to equilibrium.
Mechanism · Every disturbed system settles, they say, and the only question is how long. By their reckoning Lethegraal shortens the time constant. Nothing is removed and nothing is chosen; the same trauma metabolizes down to neutral architecture on a schedule the practitioner is not otherwise able to influence, which is why the Wellspring is prescribed and Letheveil is merely permitted. What set the schedule in the first place is not in their tables.
Letheveil · The Waters of Forgetting

Folk name the Forgetting (what carters, soldiers and the commons call it; each culture may add its own beside it).
The idea Forgetting on purpose. Learning which memories hold up the house and which ones are chains, and cutting the chains. It surfaces when denial has started to cost more than acceptance.
Kind Spirit
Titan Sylorin: what the river takes off a soul on the way to its next shape.
Operation Separation: the memories that are chains are parted from the ones that hold up the house, and skimmed off.
Hue Black-violet with color drained from the edges, because what is forgotten on purpose goes from the rim first, the chains skimmed away and the dark center left to hold the house up.
Ground Favors darkness, silence, ruins and still black water; hates crowd density and active Domains. This says where its Aether pools and thins and no more: with nothing in the world for the ground to act on, it fills a reserve from Aetheric Density like any other, and in a fight it answers to Echo Depth, the weight of memory a place holds.
Contrary Phreatis (what sinks in and returns against what is cut loose); Anamnesis (forgetting on purpose against everything keeping its past); Redemption (cutting the wound out of the story against building the self around it).
On the Body The flesh keeps its own memories, flinches and old breaks among them, and this lens lets the body put down the ones it no longer needs, so the shoulder forgets the spear that ruined it and the knee forgets to buckle at the old angle. No strength arrives with it, and a hand that has forgotten the wrong scar will walk straight back onto the blade that made it.
On the Spirit At home it goes into the Core with a skimmer and takes off the memories that are chains, one’s own or a willing other’s, and what is left runs lighter and truer. Done to the unwilling it is the crime the seal-courts were built for, and whether it can be done at a distance is argued mostly by people who cannot remember.
On Fate Forgetting a debt does not strike it off, as a great many people have been surprised to learn, but with a great effort the holder’s own end of the line can be cut, and a company that has cut its end of a rout marches back onto the same field with no memory in its knees of how that morning went. The holder pays in their own childhood, piece by piece, and what the rout cost is still owed, with the knot added, when the collector reaches the door.
Spirit Temperance through release of memory. The confessors’ reading: forgetting, the lesson of which memories are load-bearing and which are chains.
Alchemy The skimming: scum taken off the charge, with the worker’s guess at which part was scum. (the trade’s reading)
Stat Effect Strengthens Gnosis Cognition, and tests Resilience Anchoring rather than simply raising it. The practitioner learns which memories are load-bearing and which are chains.
Glyph [Stl] Still; attested on four more.
Failure Forgetting on purpose is only as good as the worker’s guess at which memories are chains, and every guess after the first is made with the memories already cut. Each pass takes off a little more, and a memory skimmed again and again wears down toward a made thing the practitioner still experiences as a memory. The Measurewrights call it generation loss.

The Measurewrights’ account. This is the guild’s theory, often right about how much and never about why.
Analogue · Lossy compression. Shannon entropy and the identification of low-information content.
Mechanism · Compression works, they explain, because most of a signal is redundant, and the art is entirely in knowing which components carry information and which merely occupy bandwidth. Their claim is that Letheveil performs that analysis on memory. It does not erase indiscriminately; it identifies what is load-bearing and discards the rest, and the practitioner’s certainty about which is which is the whole of the risk.
Mirithane · The Wellspring of Reflection

Folk name the Mirror (what carters, soldiers and the commons call it; each culture may add its own beside it).
The idea The honest mirror. The inside and the outside made one surface.
Kind Spirit
Titan Dazkar: the mirror of consequence, the same that annulled Razakiel by reflection alone.
Operation Conjunction: the inside and the outside are joined into one surface, so what leaves the soul is what is in it.
Hue Silver-violet mirror, because the inside and the outside have become one honest surface, and the aura shows what the soul is with nothing laid over it.
Ground Favors dark still water, polished black stone and silence; hates crowd density and active Domains. This says where its Aether pools and thins and no more: with nothing in the world for the ground to act on, it fills a reserve from Aetheric Density like any other, and in a fight it answers to Echo Depth, the weight of memory a place holds.
Contrary Luminalis (hiding what shows against the inside and outside made one surface); Oneirion (the surface that shows what is there against the space of what can be thought).
On the Body The body stops spending itself on concealment, with no clenched jaw, no swallowed flinch and nothing kept up for the room, and it gets back the breath all that cost. It also loses every feint it ever owned, and the sparring hall finds this out first.
On the Spirit At home the Core and what leaves it become one surface, so a working carries what the person actually is, and a soul at peace with itself throws truer than its Grade suggests. Turned on someone else, the art hands them their own soul with the flattery taken off, and whether that counts as a technique or merely as tactlessness is a dispute the Measurewrights have yet to close.
On Fate Presence turns into plain speech: a room knows what this person wants, an oath sworn under this lens cannot carry a hidden clause, and a sworn company will follow one off a cliff with nobody left to wonder about the orders. Turning that on a parley, so an enemy goes home knowing how much of his own army means to stand, strips the holder bare before every soul present and leaves them nothing private for the rest of their life, which is why it is rarely done. The knot, finding nothing of the holder’s left to uncover, falls on those nearest them, one of whose secrets comes out at a bad hour.
Spirit Temperance through stillness. The confessors’ reading: self-sight, the inside and the outside made one honest surface.
Alchemy The blick: the flash on the assay button that shows the metal exactly as it is. (the trade’s reading)
Stat Effect Strengthens Harmonics Attunement, Tempering Coherence. Output becomes a more honest reflection of internal state.
Glyph [Se] Song, [Ari] Aria, [Nx] Nexus, [Pt] Pattern, [Wvn] Weave; attested on fifteen more.


Failure · An honest mirror shows everything or it is not honest, and the idea has no way to keep one thing back. A practitioner in a state they would rather not broadcast broadcasts it perfectly. The Measurewrights call it perfect return.

The Measurewrights’ account. This is the guild’s theory, often right about how much and never about why.
Analogue · Specular reflection. The law of reflection; the phase-conjugate mirror.
Mechanism · A true mirror, they say, adds nothing. Angle in equals angle out, and fidelity is defined entirely by the absence of introduced distortion. A phase-conjugate mirror goes further and returns a wavefront that undoes its own aberration on the way back. They describe Mirithane as making the Essence Core such a surface, so what leaves the practitioner is what was in them, with no flattering correction applied in transit. Why a soul would consent to become such a surface is not a question their mirrors answer.
Nyxial · The Nocturne Flame

Folk name the Nocturne Flame (what carters, soldiers and the commons call it; each culture may add its own beside it).
The idea The even flame. A self that holds its level whatever the room does.
Kind Spirit
Titan Ilgrimm: fear turned to function, one small flame kept level in the dark.
Operation Distillation: the soul is held in an even bath whatever burns beneath it, so it gives off its own level and never boils over.
Hue Deep violet with a small cold flame, because the self holds its level whatever the room does, one small flame kept even in the dark that neither flares nor gutters.
Ground Favors darkness, silence, night watch-posts and lamp-keepers’ rooms; hates saturated Aether and crowd density. This says where its Aether pools and thins and no more: with nothing in the world for the ground to act on, it fills a reserve from Aetheric Density like any other, and in a fight it answers to Echo Depth, the weight of memory a place holds.
Contrary Thaloré (the whole weight of a feeling against a level held whatever the room does); Tarturon (the regulated flame against the reaction with no stopping condition); Transference (holding a level against giving it away down the gradient).
On the Body No flame comes of it, whatever the old name promises. The body holds its level, pulse and temper and grip the same in a burning hall as in a bath, and it can bear a long siege or a long torture without the highs that would have helped or the lows that would have warned.
On the Spirit At home the soul keeps a setpoint, and elation, terror and other people’s Pressure all arrive and fail to move the needle. Some hold that the room around such a person slowly evens out too, tempers dropping and frights going flat (the lamps said to steady are steadied by calmer hands), and those who have tried to measure it got different answers on different nights.
On Fate The odds around this person run unusually flat, with no streaks and no disasters out of nowhere, and a Fate commander’s best morning, bought at ruinous expense, goes to waste against a company held level by it. Bonds stay at the temperature they were sworn at, as spouses have been known to mention, and holding a line at that level through a long siege is a slow exhaustion, all of it, the knots included, coming out at once on the day the load lifts.
Spirit Temperance through night. The confessors’ reading: evenness.
Alchemy The Still Bath: self-limiting at the boil, whatever the fire below it does. (the trade’s reading)
Stat Effect Strengthens Harmonics Stability, Dominion Gravity, Vitality Constitution. Baseline output does not fluctuate with environmental pressure.
Glyph None attested in the Index (see Where the Registers Disagree on the hub).
Failure A level held whatever the room does is paid for somewhere, and the idea pays by keeping everything it refused to feel. Held against a load it cannot overcome, the soul stores up every correction it could not make, and when the load lifts all of it comes out at once. The Measurewrights call it integral windup.

The Measurewrights’ account. This is the guild’s theory, often right about how much and never about why.
Analogue · Thermal inertia under negative feedback. A regulated system holding setpoint against ambient.
Mechanism · A body with high heat capacity governed by a feedback loop, they say, holds its temperature regardless of what the room does, and the larger the capacity the smaller the excursion. They read Nyxial as giving the Crystal that regulation. The practitioner’s baseline does not rise in favorable conditions and does not fall in hostile ones, which is a disadvantage exactly as often as it is a defense.
Oneirion · The Wellspring of Dream

Folk name the Dream (what carters, soldiers and the commons call it; each culture may add its own beside it).
The idea Dream as a place. Work done in the space of what can be thought, reaching a soul where no line of sight runs, because no soul was ever in the room.
Kind Spirit
Titan Nysera: dream as a place. Her Somnum Flow is written in this Wellspring.
Operation Sublimation: the working is lifted off every bench into the space of what can be thought, and comes down again in a soul.
Hue Dream-lavender, because the working passes through the space of what can be thought and takes the soft, shifting color things wear in a dream, never quite fixed.
Ground Favors darkness, silence, ruins and places where people have slept for generations; hates saturated Aether and active Domains. This says where its Aether pools and thins and no more: with nothing in the world for the ground to act on, it answers in a fight only to the ground’s own measures, Aetheric Density and, on ground like this, Echo Depth, which runs high here and cheapens a Spirit working.
Contrary Mirithane (the surface that shows what is there against the space of what can be thought); Chthonica (a place with no ground against nothing but ground).
On the Body Asleep or deep in trance the body learns what the dream rehearsed, so a fighter may wake with a parry they never drilled and the bruises of a duel nobody else attended. It lends no force, and an ache carried out of the dream lasts all day with no mark to show a physician.
On the Spirit At home a working goes through the space of what can be thought and arrives at a soul, since a soul was never in the room to begin with, and it steers by whatever the sender holds of the target: a name, a face, a shared roof. The dreamer wakes shaken and changed and the furniture has not moved, and the stories in which it did are told by people selling something.
On Fate A dream shared often enough becomes a bond, and strangers keep dreaming of the same door and then keep meeting, which is the small and very strange end of it. A holder who gives a season of nights to it can send a levy onto a field it has dreamed for a week, already knowing how to run, at the price of no longer being certain which field they woke on and of a knot that falls due as a waking day gone the way a bad dream goes, and a Domain (a region where the world runs on a practitioner’s terms) built on it has terms nobody can quite recite afterward.
Spirit Temperance through imagination. The confessors’ reading: dreaming.
Alchemy The working in the mind: the operation carried out on no bench at all. (the trade’s reading)
Stat Effect Strengthens Gnosis Cognition, Dominion Sovereignty, Ardency Cascade. Workings operate through conceptual space, not only physical space.
Glyph [Ka] Dream, [Vl] Veil, [RaE] Emotion, [DmSl] Dream-Seal, [Nys] Dreamrift, [OniV] Oneiric Veil; attested on five more.
Failure A dream is a place with no ground under it, and nothing done there knows where it is in a room. A working that was true in the space of what can be thought lands nowhere in particular when it has to come down into a real one. The Measurewrights call it projection error.

The Measurewrights’ account. This is the guild’s theory, often right about how much and never about why.
Analogue · Configuration space. A system’s state as a point in an abstract high-dimensional manifold.
Mechanism · A mechanical system’s every possible arrangement, by their account, is a coordinate in a space that has no physical location, and the system’s evolution is a trajectory through it. On their reading Oneirion lets a working act on that manifold rather than on the room, and on the Soul Plane the manifold is very nearly the plain fact of things: souls have no address in a room, and what lies between two of them is how much one can hold of the other in mind. This, they say, is the mechanical reason Oneirion techniques reach targets no line of sight connects, and the reason they are so difficult to describe afterward.
Penance · The Atoning Path

Folk name the Going Back (what carters, soldiers and the commons call it; each culture may add its own beside it).
The idea Discipline. A soul made stronger on purpose, by going back again and again to exactly the places where it did wrong or was hurt.
Kind Spirit
Titan Dazkar: purification through penance, to the letter of his law.
Operation Distillation: the soul is put back through the same fire at the same fault, again and again, the way a spirit is drawn over and over, until what comes over at that point is the strongest thing in it.
Hue Dull iron, darkening, because the soul is hardest where it has gone back most, and every return darkens it like iron beaten and beaten again.
Ground Favors training yards, penitents’ stairs and any ground worn down by one person’s returning; hates uniform soft ground with no history in it. This says where its Aether pools and thins and no more: with nothing in the world for the ground to act on, it answers in a fight only to the ground’s own measures, Aetheric Density and, on ground like this, Echo Depth, which runs high here and cheapens a Spirit working.
Contrary Lethegraal (letting time take the old pain against going back to it on purpose); Absolution (the anneal against the hammer).
On the Body What the fighter has chosen to endure stops being the worst of it, and the old pain in the old place is borne further each year than any trainer says it should be. A sword cuts them exactly as it cuts anyone else, and they keep walking.
On the Spirit Each deliberate return to a fault leaves the Core harder at that point, so the place where a soul once lied or broke becomes the place it cannot be made to do so again. The Crystal is not fooled about which faults are real.
On Fate A self-imposed vow bites sooner and holds longer, so a company that ran from a field can swear itself back onto that same field every year until it stands, each return paid in real wounds and leaving it harder to break in exactly the place it broke. A vow kept pulls nothing and leaves no knot. Only the penitent’s end of the line is theirs to pay, so a wronged man may stay wronged as long as he likes, usually on the other side of the field.
Spirit Temperance through discipline.
Alchemy The hammer’s law: metal hardest where it was beaten most. (the trade’s reading)
Stat Effect Strengthens Vitality Threshold, Tempering Coherence, Resilience Integrity. The Crystal aligns more honestly with lived behavior.
Glyph None attested in the Index (see Where the Registers Disagree on the hub).
Failure Discipline knows how to go back to the fault and has no word for enough. A soul returned to the same place too many times is all hardness there with no give left in it, and the next load does not bend it. It ends it. The Measurewrights call it strain embrittlement.

The Measurewrights’ account. This is the guild’s theory, often right about how much and never about why.
Analogue · Work hardening. Dislocation multiplication under plastic strain.
Mechanism · Bend a metal past yield, they point out, and it becomes harder to bend again, because plastic deformation multiplies dislocations until they obstruct one another, so the material is strongest exactly where it was most abused. They hold that Penance imposes that constitutive behavior on the Crystal, so deliberate strain accumulates strength, and the strength is honest because it is located precisely at the sites of prior failure. What it hardens is the soul, and claims that a penitent’s skin has turned a blade are rare and argued over in every order that keeps one.
Penanceflare · The Light of Contrition

Folk name the Open Flame (what carters, soldiers and the commons call it; each culture may add its own beside it).
The idea Burning in the open. Remorse that shines on the Soul Plane, so that what the soul is and what it means can be read by anyone able to look at a soul, and honesty costs nothing because nothing is hidden anymore.
Kind Spirit
Titan Prometheus: he burns what is false, and here the false thing is whatever the penitent was hiding.
Operation Calcination: whatever the soul was hiding is burned off in the open until nothing false is left to hide behind.
Hue The full spectrum, red to white, tracking temperature, because nothing in the soul is hidden and the remorse burns in plain view at its true heat, so the color tells anyone who looks exactly how hard it burns.
Ground Favors penitents’ roads, shrines of the Penance Flame and squares of public confession; hates sealed rooms and spy-houses. This says where its Aether pools and thins and no more: with nothing in the world for the ground to act on, it answers in a fight only to the ground’s own measures, Aetheric Density and, on ground like this, Echo Depth, which runs high here and cheapens a Spirit working.
Contrary Tenebra (nothing hidden against nothing seen); Luminalis (the light that cannot hide against the light that hides what it shows).
On the Body No fire comes of it, only a body that has learned to bear being seen: a wound or a fear left unhidden stops costing the body anything to hide, and the fighter’s tells, being plain to everyone, stop being any use to anyone.
On the Spirit The Core shows what it is and what it means, so every working wears its maker’s intent on its face, and the remorse that lights it is very hard to argue with.
On Fate Everything the holder owes stands in plain view, so a company sworn to them has no rumor left to break on and will sit out a siege on what it can see it is owed. Pushing that light into the enemy’s lines, so that their men start asking to see their own captain’s accounts, burns the holder’s every shame in front of both armies, leaves a knot that brings one more to light afterward, and has been managed only a handful of times.
Spirit Temperance through remorse.
Alchemy The fire that reports itself: heat read by its color, as every alchemist reads a flame. (the trade’s reading)
Stat Effect Strengthens Ardency Compression inversely, raising a working’s visibility rather than lowering it, and Gnosis Vigilance. Workings become more visible and more honest in expression.
Glyph None primary. Attested on [Py] Pyre and [Let] Tide.


Failure · Remorse burning in the open has no way to burn quietly, because the idea will not let anything hide, the burning included. Push it past what the body can bear to show and the burning climbs faster than the showing can carry it off, so the practitioner burns brighter and hotter together, in the open, until the tissue gives out. There is also no concealment mode. The Wellspring does not permit one, and a Penanceflare practitioner who needs to hide has harmonized with the wrong Wellspring. The Measurewrights call it thermal runaway.

The Measurewrights’ account. This is the guild’s theory, often right about how much and never about why.
Analogue · Blackbody radiation. Planck’s law and the emissivity of a body that cannot hide its temperature.
Mechanism · Every body above absolute zero, they say, radiates, and the spectrum of that radiation reports its temperature to anyone with an instrument. Their account is that Penanceflare does this to the Essence Core, raising its emissivity toward unity so that remorse shows on the Soul Plane at its true heat. The practitioner’s workings become brilliantly legible to any Gnosis (the stat of reading and knowing) that can look at a soul, their intent readable in the emission, and concealment becomes impossible in exactly the measure that honesty becomes free. Almost none of this reaches the physical world, and a hand held near a penitent feels nothing. Whether the faint light some witnesses swear to on the skin is really there, and whether the burning of the Failure above is heat at all or a body agreeing with its soul, the Measurewrights have been arguing for a long time.
Redemption · The Light Reclaimed

Folk name the Scar (what carters, soldiers and the commons call it; each culture may add its own beside it).
The idea The light reclaimed. The soul’s wound becomes its strongest place, and the whole self rearranges itself around what it really lived through.
Kind Spirit
Titan Florwyn: organic memory, a wound remembered into the strongest place in the body of a soul.
Operation Conjunction: the broken place is joined back into the soul as its densest point, and the rest of the self is joined to what was truly lived.
Hue Copper-bright, because the wound has become the strongest place, and the light reclaimed shines from the old break like new copper at a mended seam.
Ground Favors infirmaries, battlefield surgeries and ground close to blood; hates sterile ground and Essence-depleted soil. This says where its Aether pools and thins and no more: with nothing in the world for the ground to act on, it answers in a fight only to the ground’s own measures, Aetheric Density and, on ground like this, Echo Depth, which runs high here and cheapens a Spirit working.
Contrary Letheveil (cutting the wound out of the story against building the self around it); Fractura (where it will break against the break made strongest).
On the Body The body stops flinching from where it was broken, and a fighter will take a blow on the old break without the old terror and put real weight on a joint no physician would trust. The bone is no denser for it, whatever the pilgrims say.
On the Spirit What wrecked the soul becomes the densest part of it, so a Core that survived a betrayal or a long captivity is hardest to move on exactly that ground. The rest of the self slowly aligns to what was truly lived, whatever had been hoped for.
On Fate An old disgrace turns, by long living, into the very thing people trust the holder for, until the day a town that spat at them sends for them to hold its walls. Once or twice in a life that can be pulled on in the field, when an enemy plans the whole attack around the place this person broke twenty years ago and the soul that has rearranged itself there bears what the rest of them could not, while everything next to the old wound quietly gives way and the knot goes looking for a place that was never broken.
Spirit Temperance through return. The confessors’ reading: being reclaimed, the wound becoming the strongest place.
Alchemy The sound weld: metal densest at the old break. (the trade’s reading)
Stat Effect Strengthens Tempering Maturity, Resilience Integrity, Dominion Fate. Past trauma sites become the strongest points in the Crystal’s architecture.
Glyph None attested in the Index (see Where the Registers Disagree on the hub).
Failure A self rebuilt around its wound leans on the wound for everything, and the idea has nothing to say about the rest. The weight goes through the old break and passes everything beside it by, and everything adjacent to the old wound quietly thins away for want of use. The Measurewrights call it stress shielding.

The Measurewrights’ account. This is the guild’s theory, often right about how much and never about why.
Analogue · Fracture callus and Wolff’s law. Bone remodeling along lines of stress.
Mechanism · Healed bone, they note, is denser at the break than the bone around it, and a limb loaded repeatedly remodels its internal architecture to align with the load it actually receives. By their reckoning Redemption applies both to the Crystal: prior damage sites become the highest-density regions, and the whole structure reorganizes toward the stresses the practitioner has genuinely lived rather than the ones they expected. All of that happens in the soul. A limb that mended straighter because its owner was reclaimed is a story every order of the Wellspring tells, and it stays rare and argued over.
Thaloré · The Wellspring of Depth

Folk name the Heavy Heart (what carters, soldiers and the commons call it; each culture may add its own beside it).
The idea Depth of feeling. Emotion given its true weight in the soul, so that a grief can press on every soul in a whole room. A soul under this lens takes the shape of what holds it, and is likelier than most to fall into Synergia (Crystals briefly sharing one working) and Echo Bonds.
Kind Spirit
Titan Sylorin: the full charge a soul carries in the current, given its true weight.
Operation Dissolution: a feeling is let down through the whole soul to its true depth, and the soul takes the shape of what holds it.
Hue The deepest teal, nearly black, because feeling given its true weight is deep water, and the deeper it goes the less light reaches it.
Ground Favors deep standing water, flooded ruins and places of drowning and mass grief; hates arid terrain and thin dry air. This says where its Aether pools and thins and no more: with nothing in the world for the ground to act on, it answers in a fight only to the ground’s own measures, Aetheric Density and, on ground like this, Echo Depth, which runs high here and cheapens a Spirit working.
Contrary Nyxial (the whole weight of a feeling against a level held whatever the room does); Abython (pressure felt in full against pressure matched away).
On the Body No force comes of it. The frame learns to stay upright and keep working under a weight of feeling that would put another mourner on the floor, and a body that has carried that can carry a broken rib.
On the Spirit Feeling takes its true weight, and a grief held deep in the Core presses outward on every other soul in the room, who go home tired and cannot say why.
On Fate A bond takes on the full depth of what is felt in it, so a widow’s claim on a house leans harder than any deed, and a company’s grief for its dead captain will hold a wall that every sum says is lost. Letting that weight down on the enemy’s camp, where it settles on whoever already half believes they did wrong, takes the holder’s whole self and leaves a knot as heavy as the grief was, and a holder whose support gives way under it is crushed by the same grief.
Spirit Temperance through immersion. The confessors’ reading: depth of feeling, emotional truth given its full weight.
Alchemy Weight in the vessel: pressure set by depth alone, whatever the shape of the glass. (the trade’s reading)
Stat Effect Strengthens Harmonics Projection, Dominion Pressure. Emotional truth acquires metaphysical weight.
Glyph [Vo] Voice, [Wh] Whisper; attested on thirteen more.
Failure A feeling given its true weight weighs on the one who feels it as surely as on the room, and the idea does not choose which way it presses. A Thaloré practitioner whose own inner support fails is crushed under the weight they were laying on everyone else. The Measurewrights call it implosion.

The Measurewrights’ account. This is the guild’s theory, often right about how much and never about why.
Analogue · Hydrostatic pressure. Pressure as the product of density, gravity, and depth.
Mechanism · Pressure at depth, they say, depends on how dense the fluid is and how far down you are, and the vessel, the volume and the surface have no say in it. They hold that Thaloré gives emotional content that same constitutive relation: density times depth, expressed as literal metaphysical weight, which is why, on their account, a Thaloré practitioner’s grief has a measurable pressure field and standing near one is physically tiring. The field is a field in the soul. It moves no air and bends no reed, and the claim of three separate towns to a wall cracked by a Thaloré mourner is argued over mostly by people who have never stood near one.

Read next: the hub, for the kinds, the lens, the Titans and the Paths; and the other three kinds: Wild, Fate, Medium.

the-magic-system/the-foundations/the-six.title: The Sixty Wellsprings
the-magic-system/the-foundations/the-six.content:
“What burns in the crucible burns in the one who tends it.”
The oldest saying of the bench, older than any register.
Fourth edition. The first edition gave every one of the sixty a physical analogue, a mechanism in that analogue’s own terms, and a failure mode following from the mechanism rather than from the mood. The second added what the trade has always known and the Register was too proud to set down on the same page: what each of the sixty means at the bench and what it does to the soul. The third turned the page right way up, so that every entry opens on the idea, the transformation and the principle, and the physics follows as the scholars’ explanation of them. This one files the sixty by where each is at home, names the Titan whose law each one is, and gives each its own color, its own ground, its own contraries and its own operation at the bench, with each failure read from the flaw in the idea. No figure has moved. The physics now sits where it belongs, last on each entry, as the Measurewrights’ account. The Measurewrights have lodged their objection in the usual place.

Nobody on the Cold Tun bridge needs the Sixty explained, because their grandmothers saw Sanne Ruddock and Ond Gravell. Same Stage (a rung of the soul’s sixteen-step climb), the same numbers on the sheet, and both banks packed to the reeds with the green sashes of the Hot Tun Ladies and the slate caps of the Quarrymen, with a man selling fried dough off a pole between them. The bridge stands where a hot spring comes up through old bedrock, so two kinds of Aether (mana, the raw stuff of magic in the world around you) pool under that one span, and each fighter stood in the same air and pulled a different one. Sanne breathed in Pyreveil and came up deep ember-orange from the ribs outward, skin flushed and bone-dry, heat-shimmer climbing both arms until the spit boiled off her lip. Ond breathed in Petralon and went the gray of a wet anvil, and the dust on the deck sagged down around his boots with a long settling groan, and everyone on the bridge felt him get heavier without being able to say how. Her fire broke over him, and he stood in it. His fist went into her guard like a dropped lintel, and she laughed with blood on her teeth, because her body had stopped minding. For the length of a long sermon neither of them could do one thing about the other, and the crowd sang all through it.
Then both bills came due inside a single breath. Sanne got both hands round his wrist and hauled, straight outward, in tension, the one direction Petralon does not answer, and the man who had just stood in a bath of fire parted at the shoulder.
He did not bend first. Stone does not. And the heat she had kept banked in her own tissue to do it had to leave by whatever was nearest, which was her palms, and she stood there on the bridge with her hands cooking and her mouth wide open while Ond Gravell, one-armed and roaring, fell on her and took them both over the rail into the Tun. Draws keep the stakes at Cold Tun. The bookies bought new roofs.
Two fighters, one bridge, one breath of the same air. The whole of the difference was which idea each of them had let govern their Aether, what it did to the soul that took it, and what it would eventually charge. Every child in the Four Quarters already half knows this, being a Fixatio child or a Tarturon child by the day of the sixty they were born on, which is stated before their age is. The rest of this page is the long version, and it is worth the lamp oil.
Four Things to Know First
Every one of the sixty answers four questions, and anyone who keeps hold of them can read any entry in this register.
Its kind: where is it at home? Each of the sixty belongs to a plane. A Wild Wellspring is at home in the Physical World, Aegor’s reality, and it is a thing you can point at: fire in the ground, stone that moves. A Spirit Wellspring is at home on the Soul Plane, Ashura’s reality, and it is a change in a soul: forgiveness, forgetting, a failure owned. A Wellspring of Fate is at home on the Plane of Fate, Bara’s, and it is a change in what holds: a bond, a debt, a name, the odds. A Medium Wellspring is at home on all three and works across the Veil between them. That makes thirty-three, fifteen, six and six, and each kind has its own page. A kind names a home and never a lock.
Its lens: what does it do to you? A soul’s power was there before any Wellspring touched it. A Wellspring is the idea that soul bases its tempering on (tempering being the slow melting down and rebuilding of the soul’s layers), and it brings that power to a point: a little at first, and with years of mastery up to double. The numbers on the sheet do not move. What grows is how much of the burn, or the ending, or the stubborn weight is in the thing that hits you.
Its Titan: whose law is it? Each of the sixty is one way a Titan’s law shows up in the world. Thirteen Titans hold the sixty between them, and every entry names its own.
Your Path: what are you doing with it? A soul has three layers, and a Path is the one it has learned to lean on: the Body Path on the Aether Shell, the Spirit Path on the Essence Core, the Fate Path on the Attraction Layer. Any Path can take any Wellspring. On its home Path a lens can reach double, and away from home half again at most, and the same Wellspring down three Paths makes three different fighters.
What follows is those four answers at length, then what the scholars make of them, and then the register itself.
What a Wellspring Is
A Wellspring is an idea that changes a soul. Each of the sixty stands for one transformation, alchemical and spiritual at once: fire that renews, the breaking point, forgiveness, the honest mirror, the cup of forgetting, the first substance. Aether comes in sixty types because there are sixty of these ideas for it to carry.
You can see a Wellspring as a source of power you pull from, and on the street everybody does. They have reason to, since the ember really is in the ground at Cold Tun and you really can fill up on it. The better description, the one the benches and the confessors held long before there were registers, is the governing idea that transforms how a soul uses Aether. Your soul was already potent before any Wellspring touched it. A Wellspring puts a lens on that magic: it takes what is already there, brings it to a point, and turns the way the power moves in you.
That is why the Sixty matter more than almost anything else on a sheet. A Stage says how far up a soul has climbed. A Wellspring says what the climb is doing to it, and two fighters of one Stage and one set of numbers can stand on one bridge and be two entirely different weather systems. The Wellspring also sets the bill, because a law taken up as your way of living goes on charging you in its own coin.
The Four Kinds
Surveyors call these the four encounter types, because the classification tells them which direction the danger arrives from. It is also the kind on every entry below, which names the plane a Wellspring is at home on and locks nobody out of it.

The classification rests on a single question: where does the effect originate, and where does it arrive?

More than half of the Sixty are physical, and most of the rest are not physical at all. A Wild Wellspring is a thing in the world: fire in the ground, stone that moves, lightning, a solution crystallizing out of itself on the bench. You can point at it, and a practitioner who takes it up shapes what their soul spends around it. A Spirit Wellspring is a change in a soul: forgiveness, forgetting, a failure owned. There is nothing to point at, and it gives its bearer no fire to throw. It usually does little or nothing to the physical world, though an edge case will always find a Measurewright: a Thaloré grief can be felt across a room, and the argument over whether that counts is older than the Guild. A Wellspring of Fate is a change in what holds: a bond, a debt, a name, the odds. There is nothing to point at there either, only what keeps happening afterward. A Medium Wellspring is at home on all three planes and crosses the Veil between them as it works. Every one of the sixty changes the soul that takes it up; the difference is whether the world shows it too, and how soon. A spiritual entry below still carries an analogue, which is the scholars’ picture of what is happening in the soul, and no one has yet watched a forgiveness anneal.






























TypeMechanismWhich WellspringsWild Physical Plane dominantThe Aether appears as a transformation of matter, a thing you can point at. The stone was there. The water was there. The metal was there. The Aether reshapes it, moves it, compresses it, grows it, burns it, and whoever harmonizes with it shapes what they spend around the thing itself: the raw Aether packed in the Shell for a Body fighter, Essence in the Core for a Spirit one. The nested depth model
The three planes are nested, not stacked.
The Plane of Fate stands above the lower realities, the lattice upon which all possibility rests. A surveyor measures from the ground he stands on and calls that depth, and a theologian points the other way, and they mean the same place. The Soul Plane lies between, the stratum through which abstract law becomes a soul’s felt truth. The Physical Plane sits at the surface (the Material Plane is the same place under its other name), where truth becomes event, body, ruin, and mountain range. Only the last two are realities in any careful sense: what stands above them is everything that flows, every possibility, idea and concept, and “plane” is a courtesy.
Fate is a precursor. A tide that falls. What is decided at Fate-depth cascades through the Soul Plane and manifests on the Physical Plane as event.
This is why the four types produce different threat profiles.
Wild operates at the surface. The danger is physical and legible.
Spirit operates from the middle layer, and the cascade runs outward: the Crystal fires, the Shell expresses, and the body, where it is reached at all, manifests what the Soul Plane authored. What reaches the surveyor comes from no outside blow. They are being authored from inside.
Fate operates from above both lower realities, and the cascade has to come through both of the others. By the time the surveyor can see what was decided, it has already happened to them, and it looks like luck.
Medium operates at the Veil itself, the threshold where one plane’s law softens into another’s. Every layer moves at once, and the movement is reciprocal. The Veil is the skin of the lower realities, with an inner fold running between Physical and Soul and an outer face where both meet Fate, and a Medium lens works along the whole of it.
Whose Law It Is: The Titans
Follow any Wellspring upward and you arrive at someone. Bara wrote the Works, the laws the world is built from. An Archon is a Work crowned, a law enthroned. Titans descend from Archons: an Archon is a principle enthroned and a Titan is the same principle bearing weight, though the pairing is ragged and the descent is argued by everyone with a chair to argue from. And the Titans are the Wellsprings themselves, and the Sixty are their manifestations. Each of the sixty is one way a Titan’s law shows up, carried by Aether (mana), which is what remains of Omnara undivided and can therefore carry any idea at all. A Titan’s Ground, on the Fourteen Titans pages, is that law at full scale. An entry in this register is the same law at the size a person can take in.
Titans bear all three planes, so the Sixty make up all three. Dazkar shows up Wild in Judicium, Spirit in Penance and Fate in Tarturon, and the Prometheus who roars in Pyreveil is the same one who will not let you hide in Penanceflare. A kind says where a showing is at home, and a Titan says whose it is. The Master Codex and the Titans’ own pages have the arguments, and this register files each of the sixty under one name.
Thirteen Titans hold the sixty. The fourteenth, Vohrin, holds none: its frost is a Titan’s own power worked at Wellspring level, with nothing standing between it and its Titan, and the Wild page carries a marked note on it as the register’s one exception. A Titan walks no Path. A Path is something a soul does, and a Titan is the law itself, so nobody fights on the Fate Path with Sylorin. A soul takes up one showing of a law and tempers on that, and harmonizing with Pyreveil has never yet got anyone an audience.

The Lens by Path
A soul meets the world through three layers, and a Path is the one it has learned to lean on. The Body Path leans on the Aether Shell and the Physical World, the Spirit Path on the Essence Core and the Soul Plane, and the Fate Path on the Attraction Layer and the Plane of Fate, what has to be so before anything can happen. The Three Paths has the whole account. A Wellspring is the lens a soul bases its tempering on, and it shapes what each Path spends, in the terms of whichever layer is doing the work: raw Aether packed in the Shell (the Charge) on the Body Path, Essence in the Core on the Spirit Path, the claim on the Attraction Layer on the Fate Path. The idea stays the same and the target changes, from matter, to what a thing means and holds, to what a thing could have been. One Aether in three people makes three different fighters, and every entry in this register says how.
