A blow’s character comes from Wellspring and Path. Give two hitters the same Flux, one under Pyreveil and one under Nihiloth, and the first blow burns and ruptures while the second ends and quiets things. Hand that Pyreveil to a thrower on the Spirit Path and it is a third blow again, arriving from sixty paces on the soul and nowhere else: it burns the grudge a man walked in with and leaves his coat unscorched. A Fate fighter’s Pyreveil is mostly reach and a room that catches, and on the one day in a long while that they pull a thread it is a fourth: an ordinary cut, arriving because a strap has already burned through. The older books put all of this down to an inborn bias in the soul toward one Wellspring or another. The trade has given that up, having never once found the bias in anyone who had not already spent ten years under the Wellspring it was supposed to explain.
Every Wellspring has a home, and a home is never a lock. A Wellspring’s kind is a qualifier naming the plane it belongs to, so the home Path of a Wild Wellspring is the Body, of a Spirit Wellspring the Spirit, and of a Wellspring of Fate the Fate Path, while a Medium Wellspring is at home on all three (the four kinds are set out above). Any Path can use any Wellspring. At home it harmonizes cleanly and can reach double the effect with years of mastery. Away from home it works in that layer’s terms, at lower-quality resonance and higher cost, and reaches half again at most. The higher cost has a plain form. Off its home the lens lowers efficiency (η, the share of what is spent that arrives as effect), and that loss multiplies with the two every working already carries, the η of the ground and the η of the worker’s Mastery on that road, so an away lens on bad ground in an untrained layer is three losses stacked. The lost share is paid in the Path’s own coin: a Body hand sheds it as heat, a Spirit hand pays it in the Core as hollowing, and a Fate hand finds it in a heavier knot. Such a lens still changes how that soul uses Aether, and plenty of famous fighters are famous for exactly that clash. A Spirit Wellspring on the Body Path still gives no fire: it changes what the body can bear. The benches keep a standing bet on the first soul to pass half again away from home, and it has never paid out.
The lens brings forward what is already there. More of the idea arrives in every blow and every working. The numbers on the sheet do not move and no stat points appear, because a lens never added any. What grows is how much of the burn, or the ending, or the stubborn weight is in the thing that hits you.
It starts small, and only years reach double. Wenna Corry of Tallow Row, a lamp-lighter’s girl who went down the Body Path with her fists, paid a year’s wages for a bottle of Ignivale at sixteen, and for her first year the lens gave her about what a good pair of bellows gives a smith: her wicks caught a shade sooner and a shade hotter than her arm alone could have managed. She lived with it for twenty-four years. By forty she could break a man’s jaw on the Tallow Row steps and his beard would be alight before his teeth landed, and the bookies stopped asking whether she had been drinking and started asking what she charged. Her cousin Perrin took the same Ignivale down the Spirit Path, putting the spark into other people’s nerve from across the Row for a living (a shy bidder, a bride at the door, a fighter between rounds, and never once a wick), and has been stuck at half again since before she caught up with him, paying more for each spark than she pays for a jaw. Each soul has said so throughout, in the window nobody else can see (the soul’s report of its own numbers to its owner, in square brackets on the page), and this is how it reads:
[Ignivale: harmonized. Lens on the Body, at home: +8%]
[Ignivale: harmonized, 24 years. Lens on the Body, at home: +100%]
[Ignivale: harmonized, 31 years. Lens on the Spirit, away: +50%]

Those figures are a sample from two sheets, every soul’s road runs at its own speed, and only the two ceilings are law. The rule under them is plain: a lens grows the way a Trait grows, by being lived with. A Draft can hand you the lens. The years are yours to live.
Each lens grows on its own. A soul with three Wellsprings has three lenses at three stages of mastery, all under the Capacity rules further down this page, and a lens compounds only with its own years.
You can see it. The Wellspring a soul has tempered on longest sets the base color of its aura. Every lens adds its texture and its own sound and smell, and a Class or a big Trait adds a shape. A trained eye at fifty paces can tell you the base lens from the hue, make a good guess at the others from the grain, and tell you from how steadily the color sits whether the lens is two years old or twenty. The Color of Essence has every hue, and each entry below carries its own.
Measurewrights at Sealhall have spent a long time arguing about what exactly gets doubled, since the number holds still and no fork rings a lens. Their working answer is to ask the person who got hit.
How you come by one
There are four roads, and most people who have more than one Wellspring have walked more than one of them. How many a soul can hold is set by its rank: one home lens to Adept, and one more safely harmonized at each rank from Expert up, so an Expert holds two, a Master three, a Paragon six. A Clouded soul that reaches for a second early risks tearing, and the base hue stays the lens tempered on longest.
At a Core, in a dungeon. Most Wellspring Cores lie in dungeons, the living underground places that grow down in floors around a Core with something guarding the heart. On a held site a person can sit at the edge of a known Wellspring, with a keeper and a baseline taken first, and come away harmonized, at a price by the hour. In a place nobody holds, a crew that goes too deep takes Wellspring Baptism whether it wanted one or not. This is the road dungeon luck runs on, and the reason a nobody with a good rope can come home changed. See Dungeons.
From a school. A sect teaches the rites for its Wellspring, along with the Releases, Domains, techniques and skills that money cannot buy, and in return you wear its colors, sing its songs and inherit its grudges. A school’s style is that lens worn by a hundred people at once, which is why you can spot it across a square.
From a Draft or a blessing. A Draft puts the lens in a bottle, and the great houses hoard the best ones. A blessing is given by a higher spirit, an Archon, an Epoch or a person of higher Temperance, for whom it costs next to nothing. Either way it can land in a soul that could never have reached it alone. A blessing shows as its own line on the sheet, and because the giver wrote that line it can lie, so what reads as a gift for years may be a curse with terms you did not read.
By birth. Some souls arrive already harmonized, by bloodline or by generations of living downwind of a concentration. The birth-day name is another matter entirely: a Fixatio child is any child born on Fixatio’s day, and being called one has never once sealed anything.
One Aether, three readings
Every one of the sixty can be read three ways, and each reading is a whole profession that thinks the other two are amateurs. These are readings and not Paths: a confessor, a bench hand and a Measurewright can all stand around one Body Path hitter and describe three different things, none of which is her Path.
As a spiritual transformation. The confessor’s reading, and the oldest: what taking this Aether into the soul does to the person who survives it. Temperance is the climb of a soul from Stage to Stage, and every Wellspring is a road on that climb, so the Fracture register names Pyreveil Temperance through burning and Absolution Temperance through forgiveness, and it gives all sixty such a name. Where the confessors read a road otherwise, the entry sets their reading beside the name, marked as such and argued over at every deathbed. To pass through a Wellspring is to be unmade just enough to keep going. Every Wellspring touches all three layers of the Crystal, rarely evenly, whichever Path the soul is on. The Essence Core decides how the soul burns, heals or empties under that law, the Aether Shell how the law moves through and around the body, and the Attraction Layer how reality, memory and people bind to the soul once the law has taken hold.
As an alchemical principle. The bench’s reading: what that same idea does to matter in a vessel. Each of the sixty is a living process, a law of transformation, and the discipline of Alchemetrica (the working of Wellspring law upon matter) is built on that fact. The reagents are the nouns and the Wellspring is the verb. Six of the sixty are at once Wellspring, cosmic principle and named bench operation, and four more lend their law to a stage of the Great Work (the seven-stage discipline an alchemist lays on the matter and on himself at once). The rest have no operation filed under their name at the Bench, though every working alchemist has an opinion about what each of them is the principle of, and those opinions appear in the entries, marked as the trade’s reading and open to a fight.
As a law of the world. The Measurewright’s reading, and the youngest: the physical analogue, the mechanism, the failure. Scholars have an account of everything, this is theirs, and it has the great merit of predicting the bill. The rest of this page gives it in full.
The correspondence is architecture rather than poetry, which is what Alchemetrica means when it says that what burns in the crucible burns in the one who tends it.

How the Scholars Explain It

“The Wellspring is neither gift nor spirit. It is a law that was already running before you noticed it, and harmonization is the act of agreeing to be measured by it.”
From the preface to the First Physical Register.

Everything below this line is the account the Measurewrights (the guild’s certified assessors of practitioners and workings) give, and every figure on this page lives in it. It may be wrong about what a Wellspring ultimately is, as the confessors will tell you, and it has never yet been wrong about what one will charge.
Why the Sixty Are Sorted by Home
The older registers arranged the Wellsprings by feeling. Grief stood with grief. Fire stood with fire because both were warm. It produced a beautiful taxonomy and a useless one, because a practitioner who knew that Cinerion and Pyreveil were both House of the Ember still had no idea why one of them refilled a reserve and the other emptied it faster.
The guild’s physics stays on each entry, last, under The Measurewrights’ account, where the analogue gives their picture of how a Wellspring behaves. The entry itself opens on the idea, which is what the Wellspring is. The kind says where it is at home, which is the one sort that has never yet misled anyone walking onto the ground.

A warning to the devotional reader. Setting a law from natural philosophy beside the Wellspring does not demote it. The Measurewrights have written down how much it will do and what it will charge; why it does anything was never theirs to write.
A warning to the Measurewright. Writing the law down does not explain why a soul that takes in Absolution stops hating its father. The physics stays on every entry, last, because its figures work. The entries have stopped pretending the physics came first, or that it was ever the reason.

What a Wellspring Physically Is
In the scholars’ terms a Wellspring is a type of Aether that carries a fixed law. Aether is what practitioners pull from the environment around them, and it comes in sixty types, fixed and counted, and each type affects the Soul Crystal differently. Take in Pyreveil and your reserve burns hotter while your body stops minding the heat. Take in Hypnather and you sleep like the dead and wake structurally different. Take in Fractura and you will never again look at a bridge, a friend or your own left wrist without seeing where it is going to go. A type of Aether is not stored anywhere and it does not belong to anyone. It runs whether observed or not, in the way that a pressure gradient runs whether or not something is standing in it.
The old registers call each type a current, and the trade still does, because Aether moves over ground the way wind moves over a field. Keep the word and lose any picture of a pipe. Nobody has ever laid a Wellspring on or shut one off at a valve, and the Measurewright who tells you otherwise is about to send you a bill.
The road into the soul is the same for all sixty: Aether is pulled in from the world through the Aether Shell (the Crystal’s outer layer, and the only door into matter), and nobody has ever worked it without pulling it in first. Older editions of this register ran the road straight on from there for everyone, refined into Essence and out through the Shell again. That is one road of three, and half of it. On the Body Path the Aether is packed in the Shell unrefined, as the Charge, and driven out through the Shell as it came. On the Spirit Path it is refined in the Soul Crystal into Essence (spiritual energy: Aether stamped with identity, the soul’s own substance) and spent through the Essence Core. On the Fate Path the Aether is refined into Essence as on the Spirit Path, and a thread is pulled down through the Attraction Layer and paid for from the soul’s own share, which is a part of that reserve and no separate purse; Thread itself is never stored. The Three Paths sets the three out with their prices. What differs among the sixty is the type. Where you stand therefore matters twice: rich ground fills you faster and thin ground starves you, and the ground decides which of the sixty is on offer. On the street this is plain sense. A brawler will say she has the ember in her, or the stone, or that she took the water at Saint Orrin’s pond, and she will say he only fights like that on hot ground. On a Guild roll all of that is harmonization, which comes next.

Harmonization is phase-locking. The Aether Shell adopts the characteristic behavior of one type of Aether so that whatever the soul works afterward is shaped by that law before it reaches the world. Nothing is added to the practitioner. The conduit is retuned, and everything that passes through it afterward carries the retuning. This is the lens, in the scholars’ words.

Said once and for all: the lock happens at the Shell, where Aether enters, the tie is held on the Attraction Layer, and the lens shapes what the lead layer works: raw Aether in the Shell for a Body fighter, Essence in the Core for a Spirit fighter, the claim on the Layer for a Fate fighter, where the Thread pulled through the claim takes its shape. The Shell is where the instruments catch the lock, since all Aether enters that way, whatever road it leaves by. On the Body Path the shaping is done right there, on Aether that never sees the refining, so a hitter’s fire is Aether burning in the Wellspring’s shape with none of the hitter in it. On the Spirit Path and the Fate Path the law seats hardest in the Essence Core or the Attraction Layer, which is the lens working in that layer’s terms.
This is why harmonization changes what a number means without changing the number. A Fortitude of 240 harmonized to Monolithion does not become a larger Fortitude. It becomes a Fortitude that behaves like a load-bearing mass rather than like tissue, with the failure curve of stone rather than the failure curve of flesh. The magnitude stays where it was and the constitutive law changes.
Most practitioners awaken three to five Wellsprings in a lifetime. Serious adepts harmonize with twelve or more. Those who embody all sixty are called Principals of Temperance, and there are not many of them, and you will not meet one.
Harmonization, Traits, and the glyph
Three things bias a Shell and they are constantly mistaken for one another.
A harmonization retunes the conduit. It is reversible in principle, it degrades if Capacity (the limit on how many Wellsprings a soul can hold at once) is exceeded, and it shapes everything passing outward for as long as it holds. The law belongs to the Aether and the practitioner has it on loan.
A Trait biases the conduit permanently. It is a law the soul itself carries, held in the Essence Core (the Crystal’s inner layer, holding identity, memory and Traits), and it writes into the Shell’s conductivity map rather than borrowing a law from outside. It cannot be dropped to make room, and it has a level of its own that rises with use and with the bearer’s overall Level and skill. This is why two practitioners harmonized to the same Wellspring produce recognizably different output: the Aether supplies one law and the Core supplies another, and the working is what comes out of both.
A glyph is a boundary condition. It creates nothing. The Wellspring’s law was already running; the glyph moves a boundary and the law does what it has always done on the far side of the new boundary. Every entry below should be read with that in mind. Nobody in this register makes fire. They establish conditions under which the ordinary behavior of heat produces fire where it previously did not, and the fire that results obeys every rule fire has ever obeyed, including the ones nobody thought about.

Sites do not check for a Crystal. Aether pooling in a valley acts on everything standing in the valley, and an unwoken soul’s Shell is sealed and cannot phase-lock, but it has an Essence Core like anyone else. Sustained residence at Active Concentration or above therefore does to a shepherd what it does to an adept, minus the harmonization and minus the vocabulary.
What it leaves behind is a Trait, formed by Wellspring Convergence, in a body that will never be screened and a life that has no framework for it. Every quarter has villages downwind of a concentration where one family has been strange for six generations, and the strangeness is lawful, inheritable, and entirely undocumented.

Where a Wellspring Pools
A Wellspring is a type of Aether and no kind of place. But a Wellspring pools.
The way groundwater is not stored in a specific container but absolutely collects in aquifers, a type of Aether concentrates where the substrate is Aether-conductive, where competing types are absent, and where enough time has passed for it to saturate the local field until the physical environment begins expressing the law passively.

A Wellspring site is the aquifer. The Aether is the water table.

Nobody has been pulling from them. The veins are full. Cores, keepers and closed ground
Common speech calls any site where a Wellspring’s Aether pools a Core, and most Cores lie in dungeons: places a Core has made around itself, or that have grown up around one, going down in floors with something guarding the heart. A dungeon is alive and learning, and scholars argue whether it thinks. The rest of the Cores are said to lie in vast territories, with the weight on “said”, and Dungeons has the whole account. Surveyors keep Wellspring Core for the top line of the Density Scale below, an Essence Core is a layer of your own Crystal, and a Measurewright who hears a ferryman call the warm pond behind the tannery the Pyreveil Core will explain all of this at length until the ferryman charges him double. This register uses the surveyor’s word, and you should use the ferryman’s if you want to get across the river.
A worked Core is a dungeon someone cleared and now holds. It recharges and it has keepers. A site people have pulled from and tended for generations refills at the rate its ground replaces what has been taken, which the numbers below will give you, and somebody always stands at the gate of it: a sect, a village, a Guild house, three brothers and a fence. Keepers charge by the hour or by the bottle. They strike, they overcharge, they play favorites, and they can close the site, turning everyone off it and working the ground shut, which no amount of Stage talks them out of unless the Stage is prepared to do it by force in front of witnesses.
The counter this hands you is the oldest in the book. Take the fight off rich ground. A fighter fat on a Core loses the fat a league down the road, on salted ground (worked by ward-cutters and hedge-workers so that Aether will not pool on it, and it gives back little for a season), on bled ground (pulled empty by a long fight or a greedy crew, just before you arrive if somebody has planned it), or on ground that was simply thin to begin with. Half the famous upsets in the brackets were won in the week before the fight, by someone quietly paying off the people who choose the field.
The second mode · Object Wellsprings
Aether of one type captured, bound, or naturally accumulated inside a vessel produces a contained domain, carried in a sword, a relic, or a formation old enough that the material and the Aether are indistinguishable.

Crevice Shale, T9, the Crevice itself: forbidden to move or hold or trade. A law about a rock, and the only such law the Accord has ever written. The most extreme Object Wellspring in the register.
The critical distinction between the two modes is interface geometry.
A site has a perimeter. The density gradient gives warning. The surveyor feels the Aether thickening as they approach the core.
An object is binary. You are holding it or you are not, and its internal domain contacts the Shell at zero distance. If the Shell is incompatible, the resulting conversation was not authorized and cannot be escaped without severing the causal relationship at the Plane of Fate (above the lower realities, the control of Attraction and Obsession and the workings of reality itself) level.
The colloquial term for an Object Wellspring whose Attraction Layer (the layer that holds bonds and claims) will not accept a termination event is cursed.

The Density Scale
The encounter type determines the direction of the danger. The density determines its magnitude.

























DensityConditionAmbient SaturationThe most common condition across the mapped world, and no kin to Aetheric Saturation, the lethal flood. A Sage can tune to it. An ordinary person feels vaguely uneasy or peaceful. The landscape carries subtle signsActive ConcentrationDense enough for persistent environmental effects. Wild sites show altered terrain; Spirit sites produce involuntary change in the soul, with the body sometimes following; Fate sites produce runs of coincidence that nobody believes before the third; Medium sites produce bidirectional effects indistinguishable from illness or hallucination. A practitioner remaining too long receives Wellspring Baptism whether they wanted it or not. Most concentrations on the New World’s arc were found during the Voyager Era; the elven old-ground’s have been pulled on since the first EonVeil-Thin NexusThe Veil between planes thins. Spiritual entities become visible. Causal threads are perceptible. Time feels wrong. Bifold Perception onset without training, involuntary Soul Drift, Echo Beast manifestationWellspring CoreThe Aether’s origin point. The aquifer’s source. Extraordinarily rare, and mostly unmapped. Nearly all of them lie at the heart of a dungeon, and the richest untouched ones are on the New World’s arc. The physical and metaphysical environments are indistinguishable, and the law the Wellspring carries is the only law operating. Walking into a Core unprepared is Wellspring Baptism at maximum intensity with no exit plan
The Density Scale in Numbers
The condition is what a surveyor writes down. The number is what the ground will actually give.
The Measurewrights reckon one EU at one megajoule, so by their arithmetic a density in EU per cubic meter is an energy density, and an energy density is a pressure. In their books a density in EU/m³ is the same figure in megapascals. That one identity is why the scale is a ceiling and not a mood. A boundary cannot be pushed into ground at a pressure the ground does not carry, and what is standing in the ground has a strength measured in the same unit.
What a site will actually give. Aether crosses a site the size of a hall in about a thousand seconds. That is the interval in which the ground replaces what has been taken from it. So a site yields at most a thousandth of its density, per second. The supply rate in AU/s (Aether Units per second, a rate of output) per cubic meter is the density in EU/m³ divided by a thousand, and the ceiling on a practitioner’s sustained output and refill is that rate across the volume his field reaches. A burst is spent out of the reserve he walked in with and owes the ground nothing until he wants it back.

In a Silence (ground where no lawful working can be authorized) the figure is zero. That is the whole of why a Silence is something other than shielding. There is nothing to pull and nothing to push into, which is also why a soul held in one reports the sensation as loneliness rather than as weakness.
Ambient Saturation is the reference. Its midpoint, one EU per cubic meter, is the ground every laddered reach is quoted against. Denser ground fills a practitioner faster and lifts his ceiling on sustained output, as the supply column shows, which is why fighters will pay a keeper for it. It does nothing for his arm’s length, and a Fate fighter, whose Range and Domain radius are most of his fighting, is crowded by rich ground worst of all. It raises the floor his own field has to stand above, and addressing range, authority radius and anchor reach all fall as the square root of the local density. Concentrated ground cuts all three to an eighteenth. A Nexus cuts them to a thousandth. A Core cuts them to a five-millionth. That last figure is the arithmetic behind the sentence in the table above: inside a Core the law the Wellspring carries is the only law operating, and a Master’s kilometer of authority is a fifth of a millimeter wide. One measure pushes the other way for one road. Thread Weight, the count of what has been decided on a piece of ground, extends a Fate fighter’s Range and the radius of his Domain, so heavy ground gives back some of what dense ground took, and the two are read together on any field a Fate lord means to hold (The Three Grounds).
Why residence changes a body. A person at rest dissipates about a hundred watts through about a fifteenth of a cubic meter, which is one and a half kilowatts per cubic meter. Active Concentration supplies ten to ten thousand kilowatts per cubic meter. The field is putting seven to seven thousand times the subject’s own metabolic power density through them, continuously, and a body has no mechanism for declining a power density. That is why Baptism at that condition is involuntary, and why it reaches the shepherd as readily as the adept.

Saturation, stated once. Saturation begins at ten thousand EU per cubic meter, the stress at which a crystal lattice fails. It is reached by leaving that much above the ground’s own density in each cubic meter of a region (a Nexus or a Core runs past the figure natively, and what those do to a visitor is the Density Scale’s business), or by sustaining more than a hundred AU/s through each square meter of the region’s boundary. The two are one statement. The second is the first carried out at the Aether’s own speed. The threshold grows with the surface while output does not, so a kilometer of open ground swallows what a hall would not. A Master’s field (Stages VIII to X, at the benchmark rate) a kilometer across puts about a fifth of one AU/s through each square meter of its edge, a five-hundredth of threshold. The same output inside a twenty-meter hall puts five hundred and fifty through each square meter, five times over, and everyone in the hall is a casualty of it. Open ground stops being the answer near the top of the ladder: an Archmaster’s benchmark through that same kilometer is eighty-odd per square meter, and the strongest Archmasters run past threshold. A drawn circle is the other half of the same arithmetic. A rite bleeding sixty EU a second into two meters of floor reaches Active Concentration within the hour and stays there, which is what the Circle step is for and what an improvised one costs.

The Attraction and Obsession Axis
A site operating under clean Attraction Force recognizes practitioners who enter it, reads the Crystal, assesses compatibility, and either permits harmonization or ignores the visitor. The experience is intense but orderly.

A site operating under Obsession Force has been corrupted. Pulled on without reciprocity. Exposed to sustained Mechanica (forbidden working that takes power without lawful consent) extraction. Saturated by wartime discharge never processed.
The Aether there does not recognize. It takes. It pulls at the Crystal whether the visitor is compatible or not.

How to Read an Entry













































































The ideaThe concept the Wellspring lays over a soul’s Aether, in plain words. Start here.The turnWhere the trade has fixed one, the moment the idea comes clear to someone working inside it.KindWild, Spirit, Fate or Medium: the plane the Wellspring is at home on, which is the Physical World, the Soul Plane, the Plane of Fate, or all three across the Veil. A qualifier and never a lock.TitanThe Titan whose law this is one showing of, with a line on how.OperationThe classical operation of the bench the idea performs (calcination, dissolution, separation, conjunction, fermentation, distillation, coagulation or sublimation), with a clause on what it does in this idea’s terms. It is the Operation on a working’s Codex line.HueThe color it gives an aura, and why, from the idea. The lens a soul has tempered on longest sets its base color, and the rest add texture.GroundThe places where its idea has long been at work, which it favors, and the places it hates. On a Wild or Medium entry this is a modifier on what the working can do, and on a Spirit or Fate entry it says where the Aether pools and no more.ContraryThe Wellsprings whose laws fight this one in a single soul, and why.On the BodyWhat the lens does on the Body Path, in the terms of the Aether Shell: blows, tissue, what the flesh can bear.On the SpiritWhat the lens does on the Spirit Path, in the terms of the Essence Core: force thrown on a soul, inscription, what a thing means and holds. It marks no matter, and a Spirit worker who wants matter moved does it through their own Shell. The line called Spirit below is another matter, the confessor’s reading of the Wellspring whatever the Path.On FateWhat the lens does on the Fate Path, in the terms of the Attraction Layer: bonds, oaths, claims and odds, and so what a Fate fighter carries in their presence and, on the rare day they pull, what they move.SpiritThe transformation it works on the soul, the road on the Temperance climb: the Fracture’s “Temperance through” name, with the confessors’ reading beside it where they read it otherwise.AlchemyThe principle it stands for at the bench: its operation or stage of the Work where it has one, otherwise the trade’s reading of what its law does to matter in a vessel.Stat EffectThe Sub-Stat (one of eight finer measures inside each main stat) modification, in the current sixty-four names: where the Fracture register names a Sub-Stat since folded into another, the effect sits on the entry that absorbed it. Behavior, never bonus.GlyphThe forms the Master Glyph Index seats on this Wellspring as primary, with a count of the others it is attested on.FailureThe characteristic malfunction, from the flaw its idea cannot hold, and how that turns on the worker. Every idea has a way of going wrong that is its own. The Measurewrights’ name for it follows.AnalogueThe Measurewrights’ account, part one: the real phenomenon the guild says the Wellspring’s behavior matches. It stands last on the entry as their theory; on the page a working is explained by its idea, and a trained mouth may borrow the analogue as a comparison.MechanismThe Measurewrights’ account, part two: their reading of what this type of Aether does to what the soul spends and to the Crystal, in the analogue’s own terms, with their figures. Often right about how much, and never about why.
Ground
Each Wellspring that acts on the world answers to the places where its idea is already at work. Aetheric Density sets the ceiling on sustained output everywhere, but a Wild or Medium lens’s own idea sets a second, narrower gate on top of it, and veterans choose ground accordingly. The Ground line on each entry says which: Pyreveil favors burned ground coming back green, kilns, forges and hot springs and hates still cold water and air that will not feed a flame, Petralon wants great masses of stone and heights under it, places that have long borne everything stood on them, and hates silt, loose sand and a drop with nothing under it, and Aurevane wants dry air and a clear line of sight and hates iron-walled rooms and dense fog, where the light is shut in or smeared before it can arrive.
These conditions bind what acts on the world, the Wild and the Medium. A Spirit Wellspring or a Wellspring of Fate has nothing in the world for the ground to favor or smother. It fills from Aetheric Density like every other lens, since every reserve is pulled Aether, and it fights on a measure of its own: a Spirit lens on Echo Depth, how thickly souls and memory lie on a place, and a lens of Fate on Thread Weight, how much has been decided there. Each band of Depth raises the yield (η) of Spirit work by a tenth, and each band of Weight does the same for a pull, exactly as each band of Density does for what acts on matter (The Three Grounds has the rolls). Its Ground line says where its Aether pools and thins, and those are nearly always the same places the Depth or the Weight is found: Catharsis gathers at bathhouses and confessionals, and Somnalis at crossroads, ferries and betting yards, and neither will light your way across a bad floor.

None of this is a prohibition. A Pyreveil practitioner in saturated cold still works. They simply pay a larger fraction of their reserve to work on ground that holds nothing of their idea, and their yield falls accordingly. Terrain is a modifier on yield (η: the share of spent power that arrives as effect), and anyone who calls it flavor has not yet paid for it.

Harmonization, Stacking, and Interference
What happens when a Crystal is asked to obey two laws at once.
A lens compounds only with its own years. Two Wellsprings never add up to one larger lens, and a second lens starts small however old the first one is. What they can do is agree. Coagula with Petralon is the bench’s standard example, since matter given form through force is one problem described twice: the two laws reinforce along the same axes, and such a soul’s Vitality and Resilience behave denser than an identical stat spread carrying neither. The numbers on the Ledger are identical. The qualitative expression is not, and anyone who has fought both can tell them apart in one exchange.
Contrary laws interfere, and the entries say which. Every further harmonization introduces resonance complexity, and each entry’s Contrary line names the pairs that will not behave and why. Contrary laws produce tension the Crystal must resolve, either by Temperance advancement or by developing a Compound Trait that holds the contradiction as a single law. Monolithion against Nihiloth is the canonical hard case, form set against the erosion of all shape. A contrary is no bar to holding both, and plenty of famous fighters are famous for exactly that, and it is the first thing a rival’s second looks for.

The ceiling is Tempering Capacity and it is not negotiable. Exceeding it does not fail gracefully by dropping the newest harmonization. It degrades all active harmonizations equally, which is how practitioners lose a decade of work by reaching for one more Wellspring in a bad hour.

Where the Registers Disagree
Attested, not reconciled.
The count · The Fracture register lists Sublimare among the Sixty. The consolidated Magic System register omits it entirely. With Sublimare restored and Phreatis counted once, the register reconciles exactly to sixty unique types. The Measurewrights record the consolidated table as the party in error and this register follows the Fracture.
Phreatis · Older registers list Phreatis twice, once as memory and once as water, which made sixty-one listings against sixty types. The idea supports the double assignment rather than resolving it: deep water and long memory are one keeping, read twice. The Measurewrights’ account says the same in its own terms, synaptic potentiation and aquifer residence as two physics describing one behavior. The entry is written once, on the Medium page, with both readings on it.
Sublimatio and Sublimare · The two have been treated as near-duplicates in prior registers on the strength of their names. Their operations separate them cleanly: Sublimatio’s is sublimation, the soul leaving its lower state in one clean step, and Sublimare’s is distillation, what is light in the soul driven up and parted from what stays. They are different operations with different residues and different failure modes, and the duplication was linguistic rather than real. (The Measurewrights put it as sublimation skipping a phase and fractional distillation separating a mixture.)
Sublimare in the Codex · Three Codex rows, the glyph [Prc] Pressure, the spell Pressure Veil and one alchemical row, still file Sublimare as cross-listed and read it as tracking phase-transition behavior. The Fracture register reads it otherwise and its bench law is distillation, and this register follows both. The Codex’s wording is recorded here and left as it stands.
Vohrin · Frost arts and cold galleries are entered all over the registers as if Vohrin were one of the sixty, and Vohrin is a Titan’s power and not one of the Sixty. The count stays at sixty. The power can be worked at Wellspring level, a cold site is filed as a Titan-touched site, and the Wild page carries a marked note with its analogue, failure and signature as the register’s one exception. Several Codex rows still give frost to Cymorath, which is the Air of Ascent and no frost Wellspring.
Petralon’s two Titans · Atla’zon’s line and Kaldrion’s both name Petralon. The register files it under Kaldrion, and for any ruling at an assay table the Titan read is Kaldrion and the table above is the authority. Atla’zon’s art stays written in Petralon, which nobody has yet had the nerve to tell either of them, and the argument is left standing in the halls, where it is a good deal older than this register and in better health.
The eleven with no form · Pyreveil, Cinerion, Manganthra, Aurevane, Nyxial, Tarturon, Ascensio, Abython, Penance, Redemption and Contrition appear in no row of the Glyph Index, primary or attested. The Index is fixed at 136 and nobody has shown whether the gap is in the record or in the world. A working under one of the eleven is written in a form seated elsewhere or in one of the unclassified Roots, which name a kind of limit and will condition any law.
Old sorting names in older sources · House of the Green Pulse, House of the Veil, House of the Black Gate and similar appear throughout the Wellspring codices and the Veil literature. These are the pre-correction feeling-first Houses and do not map cleanly onto the kinds.
The Register
Every entry gives a Wellspring its idea, its Kind, its Titan and Operation, Hue, Ground and Contrary, what it does on each Path, its Spirit and Alchemy, its Stat Effect, Glyph and Failure, and last its Analogue and Mechanism as the Measurewrights explain them. Each kind’s page opens on what that kind means and runs in alphabetical order.


Wild Wellsprings thirty-three, the kind you can point at
Spirit Wellsprings fifteen, the kind with nothing to point at
Fate Wellsprings six, the kind you only find out about afterward
Medium Wellsprings six, the kind that works on you while you work it

the-magic-system/the-foundations/the-six.title: Wild Wellsprings
the-magic-system/the-foundations/the-six.content:
Thirty-three of the Sixty, at home in the Physical World · the kind you can point at
The people of Pennyhithe will tell you about the Aldgate sisters whether you ask or not. Prudence Aldgate heated the public baths on Fish Lane with her bare hands for thirty years, a copper a tub, two if you wanted it hot enough to lift the grease, and she turned away anyone who owed her, the reeve’s wife included, and once, gloriously, the reeve. Her sister Bess kept the family’s grudges. On the night of the Herring Fair she walked down into the customs cellar under the tollhouse with a list of names and her whole body lit the white-orange of a smith’s best heat, and the crowd up on the quay heard a flame-front turn into something else.
The tollhouse roof came down in the harbor with the tollkeeper’s best hat still on its peg. The quay cheered, and the minstrels had a song by morning. The song leaves out that the shock came back up the cellar along its own path, with Bess standing at the origin of it, and that she has been deaf in both ears and short three fingers ever since. Prudence’s tubs ran on Pyraeon and Bess’s fingers went to Cataclysm, one smolder and one detonation out of the same orange fire, and a Measurewright (a certified assessor of workings) who says so in a Pennyhithe tavern should expect to be asked which sister he is calling gentle.
What Wild means · A Wild Wellspring is a thing in the world: fire in the ground, stone that moves, lightning, a solution crystallizing out of itself on the bench. Its home is the Physical World, Aegor’s ground, and its Aether (mana, the raw stuff of magic) shows up as a physical phenomenon or an alchemical transformation. The stone was there and the water was there, and the Aether reshapes them, moves them, burns them. A site of one of these alters the landscape where anyone can see it, so the surveyor’s body is a reliable instrument and his environment is not.
The lens · A soul tempered on one of these carries that thing in everything it does: a little at first, and after years of mastery on the Body Path, its home, up to double, so that the same fist at the same Grade lands with twice its idea in it, the same shoulder drives twice as much of what it has become into what it meets, and the same Fortitude behaves twice as much like the thing it has decided to be. Any Path can take any of them. Away from home half again is the most anyone has got out of one, at a higher cost and with a rougher result. The bath-house trade will tell you it shows in the water, anyone who has bought a stone Draft and then tried to dance will explain, and that is how a bridge gets knocked down badly. The full account of the lens is on the hub.
Each Wellspring below opens on what it is. The idea is the concept it lays over a soul’s Aether, and The turn, where the trade has fixed one, is the moment that idea comes clear to someone working inside it. Kind names its home plane, and never locks it. Titan is the Titan whose law it is one showing of, Hue the color it gives an aura, Ground what it favors and hates underfoot, and Contrary the Wellsprings whose laws fight it in one soul. On the Body, On the Spirit and On Fate say where the same idea lands on each Path. On the Body it shapes raw Aether packed in the Aether Shell (the layer of the soul that meets matter, and the only door into it) and works on matter, with no Essence spent and the Shell’s furnace burning off as heat. On the Spirit it shapes Essence (spiritual energy) spent through the Essence Core (the layer that holds identity and authors what a working is) and works on souls and on what a thing means and holds, never on matter, at a price paid in the Core as hollowing. On Fate it shapes the claim on the Attraction Layer (a soul’s own share of fate, its bonds, oaths, claims and odds), and the Thread pulled through that claim takes its shape, and works on what a thing could have been, and every pull leaves a knot the world collects later. Spirit is the transformation it works on the soul, one road of Temperance (the climb of a soul from Stage to Stage), and Alchemy the principle it stands for at the bench. Then come Stat Effect, what shifts on the sheet, Glyph, the forms the Index seats on it, and Failure, how it goes wrong, from the flaw its idea cannot hold. Operation, after Titan, names the bench operation the idea performs, the one a working’s Codex line carries. Last on each entry stands The Measurewrights’ account, Analogue and Mechanism: that guild’s physics of what the type of Aether does to a Soul Crystal, often right about how much and never about why. Entries run in alphabetical order.
Abython · The Abyssal Pulse

Folk name the Abyssal Pulse (what carters, soldiers and the commons call it; each culture may add its own beside it).
The idea Peace with the abyss. Matching the pressure in place of fighting it, so that the soul can walk where everyone else suffocates.
Kind Wild
Titan Zar’thuun: annihilation as peace, the dark of Abythron met on its own terms.
Operation Dissolution: the soul’s difference from the deep is loosed into it until nothing is left between them for the deep to crush.
Hue Near-black, because the soul has matched itself to the dark of the deep and keeps no light of its own to set against it.
Ground Favors great masses of stone, heights and brittle old rock or rock already under load, places where the world has long pressed hardest and a soul has the most to make peace with; hates silt and loose sand, a drop with nothing under it, and soft even ground, which press on nothing.
Contrary Thaloré (pressure felt in full against pressure matched away); Chthonica (gripping against floating free of net stress); Petralon (bearing the load against having no load to bear).
On the Body Flesh stops holding a difference against the world, so a crushing blow finds less to crush and Aether-starved ground does not suffocate the fighter who walks onto it. The same body hurried back into a rich hall comes apart in ways a diver would recognize.
On the Spirit The soul matches whatever is pressed on it, and a rival’s Aura Pressure (the felt weight of another’s power) meets nothing pushing back and little to grip. The trouble comes when it is time to throw something, since a Core with no difference in it has very little to push with.
On Fate Presence drops to exactly what the room already has, so the holder can stand unremarked in a hall full of people hunting them. Stretching that over a column, so that it passes through a hostile province with no sentry or rumor finding a difference to catch on, is the work of every waking hour of the march, and the return to ordinary company takes the holder the way a fast ascent takes a diver. The knot it leaves is a difference owed: on some later day the holder is the one thing in the room that everybody notices.
Spirit Temperance through void.
Alchemy The balanced vessel: pressure inside matched to pressure outside, so the glass has nothing to resist. (the trade’s reading)
Stat Effect Strengthens Resilience Persistence, Harmonics Stability, Vitality Tolerance. The character operates where other practitioners suffocate.
Glyph None attested in the Index (see Where the Registers Disagree on the hub).
Failure Peace with the abyss is a match and never a defense: the soul holds nothing of its own against the deep, so it cannot be hurried back out of it. Return to ordinary Aetheric density too fast and the matched interior has no time to match the room it has come into, and comes out of solution all at once, which is as unpleasant in the soul as it is in a diver. The Measurewrights call it rapid ascent.

The Measurewrights’ account. This is the guild’s theory, often right about how much and never about why.
Analogue · Pressure equalization. Neutral buoyancy and the vanishing of net stress.
Mechanism · A vessel at depth, they say, survives by matching the water, never by resisting it, because net stress is a difference and a difference of zero loads nothing. By their reckoning Abython trains the Shell to equalize rather than oppose, which is why its practitioners work in Aether-absent environments that suffocate everyone else: they have stopped holding pressure in and stopped maintaining a differential at all. Why a soul would want peace with the abyss in the first place is not a question their gauges were built to answer.
Anima Spirare · The Soul’s Breath

Folk name the Soul’s Breath (what carters, soldiers and the commons call it; each culture may add its own beside it).
The idea The breath of the whole. A body that remembers being whole and answers a small hurt with everything it has.
Kind Wild
Titan Omnis: to breathe is briefly to echo him, and this is a whole body doing it at once.
Operation Fermentation: the whole body is quickened round a small hurt, and the wound is answered with all of its own life.
Hue Bright arterial red, because the whole body’s blood comes running to the smallest hurt.
Ground Favors thick living growth, mild weather and ground close to blood, places where bodies have long answered a hurt with everything they had; hates barren ground, bitter cold and Aether-thin soil, where nothing is alive enough to answer.
Contrary Mortalis (a body refusing the gate against a soul walking to it).
On the Body A small cut draws an answer from the whole body, blood and breath arriving in a flood exactly where they are wanted, so wounds seal under the fighter’s own pulse and the last round is breathed as easily as the first. Lose the signal that says where, and the flood goes everywhere.
On the Spirit A working carries a memory of wholeness and presses it on what it touches, so a split ward, a scattered mind or a soul wounded in the Core is told what it used to be, loudly, and answers as well as it can. It closes no flesh, which is the Shell’s work, it hollows the one who sends it, and it works best on what was once alive.
On Fate Pull one bond and all of them wake: hurt one of a crew and the others feel it under the breastbone, and in the rare great working a flank struck at dawn finds the reserve already on the road with nobody able to say who sent it. It costs blood from every vein at once and cannot easily be called off, so a feint against one picket has been known to turn out the whole army and leave nothing to close the real wound, and the knot falls due the same way, some small hurt of the holder’s own answered later by far too much.
Spirit Temperance through vitality. The confessors’ reading: remembering wholeness, wounds closing because the body remembers being whole.
Alchemy The quickening: the steady blood-warmth of the Bed, in which a charge stays alive. (the trade’s reading)
Stat Effect Strengthens Vitality Hemostasis, Regeneration, Harmonics Synergy. The body pulses with living rhythm. Wounds close because the body remembers being whole.
Glyph [Leth] Blood, [Dr] Vitality, [Bst] Beast; attested on two more.
Failure The whole body answers a small hurt with everything it has, and it has no way to answer with less. Lose the sense of where the hurt is and the whole answers everywhere at once, spending its own blood and breath on every vein until nothing is left to close the wound that started it. The Measurewrights call it disseminated activation.

The Measurewrights’ account. This is the guild’s theory, often right about how much and never about why.
Analogue · The coagulation cascade and cooperative oxygen binding.
Mechanism · Hemostasis, they say, is an amplifying cascade and never one event, in which each activated factor activates many of the next, so a small injury signal produces a large and precisely localized response. Layered under it, by their reckoning, hemoglobin’s cooperative binding means the fourth oxygen loads far more readily than the first, and Anima Spirare imposes both patterns: amplification where it is needed, and a delivery curve that steepens with demand. It is a fine account of a barber’s arm and says nothing at all about why the body remembers being whole.
The story they tell.
Bertil Ashgrove kept a barber’s chair on Mill Gate with a red-striped pole and a painted board that read TWO COPPERS A WOUND, NO CREDIT FOR COLORS. The day the Millrace Boys met the Hammers of Saint Orrin on the bridge over a disputed bout, he walked into the middle of it with his sleeves rolled and arterial red brightening every vein in both arms, and he closed fifty-three wounds in an hour on both sides, each wet pulse sealing a gash, taking his two coppers each time and flatly refusing the two men who had stiffed him at the last fair. The fifty-fourth wound was a nick on his own thumb. By then the cascade had nothing left to tell it where to stop, it ran through him everywhere at once, and that one small nick bled for three days while both clubs, in the only agreement they have ever reached, took turns holding his arm up and paying for ice.
Ascensio · The Ladder of Ascent

Folk name the Ladder of Ascent (what carters, soldiers and the commons call it; each culture may add its own beside it).
The idea The ladder. The whole height climbed by steps, with no single step large enough to break you.
Kind Wild
Titan Atla’zon: which way is down, and the height paid for in his coin, one step at a time.
Operation Distillation: the same work passed up again and again by degrees, until the whole height is reached and no single pass has broken the glass.
Hue Steel gray with pulley-lines, because the height is taken by rope and tackle, each line one step that will bear the load, and never by one heave.
Ground Favors towers, cliffs, high walls and brittle old stone or stone already under load, places where people have long climbed by steps and every step had to bear them; hates silt and loose sand, a drop with no step in it, and soft even ground with nowhere to climb.
Contrary Exuroth (the ordeal against the road with no step large enough to break you); Sublimatio (every step climbed against no steps at all).
On the Body The body takes its load in steps. A fighter climbs a long fight by small increases of force, each one inside what the joints will bear, and arrives at a blow that would have torn them apart had they opened with it.
On the Spirit A working is authored in stages, each inscription standing on the last, until a long prepared piece reaches a height no single casting could survive. Anyone who interrupts it on the fourth step has saved themselves a great deal of trouble.
On Fate It hardly moves the odds on any given day, and thirty years of days is another matter: one more captain owing the right man, one more village out of forage, until the porter’s nephew is dining with the harbor court and the enemy’s army is a day short of everything. A whole war climbed this way is a life’s masterwork and its knots are deferred and stack, so the holder arrives at the top owing every step at once, and in a single fight it buys no more than a slight edge by the fourteenth exchange.
Spirit Temperance through rising.
Alchemy The degrees of fire: one heat reached by steps, where a fool reaches it at a stroke and loses the glass. (the trade’s reading)
Stat Effect Strengthens Tempering Maturity, Harmonics Attunement. Stage transitions become smoother and less violent.
Glyph None attested in the Index (see Where the Registers Disagree on the hub).
Failure A ladder makes the height bearable and never makes it lower: every step is still owed, only spread out along the climb. Practitioners mistake the absence of crisis for the absence of cost and arrive at the next Stage owing the difference. The Measurewrights call it deferred load.

The Measurewrights’ account. This is the guild’s theory, often right about how much and never about why.
Analogue · Mechanical advantage. Path-independence of gravitational potential energy.
Mechanism · Lifting a mass to a height, they say, costs the same total work by any route, but the inclined plane trades distance for peak force and so the same climb can be made without ever exceeding what the structure can bear. In their account Ascensio applies that to Threshold transitions, spreading the required change across a longer path so the Crystal never sees the peak stress that a direct ascent imposes.
Basilithe · The Stone Will

Folk name the Stone Will (what carters, soldiers and the commons call it; each culture may add its own beside it).
The idea The stone will. One note the soul holds that nobody can retune.
Kind Wild
Titan Atla’zon: permanence, one posture held because he knelt first.
Operation Coagulation: the soul is fixed on one note and set there past any retuning.
Hue Ochre-gold with quartz-clear lines, because the soul has become a standard, the gold every weight is read against and the clear line of a note that will not be moved.
Ground Favors ore-rich rock, worked stone and deep foundations, places that have long held one shape without being moved; hates open water, high peaks and decks and wagons that will not keep still.
Contrary Materia Primordia (every form against the one note); Transmutatio (one note nobody can retune against the same thing said in another key).
On the Body The Crystal’s stiffness comes down into the bones and the body refuses to be shaken, stunned or struck out of rhythm, with shockwaves passing through a stance that holds its own pitch. Every so often somebody finds that pitch with a hammer, and the fighter rings like a bell and comes apart.
On the Spirit The soul holds one note against any working that would retune it, so compulsion, false memory and imposed law slide off, and so does any new idea. Thrown, it is a dead pitch that stops an enemy’s chant from resolving, and that is about all.
On Fate A soul that cannot be retuned is a standard for other people: merchants trust their weights, and a wavering line drifts toward their pitch without noticing, which is the whole of the lens on most days. Holding that note against an enemy’s arranged panic is a contest that can crack the holder’s Crystal if lost, and an enemy who finds the one pressure that matches it brings down the man and the line together. A note held by pulling leaves a knot, which falls due on the one day that wanted bending.
Spirit Temperance through permanence. The confessors’ reading: constancy, the soul’s frequency refusing retuning.
Alchemy The Standard: the one fixed measure every other weight is read against. (the trade’s reading)
Stat Effect Strengthens Resilience Hardening, Harmonics Stability. The soul’s frequency locks and refuses retuning.
Glyph [Grv] Gravity; attested on one more.
Failure A soul that holds one note can never change it, even to get out of the way. When some outside rhythm happens to sing that very note, the soul cannot be moved off it and takes the whole of it, and rings like a bell until it comes apart. The Measurewrights call it resonant catastrophe.

The Measurewrights’ account. This is the guild’s theory, often right about how much and never about why.
Analogue · Natural frequency and stiffness-to-mass ratio. Quartz oscillator stability.
Mechanism · A body’s resonant frequency, they say, is fixed by its stiffness and its mass, and a high-stiffness low-loss structure holds that frequency against forcing so reliably that a Measurewright with a cut quartz on a string will set her water clock by it. By their reckoning Basilithe raises the Crystal’s stiffness until its resonance simply will not be driven off, which is a defense against every technique that works by imposing an external rhythm. Her clock keeps excellent time, and has never once told her what the note is for.
Cataclysm · The Shattered Law

Folk name the Blast (what carters, soldiers and the commons call it; each culture may add its own beside it).
The idea Upheaval. The moment a fire stops being a fire and becomes a blast, a change in kind as well as size, and the soul that has learned to call that moment.
Kind Wild
Titan Valmir: collapse as the moment of transition, the instant a thing changes in kind.
Operation Calcination: the burning is driven past itself until it goes over all at once into something else in kind.
Hue White-orange flash with a pale ring, because the change comes in one instant, and all it leaves is the ring where the fire went over into something else.
Ground Favors kilns and forges, mills and mines whose air is thick enough to catch, and hot springs, places where fire has long waited on the edge of going over into something worse; hates lukewarm places where nothing is hotter than anything else, cold that has soaked through everything, and air that will not feed a flame.
Contrary Solfatara (never building against everything built going at once); Lethegraal (upheaval against settling on its own schedule).
On the Body Given confinement behind it, a set stance or a wall at the enemy’s back, a blow stops being a push and goes over into a blast, and the pressure crosses the target faster than the target can flinch.
On the Spirit A working sent at a soul can change in kind partway across, leaving as a pressure and arriving as a rupture in the Core, a dread that had been building for a year going over all at once into collapse. It breaks no wall and raises no dust, and the people it arrives on rarely get to learn what it was meant to be.
On Fate Slow quarrels near this person can be brought past their point all at once, so a garrison’s ten-year feud and a month of short rations turn into a mutiny in one night, and a Domain (a region where the world runs on a practitioner’s terms) widens by whole streets as everyone picks a side. It wants confinement, it comes off perhaps once in a war, and what comes back along the same path finds the holder standing at the origin with their ears and fingers at stake, and the knot is some quarrel of the holder’s own going over, later, in one night.
Spirit Temperance through upheaval.
Alchemy The vessel’s violent end taken as a law: the moment a burning charge stops burning and becomes a blast. (the trade’s reading)
Stat Effect Strengthens Ardency Cascade, Ardency Overchannel, Dominion Radius. Area expressions become wider and more structurally coherent.
Glyph [Thn] Thunder, [Eith] Flux, [Wy] Motion; attested on five more.
Failure Upheaval needs something to hold it in before it can go over, and once it goes it does not know which side of the wall it was called from. In confinement the blast comes back along its own path, and the practitioner standing where it began takes the blast and its return together. The Measurewrights call it reflected overpressure.

The Measurewrights’ account. This is the guild’s theory, often right about how much and never about why.
Analogue · Deflagration-to-detonation transition. Blast scaling under the cube-root law.
Mechanism · A subsonic flame front, they say, that meets sufficient confinement and turbulence accelerates until the reaction couples to a shock wave and begins propagating faster than sound in the unreacted medium, so that the mechanism changes kind where a lesser one would only change degree. They hold that Cataclysm makes that transition available to what the soul spends, and that blast radius thereafter scales with the cube root of yield, which is why the Wellspring’s area effects widen coherently rather than merely spilling. Their tables for the radius are the best in the trade, and none of them says what it is in a soul that learns to call the moment.
Chthonica · The Root Deep

Folk name the Root (what carters, soldiers and the commons call it; each culture may add its own beside it).
The idea The root. Holding on by touching everything, so that whatever you stand on becomes yours to stand on.
Kind Wild
Titan Atla’zon: adhesion, the reason anything stays where it was put.
Operation Conjunction: the soul and whatever it stands on are joined at every point where they touch, until each holds the other.
Hue Dark iron-oxide, because the soul takes the color of the ground it holds to, rust and red earth.
Ground Favors ore-rich rock, worked stone and deep foundations, places where things have long held on by touching everything around them; hates open water, high peaks and anything moving underfoot, where there is nothing steady to take hold of.
Contrary Cymorath (every way open against holding to what is underfoot); Oneirion (a place with no ground against nothing but ground); Abython (gripping against floating free of net stress).
On the Body The Shell takes hold of whatever bears it with a countless fine grip, so a fighter stands on a sheer wall or a bucking deck as if it were a parlor floor and cannot be thrown off either, every blow going down into what they stand on. A wet deck or a fouled boot drops them with no warning at all.
On the Spirit From the Core it roots a working to the place, and a ward done this way sits in the stone the way a tooth sits in a jaw. Dull to throw and a fine thing to leave behind, and Spirit Path scholars on this lens tend to stop traveling.
On Fate The person and the ground become each other’s claim, so a family on its own land has a hold that bailiffs have failed to break, and a Domain raised there comes up out of the floor with its roots already in. A lifetime on one valley can turn it against an invader, the wagons miring in the one soft lane and the wells going sour in the week they are needed, while each pull draws the holder down with the water and leaves its knot in the same soil, to come up later under their own cart, and moved to a new country they are slow to know what to do with their hands.
Spirit Temperance through grounding. The confessors’ reading: rootedness.
Alchemy Lute, the humble seal: it holds because it touches everything. (the trade’s reading)
Stat Effect Strengthens Vitality Absorption, Dexterity Economy, Dominion Gravity. The practitioner roots to whatever surface they stand on.
Glyph [Sed] Sediment; attested on three more.
Failure The root holds by touching everything, so it holds nothing it cannot touch. Put wet, grease or filth between the soul and its ground and the grip lets go, all of it at once, without warning and with no halfway. The Measurewrights call it contamination.

The Measurewrights’ account. This is the guild’s theory, often right about how much and never about why.
Analogue · Static friction and molecular adhesion. Interlocking asperity; setal van der Waals contact.
Mechanism · Grip owes nothing to weight, they say. A gecko holds to glass through billions of hair-scale contacts each contributing an intermolecular attraction too small to measure alone, and by their reckoning Chthonica multiplies the Shell’s contact area with whatever surface bears it, converting proximity into anchorage, which is why its practitioners root to sheer stone and moving decks with equal indifference.
Cinerion · The Ash Veil

Folk name the Ash (what carters, soldiers and the commons call it; each culture may add its own beside it).
The idea What the fire leaves. Ash taken as treasure: every spent thing feeds the next thing, and the soul learns to live on its own aftermath.
Kind Wild
Titan Prometheus: what his fire leaves, which he has never once counted as waste.
Operation Calcination: the spent thing is burned down to its ash, and the ash is kept as treasure to feed what comes next.
Hue Gray-orange, embers showing through ash, because what the fire left is kept and the heat still lives in it.
Ground Favors burned-out ground, kilns, forges and hot springs, places where fire has long been at work and left its ash behind; hates lukewarm places where nothing has ever burned, cold that has soaked through everything, and air that will not feed a flame.
Contrary Sublimare (treasure in what stays behind against treasure in what rises).
On the Body The Shell eats its own leavings, turning waste heat and burned-off Charge into second wind, so the practitioner looks worst and feeds best at the end of a long fight.
On the Spirit What a working leaves behind feeds the next one, and the practitioner can read a thing by its residue, getting from a burned letter some of what it said.
On Fate Lost causes settle on the holder like ash in a low place, and after a long enough defeat a fighter can pull on what has been spent, so the failed feint of an hour ago becomes the place the opponent steps wrong. A beaten commander who lives on this may make the burned bridge and the dead men’s debts delay a pursuit by a week, at the cost of whatever ruin they had left to draw on, and the gift fouls and stops on the day they have spent the most. The knot of each pull is paid as one more loss, a little later, which the lens then gets to eat.
Spirit Temperance through aftermath.
Alchemy The law Calcination draws on, the Burning of the bench: strong dry heat drives off what is volatile and leaves what is fixed.
Stat Effect Strengthens Tempering Yield, Harmonics Stability. The residue of destruction becomes recovery material.
Glyph None attested in the Index (see Where the Registers Disagree on the hub).
Failure Every spent thing feeds the next, and the soul cannot refuse anything it has spent. Past a point the ash heaps up faster than it can feed anything and smothers the fire it was kept to feed, and the practitioner’s recovery fails exactly when they have spent the most. The Measurewrights call it fouling.

The Measurewrights’ account. This is the guild’s theory, often right about how much and never about why.
Analogue · Pyrolytic char and its catalytic residue. Particulate optical depth.
Mechanism · People call what survives a fire waste, the guild says, and people are wrong. Char is a high-surface-area carbon scaffold that catalyzes further reaction, and settled ash returns potassium and phosphorus to the ground that fed the fire. By their reckoning Cinerion retunes the Shell to metabolize its own combustion products, harvesting from expenditure what other practitioners simply vent, and the suspended residue also scatters incident light and Essence-sight alike. On this one the benches and the guild agree about the ash and part company over why anyone would love it.
Coagula · The Unifying Pulse

Folk name the Mending (what carters, soldiers and the commons call it; each culture may add its own beside it).
The idea Gathering the broken. Scattered pieces come back into one body without ever melting, keeping the shape they had while broken, the flesh first and then the soul that wears it.
Kind Wild
Titan Gaia: material harmony, scattered matter returned to one body.
Operation Coagulation: the scattered pieces are gathered and set back into one body without ever being melted down.
Hue Amber-gray, because the broken pieces come back still wearing the gray of their breaking, held together in amber.
Ground Favors ore-rich rock, worked stone and deep foundations, places where broken stone has long been gathered up and set back into walls; hates open water, high peaks and moving decks, where nothing scattered comes back together.
Contrary Dissolution (the bench’s oldest pair, unbinding against gathering); Fractura (gathering the broken against finding where it breaks).
On the Body Broken bone and split muscle draw back together under the Shell with no melting stage and no pause, each piece keeping the shape it had while broken, so a fighter who has been smashed gets up crooked and whole. The great Coagula brawlers look like sacks of walnuts and are extremely hard to finish.
On the Spirit In the Core the same law does the old inward work: a soul split by a bad Threshold or a bad decade gathers up its own pieces, and what it sends holds together over distance because no part of it will consent to leave. Cast on another’s scattered soul it is dear and brief, and the sender’s own Core pays, in pieces that come back to the wrong places.
On Fate Scattered things come to the same table, and feuding cousins and lost partners find themselves in one town with this person somehow always in the doorway. The great working of it, a broken army’s stragglers finding the same crossroads on the same night, leaves a knot the holder is years paying off in partings of their own, and the reassembled line keeps every seam where it was, which is the first place a sharp enemy hits.
Spirit Temperance through merging. The confessors’ reading: the Soul Plane’s unifying force, a soul gathering itself back together.
Alchemy The personal twin of Coagulatio: gathering without melting, a person’s own Setting. Basalt takes it.

Coagula is a person’s gathering, flesh and soul together, and a few fighters at great cost have thrown the same current outward over a room or the ground underfoot. It lasts as long as they hold it. Matter gathered for good belongs to Coagulatio.
Stat Effect · Strengthens Resilience Integrity, Tempering Coherence. The Crystal becomes harder to split.
Glyph · None primary. Attested on [Krn] Crown and [Wy] Motion.
Failure · Gathering without melting keeps everything the broken pieces were, the gaps between them included. The places where they never quite met stay in the mended body and the mended soul, and they are exactly where the next break will start. The Measurewrights call it residual porosity.
The Measurewrights’ account. This is the guild’s theory, often right about how much and never about why.
Analogue · Sintering. Densification by atomic diffusion below the melting point.
Mechanism · Press powder together and hold it hot, they say, though never hot enough to melt, and the particles fuse across their contact points by diffusion alone until the porosity closes and the mass behaves as one body. They read Coagula as that run on a person: a broken body, or a Crystal that has been fragmented, gathers itself without ever passing through a liquid state, which is to say without losing the shape it had while broken. That is why the guild files it Wild, since you can watch it happen to a man on the floor of a ring, whatever the confessors say it is doing in him. The law runs inward by nature, in their account. A handful of high arts throw it outward, gathering the ground under a stance or the Essence in a room into one body, and they pay for the reversal in the practitioner’s own legs and Shell.
Coagulatio · The Returning Stone

Folk name the Seed (what carters, soldiers and the commons call it; each culture may add its own beside it).
The idea Settling round a seed. Scattered things find one grain and grow out from it, denser and far less wasteful than they were.
Kind Wild
Titan Gaia: the Corpus under the crust, where what is dispersed condenses into crystalline ore.
Operation Coagulation: what is scattered settles round one grain and sets there, and the grain goes on growing after the hand is gone.
Hue Pale amber crystals, because what was scattered has set into clear grains round its seed.
Ground Favors ore-rich rock, worked stone and deep foundations, places where what was dispersed has long settled out round a seed into ore; hates open water, where everything stays dissolved, high peaks and moving decks.
Contrary Abyntheus (a soul stretched over the great distance against a soul settled round one grain); Dissolution (going into solution against coming out of it).
On the Body Raw Aether sets around one grain in the Shell the way sugar sets on a string, and what was spray becomes mass, so a punch loses almost nothing to heat on its way out and the Charge sits denser in the same body. Start too many grains at once and the fighter is left with a fine heavy sludge in the arms and no way to spend it.
On the Spirit From the Core a working sets around a chosen seed, one word or one grain of the target, and goes on growing after the hand has gone, so a seal thrown at noon may still be adding to itself by evening. It is slow work and it does not stop on request.
On Fate Whatever is scattered around the holder starts to crystallize of its own accord: hangers-on into a household, three bad debts into one very large creditor. Forcing it on a routing crowd, so that it sets into a square of spears around the one man who stopped running, comes off about as often as such a man survives and leaves a knot that sets the same way, the holder’s small troubles gathering round one grain until they are a single large one. Two of them on one field curdle an army into small loyal clumps that will not take orders from each other.
Spirit Temperance through re-forming. The confessors’ reading: settling, the scattered self finding its seed.
Alchemy One of the six Wellsprings the bench names its works after and the stage of Coagulation: a charge sets round one grain, and the grain grows on after the hand is gone. It deactivates cleanly under Preparation Failure.
Stat Effect Strengthens Ardency Compression, Tempering Clarity. Essence becomes denser and harder to waste.
Glyph [Plr] Pillar; attested on nine more.
Failure Settling needs one seed, and the idea cannot choose between seeds. Offer it too many at once and everything settles round all of them, a fine disordered mass where a sound crystal should be, and the practitioner ends with density they cannot use. The Measurewrights call it uncontrolled nucleation.

The Measurewrights’ account. This is the guild’s theory, often right about how much and never about why.
Analogue · Crystallization from supersaturated solution. Nucleation and ordered growth.
Mechanism · A supersaturated solution, they say, holds more solute than equilibrium permits and will surrender it the instant a nucleation site appears, depositing ordered solid out of apparent nothing. In their account Coagulatio is the material twin of Coagula: where that Wellspring gathers a person, this one gathers substrate, pulling what the soul spends, dispersed, out of suspension into a denser and far less wasteful phase. They can tell you to the grain how fast it grows, and nothing about what in a scattered soul wants so badly to settle.

The Crystalia note. This is the same law that governs a Threshold. A melt cools into order only around seeds that survived the heat, and what Coagulatio describes in substrate is what Traits do in a Soul Crystal.
Whether a Coagulatio practitioner can work the law on their own seat is the oldest unsettled question in the trade. The Wellspring does not say no.

Cymorath · The Air of Ascent

Folk name the Open Way (what carters, soldiers and the commons call it; each culture may add its own beside it).
The idea Freedom in the air. The world read as a set of open ways, so that moving becomes a matter of noticing which way is already open.
Kind Wild
Titan Omnis: sky and motion, the open ways left for whoever will rise.
Operation Sublimation: the soul is made volatile, so that it rises and goes by whatever way already lies open.
Hue Blue with spiraling curves, because it is the color of open sky and goes by whatever way turns open, never by a straight push.
