Ground Favors dry open air, ore-veined ground and long clear views, places where the ways have long stood open; hates rooms caged in iron, walls of heavy iron and thick fog, which close every way.
Contrary Chthonica (every way open against holding to what is underfoot); Petralon (slipping the load against being what the load stands on).
On the Body The body reads the air as a set of open ways, and the next step, leap or slip is already there to be taken, so the fighter seems to fall upward through a fight without ever pushing.
On the Spirit A working thrown on this lens finds its own road around a ward the way spirit of wine finds the neck of a still, taking whatever way lies open, which is sometimes the way it was aimed.
On Fate The holder feels chances the way a lodestone feels north and drifts toward them: the open door in a melee, the ford nobody has posted. Pulling one wide enough for an army, the gap in a line that two captains each believe the other is covering, is a feat of decades that empties them for a season, leaves a knot that shuts some door the holder was counting on, and lands everyone somewhere efficient and seldom where they promised their allies.
Spirit Temperance through freedom.
Alchemy Volatile Mercury: the spirit that finds its own road up the neck of the still. (the trade’s reading)
Stat Effect Strengthens Dexterity Celerity, Gnosis Perception. The body reads space as a language of vectors and opportunities.
Glyph No clean primary. The Codex still seats [FrTh] FrostThrone and [ObsG] Obsidian-Glacier here, a leftover from when frost was filed under this name; Cymorath is the Air of Ascent and frost belongs to Vohrin (see the note at the foot of this page). Attested on four more.
Failure Freedom in the air goes by whatever way is already open, and it has no say in which way that is. Lean on it too long and the practitioner follows the open way instead of the intended line, and arrives somewhere efficient that is not where they meant to be. The Measurewrights call it drift.

The Measurewrights’ account. This is the guild’s theory, often right about how much and never about why.
Analogue · Vector fields and the Lorentz force. Motion determined by charge, velocity, and field.
Mechanism · A charged particle in a field, they say, does not choose a direction: its path falls out of the cross product of its own velocity and the field it moves through. By their reckoning Cymorath gives the practitioner that reading of space, a set of gradients in place of a set of positions, each with a magnitude and a direction, so that movement becomes a question of which vector is already available rather than which one must be forced. The guild’s diagrams of it are beautiful, and no Cymorath fighter has ever been seen to consult one.
Dissolution · The Unbinding Stream

Folk name the Unbinding (what carters, soldiers and the commons call it; each culture may add its own beside it).
The idea Unbinding. What no longer serves is allowed to come apart on its own, and keeping anything at all becomes the work.
Kind Wild
Titan Valmir: permission to end, given to a bond.
Operation Dissolution: what no longer serves is loosed into the stream and let come apart on its own.
Hue Clear translucent violet, because what it unbinds goes clear, with nothing left holding together enough to cloud it.
Ground Favors darkness, silence, Aether-thin ground and ruins, places where things have long been let come apart; hates Aether-rich ground, crowds and active Domains, where too much is being held together at once.
Contrary Fixatio (the bond let go against the bond past going back); Coagula (the bench’s oldest pair, unbinding against gathering); Coagulatio (going into solution against coming out of it); Sublimare (mixing against parting).
On the Body It goes in with the blow, and whatever the fist touches starts to lose its argument for staying together: mail lets go of its rivets, a wound’s edges refuse to knit, a shield comes off in strips. Such a soul’s own body has to be held together on purpose, and a tired one shows it at the seams.
On the Spirit Thrown, it is a solvent for definitions: a seal loses track of which part of it was the seal, and a ward sags out of its own inscription into a puddle of good intentions. It runs slower than a blow and has never once been selective.
On Fate Bonds slacken around such a person with nobody able to name the day, and a coalition camped near one for a season may shed allies as harvests come due and old terms turn out to have lapsed. Brought to bear on one oath in the middle of a fight, so that a bodyguard’s sworn step forward arrives a moment late, it leaves a knot that is paid in kind, a bond of the holder’s own gone slack each time, and the Accord’s notaries keep a short list of who has tried.
Spirit Temperance through release. The confessors’ reading: unbinding, the soul dissolving what no longer serves its architecture.
Alchemy One of the six Wellsprings the bench names its works after and a stage of the Work, the Taking of the bench: cohesion unraveled into the menstruum. The Bench files a Dissolution Draft as a composite, and it is volatile: under Preparation Failure it does not deactivate at all.
Stat Effect Strengthens Resilience Ward, Tempering Maturity. The character dissolves what no longer serves the Crystal’s architecture.
Glyph [Blt] Blight; attested on eleven more.
Failure Unbinding lets come apart whatever stops being held, and it never asks what was holding the rest up. Tire of the work of keeping, and the soul lets go of what it needed along with what it did not, load-bearing parts and all. The Measurewrights call it indiscriminate solvency.

The Measurewrights’ account. This is the guild’s theory, often right about how much and never about why.
Analogue · Solvation. Dissolution driven by the entropy of mixing.
Mechanism · A solid dissolves, they say, because the mixed state has higher entropy than the separated one, with no attack by the solvent at all, and the process therefore runs on its own once initiated. By their reckoning Dissolution gives the Crystal that thermodynamic preference toward the unbound state, which makes shedding what no longer serves nearly effortless and makes retaining anything a matter of active work.
Eidolyn · The Shaping Mind

Folk name the Shaping Mind (what carters, soldiers and the commons call it; each culture may add its own beside it).
The idea The shaping mind. A thing imagined so hard that it stands up and has to answer for itself.
Kind Wild
Titan Nysera: Manifest Potential, an idea crystallized by force of wanting.
Operation Coagulation: what is imagined is set solid along the pattern the maker holds in mind, until it stands up and answers for itself.
Hue Violet with a lattice pattern, because the imagined thing stands up along the pattern its maker holds, line by line.
Ground Favors darkness, silence, Aether-thin ground and ruins, places empty enough that something imagined has long had room to stand; hates Aether-rich ground, crowds and active Domains, where the world is already full of other people’s shapes.
Contrary Judicium (what a thing is made of against what it has been imagined into); Nihiloth (the thing imagined into standing against the rule unmade).
On the Body At home the imagined thing grows out of the practitioner’s own Shell and has real weight: a plate of solid intent across the ribs, a third hand that can hold a spear, a fist that lands a hand’s width before the arm arrives. It breaks the way a bad casting breaks, along whatever the maker failed to picture.
On the Spirit Authored in the Core and sent, the construct stands in the souls that meet it and weighs nothing a stone would notice: a wall the mind cannot walk through, a sentinel the frightened see and the furniture does not. It does exactly as much as its maker has fully imagined. Scribes have marched a frightened company across a gorge on the conviction of a bridge far wider than the plank that was really there, and rivals have brought such a thing down by asking loudly what was holding up the middle.
On Fate What gets made solid this way is a reputation, and on most days that is the whole weapon: the ballad’s version of a person reaches the field a half step ahead of them, frightening what the original cannot. Forcing it, so that a line breaks for a charge that is forty men and a great deal of dust, takes the whole of the holder’s reserve and faithfully copies every flaw in the ballad, and sooner or later someone who knows the words fights them by it. Its knot is a tale that turns up afterward with the holder cast as the fool.
Spirit Temperance through creation. The confessors’ reading: imagining, the thing thought made solid enough to answer for.
Alchemy The mold: matter deposited along a pattern the maker imposes. (the trade’s reading)
Stat Effect Strengthens Ardency Density in summoned constructs and inscriptions, Gnosis Retention. Mental constructs gain material solidity.
Glyph None primary. Attested on [AnMa] Anamnesis, [Mn] Mnemonic, [EchoS] Echo-Scar and [Sil] Silence.
Failure A thing imagined hard enough to stand up stands up exactly as it was imagined, flaws and all. Any fault in the maker’s picture is copied faithfully at full size, and the maker is rarely able to see the fault until it is standing in front of them. The Measurewrights call it template defect.

The Measurewrights’ account. This is the guild’s theory, often right about how much and never about why.
Analogue · Templated nucleation. Ordered deposition onto an imposed pattern.
Mechanism · A supersaturated medium, they say, will not organize itself, but given a template it deposits along the template’s geometry with high fidelity and considerable strength. In their account Eidolyn makes intent the template, the construct’s solidity is real material behavior rather than illusion, and its failure modes are the failure modes of a poorly designed casting. Asked where the material comes from when a wall stands up out of nothing but conviction, they cite the template again, more slowly.
Exuroth · The Trial Flame

Folk name the Trial Flame (what carters, soldiers and the commons call it; each culture may add its own beside it).
The idea The trial by fire. Power comes only through ordeal, plunged and reheated and plunged again, until the soul holds a hardness no gentle road could have given it.
Kind Wild
Titan Prometheus: enlightenment through pain, knowledge got by suffering and kept as hardness. His Pyric Refinement is written in this Wellspring.
Operation Calcination: the soul is burned, plunged and burned again, until only the hardness that lives through the fire is left.
Hue Cherry-red cooling through straw and plum to a temper blue at the edges, because the soul wears every heat of its ordeal at once, from the plunge to the temper.
Ground Favors forges with their quenching troughs, kilns and hot springs, places where things have long gone from the fire into the cold and come out harder; hates lukewarm places that put nothing to the trial, cold that has soaked through everything, and air that will not feed a flame.
Contrary Absolution (the quench against the anneal); Ascensio (the ordeal against the road with no step large enough to break you).
On the Body Every beating and every recovery sets the Shell harder than the last, so that a fighter’s third bad season leaves a forearm that turns a blade and a threshold of pain their physician declines to test.
On the Spirit A working must fail and be thrown again before it takes an edge, and an inscription that has cracked twice and been recut holds where a clean first draft would split.
On Fate Its holders take the worst of a fight on purpose, because an oath nearly broken hardens, and one nearly broken three times can sometimes be pulled on to turn the fourth exchange, or to hold a company on the day an untried enemy line is first asked. It is paid for in near-deaths that were real and in a knot that sends one more, unasked for, afterward, and cut the interval too fine and the oath splits like steel quenched too soon, with the company still inside it.
Spirit Temperance through ordeal.
Alchemy The assayer’s trial: quench and temper, the bench’s proof by ordeal. (the trade’s reading)
Stat Effect Strengthens Ardency Overchannel, Tempering Overflow, Vitality Threshold. Pain thresholds rise. The Crystal tolerates what would shatter lesser vessels.
Glyph [Ra] Flame, [Asa] Creation, [Ve] Desire; attested on seven more.
Failure The trial gives hardness only to a soul that lives through it, and the idea cannot tell an ordeal from a ruin. Plunge again too soon, without the rest between, and the soul comes out hard, brittle and split along the lines of its own trials. The Measurewrights call it quench cracking.

The Measurewrights’ account. This is the guild’s theory, often right about how much and never about why.
Analogue · Quench and temper. Martensitic hardening followed by controlled reheat.
Mechanism · A steel quenched from austenite, they say, is hard and useless, brittle to the point of shattering, and tempering restores toughness by permitting controlled diffusion. They read Exuroth as running the Crystal on that cycle: repeated thermal shock followed by controlled recovery, so the lattice arrives at a hardness the same material could never have reached by slow cooling. Every smith in the Quarter agrees with them about the steel.
Fractura · The Breaking Point

Folk name the Crack (what carters, soldiers and the commons call it; each culture may add its own beside it).
The idea The breaking point. Everything has a place where it will go, and this lens shows it to you, in bridges, in friends and in your own left wrist.
The turn The moment catastrophe becomes clarity.
Kind Wild
Titan Valmir: he decides when a thing has endured enough, and this lens shows you where. His Canyon’s Patience is written in this Wellspring.
Operation Separation: a thing is parted along the one place where it was always going to part.
Hue Dark blued steel with hairline bright cracks, because the lens shows every flaw, and the flaws are the brightest thing in it.
Ground Favors great masses of stone, heights and brittle old rock or rock already under load, places where a breaking point has long been waiting to be found; hates silt and loose sand, a drop with nothing under it, and soft even ground, which has no place where it will go.
Contrary Orrenthal (the metal that bends under load against the place where everything breaks); Coagula (gathering the broken against finding where it breaks); Redemption (where it will break against the break made strongest).
On the Body The eye finds the flaw and the fist goes to it, so a Fractura blow lands on the one grain in a shield boss or a shinbone that was already going to fail. The same sight runs down the fighter’s own skeleton and tells them which of their bones is next.
On the Spirit A thrown working hunts the crack in what a thing claims to be, and a ward or a technique comes apart at the one assumption it never checked. Finding that assumption across a room takes longer and costs far more than finding the weak grain in a bridge.
On Fate Every line has a place where it will go, and this lens finds it before the battle does: the company that will break first, the bridge pile that will not take a second column, and the fighter whose guard has been about to fail for three exchanges. Finding it is only looking, and leaning there costs dearly in reserve and leaves a knot that falls due as a new crack in something of the holder’s own, a strap, a friendship or a wrist, and it is a miserable gift at a wedding.
Spirit Temperance through failure.
Alchemy The assayer’s blow: the ingot struck to make its flaw show. (the trade’s reading) Quartz amplifies it.
Stat Effect Strengthens Gnosis Analysis in fault-reading, Ardency Penetration, Resilience Integrity. The practitioner sees where things break and learns to break them precisely.
Glyph [Rk] Rupture, [Uur] Disruption, [Clp] Collapse, [Vorn] End; attested on four more.
Failure The lens shows where everything will go, and it cannot leave its bearer out of everything. Under strain a Fractura practitioner reads their own breaking points with perfect clarity, at the worst possible moment. The Measurewrights call it self-inspection.

The Measurewrights’ account. This is the guild’s theory, often right about how much and never about why.
Analogue · Linear elastic fracture mechanics. The Griffith criterion and the stress intensity factor.
Mechanism · Nothing fails at its theoretical strength, they say. Everything fails at a pre-existing flaw, because stress concentrates at a crack tip in proportion to the square root of the crack’s length, and once that intensity exceeds the material’s toughness the crack runs at a fraction of the speed of sound and does not stop. By their reckoning Fractura gives the practitioner sight of those flaws and the precision to load exactly one of them. Their formula finds the crack in a bridge to the inch and has never yet found the one in a friendship.
The story they tell.
Asa Birkett, a mason’s daughter out of the Ketterby yards, bet a barrel of brown ale that she could drop the Old Toll Bridge with one knuckle, and all of Ketterby came down to the bank in its feast-day reds to watch her lose. She walked out to the third pier with iron-gray light running in hairline cracks up her forearm, rapped the stone like a woman knocking at a neighbor’s door, and strolled back. For about the length of a grace nothing happened at all.
Two hundred years of bridge sat down in the river, threw a brown wave over the front row and took the toll-keeper’s cash box along with it, and she drank the barrel with the men who had bet against her. That night, wrung out and glowing, she read her own flaws for the first time, plain as a ledger: the crack in the left wrist, the one in the third vertebra, and how many more bridges each of them would stand. She has told that count to nobody, and she has not taken a bet above a pint since.
Ignivale · The Wellspring of the Spark

Folk name the Spark (what carters, soldiers and the commons call it; each culture may add its own beside it).
The idea The spark. The smallest beginning that goes on to pay for itself, so that the gap between wanting a thing and doing it closes to almost nothing.
Kind Wild
Titan Omnis: the breath before the flame, the smallest act of aspiration. His Skyfire Pulse is written in this Wellspring.
Operation Calcination: one point of fire is set to the work at the first degree, and the burning is left to pay its own way.
Hue One white-orange point, because everything it does starts from the smallest beginning there is.
Ground Favors kilns and forges, dust-thick mills and mines whose air will catch, and hot springs, places where one spark has long been enough to start everything; hates lukewarm places where nothing is hotter than anything else, cold that has soaked through everything, and air that will not feed a flame.
Contrary Pyraeon (the flare with no heat kept against the heat with no flare); Hypnather (no gap between wanting and doing against change that comes only at rest).
On the Body The gap between wanting the blow and throwing it all but closes, and the fist has left before the shoulder has told anyone.
On the Spirit A speck of Essence is enough to start a working that then pays for itself out of the soul it lands on, so a one-stroke mark of courage or of dread can go on working long after its writer would have liked it to stop.
On Fate Everyday the person simply catches: a handshake is an alliance by supper, and the rumor of them takes the next town ahead of their horse. The rare real pull wants only the smallest beginning, one stumble in a front rank that runs the whole line or a single shout of they’ve turned that becomes the turn, and it fires on whatever charge is lying about, so it has as often routed the holder’s own side and left them coughing blood. The knot is a spark as well, one small mischance of the holder’s own that catches.
Spirit Temperance through ignition.
Alchemy The first degree of fire: the smallest heat that goes on to pay for itself, which every Burning starts from. (the trade’s reading)
Stat Effect Strengthens Ardency Overchannel, Dexterity Celerity. First strikes arrive faster and cost less to start.
Glyph [Ig] Ignite, [Noq] Wind, [Vt] Vector; attested on eleven more.
Failure With the gap between wanting and doing closed, the soul has no moment left in which to decide. Any stray feeling in the room is beginning enough, and the working fires without the practitioner having decided to fire it. The Measurewrights call it preignition.

The Measurewrights’ account. This is the guild’s theory, often right about how much and never about why.
Analogue · Minimum ignition energy and the activation barrier.
Mechanism · The spark that lights a fuel-air mixture, they say, carries a fraction of a millijoule, and everything after is the reaction paying for itself. By their reckoning Ignivale reduces the activation energy of the working’s forming, so the interval between intent and expression collapses toward the physical limit of the nervous system, and first strikes arrive before the opponent has finished reading the preparation.
Judicium · The Wellspring of Truth

Folk name the Scale (what carters, soldiers and the commons call it; each culture may add its own beside it).
The idea Truth told apart. Discernment that knows what a thing is made of, and whether it is lying, from the mark it cannot help leaving.
The turn Seeing a truth no one else could see, and being right. This lens is about a truth read across a distance, with nothing of the thing having to be held, which is why it makes so few brawlers and so many people who are unbearable to lie to.
Kind Wild
Titan Dazkar: judgment and measure. His Mirrored Scale is written in this Wellspring.
Operation Separation: a thing is parted from what it claims to be, the true told apart from the false by the mark it cannot help leaving.
Hue Arc-blue with colored line-fringes, because a thing told apart shows its true parts at the edge, each in its own color.
Ground Favors dry open air, ore-veined ground and a clear line of sight, places where a thing has long been plain to see for what it is; hates rooms caged in iron, walls of heavy iron and thick fog, which hide what things are made of.
Contrary Tenebra (the mark that cannot be hidden against the art of leaving none); Eidolyn (what a thing is made of against what it has been imagined into).
On the Body The hands learn what a thing is made of on contact, so the fist goes to the crack under the paint, the old break in the rib, the flawed link in the mail.
On the Spirit Thrown as a line of reading across a room, it parts a thing from what it claims to be, and a lie under that line comes away from its maker in front of everyone.
On Fate Whatever rests on a false oath already wants to give, and a holder who has read the lie can sometimes pull that thread: the mercenary company whose contract was forged, the general whose title was, the bodyguard who swore he was ready and was not. Knowing the lie is the easy half, because no amount of knowing lifts a thread, and Judicium’s cleverest have been carried home on doors trying the other half, and those who manage it are owed a knot, usually some truth of their own told at a bad moment.
Spirit Temperance through discernment: order, measure and consequence.
Alchemy The law Separation draws on, the Parting of the bench: discernment, the parts told apart and taken apart.
Stat Effect Strengthens Gnosis Acuity and Analysis. The mind becomes a scalpel. Judicium practitioners read weakness the way literate people read text.
Glyph [Sel] Measure, [Ur] Balance, [Ar] Accord, [Krn] Crown, [IrW] Will, [Ed] Edgetruth, [Edt] Edict, [Exile] Exile, [NmEl] Name-Eater, [Flm] Judic Flame; attested on twelve more.
Failure Discernment tells everything apart and cannot choose to leave anything untold. Off guard, every object in view reports what it is made of at once, and the reader loses the power to put any of it first. Pushed past the point where a reading only reads, telling a thing apart becomes taking it apart: the read starts to pass judgment, which can turn away force or at the very top end a life, and since it has no way to look at one thing only, it takes the reader’s own memory in the same stroke. The Measurewrights call it spectral overload.

The Measurewrights’ account. This is the guild’s theory, often right about how much and never about why.
Analogue · Emission and absorption spectroscopy. Nondestructive flaw detection.
Mechanism · Every element, they say, absorbs and emits at wavelengths fixed by its own electron structure, and no substance can present another’s spectrum. By their reckoning Judicium tunes Gnosis to that principle: the practitioner reads the characteristic lines of a Crystal, a technique, or a lie, and identifies composition from signature alone, the way eddy-current inspection finds the crack under the paint without removing the paint. A lie, as the confessors keep pointing out, has no electrons.
The story they tell.
No dice yard between Marrowhold and the sea will seat Lu Qinghe, the Scalpel of the Clear Needle Hall, and three of them pay her nine silver a month to stay away. At the Autumn Assize she stood up in the gallery with arc-blue threads crossing her eyes, and read a forged land grant from forty paces: the scribe, the ink, the week it was written, and the name of the man who paid for it, who was sitting in the front row in a very good hat. His bodyman went for a knife. She told him which of his knuckles was already cracked, and he stopped to check. The Needle Hall’s colors went up in every street that night, and the Hall’s rivals started writing their contracts in the dark. What the song leaves out is the fish market at the Salt Fair, on a hot morning with her guard down, when every herring, hook, scale-pan and lying fishwife in the square reported its composition to her at once, and four apprentices carried her home on a door, screaming numbers.
Manganthra · The Catalyst of Change

Folk name the Go-Between (what carters, soldiers and the commons call it; each culture may add its own beside it).
The idea The go-between. Change that happens because something stands between two enemies and lets them meet, and a soul under this lens can hold what ought to tear it apart.
Kind Wild
Titan Prometheus: the teacher of Transmutation in the person of the go-between, who brings two enemies together and walks out unchanged.
Operation Conjunction: two enemies are brought to meet and marry on the go-between’s ground, and the go-between walks out unchanged.
Hue Orange with dark violet-brown glints, because the go-between holds two enemies side by side, and the dark one shows through without the two ever mixing.
Ground Favors kilns, forges, smelters and hot springs, places where things that would never meet have long been brought together in the fire; hates lukewarm places where nothing is hotter than anything else, cold that has soaked through everything, and air that will not feed a flame.
Contrary Fixatio (the go-between that stays out of the product against the bond nobody can leave). It is also the one lens built to hold other people’s contraries, which is what it is for.
On the Body The flesh becomes a surface where things that should never meet can meet, and one arm will carry a poison and its cure, or two Wellsprings’ quarrel, without the limb being torn by it.
On the Spirit Two workings that would wreck each other can be held side by side in the Core until they do what neither could alone, and the strange part is that the practitioner comes out of it unchanged.
On Fate With a great deal of blood the go-between can bring about a meeting that already had a way of happening: two allied captains who hate each other on the same mountain road in the same hour, a duelist’s old enemy at the ropes in the one exchange where he can do harm. It takes nothing from the deal, each such pull leaves a knot that falls due as a meeting the holder would have paid to miss, and it cannot be done often, because one bad meeting poisons the holder’s whole gift for years, and both sides go on trying to hire them regardless.
Spirit Temperance through transformation.
Alchemy The go-between that stays out of the product: two reagents held side by side until they will do what neither would alone. (the trade’s reading) Iron conducts it.
Stat Effect Strengthens Ardency Depth, Gnosis Acuity. The practitioner integrates contradictory Wellspring energies without resonance conflict.
Glyph None attested in the Index (see Where the Registers Disagree on the hub).
Failure The go-between works only by standing between and walking out unchanged, and it has no defense against a guest who will not leave. Let one thing take hold in the place where meetings happen and it sits there for good, and the practitioner loses not one harmonization but the capacity to hold any pair at all. The Measurewrights call it catalyst poisoning.

The Measurewrights’ account. This is the guild’s theory, often right about how much and never about why.
Analogue · Heterogeneous catalysis. Adsorption of incompatible reactants onto a shared surface.
Mechanism · A catalyst, they say, is not consumed and does not appear in the products. It provides a surface where two species that would never meet in bulk are held adjacent long enough to react, opening a pathway with a lower barrier than the direct route. In their account Manganthra gives the Shell that surface, which they offer as the mechanical reason a Manganthra practitioner can hold contradictory Wellsprings without resonance conflict tearing the lattice.
Materia Primordia · The First Substance

Folk name the First Stuff (what carters, soldiers and the commons call it; each culture may add its own beside it).
The idea The first substance. One self and many forms, and a soul that finds it can become its own opposite and still be itself.
Kind Wild
Titan Gaia: form itself, the source of Soul Crystal latticework. Her Flesh Remembers Stone is written in this Wellspring.
Operation Conjunction: the one substance is wed to its own opposite and goes on being itself, the marriage the bench calls the first matter.
Hue Ochre shifting between graphite-gray and diamond-clear, because the one substance is always wearing one of its forms and never the same one for long.
Ground Favors ore-rich rock, worked stone and deep foundations, places where one substance has long been worked into many forms; hates open water, high peaks and moving decks, which hold no form at all.
Contrary Oblivara (one self written down against one self in many forms); Basilithe (every form against the one note).
On the Body At home the flesh re-lattices on command, hard as diamond for one exchange and slick as graphite for the next, so the whole contest turns on what you are wearing when the blow arrives. Ingrid Stenhammar will tell you the rest for the price of a drink.
On the Spirit Inscribed on a thing or pressed on a soul, it can persuade either into another of its own lawful meanings, so a sword may be told it is a plowshare and hang quiet on its wall through a feud, and a coward may be shown the form of himself that stood. The iron stays iron throughout, since turning it to rust is Shell work. It goes no further than the thing already was, and nobody has yet talked a stone into being a bird.
On Fate Here the many forms are a person’s standing, each claim true and each with its own bonds, and after years of keeping both alive a rout arranged against the general may find only a wool merchant in the way, while the garrison that swore to the merchant opens its gates to the general. Each pull on it leaves a knot, and the knots fall due together on the day the two meet under pressure, when the world keeps whichever was on at the time, and the holder has no say in it for the rest of their life.
Spirit Temperance through origin. The confessors’ reading: re-forming, the self discovered in another of its own shapes.
Alchemy One of the six Wellsprings the bench names its works after: it re-lattices one Essence into another of its own forms. The Bench files a Materia Primordia Draft as a Coagulation.
Stat Effect Strengthens Vitality Fortitude, Dominion Gravity. The body and the Domain gain mineral-weight authority.
Glyph None primary. Attested on twelve, among them [En] Lattice, [Th] Foundation and [Tp] Topology.
Failure One self can wear many forms, but only one at a time, and it has to remember the others to come back to them. Under enough pressure it forgets, and the practitioner keeps for good whichever form they were wearing when the pressure came. The Measurewrights call it phase locking.

The Measurewrights’ account. This is the guild’s theory, often right about how much and never about why.
Analogue · Allotropy. One element, several lattices, radically different materials.
Mechanism · Graphite and diamond, they say, are the same element, and the difference is entirely in how the atoms are arranged, which is the difference between a lubricant and the hardest natural substance known. By their reckoning Materia Primordia grants the Crystal access to its own polymorphism: the same spent substance, re-latticed, expressing properties that appear to belong to different substances entirely. It is an elegant account of a diamond, and silent on how a soul finds out it can be its own opposite and still be itself.
The story they tell.
Ingrid Stenhammar fought the Stage brackets at Tollgate for six summers as the Changing Woman, and they sold out the stands to see it. In the first exchange she would go diamond from the collarbone down in a wash of amber light, and a man’s knuckles would come apart on her. In the second she re-latticed with a small bright ring you could hear at the beer stalls, soft and gray and slick as an eel in butter, and his best hold slid off her like a dropped plate. Hats went in the air. Then, in the sixth final, while she was slick and laughing, Black Anders Holm brought a twelve-pound maul down on her with everything he owned, and the pressure came. She has been graphite from the collarbone down ever since. She cannot hold a sword or take a fall, she leaves a gray streak on every door in the Quarter, and she sells her own shavings to the Tollgate wagoners as axle grease at a wicked price, with the best patter on the road.
Monolithion · The Enduring Monument

Folk name the Monument (what carters, soldiers and the commons call it; each culture may add its own beside it).
The idea The monument. A self with no seams in it, which outlasts everything and stops being a person in a room and starts being a feature of the land.
The turn Choosing to remain when every instinct demands flight. It is among the slowest of the Sixty to take hold in a soul and among the most resistant to Catalytic Collapse once it does.
Kind Wild
Titan Kaldrion: after a cataclysm he decides which ruins stand long enough to become memory, and this is a soul standing.
Operation Coagulation: the self is set so slowly into one mass that no seam is left in it.
Hue Deep amber monolith, because the self has been set into one mass with no seam in it to break the color.
Ground Favors ore-rich rock, worked stone and deep foundations, places where something has long stood until it became part of the land; hates open water, high peaks and moving decks, where nothing stays long enough to become a monument.
Contrary Nihiloth (the canonical hard case, form set against the erosion of all shape); Rebirthine (outlasting everything against breaking down to pay for the next); Verdantia (the finished monument against the self with no final size).
On the Body The slow loads that grind everyone else down, marching, hunger, a month on a wall, barely register in flesh with so few seams left in it, and a swung maul meets something closer to a cliff than a man. Getting such a person to turn around takes some planning.
On the Spirit What it sends at a soul comes out heavy and slow, more a hillside leaning on the mind than a bolt, and an inscription cut on this lens is still in force when the wall it was cut on is not.
On Fate Stay long enough and the land has to route around you: roads bend away from your valley and Aura Pressure sits in it like weather. Over decades an army that planned to cross may find its guides, its maps and its nerve all favoring the long way, and the price is the person, who has not spoken in years and has not noticed the three invasions that went around. The knot, when it falls due, is the one thing that would not go around.
Spirit Temperance through memory. The confessors’ reading: permanence, until presence becomes geological.
Alchemy The great casting: one mass cooled so slowly it has no seam in it. (the trade’s reading)
Stat Effect Strengthens Vitality Tolerance, Resilience Persistence, Dominion Gravity. Presence becomes geological.
Glyph [Inr] Inertial; attested on one more.
Failure A self with no seams has no place where a break can stop. When something finally gets into the monument it runs straight through, and when Monolithion fails it fails across the whole of the person at once. The Measurewrights call it brittle at scale.

The Measurewrights’ account. This is the guild’s theory, often right about how much and never about why.
Analogue · Grain growth and creep resistance. Single-crystal structure at geological timescale.
Mechanism · Polycrystalline metal, they say, fails at its grain boundaries under sustained high-temperature load, which is why the scholars’ ideal part for such a load would be grown as one single crystal with no boundaries to fail along. By their reckoning Monolithion drives the Crystal toward that condition: fewer internal interfaces, enormous resistance to slow deformation, and a presence that behaves less like a person occupying a room than like a feature of the terrain. Why anyone would choose to stay when every instinct says run is outside the scope of the reckoning.
Nihiloth · The Hollow Law

Folk name the Undoing (what carters, soldiers and the commons call it; each culture may add its own beside it).
The idea The hollow law. Power by negation: the rule itself unmade, and what stands in the gap.
Kind Wild
Titan Zar’thuun: the boundary between something and nothing. His Closing Eye is written in this Wellspring.
Operation Dissolution: the rule itself is loosed until nothing of it is left, and the gap is left standing where it was.
Hue Absolute dark, because where the rule is unmade nothing is left to give off a color.
Ground Favors darkness, silence, Aether-thin ground and ruins, places where rules have long since fallen away; hates Aether-rich ground, crowds and active Domains, where law is being made on every side.
Contrary Eidolyn (the thing imagined into standing against the rule unmade); Oblivara (a name that cannot be erased against a law of erasing); Monolithion (the canonical hard case, form set against the erosion of all shape).
On the Body It rides the blow as a small cancellation: a hardened Shell meets the fist and for that instant has nothing holding it up, and a swung weight arrives with its momentum gone missing. The same gap opens in the striker’s own guard, so the good ones fight as though they have already been hit.
On the Spirit Sent from the Core, it strikes one clause out of what a thing means and leaves the rest standing around without it: an heirloom blade that is suddenly only iron to the hand that swore on it, a ward that no longer recalls what it was warding. The edge is as keen as it ever was. Fine work and ruinously dear, paid for in clauses of the sender’s own, and no two Measurewrights agree on what is in the gap.
On Fate Its great terror is the Domain, where a rule removed reaches exactly as far as the practitioner’s claim on the ground, and at the far end of a life that claim can take in a field on which a chain of command or a company’s oath has nothing left holding it up. Elsewhere it is a small bleak habit in which other people’s oaths fail to bite on this person, and every rule it removes is somebody’s, since Archons and the great principles are the laws, and they have been known to notice. The knot is a rule the holder was relying on, found missing later.
Spirit Temperance through void. The confessors’ reading: negation.
Alchemy Neutralization: two reagents poured together until nothing is left in the flask that can act. (the trade’s reading)
Stat Effect Strengthens Dominion Sovereignty, Resilience Persistence, Gnosis Cognition. The practitioner imposes law through negation. Their Domain does not add rules. It removes them.
Glyph [Thru] Hollow, [Nl] Null, [Vn] Void; attested on eight more.
Failure A rule unmade is unmade for everyone, and the idea has no way to spare its maker. Everything the practitioner brought inside is subject to the same gap, including the parts of themselves they were relying on. The Measurewrights call it symmetric null.

The Measurewrights’ account. This is the guild’s theory, often right about how much and never about why.
Analogue · Destructive interference and the null field. A region genuinely empty of energy.
Mechanism · Two waves in antiphase, they say, do not conceal one another: they sum to zero, and the region between them carries no energy at all. They hold that Nihiloth builds Domains on that principle, which is why a Nihiloth Domain does not impose additional law. It cancels the law already present, and what remains inside is the absence of a rule. What a rule is, that a wave could cancel it, the guild has not yet put in writing.
Orrenthal · The Metallic Heart

Folk name the Common Heart (what carters, soldiers and the commons call it; each culture may add its own beside it).
The idea The heart held in common. A soul whose goods belong to the whole of it, which bends under load and keeps its word.
Kind Wild
Titan Kaldrion: the honestly made, which he reinforces, in a thing that bends under load and keeps its word.
Operation Conjunction: the parts of the soul are joined so that everything in it is held in common by the whole.
Hue Polished blue-silver, because a thing held in common and honestly kept has nothing hidden in it to tarnish.
Ground Favors dry open air, ore-veined ground and a clear line of sight, places where metal has long lain in the rock in common; hates rooms caged in iron, walls of heavy iron and thick fog.
Contrary Fractura (the metal that bends under load against the place where everything breaks).
On the Body A load struck on one point is borne by the whole frame, so a blow that should crack a forearm spends itself through the back and legs, and the body bends and comes back.
On the Spirit Essence held in common across the Core carries a working through itself with hardly any loss, and with no part of the person arguing with the rest they are very hard to inscribe on or to talk round.
On Fate A sworn company on this lens shares a debt and a hurt every day, and its oath bends a long way before it breaks. Its rare great working spreads the odds against one of them through all of them, so the spear meant for the standard-bearer meets a shield that had no business being there and every man in the line feels that spear go in somewhere, the knot is shared out the same way as a small misfortune apiece inside the month, and an enemy who has read this goes to work between two friends, which is where it fails.
Spirit Temperance through integrity.
Alchemy The metal as a commonwealth: a body whose parts hold everything in common and so bends without breaking. (the trade’s reading)
Stat Effect Strengthens Vitality Constitution, Resilience Integrity, Tempering Maturity. Moral density that the Crystal recognizes as structural reinforcement.
Glyph [Chw] Choir, [Br] Bridge; attested on three more.
Failure A soul held in common is only as sound as the trust between its parts, and the idea keeps no guard on that. Attack goes in along the seams between them rather than at the whole, and the soul fails at its seams while the bulk of it remains sound. The Measurewrights call it intergranular corrosion.

The Measurewrights’ account. This is the guild’s theory, often right about how much and never about why.
Analogue · Metallic bonding. The delocalized electron sea.
Mechanism · A metal, they say, is strong, conductive, and ductile for one reason: its valence electrons belong to the lattice rather than to any atom in it. Nothing is individually owned, so the structure deforms without fracturing and carries charge with little resistance, and by their reckoning Orrenthal imposes that bonding character on the Crystal. The Measurewrights note without embarrassment that the Wellspring’s moral reading and its physical reading are the same reading, and the benches note that the guild has the order the wrong way round.
Petralon · The Foundation Stone

Folk name the Foundation Stone (what carters, soldiers and the commons call it; each culture may add its own beside it).
The idea The foundation. To become what other things stand on: load taken, carried and sent down, at the price of slowly settling. Breaking, holding and rising are one law seen from three positions, and this lens treats a soul as a loaded structure, asking the only question a master mason ever asks: where the load goes, and what happens at the place it concentrates.
Kind Wild
Titan Kaldrion: load and bearing, stone taught how to carry. His Deep Grid’s Verdict is written in this Wellspring, and so is Atla’zon’s Bent Knee’s Burden, because which way is down is Atla’zon’s to hold and what stands under it is Kaldrion’s to carry.
Operation Coagulation: the soul is fixed as the foundation, set to bear and never to rise.
Hue Heavy gray, because it is the color of what everything else stands on, which nobody ever stops to look at.
Ground Favors great masses of stone, heights and brittle old rock or rock already under load, places that have long borne everything stood on them; hates silt and loose sand, a drop with nothing under it, and soft even ground that will not carry a load down.
Contrary Cymorath (slipping the load against being what the load stands on); Abython (bearing the load against having no load to bear).
On the Body Every blow that lands is handed down through the skeleton and into the floor, so the fighter grows harder to shift with each year and slower to turn. The stance sinks a little with every fight and does not always come back up.
On the Spirit A working sets where it lands and stays set, so an inscription on a threshold goes on carrying what it says for a generation and grows steadily harder to lift, and a soul on this lens can be rested on by the frightened. It sends poorly, and what it says a thing is it goes on saying long after anyone wants it said.
On Fate Whole companies come to rest on one name, and the panic and bad news that should have brought the line down can, for a day or two and at ruinous strain, go down through the holder and into the ground instead. They sink a little under each such day, each one leaving a knot that is paid as a load arriving later with nobody to hand it to, and find out late that they cannot walk out from under it, and a clever enemy pulls them sideways, at which point an army that had stopped holding itself up discovers the fact all at once.
Spirit Temperance through endurance.
Alchemy Salt in its fixed office: the foundation that bears the whole vessel and never rises. (the trade’s reading)
Stat Effect Strengthens Vitality Constitution, Dominion Gravity. The character becomes the ground beneath the ground.
Glyph [Th] Foundation, [En] Lattice, [Va] Law, [Bd] Bedrock, [Grt] Granite, [Mt] Mantle; attested on seven more.
Failure A foundation bears whatever presses down on it, and nothing ever asked it to hold on. Pull on it, the one load it does not answer, and it does not give gracefully. It parts. The Measurewrights call it tensile exposure.

The Measurewrights’ account. This is the guild’s theory, often right about how much and never about why.
Analogue · Compressive load path and creep. Stone in compression; the arch.
Mechanism · Masonry, they say, is enormously strong in compression and nearly worthless in tension, which is why the arch exists: it converts a span into a queue of compressive members. By their reckoning Petralon reorganizes the Crystal along the same principle, routing every incoming load into compression and accepting slow creep deformation as the price of never developing a tensile crack. The arch is a good comparison, and the masons who built the arches never needed the theory.
Pyraeon · The Ember Crown

Folk name the Ember (what carters, soldiers and the commons call it; each culture may add its own beside it).
The idea The ember that stays lit. Power that gives up its flare and keeps its heat for a lifetime.
Kind Wild
Titan Chronaeus: the long pace of a thing kept lit, whose war is won by people who will not live to see it.
Operation Distillation: a low fire kept under the vessel for months and years, never let flare, until what is wanted comes over drop by drop for a lifetime.
Hue Dull red glow under a crust, no flame, because the flare has been given up and only the heat is kept.
Ground Favors banked hearths, kilns, forges and hot springs, places where a fire has long been kept alive without once flaring; hates lukewarm places that keep no heat, cold that has soaked through everything, and air that will not feed a flame.
Contrary Ignivale (the flare with no heat kept against the heat with no flare); Catharsis (keeping the heat for life against setting the load down).
On the Body The flare goes and the heat stays, so the practitioner hits a little softer than anyone expects, and exactly that hard at dusk after a day of it, and again at seventy.
On the Spirit Workings burn low and very long, and a mark left on a thing stays faintly live in it, still quietly arguing about what that thing is a year after the fight is forgotten.
On Fate A claim kept banked for a lifetime can be blown on once at the end of it, and the war that turns is won by people who will not live to see it: a marriage refused here, a crossing left unbridged there, until the enemy’s great-grandson marches to a river nobody ever got around to spanning. That one breath takes all the heat the holder kept for seventy years and leaves a knot to match, which the world is in no hurry to collect, and a fighter who spends it in a single duel has nothing left for dusk.
Spirit Temperance through endurance.
Alchemy The Long Furnace’s fire: slow heat kept for months, with the charge never once flaring. (the trade’s reading)
Stat Effect Strengthens Vitality Constitution, Tempering Longevity, and Ardency Flux held over time rather than Flux at peak. Output does not fade over time. The ember persists.
Glyph [Py] Pyre, [Cin] Cinder, [Fge] Forge; attested on five more.
Failure The ember stays lit, and nothing in the idea knows how to put it out. When the practitioner lets the working go it goes on smoldering where they cannot see it, eating reserve and tissue for hours after they believed it ended. The Measurewrights call it underground propagation.

The Measurewrights’ account. This is the guild’s theory, often right about how much and never about why.
Analogue · Smoldering combustion. Flameless, diffusion-limited, self-sustaining.
Mechanism · Smoldering, they say, propagates at roughly a millimeter a minute at temperatures a third of open flame, and peat beds have burned continuously for decades because the reaction is limited only by oxidizer reaching the char. By their reckoning Pyraeon converts the Crystal’s output profile from flame to smolder: far lower instantaneous yield, and an endurance that does not decay across an engagement or across a life.
Pyreveil · The Fire of Renewal

Folk name the New Fire (what carters, soldiers and the commons call it; each culture may add its own beside it).
The idea Fire that renews. Whatever this lens touches it burns down so that something can stand up in its place, and the burning stays in the soul as strength where it would otherwise have left as smoke.
The turn The moment anger becomes purpose rather than destruction. Fire of every sort is something ending so that something else can begin, creation and destruction on one law, so nobody has ever cleanly called this lens either one.
Kind Wild
Titan Prometheus: destruction as transformation at its plainest, the burn that stays behind to feed what comes next.
Operation Calcination: burning a thing down to what will not burn, so that what is left can be built on.
Hue Deep ember-orange, steady, because the fire stays where it was lit and never flares off into smoke.
Ground Favors burned ground coming back green, kilns, forges and hot springs, places where fire has long been at work and something keeps standing up after it; hates still cold water and air that will not feed a flame.
Contrary Vantabriel (burning it down against keeping all of it).
On the Body The heat lives in the tissue, so the blow burns on contact and the body stops minding fire, having taken it in as a lodger.
On the Spirit Sent from the Core, it burns what a thing holds and leaves the thing: a grief, a grudge or an attachment goes up, the false before the solid, so a forged seal stops persuading anyone while its wax sits cool and whole on the letter. Something can stand up where the grudge was. The sender is hollowed by each burning and warmed by none of them.
On Fate On its best day a pull under this lens burns chances, provided they were already dry: the rival’s hired second with one foot out the door loses his last reason to stay, the enemy’s grain store under a season-old thatch runs out of nights on which it might not have caught, and, only at the end of a life spent learning how, a whole army finds its reasons for staying in the field gone up. The heat has to leave somehow, and it leaves through whatever tissue of the holder’s is nearest, which is why the people who have done this twice have so little skin to show for it. The knot burns a chance of the holder’s own, something that was going to happen for them and now will not, so that something else can.
Spirit Temperance through burning; destruction reborn as creation.
Alchemy The Sulfur principle at full heat: a fire that stays resident in the body it burns. (the trade’s reading)
Stat Effect Strengthens Ardency Flux, Ardency Depth, Vitality Tolerance. Output burns hotter. The body stops minding heat.
Glyph None attested in the Index (see Where the Registers Disagree on the hub).
Failure The fire cannot stop renewing. It burns things down so that something can stand up in their place, and it keeps that bargain whether or not anything is left to burn, so a working pushed past what the worker meant to clear goes on clearing the nearest thing that can be made new when the working ends, which is the worker’s own tissue. The Measurewrights call it thermal debt.

The Measurewrights’ account. This is the guild’s theory, often right about how much and never about why.
Analogue · Enthalpy of combustion, and the conservation of energy across a reaction.
Mechanism · Burning, they say, does not remove energy from a system; it re-partitions it into forms the system can no longer hold in the same shape. By their reckoning Pyreveil retunes the Shell so the Charge burns hotter, with what is released staying partly resident in the body instead of radiating away, which is why output climbs and the tissue stops registering heat as damage. Their figures for the heat are good. Their account of why the fire stays is the part the benches laugh at.
Rebirthine · The Cycle Eternal

Folk name the Wheel (what carters, soldiers and the commons call it; each culture may add its own beside it).
The idea The cycle. Loss taken as the first step of the next building, what is broken down paying for what comes up.
Kind Wild
Titan Florwyn: restorative entropy, the rule that all destruction must yield renewal. Her Green Chord is written in this Wellspring.
Operation Fermentation: what is broken down is let rot so that what comes up next can feed on it.
Hue Red with gray flecks, because the new life comes up through what was broken down to pay for it.
Ground Favors thick living growth, mild weather and ground close to blood, places where things have long died and fed what came after; hates barren ground, bitter cold and Aether-thin soil, where nothing breaks down to pay for anything.
Contrary Monolithion (outlasting everything against breaking down to pay for the next).
On the Body The body digests its own damaged flesh to pay for the new, so a burned arm feeds tomorrow’s muscle and a fighter can spend a wound like coin. Short of food and rest it goes on spending, and it does not check the balance.
On the Spirit A working takes a thing apart so that something can be authored from the wreck, which makes this a fine lens for rebuilding a ruined ward or a broken technique. It is a poor one for leaving anything as it was.
On Fate Lost ties come back as new ones: a dead friend’s daughter turns up on the doorstep, and the levy thrown away in the marsh may, at the far end of a long accounting, turn out to have bought the alliance that wins the following spring. Only real losses pay for it and each pull’s knot is one more of them, so holders keep very good accounts and spend what they love to the man, and they do not always notice when there is nothing left to spend.
Spirit Temperance through renewal. The confessors’ reading: loss, destruction treated as the first step of reconstruction.
Alchemy The law Fermentation draws on, from the Rot to the Feeding: breakdown pays for growth.
Stat Effect Strengthens Resilience Persistence, Tempering Maturity, Vitality Regeneration. The Crystal treats destruction as the first step of reconstruction.
Glyph [Vael] Renewal, [Yn] Bloom, [Cy] Cycle; attested on six more.
Failure The cycle pays for every building with a loss, and with nothing outside to break down it breaks down the worker. It eats structure faster than it rebuilds, and it does not recognize the point at which there is nothing left to spend. The Measurewrights call it autophagic collapse.

The Measurewrights’ account. This is the guild’s theory, often right about how much and never about why.
Analogue · Apoptosis and autophagy. Programmed clearance funding regeneration.
Mechanism · Controlled cell death, they say, is a service to the organism and no failure of it, and autophagy digests the cell’s own damaged components to fund the construction of new ones: catabolism pays for anabolism. By their reckoning Rebirthine makes destruction the first operation of a build sequence rather than the interruption of one, which is why its practitioners treat losses as inventory. The guild keeps the inventory and leaves the grieving to the confessors.
Solfatara · The Fuming Earth

Folk name the Fume (what carters, soldiers and the commons call it; each culture may add its own beside it).
The idea The fuming earth. Pressure let out forever and never saved up, so the soul stops building toward a blow and becomes a steady force in the room.
Kind Wild
Titan Valmir: Entropic Equilibrium, which exists so that no energy anywhere stagnates.
Operation Sublimation: what presses in the soul is given off as fume without end and never stored.
Hue Deep sulfurous red, because the pressure is let out as fume all the time and never saved up for a blaze.
Ground Favors fumaroles and sulfur vents, kilns, forges and hot springs, places where the earth has long breathed its pressure out; hates lukewarm places with nothing in them to breathe out, cold that has soaked through everything, and air that will not feed a flame.
Contrary Cataclysm (never building against everything built going at once).
On the Body The Shell never stops venting, so the body stands in a fight the way a hot spring stands in a field, pushing steadily at whatever comes close and never winding up to do it.
On the Spirit A working seeps where others would throw, and a line inscribed on a doorstep goes on breathing its meaning into the house for years at a cost nobody notices paying.
On Fate Its usual weapon is plain presence with no peak to it, which wears on a besieging camp’s sleep and nerve without anyone lifting a hand, and which the holder can keep up for a year. Pulling a thread through it is another matter: the sentry who has been about to drop his guard for a month can be made to do it tonight, and the pressure spent on him comes back as the knot, out through the weakest thing the holder ever swore.
Spirit Temperance through pressure.
Alchemy The vessel that breathes: fume let off without end, so the charge never bursts. (the trade’s reading)
Stat Effect Strengthens Tempering Clarity, Vitality Constitution, Dominion Pressure. Sustained pressure output becomes the character’s natural state.
Glyph [Slg] Slag; attested on one more.
Failure The fuming earth lets its pressure out forever and has never learned to hold any of it. Interrupt the release and the pressure does not politely wait: it finds a new way out through whatever is weakest. The Measurewrights call it vent blockage and phreatic failure.

The Measurewrights’ account. This is the guild’s theory, often right about how much and never about why.
Analogue · Fumarolic degassing. Volatile exsolution as confining pressure falls.
Mechanism · Dissolved gas, they say, stays in solution under load and comes out of it the moment the load eases, which is why a volcanic system vents continuously for centuries without erupting. By their reckoning Solfatara holds the Crystal at permanent partial exsolution, a steady controlled release rather than a stored charge, so that the practitioner does not build to a discharge and simply never stops discharging.
Sublimare · The Rising Breath

Folk name the Clearing (what carters, soldiers and the commons call it; each culture may add its own beside it).
The idea Purification by rising. What is light goes up, what remains is purer, and the soul goes on refining itself toward one clear thing.
Kind Wild
Titan Omnis: the same lesson done slowly, by parting what will rise from what will not.
Operation Distillation: what is light in the soul is driven up and parted from what stays, and what stays is purer each time.
Hue Gray graded in bands, because each band is a fraction risen and parted from the one beneath it, lighter toward the top.
Ground Favors great masses of stone, towers and heights, and brittle old rock or rock already under load, places where what is light has long been carried up and parted from what stays; hates silt and loose sand, a drop with nothing under it, and soft even ground where nothing rises out of anything.
Contrary Cinerion (treasure in what stays behind against treasure in what rises); Dissolution (mixing against parting).
On the Body Hard drilling boils the waste out of a fighter’s movement in a faint silver haze, and what stays in the hands is one motion, very pure. Ask that fighter for a different motion and watch them think about it.
On the Spirit A working run through the soul’s column parts a thing into its fractions for a moment, and what rises shows what the thing was mostly made of. It is a better assay than it is a weapon.
On Fate Ties part by how lightly they were held, so a host under this lens boils down on the march, the levies and fair-weather oaths drifting off by the hundred, and what reaches the field is a short list of people who will die there. Doing the same to an enemy’s host means staying close for a season and boiling off some of yourself, the knot being some lightly held tie of the holder’s own found gone when they reach for it, and nobody gets to choose the names on either list.
Spirit Temperance through ascent.
Alchemy The law Distillation draws on: parting by boiling point, the spirit risen and returned.
Stat Effect Strengthens Tempering Clarity, Resilience Fortification. The Crystal purifies itself, burning off impurities as silver vapor.
Glyph [Prc] Pressure; attested on four more.
Failure Rising parts only what rises differently, and some faults rise exactly as the soul does. Refining against one never ends: the practitioner runs the column indefinitely against something that goes up with every breath of them and will not be left behind. The Measurewrights call it an azeotrope.

The Measurewrights’ account. This is the guild’s theory, often right about how much and never about why.
Analogue · Fractional distillation. Separation by differential volatility.
Mechanism · A mixture heated in a column, they say, separates because its components have different vapor pressures, and the fraction that rises is not the same substance that entered. Where Sublimatio skips a phase, in their account, Sublimare separates a mixture: the Crystal is run as a column, impurity is driven off as the lighter fraction, and what descends is the practitioner refined toward a single component.
Sublimatio · The Ascending Breath

Folk name the Clean Step (what carters, soldiers and the commons call it; each culture may add its own beside it).
The idea Rising straight through. A soul that leaves its lower state behind in one clean step, with nothing spilled in between.
Kind Wild
Titan Omnis: he teaches what is in matter to rise, and this is the rising done in one step.
Operation Sublimation: the soul leaves its lower state in one clean step and rises straight through, with no state in between.
Hue Iron-gray vapor, because the soul goes straight from what it was into what rises, with nothing pooling between.
Ground Favors great masses of stone, crags and towers, and brittle old rock or rock already under load, places from which things have long gone straight up and left the lower ground behind; hates silt and loose sand, a drop with nothing under it, and soft even ground with nothing to rise from.
Contrary Anamnesis (the record kept against the lower state left behind); Ascensio (every step climbed against no steps at all); Contrition (a failure kept as armor against a lower self left behind).
On the Body Force goes from stillness to full delivery with no wind-up in between, so the tell an opponent reads for never appears. There is also no halfway at which the fighter could change their mind and pull the blow.
On the Spirit A working leaves the hand already finished, never passing a stage where it could be read, countered or corrected. The part of its author that would not make the leap stays behind and goes on complaining.
On Fate A person’s standing can change in one step, the oath-bound squire a free lord by morning, and very rarely a fight’s does the same: the line that was going to give goes from held to lost with no wavering first for a captain to catch. There is no halfway at which to stop it, so the holder pays in full whichever way it lands, and what did not rise with them stays behind with their name on it as the knot, and it sends its bill in one step too.
Spirit Temperance through refinement.
Alchemy One of the six Wellsprings the bench names its works after, mirrored in the bench’s Sublimation: it elevates without passing through the states between, with no stage at which the working can be inspected or corrected. Gold carries it.
Stat Effect Strengthens Ardency Compression, Tempering Clarity. Output becomes cleaner and sharper, with less waste per expression.
Glyph None primary. Attested on [Grs] Grace, [Dom] Dominion, [Rk] Rupture and [Exile] Exile.
Failure Rising in one clean step takes only what will make the step, and the idea has no way to bring the rest along. Everything that would not rise is still there, and it is the part of the practitioner least willing to move. The Measurewrights call it residue accumulation.

The Measurewrights’ account. This is the guild’s theory, often right about how much and never about why.
Analogue · Sublimation. Solid to vapor with no liquid phase, below the triple point.
Mechanism · At sufficiently low pressure, they say, a solid does not melt: it leaves directly, and whatever cannot make that transition stays behind as residue. They hold that Sublimatio keeps the Shell below its triple point so what the soul spends skips the intermediate state entirely: no pooling, no partial expression, no waste at the phase boundary where most practitioners lose their margin. Their diagram of the phases is correct in every line, and has no line on it for the part of a person that would not go.
Tenebra · The Hidden Shadow

Folk name the Hidden Shadow (what carters, soldiers and the commons call it; each culture may add its own beside it).
The idea The hidden shadow. Going unseen, quieter than the world around you, and the old question of what you are hiding from.
Kind Wild
Titan Ilgrimm: shadow and the secrets kept in it. His Hollow That Watches is written in this Wellspring.
Operation Separation: the soul is parted from the world’s notice and kept quieter than everything around it.
Hue Matt black-violet that absorbs light, because going unseen means giving nothing back to the one who looks.
Ground Favors darkness, silence, Aether-thin ground and ruins, places where things have long gone unseen; hates Aether-rich ground, crowds and active Domains, where too many eyes are on everything.
Contrary Penanceflare (nothing hidden against nothing seen); Judicium (the mark that cannot be hidden against the art of leaving none); Aurevane (light that arrives as sent against light that never comes back).
On the Body The Shell drinks the light and noise that reach it, and a fighter stays perfectly visible while going quieter than the background, so the strike comes from someone the eye keeps sliding off. Everything swallowed stays swallowed, a debt with a due date.
On the Spirit Cast out from the Core, the same hush is laid over what a thing is, so a hidden door simply goes unconsidered and a ward looks straight past a man who has hidden his purpose from it. It is weaker than it sounds, and anyone who has been told where to look is untroubled.
On Fate What hides this way is a person’s share of the world’s attention: creditors mislay the address, and bounty boards go stale. Stretching it over a raiding column, so that a sentry’s eye slides to the wrong ridge and men who watched it pass report nothing, is a rare and ruinous feat whose knot leaves the holder for some while the brightest thing on the hill, and friends and relief columns mislay the address too.
Spirit Temperance through secrecy. The confessors’ reading: concealment. The Heresiology’s doctrine stands beside it: the presence of shadow is no proof of heresy, and the use of shadow to erase cost, witness or responsibility often is.
Alchemy The cover-name: the recipe written to hide. (the trade’s reading) Obsidian holds it.
Stat Effect Strengthens Dexterity Feint, Harmonics Suppression, Dominion Sense. The practitioner becomes difficult to detect, read, or track by conventional or Aetheric means.
Glyph [Thal] Silence, [Stg] Stagnate; attested on five more.
Failure Going unseen is always hiding from someone, and a soul can hide only from what it has thought of. Watched from the one direction they did not plan for, a Tenebra practitioner is a very bright thing indeed. Pushed too hard, the hiding fills up: everything swallowed is still in the Shell, and a practitioner kept quieter than the world past their limit lets it all go at once and lights up on every sense in the room. The Measurewrights call it aspect dependence.

The Measurewrights’ account. This is the guild’s theory, often right about how much and never about why.
Analogue · Signal-to-noise reduction. Absorptive coating and faceted return geometry.
Mechanism · Something is undetectable, they say, when its return falls below the noise floor of whatever is looking, which is achieved by absorbing incident energy and by shaping surfaces so the little that reflects goes anywhere except back at the observer. By their reckoning Tenebra applies both to the Shell, so its practitioners stay perfectly visible and run quieter than the background, which is better. What they are hiding from is the old question, and it was never the guild’s.
The story they tell.
For seven years there was a price on the head of Hanne Mott and nobody could describe the head. She went through the Count of Wexmoor’s strong-room with his guards dicing on the other side of the door, matte black-violet swallowing the lamplight around her and every sound in the corridor going dead as wet felt. Heralds cried the bounty up from four hundred silver to two thousand, the minstrels made The Woman Who Is Not There, which gets her height and her number of legs wrong, and bookies took odds on whether she existed. She planned every angle of every job. On the tenth job a pot boy had gone up the chimney stack after pigeon eggs, and he looked straight down on her from the one direction nobody plans for, and to him she was the brightest thing on Wexmoor Hill.
“Mister! There’s a Lady!”
She left with a crossbow bolt through the shoulder, in a hay cart, at speed. The boy got a verse.
Terranova · The Living Earth

Folk name the New Ground (what carters, soldiers and the commons call it; each culture may add its own beside it).
The idea The living earth. Mending by growing, every wound answered with new ground.
Kind Wild
Titan Gaia: the living mantle itself, the ground that heals.
Operation Fermentation: every wound is leavened into new ground, the break itself made the seed of what grows over it.
Hue Pale limestone, because every wound is answered with new ground laid down where the old was broken.
Ground Favors ore-rich rock, worked stone and deep foundations, places where the ground has long healed over its own scars; hates open water, high peaks and moving decks, which give nothing to grow on.
Contrary Mortalis (every wound answered with new ground against the ending understood).
On the Body A wound here is answered by growth, new mineral and new tissue laid down along the damage, so the fighter heals by extension and the old scar becomes the strongest part of the arm. They also get larger in the places they have been hurt, and tailors charge accordingly.
On the Spirit In the Core, breakage seeds new structure, and a soul cracked by loss grows a wing it did not have. Sent into the wound in someone else’s soul it will grow what it is told there, which only menders and torturers attempt, and the line between them is a long-running argument. Flesh it leaves alone.
On Fate What gets hurt around this person tends to come back thicker, a broken friendship regrown in a new shape and a burned village replanted at their feet. A holder can draw on that in war only by taking the damage first and paying it in their own flesh, so the breach in the wall draws every mason in the district by morning while new growth crowds the holder’s own joints and the knot comes up as some trouble they had cut down, grown back thicker, and they cannot always tell you which of it they wanted.
Spirit Temperance through birth. The confessors’ reading: regrowth.
Alchemy The metal tree in the still flask: a mass that mends by growing. (the trade’s reading)
Stat Effect Strengthens Vitality Regeneration, Harmonics Synergy. The body heals by growing rather than repairing.
Glyph None primary. Attested on twelve, among them [Sed] Sediment, [Grt] Granite and [Th] Foundation.
Failure Mending by growing answers a wound with new ground and keeps no memory of the shape it was mending back to. The growth does not know when to stop, and the healed place goes on building past what was there before. The Measurewrights call it overgrowth.

The Measurewrights’ account. This is the guild’s theory, often right about how much and never about why.
Analogue · Biomineralization and self-healing composite. Nacre deposition; bacterial concrete.
Mechanism · Some structures, they say, do not get repaired: they grow their repair in place, laying down mineral along the damage front by the same process that built the original. By their reckoning Terranova gives the Crystal that behavior, which is why its practitioners heal by extension rather than by closure and why their scars are new tissue rather than sealed old tissue. The tailors’ account of it is shorter and has more numbers in it.
Transmutatio · The Law of Change

Folk name the Turning (what carters, soldiers and the commons call it; each culture may add its own beside it).
The idea Change without loss. The same thing said another way, so that what looked like a failure turns out to be fuel in an inconvenient form.
The turn Discovering that where you are is a choice. It treats a thing’s location as no less governable than its shape. A soul under it is always a little bit somewhere else, and a rough result here is a lost afternoon or a lost foot.
Kind Wild
Titan Prometheus: the first lesson of the teacher of Transmutation, that nothing is lost when a thing changes its form.
Operation Fermentation: what was spent is worked over into another form of itself, with nothing added and nothing lost.
Hue Blue-violet, because it is two colors that are one, the same thing said another way.
Ground Favors Veil-thin zones, established Realmgates (standing doorways between Realms) and surveyed ground, places where things have long gone from one place or form to another and arrived as themselves; hates warp scarring, contested Domains (spaces where one practitioner’s law outranks the world’s own habits) and unmapped terrain, where nobody knows the terms a thing started in.
Contrary Oblation (force bought with a loss against change with no loss); Basilithe (one note nobody can retune against the same thing said in another key).
On the Body A missed fist or a failed block is nothing lost, and the Shell says it over in another form, so the stumble becomes the next step and the broken punch comes back through the other hand.
On the Spirit A working gone wrong can be restated from the Core in another basis, the same quantity said another way, and a thing described from far enough round starts to answer to the new description.
On Fate A broken oath or a bad debt can be carried over into other terms by a patient holder, and in a desperate hour so can a lost exchange, what was given up in the last pass turning up as the other fighter’s wrong step in the next, the knot being the same loss owed again later in terms the holder did not choose. Carrying a lost battle over into a won road, the routed wing turning out to be why the enemy’s supply has gone astray, is a masterwork few attempt twice, because a holder who loses track of the terms they started in does not come back as anything recognizable.
Spirit Temperance through motion.
Alchemy One of the six Wellsprings the bench names its works after: it re-expresses a thing in another basis, nothing created or lost. The Bench files a Transmutatio Draft as a composite, and it is volatile: under Preparation Failure it does not deactivate at all.
Stat Effect Strengthens Ardency Overchannel, Tempering Maturity. Failed workings become fuel rather than wounds.
Glyph [Zh] Space, [Flx] Flux; attested on seven more.
Failure Change without loss holds only while someone remembers what the thing was first. Let the practitioner forget which terms they started in, and a change with nothing to return to does not bring back anything recognizable. The Measurewrights call it basis loss.

The Measurewrights’ account. This is the guild’s theory, often right about how much and never about why.
Analogue · Change of basis. Coordinate transformation under conservation.
