the-magic-system/the-soul-and-the-climb/.title: The Ladder and the Draft — Temperance, Advancement and Essence Drafts
the-magic-system/the-soul-and-the-climb/.content:
The dearest breakthrough ever poured at Marrow Fair was spoiled by a drover’s dog. Corvin Hathersage, nineteen years old and heir to the Hathersage wool money, had been told by three instructors that he had the floor for Splintering and none of the rest of it, so he hired the great stage at the autumn brackets, sold the seats at a silver mark a head, put on a gold sash and drank eleven hundred marks’ worth of breakthrough Draft in front of six thousand people, with a herald crying the price of every swallow. It worked, the way they work. His aura went from charcoal with a rumor of blue in it to a cracking web of arc-blue, every hair in the front four rows stood up, and the whole fairground watched his Crystal go to the melt. At exactly that moment Wat Kersey, a kennel-man in his rival’s pay, slipped the dog.
It was a gray bear-baiting mastiff, and it came over the rail of the great stage at a dead run and took him by the arm above the gold sash.
Whatever is in a Crystal at the moment of reorganization is built into what comes out. Hathersage arrived at Stage V before six thousand witnesses, a genuine Expert, with a lattice organized around the purest terror of his young life. He went on to kill nine men in formal duels, and he killed them superbly, with the Stage he had paid for and not one Release to his name. He could not abide a dog in the room. Dogs knew, somehow, and went for him in every yard and street from county to county, and the family spent a fair part of the wool money on men to walk ahead of him with boar-spears. The instructors tell it to every heir who comes to them asking for a bought Stage. The apothecaries sold out of that batch before the fair closed.

The Stage-by-Stage account lives in The Sixteen Stages, with each Stage given four ways: the Codex (the Accord’s master register of laws and figures) ledger line, what it is from inside the person it is happening to, what it looks like from outside, and what the folk call it. This page does not repeat it.
What this page does is join the ladder to the rest of the system: what changes in each Crystal layer (the three layers of the Soul Crystal, which is the soul itself, made a working thing) as a soul climbs, what an Essence Draft is, what money does to advancement, and why the most profitable crime in every realm exists. The climb itself, Stage, Level and the hands, is set out plainly in How Power Grows.
One sentence governs everything below. A Stage opens when its Catalyst is met and the soul’s Level can hold it, and a purse can reach only part of that: a breakthrough Draft or a blessing will supply the Catalyst, a tempering Draft will feed Level at a price of its own, and nothing sold anywhere supplies Mastery or a Release.

I · The two keys
Temperance (the climb of a soul from Stage to Stage) is subtraction. The Soul Crystal is literally the soul, and to temper it is to melt it down and rebuild it, layer by layer. Each pass tempers every layer in its own coin. It packs the Shell tighter, so the Shell can draw in, hold and drive out more raw Charge, and cleaner; it refines the Core’s Essence and makes that Essence stronger; and it firms the Layer’s claim. The layer a soul leans on is rebuilt first and hardest, so a Body soul’s melt begins in the Shell, a Spirit soul’s in the Core and a Fate soul’s in the Layer. The body comes out of it gaining Traits, as The Trait System explains under What a Trait Is. Each Stage is a structural reorganization the Crystal undergoes when accumulated pressure exceeds its current architecture, and no Stage has ever been paid out as a reward for banked experience. A Stage is held only when both keys have turned.
The Level that holds it. Every Stage is held from a Level: Murmuring from 1, Welling from 5, Ascension from 15, Flourishing from 30, Splintering from 101, Glory from 115, Refraction from 130, Transcendence from 201, Invocation from 215, Realization from 230, Dissonance from 301, Emanation from 320, Principality from 401, Zenith from 420 and Revelation from 500. Level is the count of everything hard and real a soul has lived through, and it is the half of the equation every hall’s assayers are trained to read. A Stage reached before its Level is held Overgrown: the Crystal spills power it cannot gather, lamps lean toward its owner, Mastery reads low or not at all, and no Release will come until Level catches up. The older books called this key the quantitative floor, and apothecaries’ contracts still do.
The Catalyst Condition. A specific quality of experience the Crystal requires before it will authorize the transition. A practitioner can sit with Level to spare for years of in-world time and never pass a Threshold, because the Catalyst has not occurred. Level piled past the top of a soul’s rank group with no Catalyst to the next Stage builds Residual Strain, past Level 100 below Splintering, 200 below Transcendence, 300 below Dissonance, 400 below Principality and 500 below Revelation, and the pressure shows in the room and can fracture the Crystal. The Sixteen Stages names the Catalyst for each rung, and that list is the lived road: the accident survived, the bond held, the wound made load-bearing. It gives each one in three forms, under The Climb by Path, because the Crystal makes one demand at each floor and the demand arrives in the layer the soul leans on: a Body soul meets it in the flesh and in matter, a Spirit soul in a soul or a meaning, a Fate soul in a bond, an oath or the odds. Met on the lived road, it carries the soul through the four stages of the Great Work in its lead Path’s own terms, nigredo, albedo, citrinitas and rubedo: the lead layer broken down, purified, woken and fixed. A soul on two Paths meets its lead Path’s Catalyst and is asked for no second trial. A hitter who waits for a grief to do what only a load could will wait a long time, and the halls keep lists of them.
Seclusion is kept on the Path’s own ground. The long guarded sitting before a Threshold wants ground that feeds the layer being rebuilt. A Body soul secludes on Aetheric Density, where the air itself is thick with what the Shell packs. A Spirit soul secludes in Echo Depth, among what has been felt and meant in a place for a long time. A Fate soul secludes under Thread Weight, where a great deal has been sworn, owed or decided. The Three Grounds has all three, and a sect’s seclusion caves tell you which road the sect teaches before anyone opens a door.
The lived road is one way to turn the second key. A Draft or a blessing will also turn it. Stages can simply be bought, a purse can buy the Catalyst for any rung of the ladder, and the wealthy are stronger because they are wealthy. At Zenith a Hollow Throne must still recognize the buyer, so up there money buys the attempt and not the seat. The instructors who taught for two centuries that the second key could not be drunk were teaching a comfort, frequently on a house’s retainer, and every apothecary in the bracket towns was making a living off the difference.

A soul is assembled out of what happened to it and what it could afford, and the rich get to choose the order.

So the great houses hoard the top Drafts the way other people hoard grain before a siege, and they have fought more wars over a vault than they will ever admit to. The poor rise by three roads: dungeon luck, the crew that comes up with a core nobody expected and the nerve to keep it; guild patronage, a hall that stakes a promising hand against years of commissions; and blessings, from anything strong enough to give one and bored or fond enough to bother. A commoner holding a big monster core is the single most frightening sight in any lord’s county, and lords have burned villages on the rumor of one.
What a bought Stage buys, and what it does not
A bought Stage opens the door and no more. The Stage is real: the stat ceiling lifts, the combat cap rises with the rank, the Crystal takes the Stage’s look, the color brightens, and the coil (the brass assay instrument a practitioner stands inside) reads the Stage the same however it was crossed, though it reads the seat differently, as The Sixteen Stages sets out in its appendix. Everything past the door still has to be got the long way.

































A bought Stage givesA bought Stage does not giveThe Stage’s name and rank, on every instrumentA Release. It must be found and mastered by fighting, every one of themThe stat ceiling, and the combat cap of the rankA Domain. Anyone at Stage VIII can have one; somebody has to find theirsThe Crystal’s lookLevel. The Stage runs Overgrown until Level reaches its holdA real change in what the Crystal can holdTechniques and skills. Those rise by doing themThe Path gates. The Crystal goes on reading what the soul actually doesThe ceiling of every road’s MasteryThe rung. Mastery is read from Level, and an Overgrown Crystal reads low under any ceiling
A rich Stage IX may have no Release at all, while a poor Body fighter at the same Stage has all three her road allows, and the second one tends to win. Sects teach what money cannot buy: Releases, Domains, techniques, skills and the rites for their Wellspring, along with real fights, a crew and a name, which is why a duke’s son in a gold sash will still go on his knees at a mountain gate and scrub floors for an elder who is rude to him. What he is scrubbing for depends on his road, since a Release and a Domain are three different things on the three Paths, and Releases and Domains by Path sets them side by side.
II · The arc, in five movements
Summary only. The full treatment is in The Sixteen Stages. The Catalysts named here are the lived road.
Initiate to Adept · Stages I to IV, the first part of Inner Refinement. Murmuring, Welling, Ascension, Flourishing. Better than nine souls in ten will live and die inside these four Stages, and everything the world thinks it knows about magic it knows from watching people who never left it. The Crystal opens, spills, finds direction, and stabilizes into an identity.
The first crisis · Stage V. Splintering, and the Expert’s rank. The Crystal fractures after surviving contact with something more than two full steps above what its ceiling can hold, a beast two Grades past anything it could fight or a fighter two ranks up, and the fracture runs through the layer the soul leans on. A Body soul’s breaks run through the Shell and are carried in the flesh. A Spirit soul’s run through the Core, along emotional lines, which is the form the old books give for everyone because Spirit workers wrote the old books. A Fate soul’s run through the Layer, along its bonds and its luck. On every road the break follows whatever the soul was already carrying badly. Survival is the whole requirement, and defeating the thing adds nothing.
Consolidation · Stages VI to VII. Glory and Refraction. The fractures become features, the aura starts generating environmental effects, and then the soul turns and looks at itself from outside. Refraction is where a practitioner first reads their own fracture record as an object of study.
Outer Influence · the Master’s rank, Stages VIII to X. Transcendence, Invocation, Realization. The first true Domain (a region where the world runs on the practitioner’s terms) forms from a wound consciously made load-bearing. Then the practitioner stops working alone. Then the Continuum (the lawful fabric of reality) stops resisting and starts accommodating, and the direction of that accommodation never reverses back.
Grandmaster and Archmaster · Stages XI to XIV. Dissonance, Emanation, Principality, Zenith. The chosen approach to annihilation, what radiates from a soul that came back, formal registration of a law, and finally recognition by a Hollow Throne. Zenith is conferred, and no breakthrough reaches it: a purse may buy the attempt, and the Throne still decides, as The Sixteen Stages, Appendix B has it.
Paragon · Stages XV to XVI, beyond the canon. Revelation and Apex. Archon-participant territory and then a perpetual state with no ceiling beneath Apotheosis.
III · What climbs, layer by layer
The ladder is usually read as one number going up. It is three architectures changing at different rates, and they do not change together.
Harmonization runs across all three, and it is said once on The Three Paths: the lock happens at the Shell, where Aether enters, the tie is held on the Layer, and the lens shapes what the lead layer works: raw Aether in the Shell for a Body fighter, Essence in the Core for a Spirit one, the claim on the Layer for a Fate one.









































Rank and StagesEssence Core (inner layer: identity, memory, Traits)Aether Shell (outer layer: the skin that turns power into force)Attraction Layer (the Fate-Plane layer: bonds, Domains, Wellspring ties)Initiate to Adept · I–IVIdentity assembling. Traits present but volatile, with real risk of misfire and self-harm.Forming and porous. Output arrives before control does.First harmonization. First Spirit Axis at Flourishing.Expert · V–VIWhere the Core leads, fractured along emotional lines, then processing those fractures into features.Self-conducting. Signature becomes permanent. Where the Shell leads, the Splintering breaks run here, in the flesh.Aura begins generating environmental effect. Where the Layer leads, the breaks run here, along bonds and luck.Expert to Master · VII–VIIIVisible to itself. The fracture record becomes readable.Traits externalize and interface cleanly with Wellspring dialect.Domain seed, then first true Domain.Master to Grandmaster · IX–XIIDenser after Dissonance than clean advancement can produce.Traits reach field-state and stop needing maintenance.Domain to Realm to ambient consequence. Passive miracles leak.Archmaster · XIII–XIVThe Crystal self-writes.Trait and Domain Law fuse. The Trait stops being an ability.A law with standing independent of the practitioner.
The table is one soul read evenly, and nobody is. The layer a soul leans on, which is all a Path is, climbs ahead of the other two, and the assay slip shows it. A Body fighter’s Shell reaches each row’s column first: it packs and holds more Charge than her Core can yet make sense of, and her Body Mastery reads at the Stage’s ceiling while anything she has walked or studied on the Spirit road trails it. A Spirit worker’s Core is the column that arrives early, readable to itself a Stage before the Shell has learned to say anything clearly, which is why so many of them are clumsy with a door. A Fate soul’s Layer column climbs with Level like the others until it reaches the second rung, and there it stops for good unless the soul holds a grip, a Work or a blessing, so the third column of a Fate soul’s slip is the one that surprises the clerk. Everything else about a Fate soul climbs like anyone’s. Its Fate Path Stage rises with the soul’s Stage and opens the Fate gates on schedule, and its reserve is Essence, refined in the Core as a Spirit worker’s is, because Thread is never stored and is only pulled one working at a time. Its Core column therefore runs closer behind the Layer than a hitter would guess. A soul walking two Paths shows two columns ahead and one behind, and the gap is where a careful opponent aims.

The architectural note on Dissonance. Souls that pass through Stage XI rather than around it arrive at Emanation fractured and denser than the clean path produces. Overflow, Overchannel and Persistence reach their true ceiling in no other way. Those fractures count as structure. Anyone who tells an ambitious practitioner otherwise is either being kind or has an interest in them not trying.

IV · Essence Drafts
Aether + Essence + Vessel + Glyphica (the glyph-writing that shapes a working) = Reaction. A Draft is a working stabilized into a substance, and the substance came from somewhere.



































TypeSourcePotencyRiskCreature-SourcedMagical creatures, monster cores above allHighestIdentity ContaminationMaterial-SourcedHigh-density mineralsModerateClean but weakerEnvironmentalAffinity-saturated immersionLow per unit timeNear zeroSyntheticAlchemically blendedVariable and uniqueHighest. Internal reaction.
Where the material comes from. Every substance in the ledger carries a Resonance and a Wellspring, with the kind that names its home, alongside its Bearing and Holding grades. A dragon’s scale is no generic reagent: it carries a specific Wellspring resonance, it renders at a specific grade, and that grade begins falling from the moment the animal stops. The whole beast trade is an argument with decomposition, which is why the northern runners are the profitable ones and why some rendering houses are sited beside a glacier for no other reason.
Monster cores. A monster’s core is in a way its Soul Crystal, and it is worth more the stronger the monster was. This is the lawful Crystal Draw of The Standing Index, the Creature-Sourced stock the whole trade turns on. Monsters gain Levels by killing, each other included, so an old one has done a great deal of tempering of its own, and a crew that brings up the core of a famous beast with a bounty on it has often made more in an afternoon than its home village will see in a generation. An alchemist renders the core down, taking the Essence off it into Essence Drafts, and those go overwhelmingly to one use, which is tempering: a practitioner takes the course, goes to the melt, and comes out with each layer tempered in its own coin, the lead layer first, and a body that has gained by it, and Level on the slip to show for it. A tempering course is the one place a purse touches Level, and it pays for the privilege in Identity Contamination, dose by dose. The Traits fed this way are the ordinary ones in the ordinary Reflections, see The Trait System, and they firm as the soul does, at the Mastery of its lead road.
What stock does to whom. A course is matched three ways, and a good apothecary asks all three before she takes your money. The lens: stock from the Wellspring you temper on goes in clean, and foreign stock tempers just as well and adds carry (what a soul keeps of where its stock came from), so a Pyreveil fighter drinking wolf for a season is going to notice wolf. The layer: every monster’s stone is mostly Core, whatever the beast was, so every stone renders mostly to Core stock and feeds the Core. Tempering rebuilds each layer, so a course for the Shell is made from the Salt ash of the render, the part the bench reads as body, and a Body fighter drinks more of it and a Spirit fighter less. A Body monster’s stone parts heaviest in that ash, because the Charge the beast packed all its life set into the stone, and a renderer will pay over the odds for the core of anything that killed with its weight. The third layer: shaved Layer is the black-market Fate reagent. An ordinary stone has none of it. Only a Fate monster’s stone grows a thin skin of Layer, and no bench can tell that skin from what a dresser takes off a Crystal, the richest of which comes off a dead person’s. It firms a Layer’s claim in tempering and it is the base of the Fate breakthrough Draft and of the Fate Essence Draft, which is why nobody who owns one discusses its provenance. It refills nothing. A Fate worker’s reserve is Essence, and Core stock fills it like a Spirit worker’s.
The raw core. A core can be swallowed or broken raw, which skips the alchemist’s fee and delivers everything it holds at once. Most who try it die, and a good share of the rest come out wrong: a cooper who growls at his wife and cannot say why, a girl who has stopped sleeping and started hunting. The few who come out whole are the reason it goes on happening, and every one of them is a story told in a cheap tavern to somebody with nothing left to lose.
Identity Contamination is the risk that makes Creature-Sourced Drafts both the most potent and the most carefully counted stock in any hall’s cellar, since nothing else tempers as fast and nobody with a career to protect takes it without keeping tally of the doses. The Essence taken carries the identity it came from, and an Essence Core that absorbs enough of it stops being able to say cleanly which convictions are its own. The failure mode leaves the practitioner alive, with an Attunement (how the soul tunes itself to what it works) that has quietly stopped matching their Coherence (how closely its stated Path matches how it lives), and they are the last to notice.
The great crime. A Crystal can be cut from a dead practitioner and rendered, and it makes the strongest Draft of all, because no monster that ever lived tempered as deliberately as a person who spent a lifetime at it. It is the worst crime in every realm, the most profitable, and the reason Index Grade IV stock in circulation has never balanced against what the lawful sources can produce: some of those “monster cores” came out of people. Every realm hangs for it. Every realm has at least one great family whose fortunes improved abruptly after a war.
Master Work Drafts. A Master Work is a piece that does what its Grade and material should not be able to, made once at the end of a lifetime, always Unique or Mythic, and named. The trade’s own Master Works are Drafts, and the most coveted of them is a Fate Essence Draft, which bottles the manipulation of possibility itself: the very flow and idea of a thing, set in a vial. It is extremely hard to make, there are perhaps a handful in the world at any time, and people who could afford a county have instead spent their lives trying to get near one.
Fight Drafts. Everything above works on the ladder. The Drafts a fighter carries on the belt work on the reserve: a fight Draft takes a beat to get down, refills reserve, and leaves a crash that pays for it. It follows the road of whoever drinks it. A Spirit worker’s is Core stock: what pours in is Essence with nobody’s stamp on it, and the crash is the Crystal stamping it afterward, all at once. A Body fighter’s is a Salt: raw Aether in a fraction that packs straight into the Shell, which hits like a burn going down and leaves a crash of cramps and fever in place of the stamping. A Fate worker drinks Core stock, the same bottle a Spirit worker carries, since her pulls and her vows are paid from Essence, and there is no Fate fight Draft on any lawful shelf or any other: Thread cannot be bottled for the belt because it cannot be held. Drafts are graded by the Stage they serve and priced about threefold a Stage, and counterfeits are common enough that every bracket season buries a fighter who swallowed a mouthful of chalk at the worst moment of his life.
V · What a Draft does to advancement

A tempering Draft can supply Level and a seed, and a breakthrough Draft the Catalyst itself. A blessing can supply Level, a Catalyst or both.
What no vial has ever supplied is control over what comes out. Stats forced to stay above their sustainable figure by alchemical augmentation, bloodline exploitation or external metaphysical imposition generate Crystal Fracture Events at an exponentially increasing rate until the stat collapses or the Threshold is passed through crisis. That is the lasting forced stat. A boost for the length of a fight passes the Stage’s ceiling lawfully inside the two-step cap, read on the assayers’ scale from the sustainable figure on the card, and see Stacking and Spending for that.

So, in the matter of advancement, a Draft does four things, and the trade will sell you any of them with a straight face.
The everyday use. A course of Drafts fed into honest tempering, Salts for the Shell and Core stock for the Core in the measure the road wants. Each layer is tempered in its own coin, the lead layer first, the body gains, Level climbs, and the practitioner is ahead of the neighbor who could not pay, carrying a little more of a dead beast in the Core with every dose. This is what most Drafts are for, it is the backbone of every apothecary’s year, and most of the world means nothing else by the word.
The honest shortcut. A practitioner who has met their Catalyst early and stands Overgrown, the Stage open and the Level short of its hold, can be brought up to the hold on a licensed course. Legitimate, expensive, and it shortens the months of spilling.
The breakthrough Draft. A practitioner who has not met their Catalyst is handed one in liquid form, and the Crystal goes to the melt on schedule. It is poured by Path, because the Catalyst it stands in for is met in the lead layer. A Body breakthrough Draft is built on Salt, a Spirit one on Core stock, and a Fate one on the Layer reagent, which makes the Fate Draft the dearest of the three at every Stage and the most criminal, there being almost no lawful Layer to make it from. A Draft poured for the wrong road takes a soul to the melt and asks the wrong layer the question, and the bench word for what comes out is slag. The Stage is real, and if the buyer’s Level was short of it the Crystal comes out Overgrown. Whatever the Catalyst would have taught is simply absent, and so is every Release that fighting would have found along the way, which is the whole of the difference between Corvin Hathersage and the people who wanted him dead. The price climbs about threefold a Stage on the shelf and then leaves the shelf altogether, and at the top grades these Drafts are held in house vaults, given as dowries and used as hostages.
The dishonest use. A practitioner with no Catalyst and no money for the real article can be pushed above their sustainable figure anyway, on Ladder Dust and its cousins. The Crystal will hold the numbers for a while. Then it begins fracturing, and the fracture rate compounds, and it ends one of two ways: the stat collapses, or the Threshold is forced through crisis and the practitioner arrives at the next Stage having been reorganized around whatever was in the Crystal at that moment. Whatever is in the Crystal at the moment of reorganization is built into what comes out. Somebody who forced Splintering while afraid is a permanently different practitioner from somebody who met it having decided something.
Blessings. A blessing grants a power out of a person’s natural reach, and it can grant Level, a Catalyst or both. Blessed Level with no Catalyst behind it builds Residual Strain at the old gates like any other, a Stage blessed in above its Level runs Overgrown like any other, and a stat held up by a blessing is the giver’s load until the giver lets go. It appears on the sheet as its own line, and some people have lived for years under a line that read as a gift. Its own page has the givers, the terms and the way one comes off.
What this means for the world. The trade in advancement is enormous, and it is the shape of the world. A Stage on a token tells you what somebody’s Crystal can hold; it tells you nothing about whether they ever had to. Everybody who has spent their life in the halls learns to ask the follow-up question, usually with a practice sword.
VI · Why the moment of reorganization decides everything
The mechanism under the sentences above, stated in the vocabulary of the forge rather than the vocabulary of doctrine.
A Threshold is a melt. The Crystal is carried to the point where its lattice stops holding its shape, and it is allowed to cool into a new one, layer upon layer. A melt does not cool into order on its own. Something has to survive the heat for the new lattice to grow around, and in a Soul Crystal that something is Traits.
A Trait is a law the Continuum has already accepted as reliable, and a law does not stop being reliable at temperature. This is the only property in the Crystal with that behavior, and it is why Traits decide the quality of an advancement that strain merely made possible. Strain gets a soul to the melt. Nucleation decides what the melt produces.
The consequences follow without further argument.
A seeded melt cools dense, deliberate and clean. Clarity and Compression come out ahead of where they went in. This is the clean seat.
A contradicted melt cools around seeds that disagree with each other, and the lattice records the disagreement permanently. This is the rough seat, and it is why rough-seated practitioners are unpredictable rather than weak.
An unseeded melt cools amorphous. The Stage does not advance, Clarity and Compression fall, and the weakest Trait commonly dissolves without reforming. The halls call this a Dead Set, a seat that never took. Everyone else calls it slag. Recovery is slow, partial, and the practitioner is usually the last person in the hall to accept that it happened.

This is what a Draft is actually doing. A Draft supplies an artificial seed. It gives the cooling lattice a law to grow around that the soul did not survive into existence, which is why a Draft genuinely improves the quality of an advancement and why the improvement is not the practitioner’s own. In Creature-Sourced Drafts the borrowed law arrives with the identity it was rendered from, and that is Identity Contamination stated as a structural mechanism rather than a warning.
A Draft can supply Level, a seed and a Catalyst. A rich melt is therefore the cleanest melt money can arrange, and it is cooled around somebody else’s convictions.

VII · Tempering, and what a Draft actually touches
Tempering is the stat of becoming. A high-Tempering practitioner may hold no more power than the next person, and holds it in a cleaner, deeper, structurally sounder container.
The Sub-Stats a Draft plausibly reaches: Clarity (refinement of Essence already held) and Tempering Yield (volume produced per Stage, ambient Aether absorbed rather than passed through, and the gap between generation and availability). This is where a course of Essence Drafts does its daily work. A Salt reaches a third, Compression (how cleanly the Shell works the raw Charge it holds), which is the Body fighter’s half of the same daily work, and Core stock does not touch it.
The Sub-Stats no Draft has ever reached: Coherence, the alignment between a practitioner’s stated Path and their lived behavior, which on the lived road is the structural prerequisite for Threshold eligibility, and Maturity, the degree to which prior trauma has been genuinely integrated, which is the primary Sub-Stat the Crystal consults when evaluating readiness.

Coherence is the Crystal’s internal honest scale, and it cannot be drunk. A breakthrough Draft carries a soul over the Threshold without consulting that scale, and the soul arrives on the far side reading exactly what it read before. That is the mechanical reason a bought Stage opens the door and no more, stated in the vocabulary of the stat framework rather than in the vocabulary of doctrine.

Read next: The Sixteen Stages, under The Climb by Path, for the three forms of every Catalyst and crossing; Grades, Ranks and the Aether Shell, for the numbers all of this moves; Releases and Domains by Path, for what fighting finds on each road; The Three Paths and Classes and Mastery, for what a purse cannot move; and The Sixty Wellsprings, for what the stock is stock of.

New to the climb? The plain account of it, Stage, Level and the hands, is How Power Grows. This page is every Stage in full.

What Temperance (the climb of a soul from Stage to Stage) Does to a Soul, Stage by Stage, Told Plainly

Compiled for the fighting halls of the Guild Accord by the Archives, following the Prime Instructors’ complaint that the account of the Stages in the Codex (the Accord’s master register of laws and figures) runs to eleven lines and has never once been sufficient to teach from.

It began with a pie. On the second day of the harvest fair at Pollard’s Cross, a twelve-year-old apprentice of the Copper Heron school, Stage II and in love with the pie-seller’s daughter, wanted a mutton pie hot and got it hot, and the pie went off like a dropped coal across the blue sash of a Stage III journeyman of the Tannery Hounds. The journeyman answered with the first technique he had ever built by himself. His sister, Stage IV, came through the awning. By noon a Stage VI instructor of the Herons had arrived, with the small flames on every stall leaning toward him as he crossed the square, and the crowd, which had been eating, went on eating and began to take bets. By mid-afternoon a Hounds elder at Stage VIII had opened a Domain the size of the horse market, the horses inside it were picking their way very carefully across a floor that had agreed to be somewhere else, and a man was charging a copper a head to stand on his wagon. The walls went, then Cooper Street, then the bend of the river.
At sundown a woman named Aldith Fenn, Stage X, who had been fishing four miles upstream, walked down in her hip boots, wet to the waist, and asked them to stop. They stopped. Three hundred and six people were dead, the pie-seller among them, and the ground at Pollard’s Cross has not frozen in the two centuries since.
Every child in the four quarters can skip rope to the names:

Murmur, Well, and up you Rise,
Bloom and Splinter, Glory, Eyes,
Cross the water, Call, and Stay,
Crack, and Shine, and Rule the Day,
Top of the world and one more after,
And one more yet, and skip it faster.

Those are the Sixteen, in order, and the Archives can find no fault with the rhyme. Every rung of it is famous, and every rung of it has a body count the children know by heart.
How This Is Written

“Temperance is a confession of how much you have survived, and nobody has ever confessed for free.”

The Codex records each Stage with exacting precision: its rank (the word everyone says for it, and the title a fighting guild’s token carries; in a merchant’s or a smith’s guild the same nine words grade trust in that trade, and a Grandmaster merchant may not be able to throw a punch), its stat ceiling, the Level that holds it, the ceiling it sets on Mastery, and the Catalyst Condition (the life event a soul passes through to cross, or the Draft or blessing that stands in for it) the Crystal (the Soul Crystal, which is the soul itself, melted down and rebuilt layer by layer at each crossing) requires before it will authorize the transition. Those figures are correct, they are reproduced here without alteration, and they have never taught anybody anything.
What follows sits underneath them. Each Stage is given in the same order. The ledger line is the Codex’s own figure, with the Crystal’s look set beside it. Under it stands the Catalyst, first as the Codex has it, which is the one demand the Crystal makes of every soul at that floor, and then in its three forms, because a hitter, a thrower and a puller are asked the same question and no two of them are asked it in the same place. The one they tell comes next, because no minstrel was ever paid for a ledger line and nobody ever feared a Stage they had only read about. Then what the Stage is from inside the person it is happening to, with a line for each road; what it is on each Path, since a hitter, a thrower and a puller standing on one rung are holding three different things; what it looks like, to the household or the hall or the field; what it costs to spend at that height; what the common people call it, which the Archives has three times recommended cutting and which predicts better than half the Index; then the crossing, lived, which is how the moment of passing shows on each road to the people standing nearby; and last bought versus lived, a line or two on what the purse leaves out. The whole climb is written by Path, since the Archives were told, correctly, that an account of one generic soul going up a stair describes nobody who ever went up it. The persons in the stories are mostly long dead and the stories have been improved; the Archives vouches for the corpses.

Two facts govern everything below and neither is negotiable.
The first is that a Threshold (the crossing from one Stage to the next) opens when its Catalyst Condition is met and the soul’s Level can hold the Stage. Every Catalyst named below is the lived road. A Draft or a blessing will stand in for any of them, and the Level is still owed: a Stage reached before its Level is held Overgrown until Level catches up.
The second is that a Threshold is a structural reorganization, and whatever is in the Crystal at the moment of reorganization is built into what comes out.
A soul is therefore assembled out of what happened to it and what it could afford, the rich get to choose the order, and every hall’s certification is an instrument for reading the result.
The Level on each ledger line below is the Level that holds that Stage. Level runs on above it, and runs freely inside a rank, until it passes the top of the soul’s rank group with no Catalyst to the next Stage: past 100 below Splintering, 200 below Transcendence, 300 below Dissonance, 400 below Principality and 500 below Revelation, it builds Residual Strain. Level itself moves by any real work, danger overcome above all, whichever road the Stage came by.

The Climb by Path

“Same stair, same step, and three different things waiting on it.”

A Stage belongs to the soul, and every soul climbs the same sixteen over the same floors. What the Crystal asks at each floor is one thing, and the Codex’s Catalyst line states it. Where it asks is another matter. A crossing melts the Crystal down and rebuilds it layer by layer, the layer a soul leans on is rebuilt first and hardest, and so the demand arrives in that layer’s terms.

A Body soul meets it in the flesh and in matter: a load survived that should have killed, a material understood to the grain, a body broken and rebuilt.
A Spirit soul meets it in a soul or a meaning: a grief borne, a truth faced, a self that can no longer be held as it was.
A Fate soul meets it in a bond, an oath or the odds: a vow kept at ruinous cost, a chance refused, a debt paid in full.

Each Stage below gives the shared demand and then the three trials. Five things hold for all sixteen.
The hold is shared. The Level that holds a Stage, its stat ceiling, its Mastery ceiling and the gates where Strain begins are the same on every road. Only the trial differs, and the Crystal counts the trial that lands in the layer it leans on. The halls keep long lists of hitters who waited years for a grief to do what only a load could.
Two roads, one trial. A soul walking two Paths meets the Catalyst of its lead Path, the one that holds the larger share of its practice. The second road is asked for no trial of its own. It follows, and its gates open a Stage late until it is mastered (a third road’s open two Stages late), as The Three Paths sets out.
Fate climbs like anyone. A Fate soul crosses the same floors by Catalysts made of bonds, oaths and odds, and not one of them is a pull. A vow kept spends the soul’s own share, draws no thread and leaves no knot. Its Mastery reads from Level like anyone’s, and stops at II without a grip on the thread: a Work or a blessing lifts it to the Stage’s ceiling, and nothing on this page does.
The crossing shows by road. A lived breakthrough lights the valley, and the road decides what kind of light. Every lived crossing passes the four stages of the Great Work in its own road’s terms, nigredo, albedo, citrinitas and rubedo: the lead layer broken down, purified, woken and fixed, in the flesh for a Body soul, in a soul or a meaning for a Spirit one, and in a bond, an oath or the odds for Fate. Body’s comes out through matter: heat, the ground answering, the body remade in front of people. Spirit’s comes out through souls and meaning: a room gone quiet, colors and memories shifting in everyone near. Fate’s comes out through the odds and the world settling: luck turning across the valley, oaths felt to tighten, things that were going to happen not happening. It scales with the Stage, from a kitchen at Murmuring to a kingdom at Principality. A bought breakthrough is a Draft in a quiet room on every road, and the three quiet rooms look exactly alike.
Seclusion is taken on the road’s own ground. A soul that goes into a guarded seclusion to meet its Catalyst goes where its road draws cheapest: a Body soul onto rich Aetheric ground, a Well or a deep mine; a Spirit soul down into Echo Depth, an old temple or a graveyard thick with the remembered; a Fate soul onto Thread Weight, a battlefield or a crossroads where great things were decided. The wrong ground does not stop a crossing. It makes the months longer and the slag worse, and the halls that rent out seclusion cells price them by road. See The Three Grounds.
The Bought Stage
A breakthrough Draft or a blessing delivers the Catalyst, the Crystal goes to the melt, and the soul comes out on the next rung with the stat ceiling, the rank, the Crystal’s look and the color to prove it. A house child may be four Stages up before the first real fight. The trade and its law are on The Ladder and the Draft, and every lord in the four quarters lies awake over the dungeon luck on the other side of it.
What a bought Stage lacks is exact, and the halls can list it from across a yard:

Every Release. The Path decides the count: a Body soul may find a First from IV, a Second from VII and a Third from IX, a Spirit soul a First and a Second, and a Fate soul the One at VII. Each must be found and mastered by fighting, and none is sold. A rich Stage IX may have none, while a poor Body fighter at the same Stage has all three.
The Domain. Anyone at Stage VIII can have one. Somebody still has to find theirs.
The Level. A Stage reached above its Level is held Overgrown until Level reaches the hold: power spills, lamps lean toward its owner, and no Release will come. A thin Level at a high Stage is the commonest cause of death among heirs.
The rung. A Stage sets how high Mastery may go, and the Level places the soul under it. A bought Stage opens the ceiling and leaves the Level where it was, which is how a rich Stage XII can stand under a roof marked Radiant, Overgrown, and read three rungs short of it, or nothing at all.
The Path gates. The Crystal goes on reading what the soul actually does.
Techniques and skills. Those rise by doing them.
Whatever the Catalyst would have done. A bought Flourishing has no Spirit Axis under it. A bought Glory never made the decision. A bought Transcendence carries the wound exactly as it was, now at a Master’s weight.
The valley. A lived breakthrough lights the valley, and people for miles can name the night. A bought one is a Draft in a quiet room.

Sects teach what money cannot buy: Releases, Domains, techniques, skills and the rites for their Wellspring, with real fights, a crew and a name thrown in, and they know precisely what they are selling when a duke’s daughter turns up at the gate at Stage VII asking to be hit.

The rank is what everyone says. Nobody outside a hall names a Stage in ordinary talk: a fighter is a Journeyman or a Master, and the Stage name is the precise term for when precision is wanted. In a merchant’s or a smith’s guild the same nine words are titles that grade trust in that trade, earned by the work, so a Grandmaster merchant may not be able to throw a punch.
The hold. A Stage opens when its Catalyst is met and the soul’s Level can hold it, and the Stages of one rank hold close to its floor. A Stage held under its Level is Overgrown. Level piled past the top of a rank group with no Catalyst to the next Stage builds Residual Strain: past Level 100 below Splintering, 200 below Transcendence, 300 below Dissonance, 400 below Principality and 500 below Revelation.
The Crystal’s look is what the Crystal as a whole has grown into, named in the jewelers’ words for a stone: a Seed before waking, then Clouded, Faceted, Fire, Flawless, Starred and Absolute. It follows the Stage, and nobody climbs it. Books older than the present Bench call the same looks Dormant, Awakened, Harmonic, Resonant, Radiant, Sovereign and Crystallized Soul. The Measurewrights renamed them because three of those words were also rungs on the Shell’s old ladder, and an assay slip that says Resonant twice and means two different things is a lawsuit. The jewelers also once kept a Clear look between Faceted and Fire, and an old slip that calls a Refraction Crystal Clear means Faceted.
The Mastery ceiling is the highest rung a soul’s Mastery may reach on any road at that Stage, copied from the one table on Classes and Mastery, which governs. A ceiling is a roof. The Level places a soul under it: rung I from Glory’s hold at Level 115, II from 150, III from 215, IV from 260 and V from 340. The roof rises a rung at a time up the whole climb, and a soul fresh across a Stage reads a rung under its new roof until its Level grows into the Stage, so most people at any Stage are standing a rung or two under theirs. Any rung can be held Inverted, a mark and never a rung of its own.
The early grip. Below Glory Mastery is not read, with one exception: a soul of one of the Epochs’ lines who holds the line’s instrument, a Moto with a Work of Hataraki, a Zettari with Matla, a Yukari with Null-Light, reads rung I on that instrument’s road from Ascension, and only rung I until Glory.
Fate’s grip. A Fate soul’s Mastery reads from Level like anyone’s and stops at II without a grip on the thread, a Work or a blessing; a grip lifts it to the Stage’s ceiling and never past it. A Fate fighter’s everyday weapons, Range, Aura Pressure, presence and bonds, need no rung at all, and those do grow with the Stage.
The old reckoning. The Codex’s ledger once gave each Stage a Tier of Standing, the nine ranks numbered one to nine, and a Grade ceiling, the highest letter its stats might reach, and gathered the Stages into five Bands (Mortal Foundation, Awakened, Sovereign, Mythic and Absolute). The ranks keep their words and lose their numbers, the Grade ceiling survives only as the assayers’ hidden scale under the stat ceiling, and the Bands survive as the Levels where Strain begins.
The Catalysts at a Glance
One demand to a Stage, and three places it is met. The full trials stand under each Stage’s ledger line below.

Inner Refinement: Initiate to Adept
Stages I through IV, the Clouded years. Better than nine souls in ten will live and die inside these four Stages. Everything the world thinks it knows about magic, it knows from watching people who never left it, and there are a great many of them to watch: every market has its hedge-worker and every town its sect, with its outer and inner disciples, the core disciple nobody can stand, and an elder who will tell you about it.
What changes in these Stages. The Crystal goes from Seed to Clouded at the waking and stays Clouded for all four Stages. Mastery is not read here, save the early grip of an Epoch’s child from Ascension, no Class is offered, and the share of a spend that arrives is the Stage’s own figure, climbing from about three parts in ten at Murmuring to not quite half at Flourishing. On the Body road matter answers to blows and the coat and to nothing else. On the Spirit road a line can be thrown at a soul and little more. On the Fate road there is Pressure, presence and the first bond. The Path becomes legible at Ascension, and a Body or Spirit soul’s First Release can be found at Flourishing. Auras in this Band are clouded and smoky and cling to the hands.
I · Murmuring
Initiate · Stat ceiling 50 · Holds from Level 1 · Mastery unread · Clouded Crystal
Catalyst · none is asked. The Crystal has opened, in its own season or under a Waking Draft
No trial is set and no Path is read, so what follows are occasions and not Catalysts: the kind of day on which each layer tends to open first.

Body. A Shell that is going to lead tends to open on something that happened to the body: a fever broken, a fall onto river ice, the first day of real work with a flail.
Spirit. A Core that is going to lead tends to open on a feeling too large for the child holding it: a temper at a naming feast, a first funeral, a fright in the dark.
Fate. A Layer that is going to lead tends to open on a near thing: the cart that missed, the promise a small child made in earnest and kept. It opens the Crystal and nothing more. No thread is touched.

The one they tell · The dogs of Thorn Mill went quiet on a market day, all twelve of them, in the middle of a fight over a pig’s ear. By the week’s end the whole parish was laying coin on which child it was, and the smart money was on the miller’s boy, Little Jem Sorrel, seven years old, who lost his temper at his sister’s naming feast and sent every cup on a forty-foot table into a shiver, until the ale crept over the rims and the priest stopped with his mouth open. That was all it did. His mother sat up with him for a year afterward, and three generations of instructors have quoted what she told the parish: a house with a Murmuring child in it is a house that has begun keeping a wolf, and the wolf is very small.
From inside · A hum under the sternum that answers mood and answers nothing else. Wake angry and the water in the cup by the bed is trembling before you have understood why you are angry. Want something badly and feel a pressure behind the eyes that goes nowhere and does nothing and does not stop. There is no direction in it. There is no volume to adjust. It is weather happening inside a body that has not been told there is now weather.
Children in Murmuring feel no fear of it, which adults consistently fail to predict, and a good deal of irritation. It is a noise, and they were already living in a body full of noises.
What opening does not do is hand the child anything new. Traits (standing laws a soul has survived into being) sit in the material of a soul from the beginning and run in people whose Crystal never opens at all. Murmuring arms what was already there. The quiet child who never took a fever had the Trait at four; at eleven the Crystal simply gives it a conductor and a bill.
From inside each road, so far as a lean can be called a road:

Body. The hum sits in the hands and the teeth, and the child is always a little too warm.
Spirit. The hum is other people. The mood of a room reaches the child before the room does.
Fate. There is hardly a hum at all, only a sense, now and then, that something has just been decided.

On each Path · No Path is read at Murmuring. The Crystal recognizes a road by years of use, and a Murmuring child has used nothing. What shows is a lean, the same grain the unwoken carry. Mastery is unread on every road, and what gets out of the child does so at the Stage’s own figure, about three parts in ten.

Body. The seal on the Shell has broken and the first Charge sits in it, a cupful of raw Aether (mana, in plain words) that nobody packed on purpose. Matter does nothing at the child’s word. It shivers: cups, water, a loose shutter. A lean toward this road shows as a child who is warm to hold and hard to knock over.
Spirit. The Core was the first layer to wake, and it refines a trickle of Essence (spiritual energy) without being asked. Souls do nothing for the child either, though they notice: the dogs, a grandmother, a baby that stops crying. A lean here shows as a child who knows who is in the next room.
Fate. Nothing, for nearly everyone. Even a Moto child who will one day hold a Work reads nothing yet: the blood opens its one ladder early, at Ascension, and no amount of Murmuring hurries it.

What it looks like · Almost nothing, and the almost is what matters. A quality of stillness in a room that people notice and do not name. Animals get it first. Dogs go quiet around a Murmuring child a full season before the parents work out what is happening, and every farmer in the four quarters knows to watch the dogs and not one of them would call it a diagnostic.
To a trained eye the aura is near-black with the hue already in it, a dark smear that is gone before it travels a handspan, and far too thin to sit differently on one road or another. The Crystal has gone from Seed to Clouded, the lapidary’s word for a stone you cannot yet see into: the smallest change of color on the whole ladder and the largest change of kind. The body is a child’s body. The Body-leaning ones run a little warm, the Spirit-leaning ones go very still when watched, and around the rare gripped child dropped things tend to land the right way up.
What it costs · Very little, because there is very little to spend. A Murmuring reserve is emptied by one bad temper, and the bill is a child’s bill: a flush, a sweat and a night’s fever where the lean is to the Body, and a flat gray afternoon with a word that will not come where it is to the Spirit. Nobody at this Stage pulls a thread, so nobody owes a knot. The three exhaustions set out on The Three Paths (Body runs hot and cracks, Spirit runs hollow, Fate runs unlucky) are here in miniature, and every mother of a Murmuring child has nursed one of the first two without knowing its name.
What the folk call it · Carrying a bee. A boy with a bee in him. The remedy is iron in the bed, on the reasoning that the iron takes the hum away from the child, and the reasoning is wrong in every particular and correct in its outcome, because iron does conduct and an ungoverned Crystal does shed into the nearest better conductor. A Murmuring child sleeps better with a horseshoe under the mattress. The Accord sells the guild-milled version of this as Sour Iron Filings, at a markup, to the people who invented it.
The crossing, lived · Nothing lights at Murmuring. The scale is a kitchen, and the signs are the ones the dogs already gave.

Body. The room warms by a degree, the cups shiver on the shelf, and the cat leaves the hearth.
Spirit. The house goes quiet all at once. The baby stops crying, and two people at the table find they were thinking of the same dead aunt.
Fate. For a day everything dropped in that house lands the right way up, and nobody remarks on it until later.

Bought versus lived · A Crystal that opens by itself does so in its own season, and the dogs give a season’s warning. A Waking Draft opens it on the day the family chooses, costs more than the house, and often kills or warps the child who drinks it. The ones it spares have the hum and none of the weather that would have taught them what it answers to.
II · Welling
Apprentice · Stat ceiling 100 · Holds from Level 5 · Mastery unread · Clouded Crystal
Catalyst · first genuine contact with a Wellspring’s raw Aether under personal pressure (a Wellspring being one of the Sixty, the governing idea that changes how a soul uses its power, pooling at sites common speech calls Cores, most of them at the heart of a dungeon): touched and survived, where watching and instruction count for nothing
The touch is the same for everyone, since every road draws Aether. The pressure is what differs.

Body. The pressure is on the flesh. The child is in the Core’s heat, cold or water past what a body that size should stand, and the raw Aether comes in through the skin and stays in the Shell because there was nowhere else for it to go. Most carry the scar.
Spirit. The pressure is on the self. The child touches the Wellspring while holding something too heavy to hold, a death in the house, a shame, a terror, and the Core takes the Aether in and stamps it with that. They carry no scar, and they can tell you the hour.
Fate. The pressure is a stake. Something rides on the touch: a dare taken at bad odds, a promise to go down to the Core and come back, a brother’s life. The Aether is touched as anyone’s is, and what the Layer keeps is that the odds were met. Nothing is pulled.

The one they tell · Annis Cobb of Thatcher’s Row wanted the bread oven hotter. She was eleven, it was the coldest morning of that winter, and the week before, down at the old Core in Cobble Fen, she had touched something she had told nobody about. The oven went, then the bakehouse, then nineteen roofs in a long sheet of orange that brought the whole valley out to look. Four people died in it, among them the baker, the kindest man on the Row. By the next market a sect recruiter in a green coat had paid her parents forty silver marks and driven her off in a cart, and the town was selling views of the scorch at a copper a head before she was out of sight.
From inside · It spills. Direction arrives before volume does, so the child now knows what they are reaching for and has no capacity whatever to reach for a measured amount of it. They want the cup and the cup goes over. They want the fire hotter and the linen scorches. The Shell (the Aether Shell, the soul’s outer layer that turns power into force) is forming and it is porous, and living inside a porous Shell at eleven years old is the experience of being blamed daily for things that are entirely your doing and entirely not your fault.
The Catalyst is worth sitting with. Instruction will not do it and neither will watching: a Wellspring’s Aether has to be touched, under pressure, and survived. Which means the lived gate into Welling is an accident that went badly and did not go worst. Most practitioners in the four quarters can name the day. A good number of them have a scar from it. A house child takes the same touch off a silver spoon, in a warm room with a physician standing by, and arrives at Stage II with no scar and no story, which the other children in the yard will shortly correct.
From inside each road:

Body. It spills as heat and force out of the hands, and the palms are never quite healed.
Spirit. It spills as feeling, and the child learns that the quarrel downstairs is somehow their doing.
Fate. It spills as wanting. The child wishes for a thing a little too hard and people give way without being asked, by Pressure and never by thread, and resent it afterward.

On each Path · Mastery is still unread on every road, with about a third of each spend arriving. The lean hardens here, because spilling has a direction.

Body. The Shell is forming and porous, and the Charge in it slops. Matter now does one thing for them, badly: it takes heat, force or motion from their hands in an amount they did not choose. The oven goes. A Body-leaning child has blows and the coat (the thin skin of their own aura over the body) and no more, and neither holds for long.
Spirit. The Core refines more than it can keep, and what spills is Essence, stamped and unaimed. It lands on souls. Around a Spirit-leaning child it is the household that sours, with every temper in it a little shorter and the baby awake all night. Nothing can yet be thrown on purpose.
Fate. Nothing yet, for most. The first Fate gate stands here all the same: Attunement will not pass the D band of the scale unless the Fate Path has been shown by this Stage, so a child who is going to walk that road has usually begun keeping small promises with unusual seriousness.

What it looks like · This is the year the household finds out. Broken crockery, soured milk, a scorch on a table nobody set a pot down on. Welling is when families discover what they have and decide what to do about it, and it is the year most children are sent away, and it is the year most accidents happen, in that order and for that reason.
The aura is dark char with the hue stirring under it like dye in dirty water, and for the first time it shows outside the body, clinging to the hands during a long working. On a Body-leaning child it sits on the skin like heat over a road and stays a moment on whatever they have put down. On a Spirit-leaning child it stands a finger’s width off the hands, and a careful eye will see the shadow of those hands fall slightly wrong. The Crystal is Clouded still.
What it costs · The spill is the cost. A Welling child spends without meaning to and so runs dry daily: scalded palms, a hot dry skin and cramps in the calves by evening on the Body side, and on the Spirit side a cold in the chest, a dull week and a playmate’s name gone until morning. A reserve this small refills overnight on decent ground, and most of the damage is to the crockery.
What the folk call it · The spilling year. The remedy is water. The child carries full buckets, all day, up the hill and back down, and is beaten for what they slop over the rim. It looks like cruelty and half the time it is cruelty and it is also, on the instrument, the correct training, because measuring out with the body teaches the Shell to measure out and no better method has ever been found. Every Prime Instructor in the Accord has quietly kept the practice. The published curriculum calls it graduated load discipline and does not mention the hill.

Trade note · The guild ration begins here, with Metering Tonic, which halves the spillage and produces a practitioner who measures out worse afterward than one who was never given it. The finding is fourteen years old. The ration has not changed.

The crossing, lived · The scale is a lane, and it is over in a breath.

Body. A flash of heat off the child and a ring of ground the size of a cart left scorched, frosted or soaked, in the Wellspring’s own manner, with steam standing where there was no water.
Spirit. Everyone in the lane feels one child’s fright in their own chest for the space of a breath, and the colors of the washing on the lines look wrong until evening.
Fate. A day of small strange luck along the lane: a lost ring found, every hen laying, the dice at the alehouse coming up alike. Nothing was pulled. The soul’s own share has grown, and the lane is feeling it settle.

Bought versus lived · The silver spoon delivers the touch and none of the pressure. A bought Welling has the direction and has never once been afraid of it, and the hill and the buckets are still owed.
III · Ascension
Journeyman · Stat ceiling 175 · Holds from Level 15 · Mastery unread, the early grip reading I · Clouded Crystal
Catalyst · first technique developed independently from instruction, built from the practitioner’s own understanding of their Essence (the soul’s own stuff of power) rather than received doctrine
The Codex says Essence, and means whatever the lead layer works. The thing built is the practitioner’s own on every road, and what it is built out of differs.

Body. Built from the Charge and one material known to the grain: a rope, a pestle, the hinge of the builder’s own shoulder. The understanding is of what that one thing does under load, learned by the hands, and the technique is that understanding driven out through the Shell.
Spirit. Built from one truth about a soul, worked out alone and usually unwelcome: why the big boy flinches, what the builder is in fact afraid of. The technique is that truth sent down a line.
Fate. Built from a bond, a promise or a reading of the odds: the stare that makes a bigger boy step back, the word that holds because it has never yet been broken. It is made of Range, Pressure and presence. It pulls nothing.

The one they tell · The first thing anybody builds is usually small, and Kim Dal-rae’s looked the smallest in the Mahuo country. She was fifteen, she pounded rice for a living, and what she worked out by herself over one bad winter was that a thing she threw would go straight back to wherever it had last been at rest. She called it Jeolgu Gwihwan (절구귀환), the Return to the Mortar, and the meaning got around fast on the day the tax-farmer’s man walked out of her yard with a sack he had taken off her aunt, because the pestle she threw at him went home through the sack and through the man and through the gatepost, in that order. She did it again to check. Then she sat down, and then she ran, and the ninety-mark bounty three counties posted on her ran for forty years. She outlived it.
From inside · The first thing you made yourself, working.
Everything until this moment was received. Somebody showed you and you copied it and it held, and you were proud of it, and it was never yours. Then one day you build a thing out of your own understanding of what your Essence actually does, and it holds, and the whole of Stage III is the difference between those two experiences. There is nothing else in it.
Some people weep. Most do not. The recorded pattern across four centuries of instructor notes is that the practitioner does the thing, and then does it again to check, and then sits down. Drink past this rung and you still owe it, and you will build your first real technique later on, at a higher Stage, in front of people who have stopped being polite.
From inside each road:

Body. The thing built lives in the hands, and the body knows it worked before the mind does.
Spirit. The thing built is something understood, and it cannot afterward be un-understood.
Fate. The thing built is something other people now believe about you, and you feel it hold when you lean on it.

On each Path · The Path becomes legible here, and the first gates close behind it: Fortitude will not pass the C band of the scale unless the Body Path has been shown by this Stage, nor Alacrity without the Spirit. Mastery stays unread, and four parts in ten arrive, with one exception: an Epoch’s child who holds the line’s instrument reads rung I on its road from this Stage, the early grip, and the assay houses open a separate book for them. The Codex says Essence in its Catalyst line, and for a hitter the understanding in question is of the Charge.

Body. The first technique is nearly always a blow: Charge shaped in the Shell by whatever lens the soul has touched, and driven out through a hand, a foot or a pestle. The Body Path’s bonus to Strike Force, Durability and Lifting Strength begins, at about five parts in a hundred. Matter still obeys nothing but impact. Blows and the coat.
Spirit. The first technique is a line: Essence sent out through the Core that holds together across a few paces and lands on a soul. It knocks a man’s nerve out of true or lays a moment’s dread on him, and leaves his coat unmarked. It moves no pestle. The Shell is the only door into matter, and theirs is a Stage III Shell like anybody’s.
Fate. A Fate Path Journeyman has no pull and needs none. Their first technique is made of Range, Aura Pressure, presence or a bond: the stare that makes a bigger boy step back, the promise that holds. A Moto child with a Work reads Fate I from this Stage, Touched, and knows the strap is about to go. Everyone else on the road reads nothing yet.

What it looks like · The person becomes legible. Before Ascension you could say a child had something. After it, you can say what they are, and the recruiters can price them, and the family can plan, and the Path (the route, body, spirit or fate, the Crystal habitually works through) is visible to anyone who knows how to look. This is the point at which a life stops being a question and becomes a known quantity, and there are people who never forgive it.
The aura is smoke now, tinted plainly with the lens’s color, a brown smoke over a fire school and a blue one over a storm hall, and it is the first thing about them a stranger can use. A Body Journeyman’s smoke hugs the forearms and trails off the weapon. A Spirit Journeyman’s hangs half a step off the body. A Fate Journeyman’s can hardly be seen, and the dust on the practice floor lies oddly flat around their feet. The Crystal is Clouded, with the stamp of its owner showing in it for the first time.
What it costs · This is the first Stage with a reserve worth emptying, and so the first at which the roads tire differently enough to read. At half a hitter is flushed and the haze thickens on the skin, at a quarter the calves cramp, and at a tenth a Journeyman’s Shell splits the knuckles and little else. A thrower at half has gone a shade gray, at a quarter says the wrong word, and at a tenth forgets the name of the drill. A Fate Journeyman run dry has spent nothing but their own share, owes no knot, and has a bad week of small luck. Good instructors take all three to a tenth on purpose, once, so that they will know it when it comes.
What the folk call it · Coming into the road. The first true year. A family that can afford it holds a feast, because the child’s future has just arrived and can be celebrated. A family that cannot afford it does not hold one, and the child notices, and a surprising number of Accord operatives have that particular non-event somewhere in their fracture record. The Archives has never studied this. Three Prime Instructors have asked it to.
The crossing, lived · The scale is a practice yard, and the instructors can tell the road from the far wall.

Body. The Charge sets in the Shell with a wash of heat across the yard, the packed earth takes the print of their feet and keeps it, and they stand up visibly thicker through the shoulders than they sat down.
Spirit. The yard falls silent in the middle of a sentence, and everyone watching remembers, sharply and for no reason, the first thing they themselves were ever proud of.
Fate. The dust on the yard lies flat, a quarrel that had been brewing all week between two other students goes out of both of them, and a rope that was about to part holds another year.

Bought versus lived · A purse can supply the Catalyst and cannot supply the technique. A bought Ascension has the rank and the smoke and has never built anything, and that debt is collected later, at a higher Stage, in front of people.
IV · Flourishing
Adept · Stat ceiling 275 · Holds from Level 30 · Mastery unread, the early grip reading I · Clouded Crystal
Catalyst · formation of the first genuine Spirit Axis, a bond with another soul that carries mechanical weight in the Harmonics (the stats for pulling in power and holding it in tune)
An Axis is an Axis on every road, and the Harmonics weigh it the same. How two souls come to hold each other’s load is the road’s own business.

Body. The bond is made by bearing load together: a shield wall of two, a man carried out on the back, a wound taken that was meant for the other. The Shell learns the other’s weight and the Axis forms around it. Hob Tarrant and Mags Plowright, below, are the standing case.
Spirit. The bond is made by being known. One soul lets another see what it is, the grief and the shame included, and is not put down for it, or sits with another’s grief until part of it is their own. The Core takes the second weight directly.
Fate. The bond is made by a word given: an oath sworn to one person, in Witness Wax or without it, and kept the first time keeping it costs something real. This is the road’s home ground, and the Layer needs no telling what a bond is. It is a vow, so it spends the soul’s own share, pulls no thread and leaves no knot.

The one they tell · Hob Tarrant and Mags Plowright were witnessed to each other in Witness Wax at Stoneybridge, a drover and a camp cook, and the pair of them held the Ford of Ell against a sixty-man raid with a goad, a cleaver and a great deal of swearing, their two charcoal auras, his with a rumor of rust in it and hers of amber, running together into a single roaring hoop that the minstrels got almost right. Then a fever took her, the plain kind. Hob lived eighteen more years at full power, and for all of them a bright thread of rust leaned off his left shoulder, always north, always toward one hill in the Stoneybridge burying ground, and everybody on the drove roads knew it. Reavers learned to come at him from the south. One day in his sixties they did.
From inside · The noise stops.
Identity settles. The resonance signature that will be recognizably yours for the rest of your life finishes arriving. Techniques that were separate tricks cohere into something with a style to it, and for most practitioners this is the most physically pleasant experience of their lives, a warmth low in the chest that does not go away for weeks and that nobody who has had it describes well.
And on the lived road it cannot be reached alone.

The Catalyst is a Spirit Axis. Which means every Flourished practitioner in the four quarters who walked here, every hall-raised Adept, every guild officer, every Baron’s champion and every hedge-mage who ever stabilized without a vial, arrived because somebody mattered to them enough to hold load. The Stage that stabilizes the self is gated on attaching the self to another person, permanently, in a way that registers on an instrument. A Stage IV who drank the Catalyst has the warmth in the chest and nobody on the other end of it. The coil reads the Stage the same however it was crossed, and it reads the seat differently (Appendix A), and the empty bond shows there.

From inside each road:

Body. The warmth sits in the muscle, and they stand like someone whose back is covered, because it is.
Spirit. The warmth is a second presence in the chest, and solitude is never again quite complete.
Fate. The warmth is the weight of a promise that holds, and the world feels fastened where it had been loose.

On each Path · This is the last Stage at which more than half of every spend is lost, and the first at which a First Release can be found, on the two roads that have one. Mastery stays unread, save the early grip. The Firsts are laid side by side on Releases and Domains by Path.

Body. Techniques cohere into a style, and the Charge sits evenly through the Shell for the first time. Matter still answers only to the blow and the coat. A First Release on this road is a flood: the Shell thrown open to the whole Charge at once, the flesh running hotter and heavier, every hit carrying the Charge into what it lands on, and heat coming off the skin that the front row can feel.
Spirit. The signature has settled, so a thrown line now arrives recognizably theirs, and the Axis is felt in the Core as a second weight. A First Release here lengthens the line: further, to more souls at once, through plate as if the plate were not there. It stirs not one grain of sand.
Fate. For most, the bond itself is the art. The Fate road has no First Release. From Adept through the Expert years a Fate fighter fights with Range, Aura Pressure, presence, bonds and vows, and those grow with the Stage: dust lies still, flames stand straight, and people give ground they did not decide to give. The one Release this road will ever have waits at Refraction. A holder of a Moto Work reads Fate I by the early grip, and the Stage has added nothing to it.

The Releases · Each First has its own Catalyst. It counts only once the soul stands on Flourishing, it is met against something that means it, it is never bought, and one deed opens one door.

Body, the First: the body broken, refusing to fall. The body truly breaks in a fight, bone or joint or the Shell itself, and the fighter stays on their feet and goes on acting with what is broken, by their own will and no one else’s, until the fight ends one way or the other. Winning is never asked. A caravan guard who fights out a bout on one leg and a spear butt after a drake’s tail has smashed her knee, and loses, has met it. A duelist held up by his second while he finishes has not, because somebody else refused for him, and neither has a fighter kept standing by a vow. When the First is called it very often comes up first in the limb that broke.
Spirit, the First: the self said aloud, and true. The soul says what it is, in its own words, to someone or something that denies it and has the power to make the saying false, and in the same contest proves it true by what it does. A sellsword called a coward for nine years tells the man who called him so that he is a man who runs to save his own and will not run today, and does not. A boast before a bout that an honest Journeyman then beats is no self, and a true saying in a friendly room has met no contest. The aura rises a half-step off the body in its full hue, and the bystanders remember the sentence for years and quote it slightly wrong.
Fate has no First.

What it looks like · Consistency. Their power looks like them. You can hand them a problem they have never seen and predict roughly what they will do to it, and being predictable in that specific way is the difference between a talented person and a useful one.
What is not visible from outside is that an Axis is a load-bearing member. The architecture built on it has to stand up whether or not the person is still alive to stand under it. Every Prime Instructor has seen what a Flourished practitioner does the year their Axis dies. The power holds. The power is entirely fine, and it is still shaped exactly like a bond to somebody who is not there.
The aura is warm charcoal with a rumor of the hue in it, readable at a distance by any competent Mancer, and it is still a suggestion. On the Body road it lies on the skin like heat-haze and clings for a breath to a cup or a hilt after the hand has left it. On the Spirit road it hangs its half step off, and where an Axis runs a thread of it leans toward the other person, as Hob Tarrant’s leaned north. On the Fate road there is next to nothing to see, and a dropped coin near them comes up heads more often than it should. The Crystal is in the last of its Clouded years, and the body has begun to follow the road: a Body Adept is heavier than they look and warm to the touch, a Spirit Adept is lighter on a plank than their weight allows, and animals settle near them.
What it costs · A Release is the first thing on the ladder that can empty a reserve in minutes, and the Adepts are the people who find out what lies under a tenth. Held too long, a Body First ends in steam, cramp and skin split in fine lines along the forearms. A Spirit First ends in a hollow cold and a name gone. Each release ends by itself at a tenth, and the injuries belong to the ones who force it past.
What the folk call it · Taking root. The anchoring. A bond-witness is held and somebody attests, and the parish keeps the roll in Witness Wax, and parish witness rolls are the oldest continuous documents in most of the western quarter. A village can tell you who was witnessed to whom nine generations back and cannot tell you who held the land.


The line the Accord has never published
Guild halls know the Catalyst. Which means the fastest way to Flourish a cohort is to put a cohort through something together, at risk, in circumstances that make them matter to each other, and every Prime Instructor has known this since before there was an Accord.
What is published is the training casualty figure. The Strategic Division reviews it annually and has never once moved to reduce it.


The crossing, lived · The scale is a parish, which is why the parish keeps the roll.

Body. Two auras run together where the pair stand, the heat reaches the back of the crowd, and the ground under them firms, mud going hard as a threshing floor.
Spirit. The witness-hall goes still. Every married couple in it thinks of the day they were witnessed, colors deepen for an hour, and old quarrels in the parish are found by morning to have lost their heat.
Fate. Across the parish every oath is felt to tighten. Debtors remember what they owe, a betrothal that had been wavering stops wavering, and the Wax on the roll sets harder than the weather allows.

Bought versus lived · A bought Flourishing has the warmth in the chest and nobody on the other end of it, and it has no First Release, since a Release must be found by fighting. The Crystal reads Clouded either way. The seat does not read the same.
The Breaking Years: Expert
Stages V through VII. The Codex calls this the completion of the inner phase. The instructors call it the years you find out.
What changes in these Stages. The Crystal breaks into Faceted at Splintering and stays Faceted through Refraction, its facets coming clean enough by the end to conduct on their own.
