At Glory Mastery is read for the first time, the soul makes its first offer of a Class, and the share of a spend that arrives passes from the Stage’s figure to the rung of the layer in use. The ceiling is the first rung at Glory and the second at Refraction, so the Expert years hold the distance from matter as an object to matter through contact, and from Listener to Answerer. The Second Release, Fate’s One and the Domain seed arrive at their end. Auras gain light and take a shape, and civilians begin to see them.
V · Splintering
Expert · Stat ceiling 350, unstable from 276 · Holds from Level 101 · Mastery unread, the early grip reading I · Faceted Crystal
Catalyst · surviving contact with an entity or force more than two full steps beyond what the practitioner’s ceiling can hold: a beast two Grades past anything they could fight, a fighter two ranks up, a flood or a fall of that order. Survival is the whole requirement, and defeating the thing adds nothing.
Survival is the whole requirement on every road. What has to be survived is not the same thing.

Body. The contact is a blow or a load: a drake’s tail, an avalanche, the hand of a Master who was not trying. The body takes what should have ended it, the Shell breaks, and the flesh is rebuilt around the break.
Spirit. The contact is with a soul or a meaning far too large: the full regard of a Master, the dread of a Well-born thing, the grief soaked into a battlefield. Nothing touches the body. The Core takes it and breaks, and what is asked is that the same person be there afterward.
Fate. The contact is with a weight of fate far above their own: standing inside a greater soul’s claim and keeping a bond while it is leaned on, being the one obstacle to a great house’s oath, living through a day on which the odds were plainly arranged against them by something that can arrange odds. The Layer breaks among the bonds. The Fate soul pulls nothing in surviving it.

The one they tell · A Well-spawn drake at Cold Ferry took Yrsa Kolbeinsdottir across the chest with its tail when she was a Stage IV caravan guard with nine good years behind her, and she went through the side of a barge and lived. The Crystal broke where she was already broken, which happened to be a sister. For the twenty years of her long and bloody career after that, every blow she threw went true until somebody said the name, whereupon hairline veins of blue ran through her aura and it stuttered like a struck lamp. Every rival in the north learned it. Companies took to crying her dead sister’s name across the field before the first charge, and Yrsa took to fighting with tallow in her ears and killing first whoever had cried it.
From inside · The architecture that has held you since Murmuring reaches the limit of what it can be and has to break to become larger. There is no version where it does not break. The only question anybody has ever been able to influence is where.

It fractures along emotional lines. The break runs past the injury and past the encounter that triggered it, and follows whatever the soul was already carrying badly. A practitioner who goes into Splintering with an unresolved thing comes out of it with that thing structurally present in their Crystal, permanently, in a way the coil (the assay instrument that reads a Crystal) reads.
Splintering takes a flaw the soul already had and promotes it to a load path.

Practitioners who fail do not die, mostly. They lose Sub-Stat (the finer stats beneath each main stat) progress and they sit at the ceiling of Stage IV for the rest of their working lives, and the four quarters are full of them, and they are the reason the Adept’s rank is as crowded as it is.
From inside each road:

Body. The body stops being trustworthy. The hand relied on for nine years closes a beat late.
Spirit. The self stops being trustworthy. You are not certain the grief you woke with is yours.
Fate. Your word stops being trustworthy, to you. Every promise you ever made feels heavier, and you count them at night.

On each Path · Mastery goes unread for one last Stage, and the Stage’s own figure jumps to something over six parts in ten: the Crystal has learned to stop leaking, mostly by breaking. The fracture runs through whichever layer the soul leans on.

Body. The break shows in the Shell. The Charge packs unevenly around the flaw, so a blow that has gone true for six years lands heavy or light without warning, and the coat thins over the same place every time. Matter still obeys only impact, and nothing new opens.
Spirit. The break shows in the Core, and since the Core is where the self is kept, this is the worst of the three to live in. A thrown line carries the flaw with it, and the struck sometimes feel the thrower’s grief where they should have felt their own dread.
Fate. The break shows in the Layer, among the bonds: an Axis that held load for years strains, and a vow sits heavier than it did. A gripped soul still reads only the first rung its blood opened early, and nobody sensible pulls in the bad year.

What it looks like · A person who was reliable stops being reliable. Techniques that behaved for six years behave differently, or behave the same and cost more, or work perfectly and leave the practitioner shaking. The hall watches for it and the hall cannot do anything about it, and the honest instructors say so.
The aura is fracture-streaked: hairline veins of the lens’s clear color run through the smoky field and vanish again, a flicker anyone with the Gnosis can see. On a Body road the veins run on the skin, and on Yrsa Kolbeinsdottir they ran blue. On a Spirit road they hang in the air beside the person, where the shadows were already wrong. The Crystal has become Faceted, and the jewelers chose the word with some care. A facet is a face cut on a stone so that it will return light, and Splintering does the cutting. The three layers come out of it turning over in a rhythm the Continuum can read, and a Wellspring can now be harmonized without tearing the lattice.
What it costs · Everything costs more than it did and nobody can say by how much, which is the cost. Techniques that behaved for years leave the practitioner shaking. The road’s own bill arrives early and out of order: a hitter cramps at half, a thrower loses a word at half, and the small luck around a Fate fighter curdles on a full reserve. A failed Splintering is paid for in Sub-Stat progress and a working life at the ceiling of Stage IV.
What the folk call it · The cracking. The bad year. In the eastern quarter, going to the wall. There is no folk remedy, which is itself notable in a body of practice that has a remedy for everything, and the absence is the folk tradition being accurate about something the Accord’s literature is not.

Trade note · Splinter Ration leaves the fracture coming and introduces a controlled stress-riser so the Crystal breaks at the riser rather than wherever the trauma happened to sit. That is the entire product, it is reserved to the Expert’s title, and bonded practitioners receive it while village talent does not. More of who a person becomes is decided by that supply line than by anything they will ever choose.

The crossing, lived · The scale is a mile, and it is the first crossing strangers notice.

Body. Heat, and a shock through the ground that people a mile off take for a rockfall. Where the survivor lies the earth is glazed or split, and the body that gets up is plainly not the one that went down, scarred along the line of the break.
Spirit. For a mile around, people stop what they are doing and cannot say why. Colors go thin for a day, and everyone near is visited by the memory they like least.
Fate. For a mile around, luck goes strange for a day and then settles a little higher or lower than it was. Every net comes up empty or full, and things that were certain to happen that afternoon, a foaling, a hanging, do not happen.

Bought versus lived · A breakthrough Draft spares the buyer the meeting with something two steps beyond them, and it does not spare them the break. The lived fracture runs wherever the soul was already carrying something badly. The bought one runs where the Bench put the riser, which is why the houses pay for it.
VI · Glory
Expert · Stat ceiling 400 · Holds from Level 115 · Mastery to I · Faceted Crystal
Catalyst · willingly accepting genuine soul-cost to preserve something valued above the practitioner’s own structural integrity
The decision is the Catalyst on every road, made in advance and in cold blood. The layer it is paid from is the road’s.

Body. The cost is taken in the Shell and the flesh under it. The Charge is driven past the floor on purpose, for something, in the knowledge that part of the Shell will not close again: a hand that never afterward holds a coat, an arm that stays cold, years burned as fuel. The ruin is the receipt.
Spirit. The cost is taken in the Core, which is the self: a memory given up whole, a capacity spent, a color gone out of the world for good. Tsao Qinglan’s entry in the Red Abacus ledger reads like this one, and three Halls have argued for two centuries over which road she was standing on when she paid it.
Fate. The cost is taken from the soul’s own share, as a future given up by oath. The soul refuses, aloud and for good, a chance that was truly theirs, an inheritance, a marriage, a long life, so that something else may stand, and the Layer closes over the place. It is a vow and no pull: no thread, no knot.

The one they tell · When the Yellow Dike went at Lanjiang, Tsao Qinglan of the Red Abacus Hall stood in the breach with forty outer disciples behind her and the river coming, and she named her price aloud, as her Hall’s rules require of anything expensive. She spent the part of her Crystal that knew how to be happy, or so the Hall’s ledger enters it, and nobody has found another way to read the entry. The water stopped at her shins in a brown wall three stories high, held up on nothing but deep teal light, for as long as it took the lower city to climb the hill. For the rest of her life every flame in any room she entered leaned toward her, every candle and cook-fire, and each year Lanjiang hung its streets in silk and carried her through them under ten thousand paper lanterns. She attended, every year, and never once smiled at it.
From inside · The fractures have become features. What was damage the year before is now architecture, and the practitioner can feel the difference, and the feeling is unaccountably good in a way that troubles the more thoughtful of them for years afterward.
The Catalyst is a decision, and it is the first Catalyst in the ladder that is. Murmuring happens to you. Welling happens to you. Ascension is earned but arrives sideways. Flourishing requires another person. Glory requires that you look at something that will cost you structurally and choose it anyway, knowing the price, in advance, in cold blood.

Which means every Glory Expert in the four quarters who came by this road has, at some point, deliberately damaged themselves for something. The Accord’s own literature describes this as the culture of duty. The instructors describe it as the year they learn what they will pay for.
Trade note · A breakthrough Draft at this grade takes the soul-cost without asking what it was for. The buyer pays the price and never learns what they were buying, and it is very hard to find out afterward which part of them went.

From inside each road:

Body. There is a place in the body that is gone, and the rest has grown stronger around it, as a tree grows around a nail.
Spirit. There is a place in the self you can walk around and not enter, and you know its exact shape.
Fate. There is a life you were going to have, and you can feel it not arriving.

On each Path · Mastery is read here for the first time, from Glory’s hold at Level 115, the ceiling on every road is the first rung, and the soul makes its first offer of a Class, with the first move that comes with it. From this Stage the share of a spend that arrives is set by the rung of the layer in use and no longer by the Stage: on a first rung, six or seven parts in ten.

Body. Body I, Muridic, for a soul whose lead road is the Body; a road only walked or studied reads a rung or two behind, and so reads nothing yet. The Charge leaks unevenly and loudly. The rung opens the first step of the Material Force, set out under Forms: matter as an object. What the hand is on does as it is told, the post, the door, the other man’s sword arm, and nothing the hand is not on. A smith or a mason whose trade skill reads Journeyman or better works one rung higher on their own material wherever the ceiling allows it, and at Glory the ceiling does not.
Spirit. Spirit I, Listener, for a soul whose lead road is the Spirit. Souls and meanings begin to reach them unasked: the dead in a room, the grief soaked into a coat, a lie going sour in a man’s voice. None of it can be answered yet. A thrown line still lands on a soul, at a first rung’s losses, and the lost share is paid in the Core.
Fate. Fate I, Touched, for a Fate-led soul, read here like the others, and for a Moto with a Work read since Ascension. Without a grip on the thread, a Work or a blessing, it will climb with Level to II and stop there for good, however many vows are kept. What a Fate Expert has at Glory is the Echo field and a Pressure civilians can feel, and that is a great deal.

What it looks like · The Aura, a light in the practitioner’s own color that flares brighter as they push and is now plain to any civilian, starts doing things to rooms, gently at first. The air moves differently near them, small flames lean, animals behave, and people who have never heard of Mastery (how much of a soul’s power survives the trip out through the layer it leaves by) find themselves standing slightly further away without deciding to. The Echo field forms here. This is the Stage at which a practitioner stops being a person with abilities and starts being a presence, and most of them handle it badly for a year or two.
The color is medium gray with the hue standing in it, and luminance enters for the first time, so that the color no longer has to fight its way through. The aura also takes a shape here, laid on it by the Class, and holds it. A Body aura hugs the skin like heat-haze and clings to what they touch. A Spirit aura hangs a half step off the body, and the shadows around it fall wrong. A Fate aura barely shows, and near its owner dust lies still and coins land face up. The Crystal is Faceted and turning cleanly. A Body Expert has grown dense, heavier on a scale than the eye allows and warm as a new loaf. A Spirit Expert has grown light, with a stillness dogs lie down for.
What it costs · A first rung loses a third of every spend, and Glory is where the lost share becomes large enough to trouble bystanders. A Muridic hitter at full output warms a room and at a quarter steams like a horse, and held to a tenth the skin splits along the hands. A Listener who overspends comes home hollow and cold, with a color gone flat for days and somebody’s name mislaid, which the menders will tell you is cheap. A Fate fighter who pulls on a first rung pays most of a reserve for one lean on something already on its way, and it often fails, and the knot is owed whether the pull lands or fails.
What the folk call it · Being lit. He is lit up. In the Old World temple registers the term is kindled, and the ecclesiastical usage and the tavern usage have not diverged in six hundred years, which the Archives finds remarkable and has not explained.
The crossing, lived · The scale is a town, and this is the crossing the folk name is taken from.

Body. The light is plain to every civilian for the first time. Heat rolls through the streets, the ground keeps the shape of what was done on it, and the body that walks out is denser than it went in and marked where it paid.
Spirit. The town goes silent street by street. Every lamp flame leans, colors shift a shade in every eye and do not all shift back, and each person present finds one memory brighter and one fainter than it was.
Fate. Luck turns across the town in one evening. Debts are forgiven that nobody meant to forgive, a fire that was about to start does not, and every sworn person inside the walls feels their oaths draw tight as the refused chance closes.

Bought versus lived · A bought Glory opens the ceiling and reads no rung until Level reaches the hold, pays a soul-cost without learning what it was for, and is offered a Class that reads the life as it was actually lived, quiet room included. The lived one lit a breach at Lanjiang. The bought one is a Draft, a physician and a window that says Well-Attended.
VII · Refraction
Expert · Stat ceiling 475 · Holds from Level 130 · Mastery to II · Faceted Crystal
Catalyst · first Domain seed activation, however fragile or small. Projected fields become coherent. This seed is a one-time flicker of the person’s own Trait at the Threshold, and it needs no Release. A Second Release, or Fate’s One, is what later lets a seed be called and held.
The seed is the soul’s own Trait let out for a few seconds, on every road. What lets it out, and what it lands on, follow the lead layer.

Body. The seed fires in matter. The body is pressed to the point where its Trait can no longer be kept inside the skin, by a load, a blow or one insult too many, and for seconds the ground and the things on it take the body’s law. Gaffer Tom Underhay’s pints fell upward.
Spirit. The seed fires in meaning. The soul faces something true about itself squarely, usually aloud, and for seconds the room agrees: everyone in it takes a thing for what the holder says it is. Nothing on the table moves.
Fate. The seed fires as a condition. The soul stakes a claim against the run of things, a vow held at the moment it ought to have broken, and for seconds what must be so before anything can happen is what they say it is. Every seed is a claim of the Layer, so a Fate soul comes to this one on home ground, and it is still no pull and leaves no knot.

The one they tell · Gaffer Tom Underhay of the Salt Road Foot had sat at Level 199 for twenty-two years. He was fifty-seven, with a wall eye and a pension the Foot had never paid, and on the night of the Mule and Lantern brawl somebody told him the Refraction wall was for men with better fathers. He stood up, and for four seconds every pint in that taproom fell upward. There were sixty witnesses. They describe it wrongly, each in exactly the same way, and all of them will swear the beer turned green. The Foot carried him the whole length of the garrison road on a door, with a band in front. Next morning he looked inside his own Crystal, found out what his fracture record had to say about his father, and did not speak to anyone for a year.
From inside · The soul sees itself from outside.
The Crystal that has been the unconscious medium of everything you have ever done becomes an object you can look at, and looking at it changes it, and knowing that it changes it changes it again. Gnosis (the stat of perception and understanding) undergoes a qualitative jump here that no other Stage produces, and practitioners in Refraction are notoriously difficult to be around because they have just been handed the ability to examine their own architecture and have not yet learned to stop.
The trouble is that self-examination at this depth reveals the fracture record. Everything Splintering promoted to a load path is now visible, labeled, and impossible to un-see.
From inside each road:

Body. You see the Shell from outside: every old injury and every place the Charge sits badly, laid out like a joiner’s drawing.
Spirit. You see the Core from outside, and there is the grief, labeled.
Fate. You see your bonds from outside, each promise a line leaving you, and you can count which ones you kept.

On each Path · The Mastery ceiling rises to the second rung, so a fresh Refraction soul at 130 reads I and reaches II at Level 150, and the Second Release can be found on the Body and Spirit roads, and the One on the Fate road. Either opens and powers the Domain, and at this Stage holds a seed for minutes. Releases and Domains by Path has the three kinds of field side by side.

Body. Body II, Harmonic. Matter answers through contact: what the hand touches carries the command onward, the post through the wall behind it. Losses fall from about a third to about a fifth. A trade skill at Journeyman or better lifts the rung by one on its own material, and never past the ceiling. A Body Second Release rules matter: the Charge leaves the skin and fills the ground, and inside the line weight, heat and the state of stone obey the holder. Everyone can see it.
Spirit. Spirit II, Answerer. A shade or a bound spirit will talk back, and a thrown working means something when it arrives. A Spirit Second Release rules meanings: the room looks exactly as it did, and something in it has stopped being what it was.
Fate. Persistence will not pass the S band of the scale unless the Fate Path has been shown by this Stage. A Fate soul reads I or II by its Level here, like anyone, and II is as far as a soul without a grip will ever go. The seed asks for nothing more: every Domain is a claim staked by the Attraction Layer, and it pulls no thread and leaves no knot. Fate’s One rules conditions, which is to say what has to be so before anything can happen.

The Releases · Every Second, and the One, counts only once the soul stands on Refraction, and one deed meets one Catalyst: where a deed would answer both a Release and the next Stage’s crossing, the crossing takes it, and the benches teach this to every Expert who hopes to buy two doors with one bad night.

Body, the Second: a material known so well it obeys at range. One material the fighter knows to the grain, stone, iron, timber, bone or river water, obeys them across open ground, without hand or weapon on it, in a contested fight, on purpose. A mason in a siege breach tells the fallen stones of the wall to stand and they stand, twenty paces off, while the storming party is still coming over them. The pints that fell upward at the Mule and Lantern were the seed and opened nothing else, and moving the material by the hand on it is the old rung asking nothing new. The material moves first and the field after, and the Measurewrights in the stands start writing, because the line the Charge draws along the ground is where the Domain will one day stand.
Spirit, the Second: a meaning borne for someone else. The soul takes up a meaning that belongs to someone who cannot carry it, a grief, a name, a last word, a guilt, and carries it whole in their name and in its true sense while something contests it. A sin-eater’s daughter eats the bread over a murdered magistrate and takes his last ruling into her Core, and when his killers come to the burial to have it unsaid, she says it, his words and not hers, and it stands. A widow carrying her own husband’s death has not met it, for that grief is hers, and neither has a bearer who tells the meaning as she would have liked it to be. Nothing moves; then the line of the field runs out along the floor, and inside it the meaning is simply so.
Fate, the One: a claim staked on your life, and kept. The soul names aloud a claim over something outside itself, a ground, a gate, what may happen in a place, with its own life as the forfeit, against a contestant able to take both, and keeps it unyielded until the contest ends. A toll-reeve stands in the middle of her bridge and says that nothing crosses it armed while she lives, to a company that can kill her, and holds it through the night. Holding the same bridge by a pull, so the horses go lame on the approach, counts for nothing, because a pull is not a claim, and neither does a claim yielded at the last hour, however wisely. The One is deeper than any First and counts as the road’s Second: it enlarges the claim and the Pressure as a First would, and it opens and powers the Domain. The dust lies flat from the claimant’s feet to the edge of what was claimed, and the stillness stays on that ground for a day after.

What it looks like · A Domain seed. Small, fragile, lasting seconds at its first firing, and minutes for those who later earn a Second Release or the One and can call it back, and the first genuinely uncanny thing most people will ever witness, because a Domain seed is a piece of the world briefly agreeing to different terms. Bystanders describe it wrongly and consistently, and the consistency of the wrongness is the best evidence Archives has that they are describing something real.

The wall at two hundred. The Expert years end at Level 200, and the Stage that carries a soul past it cleanly is Transcendence. A practitioner who cannot produce a Domain seed, or make a wound bear weight, or pay for either, does not slow down. Level goes on piling up past two hundred and the pressure keeps arriving, accruing as Residual Strain, degrading gain and raising Overchannel (forcing more through the Crystal than it can carry) and Backlash (a working’s force turning on its maker) risk continuously, and it does not stop building.
This is where most careers that reach the Expert’s rank end, in a long loud stall a little past two hundred: strong, competent, slowly becoming more dangerous to themselves than to anything they are pointed at, telling anyone who will buy the next round exactly who cheated them and which house brat drank past them, and dying of something else first. Every veteran corps in the four quarters is largely composed of these people, and their bitterness is a structural feature of the Accord’s officer class rather than a matter of temperament.

The color is dual-toned, base gray and the lens’s color in one field without mixing, and it shifts with the angle it is seen from. Inside a seed the light itself changes temperature, which is what the sixty witnesses at the Mule and Lantern were calling green. A Body seed is plain to everyone: the air shimmers and the cobbles do something cobbles should not. A Spirit seed changes nothing the eye can find. A Fate seed lays the dust flat. The Crystal is still Faceted, its facets come so clean that it conducts by itself, power moves in it even in silence, and its owner can see into it, which is the whole trouble with the Stage. The older jewelers called this look Clear.
What it costs · The seed is the dearest thing a soul has yet tried to hold, and it collapses when attention breaks. A Body seed throws its lost share as heat into the ground it rules and leaves the holder steaming. A Spirit seed hollows, and its holders come out of it pale, vague and unsure whose turn it is. A Fate seed costs only reserve while it stands and curdles the luck of the room when it falls. Those who cannot cross pay the other bill, Residual Strain, and go on paying it.
What the folk call it · The double sight. Twice-eyed. In the eastern quarter, a Refracted practitioner is said to have swallowed their own reflection, which is a considerably better description than the Codex manages in the same number of words.
The crossing, lived · The scale is a hall and the street outside it, for a few seconds, and then for as long as the witnesses live.

Body. The air shimmers over a taproom’s worth of ground, loose things lift or sink or sweat, the cobbles keep the mark, and the holder stands up out of it steaming and half a stone heavier.
Spirit. A hall goes quiet in the middle of a brawl. Nothing has moved, and each person in it finds that one thing they were sure of has changed places with one they were not, and an old sorrow has shifted its weight.
Fate. The dust lies flat from wall to wall, every wager in the house settles itself, and something that was about to happen in that street, a knife coming out, a roof beam finally going, does not.

Bought versus lived · The Vitrifier delivers the flicker and the Stage. It does not deliver a Second Release or the One, so a bought Refraction has a seed that fired once in a quiet room and cannot be called back, a ceiling at the second rung over a Level that may not reach the first, and a Crystal that runs Overgrown until Level holds the Stage. Gaffer Tom was carried down the garrison road on a door with a band in front. Nobody carries a house heir anywhere.
Master
Stages VIII through X. The Codex says a practitioner at this rank exercises genuine metaphysical authority. What it does not say is that authority is a relationship, and a relationship has two parties.
What changes at this rank. The Mastery ceiling climbs a rung across the rank, to the third at Transcendence and the fourth at Realization, so the Masters hold the distance from matter by recognition to matter by law, and from the Confessor to the Shepherd. The Crystal is Fire for all three Stages. The true Domain arrives, then the Body road’s Third Release, then workings that outlast their maker and, at Realization, the door to a Realm. Auras light rooms, and the land starts keeping records.
VIII · Transcendence
Master · Stat ceiling 550 · Holds from Level 201 · Mastery to III · Fire Crystal
Catalyst · resolving a core internal contradiction documented in the Crystal’s fracture record. A wound carried as structural damage and consciously processed into architecture. The first true Domain becomes possible.
The wound is the load-bearing one, the one Splintering promoted, and it lies in the layer the soul leans on. Each road has its own way of making a wound carry weight.

Body. The wound is in the body and the Shell over it: the break that set crooked, the hand that fails under load, the place the Charge has packed badly since Splintering. It is made structure by being broken again on purpose and rebuilt to carry weight through the scar. The halls call it going back under the hammer.
Spirit. The wound is a grief or a truth: the death that was their fault, the thing they are. It is faced whole, named, and made to hold weight, as Asahina Shigeko put hers on an unbarred gate.
Fate. The wound is a broken oath or a debt left standing. It is made structure by being paid in full, to the last coin and to the heirs if the creditor is dead, or by the oath being sworn again and kept this time at whatever it costs. No thread is pulled in the paying.

The one they tell · The Gate of Asahina Shigeko is the reason the Free Companies will still not march past a shut door at dusk. She had left a gate unbarred behind her when she was twenty-six, and a household died of it, and she carried that wound for forty years until she stopped on the Kaname road one autumn evening, with the maples going scarlet over her head and six hundred armored men coming up the hill, and put her whole weight on it. Kaerazu no Mon, she said, almost too low to hear: the Gate of No Returning, and the word went down the column from mouth to mouth. The road became a place where every door behind you was the one you should have shut. Six hundred men walked into it. They walked out three weeks later in their own home villages, with their armor rusted through and their swords still in their hands, and in sixty years not one of them could tell you what they had been so frightened of, or get through a doorway without looking back.
From inside · The world is read as symbol, and this is less mystical than it sounds and more disorienting. Objects retain their weight and gain a second weight. A door is a door and is also a threshold, and both facts are operative, and the practitioner has to keep functioning while holding them.
The Catalyst is the hardest on the lived road and the only one no hall can arrange, and a purse goes around it without touching it. Refraction showed the practitioner their fracture record. Transcendence requires them to take one of the wounds in it, the load-bearing one, the one Splintering promoted, and consciously make it structure. The wound stays a wound, unhealed and unreleased, and it is made to hold weight on purpose.
Practitioners fail at this for decades. There is no shortage of souls with a Master’s numbers in them sitting at Refraction in comfortable positions who simply never did the work, and the halls are polite about it, and everybody knows.
From inside each road:

Body. The scar is the strongest part of you now, and you put your weight on it first.
Spirit. The grief is a room in the house, where it used to be a hole in the floor.
Fate. The debt is paid, and for the first time in decades nothing is following you.

On each Path · The Mastery ceiling rises to the third rung, so a fresh Transcendent at 201 reads II and reaches III at Level 215. The first true Domain becomes possible, held for hours.

Body. Body III, Resonant: matter by recognition. She knows what the stone will do under load, and it does that at her word, and losses fall from about a fifth to under a tenth. A Body Domain rules matter, in yards, tight and hard, because Radius, Sovereignty and Gravity stop at the A band of the scale off the Fate Path.
Spirit. Spirit III, Confessor. They reach into a soul and find what is lodged there, and a line written on a thing carries their say on what the thing is. A Spirit Domain rules meanings, by the room, and nothing on the shelves moves.
Fate. A Fate Domain rules conditions, and with the gates open it runs to valleys, with reserve the only leash. It is a claim and not a pull, and owes no knot. A Fate Master with a grip on the thread reads II, Drawn, at the Stage’s hold and III, Spinner, from Level 215; one without stops at II, Drawn, and has the Domain all the same, since a claim needs no rung.

What it looks like · A Domain, a true one, well past the seed, grown by living and called aloud: a standing region of the world operating on the practitioner’s terms while they are present in it, and the first time most people encounter one they are frightened in a way they cannot afterwards justify. Anyone at this Stage can have one, their own concept made real, with the fame, the rivals and the bounty that follow. A bought Stage VIII has the right to one and no Domain until they have fought their way to it, and a person standing in a duke’s colors at Stage VIII with nothing to open is a sight the songs enjoy.
The color is silver-gray suffused with the lens’s hue, bright enough to light a dark room and to throw its color on the walls: dark with light in it has become light with the memory of darkness in it. The Crystal is Fire, the jeweler’s word for light split into color inside a stone, and it is the first tier at which the Crystal itself gives enough light to be seen by an eye with no training. A Body Master is as dense as green oak and warm from across a room, and the eyes have begun to catch lamplight like a cat’s. A Spirit Master shows a faint translucence at the edges against a strong light, at the rim of an ear or the fingers of a raised hand. A Fate Master looks like anyone, and crowds part for them a moment before they arrive.
What it costs · A Domain is paid for from the reserve, in the coin of its own idea, and by the collapse when it falls. A Body Domain burns its lost share in the Shell’s furnace and throws the heat into the ground it rules, and one held to a tenth leaves the holder split and steaming in a ring of baked earth. A Spirit Domain hollows, and Masters come out of a long one cold and gray and short a memory they will not get back. A Fate Domain run long sours the luck of everyone inside the line, the holder first, and maxed it calls in every knot the holder ever left outstanding. A Resonant Shell or a Confessor’s Core loses little, which only means the reserve empties on purpose.
What the folk call it · Folklore thins here, because folklore is what a community builds around a thing it lives beside, and communities do not live beside Stage VIII. What exists instead is story. Named individuals, remembered feats, and the beginnings of the process by which a person becomes a figure. The Accord’s Lattice Ledger and the ballad tradition begin describing the same people at roughly this Stage and stop agreeing almost immediately.
The crossing, lived · The scale is the valley, and this is the crossing the saying is about.

Body. The whole valley sees it: a column of the lens’s color, heat that brings blossom out of season or leaves bare scorched rock, the ground answering in a ring of raised or sunken earth, and a body walking out remade, with the old scar shining through it like a seam of ore.
Spirit. The valley goes quiet, birds included. Colors deepen for everyone in it, each person recalls the door they should have shut, and for one night nobody within sight of the place lies to anyone.
Fate. Luck turns across the valley in a night. Lost things come home, old feuds find themselves settled, every oath on every parish roll is felt to tighten, and a flood or a death the whole valley had been expecting passes it by.

Bought versus lived · A bought Transcendence has the right to a Domain and no Domain, a roof marked Resonant over a Fire Crystal that spills light it cannot gather, Overgrown and reading low until Level holds the Stage, and the wound exactly as it was, now carried at a Master’s weight. A lived one lights the valley, and the valley remembers the date.
IX · Invocation
Master · Stat ceiling 625 · Holds from Level 215 · Mastery to III · Fire Crystal
Catalyst · calling on Wellsprings, Titans, or Archonic law as co-authors of expression, and with it a first flicker of a Realm, a field capable of holding other Domains. Like the seed before it, that flicker comes once and needs no Release. The Realm itself waits behind its door at Realization, and each road has its own door.
Something larger is asked in as co-author on every road, and what is put at its disposal is the layer the soul leans on.

Body. The asking is done with the body. The soul stands on the Wellspring’s own ground and lets the lens take the Charge in the Shell without steering it, which is to hand the body over. What must be survived is the answer arriving in the flesh.
Spirit. The asking is done with the self. The Core is opened to a second voice, and the soul must remain the first one: it lets a larger meaning in and is still there afterward to disagree with it.
Fate. The asking is done by terms. The soul offers a pact, stated aloud, to the law behind a Wellspring or to an Archon’s, and is answered with terms of its own, which it accepts knowing that such things notice who breaks them. A pact is an oath. It spends the share and pulls no thread.

The one they tell · At the siege of Dornhold the Ember Deacon Clement Tull asked. That is how the song puts it, and for once the song is precise. The Duke’s marshal had opened a Domain over the walls, an honest thing of iron-gray weight that had been breaking ladders for a month, and Tull knelt in the ditch in a scorched orange cope and called on the Wellspring by its name, and something that was not Tull answered.
His field went round the marshal’s field and closed, and the marshal’s Domain hung inside his like a fly in amber, still running, with the marshal in it, and a second color came up at the edge of the orange that nobody in the camp could look at for long. The town surrendered by noon. Tull asked the fire to stop, and the Wellspring, which had preferences of its own, declined. Dornhold burned for nineteen years. Pilgrims came to watch, and the Strategic Division opened a file.
From inside · You stop working alone.
Every technique before this was the practitioner’s Crystal doing something. From Invocation, the practitioner asks, and something larger answers, and the answering is literal, unreliable and expensive. The Wellspring is a co-author. Co-authors have their own preferences and they exercise them.

The recorded psychological pattern is the most consistent in the ladder. Practitioners entering Invocation describe an enormous relief followed within a year or two by something considerably worse, as they work out that the relief was the sensation of no longer being solely responsible for their own output, and that the thing they handed responsibility to did not sign anything.

From inside each road:

Body. Your hands do a thing you did not quite tell them to do, and it is better than what you would have told them.
Spirit. There is a second voice in the Core, and it does not always wait to be asked.
Fate. You are a party to a contract, and the other party does not sleep.

On each Path · No ceiling moves. On the Body road the Third Release can be found, which fills the two-step cap on boosts by itself. And the Wellspring begins to answer. The Archives read the Realm the crossing flickered, and the one that waits at Realization, by the same division as the field under it: matter, meanings, conditions.

Body. The ceiling is still III, and an Invocation soul whose Level holds the Stage stands on it, at recognition. What changes is who is shaping the Charge. The lens in the Shell now has an author besides the fighter, so a Body working at this Stage is the world’s own Aether, in the Wellspring’s shape, at the Wellspring’s suggestion. Tull’s fire was that. A Body Realm, when it comes, rules the matter another Domain stands on.
Spirit. The Core holds a second voice. Essence is still the self, refined and stamped, and now the stamp is countersigned: a Mancer reads two authors in it. A Spirit Realm, when it comes, rules what the fields inside it are taken to mean.
Fate. A Fate Realm, when it comes, rules whether a field inside it has leave to stand. The difference between a claim and a pull matters more here than anywhere, and it is the first thing the Strategic Division’s file records: a Realm is a claim, owes no knot and can be held all day, and a pull of the same size is a Weaver’s work and the masterwork of a life.

The Release · Only the Body road has a Third, and it counts only once the soul stands on Invocation.

Body, the Third: the body remade around a wound. In the tribulation, when the Wellspring’s own Aether comes down on the flesh to test the claim, the fighter takes a new wound from it and does not heal back to the body they had. The body is remade with the wound as part of its plan, the Wellspring co-authoring the new form, and the fighter fights in that body before the day is out. A Fractura fighter’s tribulation opens a seam of light down his sword arm that never closes, and his Third comes up through it every time. A Master who has the wound closed clean by a priced mender survived the test and kept nothing of it, and letting an old wound be the one remade is Transcendence’s work, done or still owed. Afterward the wound is lit at its edges in the Wellspring’s second color, the color that will rim the Third’s field from then on.
Spirit and Fate have no Third. Their roads go deeper by what they already hold.

What it looks like · The flicker of a Realm, once, at the crossing: for a breath the Domain becomes capable of holding other Domains inside it, as the Ember Deacon’s did at Dornhold, and that breath is the point at which Stage IX practitioners become a strategic rather than a tactical consideration, and the point at which the Strategic Division starts keeping a file.
The aura is bright, and no longer wholly the practitioner’s own: a second hue comes up at the edges during an invocation, the Wellspring’s, and recedes after. The Crystal is still Fire, and its fire has gone clean: the old inclusions are all still there, they have become structure, and Trait law and Domain law are beginning to be the same law. A Body Master at this height throws warmth like a stove, a Spirit Master has a stillness that silences a rookery, and around a Fate Master the weather is a little better than it is a mile off.
What it costs · A co-author takes a share. A Body Third fills the whole boost cap by itself and empties a reserve in the time it takes to say so, in heat enough to cook a ring and split the holder to the elbow. The other roads pay the co-author in their own coin: a hollowing that takes a year of memory in one evening, or a run of luck so bad that their own name sits wrong in other mouths. Above that stands the cost no ladder lists, which is that the Wellspring may decline to stop.
What the folk call it · Nothing. Ordinary people do not have a word for Stage IX and have never needed one. The ecclesiastical traditions have several and they disagree with each other and with the Accord, and the disagreement is four hundred years old and is really an argument about whether the Wellspring answering constitutes divine favor or merely a lawful process, which is the same argument the Holy See and the Codex have been having about everything since Year Zero.
The crossing, lived · The scale is a county, and for the first time the light is not all the practitioner’s own.

Body. A second color stands in the sky over the place, the Wellspring’s, and the county’s matter answers in its manner: every hearth burning high, or every well rising, or frost in June. The one who asked gets up giving off a heat that is not altogether theirs.
Spirit. A county’s worth of people stop talking at once and feel themselves briefly overheard. Dreams are shared for a week, and the colors that come back are a little more the Wellspring’s than they were.
Fate. Across the county things settle as though a judgment had been handed down. Suits long at law resolve, the season turns on the exact day the almanac gave, and every sworn person feels their oaths draw tight, the way a line does when something large takes the other end.

Bought versus lived · The Draft stands in for the asking, so a bought Invocation has the Stage and has never been answered. It has no Third Release, the Realm’s door will not open for it at any height, and a Wellspring that has never been asked anything by them, which those who know count as the one mercy in the arrangement.
X · Realization
Master · Stat ceiling 725 · Holds from Level 230 · Mastery to IV · Fire Crystal
Catalyst · truth as lived consequence. The world answers back. Pacts, artifacts and law imprint on terrain. The Domain becomes a reality the Continuum (the lawful fabric of reality that workings write into) must accommodate.
This Catalyst is the slowest on the ladder, and no road has a short way through it. A truth has to be lived, without exception, until the world answers, and the road decides what it is lived in.

Body. The truth is lived in work on matter: decades at one wall, one forge, one road, until the thing has been told the same so many times, by hands that never once told it otherwise, that it keeps the word unasked.
Spirit. The truth is lived in witness. Odo Pennyfather sat thirty-six years on one stone and never let a false thing pass in his hearing, and the meaning set.
Fate. The truth is lived in a kept word: every pact honored and every debt paid on the day, for so long that the ground where they were sworn begins to hold other people to the same. Nothing is pulled. The Layer has simply never been given a reason to doubt.

The one they tell · A Stage X notary named Odo Pennyfather sat on one flat stone at Cray Hollow for thirty-six years witnessing bargains, because his father had witnessed on it before him. He has been dead for two centuries and nobody has told a successful lie on that stone since. Liars get a nosebleed, a slow drip onto the rock, and the rock keeps the stain. Cattle dealers pay two silver marks to close on it, and three kings have declined to treat there. A Moto envoy once stood on it a whole afternoon and said nothing at all, and the bargain he had come to close was never closed. The last man who tried to swear away a murder on it bled out through the nose before the clerk had finished the line.
From inside · The practitioner stops being the party that has to be accommodated.
At Realization the Continuum adjusts, a little, locally and grudgingly and within limits that are extremely specific, but the direction of the accommodation has reversed and it never reverses back. What the practitioner is now costs the world something to permit, and the world permits it.
The lived experience of this is reported as a species of loneliness that has no good analogue lower on the ladder, and practitioners who describe it well tend to describe it in terms of weather. You are no longer standing in it. You are part of what other people are standing in.
From inside each road:

Body. The things you made no longer need you, and you can feel them standing.
Spirit. The things you meant go on meaning it after you have left the room.
Fate. The things you swore are kept by the place now, and you are only one of the parties.

On each Path · The Mastery ceiling rises to the fourth rung, so a fresh Realization soul at 230 reads III and reaches IV at Level 260, and no Release remains to be found. What changes besides is that workings stay, and that the door to a Realm stands here.

Body. Matter keeps what it was told. A wall a Stage X hitter has leaned on for a season carries its load a century longer than its mortar should, and things made at this Stage do not need maintaining. Those on the fourth rung, Body IV, Luminous, command by law: the Shell is thin and lucid, and a river can be told how deep it is. At Realization the law outlasts the command.
Spirit. Meanings keep. A stone where true bargains were witnessed for thirty-six years goes on knowing a lie, and Odo Pennyfather’s is the standing case. Ground thick with memory is what Spirit workers pay to stand on, and a Stage X makes it by sitting still. On the fourth rung, Spirit IV, Shepherd, the soul holds many at once: a frightened company steadies around them, and a dying man’s soul stays where it is put until morning.
Fate. Pacts hold in the ground. A vow sworn in a Realized Domain binds the place along with the parties, and such places grow heavy with what was decided there, as The Three Grounds sets out. A Fate Master’s Mastery stands where Level and a grip have put it.

The Realm’s door · A Realm is a Domain grown into a field that can hold other fields inside it, still running, with their owners in them. Its edge takes the Wellspring’s second color, and the Continuum has to make room for it, which is why no door can open before Realization: this is the Stage at which the Continuum first makes room. Most who ever hold a Realm do it at Dissonance or Emanation, and a Stage X with one is the strategic weapon the Strategic Division keeps files on. Each road has its own door, its own Catalyst met under contest and never bought, and none of them is Realization’s own decades of work: the door is a single deed done afterward, with another soul’s field in the holder’s hands.

Body, through the Third: another’s world carried, and not let fall. With the Third released, the holder lets another soul’s true Domain stand on their own ground and bears its whole weight in the remade body for the full span of it, an enemy’s at full strength or an ally’s in collapse, without breaking it and without letting it fall on what stands beneath. A Master who catches a dying ally’s Domain as her reserve fails and carries it until it spends itself, so the collapse never reaches the town under it, has met it. A Master two Stages up who overwrites the enemy’s field from above has carried nothing. The Realm is matter as foundation, the ground other fields stand on, and its flaw is the foundation’s: it cannot grip, and whatever lifts away or pulls out of it parts it. Its price is settling: each holding leaves the weight of the fields carried in the holder’s body for good, until floors give under them and horses will not carry them.
Spirit, through its Second grown whole: another’s whole meaning held inside your own, and both left true. The holder, whose Second has stood as a true Domain since Transcendence, takes a rival’s true Domain inside their own and understands its law so wholly that it runs there meaning exactly what its owner means by it, while the holder’s own meaning stands around it unchanged, for the whole of the contest. A court mancer who holds a heretic’s Domain inside her own for the length of his trial, so the bench hears what his law truly is, and judges against him anyway, has met it. Holding it by taking it for something else, a madness or a trick, is a gloss laid on another’s law and counts for nothing. The Realm is the sense in which other fields are read, and its flaw is that a reading needs something to read: what means nothing passes through it. Its price is a second voice: the holder comes out of every Realm a little persuaded by the person they fought.
Fate, through the One: a claim others stand on, kept for them. The holder grants standing to another’s claim, a rival’s Domain, a truce between two holders, a city’s charter, by putting their own One beneath it as surety, life and standing pledged, and when that claim is broken or attacked keeps it for them at their own cost, against whoever breaks it, kin and allies included. A Fate Master who stands surety for a truce between two holders and enforces it against his own grandmother when she breaks it has met it. A surety who keeps the truce by pulling threads has opened no door. The Realm is the leave under which any field inside may stand at all, and its flaw is the warrant’s: if the holder breaks a word of their own while it stands, every field in it loses leave at once, theirs first. Its price is the surety’s: every claim it warranted that is later broken is billed to the holder’s standing, never as a knot.
A Realm still yields to a field two Stages up, and a bought Stage X has no door at all.

What it looks like · Terrain changes. Pacts hold in the ground. Artifacts made at Realization do not need maintaining. Regions where a Stage X practitioner spent a long time keep a set that outlasts them by generations, and half the sites the Measurewrights (trained assayers who measure power and sites) cannot attribute in the Bearing and the Holding are almost certainly this and cannot be proven to be.
The color is pale and clean, the gray gone to a whisper, and the residue of a working holds the hue for hours or days: ground a Stage X has worked on keeps their color long enough for a Mancer arriving a week later to say who was there. The Crystal is Fire, at its clearest. A Body road shows in a weight that makes floorboards complain and in eyes that shine back in the dark, a Spirit road in a body that seems lit from behind at its edges, and a Fate road in nothing on the person at all and in a market that rearranges itself as they walk through it.
What it costs · The reserve at this height is a lake, and emptying it is a public event. A Body Master at a tenth has baked the field and stands in it cracked like a dry riverbed. A Spirit Master at a tenth has forgotten a decade and may not know it. A Fate Master’s knots, where there are pulls behind them, are no longer the size of a snapped strap: a removed prerequisite falls due within the arc, and what falls due is a friend’s plan, a harvest or a bridge. The terrain keeps a copy of whichever it was.
What the folk call it · The place remembers him. Every quarter has a version and the versions are the same version. This is the point at which a practitioner stops generating stories about themselves and starts generating stories about a location, which is how you can tell, from the shape of a local legend, roughly what Stage the person at the bottom of it reached.
The crossing, lived · The scale is a district. It is the slowest crossing on the ladder to show, and the only one that never stops showing.

Body. The land takes the print: a hill that holds its slope through a flood, ground that stays warm, stone that will not weather. The body is by now what it will be for the rest of its life.
Spirit. A district’s worth of people find that a place has become solemn. Colors sit deeper there, memories told on that ground come out truer than the teller intended, and it stays so.
Fate. Across the district bargains start being kept. Odds on that ground run fair for everyone, cheats go hungry, and what was sworn there is found to bind people who never heard it sworn.

Bought versus lived · The world answers a life, and a bought Realization has not lived the one in question. The Stage and the ceiling are real. The place does not remember them, because they were never anywhere long enough, the Stage runs Overgrown until Level holds it, and no Realm’s door opens for it at any Level.
Grandmaster
Stages XI and XII. Two Stages that are one motion: the deliberate approach to annihilation, and what radiates outward from a soul that came back.
What changes at this rank. The Mastery ceiling rises once, to the fifth rung at Emanation, and no Release is left to find. The Crystal becomes Flawless at Dissonance and stays so, whatever its State. What changes is direction: at Dissonance the soul turns on itself, and at Emanation what it is begins to leak into the district with nobody holding it. The costs change hands at the same time, from the practitioner to the people who live nearby.
XI · Dissonance
Grandmaster · Stat ceiling 750 with structural instability, fracture risk above 700 · Holds from Level 301 · Mastery to IV · Flawless Crystal
Catalyst · deliberately entering contact with a force or truth capable of ending the practitioner’s existence and remaining coherent long enough to choose how they meet it
Every road walks toward the thing that can end it and chooses how to stand. The roads differ in what that thing is.

Body. It is a force. They walk into the heart of a Well, a Titan’s weather or the blow of something far above them, with the Shell already at fracture risk, and what they choose is the stance they are broken in.
Spirit. It is a truth, one the self cannot contain and remain the self. They look at it without turning away, and what they choose is who is doing the looking.
Fate. It is their own end, already arranged: a death at odds nobody could lean on, a doom, an oath whose keeping kills. The chance to step aside is offered, and it is a real one. They refuse it and choose the manner of meeting what comes. It is the largest refusal on the ladder, and it pulls nothing.

The one they tell · The Harrow Road rippled for a week, the summer Grandmaster Reva Stroud stopped being able to decide. Three villages lay flat behind her with the thatch all combed one way, and the air around her sang in standing bands you could see, the color of a furnace mouth and brighter than anybody wanted. Two Enforcement squads went up that road and came back in baskets. Sergeant Pim Ottery went third, alone, in his patrol greatcoat, carrying a covered bowl of mutton and barley, because that is the first line of the protocol. He set it down twelve paces off and told her she looked thin. She ate. It cost him both eardrums and the use of his left side, and for the next thirty years he never once paid for a drink in any town on that road.
From inside · Splintering was survival. Dissonance is chosen.
The practitioner walks toward something that can end them, arrives, remains coherent, and chooses their manner of meeting it. That is the whole Catalyst and every word of it is load-bearing. Survival will not satisfy it and victory will not satisfy it: the Crystal wants a soul that remains coherent long enough to choose.
Power and identity clash here, openly, in the Crystal, and the clash is the Stage. Practitioners trapped in Dissonance rather than passing through it are the most dangerous individuals in the four quarters by a wide margin, because they have output in the SS band of the scale organized around an unresolved contradiction and no structural reason to stop.
From inside each road:

Body. The body is at war with its own strength, and every motion is two motions.
Spirit. There are two of you in the Core, and both are telling the truth.
Fate. What you have sworn and what you are have parted company, and everything near you waits to see which will be kept.

On each Path · No ceiling moves. The clash of power and identity runs through the leading layer, and each road has its own way of being trapped.

Body. The Shell argues with itself. The Charge packs into the SS band around a contradiction and comes out as standing bands in the air, which is what combed the thatch behind Reva Stroud. Matter near a trapped Body Grandmaster obeys two laws by turns.
Spirit. The Core argues, and since the Core is the self there is nowhere outside it to stand. Souls near a trapped Spirit Grandmaster take the argument up: households quarrel, the dead will not settle, and a soul wound dealt in that state seldom closes clean.
Fate. The Layer argues, and conditions near them flicker: a thing has leave to happen and then has not. For those with a grip this is the most dangerous hour of a life in which to pull, since the price comes out of a share already at war with itself.

What it looks like · Instability that reads on any instrument and is visible to anyone in the room. The Enforcement Division has a standing protocol for a suspected Dissonance-trapped practitioner and the protocol’s first line is to establish whether the practitioner has eaten.

The architectural note. Souls that pass through Dissonance rather than around it reach the next Stage fractured and denser than the clean path produces. Overflow, Overchannel and Persistence reach their true ceiling in no other way. The fractures are features. Anyone who tells an ambitious practitioner otherwise is either being kind or has an interest in them not trying.

The color is brilliant, with a visible interference grain: standing-wave textures that shift with the Crystal’s pressure, brighter than Realization and plainly unsteady, pitch flaring on a torch where a lamp would hold. The Crystal’s look is Flawless and its State is commonly Fractured, and the Bench has been explaining for two centuries that a look says how far a stone has grown and a State says what has happened to it lately.
What it costs · Every figure above seven hundred is carried at fracture risk, so the road’s ordinary bill arrives with a second one behind it. A Body Grandmaster flagging in Dissonance cracks in the Shell and in the Crystal together. A Spirit one loses memory to the hollowing and identity to the clash, and cannot always tell which went. A Fate one finds the knots falling due early. The protocol’s bowl of mutton and barley is aimed at the plainest fact about all three: a soul that has stopped eating has stopped deciding, and this Stage is passed by deciding.
What the folk call it · The singing. Along the Harrow Road, gone to the bands. Country people live beside Stage XI no more than they live beside Stage IX, but they have buried enough of what it does to keep one piece of advice, which is the protocol’s first line said shorter: ask if she’s eaten. It is used of anyone in a dangerous temper, mostly of kin, and hardly anyone who says it knows it began as a field instruction.
The crossing, lived · The scale is a region, and the crossing runs for days. The signs of a soul passing through are the signs of a soul trapped, until the moment they stop.

Body. The air stands in visible bands for miles, thatch is combed flat, the road ripples and keeps the ripple, and what comes back down it has been broken and remade in sight of three parishes.
Spirit. A region goes quiet and stays quiet. Colors come apart at their edges, people find they hold two memories of the same morning, and when it ends everyone knows it in the same moment without being told.
Fate. Across a region nothing can be relied on, and a spun coin will not settle. Then everything settles at once: the weather, the markets and the feuds all come down on one side, and a great many things that had been going to happen quietly do not.

Bought versus lived · A Draft or a blessing large enough stands in for the choosing, which means the buyer arrives at the next Stage without ever having been asked the question. The architectural note above gives the price: a clean path, a lighter Crystal, and an Overflow, Overchannel and Persistence that never see their true ceiling.
XII · Emanation
Grandmaster · Stat ceiling 950 · Holds from Level 320 · Mastery to V · Flawless Crystal
Catalyst · emerging from Dissonance with a Crystal denser and cleaner than before entry. The fractures must have become features.
Coming back is work, and it is done in the layer that broke.

Body. The coming back is done in the body. The Shell that cracked in Dissonance is rebuilt, fracture by fracture, into something denser than an unbroken one, as a bone knits thicker at the break. It is counted done when the Charge sits in it without a single band.
Spirit. The coming back is done in the self. The two who argued in the Core are made one person who contains the argument, and it is counted done when they can say the truth that nearly ended them in an ordinary voice.
Fate. The coming back is done in the accounts. Every debt outstanding is paid in full, and for those who ever pulled, every knot is let fall due and met standing, so that the Layer comes out owing nothing to anyone. It is settlement and no pull.

The one they tell · When the chandler’s wife at Vall told the Accord’s Envoy, Grandmaster Cuthbert Ashe, that she would not be leaving her husband, he took it well. He was courteous about it, he went on with his work, and for the next three years nobody in the whole Vall valley slept past the fourth hour. Milk turned in the pail. Couples forty years married screamed at each other across the salt. Four hundred people walked out of the valley without being able to tell you why, and a good many others walked into the river. She changed her mind in the spring of the fourth year, for reasons she called her own, and that autumn the pears came in so heavy that the boughs tore off the trees in great gold heaps and every cow in the valley dropped twins. It has been Pearfall on every map since, and the Accord’s record of that posting is sealed.
From inside · Nothing has to be held any more.
Traits that required maintenance become local law. The Domain no longer needs sustaining. Passive miracles leak out of the practitioner without intention and occasionally without their knowledge, and the reports of Stage XII practitioners discovering what they have been doing to a district by being in it are consistent and entirely dark.
From inside each road:

Body. The body holds nothing back and nothing in. Warmth simply leaves it, as it leaves a hearthstone.
Spirit. Your moods have stopped being private, and you learn this from other people’s faces.
Fate. Things go your way without your asking, and you begin to be careful what you want.

On each Path · The Mastery ceiling rises to the fifth rung, the last below Ω, so a fresh Emanation soul at 320 reads IV and reaches V at Level 340. What used to be done is now simply the case, and the leading layer leaks.

Body. The Body Path’s bonus reaches its full fifth, twenty parts in a hundred on Strike Force, Durability and Lifting Strength. Matter near them takes their law without being told: stone bears more, or iron rusts faster, or the ground does not freeze. Presence alone begins to tune the Aether nearby. On the fifth rung, Body V, Radiant, matter answers by law and wide: more begins to arrive than the raw numbers suggest, and the reach runs as far as there is matter to read, armor made too heavy to lift, a blade rusting in the hand. It still needs existing substance, and every command comes back as recoil through bone and Crystal.
Spirit. Souls near them take their mood. Sleep, tempers, grief and the will to stay in a valley all follow the Core of one person, and Vall is the case every Envoy is made to read. None of it marks a wall. On the fifth rung, Spirit V, Ferryman, the soul carries others across the Veil: she guides, questions, lays to rest, carries a message and binds a lingering dead, and never returns a life.
Fate. Conditions near them lean. The pears come in heavy and the cows drop twins, or nothing in the district goes right for three years. This is no pull: it reaches for nothing above the soul and leaves no knot, being a claim that no longer needs staking. How far a Fate soul’s Mastery runs is, as ever, a matter of Level and of a grip.

What it looks like · The room is different because they are in it, and stays different for a while after they leave. Crops. Weather. Sleep. Whether arguments in a household escalate. Emanation is the Stage at which a practitioner’s mood becomes an environmental condition, and the Accord’s Envoy postings are assigned with this in mind and are never explained in those terms to the districts receiving them.
The color has begun to bleach toward white at its edges, and it projects far enough that the light in a room changes before they enter it. The lamps on Fishmonger’s Row at Tarn Quay went ochre a full ten minutes ahead of Grandmother Seok, as The Color of Essence tells it. The Crystal is at the far end of its Flawless look. A Body Grandmaster warms a hall, and the eyes shine in daylight. A Spirit Grandmaster stands in strong sun like a figure cut from horn, and the birds go quiet overhead. A Fate Grandmaster is the plainest person in the square, under better weather than the next parish has.
What it costs · Nothing has to be held, and so the cost has moved from the practitioner to the district. The lost share of a leak is still heat on the Body road, a hollowing on the Spirit road and luck on the Fate road, and at this height it is the valley that warms, the valley that goes flat and gray, and the valley whose buckles give. When a Stage XII does spend to the floor, the three bills are paid by everyone within sight. The Archives hold several accounts of a Grandmaster emptied on a single pull with nothing to show for it.
What the folk call it · A good country. A bad country. People move toward and away from Stage XII practitioners without knowing they are doing it, and settlement patterns in three quarters show it clearly, and no polity has ever admitted planning around it.
The crossing, lived · The scale is a day’s ride in every direction, and what changes does not change back.

Body. The land warms, hardens or greens to the holder’s law: ground that will not freeze, stone that bears more than stone should.
Spirit. A day’s ride of people wake from the same dream. The mood of the country changes like a change of light, and the colors there are a little the holder’s from then on.
Fate. The luck of the country sets, good or bad. Harvests, births and lawsuits all lean one way, and things the whole country had long expected quietly fail to come about.

Bought versus lived · Emanation by purse skips the coming back. The Stage is real and the leak is real, and what leaks is whatever was in the Crystal when it was melted, unexamined. A lived Emanation at least finds out what it is doing to the district, eventually.
Archmaster
Stages XIII and XIV. The furthest reach of canonical mortal coherence, and the Stage that does not end.
What changes at this rank. The Crystal becomes Starred. Mastery still stops at the fifth rung, and a soul standing on it loses nothing: at this height the Continuum supplements what is spent, and more arrives than left. A law is registered at Principality and a Throne answers at Zenith. Auras are near-white and bend the light around them.
XIII · Principality
Archmaster · Stat ceiling 1,200 · Holds from Level 401 · Mastery to V · Starred Crystal
Catalyst · Domain coherence sufficient for the Continuum to formally register a law the practitioner embodies. First World Spirit threshold.
The Continuum registers a law it has never once seen broken inside the Domain, and each road proves its law in its own stuff. Archmasters are few, and what follows is drawn from a handful of lives.

Body. The law is proven in matter. Within their Domain a thing of substance, what bears what, what burns, what falls, has been so without one exception for long enough to be entered. The trial is the exception that never comes.
Spirit. The law is proven in souls. A meaning has been held without exception, by the holder first and at whatever grief it cost them, until every soul in the Domain takes it as given.
Fate. The law is proven in conditions, and the proof is a lifetime’s oath never once broken, the days included when breaking it would have saved what they loved. The Continuum registers the condition. It grants no thread for it.

The one they tell · The law is the strong shall carry the weak, and it lives on the Qian plain whether or not Archmaster Liu Zhenhe does. He embodied it for two hundred years and the Continuum entered it. On that plain a bull will take a lame calf across its shoulders and an oak will lean to hold a sapling out of the wind, and when the Ninefold Banner marched in, fourteen thousand strong in lacquer red, every man who struck down an enemy found the man across his back and could not set him down. They found the column a month later, still on foot and still walking, each soldier carrying another soldier, a great many of them dead.
From inside · You are registered.
The Continuum has entered something. A law, singular, that the practitioner embodies and that now has standing independent of them. Practitioners at Principality report that their own doctrine has stopped being a position they hold and become a condition they occupy, and that the difference is not one they can explain to anyone below Stage XI.
Biomes carry doctrine here. The land near a Stage XIII practitioner takes more than a set: it takes an argument.
From inside each road:

Body. The land is a limb.
Spirit. Your conviction is other people’s common sense.
Fate. What you swore is simply how things go now, and you could not break it if you wished.

On each Path · The ceiling stays at V. A law is registered, and the road it was climbed by shows in what kind of law it is. Archmasters are too few to sort neatly, and the Qian plain shows all three faces of one entry.

Body. A law of matter: what bears what, what burns, what falls. On the Qian plain the oak leans to hold the sapling out of the wind.
Spirit. A law of souls and meanings: what a thing is taken to be, what is owed, who carries whom. The soldiers of the Ninefold Banner could have set the bodies down, as far as their arms went.
Fate. A law of conditions: what must be so before a thing can happen there. On that plain a blow struck had a man across the striker’s back as its consequence, and no pull was made by anyone. A Fate Archmaster with a grip reads Weaver; one without reads Drawn, however long the oath, and the Stage gave none of the difference.

What it looks like · A local force of nature with an opinion. This is the first World Spirit threshold and the beginning of the territory the Accord’s Archmaster title exists to describe, and the Concord Lattice records these individuals differently, in a register most Guildmasters will never be shown.
The color is near-white, washed in light, tinted glass held against the sun, and hard to look at directly because the eye takes its saturation for pressure. Light has begun to bend near them: a straight spear looks bowed where it passes behind the aura. The Crystal is Starred, the lapidary’s word for a stone with a star of light caught inside it that moves as the stone is turned. Self and law match so nearly that the Crystal stops reading as an object inside a person and reads as the person.
What it costs · The three exhaustions still hold when an Archmaster is driven to the floor, which the record shows very seldom, and each time it was written down as a natural disaster: a summer in which the wells ran warm, a county that could not remember its own saints’ days, a year in which nothing begun was finished. The standing cost is quieter. The law is now a condition they occupy, and they cannot put it down.
What the folk call it · They are worshipped, mostly, or feared in the specific manner reserved for weather that has taken an interest. The Holy See’s position on Stage XIII individuals has been revised four times in six centuries and the revisions track, exactly, whether the individual in question was in the Old World at the time.
The crossing, lived · The scale is a kingdom, and the accounts are few enough to be read in an afternoon.

Body. A kingdom’s ground answers on one day. Rivers, timber and stone all begin keeping the law, and the light around the holder bends.
Spirit. A kingdom falls quiet for the length of a held breath, and afterward everyone in it agrees about one thing they had never before discussed.
Fate. Across a kingdom the odds on one kind of event go overnight to nothing or to certainty, and the bookmakers close the line.

Bought versus lived · No shelf carries this and no price is posted. What sits in the great-house vaults can deliver the Catalyst, and the Continuum then registers whatever law the buyer actually embodies, which has more than once been a disappointment to the family. The Crystal comes Starred and Overgrown, and until Level holds the Stage, which at these Levels is a long time, its owner is weaker than the title.
XIV · Zenith
Archmaster · Stat ceiling 1,500 · Holds from Level 420 · Mastery to V · Starred Crystal
Catalyst · the practitioner’s accumulated doctrine becomes recognizable to a Hollow Throne, and the Throne resonates. The transition comes by recognition, and no breakthrough reaches it.
No trial can be set, because nothing is being attempted. The recognition reaches every soul the same way, and what the Throne finds to recognize is the road.

Body. A life’s work in matter: a doctrine written in what was built, borne and broken, legible in the land itself.
Spirit. A life’s meaning: a doctrine legible in the souls it passed through.
Fate. A life’s kept word: a doctrine legible in what has and has not been allowed to happen around them. Even a Throne gives no thread.

The one they tell · The Guild sent twelve Measurewrights up Mount Skarn to assay a Zenith, with assay forks, water clocks and a year’s worth of good sealed paper, under a banner and with a band as far as the snow line. They were gone three years. Eleven brought back careful accounts of the attempt. The twelfth brought back no account at all, only a basket of ripe plums picked in the snow above the tree line, where no plum has ever grown, and the Archives has filed her silence with the others, and a majority of the Division now considers it the most accurate of them. Their forks came down still ringing, thin and sweet, though nobody has struck them since. They are ringing now in a glass case on the Upper Ring at Marrowhold, where children are brought to hear them and taken away again quite quickly.
From inside · Something that was already there notices.
Every Threshold below this was crossed. Zenith is conferred, and the conferring party is a Hollow Throne, and the practitioner does not petition and cannot prepare beyond having become, over an entire life, a thing shaped like the recognition.
Reality acclimates. Story becomes law. Speed stops being assessable by conventional metrics, because movement has ceased to be the relevant variable, and the Continuum’s ordinary framework requires recalibration to register their presence as a phenomenon rather than as an event.
From inside each road, by the little that has been said:

Body. Distance has stopped. Where you mean to be and where you are do not differ.
Spirit. Every soul you ever touched is still within reach.
Fate. Nothing is uncertain anymore, and you miss it.

On each Path · The ceiling is V still, and this is the last Stage of which that is true. Movement, distance and effort stop being the relevant variables on every road.
