Body. Matter by law, as far as there is matter. A Zenith hitter does not cross a field: the field is arranged so that the blow has landed. They still cannot make substance from nothing.
Spirit. A Ferryman’s Core at its full: the dead know them by name and the Veil stands open at their word, and still no life comes back across it.
Fate. The recognition itself comes by this road, since a Hollow Throne answers what a soul is and nothing it did. Even here the Stage gives no thread.

What it looks like · Full World Spirit. There is no useful description from outside because there is no outside available to describe it from, and every attempt in the record is an account of the attempt.

The Stage that does not end. Zenith has no ceiling to break through. It is the state of a soul that has reached the upper boundary of mortal architecture and remains there, pressing against what it has not yet become, indefinitely, with no Threshold above it that a level event could reach. Everything past this point is the Apotheosis approach, and progression is the wrong word for the approach, which is a different kind of thing entirely, and the Codex says so in one line and then stops.

The color is near-white with the faintest ghost of the lens’s hue, the sun seen through colored glass, and the ghost is all that tells one Zenith from another. Light bends around them, so that they are seen a little to one side of where they stand. The Crystal is Starred, and the assay forks in the glass case at Marrowhold are the nearest anyone has come to an instrument’s account of one.
What it costs · Unassessed. The Skarn expedition was sent in part to measure a Zenith flagging and came back with eleven accounts and a basket of plums out of the snow, and the Division takes the plums for the answer: what a Zenith spends, the Continuum mostly supplies. The standing cost is the one in the note above, a soul pressing against what it has not yet become with no Threshold to end it.
What the folk call it · The top of the world, which is the fifth line of the skipping rhyme and the only name ordinary people have ever needed. In the high villages under Skarn a matter too large to argue with has gone up the mountain, meaning nobody is going to answer you.
The crossing, lived · No witness has given a usable account, and the Skarn forks are the best the Archives hold. What follows is derived from the Stages below and is offered as such.

Body. The land for leagues taking a set in one hour, and instruments left ringing.
Spirit. A quarter of the world dreaming of one person on one night.
Fate. A season in which, across a quarter, nothing happens by accident.

Bought versus lived · Zenith is conferred, and a purse buys the attempt and not the seat, as the Threshold Trade sets out at the foot of this account. Money has put a number of very rich people on a very cold mountain. It has not yet made a Throne notice one.
The Apotheosis Approach
Stages XV and XVI lie beyond the canonical fourteen. The Accord folds both into a single rank and calls it Paragon, because the Codex declines to number them and a bureaucracy cannot administer a blank.
What changes here. The Crystal is Absolute, and the Mastery ceiling on every road is Ω, where a layer dissolves as a boundary. The Archives have two names for the first of these Stages and none for the second, and every line below is correspondingly thin.
XV · Revelation
Paragon · Stat ceiling 2,200 · Holds from Level 500, and Level runs on · Mastery to Ω · Absolute Crystal
Catalyst · genuine exchange with an Archon or Titan at a level where the practitioner is a participant rather than a witness or a casualty
Neither of the two on record has said which of these was theirs. The three forms are the Codex’s derivation.

Body. The exchange is borne in the Shell: Archon-grade pressure taken in the body’s own substance and answered in kind, matter to matter.
Spirit. The exchange is of meaning: to understand such a being and be understood by it, and to remain a separate self at the end of the sentence.
Fate. The exchange is of terms, between parties, with a being that is itself a law of Fate. Something is given and something is given back. Even this is no pull, and Fate Ω is not what changes hands.

The one they tell · Two practitioners are on the record at this Stage, and every minstrel from the Chartered Arc to the southern pans has a song about one or the other. The songs run to a great many verses, in several tongues, with good tunes and excellent fights. None of them has ever been heard past the second verse. Nobody decides to stop. The singer looks up, the room has gone very warm, and everyone present finds they would rather be discussing something else.
From inside · The distinction in the Catalyst is the entire Stage. Souls meet Archons constantly, in the sense that weather meets a mountain. Revelation requires exchange, both ways, with the Crystal architecture dense enough to hold Archon-grade pressure without collapsing while it happens.
The practitioners who reach it describe the pressure and decline to describe the exchange. This has been true of every recorded instance and the Archives has stopped asking.
From inside each road, by derivation, since nobody will say:

Body. Pressure, carried.
Spirit. Being read by something that can read all of you.
Fate. Being held to your word by the thing that words are held by.

On each Path · The Mastery ceiling on every road rises to Ω, Absolute, where the layer dissolves as a boundary. Nobody who holds an Ω has filed it, so the three lines below are the Codex’s and none is a witness’s.

Body. Body Ω: matter as a whole system, the Totality Architect’s rung. Stat output stops being meaningful as a separate measurement.
Spirit. Spirit Ω: the Core dissolves as a boundary, and there stops being a clear answer to whose grief this is.
Fate. Fate Ω is where the Archons stand, Sovereign across all three planes, and no Stage delivers anyone to it without a grip. Whether either of the two on record holds one is not in the file.

What it looks like · Pressurized white: every color held in compression, as white light holds the whole spectrum. Witnesses call it all colors at once and never colorless, and their accounts fall back on temperature, on pressure, and on the particular fear of meeting something the Continuum treats as a peer. The Crystal is Absolute. It reads as a source of light that does not behave as light should, because what shines there is identity, made visible by sheer coherence.
What it costs · Not on file. Both practitioners describe the pressure of the exchange, and pressure is a cost. The Archives decline to guess which of the three exhaustions, if any, applies to a soul whose layers have stopped being boundaries.
What the folk call it · There is no word, only the songs and the second verse. In the Chartered Arc a thing nobody ever finishes saying is a third verse.
The crossing, lived · Two crossings are on record and the songs about both stop at the second verse. The Archives offer a derivation and no more.

Body. Matter across a quarter of the world answering for one instant as a single system.
Spirit. Every soul living remembering something at once, and none of them able to say what.
Fate. A day on which, the almanacs later agreed, nothing anywhere went right or wrong by chance.

Bought versus lived · The law sets no upper limit. The only thing large enough to stand in for this Catalyst is a blessing from the kind of being the Catalyst is an exchange with, which comes to the same meeting by another door.
XVI · Apex
Perpetual state · Uncapped · Absolute Crystal
Catalyst · holding a Principle in the Soul Crystal without fracturing, even momentarily, even imperfectly
A Principle is held where a layer used to be, and the Codex derives one line for each.

Body. In the Shell’s place: the whole of matter kept in one grip without the grip breaking.
Spirit. In the Core’s place: a meaning true of everything, kept by one self that stays one.
Fate. In the Layer’s place: a condition on all conditions, kept as a vow is kept. No table says what that does to the Layer’s Mastery.

The one they tell · The house of Tolly and Daughters on the Exchange Stair at Altherion has posted the same line for four hundred years, a thousand to one that somebody reaches Apex by next midsummer, and it takes a few coppers on it every season from drunks and one quiet Measurewright. It has never paid out. One spring a runner brought the family a rumor, and they closed the shop, settled every debt in the city and were gone by sundown. They came back ten years later, reopened on the same stair at the same odds, and have never said what they heard.
From inside · A Principle is a truth normally reserved for beings that have completed Apotheosis. Apex is the state of a Crystal dense enough with accumulated doctrine to contain one, briefly, badly, and not come apart.
From inside each road there is no account, and derivation yields a word apiece:

Body. Bearing.
Spirit. Knowing.
Fate. Keeping.

On each Path · Ω on every road, as at Revelation, and nothing further to open. The Codex gives one line for all three roads: the Shell, the Core and the Layer have each dissolved as a boundary, and a Principle is held where they were.

Body. Matter as a whole system, held and no longer commanded.
Spirit. Souls and meanings, with no edge left between the holder’s and anyone else’s.
Fate. The holder is part of what is being pulled on. Uurgath and Urion stand somewhere no table describes.

What it looks like · Absolute white, by the Codex’s reckoning, at which the difference between a soul’s color and the Continuum’s dissolves. What an observer would report is no longer a sight. It is the experience of standing inside a law. No practitioner has reached Apex within the documented age, so the description is a derivation, and Absolute is the Bench’s word for a Crystal it has never had on a coil.
What it costs · The Catalyst names it: holding a Principle without fracturing. The price of failing is the Crystal.
What the folk call it · One more yet, from the last line of the rhyme, and on the Exchange Stair at Altherion Tolly’s line: a thousand to one, never paid.
The crossing, lived · Never observed. By derivation it would show as the Stages below it show, with no edge to it: matter, souls and odds answering everywhere at once. The nearest thing to an account is that Tolly and Daughters once closed the shop on a rumor.
Bought versus lived · Tolly and Daughters will take the bet. Nobody sells the thing.
It is perpetual. It does not resolve into anything. It is a soul pressing forever against what it has not yet become, and nobody should mistake the Codex’s refusal to place a ceiling on it for humility. The Codex has measured everything else in this document to three figures.
Appendix A: The Seat

“Seated clean, and you can hear it. Seated rough, and so can everybody else.”

Each Threshold is a structural reorganization, and whatever is in the Crystal at the moment of reorganization is built into what comes out. The residue of that is called the seat, from the joiner’s word, because the trade took its vocabulary from people who fit things into other things for a living and had no patience for metaphysics.
A soul’s carry is whatever it has taken on from the stock it was tempered with, the origin that comes along with the Essence, graded by provenance Grade on The Standing Index (so “Index Grade IV” below is a grade of stock, and has nothing to do with Mastery).
A clean seat is carry that integrated evenly. The signature reads as one thing. Output is consistent, Traits hold, techniques behave the same way in the fourth hour as in the first.
A rough seat is carry from four Index Classes and nine sources, none of it fully integrated, the signature reading as a chord with a wrong note in the middle of it. Rough-seated practitioners are not weaker. Several of the most feared individuals in the four quarters are catastrophically rough-seated and that is precisely why nobody can predict them.

What decides a seat. A Threshold is a melt, and a melt does not cool into order unaided. Something must survive the heat for the new lattice to grow around, and the only structures in a Crystal that do are Traits, because a law the Continuum has already accepted as reliable does not stop being reliable at temperature.
Seeds that agree cool clean. Seeds that contradict each other cool rough, and the lattice keeps the argument. A soul walking two Paths seats rough for that reason, whatever stock it was tempered with, and a soul on three runs a high risk of what comes next. No adequate seed at all and the melt cools amorphous: the Stage does not advance, Clarity and Compression fall, a Trait is commonly lost outright, and the halls record a Dead Set. The trade word for the result is slag.
Carry, Drafts and rendered stock work by supplying seed the soul did not produce, and at the breakthrough grades the Catalyst along with it. That is the whole of what they do, it is real, and it is why the coil, which reads a bought Stage and a fought one the same, reads a purchased seat differently from an earned one.

The coil reads a seat in under a minute, and everything below follows from that.
What the reading is used for
Certification · Examinations read the seat before they read output, and a rough seat bars its owner from any appointment or certificate above the Adept’s, whatever title their token reads off the Stage table and whatever they can demonstrate. The stated reason is structural safety and the stated reason is true. The Accord has never addressed the other thing that is also true.
Marriage · Negotiations between the great houses now involve a coil reading as routinely as a survey of the land, and for the same reason, since both are asking what the children will inherit.
Everything else · Assay houses will read a seat for anyone with a silver mark. They are the only institution in the four quarters that will tell a person the truth about themselves for a fixed fee and no further comment.
The tells, for those who cannot afford a coil
Folk diagnosis. Unreliable in the individual case, correct often enough to have survived four centuries, and it has ended marriages.

























TellWhat it readsCold hands that never warmIndex Grade III carry off cold-blooded stock, poorly integrated. Holds in roughly two cases out of three. The exceptions are people with bad circulation.The flickerTraits coming and going without pattern. This one has left folklore behind: it is documented Starvation behavior (Charge Starvation on the Body road, Essence Starvation on the Spirit and Fate roads) in an architecture carrying more unintegrated carry than its Capacity supports, and the folk reading and the clinical reading agree exactly.Draft-markFaint discoloration in the sclera or under the nailbeds, keyed to the rendered source. Renderers name the beast from the color with a reliability that embarrasses the Archives, and nobody has taught it to anyone who did not grow up in a rendering house.The appetiteIndex Grade III carry off a predator seats an appetite that is not yours. It leaves a man no more of a killer than he was and makes him hungry in a way he cannot locate and did not ask for, and the eastern rendering districts have a word for it that the Accord’s translators decline to render into the common tongue.
What the coil is actually reading
A highborn heir tempered on entered, warranted, three-mark stock (all three Index readings on file and good) is seated clean, and the visible consequence is that their power is boring. Legible, consistent, well-behaved and boring, and the halls certify it to the Grandmaster’s title without a raised eyebrow because it will never surprise anybody.
A gutter-seated practitioner out of an eastern district is unpredictable, occasionally extraordinary, and barred from every certificate above the Adept’s.

Both are measurements. Neither is a lie. The instrument is honest and it is reading, with perfect accuracy, what somebody’s parents could afford.

Appendix B: The Threshold Trade, by Stage
Which market reaches which Stage, and what that decides.
Two kinds of bottle are sold at a Threshold, and only one of them cares which road the buyer is on. A ration builds Level, and the Level a Stage holds at is shared, so a ration is the same for a hitter, a thrower and a puller. A breakthrough Draft stands in for the Catalyst, the Catalyst is met in the layer a soul leans on, and so a breakthrough Draft is poured by road, on one of three bases:

Body: a Salt base. Raw Aether in a fraction that packs straight into the Shell, parted for the most part from the stones of Body monsters. It stands in for a trial of the flesh. It goes down like a burn, and the melt that follows runs hot.
Spirit: Core stock. Essence that nobody has stamped, from the stones of Spirit monsters for choice. It stands in for a trial of the self, and the melt is cold and quiet.
Fate: the Layer reagent. The skin shaved off a Fate monster’s stone. It stands in for a trial of bond, oath and odds, and it is the dearest of the three by a wide margin and the most criminal, since no bench can tell it from Layer shaved off a dead practitioner and no realm licenses an ounce of it. A Fate soul’s breakthrough is therefore bought in a cellar at every Stage, and the houses that raise Fate heirs keep a man for it.

A soul on two roads buys for its lead road. A Draft poured on the wrong base still melts the Crystal, and it sets around a trial the soul was never going to count.


















































TransitionWhat the market suppliesThe breakthrough Draft, by roadI to IISour Iron Filings and Hearth Ward Wax. Coppers, available in any market. Nobody’s advancement is gated here. This is the last Stage of which that is true.None is needed and none is sold. The Crystal opens the same way on every road.II to IIIMetering Tonic, sold to Apprentices, and Hillcarry Powder, sold to Journeymen. The guild ration begins. A village child reaches Ascension on the hill and the buckets; a bonded child reaches it in a third the time on Hillcarry, and both arrive, and only one of them arrives at fifteen.The rations build Level and are the same for all three. A house that wants the Catalyst bought as well pours it on a Salt base for a Body child, on Core stock for a Spirit child, and on the Layer reagent for a Fate child, in place of the one material, the one truth or the one bond the child would have found alone.III to IVAscension Ration, Accord Standard, issued to Adepts. Issued at cost against future commission, and it buys the Level Flourishing holds at, while what the Accord buys is the term. The Catalyst is a Spirit Axis, and for those with real money a breakthrough Draft supplies it, with nobody on the other end of the bond.Body: Salt base, in place of a load borne together. Spirit: Core stock, in place of being known. Fate: the Layer reagent, in place of a word given and kept, at several times the price of the other two.IV to VSplinter Ration (reserved to Experts). Decides where the fracture runs, and does nothing to stop it coming. This is the single most consequential product in the Standing Index for who a person becomes and it is not available to anybody outside the Accord. A breakthrough Draft can spare the buyer the meeting with something two steps beyond them, and Corvin Hathersage’s hound is the standing warning about what else may be in the room.The fracture runs through the lead layer, so the Ration and the Draft are both poured for it. Body: Salt base, with the riser set in the Shell. Spirit: Core stock, with the riser set in the Core. Fate: the Layer reagent, with the riser set in the Layer, among the bonds.V to VIBreakthrough Draft, at the first truly ruinous price on the ladder. The Catalyst is a decision to accept soul-cost for something, and the halls swore for centuries that nobody could sell that. Four houses sold it before anyone would admit it worked, and the early attempts are in the Striking record. The cost still gets paid.The cost is taken where the base lands. Body: Salt base, paid by the Shell and the flesh. Spirit: Core stock, paid by the Core in a memory or a capacity. Fate: the Layer reagent, paid from the share, in a chance that will not come again.VI to VIIRefraction Draught and Domain Seed Vitrifier. Both reserved, to Masters. Both Index Grade IV. From here upward, advancement runs on Crystal Draw (Index Grade IV stock, rendered from something that carried a Soul Crystal). The lawful article is a monster’s core, worth more the stronger the monster, and everybody in the trade knows what the other article is.The Vitrifier sells the flicker, and the flicker follows the base. Body: Salt base, and the seed rules matter. Spirit: Core stock, and it rules meanings. Fate: the Layer reagent, and it rules conditions. Every stone is mostly Core: a Body monster’s parts out heaviest in Salt ash, a Spirit monster’s gives the richest stock, and only a Fate monster’s grows the skin of Layer.VII to XIndex Grade IV throughout, reserved to Masters and above, procured through channels the Bench grades and does not attribute. The arithmetic between lawful supply and circulating volume has never balanced and no Division has been assigned to reconcile it, for the reason [[The Magic System/The Soul and the Climb/The Ladder and the Draft — Temperance, Advancement and Essence DraftsThe Ladder and the Draft]] gives under the great crime.X and beyondNo shelf and no posted price. The law sets no upper limit, and the Drafts that carry a soul this high are rendered from Crystals of that height or made as [[Materials, Alchemy & Trade/Alchemy/Master WorksMaster Works]], and they sit in great-house vaults, in graves, or in the bellies of ambitious second sons. A blessing from something large enough does the same work. On the lived road Dissonance is walked into, Emanation is emerged from, and Zenith is conferred by a Hollow Throne. A purse can buy the Catalyst for any Stage, and at Zenith a Throne must still recognize the buyer, so money buys the attempt and not the seat. A number of very rich people have sat a long time on a very cold mountain finding this out, and some of them are sitting there yet.
The lived road has its ground as well. A soul that goes into seclusion for a Threshold does it where its lead layer feeds: a Body soul on Aetheric Density, at a mine head or a wild valley; a Spirit soul in Echo Depth, among graves, in an old temple or the house it was born in; a Fate soul under Thread Weight, on a battlefield, in a coronation hall or at a crossroads. The sects and houses that hold such ground charge for the bench, and the price of a season on it is the cheapest entry on this page.
Read next: The Ladder and the Draft, for how the climb joins the rest of the system; Classes and Mastery, for the ceiling each Stage opens on each road and the name the soul offers from Glory on; The Three Paths, for the three roads and how each one tires; Releases and Domains by Path, for what arrives at IV, VII, VIII and IX; The Color of Essence, for the hues; The Sixty Wellsprings, for what a soul tempers on; and The Trait System, for what survives the melt.

the-magic-system/the-soul-and-the-climb/.title: The Soul and the Climb
the-magic-system/the-soul-and-the-climb/.content:
What a soul carries, what advancement does to it, and how it reads from outside.

Start with How Power Grows. The soul climbs Stages, the life climbs Level, the hands climb skills, and everything else is read from those three. Every page on this shelf is reckoned the same way.

Every bookie’s slate from Marrowhold to the southern pans carries the same three chalk marks beside a fighter’s name: rank, Path and color. At the Ox Fair brackets an Adept peat-cutter called Tansy Holroyd, her aura charcoal with a rumor of ochre in it, went nine minutes with a peat spade against an Expert sect champion in red silk, and paid out at forty to one, at a cost of three fingers. The Archives can tell you why she should have lasted four. These pages are how.
The soul in question is the Soul Crystal, and it has three layers, one to each plane. The Aether Shell meets the Physical World, the Essence Core holds identity on the Soul Plane, and the Attraction Layer is a soul’s own share of fate on the Plane of Fate. Every soul has all three, and the chalk mark called Path says which of them this one leans on. Each road spends its own thing. The Body Path works raw Aether, packed unrefined in the Shell as the Charge, and pays in the body. The Spirit Path spends Essence, which is Aether refined in the Crystal and stamped with identity, so it is the soul’s own substance, and spending it is spending yourself. The Fate Path pulls Thread, and the world collects on it later.


How Power Grows The climb in one place, for newcomers: Stage said as rank, the Catalyst and the Level that holds it, Overgrown and Residual Strain, Mastery, skills on the nine ranks, the Class, Releases by Path, the Realm’s three doors, and the old words.
The Trait System: Law, Function and the Forge What a soul carries before Stage, Path or Draft ever touches it.
The Three Paths: Routing, Recognition and the Gate The route a working takes out of a soul, how the Crystal recognizes it, what it gates, and what Fate is.
The Sixteen Stages Every Stage in full: its rank, its look, the Level that holds it and the Mastery it allows, its Catalyst on each road, the Releases at IV, VII and IX and the Realm’s door at X, with the story everyone has already heard.
The Ladder and the Draft: Temperance, Advancement and Essence Drafts The Catalyst and the Level, what a monster’s core is worth, Drafts that give Level and Drafts that give a Catalyst, and why a bought Stage is the door and nothing more.
Grades, Ranks and the Aether Shell The Grade scale things and beasts are read on and the numbers on a card are measured against, the ranks and the Levels that hold them, the Crystal’s looks, which yield to read, and who wins.
Windows and the Sheet The soul’s private report, and everyone lying about it.
Classes and Mastery What your soul thinks you are, what it hands you for it, and the Mastery that says how far your reach runs on each road, with the one yield table and the price of a pull.
Skills and Traits Skills on the nine ranks, the cap on fighting skills, when a technique jumps, Traits read at the lead road’s Mastery, and the few points that are yours to place.
Release Forms The soul’s law let off its limit in a shape found and mastered by fighting: three for the Body, two for the Spirit, and Fate’s One.
Releases and Domains by Path What a Release and a Domain do on each road: the flesh and the field for Body, the line and meaning for Spirit, the claim and conditions for Fate.
Domains The world obeying the idea: the flicker, the seed, the true Domain at Stage VIII, the Realm, what happens when two meet, and what it costs when one goes out.
Soul Wounds and the Menders What a Spirit strike does past the Shell, how the hurt shows and how long it stays, who closes it and for how much.
The Tell and the Knot: Pulling a Thread How to see a pull coming, how long you have, and what the world takes back afterward.
The Color of Essence What all of the above looks like from outside.



The Concordant Crystal: One frame shared by several souls, and what fuses and what does not. A private shelf note.

Back to The Magic System. Next shelf: Power in Use.

the-magic-system/the-soul-and-the-climb/.title: The Tell and the Knot: Pulling a Thread
the-magic-system/the-soul-and-the-climb/.content:
How to see a pull coming, how long you have, what the world takes back afterward, and what the Fate road does to the people who walk it too hard

“Luck is a loan. Ask who holds the note.”
Painted over the door of the Knot-Book Office at Sealhall, where Fate users of the Accord are invited to register what they owe, and mostly decline.

Corvin Ash, called Lucky Corvin by people who had not thought it through, fought the Thornmarket lists for nine years in a coat of green and silver checks, at Fate II, with a grip his grandmother’s blessing had given him and a reputation for winning bouts he ought to have lost. In the semi-final of his last season he was behind on every slate in the yard against a Stage VIII hitter named Brannoch Hale, and the crowd saw him do the thing he did. He went still. His breath stopped on a count of its own. The flags on the list poles, which had been snapping in a river wind, hung straight for the space of a breath, and the dust in the yard settled as if somebody had laid a hand on it. Hale’s pommel nut, which his armorer had been meaning to see to, turned a quarter and let the blade roll in his grip on the downstroke, and Corvin’s point was already inside it.
He bled from one eye, took his purse, and bought the yard a drink. An old Moto woman at the rail, who had watched the whole thing with her tea going cold, was heard to say that she would not ride with that man this week for all the silver in the Concord.
Six days later Corvin Ash rode over the Thornmarket bridge on a horse he had owned for four years, and the girth, which he had checked himself that morning, parted at the buckle. He went over the rail in his green and silver checks and broke his back on the pilings. He lived. He does not fight. The strap had been sound, as far as anyone could tell, and the saddler who made it left town.
That was a knot, and the old woman had seen it tied. This page is about both halves of what she was watching: the tell that comes before a pull, and the debt that comes after.
I. What Is Being Pulled
The Fate Path spends neither of the things the other two roads spend. A Body fighter works raw Aether through the Shell and a Spirit fighter spends Essence through the Core. A Fate fighter who reaches up takes hold of Thread: a strand of what has to be so before a thing can happen, pulled down through the Attraction Layer, which is the soul’s own share of fate. Thread is not held in reserve and cannot be stored. It is pulled for one working, paid for out of the soul’s share, and let go.
Most of what a Fate fighter does pulls nothing. Range, Aura Pressure, presence, a bond, a sworn company fighting better under her eye, a Domain: all of these spend the soul’s own share and reach for nothing above it, and none of them is the subject here. A pull is the rare thing, the reach above, where a strap that was wearing gives on the right step or a cut is made to have always been going to land. The puller’s Fate Mastery measures it, read from Level like any road’s and stopping at II for anyone without a grip, a Work or a blessing. The price table on Classes and the Three Ladders says what share of the reserve it takes. When the halls stopped reading Fate two rungs low, that table was set again against the new rungs, so that no puller’s lean grew a copper cheaper by it, and the two matters below are what the price table leaves out.
II. The Tell
Every pull has a charge, and the charge is a stillness. A Body working announces itself with heat and a Spirit working with color and a cold. A pull announces itself by things lining up.
What anyone can see, trained or not:

The puller goes still, in a way that is different from waiting. The eyes stop tracking the fight. The breath is held on a count that is not the count of the exchange.
The room settles. Dust lies down. Flags and lamp flames stop moving for a moment. A dog that was barking stops. The air goes slightly too tidy, the way a table looks when someone has squared everything on it, and people at the rope stop chewing without knowing why.
Small things agree. Dice in a cup at the back of the hall come up the same. Two strangers say the same word at once. This is the surest sign for the unwoken, and the one they talk about afterward.

What a trained sense feels, on top of that:

The odds lean. Anyone with Gnosis Perception worth a slip feels the floor of the likely tilt a degree toward the puller, the way a deck tilts before the boat has visibly moved. It has a direction, and a good reader can say whom it is leaning against.
A thread drawn taut. Closer in, and to a finer sense, there is a line under tension between the puller and one particular thing: a strap, a stone, a man’s left foot. Fate users feel it as plainly as a rope across a doorway. A Spirit fighter sees it another way, as a strain on the puller’s Core, since every pull is made by a soul and shows there before it lands.

A pull cannot be hidden entirely, by anyone, at any rung. A master makes the stillness short and the settling small, and a Work of Hataraki makes the grip sure, and the room still squares itself. The Moto teach their children to stand still all the time, which hides the first tell very well and does nothing about the dust.
How long you have
The warning runs as long as the pull takes to set, and the pull takes longer the more it asks.

























The pullThe warningWhat it looks likeA lean (a thing already on its way, helped along: the strap that was going, the wet stone)A breathThe stillness, the settling, and then the foot comes down wrong. A fighter who is watching for it has time for one actionA prerequisite removed or assigned (this cut was always going to land, this guard was never going to be there)Several heartbeatsThe puller is visibly elsewhere for the length of a slow exchange. The taut thread can be felt across a yard. A whole ring has time to notice, and a veteran has time to cross itA field (weather, supply, panic, which company breaks first)Hours, and more often daysNo single stillness. A long run of small things going one side’s way, which a Fate reader on the other side can feel building like weather. The old woman at Akagawa was two days arranging it
The counter
Reach the puller inside the warning. A pull that has not set has moved nothing, and a puller who is hit, shoved, soul-struck or simply made to breathe has to begin again, having already paid. That is the whole counter, and every veteran knows it: watch for the stillness, and when the dust lies down, go. A Body Path fighter closes, since the person at the far end of a breath’s warning is an ordinary body at its Stage. A Spirit fighter strikes the Core the thread is held in, and a wounded soul loses its grip. Another Fate user reads the lean and leans the other way.
The other counters are older than the warning. Be sound: a pull moves only what already has a way of happening, and well-kept gear on a fighter with no bad habits offers nothing to take hold of. Be bound: Persistence and Continuity push back against Dominion’s Fate, and a soul well enough anchored in its own going-on refuses the result. And in war, find the other side’s Fate users before the first spear is leveled, which is why both sides try.
III. The Knot
Every pull leaves a knot, and the world collects.
A thread pulled out of true does not go back by itself. Something that was not going to happen has happened, or has happened early, and the slack has to come from somewhere, so it comes later, from the puller, in kind. A strap snaps on her next week. A friend’s sound plan fails for no reason anyone can find. The letter that mattered goes astray. The scholars’ account is that the share of a pull that never arrives as effect does not burn off as heat, as the Shell’s share does in its furnace, or turn to hollowing, as the Core’s does: it stays on the Layer as a debt, and a debt on the Layer is collected by events. The Measurewrights argue about the wording. Nobody who has pulled a thread argues about the bill.
It is kept like a bill. Serious Fate users keep a knot-book, a ledger with what was pulled, when, how far from likely, and a blank beside it for what came back. The Moto houses keep one for each child of the blood from the first pull, in a steward’s hand, and settle nothing important in a week when a knot is known to be open. A window notes it plainly:
[Pull: landed · Fate II]
[Knot: owed · a lean · due within days]

and strikes the line when it has been paid, usually some hours after the owner has worked that out for herself.
The law of the knot

Every pull leaves one. Landed or failed. A pull that fails has still drawn the thread, and the failed ones are the bitterest to pay for.
Its size follows the pull’s distance from likely. Helping along a strap that was going leaves a small knot: a stumble, a lost purse, a bad night. Making a sound guard never have been there leaves a large one, the kind that takes a limb, a ship or a friendship. A knot is the same size as the liberty that was taken.
It falls due within days for a lean, and commonly inside the week. It falls due within the arc of events for a removed prerequisite: before the war ends, before the season of the feud is out, before the business the pull was part of is finished. A field’s knots come due in a long ugly run, and the people who move fields are usually not on their feet to see it.
It lands on the puller or on what is hers. Her own strap, her own footing, her horse, her friend’s plan, her house’s harvest. The world is not particular about which, and the collection has a way of falling on whatever she was relying on that day. This is why a Fate fighter’s friends count the days after a bout.
It comes as an ordinary accident. A knot paying out has no charge and no tell. It is a strap, a stair, a wind. The only warning is the ledger.
It cannot be pulled away. Leaning on the odds to dodge a knot is a second pull, and leaves a second knot, larger. People have tried to run ahead of their debts this way for several years together. The Archives hold what was left of them under compounding.

What does not leave one
A kept vow leaves no knot. A vow spends the soul’s own share and reaches for nothing above it. Hyeon Do-sun at Kell Harbor pulled no thread and owed the world nothing afterward: he had paid in advance, for most of his life, in the coin the vow named. This is the whole difference between the shallow water of Fate and the deep, and it is why a sworn hitter can lean on her oath every day of her life and never keep a knot-book.
Range, Aura Pressure, presence, bonds and a Domain leave none, for the same reason. A glyph’s term and a seal leave none.
What a Work does and does not do
A Work of Hataraki is an inherited grip on one function of the world. It makes the hand sure. A Work lowers the chance of failure, and it has never lowered the price or the knot. A Moto who pulls pays the same share of the reserve as anyone at her rung, bleeds the same, and owes the same, and the one advantage of the blood is that she more often gets what she paid for. The house’s real art is the bookkeeping: knowing to the day what is owed, arranging to be somewhere dull when it falls due, and never, on any account, pulling twice in a week.
Knot-cutters
There is a way to hand a knot to something else, once.
A knot-cutter is a worked piece, small, usually worn: a ring of twisted iron, a cord with a lead seal, a little hooked blade on a chain that has never been sharpened. Like the other gear of the Fate road (oath-rings, luck-tokens) a worked one lends a real margin to Dominion and to Resilience’s Continuity while it is whole. Its particular use is that it can take one knot’s debt onto itself. When the collection comes, it comes for the piece: the ring cracks across, the cord rots through in a night, the little blade is found in two halves in a sound sheath. It breaks when used, and it is used once.
They are made by Knotwrights, the fourth rung of Fate, and by nobody below, each takes its maker weeks in bed, and they are priced accordingly: by private treaty, in the range of a good warhorse for one that will carry a lean and a small estate for one rated to a removed prerequisite. None has ever been made that would carry a field. A cutter takes the debt of a knot no larger than it was made for, and a knot too big for it breaks the cutter and comes on regardless, which the buyer discovers on the day. Half of those sold are fakes, and the fakes are very good until the week they are needed.
The Moto do not wear them. Asked why, a steward of the Kōkan Line is supposed to have said that a house which pays its debts through a servant forgets what it owes.
IV. Flagging on the Fate Road
Every practitioner shows the shared tells as the reserve falls: at half the breath shortens and the aura dims, at a quarter comes tremor and a thinning color, at a tenth the aura flickers and the Trait stutters. A Fate fighter shows those faintly, because her aura barely shows to begin with, and it is easy to think she is fresh. Look at what is around her.

























ReserveWhat a Fate fighter shows, on top of the shared tellsHalfSmall luck curdles nearby. Milk turns in the next room, a die cracks, a bootlace goes. Nothing anyone would remark on aloneA quarterThings start going wrong around her now, and visibly: a bench leg gives under a bystander, a lamp chain parts, her own second drops the water. Sensible people step back from the ropeA tenthHer own name sits wrong in other mouths. The herald stumbles on it, her friends reach for it and get a cousin’s, and a clerk writing it down has to be told twice. The Layer is where a name is held, and it is running thinMaxedEvery knot she owes comes due at once. Whatever is open on the ledger, small or large, pays out in the same hour, on her and on whatever she was leaning on
The last row is what happened under the plain banner at Akagawa. The old woman had eleven years of careful setting behind that day, and she had been paying the small knots as she went, the way the house teaches. She emptied herself moving the field. Everything still owed fell due between noon and dusk, and four of her people carried home a woman who did not walk again or know her own daughters.
So a watcher can tell the three roads apart by how a fighter tires. A flagging Body fighter runs hot: heat-haze on the skin, steam off the shoulders and cramps, the skin splitting in fine lines, and at the end heat stroke. A flagging Spirit fighter goes cold and pale: the colors near her flatten, a word slips, then a name, and at the end a memory is gone for good (Soul Wounds and the Menders has that table). A flagging Fate fighter looks perfectly well, and you should move your chair.
V. The Second Case
Ser Ysolde Marrin of the Hundred Crowns, Fate III, a Spinner, with a grip a shrine’s blessing gave her in her girlhood and no house behind it, removed one prerequisite in her life. At the siege of Low Pennycrown she stood on a cart in a scarlet surcoat for the length of eleven heartbeats, in full view of both armies, with every banner on the field hanging straight, and made it so that the postern had never been barred that night. Three crossbowmen on the wall felt the air go tidy and loosed at her, and all three were a heartbeat late. The town fell by morning. She lost the sight of her left eye and most of a year.
Her knot did not come that week or that month. Her captain kept the ledger open and the company walked carefully around her until the snow. It came at the peace, in the spring, at the very end of the business the pull had been part of: the treaty that would have given her the town she had opened was sealed by a clerk who, for no reason he could afterward give, copied the wrong name into the grant. The error was sound in law. The town went to a man she despised, and she spent what was left of her fortune failing to overturn it.
She is said to count it cheap. A prerequisite removed has taken lives, and hers took a town.

Cost. The share of the reserve on the price table, the blood, and the knot: small and soon for a lean, large and later for a prerequisite, and all of them at once for anyone who empties herself.
Counter. Watch for the stillness and reach the puller before it sets. Be sound, be bound, or bring a Fate reader of your own. And if none of that is to hand, wait a week and stand well back.
Read next: The Three Paths, for Fate in a fight and at war; Classes and the Three Ladders, for the rungs of Fate and what a pull costs; Hataraki, for the Works; Vows and Oaths, for the thing that leaves no knot; and Soul Wounds and the Menders, for what the second road leaves behind.

the-magic-system/the-soul-and-the-climb/.title: The Three Paths: Routing, Recognition and the Gate
the-magic-system/the-soul-and-the-climb/.content:
You choose what you spend your life on. A Path is the name for that choice, said back to you by your own Crystal (the Soul Crystal, which is the soul itself), some years after it stopped being reversible.

The Door Wager of Kell Harbor has been lost and won again in every bracket tavern in the four quarters. Lord Ormund Rusk, drunk on his own birthday, staked four thousand silver marks that no Stage VI fighter alive could get through his four new sea-gates, nine inches of banded bronze apiece with his arms on them in blue and gold, and the harbor turned out in its thousands to watch four people try.
Una Ostrick of the Red Anvils walked up to the first gate and hit it, and every gull on the harbor went up at once, and hit it again, and on the ninth blow the bronze bowed in like a kicked pail and the hand she did it with came apart in five places, and she held the hand up to the crowd and roared. Master Bai Lüxian of the Nine Inkstones stood sixty paces off the second gate in a green robe and wrote on it from there, a line of characters burning across the metal until the hinges forgot what they were for. He shifted not an ounce of the bronze and could not have: the gate came open under its own weight, and he was the only one of the four who never had to touch it. Robin Bellamy spoke to the keeper of the third gate for the length of a cup of wine, and the man opened up, wept, and later named a daughter after him. The fourth was Hyeon Do-sun, a thin porter from the Mahuo country whom nobody had bet on, who had sworn at nineteen that he would walk through that harbor’s gate on the day his brother’s ship came home. He sat down in front of the gate and did nothing at all. The crowd laughed until dusk and then went to bed. On the third morning the watch hauled that gate open for a battered cog with a man at the rail that everyone had believed drowned for seven years, and Hyeon got up and walked through. He had let his mother die without him to keep that vow. One-Ear Pask, who held the book, paid out on three and refused the fourth, and was still refusing it in front of a magistrate twenty years later.
Four gates and three roads. The bracket crowds have four words, hitters, throwers, talkers and stayers. The Crystal has three: Body, Spirit and Fate. A talker and a stayer are on one road, and the whole difference between Robin Bellamy and Hyeon Do-sun is how far down it they had walked.
Anyone who takes from this that Fate is the road for sitting still should ask the levies who marched on Akagawa, twenty thousand spears against a Moto host of three thousand. The bridge they were counting on had a rotten pile that nobody had looked at. The general’s gray threw a shoe on the one morning it mattered. The wind came round in the hour the archers loosed, the third company heard a rumor that was very nearly true, and by noon an army that had not yet lost a single fight was running exactly where an old woman under a plain banner had spent two days arranging for it to run. Nobody on her side had raised their voice. Then they went down the riverbank and killed them, and four of them carried her home, and she did not walk again or know her own daughters. She had given eleven years to being able to do that once.
I. What a Path Is
A soul meets the world through three layers, and every soul has all three, the unwoken included. Each layer sits on its own plane, and each is a different way of touching what is there.





























LayerPlaneWhat it doesThe Path that leans on itAether ShellThe Physical WorldKnows and works physical reality: matter, force, heat, the blow and the blockBodyEssence CoreThe Soul PlaneHolds identity, memory and Traits, and works spiritual reality: souls, spirits, the dead, what a thing meansSpiritAttraction LayerThe Plane of FateA soul’s own share of fate, and its reach into the outer part of reality: what has to be so before anything can happenFate
There are two realities and one thing that is not. The three Epochs stand over the three roads. Aegor built Physical Reality, and Ashura is Spiritual Reality, and those are the lower realities: everything that is, is in one or both. Bara stands over the third, and a careful scholar stops calling it a reality at this point. Fate is everything that flows: every possibility, every idea, every concept, anything and everything that can happen in the lower realities, before it has. The Guild says “Plane of Fate” as a courtesy, the way one says “the Crown” of a very old and dangerous man. So the Body Path works on what is, the Spirit Path works on who and what it means, and the Fate Path works on what could be.
A Path is the layer a Crystal has learned to lean on, hardened by repetition into the way it meets the world best and, eventually, the way it does so without thinking.
A Path is a route and never a class. The bracket slang says hitter and thrower the way it says tall or left-handed, and crews get built around the mix, but what the soul offers its owner as a named class is a separate thing altogether, the Class, and each Path a soul walks carries a rung of Mastery beside it, read from Level under the Stage’s ceiling: Body, Spirit and Fate Mastery, which older books called Aether, Essence and Thread Class. A Path says how the power meets the world. A class says what the owner has made of their life. Plenty of drunks will argue the matter with you regardless.
What a person calls their temperament has nothing to do with it, and neither does the school on their token. Two practitioners with identical Wellsprings (the types of Aether each has tuned to, each a governing idea that changes how a soul uses its power), identical training and identical Stage will produce different results on the same problem, and the difference is which layer the working went out through, and what that layer spends.
What is being routed
Each road spends a different thing, and that is the first fact about it. Aether (mana, in plain words) is the ocean, thick in some places and thin in others, and it belongs to nobody. Only a body can draw it in, and nobody, in any art or any legend worth believing, has ever steered it in the world without drawing it in first. What happens to it after that is the road.





































PathWhat it worksWhere it is heldThe route outWhat the lost share becomesWhat it costsBodyRaw Aether, unrefinedThe Charge: Aether packed in the ShellDrawn in, packed in the Shell, shaped there by the Wellspring’s lens, driven out through the ShellHeat: the Shell’s furnace burning, on the skin and in the airThe body: Shell strain, heat, torn fiber, recoilSpiritEssence: Aether refined in the Crystal and stampedThe CoreDrawn in, refined, stamped, spent through the CoreA hollowing in the Core, and never heatThe self: hollowness, color, memoryFateThread, pulled down from FateNot held. Pulled for one working and let go. The reserve that pays for it is EssenceDown through the Attraction Layer, paid from the soul’s own share, which is part of the reserveA debt on the Layer, [[The Magic System/The Soul and the Climb/The Tell and the Knot — Pulling a Threadthe knot]]
On the Body Path the Aether is never refined. It is packed into the Shell as it came, the lens shapes it right there, and the Shell drives it out. A Body fighter’s fire is Aether burning in the Wellspring’s shape, and there is no Essence in it. The Core still authors the blow, since the will and the intent are the soul’s, but the Core decides and the Shell does the work. So a hitter spending Charge is spending the world, and what she pays is the price of handling it: the Shell is the athanor, the furnace that never goes cold, and its burning comes off her as heat, the fibers tear, and every command to matter comes back up the arm.
On the Spirit Path the Aether is refined into Essence (spiritual energy), and Essence is the soul’s own substance. Drawn into the Crystal and refined there, it takes on the stamp of whoever refined it, and from then on it is a little more of you than there was. The Essence Core is the center of all identity, and the Crystal is the soul, in so many words, so a Spirit practitioner holding a full reserve is holding herself and one spending it is spending herself. What she loses on the way is paid in the Core, as a hollowing, and none of it is heat. This is why a thrower running on empty stops being entirely the person you knew, and why nobody who has been there calls the reserve a fuel.
On the Fate Path no Thread is stored at all. Thread is Attraction Force pulled down, the pull between things taken hold of where it runs above the world, and it will not keep. A Fate soul’s reserve is Essence, refined in the Crystal exactly as a Spirit soul’s is. A thread is taken hold of, pulled for the one working, and paid for from that reserve, the soul’s own share of fate spent out through the Layer, and what is lost on the way stays on the Layer as a knot the world collects later. A vow is the other thing that spends the soul’s share. It drains the reserve like any working and refills the same way, and it pulls nothing and leaves no knot. So a Fate fighter tops up on Core stock like a thrower, and no bench anywhere pours a Draft of Thread.
One reserve, one number. A card still carries a single figure for what a soul can hold, in EU, and what fills it follows the lead Path: a Body-led soul holds most of it as Charge, and a Spirit-led or a Fate-led soul holds it as Essence. A fighter on both roads refines part of what she draws and packs the rest, and the card gives the split as a share (Charge 70% · Essence 30%), set by how she practices. Charge once packed never becomes Essence, and Essence never goes back to raw. A sealed Shell holds no Charge, which is one more thing waking changes. Measurewrights will tell you at length that the U in EU ought to stand for something else now.
Running dry differs by road. The Guild’s word for it is Starvation, and it has a form for each coin. Below a tenth of the reserve a Body fighter is in Charge Starvation, and the Shell begins drawing on the flesh itself. A Spirit fighter is in Essence Starvation, and the Core begins to fray: a name goes missing, then a year, then whose idea this was. A Fate fighter’s reserve is Essence too, so her Core frays the same way underneath, and on top of it come the tells of her own road: the luck around her curdles, then her name sits wrong in other mouths, and at the very end every knot she owes falls due at once. Section XI sets out how each road flags, so that you can tell them apart from across a yard.
Older books sort souls by an inborn bias toward one element or another. The trade has given that up. What gives a blow its character is the Wellspring a soul has tempered itself on and the Path it comes out by, and both of those can be read off a life.
The lens on each Path
A Wellspring is the lens a soul bases its tempering on, and it shapes what each Path spends. The idea stays the same and the target changes. Take Pyreveil, the fire of renewal. On the Body Path it shapes raw Aether in the Shell: the heat lives in the tissue and the blow burns on contact, and what it burns is matter. On the Spirit Path it shapes Essence in the Core and is thrown, and it burns what a soul means and holds, a grief, a grudge, an attachment, and leaves the coat unscorched. On the Fate Path it is a claim that burns its way through: it burns chances, what a thing could have been, and rivalries and oaths catch around the person who holds it.
Every Wellspring has a home: the Wild ones in the Physical World, the Spirit ones on the Soul Plane, the Wellsprings of Fate on the Plane of Fate, and a few, called Medium, at home on all three. A home is a qualifier and never a lock. Any Path can use any Wellspring. At home it harmonizes cleanly and can reach double its effect after years of mastery. Away from home the resonance is poorer, the cost is higher, and half again is the most anyone has got out of it. The cost is exact: off home, the yield (η: the share of a spend that arrives) falls, that fall multiplies with whatever the ground and the Mastery are already taking, and the lost share is paid in the road’s own coin, as heat in a Body fighter’s furnace, as hollowing in a Spirit one, and as a heavier knot on Fate. On two Paths the lens is read working by working, by the layer that working goes out through, so one person can be home with a blow and abroad with a line.
Harmonization, said once, since the trade says it four ways. The lock happens at the Shell, where Aether enters. The tie is held on the Layer, among the soul’s other bonds. The lens does its shaping in the lead layer, whichever that is: raw Aether in the Shell for a Body fighter, Essence in the Core for a Spirit fighter, and for a Fate fighter the claim on the Layer, so that any Thread pulled through that claim takes its shape. A sealed Shell therefore cannot harmonize at all, and a Spirit fighter’s lens does its work in the Core though the tie sits on the Layer and the Aether came in at the skin. A soul holds its one home lens through the Adept years, and a Clouded Crystal, Stages I to IV, can take a second, at a real risk of tearing the lattice. From the Expert years, when the stone is Faceted, it can safely take one more at each rank, which is why the careful halls make their students wait and the hungry ones do not.
II. Recognition, Not Declaration
A Crystal recognizes Path commitment, and nobody gets to declare it.
The Crystal reads behavioral pattern: the consistent routing of power through one plane’s logic over time. A practitioner who has fought exclusively through Body Path mechanics for three full Stages (rungs of the soul’s sixteen-Stage climb) has genuine Body Path alignment regardless of what they claim, what they were trained as, or what their house registered them under.
And the reverse holds, which is where careers stall. A practitioner who has occasionally used Spirit techniques while routing primarily through physical expression will find Spirit-aligned Sub-Stats (the finer stats beneath each main stat) quietly resisting advancement beyond 175 (the middle of the Measurewrights’ hidden scale) until the actual pattern of use reflects commitment. Nothing announces this. There is no refusal, no failure, no diagnosis. There is simply a ceiling that arrives earlier than it should and does not move.

This is the single most misdiagnosed condition in the trade. A practitioner stalled at 175 on a Sub-Stat they use constantly assumes insufficient training, insufficient Essence, insufficient talent, and buys accordingly.
What they have is a Crystal that has been watching them for a decade and does not agree with their account of themselves. The instructors who can identify this on sight charge what they charge for exactly one reason.

III. The Three
Body Path. The shortest road and the plainest, and the literal understanding and manipulation of physical reality: a Body master knows what stone will do under load and what heat is doing in a joint the way a mason does, and then makes it do something else. It works raw Aether, packed in the Shell as the Charge and never refined, so its price is the body’s: heat, torn fiber and recoil. A direct multiplicative bonus to Strike Force, Durability and Lifting Strength, running from five percent at early Stages to twenty percent at Stage XII and above. Body Path practitioners at equal numbers and Stage consistently out-hit, out-tank and out-lift their counterparts, and the margin widens with advancement. The trade is Range and Aura Pressure (the felt weight of a practitioner’s power on those near), which is why a Body Path practitioner has to close and everybody who fights them knows it.
That is the road at its start, and Matla, the Zettari’s instrument for addressing why matter remains matter, shows where it goes, though only a Zettari can carry Matla itself and the rest of the world climbs the same ladder by other names. The novice commands matter as an object, the adept through contact, the master through recognition, the sovereign through law, and the rare Totality Architect as a complete system. Those five are the rungs of Body Mastery (I the object, II contact, III recognition, IV law, V law and wide, Ω the whole system), and How Power Grows says which Stage and Level allow which. High enough up, which on that road means the rungs of law, a Body fighter’s reach is as far as there is matter to read: your armor gets too heavy to lift, the blade rusts in your hand, the distance between you refuses to close, and proximity alone feels as if the world has got heavier. They still cannot make matter from nothing, and every command comes back as recoil through their own bones and Crystal.
Spirit Path. Everything to do with spiritual reality: souls, spirits, the dead, the Essence in a person and the meaning in a thing. It spends Essence, through the Core. A moderate bonus to Strike Force delivered through projection, five to twenty-five percent, and no bonus at all to force delivered by hand. Some configurations take a slight penalty there. That force at range is force on souls, and on souls only. It knocks a soul out of true, lays dread on a mind or cuts a Core, it goes past plate and Durability as if they were not there, and it leaves no mark on matter: the soul wound is the hurt it deals, and Integrity and Anchoring are what answer it. The Shell is the only door into matter. A Spirit fighter who wants a stone moved moves it through her own Shell, as a Body working at whatever her Body Mastery will bear, or does not move it. What the Core can do to a thing is slower and stranger: a line written on it carries the writer’s say on what the thing is taken to be, and that is why Bai Lüxian’s hinges forgot, with every ounce of their bronze where it had been. They hit hardest at range and their force holds coherence across distance where Body Path force does not. Durability bonus is negligible and replaced by precision in defensive deployment, which means they survive through correct response rather than absorption. A Spirit Path practitioner who is caught out of position is in more trouble than anyone else in the same situation.
The road has a climb and a far end, as the others do. The climb is Spirit Mastery, and the road’s own folk names its rungs: a Listener hears, an Answerer is answered, a Confessor reads a soul whole, a Shepherd holds one, and a Ferryman holds many. The far end is Null-Light, Ashura’s own way of seeing, which the Yukari carry as the Zettari carry Matla and the Moto the Works. Its law is that to be known is to be held. A Regard can hold a dying man where he is, or run a wound through its whole course in a breath, and it gives no fire at all.
Fate Path. The hardest road there is. Fate sits above the two lower realities, and it is what has to be so before anything can happen: the law and the construction of the world itself. Before a blow lands, a strap has to hold or give. Before a wall stands, somebody has to have built it right. Before an army wins, it has to arrive. A Fate Path fighter can pull a thread of that down and move what the thing depends on, so that the result turns up without having been forced, and almost nobody can do it twice in a day. Thread is what this road spends. It is never held, it is paid for from the soul’s own share, and every pull leaves a knot the world collects afterward, on the puller, in its own time. Most of what a Fate fighter does in most fights is plainer, and it is described in the next paragraph.
In plain force they take the smallest direct bonus to Strike Force and Durability and the largest to Range, Aura Pressure, and the interaction between force and Domain (a region where the world runs on the practitioner’s terms) authority. Their projected force degrades least over distance and their presence extends across the largest volume. The ground has a say in how large: rich Aetheric ground crowds a Fate fighter’s Range and the radius of a Domain, however well it fills the reserve, and heavy Thread Weight (ground where great things were decided) extends both. Inside a formed Domain, Fate Path amplification can exceed the Body Path’s raw advantage outright. Outside it, Body Path remains king of the straight exchange, which is why no Fate fighter who wants to live agrees to one. The far reaches of the Path are gated by permission, and output never enters into it: Persistence, Continuity, Ceiling, Sovereignty, the Fate Sub-Stat itself, the far reaches of Ward, Gravity, Sense and a bloodline’s Maturity, and at the end of everything Throne, which requires Stage XIII, cannot be advanced below 1,201, and is the only Sub-Stat in the system with no practical upper boundary on this side of Apotheosis.

How each beats each
There is no better Path. Every tavern has a man who will prove otherwise for the price of a drink, and every one of them has lost money on it. Each road is good, each has plain limits, and each of the three has a way of killing each of the other two.

Body beats Spirit by getting there. A spear does not care what you mean. A working takes time to author, the distance is shorter than the Spirit fighter would like, and a dense Shell outlasts a thrown one. Spirit beats Body by going past the Shell. Armor and Durability do not cover the soul, a matter-reader has nothing to read on one, and the Spirit fighter has seen the charge from sixty paces and is somewhere else.
Body beats Fate with force and soundness. Nothing moves the odds on an avalanche. A well-kept fighter with good gear and no bad habits offers no strap to give, and a straight exchange ends before the pull can set. Fate beats Body through what closing depends on: the ground, the gear, the hour, the footing. The hardest hitter alive is no use if the blow never arrives.
Spirit beats Fate by reaching the hand on the thread. Every pull is made by a soul, it shows on the Core before it lands, and a wounded soul loses its grip. Fate beats Spirit because Spirit survives by being right. One wrong read or one spoiled stroke is enough, and the meanings a Spirit fighter works with came down from Fate in the first place.
Stage, ground and preparation decide which of these holds on the day. A wide enough Stage gap beats all of it, and a good fighter of any road walks onto a field already knowing who they do not want to meet.
This is why some Paths are combined, whatever it costs (see section V). Body and Spirit is a hitter who cannot be gone around. Body and Fate is a blow that always arrives. Spirit and Fate reads the thread and moves it. Each pair is somebody who got tired of losing to the same person.
Which layer reads what
The Core authors everything, and the layer it lands through sets the rung. Every working starts in the Core, because the Core is who is saying it, and that holds for a Body fighter’s raw Aether as much as for a thrower’s Essence: the Core decides and the Shell does the work. What it arrives on decides which road’s Mastery the clerk reads: matter reads Body, a soul or a meaning reads Spirit, a condition reads Fate. An art’s Path line picks the road, and a true pull always takes Fate on top of whatever else is being paid.

IV. The Gates
Every Sub-Stat carries a Path Alignment requirement, and the requirement is a pair: a Path, and a Temperance Stage (a rung of the soul’s sixteen-Stage climb) by which commitment to it must be demonstrated. Below that threshold the Sub-Stat advances normally. Above it, it does not advance at all.
Fortitude needs Body at Stage III to pass 175. Alacrity needs Spirit at Stage III to pass 175. Projection needs Fate at Stage III to pass 175. Persistence needs Fate at Stage VII to pass 550. The Stage in each pair is the Path Stage of that road (section V), and the Fate Path’s climbs with the soul like any other. Roughly a third of the register is open advancement with no gate, which is what makes a broadly competent practitioner possible and what makes an exceptional one so narrow. Attunement is among the open ones, since everybody tunes to a Wellspring, while Empathy, Breadth, Radius, Sovereignty and Gravity stay behind Fate gates. Working quietly is open too: a Body fighter hides a working through Compression with no gate at all, and the Fate gate at Stage VII covers only the hiding of a pull or a claim.
The points follow the road as well. Life spends most of a soul’s stat points by what it does, and what it does is mostly what its lead layer does, so a hitter’s sheet fills in Ardency, Vitality, Dexterity and Tempering, a thrower’s in Gnosis and Harmonics, and a Fate walker’s in Dominion and Resilience, and the grant a Threshold hands over leans the same way.

A character sheet read properly is a biography. The gated Sub-Stats a practitioner has cleared say what they have actually spent their life doing, and the ones they have not cleared say what they told themselves they were doing instead.

V. One Path, Two or Three
A soul has one life’s time to spend, and a Path is paid for in years. There are three ways of holding one. Studied is what anyone may do with any Path: read it, learn it, gain real knowledge and small uses of it, and open no gates by doing so. Walked means at least three parts in ten of a person’s practice have gone down that road for long enough that the Crystal counts it. Mastered means the gates on that road have stopped being an obstacle at the person’s Stage.
Each road carries a Path Stage on the card: the highest Stage whose gates that Path has opened. Mastered means the Path Stage equals the soul’s Stage, and it is read again at every Threshold, so a master of VII who crosses into VIII stands Walked on her own road until the new gates open, and a bought Stage leaves it exactly where it was. Walked means it stands behind that, with three parts in ten of practice or more. The clerk writes it Body VII Mastered · Fate VI Walked 35%. Practice on the Fate Path is counted in vows kept and bonds held, and in very little else. Its Path Stage climbs with the soul’s Stage like any road’s, gate by gate, and its Mastery reads from Level like any road’s too. The one difference is the ceiling: without a grip, a Work or a blessing, Fate’s Mastery stops at II, so Fate VIII Mastered, II is an ordinary line on a card.
