One Path is where almost everyone ends up, and the trade thinks it is correct. You can still read a Domain’s terms if you are a hitter, and most good hitters can. The other roads simply are not the goal.
Two Paths cost more than twice as much, and they leave holes. The soul is learning two things at once, and one is always ahead. A two-Path fighter on a given day may have the hands and not yet the reach, or the reach and not yet the hands, and how bad that is depends entirely on who they are and how many years they have put in. Time closes the gap in the gates. It never closes the gap in force, because a lattice holding two arguments does not set as hard as a lattice holding one. On their own ground a master of one road beats a master of two at the same Stage. Off it they may never find their opponent’s weak side at all, because the thing they read in the first exchange is only half the person.
Three Paths is the thing people say when they mean a waste of a life. It is accepted very nearly everywhere that all three cannot be mastered in one mortal span, and there is simply not the time to perfect three crafts. Anyone trying is looked down on by hall, sect and tavern alike. The Kharven say three roads, no house. Anselm Threeways of the Sallow Reach gave eighty-one years to it, died a Journeyman at everything he had ever picked up, and is remembered as a fool by everyone except his students, of whom four reached Stage IX. Whether a being with a good deal more than a mortal span can do it is the sort of question scholars enjoy, because almost nobody can check.
VI. Paths and Traits Are the Same Recognition, Read at Two Scales
This is the part the teaching literature has never joined up, and everything below follows from it.
A Trait forms when lived experience hardens into a statement the Continuum (the lawful fabric of reality) accepts as reliable. It is survived into existence rather than chosen, and the Crystal recognizes it rather than being told.
A Path is recognized the same way, off the same evidence. Consistent routing over time, read as pattern, accepted as commitment.

So a Path is what a soul’s Traits have in common, and no separate thing standing beside them.
Traits form one at a time, each out of its own survived experience. The Path is the direction they turn out to be pointing when there are enough of them to have a direction. It runs the other way too: a Trait deepens fastest when it is used through the lead layer, and it works at the lead road’s Mastery, and the mark it leaves on the body follows the road. Nobody notices it happening. It is noticed afterward, in the shape of a gate that opens easily or a gate that will not open at all.
Which is why Path commitment cannot be faked and cannot be bought. A Draft can seed a lattice and carry a soul over a Threshold. It cannot supply ten years of having been the sort of person who does that, and a bought Stage comes with its gated Sub-Stats exactly as shut as they were.

The consequences are immediate and they explain several things the registers record without explaining.
A practitioner’s Path is legible from their Traits before it is legible from their record. A physician reading Trait tissue is reading Path alignment a decade before the Crystal has finished recognizing it, which is why house physicians are paid what they are paid and why their assessments are not shown to the subject.
Traits that point one way produce a specialist. Traits that point three ways produce someone genuinely capable at everything and gated out of the high figures on all of it. This is the mechanism of Tempering Ceiling, stated in the vocabulary of behavior rather than of stats.
VII. Paths and the Seat
A Threshold is a melt, and a melt cools into order only around Traits, because a law the Continuum has accepted does not stop being reliable at temperature. The melt takes the lead layer first and hardest, and so everything about a crossing arrives in that layer’s terms. The Catalyst is one demand to a Stage, met in the flesh by a Body soul, in a soul or a meaning by a Spirit one and in a bond, an oath or the odds by a Fate one, and a soul on two roads meets its lead road’s. Seclusion before it is kept on the road’s own ground: Aetheric Density for the Body, Echo Depth for the Spirit, Thread Weight for Fate. A bought breakthrough is poured on the road’s own base as well. The Sixteen Stages gives every floor three ways.
Seeds that share a Path cool clean. They agree about which plane’s logic the new lattice should favor, and the lattice sets one way throughout. That is the clean seat, and it is why a soul that has only ever done one thing acts before it has finished thinking, narrowly and very deep.
Seeds that pull across Paths cool rough. The lattice records the disagreement permanently and the practitioner comes out with genuine capability on two routes and the whole of their force on neither.

A rough seat is cross-Path Trait architecture, and this is why rough-seated practitioners are unpredictable rather than weak. Nothing in them is damaged: they are two arguments held in one lattice, and an opponent reading them for a Body Path pattern is reading a man who is also, honestly and simultaneously, something else.
The halls cap a rough seat at Adept on certification. The halls are protecting the certificate rather than the practitioner, and several of the most feared individuals in the four quarters are catastrophically rough-seated.

And the failure case follows. A melt with no adequate seed cools amorphous, which is a Dead Set. A soul that has never committed to a route has nothing for the new lattice to grow around, which is why the practitioners most likely to come out slag are the ones who spent their whole careers keeping their options open.
VIII. Fate in a Fight, Fate at War, and How It Is Recognized
The Plane of Fate is the control of Attraction Force and Obsession Force, the pull between things and the grip that will not let go, and through those two the workings of reality itself: the manipulation of probabilities to work outside what reality already knows, so as to control the fate or predestiny of a thing. All spirits and all physical things have fates, which is why the plane reaches both worlds. The two forces are one substance held two ways. Thread is Attraction Force pulled down: a pull takes hold of the current, moves what it must and lets go. Obsession is Thread held by force, gripped past the working and kept. A held thread will sustain a working that ought to have ended, which is how the corrupted ones are fed, and it leaves a heavier knot for every hour it is held. Most of the Path spends those forces the way they already run. The far end changes how they are going to run, and the difference is the difference between swimming a river and moving it. Scholars keep a long and furious literature on whether this counts as a force at all, and the people it has been used on do not attend.
In a fight
Most of the time a Fate fighter fights with their presence. The room is heavy before they arrive, their reach is long, and everyone sworn to them fights better for it. When they pull, they fight the conditions of the fight. Across a yard you see them set: a stillness in the eyes, the breath held on a count that is not the count of the exchange, the air around them gone slightly too tidy, the way a room feels when everything in it is about to line up. Then the other fighter’s back foot comes down on the one wet stone, and the blade is already there. The cut is an ordinary cut and the wound is an ordinary wound. What was moved was everything the cut depended on, and the one who moved it is bleeding from the nose and eyes, and has perhaps half of what they walked in with. That is the first bill. The second is the knot, which arrives some days later as an accident of the puller’s own. The tell, the length of the warning and the knot have a page to themselves: The Tell and the Knot.
Nobody finds this easy, for a reason worth sitting with. Everything you understand is made of the thing you are trying to move. Your notions of cause, of likely, of what a blow is, all came out of Fate, and they cannot be reasoned into a tool to use against it. A Measurewright can describe a thread for a lifetime and never lift one. Nobody grips it bare, which is why there are different workings at all: each Work of Hataraki is a distinct, inherited way of taking hold of one function, and a Moto child gets generations of somebody else’s grip before they ever have to find their own. A Work lowers the chance of failure and never the price or the knot, and the grips do not trade. The Work is the grip, and the blood is what hands the Work down: a Moto cadet line that has the blood and was never given a Work has no grip, and stops at Fate II like anybody else. A grip lifts Fate’s ceiling to the Stage’s own, and a blessing that grants one lifts it that far and no further. For the three Epoch lines the grip opens early as well, reading rung I on its road from Ascension, the third Stage. The grip never gives the road: a Moto who reads a field and then hits it is on the Body Path with a Work beside it, paying a pull’s price whenever the Work takes hold, and gets none of the Fate Path’s Range and Pressure unless that Moto walks it too, at the two-Path price. The card keeps the grip on a line of its own, Fate Art: Work · grip · Fate rung. The rare soul with no house behind it, like Pell Oakshot at the Saltgate Fair, can win a personal grip once, and “once” is the operative word: it makes one hand sure on one thing, and lifts no ceiling.
And Fate is not empty up there. Most if not all of the Archons are Sovereign across all three planes, and on the Plane of Fate they are the most powerful things that still act there, with Bara standing somewhere above them, and their reach is greater still because they are not merely strong there: they are the laws, and the plane is the law and construction of the world. A thread may turn out to be somebody’s, and it is possible to be noticed. Some of them are deemed greater than others, and Uurgath and Urion are unparalleled in Fate, because what they are cannot be conceived. Everyone has an idea of a balance and an idea of an ending. Neither of those is what is up there.
Three more things hold it to the rules, and veterans plan their whole fight around them.

It only moves what already has a way of happening. Young Moto Naoki pronounced collapse on a sound gate at Tobishima in front of nine thousand people, and the gate stood. A strap that is wearing can give. A strap that is not wearing will not. A fighter with good gear, good footing and no bad habits gives a Fate fighter almost nothing to work with, which is one more reason everyone looks at your kit.
It costs ruinously. Low down, one lean on the odds can take a large share of the reserve and leave the body bleeding, and it often fails anyway. Fate’s yield reads off the same table as every road’s, and that has made no pull cheaper: when the halls stopped reading Fate two rungs low they set the price table again against the new rungs, so that a given puller’s lean costs exactly what it always cost, and Fate’s own price is the knot. The farther a result is from likely, the worse it gets (the price table sets rung against distance), and a working that asks for something nearly impossible will empty a Stage XII soul and still fail. Then the world collects: every pull, landed or failed, leaves a knot sized by the same distance, due within days for a lean and before the business is finished for a prerequisite removed.
It can be contested. Dominion’s Fate Sub-Stat pushes and the target’s Persistence and Continuity (the soul’s hold on going on being true) push back. A soul well enough bound simply refuses the result.

The counters follow. Bring another Fate user, who can read the weights and lean the other way. Be too sound or too well bound to move. Or get to the fighter before the result arrives, because a body at the end of a straight exchange with a Body Path veteran is an ordinary body, and they know it. The pull gives warning while it sets, a breath for a lean, several heartbeats for a prerequisite removed and far longer for a field, and reaching the puller inside that warning is the counter.
At war
A Fate commander works the whole field, on the rare day one can. Weather, supply, panic, the hour a column arrives, the company that breaks first and which way it runs. Every one of those already has a way of happening, and an army is thousands of straps wearing at once. It is a life’s masterwork at high Stage or a bloodline’s art, it may be done once in a war and it may cost the person doing it, and it is why each side’s first job is to find the other’s Fate users, ahead of even their champions. Nothing on the field looks like magic until the afterward, when the survivors sit down and count how many small things went wrong.
The Moto are what this looks like with a thousand years behind it. Their Hataraki is the deadliest lineage art on record, because it treats the world as a set of jobs that can be read, assigned and taken away, and the house’s Hataraki no Sho carries that onto the battlefield, down to the art of moving a frightened army with banners and footwork alone. Their children learn to rank a field the way other children learn sums.
How it is recognized
Body Path is proved by hitting things and being hit. Spirit Path by projecting and inscribing. The shallow water of Fate is proved in the same open way, by results that keep going your way past what luck allows, by the sworn company that keeps its word to you and the room that turns when you speak.
Read what the far end actually gates and force drops out of the pattern altogether: Persistence. Continuity. Ceiling. Sovereignty. Fate. Throne. Every one of them concerns what goes on being true when the odds say it should have stopped.

Deep Fate commitment is recognized by what a soul refuses to let end. A vow kept past the point where keeping it costs everything. A bond maintained across a death. A claim held for a century by somebody who could have put it down. Each of those is a small daily argument with what is likely, and Hyeon Do-sun, sitting in front of the fourth gate at Kell Harbor, had been winning that argument for most of his life. The Crystal reads continuity under pressure, and there is no drill that produces it and no instructor who can assign it.
This is why an army with a deep Fate practitioner in it is feared out of all proportion to its spears, why the great houses cannot manufacture one however much they spend, and why the vow is the most reliable instrument in the world for producing Fate alignment: Fate can attach to an oath, and a vow kept is continuity, performed daily, for years, in front of a Crystal that is counting.

It is also why no Choir of the Celestial Host walks far down the Fate Path. A Celestial’s Crystal is externally anchored, pulling its power from another’s Throne rather than growing its own, and a being wired that way can bond for ever and has never once had to hold anything by itself. The Grand Angel threshold and the deep Fate gate are the same gate, and Faisal spent eleven thousand years walking through it.
Fate Arts and blessings
Real Fate Arts are rare and run mostly by bloodline. Hataraki and a few other bloodlines hold them, some high-Stage masters reach them late along this Path, and the Path stays very hard all the way up. They are considered incredibly overpowered by everyone who has ever been on the wrong side of one, and the charge is fair. Most people only ever touch Fate from the outside, through a blessing or a Master Work Draft: a Fate Essence Draft lends the touch for a price few can name, and it no more makes a Fate Path practitioner than a borrowed horse makes a cavalryman.
Fate is more tied to blessings than to anything else. A blessing need not go through Fate, but most do, because the Plane of Fate represents the possibility of all things. Hataraki can take a blessing back or remove it, which is a large part of why that name is said quietly. It takes two Works, or two Moto, because one grip does one job. The Ladder and the Draft has the rest.
IX. The Unawakened Have Paths Too
An unwoken soul (the sealed Shell) has Traits, refines by the Weathering (the slow hardening hard living gives a soul, without magic), and hardens along the direction it was already being used. Grain is single-axis by definition, which makes a weathered soul functionally single-Path with no waking Crystal to recognize it and no gate for the recognition to open.

A forty-year mason is Body Path. A forty-year midwife is Fate Path. Neither will ever be told, neither would know what the words meant, and the alignment is as real as any registered practitioner’s and considerably more consistent.

The screening apparatus reads Crystals. The coil (the assay instrument that reads a Crystal), the Refinement Spectrum and the Tiered Path all measure a Path by measuring output, and a soul with no output returns nothing on any of them. This is the same blind spot three separate registers carry, and it is one blind spot rather than three.
X. Drift
Tempering Coherence is the alignment between a practitioner’s Path and their lived behavior, and on the lived road it is the structural prerequisite for Threshold eligibility. A soul whose routing has drifted from its recognized Path receives no punishment and no authorization.
The presentation is slow and unmistakable to anyone who has seen it before. Output falls with no injury behind it. Gated Sub-Stats stop moving. A Threshold that should have come does not come, and the practitioner is quantitatively ready for years. Traits begin to argue with their bearer, because a Trait is a standing law and the bearer has started living against it.

Nothing corrects this except changing what the person actually does. Instruction does not touch it. A breakthrough Draft will carry a drifted soul over the Threshold regardless, and the drift goes over with it. A Draft seeds a lattice and cannot seed a decade of conduct.
The orders understand this and the great houses find it insulting, which is most of the difference between the two institutions and all of the difference in what comes out of their Thresholds.

XI. How It Reads
Across a yard, a Path is a habit of body before it is anything else. The Body Path practitioner closes without deciding to. The Spirit Path practitioner backs off half a step and is already reading. The Fate Path practitioner speaks first and the room reorganizes, and the one from the far end does not move at all, and whatever they said last week is still true. A two-Path fighter does one of those first and then, usually at the worst moment for you, the other.
And a Path is read again by how its walker flags. Everyone shows the shared tells as the reserve falls: the breath shortens and the aura dims at half, tremor and thinning color at a quarter, a flickering aura and a stuttering Trait at a tenth, and heat, blood and a cracking aura at the end. On top of those each road tires in its own way, because each is spending a different thing.

A hitter who is nearly done is red, wet and steaming. A thrower who is nearly done is gray, cold and calling her second by the wrong name. A Fate fighter who is nearly done looks much as she did, and the bench behind you has just lost a leg. Her reserve is Essence, so under the bad luck her Core is fraying like a thrower’s, and the careful opponent listens for the slipped name as well as watching the furniture. Soul Wounds and the Menders has the Spirit road’s bill in full, and The Tell and the Knot has Fate’s.

An opponent who has correctly identified a Path knows what the other man cannot do. That is the whole of the read, and it is worth more than knowing any technique he has.

Read next: The Sixteen Stages, for what the climb does to the person on it; How Power Grows, for Mastery and the rungs; The Trait System, for what section VI is about; Domains, for what each road does with a claim; Soul Wounds and the Menders, for what a Spirit strike leaves and who closes it; The Tell and the Knot, for spotting a pull and paying for one; and Windows and the Sheet, for how all of it reads on the line.

the-magic-system/the-soul-and-the-climb/.title: The Trait System: Law, Function and the Forge
the-magic-system/the-soul-and-the-climb/.content:
Belief, once survived, becomes law. What survives the melt is what was always real.

On the Marrowhold rim the neighbors paid Ibbet Lowe double for her washing, year on year for forty-one years, and never asked why. Wine came out. Blood came out. A bride’s shame came out of a sheet the morning after, for a fee and no questions. Nobody had ever screened her and nobody had reason to, so when Lord Hask’s champion rode down Tub Lane to collect the street’s back rent, in a surcoat of snow-white wool with a lance at his knee and the whole lane hanging out of its windows in yellow and rust-red shirts, what Ser Gervase Breck saw was a broad old woman with bleached hands and a wet sheet. He put the lance through her son. The shock of it opened her Crystal, which happens to about one soul in a generation and kills most of them, and she took him by the surcoat with both hands, twisted, and screamed the only thing she had ever promised a customer.
"It Comes Up White!"
The blood came out of Ser Gervase Breck. It came through his skin and through his mail, all of it, in one fine red sheet, and it ran away down Tub Lane to the gutter while the surcoat stayed perfectly white. The man inside had time to look surprised.
She lived twenty-two more years and it charged her in its own coin. Nothing stayed on her. A bruise went in an hour and ink in a day, and in her last winters the faces of the people she loved went the same way, until she was calling her daughter “miss” and thanking her for the custom. The Measurewrights have spent eighty years arguing which Wellspring owns that law, Dissolution’s solvents or Basilithe’s surfaces, and the laundresses of the rim, who consider the matter closed, light a candle to her every wash day.
Forty-one years of clean linen and one afternoon on Tub Lane were the same law at two amplitudes, which is the whole subject of this page.
I. The Standing Principle
Nothing in a soul improves without strain. There is no route to power in the world that does not run through the near-loss of the thing being improved. A Soul Crystal (the soul itself, in the form that holds and works magic) that is comfortable does not densify. A Soul Crystal that is comfortable does not reorganize. Growth requires the Crystal be driven to the edge of its structural tolerance and held there, by breath pulled in at a Core (a site where a Wellspring’s Aether pools, most often at the heart of a dungeon) or on any ground rich in Aether until the body shakes, by sparring and real fights, by a course of Drafts taken to the limit, Salts for the Shell and Core stock for the Core, or by the long hunger of seclusion before a Threshold, kept on the ground of the soul’s own Path, and at that edge it means exhaustion past the point of usefulness, injury past the point of safety, or genuine proximity to death.
This is the whole reason Temperance (the climb of a soul from Stage to Stage) exists as a discipline rather than a curriculum. Instruction can tell a practitioner what to do. It cannot supply the strain. Consequence supplies the strain, and a rich man’s Draft will take him straight to the edge of it, but the edge has to be stood on by whoever is climbing. Where the edge lies depends on the road. The Crystal asks its question in the layer a soul leans on, in flesh and matter for the Body Path, in a soul or a meaning for the Spirit, in a bond, an oath or the odds for Fate, and The Sixteen Stages gives every Catalyst in those three forms under The Climb by Path.
Temperance is a melt. The Crystal is brought to the temperature at which its lattice loses its shape, and it is allowed to cool into a new one, each layer melted down and rebuilt in its turn. Each layer comes out tempered in its own coin, and the layer the soul leans on is rebuilt first: the Shell packs and holds more raw Charge, the Core’s Essence is refined and stronger, and the Layer’s claim firms, though no melt has ever moved a rung of Fate Mastery, which is read from Level. The body comes out gaining Traits (II, below, says how). The new lattice can be better than the old: denser, cleaner, more capacious, more honest about what the bearer actually is. It can also be worse. Nothing guarantees the second shape improves on the first.
What determines the outcome is Traits.
II. What a Trait Is
A Trait is a standing law held in the Essence Core (the soul’s inner layer, holding identity, memory and Traits). It forms when lived experience hardens into a statement the Continuum (the lawful fabric of reality) accepts as reliable, and thereafter the soul runs on that statement the way a body runs on a heartbeat, without deliberation and without pause. The Core sits on the Soul Plane, inside the two layers that carry a Trait out into the world: the Aether Shell, which meets the Physical World, and the Attraction Layer, a soul’s own share of fate on the Plane of Fate.
A Trait is survived into existence, never taught, and a course of Essence Drafts can feed what is being survived without changing that. Tempering both raises the Traits a soul already has and can leave it with new ones, because a melt is itself something survived: a new Trait comes out of the heat when what the soul endured there hardens into law, and the Draft that took it to the melt fed the fire without writing the law. The four harmonics that must fall into coherence for one to form are the Essence Core holding the emotional truth, the Attraction Layer bending recognition toward it, the Aether Shell expressing force born from it, and the Temperance Field keeping the whole arrangement from collapsing under its own weight.
One idea, three sizes. A Trait is the idea. A Release is that idea worn on a transformed body, and a Domain is the world obeying it, so that a practitioner’s whole ladder can be said in one breath, and a card that cannot say it that way is badly written. Any concept will serve, a door, a stain, a bad mood, a ring of keys, if the person pushes it to a terrifying place. The concept comes first. The Wellspring and glyph that account for it come after, because an archivist has to file it under one of the Sixty, which stay fixed, and the filing is usually where the argument starts. See Release Forms for the second and third sizes, and Releases and Domains by Path for how differently the three roads wear them.
III. Where Traits Live
A Trait belongs to the soul. An open Soul Crystal only arms it.
The Soul Crystal is the soul, sealed or open, and opening it makes a Trait legible, dangerous and expensive. The material of the soul makes it at all. A Trait is woven into the fiber of a person’s original Essence, present in the material of the soul before the Crystal ever opens, and it persists in unwoken bearers whose Crystal is sealed and almost always stays sealed their whole lives; a rare few are woken by crisis, a master’s forcing or a tribulation, at great cost, and a Waking Draft or a blessing can do it for those who can get one. See The Gate.
This has three consequences worth stating plainly.
First, the overwhelming majority of people in the world carry Traits. A woman whose bread rises when the same flour fails in her neighbor’s hands, a smith whose welds hold past what the iron should permit, a man who has never in sixty years taken a fever: these are Traits, running at an amplitude too low to register as anything but character. Every quarter has a folk vocabulary for them, a knack in the Common tongue and half a dozen ruder words elsewhere, and every one of those vocabularies is describing something real.
Give the same small law a woken Crystal at the lowest Stages and it becomes a trade. Lamp-wardens keeping a street lit by hand and by the job, ward-cutters, hedge-workers, the cobbler whose heels never wear: petty powers, worked with the hands and paid for in coin, and every one of these people can overcharge you, go on strike or shut the door in your face.
Second, a Trait is not evidence of an open Crystal. Testing for one by looking for the other produces false negatives constantly, which is a live institutional problem for any body that screens for practitioners.
Third, awakening itself grants a person no new Traits: it reveals and arms the ones already in the material. A practitioner’s Primary Trait was there before the Crystal opened, doing quiet work nobody attributed to anything.
IV. The Weathering
Unwoken souls also refine under strain. The process is real, it is lifelong, and it is not Temperance.
Temperance is a melt and a recasting. The Crystal loses its shape entirely and reforms around whatever held true through the heat. The Weathering is the same pressure applied without the melt. The soul stays solid and hardens in place, along the direction it was already being used, the way a beam takes a permanent set under load or a hand takes a callus exactly where the tool sits. The trade word is borrowed from the joiners, the same word the halls use for a Crystal’s seat, and the borrowing is deliberate.
What this produces: a real and measurable strengthening of whatever the person already was, and no capacity whatsoever to become something else. A fisherman weathered by forty years of cold water acquires a cold tolerance that will outperform a practitioner three Stages above him who never spent a point on the cold. He cannot convert one hour of it into anything but cold tolerance. The grain runs one way and it will never run another.
The common word for it in most working registers is grain. A weathered man is said to have grain, or to be set. In Kharven the compliment is that a man has taken his set clean, and the insult is that he set crooked, which means the hardship shaped him and shaped him wrong.
The political weight here is the important part. The elite hold no advantage in soul material. Their advantage is access to the melt. A commoner’s soul can only ever harden in the direction his life already pushed it. A house son can be melted and recast toward whatever the house needs. That is the actual mechanism of hereditary advantage in the Dark Ages, and the houses know it, and their scholars have written a great deal to say it is something else.
V. What a Trait Does to the Body
A Trait held in the Essence Core is a permanent bias written into the Aether Shell’s conductivity map. Whatever goes out through the biased region does not behave as it does elsewhere in the Shell, and for a Body fighter that is raw Charge, packed there and driven out unrefined, while for anyone else it is the part of a Core-authored working that has to leave by the Shell to touch matter at all. Because the Shell is the layer that meets the Physical World, the bias does not stay metaphysical. It expresses in tissue.
The practical result is that a Trait edits the body’s baseline rather than adding an effect to it. Nothing is bolted on. The organism is quietly rewritten toward the law, over years, in the ordinary currency of biology.
What this looks like at autopsy and under a physician’s hand:

Density Traits deposit mineral into the periosteum and thicken cortical bone past what mechanical load explains. Borin Ironheart’s frame is the reference case. The bone is heavier than the man’s diet or labor can account for.
Speed Traits show as tendon elasticity outside normal range, unusually heavy myelination on motor tracts, and a lactate handling curve that does not match the muscle mass.
Endurance and thermal Traits rebuild the vasculature: shunt architecture in the extremities, altered brown-fat distribution, a resting core temperature offset from the population mean.
Perception Traits thicken the relevant sensory apparatus and, more tellingly, reorganize the tissue behind it. The eye is ordinary. The tract is not.
Fate-seeded Traits are the hardest to read on a table and never absent. They show as vascular and neural asymmetry with no traumatic cause, laid down along the lines the bond ran.
Trait tissue does not heal on the ordinary schedule. It is being maintained against a standing law rather than a healing plan, so it either restores itself faster than it has any right to or refuses to restore at all. Both are diagnostic.

The mark follows the Path. The same law written into three souls marks three bodies differently, because the lead layer does most of the carrying. In a Body-led soul the Shell carries it, and the list above reads at its plainest: the law goes down in bone, fiber and vessel, heavy and warm, and a death-house keeper can find it with her hands. In a Spirit-led soul the Core carries it and the flesh is marked lightly. The tissue behind the sense is reorganized while the organ stays ordinary, the body runs light and still, and the mark a keeper looks for is in the nerve and not the bone. In a Fate-led soul the body keeps least of all, the faint asymmetry of the last entry and little more, and the law shows instead in what happens around the bearer: the queue that is short, the weather that suits. The Color of Essence sets the three bodies side by side under what the climb does to the flesh.
A body is a Trait record. Anyone who handles the dead as a profession can read a fair portion of what a person was off the corpse, and a good death-house keeper can do it better than a living practitioner’s own instructor.
VI. The Four Reflections
As Fracture of Worlds, Part Twenty sets them down, with function and bodily signature added.
Primary, the Innate Reflection. Formed from origin, the first Temperance imprint and the lived Path. Always running, never removable, modest and constant. Function: it sets the direction of least resistance for everything the soul will ever do. Bodily signature: constitutional, present from childhood, indistinguishable from temperament until someone measures it.
Secondary, the Tempered Reflection. Forged by trauma, revelation, sustained Wellspring exposure, or a decisive choice. Conditional and triggered. Function: it is the soul’s scar turned into an instrument. Bodily signature: acute. Activation is a physiological event, with vascular and thermal signs, a catecholamine-shaped surge, and a debt afterward that must be paid in fatigue whether or not the bearer is willing to stop.
Inherited, the Lineage Reflection. Carried by bloodline, ancestral resonance, reincarnational echo, or a pact maintained across generations. Function: it runs whether or not the bearer consents to it, because it was written into the Core before the Core had a self to consent with. Governed by Tempering Maturity (how fully a soul has integrated its past hurts), which decides whether the bloodline cooperates or ambushes. Bodily signature: frequently visible from birth as a mark, a pigmentation, a malformation, a structural oddity that runs in the family and that nobody has previously connected to the law it encodes.
Passive, the Resonant Reflection. Stabilized by long emotional pattern, continuous Essence exposure, or deep habit etched into the Crystal. Always active, low cost, no conscious control. Function: it is the atmosphere a person carries. Bodily signature: posture, gait, thermoregulation, scent, and the ambient behavior of a room the bearer has been sitting in for an hour. The cheapest Trait class and the most identifying, which is why counter-intelligence work cares about Passive Traits far more than about Secondary ones.
Compound Traits. Two or more Reflections fused into a single law. Fewer, stronger principles. Catalytic, and catastrophic if the fused law contradicts the self.
Higher-Imprint Traits. Marked by Archons, Titans, or World Spirit Realms. These behave as miniaturized Principles rather than personal talents and do not obey the ordinary scaling table.
VII. How Deep a Trait Runs
The Reflections say what kind of law a Trait is. They do not say how loud it runs, and Ibbet Lowe’s linen and Ibbet Lowe’s afternoon on Tub Lane are the plainest proof on file that the same law comes in very different sizes.
A Trait has no level of its own. It works at the Mastery of its bearer’s lead road, so it runs as deep as the soul has learned to work that road’s substance, and it deepens as that Mastery rises with Level. A law a Body fighter drives out through the Shell every day runs at their Body Mastery; the same law in a Spirit worker runs at her Spirit Mastery, however rarely she lets it leak into her footwork; and a Fate worker’s Trait runs at Fate Mastery, on what it does to bonds and odds. Below Glory, where no Mastery is read, a Trait works at its base, as Ibbet Lowe’s did for forty-one years at the tubs. That is why a fighter who has spent thirty years leaning on one law carries it far deeper than a prodigy who has merely had it longer: the thirty years are Level, and the Level is Mastery. A teacher can still show a practitioner where the law has more room than they have been giving it, and a tempering course still feeds what is being survived. The soul reports the depth on its owner’s window (the soul reporting its numbers to its owner, seen by nobody else) by the Mastery it works at:
[Trait: It Comes Up White · at its base]
[Mastery: not yet read]

A deeper Trait means its four offices (below) press harder: a steeper Bias, more that it Permits, a stronger seed in the melt, and a higher Ceiling. Its Release and its Domain are the same law escalating, and they run at the same Mastery. It also means the Rigidity Effect has grown along with it, since the more absolute a law becomes, the less room its bearer has to contradict it. Techniques work differently, and no window ever gives them a level; a technique simply takes a bigger name when it jumps, and the old one stays in use.
VIII. The Four Offices of a Trait
Why Traits decide a life, stated as function.
One. Bias. A Trait permanently tilts the expression of the stats it touches. This is the smallest of the four offices and the only one commonly discussed.
Two. Permission. Certain Abilities and Techniques cannot exist without a matching Trait, at any Stage, with any instruction, for any expenditure. The Trait is a structural prerequisite rather than an advantage. A Signature Technique is by definition a working that only one person’s Trait architecture permits. This is why a kit reads as one concept with a growing list of named moves: every move has to be something that concept can lawfully do.
Three. Nucleation.
When a Threshold triggers and the Crystal melts, something must survive the heat for the new lattice to grow around. Traits are those seeds. They are the only structures in the Crystal that hold shape through the melt, because a law that the Continuum has accepted as reliable does not stop being reliable at temperature.
A melt with strong, coherent, well-aligned Trait seeds cools into a dense, deliberate, high-Clarity (refinement of the Essence held) lattice. A melt with few seeds, or with seeds that contradict one another, cools without organization. This is why two practitioners with identical training, identical Wellspring access and identical strain histories come out of the same Threshold at wildly different quality. The strain got them to the melt. The Traits decided what the melt produced.

Nucleation is a Wellspring law, no analogy about it, and it has been in the register the whole time.
Coagulatio, the Returning Stone, is the idea of settling round a seed: what is scattered finds one grain and sets there, and goes on growing after the hand is gone. Its flaw is that it cannot choose between seeds, and offered too many at once everything settles round all of them, a fine disordered mass where a sound crystal should be. That is a Threshold, described by people who were not thinking about souls. The Measurewrights file the same law as crystallization from a supersaturated solution, with uncontrolled nucleation as its failure, and they have the shape of it exactly and the reason not at all.
Which gives Coagulatio harmonization a mechanical relationship to its bearer’s own advancement that no other Wellspring has, and gives the Crystalia trade its oldest unresolved argument: whether a practitioner who works the law of nucleation can work it on themselves. Nobody has published a result. Several have stopped answering letters.

Four. Ceiling. Tempering Ceiling is largely an expression of Trait architecture. How far a soul can go is a question about how much structure it has that can survive being unmade repeatedly.
IX. Why the Stages Matter
Level and Stage are frequently confused, including by people who ought to know better, and the confusion makes both look decorative.
Level counts pressure. It is the sediment of genuine contact with consequence, densification counted and expressed as a number, and it moves by any real work: danger overcome most of all, and killing one thing stronger than you more than a hundred weak kills, which is why crews have come to knives over who got the kill, but also a flood night held, a plague nursed through, fifty years at a trade. It accumulates.
Stage counts reorganization. It is a structural event, triggered by a quantitative floor, the Level the new Stage needs to hold, plus a Catalyst Condition, a specific quality of experience the Crystal requires before it will authorize the transition, or the same key handed over in a Draft or a blessing. The Catalyst is one demand met in the layer the soul leans on, and a soul on two Paths meets its lead Path’s. It does not accumulate. It happens or it does not.
The two are held against each other in both directions. A Stage opens only when its Catalyst is met and the soul’s Level can hold it, and each Stage has its hold, set out in How Power Grows. A Stage got ahead of its hold, bought or met early, leaves the Crystal Overgrown, spilling power with no Release to give it, until Level catches up. The other way round is the more dangerous. Level runs on without a Catalyst, and inside a rank that is ordinary, but past the old gates it has nowhere to go:

Stages I to IV, Initiate to Adept: past Level 100.
Stages V to VII, the Expert years: past Level 200.
Stages VIII to X, Master: past Level 300.
Stages XI and XII, Grandmaster: past Level 400.
Stages XIII and XIV, Archmaster: past Level 500.
Past those, with no Catalyst to the next Stage, the pressure accrues as Residual Strain, which degrades the gain of Level and raises Overchannel (forcing more through the Crystal than it can carry) and Backlash (a working’s force turning on its maker) risk continuously, shows in the room, and does not stop building. The soul either passes the Threshold or fractures under the weight. Strain can also break a seal that never broke, which is how the late wakings come about, and it was very likely Strain, forty-one years of it, that the lance found ready in Ibbet Lowe.

This is the whole explanation of the Level 200 wall. The world has plenty of people who can grind pressure and very few who can produce the Catalyst for Stage VIII, Transcendence, the floor of the Master rank and of the first true Domain, or who can pay a house’s price for the Draft that does it for them. Most Experts who climb that far spend the back half of their careers stalled past two hundred, accumulating Residual Strain, becoming slowly more dangerous to themselves, and dying of something unrelated before the Threshold ever arrives. That population, stalled and straining and loudly bitter about it, buying rounds and naming names, is the ordinary composition of every veteran corps in every army on the continent.
Aptitude decides whether a Threshold happens cleanly, catastrophically, or at all. Tempering Maturity smooths the ascent. On the lived road Tempering Coherence is the structural prerequisite for eligibility, the Crystal’s honest scale, and a practitioner whose stated Path (the route, body, spirit or fate, their Crystal works through) and lived behavior have drifted apart will be quantitatively ready for years and never authorized. Maturity is also what the Crystal actually consults.
A soul advances when it has genuinely changed, or when somebody has paid to have the change delivered. Effort alone gets it to the door and holds it there.
X. Foreign Elements and Essence Drafts
A Draft of Essence is a set of properties stripped from an object and held in a vial as spiritual energy. The commonest source at the upper end is a monster’s core, which is in a way its Soul Crystal and is rendered down by an alchemist for the Essence in it, and the commonest use is tempering: the Essence is taken into the melt, and the bearer comes out refined, with a body that has gained by it and Traits that have climbed. Alchemy of the higher orders is scarce, the guilds release higher-ranked Drafts only at prices structured to be refusals, and the great houses hoard the top of the market in their own vaults. The lesser grades run everywhere, from corner apothecaries to smugglers’ holds, counterfeits among them, and the breakthrough grades are fought over like treasure.
Function, stated against the nucleation model: a Draft is an artificial seed. Administered into the melt, it supplies structure the soul did not itself produce, and the cooling lattice grows around a law that was never survived into existence.
This is why Drafts work and why they are dangerous in the same sentence. A borrowed seed yields a genuine gain in Stage quality, and it yields a region of lattice that does not answer to the bearer’s own account of himself. Where the Draft is Creature-Sourced this is the mechanism underneath Identity Contamination: the seed carries the identity it was rendered from, the lattice grows to that law, and the bearer’s Attunement (how the soul tunes itself to what it works) quietly stops matching their Coherence. The bearer acquires a rigidity he did not earn and cannot argue with, because the Rigidity Effect scales with how absolute a law is and has nothing at all to do with whether the bearer agrees with it.
A melt seeded from a vial still produces a practitioner reorganized around whatever was in the vial. See The Ladder and the Draft for the trade.
Old families are strange for structural reasons. Six generations of purchased seeds produce a lineage running on laws none of its living members ever survived into being true.
XI. Failure States
Dead Set. A melt that cools without adequate nucleation. In the halls’ vocabulary it is a seat that never took. The Threshold triggers, the Crystal liquefies, and it sets amorphous. The practitioner emerges at the same Stage with reduced Clarity, reduced Compression, and commonly one Trait fewer than they went in with, the weakest seed having dissolved without reforming. The vulgar term across most working registers is slag. In Kharven: he came out slag. Recovery is possible and slow and never complete.
Overgrowth. A Trait expanding past the soul’s capacity to guide it. Bodily mutation, Essence warping, environmental distortion, unintended Domain (a region where the world runs on the bearer’s terms) formation. The warning sign is a Trait acting when the bearer did not will it.
Shear Break. The Trait collapses, inverts, or turns on the bearer after they have repeatedly denied the truth that birthed it, which is how a broken vow goes on to kill. The most common death for a practitioner who has changed his mind about who he is and not told his soul.
Resonance Fatigue. Exhaustion, a drained reserve, slowed recovery from overuse.
The Flicker. Traits coming and going without pattern under Starvation, the state of a soul run below a tenth of its reserve. A Trait is a standing bias maintained across the Shell, and a soul below its working reserve cannot maintain a bias, so the law drops out and returns as the reserve moves. Starvation has a form for each road, and the Flicker follows it. Charge Starvation is the Body fighter’s: the Shell cracks and draws on the flesh itself, and the Trait stutters with the heat, dropping out as a cramp takes the limb it lives in. Essence Starvation is the Spirit worker’s: the Core frays, names first, and the Trait goes with the memory it was survived out of, so that a law drops out at the moment its bearer cannot think why she holds it. A Fate worker’s reserve is Essence too, so hers is Essence Starvation with the Fate tells laid over it: her luck curdles, then her own name sits wrong in other mouths, and at the bottom every knot she owes comes due together, with the Trait flickering through all of it. The Three Paths has the table of how each road tires. The folk reading and the clinical reading of this one agree exactly, which is rare enough that the Archives keeps it as a demonstration.
The Rigidity Effect. The more absolute a Trait’s law, the less the soul can safely contradict it. Power and inflexibility are the same purchase.
XII. What the Institutions Do With This
The Accord screens for Crystals that have stirred and reports the result as a screening for Traits, because the two produce nearly the same list at the top and wildly different lists at the bottom. Every screening season produces a quantity of false negatives: unwoken souls carrying strong Traits, filed as commons, hired as labor, occasionally lethal.
Great houses screen differently and earlier. A house physician reads infants for Inherited marks inside the first month, and the family knows by the child’s first winter roughly what it has bought. The reading is taken off the body, because the body is where the law shows.
Death-house keepers, coroners and the better battlefield surgeons read Traits off the dead as a matter of course. This is the largest unregulated intelligence channel in the four quarters. A house that loses a practitioner in the field and does not recover the body has published his architecture to whoever holds the ground.
Draft brokers sell nucleation and describe it as strength, and for a practitioner with a thin purse it may be the only strength on offer. A man who has bought his last two Stages is usually detectable by the way his convictions do not bend, and by how recently he acquired them.
The Weathering has no institution at all, which is the most telling fact about it. Nothing screens for grain, nothing certifies it, and nothing trades in it. A weathered soul produces no fee.
Read next: The Three Paths, for the direction a soul’s Traits turn out to point; Release Forms and Domains, for the same idea at its second and third sizes; and Releases and Domains by Path, for those two sizes on each road.

the-magic-system/the-soul-and-the-climb/.title: Grades, Ranks and the Aether Shell
the-magic-system/the-soul-and-the-climb/.content:
The climb itself is set out plainly in How Power Grows: the soul climbs Stages, the life climbs Level, the hands climb skills. This page keeps the scales underneath, the Grade that things and beasts are read on, the ranks and the Levels that hold them, and the Mastery that says how much of a soul’s power gets out. The older registers filed it as Tier Grade, Bands and the Aether Shell, and the old name still opens the drawer.


“Power is how cleanly you pass the infinite through the finite, whatever you happen to be holding.”
Three separate measurements, constantly confused for one another. Level counts how many times a Crystal (the Soul Crystal, which is the soul itself, holding power and sending it outward) has densified. The Grade reports raw magnitude: of a sword, a bolt or a beast aloud, and of the numbers on a person’s card only in the assayers’ arithmetic, never of the person. Mastery reports how much of that magnitude survives the trip out through the layer it leaves by, the Shell (the Crystal’s outer layer, which turns inner power into outward force) for the Body road and the Core and the Layer for the other two. A practitioner is described by the Stage, by all three measurements and by the gaps between them.

A slate hangs under glass in the market hall at Harl Cross, chalked on the night of the Barn and the Clerk. Gerda Holt, whom the Salt Dogs’ songs called the Barn, stood a head over the rail in a rust-colored leather apron, a Glory Expert with Level 198 on her sheet, an Ardency (the stat for how hard a soul hits through the layer it leans on) of 2,600, and, on the Body Path, a Shell that read Body I under the Class name Wallbreaker. Mun Seo-yeon kept the accounts at a rope-walk, had come straight from work in her sleeve-guards, and carried Refraction, Level 190, an Ardency of 1,700 and, on the Spirit Path, a Core that read Spirit II under the Class name Auditor. The slate went five to one on the Barn, because everybody in the Cross bet the first number they could read. Holt’s opening punch missed and took the front off the grain hall and the front off the hall behind it, with orange steam pouring off her shoulders, because what she threw was the Charge, raw Aether packed unrefined in her Shell, and better than a third of everything she spent was leaving her as heat. By the differential rule (below) she wins any direct exchange, and Mun declined to offer her one. She went round and round the market in her sleeve-guards, spending a fraction of the price for every blow she threw from the Core, blows that left the Barn’s hide alone and landed on the soul inside it, and taking one in return that cost her two ribs and most of an ear, while every roof in the Cross howled at her to stand still. What Mun lost on each spend she lost in the Core, where no steam shows: the colors of the awnings went a little flat around her, and that was all the crowd got. Seven minutes in, the Barn’s color began to stutter and her arms came down, at a tenth of her reserve, with fine red lines opening in the skin of her forearms where the Shell had started drawing on the flesh, and most of the east side of the market in ruins. Mun walked up and broke her jaw, by hand, since a Core has no door into a jawbone. Two bookies went in the river that night, and the Salt Dogs now sing a different verse.
Three numbers were on that slate, and the crowd had read one.
Level, the Ranks and the Old Gates
Level is the count of how many times a Soul Crystal has meaningfully densified. Age has nothing to do with it and neither do training hours. It is the sediment of genuine contact with consequence, counted, compressed, and expressed as a number, and any real work moves it: a flood night held, a plague nursed through, fifty years at a trade. Danger overcome moves it most, and killing one thing stronger than you moves it more than a hundred weak kills, which has made a science of the last blow, and crews argue over who got the kill long after they have stopped arguing over the money.
The ceiling is 500 for every practitioner below Stage (one of the sixteen rungs of a soul’s refinement) XV. This is as much as a mortal Soul Crystal can contain before the distinction between practitioner and Principle collapses entirely. A soul below Stage XV that reaches Level 500 and goes on taking pressure gets no more Levels for it. It begins the Apotheosis approach (the slow crossing from practitioner into living law), and the Archives stopped trying to put a number on that some time ago. Paragons (the highest rank, Stages XV and XVI) exceed Level 500: Level keeps rising past it with no ceiling, and the Codex declines to number it.

A Stage opens when its Catalyst (an event hard enough to force the next Stage, or the same key handed over in a Draft or a blessing) has been met and the soul’s Level can hold it. Each Stage holds from a Level of its own, and the Stages of one rank hold close to its floor.

A soul accumulates Level by real work and Stage by Catalyst, and the two arrive on unrelated schedules. The Catalyst is one demand to a Stage, and it arrives in the terms of the layer a soul leans on: in flesh and matter for a Body soul, in a soul or a meaning for a Spirit one, in a bond, an oath or the odds for a Fate one. The Sixteen Stages gives all three forms for every floor. Nothing stops a practitioner from grinding on to Level 180 at Stage IV if no Catalyst has ever reached them and they cannot pay for one. From Level 100 the pressure builds with nowhere to go, as Residual Strain: it shows in the room, water that will not lie flat and dogs that will not settle, it degrades what the next Levels give and raises Overchannel and Backlash risk, and held long enough it can fracture the Crystal. They will be strong, wrong-shaped and stuck at the gate, and their sheet will read as an error to anyone who cannot tell the two keys apart. Strain can also break a seal that was never broken, which is why late wakings in a widow of fifty or a drover of sixty are a known thing.
The reverse case is the house heir. Stages can be bought, and a soul that takes Catalysts faster than it takes Level arrives at a high Stage on a thin Level, holding architecture it has not earned the density to fill, Overgrown: its power spills, lamps lean toward it, its Mastery reads low or not at all, and no Release will come until Level catches up. It is the most common way for a great family’s second son to die in his first real fight.
A blessing can hand someone Levels out of their natural reach, and blessed Level with no Catalyst behind it builds Strain at the same gates as anyone’s. The rich have learned to read whether a blessing carries the Catalyst too.

The Clouded years, Initiate to Adept, are the age of first contact, when the Crystal is porous and half made, and no later years will ever go as fast, because it is still learning the shape of what it holds: the Charge (Aether pulled in from the world and packed raw in the Shell) on a Body soul, and Essence (Aether refined in the Crystal and stamped with its owner) on a Spirit or a Fate one. Everybody on a market street who can warm a kettle is in these four Stages. They are a real danger to a tavern and a matter of no interest to an Archon (one of the fourteen great powers that embody cosmic law).
The Expert years come after the first meeting with something a great deal bigger than you. The Crystal starts to show its character, a signature its owner will carry for life, and tricks start to cohere into a style. On the far edge of them, at Stage VII, comes the first flicker of a Domain (a space where one’s own law outranks the world’s).
A Master is where a room starts doing what it is told. An aura leans on weaker ones with no effort at all, a technique carries the weight of doctrine, and the dogs get up and leave before the visitor has reached the gate.
A Grandmaster has stopped being counted in techniques. They are counted in what their being there does to the land around them, the crops and weather and sleep of a valley, and the Domain that had to be held is now simply how things are in that direction.
An Archmaster is measured against Archons and Titans. Individual combat has become a side issue, and the serious arena is the contest of Domains, Principles and whole lifetimes of doctrine pressing on the Continuum (the whole lawful order of reality) itself.
The older registers grouped the Levels into five Bands of a hundred, Mortal Foundation, Awakened, Sovereign, Mythic and Absolute, each with a gate that stopped the counter dead; the gates survive as the Levels where Strain begins, and a Master is still “a Sovereign” in the North.

A Grade is the letter that says what size of thing a thing is: a sword, a crossbow bolt, a ballista shaft, a beast and the bounty on it. Appraisers say it aloud for a fee, every bounty board posts it beside the price, every child in the four quarters knows the letters, and the bookies quote them like the price of bread. A person carries no Grade, aloud or in a window. The same scale lies under every number on a person’s card all the same, and the assayers read a person’s figures against it in their arithmetic and never say the letter. The Stage’s ceiling caps the number, so no stat reaches a band its Crystal has not crossed the Threshold to carry.

For a person, the table reads a Sub-Stat’s number (one of eight finer measures inside each main stat). The Stage’s ceiling and the Path gates (limits set by the Plane a soul’s growth leans toward) both bind the Sub-Stat, and every threshold in the gate tables and the Resonant Pairs is a figure on that Sub-Stat’s own number.
A Primary is the combined total of its eight Sub-Stats, and the assayers read its mean. Points go on Sub-Stats only, and the Primary is the arithmetic afterward. Eight Ardency Sub-Stats totaling 2,400 give a mean of 300, which sits where a Grade A beast’s blow sits. The total is what the sheet records, and the mean is what an assessor reads. Dominion alone divides by seven, because Throne stands outside its total. The full treatment is in Fracture of Worlds, Parts One to Three and Parts Four to Ten.
The differential rule. One full step on the scale over an opponent in the stat in use wins a direct exchange of that stat without much of a contest. Two steps is one-sided. At three, the lower fighter has stopped being in a fight and is surviving an event.

What a practitioner can pay for a row of this table. The attack-output column reads EU delivered; a reserve is EU (Essence Units, a soul’s stored power, whether it is held as Charge or as Essence). EU delivered = EU spent × η, the yield (η) being the share of a spend that reaches the world, as a distillation has its yield, and the Grade is the row whose band holds the result. The joules beside it are the Measurewrights’ conversion, 1 EU = 1 MJ, and the tons of TNT follow from those. It is worked end to end, EU to Grade to the guild’s joules and tons, in The Essence Ledger, Fracture of Worlds Part Twenty-Three.
Inside one step. Two fighters whose numbers sit in the same band settle it by technique, wits, position and how their Sub-Stats are built. A fighter at the top of the B band, stat value 275, delivers about forty-four times the EU of one at the bottom, stat value 176, and by the guild’s reckoning roughly five times the peak force, and both sit in the same band. That is a real gap and not always a decisive one, because technique, a Wellspring’s lens (one of the Sixty, the governing idea that changes how a soul uses its power) and Path bonuses can close it or turn it round. At its home Path a Wellspring can even double its effect, starting small and reaching double only with years of mastery, and half again is the most it reaches away from home, and that shows up here as a fighter whose row on the table undersells them. A Path’s force bonus and a lens both apply after the band is read, so neither has ever moved the step, and neither counts on the two-step cap.

The Sharp-Blunt Asymmetry
Edged weapons and piercing techniques concentrate energy into smaller contact areas, producing higher local pressures than blunt-force equivalents at the same total energy yield.
A swordsman in the F band delivering 0.2 MN of force through a blade edge contacting roughly one square millimeter produces a local pressure of 200 GPa, exceeding the compressive strength of virtually all natural and most Essence-reinforced materials of that weight. The same 0.2 MN delivered through a fist contacting one hundred square centimeters produces 20 MPa, sufficient to crack stone but not to bisect steel.
The Continuum tracks total energy for comparison on the scale but tracks local pressure for material interaction. The ratio is ten thousand to one at any force, which is why a swordsman can cut through materials that a brawler with the same numbers can only dent, and why the brawler can shatter structures that the swordsman can only slice.
Overchannel Spikes

The rows above are sustainable output. An overchannel, forcing the Crystal past its safe ceiling, can spike Strike Force and Lifting Strength to two to five times that for a moment, depending on the Ardency Overchannel Sub-Stat’s number and how much Crystal Fracture the fighter is willing to risk.
It always bills. Every overchannel leaves structural damage that must be healed by rest, alchemy or the next Threshold, and a fighter who makes a habit of it builds up fractures that eventually stay. Some fractures become architectural features. Most become liabilities.

The three-copper bolt. A crossbow bolt is the cheapest thing in the world that can kill a high-Stage fighter in a room, because a fighter’s speed, read on the scale, meets it against the fixed threat Grade every missile carries by its kind (sling stone, hunting arrow, war-bow shaft, crossbow bolt, ballista bolt, a worked missile taking its maker’s Grade) and because reinforcement, the aura coat a fighter trusts to stop it, goes out on anyone asleep, drugged or surprised. Margrave Ulf Stavang, a Master of Stage VIII and the terror of three rivers, died at his own daughter’s wedding from one bolt out of the musicians’ gallery, loosed by a boy paid six coppers, because he was looking at his daughter. The Reaction table above promises a reading of the loose. It has never promised that you will be looking.

The Sheet and the Window
Everyone in the trade has a sheet, whether or not they have ever seen it written out.
A window is the soul reporting its numbers to its owner in their own tongue. The Soul Crystal is the soul and the Continuum measures it, so the report is simply there when the owner looks, and no one else can see it. Scholars argue about who built it, and a Measurewright will tell you nobody did. A window shows a few figures, percentages, bars, Level and the ranks of skills, and never a letter: the soul has never once graded its owner like a sword. It shows no EU, AU/s or yield, the assayers’ figures set out further down this page, and it has never once told anyone the state of their wounds in a way that made them feel better.
A normal look shows the Eight Primaries with their totals, and a Sub-Stat appears when it is used or when it moves. The full sixty-four remain there to study for anyone with the patience. This one is the Clerk’s, on the evening of the Harl Cross market:

The last line is the reserve, and it is named for what fills it: Essence on a Spirit-led soul like the Clerk’s, Charge on a Body-led one like the Barn’s. A Fate-led soul’s bar reads Essence too, because Thread is never stored and what a Fate worker holds is refined like a Spirit worker’s.
Life spends most of the points. What you do raises those stats, and what you do is mostly what your lead layer does, so a hitter’s points pile up in Ardency, Vitality, Dexterity and Tempering, a thrower’s in Gnosis and Harmonics, and a Fate walker’s in Dominion and Resilience. A few points are yours to place at each Stage, and the grant a Threshold hands over leans the same way as the road. That is why a cobbler’s son and a duke’s son with the same Level read so differently and why a sheet read properly is a biography. Race and lineage show on the sheet and shape base stats and what comes easily, and that goes for classes and suitable Wellsprings too. Skills rise with use and show on the nine ranks, Initiate to Paragon: every practitioner has them, from Footwork to Appraisal to Rendering, and techniques are named things done with them. Drafts, runes, tags and chants are all skills and trades of this kind, open to anyone who will put in the years, though all but the pouring want a woken Crystal. Traits have no levels, and read at the lead Path’s Mastery. Techniques show no level and take a bigger name when they jump. A blessing gets its own line, and since the giver wrote that line, it can lie.
A window speaks only to its owner. Reading anybody else is the work of a stronger Gnosis Perception against a weaker Resilience Ward; everything else is an estimate said aloud, and people can hide or fake what they show. Instruments read everyone. Monsters are on the same scale: a monster has a Stage, a Level and a lean toward one Path underneath, gains its Levels by killing and changes form at its own thresholds, and the boards know it by its Grade, the same letter a sword carries, posted beside the bounty, as the Bestiary sets out. So a monster has Pressure like anything else at its height, a Path, and Mastery on it. How it lives sets the Path, and the kind of its Wellspring only leans it: a thing that hunts by weight and hide is a Body monster whatever it was born beside. A famous one can show a Release. None takes a class, since a class is what a soul says about a life it has thought over. A weak reader gets question marks where the numbers should be, usually at the moment it matters most.

Titles and this table. The nine titles, Initiate through Paragon, are the same nine words as the ranks of the Stages, the same in every guild, and they grade trust in that trade, earned by commissions: a merchant may deal up to his, a craftsman make up to hers, an adventurer take bounties up to the Grade the Accord allows the title. Fighting guilds also ask the title’s own rank in Stage, so a Journeyman’s token on a fighter needs Stage III behind it, and only there does a title also tell you how dangerous someone is. A Grandmaster merchant may not be able to throw a punch.

The Aether Shell and Mastery
Where the Stage measures the refinement of the whole Crystal, each layer tempered in its own coin (the Shell packing and holding more raw Charge, the Essence Core, the inner layer of identity, memory and Traits, refining its Essence, the Attraction Layer firming its claim), and the Grade scale measures raw magnitude, Body Mastery measures how cleanly the Aether Shell conducts power outward into matter. What it conducts is raw Aether: on the Body Path the Shell holds it unrefined as the Charge, the Wellspring’s lens shapes it there, and it leaves by the same door. It is the Shell’s transparency, and that transparency is how strong a person’s influence on the physical world is: of what the Essence Core intends, the share that actually arrives. The Shell is also the only door into matter that a soul has, so a Spirit worker who wants a stone moved moves it through their own Shell, at whatever Body Mastery they have, which for a soul that has never walked or studied the Body road reads nothing at all. The Core and the Layer carry their Mastery on the same table, set out below. Beside all three, and no part of any of them, sits the name.
The Class the Soul Offers
At Glory, with the first rung of Mastery, the soul offers its owner a named class that fits how they have lived. The name arrives on the window, and it is usually a remark on the owner: Wallbreaker, Auditor, Ferryman, Gravedigger’s Friend, Last Man Standing. Each offer brings one move that fits the name and a lean on where life will spend the person’s stat points from then on. Some classes are shared by thousands, every hedge-rank Wallbreaker in the four quarters having roughly the same shoulders, and some have been held by exactly one person in the history of the Archives. The offer comes through the lead layer, so it carries the flavor of the road: the Shell offers names about what a person did to matter, the Core names about what they came to know or carry, the Layer names about what they kept and what they are owed. The Barn was offered Wallbreaker and the Clerk Auditor, and nobody at Harl Cross needed that explained. Surprises are allowed, and the Archives hold a Body-led drayman of forty years’ standing whose soul offered him Witness, to his lasting annoyance.
It evolves when the lead Mastery rises. Each time the rung of the person’s lead road climbs, the class is offered again in a form chosen from what they actually did with the last one, so two Auditors on the second rung can come out on the third as a Reckoner and a Debt Collector, and a soul with a false account of itself will find the window declining to share that account. The class has no numbers of its own. The rungs belong to Mastery, and from Glory they set the yield (η, the share of each spend that arrives as effect) for whatever goes out through each layer: the name changes, and the share that arrives follows the layer. Classes and Mastery has the whole of it.
The one wild concept stays the person’s own. A class is what the soul says about a life. A concept is what the person decided to do about it, and the class gets no vote on that: a Stage VII Auditor may well fight with soup. Cooks and Measurewrights will both tell you the two sometimes lean together, and the songs mix them up constantly.
Scholars of a certain age still score a Shell by a sum they call the Aether Index, conductivity against purity with something added for how long it holds, and it is a fine way to pass a winter, since nothing on any sheet has ever read it.
