From Level 260, at Realization at the earliest.Negligible. Precision exceeds baseline stat valuesV · RadiantThe world-bending Shell. Aether bends toward the bearer. Currents curve around their presence. They can stabilize Realmgates (standing doorways between Realms), hold Domains against collapse, and speak Parun (the root script of law that reality reads) motifs into matter. The line between intention and environment begins to blur. From Level 340, a Grandmaster at Emanation at the earliest.Output begins exceeding what the raw numbers suggestInvertedAny rung held inside out. Polarity reverses. Instead of emitting, the Shell devours, remembers, and reflects. Inverted conductors channel absence, silence, and negation without erasing themselves. They interface most directly with Nihiloth, Vantabriel and the other Wellsprings of absence, and with Titanic depths. A mark beside the rung, never a rung: Body IV Inverted. The old books called it Voidic and numbered it sixth.Qualitatively different. Their Ardency does not deal damage. It removes thingsΩ · AbsoluteThe threshold Shell. The Aether Shell dissolves as a distinct boundary. Being and Continuum interpenetrate. Every fragment of the self conducts law with minimal deviation. Paragon, Absolute Crystal. Archons, Titans, and World Spirits who have crossed the Apotheosis Threshold exist at this clarity.Stat output is no longer meaningful as a separate measurement

The interaction is not linear. The jump from rung II to rung III produces the largest single improvement in stat-to-output fidelity. Holding a rung Inverted produces the most dramatic qualitative shift, from conventional force expression to inverted, negation-based expression. Ω produces output the stat system can no longer meaningfully track.

The Same Rungs on the Other Two Roads
The Shell is one layer of three, and the Core and the Layer read on the same rungs, I to V and Ω, from the same Level, under the same ceilings. Spirit Mastery is the Essence Core and a person’s influence on spiritual reality. Fate Mastery is the Attraction Layer and how much of Fate they can pull down and hold. Any of them can be held Inverted.






















































RungBody (matter)Spirit (souls and meanings)Fate (odds and conditions)Yield (η)IMuridic: the objectListener: hearsTouched: a lean0.60 to 0.70IIHarmonic: by contactAnswerer: is answeredDrawn: a lean, held0.75 to 0.85IIIResonant: by recognitionConfessor: reads whollySpinner: a prerequisite0.90 to 0.95IVLuminous: by lawShepherd: holdsKnotwright: a prerequisite, sureabout 0.97VRadiant: by law, wideFerryman: holds manyWeaver: a field1.00 and aboveΩAbsolute: the whole systemAbsolute: all of itAbsolute: all of itno longer a measurement
One table sets the yield on all three roads, read from the Mastery of the Path a working lands through. What becomes of the lost share follows the road: heat in the Shell, a hollowing in the Core, a knot on the Layer. Fate has one hard limit: without a grip on the thread it stops at II, however long the soul lives, and a grip is a Work or a blessing. A grip lifts the ceiling to the Stage’s, and no further. A Walked second Path reads a rung behind the lead until it is mastered, and a Studied one two behind, stopping at II. Classes and Mastery has what each rung can do on each road.
What Clears a Shell
The rung is read from Level, and nobody climbs it on purpose. For a Body-led soul the work is the Charge itself, packed, shaped, driven out and paid for in recoil year on year, and every hard year of it is Level. For anyone else the Shell clears as the life does. The halls still teach four older roads to a clearer Shell, and the Archives now count what each does as Level, as lenses, or as the state of the Crystal, never as a rung handed over. A Body fighter may take them too. Each step removes interference: ego noise, denial, unprocessed fracture, clinging to false narratives.

Temperance Refinement gradual clarity through discipline and self-confrontation. The most common and safest path. A Threshold tempers each layer in its own coin, the lead layer first and hardest, and the Shell comes out of the melt able to pack and hold more than it went in with, whichever layer led.
Wellspring Baptism deep immersion in a Wellspring’s Aether, usually at a Core (a site where that Aether pools), forcibly realigning the Shell’s resonance. Potent, perilous, often irreversible.
Aether Forge Rites Mechanica (forbidden working that takes power without lawful consent) and ritual that widen conductivity or restructure the Shell directly, sometimes at the cost of memory, autonomy, or Essence stability.
Higher Resonance Infusion alignment with Archonic principle, Titanic depth, or world-bearing law that rewrites the Shell from above, a blessing being the commonest way to receive one.

Variants and Anomalies

Rot-Born Conductors channel Aether through damaged or corrupted Shells. Output can be immense, but each working corrodes the lattice further. Every stat expression carries a hidden cost in Crystal integrity.
Synthetic Aetherics bear worked or grafted Shells. They may read a rung above what their Level should give for a while, yet suffer accelerated decay, instability, or identity drift. Their Shell can outpace their Core’s actual Temperance by a dangerous margin.
Split-Shell Entities possess dual polarity, luminous and voidic channels braided through one soul. Capable of rare paradoxical feats but prone to fracture, inversion, or self-annihilation. May read one rung plain and Inverted at once.

The older registers kept three separate ladders here, Aether Class, Essence Class and Thread Class, each Ø to Ω with a sixth lateral rung; they are Mastery now, and their rung names are the folk names above.
The Crystal’s Looks
THE SOUL CRYSTALThree layers, one for each plane; every soul has all three, and a Path is the one it leans onAttraction LayerFate Path · Plane of FateBonds, oaths, Domains: its own share of fate.A harmonization’s tie is held here.Fate Mastery sets the yield through this layer.Aether ShellBody Path · Physical WorldThe skin power passes through on the way out.Harmonization locks here, as Aether enters.Body Mastery sets the yield through this layer.Essence CoreSpirit Path · Soul PlaneIdentity, memory and Traits: the soul’s ownstanding law. It authors every working.Spirit Mastery sets the yield through this layer.Yield (η), the share of a spend that arrives, reads from the Mastery of the Path in use.

“To refine the soul is to remove everything that was never truly part of the design, and polish has nothing to do with it.”

The Crystal is the soul, and it has a look: what the whole stone has grown into, seen by anyone who can see a soul, in the jewelers’ words. Each Threshold melts the layers down and rebuilds them, the layer the soul leans on first and hardest, and each is tempered in its own coin: the Shell comes out packing and holding more raw Charge, the Core’s Essence comes out more finely refined, and the Layer’s claim comes out firmer. The look follows the Stage. It is a description, nobody climbs it, and a bought Stage takes its look the day the Draft goes down. What tells on a bought Stage is the Crystal’s state: a house heir who drank his way to Transcendence has a Fire Crystal that spills light it cannot gather, Overgrown, and it is a good part of what the coil means when it reads his seat.





























LayerPlaneWhat it doesThe Path that leans on itAether ShellThe Physical WorldMeets matter: the blow, the block, the weight, the heatBodyEssence CoreThe Soul PlaneHolds identity, memory and Traits, and authors what a working isSpiritAttraction LayerThe Plane of FateA soul’s own share of fate: its bonds, its oaths, its claims and its odds, and its reach toward what has to be so before anything can happenFate
Every soul has all three layers, the unwoken included, and a Path is the one its Crystal has learned to lean on. Essence is Aether refined in the Crystal and stamped with identity. The Core is the center of identity and the Crystal is the soul, so Essence is the soul’s own substance, and spending it is spending yourself. That is the Spirit Path’s bill, and a vow’s. The Charge a Body fighter holds is Aether that never went through the refining, packed raw in the Shell, so spending it is spending the world, and the body pays for the handling. Thread is held by nobody: a Fate worker pulls it down through the Attraction Layer one working at a time and pays from the soul’s own share, which is part of the reserve. A Fate-led soul refines its Aether into Essence as a Spirit one does, and that Essence is what its pulls and its vows are paid in. The Core still authors all three, since the will, the intent and the lens come from the soul whichever layer does the work.













































LookConditionStagesSeedSealed and silent. Precedes all awakening. The Crystal exists but has not yet opened. The soul is fully furnished all the same and continues to refine by the Weathering, which is why the great majority of the world’s Traits sit in bodies that will never be screened.The unwokenCloudedThe Crystal has opened and begun to circulate what it draws. Traits that were already present in the soul become armed, expressible, and expensive, in the Core, which is where they were sitting all along. The layer that works first is the one the soul leans on: the Shell packing its first Charge on a Body soul, the Core refining its first Essence on a Spirit or a Fate one. A Wellspring can be harmonized this early, at a real risk of tearing the lattice.Initiate to Adept · Stages I–IVFacetedThe three layers have found a recurring rhythm. Essence, Aether, and Attraction circulate in a pattern the Continuum can read consistently. Wellspring harmonization becomes safe: from here the lattice takes a lens without tearing. By Refraction the Crystal self-conducts, power moves in it even in silence, and its resonance signature becomes a permanent feature of the Continuum’s local accounting.Expert · Stages V–VIIFireThe Attraction Layer (the Crystal’s layer that holds bonds, vows and Domains) gains territorial durability. The first true Domain becomes possible. The Crystal’s existence exerts topological pressure on its surroundings.Master · Stages VIII–XFlawlessTrait law and Domain law begin to be the same law. The Crystal has gone past being a container for power and become a generator of local metaphysical conditions.Grandmaster · Stages XI–XIIStarredSelf and law correspond with near-perfect precision. The Crystal becomes an exact instrument of identity. Thought carries causal weight.Archmaster · Stages XIII–XIVAbsoluteThe Crystal dissolves as a distinct boundary between self and Continuum. Being and law interpenetrate.Paragon · Stages XV–XVI
The names are a jeweler’s, each for what a reader sees in the stone: a seed, a stone full of cloud, one that has taken faces, one that splits light into color, one with nothing in it under any glass, one with a star caught inside, and one that is all light. Old books, songs and assay slips call the first of them Dormant, Awakened, Harmonic, Resonant, Radiant, Sovereign and the Crystallized Soul, and the Measurewrights retired those because Harmonic, Resonant and Radiant are also the folk names of Body Mastery’s rungs and Awakened and Sovereign were also old Bands. The jewelers once kept a Clear look between Faceted and Fire as well; a Refraction soul reads Faceted now, and an old slip that says Clear means the same.
What a look is from outside. The aura is the look at arm’s length. Its hue is the Wellspring’s and never changes with the climb; its clarity is the look’s, smoke at Clouded, clearing through Faceted, throwing its own light at Fire, and bending the daylight around it by Starred. Where it sits is the Path’s: on the skin like heat-haze for the Body, a half-step off the body for the Spirit, and hardly anywhere for Fate. The Color of Essence sets Stage, look, clarity, aura and body side by side.
Crystal States
Separate from the look. A Crystal of any look can occupy any of these.
Fractured · split by contradiction or strain. The Core leaks, the Shell destabilizes, the Layer weakens. Thought becomes difficult to trust. Can heal through Temperance advancement, alchemical treatment, or the integration of fracture into architectural feature, which is the Dissonance path.
Refined · balanced and coherent. Essence moves in rhythm, Aether conducts cleanly, Attraction Force binds without overreach. The standard healthy state, and rarer among veterans than the recruiting bills on the tavern doors suggest.
Overgrown · a Stage held under its Level. Power spills outward, emotions distort nearby space, the soul wounds its own surroundings, Mastery reads low or not at all, and no Release will come until Level reaches the Stage’s hold. Whether the Stage was bought by a great house or met early by a prodigy makes no difference: the heir and the prodigy are the same case.
Crystallized, which old slips sometimes enter as a fourth State, is not one. It is the old name of the Starred look, and self-as-law belongs to that look alone.
Reserve, Rate, and Yield
Nobody’s reserve refills out of thin air, thin air being precisely the trouble. Every practitioner draws Aether (mana, in the plainer books) in from the ground they stand on, and nobody on any road has ever worked a grain of it they did not first pull inside, whatever the songs about wind-callers say. So where you stand matters: rich ground fills you faster and thin ground starves you. The scholar’s term for the richness is Aetheric Density, and a sect that holds a rich valley will fight for it like a fair crowd holding the good bench. A Wellspring site, a Core in common speech (no relation to the Essence Core inside the Crystal), mostly lies at the heart of a dungeon. A worked Core is a dungeon someone cleared and now holds: it recharges and has keepers, and its keepers can close it. The old counter to anybody with a large reserve and a long fight ahead of them is therefore to take the fight off rich ground and onto salted, bled or thin ground, and let the figures below do the work.
Density fills every reserve, since every road draws Aether. Two other readings of the ground matter to two of the roads, and The Three Grounds has them in full. Echo Depth (graveyards, temples, old homes thick with memory) raises the yield of Spirit workings, and Thread Weight (battlefields, coronation halls, crossroads) raises it for Fate pulls, each by a tenth to the band, exactly as Density does for what leaves by the Shell. The three do not all pull one way. Rich Aetheric ground still crowds a Fate fighter’s Range and the radius of a Domain, the air being too full of everything else, and heavy Thread Weight extends them. Seclusion before a Threshold is kept on the road’s own ground for the same reason: a Body soul on Density, a Spirit soul in Depth, a Fate soul under Weight.
The Three Routes
What happens to the Aether once it is inside depends on the road, and the three roads spend three different things. Fighters call them Aether Manipulation, Essence Manipulation and Thread Manipulation, and for once the common names are exactly right.





































RoutePath and layerWhat is workedWhere it is heldThe lost share becomesWhat it costsChargeBody · Aether ShellRaw Aether, unrefinedPacked in the ShellHeat, the Shell’s furnace burningThe body: Shell strain, heat, torn fiber, recoilEssenceSpirit · Essence CoreAether refined in the Crystal and stamped with identity (spiritual energy)The CoreHollowing in the Core, and never heatThe self: hollowness, color, memoryThreadFate · Attraction LayerA thread pulled down from FateNot held. Pulled per working and paid from the soul’s own share, which is part of the reserve, held as EssenceA knot, which the world collects laterLuck, afterward
The Charge route. Aether is drawn in, packed in the Shell, shaped there by the Wellspring’s lens and driven out through the Shell. It never passes through the refining, so a Body fighter’s fire is Aether burning in the Wellspring’s shape and has none of the fighter in it. The Core decides and the Shell does the work. Every part of the spend that fails to arrive burns off in the Shell’s furnace as heat, which is why the Barn steamed.
The Essence route. Aether is drawn in, refined in the Crystal into Essence, stamped, and spent through the Core. What fails to arrive is paid where it was spent, as a hollowing in the Core, and blood and pallor are only the report of it. A Spirit worker at full stretch does not get hot. The Clerk went round the market for seven minutes with a dry collar. Force thrown this way lands on souls: a soul knocked out of true, dread laid on a mind, a Core wounded. It has no purchase on a jawbone.
The Thread route. No Thread is stored. A Fate worker’s reserve is Essence, refined in the Crystal like a Spirit worker’s, and a thread is pulled down through the Attraction Layer for the one working and paid for out of that reserve, the soul’s own share spent through the Layer. The share that fails to arrive becomes the knot. A vow draws on the same purse: it drains the reserve like any working, goes out through the Layer, pulls nothing and leaves no knot, and it refills the way everything else does. A Measurewright still grumbles about all three names, chiefly at students who hear Aether Manipulation and conclude they can skip the body’s bill.
One reserve, one number. A soul has a single capacity, written in EU on its card and its assay slip, and the guild reckons 1 EU at 1 MJ whichever road it leaves by. What fills that capacity follows the lead Path: a Body-led soul holds most of it as Charge, and a Spirit-led or a Fate-led soul holds it as Essence. Scholars write EU for both, and a Measurewright will tell you at length that the U ought to stand for something else now. Someone who walks Body and Spirit together refines part of what they draw and leaves the rest raw, and the card gives the split as a share (Charge 70% · Essence 30%), set by how they practice. The two do not trade back: Charge once held is never refined into Essence, and Essence never goes back to raw. A sealed Shell holds no Charge at all, which is the plain meaning of unwoken, and waking breaks the seal.
Topping up in a fight. A fight Draft follows the road of whoever drinks it. Core stock feeds the Core with Essence that arrives unstamped, and the crash afterward is the stamping. A Body fighter’s fight Draft is a Salt: raw Aether in a fraction that packs straight into the Shell. It goes down like swallowing a burn, and it leaves a crash of cramps and fever where the Spirit worker gets the stamping. There is no fight Draft for Fate. A Fate fighter’s reserve is Essence, so she drinks Core stock like a thrower and takes the same crash.





















EU · Essence UnitsThe raw reserve. Total volume of usable power the soul holds at any given moment, Charge in the Shell and Essence in the Core counted together as one figure, still called Essence Volume in the older books. Set by Level and capped by Stage. A practitioner operating below ten percent EU suffers Starvation: reduced stat expression and Trait flickering on every road, and then the road’s own bill. In Charge Starvation a Body fighter’s Shell starts drawing on the flesh itself, and the skin splits in fine lines as the Charge is taken out of the meat. In Essence Starvation a Spirit worker’s Core frays, names first and then memory, since what is running out is the self. A Fate worker’s reserve is Essence, so hers is Essence Starvation as well, the Core fraying underneath, with the Fate tells laid over it: luck curdling, then her own name sitting wrong in other mouths, and at the very end every knot she owes falling due together.Flux Density · EU/gThe compression ratio. How much power is packed per unit of Crystal mass. Higher Flux Density means greater output taken from the same reserve. It is the same number on every Path.AU/s · Aether Units per secondThe rate a practitioner spends at full output. Governed by Ardency Flux, Ardency Alacrity, and Tempering Yield. AU/s = Flux Density × η, and the power that actually lands is AU/s × η. So the yield counts twice, on purpose: once for how much the layer in use can move, and once for what survives the trip.Yield · ηThe share of a spend that arrives as intended effect; the Measurewrights’ older word is efficiency. The Mastery of the Path a working lands through sets it: Body for a working that leaves by the Shell, Spirit for one spent through the Core, Fate for a pull. What becomes of the rest follows the layer too. An η of 0.50 through the Shell burns half of every expenditure off in the Shell’s furnace as heat, with noise and structural bleed; the same figure through the Core is paid as hollowing, and through the Layer as a knot. This is why a Spirit master’s great Flux, turned on matter through a Shell he never trained, mostly burns off as heat on his own skin. The single most important variable in sustained combat. At full output a higher yield empties the reserve faster, and for the same delivered effect it makes the reserve last longer, which is the whole of what happened to the Barn. Governed by the Mastery of the Path in use, Tempering Clarity, and Ardency Compression: the rung sets the band, and Clarity and Compression set the place inside it. Two more things multiply with it. The ground does, by its band, Density for the Shell, Echo Depth for the Core and Thread Weight for a pull. A Wellspring worked away from its home plane does, lowering the yield again, and the share lost that way is paid in the road’s own coin like any other: heat for the Body, hollowing for the Spirit, a heavier knot for Fate.
None of these four figures appears on a window. They are how assayers and scholars do the sums, and the owner sees only the bar, the percentage and the shake in their own hands.
Yield by Mastery, and by Rank for the Unread
Which figure to read. From Glory, the Mastery of the Path a working lands through sets its yield, on the one table above: Body for what leaves by the Shell, Spirit for what is authored in the Core, Fate for a pull. The table below is two other things: the figure for the unread at Stages I to V, and a field average above them, what the fighting halls expect of a stranger at that rank before anyone has read him. A read rung overrides it, and a registered card’s own figure governs its holder. So a Stage VII Clerk on Spirit II runs 0.75 to 0.85 through the Core, whatever the Expert row says, and a Radiant Shell at Stage XII runs above 1.0 while the Grandmaster row reads 0.85 to 0.90, because most Grandmasters are still some way under the ceiling their Stage opened.























































Rank · StagesYield (η)What changedInitiate · Murmuring~0.30Enormous waste. Techniques feel like shouting into wind.Apprentice · Welling~0.35The leak is still the loudest thing about the practitioner.Journeyman · Ascension~0.40Waste becomes predictable, which is the first thing that can be trained against.Adept · Flourishing~0.45The last rank at which more than half of every expenditure is lost.Expert · Splintering to Refraction0.60 – 0.70First genuine yield; the Crystal has learned to stop leaking. Dual sight at Refraction allows the practitioner to observe and correct their own waste in real time.Master · Transcendence to Realization0.70 – 0.80First true Domain, providing a feedback loop that recycles ambient bleed. Pacts, artifacts and law imprint on terrain, creating persistent gains in familiar ground.Grandmaster · Dissonance to Emanation0.85 – 0.90Traits become local law. Mere presence begins optimizing Aether flow in the vicinity.Archmaster · Principality to Zenith0.95 – 1.2Biomes carry the practitioner’s doctrine. Above 1.0 the practitioner produces more coherent output than they spend. Nobody is getting free energy: the Continuum is recognizing their expression as law and supplementing it with ambient flow. The environment becomes a co-author.Paragon · Revelation to Apexabove 1.2, unboundedNo figure has been measured. The lettered scale has no rung here, and the Archives leave the gap open rather than fill it with a guess.
Domains
A Domain is a space where a soul’s own law outranks the world’s, and it has a page of its own. The short of it, since people will ask: a soul grows one by living, and a Second Release, or Fate’s One, opens and powers it, by name, called aloud. The Stage grants it and no number ever does. Dominion (the stat of presence and authority over space) and the lead Path’s Mastery decide how wide it runs and how steady it stands, with the Fate gates on Radius, Sovereignty and Gravity capping it at the A band of the scale for anyone who has not walked that road. What it rules follows the road, as its page sets out: matter for the Body, meanings for the Spirit, conditions for Fate, and the first flicker of one follows the road in the same way. Rich Aetheric ground crowds a Domain’s radius, and a Fate fighter’s Range with it, and heavy Thread Weight extends both. Anyone at Stage VIII can have one, a bought Stage VIII has the right and none of the finding, and the two-step boost cap stands inside it.

































StageWhat the Domain isThe Threshold into VIIThe flicker. A one-time burst of the person’s own Trait, usually seconds long, with no Release under it. It follows the road: a Body flicker rules matter, a Spirit one meanings, a Fate one conditions.VII · RefractionThe seed. With a Second Release, or Fate’s One, the flicker can be called back and held for minutes. It collapses if attention breaks.VIII · TranscendenceThe first true Domain, held for hours and steady under small disruption.IX · InvocationThe Catalyst into IX carries a first flicker of a Realm, once, on the same road as the Domain under it: a field that can hold other fields, for a breath.X · RealizationThe Realm’s door, by road and never for a bought Stage: Body through the Third Release, Spirit through its Second grown whole, Fate through the One. Pacts, artifacts and law set into the terrain.XI – XII · Dissonance to EmanationIts effects leak with nobody holding them. Traits become local law, and the Domain has turned from something done into something that simply is the case.
Read next: Windows and the Sheet, for what an owner actually sees of all this; Classes and Mastery, for the name the soul offers and Mastery on all three roads; and The Three Paths, for which layer reads what.

the-magic-system/the-soul-and-the-climb/.content:
“Everyone in this room knows exactly how much they have left, and not one of them can prove it to you. Bet accordingly.”
Bookie’s patter, Sealhall arena, on any day of the year

Forty thousand people were on their feet in the bone arena at Sealhall, under the blue and orange banners and the great curved ribs of whatever died there, on the last day of the Waxgate Sweepstakes. Dagny Thorn, known from the arena steps to the salt road as the Bad Debt, had just taken a shoulder-high hammer-swing from Seo Min-ho that lifted her clean off the sand. It broke her right collarbone so badly that the end stood up under the skin like a tent peg and her arm hung off it dead to the fingertips. She got up with her mouth full of blood. This is what she was looking at, and it was for her eyes alone:
[Hit: right collarbone broken. Arm down. Vitality 44%]
[Charge: 3% ▓░░░░░░░░░]
[Skill: Bearing Blows, Adept to Expert]

She spat a tooth, spread her one good arm to the whole arena, and bellowed.
"HALF MY RESERVE LEFT, Min-ho! How's Yours?"
Min-ho’s own window said thirty percent, and his left eye was swollen shut and full of blood. He looked her over with the eye he had. His Gnosis Perception (the stat of sensing what a soul is) sat a full step under her Resilience Ward on the scale the Measurewrights keep beneath the numbers (the stat that keeps other people out of yours), so all his soul would give him on her was question marks. He saw a fighter still standing, grinning, and roaring about it. He had a wife in Verath. He dropped the hammer and yielded, and the Bad Debt won the Sweepstakes on an arm’s length of pure lying, with her color stuttering thin around her ribs in front of everyone who knew to look.
One man did know to look. Up in the fourth tier a Measurewright (one of the guild that keeps the world’s tables and argues about them) with a Perception past three hundred had read the whole window off her before she opened her mouth, the moment the swing landed, and had gone down to the rail and quietly doubled his money. The Accord’s inquiry ran for three months and found nothing, because shouting a number at a man is no crime and no one had asked her to swear to it. That is the window in one afternoon: a private report, a public lie, a stronger eye in the stands, and a very great deal of money riding on the gap.
What a Window Is
A window is the soul reporting its numbers to its owner, in its owner’s own tongue, and no one else can see it. The Soul Crystal is the soul, and the Continuum (the whole lawful order of reality) measures it. The report follows from those two facts, or so the Measurewrights will tell you for the price of a drink. It comes when called and it comes unasked, in the middle of a fight, the moment there is something to report. A Moto reads hers in Moto, a Kharven drover reads his in the language he swears in, and a Marrowkin window puts the doer at the front of every line and the tally at the back, as that language has always done.
Everyone has one, the unwoken included. A baker has a Baking skill and a little sheet. Waking (the opening of the Crystal, which turns a soul into a practitioner) opens the rest of it.
Nobody else can see it, and the owner cannot show it. No trick of light, no shared Domain and no amount of pointing will put your window in front of another person’s eyes. All anyone can see is your eyes going to the middle distance, and every people has its own slang for that. A Kharven is checking the bill. A Marrowkin takes the tally. Accord hands read their own file. Soldiers from the Ochre Fields say a man is counting his brothers, and they will fight you if you ask why.
The word people use for the whole of what it shows is the sheet.
What It Shows, and What It Hides
A window shows numbers, ranks, Mastery, percentages and bars, and it never gives its owner a letter. Grades are for blades, beasts and bounties. A normal look gives the full sheet:
[Mun Seo-yeon · Level 190 · Stage VII, Refraction · Expert]
[Human, Sum-gol lineage]
[Class: Auditor]
[Path: Spirit · Spirit II]
[Ardency 212 · Vitality 74 · Gnosis 140 · Dexterity 128]
[Harmonics 88 · Resilience 41 · Tempering 37 · Dominion 19]
[Trait: Every Column Balances · at Spirit II]
[Skills: Bookkeeping Master · Footwork Journeyman · Appraisal Journeyman · Knife Apprentice]
[Blessings: none]
[Essence: 58%]

From the top: name, Level, Stage and the rank people say for it. Further down comes the Path, which says which of the soul’s three layers the Crystal leans on: the Aether Shell in the Physical World for Body, the Essence Core on the Soul Plane for Spirit, the Attraction Layer on the Plane of Fate for Fate. A soul on two Paths shows both, the one behind second (Path: Body, Spirit), and a Path only studied shows nowhere. A registered card spells it out by Path Stage, the highest Stage whose gates that road has opened: Body VII Mastered · Fate VI Walked 35%. A Work of Hataraki or any other real grip is no Trait, technique, blessing or Class, so a card gives it a line of its own, Fate Art: Work · grip · Fate rung, as in Fate Art: Ruin · inherited · Fate I on a Moto who may stand on any road at all. Then race and lineage, which shape base stats and what comes easily. Then the Class, the name the soul has offered for how the person has lived, and beside the Path the Mastery of each road walked, from Glory on, read from Level under the Stage’s ceiling: a numeral, I to V, and Ω for the very few, and nothing at all for a road not walked. Then the Eight Primaries, each given as the mean of its eight Sub-Stats, each Trait with the Mastery it works at, and each skill with its rank, Initiate to Paragon, the blessings, each on its own line, and the reserve, which the window names for what fills it. A Spirit-led soul like the Clerk’s reads Essence, Aether refined and stamped in the Crystal and held in the Core. A Body-led soul reads Charge, raw Aether packed unrefined in the Shell. A soul on both roads gets both bars, one under the other. A Fate-led soul reads Essence as well: a Fate worker refines Aether in the Crystal as a Spirit worker does and pays her pulls and her vows from that, and Thread never appears as a bar on any window, because it is never stored and is only pulled one working at a time. A soul that has not yet settled on a road reads plain Reserve. It is one capacity whatever the word on it, and people go on saying reserve aloud for all of them. A Sub-Stat (one of the eight finer measures inside each Primary) appears when it is used or when it moves, and the full sixty-four remain there to study for anyone with the patience. Vows, crew bonds and contracts get their own lines when the owner has them.
A Trait’s lean shows in the numbers. A Trait that is always running shifts the stat itself, and the window shows the shifted number with nothing to mark it. A Trait that runs only in its own conditions shows both numbers, the plain one first, and names the condition:
[Absorption 140 · 190 while It Comes Up White holds]

The second number is live only while the condition is, and both kinds of lean count on the cap on boosts, two steps on the hidden scale.
Worked gear shows, and plain gear does not. A plain helm is a helm and the window has nothing to say about it. A worked piece (runed, Draft-tempered, or made of monster parts) multiplies the whole Primary it was made for, all eight of its Sub-Stats together, and the figures are read again from there. The piece keeps its own Grade and Rarity, and the window gives them, because a helm is a thing. It also takes a small steady draw on the reserve to keep it lit, which the window gives as light, steady or heavy, and names by the layer the piece draws on. Armor and weapons draw on the Shell, soul-wards and charms on the Core, oath-rings and luck-tokens on the Layer, and all of it is paid from the one reserve:
[Worn: Ashjaw Helm · Rare · Grade B]
[Gnosis ×1.15]
[Shell draw: light]

Bonded gear’s multipliers grow with the bearer, and the block changes as they do. All of a person’s gear together multiplies any one Primary by half again at most, a cap of its own beside the two-step one. The sustainable figure is read with the gear off. Gear multiplies on top of it and moves the numbers the window shows, and the two-step cap on boosts counts from the bare figure underneath. A piece above its wearer’s Stage works at half its multiplier or fights them, and the trade-offs are real, so a suit of heavy plate reads [Vitality ×1.3 · Dexterity ×0.85] and means both. A true relic gives its bearer the same question marks it gives everyone else. Worn Power has the whole of it.
A commoner’s window is small and useful. It holds a Level, a few trade skills and her health, with no Essence and no class:
[Hanne Oster · Human · Level 6]
[Health: good · Back: complaining]
[Skills: Baking Journeyman · Sums Apprentice · Getting Up Early Journeyman]

Hanne Oster has read that every morning for forty years, and she reads it the way you would read the weather.
It hides a good deal, and the list is worth learning by heart.

EU, AU/s and yield (η). Essence Units, the output rate and the yield, the share of a spend that arrives, the assayers’ sums set out in Tier Grade, Bands & the Aether Shell. The owner gets the bar, the percentage and the shake in their own hands.
A letter. The window says 288 and stops there. Where 288 falls on the scale the assayers keep for beasts and blades is their arithmetic, done with a coil and a fee, and the soul has never once called its owner a letter.
Any level on a technique. Techniques show no level and take a bigger name when they jump.
Other people. Reading anyone else takes Gnosis (below), and the result is your own soul’s account of them, wrong in its own ways.
Why. It reports the blow after the blow. It has never warned anyone of anything, and it does not explain itself.
The truth of a blessing. The giver wrote that line.

The body comes first and the window follows. The tells on the body have always arrived ahead of the report: at half the reserve the breath shortens and the aura dims, at a quarter the hands shake and the color thins, at a tenth the aura flickers and the Trait stutters. Those are shared by everyone. On top of them each road tires in its own way, because each is spending a different thing: a Body fighter runs hot and the skin splits, a Spirit worker runs hollow and loses colors and then names, and around a Fate worker the luck curdles. Below a tenth lies Starvation, Charge Starvation for a Body fighter and Essence Starvation for a Spirit or a Fate one. The Three Paths gives the table under How It Reads. An old teacher will tell you to fight your lungs and read your window afterward, and the practitioners who live longest take the advice.
In a Fight
Windows come often and in detail once blows land, in short blocks, for damage, skill gains and reserve. Each block follows the thing it reports. Here is the Clerk’s evening at the Harl Cross market, from the middle of it:
[Left ribs: two cracked · Vitality holding]
[Skill rising: Footwork Journeyman, 91%]
[Essence: 41%]

A sequence off a sharper afternoon, read in order by a mid-rank Body fighter with a bad morning coming:
[Pressure: Stage VIII above you. Focus down a step.]

[Evaded. Reflex 204, in use.]
[Hit: left ear gone at the rim. Vitality 96%]

[Coat: thin on the left. Charge: 51% ▓▓▓▓▓░░░░░]

[Hit: left forearm broken through. Grip gone. Vitality 71%]
[Charge: 44% ▓▓▓▓░░░░░░]
[Skill: Bearing Blows, Journeyman, 88%]

Pressure is felt first. The felt weight of a stronger soul shows in the room, in the lamp flames, the dogs, the sweat on your lip, and only then does the window report it as a line. A Grandmaster merchant with no fighting Stage has no Pressure at all, and his bookkeeper has been looking for the line for years.
A wound is a status line, and it stays. It says what the wound stops you doing, and it sits on the sheet until someone treats it. Healers and healing Drafts fix it for a price, slowly at a low one and fast at a high one, so a rich fighter walks off what cripples a poor one for life. A retired spearman at Tollgarth has been reading the same line for thirty-one years:
[Right knee: torn. Will not bear weight. Untreated.]

A soul wound is a status line too. A blow that goes past the Shell and lands on the Core leaves no mark on the skin, and the window reports it like any other injury, by what it has taken: a color gone flat, a sense dulled, a memory worn thin. A shallow one closes in days and a deep one in seasons. One left untreated past a season, or struck a second time in the same place, sets for life. Soul-menders are a trade and they charge like one, and even a wound well mended leaves a pale place in the Core that a good Analysis can read years afterward.
[Soul wound: Core, shallow. Reds gone flat. Untreated.]

[Soul wound: Core, deep. Your mother's voice: thin. Set.]

A crew shows. A real bond shows as a line on the window, shares a little Level gain and puts the crew’s bars in the corner of a fight. It cannot be bought or declared. It has to be earned, and betrayal breaks it visibly, on the window of everyone it touches, in the middle of whatever they were doing:
[Crew: The Wet Sevens · bond holding]
[Hob ▓▓▓▓▓▓░░░░ · Marit ▓▓▓░░░░░░░ · Dov ▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓░]

[Crew: The Wet Sevens · bond broken: Dov]

A vow shows its terms. A vow is small Fate, a person binding their own probability, and anyone can make one. It spends the soul’s own share, where a pull reaches above it, which is why a fishwife who has never read a rung of Fate can swear one that holds. The share is part of the reserve: a vow drains it like any working, spent through the Layer, and it refills the same way. Spoken aloud, with or without a witness, it arrives on the window with its bargain and its terms. Breaking it lands at once, by those terms. Each vow counts against the two-step cap on boosts. See Vows and Oaths:
[Vow: "This hand stays down until he is dead."]
[Bargain: Ardency one step up · Left hand dead until then]
[Breach: lands at once]

A pull leaves a knot, and the knot shows. A vow kept costs nothing further, because it spends only what was the soul’s own. A true pull on a thread reaches above that share and bends what was likely, and every one of them leaves a knot that the world collects later: a strap that gives on the puller next week, a friend’s plan that fails for no reason anyone can find. The window enters it at the moment of the pull and keeps it until it is paid. Its size follows how far the pull was from likely. A lean on the odds falls due within days, and a removed prerequisite within the season’s troubles. An inherited Work makes the pull less likely to fail and takes nothing off the knot.
[Pull: his girth-strap gave]
[Knot: one, small. Owed within days.]

[Knot: paid. Your own bootlace, on the stair.]

A contract has a sheet. A bound spirit or beast has its own window, read by its holder. Its Level grows, its terms show, and it can evolve, or be stolen by contract:
[Bound: Old Sorrel, marsh-spirit · Level 41]
[Terms: one drowned thing at each new moon]
[Owed: 2]

At the Thresholds
A window earns its keep at the big moments.
A Level. Level moves by danger overcome, so killing something stronger moves it more than a hundred weak kills, and crews have come to knives over who got the kill. The window settles that for the person holding it, and for nobody else.
[Level: 61 to 68]
[Skill: Knots, Apprentice to Journeyman]

A Trait gets no line here. It has no level to climb, and it deepens only when the Mastery it works at rises.
A technique jumping. Techniques show no level, so the window marks a jump by the name. It comes when the skill under the technique has gained a rank and a fight or a scene has pushed the technique past its old limit, and it gives one thing: power, reach, speed or a lower cost, sometimes with a condition attached. The new name arrives in capitals, and the old name stays on the sheet and in use.
[Skill: Brawling, Apprentice to Journeyman]
[Short Right Hand is now THE RIGHT HAND OF THE RIVER WARD]
[Gained: reach · Condition: both feet planted]
[Short Right Hand: kept]

Waking. The commoner’s little sheet opens out. Most souls that wake are taught to, as The Gate explains, and the rest get there by crisis or out of a bottle. A Waking Draft is very dear and often kills or warps a child, and most of the rich buy one for their children anyway, while commoners sell themselves into guild debt for it. Those who come through read something like this:
[Crystal: open]
[Stage I, Murmuring]
[Reserve: 100% ▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓]
[Vitality 14 · Ardency 6 · Gnosis 12 · Dexterity 15]

A Class. The soul’s offer, with its names, first at Glory, with Mastery I, and again each time the lead road’s Mastery rises a rung, each new name bringing one move that fits it and a lean on where life will spend the person’s stat points. The offer comes through the lead layer, so the names lean the way the road does: a Body soul is mostly offered names of work and matter, a Spirit soul names of souls and meanings, a Fate soul names of bonds, debts and odds, and every so often the soul offers something from clean off the road and enjoys the silence. The roads behind the lead move without ceremony, as one numeral changing on the line, and a Fate-led soul with no grip, whose road stops at II, waits a long time for a third name that does not come. See Classes and the Three Ladders.
[Mastery: Spirit II]
[Your life has earned:]
  Auditor
  Rope-Walk Clerk
[Choose.]

A breakthrough. A lived one is loud and transforms you with the window lighting up, and a bought one is a Draft in a quiet room with a physician standing by. A lived one passes the Great Work in its own road’s terms, nigredo, albedo, citrinitas and rubedo: the soul broken down, purified, woken and fixed. Crisis, seclusion and tribulation all still happen, each in the form of the soul’s own road: the Catalyst is met in the layer the soul leans on, seclusion is kept on that Path’s own ground, and the bought kind is poured by Path, on Salt for Body, Core stock for Spirit and the Layer reagent for Fate. The Sixteen Stages gives every crossing three ways under The Climb by Path. The sheet shows the same Stage in both cases, and that has started more fights than any other line on it.
[STAGE VIII: TRANSCENDENCE]
[Crystal: melted and rebuilt, layer by layer]
[Ceiling lifted · Points to place: ▓▓░░░░░░░░]
[Trait: Banked Coal, at Body II]

[Stage VIII, Transcendence]
[Ceiling lifted · Points to place: ▓▓░░░░░░░░]
[Crystal: Overgrown]
[Physician: present]

Taverns tell the second block as a joke, and the last line is the joke.
A Release or a Domain. Calling a Release fills the window with its name and what changed, and a timer bar starts to drain. The same goes for a Domain, the space where a soul’s own law outranks the world’s settled habits. Both are big and loud on the window for the owner alone, whatever the room is doing, and the two-step cap stands inside them. What the room is doing depends on the road, and Releases and Domains by Path has that.
[FIRST RELEASE: THE LONG YOKE]
[Ardency: top of band]
[Charge: 47% ▓▓▓▓▓░░░░░]
[Holds: ▓▓▓▓▓▓▓░░░]

[DOMAIN: THE WHOLE SHIFT]
[Changed: within the yard the bell decides who may rest]
[Ardency: two steps up · cap reached]
[Held: ██████░░░░]

How a Blessing Lies
A blessing grants a power out of a person’s natural reach, even in Level. It shows on the sheet as its own line, and that line can lie, because the giver wrote it. Every other line on a window is the soul reporting on itself. This is the one line on it with an outside author.
King Godric Fenn of Pennycrown, on the night his cousin’s army reached the walls, prayed at a spring he had been told to leave alone, and woke with this:
[Blessing: Favor of the Spring]
[You will not be unseated.]

He wept for joy and rode out, and he was not unseated. Lances broke on him, and he stayed in the saddle with the horse going down under him twice. He rode home victorious and found he could not get off. The horse died in the courtyard eleven days later, and when his men had cut him free of it and set him on the throne to recover, he found he could not get off that either. He has held it for twenty-three years, on a great many cushions, and he has outlived four sons who tried to take it from him. His window still reads Favor.
A curse is often a blessing with terms you did not read, or from a giver who does not care what you want. Nobody can tell at first, and some are both. The sailor’s Favor of the Tide-Mother says You will not drown, and every sailor who has had that line will tell you it is true. Read it again.
Those who hold Hataraki, the Moto’s governing power, can take a blessing back or remove it, which is one reason people are so afraid of them. It takes two Works or two Moto, and the line simply goes:
[Blessing: removed]

When Your Own Window Lies
The soul does not lie to its owner of its own accord, with the one exception above. A strong mind-worker can. The arts that do it run on the Wellsprings of memory, sleep and reflection (Letheveil, Hypnather, Mirithane and their neighbors), and a strong enough hand there can reach the report itself: show false numbers, hide a line, tell a man at nine percent that he has plenty.
It stays a violation with a cost, on the victim and on the user both, and every realm’s law around it is an argument. Gnosis gives a fair counter. A stronger Perception notices that the report has stopped matching the soul, and everyone has the plain counter of their own body, since a window can say eighty percent and your lungs will still tell you the truth. Veterans who have fought mind-workers count their breath against their reserve line, and anyone who has lost a friend that way does it for life.
Reading Other People
A stronger Gnosis Perception reads a weaker Resilience Ward, a step or more ahead on the hidden scale, and everything else is an estimate said aloud. Your own soul gives you the result as a window, with its gaps showing:
[Read: Dagny Thorn · Level 188 · Stage VII · Expert]
[Charge: 3% · Vitality 44%]

And the same read from a weaker eye:
[Read: ??? · Level ??? · Stage ?]


The trained talk about it constantly. Fighters and onlookers rank each other aloud, read shoulders and breath, and argue over it through the whole fight. Stage IX? Look at his feet. That’s a VII in a good coat. All of it is estimate, and a confident wrong one has won as many fights as a right one.
People hide and fake it. Holding Pressure in, thinning the coat, walking like a tired man and flaring an aura brighter than the reserve behind it can pay for are all arts. Suppression and Feint are real Sub-Stats, and a person with a high Ward can stand in a crowded room and be nobody.
Instruments read everyone. Stand in the coil and the clerk writes down your Stage, Level, Mastery and yield, and where every number falls on the hidden scale, which is more than your own window will tell you. It takes the fee and your standing in the coil, and it will not read your blessings or your class name.
Monsters sit on the same scale, and carry the letter people do not. A monster has a Stage and a Level underneath, the same as anyone, and it is known and bountied by its Grade, which is what every board posts beside the price. It has Pressure, a Path set by how it lives and Mastery on that road, and it never takes a class. A weak reader gets question marks, usually at the moment it matters most. A famous one carries a name, an epithet and a bounty on top of it. See The Bestiary.
Items take an Appraisal skill. An Appraisal skill and an assay instrument read a piece of gear, and a good forger beats a weak appraiser. True relics of the Great Spirit War read as question marks to anyone, and some have opinions about who holds them.

How People Brag and Lie
Since nobody can see your window, your window is whatever you say it is, until somebody with the right to ask makes you pay for it.
In the street, say what you like. Everyone shouts their Level at the brawl and rounds up. A bare claim costs nothing, and the Bad Debt won a Sweepstakes on one.
On the slate, you pay the bookies’ rate. Odds-men chalk what they can get, and heralds cry their own numbers. The Accord keeps a roll, each realm and sect keeps a list, minstrels get the details wrong in rhyme, and these rankings all disagree. Getting on any of them makes you a target.
At a hiring, they ask for proof. A crew or a lord wants more than your word. They will want an assay slip with a seal on it, which costs a silver mark at the house and can be forged, and forging a token is a great crime, which keeps the price of a good forgery high. A sensible employer also hires a reader, and has you lift something heavy.
At court, you swear. A proper court makes you swear to what your sheet shows. Lying under a proper oath costs you, because an oath is small Fate, and the cost lands on your own window, where only you can see it. Only an assay can check what you said.
[Oath: "Level 140, as my sheet shows." Sworn false.]
[Terms: every chance goes against you until it is unsaid.]

Lawyers fight over the exact wording, and they eat well on it. As my sheet shows and as I am are different oaths. A man with a lying blessing can swear to it in perfect safety, and so can a man whose window has been tampered with. A Bench in the Concord spent four years on whether a false Level sworn on a mind-touched sheet was perjury, and gave up when both advocates were found to have been touched.
At home, you push. Everybody reads their own sheet, and that shapes a society to its roots. Parents push their children from the first Level. A six-year-old in a Hammerford market will tell you her Sums before her name, because her mother made her practice saying it. Whole villages know whose son has which skill, and matches are made on it, on the parents’ word.
Who Built It
The oldest quarrel in the Measurewrights’ hall, carried on at weddings, in long letters and on two occasions with knives.
The Null School holds that nobody built it. The Crystal is the soul, the Continuum measures it, and a thing measured and a thing aware of being measured will report. The window is what it feels like to be a soul with a bill. This is the position of most working Measurewrights, chiefly because it requires no further funding.
The Author School points at the tongues. Bridge-slang from Kingsbridge turns up on a Kingsbridge docker’s window within the year. A report that keeps up with slang, they say, has someone doing the translating, and it uses complaining for a back. They have also noticed that blessings prove a window can be written on from outside, and they would like to know who wrote the rest. They have no candidate they will sign their names to, and three they will mention after dark.
The Mirror School answers that the slang is the owner’s own. The soul speaks to itself in the only words it has, and nothing on the window has ever told anybody something they could not, in principle, have felt. This view is strong among healers. It is weak among anyone who has read a skill they did not know they had.
The old beings have been no help. A Measurewright’s expedition once asked a very old thing in a very old battlefield who had built the window. After some thought it asked what a window was. Nobody present could show it one.
Every faith has its own answer, and real wars come of it. Moto speak to their dead, and many hold that the numbers are their ancestors’ reckoning of them, kept as carefully as the family altar. The Marrowkin tally their dead, and they see no mystery here: it is the hold’s Tally, entered by the one in whom it is kept. Kharven price theirs, and a Kharven priest will tell you that somebody holds your note, and that you will meet him. Sancta Lux, which claims jurisdiction over oath and status, treats a window as a sworn witness inside you, and will ask you what it said. The Verdant Orcs regard the sheet as rings in a tree, and think it strange that anyone needs it read. And the river towns of Hallenfeld fought the towns of the Golden Hollow for six summers over whether a priest could lawfully require a child to read her window aloud at confirmation, in a war that killed some eleven thousand people and ended with both sides still doing what they had been doing.
The Archives take no position. They note that the window has been asked, by a great many people, in a great many tongues, and it reports only that their reserve is down.
Read next: How Power Grows, Skills and Trait Levels, Classes and the Three Ladders, and The Three Paths for what the top line of the sheet is saying.

the-magic-system/the-spell-index/applied.title: Applied Workings
the-magic-system/the-spell-index/applied.content:
The workings of the trade: what practitioners actually cast, built on the roots and the Wellsprings.
Part of The Spell Index. 63 entries. Each gives the working’s glyphs and least Temperance, the Stage with its rank, its Wellspring and operation, what sets it off and what it does, how it works by its idea, and what it costs and what answers it.
Abyssal Sway
Applied · [Ab] Abyss · Flourishing and above

























WellspringAbyntheus (Spirit)Second WellspringDissolutionOperationSublimationTemperanceFlourishing (Adept) and above
Effect. Deep-pressure column that equalizes incoming force.
How it works.

The idea. Vastness. The great scale read off the small vessel, a mortal soul stretched to take in things far too large for it. Dissolution’s idea rides with it (unbinding, what no longer serves is allowed to come apart on its own, and keeping anything at all becomes the work).
The operation. Sublimation. The small soul is raised toward the great scale and brought back down still holding it.
In the worker. Held to Flourishing or past, the idea is set as law by [Ab] Abyss, and the world gives way that far: deep-pressure column that equalizes incoming force.
Price in the self. Reserve, plus overpressure rebounds.
Flaw. The small vessel can hold the great scale only while it still knows it is small. Stretched too long between the near end and the far one, the soul loses its sense of how the two fit together, and what comes back to it is noise the practitioner is nonetheless convinced is a signal.
Counter. [RenB] Boundary refuses its claim before it settles; the contrary idea is Coagulatio.
The Measurewrights’ line. Very-long-wavelength propagation and interferometry.

Cost and backlash. Overpressure rebounds
Counterplay. [RenB] Boundary
Anamnesis Chain
Applied · [AnMa] Anamnesis · Refraction and above

























WellspringAnamnesis (Medium)Second WellspringHypnatherOperationSeparationTemperanceRefraction (Expert) and above
Effect. Chains total recall across multiple linked minds; used in Dream Oath swearing.
How it works.

The idea. Remembrance. Everything keeps its past, and a soul under this lens can touch a thing and read it. Hypnather’s idea rides with it (the sleep crown, change that comes only at rest, the soul setting itself in order in the dark while nothing is asked of it).
The operation. Separation. The past a thing has kept is parted from it and read, as the residue is parted from the vessel that held it.
In the worker. Held to Refraction or past, the idea is set as law by [AnMa] Anamnesis, and the world gives way that far: chains total recall across multiple linked minds; used in Dream Oath swearing.
Price in the self. Reserve, plus mind-bleed; weakest link shatters chain for all.
Flaw. Everything keeps its past, and the reading becomes part of that past the moment it is made. A careless hand laid on the record writes itself over what it came to read, so a careless practitioner erases the record in the act of taking it.
Counter. [Vel] Mind refuses its claim before it settles; the contrary idea is Letheveil or Sublimatio.
The Measurewrights’ line. Remanent magnetization and thermoluminescent dosimetry.

Cost and backlash. Mind-bleed; weakest link shatters chain for all
Counterplay. [Vel] Mind
Aperture Weir
Applied · [Ap] Aperture · Flourishing and above

























WellspringPhreatis (Medium)Second WellspringFixatioOperationDissolutionTemperanceFlourishing (Adept) and above
Effect. Valve control with safety catch against over-spill.
How it works.

The idea. Memory as deep water. What is lived sinks in, is built into you, and comes back long after the weather has changed. Fixatio’s idea rides with it (commitment, what is bound here stays bound, because the way back has stopped existing).
The operation. Dissolution. What is lived is taken down into the deep water and held there in solution, to be given back whole long after.
In the worker. Held to Flourishing or past, the idea is set as law by [Ap] Aperture, and the world gives way that far: valve control with safety catch against over-spill.
Price in the self. Reserve, plus edge overload if mistuned.
Flaw. Deep water does not ask what is sinking into it. Whatever is lived goes down and is built in, and nothing can be fished back out of it later on its own, so a falsified memory comes back up as readily as a true one.
Counter. [Flx] Flux refuses its claim before it settles; the contrary idea is Letheveil.
The Measurewrights’ line. Long-term potentiation on the one reading.

Cost and backlash. Edge overload if mistuned
Counterplay. [Flx] Flux
Aria of Balance
Applied · [Ari] Aria · Flourishing and above

























WellspringMirithane (Spirit)Second WellspringJudiciumOperationConjunctionTemperanceFlourishing (Adept) and above
Effect. Sustained song keeps team equilibrium under fire.
How it works.

The idea. The honest mirror. The inside and the outside made one surface. Judicium’s idea rides with it (truth told apart, discernment that knows what a thing is made of, and whether it is lying, from the mark it cannot help leaving).
The operation. Conjunction. The inside and the outside are joined into one surface, so what leaves the soul is what is in it.
In the worker. Held to Flourishing or past, the idea is set as law by [Ari] Aria, and the world gives way that far: sustained song keeps team equilibrium under fire.
Price in the self. Reserve, plus song muffled by damp.
Flaw. An honest mirror shows everything or it is not honest, and the idea has no way to keep one thing back. A practitioner in a state they would rather not broadcast broadcasts it perfectly.
Counter. [Sil] Silence refuses its claim before it settles; the contrary idea is Luminalis or Oneirion.
The Measurewrights’ line. Specular reflection.

Cost and backlash. Song muffled by damp
Counterplay. [Sil] Silence
Beast Bridge
Applied · [Bst] Beast · Flourishing and above

























WellspringAnima Spirare (Wild)Second WellspringVerdantiaOperationFermentationTemperanceFlourishing (Adept) and above

Price in the self. Reserve, plus Unanchored if ground shifts; auto-detonates on caster proximity.
Flaw. The ember stays lit, and nothing in the idea knows how to put it out. When the practitioner lets the working go it goes on smoldering where they cannot see it, eating reserve and tissue for hours after they believed it ended.
Counter. [Let] Tide refuses its claim before it settles; the contrary idea is Ignivale or Catharsis.
The Measurewrights’ line. Smoldering combustion.

Cost and backlash. Unanchored if ground shifts; auto-detonates on caster proximity
Counterplay. [Let] Tide
Ruptured Pattern
Applied · [Rk] Rupture · Refraction and above

























WellspringFractura (Wild)Second WellspringCataclysmOperationSeparationTemperanceRefraction (Expert) and above
Effect. Tears repeating enemy scripts by breaking their tessellation nodes.
How it works.

The idea. The breaking point. Everything has a place where it will go, and this lens shows it to you, in bridges, in friends and in your own left wrist. Cataclysm’s idea rides with it (upheaval, the moment a fire stops being a fire and becomes a blast, a change in kind as well as size, and the soul that has learned to call that moment).
The operation. Separation. A thing is parted along the one place where it was always going to part.
In the worker. Held to Refraction or past, the idea is set as law by [Rk] Rupture, and the world gives way that far: tears repeating enemy scripts by breaking their tessellation nodes.
Price in the self. Reserve, plus collateral breakup.
Flaw. The lens shows where everything will go, and it cannot leave its bearer out of everything. Under strain a Fractura practitioner reads their own breaking points with perfect clarity, at the worst possible moment.
Counter. [Knt] Knot refuses its claim before it settles; the contrary idea is Orrenthal, Coagula or Redemption.
The Measurewrights’ line. Linear elastic fracture mechanics.

Cost and backlash. Collateral breakup
Counterplay. [Knt] Knot
Sediment Reading
Applied · [Sed] Sediment · Glory and above

























WellspringChthonica (Wild)Second WellspringAnamnesisOperationConjunctionTemperanceGlory (Expert) and above
Effect. Reads the geological record of a site; reveals prior battles, rites, or buried Domains.
How it works.

The idea. The root. Holding on by touching everything, so that whatever you stand on becomes yours to stand on. Anamnesis’s idea rides with it (remembrance, everything keeps its past, and a soul under this lens can touch a thing and read it).
The operation. Conjunction. The soul and whatever it stands on are joined at every point where they touch, until each holds the other.
In the worker. Held to Glory or past, the idea is set as law by [Sed] Sediment, and the world gives way that far: reads the geological record of a site; reveals prior battles, rites, or buried Domains.
Price in the self. Reserve, plus geological nausea; caster feels millennial weight.
Flaw. The root holds by touching everything, so it holds nothing it cannot touch. Put wet, grease or filth between the soul and its ground and the grip lets go, all of it at once, without warning and with no halfway.
Counter. [Kael] Ruin refuses its claim before it settles; the contrary idea is Cymorath, Oneirion or Abython.
The Measurewrights’ line. Static friction and molecular adhesion.

Cost and backlash. Geological nausea; caster feels millennial weight
Counterplay. [Kael] Ruin
Severed Rot
Applied · [Sv] Sever · Refraction and above

























WellspringCatharsis (Spirit)Second WellspringMortalisOperationDissolutionTemperanceRefraction (Expert) and above
Effect. Cuts rot-thread from a living host for burning.
How it works.

The idea. Letting go. A load set down so completely that the setting down spends it, and the soul comes out on the other side lighter and changed. Mortalis’s idea rides with it (the black gate, ending looked at squarely and understood as a passage with its own law, by a soul that has stopped fearing it and has started, a little, to cool).
The operation. Dissolution. The hard thing held in the soul is loosed into the change of state and is gone into it.
In the worker. Held to Refraction or past, the idea is set as law by [Sv] Sever, and the world gives way that far: cuts rot-thread from a living host for burning.
Price in the self. Reserve, plus Carapace shields thread.
Flaw. Nothing can be let go that has not first been admitted. A soul on this lens that will not say what it is carrying cannot set it down, so the load goes on gathering past the hour it should have gone, and when the admission finally comes it comes all at once and takes everything near it down with the load.
Counter. [Bd] Bedrock refuses its claim before it settles; the contrary idea is Pyraeon or Vantabriel.
The Measurewrights’ line. Latent heat of phase change.

Cost and backlash. Carapace shields thread
Counterplay. [Bd] Bedrock
Slag Joint
Applied · [Slg] Slag · Flourishing and above

























WellspringSolfatara (Wild)Second WellspringCoagulatioOperationSublimationTemperanceFlourishing (Adept) and above
Effect. Melts and re-fuses a seam into stronger dovetail.
How it works.

The idea. The fuming earth. Pressure let out forever and never saved up, so the soul stops building toward a blow and becomes a steady force in the room. Coagulatio’s idea rides with it (settling round a seed, scattered things find one grain and grow out from it, denser and far less wasteful than they were).
The operation. Sublimation. What presses in the soul is given off as fume without end and never stored.
In the worker. Held to Flourishing or past, the idea is set as law by [Slg] Slag, and the world gives way that far: melts and re-fuses a seam into stronger dovetail.
Price in the self. Reserve, plus impurity inclusions.
Flaw. The fuming earth lets its pressure out forever and has never learned to hold any of it. Interrupt the release and the pressure does not politely wait: it finds a new way out through whatever is weakest.
Counter. [Rk] Rupture refuses its claim before it settles; the contrary idea is Cataclysm.
The Measurewrights’ line. Fumarolic degassing.

Cost and backlash. Impurity inclusions
Counterplay. [Rk] Rupture

Applied · [SoulDr] Soul-Drift · Glory and above

























WellspringSomnalis (Fate)Second WellspringMortalisOperationFermentationTemperanceGlory (Expert) and above
Effect. Projects consciousness through Auren’s gate without full death; scouting the Pale Realms.
How it works.

The idea. Living among what might be. The near possibilities of the Plane of Fate held in view at once, each with its odds on it, and a soul at ease in the not knowing. Mortalis’s idea rides with it (the black gate, ending looked at squarely and understood as a passage with its own law, by a soul that has stopped fearing it and has started, a little, to cool).
The operation. Fermentation. What is about to happen is kept working in the vessel, every way it might yet go still alive in it and none of them settled.
In the worker. Held to Glory or past, the idea is set as law by [SoulDr] Soul-Drift, and the world gives way that far: Projects consciousness through Auren’s gate without full death; scouting the Pale Realms.
Price in the self. Reserve, plus body left defenseless; Return glyph must be pre-placed or soul strays.
Flaw. The idea holds only while nothing is certain. A soul that lets one bright branch stand for the whole river has stopped living among what might be and started believing, and it acts on that branch with everything it has, though it carried eleven percent of the weight.
Counter. [Rt] Return refuses its claim before it settles; the contrary idea is Fixatio.
The Measurewrights’ line. Ensemble forecasting.

Cost and backlash. Body left defenseless; Return glyph must be pre-placed or soul strays
Counterplay. [Rt] Return
