the-magic-system/the-spell-index/index.content:
Every attested working in the Master Codex, 109 of them, filed by kind
A working is a Wellspring’s idea, set as law by its glyphs and held by a soul tempered far enough to hold it. This index files every attested one the same way: the glyphs it is written in, the least Temperance that can hold it, the Wellspring whose idea it runs on and the operation that idea performs, what sets it off, what it does, how it works, what it costs the worker and what answers it.
The idea and its operation come from the Sixty; the glyphs from the Master Glyph Index. The Measurewrights’ line at the foot of each account is the guild’s own reckoning, often right about how much and never about why.
The four shelves






























ShelfEntriesWhat is on itRoot Invocations14The fourteen root invocations, one to each Archon: the working an Archon’s own law makes when it is called by its glyphs.Titan-Keyed Arts14The fourteen arts keyed to a Titan’s law, each the Titan’s ground worked at a size a soul can carry.Applied Workings63The workings of the trade: what practitioners actually cast, built on the roots and the Wellsprings.Root Echoes18Applied workings that echo a root invocation, the root’s shape carried down into common use.
How to read an entry

The line under the name gives the shelf, the glyphs the working is written in and the least Temperance that can hold it.
Wellspring and operation say which idea the working runs on and what that idea does at the bench.
Trigger is what has to be true before the working will take. Effect is what it does.
How it works is the working by its idea: the idea, the operation, what happens in the worker, the price in the self, the flaw, the counter, and last the Measurewrights’ line.
In numbers, the target, cost and backlash and counterplay follow.

the-magic-system/the-spell-index/titan-k.title: Titan-Keyed Arts
the-magic-system/the-spell-index/titan-k.content:
The fourteen arts keyed to a Titan’s law, each the Titan’s ground worked at a size a soul can carry.
Part of The Spell Index. 14 entries. Each gives the working’s glyphs and least Temperance, its Wellspring and operation, what sets it off and what it does, how it works by its idea, and what it costs and what answers it.
The Titans themselves, and the fuller story of each art, are on The Fourteen Titans pages.
Flesh Remembers Stone
Titan-keyed art · [Th] Foundation + [Ma] Recall · Zenith and above





















WellspringMateria Primordia (Wild)OperationConjunctionTemperanceZenith and above
Trigger. Requires direct skin contact with the target tissue, bone, or soil.
Effect. Crystallizes living Essence into Soul-Crystal-grade matter on contact, letting the caster reforge flesh, bone, or soil directly into stable lattice, as Gaia’s own Wellspring does beneath the world’s crust.
How it works.

The idea. The first substance. One self and many forms, and a soul that finds it can become its own opposite and still be itself.
The operation. Conjunction. The one substance is wed to its own opposite and goes on being itself, the marriage the bench calls the first matter.
In the worker. Held to Zenith or past, the idea is set as law by [Th] Foundation + [Ma] Recall, and the world gives way that far: crystallizes living Essence into Soul-Crystal-grade matter on contact, letting the caster reforge flesh, bone, or soil directly into stable lattice, as Gaia’s own Wellspring does beneath the world’s crust.
Price in the self. Reserve, plus Caster’s hands take the heaviest exposure; repeated use produces genuine mineral deposits under the caster’s own skin over a career.
Flaw. One self can wear many forms, but only one at a time, and it has to remember the others to come back to them. Under enough pressure it forgets, and the practitioner keeps for good whichever form they were wearing when the pressure came.
Counter. [Uur] Disruption refuses its claim before it settles; the contrary idea is Oblivara or Basilithe.
The Measurewrights’ line. Allotropy.

In numbers. Crystallization front advances roughly one centimeter per second along tissue, faster through soil and loose stone.
The target. Affected matter takes on visible mineral sheen and rigidity while retaining its original shape, per Gaia’s own manifestation.
Cost and backlash. Caster’s hands take the heaviest exposure; repeated use produces genuine mineral deposits under the caster’s own skin over a career.
Counterplay. [Uur] Disruption unmakes the stone before it has finished setting, and flesh forced back out of half-made stone is its own kind of trauma.
The Bent Knee’s Burden
Titan-keyed art · [Th] Foundation + [Len] Line · Zenith and above





















WellspringPetralon (Wild)OperationCoagulationTemperanceZenith and above
Trigger. Cast only within a Domain whose weight and order are already visibly failing (a sagging structure, a buckling timeline).
Effect. Locks a Domain’s weight and causal sequence to Atla’zon’s own kneeling burden, granting immense structural and temporal stability at the cost of freezing all forward motion within the field.
How it works.

The idea. The foundation. To become what other things stand on: load taken, carried and sent down, at the price of slowly settling. Breaking, holding and rising are one law seen from three positions, and this lens treats a soul as a loaded structure, asking the only question a master mason ever asks: where the load goes, and what happens at the place it concentrates.
The operation. Coagulation. The soul is fixed as the foundation, set to bear and never to rise.
In the worker. Held to Zenith or past, the idea is set as law by [Th] Foundation + [Len] Line, and the world gives way that far: locks a Domain’s weight and causal sequence to Atla’zon’s own kneeling burden, granting immense structural and temporal stability at the cost of freezing all forward motion within the field.
Price in the self. Reserve, plus the caster’s own joints and breath take on Atla’zon’s characteristic strain — genuine physical burden, not metaphor, for hours after release.
Flaw. A foundation bears whatever presses down on it, and nothing ever asked it to hold on. Pull on it, the one load it does not answer, and it does not give gracefully. It parts.
Counter. [Wy] Motion refuses its claim before it settles; the contrary idea is Cymorath or Abython.
The Measurewrights’ line. Compressive load path and creep.

In numbers. Field-wide time dilation caps at roughly 0.3x normal flow rate for the duration; structural load tolerance roughly doubles.
The target. Anything inside the field moves and ages measurably slower relative to the outside; falling objects behave as though gravity itself thickened.
Cost and backlash. The caster’s own joints and breath take on Atla’zon’s characteristic strain — genuine physical burden, not metaphor, for hours after release.
Counterplay. [Wy] Motion brought in at the field’s edge runs inward as a wave of motion given back, and the locked burden lets go all at once rather than gradually.
The Canyon’s Patience
Titan-keyed art · [Uur] Disruption + [Vorn] End · Zenith and above





















WellspringFractura (Wild)OperationSeparationTemperanceZenith and above
Trigger. Target must already be structurally or morally compromised — the glyph guides an existing fault line, it does not create one.
Effect. Guides a controlled, purposeful collapse through a target structure or curse, ensuring the fall clears space rather than merely destroying, as Valmir intends.
How it works.

The idea. The breaking point. Everything has a place where it will go, and this lens shows it to you, in bridges, in friends and in your own left wrist.
The operation. Separation. A thing is parted along the one place where it was always going to part.
In the worker. Held to Zenith or past, the idea is set as law by [Uur] Disruption + [Vorn] End, and the world gives way that far: guides a controlled, purposeful collapse through a target structure or curse, ensuring the fall clears space rather than merely destroying, as Valmir intends.
Price in the self. Reserve, plus if the caster’s own resentments toward the target are unresolved, the collapse tends to ‘choose’ a more destructive trajectory than intended.
Flaw. The lens shows where everything will go, and it cannot leave its bearer out of everything. Under strain a Fractura practitioner reads their own breaking points with perfect clarity, at the worst possible moment.
Counter. [Th] Foundation refuses its claim before it settles; the contrary idea is Orrenthal, Coagula or Redemption.
The Measurewrights’ line. Linear elastic fracture mechanics.

In numbers. Collapse trajectory can be bent up to roughly 30 degrees from the structure’s natural failure line before it resists further steering.
The target. The structure falls along the chosen path, sparing anything outside the redirected collapse zone.
Cost and backlash. If the caster’s own resentments toward the target are unresolved, the collapse tends to ‘choose’ a more destructive trajectory than intended.
Counterplay. [Th] Foundation reinforces the natural fault line before the redirect takes hold, refusing the bend and forcing the original, unsteered collapse instead.
The Closing Eye
Titan-keyed art · [Thru] Hollow + [Au] Death · Revelation and above





















WellspringNihiloth (Wild)OperationDissolutionTemperanceRevelation and above
Trigger. Cast only on a region already showing measurable Essence overcharge (visible saturation, unstable ambient resonance).
Effect. Cleanses a region of overaccumulated Essence by absorbing it into inverted null-space, the way Zar’thuun’s own Wellspring holds absence in shape.
How it works.

The idea. The hollow law. Power by negation: the rule itself unmade, and what stands in the gap.
The operation. Dissolution. The rule itself is loosed until nothing of it is left, and the gap is left standing where it was.
In the worker. Held to Revelation or past, the idea is set as law by [Thru] Hollow + [Au] Death, and the world gives way that far: cleanses a region of overaccumulated Essence by absorbing it into inverted null-space, the way Zar’thuun’s own Wellspring holds absence in shape.
Price in the self. Reserve, plus prolonged proximity erases small, low-significance memories from everyone nearby along with the excess Essence — the mercy and the erasure are mechanically the same process.
Flaw. A rule unmade is unmade for everyone, and the idea has no way to spare its maker. Everything the practitioner brought inside is subject to the same gap, including the parts of themselves they were relying on.
Counter. [El] Life refuses its claim before it settles; the contrary idea is Eidolyn, Oblivara or Monolithion.
The Measurewrights’ line. Destructive interference and the null field.

In numbers. Absorption capacity scales with the null-field’s radius, typically clearing a 10-15 meter overcharge zone per casting.
The target. The overcharged region returns to stable baseline Essence density almost immediately.
Cost and backlash. Prolonged proximity erases small, low-significance memories from everyone nearby along with the excess Essence — the mercy and the erasure are mechanically the same process.
Counterplay. [El] Life reintroduces active Essence generation into the field faster than the sink can absorb it, overwhelming the null-field’s capacity.
The Deep Grid’s Verdict
Titan-keyed art · [Th] Foundation + [Ur] Balance · Zenith and above





















WellspringPetralon (Wild)OperationCoagulationTemperanceZenith and above
Trigger. Cast directly against a structure, army, or soul whose bearing capacity is genuinely in question.
Effect. Translates any burden placed on a structure, army, or soul into honest geometry, revealing exactly whether it can bear what’s asked of it, per Kaldrion’s own law.
How it works.

The idea. The foundation. To become what other things stand on: load taken, carried and sent down, at the price of slowly settling. Breaking, holding and rising are one law seen from three positions, and this lens treats a soul as a loaded structure, asking the only question a master mason ever asks: where the load goes, and what happens at the place it concentrates.
The operation. Coagulation. The soul is fixed as the foundation, set to bear and never to rise.
In the worker. Held to Zenith or past, the idea is set as law by [Th] Foundation + [Ur] Balance, and the world gives way that far: translates any burden placed on a structure, army, or soul into honest geometry, revealing exactly whether it can bear what’s asked of it, per Kaldrion’s own law.
Price in the self. Reserve, plus none to the caster directly — the cost falls entirely on the target being tested, which is why this working is reserved for genuine, consequential verdicts.
Flaw. A foundation bears whatever presses down on it, and nothing ever asked it to hold on. Pull on it, the one load it does not answer, and it does not give gracefully. It parts.
Counter. [Uur] Disruption refuses its claim before it settles; the contrary idea is Cymorath or Abython.
The Measurewrights’ line. Compressive load path and creep.

In numbers. Verdict resolves within a single second regardless of the structure’s complexity.
The target. A structure/soul that can bear the load holds visibly firmer; one that cannot begins failing at its actual weakest point immediately.
Cost and backlash. None to the caster directly — the cost falls entirely on the target being tested, which is why this working is reserved for genuine, consequential verdicts.
Counterplay. [Uur] Disruption corrupts the load-path reading itself, producing a false verdict that can mask a genuinely failing structure or condemn a sound one.
The Era-Forge’s Toll
Titan-keyed art · [Cro] Cycle + [Len] Line · Zenith and above





















WellspringLethegraal (Spirit)OperationDissolutionTemperanceZenith and above
Trigger. Requires a conflict or era that has been genuinely stalled — not merely slow, but structurally unable to resolve on its own.
Effect. Compacts unresolved tension in a Domain into forced historical resolution, ending a stalled conflict or stagnant era by grinding it forward through sheer accumulated consequence, per Chronaeus’s law.
How it works.

The idea. The cup. Time’s mercy hurried along: old pain settles on its own schedule, and no hand chooses what falls.
The operation. Dissolution. Old pain is loosened into the soul on its own schedule until nothing of it is left but plain structure that holds weight.
In the worker. Held to Zenith or past, the idea is set as law by [Cro] Cycle + [Len] Line, and the world gives way that far: compacts unresolved tension in a Domain into forced historical resolution, ending a stalled conflict or stagnant era by grinding it forward through sheer accumulated consequence, per Chronaeus’s law.
Price in the self. Reserve, plus the acceleration doesn’t discriminate meaning from suffering; innocents living through the compressed era age and suffer at the same forced rate as the resolution itself.
Flaw. The cup can hurry time’s mercy and cannot choose where the settling stops, because no hand chooses what falls. Hurry it too far and the old pain does not come to rest but swings past it on every cycle, and the practitioner rocks back and forth rather than settling.
Counter. [Ser] Renewal refuses its claim before it settles; the contrary idea is Cataclysm, Penance or Contrition.
The Measurewrights’ line. Relaxation time.

In numbers. Compression ratio is typically 10:1 to 50:1 — a decade of stalled tension can resolve in roughly a season.
The target. The stalled conflict or era reaches a genuine resolution point, for good or ill, rather than continuing indefinitely.
Cost and backlash. The acceleration doesn’t discriminate meaning from suffering; innocents living through the compressed era age and suffer at the same forced rate as the resolution itself.
Counterplay. [Ser] Renewal introduces a genuinely new growth-vector into the compressed timeline, diffusing the stored pressure into gradual change instead of a single forced toll.
The Ferryman’s Current
Titan-keyed art · [Au] Death + [Vor] Return · Zenith and above





















WellspringSomnalis (Fate)OperationFermentationTemperanceZenith and above
Trigger. Cast at the exact moment of death, not before or after.
Effect. Rides the Ethereal Flow itself, carrying a soul between death and re-embodiment along Sylorin’s own current rather than waiting for natural passage.
How it works.

The idea. Living among what might be. The near possibilities of the Plane of Fate held in view at once, each with its odds on it, and a soul at ease in the not knowing.
The operation. Fermentation. What is about to happen is kept working in the vessel, every way it might yet go still alive in it and none of them settled.
In the worker. Held to Zenith or past, the idea is set as law by [Au] Death + [Vor] Return, and the world gives way that far: rides the Ethereal Flow itself, carrying a soul between death and re-embodiment along Sylorin’s own current rather than waiting for natural passage.
Price in the self. Reserve, plus A soul moved this fast arrives with the full, undiminished emotional charge of its death still attached — genuine trauma the receiving body/vessel must be ready to handle immediately.
Flaw. The idea holds only while nothing is certain. A soul that lets one bright branch stand for the whole river has stopped living among what might be and started believing, and it acts on that branch with everything it has, though it carried eleven percent of the weight.
Counter. [Wy] Motion refuses its claim before it settles; the contrary idea is Fixatio.
The Measurewrights’ line. Ensemble forecasting.

In numbers. Passage time drops from the natural hours-to-days window to under a minute.
The target. The departing soul arrives at its next state with full continuity of self, without the disorientation of unassisted drift.
Cost and backlash. A soul moved this fast arrives with the full, undiminished emotional charge of its death still attached — genuine trauma the receiving body/vessel must be ready to handle immediately.
Counterplay. [Wy] Motion introduces turbulence into the current itself, which can strand or scatter the soul mid-passage.
The Green Chord
Titan-keyed art · [Vael] Renewal + [Yn] Bloom · Zenith and above





















WellspringRebirthine (Wild)OperationFermentationTemperanceZenith and above
Trigger. Requires the dying practitioner’s active, willing consent — the transfer cannot be forced.
Effect. Transfers an incomplete Temperance path or dying Trait directly into a successor vessel, the way a bloodline’s lost art resurfaces generations later under Florwyn’s law.
How it works.

The idea. The cycle. Loss taken as the first step of the next building, what is broken down paying for what comes up.
The operation. Fermentation. What is broken down is let rot so that what comes up next can feed on it.
In the worker. Held to Zenith or past, the idea is set as law by [Vael] Renewal + [Yn] Bloom, and the world gives way that far: transfers an incomplete Temperance path or dying Trait directly into a successor vessel, the way a bloodline’s lost art resurfaces generations later under Florwyn’s law.
Price in the self. Reserve, plus Personality bleed-through is standard, not exceptional; successors report intrusive thoughts and reflexes not their own for weeks afterward.
Flaw. The cycle pays for every building with a loss, and with nothing outside to break down it breaks down the worker. It eats structure faster than it rebuilds, and it does not recognize the point at which there is nothing left to spend.
Counter. [Uur] Disruption refuses its claim before it settles; the contrary idea is Monolithion.
The Measurewrights’ line. Apoptosis and autophagy.

In numbers. Transfer completes within the dying practitioner’s final minutes; the successor’s own Temperance Stage shifts by up to two Stages immediately.
The target. Successor experiences the inherited path as sudden, vivid procedural memory — knowing how without having practiced.
Cost and backlash. Personality bleed-through is standard, not exceptional; successors report intrusive thoughts and reflexes not their own for weeks afterward.
Counterplay. [Uur] Disruption corrupts the transcription mid-transfer, producing a successor with fragments of the path and none of its coherence — often worse than no transfer at all.
The Hollow That Watches
Titan-keyed art · [Thal] Silence + [Ie] Perception · Zenith and above





















WellspringTenebra (Wild)OperationSeparationTemperanceZenith and above
Trigger. Requires total ambient silence already present or actively enforced before the glyph can take hold.
Effect. Silences a region and forces every mind within it to confront one true fear directly, extracting the revelation that follows, per Ilgrimm’s own law.
How it works.

The idea. The hidden shadow. Going unseen, quieter than the world around you, and the old question of what you are hiding from.
The operation. Separation. The soul is parted from the world’s notice and kept quieter than everything around it.
In the worker. Held to Zenith or past, the idea is set as law by [Thal] Silence + [Ie] Perception, and the world gives way that far: silences a region and forces every mind within it to confront one true fear directly, extracting the revelation that follows, per Ilgrimm’s own law.
Price in the self. Reserve, plus the caster is not exempted by the silence they enforced; their own fear surfaces in the same beat as everyone else’s.
Flaw. Going unseen is always hiding from someone, and a soul can hide only from what it has thought of. Watched from the one direction they did not plan for, a Tenebra practitioner is a very bright thing indeed. Pushed too hard, the hiding fills up: everything swallowed is still in the Shell, and a practitioner kept quieter than the world past their limit lets it all go at once and lights up on every sense in the room.
Counter. [Se] Song refuses its claim before it settles; the contrary idea is Penanceflare, Judicium or Aurevane.
The Measurewrights’ line. Signal-to-noise reduction.

In numbers. The revelation lasts a single beat — under one second of subjective exposure — but the psychological aftereffect lasts far longer.
The target. Each mind confronts its single most load-bearing fear, not a generic or random one; the specificity is what makes the revelation useful (or devastating).
Cost and backlash. The caster is not exempted by the silence they enforced; their own fear surfaces in the same beat as everyone else’s.
Counterplay. [Se] Song reintroduces harmonic noise into the silence, and the beam cannot form without a genuinely quiet field to strobe through.
The Mirrored Scale
Titan-keyed art · [Ur] Balance + [Sel] Measure · Zenith and above





















WellspringJudicium (Wild)OperationSeparationTemperanceZenith and above
Trigger. Requires an actual signed, sworn, or spoken commitment already in effect — the glyph mirrors real reciprocity, it cannot invent an obligation.
Effect. Mirrors all incoming Essence back upon its source in exact kind — the metaphysical basis of karmic reciprocity, made instantaneous through Dazkar’s own Wellspring.
How it works.

The idea. Truth told apart. Discernment that knows what a thing is made of, and whether it is lying, from the mark it cannot help leaving.
The operation. Separation. A thing is parted from what it claims to be, the true told apart from the false by the mark it cannot help leaving.
In the worker. Held to Zenith or past, the idea is set as law by [Ur] Balance + [Sel] Measure, and the world gives way that far: mirrors all incoming Essence back upon its source in exact kind — the metaphysical basis of karmic reciprocity, made instantaneous through Dazkar’s own Wellspring.
Price in the self. Reserve, plus the caster is bound by the same mirror for the working’s duration — any cruelty in how they cast it returns to them first, before it ever reaches the target.
Flaw. Discernment tells everything apart and cannot choose to leave anything untold. Off guard, every object in view reports what it is made of at once, and the reader loses the power to put any of it first. Pushed past the point where a reading only reads, telling a thing apart becomes taking it apart: the read starts to pass judgment, which can turn away force or at the very top end a life, and since it has no way to look at one thing only, it takes the reader’s own memory in the same stroke.
Counter. [Ve] Desire refuses its claim before it settles; the contrary idea is Tenebra or Eidolyn.
The Measurewrights’ line. Emission and absorption spectroscopy.

In numbers. Reflection is exact to within the same Stage-band the caster operates in; no amplification or attenuation.
The target. Whoever breaks the commitment receives back precisely the Essence-cost of the harm they caused, undiminished.
Cost and backlash. The caster is bound by the same mirror for the working’s duration — any cruelty in how they cast it returns to them first, before it ever reaches the target.
Counterplay. [Ve] Desire introduces a new, unmirrored want into the field, breaking the closed reflective loop the working depends on.
The Pyric Refinement
Titan-keyed art · [Ra] Flame + [Asa] Creation · Zenith and above





















WellspringExuroth (Wild)OperationCalcinationTemperanceZenith and above
Trigger. Requires the caster to name, honestly, one thing about the target fragment/artifact that is false or unworthy.
Effect. Burns away everything false or unworthy in a soul fragment or artifact, refining what remains into pure, usable Essence vapor, by Prometheus’s law that what is false must burn so that what is true can be refined out of it.
How it works.

The idea. The trial by fire. Power comes only through ordeal, plunged and reheated and plunged again, until the soul holds a hardness no gentle road could have given it.
The operation. Calcination. The soul is burned, plunged and burned again, until only the hardness that lives through the fire is left.
In the worker. Held to Zenith or past, the idea is set as law by [Ra] Flame + [Asa] Creation, and the world gives way that far: burns away everything false or unworthy in a soul fragment or artifact, refining what remains into pure, usable Essence vapor, by Prometheus’s law that what is false must burn so that what is true can be refined out of it.
Price in the self. Reserve, plus the process cannot distinguish sentiment from falsehood with full precision — genuinely valued memories attached to the false part burn away too.
Flaw. The trial gives hardness only to a soul that lives through it, and the idea cannot tell an ordeal from a ruin. Plunge again too soon, without the rest between, and the soul comes out hard, brittle and split along the lines of its own trials.
Counter. [Vael] Renewal refuses its claim before it settles; the contrary idea is Absolution or Ascensio.
The Measurewrights’ line. Quench and temper.

In numbers. Refinement removes roughly the bottom 20-40% of a fragment’s Essence-purity, proportional to how much falsity the caster correctly identified.
The target. What remains afterward is measurably more stable and ‘honest’ by every Harmonics Fidelity metric.
Cost and backlash. The process cannot distinguish sentiment from falsehood with full precision — genuinely valued memories attached to the false part burn away too.
Counterplay. [Vael] Renewal reintroduces new growth into the fragment mid-burn, diluting the purity threshold and letting false material survive alongside true.
The Skyfire Pulse
Titan-keyed art · [Wy] Motion + [Noq] Wind · Zenith and above





















WellspringIgnivale (Wild)OperationCalcinationTemperanceZenith and above
Trigger. Requires a genuine exhale — the working cannot be cast while holding breath or through an external air source.
Effect. Exhales a ribbon of purifying plasma that burns Essence impurities from everyone in its path and reawakens dormant Wellsprings, echoing Omnis’s own periodic Skyfire Pulse.
How it works.

The idea. The spark. The smallest beginning that goes on to pay for itself, so that the gap between wanting a thing and doing it closes to almost nothing.
The operation. Calcination. One point of fire is set to the work at the first degree, and the burning is left to pay its own way.
In the worker. Held to Zenith or past, the idea is set as law by [Wy] Motion + [Noq] Wind, and the world gives way that far: exhales a ribbon of purifying plasma that burns Essence impurities from everyone in its path and reawakens dormant Wellsprings, echoing Omnis’s own periodic Skyfire Pulse.
Price in the self. Reserve, plus the caster’s own respiratory system takes the first pass of the purification, leaving a raw throat and reduced stamina for hours.
Flaw. With the gap between wanting and doing closed, the soul has no moment left in which to decide. Any stray feeling in the room is beginning enough, and the working fires without the practitioner having decided to fire it.
Counter. [Au] Death refuses its claim before it settles; the contrary idea is Pyraeon or Hypnather.
The Measurewrights’ line. Minimum ignition energy and the activation barrier.

In numbers. Burn radius and duration scale with lung capacity and Stage; typical range is a 4-6 meter cone lasting under two seconds.
The target. Impurities/corruption in the swept area burn away cleanly; healthy tissue and Essence pass through unharmed.
Cost and backlash. The caster’s own respiratory system takes the first pass of the purification, leaving a raw throat and reduced stamina for hours.
Counterplay. [Au] Death starves the working of the sustained breath-rhythm it needs, cutting the Pulse short before it completes its sweep.
The Somnum Flow
Titan-keyed art · [Ka] Dream + [Vl] Veil · Zenith and above





















WellspringOneirion (Spirit)OperationSublimationTemperanceZenith and above
Trigger. Requires the caster to have first witnessed the target’s genuine, unguarded self-image (not a performed one).
Effect. Opens the Somnum Flow directly, letting the caster reshape a target’s self-image at the root — redefining what they believe themselves to be, and therefore what they can become.
How it works.

The idea. Dream as a place. Work done in the space of what can be thought, reaching a soul where no line of sight runs, because no soul was ever in the room.
The operation. Sublimation. The working is lifted off every bench into the space of what can be thought, and comes down again in a soul.
In the worker. Held to Zenith or past, the idea is set as law by [Ka] Dream + [Vl] Veil, and the world gives way that far: opens the Somnum Flow directly, letting the caster reshape a target’s self-image at the root — redefining what they believe themselves to be, and therefore what they can become.
Price in the self. Reserve, plus the channel is bidirectional while open; the caster’s own self-image is exposed to reciprocal reshaping for as long as it stays active.
Flaw. A dream is a place with no ground under it, and nothing done there knows where it is in a room. A working that was true in the space of what can be thought lands nowhere in particular when it has to come down into a real one.
Counter. [Ie] Perception refuses its claim before it settles; the contrary idea is Mirithane or Chthonica.
The Measurewrights’ line. Configuration space.

In numbers. Reshaping takes effect gradually over days, consistent with genuine belief change rather than instant compulsion.
The target. The target’s behavior, confidence, and capabilities shift to match the new self-image over that window — a real, not cosmetic, change.
Cost and backlash. The channel is bidirectional while open; the caster’s own self-image is exposed to reciprocal reshaping for as long as it stays active.
Counterplay. [Ie] Perception lets the target compare their reshaped self-image against an outside, trusted witness’s account, and the discrepancy collapses the rewrite.
The Stillwater Rite
Titan-keyed art · [Vor] Return + [Cro] Cycle · Revelation and above





















WellspringCymorath (Wild)OperationSublimationTemperanceRevelation and above
Trigger. Requires the target to already be in genuine crisis (dying, catastrophically wounded, or cursed beyond normal stabilization).
Effect. Holds a target’s Essence motionless in perfectly reflective stasis, neither emitting nor absorbing, until the caster chooses to release it — Vohrin’s own Stillwater law made portable.
How it works.

The idea. Freedom in the air. The world read as a set of open ways, so that moving becomes a matter of noticing which way is already open.
The operation. Sublimation. The soul is made volatile, so that it rises and goes by whatever way already lies open.
In the worker. Held to Revelation or past, the idea is set as law by [Vor] Return + [Cro] Cycle, and the world gives way that far: holds a target’s Essence motionless in perfectly reflective stasis, neither emitting nor absorbing, until the caster chooses to release it — Vohrin’s own Stillwater law made portable.
Price in the self. Reserve, plus held too long, the target begins to forget their own purpose for living, per Vohrin’s law — stasis without end curdles into a different kind of ending.
Flaw. Freedom in the air goes by whatever way is already open, and it has no say in which way that is. Lean on it too long and the practitioner follows the open way instead of the intended line, and arrives somewhere efficient that is not where they meant to be.
Counter. [Ra] Flame refuses its claim before it settles; the contrary idea is Chthonica or Petralon.
The Measurewrights’ line. Vector fields and the Lorentz force.

In numbers. Stasis can hold indefinitely with no measurable degradation, unlike ordinary preservation methods which slowly fail.
The target. The target neither worsens nor improves for the stasis’s duration — frozen exactly at the moment of casting.
Cost and backlash. Held too long, the target begins to forget their own purpose for living, per Vohrin’s law — stasis without end curdles into a different kind of ending.
Counterplay. [Ra] Flame brings want and heat back into the stillness, and once the stillness is broken the target falls back into normal (and often catastrophic) time.

the-war-cycle/the-army/index.content:
The muster song of the Red Ferry Company runs to nineteen verses, of which two concern the enemy and the other seventeen concern the pay.
What an army is made of, who pays for it, and how it moves.


The Order of Battle What an army is made of, and who owns it
The Long March Bread moves. Essence does not
The Fisc — Paying for a Siege Sieges are lost in ledgers far more often than on walls. This is the clock under the Kharven arc.



Read next: The Order of Battle; The Practitioner Problem, for the practitioner in the line; The Sixteen Stages, for what a Stage is worth in a levy.

the-war-cycle/the-army/the-fisc-—-paying.title: The Fisc — Paying for a Siege
the-war-cycle/the-army/the-fisc-—-paying.content:
The funeral of Captain Thora Hjerting is the best-attended audit in the north. She held the Third Wall at Brennholt through the winter of the Short Mark, and when she dropped dead on the fire-step in the eleventh week, six hundred men carried her through the snow on a shield painted blue and gold, with horns and the whole hold following and the sutlers’ wives handing out hot ale. At the graveside Fat Tormod, sutler to the Third Wall, climbed onto a barrel with her account book, wept, and read out what she owed him, and the crowd slowly understood what they were hearing. She had been paying the company herself since the sixth week. Her horse had gone first, then her mother’s silver, then the gold from her back teeth, and she had died of hunger with a full company at her back and told nobody. The reeve’s paymaster had come for the ale. When Tormod finished, the Third Wall put down its cups without a word, formed up in the yard in perfect order, with no officer left to tell it to, and stood looking at him.
Nobody in Brennholt was shouting, and the paymaster lived to describe it, so I can report that he found the silence worse. Everything that follows concerns how a crown gets to that yard, and how the man on the other side of the wall is getting there too.
Sieges are lost in ledgers far more often than on walls. This is the clock under the Kharven arc.

The whole art of war is reduced to money.

I. The Governing Question
Kharven has never been issued an Accord instrument and has never asked for one. That is a boast in peacetime and a noose in a siege, because the Accord’s credit runs on the Accord’s instruments, and an instrument only binds inside the Accord’s jurisdiction.
So the Seat’s real problem lies well behind the wall.
To borrow at scale, Kharven must accept an instrument. To accept an instrument is to accept the jurisdiction that enforces it. A factor house will lend against a bill it can sue on. It will not lend against a custom that has never been written and cannot be cited in any court that exists.
Everything below is the Seat trying to avoid signing, and running out of ways.
II. What the Seat Can Actually Raise
Six instruments. Each pays this season and costs something next.
1. The stack levy
Compulsory purchase of stores at a price the Crown sets, against a tally, redeemable later. Woodpiles, root caches, borts, seal fat, hides, horn, bone.
This is the fastest revenue available and the most dangerous thing the Seat can do, because in a country whose religion is the Sky, a low stack is a moral condition rather than a misfortune. How’s your stack is a diagnostic. A household stripped by the levy has been made, in the eyes of everybody who greets it, into the kind of household that failed to prepare.
The historical pattern is exact and should run in full. Purveyance produced abuse and corruption on a scale that forced nationwide investigations and the removal of most purveyors from office; it was eventually surrendered for military purposes under sustained pressure; and it was revived at the next war with instructions that purveyors be fair, pay a fair price, and leave the temples alone. Every one of those three instructions was issued because the opposite happened last time.
Cost next season: the tallies. A tally is a promise, the Crown has issued thousands, and the day they are presented is a day the Crown chooses between paying and being seen not to.
2. Labor-debt and meat-sharing
The customary instruments, unwritten, enormously powerful, and unenforceable against a man who simply refuses. The Seat can call on them, and the calling works because refusing is socially ruinous rather than illegal.
This is real revenue with one hard limit: it can be called once well and twice badly. A custom leaned on until it breaks does not come back, and the households know exactly how many times it has been called this winter, because that is the kind of thing households count.
3. The forced loan
The great households are asked for silver, in a room, individually, by name, with the amount already written. Nobody refuses in the room. What happens afterward is that the amount is remembered, the loan is not repaid on time, and a forced loan converts a supporter into a creditor, which is a different political animal entirely.
4. Debasement
The Crown’s coin, reduced in fineness, minted in greater number from the same metal.
Debasement is a fiscal weapon, chosen on purpose, and it works. The Great Debasement financed a real war effectively, and the tell separating an aggressive debasement from a defensive one sits in the mint accounts: mintage fees run high on an aggressive debasement and low on a defensive one. Anybody with the mint rolls can tell which one the Crown is running, and the assay houses always find out.
And the four quarters have their own trap already built. Silver is the accounting unit of every serious ledger in the four quarters, and the western silver mark is the standard the Accord quotes everything against. A Kharven mark that no longer holds its fineness is a mark the assay houses will discount, and a discounted coin buys less from exactly the merchants a besieged capital needs most.
Cost next season: the discount is permanent and arrives faster than the benefit. Grain sellers reprice within a turn. Wages reprice within three.
5. Sale of standing
Offices, exemptions, hunting rights, precedence, and the right to be excused the levy. The last of those is the one that actually sells, and it guarantees the levy falls hardest on households with no silver to buy their way out, which is the households the Sky faith says should be given the first bowl.
6. Accord credit
A bill of exchange drawn on a factor house, remitted to the Seat, discounted heavily for distance and for risk. The only instrument on the list that produces silver in quantity and quickly.
And the terms are the plot. A factor house lends against enforceable security. Enforceable means a court. The court is the Accord’s. So the security offered is some combination of the customs on a named road, the Wellspring beneath a named holding, a Guild charter over the Seat’s own market, or the right to seat a Regional Envoy. Every one of those is a piece of jurisdiction, and once one is signed the rest become negotiable.
A crown that signs is solvent and is no longer sovereign in the way it was last week. A crown that refuses keeps something nobody can eat.
III. The Pay Clock
The mechanism that makes the fisc a timer rather than a background fact.
Pay must reach the men across distance, with sufficient regularity to prevent mutiny, and in denominations small enough to spend locally. All three conditions, every time. Failure of any one is failure of all.
The third is the one that will bite Kharven, because the mechanism is already there. Copper is the money of ordinary life and the only metal money most people ever hold. Copper is also the windings of every great array (a standing runed working), laid by hand and worth more by weight melted than struck, and every great array raised in two centuries has produced a copper famine within three years. A siege raises arrays, on both sides of the wall. The Seat can hold silver and still be unable to pay a soldier, because there is nothing in the chest a soldier can buy bread with.
What keeps an army fed in the meantime is short-term credit: unpaid bills to suppliers, advances made by officers out of their own pockets, and temporary loans arranged by intermediaries. That is the life thread of army finance and it is invisible until it snaps. Long before a mutiny there is a captain who has been paying his own company for six weeks and has stopped sleeping.
The dissolution schedule involves no dice. It is a sequence of things that happen.

































ArrearsWhat happensOne turnGrumbling. Sutlers extend credit and mark it upTwo turnsOfficers begin advancing pay themselves. Small theft becomes normal and goes unpunished, because punishing it would mean admitting why it is happeningThree turnsForaging becomes indistinguishable from robbery in the surrounding district. The district stops selling and starts hidingFour turnsDesertion by ones and twos, at night, from the least-watched posts, by the men with families near enough to reachFive turnsThe line holds together and presents. Men assemble in order, without officers, and ask for what they are owed. A riot would be far less dangerousBeyondUnpaid troops have historically marched, leaderless, on the nearest thing worth taking, and taken it
The presentation is the beat worth writing. A formation, silent, correct, standing where it can be seen, waiting, with no mob in it anywhere. Every officer present knows exactly what it is.
IV. The Other Ledger
The besieger is not solvent either, and this is the part fiction forgets.
An army sitting outside a wall eats every day and produces nothing. Its costs are worse per head than the defender’s, because the defender is at home and the besieger’s every loaf has been carried. Sieges are races between two failing treasuries, and the wall is a way of keeping score.
Contribution. Payment taken from the surrounding country in exchange for not sacking it. The largest single revenue a besieging army has, collected systematically, with schedules and receipts, turning the countryside around a siege into a taxed province of the invader within a season.
Foraging, which is contribution without the receipt, and which begins automatically as soon as the besieger’s own pay is late.
Ransom, which is why a valuable prisoner is a fiscal event before he is anything else.
And the sack, which discipline has very little to do with. It is the settlement of arrears by other means, understood as such by every soldier and every commander, which is why the terms offered before a storm are a real negotiation about money rather than a courtesy.
So the defender has a lever nobody uses in fiction. A besieging army four turns in arrears is an army whose commander needs a settlement more than the defender does. The Seat that knows how far behind the enemy’s pay is knows more than the Seat that knows where his engines are.

Read next: What Things Cost, for the prices; Monster Cores, for the cores and bought Stages that are war materiel.

the-war-cycle/the-army/the-long-march.title: The Long March
the-war-cycle/the-army/the-long-march.content:
Marshal Odo Hartshorn of Wend is remembered for one idea. In the spring of his last campaign he proposed to carry his practitioners’ refills along with them, the way he carried their biscuit, and he sent three hundred sealed casks of Grade I stock (raw Aether out of a vein) up the Wend road on sixty ox-wagons painted red and gold, with a band in front. Sealed stock leaks, and it leaks faster when jolted and faster beside other stock. By the ninth day the column shone. The oxen’s breath came out rose-colored, the carters’ hands glowed to the wrist, the ruts behind the wagons held a pale light till morning, and a shepherd boy thirty miles off was able to tell the enemy’s scouts exactly where to ride, adding that it was very pretty. At the far end, four days past his last vein, Hartshorn ordered a cask broached for Dame Alienor Crane, the best practitioner he had, in front of the staff. She drank a pint on his word. She was sick for nineteen days, with her aura the color of a week-old bruise, and the rest of the casks went into one excellent ward around a market town nobody needed. The ranks called him Old Moonshine until they ran out of food, and then they called him something else.
Hartshorn’s mistake is the subject of this document. Two kinds of supply feed an army, one of them will go in a wagon and the other will not, and the people who wrote the following had been counting the difference for four hundred years.
Supply, Distance, and the Refilling of Magazines

Issued jointly by the Logistics and Supply Division and the Strategic Division. The vein schedules appended to the original are not reproduced.
Third of the War Cycle.
Bread moves. Essence does not.
Every strategic decision the Accord has ever made follows from those five words.

The Two Supplies
An army requires two things it cannot manufacture in the field, and they behave in opposite ways.
The first is food, fodder, bolts, iron and cloth. Heavy, dull, and perfectly transportable. They can be stockpiled, requisitioned, seized, spoiled and counted. Their arithmetic is unforgiving and entirely soluble by anyone willing to do it.
The second is Essence, and it cannot be supplied at all in the sense a quartermaster means.
Why Essence cannot be shipped





















PropertyConsequenceIt leaksSealed stock loses measurably in transit and loses faster under motion, heat and proximity to other stock. A cask that left the depot full arrives at a figure the assay houses can predict and the quartermaster cannot preventIt cannot be assayed in the fieldClass (where the stock came from), Fidelity (how close it runs to the reference figure) and Carry (how much of its origin came with it) require a coil (the assay house’s great brass instrument), a reference salt and a Measurewright. None of these travels. A commander in the field holds stock whose actual contents are a matter of faith in the seal on itIt does not survive its ownerEssence organized by a Soul Crystal dies with the Crystal. A practitioner cannot be topped up from a barrel any more than a man can be topped up from another man’s blood without consequence. Grade I stock pulled from a vein can fuel an array (a standing runed working). It cannot refill a practitioner

The conclusion has governed Accord strategy for four centuries and is stated in the Division’s manuals in one line. A practitioner is refilled by the ground they stand on, or not at all.

A practitioner pulls Aether out of the world around them, refines it in the Soul Crystal into Essence, and holds that Essence as reserve, so where they stand decides how fast they fill. A Wellspring is one of the sixty types of Aether, and a site where one type pools is called a Core in common speech, fed by a channel the surveys call a vein. Rich ground fills a fighter in hours and thin ground starves them for days. The ranks say fat ground and lean ground, and any sergeant can tell you which he is standing on by how his practitioner’s temper is holding. A fight Draft (a bottled working) is the one exception anybody has found, and it is a loan: one fighter, one bad minute, and a crash that collects with interest. No quartermaster has ever supplied a march on them, though several have died trying.
The Vein Map Is the Road Map
Show a competent Crown marshal the saturation survey and he can draw you the campaign without being told the objective.
Because a practitioner refills at any useful rate only on rich ground, and rich ground lies along the veins, an army carrying practitioners is chained to Wellspring geography in a way an ordinary army is not chained to anything.
Campaign routes run vein to vein. The distance between usable veins sets the maximum operational reach of any force that intends to fight with practitioners at the far end of it. A commander who marches four days past his last vein is marching an increasingly ordinary army, and every day beyond that point he is closer to fielding twelve thousand people and no siege engines.

Veins are objectives whether or not anyone wants them. Half the sieges in the record are of places nobody valued, sited where they are because a vein is under them. The town grew around the vein, the fort was built to hold the town, and four centuries later two armies are killing each other over a market square because of geology.

Denial is cheaper than capture · A vein never has to be taken. It only has to be made useless. A Sealwright team can foul its usable output for a fortnight at a fraction of the cost of holding it, a pair of hired hedge-workers (country practitioners, paid by the job) can salt the ground above it so that Aether will not pool there, and a keeper with a grudge or a purse in his hand can simply close the Core. The old soldier’s rule is to take the fight off rich ground and onto salted, bled or thin ground, and let the other side discover what they had been standing on. The Accord’s own law restricts this severely. The Accord’s own forces have done it eleven times under Writ.
Replenishment is slow and public · Pulling from a vein takes hours, cannot be hurried, and produces a signature the War-Priests of the opposing side can read at distance. An army that is refilling has announced where it is and that it is currently unable to fight. Interdiction of replenishment is the single most productive operation available to a competent staff and the least glamorous.
Poor ground breaks coalitions · Contingents that have marched past their last vein begin to argue about who gets the next one. The Division’s field manuals include a procedure for allocating vein access between allied contingents. The procedure has never worked.
The Ordinary Arithmetic
Unchanged by any amount of metaphysics, and the reason most campaigns fail.
A man · Roughly a pound and a half of grain a day, more under load and in cold. Bread and biscuit keep; flour keeps better; grain keeps best and requires mills, which is why armies capture mills.

A horse · Roughly ten times a man’s weight in fodder, and this single figure governs everything.
Fodder is bulk, bulk is wagons, wagons need horses, and horses need fodder. An army’s transport eats its own cargo, and past a certain distance from the depot the wagons are carrying nothing but the food of the animals pulling them.

March rate · Twelve miles a day on road for a formed column. Ten for the baggage, which is why the baggage is always behind and why an army that outruns its train is an army that will halt. Off road, in weather, or through country that has been stripped, less, and sometimes nothing.
Water · Considered last and kills first. An army standing still fouls its own water within days.
Foraging and the fed-forward problem
An army that stops eats out its surroundings in about a week and then must move or starve. The instinct of the inexperienced is to fall back on the depot. The correct answer, and the one every experienced commander reaches, is to go forward into country that has not been stripped.

This is why armies advance when they appear to have no reason to, why retreats are more lethal than advances, and why a force driven back over ground it has already consumed dies in numbers no battle would produce.

The Season
Campaigns run from the first grass to the end of harvest and stop, because horses cannot eat what is not growing and transported dry fodder consumes the transport that carries it.

The tightest weeks are those before harvest, when last year’s stores are gone and this year’s is standing green in the field.
Armies moving in that window take the crop before it ripens, which feeds them badly and starves the district completely, and the second-order deaths from that decision exceed the battle’s by an order the Division does not publish.

Winter quarters are billeted on the countryside. The army stops being an army and becomes forty thousand unwelcome guests.
Why the Accord campaigns in winter anyway
Because the vein does not care what season it is, and a force willing to accept the fodder cost can reach an objective in the months when nobody expects a force to be able to reach anything.
Three of the Legion’s four decisive campaigns were winter campaigns. The Division’s own accounting notes that the objectives were taken, that the horse establishment was destroyed in each case, and that the replacement of horses took longer than the replacement of men.
Field Alchemy
What can and cannot be produced on campaign, and why the answer is less than commanders assume.
The Long Furnace does not move. Neither does a certified circle, a sealed workshop, a coil (the assay instrument), or a Measurewright’s reference salt. The consequence is that a campaign column can produce nothing above the third tier and can assay nothing at all.
What Travels
Wick-Salt · Cutwater Tincture · Bone-Gray Compress · Deadlight Phials · Gray Standing Chalk.
Household and field stock, made elsewhere, carried sealed, used and discarded
What Can Be Made In A Column
Repairs, dressings, luting for what is already assembled, and the re-sealing of stock whose seals have failed in transit.
Nothing that requires sustained heat or a standing
What Cannot
Everything reserved above Tier Four, all Threshold work, and every Conjunction.
A Conjunction bench requires a wall built light on purpose and a column has no walls at all
So the alchemical arm of a campaign is a distribution problem rather than a production one, and the officer responsible for it is a clerk with a manifest rather than a master with a crucible. Guild companies bring their own and share nothing.
Unresolved Entries
Transit loss · Sealed stock loses at a rate the assay houses can predict and no workshop can prevent. Four sealing improvements have been entered in the last century. The rate has not moved.
Vein denial under Accord law · Restricted severely, done eleven times under Writ. Whether the restriction binds contracted companies operating on Accord commission is the same unexamined question raised in the Order of Battle and has the same answer, which is that nobody has asked.
Allocation between contingents · The procedure exists. The procedure has never worked. No replacement has been drafted.

Whether a practitioner can be refilled from a Crystal · Not from a vessel, not from a barrel, and not from another living practitioner by any lawful means.
The qualifier in that sentence has been queried twice and struck twice.


Read next: Stacking and Spending, for what a reserve can bear; The Common Drafts, for what is in the wagon.
